Description: The harmony between the three co-owners of this restaurant is clearly evident, as they all have the same vision – something that can also seen in the professionalism of the staff, who are always ready to enhance the guest experience. In this contemporary space with an urban vibe that blends in perfectly with its paintings, tiled walls and natural stone, the main features here are the elegant counter, where customers can watch the magic happen, plus the charming outdoor patio. At the helm in the kitchen, French chef Hervé Pronzato (after whom the restaurant takes its name, ably assisted by Grigoris Kikis and George Efthimopoulos (front of house manager), conjures up fusion dishes influenced by French, Asian and Italian cuisine which can savoured on a single tasting menu. Standout options include “The Amberjack” and “The Vanilla”, each prepared with perfect balance and finesse. When you make your reservation, you will receive a digital code that gets you through the front door!

Name: Hytra
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant with plenty of innate charm, this could be the perfect option for you. Hytra is located inside the lush garden of Megaron Music hall, in a modern building that blends the fine aspects of contemporary design, the breathtaking view of Athens and the Athenian sky. Housing a balcony, a unique dining experience is offered under the stars and a warm, atmospheric inside dining area where guests can enjoy memorable dining experiences. The contemporary-style Greek cuisine on offer here, featuring fine textures and meticulous presentation, is based around Greek ingredients and herbs grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, all of which are very clearly evident in its sauces, creams, seasonings, and even its cocktails. Choose between the à la carte and tree enticing tasting menus, one of which (Think Green) is vegetarian.

Name: CTC Urban Gastronomy
Description: If a dining experience under the stars appeals to you, this highly-sought-after restaurant, particularly during the summer months, will definitely fit the bill thanks to its charming urban terrace dotted with verdant trees and shrubs. Nor will the interior disappoint, with an elegant dining room decorated in soft colours and boasting a sophisticated ambience and subdued lighting. Here, chef Alexandros Tsiotinis, ably supported by his team, champions modern Mediterranean cuisine that is characterised by dishes that are meticulously prepared and extremely creative. More often than not based around classic dishes, including some from abroad, these are showcased in options Such as sea bass ceviche, Pesto calamari and a reinterpreted version of Tarte tatin. The surprise 11-course tasting menu is gradually revealed by serving staff as if they are unveiling a secret. You can also choose some excellent wine pairings to accompany you on this gastronomic journey!

Name: Spondi
Description: In this elegant restaurant close to a busy square behind the ancient Panathenaic Stadium, enjoy highly professional service, attractive vaulted dining rooms, and two Mediterranean-inspired terraces perfect for alfresco dining and a romantic candlelit supper. The cooking here is centred around elaborate and highly visual contemporary French cuisine that is showcased via an array of à la carte dishes as well as on an enticing “Discovery” tasting menu. Seasonal produce is very much to the fore here, although some ever-popular ingredients (crab, langoustine, lamb, chocolate etc) feature all year round. Particularly friendly and attentive service is a constant here!

Name: The Zillers Rooftop Gastronomy
Description: This restaurant occupies the former family home of the German architect Ernst Zillers, who came to Athens to design some of its public buildings, fell in love with the city and remained here for the rest of his life. The building, which is situated next to the Greek Orthodox cathedral and has now been converted into a hotel (Zillers Boutique Hotel), boasts a rooftop terrace and multi-purpose Roof Garden with fine view of the cathedral and the Acropolis. The Zillers restaurant is only open in the evening and chef Vasilis Roussos offers two tasting menus: Synecdoche and Synthesis, both with creative dishes of traditional Greek influence and touches of international flavour. One standout dish was the Prawn Valley, a refreshing combination of raw prawns with a delicate tomato sauce, bergamot and kumquat that will definitely leave a lasting memory. The wine list also features a variety of Greek options to pair with your meal.

Name: Pelagos
Description: If you’re keen to escape the hustle and bustle of Athens, why not consider a visit to the Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel, a luxury resort located to the south of the Greek capital? At Pelagos, a restaurant that delights guests with its spacious sea-view terrace, enjoy Mediterranean cuisine with an Italian touch and classic French influence. In the kitchen, where talented chef Luca Piscazzi is at the helm, the cooking showcases a successful fusion of solid technique which extracts maximum benefit from local ingredients. The end result is highlighted in an à la carte menu and three tasting menus: Discovery, designed in the winter, when the chef explores the islands in search of ingredients and inspiration to bring life to the menu; Adventure, the most extensive, combining creations from the other two options; and the enticing The Best Of, that brings together superb dishes created by the chef during his career. We recommend booking a table on the veranda to enjoy the magical views.

Name: Soil
Description: There are just a few restaurants capable of creating a connection between food, nature and a love of one’s country, but here chef Tasos Mantis manages to express his full passion for all three through his cooking. The experience starts with a presentation of the stars of the show here, namely the aromatic herbs used in Soil’s dishes, many of which are sourced from the vegetable garden tended by the chef’s father. The cuisine is highlighted on a single tasting menu which showcases creativity and quality, which can be enjoyed either at the chef’s table, in the bright lounge or in the pleasant winter garden which, despite its name, is used all year round. The prawns with orange, marigold and mussels, prepared in a papillote of kombu seaweed, is a signature dish here, the finishing touches to which are added by the chef at your table. This and other superb menu options are accompanied by superb drinks pairings, including wine, fresh juices and low-alcohol and alcohol-free beverages.

Name: Pinus im Seegut
Description: Following stints at some prestigious restaurants, Philipp Heid has been head chef at the Pinus restaurant at Seegut Zeppelin hotel since May 2024. Here, he has created a laid-back sharing concept featuring light, modern dishes. Mouthwatering examples include buckwheat spaetzle with Heggelbach cheese, kale and buttered breadcrumbs, or smoked beetroot with Alb-Leisa lentils, herb cream and caraway. The menu is predominantly vegetarian, but there are also meat options. Feel free to order as you please – there's no traditional menu progression, and sharing is also possible. The dishes are arranged according to their flavour profiles, eg fruity, spicy, with roasted notes, earthy, plant-forward… In addition to fine wines, they have a wide range of alcohol-free alternatives. The decor is contemporary and upscale, but the atmosphere is comfortably relaxed. There is also a terrace overlooking the lake and the Alps.

Name: Rotes Ross
Description: If you are a fan of fresh and seasonal regional cuisine, the Bogner family's restaurant will be right up your street. This place is cosy and the service comes courtesy of friendly and well-drilled waitstaff managed by the lady of the house. As for the wine, the focus is also on the region. In summer, the leafy courtyard terrace is in great demand. You can also spend the night in one of the well-kept, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Poststuben
Description: It is hardly surprising that this restaurant is so popular. As well as charming and attentive service, diners are drawn by the regionally influenced cuisine conjured up by chef-patron Sven Molitor. Made using carefully selected ingredients, his dishes reveal talent and good craftsmanship. They are down-to-earth, but also show a certain finesse here and there. On the menu, for example, the delicious spinach and cheese dumplings will whet your appetite. The likeable traditional family-run hotel Die Post offers well-kept, contemporary guestrooms for overnight stays – an ideal base for exploring the beautiful surroundings of the village, which is located in the Meerfelder Maar volcanic crater.

Name: Im Kittchen
Description: This little restaurant is located in the middle of the old town, in a narrow side street near the Eiermarkt. The dining area has a rustic feel and tightly packed table, which contributes to the charming atmosphere, as does the cordial proprietress, who is in charge of the service. The delicious options are written on the blackboard and also come in smaller portions as a surprise menu. The impressive wine list features around 230 labels.

Name: Vier Jahreszeiten Restaurant Imhof
Description: You will certainly eat well at Andreas Imhof's restaurant. The cuisine is shaped by regional influences and stands out for its craftsmanship and flavour. Ingredients are selected with seasonality in mind. Diners can choose between a well-curated à la carte selection and a three-course set menu. Dishes made with Allgäu heifer, for example, are popular. The bright and inviting interior has a sleek, modern design; outside, the beer garden is presided over by an impressive lime tree. Tip: A budget-friendly lunch special is served daily.

Name: Gutshof Andres
Description: Surrounded by venerable old trees, this listed manor house has been owned by the same family since 1839. It boasts a delightful beer garden overlooking a small lake. Your hosts put everything they have into providing friendly service and fresh, seasonal regional cuisine. Their focus on sustainability is apparent in their selection of ingredients, some of which they make themselves. House-made spreads, sauces, brandies etc are also available for purchase. Should you wish to stay the night in this lovely, quiet spot, there are two flats in the former brewery, chic, modern double rooms in the coach house, and a comfortable holiday home – Gutsverwalter Haus. A practical tip: there are two charging stations for electric cars.

Name: Scheidels Restaurant zum Kranz
Description: Conscious of their long family history (the restaurant is now run by the seventh generation), the owners here are committed to maintaining their traditions yet the food remains resolutely down-to-earth. Charming historic ambience, plus warm and welcoming staff. Simple, tasty dishes take pride of place, inspired by regional and seasonal produce. A vegetarian menu is also available.

Name: Gasthaus Widmann's Löwen
Description: At the Widmann family's restaurant, seasonal cuisine that places great emphasis on regional ingredients is served in a cosy setting. There is an appealing range of à la carte options, including classics such as Maultaschen (Swabian dumplings), tripe or Zwiebelrostbraten (steak with onions and gravy), as well as a three- or four-course set menu (vegetarian version available). Tip: Be sure to make the most of the lovely beer garden in summer – it really is a delightful spot! Cookery classes and various other events are held here, plus they run their "Genuss-Shop" in the centre of Zang.

Name: Gaststube
Description: Housed inside Krone is this pleasant, cosy and down-to-earth restaurant that is also run by the Wölfelschneider family. The Gaststube menu will appeal to those who appreciate regional, home-style cooking, a case in point being the fillet of Odenwald trout on a bed of leek and chanterelle mushrooms with a cider and herb sauce. Mediterranean influences can also be detected on the menu. In addition to the delicious food, a highlight is the friendly service, which contributes to the congenial atmosphere. In summer, the terrace is idyllic!

Name: Weißes Roß
Description: This restaurant serves as a delightful alternative to the fine dining restaurant at the long-established Weißes Roß spa hotel. The menu features flavoursome regional fare made with fresh seasonal produce – the meat comes from the hotel's own butchery. Additionally, the pop-up restaurant Wurzel serves vegan options. Besides the classic Wiener schnitzel, or char with pearl barley, Savoy cabbage and pickled porcini, you can opt for 100% plant-based dishes such as Jerusalem artichoke soup with lovage and pine nuts. As for the decor, it runs the gamut from charming and traditional, to stylish and chic, to modern and elegant.

Name: Stube ZWEI.NULL
Description: Since January 2025, Gasthof zum Bad has had this interesting alternative to its fine dining restaurant for evening meals – and diners have been lapping up the pleasingly unpretentious concept. Chef-owner Hans Häge serves up delicious regional classics that draw on his family's traditional recipes. Don't miss out on enticing options on the menu such as rump steak of Bavarian beef or lentils with spaetzle & Vienna sausage, or "Badwirt's Maultaschensuppe".

Name: YALDY
Address: Moselstraße 15, Frankfurt on the Main, 60329, Germany
Description: Located in the centre of Bahnhofsviertel – a stone's throw from Moseleck, a legendary rustic pub – this pleasingly unpretentious establishment is a delightfully laid-back setting in which to savour good food or a cocktail. Dishes are designed for sharing. Options range from the hearty "quail, demi-glace, flatbread" (eating with your hands is allowed) to the more sophisticated "crudo, blood orange, horseradish". Be sure to sample something from the cocktail menu! "Yaldy", by the way, is a Scottish exclamation of excitement and enthusiasm. Tip: Definitely make a reservation – this place is always packed!

Name: Ai Pero
Description: This modern restaurant has everything you would want from an Italian trattoria: an enjoyably lively vibe, fitting background music and fresh Italian dishes served at small wooden tables! The food revolves around quality ingredients, craftsmanship and flavour – and wallet-friendly prices. There is of course excellent house-made pasta, as in the ravioli with pecorino and fig, black salsify and radicchio. The pizza oven is also fired up in the evening. After dinner, why not take a stroll in the beautiful old town? Incidentally, Ai Pero belongs to PURS Fine Hotels & Restaurants.

Name: Ziegler
Description: It is well worth making the trip to Jacqueline and Alexander Hahn's restaurant in the Hohensachsen neighbourhood, where you will be rewarded with a pleasant atmosphere and really good food. Not only is the quality spot-on, but there is also an impressive array of dishes, ranging from classic options like Zwiebelrostbraten or Wiener schnitzel to international offerings such as Kashmir curry soup or beef fillet tataki. Food is served in an upscale, tastefully modern setting featuring clean lines and soothing tones.

Name: Geberts Weinstuben
Description: Frank Gebert is all about packing flavours and aromas into classic cuisine. He is fond of using regional and seasonal ingredients in dishes such as trout soup with julienned vegetables or local venison ragout with creamed savoy cabbage. Tip: Try the reasonably priced three-course set menu. The stylish, cosy atmosphere is pleasant, and the senior manager welcomes diners with the characteristic charm of folk from Mainz – regulars appreciate the family atmosphere. The restaurant is not far from the Old Town, within spitting distance of the Rhine, and has a lovely vine-clad terrace in the courtyard.

Name: RÖHMS DELI
Description: A pleasantly straightforward concept that goes down well with restaurant-goers. The seasonal and internationally influenced cuisine is served in a friendly, modern atmosphere. The à la carte menu is complemented by daily specials on the board. At lunchtime, there is an additional dish of the day. For those with a sweet tooth, the counter displaying fine home-made pastries is a highlight! Attentive service. The terrace – in a traffic-calmed area here in the middle of the city – is also pleasant. There is a pretty holiday apartment for overnight stays.

Name: Capricorn [ i ] Aries Brasserie
Description: Located in Südstadt, a neighbourhood known for its distinctive character, this inviting and easygoing restaurant is very popular and has its fair share of regulars – reservations are advised. Welcoming and lively, it's everything a brasserie should be. The menu, too, is down-to-earth, including mouthwatering options – house-made venison ham, brasserie classics such as duck liver terrine or steak-frites, as well as vegetarian dishes. Tip: Take a punt on the moderately priced surprise menu. Friendly and professional service. Small pavement terrace in front of the building.

Name: Allgäuer Stuben
Address: Lindauer Straße 75, Isny im Allgäu, 88316, Germany
Description: Good food and a pleasant family-style atmosphere are the main draws of this restaurant run by the cordial Rimmele family, whose dedication to their work is palpable – that is certainly the case for chef Susanne Rimmele. She cooks regional as well as Mediterranean dishes. The menu includes options such as beef goulash with seasonal vegetables and bread dumplings, and house-made ricotta and spinach ravioli with braised tomatoes. The front-of-house team are charming and provide service with a smile. Tip: the delightful terrace. They also offer cookery classes, tackling pasta, asparagus or game. Pleasant overnight accommodation is available at Hotel Hohe Linde.

Name: Die Windmühle
Description: In this former corn mill, the Lemke family now run a restaurant that serves excellent food. There are two comfortable dining spaces – the Mühlenstube and the Kaminzimmer – plus a delightful terrace where you can tuck into delicious seasonal and regional dishes. Opt for one of two set menus ("Westfälisch Genießen-Menü" or "Unser Windmühlen-Menü"), or go à la carte. The friendly and attentive front-of-house team take delight in talking diners through their selection of German wines.

Name: Ehemalige Sparkasse
Description: This is the second restaurant run by Florian Kellerbauer in the historical centre of Dinkelsbühl. Housed in a former bank, a short walk from his Altdeutsches Restaurant, the chef-patron has created a dining experience centred on "Heimat" cuisine. Fresh, locally sourced ingredients take pride of place in the seasonally inspired dishes. À la carte options include Franconian beef Zwiebelrostbraten with potato noodles and green salad, and pike-perch fillet, tomato jus, root vegetables and pesto ravioli. The wine list features labels from Franconia, elsewhere in Germany and beyond. In addition to the restaurant, there are also well-appointed guestrooms plus a sauna and workout space.

Name: Gasthaus zur Kanne
Description: "The oldest inn in the Palatinate" has been around since 1160 – as it says on the façade. Given that the hosts are dedicated, the atmosphere is charming, and the cuisine is top notch, it's no surprise that it's popular with many (regular) guests – and it's best to book ahead. The restaurant is divided into different rooms, which creates a certain intimacy. Historical and modern details have been successfully combined, with eye-catching features such as wonderful old tiled stoves and a brick fountain. Regional cuisine is served in the form of a lovely à la carte selection, with Palatinate classics sometimes getting a modern makeover. Appetising dishes include Grumbeersupp (hearty potato soup with pulled steamed dumplings) and Saumagen Roulette (a variation on the classic Palatinate stuffed pig's stomach). The selection of Palatinate wines is also appealing – and there is a wine bar too. The terrace in the inner courtyard is truly charming.

Name: Schwingshackl HEIMATKÜCHE
Description: Here at the Naturhotel Rebling, situated at an altitude of 610m, you can expect not only spectacular views of the region (with visibility up to 100km on a clear day), but also delicious cuisine imbued with seasonal flavours. Katharina and Erich Schwingshackl invite you to experience HEIMATKÜCHE, an appealing alternative to fine dining restaurant ESSKULTUR. Katharina manages the restaurant floor, providing friendly and attentive service, Erich cooks up dishes such as South Tyrolean Schlutzkrapfen (stuffed pasta) with brown hay-milk butter, or game ragout with organic egg spaetzle. The Wiener schnitzel is also to be recommended. You can opt for a four-course set menu or go à la carte. They also have their own game reserve with deer and a few Galloway cows, as well as their own fruit trees and spring water. The dining areas are inviting, ranging from small cosy spaces to bright and welcoming rooms with amazing views that can also be taken in from the balcony terrace in summer. In addition to comfortable guestrooms, overnight guests have access to a lovely spa suite.

Name: Michels Stern
Description: The Michel family have always run their restaurant with great dedication, and now the fourth generation is at the helm. Two brothers make this an experience to remember: Wolfgang draws on good produce to cook tasty dishes ranging from traditional home-style fare to refined cuisine. Stefan will be delighted to recommend the right Franconian wine to go with your food. Plus well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Alter Esel
Description: The couple who run this restaurant put everything they have into creating a warm atmosphere and serving seasonal cuisine that draws on regional and Mediterranean influences. The set menu also comes in a vegetarian version. In addition to the cosy, lovingly decorated dining area inside, there are a handful of outdoor tables affording views of the historical buildings of this charming little town. This business is a Slow Food member and is committed to sustainability.

Name: Harmonie
Description: This charming building dating from 1823 has not shed its traditional character – lovely old wood panelling makes it really cosy! Here you will get to enjoy friendly service and regional, seasonal dishes, such as braised leg of venison. At the entrance you can sneak a peek into the kitchens.

Name: Gasthof Brink
Description: A place with charm! The traditional style that is cultivated here will evoke childhood memories for many diners. Family-run since 1880, the restaurant serves classic French cuisine that is down to earth and delicious. The pleasant setting has an elegant feel. The house-made pâtés and terrines are just as popular as the saddle of veal with Béarnaise sauce or the sole meunière.

Name: LAMM
Description: A really cosy place, where you will also eat very well: seasonal Swabian-Baden cuisine, with an emphasis on regional produce; some of the meat comes from the restaurant's own highland cattle. Some dishes are labelled ‘Naturparkwirte’ (nature park hosts). There are good wines to accompany your meal, as well as a special whisky offer. In summer, try and bag a spot on the terrace. Pleasant guestrooms also available.

Name: Gasthaus Scherz
Description: Born in Vorarlberg, but no stranger to Cologne's restaurant scene, Michael Scherz showcases the cuisine of his home country. The menu is divided into Austrian classics, including Tafelspitz (boiled beef), Wiener schnitzel and Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake with raisins), and "new classics with a twist", such as "Drei-Käse-Hoch, corn soufflé, green asparagus and artichoke" – to be washed down with good wines from Austria. The pleasant and professional team provides speedy, friendly, laid-back service. There is also a nice bar. The terrace to the rear of the restaurant is another appealing spot. Good to know: the restaurant is easily accessible from the city centre by tram.

Name: Zum Rebstock
Description: A fun place to eat! This handsome historical half-timbered house has been in the same family since 1750. Sit back in the delightful wood-panelled interior as the cordial front-of-house team brings out really good Baden cuisine, which can also be enjoyed on the terrace in summer. The menu includes dishes such as pikeperch-salmon dumplings, and stuffed guinea fowl breast with a chive cream sauce to whet your appetite. Tip: Sample the tempting little starters and desserts (look for the "Versucherle" sections on the menu)! With some 500 labels, the wine list is excellent. To take home: house-made cherry and plum brandies. The establishment also has well-kept guestrooms.

Name: zweiTRAUM mit WEBERSTUBE
Description: Hotel BEI SCHUMANN has unveiled its new culinary concept, uniting the long-established WEBERSTUBE and zweiTRAUM in a single restaurant. The kitchen is guided by a strong sense of regional identity and seasonal availability. Diners can opt for a three- to six-course menu with optional wine or alcohol-free pairings, or choose from an à la carte selection including dishes such as "pumpkin essence, dark bread dumpling, apple, chives" or "organic carp fillet in beer batter, warm potato and swede salad, lemon remoulade".

Name: HENNE.Weinbar
Description: Set in the heart of the old town, Hendrik ("Henne") Olfen's appealing bistro-style restaurant has a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere – and it's really popular! Likewise, the excellent food, which represents great value for money, goes down well! There is a simple menu at lunchtime and, in the evening, a range of modern, seasonal tapas-style plates that are ideal for sharing. The wine list is divided into three categories: #classic, #freakshow and #icon. For al fresco dining, there are tables on a charming courtyard terrace and on the pavement in front of the building.

Name: Zur Glocke
Address: Friedrich-von-Teck-Straße 12, Höchstädt an der Donau, 89420, Germany
Description: The Stoiber family put their heart and soul into running this modern restaurant. Their commitment is particularly evident in the excellent cuisine, which follows the seasons and draws on quality ingredients. There are three set menus, one of them vegetarian, and all courses can also be ordered à la carte. Mouthwatering creations include beetroot with porcini ice cream, quail and mushrooms, or cream of sweetcorn soup with wild prawn, polenta and popcorn. Diners are treated to attentive service in an inviting setting: Pale wood, clean lines, exposed concrete and restrained decorative details create a refined, minimalist feel. The terrace in the front garden is ideal for warm summer days. For overnight stays, there are two categories of contemporary guestrooms: "Design" (in a new building) and "Classic" (in the original building).

Name: Seehof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Boasting a lovely lakeside location on the marina, this restaurant offers a popular terrace as well as its “Badische Weinstube” and panoramic “Alois” dining rooms. Flavourful and classic artisan dishes feature on the menu. Tip: the local classics ("Alemannische Klassiker"). Accommodation is also available – the “boathouse” and rooms with views are particularly recommended.

Name: Felsenbirne
Description: This restaurant with a friendly atmosphere and a sleek modern interior is located on a cobbled street in the pretty old town, not far from the Elbe. Chef-patron Felix Mikulla uses seasonal ingredients – his dishes are fresh and delicious, as well as good value. The menu also includes vegetarian and vegan options. In summer, diners can make the most of the terrace in the inner courtyard.

Name: Flux - Biorestaurant Werratal
Description: Unpretentious, natural, simple and honest – that's the motto here. The dishes, which are created using organic seasonal produce sourced from the region wherever possible, are packed with flavour. The menu is vegan/vegetarian, but meat and fish can be ordered as add-ons. Gluten- and lactose-free options are also available. In summer, the garden is idyllic. Cosy guestrooms at Biohotel Werratal.

Name: ROSE
Description: For the Tress family, everything revolves around organic food, with a focus on vegetarian and vegan cuisine. The complex, carefully considered dishes win diners over with their depth of flavour and aroma – the pea and broad bean tartare, for instance, makes a lasting impression. Meat can be ordered as a side dish – here, they follow the principle of nose-to-tail eating. The portions are kept on the smaller side, so sharing is a good option if you would like to try a variety of dishes. All the wines to accompany this regional cooking are Demeter-certified. It's lovely to sit on the terrace in the shade of a chestnut tree. Tip: Should you wish to stay over, there is the guesthouse opposite.

Name: Froschgrundsee
Description: This appealing country house lies above a small lake, in the town's Schönstädt neighbourhood. Hannes Scammell shows his culinary mettle, cooking up fresh and tasty seasonal dishes. You can also dine outside. At lunchtime, the menu is somewhat reduced. The good cuisine is complemented by the friendly service provided by the hostess. Barbecue fans, take note: they also organise regular evening events dedicated to grilled meats.

Name: Berggasthof Schlüssel
Description: This mountain hotel and restaurant, which has been around for well over 100 years, has various comfortable rustic-style rooms, in which guests tuck into regional cuisine with a contemporary twist, crafted by chef-patron Jakob Brasch. The menu features a bouillabaisse-inspired fish soup, a wonderful beef broth with Flädle (pancake strips) or a classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) in horseradish sauce. In the evening there is also a more ambitious five-course set menu; a selection of traditional snacks is available throughout the day. Tip: Ask for table 15 by the tiled stove. Given the location in the Pfaffenberg area, at 700m above sea level, the terrace comes into its own in summer, affording views across the region. Well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Wilde Klosterküche
Description: This restaurant is located close to the 13C Cistercian monastery and its Baroque church. Inside, the decor is chic, modern and laid back, and the kitchen is open to view. The dishes served here are pleasantly down to earth and packed with flavour, and put the emphasis on sustainability. Ingredients are chosen according to the season and predominantly sourced from within a 50km radius. Opt for the six-course set menu – with meat or vegetarian – or go à la carte. A vegan option is also available upon request in advance. One standout recommendation is the rich beetroot prepared in various textures and served with flakes of aromatic yet mild goat's cream cheese. Interesting: They make their own gin. Comfortable accommodation is available at the small Klosterhotel.

Name: Landgasthof Zur Post
Description: Owned by the same family since 1870, this restaurant is now in its sixth generation. They are passionate about cooking, and use fresh produce sourced almost entirely from regional suppliers to serve up sustainable, locally sourced cuisine at reasonable prices. The delicious dishes cooked up by the chef showcase his experience in fine dining. In addition to the appealing à la carte options, a seasonal three-course set menu is also on offer. The ambience is cosy and rustic; in summer the terrace commands lovely views of Nieder-Moos. Five guestrooms and a holiday apartment are available for overnight stays.

Name: Feilmeiers Landleben
Description: This cosy and modern restaurant knows how to makes diners feel welcome. For Johann (who goes by Hans) Feilmeier, his "country life" cooking reflects both a love of his native region and a sense of duty. He cooks regionally and seasonally inspired food. Choose from one of the different set menus or order à la carte. Extremely charming and cordial service - matching wine advice included. Tip: the home-made jams!

Name: Talblick
Description: Brothers Claus and Rainer Weitbrecht are carrying on the tradition of their parents' business – the dedication of the whole family is palpable. As head chef, Claus Weitbrecht delights diners with both Swabian and international cuisine, including vegetarian dishes. The craftsmanship and harmonious flavours are excellent in equal measure. There is also a well-curated wine list. For a more upscale alternative, head to the hotel's Gourmetrestaurant. Comfortable guestrooms available.

Name: Speisemeisterei Burgthalschenke
Description: The Großhammer family runs this long-standing regional institution with genuine passion. For many years, it has been a beacon of consistency and quality. Their flavoursome dishes are oriented towards the seasons, with regional ingredients taking centre stage. In addition to the four-course set menu, you can choose à la carte from options such as cream of pumpkin soup or crispy farmhouse duck. Occupying three levels, the interior has a rural feel, and is complemented by a lovely terrace. Cordial and seamless service. Practical for motorists: large car park.

Name: Gasthof Blumenthal
Description: A family business in its sixth generation, this is all you could wish for from a Franconian inn. The interior is cosy and the beer garden, which is largely sheltered from the elements, is fabulous. Served in a pleasingly laid-back and extremely charming atmosphere, the menu features down-to-earth, unfussy dishes that are big on flavour and showcase the kitchen team's craftsmanship and good-quality regional and seasonal ingredients. Tip: They breed their own char and trout!

Name: Anetseder
Description: Traditional German public house culture is alive and well here, and at the same time they tap into the zeitgeist. The lovely dining space has a high ceiling and a trendy, modern feel and the waitstaff are friendly. They serve fresh and tasty food, with seasonal ingredients, preferably from the region, taking pride of place.

Name: Kamin- und Bauernstube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Among the dining options at the exclusive Hotel Dollenberg, you can choose to eat in the cosy, rustic-style Bauernstube, the elegant fireside Kaminstube or out on the wonderful spacious terrace – both the terrace and the Kaminstube offer beautiful views of the Black Forest. Whichever space you opt for, you can look forward to regional and seasonal cuisine. The menu includes Renchtäler Black Forest trout and dishes for two, such as Chateaubriand. There are various choice set menus and an a la carte offer. A favourite: the set menu of the week. The excellent wine list served in the fine dining restaurant is also available here!

Name: MEIER
Description: This restaurant in a fabulous countryside location boasts a delightful garden and terrace. Inside, the decor is a winning blend of tradition and modernity. The Meier family also runs the gorgeous HILZHOF, a hotel with chic guestrooms, and the compact fine dining restaurant HIO. At MEIER, the really delicious cuisine perfectly reflects a house motto that translates as "the field cooks". They make use of organic produce sourced from the region or even from their own vegetable field or herb garden. Culinary pleasure and sustainability go hand in hand here. Charming front-of-house team.

Name: Zum Kreuz
Description: This inn has existed since 1683. Matthias Schwer is the 4th generation of the family to carry on the tradition. Here, just outside St Märgen at an altitude of approx. 1 030m, a father-and-son team cook up quality seasonal fare, including local game, and classics such as maultaschen and schnitzel. There is an à la carte menu, the "Tradition" set menu and the vegetable "Gemussmenü" (only by ordering in advance). Comfortable guestrooms and holiday apartments for overnight guests.

Name: Gasthof Alpenrose
Description: This long-established inn by the church is always busy and much loved by its many regulars. Appearing in records as a tavern as early as the 16C, it has now been run by the same family for five generations. The cosy interior features an old tiled stove providing warmth in winter. In summer, a secluded beer garden, a veranda and even a rooftop terrace beckon. The Bavarian and Styrian cuisine includes appetising options such as venison goulash with butter spaetzle, red cabbage and aronia berries. Seasonal ingredients from the immediate area are used whenever possible. It is a real plus that on every day that it is open for dinner, the restaurant also serves lunch. Attractive guestrooms.

Name: EssBar fein & pfiffig
Description: This inconspicuous-looking restaurant is a stone's throw from the Hofgarten public park. Chef Daniel Baur and Olga Jorich have plenty of regulars here, and with good reason. The fresh, flavoursome dishes are carefully crafted using quality ingredients and represent excellent value for money. The veal rissoles are well worth trying. Neither will you be disappointed by the wine list! Olga Jorich's friendly and thoughtful approach to running the service plays a key role in creating the inviting atmosphere. Charming sheltered terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Gasthaus Goldener Stern
Description: Run with great dedication by the same family for three generations, this place operates as a traditional Gasthaus at lunchtime and as a casual-fine dining restaurant in the evening. The inviting interior is modern yet cosy, and the cuisine, inspired by contemporary trends, emphasises seasonal, regional ingredients. Local producers are proudly showcased, supplying the restaurant with meat, fish, eggs, cheese and more. A fine example of the meticulously crafted dishes is Böfflamot (Bavarian bœuf à la mode – slow‑braised beef in wine sauce) made with Wittelsbach ox from Hofmetzger Ottillinger, cold-stirred lingonberries, roasted celeriac cream, glazed vegetables and pretzel dumplings. Friendly and adept front-of-house team. The Eichen Loft can be booked for events, and the stylish wine shop can be reserved from October to April for celebrations (max. 12 people). The pleasant beer garden has a slightly shorter menu.

Name: Barra
Description: Hip, international, casual and lively would be a pretty accurate description of this inconspicuous restaurant. A thoroughly and unabashedly trendy concept, from the minimalist urban look and relaxed, pleasingly neighbourly atmosphere to the nicely pared-down modern cuisine that is ideal for sharing, and that goes for the "Sharing" menu or the à la carte options. The tuna with green tomatoes is fantastic, for example, as are the noodles that are rolled in-house – they are always on the menu. Select ingredients, some regional, are par for the course here. Tip: From the seats at the counter you have a very good view of what's happening in the kitchen.

Name: Little John's
Description: Housed in a spruce building dating from 1905, Tim Lellau's appealingly laid-back restaurant has a Scandinavian feel. The waitstaff are attentive and well-drilled as they serve high-quality, fresh cuisine. Diners can opt for a three- to five-course menu or select dishes à la carte. At lunchtime the three-course set menu is reasonably priced. From the entrance area, you can see into the kitchen, which is sure to whet your appetite!

Name: Am Kring - Büschker's Stuben
Description: This spruce restaurant, so typical of the region, is located right next to the church in a small village near Vreden. The menu takes its cue from the seasons. Generous servings and traditional preparation methods characterise the dishes, but the chef adds a modern twist with subtle details during plating. Standout examples of the flavoursome cuisine are the pike-perch with freshly whipped Hollandaise sauce, or the premium entrecôte. Friendly and professional service. Modern guestrooms are available at Am Kring hotel.

Name: Landhaus Tanner
Description: Diners are assured of warm hospitality courtesy of Stefanie and Franz Tanner at this establishment that has been run by the family since 1995. Their dedication is palpable in the chic, modern Alpine-style guestrooms, the tasteful restaurant with its lounge atmosphere and, finally, the excellent food. Dishes such as "venison ragout, Martl's hunt, mushroom rösti, cranberries, celery purée, pretzel dumplings" are seasonal and made with select ingredients that are sourced almost exclusively from the region and preferably organic. The lunch set menu is enticing. The kitchens are open for hot meals September to April Mon-Wed 5-9pm and Thu-Sat 12-9pm; May to August Tue-Sat 12-9pm. Tip: Regular culinary events can be found on the calendar. The restaurant is also a member of the Slow Food community.

Name: Tölzer Schießstätte - Hager
Description: This gem of a restaurant brimming with traditional Bavarian charm serves exceptional food in an inviting rustic setting. It is understandably popular, so be sure to book well in advance! Andreas and Michaela Hager form a harmonious team and this is clearly reflected in the delicious dishes they craft. Their short menu showcases superb local ingredients in classic dishes such as liver dumpling soup, Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) with horseradish or salmon trout fillet with a mustard sauce. The 3-course menu is also interesting. Service comes courtesy of a friendly front-of-house team.

Name: Weinhaus Zum Ritter
Description: This really lovely restaurant is deservedly popular. Accommodated in a converted 500-year-old farmhouse, it boasts a charming dining area with a cosy atmosphere, and an eye-catching old Swiss church window. In the small open kitchen, chef-patron Thomas Hausin conjures up fresh, regional dishes that are rife with robust flavours and won't break the bank. Attentive service courtesy of the friendly hostess. N.B. Different opening hours in summer.

Name: Landgasthof Rebstock
Description: In the heart of the wine village, the Keller family runs this cosy, rustic, centuries-old house, where the welcoming hosts offer fresh, seasonally inspired cuisine. They like to use ingredients from the region, but international influences can also be detected on the menu. The service is professional and very attentive. They also have guestrooms.

Name: Gasthaus Hofmann
Description: It is no wonder that this inn run by Bettina Hofmann attracts so many regulars – diners are won over by the cosy, elegantly furnished interior, as well as the exceptional food. Her appetising cuisine is regional, seasonal and dotted with modern influences, and the wines are excellent. In addition, they serve a vegetarian set menu. The service is friendly and well organised. There are also comfortable guestrooms. The eggs served at breakfast are laid by the establishment's own hens!

Name: Jägerwirt
Description: With its cosy rustic-style interior, charming service and down-to-earth, flavoursome cuisine, this is the archetypal Bavarian inn at its best. The menu features regional dishes and Mediterranean-influenced options. The chefs make a point of sourcing their ingredients locally and work with trusted producers. Alongside the standard menu, there is a varying menu of the day plus a weekly special. Popular grilled veal and pork hock dishes, as well as goose and duck, are also available if ordered in advance. The rural location is also delightful.

Name: derWaldfrieden
Description: Run by the Hupfer family, this establishment enjoys a tranquil location on the Herrenschwand high plateau, 1 020m above sea level. This stunning setting is surrounded by an abundance of greenery – unsurprisingly, tables on the garden terrace are coveted. Son Volker delivers exceptional cuisine that is entirely centered on the region and the season. In addition to set menus (regular or vegan) and à la carte dishes, there is a selection of traditional Black Forest snacks. Overnight accommodation in this picturesque corner of Todtnau can easily be arranged – guestrooms are available in stammHaus and spaHaus.

Name: Gasthof zur Sonne
Description: This charming traditional inn with its striking red façade may be a little off the beaten track, but the flavoursome regional and Mediterranean cuisine served here makes the journey worthwhile. Be sure to set aside some time because Egbert Tribelhorn is the sole chef at work here, and he takes great pride in the quality and meticulous preparation of his creations. Your patience will be rewarded with impeccably crafted and bold classic dishes. Diners often opt for the "Sonnen-Menü" set menu, but the à la carte options are also very popular. The house-made ravioli are a must-try.The restaurant also has three simple but beautifully kept guestrooms.

Name: Forst's Landhaus
Description: Run with great dedication, this restaurant is located by a small stream – tables on the terrace overlooking the water are in great demand! The seasonal menu uses plenty of regional produce, such as lamb from the Bavarian Jura. The vegetarian dishes are also appealing, imaginative and delicious! The friendly maître d' provides good service with a personal touch. There are simple but well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthof Berghof - Ursprung
Description: "Tradition meets modernity" is the theme here when it comes to both the decor and the flavoursome cuisine, which emphasises seasonal produce. The menu tempts diners with barbecued specialities and classics such as Franconian Fleckvieh beef roulade, or pike-perch fillet on a bed of creamed sauerkraut, not forgetting the Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with vanilla ice cream and apple compote. Be sure to take advantage of the inviting courtyard terrace in summer! For overnight stays, there are well-kept guestrooms and a lovely modern holiday home.

Name: Klösterle Hof
Description: Chef Markus Klein and his wife put their heart and soul into running this restaurant. In a spruce rustic-style decor – or out on the lovely terrace in summer – friendly waitstaff serve up delicious regional and seasonal cuisine made using good-quality ingredients. House specialties include golden trout and brown trout, sourced from Lohmühle trout farm in Alpirsbach. Good to know: Hot meals are served from noon to 8pm. Tip for overnight guests: Ask for the "Wohlfühl" or "Komfort" guestrooms.

Name: Gehrlein's Hardtwald
Description: Somewhat tucked away, the Gehrlein family's restaurant boasts a welcoming interior, as well as a lovely garden terrace. Meticulously crafted using the finest ingredients, the dishes served here are remarkably flavoursome. Chef-patron Martin Gehrlein has a penchant for fish – whether fried pike-perch with potato salad or sea bass with gnocchi. Led by the proprietress, the highly committed and friendly service team guarantees a seamless dining experience. The guesthouse opposite provides comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Zum Lamm
Description: This inn is everything you could wish for! Your cordial hosts, Ulrike and Manfred Kreger, put their heart and soul into running this popular restaurant. He is the chef and specialises in regional cuisine – one of his specialities is pike-perch from the Rhine, which is practically on the doorstep! Another equally delicious option is the herb-crusted rack of lamb with mint sauce, grilled watermelon and gnocchi. In summer, the tables in the garden to the rear of the building are in high demand. Smart guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Mühlenhelle - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This charming bistro set up in a pleasantly light and airy space is an attractive alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The food here is also top-notch, with Michael Quendler preparing delicious seasonal cuisine in the open kitchen. Much of the food also draws on tradition and showcases the region. Take, for example, the variation of Lambachtal salmon trout or the pan-fried Eifel pork blood sausage – two knockout dishes that linger in the memory. An appealing selection of wines is also on offer. Cordial service with a personal touch.

Name: Zum Vaas
Description: It is always a delight to visit a friendly and welcoming restaurant with a lively atmosphere. This one can look back on over 150 years of tradition and boasts a spruce, upscale interior. The service is cordial and attentive, and the food is delicious and made using high-quality ingredients from carefully selected producers. In addition to the menu of the day, which also features Mediterranean touches, there are the Vaas classics, such as roast Swabian-Hall pork. The impressive wine list comprises a remarkable range of vintage wines from various producers – predominantly from Germany and France, but also from Austria and other Old World countries. Comfortable guestrooms are available in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Löwen
Description: Representing the fourth generation at the helm, Roman Pfaff has brought a breath of fresh air to this charming traditional restaurant; the inviting garden terrace is a wonderful spot to kick back with a view of the greenery! The quality ingredients are sourced almost exclusively from the (Lake Constance) region – information about their provenance features on the menu – but international flavours come into play too. In addition to one or two classics, the team cooks up modern-inspired dishes such as "Courgette yoghurt chilled fruit soup, lemon oil feta & almond thyme crunch" and "Roasted Allgäu carp fillet, yellow tomato and caper sugo, herb couscous". Tip: As the restaurant is very busy, it's advisable to book! There are also two rather simple but lovingly designed holiday flats right next door in the charming Hexenhäusle.

Name: Weinstube Brand
Description: Here, diners can look forward to really good food which is both fresh and seasonal, as well as cordial service. Everything is pleasantly down-to-earth – just as you would expect in a wine tavern. The wine and game, like most of the produce, come from the region. Whether you opt for the classic rump steak, one of the daily specials or a vegetarian dish, be sure to leave room for the molten chocolate cake – just heavenly! Delightful courtyard terrace. In short: a fun dining experience!

Name: Münstermanns Kontor
Description: What started as a shop selling eggs and butter later became a delicatessen and today this spot is a popular bistro with a pleasingly lively urban atmosphere and an open kitchen. The tasty dishes include German classics such as currywurst and Wiener schnitzel, but also international dishes. The food is accompanied by decent wines by the glass, and the service is friendly. Open from noon to 8pm, last orders 6.30pm. NB: They don't take reservations at lunchtime – so come early, as the place gets very busy.

Name: DELI
Description: Here, in an appealingly down-to-earth and relaxed atmosphere, you can enjoy interesting international cuisine that is based on the seasons and drawn from select ingredients. The terrace on Niagaraplatz, a square with a waterfall feature, is also charming… The traditional hooded beach chairs are great for really chilling out. Good to know: They serve hot food all day.

Name: Dutters Stube
Description: The Dutter family have been running this charming 16C inn for four generations, and the seasonal and regional cuisine served here is a hit. Their Stubenrestaurant is more sophisticated (the set menu is popular); the Dorfwirtschaft serves simpler fare, such as flammkuchen and rump steak. As an alternative to the terrace, there is the pretty summerhouse. Chef Arthur Dutter is a member of the charity Deutsche Fußballköche (German football chefs).

Name: Rössle
Description: This family-run restaurant serves delicious, fresh food made with choice ingredients. Alongside the interesting "Chef's Menu" and classics, the specials are written up on the blackboard – it is well worth taking a punt on the likes of "house-made venison patties with juniper cream" or "medallions of Breton monkfish with saffron sauce". Add to that attentive service, a friendly atmosphere and a lovely terrace. Tip: The guestrooms feature an attractive blend of warm wood and sleek design.

Name: Sommerau
Description: The trip to the Hegar family's restaurant just outside Bonndorf is definitely worth it! Nestled in a quiet valley, surrounded by woods and meadows, the setting could not be more idyllic. There's an inviting terrace, but you can also enjoy the view from inside. The cuisine is regional and seasonal, including French and Mediterranean influences. The dishes are meticulously crafted and packed with flavour. Great care is taken to source ingredients that reflect the restaurant's commitment to sustainability. The wine list showcases a number of gems from the region, with a special emphasis on Baden Burgundy – the selection of half bottles is excellent. In the hotel of the same name, there are cosy, modern guestrooms and a beautiful sauna house, plus a natural swimming pond. And so that you can really unplug and unwind, there's no Wi-Fi or mobile phone reception!

Name: Fährhaus
Description: Practically right behind the dike and just a few minutes' walk from the ferry port, this restaurant serves distinctly local cuisine made with produce sourced from local fishers and farmers. Completely unpretentious and free from unnecessary frills, owner Gerold Janssen's dishes are brimming with freshness and flavour, as in the Helgoland crab cocktail or the crispy baked plaice fillets. Good to know: Well-kept guestrooms are available for overnight stays or holidays.

Name: Lucky Leek
Description: "Fine Natural Dining" is the concept here at this pleasant restaurant. Charming staff serve up fully vegan cuisine in the form of a three- to seven-course tasting menu – it's also possible to order à la carte. Made with seasonal vegetables, the creative, plant-based dishes are packed with flavour, and they are just as popular with international visitors as they are with locals. In summer, the best place to dine is on the terrace out front.

Name: Sennhütte
Description: Family hospitality is the name of the game here! Since 1918, the Grether family have put their heart and soul into this place and not least into the good food, made mostly with regional produce. Dishes ranging from traditional to slightly more sophisticated are served in a space divided into smaller rooms or out on the lovely verdant terrace. Snacks and cakes are available throughout the day. They have their own distillery, smokehouse and Alpine dairy. Pretty, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Weedenhof
Address: Mainzer Straße 6, Jugenheim in Rheinhessen, 55270, Germany
Description: The restaurant is wonderfully cosy with its rustic exposed timber frame and dry-stone interior. Michael Knöll conjures up cuisine that combines Mediterranean and regional influences, making use of excellent produce to deliver flavoursome dishes. Choose between à la carte options and seasonal set menus, including a vegetarian version. They also have lovely and well-maintained guestrooms.

Name: Remi
Description: This urban-cool restaurant in the building of publishing house Suhrkamp-Verlag has a sleek design with its floor-to-ceiling windows, and the open kitchen in the middle is the defining feature of the space. The seasonal dishes prepared in view of diners are pleasingly intelligible and without unnecessary flourishes. The affordable lunch deal is also very popular. Their true feel-good dishes range from "fennel risotto, radicchio" to "mackerel, corn, tomatillo". In summer, the lovely terrace is a real draw. The restaurant has many regulars, so it's best to book.

Name: Landgasthaus Gidibauer-Hof
Description: You eat well here, and furthermore the regional cuisine comes at very fair prices. The home-reared beef, for example, is sure to whet the appetite. The ambience is friendly, cosy and rustic. The converted cowshed is a great venue for parties. In the hotel of the same name, the guestrooms are furnished with natural wood furniture.

Name: Restaurant Corona im Hotel zur Post
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It's a real treat to eat here! In this classic restaurant, Sergio and Kerstin Corona work as a well-coordinated team, providing charming service and Mediterranean-inspired cuisine. In addition to the "Méditerranée" and "Corona" set menus, from which you can also choose à la carte, there is also a bargain to be had in the three-course lunch menu.

Name: Poppenborg's Stübchen
Description: This is the more relaxed alternative to Poppenborg's more traditional eatery. Try the Atlantic sea wolf with mustard sauce or the Westphalian-style boiled top-side of veal. Pretty garden terrace.

Name: Nil
Description: Diners are bound to enjoy their time here! This restaurant in the trendy Schanze district has a delightful ambience, the service is informal and friendly, and you can certainly expect to eat well. The delicious food follows the seasons and draws on international influences. Opt for the five-course set menu. Excellent and reasonably priced short wine list.

Name: Freihaus Brenner
Description: This lakeside inn overlooking Tegernsee is picture perfect; in summer, the terrace is the stuff of dreams. The interior is especially inviting, with cosy dining spaces done out in warm wood. The menu features delicious regional classics such as roast pork with dumplings or locally caught char with parsley potatoes, as well as more upscale fare such as turbot fillet with pumpkin risotto. The service is friendly and efficient, and the staff are all dressed in traditional Bavarian attire. Gorgeous suite on the top floor.

Name: Gasthaus Egertal
Description: The Rupprecht family keep things cosy in their pretty, traditional restaurant. Rustic details such as brick vaulted ceilings and natural stone walls combine with more modern touches to create a welcoming and relaxed atmosphere. There are two set menus and an appealing à la carte selection. The flavourful dishes take inspiration from both regional and classic recipes – think Label Rouge salmon fillet prepared confit-style in brown butter, with chives, lemon and Maldon sea salt. Somewhat simpler but no less tempting are dishes such as pork fillet with a peppercorn sauce or beef cheeks in vegetable broth. The terrace out front is inviting in summer.

Name: Wirtsstube im Hotel Burkhard
Description: In the second restaurant of the hotel Landgasthof Burkhard, the cuisine is somewhat simpler, which does not detract from the quality. Dishes range from cordon bleu to sea bream with lemon. The dining areas are cosy and prettily done out – you can choose to enjoy your meal in the Wirtsstube or the Esszimmer. The inner courtyard terrace, which is shared with the Kaminstube, is also very appealing.

Name: Landgasthaus Hirsch
Description: The Waldenmaier family (now in its fourth generation) cooks excellent regional fare with seasonal produce. A variety of three-course set menus is available, including one that is vegetarian and one featuring fish. Dishes can also be ordered à la carte or mixed and matched as desired. Additionally, there are one or two "special recommendations". What's more, they hunt their own game and distil their own schnapps! While chef-patron Sven cooks, Simone provides cordial service. This cosy and charmingly decorated restaurant is located on the first floor, as is the gorgeous balcony terrace.

Name: Erbgericht Tautewalde
Description: Inside, the modern dining rooms are done out in a pretty, rural style; outside, there is a lovely courtyard with a view of the kitchen. The seasonal cuisine is regional and international, and they are keen to use local produce. You can choose between the "Landidyll" set menu and "A la carte menu". And those who want to do without meat can look forward to a vegan set menu. Overnight accommodation in the traditional Erbgericht.

Name: Die Krone
Description: Chef Volker Lahn continues the family tradition in the kitchen at Die Krone. The cosy Baden setting of the dining rooms is matched by good local Baden cooking. The seasonal fare is available in the form of a set menu or à la carte.

Name: Bauernstuben
Description: This cosy rustic-style restaurant is housed in the venerable Ochsen Post. The menu features the traditional cuisines of Baden and Swabia, as well as internationally influenced dishes. Along with Maultaschen, Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) and steaks, there are also less conventional options such as sour kidney or tripe soup. Diners can also look forward to a delightful terrace, attentive service and a well-curated wine list that includes a number of rare gems. Tip: You can purchase their wonderful bread to take home, and some meat dishes are also available for takeaway. Lovely guestrooms.

Name: MundArt2015
Description: Nestled in a picturesque spot not far from Salzburg, the attractive Gut Edermann hotel awaits you with tastefully designed guestrooms and a 2 700m2 spa area, as well as appealing dining options. In a warm and welcoming setting, friendly waitstaff serve up flavoursome seasonal dishes such as veal topside terrine with wasabi, pumpkin and lemongrass, or young venison ragout with chestnut spaetzle and wild lingonberries. Alongside a set menu, there is also an appealing à la carte selection. Tip: Be sure to book in advance.

Name: Graf Everstein
Description: The Multhoff family's restaurant draws in diners with the promise of skilfully prepared food and wonderful views over the Weser. The friendly and attentive staff serve up beautifully fresh cuisine that sets great store by both seasonal produce and selected ingredients.

Name: Gutsküche
Description: It is a real pleasure to see the terrific produce gracing the plates at Gutsküche, just outside Hamburg – this is sustainable gastronomy par excellence! The organic ingredients from their own estate, Hofgut Wulksfelde, are the absolute focal point of the cooking, and the menu features vegetarian dishes that can be supplemented with fish, poultry and meat "garnishes". GUT's caprese with hand-scooped buffalo mozzarella, rocket and tomato pesto, for example, is a marvellous seasonal dish – the wonderful aroma of fully ripe tomatoes remains in the memory! Tip: Snacks can be purchased at GutsDeli and delicatessen shop, as well as organic produce in the on-site farm shop. In summer: organic ice cream in the lovely GutsGarten.

Name: Gasthaus Schwanen
Description: This inn is everything you could wish for! Nestled in the heart of the sleepy hamlet of Schwaningen, the family-run establishment has been welcoming diners for three generations. Inside, a cosy ambiance awaits, while outside, the idyllic garden terrace with its shady chestnut tree beckons. The food is outstanding – their wild boar ravioli in sage butter is a house speciality. They make a point of using regional ingredients, some of which they produce themselves: They have their own chickens and eggs, hunt their own game, keep bees, bake their own bread, make juices, liqueurs and spirits… Both Gasthaus Schwanen and Villa Pfarrhus, which boasts a beautiful garden, have guestrooms.

Name: Landhaus Zum Rössle
Description: Family tradition since 1780! Here the hospitality extended to diners is just as important as the tasty cuisine made from regional produce. Besides classic dishes, a surprise menu is also served. In summer the garden is a delight! There is a fantastic barn venue for parties. You can also stay overnight.

Name: Lohmayr Stub'n
Description: The popularity of this place is well-deserved! Chef Sebastian Oberholzner puts his heart and soul into his cooking, meaning his delicious dishes are much in demand. He uses seasonal and regional ingredients, making sure to know his suppliers and the origin of the produce. You can choose from a variety of set menus and à la carte options. You might be lucky enough to try the braised veal cheeks in a Cabernet reduction – a seemingly simple dish, but its masterful preparation reflects the restaurant's respect for time-honoured recipes. There is also a good selection of wines. Diners enjoy charming service in the setting of a fine historical building. Tip: Be sure to book!

Name: Sticky Fingers
Description: Located in the beautiful Old Town, this is a fashionable restaurant and bar. The decor and background music are very much on trend and lend this laid-back establishment something of a club atmosphere. The intriguing international menu features flavoursome options including "Sticky's Breakfast, Imperial Caviar, vodka shot" or "flamed salmon, ponzu, sushi rice, spicy radish, ginger". Alternatively, you could opt for the three-course "Sticky Styled" surprise menu – for the whole table – with dessert available as an optional extra. Friendly service. As well as wines, there is an extensive selection of cocktails, another big draw. In summer, a few tables are set out on the terrace in front of the restaurant.

Name: Feine Speiseschenke
Description: This friendly restaurant is located in a small village in a quiet side valley surrounded by woods and meadows. It offers seasonal cuisine bearing regional and international influences. They even raise Scottish Highland cattle here. You can choose from various set menus (including a vegetarian one) or go à la carte and opt for one of the classic dishes.

Name: Das Fetzwerk
Description: Das Fetzwerk feels modern and pleasantly uncomplicated - this applies as much to the trendy ambience as the food. Tasty, fresh dishes with a certain pizazz are served here. The service is friendly and attentive. The restaurant is located in the comfortable Das Freiberg hotel. Open from 12 noon. Tip for sunny days: the terrace.

Name: Landhotel zum Hirsch
Description: This traditional inn dating back over 300 years serves regional cuisine made with seasonal and predominantly locally sourced ingredients. The menu ranges from classics such as Hirschwirts Gaisburger Marsch (a traditional Swabian beef stew) and Swabian tripe ragout to Mediterranean-influenced dishes such as fried Atlantic sea bream fillet with a white wine sauce on bell peppers and courgettes with risotto. This elegant family-run establishment has comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Das August
Description: It's no wonder this place is so popular! The Gehrke family have made it a point of honour to uphold their long-standing tradition of offering outstanding cuisine, plus friendly service and an inviting atmosphere. The food is fresh, seasonal and made with select ingredients. The menu includes, for example, vegetable curry, roast corn-fed chicken breast with mushrooms or local game. There is also an impressive selection of schnitzels. Well-stocked wine cabinet. Attractive guestrooms at Schmiedegasthaus Gehrke.

Name: Auers Schlosswirtschaft
Description: It's no surprise that this restaurant, run with dedication for over 30 years, is so popular! Diners are won over by both the cosy space that is beautifully done out to exude rustic charm and chef Astrid Hilse's fresh cuisine, which takes the form of a menu that changes on a daily basis. Top-notch produce goes into seasonal dishes with a definite wow factor, such as braised lemon chicken with roasted vegetables and garlic potatoes, or local lamb prepared two ways and served with olive confit and green beans. The service is friendly – and the chef, too, gets in on the act. Attractive tree-shaded terrace. N.B. Credit cards are not accepted.

Name: HYGGE Brasserie & Bar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This hip place is named after the concept of hygge. In Danish and Norwegian, this describes a feeling of cosy wellbeing and comfortable conviviality – very fitting for the atmosphere conjured up in this pretty half-timbered house, which used to be a stable for polo horses. Allying rustic timber elements and modern design, the interior is chic and stylish, with the central fireplace as the focal point. The atmosphere is pleasantly lively. Unfussy seasonal dishes make up the HYGGE set menu and surprise menu; alternatively go à la carte – there are great vegetarian options, too. Or why not order a selection of plates for everyone in your party to tuck into? Appealing wine list. The trendy bar lounge is also popular, as is the charming terrace in summer.

Name: Zur Krone
Description: In the centre of the village you will find this charming restaurant with its comfortable dining rooms. Ralf Restel serves simple, flavoursome regional fare with international influences. Try the boiled rump of beef with herb sauce and pan-fried potatoes or the breast of corn-fed chicken with stir-fried vegetables and curry sauce. In summer the best tables are those outside on the quiet leafy terrace.

Name: Rührberger Hof
Description: The historical Rührberger Hof estate, which is home to this long-established family business, has been around since 1902. The fact that it was once used for farming is no longer apparent today. The pleasingly modern interior is an attractive setting in which to savour the excellent cuisine of brothers Christoph und Felix Düster. This is based on classical foundations and takes its cue from the region and the seasons. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced set menu of the day is very popular. There are also well-kept contemporary-style guestrooms.

Name: Fürstenfelder
Description: This former monastery makes for a wonderful setting. In what was once the cattle shed, the impressive Bohemian vaulted ceiling has been incorporated into the modern interior design, with a centrally positioned open kitchen. Out in the courtyard of the Cistercian monastery, there is a lovely terrace, slightly separated from the beer garden. The menu is varied, featuring dishes with a modern twist and made with sustainably produced (organic) regional produce. Options include dishes from the Josper grill, as well as vegetarian and vegan alternatives. Lunchtime buffet.

Name: Staudenwirt
Description: This well-established restaurant with its spruce little hotel has been run by the same family for three generations. Each dining area has quite a different style, from rustic to pleasingly contemporary, plus there is a delightful terrace. The menu features a diverse range of options, from comforting regional fare such as half a rotisserie chicken, or "Grandma Hilde's Rohrnudel" (oven-baked yeast dumplings) for dessert, as well as modern, seasonal and internationally influenced dishes. Vegetarians are well catered for, too. Fantastic value for money!

Name: Zur Krone
Description: Set in a spruce country house, this establishment has been run with great dedication and a sense of tradition by nine successive generations of the same family for over 200 years. Taking its cue from the seasons, the ingredient-led cuisine is flavoursome. Asparagus dishes are served in spring, game and goose in winter. For those with a sweet tooth, the meringue with cream, vanilla ice cream and egg liqueur is a must-try! Food is served in the cosy interior or out on the gorgeous terrace.

Name: Aschbacher Hof
Description: This pretty country hotel run by the Lechner family offers not only fabulous views of the region and tasteful, cosy rooms but also exceptionally good, fresh cooking. The regional and seasonal dishes include game as well as classics like Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy). Wonderful terrace.

Name: Die Pfarrwirtschaft
Description: This is not just Thomas Merkle's second restaurant, but a hotspot in its own right. The tasty food is wonderfully unpretentious and based on very good ingredients. Tip: Try one of the Black Forest beef dishes. The burgers are also very popular. In addition, the restaurant proposes an interesting weekly menu. Your meal here is enhanced by friendly and attentive service, a pleasingly informal vibe and a really modern aesthetic with a rustic edge. Needless to say, guests find themselves drawn to the beautiful garden in summer. In short, a place that fosters a feeling of well-being!

Name: Long March Canteen
Description: Currently one of "the" places to eat, Long March offers a dimly lit interior, informal service and a kitchen open to the diners’ gaze. The menu features Cantonese fare in the form of a variety of dim sum and dumpling dishes. Wide selection of wines, spirits, cocktails and tall drinks.

Name: Landgenuss
Description: Run by the Hämmerle family, this restaurant enjoys great popularity, so it is advisable to book well in advance! With a friendly country house feel, charming service and great food, this place is a nice alternative to the gourmet restaurant. Made with plenty of local produce, the dishes served here are seasonal with occasional Mediterranean touches. The wide-ranging menu includes their "Original Wiener schnitzel" and sea bass with rosemary and thyme. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace.

Name: Hirsch
Description: This picture-perfect Baden country inn boasts tastefully designed, inviting guestrooms and serves excellent food. The owner's son-in-law runs the kitchen, serving up regional cuisine that showcases seasonal produce – dishes such as braised beef cheeks in a Burgundy sauce or saddle of venison with cranberries and spaetzle are especially popular. Putting the emphasis on flavour and proper seasoning, only the finest and freshest ingredients are used. Charming and professional front-of-house team.

Name: Zur Linde
Description: Having made a name for itself decades ago, this restaurant is a local institution. It specialises in both fine dining and traditional Swabian fare that is made with high-quality ingredients, delicious and reasonably priced. The Maultaschen are a standout. When it comes to meat products, they have their own on-site butcher shop to fall back on. The specials, which change every day, are especially popular. Although dominated by regional selections, the wine list also boasts a range of Bordeaux, including some iconic names. Tip: Pick up some soups, sauces, sausages and meats from their shop. The ultra-modern apartments in the annexe are ideal for long-stay guests.

Name: Das Jagdhaus
Description: Built in 1856, this charming timber house with three dining areas is a really pleasant alternative to the other restaurants run by the Bolkart-Fetz family in Oberstdorf. Only ingredients sourced from within Germany – and preferably from the region – go into the dishes on the traditional menu, including some excellent game options. As well as the three- or four-course "Prinzregentenmenü", there is a range of à la carte dishes to choose from. Very nice selection of wines. Head for the lovely beer garden shaded by chestnut trees.

Name: Zum Dückerstieg
Description: A pretty and cosy restaurant with rural flair, serving seasonal and regional cuisine. Here, you can look forward to flavoursome dishes that pack a punch. The extensive menu features mouthwatering options such as pan-seared char fillet on asparagus and potato ragout, the classic cold roast beef with remoulade, pan-fried potatoes and salad, or the smoked braised meat and medium-rare rump of Holstein beef on a bed of potato and root vegetables. Be sure to save some room for dessert, too. Steeped in tradition, this family-run business – now in its fourth generation – also has attractive, comfortable guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Zur Flottbeker Schmiede
Description: Experience a slice of Portugal in Hamburg! The setting, a heritage-protected historical forge, exudes traditional German charm with its authentic decor and period open fireplace. It makes for a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere in which to tuck into delicious freshly made, fuss-free tapas. The chef-patron serves up genuine Portuguese cuisine but incorporates international influences. Try, for example, her "barbecued calamari, marinade, garlic" or "roasted miso cauliflower, white bean purée, coriander chimichurri". The well-curated wine list is dedicated to Portuguese labels.

Name: Hirsch & Jägerstüberl - Ostiner Stub'n
Address: Schlierseer Straße 60, Gmund am Tegernsee, 83703, Germany
Description: This typical regional inn proposes two separate culinary concepts: The fine dining restaurant is open Fri to Sun evenings, and the more rustic Hirsch & Jägerstüberl is open Wed to Fri from 6pm and Sat to Sun 12-2.30pm and 6-9.30pm. The emphasis is on produce from the region, and the dishes take their cue from the changing seasons. The fine dining restaurant also serves set menus. Attentive service. In summer, tables on the lovely terrace overlooking the garden are much in demand.

Name: Schwarzkopf
Description: Run by Stefan Pumm and his charming wife Anja, this restaurant serves delicious regional fare made from the freshest ingredients. Alongside the set menus, there is a well-curated à la carte selection. Highlights include house-made potato gnocchi with green asparagus, and Spessart beef shoulder braised in red wine. A perennial favourite: Chateaubriand with Béarnaise sauce, served for two. Dine in the elegant wood-panelled dining room or out on the lovely terrace. Well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: Schäck's Adler
Description: Christoph and Sandra Schäck have brought to life this picture-perfect hotel. The atmosphere in the wood-panelled dining rooms is really cosy, the service is very friendly, the cuisine is ambitious and tasty – the emphasis is on regional ingredients and seasonal produce. There is also the appealing Strumbel Bar and a number of extremely well-kept rooms.

Name: Weinhaus Stern
Description: A popular address and deservedly so: an inviting, rustic-style interior, a pretty courtyard, friendly service and, last but not least, good seasonal cuisine. Chef Klaus Markert relies on honest craftsmanship and flavours, along with fine wines from the region. Be sure to try the house brandy production. Charming guestrooms are also available, and there are home-made fruit jams for breakfast.

Name: Gasthaus Ödenturm
Description: As if straight out of a picture book, this beautiful inn stands on the edge of the forest. Inside, a warm and welcoming atmosphere reigns; outside, there is a charming terrace. Ernst Hunger Jr and his wife Brigitte run this long-standing family business with great dedication, delighting diners with good food and friendly service. The cooking is regional but also features Mediterranean and contemporary influences – from steak and fish to locally hunted game and vegetarian options. The dishes are delicious and very reasonably priced. The bottom line: this is a place people love – so be sure to reserve in advance. Modern, cosy guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthaus Weißenbeck
Description: You will find plenty of satisfied customers here, and no wonder! The mother and daughter Weissenbeck team cook up a storm using regional and seasonal produce – and the prices are fair. The lovely inn also makes for a cosy setting, and in summer the delightful garden terrace is most inviting.

Name: Dorfstuben
Description: The two charming farmhouse dining rooms (the "Clock Room" and the "Förster Jakob Room", which date back to the 19C, have been lovingly and authentically decorated down to every last detailare. Extremely cordial waitresses in traditional dirndl attire serve excellent seasonal and regional cuisine, including game from the hotel's own hunting grounds and trout from its fish farm. The braised beef roulade in Pinot Noir sauce is equally tempting. "Dorfstuben Classics" such as, such as the Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with maultasche and sauerkraut are also popular, not to mention the wonderful apple cakes! Tip: Take a look at the set menu of the day.

Name: Weisses Rössl
