The ample garden and the Wine Club, with direct sales to the public at attractive prices, are other interesting draws!

Name: Pigmeu
Address: Rua do 4 De Infantaria 68, Lisbon, 1350-274, Portugal
Description: A few metres north of the leafy Jardim da Parada, in Lisbon’s Campo de Ourique district, there is a very simple restaurant where… the cooking and character matter far more than comfort! Everything revolves around pork (which partly explains the name of the place), a product that Chef Miguel Azevedo Peres and his executive chef Alexandre Ballarin uses in its entirety, from snout to tail. On the menu, you will find the house classics, such as Torresmo do Rissol (crispy pork crackling), Croquetes do Pigmeu (Pigmeu croquettes), and the popular Bifana Porcalhona (a hearty pork sandwich), along with some delicious offal dishes that you simply must try.

Name: Inato Bistrô
Description: The restaurant’s name is inspired by “InATO”, evoking something in motion — a concept also reflected in the menu, where dishes are served in different acts (Acts I, II, III and IV) or in a tasting menu composed of VII acts. This original bistro‑style restaurant, led by young chefs Miguel Rodrigues and Tiago Costa, presents a creative proposal that marries national and international influences, always crafted with products of excellent quality. Our recommendation? Start with Focaccias stuffed with oxtail with a gentle truffle sauce, then the house’s true star of the show, seafood rice with scarlet prawn, and finish with the classic Pudim Abade Priscos (rich caramel custard) accompanied by basil ice cream and moscatel reduction.

Name: Olaias
Address: Rua Abade Pedro 2 - Centro de Artes e Espectáculos, Figueira da Foz, 3080 081, Portugal
Description: In this restaurant you will have reason to return at any time of year, as the house speciality, Carolino rice from the Mondego — a Portuguese variety grown on the Mondego river — varies with the seasons, so you will always have a new option to savour. From chef Mónica Gomes’s hands, besides the rice dishes made in a clay oven, come house‑baked breads served still warm, the delicious Rissol da Tia Fernanda (Portuguese croquette)… Among the rice options — duck, fish or octopus — you will always make a sound choice, and to finish, our strong recommendation is the Tiramisù made to order with excellent texture. The restaurant is located in the Centro de Artes e Espectáculos (Arts and Performances Centre) and presents careful décor, with large panoramic doors offering lovely views, as well as a comprehensive garrafeira (wine cellar/collection) under sommelier Pedro Ferreira, who is always ready to advise you!

Name: Carnal
Description: This lively, centrally located restaurant quickly gained popularity for being owned by the well-known Chef Ljubomir Stanisic (head of the 100 Maneiras group). It describes itself as a Mexican gastrobar and is one of those casual places that entices your taste buds. The dishes, generally quite well-balanced, are designed for a modern and informal ambience, with subtle nods to Mexican culture, striking the right harmony of flavour and heat in each creation. On the menu, featuring typical antojitos, tostadas, gringas and the famous tacos (don’t miss the tacos al pastor or the cauliflower tacos), you’ll also find bolder or more daring options like guacamole with insects or chicharrón (both dishes include larvae and crickets). Be sure to try one of their tequila cocktails!

Name: Norma
Address: Rua Doutor José Sampaio 35, Guimaraes, 4810 275, Portugal
Description: Housed in an old building that almost goes unnoticed among its neighbours. This restaurant enjoys privileged views from its terrace, where you can contemplate the Church of São Gualter – an iconic symbol of the city. At the stove is Chef Miguel Marques, who boasts wide experience in renowned restaurants in Zurich, Munich and Portugal, and presents a menu inspired by human "Evolution", reflected in dishes that hark back to the past and others that draw on culinary progress. His proposal revolves around a single seven-course tasting menu, à la carte options and a weekly menu that changes each season, alongside an interesting selection of Portuguese wines!

Name: Zunzum Gastrobar
Address: Avenida Infante D. Henrique. Doca do Jardim do Tabaco, Lisbon, 1100-651, Portugal
Description: In this elegant restaurant full of light, set in a modern, fully glazed building near the Lisbon Cruise Terminal (opposite the intriguing Museu do Lactário), the famous Chef Marlene Vieira makes a case for a top-notch contemporary concept, always grounded in the traditional Portuguese culinary repertoire, yet open to inspiration from other cuisines around the globe. It is surprising both due to its interior décor, dominated by white and red tones, and its pleasant terrace overlooking the Tagus. Interesting dishes? Algarve pink prawns with seaweed and lemon butter; Alentejo pork chop with fried polenta and roasted pepper ketchup; creamy shellfish and coriander rice...

Name: Ofício - Wine & Dining Room
Address: Rua Nova da Trindade 11, Lisbon, 1200-301, Portugal
Description: This restaurant, located in the heart of Chiado and close to the Jesuit church of São Roque, was born under the philosophy of a contemporary taberna (tavern), however… it is now taking a new path! The starting point is the recreation of Portuguese recipes in the light of current knowledge, always respecting the product and its origins, but without setting limits. The chef at the helm, Maurício Varela, champions a fluid proposal that seeks balance between cold and hot cooking, with constant references to the memory of Portuguese cuisine, spanning from traditional churrasco (barbecue) to conservas (preserves), as well as escabeches and smoked preparations. For them, in pursuit of a living offering, proximity and freshness of raw materials are fundamental to the creative process.

Name: Lilli Wirtshaus
Description: Whether in the evening or at lunchtime, a meal at this restaurant is well worth it. Indulge in delicious and down-to-earth traditional tavern fare; at dinnertime, there is also the option of a fine dining set menu – reservations required. Chef Walter Triebl only works with top-quality ingredients, which are showcased in his à la carte options, such as fish soup and Wiener schnitzel. The modern interior design, which seamlessly incorporates historical architectural elements, is also very attractive. In summer, the huge glass partition can be opened up to the adjoining garden, so that the indoor and outdoor areas merge.

Name: Secco
Description: Compact, intimate and colourful, this pleasant bistro set in a picturesque cobbled lane in the old town offers a relaxed alternative to the Schwarzer Adler restaurant. You immediately get a sense that the team supporting chef-patron Johannes Nuding enjoy their work! At lunchtime, there is a two- or three-course set menu with a choice of dishes; from 5pm an interesting selection of simple options is served, ranging from onion soup to quiche and Thai curry to a stove-top fish dish or baked guinea fowl. Friendly service, in which the owners participate.

Name: Wörgötter - Wirtshaus
Description: Located right in the town centre, this spruce inn has an eventful history that stretches back to 1800. The success of this inviting family-run restaurant now lies in the hands of Florian Wörgötter, who represents the third generation. Working alongside his father, Mathias, he uses seasonal produce to rustle up Austrian classics with a judicious modern twist. Dishes such as trout fillet with tender wheat, chicory and fennel, or Mariazell venison ragout with sour cream spaetzle, mushrooms and red cabbage are simply delicious. The "Business Lunch" is a moderately priced set menu served Wed-Fri. Renate (the mother) and her partner Julia are in charge of the service. Be sure to make a reservation – this place is always packed! Tip: There is also a fine dining restaurant that serves an ambitious and creative modern surprise menu three days a week.

Name: Freigeist
Description: This place may have a resolutely relaxed atmosphere, but in no way does that detract from the high degree of professionalism in both the service, courtesy of friendly owner Bernd Mossmann, and Paul Hunger's cuisine. The chef turns out fuss-free dishes made using top-notch, mostly organic regional produce – the full-bodied beef broth with root vegetables is a delicious way to kick off your meal. The interesting decor featuring unique decorative elements makes for a charming vintage feel. When the weather is nice, head for the inviting terrace. A somewhat simpler, pared-back menu is served at lunchtime.

Name: Schlosskeller Wirtshaus
Description: This cosy restaurant decorated with gorgeous wood panelling is another culinary option within the Schlosskeller world of gastronomy. As an alternative to Gourmetstube, Wirtshaus serves up flavoursome dishes that tap into the regional repertoire and are in step with the seasons. Austrian classics such as Backhenderl (Viennese fried chicken) also feature on the menu. Save room for the apricot dumplings for dessert! The sharing menu for two, comprising eight small courses is also a good idea (Thu-Sat). Pizza is served on Wednesdays. The cordial and highly proficient service extends to competent wine recommendations. The fantastic view of the picture-perfect landscape of vineyards and forests draws guests to the terrace in summer.

Name: Landgasthof Hinterleithner
Description: The menu at this inviting restaurant features a fantastic range of regional classics and Asian dishes. Popular choices range from Wiener schnitzel to pan-fried Arctic char or Thai curry. No matter what you plump for, you can expect high-quality ingredients, skilful preparation, character and plenty of flavour. Warm wood panelling lends the dining spaces a cosy rustic feel; friendly and professional service make your dining experience complete. In summer, the charming terrace beckons.

Name: Göttfried
Description: Run by husband-and-wife team Simone and Christian Göttfried, this inviting restaurant boasts a charming location in the old town – the main square is just around the corner and the Danube is also very close by. The interior beautifully combines modern style with historical features such as a vaulted ceiling and wood panelling. Front of house, the owner and her team provide attentive service. Meanwhile, chef-patron Christian Göttfried focuses on cooking excellent food – expect regional, seasonal cuisine with a Mediterranean twist. Both the organic veal Wiener schnitzel and the branzino with a parsley vinaigrette are highly recommended. The wine list boasts some 350 labels, principally of Austrian provenance. There is also a small wine shop and tables are laid out in the lovely quiet courtyard. The hotel offers contemporary, cosy guestrooms.

Name: Ziegelwerk Gasthaus
Address: Ziegelofengasse 28, Wimpassing an der Leitha, 2485, Austria
Description: This haven of culinary delights is housed in a former brickworks. The design of the interior purposefully drew on and preserved long-standing structures such as brick and quarry stone masonry, combining them with sleek, modern elements. A restored old oven makes for an eye-catching feature. Large windows allow the light to flood in while affording diners views of their surroundings. In summer, you can sit in the glorious beer garden. Owner Werner Tschiedel channels the spirit of a modern inn, serving flavourful, straightforward and strictly regional cuisine, such as greaves dumplings, warm cabbage salad, caraway juice or venison schnitzel in a pumpkin seed crumb, potato salad with mayonnaise, cranberries. To be washed down with a wine from a predominantly Austrian selection, many of which are organic or biodynamic.

Name: Mohrenwirt
Description: This restaurant has the feel of a favourite neighbourhood hangout. Steeped in tradition, it is located in the heart of Graz's old town, between Kunsthaus Graz and the church, Mariahilfkirche. From the terrace, you have a front-row view of the city. This pleasantly modern, rustic-style establishment is run by Romana Maria Pieber and Lukas Lepsic, who are committed to sustainable practices and using organic produce. The menu features regional and traditional Austrian fare with modern and seasonal influences, eg organic Backhendl (breaded fried chicken) in a basket, or organic lamb sugo with aubergine, polenta, sheep's-milk yoghurt and lemon pickle. On Saturdays, there is also boiled organic beef served in a traditional copper pot. Book early to avoid disappointment! Small set menu available 2-5pm.

Name: Scherer
Description: The restaurant of Almfamilyhotel Scherer, which is right at the foot of the ski slope, ticks a lot of boxes: cheerful, modern Alpine decor, attentive service and, above all, delicious food that showcases carefully selected seasonal produce. You don't have to be a hotel guest to fall in love with delicious dishes served here, such as braised piglet cheeks with creamed parsnips, crispy apricot and rosemary dumplings, and asparagus. Lunch and dinner can be ordered à la carte. Additionally, you have the option to pre-order the surprise menu for the evening – named "THE TASTE", it comprises at least 12 creative and mostly regionally inspired courses, and the value for money is excellent.

Name: Die Schmiede
Description: Are you a fan of no-frills cuisine that stands out for its craftsmanship and flavour as well as the quality of its regional ingredients? In addition to classic Austrian fare such as Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), Wiener schnitzel etc, you can indulge in dishes such as fried lake trout with Mediterranean pearl barley and a Riesling foam, or roast lamb with Serviettenknödel (bread dumplings). Diners will appreciate the attentive, friendly service and cosy interior done out in a modern style and warm tones. The gorgeous wine cellar dates back to the 16C. Head for the terrace with a view of the Höllengebirge mountains.

Name: Mocking das Wirtshaus
Description: Right at the foot of the famous Streif ski piste, just a stone's throw from the Hahnenkamm cable car, you will find this business run by siblings Martin Huber and Andrea Posch. Now this is how you imagine a modern inn! Lots of wood and stone lend the place a rustic charm, yet the overall decor is stylish. The regionally inspired dishes include home-grown vegetables. If you like it spicy, you'll love their kimchi, fermented in-house! Or perhaps a dish from the chef's childhood? Take, for example, daumnidei (Austrian gnocchi) with sauerkraut browned in butter and apple compote, or spinach dumplings with brown butter and mountain cheese. Tip: cosy après-ski area at the end of the ski run. Car park directly in front of the building (for a charge; free with a minimum spend at the Wirtshaus).

Name: Malerwinkl
Description: Whether you prefer traditional Styrian cuisine or more sophisticated fare with a modern touch, this restaurant caters to your tastes. Almost exclusively regional ingredients are used in the set menu and à la carte dishes, eg char with kohlrabi, peas and vegetables and a truffle hollandaise sauce. The wine list with a focus on Austria is appealing, and the selection of wines by the glass is also good. You can opt for a table in the main dining area, in the bright winter garden or on the beautiful terrace. The restaurant is located in an "art hotel", which has 10 individual guestrooms and a holiday apartment. Take a look around the garden with its sculptures by Peter Troißinger Sr – chef, sculptor and painter.

Name: Chez Bernard
Description: Close to the Mariahilfer Straße shopping drag, on the seventh floor of the chic MOTTO boutique hotel, this restaurant has really distinctive architecture. The tasteful upscale interior will appeal to diners, as will the pleasantly lounge-like atmosphere. Be sure to check out the interesting bar too. The food is uncomplicated and unpretentious. Try the bouillabaisse – one of the classics! – and don't forgo the apricot dumplings. One floor up is the rooftop terrace, which boasts a magnificent view, and, although it only serves a smaller menu, is nonetheless the place to be!

Name: s'Morent
Description: Reference to a farm in the centre of the village first appears in 1764; many years later it was taken over by the Morent family and became a village inn. Now the presence of daughter Lisa and her partner is like a breath of fresh air. They devise a short, season-focused menu comprising tasty, pleasingly pared-back dishes made from good – predominantly regional – ingredients. The space has a rustic-style wooden ceiling and a beautifully sleek and modern feel. Per sitting, this amiable couple can accommodate 20 diners, who are treated to cordial and attentive service. From the entrance area, you can catch a glimpse of the action in the kitchen.

Name: Meierei im Stadtpark
Description: One floor below the Reitbauer family's fine dining restaurant, you’ll find another upmarket eatery. In addition to around 150 wonderfully matured cheeses, it boasts delicious classics, such as Wiener schnitzel made with suckling calf and, of course, Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake). Alternatively, there is fried carp or goat kid. The dinner and lunch menus differ slightly. You can also enjoy breakfast here. The view of the River Wien and Stadtpark is fantastic, making the terrace hot property in summer.

Name: Mochi
Description: A lively, informal restaurant serving authentic Japanese cuisine with some more modern twists, at moderate prices. You can watch the chefs at work as they prepare sushi rolls, yakitori or gyu don. At lunchtime, the food is served in bowls; in the evening the presentation is a bit more elaborate. In summer, the terrace in front of the building makes for a lovely spot. Tables are much in demand, so book early! The establishment also runs a takeaway right across the street.

Name: Das Pfleger
Description: This restaurant is located on a high plateau on the Pustertaler Höhenstraße (Val Pusteria Scenic Road) at an altitude of over 1 200m – its terrace with views of the Dolomites and Carnic Alps is enchanting. Ensconced in the hotel of the same name, run by the Mascher family, son Tom and his kitchen team cook seasonal regional fare, incorporating just the right amount of modern creativity. From the "Your Choice" section, you can choose à la carte, eg trout, walnut espuma, balsamic shallots, or steak, parsnip, curried potato and soya; alternatively there is the "Chef's Choice" surprise set menu comprising four or five courses. A shorter menu is served at lunchtime on Sundays.

Name: Ernele
Description: At this restaurant, sustainability is more than an idea; you can see it in practice, not least in Felix Groß's cuisine. He cooks with a close eye on the seasons, and almost all ingredients are sourced from the immediate vicinity – within a 100km radius. The ibex ragout with pumpkin espuma and tarragon, for example, is very carefully prepared and really delicious. Be sure to save room for one of the desserts, such as salted caramel ice cream with blueberries and walnuts! Modern lines and a touch of rusticity are combined in the decor. The open kitchen and large shelves stacked with all kinds of products that are available to purchase draw the eye. This is the second restaurant within the hotel Das Schiff, alongside Wälder Stube 1840.

Name: Gasthaus Zum fröhlichen Arbeiter
Description: This spruce family-run inn has been welcoming diners for 100 years. Owner and head chef Hannes Tschida showcases his love for the Seewinkel region through dishes incorporating plenty of local ingredients. The wide-ranging à la carte options include Grammelknödel (potato dumplings stuffed with greaves), beef goulash, trout ceviche, dry-aged steak and Lake Neusiedl catfish. There is also a four- to six-course surprise menu. To complement the bold flavours of the cuisine, an impressive wine list dominated by Austrian labels is available. The restaurant itself has two indoor dining spaces: one oozing traditional charm, the other more modern with a conservatory feel. The friendly and attentive service is appreciated by regulars and newcomers alike.

Name: Gufer 55
Description: Diners are spoilt for choice here! The variety of delicious dishes on offer ranges from wonderful starters such as vitello tonnato and delicious soups to risotto and Thai curry and Austrian classics such as Tafelspitz (beef boiled in broth), Wiener schnitzel or local char – all prepared using good, fresh produce. For dessert, the poppy seed noodles, for example, are extremely tempting. The atmosphere in this lively restaurant in the centre of the village is also inviting with its cosy, modern decor. Friendly service, and in summer be sure to make the most of the lovely terrace in front of the building.

Name: Fossil
Address: Kellergasse 6K, Purbach am Neusiedler See, 7083, Austria
Description: The name "Fossil" was not simply plucked out of thin air: This restaurant is actually located in a Muschelkalk limestone wine cellar dating back to 1870. At the entrance on the historical Kellerplatz, you are greeted by a plant-filled Mediterranean-style terrace. Then take just a few steps down, walk past the open kitchen and into the bright and imposing barrel vault, which makes for an enchanting setting. Chef-patron Thomas Daniel Pugel has been cooking here since 2015. Between noon and 9pm, he serves up regional and seasonal cuisine that is rooted in Austrian tradition yet incorporates modern influences – wild pike-perch fillet with fermented beetroot, Jerusalem artichoke and gnocchi, or Backhendl (breaded fried chicken) served with a potato and lamb's lettuce salad. Choose à la carte or the set menu of four or six courses.

Name: Woracziczky
Description: Diners are given a warm welcome In this pleasingly informal inn (pronounced "Vorashitsky"). Both its laid-back atmosphere and Viennese cuisine are a hit, with house specialities such as beef tartare with avocado, or Tafelspitz (boiled veal) served with a creamy chanterelle sauce. The reasonably priced lunchtime set menu, which changes daily, is especially popular.

Name: LOLA
Description: A word to the wise: You should definitely make a reservation because this cosy bistro-style restaurant with the soul of a Spanish tapas bar is extremely popular. For one, the atmosphere is pleasingly lively and the decor is charming, with its high ceilings and striking bar that draws the eye. And then there is the food: they serve tasty tapas from different regions of Spain – these small plates are perfect for sharing! The mouthwatering menu ranges from Iberian ham and Manchego cheese to tortilla de patatas, and grilled red tuna steak with avocado salad to crema catalana. When it comes to wine, the focus is also on Spanish labels.

Name: Thaller - Gasthaus
Address: Am Kirchplatz 4, Sankt Veit am Vogau, 8423, Austria
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This attractive establishment opposite the imposing parish church is steeped in tradition. In addition to the fine dining restaurant that serves a set menu in the evening, the Thaller family also runs Gasthaus as an alternative, for a more down-to-earth lunch experience. The hearty country-style cuisine has a focus on sustainability, drawing on select seasonal ingredients from the region, such as pike perch, cucumber, Topaz apple, Meyer lemon… or potato gnocchi, chanterelles, Straden truffle, smoked cheese. Much of the produce used comes from the restaurant's own garden and fish pond. One special feature is the attractive old wood-fired stove on which the dishes are prepared. Owners Norbert and Manuela Thaller divide the labour between themselves – his domain is the kitchen; she is in charge of the restaurant floor. Attending to guests in the cosy dining area, she is happy to explain the philosophy behind their sustainable approach.

Name: Wirtshaus Krainer
Description: The Krainers offer a comprehensive experience with their family-run restaurant, café and hotel. In a bright and modern conservatory-like setting, Andreas Krainer serves up delicious Austrian dishes made with in-season local produce. Some highlights on the menu include the house goulash, Pöllau beef steaks and Mürztal fish hash, along with traditional Austrian desserts. In addition to the Wirtshaus offering, there is also a fine dining restaurant experience in the evening. And it is certainly worth calling by the cake buffet in the café. Hotel patrons can look forward to cosy accommodation, as well as a stylish and modern sauna and relaxation area.

Name: Wirtshaus Steirereck am POGUSCH
Description: A meal here is a delightful experience! The kitchen team has an abundance of excellent ingredients at its fingertips, from its own farm or from the surrounding area – something you rarely find! On Wednesdays the spotlight is on garden, field and forest, on Thursdays on offal, on Fridays on freshwater fish, and on Saturdays they mix it up. Attentive service courtesy of well-trained staff, who are happy to provide information about the sustainable philosophy. In addition to the inviting series of dining areas ranging from cosy and rustic to light and modern, there is also a terrific terrace with a beautiful view. As a convivial alternative, the ‘Schankkuchl’ offers meals prepared over a fire or steam at a communal table (Thurs.-Sat.). This wonderful estate surrounded by nature is also an unusual place to stay overnight: Here you will find very individual accommodation, from the ultra-modern tree house and former stables to the converted hunting lodge or the glass house.

Name: Hueber der Wirt in Bründl
Address: Sankt Georgen an der Leys 18, Sankt Georgen an der Leys, 3282, Austria
Location: Sankt Georgen an der Leys, Austria
Description: A picture-perfect location where you can enjoy delicious food without breaking the bank. The cuisine stands out for its intensity, complexity and aromatic richness. In addition to delicious regional classics, the menu features sophisticated dishes such as sturgeon with young peas, asparagus and Alpine caviar. At lunchtime, hearty traditional fare is the name of the game; the evenings are reserved for fine dining. Friendly service, cosy modern decor. In summer, make the most of the small garden to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Gasthof Adler
Description: Here, the cooking has been taken back to basics, with the focus placed squarely on the first-rate regional produce. The cuisine of Felix Messner – who runs the restaurant together with his brother Florian – is inspired by Austria and Vorarlberg. The simplicity of the fresh, flavourful dishes (eg breaded fried chicken, potato salad, pumpkin seed oil) is in keeping with the decor in this timber building on the village square, which was erected in 1756 and renovated according to historical models. Warm wood panelling from floor to ceiling makes for a cosy interior. There are also smart guest rooms in a modern regional style.

Name: Krispels Genusstheater
Description: The Krispel family, who have forged an interesting bridge here between Genusstheater and their stylishly designed winery, welcome you with a striking contrast of old and new architecture. The lovely restaurant itself and the gorgeous courtyard terrace are equally inviting. Both hearty traditional fare and fine dining cuisine feature on the menu. Flavoursome dishes are made with top-drawer ingredients from the region – including, most notably, organic pork from the owners' own woolly pig stock. The exceptional wine list boasts over 600 labels, naturally featuring the estate's own wines among the highlights. Attentive and professional service.

Name: Das Bräu
Address: Am Anger 1, Nußdorf am Attersee, 4865, Austria
Description: An establishment that is a delight in every respect! The fantastic lakeside location by Attersee alone makes a visit worthwhile, as does the pleasingly relaxed atmosphere, which combines rural charm with more modern features, as well as the beautiful terrace. And then there's the cuisine, which has classic Austrian roots. The dishes that grace the menu are tasty and prepared without much ado - "Wiener schnitzel made from saddle of veal" or half a roast chicken; the odd Mediterranean influence also makes its presence felt. Many of the wines on the 500-plus list are from Austria. The Hotel Aichinger has attractive, modern guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Landgasthof Haslauerhof
Address: Hauptstraße 17, Haslau an der Donau, 2402, Austria
Description: A tip to start off with: in summer, don't miss out on the terrace with a view of the Danube – it's idyllic! That's not to say the kitchen doesn't also deliver its fair share of delights: the beautifully prepared regional dishes are packed with flavour, from Wiener schnitzel (made with veal), potatoes and lamb's lettuce salad, to delicious ravioli or Arctic char fillet, to 24hr-braised ox cheek. Be sure to try the house-made vinegar-based lemonades, too. Hot meals served throughout the day.

Name: Carnozet
Description: Tastefully done out in a modern take on Alpine style, this restaurant provides both excellent food and friendly service. The menu features an appealing selection of seasonal dishes, mostly made from locally sourced produce. We highly recommend the grey cattle goulash with Walser Knöpfle (similar to spaetzle).

Name: MAST Weinbistro
Description: Set in a historical town house, this trendy place is a winning combination of modern wine bar and upscale bistro. It is very popular for its great food, is made with seasonal ingredients sourced from local producers – and at fantastic value for money. Organic and biodynamic wines are recommended to accompany your choice of dishes. There is an appealing outdoor dining area, too.

Name: Krone Hittisau
Description: The town-centre hotel, Krone Hittisau, dates back to 1838. Today, the restaurant on its first floor serves regional and seasonal cuisine with an emphasis on sustainability. Fantastic ingredients are showcased in delicious dishes such as fillet of char with coriander lentils, ginger and lemon foam, and ricotta gnocchi. Diners can also look forward to charming and attentive service in a thoroughly inviting setting. The tasteful blend of clean lines and warm wood finishings (all the lovely furniture is made by carpenters from the Bregenz Forest) can be found both in the guestrooms and the restaurant.

Name: Saluti
Description: You can tell that an experienced chef is at work here! Ernst Moser serves up an appealing range of sophisticated dishes, including pizza and pasta, which can be ordered as a set menu or à la carte. Diners choose from options such as vitello forello, pigeon royale, glazed belly of Alpine pork, and spaghetti "Ernesto". Plus there is a well-curated wine list and friendly, attentive service. The restaurant, which adjoins a tennis centre, is not only popular with locals and regulars, so don't forget to make a reservation. You can also make the most of the small terrace.

Name: Gründler's Genießer Wirtshaus
Description: This is the somewhat simpler and entirely regionally oriented alternative to the Gründler family's small restaurant Gourmet Stüberl. Also located in the Hotel Alpin, the same high cooking standards apply – the food is clearly structured, very carefully prepared and fresh as can be. Shining examples include trout carpaccio, radish, caviar, pumpkin, crab crunch, or lamb liver, apple, potato cream, peas, bacon. The space is bright, the atmosphere friendly, the service attentive and proficient. The excellent wine list has over 250 labels, with Austria particularly well represented.

Name: Schwanen
Description: Organic is the watchword here, from the sustainably sourced produce used in the kitchen to the furnishings chosen for the restaurant and hotel of the same name – the latter were crafted by local artisans from untreated natural materials. Many of the ingredients are grown in the on-site garden; fermented and pickled foods are also used. The menu tempts diners with options such as medium-rare flank steak of Schönenbach venison with creamy sweet potato. The plant-based options, such as the hand-made gnocchi with colewort and Vetterhof beetroot, are well worth trying. Fans of organic or natural wines will find an impressive selection here.

Name: Jerár
Description: Although located away from the tourist heart of the city, Jerár is winning new fans thanks to the cuisine on offer here. In this spacious and informal restaurant with a kitchen that opens out on to the dining room, chef Charis Nikolouzos showcases internationally inspired cooking that combines Greek roots (thanks to his connections with small-scale producers who supply him with his fresh ingredients) and French and Italian culinary detail. On the à la carte, featuring abundant dishes made for sharing, we particularly liked the Cacio e Pepe with “Mikrolimano Shrimp”.

Name: Pharaoh
Description: This restaurant boasts a concept that takes guests back in time thanks to its focus on the flavours of bygone days. At Pharaoh you won’t find modern cookers as every dish here is cooked using wood or charcoal as in olden days, endowing everything with a sense of simplicity and authenticity. The decor is a show in itself, with its combination of modern and industrial styles, open-view kitchen, plus a spacious balcony on which to enjoy your meal. Chef Manolis Papoutsakis’ cooking revisits Greece’s culinary traditions, but with a contemporary touch, as witnessed in dishes such as Tarama with bottarga, Dolmadakia, Chestnut stew, Slow-cooked lamb with Greek traditional pasta, Galaktoboureko (Greek custard dessert)... In the evening, a DJ adds to the atmosphere with music played on vinyl discs, so if you don’t want to miss out make sure you book in advance.

Name: Cerdo Negro 1985
Description: This restaurant has reinvented itself over the years and what started out as a small tavern is now a vibrant multi-cultural dining space. Occupying an old Greek house with a charming covered patio near the Kerameikos archaeological site, it provides the perfect setting in which to sample contemporary international cuisine. Run in relaxed fashion by the Alexopoulos brothers, the restaurant serves dishes that combine Greek heritage with the brothers’ passion for Spanish cuisine, with fire and smoke adding the finishing touch to the flavours on offer. Choose between à la carte options and a six-course tasting menu entitled Taste of Cerdo Negro. We can highly recommend the homemade bread as well as the “Welcome to Cerdo Negro” starter.

Name: Akra
Description: A unique and special experience in which the chef does the cooking next to your table or at the wood-fired grill in front of you while you are seated at the counter. In addition, there’s also a bakery at the front of the establishment offering delicacies baked in ovens distributed around the room, that dispense their enticing aromas to add to the sensorial experience. Renowned chefs Giannis Loukakis and Spiros Pediaditakis run this small space in the charming Pangrati district of the city, where the young and relaxed vibe provides the backdrop for uncomplicated cuisine that is nevertheless full of personality and prepared with fresh, seasonal ingredients. The menu is refreshed every day, with dishes superbly cooked in the wood-fired oven taking centre stage.

Name: Fine Mess Smokehouse
Description: If you’re a fan of smokehouse-style dishes teeming with flavour which take the American barbecue concept to another level, you’ll want to add this eatery to your list, as you won’t find anything remotely similar anywhere else in the city. This informal restaurant focuses on “Low & Slow” barbecue, featuring both à la carte options and a seasonal tasting menu that includes meticulously curated pairings of wine and classic old-fashioned cocktails. Head chef Elena Kaperda is also the face of the “Lick the Spoon” project—a unique patisserie workshop.

Name: Nolan
Description: This new Nolan 2.0 version of the restaurant has chef Michalis Nourloglou in charge of the kitchen, where he follows the same concept and conjures up a combination of Greek cuisine with other dishes from around the world. The menu here is simple and concise, with options that include sea bream tartare, made with fresh fish of the day and served with dried fruits and a hint of citrus, and the mouthwatering shredded and breaded beef cheeks on a bed of cream along with a topping of truffles. The ambience here exudes relaxed joviality and a light, airy feel thanks to the large windows, and is enhanced by excellent service.

Name: Morel Bistroo
Description: This brightly decorated neighbourhood bistro is the younger sister of Rado in Tallinn’s Old Town, and comes with a slightly more casual feel. The dinner menu is short but appealing, so you might still find it hard to choose, and the well-priced modern dishes include something for everyone. Weekdays also see a straightforward ‘lunchtime plate’, while at the weekends you’re encouraged to linger longer over a leisurely brunch. The ingredient-led cooking is wholesome and satisfying, and the wine list is equally attractive in both content and price. The super friendly team only add to the experience.

Name: TOKO
Description: On the banks of the Emajõgi River, which runs through the centre of Tartu, you’ll find this modern whitewashed building that is the sister of Tuljak, NOA and NOA Chef’s Hall. In winter, cosy up in the homely interior; in summer, head out to the pavement terrace or up to the rooftop to really make the most of the location. Expect a short menu with international leanings – you might find ‘TOKO Taco’ (chicken thighs on a paratha) or black cod with miso and beurre blanc – and if you fancy starting with a touch of luxury they offer a 'bump' of salty caviar. A sundowner here is an absolute must.

Name: NOA
Description: Set in a delightful coastal spot looking back towards the city by way of the Baltic Sea, this beach house style restaurant brings plenty of cheer to proceedings thanks its to colourful fabrics and full-length windows that flood the room with light. It’s a large building – home too to NOA Chef’s Hall – clad with wood and filled with natural materials, giving it something of a New England look, but it’s the terrace that’s the place to be when the weather’s right. Dishes could include the likes of tuna crudo, blood orange, chilli and coriander followed by vongole linguine with venus and razor clams.

Name: Tchaikovsky
Description: Set within the well-known Hotel Telegraaf, in the heart of the Old Town, this glass-roofed restaurant has something of a celebratory feel, courtesy of a beautiful chandelier and walls hung with gilt-framed pictures. To the side of the hotel is its large summer terrace, while at the head of the room a living wall, set behind glass, brings the outside inside year-round. Refined cooking has a classical French base with Russian influences and modern overtones – the Siberian dumplings, which come with the likes of horseradish beurre blanc, are a must-try.

Name: Lee Brasserie
Description: With its ornate columns, a terrace that stands at the foot of the old city walls and a name that refers to the ancient communal fireplace around which families would sit to prepare a meal, there's a historic undertone to this cosy restaurant. Powder blue walls, red banquettes and wooden furnishings give the room a subtle French brasserie feel – and the concise menu brings some Gallic influences into play too. Sharing is encouraged, but the best way to enjoy the experience is to order the tasting menu. Dishes could include sourdough waffles with trout roe or beef tenderloin with kampot pepper.

Name: Osteria il Cru
Description: Spread between the basement and the ground floor of a small hotel in the Old Town, CRU has been reborn as Osteria il Cru – and both its new name and the olive tree at the centre of the cosy room give a good indication of its new direction. Head Chef Ivari Vokk leads a newly formed kitchen team in creating Italian dishes that exhibit all the flavours you know and love, enhanced by a few personal twists. The extensive menu represents good value and offers plenty of choice, including the likes of spinach and ricotta stuffed zucchini flowers, parmigiana di melanzane and delicious homemade pastas.

Name: Fotografiska
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Above the Fotografiska photo gallery sits an equally striking restaurant offering picture-perfect views out across the Old Town; be sure to make the most of this by either starting or ending your night with cocktails in the rooftop bar. A concept of ‘Sustainable Pleasure’ leads the way, with a ‘leaf-to-root, nose-to-tail’ ethos and a zero-waste approach leading the way. Organic ingredients that are farmed with ecology in mind are showcased in a highly original selection of assured, understated dishes like rabbit agnolotti or apple pie with chanterelle ice cream. On summer Sundays they offer a themed brunch.

Name: VÕIVÕI
Description: VÕIVÕI sits within a modern office building, and its upper level is home to a smart cocktail bar and lounge – the perfect spot to either start or end your evening. Fire and butter lead the way on the boldly flavoured menus, with fish, meat and game all cooked over wood to impart a smokey flavour, and a ‘butter index’ illustrating the quantities used within each dish (which could include the likes of pikeperch with carrot cream and beurre blanc). Don’t miss the dumplings prepared according to the chef's grandma's special recipe, with each one folded by Mama Djatšuk herself using a masterful technique.

Name: Hiis
Description: Head east towards the coast and you’ll find yourself in a rural setting that plays host to this old farmhouse on the Taju Estate. Hiis translates as ‘secret grove’ or ‘holy site’ and, along with the forest and garden, the restaurant operates as a collective dedicated to the health and wellbeing of others. Here, Daanius Aas offers a 15-course menu of ingredients foraged from the surrounding land, as well as lesser-used cuts of meat and fish, to just six tables. Creativity leads the way, with detailed techniques used to capture the best flavours and textures, and childhood memories also coming into play.

Name: Joyce
Address: V Spaa Hotell, Riia 2, Tartu, 51004, Estonia
Description: A modern shopping centre in the heart of the city plays host to this large, split-level brasserie with bold décor, a popular cocktail bar and a buzzy vibe. Attractively presented dishes mix local and Baltic influences: the kitchen adds creative twists and flavours pack a punch.

Name: Pull
Description: Within the rejuvenated pre-war industrial area of the ‘Rotermann Factories’ sits an impressive 19th-century grain elevator and, inside that, this fittingly rustic restaurant proudly displaying exposed stone walls and concrete pillars amongst other original features. At dinner, the wide-ranging menu of generously proportioned Estonian dishes focuses largely on meats and steaks from the charcoal grill – including their signature 'Dirty Steak' – while at lunchtime nearly everyone is here for their great value dish of the day. A good range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks accompanies.

Name: Wicca
Address: LaSpa Hotel, Puhkekodu tee 4, Laulasmaa, 76702, Estonia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Angelica Udeküll is not only a well-known TV chef but also a torchbearer for Estonian cuisine. Her elegant restaurant at the LaSpa hotel sits in a beautifully tranquil spot overlooking the pine trees and the sea – the perfect location to showcase her ethical cuisine. Cooking is original, ranging from interpretations of her grandmother's recipes to dishes which incorporate elements from her travels. The drinks menu is split in two to offer the choice of either international beverages or local flavours that celebrate the region's heritage.

Name: Hõlm
Description: Hotel Lydia welcomed its first guests in 2016, but its story stretches back to the 1800s – and it’s this heritage that inspired both the hotel’s name and that of its restaurant. Lydia Grünmann Hõlm, the founders’ beloved grandmother, is not just referenced here in name though, as it’s her recipes that shape the cuisine, taken from a cookbook she wrote in 1925. That’s not to say that this restaurant is traditional; in fact, it’s quite the opposite. This a smart, modern spot both in looks and style, where the cooking takes on an ambitious, contemporary approach that comprises many different elements.

Name: Art Priori
Description: Set in the heart of the Old Town, this is a wonderfully elegant, romantic spot, where two striking rooms ooze period charm and an eclectic mix of artwork fills the walls. In contrast, the food is modern and understated. Well-formed dishes give each core ingredient the space to shine, with unadulterated flavours fitting together seamlessly. You might find earthy yellow beetroot paired with soft goat’s cheese or wonderfully mature venison with a silky celeriac purée. Friendly service and a great choice of cocktails and wines by the glass finishes things off perfectly.

Name: Rado
Description: Personally run Rado is a place of contrasts. It’s located in the delightfully historic Old Town but has a stylish modern interior. And the buzzy vibe of its ground floor gives way to a more intimate atmosphere in the basement. What is consistent throughout is the service. The chatty, knowledgeable team will guide you through the daily blackboard menu, whose terse descriptions mask ambitious dishes guided by the seasons, maybe ‘Cauliflower’, served with a thick thyme sauce and topped with parmesan, or ‘Lamb Liver’, presented on a bed of creamy mash and accompanied by bitter chicory leaves and sharp pickled mushrooms.

Name: RADIO
Description: Part wine shop, part café-cum-bistro, this neighbourhood establishment is all things to all people. You enter via a shop packed full of interesting wines, before heading through the restaurant where a glass wine cave takes centre stage. The room has a bistro feel – there are even a few sofas available for those who like it super laid-back – and dishes come in the form of medium-sized plates that are designed for sharing. From sausage soup to cured trout or onion pie, each dish comes with the perfect wine recommendation.

Name: ÂME
Address: Nunne Boutique Hotel, Nunne 14, Tallinn, 10133, Estonia
Description: Housed within a small boutique hotel on the edge of the Old Town is this elegant restaurant where the old and the new combine: part of the medieval city wall runs down one side of the room, yet it also has a contemporary, design-led style. Âme is French for ‘soul’ and, while the appealingly understated dishes certainly have a French heart, flavours are also drawn from around the globe. They describe their cooking as ‘dishes that feed the soul’; opt for the tasting menu to sample a range of these dishes, such as grilled Norwegian langoustine or wafer with coffee cream and lingonberries.

Name: SOO
Address: Maidla Nature Resort, Maidla Mõis 1, Maidla, 79408, Estonia
Description: This intimate restaurant resides in the former gatehouse of the Maidla Estate and its cosy, home-spun charm is a nod to its history. Finnish chef Karoliina Jaakkola has really made the place her own, telling a very personal story through a surprise menu that maps out her life: the fish soup is a childhood memory, the pasta she learned to make in New Zealand and the newer dishes incorporate Japanese elements from her latest travels. Pastry is her first love, and that shows through the lovingly prepared selection of desserts, but she also has a passion for discovery and pushing her own boundaries.

Name: Kolm Sõsarat
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Three Sisters run this small, remotely set restaurant and each has their role to play: Kerti does the cooking, Triin looks after the service and Kadri tends to the kitchen garden. The playful set menu is a showcase of the area, featuring top quality produce from their garden and farm – such as in the country-style mushroom, potato and sauerkraut – while superb honey from their father’s long-established hives is celebrated in desserts such as honey, apple and milk with sea buckthorn. This is a truly special place where the passion of the team is palpable, as they go above and beyond to care for every guest.

Name: Gianni
Description: Pop into the café for coffee and cake, or dine in a more cossetted environment in the modern restaurant. The charming team are eager to please and will even skilfully fillet your fish at the table for you. The comprehensive menu offers all the Italian dishes you know and love; the saltimbocca is a highlight.

Name: Horisont
Description: Arrive early for an aperitif in the bar, which affords stunning panoramic views towards the harbour from the 30th floor of the smart Swissotel Tallinn hotel. There’s a formal feel to the room, with modern European menus to match; to see the full talents of the kitchen, go for the tasting menu.

Name: Mon Repos
Description: This former imperial summer residence comes with a charming interior which blends original stained glass windows and panelled ceilings with sleek, modern furnishings. The modern menu reflects the locale and extends across to the Mediterranean, with colourfully presented dishes exhibiting flavours and textures which have been well thought through. The gravlax with beets, horseradish and blinis is a must to start, and to finish the tiramisu is a winner. The lovely terrace looking out over Kadriorg Park is a popular spot.

Name: Moon
Description: Sitting within a former industrial complex, Telliskivi TLN is a thriving cultural and business centre. Amongst its many outlets sits Moon (Estonian for ‘poppy’) – a former blacksmith's from the Tsarist era – where the charming team greet both locals and visitors as if they are regulars. Their mantra is ‘simple, honest, local and sustainable’ – and that’s exactly what they do here. The seasonally changing menu comprises flavoursome Slavic dishes; be sure to start with some of the tempting snacks before moving on to the likes of Siberian dumplings or carp in sour cream with tomato and caper salad.

Name: Mere 38
Description: Set in a quiet village, this green-painted wooden house boasts both a fashionable New England style restaurant and smart apartments. It has a cosy dining room with fleece-covered chairs, as well as a lovely summer terrace. Dishes are largely Mediterranean influenced and are vibrant and full of flavour.

Name: Koyo
Address: The Burman Hotel, Dunkri 8, Tallinn, 10123, Estonia
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Notable sake list
Description: Chef Kazuto Hokari relocated from Japan to open this restaurant and share his love of his native cuisine. 11 bright-red upholstered seats skirt an L-shaped counter in the stylish dining room, where Kazuto serves his omakase menu to two sittings of guests each evening. Sushi is the main event, with the eel and akami tuna particular highlights and also a favourite of the chef himself. He fully guides guests through the menu in an informative and personable way, and service is professional and engaging all-round. A concise but carefully selected range of wines, champagnes and sakes complete the picture.

Name: Shang Shi
Address: The Burman Hotel, Rataskaevu 5, Tallinn, 10123, Estonia
Description: The name, ‘Royal Feast’, gives a good indication as to what to expect here. The understatedly elegant interior dreamed up by Macanese designers creates a calming setting in which to enjoy luxurious ingredients such as King crab from Norway and abalone from South Africa – and then there’s the house speciality, Peking duck, which is carved at the table, where you’re given the option to add Beluga caviar! The wine and cocktail list is one of the most impressive in the city, while the cellar bar, Fox Den, specialises in whisky. If you really want to make a night of it, finish up in The Bombay Club casino.

Name: Barbarea
Description: A former rubber boot factory in an up-and-coming area plays host to this city hotspot, which starts the day as a bakery and then morphs into a stylish, laid-back bistro in the evening. Family-style dining is at the heart of their ethos and the vibrant, flavour-packed sharing plates follow the seasons, with 50-75% of the ingredients (depending on the month) having been produced organically. The wine list comprises a good selection of natural, organic and biodynamic wines, and they have a wine bar next door where you can continue your night.

Name: R14
Description: The impressive 19C stone-built powerplant of the Rotermann factories is now a wine-shop-cum-wine-bar with a rustic, laid-back vibe, where a glass-walled wine cellar takes centre stage. Good value, unfussy Mediterranean dishes have a leaning towards Italy; come on a Sunday if you’re a fan of brunch.

Name: Puri
Description: Part of the marina development northwest of the city centre is this striking modernist building with an equally impressive split-level interior boasting floor-to-ceiling windows and contemporary blonde wood furnishings. Creative modern cooking sees seafood dishes taking the starring role; maybe start with a wine ‘baba’ topped with succulent langoustines before moving on to gratinated crab with creamy risotto. To accompany are a great selection of wines by the glass, with everything brought to the table by a cheery team.

Name: Rado Haapsalu
Description: Sister to the restaurant of the same name in Tallinn – and also with their signature bicycle parked outside – is this bright, modern bistro run by a sweet, friendly team. The small menu is chalked up on the blackboard and the fresh, unfussy cooking represents great value. In summer, head for the terrace at the back.

Name: Paju Villa
Description: The suburb of Nõmme is home to this elegant art nouveau villa named after Karoline Paju, who built the house in 1931. Dining takes place over two floors, with several small, interconnecting rooms creating a stylish and intimate space. Instead of being listed under the usual headings of ‘Starters’, ‘Mains’ and ‘Desserts’, the appealing dishes are presented under the tempting-sounding sections of 'Can’t Resist', 'For a Real Gourmand' and 'Cherry on Top'. The menu may be small, but modern twists bring an extra element to the classically based recipes, ensuring there’s something to appeal to one and all.

Name: Herrenhaus
Description: Herrenhaus is located in the centre of the picturesque old town. A cloister, where you will find a quaint little terrace during the summer, leads you to the restaurant on the first floor. The historical setting adds to the warm and welcoming atmosphere. The delicious food is prepared using select in-season regional produce. The dishes are served à la carte or in the form of a set menu. Tip: Inexpensive lunch deal. The genial and obliging waitstaff will be happy to advise you on your choices. There is also an attractively priced wine list dedicated to German, Austrian and Italian labels.

Name: La Maison d'Avignon
Description: Once the sommelier at Petit Amour on Spritzenplatz, Mathias Mercier has now realised his dream and opened his own restaurant just a short distance away. In a relaxed setting, diners are offered a small à la carte selection; if they wish, they can create a small set menu comprising three to six courses from the individual dishes. Alternatively, they can opt for the nine-course tasting menu – the value for money is excellent. The cuisine clearly draws on the chef-patron's southern French roots, featuring delicacies such as fougasse with a superb anchoïade (anchovy sauce) and pralines infused with lavender or pastis. A standout dish is the sea bass with peach, verbena and navy beans. The wine list includes some rare gems at reasonable prices. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: GRETA OTO Munich
Description: For starters, the location right on the square known by locals as "Stachus" is nothing short of exclusive. GRETA OTO is housed within the luxurious and contemporary new Königshof hotel, on the ninth floor to be precise, affording fantastic views of the city of Munich and the Frauenkirche. The restaurant is no less chic and sophisticated than the hotel itself. Calm warm hues and dimmed lighting create an intimate atmosphere. The cuisine is Latin American with modern international influences, from Peruvian ceviche to Brazilian fillet steak and grilled octopus. The wine list to accompany the food is international. Tip: They have a private table – "La Mesa" – that you can book for special occasions. There is also a bar and a lounge terrace.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: With this concept, Tim Raue has tapped into the zeitgeist. The ambiance feels like that of a French brasserie – stylish yet cosy. Service is well-organised, friendly and attentive, and the delicious food is prepared using select ingredients. Diners can order à la carte or compose their own four-course set menu, which can also be vegan. Classics such as beef Wellington (served for two) are available too, as well as seasonal dishes.

Name: Otto
Description: Conveniently located in the city centre, a stone's throw from the cathedral and the Rhine River, this is the second maiBeck restaurant. In a trendy and chic setting, Jan C Maier and Tobias Becker serve up modern Italian cuisine with a focus on fish and seafood, although vegetarian options are also available. The pasta dishes are highly recommended. In addition to the excellent à la carte selection, the six-course "La Sera" set menu is available in the evening. The wine list is exclusively Italian. The front-of-house team are dedicated and attentive – the chefs also help to serve the food.

Name: Restaurant 1250
Description: Even the drive up to the Boutique Hotel Blaue Burg is an exceptional experience: the view of the region is breathtaking, with a new photo opportunity at every turn. Against this sensational backdrop, the Schlachter family, known for their dedication to the job and their reliably good food, serves seasonally and regionally minded cuisine at Restaurant 1250 – making it a wonderful alternative to the fine dining restaurant, PAVO. The terrace with a view in the direction of the castle and Austria is simply divine. Good to know: they also serve lunch.

Name: Yabase
Description: Calling all Japanese food aficionados! For an authentic experience, head to this restaurant in the centre of Düsseldorf's Japanese quarter. Behind a rather unassuming exterior an upscale minimalist-style space awaits. The service is friendly and professional. In the kitchen, top-notch fresh ingredients meet expert preparation techniques. The sushi and sashimi offer exceptional value, but more adventurous diners should try the unaju (rice bowl with barbecued eel) or the barbecued tuna head with vinegar for a real explosion of flavour. Complement your meal with some warm sake or Japanese beer. It is rare to get a table on the spur of the moment, so make sure you book in the evening. With a bit of luck, you can dine directly at the counter with its fish display case and watch the chefs at work. Lunch reservations are not possible – diners often queue at the entrance even before opening time.

Name: buffet Kull bar
Description: A word to the wise: Book ahead to avoid disappointment at this trendy restaurant in the centre of Munich! The "French bistro meets New York steakhouse" concept is a hit. The atmosphere is lively, the tables are close together, and the service is both lively and attentive. But above all, it's the cuisine that impresses: Here, the focus is clearly on taste and ingredients – no visual frills needed. The cooking is precise and unpretentious. Mouth-watering options include the NY-style fillet steak with maître d'hôtel butter. For dessert, why not try the tarte Tatin served with vanilla ice cream and crème fraîche?

Name: Celia
Description: For an authentic taste of Mexico in Düsseldorf, head to Celia in the bustling Bilker Kirche area. Rene Brauchle, of Mexican-German heritage and born in Venezuela, and Florentina Assis, a native Chilean, have been sharing their passion for Latin American cuisine here since summer 2024. The joy and enthusiasm of your cordial hosts is palpable, and they clearly love what they do: he is in charge of the kitchen, and she presides front-of-house. Once you have tried his mouthwatering dishes such as the taco pescado, the ceviche or the cochinita, you'll be hooked and eager to return. Fun fact: this friendly, modern restaurant is named after Rene's grandmother, who inspired his love of cooking.

Name: Restaurant Kurt im Gutshaus
Description: A truly idyllic location. A cobblestone drive meanders through the stunning estate to the lovingly restored historical manor that houses this restaurant. Inside, contemporary design elements have been seamlessly incorporated into the classically elegant decor. The terrace overlooking the grounds is glorious in summer! Expect clearly structured modern cuisine notable for their finesse and pleasing contrasts. Chef Mehmet Kaan Verdo works primarily with regional ingredients sourced within a 100km radius, drawing on his Turkish-Italian roots and skilfully incorporating classic French techniques and seasonal nuances. There are two set menus: "Nachbarschaft" ("Neighbourhood") and the vegetarian "Ackerland" ("Farmland"). Each comes in four to six courses, featuring dishes such as lamb shoulder with radicchio, morels and hibiscus, or celery, truffle, leek and egg yolk. Dishes can also be ordered individually. Friendly service and astute by-the-glass wine recommendations add the finishing touch. The wine list features labels from around the globe. Tastefully furnished guestrooms are available at Gutshaus Stolpe hotel.

Name: Le Canard
Description: Architect Meinhard von Gerkan has designed an impressive location here with his semi-circular building reminiscent of a steamship. The large windows on all sides and the magnificent terrace afford mesmerising views of the Elbe and the ever-bustling container port! This visual treat is complemented by a delightfully elegant modern decor, friendly and attentive service, and contemporary French cuisine served as a set menu or à la carte. Premium ingredients and masterful preparation are showcased in dishes such as tender Wagyu roast beef accompanied by a bold Bordelaise sauce and celeriac mille-feuille. Lunch is also served Fri and Sat.

Name: Acetaia
Description: This delightful restaurant with a cosy atmosphere, Jugendstil decor and charming service has been around since 1999. It brings not only Italian joie de vivre but also Italian cuisine to the table – try the sheep's-cheese ravioli! If you are open to letting the kitchen surprise you, take a punt on the four-course "Giorgio's Set Menu". Alongside a good Italian selection, the wine list includes some rarities from France. Incidentally, you also have the opportunity to purchase the aged balsamic vinegar after which this place is named. In summer, head for the shady terrace. The location by the Nymphenburg Canal is conducive to taking a stroll.

Name: Atelier Gourmet
Description: Small, intimate, lively and popular, Atelier Gourmet is quite simply a great little restaurant. The food is fresh, delicious and good value for money thanks to chef Bousquet. It is served in a casual, friendly atmosphere with efficient service and good wine recommendations from the female owner. Try the capon and duck crépinette.

Name: Ouzeria
Description: Maria Karpathiotaki and her partner Nikos Kasotakis have taken over her parents' Greek restaurant in the Belgian Quarter and turned it into a hip and vibrant fine dining spot. In a trendy bistro-style setting, friendly service comes courtesy of the proprietress. For a special experience, grab one of the six seats at the counter with a pass-through to the kitchen, where chef Nikos crafts modern and creative dishes with both Mediterranean and Asian influences. The menu includes a lovely selection of starters, plated in slightly smaller portions that are good for sharing and for trying out several – examples include scallops with Savoy cabbage, lime mayonnaise, and wild garlic and almond sauce, or half a corn-fed poularde breast with fermented celeriac, baby pak choi, ponzu, and miso and Samos Nectar espuma. Naturally, the menu also features ouzo. There is a small terrace laid out on the pavement.

Name: Gasthof zum Kranz
Description: Built in 1769 and run by the same family for seven generations, the interior at Zum Kranz is modern and elegant in the minimalist style. The kitchens produce flavoursome, classic, international fare. If you come in the autumn, make sure you try the game!

Name: Freisinger Hof
Description: It is easy to see why this charming inn dating from 1875 is always busy. It boasts a stylish interior, a lively atmosphere and delicious food. There are classics from Bavaria and Austria – the focus is on beef but there is also Backhendl (breaded fried chicken). If you're lucky, you'll be able to try the fabulous creamy veal goulash at lunchtime. Quick and helpful service. You can have a comfortable stay in one of the well-maintained guestrooms.

Name: Le Schloss Halberg
Description: The restaurant nestled in one wing of the castle, which was built between 1877 and 1880, has rightly proved to be a hit with diners. Its popularity is due both to the beautiful historical estate with its delightful terrace, and to the classic French cuisine – eschewing unnecessary frills in favour of full-bodied flavour, it is made with fresh top-notch ingredients. The speciality of beef fillet tartare with French fries and salad is prepared tableside. France also makes its presence felt in the savvy wine list.

Name: VOX Restaurant
Description: Housed in Berlin's Grand Hyatt, very close to Potsdamer Platz, this is a modern and spacious restaurant with an open layout. Diners can enjoy an interesting fusion of authentic Japanese sushi and contemporary cuisine, either à la carte or as a five-course set menu. Friendly service completes the experience. Seats at the sushi counter are particularly popular. Tip: Alongside a fine selection of wines, there are creative cocktails, mocktails and a truly impressive array of whiskies from across the globe – the fabulous bar is not to be missed.

Name: Park Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located at Parkhotel Bremen, this restaurant occupies an elegant conservatory overlooking the Bürgerpark and the lake (Hollersee). Frank Seyfried, previously at Gotthardt's in Koblenz, runs the kitchen, serving up a contemporary take on classic cuisine. Create your own three- to six-course set menu from a tempting array of dishes. The good food is complemented by friendly and adept service.

Name: Huber
Description: Sandra and Michael Huber run their sleek, minimalist-style restaurant In an attractive residential area of Bogenhausen. Here, they serve flavoursome and ambitious contemporary cuisine that makes a pleasingly down-to-earth impression. There is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), each comprising four or six courses, with dishes such as spinach with organic egg and Perigord truffle or skrei, beans and 'nduja. The wine list has a few gems in store, with plenty of appealing options for every budget.

Name: VINOTHEK by Geisel
Description: Housed in the luxurious EXCELSIOR by Geisel hotel in the centre of Munich, not far from Stachus, Vinothek is a relaxed establishment done out in a cosy rustic style. The high cross-vaulted ceiling certainly has the wow factor, as does the array of decorative wine bottles. As you might expect from the name of this restaurant, delicious dishes that are inspired by the region and the Mediterranean – such as octopus carpaccio with fennel salad, potato, tomato and basil, or glazed veal cheek with truffle sauce, celeriac and mashed potato – are accompanied by a terrific selection of international wines. Comprising around 800 items, the list is dominated by German, French and Austrian labels. Tip: Check out their reasonably priced lunchtime set menu, which includes coffee and water. Cookery courses and "kitchen parties" are also organised.

Name: Weinhaus Neuner
Description: With its cross-vaulted ceiling, herringbone parquet and wood panelling, this old restaurant has lost nothing of its traditional charm. The food is just what you would expect from an upmarket Munich inn – try the flaky pastry crust chicken fricassee pie. The Kaiserschmarrn for two is also a firm favourite! Nice wine list with a good selection of champagnes.

Name: Landhaus Hadrys
Address: An der Halberstädter Chaussee 1, Magdeburg, 39116, Germany
Description: The name Sebastian Hadrys has been synonymous with quality cuisine since 2003. His seasonal dishes have a Mediterranean edge. In addition to an enticing à la carte selection, there is a sophisticated set menu comprising four to nine courses, as well as a special set menu to kick off the weekend on Friday evenings. The wine list is also very good. The pleasingly bright, modern space has a casual feel, plus a large terrace. Experienced staff provide friendly service. Tip: Cookery courses are also organised here.

Name: Zur Mühle
Description: In their well-established restaurant – it’s been in the same family since 1895 – Hermann and Kerstin Berger prepare internationally inspired cuisine such as sliced salmon in a rocket and pesto crust with teriyaki beans, mashed potato and sweet mustard. The interior is cosy with a modern note.

Name: Gasthaus
Description: Like the gourmet restaurant, Gasthaus also combines modernity and tradition, from the decor down to the menu. While things are a bit more casual here, the cooking is also really good – the quality of the sauces alone will convince you of that! You can put together your own menu – and even make it vegetarian. Friendly service.

Name: Locanda Grappolo d'Oro
Description: It really is a joy to dine at this restaurant, which has been run by the same family with great dedication for years. The decor is bright and cheerful, and warm hospitality and service come courtesy of the lady of the house. The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is fresh and delicious. The pasta, the gnocchi, the bread… It's all house-made. No wonder this place draws so many regulars from the region.

Name: Hebelstube
Description: This establishment has been a familiar and beloved landmark for decades. The long-established Hotel Alte Post offers contemporary-style guestrooms, and the restaurant serves a modern take on classic and regional dishes, such as salmon trout ceviche or dry-aged saddle of back, prepared by new chef duo Nicolas Volk and Christoph Dees and team. The wine list predominantly features labels from the region. Diners can also look forward to a friendly and charming atmosphere, as well as attentive service. The terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Johanna Berger
Description: Tucked away in a fine 19C building in the centre of Lübeck, this restaurant has a charming interior with wooden flooring, chandeliers and an elegant feel. The pretty terrace enjoys an appealing location to the rear of the building. On the menu: a modern take on Mediterranean cuisine, available as a surprise menu or à la carte. Nice selection of German and international wines, also available by the glass.

Name: Weinhaus Anker
Description: Run with great dedication, this restaurant is steeped in tradition. The original charm of the building has been beautifully retained in the dining spaces – eg the Alte Stube with its wood panelling and ceiling paintings, and Im Fachwerk with its combination of rustic old beams and modern design features. The cuisine is predominantly regional, but the menu also includes French-influenced dishes. Friendly service. Tip: The Holzfasskeller, a 400-year-old wine cellar, can be booked for events. Well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: handicap.
Description: There is temporarily a change of concept here, with an amended menu, "Restaurant Würzburger Bau", being served until the end of June. From July onwards, fine dining cuisine will be back. As its name suggests, this tastefully decorated restaurant in a side wing of Hotel Anne-Sophie employs differently abled people, and the success of the initiative is clear to see in the great team. In the stylish decor, clean lines meet artwork, including a celestial painting by Markus Schmidgall on the high ceiling. The small terrace in the courtyard is delightful on a fine summer's day.

Name: schuberts
Description: Located in the centre of town, right by the Lauter River, this popular restaurant has a casual brasserie feel and serves flavoursome regional and seasonal cuisine that draws on Mediterranean influences. The daily special, "Schuberts Schneller Teller" ("Schubert's Quick Plate"), is a hit at lunchtime. Entennest is a cosy and charming wine tavern that makes for a more rustic alternative – the menu is the same here in the evening. If you would like to stay overnight, the hotel of the same name has attractive individually furnished guestrooms.

Name: Hinterding
Description: Dating back to 1904, this spruce urban villa has been known as a stylish culinary destination for aeons. Owners Klaus Weingartz (kitchen) and Elke Zeitner (front of house) have been running this establishment with great dedication since 2011. Ambitious classic cuisine made with select ingredients is served by charming waitstaff in comfortable and elegant dining rooms with high ceilings, or out on the gorgeous terrace. Set menus can even be pre-ordered to take home. Cookery classes and overnight accommodation are also available.

Name: Villa Feer
Description: Owner Kathrin Bucher has been running this restaurant in an attractive old villa near Lörrach exhibition centre since 2012. Dine in the cosy, bright interior or, in summer, out on the wonderful terrace. They serve lunch only: until 3pm you can order the set menu or from a small menu compiled from favourite dishes of the last decade. After that, there are desserts and ice creams/sorbets until 5pm.

Name: Gasthaus Stappen
Description: Steeped in tradition, this establishment is run with great dedication. Diners are drawn by the attentive service provided by the friendly and adept staff, as well as the excellent food. The regional cuisine is replete with international influences. The leafy terrace is delightful in summer. Ask about the wine tastings held in the wine shop. Tip: There are chic, modern guestrooms should you wish to stay overnight. N.B. card payment only.

Name: Planerts
Description: Casual fine dining near the church (Nikolaikirche) and opera house (Leipzig Oper). The high ceilings, exposed ventilation shafts, urban design and open kitchen create an on-trend industrial-style interior in which to savour cuisine with Asian influences. The dishes can be combined to compose a set menu or chosen à la carte. Friendly service and good wine recommendations. Thu-Sat, lunch takes the form of a dish of the day or a three-course set menu.

Name: Hirsch Genusshandwerk
Description: This lovely village inn serves dishes with classical foundations and modern inspirations. The seasons call the shots, and there is a preference for quality produce sourced locally or even grown in the restaurant's own garden. Sustainability is clearly a priority here. Led by the proprietress, the cordial and competent front-of-house team helps create the welcoming atmosphere. The terrace is delightful in summer. They also have their own distillery.

Name: ZEN Japanese Restaurant
Description: Located in a residential area, this restaurant is a firm favourite with fans of Japanese cuisine. In a pared-back Far Eastern-style setting, diners can look forward to a pleasantly lively atmosphere, as well as friendly and professional service with an authentic Japanese touch. It is clear that a well-coordinated team is at work here. Your options include gyoza, tempura, grilled and pan-fried dishes, udon, sushi and sashimi, plus a large omakase set menu. Wine, sake and Japanese whisky to go with it.

Name: Caroussel Nouvelle
Description: In the attractive Hotel Bülow Palais in Dresden's Baroque quarter, the bistro and winter garden have been combined in the Caroussel Nouvelle, with a stylish interior by star designer Carlo Rampazzi. At lunchtime and in the evening, there is a "Classics" menu, along with two additional tasting menus, one of which is vegetarian, on Tue-Sat evenings. The seasonal dishes are in a classic French vein and inspired by the region. For an aperitif or digestif, head to the Palais Bar and Cigar Lounge.

Name: NeoBiota
Description: Chef-patrons Sonja Baumann and Erik Scheffler propose ingredient-forward, seasonal cuisine. The majority of the ingredients are sourced from the surrounding area, and some are even foraged by the chefs themselves. The food is predominantly vegan-vegetarian, with pescetarian and "omnivore" options available. In the evening, as Biota, they serve a set menu composed of four, six or eight courses, including dishes such as Eifel salmon trout with pepper and habañero or broad beans with nettles and potatoes. The house classic, "Viking muesli", is often served as an amuse-bouche. The wine list centres on organic, biodynamic and natural wines. The set menu is accompanied by a good selection of wines by the glass or alcohol-free drinks. The appealing space has a clean-lined, modern style; the terrace is also lovely. As Neo, they serve an enjoyable breakfast from 10am to 3pm.

Name: Gruber's Restaurant
Description: Austrian cuisine is served in this charming restaurant with its various tastefully decorated rooms and pretty terrace. Whether traditional (such as the excellent schnitzels and memorable Kaiserschmarrn – shredded pancakes) or modern (Carinthian cheese noodles, pointed cabbage and blueberries), the dishes are always made from carefully chosen ingredients. More limited options, plus a schnitzel menu at lunchtime.

Name: Alfredo
Description: If you are in the mood for authentic Italian cuisine in Cologne, Roberto Carturan is your man. His father, Alfredo, laid the foundations for upscale Italian cuisine in 1973, and the second generation of the Carturan family has cultivated a straightforward and minimalist style of cooking. Without a doubt, the house classic is the pappardelle with braised duck. The charming chef-patron is on hand and will talk you through the menu in person. The atmosphere is relaxed – the focus is on pleasure. You can feel that the whole team is genuinely invested in your experience. Besides cooking, Roberto Carturan has another talent: he is a trained singer – on Friday evenings there's the "musical culinary soirée": a six-course set menu with a performance by him as the finale! One practical tip: Parking is available in the Opern Passagen shopping centre located behind the restaurant. You might also take the opportunity to see the original 4711 store with its famous carillon.

Name: Alte Mühle Thomas Höreth
Description: With this individual and thoroughly charming establishment the Höreth family have created a wonderful retreat. The guest lounges are lovingly decorated and the inner courtyard is idyllic. This is a real gem of a place, which also has its own wine estate. Slightly higher up, charming rooms are available for guests to stay the night.
