Name: Oberländer Weinstube
Description: This townhouse, built in 1826, is full of charm: inside you sit in a cosy, traditional wood-panelled decor, while the charming courtyard beckons outside. And in addition they take really friendly care of you. The kitchen turns out dishes that are adapted to the seasons and really tasty. At lunchtime you choose from a smaller menu.

Name: Weingärtnerhaus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Not only does this place promise good food, but the setting is also inviting: the restaurant is located in a lovely winegrower's house (named after the vineyards below). Built in 1542, it stands directly on the historical estate of Schloss Leitheim. Season-driven cuisine is served in a lovely, cosy interior. On Sundays and Mondays there is a more limited offering in the form of the Azubi-Menü devised by the trainee chefs. Tip: The wine list includes a number of South African vintages. Should you wish to stay overnight, the Schloss Leitheim hotel has inviting guestrooms.

Name: Landgrafen
Description: The restaurant close to the observation tower, also known as the Balcony of Jena, serves regional cuisine and offers a fantastic view over the city. Three individual rooms are available: country, Art Deco or honeymoon.

Name: Alemannenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This historical Black Forest establishment in an idyllic location is thoroughly inviting. Inside, an attractive upscale dining space exuding bags of regional charm awaits. Affording magnificent views of the lake, the terrace beckons in summer. The menu takes its cue from the seasons and includes dishes such as Black Forest trout fillets with pickled cherry tomatoes, courgettes and parsley mashed potatoes or French corn-fed poularde breast, tender young beans and thyme pasta. There is also a "Gourmetmenü" comprising five or eight courses with wine pairings. Options are more limited at lunchtime. For overnight stays, the boutique hotel of the same name has guestrooms that seamlessly blend modern and traditional elements.

Name: Krone
Description: Krone has been properly invested in: from the façade to the hotel rooms, everything is chic and high quality, the restaurant is modern and sleek. The food is very good, with select produce turned into aromatic dishes with plenty of flavour. At lunchtime, a smaller range of interesting options. If you are staying longer, Basel and Alsace are very close by.

Name: Gasthaus Spieker
Description: Gasthaus Spieker serves regional cuisine with a Mediterranean touch including "Spieker’s Tasty Tapas" and ragout of lamb with bulgur wheat, green asparagus and crème fraîche served in its tasteful, beautifully decorated dining rooms. For those who fancy an extra glass of wine there are also a number of well-kept guestrooms.

Name: SCALA - Das Turm Restaurant
Description: At 128m above street level, the striking JenTower affords fantastic views of the city and surrounding area! The cuisine is modern and international: dinner takes the form of a sharing menu comprising three to five courses (vegetarian version available); the lunchtime selection is a little more streamlined. Tip: From the Neue Mitte multi-storey car park, take the lifts up to the restaurant (there is a sign). Hotel on the floors below the restaurant.

Name: Heinzler am See
Description: Whether you are in the mood for regional comfort food or something more international, the Heinzler brothers have got it covered. Their wide-ranging menu includes Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy), Arctic char and whitefish fillets, and yellowfin tuna sashimi. There is also an appealing selection of barbecue dishes with a choice of side dishes and sauces. You can choose to dine in the cosy Jagdstube ("hunting lounge") with its winning blend of traditional charm and modern design, or the lovely Panorama-Restaurant, whose large windows afford stunning views. Not forgetting the fabulous terrace almost touching the water! The waitstaff are personable and attentive – service is clearly a serious matter here. Tasteful and comfortable guestrooms available at the hotel, which also boasts a private beach area at the lake and a private jetty.

The name of the game here is a culinary fusion of Peru and Italy. Drawing on his Peruvian heritage and inspired by life in Italy, head chef Matias Diaz weaves together produce from both countries in his "136 Experience Menü", a set menu that changes every two months. The restaurant's trendy vintage decor brims with charm. In summer, there are also tables outside.

Name: Freihardt
Description: Eating here is a real pleasure! The cuisine is international and seasonal, the highlight being the Bavarian beef steaks. They also serve burgers on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Head here on a Saturday for a three-course surprise lunch or on a Sunday for a traditional home-style roast. A friendly atmosphere reigns in the restaurant and its conservatory, and the terrace on the busy street is a place "to see and be seen". Right next door is the restaurant's own butcher's shop, which for many years has employed so-called humane slaughtering methods.

Name: Ole Liese
Description: Steeped in history, Gut Panker is a truly idyllic spot. The tranquil estate is the epitome of rural charm and is also known as a Trakehner stud farm – it forms the perfect backdrop for Hotel & Restaurant Ole Liese. The motto "Sunday cooking. Every day" underpins a menu of regional seasonal fare, which is served in the cosy, rustic interior, or out on the lovely terrace in summer. In addition, the estate's pretty café in the old night watchman's lodge serves coffee and cake from 2-5pm, and on Sundays, brunch is available by prior reservation. Overnight stays are possible in stylish, individually decorated guestrooms.

Name: aerde
Description: Housed within the imposing building designed by architectural firm Robertneun in the Lokdepot development, this compact restaurant is well worth seeking out. In the kitchen, set on a mezzanine above the dining space, the chefs create modern dishes designed for sharing. Seasonal ingredients take centre stage, with fermentation playing a key role – a theme echoed by the decorative jars displayed throughout the pared-back interior, which features clean lines, wood finishings and earthy hues. Capacity is limited to a few small tables, a communal table in the middle and the bar counter. The atmosphere is neighbourly and personal; service is friendly and adept. The team are happy to provide drinks recommendations, drawing from an exciting selection.

Name: Teko by Lange Rodriguez
Description: Teko refers to "culture" in Spanish. As the son of a German father and Bolivian mother, owner Hans Robert Lange Rodriguez adheres to a mantra of "two cultures, one flavour". His set menu sees influences from both South America and Germany, with the traditional meeting the modern. Choose either the five- or seven-course format of the set menu, which includes dishes such as "Wagyu, leek, ulupica pepper, quinoa, pimiento" or "hiromasa, sandia, chontaduro, coconut, nori". There is also a vegetarian version of the set menu. Attentive and professional service. The cosy modern space is decorated with pictures and pleasant background music for a South American vibe.

Name: Fa:me
Description: This intimate little restaurant with a buzzing, neighbourly atmosphere calls itself a "gastrobar", and that pretty much hits the nail on the head, as food and drinks have equal billing here. Located in the Kreuzkölln neighbourhood, this place is run by the two owners, who divide their time between the kitchen and service. Although limited, the à la carte selection is well-devised, comprising ambitious modern dishes. There is also a 10-course tasting menu for two or more people to share. A glance at the drinks menu is enough to reveal their passion for carefully selected wines, their own cocktail creations and house-made kombucha – and guests are taken through the options by the charming and enthusiastic staff, who bring a pleasingly personal touch.

Name: Gasthaus zum Raben
Description: This charming farmhouse dating back to 1604 is truly idyllic! Set at an altitude of around 600m, it boasts a beautiful location with views of Freiburg. Inside, low ceilings, rustic wooden seats and benches, wooden floorboards and an old tiled stove make for a cosy atmosphere and tap into the character of the region. Dedicated owners Melanie and Pierre Barrel are in the thick of the action here – she heads up the friendly and professional service team; he runs the kitchen. Diners are served a "carte blanche" menu of four or six courses, inspired by the seasons and the proprietors' French heritage. In addition to the restaurant, there is a bistro section with a short à la carte menu. The garden and terrace are real highlights – in summer, guests naturally gravitate outdoors. Those looking to stay a little longer and explore the wonderful Black Forest landscape can spend the night in one of the attractive, comfortable rooms available in the charming guesthouse.

Name: Schote
Description: After Nelson Müller and his entire team moved from Essen to Bergisch Gladbach, the likeable restaurateur and celebrity chef now offers his fine dining cuisine at the Diepeschrather Mühle, a former mill set in beautiful natural surroundings. They serve a modern, seasonal set menu comprising five or seven courses – the delicious tapas are a great way to start the meal. The vegetarian version of the set menu, dubbed "No Meat No Fish", needs to be booked two days in advance. You can also opt into the wine pairings. Here at the new location, there is also an alternative restaurant: Müllers in der Mühle brasserie. For a really chic overnight stay, this gorgeous property also houses an exquisite boutique hotel with tasteful, modern guestrooms and suites, as well as an attractive wellness and spa area.

Name: Feine Kost
Description: In August 2024 Mario Pattis established his Feine Kost restaurant, which entices diners with an appealing variety of modern-creative and classic cuisine. In a chic neighbourhood of Dresden Neustadt, the establishment serves dishes that are packed with flavours and interesting textures – these are organised into a set dinner menu with a choice of main course and dessert. The starter variation with various small dishes such as ‘duck liver, apricot jam, toasted brioche’ is a real delight. The wine pairing is also recommended. The decor is sleek and modern, with an eye-catching wall decorated with porcelain crockery. Large windows look out onto the beautiful terrace laid out in the charming courtyard, which is accessed via the restaurant. The atmosphere is relaxed and the service professional. For a simpler alternative, Kantine is a charming option on the same premises.

Name: Untere Apotheke
Description: With its chic and trendy bistro feel and easygoing buzz, this restaurant right on Marktplatz is especially inviting. The food is in keeping with the modern setting, with a thoughtfully compiled menu featuring creative dishes based on classic recipes. Ambitious, precisely crafted and visually very appealing, these are prepared in a small glass-fronted kitchen – diners in the four counter seats are guaranteed some fascinating insights. In addition to the à la carte selection, there are two set menus. At lunchtime, the options are somewhat simpler and more limited. A fantastic initiative: In collaboration with a local vocational training centre (Berufsbildungswerk Waiblingen) , they run a garden project on Schmidberger Feld, embracing a farm-to-table approach. Tip for motorists: Marktgarage underground car park is nearby.

Name: Dallmayr Bar & Grill
Description: Located next to the delicatessen on the ground floor, this Dallmayr restaurant is steeped in tradition and offers a lively and relaxed, yet stylish dining experience. At closely spaced tables, diners enjoy prompt and adept service provided by a courteous and well-staffed front-of-house team in white uniforms. From oysters and caviar to seafood and Bavarian ribeye with balsamic pearl-glazed onions, the international menu certainly whets the appetite. Be sure to sample the beef tomato with feta, honey and sesame. The bar is another highlight, perfect for unwinding with a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Marly Privé
Description: The restaurant previously known as "Marly" has moved and is now operating under the name of Marly Privé. In its smaller space, this eatery serves classic French cuisine made from top-notch ingredients – chef-owner Gregor Ruppenthal's love for France is on full display. Accessed via Le comptoir 17, a cosy back room accommodates up to 12 diners who sit down to a five- or seven-course tasting menu – a four- or five-course version is served on Fridays. Dishes have names such as "Our octopus salad depuis 1999" or "Line-caught sea bass from Quiberon, leek, nori, pink onions", and are accompanied by a well-curated wine list. The service is friendly and attentive. Tip: Don't forget to reserve your spot!

Name: Silberstreif
Description: The Naturresort & Spa Schindelbruch features an ambitious restaurant concept called Silberstreif ("Silver Lining"), named after the 2022 butterfly of the year. Head chef Eric Jadischke and the young team rustle up contemporary cuisine inspired by the Harz region and its seasons. Some of the ingredients come from the garden that was planted with the restaurant's needs in mind. There is a five- to seven-course set menu, with corresponding wine or non-alcoholic pairings on request. Service is friendly and attentive. You might be interested to know that the dishes are served on Ritter von Kempski collection porcelain, designed by MEISSEN exclusively for this restaurant. The impressive pieces by artist Johann Elias Ridinger draw the eye with their hunting and forest motifs – a nod to the restaurant's close connection with nature. The hotel has tasteful guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Aifach Reisers
Description: On the site of the city's erstwhile covered market, Bernhard Reiser – inspired by that previous vocation – has brought to life a friendly, casual, seasonal restaurant concept. At lunchtime, a concise, reasonably priced menu including an enticing three-course set menu is served; in the evening, the cuisine is more ambitious and comes in à la carte or surprise menu form. Tables are laid out on the ground floor and in the gallery. From some seats you have a direct view of the action in the open kitchen on the lower level. In summer, head for the terrace overlooking the market square.

Name: Lido Hafen
Description: The location in the MedienHafen (Media Harbour) is remarkable in its own right: the restaurant occupies a minimalist glass cube hovering over the water, accessible via a bridge. The dedicated owners are a husband-and-wife team, who some might know from the restaurants Fritz's Frau Franzi and Pink Pepper. Ramona Kriegel heads up the friendly and professional service team while Benjamin Kriegel prepares a modern set menu comprising five to seven courses. The chef takes pride in his ingredients, which are always in season and of the finest quality. Wine pairings available.

Name: MA PETITE CHAMBRE
Description: Carina and Christoph Schmah now have a wonderful second eatery for their hotel and restaurant, Landhaus Halferschenke, in the form of this small fine dining restaurant. Behind the pretty quarry stone façade of this historical building, the space has a pleasantly calm and elegant atmosphere. Expert wine recommendations come courtesy of the cordial and proficient service team. The food is modern but grounded in the classics, with the chef-patron rustling up a six- to eight-course set menu out of top-notch ingredients. The restaurant has just four tables, for up to 12 guests, so be sure to book!

Name: Johannas
Description: With its appealing upscale decor, gorgeous courtyard terrace and good food, the restaurant in the family-run Hotel Neumayr is certainly inviting. The ambitious, seasonal cuisine is based on fresh, premium ingredients that are sourced from the region – some even come from the restaurant's own garden. Choose between the set menu and the à la carte dishes; game and offal specialities are a firm fixture on the menu. The chef's passion for wine is reflected in the impressive wine list, which features over 2 000 labels for connoisseurs to peruse. The selection is international, but Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from Burgundy take pride of place. Such a range in small-bottle format is quite something to behold. The waitstaff are professional, friendly and approachable.

Name: Il Borgo
Description: This Italian restaurant has been a mainstay of Schwabing's culinary scene since 1989. The interior is modern and elegant yet cosy, with the current decor successfully incorporating the old wall tiles and original bar. The menu sticks close to the seasons. In addition to the five-course tasting menu, there is an à la carte selection – from delicious pasta dishes to branzino al sale (salt-baked sea bass) for two.

Name: AL FORNO
Description: For fans of authentic Italian food, this ristorante makes for a pleasing alternative to JUWEL and WEBERSTUBE, the other two restaurants to be found here in the Hotel BEI SCHUMANN. Soak up the atmosphere in the wonderfully cosy dining area, in which Italian background music brings that feel-good factor, while the team in the open kitchen conjure up delicious fish and meat dishes, as well as classics such as antipasti, pasta and pizza cooked in the brick oven – the pizzas are available in smaller sizes, too. Desserts such as the zabaione di Marsala are also delicious. Speciality in winter: spaghetti from the parmesan cheese wheel. In summer, head for the pleasant terrace overlooking the SEEWUNDERBAR.

Name: Weinwirtschaft Kleines Jacob
Description: As soon as you enter this restaurant, you fall into the embrace of its inviting atmosphere: Charming tavern-style decor, soft candlelight and warm, attentive service make for a delightful setting – no wonder so many locals flock here as regulars. The Austrian cuisine is a hit – the "Schmankerl Brett" (snack platter) and stone-baked flammkuchen, as well as Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) and Wiener schnitzel are crowds-pleasers, not forgetting the caramelised Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with stewed plums. There is also an appealing three- or four-course set menu dubbed "Lütten Jacob Genusstafel". The wine list is exclusively Austrian, and some labels are available by the glass. No wonder this place has become a favourite of so many foodies!

Name: Einhorn
Description: This handsome inn steeped in history has been given a successful modern makeover. Inside, the pleasant decor is characterised by clear lines, warm wooden finishings and a palette of neutrals; outside, behind the building, the pretty, secluded terrace is extremely inviting. The menu features typical Swabian dishes, but also more sophisticated international dishes. You can opt for a set menu or select dishes from the à la carte menu.

Name: Hippocampus
Description: In the city's well-heeled Bogenhausen area, Hippocampus is no run-of-the-mill Italian restaurant; it is a ristorante with real character. The reins of this family business have now been passed on to the next generation, which is upholding the tradition of serving Italian cuisine. Order à la carte dishes or opt for the surprise menu. A two-course set lunch is available Wed-Fri. The impressive wine list features around 160 Italian labels. Expect attentive service, delivered with Italian charm. Add to this an attractive interior with stylish details such as half-wall panelling in walnut wood, marble floors and Art Nouveau lamps. The terrace is equally inviting.

Name: Galleria
Description: This extremely pleasant establishment is an institution here in the city centre – the small restaurant near Marienplatz has been around since 1998. A friendly atmosphere is fostered by the modern decor, with pictures and wine racks adding a nice decorative touch – royal blue gives the whole place a maritime feel. They serve really good Italian cuisine, including classics such as vitello tonnato and house-made pasta. At lunchtime, diners appreciate the competitively priced lunch set menu. The extensive wine list featuring wines from Italy is on point. Staff are attentive and knowledgeable. In summer, a table on the small terrace is a tempting prospect.

Name: Blauer Bock
Description: A cornerstone of the fine dining scene for years, this restaurant is housed in the spruce hotel of the same name, nestled in the centre of Munich – a stone's throw from the Viktualienmarkt and the city museum. The decor is tasteful, sleek and contemporary in style, with striking pictures adorning the walls. The cuisine is classic with a modern twist, and the menu includes mouthwatering options such as braised veal shoulder or sole for two. Outside, the tables overlooking the pedestrian area are in high demand.

Name: Little London
Description: This lively steakhouse not far from the Isartor is fronted by a classic bar of impressive dimensions – there are over 320 types of gin to choose from here! The attractive interior design successfully brings together a certain rusticity and a touch of English elegance. Meat eaters can look forward to high-quality cuts cooked on the Montague grill – tantalising examples include US Black Angus Prime Beef and Wagyu Kagoshima A5. There are over 250 wines on the wine list. Tip: Why not sign up for one of their beef-tasting sessions? With its various lounges, the restaurant also caters to private parties.

Name: Matsuhisa Munich
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted
Description: In keeping with the high standards of the luxurious Mandarin Oriental, this elegant minimalist-style restaurant is run by Nobu Matsuhisa, a renowned restaurateur with a global presence. The menu features a fusion of Japanese and Peruvian cuisines. As well as sushi and sashimi, there are exciting options such as Peruvian rib eye anticucho (skewers) or the house classic, black cod. Dishes are intended for sharing, allowing you to discover a kaleidoscope of flavours. In summer, you can dine on the hotel's roof terrace and take in fantastic views over Munich.

Name: Jin
Description: This restaurant that has been around for 20 years is certainly an institution. The many regulars appreciate the upscale minimalist-style interior inspired by the Far East, and the flavoursome pan-Asian cuisine, in which a distinct Chinese edge, as well as Japanese and European influences, can be detected. Diners can choose between the "Jins Degustation" set menu and an appealing à la carte selection. We particularly recommend the spring rolls, the bluefin tuna tartare and the handmade dim sum. The wine list is also excellent – connoisseurs will find something to their liking here.

Name: KOI
Description: Fans of modern Japanese cuisine should head here for the extensive range of sushi, as well as meat, fish and vegetable dishes and snacks. Some items are cooked on the Robata charcoal grill. Tempting options include "beef fillet teriyaki, Jerusalem artichoke chips, wafu" or "grilled miso aubergine, daikon salsa". With its dark wood, warm lighting and stylish details, the interior has an elegant, urban atmosphere; meanwhile, the bar on the upper floor exudes a loungey vibe. On fine summer days, the terrace is highly prized.

Name: Landhaus Mönchenwerth
Description: This inviting establishment has its fair share of regulars, and deservedly so. One of the main attractions is its location right by the Rhine – tables with a view of the river, as well as those on the gorgeous terrace, are in high demand. No less captivating are the creations of chef-patron Guy de Vries, whose French heritage shines through in work. Drawing from the bounty of each season, he concocts mouthwatering plates with a Mediterranean twist. The well-curated wine list includes an impressive selection of Champagnes. Friendly and adept service.

Name: Landhotel Donner
Description: Here you can enjoy classic regional cuisine – for example the menu features braised wild boar in a juniper jus. The decor is warm and welcoming, the pretty country-style dining rooms boast classy soft furnishings and warm wood. Don't miss the home-made cakes served in the afternoons on the pretty garden terrace. You can also stay overnight in well-kept accommodation.

Name: Gräfinthaler Hof
Description: In this somewhat more remote part of the Bliesgau region, you will feel most welcome in this gorgeous location that was once home to a monastery complex dating back to the 13C. Inside, an elegant atmosphere prevails; outside, there is a charming terrace shaded by trees. Ambitious dishes are created with terrific ingredients – the roast dry-aged pork chop (matured on the bone for 21 days), with sage, Serrano ham, market vegetables and potato fritters, for example, is a wonderful meat option. There are two set menus – one meat, one vegetarian – or you can dine à la carte.

Name: Wettsteins Restaurant
Description: This beautiful property is a little out of the way – on summer days, diners can enjoy sitting out on the terrace. The restaurant has been around for many years. In addition to cordial hosts and friendly service, the programme here includes regionally influenced cuisine, which you can choose to sample as a set menu or à la carte. The menu also features barbecued meat, such as rump steak, and classics like schnitzel and roast joint.

Name: Michaelis
Description: Tasty and fresh food is served in this refined restaurant in a restored building from the Wilhelminian period, which also houses the comfortable hotel of the same name. The menu is seasonal – there are various set menus (one of which is vegetarian) and a sophisticated à la carte selection. Friendly and attentive service. In summer, the terrace behind the house is very appealing.

Name: Schuppen 13
Description: The Pusceddu family’s restaurant is located right on the marina and from the outside looks a little like a boathouse. The food within is classic Italian cuisine meticulously prepared using fresh produce. Try the delicious baby squid braised in tomato stock with pan-fried polenta.

Name: Schweizer Wirt
Description: This place has been synonymous with tasty cuisine for years. The fresh, regional dishes are made with excellent ingredients. Stripped back to the essentials, they eschew any frills. The atmosphere in the restaurant is charming and the waitstaff are friendly. This beautifully situated traditional inn also has a fabulous terrace. You can park directly in front of the building.

Name: RIVA
Description: The fantastic location by the lake is a draw in itself – a spot on the lovely terrace with a view of the water is of course particularly sought after! But the interior of this bright, elegant restaurant inside the hotel of the same name is also appealing – the floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the lake can be opened up. The seasonal cuisine is predominantly regional, with international influences, Mediterranean or occasionally Asian touches. The menu also features classic dishes. Chic bar and relaxed outdoor lounge.

Name: Le comptoir 17
Description: The addition of "Bistrot Parisien" to the name tells diners exactly what to expect. If you like a friendly, down-to-earth bistro atmosphere and classic French cuisine, then this is the place for you! Here, the emphasis is on the excellent ingredients that are used to make their house specialities such as blood sausage, beef tartare, mussels or fish soup. As well as the regular menu, there are specials written up on the blackboard.

Name: Schwanen
Description: Here, the Swabian Jura theme is writ large. The menu changes with the seasons and puts the emphasis on top-quality ingredients, most of which are sourced from the surrounding area. A huge panorama of the Swabian Jura landscape is the most striking feature of the modern yet cosy dining area – it couldn't be more apt. Tip: Given the restaurant's proximity to OUTLETCITY, keen shoppers might consider an overnight stay in one of the hotel's stylish guestrooms.

Name: Lindenhof 1887
Description: This North German family-run establishment is pretty as a picture! After being welcomed into the attractive inn built in 1887 with a lively local greeting ("moin"), you can expect good, attentive service in a modern and thoroughly chic ambience. Chef Tjark-Peter Maaß cooks tasty dishes of a regional bent. For example, the fried North Sea plaice, fried potatoes, cucumber salad, Tönning shrimps is a tasty and fresh option – one of the classics. There are also some appealing and cosy guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Rôtisserie Jagdhof Stuben
Description: The cosy atmosphere and rustic charm of the Rôtisserie at the upscale Jagdhof Glashütte hotel are hard to beat – the warm wood panelling, a roaring fire in the hearth and a decorative old kitchen. And then there is the amiable and attentive front-of-house team, and a menu packed with classics. Excellent recommendations include Wittgenstein venison ragout and Wiener schnitzel made from milk-fed veal.

Name: C'est la vie
Description: This restaurant is dedicated to the French way of life. As you sit comfortably at your table in the stylish modern interior, looking out through the floor-to-ceiling windows, the dedicated team busy themselves in the open kitchen, cooking up modern interpretations of dishes such as sea bass with root vegetables and potato croissant or Bresse chicken with morels, shimeji mushrooms and vin jaune. The creations are organised into two set menus – one vegetarian, one with meat – and accompanied by exclusively French wine, which are charmingly and skilfully presented at your table with the aid of a map. The wines can also be purchased in the shop. Tip: There is parking in the garage right next door.

Name: Christoph Pauls Restaurant
Description: No stranger to the Rhineland's restaurant scene, Christoph Paul runs this trendy modern restaurant with his wife Juliane. The striking religious imagery on the wall is a reminder of the site's former vocation as a chapel. A seasonal three- or four-course set menu with a choice of dishes is served. The terrace laid out beneath venerable old trees is delightful. A parking space can be reserved upon request.

Name: Tafelhaus
Description: The tastefully modern restaurant of Neckartal business hotel is run with dedication. The regional cuisine draws on international influences and is made using top-notch seasonal produce. In addition to the menu, there are also daily specials presented verbally. Owner Bernd Nödinger brings not only professional competence but also a friendly and personal touch to the service. The beverage recommendations are also spot on – thanks to the Coravin system, you can even enjoy high-quality wines by the glass. There is a delightful terrace in summer, and that space gives way to the Tafelhütte event venue in winter. The restaurant is open for lunch on Wednesdays and Thursdays – please book in advance. Reservations for Sundays and Mondays are possible by prior arrangement.

Name: Villa Rothschild Grill & Health
Address: Im Rothschildpark 1, Königstein im Taunus, 61462, Germany
Description: Located in a park, this smart bankers' villa dating from 1894 is home to a stylish boutique hotel as well as this chic, modern and elegant restaurant. Patrick Bittner, who previously made a name for himself at Frankfurt's Français, where he was head chef for many years, is now at the helm here. The classic cuisine has international influences, and the dishes are served à la carte. Good news for oyster enthusiasts: There are always three varieties to choose from. The modern and elegant interior is tastefully decorated, with a striking open fireplace in the centre of the room serving as the focal point and creating a wonderful atmosphere in winter. In summer, the lovely terrace beckons. Tip: Head to Titian's Bar for a digestif. Lunch is also available on Sundays – ideal for day trippers.

Name: Landgasthof Hirschen
Description: The dedication of chef Verena Martin and her team is palpable. In a charming setting diners enjoy cordial service and good food that is made primarily with produce from the region and draws inspiration from the seasons. The kitchen staff put their heart and soul into their work – the motto here is ä weng eppis Feins, or "a little something fine" in the local dialect. Tip: "Unser badisches Menü" or "Unser großes Menü" (for two or more people).

The inscription "1906" is still to be seen above the timeworn arch at the entrance of this building in the centre of the old town. Having been completely gutted and meticulously rebuilt, the property now houses an invitingly chic, modern restaurant with large windows and an impressive open kitchen. The sophisticated dishes seamlessly highlight select ingredients with modern accents. Diners are offered a choice of various set menus; individual courses can also be ordered à la carte. Recommendations from the short, well curated wine list are always spot on. There is also a brasserie under the same roof.

Name: Atable im Amtshaus
Description: Surrounded by the town wall, the Amtshaus hotel boasts a lovely location in Freinsheim's old town, which is well worth a visit. The courtyard with its idyllic terrace leads to this chic restaurant, which is distinguished by its white cross vaults supported by columns. Chef Swen Bultmann cooks classic French dishes made from fine ingredients and inspired by the seasons. Diners can choose between a three- to six-course menu (vegetarian version available) or order à la carte. The food is accompanied by a well-curated and extensive selection of wines. An appealing and reasonably priced set menu is served at lunchtime. There are also tastefully appointed guestrooms – as in the restaurant, the decor harmoniously incorporates modern design into the historical setting.

Name: Café Rapp
Description: A visit to this delightful village is definitely worthwhile! Originally a bakery and café, this family-run establishment has evolved into a restaurant serving flavoursome, meticulously prepared dishes that take their cue from the changing seasons. As well as à la carte options, there is a choice of set menus. The upscale setting has a classic aesthetic. Attentive service comes courtesy of a well-organised and adept front-of-house team. A must in the afternoon: the delicious freshly baked cakes! Pretty guestrooms.

Name: Hanse Stube
Description: The exclusive Excelsior Hotel Ernst, right opposite the cathedral, is home to this tasteful and extremely elegant restaurant. With its dark wood panelling, it is an absolute classic, and something of a home from home for Cologne society. Hanse Stube offers ambitious classic cuisine with modern influences, in the form of a four- to six-course menu or à la carte. The special caviar selection is also worth considering. At lunchtime, there is an additional short set menu. Excellent wine list, friendly, proficient service, and a beautiful terrace. The restaurant can be accessed via the hotel entrance.

Name: Ressmann's Residence
Description: The modern decor, with its sleek design and light, warm tones, is a hit with diners, as are the ambitious, international, seasonal cuisine and fine wines. Tip: At lunchtime, you can put together your own inexpensive three-course menu or simply order à la carte. For those hot summer days, one of the dining rooms is air-conditioned, but if you would rather sit outside, there is a lovely garden terrace tucked away behind the building. Overnight accommodation is also available.

Name: Landgasthof Löwen
Address: Kirchdorfer Straße 8, Kirchdorf an der Iller, 88457, Germany
Description: Alexander Ruhland represents the fourth generation of his family to run this traditional country inn, and his kitchen turns out top-notch dishes. Two set menus are proposed: a seasonal one comprising three courses and a more ambitious four-course fine dining menu. There is also an à la carte selection featuring classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with Allgäu beef loin, as well as international dishes and vegetarian options.

Name: Das Obers
Description: In the smart Gern neighbourhood, a short distance from Nymphenburg Palace, Jürgen Wolfsgruber – known for his restaurants in Schwabing, Sparkling Bistro and Das Tschecherl – has now opened another inviting establishment serving Austrian-inspired cuisine. Diners can either opt for the five-course "Ö-Makase" surprise menu or choose from the small selection of appealing à a la carte options such as Grammelknödel (potato dumplings stuffed with greaves) or soused brown trout. Attentive service comes courtesy of a well-coordinated team of friendly and adept waitstaff, who reliably provide astute wine recommendations. The well-curated wine list includes options by the glass. A laid-back bistro atmosphere reigns inside; outside, there is a lovely terrace.

Name: BECKERS
Description: The atmosphere in this attractive historical corner-plot building is pleasingly casual. Featuring high ceilings, warm wood panelling, cosy booths and large arched windows, the pretty dining space has the feel of a classic bistro. There is also a bar, and in summer a terrace is set up out front, giving onto the street. The menu includes flavoursome dishes such as oysters, beef tartare, fine fish dishes and premium steaks. Tempting options on the shorter lunch menu include veal meatballs with carrots and mashed potatoes.

Name: die kleine Linde
Description: This compact restaurant started out in autumn 2024 as a pop-up serving dishes à la carte. Today, it opens its doors in the evenings to present modern and creative cuisine in the form of two exciting five- or seven-course set menus: "Eine Rundreise" and the vegetarian "Botanischer Garten". At the helm in the kitchen, Valentin Thesing (previously at Aqua in Wolfsburg) crafts dishes such as "egg, beetroot, spinach" and "pork jowl, carrot, carrot blossom honey" – expect expression, finesse and a perfect balance of flavours, complemented by robust sauces and stocks. The restaurant is housed in the stately, lovingly renovated Jugendstil building of the Lindenhof. Historical details such as high ceilings and striking pillars, wood panelling, charming old windows and lovely herringbone hardwood flooring have been tastefully incorporated into sleek, modern interior design. The atmosphere is pleasingly informal, and the service is attentive and professional.

Name: Bardele
Description: A pleasingly vibrant restaurant and bar reminiscent of a traditional trattoria. In keeping with the Italian spirit, chef-patron Tyler Hanse serves up traditional yet ambitiously executed cucina italiana, with house-made pasta as the main event. The dishes are based on precise craftsmanship, creative expression and flavour – you can lose yourself in delicious dishes (some have a slightly more rustic presentation), eg gnocchi di patate con taleggio. Choose from the à la carte menu or put your trust in the surprise menu. The classic interior, peppered with more modern, designer touches, is appealing. Attentive and polished service.

Name: Feinkost Kantine Mario Pattis
Description: This appealing concept combining delicatessen, café and bistro is the "little brother", as it were, of Feine Kost. Sharing the same premises, both belong to seasoned chef Mario Pattis. Kantine – open during the day – has a short menu that is supplemented by a handful of daily specials. The recipes stick close to the seasons and to products available in the delicatessen. Thanks to the open kitchen, diners are able to watch as delicious, meticulous dishes that won't break the bank are carefully prepared – the quiche is particularly popular. The service is friendly and down-to-earth. Tip: Choose a nice bottle of wine or something delicious from the extensive delicatessen selection to take home with you. The restaurant is slightly hidden away in a tree-lined courtyard, where tables are set up on the pretty terrace for al fresco dining in summer.

Name: Le petit CINQ
Description: This is a pleasant alternative to the two-star restaurant Esplanade in the tastefully designed boutique hotel of the same name. Modern cuisine made with seasonal ingredients is served in two three- or four-course set menus; these change on a weekly basis and one is vegetarian. Le petit CINQ takes up residence in the beautiful rooms of the fine dining restaurant when the latter is closed – Sunday to Tuesday, you can eat both lunch and dinner here. David Wottke, long-time sous chef to Esplanade's head chef Silio Del Fabro, is in charge of the kitchen.

Name: Edda Brasserie
Description: With this tasteful brasserie in the city centre, Alina Meissner-Bebrout offers a delightful alternative to her restaurant bi:braud. The cuisine takes its cue from the changing seasons. In an inviting and laid-back setting, diners can savour the freshly prepared dishes of the day, including classics such as buffalo tartare and Wiener schnitzel. Options are somewhat more limited on Mondays. In summer, the terrace seating overlooking the pedestrianised zone is inviting.

Name: Fachwerk
Description: This restaurant takes its name from the half-timbered façade of Hotel Stadt Kassel, in which it is housed. Located in the town centre, the building dates back to the 17C. The cosy interior is a harmonious blend of modern design and historical elements such as exposed wooden beams and brickwork. In this setting, contemporary seasonal cuisine is served as a three- to five-course set menu or à la carte. To top it all off, you have a friendly and dedicated front-of-house team, as well as an exceptional wine list comprising over 1 500 labels, including some outstanding Rieslings from Germany.

Name: Ostseelounge
Description: Housed in Strandhotel Dünenmeer, Ostseelounge has much to offer. The floor-to-ceiling windows of this clean-lined, chic restaurant afford wonderful views of the dunes and the sea (sometimes with romantic sunsets!). The set menu, inspired by modern culinary trends and the changing seasons, comes in a conventional and a vegetarian version, each with three, five or seven courses. Wine pairings are available upon request. Tip: Book a place at the chef's table right by the open kitchen for some intriguing insights. Waitstaff are friendly and attentive. There is also a lovely terrace. For an à la carte alternative, the hotel has another restaurant: Kaminlounge.

Name: La Bohème
Description: A pleasingly convivial and relaxed place to eat. If you appreciate high-quality steak cuts, then this restaurant with a trendy urban atmosphere is just the ticket. But the menu also whets your appetite with a host of other dishes and delicious desserts. The sharing options (vegetarian versions available) will give you a good impression of the cuisine here. Popular brunch on Saturdays and Sundays. Tip for car drivers: Public car park "Schwabinger Tor".

Name: Brasserie Cuvilliés
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Brasserie fare inspired by Bavarian-Alpine cuisine is the order of the day at the restaurant of the Rosewood Munich hotel. Classic, modern and traditional elements come together here. In the evening, dishes such as bouillabaisse or chicken from Landshut with corn, spinach and a pepper foam grace the menu; at lunchtime, tempting options include "Cuvilliés Burger" or quark pizokel. Wiener schnitzel is a mainstay on the menu. The daily-changing lunch menu with a choice of dishes is also worth perusing. The space has a chic brasserie feel and an open kitchen that can be seen from the dining area. Qu'ils mangent de la Brioche by ceramic artist Angelika Maria Stiegler also draws the eye. In addition, there is the inviting Bar Montez, the winter garden for afternoon tea and the Palaishof terrace. The central location, not far from the Feldherrnhalle and opera house, is perfect for a stroll along the exclusive Theatinerstraße.

Name: Vinaiolo
Description: Even over 25 years after it opened, Vinaiolo continues to bring a slice of la dolce vita to Haidhausen. A charming team provides seamless, attentive service, with a spirit that is tipicamente italiano. The food, too, is Italian: for example, pumpkin risotto with Tuscan pecorino cream or pink-roasted tuna, broccoli, Taggiasca olive tapenade and sun-dried tomatoes. In the evening, there is a set menu and à la carte dishes to choose from. Lunchtime brings tempting options in the form of a reasonably priced set menu written on the board. The wine list features a very appealing selection of Italian wines. The cosy, authentic atmosphere is accentuated by furnishings salvaged from a Trieste grocer's shop dating back to 1904!

Name: Winzerhaus Rebstock
Description: Following stints at various MICHELIN-starred establishments, Konstantin Keller has taken over this much-loved traditional inn. He is the youngest son of the Keller family, who run Schwarzer Adler across the road. "Down-to-earth, regionally inspired cuisine: the best of the simple things" – that's the promise here, and it could hardly be more apt. Eschewing superfluous creative flourishes, the cuisine is all about quality ingredients, meticulous craftsmanship and full, authentic flavours. Put simply: The food is just fantastic! This holds true for the cordon bleu, the escargots with garlic and parsley butter or the pâté de campagne, not to mention the Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) – the version made with dry-aged Black Forest herb-fed pork variant is interesting. There are also daily specials and a short afternoon menu. The wine list features a selection from the restaurant's own estate (Franz Keller) along with other German and international labels. In fine weather, be sure to make the most of the charming courtyard terrace.

Name: Bavarie
Description: Regionality and sustainability are two principles that underpin Bavarie, here at BMW Welt. This translates into combining elements of Bavarian and French cuisine with a focus on high-quality produce. You can dine à la carte or take the set menu – there is also a vegan option, plus a three-course business lunch deal. The atmosphere in the spacious, airy, high-ceilinged room is pleasant. Nice terrace with a view of the Olympic Park and Tower.

Name: Martinelli
Description: If you’re looking for Italian hospitality and the food that goes with it, Martinelli offers seasonal, modern cuisine including dishes such as pecorino ravioli with walnut and balsamic vinegar or saddle of venison with quince. And to whet your appetite, there’s always a plate of air-dried ham and some delicious bread.

Name: Pfistermühle
Description: Once a ducal mill dating from 1573, Pfistermühle delights diners with its stylish Bavarian setting (including a lovely vaulted ceiling). The "Pfistermühlen Brettl" lunchtime set menu (Mon-Fri) with its four small courses (including vegetarian options) is great value. Good location only a stone's throw from the famous Platzl.

Name: Schwarzreiter Restaurant
Description: This fine dining restaurant boasts an exclusive location in the famous Maximilianstraße, more precisely within the legendary Munich luxury hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, complete with its own entrance from the street. The atmosphere is elegant without being stuffy; indeed, the sophisticated, modern and chic interior makes for a pleasingly urban ambience. The approachable and well-trained front-of-house team, who are always attentive and courteous but by no means intrusive, is the perfect fit. Then there is the cosmopolitan cuisine of Franz-Josef Unterlechner, who uses top-notch ingredients from the region and beyond. The Balfego tuna cheek, white onion, Alba truffle, for example, showed us how successfully he brings to life his own ideas. A good all-day alternative, should you need one, is the pleasant Tagesbar, where the food is cooked by the same team. Incidentally, the name ‘Schwarzreiter’ comes from a small fish from the Königssee.

Name: Bratwursthäusle
Description: A trip to Nuremberg wouldn't be complete without trying the city's famous Rostbratwürste! Look no further than this little old stone house on Marktplatz next to Sebalduskirche. Sausages have been sold here since 1312. The interior is rustic and charming, the beechwood barbecue being the centrepiece. Their wonderful sausages are made fresh every morning in their on-site butchery. They are served with sauerkraut and/or potato salad – simply delicious! For the full experience, wash it down with a draught beer. If you're not in the mood for sausages, the menu includes alternatives such as pork shoulder, offal dishes and other snacks. In the summer, the delightful terrace is a popular spot.

Name: Frau Specht
Description: "Dinner is ready" is the slogan here. You ring the doorbell before being escorted into this somewhat hidden little restaurant with a modern, minimalist decor. You are shown to your table in a pleasantly intimate living room-style interior – with a small open kitchen and just a handful of tables, it makes for a private atmosphere. The service comes with a personal touch: your cordial hostess, Yvonne Specht, after whom the restaurant is named, will also recommend just the right wines from the extensive list of top-draw international labels. In the kitchen, head chef Dirk Brendel cooks up an ambitious seven-course surprise menu in the evening, further embellishing it with a variety of additional small dishes. The menu is devised based on the season and the availability of the ingredients. The cuisine is classic and Mediterranean, but also includes international flavours.

Name: Käfer-Schänke
Description: The name "Käfer" has become synonymous with Munich's gastronomy scene. The ace up the sleeve of this Munich institution: the restaurant and delicatessen being under one roof means you can be sure that you are dealing with top-drawer ingredients. These are used in classics such as beef tartare, lobster stew or roast duck for two, served in two courses. The atmosphere is cosy, the service professional and friendly. An additional feature is that they have a number of individually designed function rooms available for special occasions.

Name: Pageou
Description: Located in the CityQuartier Fünf Höfe shopping centre, the chic restaurant of renowned TV chef Ali Güngörmüs is named after his hometown in the Turkish province of Tunceli. Here, his team serves Middle Eastern cuisine that draws on classic French influences and is available as a four-course vegetarian "Levante Menu" and as a five- or six-course "Chef Menu". A starter dubbed "Meze", for example, is a great option comprising various small dishes. A number of noteworthy Turkish labels are included in the extensive wine list. The lovely sheltered terrace is delightful on summer days.

Name: Nymphenburger Hof
Description: Steeped in tradition, this charming establishment is the epitome of a classic restaurant, both in terms of its decor and cuisine, which draws on regional, Austrian, Mediterranean and French influences. The long-serving chef hails from Styria, which explains why the wine list is exclusively dedicated to Austrian labels. Delightful secluded terrace.

Name: Garden-Restaurant
Description: With a fabulous light and high-ceilinged industrial-style conservatory by Belgian interior designer and art dealer Axel Vervoord, the restaurant in the luxurious Grand Hotel Bayerischer Hof is exceptionally chic. At the stove, Philipp Pfisterer certainly knows his craft. He and his team cook up classics such as beef tartare, as well as modern dishes such as "fillet of sturgeon from Lombardy with an almond crust & saffron cream" or "grilled flank steak with salsa verde". At lunchtime, the two- or three-course business lunch is a good deal. The very quiet location is also pleasant – and something of a rarity in such a central part of Munich.

Name: Lamm
Description: For a start, the impeccable façade is inviting, and inside the decor is charming, the service extremely cordial and the food an absolute treat! Choose between the "Bodenständig", "Classic" and "Vegetarian" set menus, in either a three- or four-course format, or order individual courses à la carte – everything is prepared using selected seasonal ingredients. In summer, the delightful garden terrace is a real draw.

Name: Gasthof Widmann
Description: You can clearly taste the enthusiasm that goes into preparing the food here. Seasonal and international dishes are served alongside regional fare, in a six-course set menu. A friendly front-of-house team presides over the two cosy dining rooms. Wed. - Sat. you are welcome from 6 pm.

Name: Gasthof Ochsen
Description: This welcoming inn that is run with great dedication has been in the family since it was founded in 1763. This place is really inviting with its charming dining areas, gorgeous terrace and courtyard. Taking its cue from the changing seasons and Baden culinary tradition, the menu includes specialities of the house such as saddle of veal and offal. Comfortable overnight accommodation available.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: This is MICHELIN-starred chef Tim Raue's take on a French brasserie. The restaurant mirrors the Colette brasseries in Berlin and Munich with an interesting modern dining concept: Diners can order à la carte or compose their own four-course set menu, which can also be vegan. Classics such as beef Wellington (served for two) are available too, as are seasonal dishes. The highlight here is the first-floor terrace overlooking the pedestrian area – but seating is limited, so you'd be well advised to book!

Name: Kurlbaum
Description: Michael Kurlbaum has run his restaurant with great dedication since 1986. Spread over two floors, this place exudes a timeless elegance – in summer, a few additional tables are set up out front in the pedestrian zone. There are plenty of regulars who come for the classic cuisine. Lunch in the bistro area on the ground floor is popular too – they serve a moderately priced two-course set menu that changes weekly. This includes a bottle of water, and dessert is available as an optional extra. If you order in advance, you can also choose from the evening menu at lunchtime. Convenient for motorists: Kastell car park in Haagstraße close by.

Name: Zur Linde
Description: The fifth generation is now in charge of this family-run establishment. Sandra and Marco Linden are committed to creating a charming atmosphere and serving good food here. She courteously and competently oversees the service; he cooks up tasty regional and seasonal dishes, which are always modern in inspiration – served as a set menu or À la carte.

Name: Von Korff
Description: This patrician house, successfully remodelled and extended, has an appealing feel of modernity with its clean, simple forms and abundant light. Good selection of Bordeaux wines.

Name: Fleur de Sel
Description: This restaurant in a residential area in Maintal-Dörnigheim brings a slice of France to the Rhine-Main area. You can look forward to experiencing French-Mediterranean flair, both in terms of the feel of the place and Patrick Theumer's seasonally influenced cuisine. The three set menus, one of which is vegetarian, are particularly appealing. Friendly service headed by host Yasemin Theumer. It is also pleasant to dine on the beautifully verdant terrace.

Name: Gutsschenke
Description: This restaurant's tasteful modern interior design has been beautifully integrated into the historical setting of the 150-year-old Monrepos estate. Outside, there is a delightful terrace under the shade of chestnut trees. The seasonally influenced cuisine is served in the form of a set menu (vegetarian version available) and à la carte. Options include classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with champagne sauerkraut, as well as modern dishes such as wild garlic risotto with red prawns marinated in rosemary and burrata. Tip: Take a walk through the beautiful park and take in the view of the lake and golf course.

Name: Le Stollberg
Description: This charming little restaurant is run with a very personal touch by chef-patron Anette Huber. She serves up good-quality, fresh cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons and draws on French and Mediterranean influences. The front-of-house team is friendly and well drilled, providing astute wine recommendations. Tip: The appealing lunch menu is great value for money! Plus light bites are served in the daytime bistro Le Petit Stollberg opposite.

Name: Brasserie Les Deux
Description: If you like a lively, modern bistro, you’ll enjoy the seasonal, international dishes (such as gnocchi with asparagus and black tiger prawns) served here on the ground floor of Les Deux. Alternatively, try one of the “old” or “new” classics such as mini burgers or beef tartare with imperial caviar.

Name: Im Gütchen
Description: This elegant modern restaurant is accommodated in a charming Baroque mansion within the historical Schlosspark. In an airy, high-ceilinged space, diners are served classic cuisine with regional and Mediterranean sides, for you to pick à la carte or as a set menu. The proprietor himself runs the kitchen, using good-quality ingredients to cook up tasty dishes, while the lady of the house takes care of diners in a cordial manner. On hot summer days, make a beeline for the marvellous terrace.

Name: Der Löwe
Description: For years, the Sauters' well-kept establishment has been lauded for its delicious cuisine. Game from the region is one popular choice here, but their dishes with an international spin have also garnered favour with customers. Friendly, attentive service; tasteful setting. Tip: On Wednesday evenings, they serve a four-course surprise menu at an affordable price.

Name: Fegers Grüner Baum
Description: It is delightful to sit in the shade of the large chestnut tree on the terrace to the rear of this inn, which dates back over 300 years, but the interior is also cosy. Either way, your dedicated hosts are always on hand. They serve Baden cuisine such as Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) with red cabbage, or pikeperch on a bed of creamed sauerkraut.

Name: Spessarttor
Address: Wombacher Straße 140, Lohr am Main, 97816, Germany
Description: This long-established family business is a well-run affair, with diners settling into the cosy dining rooms to enjoy regional fare. On the menu, tasty dishes such as roast venison with red cabbage and dumplings will whet your appetite. You can stay overnight in the inn or in the guesthouse located 300m away.

Name: Waldgasthof am Letten
Address: Letten 13, Lauf an der Pegnitz, 91207, Germany
Description: This restaurant has various dining spaces with a charming rustic feel – including lovely cosy alcoves – where diners tuck into seasonal cuisine that is regional but also draws on international influences. Served by friendly and attentive waitstaff, the food is prepared with fresh, good-quality ingredients. Affording views of the verdant surroundings, the terraces in front and to the rear of the building are delightful in summer. This family-run establishment is also ideal for an overnight stay – on the edge of the forest, yet with good transport connections.

Name: Schaarschmidt's
Description: This building on a corner plot with a gorgeous leafy façade is home to a cosy restaurant that is run with great dedication. Its many regulars come in droves to enjoy specialities of Saxon cuisine – the beef roulade is a firm favourite! The friendly waitstaff will gladly talk you through the options on the menu. Head for the lovely small terrace planted with trees.

Name: Backmulde
Description: This is just the sort of restaurant you would like to have in your neighbourhood. At this lovely location in the Old Town, in the cosy atmosphere of a charming centuries-old half-timbered house, you can look forward to great food and select wines and expert recommendations. The ambitious food is rooted in classic French cuisine and courts modern trends. In addition to the seasonal menu, daily specials feature on the blackboard. The service is attentive and seamless – and the presence of the chef brings a personal touch. Tip: Take a look around the wine shop opposite.

Name: EigenArt
Description: This restaurant is set in a spruce townhouse centrally located close to Marktplatz. It is hardly surprising that there are so many regulars, given the very pleasant atmosphere and friendly service. The cuisine is seasonal and can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte. By prior arrangement, you can also make reservations for lunch and at weekends.

Name: Münsters
Description: This extremely popular place boasts fresh and flavoursome cuisine in the form of a short menu that changes with the seasons. Tables without tablecloths, wooden floorboards and partly exposed brick walls, as well as appealing wine-themed decorative details make for a cosy bistro feel with a rustic touch. The service is laid-back, friendly and attentive. The chef also gets in on the action front of house, providing charming service and excellent wine recommendations. There's also a great beer garden!

Name: Hardthaus
Description: In this listed building, you are immersed in the charming ambience of what used to be a shop selling goods from the colonies. The floor-to-ceiling dark wooden shelves lining the walls, laden with all manner of decorative items, and the rustic old floorboards are striking. Fuss-free yet flavoursome dishes are served in generous portions at the elegantly set, bare wooden tables. The cuisine embraces international influences, with dishes on the menu such as "creamy spicy" king prawn with pea shoots and mango, or crown of Scottish lamb with a potato and olive oil purée, wild broccoli and a thyme jus. In summer, the terrace on the market square comes into its own. The 600-year-old vaulted cellar is a fantastic venue, especially for private functions. The pretty little boutique hotel opposite boasts lovely guestrooms.

Name: Kitchen Library
Description: A great team of two, Daniela and Udo Knörlein run this place together - she looks after the guests cordially, while he cooks up the international "Kleine Dinger" set menu. Available with either four or five courses, an eight-course version for sharing is also possible. The characterful decor is reminiscent of a library: rustic-style charm and over 600 collector's items related to cookery.

Name: Piccolo
Description: You may not see the cathedral here in Porz-Langel, but you do pretty much have front row seats onto the Rhine! This restaurant serves classic cuisine with seasonal and Mediterranean influences, prepared using decent ingredients, most of which are sourced from the region. You can choose à la carte or put together your own three-course menu for a set price. The friendly staff also have plenty of good wine recommendations up their sleeve, drawing on the decent selection with a focus on Austria and Germany.

Name: ACHT
Description: A trendy, urban establishment in the Spichern Höfe complex on the edge of the Belgian Quarter. Diners sit at wooden tables in a pleasantly unpretentious atmosphere; attentive service provided by charming waitstaff. Flavoursome, down-to-earth dishes based on regional and international ingredients are cooked up in the open kitchen. In summer, the gorgeous courtyard is much sought after.

Name: Hirsch
Description: This upscale restaurant serves classic cuisine that draws on Baden's culinary tradition and is made predominantly with regional ingredients. Options such as braised veal cheeks or a tasty fish medley in beurre blanc are sure to whet the appetite. Abundant wood and decorative features provide a cosy backdrop. In summer, head for the lovely verdant terrace. Very friendly service. Given the proximity to Strasbourg, the Black Forest and Europa-Park, it is also worth considering staying in one of Hirsch's well-kept guestrooms or apartments.

Name: Schlegelhof
Description: The charming boutique hotel Schlegelhof boasts not only elegantly appointed rooms, but also culinary excellence courtesy of Marianne and Martin Schlegel. The cuisine is rooted in classic culinary tradition and takes its cue from the seasons. Dishes showcase the finest ingredients, often sourced locally, alongside fruit and herbs from the hotel's own garden. There are various set menus and à la carte options. Classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) and Wiener schnitzel feature, as do more sophisticated numbers such as Atlantic monkfish with beetroot, capers, and potato mousseline. The waitstaff are laid back yet attentive. Decked out in light wood, the interior is sleek and inviting. Floor-to-ceiling windows look out onto the garden and splendid summer terrace.

Name: Zum Riesen
Description: The Wenz family put their heart and soul into running this place, and quality is also a top priority in the kitchen. Good-quality regional and seasonal ingredients are used to rustle up modern-inspired dishes, which are also served in the form of a set menu. Choose a regional wine to go with your food. In summer, the terrace in the courtyard is a secluded spot. There are lovely individually decorated guestrooms too.

Name: Schloss Loersfeld
Description: The centuries-old castle with its extensive grounds is a magnificent property, boasting stylish rooms and salons displaying period details behind its massive old walls. This stately backdrop makes for a fabulous setting in which to relish classic cuisine either à la carte or in the form of a three- to six-course set menu. Caviar or oysters are popular appetisers, followed by tempting dishes such as "smoked eel, eel glaze, beetroot, potato, radish" or "lobster tail, mandarin, kumquat, walnut, gin gel, bergamot beurre blanc". Friendly and attentive service. Tip: There is an interesting set menu at lunchtime. In an adjacent building, three pretty apartments accommodate overnight guests.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description: It is not without good reason that this 300-year-old restaurant has so many regulars. Here, they honour tradition while managing to keep up with the times – and that goes for both the decor and the food, which is not only beautifully presented but also of the highest quality. The Swabian cuisine follows the seasons and draws on international influences. The emphasis is on regional ingredients, including meat and sausage products made on site in their own butcher's shop. As well as à la carte dishes, a three- or four-course set menu is available.

Name: Poisson
Description: Top quality products are deliciously prepared at this modern bistro with a fish orientated menu. The chef allows Asian, as well as Mediterranean and classic components to influence his food.

Name: Osteria La Fenice
Description: A slice of Italy in Cuxhaven! Behind a rather unassuming façade on a busy shopping street, a truly welcoming osteria ambiance awaits – the decor features decorative wine racks, closely spaced marble tables and even a Vespa! Not to forget the authentic Italian cuisine made with high-quality, fresh ingredients – the sourdough bread and pasta are both made in-house. The wine list showcases Italian labels. Tip: Italian food items can be purchased to take home.

Name: LUISE
Description: The beautiful landscape here is perfectly complemented by the elliptical shape of Luisenhöhe wellness and health resort, which gracefully blends into its surroundings. Inside, too, modern design and high-quality natural materials make for an attractive decor that pays homage to the region – that goes for the guestrooms, the spa and the restaurant. The latter has a pleasantly laid-back feel, and floor-to-ceiling windows look out over the Black Forest and the Schauinsland mountain – only the view from the fabulous terrace can beat it. Prepared in the open kitchen, the four-course vegetarian set menu can be supplemented with a fish or meat dish, or veganised. The emphasis on regional sourcing and top-quality ingredients is demonstrated by compositions such as "sunflower seeds/zucchini/tarragon + pasture-raised chicken from the Black Forest". The excellent wine list features a good selection of German and international labels. The futuristic design of the passage that leads from the multi-storey car park to the hotel is also impressive.

Name: Inzlinger Wasserschloss
Description: With over 500 years of history to its name, plus a stylish interior, this moated castle near the Swiss border has for years been synonymous with classic French cuisine made from top-notch produce. You can dine à la carte or choose the set menu – there is also a vegetarian or vegan option. Accompany your food with one of the great wine recommendations. Our tip: The guesthouse 150m away has terrific rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Henrich HÖER's Speisezimmer
Description: The 400-year-old half-timbered house, which houses Hotel Höerhof and this charming restaurant, makes you feel at home. The combination of historical surroundings and modern touches makes for a special atmosphere, to which the warm service provided by the owner also contributes. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in the secluded courtyard! The excellent cuisine comes à la carte ("Kleine Schlemmerkarte", Tue-Sat), as a seasonal set menu (Tue-Sat) and a fine dining set menu ("Genusswelten", Thu evening-Sat).

Name: Nightingale Thai Cuisine & Bar
Description: Having spent years in the bustling metropolis of Bangkok, Dominik and May Carqueville are bringing a slice of the Far East to Dachau. Born and raised in Thailand, the chef has an innate talent for working with authentic Thai flavours. She skilfully incorporates contemporary influences and locally-sourced ingredients into the traditional cuisine of her homeland. Using only the freshest ingredients, she crafts dishes such as Ma Hor (caramelised minced pork with peanuts, pineapple, coriander and chilli) or pan-seared sea bass fillet in a choo chee curry sauce with kaffir lime leaves. Dishes can also be ordered to share. The trendy and chic setting is a combination of restaurant and bar – the latter serves cocktails, beer, wine and house-made soft drinks, as well as finger food. The name "Nightingale" is a nod to Bangkok's vibrant nightlife.

Name: Stern's Restaurant
Description: Housed in the long-established Zum Stern hotel, this restaurant has a charming rustic feel with its wood panelling and lovely white tiled stove. The cuisine is regional but draws on international influences. There are two set menus to choose from (one of which is vegetarian), as well as an à la carte selection including barbecued steaks. The options are a little more limited at lunchtime.

Name: Die Scheuer
Description: Once known as the Hammelsche Scheune, this 17C barn converted into a pretty half-timbered building has bags of charm. This family business a stone's throw from the market square is run with great dedication, and attracts many regulars. In summer, there is a lovely terrace out front. The interior makes for a cosy setting in which to savour delicious food such as locally hunted game. The restaurant endeavours to source ingredients locally and knows its suppliers personally.

Name: Wirtschaft von Johann Gerner
Description: The journey out here to the countryside is well worth it, because Detlef Gerner and his wife Tanja live and breathe hospitality par excellence in their cosy restaurant. The hand-written menu features flavoursome dishes based on seasonal and predominantly regional produce – incidentally, they bake their own bread. In summer, you can sit on the terrace out front. Overnight accommodation in the pretty "Häusla" (for two to seven people).

Name: KINK Bar & Restaurant
Description: This easygoing urban dining concept places equal emphasis on modern cuisine and a vibrant bar culture. The food is pleasingly down to earth yet individual in character – the dishes are ideal for sharing, including as a dedicated sharing menu. This culinary experience is complemented by a standalone bar serving inventive drink creations. The welcoming, informal service matches the stylish, contemporary energy of the space. There is also a lovely terrace. This hip establishment is located at Pfefferberg – once a brewery site, now a cultural venue.

Name: Rutz - Zollhaus
Description: This restaurant's location on the Landwehrkanal truly lends it something special. In summer you can make the most of the covered terrace but the interior of this former customs house is also appealing, with its tasteful furnishings and relaxed atmosphere. The menu puts a modern spin on classic German fare. Note the selection of high-grade cold meats, to be ordered as a starter or side dish.

Name: Marktwirtschaft Besigheim
Description: This charmingly laid-back restaurant serves dishes made with regional and seasonal ingredients, drawing on influences from the Mediterranean and beyond. The best way to experience the culinary artistry is through the six-course set menu. There is also a popular lunch deal that changes weekly. In the summer, the terrace on the charming little market square beckons, whether for a meal, a glass of wine or a coffee. The service is friendly and attentive. Across the street is the Marktkeller brasserie and wine bar. They also put on regular themed evenings. Tip: Take a stroll through the enchanting little half-timbered town!

Name: Julius
Description: This restaurant is in a sense the younger sibling of ernst, Dylan Watson-Brawn and Spencer Christenson's restaurant. Its interior is minimalist and sleek, the atmosphere youthful and laid-back. The kitchen, which is visible behind the counter, sends out creative dishes, which are also available in the form of a tasting menu in the evening, if booked in advance. A shorter lunch menu is served at weekends. You can also come for breakfast and brunch, as well as coffee, pastries and snacks during the day.

Name: Oktopussy
Description: At the restaurant of the New Wave hotel, the food is down-to-earth and delicious, and while it revolves around the region, it has an international twist – for example, the menu features dishes such as "Japanese-style grilled wild sea bass fillet" and the interesting "Oktopussy" set menu (also available in a vegetarian version). The sleek, modern interior with a maritime feel, an open kitchen and a custom-built table for larger groups is appealing. Service is cordial and laid-back. In summer, make a beeline for the secluded courtyard terrace. From May, the rooftop bar is open for delicious cocktails in a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Atlantik
Description: Located in the Dreimühlenviertel, this charming old brick building was a fish market back when it was set amid an abattoir and wholesale butchers. Now it has evolved into this attractive restaurant, which has been designed with an individual touch. Although seafood dominates the menu, it is far from being the only option. Those who prefer meat can indulge in a fillet of beef, to name but one example. Highly recommended for groups: a whole fish to share, eg. turbot, char or Atlantic lobster. Be sure to leave room for dessert – the chocolate cake is a tempting proposition! To accompany your meal, there is an extensive selection of fine wines to choose from.

Name: Nigrum
Description: An impressive cross vault, elegant dark tones, designer elements, works of art – these former stables overlooking the city and a stone's throw from the New Castle have been stylishly converted. Drawing on modern influences, a three- to eight-course set menu is served – Beef tartare (classically prepared at the table) is available as an optional extra course. There is also a chic bar for an aperitif or digestif. Tip: You can reach the restaurant from the pedestrian area via the Burgstaffeln steps. There are several car parking spaces in front of the restaurant.

Name: ESTIMA by Catalana
Description: Located in the heart of the Old Town, not far from the cathedral, this tasteful little restaurant prepares Catalan-inspired dishes in an open kitchen. At the helm in the kitchen is Jürgen Birth, who skilfully weaves both Spanish and French elements into his modern set menu. For example, scallops with brandade are followed by his "Hamburgesa 2.0" with Bellota Ibérico pork cheeks. His penchant for patisserie is also evident in the wonderfully refreshing mandarin sorbet pre-dessert. Choose between a conventional and a vegetarian set menu option – a pescetarian variant is also possible. Furthermore, the "Kennenlern-Menü" serves as an introduction to the restaurant's cuisine, as well as the shorter "TAPAS menu". To accompany the food, there are select Spanish wines, which owner Jan-Hendrik Feldner takes pride in presenting – diners are spoiled with attentive, personal service.

Name: ITO
Description: In this trendy Japanese restaurant in the Belgian Quarter, Kengo Nishimi uses top-notch ingredients to create clearly structured dishes in which traditional Japanese cuisine is laced with modern European influences. In the evening, Japanese classics such as tempura, sashimi and sushi can be ordered à la carte, plus there is an extensive omakase menu. At lunchtime, a moderately priced set menu is available. In the front part of the restaurant, you can watch the chef at work at the sushi counter.

Name: Portomarin
Description: Red-painted walls and light wooden flooring sets the mood for dishes from the Iberian peninsula. From tapas to dessert, the menu is Spanish.

Name: Diergardts Kühler Grund
Description: Established in 1904, this family-run restaurant is now in its fourth generation, with Philipp Diergardt now at the helm. He is passionate about cooking up traditional, seasonal cuisine that draws on locally sourced ingredients. The extensive menu is extremely appealing, making it difficult to choose. In addition to the fairly priced set menu ("Heimatmenü"), there are also classics such as bouillabaisse or Wiener schnitzel, as well as weekly specials that change with the seasons and dishes for two or more people. Wine connoisseurs will find plenty to enjoy here, and all reasonably priced. The fine selection of high-end German wines and French vintages is of particular note. Then there is the tasteful country house ambience, gorgeous terrace and attentive service.

Name: Appare
Description: Here, traditional Japanese food – washoku – is skilfully combined with modern influences, blending Far Eastern spices and cooking methods with European food. There is a short lunch menu and a more elaborate dinner menu. In Japanese "appare" is an exclamation of enthusiasm.

Name: Regional
Description: After being refurbished and rejuvenated, Regional has moved into the former Herrehus of Schloss Reinach. The name says it all: to create their tasty, punchy dishes, almost exclusively Baden and Black Forest produce is used, and the majority of it is also organic. It's a joy to sit on the patio terrace!

Name: philipps restaurant
Description: A really appealing restaurant in the Schanzenviertel neighbourhood. A few steps lead down to this lively, modern establishment on the lower ground floor, where friendly and dedicated waitstaff serve fresh international cuisine. Tip: Be sure to make a reservation – this place is small and extremely popular!

Name: Gute Stube im Parkhotel
Description: The modern and elegant restaurant complete with conservatory and roof terrace is housed in a pretty palace building near Herne's Stadtgarten.
