The contemporary cuisine takes the form of seasonal set menus and à la carte dishes, including vegetarian options. The chefs try to use regional produce as much as possible. Friendly service. For a simpler alternative in the evening, head to Das Stübchen for classic fare or to the beer garden. Parkhotel offers cosy guestrooms. Tip: Enjoy a short walk through the beautiful Stadtgarten. A longer route takes you to the debris field of the (closed) Mont Cenis colliery – right next to it is the viewing platform at the Mont Cenis Academy, which affords fantastic views.

Name: Clouds - Heaven's Bar & Kitchen
Description: Temporarily closed.Just 50 seconds in the lift and you are up on the 23rd floor, from which the view is simply magnificent. Modern cuisine is served in an urban-style interior: enquire about the extensive selection of meats; vegetarians are also catered for. In addition, there's a good bar serving a snack menu from 5pm. In summer, weather permitting, head to the 24th-floor Heaven's Nest for drinks and light bites.

Name: Die Alte Schule
Description: Torben Tönsing, scion of a well-known family of restaurateurs in Herford, took over this restaurant from his parents in 2017. He focuses on contemporary cuisine that draws on both regional and international influences. The 17C half-timbered building has a charming atmosphere – food is served on different levels, and in summer the secluded terrace comes into its own. Excellent wine selection – they even have their own wine shop.

Name: Belvedere
Description: The culinary flagship of the A-ROSA Strandidyll Heringsdorf hotel. From your table in the fourth-floor dining area, which with its glass dome has an elegant modern feel , you can take in the wonderful view over the hotel grounds all the way to the Baltic Sea. The cuisine is classic in its foundations and partly based on regional produce. You are free to put together your own set menu. Friendly and well-drilled waitstaff. Tip: Your aperitif is best enjoyed on the gorgeous terrace.

Name: Papageno
Description: Even after moving to the centre of Konstanz, Patrick Stier has remained true to his style. He serves up classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences – think sea bass grenobloise with artichokes and a saffron emulsion or saddle of venison with a sour cherry game jus, warm pointed cabbage salad, port wine cherries, macadamia nuts and Topfenknödel (curd dumplings). Diners can choose between the "Gourmet" and "Vegetarian Gourmet" set menus and à la carte dishes.

Name: Clinton's
Description: Near the outskirts of Berlin, this restaurant is housed on the first floor of the European headquarters of the fashion company Clinton. The decor is up to the minute, as is the seasonally influenced cuisine – choose between a four- or six-course set menu and their à la carte "Signature" dishes, from "Berlin Blutwurst, sauerkraut, green back bacon, cassis, mustard" to "300g beef – roast beef, fillet, 16hr-cooked ox shoulder, truffle purée, teriyaki, vegetables from the farm". Fans of dry-aged steaks are also in for a treat. The service is attentive and the waitstaff professional. From some tables you can sneak a peek into the Clinton outlet.

Name: Fleher Hof
Description: A little out of the way, this traditional restaurant has a cosy interior, with all the charm of wood-panelled walls, old floorboards and wooden tables. Then there is the tasty cuisine, which includes flavoursome classics with a modern touch. Choose from the à la carte selection, or opt for one of the set menus ("Hof Menü", "Bistro Menü" or vegetarian). This pleasant restaurant is popular, so be sure to book in good time! N.B. Although finding a parking space may not be easy, it's definitely worth coming.

Name: Kuro Mori
Description: Kuro Mori is Japanese for"black forest", neatly capturing the "Black Forest meets Asia" concept here. In an open kitchen, modern dishes are conjured up from high-quality ingredients . Tempting examples include sea bass kinilaw with calamansi, carrot, tamarind and coconut, and veal – saddle and gyoza – with cauliflower, coriander, and pommes dauphine. The stylish urban setting is pleasingly laid-back, with striking details such as exposed brick walls and a cobblestone floor; the high ceilings towards the rear are especially impressive. The location in Freiburg's Old Town, with terrace seating along the pedestrian area in summer, is another plus.

Name: Das Bootshaus
Description: The restaurant at lifestyle hotel Papa Rhein sports a tasteful vintage maritime look and serves good food made with the freshest ingredients. Each evening, a new three-course set menu is presented, in a vegetarian or omnivore version – the latter with options. Lunch is à la carte. The front-of-house team pulls out all the stops but keeps things informal. There is a wonderful view of the Rhine and the surrounding vineyards – in summer, the delightful terrace beckons! In the bar, sand underfoot brings that beach feeling indoors.

Name: mural
Description: The location is special in its own right: This restaurant is tucked away inside MUCA (Museum of Urban and Contemporary Art), and this is the inspiration behind the interior design. The open kitchen allows you to watch the chefs prepare their modern and creative four-course set menu – available with meat and fish or in a vegetarian version. Sourced within the region, the ingredients are of outstanding quality. The high-end wine list is wide-ranging and features some excellent natural wines, too. There are also wine or alcohol-free pairings to go with the set menu. Service is friendly and personable. The restaurant is also open for lunch – dishes can be ordered à la carte or as a set menu comprising two to four courses.

Name: Fine Dining by Phillip Probst
Description: Located in The Liberty hotel, this is a tastefully modern fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows that afford a view of the small harbour. There is also a gorgeous terrace. Chef Phillip Probst and his team use excellent ingredients to create an interesting set menu comprising four to eight courses. The dishes are contemporary, yet classical in their foundations, and the wonderfully intense sauces deserve a mention. Shining examples are the cauliflower polonaise (served with an exquisite beurre blanc enhanced with Imperial caviar) and the beetroot with barbecued eel. The fairly priced wine list is another highlight. The well-drilled front-of-house team are friendly and attentive – they really pull out all the stops! Part of the same business, the restaurant next door, Mulberry Street, proposes a short menu of contemporary dishes.

Name: DAS GOLDSTEIN BY GOLLNER'S
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It's quite unexpected to come across such a chic restaurant in a remote wooded area like this. But the journey is absolutely worth making. Set in the former rifle club house about 5km from the city centre, this establishment boasts a tastefully sleek and upscale interior. It serves freshly prepared, predominantly Austrian cuisine, but the menu also features international dishes, some with Asian influences. The walk-in wine cellar and extensive wine list are a draw in themselves.

Name: The Sakai
Address: Hedderichstraße 69, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
Description: With Hiroshi Sakai at the helm here, you're in the hands of a real sushi master. This basement restaurant is done out in authentic Japanese style: sleek and minimalist. From the seats at the counter, you can watch the food being prepared. They serve an omakase menu, which also comes in a vegan version. The service comes courtesy of a very friendly and professional front-of-house team. Great sake selection.

Name: Golden Phoenix
Description: Temporarily closed.This restaurant belonging to The Duc Ngo, owner of multiple restaurants, is located in the stylish Provocateur hotel. Expect a personable welcome and an informal atmosphere in this chic space with a visible kitchen. The French-influenced Chinese cuisine includes everything from interesting dim sum to sea bass, spinach, beurre blanc. Alternatively, you can eat in the adjoining bar. There are also outdoor tables: on the hotel terrace or on the pavement out front.

Name: Funky Fisch
Description: Are you in the mood for fish of the uncomplicated and Asian-inspired variety? Then head to the trendy and lively Funky Fisch by The Duc Ngo. The centrepiece is the large fish counter, where you choose the fish you want to eat, which is then prepared in the open kitchen. A wide range of Asian food, from Chinese to Vietnamese, is served, with influences from all over the world.

Name: HEIMAT
Description: Restaurant HEIMAT, Auerhahn Stuben, Bayern Stuben and Tiroler Stuben – the elegant hotel of the same name, which also has a spa, offers diners a variety of restaurant option, all of which are elegant and inviting. The terrace, in particular, with its panoramic mountain view is quite an event – it's a great place to soak up the idyllic surroundings! The cuisine is seasonal, with an emphasis on sustainability; the majority of the ingredients come from within an 80km radius. The menu also features classics such as Wiener schnitzel or chateaubriand for two.

Name: Pure Wine & Food
Description: The atmosphere here is pleasingly laid-back and trendy – in summer, the lovely terrace in front of the building gives you that holiday feeling. Using the freshest ingredients, the kitchen team serves up pared-back, modern Mediterranean cuisine. Diners choose between the "Chef's Choice" set menu, a vegetarian set menu and à la carte dishes. Given the restaurant's name, it is no surprise that wine plays an important role. The friendly and adept waitstaff will gladly recommend a suitable pairing for any dish. The terrific wine list comprises over 250 (organic) labels – also available to take away. Tip: Book a wine tasting.

Name: Bootshaus Bar & Grill
Description: Bootshaus is located in the heart of Hamburg's HafenCity. From the comfortable "Boot" (boat) dining area, watch the action in the open kitchen or look out over the marina (Grasbrookhafen) from the light and airy bar area. In summer the waterfront terrace beckons. The Josper grill takes centre stage, with cuts such as New York strip, rib-eye and porterhouse cooked to perfection! There is also a large selection of side dishes and delicious sauces. Keep an eye out for the seafood specials and the "Chef's Choice" deal. The early opening times (from 5.30pm) make this an ideal spot for dinner before a concert at the nearby Elbphilharmonie – or perhaps a drink at the bar afterwards.

Name: POTS
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Relaxed, chic and stylish! The eye-catching features of the Ritz-Carlton's restaurant are its striking decor and large open kitchen. The chefs put a modern spin on traditional German cuisine in dishes such as Königsberger Klopse (meatballs in a white wine sauce) with capers and yellow beetroot. There are also options for sharing. Alternatively, take a punt on the surprise menu. The lunch deal is also popular. Friendly and adept service.

Name: esskunst
Description: The former hall of a bank is now a smart and sophisticated restaurant serving ambitious cuisine. Here, culinary tradition is tastefully combined with modern trends. On the menu, for example: char fillet, strudel dough, celery, turnips, kohlrabi. Tip: try the home-made pralines with your coffee. Charming, attentive and experienced service.

Name: Ente-Bistro
Description: This little offshoot of the famous Ente restaurant is also firmly established in the city. The ambience is typical of a bistro: narrow, cosy, lots of photos on the walls testifying to well-known patrons. Floor to ceiling windows make the premises nice and light. The cuisine is classically French and imbued with seasonal and Mediterranean influences.

Name: Kaltwassers Wohnzimmer
Description: Wohnzimmer offers a cosy "living room" feel with some charming nostalgic touches inside and a designer atrium with view of the glazed kitchens in the interior courtyard. The modern regional cuisine uses fresh quality produce and includes dishes such as Wels catfish served with mashed potatoes and apples, kohlrabi and Ahle Worscht sausage.

Name: Terra
Description: This restaurant in the attractive Ritz-Carlton hotel boasts a bright and elegantly modern interior with captivating views of the VW works and the harbour basin afforded by floor-to-ceiling windows. The cuisine takes its cue from the seasons and showcases quality produce from the region and elsewhere in the country. One of their signature dishes is braised veal cheek with mustard jus. Good vegetarian options.

Name: Lucente
Description: If you are on the lookout for good Italian cuisine in Rüttenscheid then this ristorante is the place for you. The menu includes classics such as vitello tonnato and house-made ravioli. The daily specials on the blackboard and recommendations announced by waitstaff are also interesting. The atmosphere is young, fresh, friendly - Italian joie de vivre is in the air here!

Name: Saxlers Restaurant
Description: This restaurant is housed in the inviting Weinhotel St. Stephanus on the riverside promenade and not far from the old market square. In a refined setting, the friendly and committed hosts serve delicious food made with top-notch ingredients, vegetarian options included. The menu features classic dishes and regional specialities. Tip: Leave room for the delicious desserts! In the basement, the Braukeller serves Kloster Machern beer.

Name: Schimmel's
Description: This restaurant's striking red façade draws the eye. The smart interior is modern and stylish, and the atmosphere is welcoming – the wooden tables are a nice touch. In the open kitchen, regional dishes are prepared, occasionally incorporating influences from around the globe. Diners can choose between the two set menus or order à la carte. The soups, for example, are delicious, but so is the fresh fish! The proprietress ensures cordial and attentive service. They also offer pretty guestrooms and holiday flats.

Name: ESSLIBRIS
Description: ESSLIBRIS offers a relaxed, elegant atmosphere with a fine view of the garden. The food on offer is a mix of Mediterranean and regional. Try the suckling calf fillet and ravioli with carrots, parsley root and shallots. The kitchen is pleased to meet personal requests.

Name: Kaisers Eck
Description: Situated by Ahlbeck's main church, this cosy restaurant with its pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere is run by a husband-and-wife team – she manages the waitstaff in her friendly and relaxed manner while he does the cooking. The cuisine is predominantly regional, and the "Lieblingsmenü" is a hit. However, there are plenty of other options that whet the appetite – the decision won't be easy.

Name: AnnA
Description: This restaurant inside the luxury Hotel Elephant is bathed in natural light thanks to its enormous windows. Seated beneath the high ceiling, diners can take in the exclusive ambience, including decorative pictures in the entrance area. Head for the delightful terrace in summer. The cuisine is modern and creative with a regional twist. Mouthwatering options include cod and creamy leeks with pasta and tomato and, for dessert, apple and white chocolate bread pudding and vanilla ice cream. At lunchtime, diners can order à la carte. In the evenings, an interesting set menu is also available, which also comes in a vegetarian version. Be sure to take a stroll through the attractive old town.

Name: Schloss Monaise
Description: With Hubert Scheid's cuisine, this place is nothing short of a culinary institution in the region. His signature style comprises pleasantly straightforward dishes made from excellent ingredients – served à la carte or as a set menu. The restaurant occupies stylish, high-ceilinged rooms that channel the stately flair of these premises dating back to 1783 – once a summer residence. Or you can dine on the wonderful terrace with a view of the surrounding nature and the Moselle. It's also worth taking a look at the wine list, which features many a big name.

Name: Schranners Waldhorn
Description: Maximilian and Marie-Luise Schranner's establishment is a haven of comfort and calm. They have lovingly transformed this traditional inn with a tasteful interior design concept. At the helm, Maximilian Schranner specialises in classic cuisine and proposes three set menus: the "Menü Gourmet", the "Menü vegetarisch" and the "Wirthaus-Menü" – but you can also order dishes from these à la carte. There is also a very reasonably priced set menu at lunchtime. On warm days, the gorgeous terrace on the Seebach with its views of the castle is a particular highlight.

Name: Salt & Silver
Description: The concept at Salt & Silver in St Pauli is "wanderlust cuisine à la carte". With views of the Elbe, diners choose from a seasonally changing à la carte menu that fuses regional ingredients with Mediterranean influences and international twists. Dishes include, for example, cod with pil-pil, chickpeas, potatoes and Kalamata olives, or grilled kale with hollandaise and chilli crunch. A tasting menu for sharing is also available. The pleasingly relaxed atmosphere is enhanced by unflappable and highly professional service, provided by a cheerfully charming and laid-back front-of-house team.

Name: Landhaus Halferschenke
Description: In this beautiful quarry-stone building dating from 1832, the Schmah family serve ambitious cuisine that revolves around top-notch ingredients and the seasons – from sole and Aubrac beef to oysters and turbot from Brittany. You can opt to dine à la carte or go for a set menu. In addition to the food, diners can look forward to attentive service in a tasteful setting with a country-house feel. In summer, the gorgeous terrace beckons. In addition, MA PETITE CHAMBRE is a small gourmet haven serving a set menu. They have four well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Genussschmiede
Description: This blacksmith's shop dating back to 1682 is now devoted to modern cuisine that follows the seasons and draws on fresh, mainly regional ingredients. The interior is pleasingly trendy and minimalist, with a dining area laid out beneath a high steel ceiling. Diners choose between a 5-course set menu and à la carte dishes. Vegetarians are also well catered for on the menu.

Name: Hohenhaus Grill
Description: This is the second restaurant of the idyllically situated Hohenhaus hotel, a magnificent property steeped in history. The interior has a classic, rustic decor and a warm atmosphere – plus a lovely 18C tiled stove. The seasonal cuisine is based on premium ingredients, sourced from the region for the most part. Delicious options include barbecued wild game sausage made with meat hunted on site and served with Hohenhaus potato mash, or braised local mutton. It is a treat to sit on the terrace and take in the surrounding countryside.

Name: Chambao
Description: This appealing restaurant is all about sharing. Good-quality ingredients go into imaginative dishes that you can combine as you see fit to create your own set menu. Another lovely idea is the "Heidelberg Menü": a culinary guided tour of the city, available in either a classic or vegetarian version. Some tables afford a view into the glass-fronted kitchen. The staff are friendly and professional, and you can trust the wine recommendations without hesitation. Chambino bar and bistro is located almost opposite. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous, lively terrace overlooking the Alte Brücke (Old Bridge).

Name: Hofgut Hohenkarpfen
Description: This restaurant enjoys a wonderful location in the middle Baden-Württemberg's oldest nature reserve and boasts stunning views – it's well worth booking a table on the terrace. In what was once the dairy of the over 300-year-old farmstead, diners are pampered with delicious food and attentive service. The modern cuisine incorporates classic and regional influences, as well as international, sometimes Asian touches. The former barn of the heritage-protected estate has been transformed into a hotel with attractive and cosy minimalist-style guestrooms. Tip: Take the time to look around the art museum.

Name: Sansibar
Description: A restaurant with cult status! This smart beach cabin is a much sought-after place to eat. It takes five minutes to reach it on foot through the dunes – or you can use the shuttle service. Fancy a Sansibar classic such as rice pudding with red fruit jelly? Or perhaps you'd prefer something more sophisticated? Superb wine list. No reservations taken at lunchtime. There is a playground for children next to the restaurant.

Name: Zur Schlupp
Description: The Ehrhardt family are passionate about their charming little restaurant, in a building dating back to 1608. The atmosphere is cosy, and the cuisine is fresh and in tune with the seasons – two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, complement the à la carte menu. And why not try one of the fine wines from the region with your food? Don't forget to book. Tip: The courtyard is a romantic spot in summer!

Name: Gocklwirt
Description: What is it that draws regulars and day trippers here in equal numbers? The richly decorated space is wonderfully rustic and the remarkable collection of farm machinery is well worth seeing. Classic international and regional dishes such as Böfflamott (beef in red wine), rooster burger and saddle of lamb in a herb crust are served, as well as a seasonal set menu. Three individually decorated double rooms can be booked for overnight stays in the building next door.

Name: Gengs Linde
Description: Christian Geng offers fresh and flavoursome cuisine that is traditional with international influences. His fashionable restaurant combines clean, modern lines with warm wood. Try the veal cordon bleu or the rack of lamb baked in a herb crust with peperonata and homemade gnocchi.

Name: Klebers
Description: Whether you are seated in the pleasantly bright interior or on the delightful terrace in summer, you can look forward to friendly and charming service as well as international and regional cuisine made from excellent produce. There are various set menus (including a vegetarian one) to choose from, plus a selection of dishes à la carte. The restaurant is housed in the tasteful Kleber Post hotel.

Name: Gasthof Schütte
Description: This region, which is a popular destination for hiking and cycling enthusiasts, is home to this traditional family-run country hotel with its own spa facilities and lovely restaurant. There are regional, classic and international dishes on the menu, which is somewhat more limited at lunchtime. In winter, an open fireplace adds to the charming atmosphere.

Name: Zum Ochsen
Description: The atmosphere is really cosy in this restaurant, which is charmingly done out in the traditional style typical of the region. The kitchen serves up flavoursome, ambitious dishes with a regional and seasonal focus, as well as the occasional international twist. For overnight guests, this long-standing family-run establishment offers comfortable guestrooms and a spa with a range of facilities and treatments and a swimming pool.

Name: Gourmetrestaurant "1751"
Description: Located in the heart of the city, in a wine merchant's house dating back over 250 years, this restaurant is considered one of the finest in the region. This delightful historical setting boasts a beautifully restored barrel-vaulted ceiling. The team led by chef Marcel Kube serves up modern cuisine, drawing on seasonal influences and using mostly regional ingredients. They serve an ambitious set menu that while plant-forward also includes one fish and one meat option. Choose between the five- or seven-course format; it is possible to add an extra course. The wine list includes a few rare gems! Weinhaus Uhle hotel has tastefully designed guestrooms. Incidentally, the property has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2024.

Name: Gutshaus Kubbelkow
Description: With its smart façade and stylish dining rooms, this listed manor house set in wonderfully peaceful grounds has lost nothing of its 1908 charm. It serves fresh, ambitious cuisine including lagoon-fished zander with jellied bouillabaisse broth and pan-fried asparagus. The idyllic location makes the tasteful upmarket guestrooms dotted with antique furniture all the more inviting, as does the excellent breakfast.

Name: Restaurant Quack in der Villa Weismüller
Description: It's a treat to sit either out on the terrace overlooking the city or inside – in a tastefully decorated dining area blending elegance and trendy chic styling. The ambitious seasonal cuisine has distinct Mediterranean and regional influences. Various set menus feature dishes such as corn-fed Bresse chicken cooked with truffles and served with kohlrabi, chicory and gnocchi or Breton turbot, mashed potatoes with artichokes and baby spinach. The Chef's Table is an interesting affair: counter seating with a view into the kitchen, and a surprise menu. Good wine list. Comfortable apartments are available for a stylish stay. N.B. The property is accessed via a narrow private road.

Name: Lazarus Stube im Oberschwäbischen Hof
Description: Do you fancy some really tasty seasonal regional cuisine, including classics such as Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) or house-made Maultaschen (Swabian dumplings)? Here at Lazarus Stube, good, fresh, often locally sourced ingredients go into appealing à la carte dishes and specials that change with the seasons. Friendly, attentive service. For more ambitious cooking, look to the tasting menu (vegetarian or omnivore) of the second restaurant, Esszimmer. The excellent, wide-ranging selection of wines is the same in both establishments. Modern and functional guestrooms available next door at Oberschwäbischer Hof.

Name: Traube
Description: Run with great dedication in the heart of the old Rohrbach district, this lovely traditional restaurant has a cosy interior featuring a blend of traditional and modern elements. Chef Ole Hake's ambitious dishes are made with carefully selected regional ingredients, for example excellent game. His commitment to sustainability is palpable. The seasonal seven-course set menu comes in an omnivore or vegan version. There is also a well-curated wine list with an emphasis on German labels. These can also be enjoyed in the wine bar with snacks or a light meal. Tip for motorists: the public car park at the nearby Thorax Clinic is convenient.

Name: east
Description: This restaurant, housed in the stylish hotel of the same name, is quite striking on account of the fantastic industrial architecture of the former iron foundry and the slick, chic interior. The centrepiece here in what was once the factory hall is the sushi counter. The menu features modern international dishes. A tip for meat lovers: fine steaks from the Southbend Grill.

Name: Grenzhof
Description: At Grenzhof, chef Sebastian Andrée and his team are strongly influenced by the seasons and their produce in their modern cuisine, which is served as a three to six-course menu and an appealing à la carte selection. In nice weather, the Kastanienhof is absolutely idyllic; on less clement days and in winter, the Gutsstube with its rural-style decor is welcoming. At lunchtime, options are limited to a lunch buffet and a short lunch menu. They also rent out various spaces for private events. For overnight stays, they propose attractive and inviting country house-style and themed guestrooms.

Name: Landhotel Krone
Description: Here, tradition rubs shoulders with current trends in cosy little spaces that feature an attractive blend of old brickwork, wood, steel and glass. The regional and seasonal cuisine is scattered with international influences. Medieval vaulted cellar for events. This family-run business also offers attractive, individually designed guestrooms and wellness facilities.

Name: Bayerischer Hof
Description: In this well-kept restaurant run by the Leykauf family, you can expect a relaxed atmosphere and flavoursome, fresh cuisine prepared by the chef-patron, as well as friendly and attentive service overseen by the lady of the house – this is hospitality as it should be! The wine list predominantly features local produce. There are also reasonably priced guestrooms, varying in style from simple to modern.

Name: Weisser Bock
Description: Pretty details such as wood panelling and historical photos contribute to the cosy atmosphere in this traditional establishment. The kitchen serves up a fine selection of dishes made from regional and international ingredients, from which you can choose a three- to six-course menu. The à la carte menu includes appetising dishes such as "beef tartare, anchovies, brioche, caviar" and "turbot, wild cauliflower, capers". The hotel of the same name has comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms. The central location is another trump card.

Name: Rehbergers im Schloss Hohenstein
Description: This stunning castle, which is mentioned in written records as early as the 14C, boasts an idyllic location in beautiful grounds. In addition to their tastefully decorated hotel, Alexandra and Andreas Rehberger run this appealing restaurant with a winter garden overlooking the castle courtyard. The chef-patron – no stranger to the restaurant scene – turns his hand to cooking contemporary seasonal cuisine with ingredients from the region; the proprietress delivers Austrian charm and good wine recommendations.

Name: Die Kurfürstenstube
Description: A classic of Heidelberg's dining scene! In the restaurant of the stylish grand hotel Der Europäische Hof Heidelberg, with its individually designed guestrooms and suites, the mighty coffered ceiling and wall panelling with beautiful inlays preserve a piece of history. The cuisine is based on the classics, and only the very best ingredients are used in the ambitious dishes. Choose à la carte or go for the set menu, available in various lengths. The wine list, specialising in German, French and Italian labels, is also excellent. The highly friendly, professional and attentive service is in keeping with the style of the place. In the summer months, a slightly simpler menu is served in the "Sommerrestaurant", which has a terrace and a pleasant, airy atmosphere.

Name: Magnifico da Umberto
Description: Umberto Scuccia is a well-known figure in Heilbronn. Here on the 12th floor of the WTZ Tower he runs an upmarket, minimalist-style restaurant offering both pleasantly pared-down Italian cuisine with the accent on top-quality produce and a wonderful view of the city.

Name: Bachmaier
Description: Ulrike and Otto Bachmaier have been running their restaurant for many years. The modern decor is delightful and you can watch the river traffic on the Neckar through the floor-to-ceiling windows, as well as from the terrace. Friendly and adept service comes courtesy of the lady of the house while the chef-patron delivers seasonal dishes such as Obsiblue prawn soup with ginger, or braised shoulder of locally hunted venison, glazed in the pan, with Swede, palm tree kale and celeriac. A vegetarian set menu is available by prior arrangement. Good wine pairings. Tip: Book well in advance.

Name: 20zwanzig
Description: Nestled in a quiet location on the outskirts of town, Hotel Freiwerk's core building is a spruce half-timbered villa dating back to 1894. Its restaurant, 20zwanzig, is housed in the modern extension built in 2020. The chic, trendy interior has large floor-to-ceiling windows that affords a splendid view of the surrounding greenery. The cooking is contemporary and seasonally inspired. Classics on the menu include Oldenburg duck and locally hunted game. Diners can opt for a surprise menu of flexible length or order à la carte. Friendly and professional waitstaff.

Name: Intuu
Description: Ensconced in the Freigeist hotel is this appealingly modern and lively restaurant. Diners have the option of sitting at the counter with views of the action in the open kitchen, as the team prepares a broad offering of Japanese and South American cuisine: dishes range from sushi and sashimi, tempura and yakitori to meats grilled in the Josper oven. These are also perfect plates for sharing.

Name: Chang Bistro
Description: This smart and trendy bistro version of the main restaurant, Chang, in Grünwald features mostly Thai cuisine and dishes with influences from Japan. Here, too, the emphasis is on high-quality ingredients. The Thai curries as well as the sushi can be highly recommended. At lunchtime there is also a daily changing lunch menu. Lovely terrace, as well as covered winter garden-style dining space.

Name: Rubens
Description: This pretty restaurant owned by friendly hosts Cornelia Stolzer and Ruben Baumgart – she is Austrian and he is German-Austrian – is something of an Alpine hot spot. Accordingly, classics such as Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), Alt-Wiener Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) or Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake), as well as modern dishes feature on the menu. Charming, well-trained waitstaff and a decent selection of Austrian wines. Incidentally, the pumpkin seed oil comes from the proprietress's village.

Name: Wintergarten
Description: The tastefully designed conservatory restaurant of the long-established Brenners Park-Hotel & Spa is a light and airy space with floor-to-ceiling glazing that affords a splendid view of the leafy gardens – and the terrace is, of course, especially inviting. In the evening, the classic and seasonal dishes can be enjoyed as a set menu or ordered à la carte. Vegetarian options are also available. A three-course set menu is served at lunchtime from Monday to Friday.

Name: Puricelli
Description: The location in the old castle ruins is glorious, and the view of the Rhine is spectacular – best enjoyed from the terrace. Inside, floor-to-ceiling windows frame the scenery beautifully. The kitchen takes its cue from the changing seasons and region, showcasing produce such as organic veal and venison from Oberheimbach, salmon trout from the Wisper Valley, zander from Lake Laach and vegetables and herbs from the castle's own garden. Alongside an excellent à la carte selection, there’s a choice of two set menus – one larger, one smaller. The wine list highlights local estates, including the castle’s own wine from its surrounding slopes. Burg Reichenstein hotel offers attractive, individually decorated guestrooms. Tip: Regular events are held here. A visit to the castle museum is definitely worthwhile.

Name: Staudi's
Description: Once a butcher's, now a really pretty little restaurant with a bistro feel. Decorative relics of the past such as tiled floors and stained glass in the ceiling make for a charming interior. Diners also enjoy cordial service and modern, seasonal dishes, served in the form of a four-, five-, or six-course tasting menu. A vegetarian alternative is available, too. In good weather, you can make the most of the lovely terrace laid out in front of the restaurant. The Stube can be booked as a separate room for private events (Nov-Mar).

Name: Restaurant 1463
Description: This building, dating from 1463, exudes rustic charm both inside and out. Dark wood finishings and low ceilings add to the cosy feel of the two small dining spaces on the first floor. The secluded terrace in the quiet courtyard is also delightful. Verena and Henning Weick, your cordial hosts, run the establishment as a team – she handles service, he is in charge of the kitchen. Diners can choose between two set menus (with optional wine pairings), and each course can also be found in the tempting à la carte selection. There are six lovely comfortable apartments for overnight stays.

Name: Überland
Description: In less than a minute, the lift takes you up to the 18th floor of the BraWoPark building near Hauptbahnhof. People come here to enjoy modern cuisine in a trendy, chic setting – not to mention the view. Try the choice cuts of the excellent beef aged in-house. Incidentally, the concept is the brainchild of TV chef and food professional Tim Mälzer. NB: two sittings per evening. On the floor above, rooftop bar and terrace.

Name: Jan Diekjobst Restaurant
Description: Dating from the 16C, Detmolder Hof not only offers comfortable classical accommodation, but it is also home to Jan Diekjobst's restaurant, which is worth seeking out in its own right. After stints at Victor's FINE DINING by Christian Bau in Perl-Nennig and The Table Kevin Fehling in Hamburg (and others), here the chef cooks up a modern take on classic cuisine. The dishes, prepared with carefully selected ingredients, are available as a three-, five-, or seven-course set menu; the vegetarian version has three or five courses. À la carte dining is also possible. From Thu to Sat, there is also a "Gourmet Lunch". Service is very friendly and attentive. The interior is done out in a tasteful brasserie style, with high ceilings, a striking chandelier and handsome hardwood floors, as well as an open kitchen. In summer, the terrace in front of the building beckons.

Name: Eiden Restaurant
Description: The location of this hunting lodge, set amid almost 25 acres of parkland, is superb. The lovely restaurant includes a conservatory and a wonderful garden terrace.

Name: Gänsweid
Description: In this carefully restored former garage, it is a case of ‘olive oil not engine oil’! Enjoy your meal in a relaxed atmosphere where you can watch the cooks preparing their fresh mixture of Swabian and Mediterranean dishes in the kitchen. Simple, good value menu only at lunchtimes.

Name: Berghotel Wiedener Eck
Description: Marie and Lorenz Wissler represent the fourth generation of their family to run Berghotel Wiedener Eck, which enjoys an idyllic location at over 1 000m above sea level – the view of the valley is stunning! For overnight stays, there are attractive, cosy guestrooms, and the restaurant is brimming with traditional Black Forest charm, interspersed with modern touches. In the restaurant, you can look forward to friendly and courteous service, as well as regional cuisine and dishes that draw on the culinary traditions of France and the Mediterranean, all made from fresh high-quality ingredients – the chef even hunts his own game. In the evenings, there is a set menu that changes every day, plus the seasonal "Wiedener Eck Menü". You can also order the individual courses of both à la carte. Tip: The surrounding forests and meadows make this hotel a perfect starting point for hikes!

Name: CARALEON
Description: This tastefully designed restaurant is housed in the small boutique hotel of the same name, which enjoys a fabulous location in the Wasserburger Bucht and boasts stunning lake views. It specialises in modern European cuisine infused with authentic Peruvian influences. There is a small selection of à la carte options as well as a five-course set menu (by advance booking only) – the chefs themselves serve the dishes, adding a distinctive personal touch. The 300 labels on offer showcase wines from Bordeaux to Slovakia. Alternatively, there is a good range of non-alcoholic drinks to accompany your food. Every Sunday from 12pm to 6.30pm is "Family & Friends", when à la carte classics are served, such as parihuela (Peruvian bouillabaisse), Wiener schnitzel or Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancakes). Tip: Head to the Sunset Lounge for a nightcap by the lake.

Name: zeit|geist
Description: The centuries-old Walk'sche Haus in the heart of Weingarten abounds with charm. Outside it's the pretty half-timbered façade that catches the eye; inside, the combination of sleek modern design and a touch of rusticity makes for a particularly pleasing ambience. Sebastian Syrbe cooks up modern dishes based on classical foundations, such as "onsen egg, soy, spinach, nut butter" or "suckling pig, beetroot, horseradish, chives". You can choose à la carte or opt for a surprise menu comprising four, six or eight courses. Tip: In summer, be sure to get a spot on the gorgeous terrace overlooking the Walzbach stream! For a more wallet-friendly alternative, head to stil|bruch. There are also pleasant guestrooms, should you wish to stay the night here.

Name: Treibgut
Description: As a sophisticated alternative to Seestern, Treibgut adds to the gourmet credentials of the Lago hotel. Modern cuisine is served in a trendy and exceedingly stylish setting. There are also dishes designed for sharing, such as steaks, whole fish or traditional grazing board. A fine selection of products from the in-house bakery, butchery and ice creamery is available. In summer, the lakeside setting is best enjoyed on the terrace.

Name: Zum Adler
Description: Bearing its name of old, this modern restaurant carries on the tradition of the original 19C Zum Adler inn. Today it is lovely and light inside, with a smart and minimalist decor. The focus lies squarely on high-quality meat, such as Wagyu beef steak. Fish and vegan options also available. At lunchtime there is a smaller offer with a reasonably priced lunch menu - but you can also choose from the steak menu.

Name: Rindenmühle
Description: Take a seat in the elegant yet cosy, country-style interior – or, in summer, out on the beautiful garden terrace – and choose from a seasonal menu. Vegetarians are also catered for. For overnight guests there are cosy contemporary guestrooms.

Name: Zum Storchen
Description: This establishment is run by the Trienen family in a beautifully renovated old townhouse. The food here is exceptional; the cuisine is seasonal and regional, drawing on modern and international influences. Tip: Try the daily specials as a set menu. There are two pleasant terraces: one out on the pavement, and one in the courtyard to the rear of the building, which is quieter. Comfortable modern guestrooms.

Name: bistronauten
Description: A word to the wise: make sure you book, as this really appealing restaurant is always busy! Housed in an old railway station dating from 1903, the atmosphere is laid-back, the decor modern with industrial charm and the food excellent. On the blackboard there is a seasonal set menu – choose between meat, fish and vegetarian for the main course. They also have a selection of German wines. Dine at the counter to watch the chefs at work in the open kitchen.

Name: Die Traube
Description: This gorgeous half-timbered house dating back to 1647 boasts a cosy interior with banquette seats and ambitious seasonal Mediterranean cuisine made from excellent ingredients. The terrace in front of the old barn with its glockenspiel clock is also very appealing. Tip: There is a public car park just around the corner.

Name: Landgasthof Backers
Description: The Backers family business has a long tradition to its name, stretching back to 1843. Today, the sixth and seventh generations are running the show with great dedication. The fresh and flavoursome food draws on the region and the seasons, and ingredients are sourced locally wherever possible, including the venison and Diepholz geese. The restaurant is a long-standing member of the Slow Food community. There are also a few comfortable guestrooms. Try the "Backers zum Kennenlernen" deal: four-course regional set menu with drinks, plus overnight accommodation.

Name: Die Achkarrer Krone
Description: The culinary tradition at Zur Krone dates back to 1561. Today you can look forward to a plate of calf’s kidney, tripe or oxtail stew, and in summer, a delicious sausage salad. The Baden cuisine and wines can be enjoyed in the cosy dining room or on the terrace. Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Pades Restaurant
Description: Wolfgang Pade offers a constantly changing menu, which is based on the availability of produce and relies on regional producers. Please note that there are only two service times: 5.45pm and 8.15pm – so make your reservation in good time! The garden terrace behind the pretty patrician house is magnificent.

Name: BECKER'S Weinhaus
Description: The original building, which houses this, the second Becker's restaurant, stands in contrast to the modern new hotel building. The abundance of pale woodwork makes it nice and cosy in this space, which leads into an adjoining vaulted brick cellar. Choose between a three- or four-course set menu and à la carte options. The "business lunch" deal and the "quick lunch" daily special are popular. Pretty terrace.

Name: Kräutergarten
Description: The friendly and dedicated hosts have been running this restaurant with an appealing elegant interior since 1983. It is with good reason that they have won over their many regulars: their classically oriented cuisine is seasonal and focuses on the quality and freshness of the ingredients. The service comes courtesy of attentive waitstaff. You'll certainly want to come back again!

Name: Forsthaus Ilkahöhe
Description: The idyllic hilltop location with its fantastic view across Tutzing to the lake is a huge draw of this restaurant – the terrace is fabulous! This converted forester's lodge has an attractive, upscale interior that combines modern style and regional touches. The menu features seasonal dishes made with select ingredients. Mediterranean and international influences are as prominent as the regional classics. While only a small selection of simpler dishes is served at lunchtime, things take a more ambitious turn in the evening. There is also a self-service beer garden.

Name: Gasthof Kreuz
Description: This traditional hotel and restaurant located at the edge of the pedestrian area has a gorgeous terrace overlooking the Gut Betha Fountain. On the menu: regional and seasonal cuisine, including locally hunted game. In addition to à la carte dishes, there is an inexpensive three-course set menu ("Regiomenü"), to be relished in a pleasant atmosphere. The wine list has some surprising rarities in store, and the service is cordial and attentive. They offer several immaculate guestrooms in the building itself, plus holiday apartments within walking distance. You can park free of charge just a few minutes' walk away (Parkplatz Bleiche).

Name: La Maison Eric
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace
Description: This absolute gem of an old half-timbered house is tucked away in a side street. The interior is tastefully decorated and replete with charming details; outside, a gorgeous terrace gives onto the wonderful garden. Classic French cuisine is served as a four-course lunch menu. Fresh, top-quality ingredients go into dishes such as sea bass fillet with fennel risotto or Barbary duck breast with root vegetable purée. Attentive, courteous and committed to the well-being of his guests, owner Eric Grandgirard is always on hand and glad to recommend wine pairings from a list dominated by local and French labels.

Name: Nannina
Description: In her tiny restaurant, host Giovanna Di Tommaso (known as Nannina) devotes herself tirelessly to her passion: Italian cuisine. Prepared with fresh high-quality ingredients, her dishes are ambitious and packed with flavour. As well as an extensive à la carte menu, there are three different set menus – one for two or more people and another for four. Delightful terrace to the rear of the building. Practical: The restaurant has its own car park.

Name: ZUM HIRSCHEN beim stöckeler
Description: This family-run restaurant is firmly established in the village and surrounding area. The cosy, rustic dining rooms and pretty terrace in the shadow of the church making an ideal setting for its seasonal, regional cuisine. There is also a good selection of gluten-free dishes. The matching wines are offered. Overnight guests can look forward to pretty, modern Alpine rooms and a good breakfast – taken on the balcony terrace perhaps?

Name: möbius - das restaurant
Description: Run by Tommy R. Möbius and his wife, this small restaurant makes a chic impression. In this modern and tastefully designed space, she leads the service with warmth, professionalism and a personal touch. In the evening, the chef-patron creates bold and ambitious cuisine based on classical foundations. Dishes such as "WALD.WASSER – wild mushroom consommé, stuffed paccheri, caraway crisp" or "TAFEL ABER SPITZ – grilled veal topside from Höllerschmid, spinach, rösti, apple and horseradish sauce, jellied stock" are served as a set menu or à la carte. Simpler menu at lunchtime. Tip: Delicatessen items can be purchased to take home. In addition, there are regular themed dinner menus and cookery courses.

Name: Habbel's
Description: Habbel’s offers a fine-dining experience beyond compare. International dishes such as tuna carpaccio coated in wasabi-sesame seeds and saddle of lamb in thyme foam with grilled vegetables feature on the menu, while the wine list offers around 1, 000 wines and spirits from the Habbel in-house distillery, including a 1977-vintage whisky!

Name: Christophorus
Description: For car enthusiasts who are fans of quality cuisine: here you can take in views of the Porsche Museum or Porscheplatz as you tuck into Mediterranean and international fare such as pluma bellota Ibérico taco with pineapple and pink peppercorn chutney, or barbecued US prime beef. You can also opt for a six- or nine-course tasting menu. The open kitchen offers some fascinating insights. Impressive wine list comprising over 500 items. A lift takes you straight from the car park to the restaurant on the third floor.

Name: Alois-Anton Kaminrestaurant
Description: A good alternative to the fine dining restaurant of the Park-Hotel Egerner Höfe. The choice is yours: dine in the cosy Bavarian-style dining rooms dubbed "Alois" and "Anton" or in the more upmarket Kaminrestaurant. Just as charming is the terrace, which is sheltered from the wind and has a view of the pastures and mountains. Either way, you can enjoy cordial service and regional and seasonal dishes in a pleasantly laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Gasthof Hirsch
Description: Set in the centre of this Black Forest village, this attractive restaurant dating back to 1748 is popular for its robust cuisine with classic foundations and plenty of flavour – the sauces are also fantastic! This is all testament to the skill of owner Thomas Zimmermann, who uses select ingredients in his dishes. The atmosphere, too, is just right, thanks to the lovely decor and the exceedingly friendly, attentive hostess. Tip: There are also some individually designed, upscale guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: HerR
Address: Herrngasse 20, Rothenburg ob der Tauber, 91541, Germany
Description: Located in the old town, the pretty Hotel herrnschlösschen is home to a delightful little restaurant, whose stylish modern interior design seamlessly incorporates the building's historical architectural features – note the huge wooden beam dating back to 1526! Named "INNOVATIVE KLASSIK By Sascha Bungeroth", the set menu comprises five courses and a few added extras. The chef takes his cue from the seasons, with dishes such as pickled Canadian scallops with beetroot, apple and shiso or raw Taubertal Wagyu beef, marinated and served with horseradish, mustard and smoked eel. The charming waitstaff will recommend the perfect wine to accompany your meal. Fabulous terrace in the baroque garden!

Name: Zur Sonne
Description: Run by the Glück family, this place serves fantastic seasonal dishes and regional classics. From game to Altmühltal lamb and their unique "Sauerbraten 2.0", the menu is packed with delicious options. With a clear commitment to sustainability and a preference for local produce, the kitchen team serves up dishes that are beautifully balanced in flavour. The bright, modern conservatory is a delightful space, as is the splendid terrace in summer. Comfortable and attractive guestrooms.

Name: Krone
Description: Nestled in the heart of Steinenbronn, this family-run establishment has been welcoming diners for many years. Here, modernity meets tradition in both the decor and the cuisine. The menu features timeless classics such as pork fillet in a creamy sauce, alongside more ambitious dishes, some made with game that they hunt themselves. For a pleasant, laid-back alternative, head to Krönle – the options written up on the board are very reasonably priced. Some house-made food items such as greaves lard spread, tripe, spaetzle, sauces and maultaschen can be purchased to take home. Decent guestrooms.

Name: Cube
Description: The absolutely fabulous location is as much of a draw as the glass architecture, the design and the ambitious international cuisine. There is a simpler lunch menu, too. The o.T. Bar serves breakfast, cake and after-work drinks. The lovely terrace is positioned on Schlossplatz, a square in front of the art museum. Tip for theatre- and concert-goers: Ask about their "late-night" dining slot.

Name: Schweizers Restaurant
Description: Originally opened in 1903 as Schweizer Hof, this restaurant is housed in a painstakingly restored listed building. In the aesthetically pleasing Jugendstil setting of this neighbourhood restaurant, the atmosphere is welcoming, thanks in no small part to the charming staff. A well-coordinated team in both the kitchen and front of house ensures a wonderful evening. Savour the five- to seven-course set menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. The flavoursome dishes showcase precise technique and high-quality ingredients. There is a well-curated wine list, as well as pairings by the glass. The quiet shady courtyard terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Königshafen
Description: The journey up to the north of the island is well worth it! Here, family tradition dates back to 1881, with the fifth generation currently looking after this spruce house with a white-brick façade, serving good regional and seasonal cuisine. Nice garden terrace behind the house. Tip: They are always well booked, so you should book early!

Name: mundart Restaurant
Description: Set in the heart of a quaint wine-growing village, the old house is an enchanting destination. The menu features flavoursome dishes with both classic and Mediterranean influences, such as grilled octopus with celeriac cream and lime, or veal loin and braised pork cheek with mashed potatoes. Dine in the charmingly rustic yet modern interior or out on the terrace in the lovely courtyard. The converted barn is perfect for private events.

Name: Hugenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: Inside Hugenhof is every bit as attractive as its exterior suggests with its lovely high ceilings, cosy old beams and a roaring open fire in winter. Every evening brings a different 4-course menu, which chef Klaus Ditz will announce at your table. This is accompanied by expert wine selections from his fellow chef and sommelier. The rooms are simple but smart.

Name: Zur Sonne
Description: Hanspeter Rombach attaches great importance to organic ingredients in his inviting, friendly restaurant. The cuisine is regional and classical: on the menu, for example, local venison ragout in Spätburgunder sauce or filet of organic salmon and wild gambas in pumpkin juice sauce. There are also cosy guestrooms and a pretty sauna area.

Name: Reck's
Description: Cuisine, art and accommodation are combined in this long-running family business. Three sisters run both the hotel – with some classic, some stylishly modern guestrooms – and the restaurant, which offers really good seasonally influenced cuisine. There are three cosy dining areas inside; outside, there are tables on the terrace in the shade of the plane trees, which affords views of the orchards! There is art displayed everywhere in the house.

Name: Kirschner Stuben
Description: This warm and welcoming place exudes a charming liveliness. The terrace overlooking the lake is an absolute delight. Complementing the inviting ambiance is a delectable selection of regional cuisine. An appealing array of fresh, flavoursome dishes awaits, ranging from braised veal cheeks to game and fish from Tegernsee. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally. At lunchtime there is a speciality menu. Maier zum Kirschner Hotel proposes pretty guestrooms imbued with Alpine charm.

Name: Landhaus Hohenlohe
Description: This long-standing family business, now with Matthias Mack at the helm, is run according to a winning formula. In a very pleasant informal atmosphere, extremely friendly and experienced waitstaff are always on hand. The delicious food is freshly prepared and feautures regional and international influences. You can compose a three- or four-course set menu from the appealing list of options (also vegetarian) or order à la carte. Appetising dishes include porcini ravioli, baby spinach, Brettenfeld Jerusalem artichokes, truffle fonduta. The restaurant also has its own herb and vegetable garden. Overnight accommodation is available in this well-kept country house nestled in a residential area.

Name: Juliette
Description: Are you looking for a slice of the French way of life in the middle of Potsdam? In the Holländisches Viertel (Dutch Quarter), you will find this beautifully designed restaurant, which is housed in a charming 17C half-timbered house. The dining space comprises three different levels, where you can enjoy ambitious classic cuisine accompanied by just the right wine, as a discreet soundtrack plays in the background. In addition to the menu, you can also choose a few dishes à la carte. If the weather is nice, would you like an aperitif at one of the small tables on the pavement before your meal?

Name: Bistro
Description: The bistro at the exclusive Gut Lärchenhof golf club on the outskirts of Cologne offers a somewhat simpler alternative to the eponymous fine dining restaurant, but you are just as assured of flavour and freshness – at both lunch and dinner. They serve dishes ranging from Currywurst to Königsberger Klopse (meatballs) and caviar. Needless to say, the terrace overlooking the green is delightful!

Name: Domschenke
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-run restaurant is now in its third generation. Whether you sit in the rustic-style dining area with its regulars' table or in the pleasant conservatory, you are assured of friendly service. The menu features home-style, regional and more sophisticated dishes. Order à la carte or opt for one of the daily specials on the blackboard. In summer, make a beeline for the outdoor seating area, which is shaded by old trees.

Name: Heim's Restaurant
Address: Moselstraße 27, Reil an der Mosel, 56861, Germany
Description: The food served in this 300-year-old restaurant is honest, fresh and full of flavour. Classic and regional cuisine is served throughout the day (kitchen opening hours: 12-8.30pm), taking the form of dishes such as cod à la grenobloise with spinach and mashed potatoes or "Original Wiener Schnitzel" with fried potatoes, salad and cranberries. You will be able to find just the right Moselle wine to accompany your meal. Service comes courtesy of a friendly and proficient team, the atmosphere is pleasant, and in summer, the wonderful terrace with a view of the vineyards and Moselle beckons. The Reiler Hof hotel has lovely guestrooms.

Name: Ganter Restaurant Mohren
Description: Whether you opt for a cosy-rustic or a chic-modern interior, the food on offer here is fresh and regional with international influences. Try the char with pearl barley, herbs, almonds and madras curry spices.

Name: Gasthaus Cervus
Description: At this well-run, rustic-style restaurant located in the town centre, Johannes Füller serves up regionally influenced cuisine strewn with international touches. The dishes are lovingly prepared and delicious – the speciality is Rostbraten (roast beef with all the trimmings). You can choose between a set menu and à la carte options. Simpler and shorter lunchtime menu. From some tables you can steal glimpses into the kitchen. In summer, the courtyard is a charming spot.

Name: Landhaus Drei Raben
Description: The Koep family has been synonymous with excellent cuisine since 1995… and you can expect just that when you come to eat here on this property on the 18C Landgut Jaquetrois. This former agricultural estate is planted with beautiful old trees. The restaurant has a cosy dining area (warming fireplace in winter) and a fabulous terrace with views over the Mahnensee – especially charming at sunset! The food is international, regional and seasonal. Tip: Coffee and cake are served on Sundays.

Name: Schloss Niederweis
Description: This tasteful restaurant is housed in the converted corn barn of a magnificent Baroque castle dating from 1751. The decor is a fascinating blend of rustic cachet and modern design – the open truss roof is striking and the two historical carriages on the wall are certainly eye-catching! Sample the flavoursome dishes à la carte or as a set menu, washed down by your choice from the terrific wine list that includes rare finds, including by the glass. Charming garden, a banquet hall and a registry office. On a practical note: easy parking.

Name: IU & ON
Description: This family business in the heart of Nuremberg has been around since 1972! Many regulars keep coming back, having been won over by the aromatic dishes, which include classics like laab and tom yum. Add to that a clean-lined, minimalist-style interior and friendly service. By the way, the restaurant takes its name from the sisters Iu and On who cook here.

Name: Wilde Triebe
Description: Set in refurbished former railway buildings dating back over 150 years, Wilde Triebe offers a minimalist, imaginative and fashionable mix of art and food. The flavoursome, seasonal, regional fare is served in an upmarket brick, concrete, steel and wood interior on the restaurant’s own tableware. Great garden.

Name: MINNECI
Description: The historical character of this town house dating back to 1560 makes it the perfect setting for an Italian restaurant. Here, diners can either opt for a four- to six-course set menu or order à la carte – think flavoursome Mediterranean dishes such as ravioli with wild mushrooms, sage and balsamic vinegar. At lunchtime, there is a smaller, more budget-friendly set menu. Friendly service comes courtesy of charming waitstaff. Delightful terrace in front of the building. For those coming by car: there is a public car park next door.

Name: Schloss Restaurant Venus
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park
Description: Set in the "Versailles of Westphalia", this classic, distinguished restaurant has vaulted ceilings and numerous paintings by owner Franz L Lauter, an avid painter. A seasonal set menu is available in the evening (from 5pm). At lunchtime on Thursday to Saturday, there are set menus. Tip: Either before or after dinner, why not take a walk around the castle and park?

Name: ZweiSinn Meiers | Bistro
Description: If a really nice bistro in Nuremberg is what you are looking for, then this is the place for you! A pleasant, refined atmosphere, friendly service, and good food await you here. The modern and Mediterranean-inspired à la carte selection is appealing, and there is also a caviar menu. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced daily special is always in demand. Tip: On Wednesday and Thursday evenings, selected dishes from the menu of the fine dining restaurant, which is located in the same building, go into a three-course business menu (sparkling wine included). They also offer fine wines by the glass and top-drawer alcohol-free alternatives.

Name: Historisches Gasthaus Sanct Peter Restaurant Weinkirche
Description: Having been renovated following the disastrous floods of 2021, this restaurant gives off an impression of classical elegance. A 13C church with a gallery forms the core of the establishment. There are also two other attractive dining spaces (called Alte Lay and Walporzheimer Himmelchen). The delightful terrace to the rear of the building offers a view of the greenery. The menu features dishes with regional, seasonal and international influences. Classics include braised ox cheeks in Ahr valley Burgundy sauce, and turbot in Ahr valley blanc de noir sauce. The selection of Broggsitter wines is impressive, and there is a well-stocked wine shop on site, too. From 2-6pm, you can order from the smaller menu, with options such as the platter of cold meats and cheeses. They also run Hotel Sanct Peter in the town.

Name: Imperial by Alexander Herrmann
Description: The location that houses this restaurant is interesting in the way it blends the architectural details of the old building, such as high ceilings and large arched windows, into the modern, chic-meets-urban look. In this stylish yet relaxed setting, diners are treated to warm hospitality and can watch Michael Seitz at work in the open kitchen, as he cooks up international dishes with a Franconian twist. For parties of two or more people, the sharing menus "Celebration Mood" and "Glamour Mood" are highly recommended, as well as the "Nuremberg Menu", which presents Franconia's Top Ten dishes in a whole new way. Tip: The "OpenHausBrunch" takes place on certain Sundays, and there are other regular events.

Name: Cornelia Poletto
Description: A really appealing restaurant in a great location! The upscale, modern and elegant interior is a delightful setting in which to enjoy the fresh Mediterranean cuisine. With clear Italian influences, an interesting three-course set menu is served at lunchtime; in the evening, a larger set menu is proposed, along with a selection of delicious à la carte options. Be sure to try the antipasti! The service is friendly and professional. Tip: In summer, there are also a few tables on the pavement in front of the building. Between the restaurant and the cookery school, Paola's is a bar-cum-deli – ideal for an aperitif or cocktails.

Name: Spielweg
Description: First mentioned in records in 1705, the original Spielweg building, managed by the Fuchs family, makes for a wonderfully cosy setting. The charming dining rooms are done out in traditional Black Forest style and the service is extremely friendly and attentive. Diners can expect classic regional cuisine that is ambitious and full of flavour, as in the warm smoked char from the Wutach in a cold potato and leek broth. It also draws on Asian influences, cf. their wild boar dim sum with soy sauce – Asian cuisine is one of the young chef's passions. The lunchtime menu proposes somewhat simpler fare, making this place an ideal stop-off for a light meal during a hike. You can stay overnight in well-kept, individually furnished guestrooms.

Name: Turmstube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the friendly atmosphere of this elegant space, the delicious and seasonally inspired cuisine with international influences is made with select ingredients, sourced from the region wherever possible. Diners can choose between the set menu ("Genießermenü") or the à la carte options. Tip: Take in the lovely view from the terrace. For those who would like to stay a little longer, Der Birkenhof hotel promises patrons a comfortable stay complete with spa facilities.

Name: Steinheuers Landgasthof Poststuben
Description: By no means a lesser version of Steinheuer, this is a restaurant in its own right where everything is cooked fresh. Taking its cue from the seasons, the menu features regional classics and international dishes. The same well-stocked wine list is presented here as in the fine dining restaurant. Dine in the cosy interior, or head out to the delightful leafy terrace. For overnight stays, there are double rooms available in the main building, as well as a comfortable guesthouse.

Name: Christians Restaurant
Description: Run by Sandy and Christian Heß, this is an appealing restaurant – and that goes for the atmosphere as well as the cuisine. The interior is sleek, bright and welcoming, with beautiful arched windows affording a view of the Neckar River. And then there's the terrace overlooking the water – a truly idyllic spot in which to dine in fine weather! The cuisine is contemporary with a Mediterranean touch – opt for a set menu or order à la carte. This lovely space can also be used for private functions.

Name: Joseph Naus Stub'n
Description: This restaurant, named after the first climber to reach the summit of the Zugspitze, is not just an attractive place where service comes courtesy of very friendly staff; the food here is also delicious. At lunchtime, there is a reasonably priced two-course set menu and a small à la carte menu. In the evening, peruse the large menu, from which you can order either à la carte or a set menu. Hotel Zugspitze also has well-kept guestrooms, should you wish to stay overnight.

Name: Ponyhof Stammhaus by Tobias Wussler
Description: The sort of restaurant you would love to have in your own neighbourhood. This long-standing family-run establishment delights guests with classics like cordon bleu, as well as contemporary creations such as scallops with pumpkin, curry and lemongrass – and, of course, excellent charcoal-grilled steaks. The menu, which features plenty of comforting soul food dishes, is complemented by friendly service and an inviting setting that makes it easy to linger. In summer, the terrace is divine. Unsurprisingly, this charming spot is also a popular choice for weddings.

Name: CARLS Brasserie an der Elbphilharmonie
Description: As you take in the view of the Elbe River and the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, you can soak up the lively and casual yet elegant brasserie atmosphere and enjoy sophisticated North German cuisine such as fish stew or whole sole. The unique location means that window seats are in demand. And in summer, diners make a beeline for the terrace. The bistro next door serves bowls and tartines. A wine bar is also part of the premises.

Name: Zipang
Description: Zipang translates to "kingdom of the rising sun" – everything about this restaurant, from the modern minimalist decor to the menu, is a celebration of the Far East. The food is definitely something to get excited about – with meticulous attention to detail, the finest ingredients are prepared using authentic Japanese techniques. At lunchtime, excellent value for money; in the evening, the mood is more upscale, with a six- or eight-course tasting menu featuring dishes such as hamachi with mackerel, yuba, Japanese mayonnaise and summer vegetables, or tuna with shungiku wasabi sauce and shrimp croquette. Great selection of top-shelf sake! Friendly service.

Name: Kamino
Description: The Zumkeller family have transformed what was once Chämi-Hüsli into this cosy restaurant and tapas bar – the striking fireplace with extended flue after which Kamino is named presides in the middle of the dining area, which has a high ceiling and a round floor plan. The classic and Mediterranean cuisine always has a modern touch and a certain pizazz. Dishes such as roasted sea bass fillet with home-made tagliarini and lobster cream give the tasty tapas a run for their money. The icing on the cake is the charming service provided by owner Stefanie Zumkeller and her team. For an overnight stay, there are three pretty and cosy guestrooms.

Name: NIKKEI NINE
Description: You should not hesitate to make a reservation at this culinary hotspot in Hamburg. Located in the luxurious Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten, the restaurant has a stylish and elegant ambience, courtesy of an interior done out in dark wood, cream and gold tones. On the menu: Japanese-international fusion cuisine. The service is very friendly and attentive. They also have a cool bar.

Name: Hirschen
Address: Breisgauer Straße 47, Freiburg im Breisgau, 79110, Germany
Description: One of Freiburg's culinary institutions, Hirschen draws diners to the peaceful neighbourhood of Lehen. An authentic and cosy Baden-style atmosphere awaits you in the dining area of this charming historic inn, which is run with dedication by the Baumgartner family. For years, the kitchen has been renowned for its masterful blend of regional fare and classic French cuisine. Dishes such as Baden lamb's lettuce with roasted goose liver and black truffle, and "winemaker's skrei" with cabbage braised in champagne, glazed grapes, bacon strips, butter croutons and mashed potatoes showcase the finest, freshest ingredients. The carefully curated wine list also highlights wines from Baden and France, including prestigious labels such as Romanée Conti. Service is friendly and attentive. The restaurant is part of the hotel of the same name.

Name: Goldener Karpfen
Description: In this historical house, seasonal international cuisine with classic regional roots is prepared from select fresh produce. Tip: the classic beef tartare. To be accompanied by a choice of international wines. The interior is elegant and cosy at the same time; in summer you can sit outside. For overnight stays there are comfortable guestrooms ranging from stylishly refined to modern chic.

Name: Hirschen
Description: A beloved fixture in the valley, this restaurant is part of the long-established hotel of the same name, located right in the heart of the village on the banks of Glotter River. In its rustic yet elegant interiors, diners are waited on by a friendly front-of-house team. For decades, the kitchen has showcased the best of Baden and French cuisine, with a pronounced emphasis on seasonality – be it game, mushrooms or asparagus. Both at lunchtime and in the evenings, the cooking is ambitious. Dishes such as grilled octopus served on a bed of curried lentils and vegetables, or veal loin in a cream sauce with chanterelles are available à la carte or in the set menu. The wine list is dominated by labels from the Baden region.

Name: Zenzakan
Address: Taunusanlage 15, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
Description: Since opening in 2009, this has been a go-to classic in the city's financial hub. Somewhat hidden away, this elegant and stylish restaurant is accessible via a courtyard. The interior, done out in dark tones with dimmed lighting, smacks of the Far East (the terracotta warriors are eye-catching). The atmosphere is lively, and contemporary music provides the acoustic backdrop. The menu includes a wide selection of pan-Asian dishes ranging from sushi and sashimi to classic curries and robata grill specialities. Dishes such as velveted black pepper beef or char siu chicken are especially tempting.

Name: Zum Krug
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This place has a long history that stretches back to 1720, and the Laufer family has now been at the helm for three generations. Behind the gorgeous historical façade, the cosy dining spaces exude traditional charm. Theregional and international cuisine takes its cue from the seasons, and the menu includes dishes such as a Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) of organic pasture-fed beef with potato dumplings and cranberries. The friendly and professional waitstaff will be happy to recommend fine Rheingau wines from the estate to accompany your meal. Delightful courtyard terrace. Smart guestrooms – some are especially modern.

Name: Rebstock
Description: Rebstock offers comfortable, country-style dining rooms, attentive service and good regional fare including snail soup, pike dumplings and venison ragout. In summer the idyllic terrace offers views of the surrounding parkland and the Black Forest, while another attraction is the large selection of home-made cakes and pastries.

Name: Lohninger
Address: Schweizer Straße 1, Frankfurt on the Main, 60594, Germany
Description: Set on the banks of the River Main in Frankfurt, this restaurant tastefully blends the classic flair of the old building in which it is housed – beautiful high stucco ceilings, herringbone floorboards – with modern minimalist design. The cuisine draws on the Lohninger family's Austrian roots as well as Asian and Mediterranean influences, and the menu has been divided into two sections accordingly: "Die Heimat" (homeland) and "Die Welt" (the world). The dishes stand out for their finesse, intense flavours and the quality of the ingredients; chef-patron Mario Lohninger and his kitchen team are careful to avoid gimmickry and place the emphasis on flavour. This holds for both classics and signature dishes such as Carinthian Schlutzkrapfen (high-Alpine cheese ravioli), Imperial and Royal ox cheek goulash, or Spencer Gulf kingfish sashimi with foie gras, pickled vegetables and a buttermilk and horseradish dressing. The front-of-house team is friendly, attentive and pleasingly relaxed and down-to-earth – anything but stuffy.

Name: Bastian's Restaurant
Description: This country inn with its bright, tastefully decorated interior and beautiful, partly covered terrace specialises in serving culinary classics that evolve with the seasons. There are two set menus (one of which is vegetarian) comprising four to seven courses. The quality of the ingredients, which are mostly locally sourced, is beyond question. Great value for money. The service is very friendly and charming.

Name: Weinstube Sibylla
Description: A good place to come for unpretentious cuisine. The menu ranges from classics such as Wiener schnitzel or Berlin-style calf's liver to a "Gourmet Tradition" section featuring dishes such as saddle and shoulder of venison in pasta sheets, with tenderstem broccoli and an elderberry jus. There is also a selection of vegetarian dishes and a range of delicious desserts. Lovely old wooden floors, wood-panelled walls and pretty decorations make for a charming atmosphere. The verdant terrace is also inviting. Guestrooms are available in the adjoining Erbprinz hotel.

Name: Kupferpfanne
Description: Erwin Weidenhiller's restaurant, in a central location opposite the town hall, has been a classic on Fürth's food scene for decades. In the comfortable and elegant interior, they serve classic cuisine with seasonal and international-Mediterranean influences, made with good-quality produce. Tip: the reasonably priced lunch menu.

Name: Hartmaier's Villa
Description: This modern restaurant is housed in a pretty villa dating back to 1816. The Hartmaier family and their team have been serving up good food here for many years. The menu is wide-ranging, characterised by seasonal, regional and international influences – from Zwiebelrostbraten (steak with onion rings), beans with bacon and roast potatoes to wild-caught Icelandic redfish fillet with pak choi and spinach and ricotta ravioli. At lunchtime, people flock here for the bargain set menu with a choice of starters and mains. The feel of the place is both elegant and more casual, with a lovely leafy terrace in front of the building. Tip: You can buy wines to take home at their Vinothek.

Name: Landgasthaus Schuster
Description: The Schuster family's country inn is thoroughly charming! This is primarily down to the warm hospitality extended by the lady of the house, and the tasteful interior design. And then there are the chef-patron's seasonally influenced classic dishes such as pike-perch sausage accompanied by creamed sauerkraut with dates, or venison with nuts, black walnut sauce, cranberries and Savoy cabbage. Individual courses from each of the two set menus ("Tradition" and "Genusswerk") can be ordered à la carte. Decent wine selection with good options available by the glass.

Name: Stüble
Description: Stüble is the tasteful, rustic-style à la carte restaurant of Wellness Lauterbad, a chic spa hotel.
