In the cosy and comfortable wood-panelled space, the service is friendly and attentive. The regional and seasonal cuisine has international influences. Order à la carte or plump for a three- or four-course set menu. In summer, you can drink in the view of the countryside from the terrace.

Name: Lindenhof
Description: Like their hotel with its cosy individually designed guestrooms, the Hankhs' restaurant is also very popular. This is down to the excellent seasonal cuisine, which has regional and Mediterranean influences. A great deal of dedication and care is invested in preparing the often complex dishes. You can order à la carte or opt for a set menu (vegetarian version available). Friendly and competent waitstaff. The small terraces in front of and to the rear of the building are delightful.

Name: Das Ballenberger
Description: A friendly, modern restaurant in the centre of the old town close to the historic Krämerbrücke bridge, Das Ballenberger serves seasonal, international cuisine including scallops with two kinds of asparagus and orange. You’ll also find some mouthwatering home-made cakes and a delicious breakfast from 9 am after a stay in one of the five charming overnight apartments.

Name: Bistro Fatal
Description: It would be a shame (perhaps even a fatal mistake) not to get to know Alexandre and Sarah Bourgeuil's pleasantly unpretentious bistro, where savoir-vivre is the order of the day. The classic French menu is enticing, featuring staples such as beef tartare, chocolate soufflé and – of course – oysters. The food here is excellent. You can pick dishes to make up your own three-course "Toi & Moi" set menu – vegetarian options are also available. In summer, a terrace is set up on the pavement in front of the building. N.B. Finding a parking space nearby is not easy.

Name: VIDA
Description: This place has it all: a stylish, upscale decor, enthusiastic, professional and friendly service, and creative international cuisine incorporating both Asian and Mediterranean influences. Diners are offered a choice between the "VIDA" set menu – with meat or vegetarian – and a range of à la carte dishes. The attentive and well-drilled service team is also on hand to offer expert wine recommendations – there is an attractive selection to choose from. Wine pairings to complement the set menu are also available. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif or digestif at the VIDA bar.

Name: Kronenschlösschen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Here, diners can sit beneath a stylishly painted historical ceiling or out on the pretty terrace with adjoining garden. The kitchen draws on traditional French cuisine to propose creative dishes in the form of a four- to six-course menu. Plus the wine list is one of the best in Germany. Alternatively, try the bistro. Guests can also stay overnight in the hotel of the same name in cosy, well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: Il Cortile
Description: You get to this restaurant, which is located in a pretty little courtyard in Erfurt's old town via Johannesstraße. In a cosy atmosphere, diners tuck into Mediterranean-inspired cuisine that draws on flavours from all over the world. The menu features dishes such as "Ricotta, truffle, pea, Serrano", "Salsiccia, capers, sugar snap pea" or "Fjord trout, grape, risotto, truffle".

Name: Weinrestaurant Turmschänke
Description: In this restaurant in the Nicolaiturm, the lovely historical details, such as paintings and original furniture dating from 1912, foster a rustic yet elegant feel. The waitstaff are pleasingly laid-back and down-to-earth. Meticulously prepared seasonal dishes are served as a set menu or à la carte; mouthwatering options from the barbecue are also available. Complete with helpful descriptions, the wine list comprises some 140 items – most are from the region, but international labels also feature. Special wine evenings are also hosted here.

Name: Gambero Rosso da Domenico
Description: Domenico Cannizzaro has been on a mission to showcase Italian cuisine in Franconia for well over 20 years, and has run this restaurant at the small marina with his wife, Teresa, since 2012. Here, they live and breathe hospitality, serving two set menus, "Domenico" and "Teresuzza", which each comprise three or four courses – it's also possible to mix and match. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the chef-patron himself. Gorgeous terrace overlooking the Main River.

Name: Taverna & Trattoria Palio
Description: Palio offers fresh Italian fare from the open kitchen in a relaxed trattoria-style atmosphere – you simply have to try one of the pasta dishes! The seasonal set menus are also interesting. There’s also a lovely terrace in the shade of some old chestnut trees.

Name: Restaurant Villa Esche
Description: Built in 1903, the former coach house of Villa Esche (now the Henry van de Velde Museum) houses this bright, tastefully designed restaurant where diners can enjoy attentive service and top-notch seasonal cuisine. Opt for the four-course menu or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the options are slightly more limited but include moderately priced daily specials. Delightful terrace overlooking the grounds.

Name: Redüttchen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: What was once the gardener's cottage at the 18C La Redoute ballroom and concert hall is a feel-good place that has won over more than its fair share of regulars. The restaurant's appeal lies not only in its extremely charming ambience, but also in Matthias Pietsch's innovative take on modern cuisine and the experienced, courteous and cordial service. The pleasant dining area is laid out over two levels, and the terrace to the rear of the building is also a lovely spot.

Name: Brasserie Colette Tim Raue
Description: A big name on the fine dining scene, Tim Raue has created a pleasingly down-to-earth brasserie of the sort you might expect to find in Paris. This place has a modern feel tempered by a slight touch of nostalgia. The excellent food comes in the form of an interesting contemporary concept: diners can choose à la carte or put together their own four-course meal – a vegan version is also possible. The menu features classics such as beef Wellington for two and seasonal dishes.

Name: eins44
Description: This restaurant tucked away in the third courtyard of the Otto-Reichel-Höfe is a real success story. Inside, the converted distillery exudes a casual, trendy "urban loft" atmosphere with an industrial feel. Diners sit at beautiful solid old beechwood tables and tuck into ingredient-led seasonal cuisine. The modern, creative dishes are served in the form of a reasonably priced five-course set menu – either with meat/fish or vegetarian. Service is provided by a dedicated and friendly team.

Name: maiBeck
Description: Run by Jan Cornelius Maier and Tobias Becker (hence the contraction "maiBeck"), this inviting restaurant serves modern cuisine made from select ingredients. The decor strikes just the right note: upscale yet unpretentious; the service is friendly. The wine list offers excellent value for money, particularly the bottles. Finally, the location between the cathedral and the Rhine means that the terrace is a place to see and be seen. Tip: Take a stroll through the Old Town before or after you dine. Handy for motorists: The Philharmonie underground car park is just around the corner.

Name: Schwanen
Description: This family business has been going for three generations. The dishes served in this chic, modern restaurant are made with preference for regional produce and sing with freshness and flavour. For a bistro alternative, Karl Benz Stube has a short menu featuring traditional Swabian fare. There are also suitable spaces for special occasions available and practical guestrooms with contemporary decor. Tip: the "Kultur & Genuss" events.

Name: Wappen-Saal
Description: This imposing castle estate provides a truly unique setting for dining. Before taking a seat in the stately Wappensaal in the Schlosshotel at Burg Schlitz, take a leisurely stroll along the Goetheweg. Experience the historical ambiance of this restaurant as you savour a four- to six-course menu of ambitious classic cuisine beneath an impressive high ceiling. The charming and experienced staff will be happy to help you choose the perfect accompaniment to your meal from the well-curated wine list.

Name: Hubertushof
Address: Arzheimer Straße 5, Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz, 76831, Germany
Location: Ilbesheim bei Landau in der Pfalz, Germany
Description: Remaining true to the Südliche Weinstraße, Sandra Bernhard and Jochen Sitter moved from Birkweiler to this 300 year-old former coaching house, which they run with great dedication and charm. The chef cooks traditional and modern, but above all, flavoursome fare. Dishes include classics such as pan-friend black pudding and Saumagen (stuffed pig’s stomach). The interior courtyard is gorgeous.

Name: Das Tschecherl
Description: This small restaurant is an offshoot of Jürgen Wolfsgruber's Sparkling Bistro, which is located nearby. The cuisine has a distinctly Austrian bias, with dishes such as pike-perch fished in the Salzkammergut region, Szeged cabbage and caraway potatoes featuring on the concise menu. On these premises where legendary chef Hans Haas of Tantris fame used to have his cookery school, the decor is now pleasantly sleek and pared back. A competent team takes care of the service; you get interesting glimpses of the action in the open kitchen. The restaurant is open from 12-8pm.

Name: Zehntkeller
Description: Located in the middle of the village, this traditional establishment serves good regional and seasonal cuisine. The menu features mouth-watering dishes such as braised beef cheek in a Pinot noir sauce. Opt for a four-course set menu or order à la carte. The house proposes its own organic wines. Very friendly and well-drilled service, a cosy interior, and a lovely terrace laid out under the wisteria. The hotel of the same name has stylish, classic guestrooms.

Name: Zur Iphöfer Kammer
Description: This picture-perfect Gasthaus is located on Marktplatz, in the centre of this quaint wine-growing town. The lovely little terrace is as inviting as the elegantly charming interior. Your dedicated hosts, Heidrun Kaufmann and Markus Lösch, really know how to create a warm and welcoming atmosphere: she provides cordial service with a personal touch; he cooks up ambitious dishes brimming with bold flavours – venison ragout fin with rye bread gnocchi, or sea bass with artichokes and lemon polenta. Excellent wines from Wirsing wine estate.

Name: Danzer's
Description: The contemporary ambience in a sleek and at the same time homely style makes for an appealing start – not to mention the terrace with a view of the dike. The food is international and regional, such as fillet of sea bass in bacon butter with wok-fried savoy cabbage. Short lunch menu.

Name: Westphalenhof
Description: This stylish and sophisticated restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a residential area. Here, the Westphal brothers – one is the chef, the other the sommelier – delight diners with delicious food and excellent wine recommendations. The menu features international dishes that take their cue from the seasons, such as confit halibut fillet in nut butter, potato scales, cauliflower cream, dried tomatoes and Sardinian pasta. The walk-in wine cellar accommodates 120 different labels. The restaurant is also open for lunch on Saturdays and Sundays.

Name: Adler Stuben
Description: The traditional Parkhotel Adler, which has been a family-run business for over 500 years, is home to this historical Black Forest establishment whose origins date back to 1639. It has five really pleasant dining areas, from the charming "Stube" with its old wood panelling and a low ceiling, to the chic "Bergkristall", and of course the terrace. The cuisine comprises Baden and international dishes; vegetarian options are also available. The wine list features a good selection of wines from the region. For an overnight stay, there are cosy, elegant guestrooms.

Name: FLYGGE
Description: An interesting location! The restaurant of chef-patron Mathias Apelt and his partner Britta Künzl is housed in the canoe club; it has a cool, pared-back design with an urban boathouse feel. There is also a wonderful view of the fjord – needless to say, a spot on the terrace is a tempting prospect. The open kitchen serves Nordic-inspired and regionally based soul food, eg bouillabaisse made with Baltic fish and rouille, which, although different to the original from the South of France, is just as delicious!

Name: Schwane 1404
Description: In this centuries-old inn in the beautiful old town, this is a truly charming alternative to the fine dining restaurant. Both the inviting, rustic-style restaurant room and fantastic inner courtyard are appealing places to eat. In the evening, you can order modern-inspired classic dishes à la carte or opt for the "Romantik" set menu. Many of the ingredients are locally sourced; some of the vegetables are from their own garden, and they have their own wines. Hearty meals (‘Brotzeit’) are served at lunchtime.

Name: Am Osterfeuer
Description: First opened as a bakery 100 years ago, this family-run establishment is now in its fourth generation. Hans-Jörg Dunker and his team have long been synonymous with quality and Westphalian cuisine with an international twist. The restaurant interior is attractive and cheerful, having been given a skilful modern makeover, but care has been taken to leave the traditional character of the building intact. One of the chef's specialities is the wonderful fish and shellfish soup with aioli, bread and Parmesan. A gorgeous terrace for summer. There is also a charming hall available for festivities.

Name: Wieland-Stuben
Description: This restaurant has become something of an institution in the region. The Wieland-Stuben has been a byword for classic cuisine since 1965. The elegant, tastefully decorated dining area makes for a really appealing setting, as does the gorgeous garden terrace. In their classic French cuisine, Lukas Erfurth and his team use only selected ingredients that impress with their freshness and quality. You can opt for the set menu or dine à la carte. The excellent service comes courtesy of a team headed up by sommelier Ronja. On Sundays, there is a three-course set menu (no à la carte dishes).

Name: Madame Ngo - Une Brasserie Hanoi
Description: It is definitely worth waiting for one of the coveted tables here! This charmingly informal restaurant is very popular due to its simple but excellent Vietnamese cuisine, which is also inexpensive. There is an enticing aroma from the bubbling pots in the open kitchen – a large bowl of authentic “pho” (noodle soup) is practically a must!

Name: Jacobs Restaurant
Description: Accommodated in Hotel Louis C. Jacob, which boasts a prime location, this restaurant serves modern cuisine with classic touches in an elegant setting. Diners can order à la carte or opt for one of the set menus (conventional or vegetarian). Among the standout dishes are the lobster foam soup and the braised ox shoulder. The Vierland duck served in four courses is a classic option for two. Well-curated wine list. The seating out on Lindenterrasse, overlooking the Elbe River, is undoubtedly the highlight in summer.

Name: Otto
Description: This compact restaurant has an appealingly lively atmosphere. The friendly vibe is due in no small part to the fantastic, well-drilled team, who have a personalised touch when it comes to looking after diners. The open kitchen – overlooking which there are also a few seats at the bar – sends out seasonal, modern, pared-down dishes with Nordic influences, all made using locally sourced ingredients. You can choose between the sharing menu and à la carte dishes. Vegetarians are also catered for. There is a rather short but carefully curated wine list with a predilection for natural and orange wines. Small terrace in front of the restaurant. This very popular restaurant has limited seating, so be sure to book in advance!

Name: Roku - Japanese Dining & Wine
Description: This is the third restaurant to be opened by Yoshizumi Nagaya in Düsseldorf. The atmosphere is trendy, modern and relaxed. The Japanese menu ranges from a variety of appealing starters and a fine selection of sushi and sashimi to tempura, fish and meat dishes – including, for example, A5 Wagyu steak. There is a good, predominantly German wine list and a selection of sake. Tip: Lunch Wed-Fri.

Name: Il Teatro²
Description: Founded in 1984, this family-run establishment located close to the Staatstheater (hence the name) is now run by the second generation, with Daniele di Sario taking the helm several years ago. He delivers classic Italian and French-style cuisine that is in keeping with the zeitgeist: The spaghetti carbonara, turbot with Champagne sauce or lemon dessert ("Kreation von der Zitrone") are shining examples. In keeping with the name of the restaurant, the menu is divided into different sections: Act 1, Intermezzo, Act 2 and Epilogue. Veteran chef Giovanni likes to get in on the action front of house, joining forces with the enthusiastic and attentive service team. In summer, the terrace seating out on the wide pavement is especially appealing.

Name: Klinker
Description: It's no surprise that this spot in central Harvestehude draws such a crowd, with its trendy urban design, lively atmosphere and floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the street's activities – plus terrace tables available in summer. The food is predominantly vegetarian. The establishment's commitment to ecology and sustainability is reflected in the exclusive use of regional ingredients, primarily sourced from Demeter farms. Fermenting and preserving are also part of their practice – with about 3 000 jars of preserves in stock, their dedication speaks for itself! Some jars are also used as decoration in the restaurant. Tip: The sharing option allows you to sample various dishes. Highlights include the salsify "carbonara" with Parmesan and hazelnut, and yellow carrots with saffron and chives.

Name: Chang
Description: This restaurant serves a wide range of Asian cuisine – sushi, curries and wok dishes are the highlights, and the focus is squarely on the quality of the ingredients. Inside, there is a minimalist decor and open kitchen; outside, a lovely covered terrace. The trip to Grünwald is definitely worthwhile. Marily, which sells ice cream and confectionery in summer, is housed in the same building. Tip: Park free of charge in the multi-storey car park on Marktplatz a few metres away.

Name: Kurpfalz Weinstuben
Description: A typical Palatinate wine tavern in the middle of Berlin? At Adenauerplatz near Ku'damm, you will find this traditional bar tucked away in a courtyard. In cosy, rustic rooms you can enjoy home-style cooking and regional classics, along with 50 wines served by the glass and 800 on the wine list. Short menu of the day at lunchtime.

Name: Hirschkönig
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Here, rural charm combines with elegant and contemporary interior design to create a welcoming setting – that goes for both the Hirschen hotel and its small fine dining restaurant with its upscale, sleek and stylish dining space. The modern and seasonal set menu, "Feld & Flur" ("Field & Fell"), is composed of six or seven courses imbued with a hint of the Mediterranean, such as wild garlic ravioli with tomato. Wine pairings are available upon request. Head to the delicatessen for house-made specialities such as chutneys, pickles and cured meats.

Name: Phaedra
Description: Are you in the mood for Mediterranean cuisine with Greek influences? Then try, for example, the fried halibut with a chive beurre blanc and trout caviar or the house-made mezze – to share or as a starter. Good produce is used, including meat from Franz Keller and wild-caught prawns. The place has an appealingly trendy bistro look and a pleasantly relaxed atmosphere. Diners take their seats at regular tables or high tables – the latter offer partial views into the open kitchen. Tip for motorists: public multi-storey car park opposite.

Name: Freilinger Wirt
Description: This traditional Bavarian inn has been around since 1870 and today it boasts a lovely blend of clean, modern design and warm wood. The patron and chef is a master butcher and his experience working at renowned restaurants can be seen in his good seasonal dishes. The large terrace is popular.

Name: 20° RESTOBAR
Description: This modern, unpretentious restaurant with a terrace, bar and lovely inner courtyard is located in the centre of town. In a pleasantly lively atmosphere, you can enjoy Spanish-Mediterranean cuisine: in addition to fish, meat, rice and potato dishes, you will of course also find tapas, croquetas and the like. In keeping with the Mediterranean concept, the name refers to the average water temperature around the island of Mallorca.

Name: Oechsle
Description: Serving flavoursome dishes made from fresh, high-quality ingredients in a pleasant contemporary atmosphere, this restaurant on the corner is a real gem. Its short menu draws on both Mediterranean and classical influences. This place also doubles as a wine bar, so you can look forward to a well-curated wine list. Experienced and charming waitstaff provide great service with a personal touch. In summer, the tables out front, facing the street, are in high demand.

Name: XO Seafoodbar
Description: As well as haebel, just across the street, Fabio Haebel runs this trendy, laid-back establishment in the heart of St Pauli. Occupying two floors, the restaurant has an agreeably lively atmosphere. Upstairs there are also a few seats at a counter facing the open kitchen. The food is modern and seasonal, with a focus on seafood specialties, including oysters, monkfish schnitzel and grilled prawns, and of course the famous "Pasta Krabbe". Alternatively, you could opt for "Chef's Choice" – a selection of items picked from the menu by the kitchen team. Tip: Treat yourself to a cocktail at the small bar. In summer, head for the terrace and soak up the buzzy atmosphere.

Name: Bistro oma & enkel
Description: oma & enkel ("grandma & grandchild") is the culinary concept at this bistro in the long-established Posthotel. The name symbolises a bridging of the gap between the generations, from the traditional to the modern. Recipes of yesteryear are brought up to date and classics of Franconian cuisine are given a contemporary twist. In a pleasingly laid-back atmosphere, choose between "Franconian tapas", the "Signature Menu" or the "Duck Menu". Don't miss out on the Franconian bouillabaisse or the apricot dumplings.

Name: Thuns Dorfkrug
Description: This restaurant offers beautifully laid tables, attentive service and good cuisine offering a mix of regional and international elements. The simple and elegant style of the decor features attractive contemporary pictures and parquet flooring. The guestrooms are in a clean-lined, modern style.

Name: martino.kitchen
Description: This pleasant, well-run little restaurant in the town centre has a friendly atmosphere and trendy vibe. Led by chef Martino Stirn, after whom the restaurant is named, the team sends out tasty Mediterranean/Italian dishes made in the open kitchen using seasonal ingredients. In addition to the à la carte selection, in the evening there is the option of ordering a surprise menu. Lunch options are more limited. The lady of the house provides charming service. In summer, from the terrace you can hear the carillon of the majestic church, the nearby Marktkirche, ringing at given times.

Name: Scala
Description: This modern restaurant boasts beautiful views across the lake and a delightful terrace. It also serves seasonal dishes with an emphasis on regional ingredients, and the vegetable and animal produce are used in their entirety. A smaller selection of dishes is served at lunchtime. Friendly service and fine wines.

Name: Ratsstube
Description: In the former town hall, you can now dine in a stylish and inviting space that combines contemporary design with the warmth of wood and natural tones. The cuisine is ambitious, creative and modern, but at the same time pleasantly down-to-earth. The names of the dishes are original, such as "H2O" (cold watermelon and cucumber soup, trout ceviche) or "Haarscharf" ("Razor-sharp") (medium-rare wild boar, spring onion and beetroot ragout, garden herbs, horseradish pasta). The presentation is colourful and very visually appealing. In summer, there is pleasant terrace seating in the shade of lime trees. Good overnight accommodation available.

Name: Steinbuck Stube
Description: In the centre of town is this pretty, lavishly restored 400-year-old house. You can sit in the cosy, tastefully decorated restaurant, in the modern wine bar or on the terrace that adjoins the two. There, you will be served seasonal and Mediterranean-influenced classic dishes, accompanied exclusively by regional wines. There are also guestrooms for a pleasant overnight stay.

Name: Park-Restaurant Vogelherd
Description: Quality restaurant in a former manor house famous for its good seasonal cuisine. You can also dine on the attractive terrace alongside a small pond.

Name: Brunnenstuben
Description: Don’t be put off by the somewhat unprepossessing exterior at Brunnenstuben because the food is excellent! Petra and Thorsten Beyer – she running the kitchen, he managing the friendly and professional front-of-house team – serve flavoursome Swabian fare including an excellent Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions).

Name: Johanniter-Kreuz
Description: This former farmhouse, which is over 350 years old, has been turned into the lovely Johanniter-Kreuz Romantik Hotel, complete with a tasteful, rustic-style restaurant in what was once the stable. Old beams and a central fireplace lend the space a cosy atmosphere. The food is rooted in classical culinary tradition, with regional influences and close ties to the seasons. Vegetarians are also catered for, and there is a decent wine selection.

Name: Gastraum
Description: This modern extension of the attractive Villa Hügel (1914) has a sleek and elegant feel. The ceiling-to-floor windows afford an impressive view of Trier, and the terrace is a particularly sought-after spot in this regard! Savour fresh, contemporary dishes made from good-quality ingredients and washed down with regional wines. The young team in charge of serving you are charming and professional. Cosy guestrooms and a lovely relaxation suite await overnight guests.

Name: Fässle le Restaurant
Description: For years this has been a favourite in the city, drawing plenty of loyal regulars and newcomers alike. In his cosy restaurant in the Degerloch neighbourhood, Patrick Giboin presents his take on classic French cuisine both as a set menu and à la carte. Vegetarians are also well catered for, and children's menus are available, too. At lunchtime during the week, the prices are somewhat lower – the Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) is especially popular. Tables on the terrace are coveted in summer.

Name: Ambiente
Description: Few would suspect that such a stylish restaurant could be found on this rather unremarkable industrial estate. In summer, a lovely terrace adds to the appeal. The friendly proprietress provides highly attentive service while the chef-patron transforms top-quality ingredients into freshly prepared classic dishes such as venison saddle with nut crust, savoy cabbage, gnocchi and juniper jus. Three set menus are available (one of them vegetarian), and dishes may also be ordered à la carte.

Name: Dorfstube
Description: It's no wonder people that love to eat here! In addition to its fine dining restaurant, Hotel Hirsch has its Dorfstube, which is a great option for fans of Swabian cuisine. In the cosy old dining space, completely done out in wood, you can tuck into specialities such as tripe, maultaschen and Zwiebelrostbraten (roast beef with onions). Vegetarian options are also on the menu. The delicious dishes are all made using regional produce. Friendly service. We highly recommend staying overnight. The guestrooms are really lovely and inviting.

Name: BECKER'S
Description: In keeping with the architecturally interesting design hotel of the same name, a high-quality fine dining restaurant done out in a chic, minimalist style awaits you here. The interior boasts leather shell chairs, elegant hardwood floors and grey panelling on the walls – a lovely setting in which to enjoy a modern menu made with selected ingredients, to the sound of contemporary background music. Choose between the four- to six-course variants. Incidentally, chef-patron Wolfgang Becker is not only a cook, but also has a penchant for fine wines. He trained as a winemaker and the wine list features wines from his own vineyard, which he and his wife Christine run – the fifth generation of the family to do so.

Name: Uwe & Uli - Zuhause bei uns
Description: A listed building standing directly on the market square, the 17C Liefrink House has an appealing exterior. Behind the pretty half-timbered façade is a charming, modern restaurant (formerly “essWebers - Küche am Markt” but now with a new name) which serves seasonal, international cuisine. The chef's set menu is complemented by a number of à-la-carte options.

Name: Seehalde
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Run by the Gruler brothers, this restaurant boasts a stunning lakeside location – tables on the terrace are much coveted in summer! The fresh and ambitious cuisine is also a major draw. The menu takes its cue from the region and the seasons with a classic bent. Fish from Lake Constance is also served and is even the focus of a three- or four-course set menu for two people. There is also a set menu based on regional classics. Alternatively, take your pick from the appealing à la carte selection. The well-curated wine list includes some gems, too. Well-drilled front-of house team. Tip: Take some homemade bouillabaisse in a jar with you to enjoy at home. There are well-kept guestrooms as well - most of them look out to the lake.

Name: Zur Tanne
Description: The setting could not be more charming: a gorgeous centuries-old Black Forest house with a cosy, rustic-looking interior. As for the food, top-notch seasonal ingredients from the region and the seasons go into flavoursome dishes. Attentive service. The well-kept guestrooms don't have TV, but in this idyllic village setting, you'd rather enjoy the peace and quiet anyway!

Name: Zur Linde
Description: The Trautwein brothers run this former coaching inn with great dedication. Some 300 years old, it features a charming blend of historical and modern decor. The menu includes Swabian classics such as Gaisburger Marsch (traditional beef stew), Maultaschen and Zwiebelrostbraten (beef and onions in gravy), alongside seasonal dishes such as pink-roasted lamb rump with beans done two ways and polenta with herbs, as well as vegetarian options. A lovely leafy terrace lies to the rear of the building. A rustic vaulted cellar can be booked for private functions. Tip: The shop sells soups, sauces, Maultaschen and spaetzle to take away.

Name: Bootshaus
Description: The beachside location is simply idyllic – you can't get much closer to the Baltic Sea! In this restaurant at the Weissenhaus Private Nature Luxury Resort, diners are shown to their tables in a modern interior with a glazed façade that affords fantastic views. But it is of course the terrace that is the top attraction! The food is a fresh blend of Mediterranean fare – somewhat simpler at lunchtime, more sophisticated in the evening, from classic dishes to elegant culinary compositions. Service runs from 12:00 to 17:00, and in the evening (by reservation) from 18:00 to 21:30.

Name: Meister Lampe
Description: It's a real pleasure to eat here, and there's a good reason for that: chef-patron Daniel Stübler clearly puts his heart and soul into running his cosy little restaurant. He cooks up excellent regional and international dishes, and also does the serving himself – not only is he highly accomplished at what he does, he is also an extremely cordial host and single-handedly creates a fantastic atmosphere! The carefully curated wine list is also remarkable, featuring wines from Baden-Württemberg, Baden and the Palatinate only.

Name: Zum Hirsch
Description: Familiar faces in the region, Markus and Britta Nagy are known as ambitious restaurateurs. Here, in their charming half-timbered inn dating back to 1688, they serve regional and Mediterranean-inspired fare. In addition to an à la carte menu, there is a three- to five-course set menu in the evening and the reasonably priced three-course "Eat & Talk" set menu at lunchtime (Tue-Fri). On Friday and Saturday, for dinner, diners choose between two set menus (no à la carte). In winter, the room with a fireplace is cosy; in summer, the lovely terrace beckons. Well-kept overnight accommodation available.

Name: Villa Hammerschmiede
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a charming villa dating back to 1893, this is a thoroughly inviting destination. Whether seated in one of the comfortable dining areas or the light and airy pavilion, you can look forward to ambitious, classic and regional cuisine, presented in the appealing "Villa Lunch" set menu or in the evening the three- to five-course "Feinschmecker-Menü". There is also an à la carte selection featuring dishes such as farm-raised duck with red cabbage and creamed chestnuts, or Dover sole for two. The terrace is especially lovely in summer, and comfortable accommodation is available as well.

Name: goldener Adler
Description: Everyone would love to have a cosy and buzzing restaurant like this in their neighbourhood! The contemporary decor strikes a rustic note; the traditional regional cuisine is based on fresh produce. The menu ranges from classics such as cordon bleu with potato salad to internationally inspired dishes such as pan-fried prawns with shellfish noodles. Vegetarian options are also available. The beautiful large terrace (you can park here in winter) is a stand-out feature in this city-centre location.

Name: Krietsch
Description: This centuries-old establishment has a rich and eventful past, having functioned at various times as an arms factory, an orphanage, a prison and finally the restaurant Fuggerei. Today, as Krietsch, it serves seasonal, regional cuisine, but it also draws on international influences. As well as flavoursome dishes à la carte, such as Black Angus Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast) with bread dumplings and Brussels sprouts with bacon, a six-course set menu is available on Thu-Sat evenings (with 48hr notice). At lunchtime, a daily set menu is served. The interior boasts a soaring period vaulted ceiling, and there is a gorgeous terrace outside. Tip: Take the opportunity to visit the minster right behind the restaurant.

Name: Der Engel
Description: The perfect example of a traditional Baden inn! This family-run establishment has been welcoming guests since 1764, offering a consistently enjoyable experience. Behind its old half-timbered walls, there are charming dining areas – some more traditional, others more modern. In a warm and welcoming atmosphere, diners tuck into delicious regional fare. Options include classic dishes, daily specials and set menus. Tip: There is a fantastic selection of digestifs. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: Gourmetfabrik
Description: This restaurant boasts a gorgeous location at Lake Schwerin. Inside, the atmosphere is pleasingly laid back; the decor is modern, and you can see into the open kitchen. Out on the terrace you can take in the view of the small harbour. The reasonably priced daily set menu, served at lunchtime, is a hit. In the evening, you can choose from a good variety of dishes, including steaks listed on the specials board. Only the finest regional and seasonal ingredients are used. Tip: They also hold cookery classes.

Name: Die Alte Brauerei
Description: This establishment started out in 1877 as Becker-Brauerei and the interior decor incorporates a combination of historical, rustic and modern elements. In today's iteration of the restaurant, Florian Dauphin, son of the friendly owners, Eric and Isabelle Dauphin, heads up the kitchen team. Lorena-Jil, his charming wife, manages the service with professionalism, care and attention. You will be treated to seasonally influenced French dishes – choose à la carte or go for one of the set menus: the four-course "Découverte" or six-course "Signature". During the week, they propose a reasonably priced lunch deal. The restaurant is accessed via the courtyard. The terrace is lovely. It is also possible to stay overnight in one of the six guestrooms, each individually designed by artist Margret Lafontaine.

Name: Hermannshof
Description: Temporarily closed.This is the second restaurant of the tasteful BollAnts Spa im Park hotel. Like the first, it has a fine vaulted ceiling and an exceptionally beautiful interior done out in an attractive vintage look. The terrace in the courtyard is also inviting. Mediterranean cuisine with regional influences is served in two set menus that change daily and with courses that can be mixed and matched.

Name: Kings and Queens
Description: This small restaurant has plenty of regulars, who are drawn by the modern and elegant decor, the friendly and professional service and the seasonal international cuisine. A choice of three menus, one of which is vegetarian, is proposed. You can also swap out courses or order à la carte. The wine list is sure to please, with an especially well-curated selection of labels from the region.

Name: Weinstube am Brühl
Description: These former stables have been converted into a delightful restaurant, in which terracotta tiles, warm colours and an old brick ceiling lend a real country feel. The international cuisine on offer follows the seasons closely. The six-course "Weinstuben-Menü" (with vegan/vegetarian alternatives) comes with optional wine pairings. À la carte dining is also possible. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and adept front-of-house team. Tip: Summer barbecue evenings (Jun-Aug) – booking recommended. Charming and elegant guestrooms are available in the Hotel Am Brühl.

Name: Schlossanger Alp
Description: Set against the backdrop of the Allgäu Alps, this hotel has tasteful, comfortable guestrooms and a lovely, inviting restaurant in which cosy Alpine vibes meet elegant table settings. Affording stunning views, the terrace is a wonderful spot for a meal in summer! The menu is varied: at lunchtime (from 1pm) there is a three-course set menu and à la carte dishes, including "small bites to share"; in the evening the selection includes their "Signature Menu", as well as dishes ranging from braised vegetable ravioli to lobster, and venison loin to Gröstl (pan-fried potatoes). The extensive wine list encompasses a fine selection.

Name: Hoppe's
Description: The atmosphere is welcoming and lively, and the food is great – it's no wonder that people come back again and again. The menu features dishes from Alsace and Baden, with mouthwatering options such as "coq au vin à la chef", beef sirloin served with roasted onions and spaetzle, or Baden-style pike dumplings. They also do Flammkuchen. There is outdoor seating to the front of the building.

Name: Weingut
Description: After a stroll through the city, how about dinner at a chic restaurant with a trendy modern decor? There are plenty of options to choose from here at Weingut, including house specialities, steaks, plus a selection of dishes that changes every week (see the "Wochenkarte"). Alternatively, you could simply opt for tapas or a glass of wine – you can also buy bottles to take home. The service is very friendly and attentive. Decorative wine racks and high tables contribute to the pleasant wine bar atmosphere of the place. There are two reservation times: 17:30 - 20:00 and from 20:15.

Name: Fährhütte 14
Description: This restaurant, an offshoot of Überfahrt, enjoys an idyllic lakeside location. The modern decor has a touch of rustic maritime flair while the service is friendly and accomplished. International and seasonal dishes. You will also have the opportunity to rent a deckchair on the beach! N.B. the restaurant is not accessible by car – getting there involves a 300m walk.

Name: La Bouche et El Pato
Description: This bistro with a pleasant, cosy atmosphere is located in the middle of the city – the cathedral is just a stone's throw away. La Bouche is on the ground floor and El Pato is on the first floor, but diners enjoy the same international and Mediterranean dishes on both levels. One speciality is beef bourguignon with French Charolais beef. In addition to à la carte dishes, there are two set menus, one of which has dishes for sharing, tapas-style. Cordial service. The terrace in the pedestrian zone is also appealing.

Name: Kugelmühle
Description: Max Matreux has been at the helm of this minimalist-style restaurant in the side wing of a factory since 2001. He is a strong advocate for sustainability, as is apparent in his classic cuisine, which features seasonal and regional ingredients. A three- to five-course set menu is proposed, as well as an à la carte selection. Tip: Ask about the "Bib Gourmand" set menu. Friendly and well-trained waitstaff.

Name: Heldmann & Herzhaft
Description: Originally the home of an industrialist, this smart 19C villa now houses this splendid restaurant, with its high ceilings, fine parquet flooring and elegant table settings – the perfect setting to enjoy Ulrich Heldmann's ambitious cuisine. Whether you opt for the seasonal set menu or order à la carte, you will be served meticulously prepared, flavoursome dishes made with fresh ingredients. The terrace is of course the place to go in summer. Wednesdays and Thursdays also open at lunchtime.

Name: Gastwirtschaft Ferdinand Reuter
Description: This traditional family-run establishment serves good-quality regional cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons. Classic fare and more sophisticated dishes both feature on the menu. The atmosphere is friendly and cosy – in the more modern section, diners take their seats at long wooden tables. Hotel Reuter, which houses this restaurant, has comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Adler
Description: The atmosphere in this historical inn is cosy and rustic. The cordial and welcoming service staff is led by the charming Styrian manager, who herself is a fantastic host! In the kitchen, a father-and-son team prepares flavoursome dishes using high-quality ingredients. The menu is divided into two sections: classic Swabian dishes such as Kutteln in Lemberger (a tripe speciality) or house-made maultaschen, and sophisticated dishes like Japanese ramen soup or Breton monkfish with cauliflower and almond puree. An old jukebox provides the background music. Tip: The restaurant produces its own range of schnapps.

Name: Kraftwerk
Description: This restaurant housed in a converted power station is more than a stylish location – it also serves extremely good food. The cuisine combines classic, Mediterranean and Austrian influences, including appetising dishes such as lobster with truffle sauce, beef fillet Rossini; the "Austrian classics" section on the menu features the likes of "Bertl's Kalbsfleischpflanzerl mit Kartoffel-Rahmgurkensalat" (veal patties with potato salad in a creamy cucumber sauce). In addition to à la carte dishes, there are two set menus: "Kraftwerk Classics" and "Kraftwerk Finest". The international wine list is comprehensive. In summer, tables are set up on the terrace. Friendly, attentive and professional service.

Name: Ondersch Genusswirtschaft
Description: Going by the name "Ondersch" (a dialect word meaning different), this establishment located in the multipurpose "LOFT" building offers a cinema, a street-food bar and a gourmet restaurant. On the upper floor, a lively, urban atmosphere provides the setting for tasty modern cuisine made from seasonal and regional produce.

Name: Alpenkönig - Esslust
Description: Diners take their seats in a lovely, upscale dining space comprising areas that range in style from traditional charm to modern chic. A cordial and professional front-of-house team serves fresh regional cuisine that draws on the seasons and Mediterranean influences. You can go à la carte or choose dishes for the three or four courses of your own set menu. There is also an appealing wine list. The restaurant is located in the attractive Alpenkönig hotel, which has inviting guestrooms and modern wellness facilities, set in the gorgeous Allgäu landscape.

Name: Würzhaus
Description: This really is an appealing restaurant. At lunchtime, things are toned down a little, with reasonably priced options (à la carte or a small set menu). In the evening, there is an ambitious set menu that comes in four to six flavourful courses. Head chef Diana Burkel is committed to using locally sourced ingredients. The dedication to sustainability extends to the wine selection – the list is dominated by organic, biodynamic and natural wines. The service is friendly and attentive, and the atmosphere is welcoming.

Name: Villa Medici
Description: This spruce villa enjoys a delightful location in a quiet residential area on the outskirts of the city. Diners here are pampered with friendly service, Mediterranean flavours and Italian wines in a chic and inviting atmosphere. In addition to à la carte options, there are daily specials and a tasting menu. A charming terrace is laid out to the side. Plus, there are five attractive guestrooms.

Name: von Rhemen
Description: The restaurant at the stylish Schloss Wilkinghege hotel features an elegant and lofty dining room with an ornate stucco ceiling and bags of historical charm. The cuisine is classic and very seasonal – order à la carte or opt for one of the set menus. The selection varies slightly depending on the day of the week. Service is friendly and adept. Given the grand setting, guests are often tempted to book a room for the night.

Name: LENZ
Description: Lenz Leslie Himmelheber pours his heart and soul into his cheerful, modern restaurant and his style of hosting has a distinctive personal touch. In season, the self-proclaimed "duckman" carves his signature Vierlande duck at your table. The menu also includes regional, seasonal and cosmopolitan cuisine with dishes such as salmon tartare with ponzu beurre noisette, pear and avocado, or "Wiener schnitzel deluxe" with cucumber salad, truffle chips and truffle mayonnaise. A separate lunch menu featuring simpler and more affordable dishes is another highlight. The food is complemented by an appealing wine list, service is attentive, and the bright conservatory can be opened up in summer!

Name: Fischereihafen Restaurant
Description: This is and remains an institution – something of a home from home for Hamburg's fish lovers, young and old! A constant stream of international customers comes and goes from lunchtime to evening. In an elegant setting boasting traditional Hanseatic decor and a view of the harbour, quality fish from the fish market is served at the height of freshness. Classic dishes include turbot or lobster in different variations, but the menu also includes Asian and Mediterranean-influenced options.

Name: Henriks
Description: Some ambitious cooking goes on in this elegantly designed restaurant, where the menu includes Asian, Mediterranean and regional cuisine with dishes ranging from Wiener Schnitzel to lobster. There’s a good selection of wines to accompany the food, plus a popular spacious terrace and lounge.

Name: Bahnhöfle
Description: Run by Thierry and Elisabeth Falconnier, this charming restaurant is a real institution in the Freiburg area. Set in a little house by Gundelfingen's railway station, the place has a cheerful, easygoing feel. Inside, watercolours by the owners' daughter adorn the walls; outside, the cosy terrace is lovely in summer. True to his roots, the chef-patron serves up French cuisine – pleasingly pared down, brimming with flavour and made from excellent ingredients. Fish is the speciality here: think salmon carpaccio, monkfish with porcini or grilled sea bass. Meat lovers are also well catered for, with highlights such as Ibérico pork chop or braised beef cheeks.

Name: Farmerhaus
Description: African produce enriches the cuisine, which is international in character. Wood carvings and trophies from the country where the dishes originated are interesting to look at.

Name: Die Reichsstadt
Description: This is the restaurant of the chic hotel of the same name, which provides the historical backdrop for your meal. The tasteful dining area is done out with high-end furnishings and a modern eye. Staff are friendly and professional as they set about serving you fine Baden classics, modernised French dishes, which you can choose à la carte or combine into a set menu – a vegetarian version is also available. The "Taste Menu" comprising six or seven small courses is also an excellent recommendation. In summer, the garden is magical!

Name: Zum Rössl
Description: This long-standing family-run establishment is housed in a former coaching inn dating back to 1642. In the charming, traditionally styled restaurant, you can choose between regional classics and seasonal dishes, some with a Mediterranean twist. Menu highlights include boiled beef brisket with sweet-and-sour fruits, horseradish sauce and potatoes, or French bouillabaisse with toasted bread and rouille sauce. A surprise menu can also be pre-ordered. The lunch options are particularly appealing. Tip: In good weather, make a beeline for the idyllic terrace!

Name: Kinfelts Kitchen & Wine
Description: Located near the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, this restaurant embodies the quintessential HafenCity style. The interior is simple yet chic; the large windows allow natural light to stream into the space and afford compelling views of the Elbe canal. Kirill Kinfelt, who made his reputation at Trüffelschwein, serves up classically rooted contemporary cuisine made from top-notch ingredients, eg king prawn with buttermilk, chilli and Thai basil, or monkfish with fregola sarda, radish and herbs. An outstanding selection of international wines and expert recommendations. For dinner reservations, choose between two seatings.

Name: EssensArt
Description: This restaurant in a residential area has made a name for itself with its seasonal and internationally influenced cuisine. Since 2010, the cordial hosts have been committed to their guests' happiness. Delicious dishes are available in the form of two set menus – one of which is vegetarian – or à la carte. Friendly atmosphere; a nice covered terrace outside.

Name: Alter Wirt
Description: This inn has a long-standing tradition of hospitality. A relaxed atmosphere reigns in the delightful interior, which combines modern elements with rustic charm. Outside, the lovely terrace is shaded by chestnut trees. With an emphasis on organic and locally sourced ingredients, the menu features regional fare and takes its cue from the seasons. Daily specials are also available. For overnight stays, there are well-appointed guestrooms furnished with natural materials and designed with sustainability in mind.

Name: Brasserie
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: If you don’t fancy the gourmet cuisine on offer at Meierei, you can enjoy fresh, international fare or just a slice of home-made cake in the less formal atmosphere of the Brasserie.

Name: Cox
Description: With its charmingly laid-back feel, this place is everything a bistro should be and, unsurprisingly, draws a diverse crowd. Diners appreciate both the thoughtfully curated, internationally inspired menu and the amiable, attentive staff, who help create the welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Witwenball
Description: What makes this deluxe bistro in Hamburg's bustling Schanzenviertel so beloved? A perfect blend of cuisine, service and atmosphere. Once a dance hall, this place now exudes a laid-back yet lively energy, and feels at once trendy and chic with its decorative wine racks – the white marble counter in the middle of the space is a striking feature. The delicious contemporary food incorporates regional, seasonal, and international influences. Order à la carte or compile your own four-course "Your Choice" set menu, with a fish, a meat or vegetarian option for the main course. Wiener schnitzel is also always available on Sundays. The impressive wine list comprises over 500 items, and the staff provide expert guidance. Alternatively, you could have a cocktail. Lovely pavement terrace.

Name: Zum Goldenen Engel
Description: This traditional 16C inn right next to the church has been rebuilt in a way that is absolutely true to the original. You will feel completely at home in the lovingly decorated restaurant, thanks not only to the atmosphere and the competent, charming front-of-house team, but also of course to the high-quality food. Many ingredients come from the region. Plus they have cosy guestrooms.

Name: Villa Busch
Description: This beautiful, lavishly refurbished villa in an elevated location not only boasts a lovely terrace for summer, but the interior of the restaurant is also tasteful with its stuccoed ceilings, wooden floorboards and modern designer chairs. The chef-patron's kitchen team creates dishes with Mediterranean and Asian influences, including many fish specialities. Plus, you are waited on by a warm and charming front-of-house team.

Name: Brook
Description: International, German and classical influences are at play here, e.g. loin of lamb with string beans and Parmesan potatoes or venison with Brussels sprouts and chestnuts. In the evening, the beautifully illuminated Speicherstadt opposite is a sight to behold!

Name: Schneider Stube
Description: Hotel Tuchmacher, ensconced in a pretty Renaissance town house with this delightfully cosy restaurant, is an institution here in Görlitz. The classic regional menu includes dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, stewed rabbit leg on Leipziger Allerlei vegetables, and stewed brook trout roll on pickled vegetables. Almost all of the wines are also available by the glass. In summer, the courtyard with its terrace is absolutely idyllic! "Bleicherstube" and "Zunftsaal" are their attractive salons. The location in the heart of the old town is charming – it is next to the church (Pfarrkirche St Peter and Paul) and not far from the Lausatian Neiße River that borders Germany, Poland and the Czech Republic.

Name: Frankfurter Botschaft
Address: Westhafenplatz 6, Frankfurt on the Main, 60327, Germany
Description: A really cool location - the spot directly on the Westhafen makes the terrace a real highlight! But it's also pleasant to sit in the smartly decorated interior; windows on all sides mean you also have a view of the water from here. The food is international. Furthermore, they also offer valet parking - it's best to put in your request when you make your reservation.

Name: Zöllner's Weinstube
Description: Surrounded by splendid gardens, this 18C half-timbered sandstone building is as charming on the outside as it is on the inside. Sitting beneath a striking vaulted ceiling, diners can enjoy regional as well as Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made from first-rate produce. There is also an excellent selection of Franconian wines. In summer, the terrace is a must!

Name: SonneStuben
Description: The regional and seasonal cuisine served here wins diners over with the flavours it exudes and its technical prowess. Examples include fillet of regional salmon trout, pak choi, saffron sauce, and braised ragout of local venison, creamed kohlrabi, fried mushrooms. In "Sonne Sharing Style" (for four or more people), the chefs put together a selection of dishes for diners to share. The pretty, cosy dining area affords views of the old town's historical half-timbered façades; having your meal out on the terrace that overlooks Marktplatz is a pleasant option. They are also open for lunch. Tip: It is worthwhile taking a stroll through the town. You can spend the night at Die Sonne Frankenberg hotel.

Name: Mühlenhof
Description: It is little wonder that Anette and Stefan Rottler's hotel is so popular: Their restaurant serves classic Baden dishes made with top-quality ingredients – from snail soup to pork fillet in cream of mushroom sauce to Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy). The smaller dishes and reasonably priced set menu of the day are also much in demand. The wine list is dedicated to local labels. Friendly and attentive service. Food is served in various dining rooms, some with a cosy, regional feel, others with a fresh and modern look. Delightful covered terrace.

Name: Medici
Address: Weißadlergasse 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description: Two brothers are your hosts in this city centre restaurant. International dishes with a Mediterranean influence are served in a modern atmosphere.

Name: Bistro Villa Merton
Address: Am Leonhardsbrunn 12, Frankfurt on the Main, 60487, Germany
Description: Located just outside Frankfurt, north of the Palmengarten, Bistro Villa Merton is a lovely alternative to the fine dining restaurant. While the latter welcomes diners in the evening, the bistro is only open at lunchtime. In the spruce villa built in neo-Baroque style, you can take a seat in an inviting decor done out with an elegant touch to enjoy high-quality regional and international cuisine infused with seasonal influences. An appealing lunchtime set menu is on offer, as well as several à la carte options. The appetising dishes include breast and leg of guinea fowl and classics such as Wiener schnitzel made with veal. Excellent wine recommendations are to be had from the friendly and knowledgeable front-of-house team. Tip: There is a fantastic selection of champagnes. The terrace is also a pleasant place to sit. Good to know: Regular events are also held here.

Name: Brasserie Stadthaus
Description: This attractive brasserie with its striking high coffered ceiling and pretty interior courtyard promises a genuine French dining experience. Try the tourte de queue de boeuf (oxtail pie) or the seafood platter followed by the tarte au citron. All the wines are French.

Name: The Duchy
Description: On the first floor of the luxurious Breidenbacher Hof, overlooking Heinrich-Heine-Allee, this is an elegant brasserie. The cuisine is a broad mix, from sashimi and ceviche to beef tartare or ravioli, not to mention the steaks. They set great store by the origin of their ingredients, working with regional producers – and they keep their own chickens and cows. Decent wine selection.

Name: Butcher's american steakhouse
Description: At Butcher's american steakhouse you can enjoy fine Nebraska beef that the chef presents to the table personally. The cosy restaurant is dominated by dark wood and warm colours.

Name: Adler Wirtschaft
Description: Established in 1993, Franz Keller's family-run Adler Wirtschaft is an institution in the region. Inside this charming little half-timbered house, the atmosphere is cosy and down-to-earth – traditional tavern culture is still alive and well here. Even from the entrance, diners can catch a glimpse of the Molteni stove, on which the flavoursome dishes are prepared. The concept: you choose dishes to make up your own fixed-price menu – opt for "Das kleine Abendessen" ("The Small Dinner") or "Das große Abendessen" ("The Large Dinner"). The steak selection is tempting as well. Good to know: They use pork from Bentheim Black Pied pigs and beef from Charolais and Limousin pasture-raised cattle, sourced from their own farm in the Taunus region (Falkenhof). In summer, there is a lovely terrace with shade sails behind the building. N.B. Bill for the whole table only.

Name: Saittavini
Description: Combining a bistro, wine bar and delicatessen, this friendly restaurant serves Italian food (including a lovely small antipasto counter). They also sell over a 1 000 different wines in the wine shop and a range of Italian specialities in the delicatessen.

Name: Restaurant Baiken by Schröer
Description: Set amid the vines, and with a magnificent view of the vineyards and Eltville, the location is truly magical. In summer, the terrace is of course very popular. This restaurant run by Dirk Schröer and Amila Begic-Schröer is part of the Kloster Eberbach wine estate on the Rauenthaler Baiken. The chef adheres to a strictly classical and fuss-free style of cooking, showcasing outstanding, impeccably fresh ingredients, as in the saddle of venison in a bread crust with wild mushrooms, apricot and pointed cabbage. You can order à la carte or choose from different set menus, for example, the enticing and reasonably priced three-course "Afterwork Menu" (including wine and water) on Mon, Thu and Fri. The wine list is dominated by the Hessische Staatsweingüter wine estates. The decor is tastefully understated and attentive service comes courtesy of a front-of-house team who are friendly, professional and always on hand – pleasant atmosphere guaranteed.

Name: Mon Amie Maxi
Address: Bockenheimer Landstraße 31, Frankfurt on the Main, 60325, Germany
Description: Housed in a villa dating from 1925, this restaurant is chic, almost opulent – the wonderfully lively atmosphere is complemented by friendly, attentive and adept service. To the side is Raw Bar, and there is an open kitchen. The menu features French cuisine, including oysters, lobster cocktail, offal dishes and high-quality barbecued steak. Good, exclusive wine selection.

Name: Gasthaus Landbrecht
Description: Set in the tranquil hamlet of Haindlfing, this family-run country inn has been in operation for more than 100 years and is now helmed by fifth-generation chef-patron Maximilian Landbrecht. Dedicated to working with select regional ingredients, often sourced from organic producers, he presents flavoursome, meticulously prepared dishes that celebrate local produce with occasional Mediterranean accents. Notable examples include Ampertal beef broth with toasted farmhouse bread and brown onion, and pan-seared Freising brook trout with herb butter, a vegetable medley and sautéed potatoes. Both the Gaststube and the more elegant Esszimmer (dining room), which features a lovely tiled stove, provide a cosy setting; in summer, the terrace beckons. A bright ballroom and the rustic Wirts Chalet can be booked for private functions. Smart modern apartments available for overnight stays.

Name: Eiflers Zeiten
Description: The pleasant, rustic-style alternative to Bembergs Häuschen has a distinctly cosy feel. The menu features mouthwatering regional classics such as roast Eifel beef with roast potatoes, as well as internationally influenced dishes such as cod with a lemon crunch topping and Chinese cabbage. There are also daily changing specials. The two chandeliers fashioned from bottles are sure to draw the eye! The view through the windowed façade onto the pond is also lovely.

Name: Landhaus am See
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A pleasant dining experience: a lovely country-style interior, great terrace and views of the garden and lake. The food is seasonal and regional. You can also get hold of your own copy of their recipe book. For overnight guests, there are really pretty, individually decorated rooms available.

Name: WEINreich
Description: A modern wine bar in a tranquil little village. The historical setting has been given a makeover including attractive decorative touches; to complement the numerous wine bottles on display, the ceiling is adorned with a depiction of the wine route marked with its famous wine villages. Outside, there is a charming courtyard terrace. Led by Jeanette and Henning Weinheimer, the very friendly and proficient team go about their work with great dedication, serving high-quality regional and seasonal cuisine – as a set menu or à la carte. Meat-eaters should ask about their "Steak Weeks"; Sunday roast is available if pre-ordered. You can also purchase their bread, which they bake on site. For overnight stays there are really pleasant guestrooms.

Name: Schmidt's
Description: This restaurant is housed in the Hellerauer Werkstätten für Handwerkskunst (a workshop founded in 1909 by Karl Schmidt). Served in a modern bistro atmosphere, the classically based food has seasonal and regional influences, and is made with carefully selected ingredients, which are prepared for maximum flavour and minimum fuss. Having difficulty deciding? Then go for the surprise menu ("Schmidt's Karte rauf und runter"). The affordable lunch deal goes down a treat, and the terrace is also lovely.

Name: Köllner's Landhaus
Description: Set in grounds covering 11 000m² this charming half-timbered house dating from 1589 is a picture-book property with a country house-style interior that certainly does it justice. Then there is the excellent regional and international cuisine. You might also choose to spend the night in one of the comfortable and modern guestrooms.

Name: St. Urban
Description: Along with the fine dining restaurant Schwarzer Hahn, St. Urban is part of the appealing culinary microcosm of the lovely Deidesheimer Hof hotel, which is located right on the historical market square. The cosy interior exudes the traditional charm of a Palatinate inn. Good regional and seasonal cuisine is served, à la carte or as a set menu. The menu also includes the classic "Palatinate Favourite – Saumagen (stuffed pig's stomach), Bratwurst and liver dumplings with sauerkraut and mashed potatoes".

Name: Zucker
Description: The name sort of gives it away if you have any German: This attractive modern brasserie is housed in a former sugar factory, now a listed building. Exposed red brick walls and high ceilings give the setting an appealing industrial feel. In summer, the terrace is shaded by awnings. Flavoursome seasonally inspired dishes are served à la carte, with an additional set menu available. The waitstaff are pleasantly down-to-earth, very friendly and well organised.

Name: Reussenstein
Description: Everything here is "100% Swabian". All the ingredients come from Württemberg, and the menu is entirely dedicated to regional fare. If you are ordering à la carte, you pick your main dish by its key ingredient (eg beef, game or freshwater fish) and it comes served on a special ash wood tiered platter that was custom-made for the restaurant. The glass partition means there are interesting glimpses into the kitchen, plus the service is very cordial. The vaulted cellar houses a further restaurant, Wild, where a seasonal set menu featuring game is served on Friday evenings. At dinnertime Tue-Thu, this menu is available exclusively for small groups. Their novel "Spätzle Drive-in" is open throughout the day. This long-standing family business also has cosy modern guestrooms.

Name: Krone
Description: This long-standing family business is run with real dedication. No compromises are made when it comes to the quality of the produce, and the dishes taste great! No wonder the restaurant is widely known and popular – this also means it is better to make a reservation. Tip: the very reasonably priced lunch menu.

Name: der allerKrug
Description: Here at der allerKrug with its friendly hosts Sven Hütten and Petra Tiecke-Hütten, you can look forward to carefully and skilfully prepared dishes. The dishes are based on country cuisine with international influences, plus there’s an attractive terrace to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Leopold
Description: This lavishly converted stable of the Von Winning winery (part of the Bassermann-Jordan empire) is an impressively modern and extremely popular restaurant that serves excellent food. The menu includes a selection of international and Palatinate dishes. Lovely terrace. It can also be booked as a fantastic location for events. The restaurant was named after Leopold von Winning, founder of the winery.

Name: Kucher's Weinwirtschaft
Description: The mismatched antique tables and chairs, the pretty decoration and the almost familial atmosphere lend this place a charming feel. The Swabian-style sour kidneys with sautéed potatoes have been on the menu here forever – a classic with its own loyal following. In addition, the menu includes contemporary dishes such as braised Ellscheid lemon chicken with Mediterranean vegetables. Most of the meat used by Florian Kucher and his team to create their seasonal regional fare comes from the Eifel area. Be sure to peruse the wine list – wine is a passion of senior chef Martin Kucher and he will be happy to advise you.

Name: Restaurant 1718
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At 1718, elegant period architectural elements blend beautifully with modern design. Part of Ketschauer Hof hotel, the restaurant sits across from the fine dining restaurant L.A. Jordan – separating them is a lovely terrace in the peaceful, verdant courtyard. On the menu, French and international cuisine are the order of the day, accompanied by a superb selection of wines from the Palatinate and beyond. Tip: The establishment runs a wine shop around the corner.

Name: Bergfriedel
Description: This establishment has been run by the same family with great dedication for years! The welcoming team serves delicious, fresh food that diners can enjoy as they take in the views over the Bühlertal. They follow a philosophy that is close to nature - and their own chickens in the garden fit in nicely. The wide-ranging menu includes traditional cuisine from Baden, vegetarian/vegan dishes and gourmet specialities. Add to that an extensive wine list. The chic restaurant extension is done out in a modern take on regional style. Pleasant overnight accommodation is available – the rooms and suites ("Natur-Zimmer" and "Natur-Suiten") are done out in locally sourced materials and are contemporary in their design.

Name: Schapers
Description: A family-run place where you will be treated to friendly and cordial service. As for the food, you can look forward to ambitious classic cuisine brimming with regional influences. Choose from the à la carte offering or the set menus drawn from it, which include a vegetarian set menu. The terrace is lovely. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are comfortable and convenient guestrooms available, distributed over two buildings.

Name: Berchtesgadener Esszimmer
Description: This long-established inn run by Maximilian and Roxana Kühbeck with great dedication has bags of character. As the charming couple work alone, service can occasionally take a little longer, but this only enhances the pleasingly warm atmosphere. Their seasonal dishes are made with carefully selected ingredients from the immediate area – herbs, for instance, are foraged, or harvested from their own organic garden. There are two set menus, one of which is vegetarian, plus an à la carte selection. In addition to the cosy little dining space with its vaulted ceiling, there are two very popular "Kitchen Tables" for those who wish to see the chefs at work.

Name: Behl's Restaurant
Description: The dedication of the Behl family is palpable whether you're staying in their Genusshotel with its cheerful and cosy guestrooms or dining in the restaurant, complete with charming shaded courtyard terrace. You can look forward to a welcoming atmosphere and delicious dishes made with locally sourced produce such as Blankenbach brook trout or Spessart pasture-raised beef. They also host regular Brennabende ("spirit evenings") in the distillery, including a set menu with spirit pairings and a demonstration.

Name: Stubersheimer Hof
Description: The tasteful decor of this lovingly restored old farmhouse exudes rural charm. In the pleasant dining area with its attractive wooden flooring, diners are treated to a friendly welcome and delicious regional fare prepared by the junior chef. In summer, there's no better place to dine than in the charming courtyard. And if you're looking for a place to stay overnight, the family-run business also has lovely guestrooms available.

Name: Forellenhof
Description: The diversity of the Bareiss culinary empire knows no bounds! The historic and idyllically located Forellenhof has been transformed into a charming restaurant open to all-comers from 11:30 am to 5: 30 pm, Fridays from 11:30 am. to 10 pm. The emphasis here is on freshwater fish – from their own fish farm – but they also serve snacks. Tip: you can buy fresh fish in the Forellenlädle (9am-noon).

Name: GRACE
Description: "The place to be" in Berlin! A really appealing and stylish restaurant that oozes glamour and counts Hollywood stars among its patrons. Dishes with Asian-Californian and European flavours are served. A must: after the meal, a cocktail in the rooftop bar lounge! The restaurant is located in the tasteful, high-quality designed "Hotel Zoo" in a great location directly on Kurfürstendamm.

Name: INDIA CLUB
Description: Authentic Indian cuisine is to be found in Berlin! At India Club, the self-styled "rustic cuisine" with its roots in North India includes delicious curries and original tandoori dishes, as well as numerous vegetarian and vegan options. In addition to the appealing à la carte menu, the three-course surprise menu is highly recommended, as it gives a good overview of this style of cuisine. Many ingredients are sourced from the restaurant's own organic farm (Gut Vorder Bollhagen) on the Baltic Sea. With its mahogany furniture, dark wood panelling, bright colours and traditional patterns, the elegant interior has an almost festive atmosphere and exudes Indian flair. The restaurant is located not far from the Brandenburg Gate, at the rear of the exclusive Hotel Adlon.

Name: Rolin
Description: Elegant ambience, friendly service, tasty and ambitious international, classic and seasonal cuisine – on the menu e. g. fillet of North Sea cod with a horseradish, honey and rosemary crust. Incidentally, "Rolin" is the name of a ship's captain. Hotel Cap Polonio has well-kept rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Beesten
Description: Since 1906, over four generations, the Beesten family has put its heart and soul into running this traditional inn in the heart of Rheine. The owner himself is at the helm in the kitchen, preparing classic French and German cuisine peppered with seasonal influences. The interior is elegant and tasteful, while the service is charming. Take a seat on the terrace under the lovely old chestnut trees.

Name: Koch und Kellner
Description: A cornerstone of the Nuremberg fine dining scene. The set menu, written up on a large board, comprises nine courses, but for those with a smaller appetite, it can also be shortened. The dishes are crafted from carefully selected ingredients and are quite aptly described as "modernised classics". Besides the chef, owner and waiter Frank Mackert is always on hand with his inimitable Franconian charm. Thanks to his extensive wine expertise, he can confidently guide you through the 500-label list. Clear lines, a warm colour palette and parquet flooring make for a lovely setting. By reservation only: Mon-Sat lunchtime (11.30am-2.30pm).

Name: Alte Mühle
Description: This friendly, well-run restaurant with its appealingly pared-back style adjoins the historical building of a grain mill, which has been converted into guest accommodation. Service is provided by attentive and professional staff, as you tuck into Mediterranean, regional and seasonal cuisine. In addition to à la carte dishes, a set menu is also available.

Name: Stumpenhof
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: It's impossible not to feel comfortable when you're in such good hands! The service in this long-standing family business is exceptionally friendly, and the owner herself always has a smile and a friendly word for her guests. The menu has something for everyone, from affordable lunch set menus and daily specials to traditional regional dishes and light bites. Lovely terrace.

Name: Lumperhof
Description: This family-run inn is a lovely spot in the countryside and has a charming terrace shaded by a majestic old lime tree. The menu is varied and full of delicious options. Made with regional and seasonal produce, the dishes draw on Mediterranean, Middle Eastern and Asian influences. Options such as the cream of sweetcorn soup with deep-fried mussels and purple curry, or the Allgäu cheese spaetzle with melted onions and a green salad are sure to whet the appetite. In the evening, you can dine à la carte or opt for a set menu comprising three or five courses. Cash payments only.

Name: Culinarium
Description: This chic, pared-back restaurant with a lovely terrace area is located in the Weingut Matthias Dostert, a winery that also offers cosy guestrooms. Chef Walter Curman draws on his considerable craftsmanship to meticulously create flavoursome dishes. The classics on the menu hint at his Austrian origins – try the appetising Kaspressknödel (pressed cheese dumplings) or Alt Wiener Kaiserschmarrn (Viennese pancake)!

Name: Die Halde
Description: Situated at an altitude of 1 147m, this stylish restaurant successfully bridges the gap between history and modernity! The food is served in cosy traditional dining rooms, where guests are looked after by friendly, well-trained staff. Local produce is favoured, and the water comes from the house's mountain spring. There are also lovely guestrooms done out in a modern, regional style.

Name: freistil.
Description: In addition to an appealing modern decor featuring sleek design and warm wooden fittings, diners can look forward to a selection of regional and seasonal dishes (including vegetarian and vegan options) that can be put together to create a set menu or ordered à la carte. For overnight stays, the boutique hotel has attractive, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Sülbecker Krug
Description: Calling all steak lovers! This restaurant is known for its exceptional cuts of meat, cooked in an oven heated to 800°C. The menu features classics such as rib-eye, flank steak and tenderloin – all served on a wooden board with superb sauces. Consider ordering the delicious bao buns or duck spring rolls to start your meal. They also have a wine bar. Various promotions are offered throughout the year – don't hesitate to enquire!

Name: Gasthaus Sternen Post
Description: Since 2006, Bernd Lutz and his wife Rosemarie have been welcoming guests to their charming inn dating back to 1875. The chef-patron and his team serve up flavoursome classic seasonal dishes (eg cured salmon with pearl barley, beetroot and horseradish, or pan-fried veal sweetbreads with leaf spinach and spaetzle (a Swabian pasta speciality) made using a wealth of locally sourced produce. The appealing wine list features a well-curated selection of local vintages. Charming interior; gorgeous terrace. The service, led by the proprietress, is exceptionally friendly and attentive. For those wishing to stay overnight, cosy guestrooms and an attractive holiday apartment are available.

Name: Torkel
