Description: The Stoppel family serve not only cuisine underpinned by Mediterranean and classic influences, but also plenty of regional dishes. If you are having trouble choosing, a failsafe option is the short "Fine Dining Menü". It's also well worth perusing the wine list. Sit back and enjoy your meal in the inviting dining space or out on the pretty terrace. The hotel of the same name has lovely cosy guestrooms.

Name: Sternenschanz
Description: A fun dining experience! The Linck family - now in its fourth generation - put their heart and soul into running this delightful restaurant. Diners can look forward to friendly service and the chance to eat really well without breaking the bank. The menu focuses on Swabian fare and home-style cooking, with dishes such as Flädlesuppe (pancake soup) and creamy veal goulash. No wonder there are so many regulars! In summer, the gorgeous garden terrace beckons.

Name: Hermannshöhle
Description: Set in a former ferry house dating back to 1517, this establishment has been run by Wigbert Weck since 2007 and has a loyal following of regulars. The dishes created by the chef-patron are skillfully prepared from fresh ingredients with no unnecessary embellishments, and they are delicious! Tip: the surprise menu (only for the whole table). Complete with a glass-fronted wine refrigerator full of regional wines, the interior has the feel of a modern wine bar. Outside, the lovely terrace overlooks the Nahe River, which is just across the road. Two holiday flats can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: Postschänke
Description: With its cosy and lively atmosphere, Postschänke is a fantastic alternative to Zur Post, the fine-dining restaurant. Here, the delicious seasonal cuisine made with select, fresh ingredients goes down a treat. They serve a daily set menu with options, as well as daily specials. The service is exceedingly friendly and attentive.

Name: Spinne
Address: Eichkehle 58, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, 67433, Germany
Description: This restaurant situated on the forest's edge sticks to a simple winning formula, with a focus on regional and seasonal cuisine prepared using the finest ingredients. Perhaps you'd like to try the surprise menu? Take a seat out on the lovely terrace. Welcoming and modern guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: Hackbarth's Restaurant
Description: In the trendy, chic interior behind the red front door, a welcoming team and attentive service await you. The modern cuisine combines regional and international elements, Mediterranean and Far Eastern influences and seasonal produce. In addition to the à la carte selection, there is a five-course surprise menu. The tapas menu served on Tue and Thu is worth checking out. Nicely curated wine list. Lovely terrace. Tip: It is advisable to make a reservation for the weekend (Fri and Sat).

Name: DAS BERNHARDS
Description: The Bernhard family's centrally located restaurant is cosy in its rustic charm, attracting many regular guests who appreciate both the cordial, attentive service and the excellent food. The menu features regional and seasonal dishes alongside Swiss classics such as "Züri Gschnätzlets – veal strips, creamy mushroom sauce, cognac, authentic Swiss rösti", reflecting the family's Graubünden roots. The daily specials are especially popular at lunch. The terrace is lovely in summer.

Name: Zirbelstube
Description: The journey to this friendly family-run establishment on the outskirts of Nuremberg is well worthwhile. Set in a smart sandstone building (1860), Zirbelstube boasts an attractive main dining space and a separate room with a vaulted ceiling. They serve good regional and seasonal cuisine with classical and international influences in the form of two set menus featuring dishes you can mix and match, such as pan-fried octopus with fennel and beans, labneh and olive tapenade, or Franconian Sauerbraten (marinated pot roast), red cabbage and cranberry salad, dried fruit and bread dumplings. Delightful terrace. Attractive guestrooms.

Name: Novalis
Description: Diners can opt to eat inside, in the stylish, elegant restaurant, or outside with a view of the historical castle grounds. The seasonal food is positively packed with flavours and aromas, and made with top-notch produce – regional wherever possible – such as game that they have hunted themselves or smoked fish from Leinetal. There is also a vegetarian set menu. The service is cordial and professional. Tip: The wine list comprises a broad selection of French red wines, alongside gin, korn schnapps, vodka and whiskey from the restaurant's own Hardenberg Distillery. "Novalis" comes from an ancestor of the owners – it is the pseudonym of writer Georg Philipp Friedrich Freiherr von Hardenberg. Hardenberg BurgHotel promises an overnight stay in tasteful accommodation.

Name: Gaststube Zum Klosterbräu
Address: Kirchplatz 1, Neuburg an der Donau, 86633, Germany
Description: This is how you imagine a historical Bavarian restaurant: wooden beams on the ceiling, floorboards, tiled stove – rustic, inviting and wonderfully cosy (or "zünftig" as they say in these parts). There is also a wonderful terrace. The cuisine is classic, regional and seasonal – served à la carte or in three set menus, one of which is vegetarian. There is a good selection of wines to choose from. Tip: well-priced lunch menu with two or three courses (Tues. to Fri., except public holidays). You can also visit the Baroque Münster Heilig Kreuz in Bergen.

Name: Kaiserblick
Description: This eatery is a good alternative to the Brockel Schlimbach restaurant at Nideggen's centuries-old castle, Burg Nideggen. They serve market-based cuisine in the form of regional dishes, prepared from fresh seasonal ingredients mainly sourced from suppliers and producers in the region. The interior decor is modern and the front-of-house team is very friendly and obliging. Weather permitting, you can dine on the pretty terrace in the castle courtyard.

Name: Stüffel
Description: The riverside location right by the Isekai is every bit as appealing as the contemporary seasonal cuisine with Mediterranean and regional influences, made with choice ingredients. The menu includes, for example, Husum pasture-raised beef tartare, or poached cod with balsamic lentils, as well as classics such as beef fillet and lobster ravioli. The wine list is well chosen – the chef will be happy to guide you. You can eat in the stylish modern bistro or outside on the waterfront. There is also a wine bar in the building.

Name: Herzog von Burgund
Description: First you admire the attractive exterior of this stylish townhouse. Then, inside, the impressive, heritage-protected staircase. The two dining spaces (Erftzimmer and Gartenzimmer) form a classically elegant setting – the paintings by Düsseldorf artist Markus Tollmann draw the eye. The menu has a seasonal focus, and Wiener schnitzel is a house speciality. Friendly and experienced waitstaff. Delightful outdoor seating: The terrace is a verdant oasis in the heart of the city!

Name: Wirtshaus zur Sonne
Description: This restaurant has been in the same family for over 300 years. Diners can sit inside in the wonderful, wood-panelled dining room or outside on the pretty garden terrace to enjoy the flavoursome fare. This includes tafelspitz (boiled topside of beef) galantine with radish carpaccio or pan-fried skrei cod with tomatoes and herbs.

Name: Husar
Description: Charming dining rooms await behind the painted façade of this inn, which has stood for over 400 years. Here, diners are treated to attentive service as they tuck into classic cuisine. The dishes are packed with flavour and made with good-quality ingredients; attention is paid to seasonality, and a regional produce is given preferential treatment. Started in 1986, the Merget family business continues today, having resumed in 2004 after a brief hiatus.

Name: GRILL
Description: In this restaurant housed in Hotel Vier Jahreszeiten by Hamburg's Inner Alster lake, Caucasian walnut wood, warm colours such as olive green and pigeon blue, along with a log fire create an elegant yet cosy setting that harmoniously blends traditional and modern elements. On the menu: seafood specialities such as oysters and lobster, along with classics such as steak tartare and special cuts of meat cooked in the Southbend infrared broiler.

Name: Gasthaus Adler
Description: Savour classic Baden fare with French and international influences in these cosy, quintessentially "Black Forest" dining rooms. In winter, for example, the game and goose dishes are popular. In summer, there is outside seating in the Adler Gärtle. The service is friendly and there are comfortable guestrooms, some simpler than others.

Name: H'manns
Description: The Hegmanns run this genuinely charming restaurant that is a hit with diners. Only the best produce makes its way into the dishes, which are meticulously prepared to bring out the full flavour of the ingredients. On Fri-Sun, two four- to eight-course seasonal set menus, one of which is vegetarian, are served. On Mon, tapas menu only – to be washed down with something from the promising wine selection. Extremely friendly waitstaff. Tip: The chef's table is very close to the kitchen but sheltered from the thick of the action.

Name: Das Esszimmer
Address: Hintergasse 38, Neustadt an der Weinstraße, 67433, Germany
Description: A lovely restaurant in the Old Town: the welcoming, sleek and modern setting is bound to appeal, and the atmosphere is pleasantly intimate, the service is attentive and well trained. You can watch Italian/Mediterranean dishes being prepared in the open kitchen. Look out for the "speciality days". On Thursdays: tasting menu only. The terrace in front of the house is also a pleasant place to sit.

Name: Spitzweg
Description: This place has been serving up consistently good food for years – there's a reason why it attracts so many regulars. On the menu: seasonal, regional and international dishes. The sleek, modern decor boasting a bold red colour scheme and paintings on the walls is stylish. Friendly and professional service. The lively terrace set up on the pavement is a lovely place to sit. There is also an annexe for private events.

Name: Ostaria da Gino
Description: This delightful family-run restaurant's enduring popularity among regulars is a testament to the unwavering dedication and passion that have been poured into its operations for the past 40 years. Authentic Italian cuisine is served in a laid-back setting with bags of charm! Staff will be happy to guide you through the options written up on the board and recommend the right wine. Tip: the moderately priced lunch deal. Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home.

Name: Der Kaiserhof
Description: Run by the same family for four generations, Kaiserhof has a surprisingly chic and fresh interior behind its deceptively traditional façade. The tastefully designed dining space is accessed via the open kitchen – diners can also watch the chefs at work. The concept here is a seasonally orientated "Culinary Journey" in six courses – for which you should allow plenty of time. Vegetarian dishes such as aubergine with pointed cabbage and Parmesan are just as enticing as the duck with Savoy cabbage and blackcurrant. Friendly and attentive front-of-house team. The chefs are involved in serving and talk you through the dishes. In summer, head for the terrace in the small courtyard. There are well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Jagstmühle
Description: With its cosy yet elegant interior and charming terrace, the restaurant blends wonderfully into the picture-perfect scene of the estate, which stands against the romantic backdrop of the River Jagst. The light hues of the wood panelling, the tiled stove and pretty fabrics all contribute to the inviting atmosphere. The food draws on international influences, with subtle Asian touches here and there. Dine à la carte or opt for the set menu (omnivore or vegetarian). Alternatively, the pleasant Mühlenscheune serves regional cuisine. There are also lovely guestrooms.

Name: Lamm
Description: A tasteful, modern interior incorporating a sleek design, premium materials and warm tones goes hand in hand with the hospitality of a traditional inn. The menu whets the appetite with an interesting array of regional and international dishes, such as roast Angus beef served with two kinds of onions, warm potato salad and maultaschen>/i> (Swabian dumplings) sautéed in butter or Barbary duck breast accompanied by stir-fried Asian vegetables and Himalayan basmati rice. The five different set menus, which include a vegan one, are also excellent. A very popular establishment – book early if you are looking to come at the weekend!

Name: Rive Fish & Faible
Description: Sitting right on the port, this bistro is run by the same team as Tschebull. It serves good quality, flavoursome seafood and grilled meats alongside classic dishes such as Hamburger Pannfisch and Wiener Schnitzel. In summer the wonderful terrace is a must! Hot food served throughout the day.

Name: Rüssel's Hasenpfeffer
Description: This excellent alternative to Rüssel'schen fine dining restaurant is very popular with guests! Here in the left-hand side of this attractive country house, the buzzy atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back; the tasty food is made using good-quality ingredients. Classic cuisine with regional influences can be enjoyed as a set menu or à la carte – game and braised meat are among the favourites.

Name: heyligenstaedt
Description: The high ceilings, steel girders, large mullioned windows and sections of exposed brick wall show a conscious effort to retain some of the industrial charm of this old factory building: these features have been merged into the chic, modern design. The tasty cuisine has international and seasonal roots; smaller menu at lunchtime. Friendly service, and the adjoining boutique hotel has trendy guestrooms and rooftop sauna area.

Name: Jennerwein
Address: Münchner Straße 127, Gmund am Tegernsee, 83703, Germany
Description: A truly delightful establishment with a charmingly rustic inn atmosphere – it's genuinely cosy here. The menu includes freshly prepared seasonal Bavarian cuisine such as braised shoulder of lamb with root vegetables, or beef tenderloin on a bed of fried mushrooms and potatoes, as well as parmesan risotto with king prawns. More limited options at lunchtime.

Name: Schillingshof
Description: Schillingshof has been around since 1648. The family business takes pride in providing first-rate hospitality. Behind the spruce half-timbered façade, you will find an elegant interior where diners enjoy attentive and cordial service and, last but not least, classic cuisine. Made using carefully selected ingredients, the dishes are pared down to the essentials. There are various set menus and tempting à la carte options such as confit char on a bed of mussel risotto with lime foam, or veal fillet "saltimbocca" with rosemary gnocchi, vegetables and sauce divine. The wine list is also fantastic – sometimes, a Mediterranean antipasti platter and a good bottle of wine are all you need. Lovely guestrooms.

Name: Posthörnle
Description: This casual, minimalist-style little restaurant is housed in one of the oldest taverns in the town. It serves fresh, seasonal cuisine with dishes ranging from venison rissoles with black mustard to pan-fried zander with oranges and chicory.

Name: STRAUCHS FALCO
Description: This smart and stylish restaurant is next to the Maritime Museum. Situated in the Elbarkaden in the middle of HafenCity, it also boasts an appealing terrace. The menu features a variety of cuisines from around the globe, including specialities from the barbecue, Mediterranean dishes, such as fish and shellfish soup, German classics like Labskaus (meat stew) and Wiener schnitzel, as well as pasta. Additionally, there is the Bar & Deli.

Name: Wirtshaus zum Herrmannsdorfer Schweinsbräu
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: "Dishes that can't be pigeonholed" – such is the name of the game for chef Olimpia Cario. In her surprise set menu, she gives free rein to her creativity, cooking up unusual combinations such as chicken, trout, egg, cucumber, corn and redcurrants. She uses seasonal produce and high-quality ingredients, often grown on her own farm. The interior itself has an eye-catching design, with a large, high-ceilinged space reminiscent of a modern rustic barn on account of the beam construction climbing up into the roof.

Name: Zur Krone
Description: The Isele family has been cultivating the art of hospitality in this traditional building since 1854. The interior boasts a pleasant atmosphere in which to enjoy classic German cuisine that is seasonal, carefully prepared and based on a range of regional ingredients. The home-made terrines and desserts are definitely worth trying – the diet will have to wait! The wine list also has a very regional slant. In addition, there are comfortable, tastefully decorated guestrooms in which you will be tempted to stay for more than one night!

Name: L'arte in cucina
Description: This attractive restaurant opposite the Basilika St. Margareta is a rare example of an authentic Italian ristorante, where the cuisine of Tuscany is served with love and culinary flair. Specialities from the chef's Tuscan homeland such as gnudi (a kind of gnocchi) or "Il Coniglio" (rabbit). The pasta is house-made.

Name: Hopmanns Olive
Description: With great dedication, the Hopmanns have been running this friendly, sleek, modern restaurant for over 20 years – Ingo heads up the kitchen; Petra is in charge front of house. Based on classical foundations, the cuisine is seasonal and draws on Mediterranean inspirations. One of the classics is, for example, gently braised lamb shank. In summer, you can also take advantage of the gorgeous terrace. Tip: The adjoining historical engine shed is an ideal location to book for events.

Name: Basho-An
Description: Located near the pedestrian zone, this restaurant is a popular spot for authentic Japanese cuisine. If you want to avoid disappointment, be sure to make your reservations in good time! The decor is characteristically minimalist; there are also a few seats at the sushi counter. Tip: the reasonably priced lunchtime set menu. The options for dinner are wider ranging. At both lunchtime and in the evening, vegetarian dishes are also available. The wine list also includes sake, of course, and some regional wines.

Name: Zum Goldenen Anker
Description: Not only does this 18C hotel offer a comfortable stay (opt for one of the newer guestrooms), it is also a popular modern take on a rural restaurant. Diners are waited on by a friendly front-of-house team in an attractive modern setting with a rustic touch. The food is flavoursome, fresh and seasonal. The main courses are also available in smaller portions. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Torschänke
Description: Right next to the Obertor (the historical city gate), Torschänke is a really inviting restaurant. The atmosphere inside is cosy and pleasingly down to earth, and outside there is a lovely, leafy terrace. Dishes with French and Mediterranean influences are prepared using top-notch fresh produce and served by a friendly, attentive and proficient front-of-house team.

Name: La Cuisine Mario Kalweit
Description: A nicely restored building from the late 19th century houses this stylish, modern, elegant restaurant serving creative cuisine. Pleasant terrace.

Name: Zu den drei Linden - Lindenblüte
Description: Tanja and Thomas Siemes run their family business with great dedication, and the food here is exceptional. He cooks up international cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons and incorporates Mediterranean and regional influences; she provides charming service. You can opt for the set menu or order dishes à la carte, such as the mouthwatering crispy fried loup de mer with spinach and Carmague rice. The atmosphere is friendly and the decor has an elegant Mediterranean feel.

Name: Kölbl
Description: Plenty of regulars come here to enjoy the regional and international cuisine served à la carte or in the form of a four-course set menu – a vegetarian version is also available. Diners can sit in one of the cosy dining rooms or on the courtyard terrace to enjoy the seasonal dishes. The guestrooms are ideal for overnight stays.

Name: Sette Feinbistro
Description: Somewhat tucked away in the pedestrian precinct, this gem has been run with great dedication by the Tegge family for many years. The name "Feinbistro" encompasses both a delicatessen and a restaurant serving Mediterranean and regional cuisine. Breakfast is also available. Don't forget to purchase delicacies such as jam, cheese and wine etc from the shop to enjoy at home.

Name: MAXIME de Guy Graessel
Description: An appealing modern restaurant with an intimate atmosphere. Chef-patron Guy Graessel, who hails from Alsace, specialises in classic fare from Alsace and Baden. Diner choose between the five-course surprise menu (for two or more people) and à la carte dishes. For al fresco dining, there are tables in the charming verdant garden courtyard. Drinks are also served on the terrace in the pedestrian precinct Tip: Located in the entrance area, Café Hesselbacher has house-made cakes, tarts and pastries for sale at the weekend, over the counter or pre-ordered. For motorists, there is a car park – Parkhaus Löwenhof – not far from the restaurant.

Name: Zum Goldenen Pflug
Description: In one of the oldest inns in the region, tradition is celebrated, but not at the expense of progress. There are a number of charming dining areas in which to enjoy dishes such as Rindertafelspitz aus dem Kupferpfandl (boiled beef fillet from the copper pot), apple horseradish, chive sauce, creamed spinach and sautéed potatoes and, for dessert, Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake) with plum compote and whipped cream. Order à la carte or opt for the "Signature Menu" for two or more diners.

Name: ESSperiment
Description: This relaxed modern restaurant with its lovely terrace offers a bistro menu at lunchtimes and fine dining in the evenings. The food is fresh and flavoursome. Try the saddle of venison with muesli, black salsify, pear and layered potato cake.

Name: Orania.Berlin
Description: The restaurant belonging to the lovely hotel that shares its name has a stylish, warm and relaxed ambience. The lobby and bar (with its interesting cocktail menu) are directly adjacent. Modern, creative dishes are sent out of the large open kitchen that draws the eye. Attentive and accomplished service. Try the four-course "Xberg Duck" set menu (min. two people).

Name: alexxanders
Description: Located in a residential area, this restaurant boasts a stylish interior and a courtyard terrace with a beautifully landscaped little garden. The flavoursome dishes draw inspiration from around the globe and incorporate Mediterranean and seasonal influences. Why not enjoy an aperitif at the bar before your meal? The wine list is also worth a look. Guestrooms with modern interior design are available in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Altdeutsches Restaurant
Description: Florian Kellerbauer's kitchen philosophy centres on quality ingredients, with a strong commitment to regional and seasonal sourcing. Diners can opt for a set menu – either with meat or vegetarian – comprising four, five or six courses. You can also order à la carte. The service is friendly, attentive and professional. The restaurant occupies a prime spot in the historical centre – Kirche St Georg just opposite is well worth a visit. For overnight stays, there is Hotel Deutsches Haus, a patrician house dating from 1440, or in the Ehemalige Sparkasse, both just 50m away.

Name: Warias Am Markt
Description: Diners can expect regional and seasonal cuisine that makes use of excellent produce – the daily specials are always a good option. The menu features timeless favourites such as beef carpaccio with pesto and Belper Knolle cheese, or pan-seared fish-of-the-day with potato and cucumber salad. The single five- or nine-course surprise menu served on Friday and Saturday evenings available only by reservation. The restaurant has a convivial atmosphere, and the outdoor terrace is a delightful spot. Conveniently, the establishment has well-kept, light and airy guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Lockstein 1
Description: This really is a special place: you enter the charming kitchen through the 500-year-old farmhouse, which is run by an established mother-and-daughter team. They inject love and skill into their cooking, which takes the form of a vegetarian set menu comprising fresh dishes made using regional produce. The two pretty holiday flats are also popular.

Name: Rebstock-Stube
Description: A cosy atmosphere reigns in this lovely inn run by the Frey family. The decor is inviting, with dark wood panelling and neatly laid tables at which the classic cuisine of chef Axel Frey is served. Dishes such as "pike dumplings, leaf spinach, lobster sauce" or "boiled veal 'pink', Maultasche (German raviolo), braised vegetables, herb velouté" make an impression with their flavour and quality. You can choose à la carte or opt for a set menu. The wine list is also definitely worth a look! The service is friendly and attentive. The terrace is wonderful for those summer days. Tip: Visit the local history museum next door.

Name: Landhaus Gräfenthal
Description: Steeped in tradition, this establishment has a solid reputation in the area. Peter Lauterbach represents the fourth generation to run this family restaurant in an idyllic location. The food is a contemporary take on regional, seasonal cuisine and influenced by Mediterranean culinary tradition. Inside, pale wood, a tiled stove and pleasing decorative touches make for an inviting setting; outside there is a beautiful garden terrace. With warm and attentive service, this place has everything it takes to ensure a comfortable dining experience.

Name: Crackers
Description: You’ll find this trendy eatery one floor below Cookies Cream. Ring the bell and the staff will lead you through the kitchen into a large and lively restaurant with a high ceiling and dim lights. The menu offers a range of ambitious meat and fish dishes.

Name: Schlosskeller
Description: When it comes to the setting, the lovingly decorated vaulted cellar is really cosy, and the terrace by the castle pond is fantastic! The seasonal cuisine is in a regional vein, ranging from classic Wiener schnitzel to roasted fillet of sea bass with a rosehip foam. They are also open at lunchtime, which is excellent news.

Name: Die Klosterschänke
Description: Idyllically set a few kilometres from the city centre, this warm and welcoming family-run restaurant boasts a magnificent terrace affording splendid views of the Rhine plain. The chef cooks up regional and seasonal cuisine along with a selection of Italian dishes. The mouthwatering options include a classic cordon bleu with Black Forest ham and Alpine cheese, and saltimbocca alla romana from the chef's homeland.

Name: Le Comptoir
Description: Located in the Nauwieser Viertel, this restaurant is housed in an old sandstone and brick building, incidentally the birthplace of director Max Ophüls. An attractive modern interior and a friendly atmosphere await you here. The seats at the counter ("le comptoir" in French – hence the name of this establishment) are very popular. In the evenings, a modern seasonal set menu comprising four or five courses is served.

Name: Brauereigasthof Aying
Description: The restaurant is part of the picture-perfect Brauereigasthof Hotel Aying is a family-run establishment steeped in tradition and now run by the seventh generation. Diners are treated to warm hospitality in an upscale yet cosy setting. The terrace to the rear of the building is delightful in summer. The menu features exquisite regional and seasonal dishes, crafted from carefully selected produce of the highest quality – the restaurant has its own herd of Pinzgau beef cattle, as well as a hunter, who provides the game. In addition to the selection of fine wines, there are of course Ayinger beer specialities. Good event facilities. Comfortable and tastefully decorated guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Brasserie Lamazère
Description: Ready for a dose of French savoir-vivre in Berlin? You almost feel like you are in France here in the heart of Charlottenburg at Brasserie Lamazère thanks to its charming, down-to-earth and lively atmosphere. The regularly changing seasonal dishes are chalked up on the blackboard. You can put together your menu (starter, main, dessert) from a fine selection. They will be happy to recommend a good French wine pairing to accompany your food – the appealing and reasonably priced wine list is proprietor Régis Lamazère's passion.

Name: Landgasthaus Zum Kreuz
Description: The appealing alliance of regional and modern influences is omnipresent at the Neumaier family's establishment – whether in the cosy restaurant, the food or the lovely comfortable guestrooms in the Speicher guesthouse next door. Chef-owner Peter Neumaier's sons Lars and Tim are now also involved in the kitchen. The menu features classic and seasonal dishes – be sure to check out the "mini Versucherle" (mini appetisers). You can eat à la carte or choose a set menu – vegetarian options are also available. Owner Michaela Neumaier heads up the team providing friendly service. In summer, the wonderful terrace is the best place to soak up the gorgeous rural location!

Name: Berghofstüble
Description: This restaurant enjoys a stunning location up above the town. The interior has a pleasing design and there is an attractive conservatory with a pretty terrace outside offering impressive views. The cuisine is based on good, fresh produce with appetising dishes such as Skrei cod on leaf spinach in beurre blanc.

Name: GUI
Description: It's a good idea to book, because this lively bistro in the middle of town has more than its fair share of regulars! The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine also has regional influences. The quality of the ingredients is first rate, from the fresh pasta with porcini to the cod and the tender venison fillet. The modern interior decor is pleasant – the floor-to-ceiling shelf with decorative wine bottles draws the eye, as does the open kitchen with one striking red wall. In summer, the terrace in the pedestrian area is very inviting. Incidentally, ĝui means "enjoy" in the international language of Esperanto.

Name: Schwarzmatt
Description: Served à la carte or as a set menu, classic cuisine made with seasonal produce is the order of the day here. The upscale interior is very comfortable, with harmonious, lovingly arranged decorative objects – it certainly does full justice to the luxurious setting of the traditional holiday hotel of the same name in which this restaurant is housed. For overnight stays, there are elegant country-house-style guestrooms – this is after all the sister hotel of Baiersbronn's Hotel Bareiss. Make a beeline for the gorgeous garden terrace in summer. A must in the afternoon: cakes made to Hermine Bareiss's old recipes!

Name: Abt- und Schäferstube
Description: The location – the beautiful grounds of a centuries-old monastery estate surrounded by nature – is the very epitome of peace and quiet. Oozing historical, rustic charm, the restaurant serves classic, seasonal cuisine with a distinct modern influence. You can order à la carte or opt for the set menu (up to six courses). The service is competent and friendly. The terrace with a view of the Odenwald forest is particularly pleasant, and the well-stocked vaulted wine cellar dating back to 1524 is also worth seeing. For an overnight stay, the Der Schafhof hotel has well-kept guestrooms. Be sure to take a look at the collection of carriages.

Name: WEINrestaurant Ayler Kupp
Description: While you tuck into the fresh seasonal dishes, which the chefs here cook up with produce from the region, you can take in the vineyards and the lovely garden. There are two set menus, each made up of three to five courses; you can also choose individual dishes à la carte. The wine list includes Riesling from the neighbouring wine estate. They also offer accommodation in inviting, well-kept guestrooms in the hotel.

Name: Gasthaus Assenmacher
Description: It's clear that Christian and Christa Storch put their heart and soul into running this place. The chef-patron wins over diners with his modern take on classic cuisine. Eschewing any gimmickry, he lays the focus squarely on quality produce and flavour. The lady of the house manages the friendly and attentive waitstaff. Pleasant little terrace to the rear of the building. Decent accommodation options at the hotel.

Name: Die Ratsstuben
Description: One draw of this restaurant is its beautiful location in the centre of the pretty old town on the Alb River, another is its chic, modern interior. The cuisine is based on high-quality ingredients and ranges from classics such as house-made maultaschen to international specialities such as barbecued octopus and burgers, and not forgetting the various tartare options. The waitstaff are friendly and well trained. In summer, the terrace overlooking the square is a delightful spot where you will be serenaded by the carillon music from the town hall tower.

Name: Trichards
Description: This chic and modern restaurant-cum-wine bar is located in Munich's Lehel neighbourhood. The owner comes from France, which is reflected in the cooking style. Tip: The "Bouillabaisse-style noble fish and gamba with rouille" is a year-round speciality. The seasonal dishes can be accompanied by your choice from the comprehensive wine list. Ideal for those who like to eat al fresco – the terrace and garden are covered and as such protected from the elements.

Name: SCHORN by Lukas Schild
Description: With Lukas Schild as chef-patron, this restaurant in the Bilk neighbourhood boasts a big name in the Düsseldorf fine dining scene. Select ingredients go into ambitious seasonal cooking – the dishes draw on the classics. The set menu comes in a four- to seven-course version, or you can take your pick from the à la carte selection. The team is friendly and knowledgeable – the chef comes to your table and talks you through the dishes. The appealing wine list comprises mostly German and French labels. The restaurant has a charming, intimate feel, with decorative features including an old stove, a wine barrel serving as a digestif table and modern paintings. The terrace is lovely in summer.

Name: Müllers auf der Rü
Description: Nelson Müller's fine dining restaurant, Schote, may have moved to Bergisch Gladbach, but this cherished Essen-based establishment at Rüttenscheider Stern U-Bahn station has stayed put. This is a market hall-style brasserie integrated into a shopping arcade. Sitting at high tables, diners tuck into delicious dishes ranging from currywurst to turbot, prepared in the centrally positioned open kitchen. Friendly service. Tip for motorists: public multi-storey car park around the corner.

Name: Zum Simonbräu
Description: A down-to-earth pub, just the way we like them! Part of the Bitburger Brewery, this place has an attractive decor of solid wooden tables (no tablecloths here!), walls decorated with pictures, and modern details that foster a pleasantly lively atmosphere. The charming team serves home-style regional dishes, as well as more sophisticated options. Cordon bleu with Eifelschwein pork and "Ōra King salmon – tartare & fried" whet the appetite. The inexpensive dish of the day is popular with the lunchtime crowd. You can also spend the night in one of the spruce guestrooms.

Name: Der Dantler
Description: A tip to start with: reserve well in advance! Given the great value for money and the relaxed atmosphere, it's no surprise that they tend to get booked up. They call themselves the "Bavarian Deli". In the interior done out in a slick Alpine/country-style style, the service is personable and relaxed. At lunchtime you can order pasta, a pastrami sandwich, ramen or the fish dish of the day à la carte, or the three-course "business lunch". In the evening, creative modern cuisine is served in the form of a set menu – a vegetarian or pescetarian version is also available (request this when you book). There is also a wine bar next door.

Name: Das Esszimmer
Description: A small, neat house on the outskirts of the city centre houses this pretty restaurant with its modern and minimalist design. The cuisine is also modern; one of the menus is vegetarian. The choice of accompanying beverages includes not only wines but also an alcohol-free alternative. Pleasantly relaxed, friendly and professional service.

Name: Mine
Description: Very close to Ku'damm, this chic and laid-back establishment is run by a family that already has restaurants in St Petersburg and Moscow. The premises actually used to be home to Berlin's smallest bar. A charming pavement terrace beckons in front of the restaurant. Their Italian cuisine (including classics such as vitello tonnato or pasta) also draws on international and seasonal influences. Opt for the "Greatest Hits" set menu (two or more people) for a tempting selection of dishes. Nicely curated wine list. The wine cellar can also be booked for private dinners or chef's table events.

Name: Carte blanche
Address: Egenolffstraße 39, Frankfurt on the Main, 60316, Germany
Description: As the name "Carte Blanche" suggests, there is no fixed menu here; instead a surprise six-course menu is served – and a four-course version is also available Wed-Thu. Wine pairings for the individual courses are available upon request. The cuisine is modern and seasonal – the summery tomato salad with mackerel ceviche or the charcoal-grilled sturgeon are tempting options. The emphasis is on artisanal craftsmanship; even the bread is made in-house. The restaurant boasts a lovely location in an attractive historical building on a corner plot with high ceilings decorated with moulding, and unique interior details that contribute to a charming atmosphere.

Name: Valentin
Description: In a small side street in the island's old town, you will find this restaurant in a lovely vaulted cellar. In a stylish and modern setting, you can enjoy seasonal cuisine made with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Opt for a set menu comprising four or seven courses, or choose from the small à la carte selection. At lunchtime, the options are more limited. Friendly front-of-house team. The secluded terrace in the courtyard is a pleasant spot. There is also a wine bar.

Name: sushi Lounge
Description: The latest culinary hotspot at FAVORITE Parkhotel is a restaurant within a restaurant! Sushi lounge is located inside the hotel's Weinbar. Only sushi and sashimi are on the menu in this compact space, and everything is made with the finest produce – something for which FAVORITE Restaurant also has a reputation. Must-try nigiri: otoro for melt-in-your-mouth richness, scallops for pristine freshness or unagi for bold umami.

Name: Lang is her
Description: After a number of years working at the restaurant Alte Pfarrey in Neuleiningen in the Palatinate, Bettina and Silvio Lange are back at their previous place of work, namely Hotel an der Wasserburg. Back in the day, they were chefs at the (since closed) Saphir restaurant; today they are working with the Rohde family, the owners, to bring to life the "Lang is her" concept. The restaurant serves modern and international cuisine with seasonal influences – opt for "Lange's Menu", a three- to seven-course set menu, or go à la carte. Whether seated in the restaurant room, with its friendly, chic feel or, in summer, on the lovely terrace with a walnut tree, you will enjoy cordial, attentive service. You will be recommended a suitable wine from the well-stocked German/international list. The restaurant also has a bar with an additional small menu. Cookery courses are also offered. Tip: The medieval castle, Burg Neuhaus, is within walking distance.

Name: 5 SEN:SES by Mario Aliberti
Description: At this fine addition to Karlsruhe's culinary scene, chef-patron Mario Aliberti fuses Italian cuisine with Asian influences. An appealing range of dishes is available: Lunchtime features reasonably priced set menus, plus a small selection from the evening menu. At dinnertime, there is a fine dining menu, an Italian menu and a sharing menu, as well as an extensive à la carte selection. Octopus cooked in black beer with ponzu beurre blanc and black garlic is a house classic. It is worth perusing the well-stocked wine list, too. The inviting modern interior exudes a distinctly loungey feel. In summer, head for the quiet terrace laid out right in front of the restaurant.

Name: Félix
Description: The trip out of Hamburg city centre to the well-to-do Hochkamp neighbourhood is well worth it, as the many locals who regularly dine here will confirm. Fitting seamlessly into the villa-studded neighbourhood, this elegant little bistro boasts an upscale modern interior. The service is warm and professional. From some tables, diners can see through the glass partition into the kitchen. Félix Bechtolf – after whom the establishment is named – and his team craft classic French dishes including plenty of fish and seafood. The quality of the ingredients and meticulous preparation never fail to impress. Order à la carte or opt for the three-course set menu, which changes every week. The well-curated wine list features premium French labels. Open for lunch on Saturdays. Tip: In fine weather, take a stroll along the Elbchaussee.

Name: DAS MAXI - GENUSSREICH
Description: Das Maxi has proven to be a successful addition to Das Freiberg hotel and is an appealing dining option – and not only for hotel guests. The kitchen specialises in contemporary, mostly Mediterranean dishes with seasonal influences. In addition to the set menu, which changes daily, there is also a small à la carte selection. Food is served in tastefully designed dining areas, and there is additional garden seating available for the summer months. The wine list, featuring international labels, is second to none. The gorgeous guestrooms have magnificent views of the mountains.

Name: alto
Description: This restaurant in the Atlantic Grand Hotel has a tastefully sleek interior, with dark wood panelling, large modern fixtures, as well as designer upholstered chairs in red and brown. The conservatory extension is also a lovely spot, as is the courtyard garden in fine weather – an Alpine-style hut is erected here every winter. The menu features classic dishes with a modern twist, plus classics such as schnitzel. Incidentally, the crockery is custom-made in Bremen. The location in the old town is ideal, with all the main attractions – the Weser River, Schnoor, Rathaus, Kunsthalle – just a short walk away.

Name: Altes Rathaus by What the Food
Description: A truly delightful example of casual, down-to-earth dining that brings pleasure and joy! This restaurant is housed in a picturesque half-timbered house in the pedestrian area. The interior is modern and minimalist, and outside there is a charming terrace overlooking the forecourt. Chef-patron Patrick Schubert cooks up dishes that are creative and full of flavour – opt for his ambitious signature set menu ("Da kommsch rum") or choose from the somewhat simpler à la carte selection. Options are more limited at lunchtime. Friendly and competent service comes courtesy of maître d' Anne Henrichs. Good to know: they have a food truck that can be booked for special occasions.

Name: Müllers auf Norderney
Description: Affording unobstructed views of the sea, 1884's exclusive location alone is a major draw. The charming little boutique hotel is a spa-style building complex composed of Villa Mathilde and the adjoining Villa Olga. It is also home to a chic restaurant with modern and minimalist interior design and a fabulous terrace. In the kitchen, Nelson Müller's team prepares flavoursome and pleasingly uncomplicated dishes from fresh, good-quality ingredients. Soul food would be an apt label for this cuisine.

Name: Daniels
Description: Located in the centre of Kusel's old town, right on the market square, this renovated townhouse is certainly charming. Out front, there are a few trees and a fountain – the terrace seating here is delightful in summer. The place has a modern feel and a laid-back, friendly atmosphere. Wooden ceiling beams and exposed old sandstone masonry hark back to a bygone era. Ulrike and Daniel Bößhar deliver attentive service and ambitious cuisine in the form of a set menu inspired by modern culinary trends and ranging from three to seven courses. From the carefully crafted amuse-bouches to hearty dishes such as celeriac soup enriched with autumn truffle and Ibérico pork cheek, their detailed, flavour-led approach is unmistakable.

Name: Restaurant Mühle
Description: Using only the freshest premium ingredients, this restaurant presents a contemporary blend of regional, seasonal and Mediterranean influences. Enjoy friendly and attentive service in the invitingly elegant country-style dining space, or out on the lovely terrace in summer. Cosy, comfortable guestrooms await you in the hotel. On the practical side: it is only about 15min by car to Basel, the airport and the exhibition centre.

Name: Jäger & Lustig
Description: What a cosy and quaint-feeling place, serving what the owners term "Heimatküche": think hearty, fresh, flavoursome cuisine. Classic German dishes are the stars of the show – game and goose are specialities of the house. They are at pains to use regional ingredients and remain aligned with the seasons. Service courtesy of friendly and competent staff. Make the most of the beer garden in summer.

Name: Lou im Cavalierhaus
Description: The estate is worth a visit in its own right. The palace and 620ha Branitz Park landscaped by Prince Hermann von Pückler in the 19C are conducive to a stroll. Lou (a nickname given to Prince Pückler) is an elegant restaurant housed in the smart Kavaliersbau (squire's lodge). Here, chef-patron Tim Sillack serves up modern seasonal cuisine with an artful juxtaposition of regional and international influences. The individual courses of the menu can also be ordered à la carte. "Pückler Eis" (Neapolitan ice cream) has a permanent place on the menu and is something of a signature dessert. There are also three tastefully furnished guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Les Deux Dienstbach
Description: Les Deux Dienstbach refers to the two sisters who founded this restaurant at the renowned Weingut Künstler and whose French roots influence the cuisine. Nathalie Dienstbach has since returned to her native Normandy, leaving seasoned owner Jennifer Himmel (née Dienstbach) in charge of overseeing both the restaurant floor and the kitchen. She is joined by chef Christian Aguilar, who creates a three- to seven-course set menu using select ingredients. The food is accompanied by wines from France and Weingut Künstler. The setting is also appealing with its colour palette of muted tones, and smart, modern interior design features make for a tasteful interior in the heart of this historical building. On Sunday lunchtimes, you can dine à la carte.

Name: Schwitzer's PUR
Description: There have been some developments at Schwitzer's. In the newly refurbished rooms of the former fine dining restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows affording views of the park grounds, diners are invited to embark on a culinary adventure that takes its cue from the seasons. Depending on the time of year, varying styles of cuisine are proposed – à la carte or as a three-course surprise set menu. Schwitzer's Hotel am Park has upscale guestrooms.

Name: Zwo20
Description: The name of this restaurant refers to the year 2020, in which Andrea von Csiszer (head chef) and Sophie Herzog (the cordial and highly adept maître d') set up shop. Diners are drawn here not only by the somewhat unusual setting in a historical chapel with striking features such as vaults and ceiling paintings, but also the trendy and laid-back atmosphere, as well as the intriguing culinary concept: Asian sharing cuisine with a European twist. You can put together an assortment of several small, cleverly devised dishes to share, such as "Peking pork 24hr sous vide" with fried onion, soya and honey, or cauliflower wings with red cabbage, sweet chilli, fennel and potato. The location in the centre of the old town, caught between the Danube and the Inn, near the Dreiflüsseeck (three-river confluence), is also delightful. Tip: Römerplatz multi-storey car park just a few minutes' walk away.

Name: Fangfrisch
Description: A friendly, laid-back restaurant located on the edge of the city centre, only five minutes from the Holstentor. Trendy industrial-style design, very friendly and relaxed young service team and, last but not least, tasty modern cuisine. The emphasis is on regional ingredients – for example, organically farmed catfish from Brandenburg. Hot meals are served all day, but there are also sandwiches and fish rolls to go.

Name: JAPATAPA TOSHIBAR
Description: Japatapa Toshibar is tucked away in a side street near Münchner Freiheit in the Schwabing district. Having formerly run the restaurant Toshi for a long time, owners Toshio and Tamiko Kobatake are no strangers to Munich's gastronomy scene. The small space, in which you sit at the counter or a small table, is done out in a minimalist style. Kobatake's cuisine is authentically Japanese: you should definitely try the tasty sushi, but dishes such as onsen egg with caviar and dashi broth or black cod grilled with saikyo miso are also tempting. The proprietress provides discreet and friendly service, and there is a good selection of wines as well as an impressive number of sakes.

Name: Macionga
Description: This attractive, sleek restaurant located close to Ku'damm (Kurfürstendamm) is named after its owner – sommelier and winemaker André Macionga. In keeping with his passion for wine, the wine list is very nicely curated, and the restaurant also has its own wine shop. Chef Christopher Wecker builds on stints in various Tim Raue kitchens, successfully incorporating his own ideas. He rustles up modern dishes with a seasonal bent, such as "scallop, coconut, sweet and sour pumpkin, buttered dashi broth" or "chicken fricassee CW, truffle, black walnut, Madeira jus," not to mention his unique take on a Poire belle Hélène, the classic pear dessert. The portion size means you can try several different dishes – a concept that is entirely in keeping with modern trends and goes down very well with diners.

Name: Feinschliff
Description: This restaurant in the town centre has a trendy, chic interior and a window through which you can see the chefs at work in the centrally positioned kitchen. The large floor-to-ceiling windows look out onto Kirchplatz and Pfarrkirche St Peter. In the evening, the modern menu with subtle Asian influences comprises four regularly changing courses, for example, "tuna, veal, capers" or "venison, parsley root, mushrooms". Service starts for everyone at 6.30pm (no walk-ins). Decent, reasonably priced wine pairings. At lunchtime, only a dish of the day is served. Tip: There is a public car park 150m away (Schießberg 1).

Name: Margaux
Address: Kornmarkt 7, Limburg an der Lahn, 65549, Germany
Description: Behind the beautiful historical half-timbered façade of this listed 14C building in the heart of the Old Town, there lies a tasteful, modern interior. In this setting, Fabian Sollbach serves up a modern take on French cuisine, in which select ingredients take centre stage. The ambitious dishes include elegant fjord trout with Maine lobster and pearl barley. The attractively priced lunch menu is also very popular. There are a handful of places to be had on the small gallery level and, in summer, tables are set up on an inviting terrace on the Kornmarkt. Tip: The cathedral is just a stone's throw away – it is well worth having a stroll through the charming Old Town.

Name: WurzelWerk
Description: This restaurant lives up to its name: Wurzel, meaning "root", signifies a dedication to the local terroir, Werk, meaning "craft", highlights a commitment to artisanal cooking techniques – chef-patron Benjamin Bendzko puts both into practice in his market-fresh cuisine. Exceptional and almost exclusively regional ingredients are used to create flavoursome and pleasingly down-to-earth dishes. Two buildings, built in 1875 as a farmstead, now house a guesthouse (with a café at weekends) and this restaurant, whose rustic charm and pretty decor make for a cosy atmosphere. In summer, the garden terrace is the place to be.

Name: Berta
Description: Berta would be very proud of her grandson, chef Assaf Granit, who has named this appealing restaurant after her. The energy of the chefs in the open kitchen, nestled behind the counter, is infectious, as they fill the colourful dining space with a vibrant and convivial atmosphere. A lively scenario, for which the menu is a perfect match: it is a veritable celebration of family recipes from Jerusalem infused with the modern spirit of Berlin. The "Frenavon" bread with tahini and tomatoes served beforehand is downright addictive. It is practically impossible to resist the charm of this restaurant!

Name: Porte Neuf
Description: Among Detmold's restaurants, this spot on the outskirts of the Old Town is a fantastic find. Chef-patron Daniel C Fischer presents ambitious dishes that meld French and Far Eastern elements with a modern twist. The set menu comes in a four- or six-course format, and can be extended to nine courses with advance notice. The wonderful food is complemented by dedicated, friendly service and expert wine recommendations. The chefs bring their dishes to your table personally. The intimate restaurant's chic, modern design creates a warm and inviting atmosphere. There is also a lovely terrace for an aperitif, digestif or coffee.

Name: Restaurant 1831
Description: Even the route to the magnificent moated castle, a 17C architectural gem, is an experience – you get to this stunning estate through a wooded area, then a bridge over the moat leads into the beautiful inner courtyard. The restaurant allies the character of this site steeped in history with modern comfort and winter garden-style. The view through the large glazed front is fabulous, not to mention the terrace! They serve a 4-, 5- or 6-course set menu of modern inspiration – on reservation also vegetarian. You can choose the matching wine or non-alcoholic pairing.

Name: Villa's Wine & Dine
Address: Moselstraße 5, Reil an der Mosel, 56861, Germany
Description: The fine dining restaurant of Villa Melsheimer serves imaginative and creative modern dishes made from excellent fresh ingredients. One of the three set menus is vegetarian. You can also go à la carte. In summer, the truly beautiful terrace overlooking the Moselle is a huge draw! In the event the weather does not cooperate, you can also enjoy the view from the bright conservatory. The boutique hotel has comfortable guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Vinophil
Description: The name says it all: wine plays a starring role here. This chic yet relaxed restaurant also boasts its own wine shop. Hosted by an enthusiastic duo – one a chef, the other a sommelier – diners can expect sound wine recommendations to accompany the flavoursome, modern-inspired cuisine. The menu features dishes such as crayfish cocktail with wild herb salad, mango, papaya and dill, or Ibérico pork chop with baked polenta, peppers and smoked almonds. Don't miss their streamlined lunch specials or the wine club evenings. The cocktail list also offers plenty of interesting options. The friendly and adept service further adds to the welcoming atmosphere.

Name: Benders
Description: This chic and modern restaurant has found the perfect home within the pretty half-timbered building of the long-established Birkenfelder Hof. It is an ideal setting for "casual dining". The atmosphere is also suitably relaxed, the waitstaff are experienced and friendly, and the delicious seasonal modern cuisine, which draws on French, Mediterranean and regional influences, incorporates the occasional Asian touch. The successful synthesis of different culinary styles is evident in dishes such as "Breton monkfish, dashi beurre blanc, pak choi, Sardinian pasta, tomato and pine nut vinaigrette". Classics such as roast beef, burgers (Tue-Wed only) and Wiener schnitzel (Thu only) are also tempting. It is pleasant to dine al fresco on the beautifully landscaped terrace. Well-maintained guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Konrad's
Address: Platz der Vereinten Nationen 4, Bonn, 53113, Germany
Description: This restaurant on the 17th floor of the Marriott Hotel has the "wow" factor of a great view over Bonn through its floor-to-ceiling windows. In the open kitchens they cook up modern dishes with Mediterranean influences. Pre- or after-dinner drinks are served in the bar right next door. Parking is available in the underground garage, and the lift leads directly to the restaurant.

Name: Eatrenalin
Description: An almost futuristic spin on the fine dining experience! Using the online ticket system, you choose one of two eight-course set menus – "Red Dimensions" with fish and meat or "Green Dimensions" as a vegetarian option – and select your drinks in advance. Those who want extras can choose both menus in the variants "Exclusive Dinner", "Champagne Dinner" or "Sommelier Dinner". During the 2hr "Eatrenalin Experience", you are guided through different themed worlds and rooms on ultra-modern "floating chairs", starting in the lounge and continuing through "Waterfall", "Discovery", "Ocean", "Taste", "Umami" and "Universe" to "Incarnation", in which tailored appetisers and dishes are served. Peter Hagen-Wiest is the man behind this unique culinary concept, and he has brought various star chefs in to create dishes inspired by modern, creative, international and classic influences. The evening is clearly structured and seamlessly organised, ending with refined drinks in the bar.

Name: KRasserie im verve⁵
Description: A former textile factory has been transformed into a modern brasserie and event space, creating an attractive new destination. The exposed concrete and ventilation pipes give the space an industrial feel; minimalist design and decorative art create a modern and stylish look. The floor-to-ceiling windows can be opened up in the warmer months – there's a small terrace out front. Fresh and flavoursome dishes drawing on regional and international influences are served à la carte or as a set menu named "Herzstück". The rooftop bar is great in summer (Thu-Sat).

Name: Melkhus
Description: The former cowshed of the beautifully renovated historical Immenhof estate houses this charming alternative to the Rodesand restaurant. The cuisine, made with top-quality, fresh produce, is traditional, regional and seasonal. Holstein-style sour meat is one of the classics on the menu. The 48hr-braised beef cheek and baked pike dumplings are also sure to whet the appetite. Vegetarian options are available too. The food is complemented by friendly service and a cosy, rustic atmosphere – the open fireplace is a nice touch. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace, which overlooks the lake. Good news: The restaurant is open seven days a week for lunch and dinner! Coffee and cake are served in the afternoon. Pick up some home-made jam, souvenirs etc at the farm shop.

Name: In Vino Veritas
Address: Steinacher Straße 9, Haslach im Kinzigtal, 77716, Germany
Description: Inga and Ralf Müller have made a name for themselves with this friendly restaurant. This is due in no small part to the international and regional cuisine, which is made with very good, often local ingredients. The service is attentive and charming. In summer, you can dine on simpler fare in the charming courtyard with its vine arbour. There are chic, modern guestrooms and apartments for overnight stays.

Name: Rodesand
Description: In an idyllic lakeside location by the Kellersee, this estate was made famous by the German cult film series Immenhof. Nowadays, within the pretty white walls of the manor house, diners tuck into ambitious fish and vegetarian/vegan dishes, such as "mildly smoked North Sea mackerel, celery, cranberry, horseradish" or "porcini agnolotti, braised leek, pickled cherry tomatoes, hazelnut foam". Choose between the set menu and à la carte options… The barbecued fish options are sure to whet the appetite. The interior design is truly lovely: With seven tables, the main room has an elegant modern feel. There are also two private dining spaces for smaller parties, and Jantzens Bar (with a cigar lounge), where sushi is served. Delightful terrace with a view of the surrounding countryside. Tip: "Teatime" on Sat and Sun. Hotel, riding facilities and farm shop on site.

Name: Ontra
Description: This restaurant with a tastefully designed modern interior is located in TechSquare, the new centre for digitalisation south of the city centre. A friendly and professional team serves up seasonal cuisine that also includes vegetarian dishes. The shorter lunchtime menu proposes some cheaper options. The neighbouring Ontra's Gourmetstube serves a fixed set menu made up of seven courses in the evening.

Name: Kuhlemann
Address: Freyung 39, Neustadt an der Waldnaab, 92660, Germany
Description: You can tell from the food that the chef has worked in some top establishments. Here in the restaurant of the family-run Grader hotel, his interesting cooking style translates into a creative set menu. This is accompanied by an appealing and concise wine list. The attractive setting blends rustic and modern features.

Name: PIER 6
Description: This stylish restaurant in the Havenwelten quarter delights diners with modern dishes made with locally sourced seasonal ingredients. Mouthwatering options on menu include Heligoland lobster bisque and skrei fillet with a tomato and thyme crust. Wallet-friendly lunch specials such as beef roulades or goulash also have their fans. The tables near the windows and on the terrace are especially coveted – the view of the New Harbour is beautiful. Given the popularity of this place, it's definitely best to book in advance.

Name: riva
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in Kaisergarten Hotel – the sister establishment of Ketschauer Hof, also located in central Deidesheim – this restaurant has a sleek interior done out in light natural tones. In this setting, pleasingly laid-back, friendly and professional waitstaff serve up delicious international and Mediterranean cuisine. The menu also features barbecued meats prepared on the Big Green Egg, along with options for fans of pizza. The selection of wines from the hotel group's own vineyards is excellent. RIVA Bar-Lounge is the perfect spot for a cocktail. The terrace overlooking the garden is delightful in summer.

Name: Landhaus Rössle
Description: Expect ambitious cuisine is in a classic/French vein with regional and seasonal influences – dishes include the likes of seared scallops on orange fennel, and the classic Zwiebelrostbraten (beef and onions in gravy). You can dine à la carte or opt for the set menu – available in an omnivore or vegetarian version. Attentive and charming service is the forte of the lady of the house. The interior is modern and elegant, and in winter tables by the fireplace are very much in demand. In summer, the garden terrace is a boon. There are attractive rooms for overnight guests.

Name: Gasthaus Lege
Description: This spruce restaurant blends seamlessly into the tranquil village atmosphere of the Thönse district. A feel-good dining experience is guaranteed at this warm and welcoming restaurant run with great dedication by Claudia and Hinrich Schulze. And that's to say nothing of the terrific cuisine, which comes in the form of two set menus: "Gaumenfreude" and (vegetarian) "Gartenliebe" – available in three- to seven-course variants. Classic dishes such as "Kalbstafelspitz (veal rump cap), porcini sauce, colourful Swiss chard, nut butter dumplings" bowl diners over with their excellent ingredients and meticulous craftsmanship. Under the tutelage of Claudia Schulz, the waitstaff provide friendly, proficient and professional service, including astute recommendations when it comes to drinks.

Name: Kantiners
Description: Hotel Waldkrug is a traditional family business in a green and leafy location, and its restaurant is tastefully designed with modern touches. The menu includes good modern bistro dishes in a French vein – think beef carpaccio, Caesar salad or grilled steaks – but also traditional regional dishes, such as beef consommé with marrow dumplings, or schnitzel. In addition, they have pretty terraces at the front and to the rear of the building. The cosy Barstube in the front area is another really lovely option.

Name: Das Alte Haus
Description: Enrico Dunkel and his small restaurant have been a well-established part of the city's culinary landscape for years. His cooking style is ambitious, creative and draws on international influences. The set menu can comprise five, six or seven courses. Choose your accompaniment from the extensive selection of fine German wines. There is also a pairing menu. The interior is modern yet cosy. In summer, the pretty terrace beckons.

Name: Adler
Description: Here, traditional Swabian cuisine meets global influences, blending local and international flavours. Enjoy cordial service in the comfort of either the main dining room steeped in history or the charming inner courtyard. The kitchen serves up seasonally influenced dishes. One of the most tempting dishes is the house classic: Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy) with maultaschen, spaetzle and salad. Chic guestrooms are available for overnight stays. On Tuesday evenings, the restaurant is only open to hotel patrons.

Name: Al Pappagallo
Description: An elegant restaurant with a lovely, light-filled winter garden and a delightful outdoor space – the latter is all the more appealing for being discreetly located within a beautiful inner courtyard. The kitchen serves classic Italian dishes, crafted from high-quality produce – the pasta is a particular highlight! The enthusiastic front-of-house team is friendly and attentive. You will also see the chef himself making his way around the restaurant and chatting with diners.

Name: Strandhaus
Description: A beach house (Strandhaus) right in the heart of Bonn – who would have thought? The delightful maritime decor and laid-back atmosphere transport you to a seaside retreat. Not forgetting the cosy secluded terrace. This is the perfect setting for a Mediterranean-influenced cuisine, with fish at the heart of it all. Using only the finest ingredients, the chef creates flavoursome dishes with a unique twist, available both à la carte and as a tasting menu. As well as fish, there are meat options and a dedicated vegetarian set menu.

Name: Lammershof Stuben
Description: To start with, the location on a 45ha estate is terrific. The cosy space with a tiled stove that draws the eye exudes rustic charm and a certain chic. Specialities include various dishes featuring meat from bison they have reared on their own farm. Note: On Mondays only bison burgers, or veggie burgers, are served. Tip: the marvellous terrace with a view of the countryside! There is also the ‘WILD X BERG’ restaurant, where you can enjoy a three or four-course menu on Saturdays from 6 p.m. The small Lammershof hotel, the main building of which dates from 1709, has cosy guestrooms.

Name: Jagdhaus Waldfrieden
Description: Choose whether to enjoy your meal in the cosy dining room with its open fireplace, in the airy conservatory or on the lovely terrace shaded by trees… This restaurant is a charming location in which to sample good regional food: the menu includes dishes such as Glückstädter Matjes (PDO preserved herring) or fillet of wild boar, cooked rare in a juniper berry jus. Tip: The lunch set menu is an excellent deal. Should you wish to stay overnight, the pretty guestrooms are very inviting and all individually decorated.

Name: Rocus
Description: Housed in an attractively converted railway building dating from 1904, this restaurant proposes ambitious cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons – available à la carte or as a set menu. Dine al fresco in the courtyard or on the terrace facing the railway line. A table in the wine cellar, surrounded by Spanish red wines, comes highly recommended.

Name: Rössle
Description: This family-run business is now in its fourth generation. Behind a smart half-timbered façade, diners can choose from seasonal cuisine with some international influences and classics with a connection to the region. There are guestrooms done out in a modern Black Forest style. If you fancy a little excursion, the monastery complex and brewery are both within easy walking distance.

Name: Engelwirts-Stube
Description: This lovely restaurant with its delightful terrace overlooking the garden serves regional and seasonal cuisine with the odd nod to international culinary traditions. A friendly and well-drilled front-of-house team help to create an inviting atmosphere. Tip: If you want to be close to the action, book the Chef's Table in the kitchen ( minimum 6 people). And if you wish to spend a little longer here, Hotel Engel Obertal offers comfortable, stylish guestrooms and fantastic facilities to help make your stay a relaxing one.

Name: Tomatissimo
Description: This popular restaurant with a friendly atmosphere lies slightly outside the city, in a small village. In summer you can make the most of the wonderful terrace by the village fountain, in the shade of the chestnut trees. Bernhard Grubmüller and his kitchen team serve up a conventional and a vegetarian set menu, as well as à la carte dishes, including charcoal-grilled dry-aged beef from their own maturing cabinet. The surprise menu comprising new small courses gives a good overview of the cuisine. Tip: Bernhards Küchentisch for smaller groups (on prior reservation).

Name: Bocca di Bacco
Description: On the outside, a smart historical façade, on the inside an attractively modern and elegant restaurant complete with bar and lounge. Visible through its glass panes, the kitchen turns out Italian cooking. Needless to say, the pasta is home-made. To be paired with one of their great Tuscan wines.

Name: Johann Grill
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Overlooking Berchtesgaden, surrounded by stunning natural beauty and with a magnificent mountain backdrop, the location is to die for! At the restaurant of the luxurious Kempinski Hotel Berchtesgaden, you can enjoy delicious seasonal cuisine made with fresh, local ingredients. For dessert, we highly recommend the Eckerbichl-Haustorte. The sleek, modern interior design is a draw in itself. Incidentally, the restaurant is named after the first person to climb the east face of the Watzmann and Germany's first official mountain guide. Weather permitting, be sure to make the most of the spacious terrace. Tip: A short path around the hotel affords panoramic views of the mountains – especially magical at sunset.

Name: Hof Grothues-Potthoff - Hasenklee
Description: A charming modern restaurant serving ambitious seasonal cuisine that is strongly influenced by the region and often incorporates home-grown fruit and vegetables. The set menu has four, six or eight courses; its vegetarian counterpart comes in a four- or five-course format. The service is friendly and the wine recommendations helpful. In the attractive courtyard, there is also a bakery, a farm shop and a farm café, as well as a hotel. Alternatively, Hasenpfeffer is open in the evenings for traditional dishes with modern influences.

Name: James Farmhouse
Description: Fresh and tasty cuisine is served here, and the menu is strongly influenced by the restaurant's own farm. For example, they raise their own Husum red pied pigs, chickens and German Angus cattle – exceptionally tender rump steaks guaranteed. The decor is a blend of industrial chic and charming retro style. Very friendly service. There is a smaller menu at lunchtime. Alongside the restaurants Das Grace and Minato, this is another dining option at the Hotel Das James, which enjoys a charming location on the harbour.

Name: Landgasthof Adler
Description: This centuries-old inn has long been known in the region for serving good food. Since February 2022, chef Michael Vogel has been perpetuating this tradition as the chef-patron with great dedication – he had already worked here years earlier and took over the reins after a stint under top chef Andreas Caminada. The restaurant serves seasonally inspired dishes, available as a surprise menu or à la carte. The inviting decor seamlessly blends tradition and modern design. Tip: The charming guestrooms complement the restaurant perfectly and reflect the establishment's distinctive character.

Name: mondi
Description: Owner Pelle Kossmann and his young team are committed to implementing their own culinary ideas here. The set menu changes every fortnight and is made with select seasonal ingredients sourced from regional producers; some of the livestock and vegetables are raised or grown exclusively for this restaurant. The chefs also adhere to the principle of nose-to-tail eating. The decor is sleek and modern, with a partially visible kitchen and friendly, laid-back service. Fixed charge for table water.

Name: Ratsstube
Description: Antje and Ronny Pester's charming restaurant is in the centre of the village, in the side building of the town hall. In a lovely cosy interior, they serve up ambitious modern cuisine that follows the seasons. Plump for either the à la carte menu to be found in the "Gourmet Bistro" section or the four- to six-course set menu dubbed "Menü Restaurant" – a vegetarian version of which can be pre-ordered. The service is attentive and obliging, and the owner's wine recommendations are spot on. There is a lovely terrace to the rear of the building.

Name: Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Bistro is housed in Parkhotel Quellenhof, the flagship of Aachen's hotel scene – the marble lobby and the fireplace and tearoom with its exquisite wood panelling are well worth seeing. Classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences is served in a stylish, minimalist-style dining space. The appealing evening menu features dishes such as Black Angus beef tartare with brioche, lobster foam soup with lobster ravioli and tarragon, and Wiener schnitzel with potato and cucumber salad, as well as vegetarian options. There is a smaller selection of dishes available at lunchtime and a snack menu in the afternoon. The terrace overlooking the park is a delightful spot.

Name: Beetle
Description: Environmental awareness and sustainability have always been key in every aspect of this restaurant certified as organic – from the tasteful interior design to the staff uniform and not least the food. Following a change of concept, the menu now features meat and fish alongside the tried-and-tested vegetarian and vegan dishes. Mouthwatering options include radicchio risotto with pan-fried oyster mushrooms and mushroom foam, or brook trout meunière with brown butter, almonds, lemon, creamed spinach and potato mousseline. The front-of-house team is exceptionally friendly and attentive. Most of the wines – which are from Germany, Austria and Italy/South Tyrol – are organic or biodynamic. Lovely covered terrace.

Name: Schorse im Leineschloss
Description: This pleasantly down-to-earth restaurant is the second in the cube-like extension of the Leineschloss, along with Votum. The flavoursome food is made with select ingredients and draws on French influences. The fish soup or the pulpo salad are tasty, for example. They also serve a simpler quick lunch set menu. Delightful terraces at the Leinewehr and on Platz der Göttinger Sieben.

Name: YOSO Asian Comfort Food
Description: Peter Fridén, who also heads up the kitchen at PURS in Andernach, calls his concept "Asian Comfort Food". Serving up sushi and sashimi, as well as dishes such as shoyu ramen, bao chasu and chicken yakitori, he is dedicated to showcasing Far Eastern flavours. Perfectly suited for sharing, these dishes can also be ordered online to take away. The dining space has a chic urban feel, featuring sleek modern design with a Far Eastern touch. The restaurant is located in the historical centre of Andernach right by the boutique hotel Am Ochsentor. Italian trattoria Ai Pero is next door.

Name: Renoir
Description: This restaurant has been building on a solid reputation for over 30 years, serving classic cuisine and a sophisticated yet pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere. Delicious dishes are served as a seasonal menu comprising three to five courses or à la carte. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the maître d', who happens to be a trained sommelier. Tip: The small gallery in the building is definitely worth a visit.

Name: Restaurant zum Bären
Description: The Buggle family has been running this traditional restaurant in the idyllic Lahn Valley since 1827 and chef Joachim Buggle represents the eighth generation to take the helm. He has brought in an impressive concept revolving around culinary classics, serving flavour-intensive, unpretentious dishes. Appetising examples include braised venison shoulder with house-made spaetzle, wild cranberries and glazed pointed cabbage, or grilled calamaretti with lemon risoni, green asparagus and a crustacean foam. Food is served from noon to 9pm Thu-Sun. There is a three-course lunch menu Thu-Sat. On certain dates, they propose a four-course surprise menu. With its beautiful country-style interior, the restaurant has a pleasant, cosy atmosphere; the Weinstube exudes a slightly more rustic feel. And they have another ace up their sleeve in the form of a wonderful terrace in the shade of the lime trees! The front-of-house team provides charming and cordial service… and Landhotel zum Bären is an excellent overnight option.

Name: AS am See
Description: "AS" refers to both the lakeside location (am See: Scharmützelsee) and the initials of chef-patron Andreas Staack. In this inviting, friendly place – a cross between a wine bar and a bistro – the affable owner devises a five-course menu out of his modern dishes, such as "gnocchi, morel cream, sot-l'y-laisse" and "sea bass, fennel, mussel cream". The quality of the ingredients is top notch, and the bill is good value for money. On Sundays, the set menu is available at lunchtime. The restaurant is nestled in a side street in a quiet, leafy residential area a stone's throw from the spa gardens. It also has a lovely terrace. Tip: Take a walk around the picturesque lake before your meal.

Name: Heiligenstein
Description: Come here to enjoy classic seasonal cuisine in an inviting, modern atmosphere. High-quality, fresh ingredients are prepared in an agreeably straightforward way that brings out their flavour. Choose between an à la carte menu and a three- or four-course set menu. Then there's the excellent wine list featuring over 400 selections. In summer, tables are laid out on a wonderful terrace.
