The hotel boasts a peaceful location and lovely cosy guestrooms – and the abundance of greenery and surrounding forest mean it is also a good starting point for hikes.

Name: moriki
Description: Situated very close to the Festspielhaus (opera and concert house), the restaurant of Roomers hotel serves pan-Asian cuisine and a wide range of sushi. The menu reads, for example, "sake teriyaki – Scottish salmon, teriyaki glaze, sweet cucumber, rice". In a setting that is upscale and very much on trend, a young and enthusiastic front-of-house team provides competent service while maintaining a laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Bar Mural
Description: This hip bar is loud, lively and trendy – and therein lies its charm! In addition to the regularly changing à la carte selection of high-quality small bites and delicious dishes – also suitable for sharing – there is a wallet-friendly four-course set menu ("Chef's Choice"). For drink recommendations, just ask the proficient and laid-back waitstaff. The moderately priced wine list includes a decent selection of wines by the glass. For al fresco dining, tables are laid out on the terrace in the courtyard behind the restaurant and on the pavement in front of the building.

Name: Kaminstube
Description: The stylish and elegant dining area boasts the fireplace after which this restaurant is named. Classic and traditional cuisine with international influences is served – small portions are also possible. The terrace with a view of the Ellbachtal is popular in summer.

Name: Asam Schlössl
Description: In his charming restaurant, nestled in the historical Asam Schlössl of 1687 just outside the city centre, Irish-born Shane McMahon expertly weaves his personal touch into delicious Bavarian cuisine. The menu features hearty classics such as roast pork with cracklings and dark beer jus, as well as modern dishes such as barbecued octopus with spicy ox muzzle salad, and steaks done on the Big Green Egg or the "Schlössl Sharing Brettl" (an assortment of snacks for sharing). Both the atmospheric rustic interior and the secluded Schlösslgarten are inviting . Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Gasthaus Sonne
Description: In this historic inn with a lovely half-timbered façade and a cosy rural-style feel inside, the young owner serves up dishes such as braised knuckle of pasture-raised lamb with Madeira, or pike-perch fillet with chanterelles. The terrace lies under a big old chestnut tree. There are also guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: CARTE BLANCHE
Description: Housed within SO/ Berlin Das Stue hotel, on the edge of the Großer Tiergarten and right next to the Spanish Embassy, this restaurant is not to be missed. The modern, elegant and cosy design fosters a relaxed atmosphere that puts diners in mind of an upscale living room. The French-influenced cuisine includes classics such as beef tartare, grilled entrecôte or moules marinières. You can also sip on an aperitif or digestif in Stue Bar, which is right next to the restaurant. In fine weather, the quiet, leafy courtyard terrace is a lovely spot – exclusive access for hotel patrons to the Zoo Berlin is a real highlight of staying here! Tip: An attractively priced set menu is served at lunchtime.

Name: am kai | restaurnt. seafood. drinks. elbblick
Description: This pleasant restaurant right on the waterfront is trendy, hip and relaxed, and offers a super view of the container port – especially from the terrace in summer! The kitchen serves modern seafood dishes such as "prawn tempura, kimchi, nuoc cham, passion fruit" and "monkfish BBQ, grilled corn, plum, tarragon". Meat eaters, too, are bound to find something to their liking; there are also vegetarian/vegan options. In addition to a varied à la carte selection, the restaurant offers a seasonal menu and a sharing menu (for two or more people).

Name: Brasserie Ehrlich
Description: A French-style brasserie par excellence. Stephan Fröhlich and his wife Nadine run their small restaurant with a personal touch – he is the head chef and she is the sommelier. In this cosy setting, diners can look forward to friendly service and good seasonal cuisine in the form of two set menus. Given the popularity of the place, it is advisable to book in advance. In summer the gorgeous terrace beckons. Tip: Delicatessen goods can be purchased to take home. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: 893 Ryotei
Description: The mirrored, graffiti-covered façade gives no hint of the restaurant that lies behind it. But despite appearances, this restaurant is a hit, drawing in diners in their droves. The trendy interior is done out in black and furnished with small tables. Guests bask in a lively atmosphere that centres around the open kitchen. Here, The Duc Ngo serves up a wide range of Japanese cuisine, infused with other Asian, South American and European influences, incorporating a wealth of spices. The menu includes traditional favourites such as sushi, sashimi, tempura and tataki, as well as more creative options like "sashimi taquitos", "tai yuzu truffle" and "unagi royal".

Name: Tischlein Deck Dich by Lilly
Description: Having worked at Lilly in Neupotz, Stefan Echle (service) and Matthis Nowak (kitchen) have found their new vocation – in the vaulted cellar of the separately run Villa Königsgarten hotel (formerly Weingut Diehl). A few steps lead down from the courtyard to the restaurant. As you make your way to the dining area, you can take a peek into the glass-paned kitchen, while the modern, seasonal set menu, which offers a choice of options for each course, is being prepared. The three-course surprise menu on Wednesdays and Thursdays is also worth a look. Named after a fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm (The Lying Goat), the restaurant has a modern, elegant interior with historical details. Great service comes courtesy of a friendly and well-trained front-of-house team. The idyllic location in a village surrounded by vineyards, at the foothills of the Palatinate Forest, offers endless possibilities for excursions.

Name: Schupps
Description: Regina and Markus Schupp, after whom this restaurant is named, are both professionally trained chefs. Here they rustle up seasonal dishes inspired by the cuisines of France and Germany. Delicious examples include scallops au gratin with green asparagus, Jerusalem artichoke and almond, or venison ragout with cranberries, Brussels sprout leaves and sour cream. Those who wish to savour a more extensive meal can put together their own set menu comprising three to five courses for a fixed price. At lunchtime, the inexpensive daily specials are ideal for a quick meal. This friendly little restaurant also has a terrace for sunny days. Tip: free parking available along the street.

Name: ICHI
Description: If you are looking to experience Japanese cuisine in Kiel, this city-centre restaurant with a modern and minimalist design is just the place. Laid out over two levels and boasting floor-to-ceiling windows, it extends diners a very warm welcome. Authentic Japanese dishes including sushi and sashimi are conjured up in the partially visible kitchen. Order à la carte or opt for a set menu – vegan options are also available. The restaurant is conveniently located close to the pedestrian area and the harbour with its cruise terminals. Tip: Park your car in the Schlossgarage, which is just a 3min walk away.

Name: Stilbruch
Description: This smart restaurant proposes a surprise menu comprising four to seven courses, in which good use is made not only of regional but also international ingredients. Diners are treated to dishes such as Atlantic cod with spinach cream, wild broccoli, king oyster mushrooms, walnuts and a Parmesan beurre blanc. A vegan set menu is also available. The friendly and courteous front-of-house team will also be able to help you choose the perfect bottle of wine. In summer, secure yourself a spot on the cosy terrace.

Name: NaNum
Description: As soon as you enter the restaurant, you can see into the open kitchen, where chef Jinok Kim puts a modern spin on the culinary traditions of her Korean homeland. Using regional ingredients, some from the restaurant's own garden in Brandenburg, she shows a particular interest in fermented foods. The ingredient-led dishes are beautifully precise. Natural wines accompany the five-course set menu (vegetarian or with meat) served on Wednesdays and Thursdays, and the seven-course set menu (vegetarian or with fish) available on Fridays and Saturdays. The space is pleasantly pared back and the service is very friendly. Jinok Kim is also a ceramicist and makes the crockery on which the dishes are served – the studio is also located in the building. The restaurant is located not far from Checkpoint Charlie, on a small square (with a lovely terrace) opposite the Jewish Museum.

Name: STUBN in der Frasdorfer Hütte
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace
Description: This exclusive mountain-top location, surrounded by woods and meadows, really is the stuff of dreams. What was once a hiking lodge is now a cosy restaurant serving modern Alpine cuisine that can only be reached on foot (50 minutes from the Lederstube car park) or by booking a shuttle bus. Diners seated at the front can see the chefs at work in the open kitchen, grilling top-quality produce over an open fire. A shining example is the super-fresh Chiemsee pike-perch with bold roasted aromas, accompanied by an intensely flavoursome Jerusalem artichoke puree and crunchy rapini – a delightfully accessible combination. You can choose à la carte from a short list of options or have a surprise menu put together for you. The evening menu is also available at lunchtime, if requested in advance. The wine list is very well curated and the waitstaff are highly adept. The terrace is wonderful in summer! Simple guestrooms can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: HIO
Description: "HIO" is the nickname of the small village that is home to this restaurant. In the five-course tasting menu proposed here, vegetables take centre stage. Much of the produce comes from the restaurant's own garden, which is right by the house, or from local farmers. The chic and modern interior incorporates a smattering of rustic touches, with the open kitchen being a focal point. With just 16 places, the restaurant has something akin to a family atmosphere, and the service is friendly, pleasingly laid-back and professional. Upon arrival, guests are taken outside to enjoy hors-d'oeuvres by the charcoal grill and hear about the sustainable philosophy in place here. In addition to HIO, HILZHOF also houses another restaurant – MEIER – plus a handful of guestrooms.

Name: Lemabri
Description: Despite its somewhat unusual location in an industrial estate, this restaurant run by Sarah Henke and Christian Eckhardt has diners coming in droves. Building on successful stints in Andernach ( at YOSO and PURS respectively), the duo set up shop here with a casual and varied concept. In a spacious setting with chic modern interior design, the kitchen team serves up a wide-ranging selection of plates that are perfect for sharing. The extensive menu includes Asian and regional dishes, as well as pasta and fantastic pizzas from the large Morello Forni pizza oven. Children are also welcome – they will love the children's menu and play area.

Name: Zum Wendl
Description: This restaurant dating back to 1889 has a long history to its name. Today, Bavarian-style cuisine is the name of the game, presented in both traditional and modern guises. Fine examples include Bavarian Forest venison roulade stuffed with smoked meat, cranberries and pickled vegetables, mashed parsnip and potato, and a red cabbage roll, or pan-fried Breitenberg char with wild broccoli, spicy curry carrot puree, aniseed crust and lime foam. Alternatively, "Signature Dishes" such as Wiener schnitzel, cordon bleu and roast onion are available. We also recommend the two three- to four-course menus. The restaurant is housed in the hotel of the same name, which has a small spa area. This a great place to spend the night – then you can take full advantage of the excellent wine list. It features a good 180 items and is mostly devoted to German wines, especially Riesling.

Name: Die Speiserei im Maier
Description: The restaurant at Hotel Maier (a family-run establishment since its founding as a café and guesthouse in 1936) serves cuisine that showcases fresh seasonal regional produce; it is also, for the most part, organic and sourced as locally as possible. Order à la carte or opt for a three- to five-course set menu. In the inviting space, the original traditional character has been preserved, but given an elegant update courtesy of discreet modern accents. There is also a spacious courtyard terrace for those who enjoy dining al fresco. Friendly and professional service.

Name: Caro's
Description: Having relocated within Tübingen, Caro's now boasts a prime location right by the Neckar River. The interior decor is sleek and modern, and the contemporary cuisine includes vegetarian and vegan options, with dishes ranging from yellowfin tuna tatare to stuffed kohlrabi and roast poussin. Opt for the set menu or go à la carte. There is also a bar. Tip: Delicious food items can be purchased to take home.

Name: Springbrunnen SKLENAR
Description: After almost 30 years in Mallorca, Czech-born Martin Sklenar and his wife Lucie swapped the Balearic island for the vineyards of Oberkirch. In their restaurant, they propose an interesting blend of regional (Baden), Mallorcan and Bohemian-inspired cuisine. This is served in a cosy interior with a slightly rustic feel, or out on the wonderful terrace known as the Weinberggarten. There is also a vegetarian/vegan set menu. The ingredient-led dishes can be accompanied by your choice of wine from a predominantly regional selection.

Name: [w]einklang
Description: A cosy atmosphere reigns in this chic little restaurant in the northwest of Nuremberg, with wine racks adding a nice decorative touch. In this setting, chef-owner Tomas Spanu serves a four- or five-course set menu, of which a vegetarian version is also an option, and an à la carte menu. The chef – who, as it happens, is of Sardinian-French heritage – cooks in a pleasingly streamlined and ingredient-led style. The friendly and attentive service is the icing on the cake. You'll definitely want to keep coming back for more! NIAN BISTRO is also part of the establishment.

Name: Limbourg
Description: A wonderful addition to the Belgian Quarter's fine dining scene. The atmosphere is pleasingly laid-back and the vibe tasteful, whether you dine in the ground-floor space or at BelEtage. Chef-patron Alen Radic showcases his cosmopolitan cuisine, which draws on French influences and is made with fresh, good-quality ingredients – served as a five- or nine-course set menu of which there are two versions: "classique" and "veggie". During the week, there is also a five-course lunch, which includes dishes from the evening menu. The sheltered courtyard terrace is particularly inviting in summer.

Name: Lovis
Description: An impressive architectural feat – a former prison has been transformed into an attractive restaurant. High ceilings and exposed brick walls, sleek interior design and a great lighting concept make for a special atmosphere. Diners take their seats in the former lock yard, now covered and fitted with large windows – the "Aquarium" room is truly original. The modern vegetable-oriented cuisine is available as a set menu or à la carte – regular, vegetarian or also vegan upon request. A selection of wines from around the globe. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif in the lovely bar, which also boasts a terrace. You can enjoy a night in Wilmina, the adjacent hotel.

Name: Die Bürgermeisterei 1728
Description: A location steeped in history in which to enjoy a meal! The lovingly restored building, which gives directly onto the market square, was once the mayor's residence and dates back to 1728. The elegant fusion of modern style and historical details lends the place atmosphere. The evening menu is ambitious, fresh and full of flavour, with appetising options such as beef bourgignon, dried fig crumble and potato-parsnip mash. The small selection of seasonal dishes is also proposed in the form of set menus, one of which is vegetarian. In summer, make the most of the secluded terrace.

Name: Fachwerk
Description: Semi Hassine and Patrizia Weidemann-Hassine run this restaurant in the old town, where exposed timber beams lend the space a charming rustic feel. The lovely terrace commands a view of the old half-timbered façades all around. On the menu: Westphalian cuisine with Mediterranean and subtle Eastern influences. Tip: the attractive changing seasonal set menu. Hot food is served from 4pm; on Saturdays from noon, all day.

Name: BEES Restaurant
Address: Am Rottland 6, Rüdesheim am Rhein, 65385, Germany
Description: This attractive restaurant serving appealing seasonal cuisine is housed in the premises of a former Asbach Uralt brandy distillery. The set menu includes a minimum of four courses, but you can also order à la carte. Sit back to savour your meal and enjoy friendly service in this chic setting with a partially visible kitchen. Tables are set up to create a pleasant terrace in summer. Tip for motorists: there is also a public car park near the train station and the Rhine.

Name: Eulenstein
Description: Taking its cue from the seasons and made with select ingredients, the food here is meticulously prepared, flavoursome and fresh – it is clear that chef Steve Eulenstein has worked at some top-flight establishments in his time. He proposes two set menus as well as classics such as rump steak. The dining space is attractive and minimalist in style, and the service is friendly and professional. The location in a residential area just a few minutes' drive from the BAB 3 motorway is also convenient.

Name: Pierburg - Erika Bergheim
Description: Located in the rural outskirts of Essen, Pierburg has been welcoming diners since 1901. With many years of experience in the top league of gastronomy under her belt, Erika Bergheim is now at the helm, cooking up internationally and seasonally inspired dishes. You can choose from the à la carte selection, named "Pierburg Karte", or opt for the "Selection E.B." set menu – the individual courses can be ordered à la carte, too. There is also an extensive, well-curated wine list. Friendly service and a tasteful contemporary setting, with certain tables affording a glimpse into the kitchen. Gorgeous terrace.

Name: Weinbistro "George"
Description: This bistro, too, is definitely worth a visit. The second dining option in the Weinhaus Uhle hotel is at once a wine shop and an appealing restaurant and is open all day long. Seated at wooden tables in an attractive space, you enjoy à la carte dishes or a three- or four-course menu. For chef Marcel Kube and his team, regional ingredients are key. Classics include "Die Fischsuppe" (fish soup) and "Der Uhlsche Klops" (meatballs). There is also a good wine selection. In summer, tables are set up on the street out front.

Name: vierzehn 85
Description: The former tithe farm from 1485 - still with a beautiful half-timbered facade - offers homely, modern guest rooms and a very nice, tasteful and casual restaurant on two floors with smaller and larger rooms and charming niches. The kitchen serves really good contemporary dishes from many regional and always seasonal products. Wines from the own vineyard. In summer, the terrace is inviting.

Name: Wibbelings Hof
Description: Sandra and Jörn Haumann have turned the family-owned estate, which dates back to 1899, into a charming restaurant. While he takes care of the service, she prepares an ambitious set menu that takes its cue from the seasons; some of the ingredients are home-grown. Food is served in a lovely high-ceilinged room, whose modern interior design incorporates decorative features such as a wine rack, a workbench and large pictures. This space also makes an ideal venue for events and weddings. Tip: the farm shop (open on Wed and Thu afternoons).

Name: PULS
Description: With this culinary hotspot located in the chic boutique hotel Legend, Daniel Gottschlich (known from Ox & Klee) has another restaurant concept to his name in the cathedral city. The vibe here is lively, modern and urban. You can dine at the bar, at one of the high tables or at a regular table. In summer, there is the gorgeous terrace. Johannes Langenstück's kitchen team serves up bar food as well as dishes for sharing – also available in individual portions. Or would you prefer the surprise menu "Chefs Choice"? Decent wine list and an appealing cocktail selection including their "Signature" drinks.

Name: Minato
Description: This is just one of the options in the diverse range of restaurants within the Das James hotel, which is housed in a former naval building at the marina. Here you can look forward to truly authentic Japanese cuisine in the form of two set menus: the "James Sushi Menu" and the "Omakase" surprise menu. The chic design with a subtle Far Eastern touch and the friendly, competent service create a harmonious atmosphere. Minato is an appealing alternative to the restaurant's Das Grace and James Farmhouse and, as such, has many regular guests.

Name: Westerndorfer Stube
Description: Housed in Landgasthof Karner, this cosy eatery makes for a lovely down-to-earth alternative to the adjacent fine dining restaurant. The outstanding chef, Hannes Fussel, proves that he is also a master of home-style cooking, turning seemingly simple dishes into a delight for the palate! Think lamb lights, Wiener schnitzel or the classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) – diners are bowled over by the depth of flavour and presentation. Regional ingredients take centre stage, and the decor complements this perfectly: rustic charm and subtle modern elements make for a harmonious whole.

Name: Oukan
Description: It's worth seeking out this restaurant, the entrance of which is a bit hidden. A long, mirrored corridor leads you to an interior characterised by distinctive architecture and a clean-lined, minimalist, Far Eastern design. The food is no less interesting: The Japanese-inspired cuisine is completely vegan, with fermented food playing a major role – hence having built their own Fermentation Lab. The creative seven-course set menu can be extended by an additional course. The dishes seem pleasingly pared back, although a lot of effort has gone into them. An individual signature is evident, for example, in the delicate maitake with robust roasted aromas and a subtle note of thyme, accompanied by a sensational sauce made from mushrooms, sake, port wine, vanilla and coffee, which inspires with fantastic depth. The intriguing tea pairings are an absolute must! Top-notch teas are celebrated here and presented in depth. It is also possible to go for a mixture of tea and other drinks pairings.

Name: plaisir by Hamid Heidarzadeh
Description: The minimalist, elegant look immediately catches the eye, with its gorgeous terrazzo flooring, clean-lined, pared-back design in black and white, and high ceilings with stunning mouldings. Chef Hamid Heidarzadeh blends classic foundations and modern elements to interesting effect, incorporating subtle Asian and Mediterranean influences. Two set menus are available in a three- or five-course format – one vegetarian ("Pflanzenfresser/-innen"), one with meat ("Fleischfresser/-innen"). The names belie finely tuned and precisely crafted dishes with full-bodied taste profiles, such as the boldly seasoned tartare of Balfego tuna with hints of spiciness courtesy of jalapeno cream, and beautiful layers of acidity thanks to the vinegar mayonnaise, as well as the freshness of subtly sweet grapefruit ice cream, plated on an aromatic salad of finely diced tomatoes. The laid-back yet discreet service is pleasant, and the chefs also join in with the service.

Name: Café GUPI
Description: Set up in what was the gardener's house on a historical country estate, this is the trendy restaurant-bar concept of the Düster and Schneider restaurateur and winemaking families. Their tasty modern dishes made with seasonal ingredients are served à la carte or as a set menu. In summer, the terrace shaded by the large trees of the lovely Läublin Park is highly inviting. The name of the restaurant is derived from the regional "GuPi" wines (Gutedel and Pinot Noir). Tip: Booking advisable.

Name: Ursprung
Description: This smart restaurant is set in the family-run Hotel Aquarium, which is located in the heart of the beautiful city centre. With Jan Boddenberg, the third generation is now at the helm. As head chef, he curates a modern set menu and delivers classic, regional dishes, attaching importance to good produce and seasonality. Friendly service.

Name: Goldmund
Address: Schöne Aussicht 2, Frankfurt on the Main, 60311, Germany
Description: The restaurant in the Literaturhaus, set on the banks of the Main, has an extremely stylish and upscale interior. The large bar area and the striking portraits of international figures from the arts draw the eye as you savour food that tends towards the classical. The adjoining Kaminzimmer ("fireplace room") is also very pleasant. Plenty of places to park behind the restaurant. This address is also ideal as an event location.

Name: Weinstube Baldreit
Description: This lovely wine tavern may be somewhat hidden away in its pleasantly quiet location, but it is well worth seeking out – especially in summer, when the charming secluded courtyard terrace comes into its own. Along with a relaxed atmosphere with rustic charm and friendly service, diners can look forward to an array of different flammkuchen, speciality mussel dishes and regional classics. The seasonal specials of the day are written up on a wooden board or presented verbally. The restaurant has plenty of regulars and is always busy, so it's advisable to make a reservation!

Name: Sorriso
Address: Oppenheimer Landstr. 49, Frankfurt on the Main, 60596, Germany
Description: In a smart building occupying a corner plot in the Sachsenhausen district, this tastefully designed restaurant serves modern Mediterranean-inspired cuisine made with top-notch ingredients. There are two set menus, one of which is 100% vegan. The owner has some great wine recommendations up his sleeve. Pleasant terrace for summer.

Name: Küppersmühle Restaurant
Description: A fantastic location with an old industrial atmosphere, view of the inner harbour, and terrace right by the water. This urban-style interior is the backdrop for ambitious modern cuisine with and international influences – the menu includes, for example, tataki of Faroe salmon with buttermilk and coriander broth. At lunchtime, there is a slightly different menu, with a selection from the evening menu. In the KÜ shop, you can buy many delicious items to enjoy at home. Tip: The Küppersmühle Museum right next door is worth a visit.

Name: Inspektorenhaus
Description: In the city centre, opposite the brick-built Gothic town hall, is the Inspektorenhaus, from which the inspector used to keep an eye on the market and the activity it harboured. Nowadays it is a restaurant with a cosy ambience and distinct charm, thanks to old wooden beams and pretty decorations. In summer, you can sit outside in the courtyard garden. Two seasonal set menus are served, one with fish, one with meat. Friendly service.

The Stadtgarten Pavilion (1936) has been given a new lease of life with a trendy-chic feel, plus a good dose of glamour! The ingredient-led cuisine blends modern and classic techniques. Food is served throughout the day: The "Business Lunch" is available until 3pm, daily specials until 5pm. In the evening, there is a broader range of options. Diners can opt for a set menu featuring à la carte dishes for both lunch and dinner. Those in the mood for classics such as Wiener schnitzel or beef goulash, or who prefer a pizza, will not be disappointed. The terrace overlooking the small park is lovely. Very good, wide-ranging wine list. For a classic bar experience, check out Pino's Bar, which also has an outdoor lounge.

Name: Dae Mon
Description: This chic and rather stylish restaurant is an interesting option. The food is dubbed "open-minded cuisine": modern dishes that combine the techniques and flavours of Japanese and Korean cuisine in a variety of ways – for example, street food influences make their presence felt. There is also a creative vegetarian version of the set menu. Tip: As an alternative to wine, they propose a beautifully curated cold Asian tea pairing – a real treat for all those who like to go alcohol-free.

Name: Diekmann
Description: In the mood for the charm of a typical bistro setting? At the front, amid decorative wine racks from an old colonial goods shop, is a casual dining area with high tables positioned around a free-standing oyster bar. Alternatively, nab one of the small tables in the charming minimalist-style space at the back of the premises. In the evening, ambitious French and German dishes are served à la carte or as a tasting menu. Lunchtime options are more limited but moderately priced – water, bread and espresso are included. The impressive oyster menu is available at both mealtimes.

Name: Broeding
Description: This lively restaurant is an institution in Neuhausen. In an outwardly unassuming-looking building on a residential street, diners tuck into delicious, pared-back dishes made with excellent ingredients (mostly organic or Demeter-certified) sourced in the Alpine and pre-Alpine regions. From Mon-Thu, diners can opt for a three- to five-course version of the set menu; Fri-Sat, there is just the one five-course variant – or if you arrive at 6pm, you can go for the three-course early evening set menu. The pleasingly laid-back atmosphere is in no small part down to the friendly, attentive and unpretentious service, which comes complete with expert guidance when it comes to the terrific wine list, which focuses on Austrian wine-growing regions. In summer, the secluded inner courtyard terrace beckons. Tip: From 3pm onwards, Austrian wines can be purchased from the well-stocked wine shop to enjoy at home.

Name: Höfli
Description: The charming Höfli blends seamlessly into the picturesque old town setting. The enchanting cobblestone courtyard invites you to dine under the summer sky, surrounded by historical walls and half-timbered buildings. The interior is just as pleasant with its sleek, contemporary feel. While maître d' Alexandra Killy ensures a warm welcome, her husband, Marco, prepares delicious and neatly crafted dishes. His classical training shines through in dishes such as foie gras tiramisu with mascarpone, quince, coffee and brioche, or John Dory with fregola sarda and a pointed pepper broth.

Name: Drexlers
Description: Since 2007, this bright, modern restaurant right next to Colombipark has been something of an institution in Freiburg. Service is friendly and adept and the atmosphere warm and welcoming. Showcasing regional produce and sustainable practices, the ambitious seasonally inspired cuisine draws on French and Italian influences. The four- to six-course set menu comes in a "classic" or vegetarian version. On Mondays and Thursdays you can also order individual courses à la carte. Great selection of reasonably priced wines – courtesy of their own wine shop. Tip for motorists: Rotteck underground car park is within walking distance.

Name: Franziska
Address: Hainer Weg 72, Frankfurt on the Main, 60599, Germany
Description: It takes 40 seconds in the lift up to the top of the Henninger Turm. As well as its magnificent views over the Frankfurt skyline, this restaurant proposes "Progressive German Vintage Cuisine". The name is a tribute to the great-aunt of the Mook Group founder. Cocktails in the Barrel Bar. Terrace one floor down. Online bookings only.

Name: Krone
Description: You will feel at home here for a number of reasons. Not only can you enjoy the modern, classic and seasonal cuisine showcasing local produce, but there is also the friendly, attentive service that comes courtesy of the owner and her team, who also know their way around the wine list. The elegantly pared-down interior is equally inviting, not to mention the beautiful garden with shaded seating that draws diners in summer. Well-kept guestrooms are available should you wish to stay the night.

Name: Waldhorn
Description: This restaurant in Stuttgart's Rohr neighbourhood serves an intriguing take on classic French cuisine that draws on Spanish and Swabian influences. This concept wasn't simply plucked out of thin air: the two chefs – José María González Sampedro, who hails from Mallorca, and Caroline Autenrieth from Swabia – met while working in a restaurant in Marseille. The six courses on their surprise menu include deliciously aromatic lamb and braised shallot with a filling of blood sausage ragout with Mediterranean spices. At lunchtime, a three-course menu is offered. In the attractive seating area, old wood panelling and modern furnishings add to the charm.

Name: Genießer Stube - Daniel Raub
Description: Daniel Raub represents the third generation at the helm of this family-run business. At Genießer Stube, one of the restaurants of Romantik Hotel Landhaus Biewald, he serves up classic French-based cuisine with a seasonal focus, eschewing any frills and putting his ingredients centre stage. In the evening there is the set menu ("Genießer Menü") that comes in four, six or eight courses. You can also opt for fine wine pairings. The wine list is also worth a look. In winter, food is served in the cosy dining room with its old wooden beamed ceiling. In summer, you can also dine in the conservatory or on the terrace. Professional service is provided by a charming front-of-house team. The second restaurant, Zur Tränke, is housed in the newly constructed modern hotel building. In addition to comfortable accommodation, overnight guests can look forward to a fantastic breakfast. Tip: Museum Friedland is just round the corner.

Name: KIKU Restaurant by Jan Fribus
Description: Kiku means "chrysanthemum" – the Japanese national flower – and, indeed, the cuisine here is strongly marked by Japanese elements, along with seasonal influences and the odd subtle classic French touch. Comprising eight courses, the set menu features dishes such as dim sum with prawns and bisque, and hibachi venison with pumpkin and hoisin. The restaurant is located in a tastefully restored historical building in a small street lined with half-timbered façades, not far from the city centre. Inside, the atmosphere is laid back and elegant, and there is a secluded terrace in the courtyard. The service is friendly and informal – the charming chefs also come to your table to talk you through their dishes. A short yet carefully curated wine list complements the food perfectly, and most wines are available by the glass. Tip: Just upstairs from the restaurant, Anno 1560 offers cosy and stylish apartments.

Name: dario&
Description: The chef behind the name is Dario Breuer. He serves modern, creative dishes that are pleasingly minimalist and clearly structured. The "&" in the name deliberately leaves plenty of room for interpretation, because everyone should feel at home here – whether you like laid-back or ambitious cuisine, whether you are here for a meal with friends or colleagues, whether you want to push the boat out or perhaps just drop in for a glass of wine. True, indeed, to its byline: "casual fine dining". They offer a set menu with four, six, seven or nine courses, and a vegetarian option is also available. The wine list is impressive, with more than 300 items, including big names as well as new finds and a champagne section.

Name: fine.wine.dine.
Description: Located in the pedestrian area, not far from the Rhine River, this modern yet cosy little restaurant serves ambitious seasonal cuisine in the evening. You can either order the set menu or choose à la carte; on Wednesday and Thursday evenings there is also an appealing sharing menu for two. Vegetarian options are also available if ordered in advance. For lunch, there are simpler, more moderately priced daily specials. Delicatessen goods and wine can be purchased to enjoy at home.

Name: Laesâ
Description: Murrhardther Hof, a culinary institution since 1920, has launched an inspired new concept. What sets it apart is that all diners are seated at a long solid-beechwood table – perfect for mingling, but with enough space for this not to be obligatory. From your seat, you can even catch a glimpse of the open kitchen, where Moritz Bilsing and Emilio Löffler run the show. Dishes are clearly and thoughtfully composed – pared down to the essentials, almost to the point of minimalism. A fine example, with harmonious flavours and delicate contrasts, is the rolled turbot fillet: moist and tender, served with a dollop of wonderfully salty fine-beaded caviar, as well as aromatic barley, sweet apricots and a mild, buttery curry sauce. The single set menu comes in four to six courses, which are punctuated by refined little extras. The experience is complemented by the expert and friendly service, with sommelier Nikolas Reidt providing excellent wine recommendations. As an alternative to wine, there are interesting house-made alcohol-free pairings to go with the set menu.

Name: Zauberberg
Description: The name translates as "magic mountain", and the name is fitting for a number of reasons. For one, dedicated host Claudia Kimbacher, who adds a pleasantly personal touch to the service with her remarkably warm manner and is also happy to assist you in choosing your wines. Then there is Sven Gerlach's cuisine, which comes in the form of a surprise menu comprising five to six modern and creative courses. If you would like a vegetarian option, please indicate this when making your reservation. From January to November, a three-course "Work Day Supper" set menu is also available Tue-Thu by advance booking. As for the restaurant itself, inside the atmosphere is friendly with an elegant feel to the decor; outside there is a lovely terrace that is very popular on warm summer evenings.

Name: The Wild Duck
Description: This young and fresh addition to Hanover's fine dining scene is proving to be a hit – and with good reason. Part of the appeal is the upscale and tastefully trendy decor. Diners are also attracted by the modern and pleasingly pared-down cuisine. In the evening, dishes such as duck, chicory, black garlic and plum, or seaweed, aubergine and Thai curry are served in the form of a set menu – vegetarian and vegan options are available too. The friendly waitstaff will gladly recommend the perfect wine accompaniment.

Name: IL Sommelier
Description: Behind the unassuming façade of a modern building in the Trudering district, this is a real gem of a restaurant. In the chic, contemporary space, diners are served authentic, flavoursome, down-to-earth cucina italiana. The dishes on the menu are sophisticated but not pretentious, and include tortelli with a cheese and aubergine filling or beef cheek braised with sweet potato mash. The wine list features Italian wines exclusively. In summer, the quiet terrace to the rear of the property beckons.

Name: Waldschlössle
Description: After driving past seemingly endless rows of vines, you will eventually reach this small vineyard, where a traditional mountain inn has been reimagined as a trendy and modern dining destination. Floor-to-ceiling windows showcase breathtaking panoramic views of the region. There is also a terrace. "Fine Swabian cuisine" is the name of the game at this restaurant, which is run by a young couple – Annika Braun presides front-of-house and her husband, Manuel, is the chef. He mainly uses locally sourced ingredients, following the seasonal availability of produce, and also likes to incorporate elements of other cuisines. The menu includes dishes such as vitello forello (medium-rare boiled veal, smoked trout cream, Fellbach verjus) and Brunnenhof Mäusdorf rooster with crispy skin accompanied by a sour vegetable chutney, artichoke purée and polenta sticks.

Name: Kulinarium
Address: Friedrichsplatz 4, Röthenbach an der Pegnitz, 90552, Germany
Description: This delightful restaurant is nestled in a spruce half-timbered building in the heart of Röthenbach an der Pegnitz, just outside Nuremberg. Modern interior design incorporating a rustic wooden beam ceiling creates a cosy atmosphere. You can feel commitment and passion here. Gerald Hoffmann, a well-known chef in the region and most recently head chef at Koch und Kellner, is in charge in the kitchen. His wife presides over the service, adding a soupçon of heartfelt charm to every interaction. There is a seasonally orientated set menu that is prepared using mainly regional ingredients. In summer you can sit on the terrace in the front garden. There is also a small hotel in the building.

Name: Halbstück
Description: The Knipsers, a well-known Laumersheim winemaking family, opened Halbstück back in 2014 as a Weinstube. Now it is Alsace native Christian Rubert – also known from Karlbacher, a restaurant in Großkarlbach – who is in charge in the kitchen. Influences from his homeland are evident in his dishes, which pair beautifully with the finest wines from Weingut Knisper. The appealing dinner menu includes French classics such as bouillabaisse, and halibut in lobster sauce. Or feel free to choose from the daily specials. At lunchtime, there is a three- to five-course menu. Laura Rubert ensures that guests receive a warm welcome in this cosy atmosphere. Lovely courtyard. Tip: They also offer interesting culinary events and wine tastings (for 10 people or more). In addition, rooms can be booked for weddings and conferences. A holiday flat is available to rent out, too.

Name: Stresa
Description: A chic, modern and pleasingly neighbourly vibe makes itself felt in this restaurant in the attractive historical district of Striesen, which inspired the name of this place. Walls decorated with artwork by local artists, as well as the open kitchen draw the eye. In the evening, there is a choice of two set menus (omnivore and vegetarian/vegan) composed of three to six courses, or à la carte dishes. The menu changes regularly and takes its cue from the seasons. At lunchtime diners take their pick from a range of options on the "Bistro Menu". Friendly and relaxed service.

Name: Schlossberg
Description: The location on the Schlossberg (castle hill) is fantastic in its own right: located right beside Vauban fortress, the business travellers' hotel that houses this restaurant towers over the city and affords a one-of-a-kind view – best enjoyed from the terrace. The interior is also delightful with its sleek contemporary design, coupled with panoramic vistas through generous windows. The menu changes with the seasons and features classic dishes with international twists. Order à la carte or opt for the set menu of the month (three or four courses).

Name: Ebanat
Description: Surrounded by vineyards, this modern restaurant boasts a beautiful location on the premises of Weingut Kopp, a Demeter winery complete with its own wine shop. As you savour classic seasonal cuisine that draws on international influences, you can take in the view of the vines and the plain, to which the name makes reference (the village of Ebenung used to be called "Ebanat", a derivation of the Old High German word for "plain"). Made with locally sourced ingredients wherever possible, the excellent food can be accompanied by the restaurant's own wines. Friendly and professional service.

Name: Richard Bistro
Description: Hans Richard made a name for himself with his restaurant Richard, housed here in the former Köpenicker Hof, which dates back to 1892. He and his team have now turned their attention to a pleasingly down-to-earth bistro concept. Drawing inspiration from the Mediterranean, they rustle up modern dishes, such as baked monkfish with fennel and a tarragon and caper sauce, using select ingredients. The interior is a beautiful blend of old and new, featuring a stunning high wooden ceiling and contemporary artwork.

Name: Whiskyplaza
Description: By the Nikolaifleet canal, one of the oldest buildings in Hamburg, which is located in the city's oldest street, is home to this appealing bar-cum-restaurant. Spanning a few floors, the space capitalises on the historical charm of the original structure (1697): Crystal chandeliers, wooden beams and modern furnishings as well as shelves lined with decorative bottles all come together to create a genuinely warm ambiance. The kitchen serves its modern take on classic cuisine as a sophisticated set menu or à la carte. Highlights include scallop with barley, salt marsh herbs, apple, seaweed caviar and beurre blanc, or flat iron steak with pumpkin seed dumplings, kalette, mushrooms, apple and cheese. Given the restaurant's name, it might come as no surprise that the extensive selection of spirits includes around 1 100 whiskies.

Name: Rebblick
Description: Housed in Korb's Remstalhalle, this restaurant with an attractive glass façade has retained a certain 1970s feel, while incorporating chic modern design features. Jochen Gromann serves up flavoursome seasonal cuisine drawing on regional and international influences. In addition to à la carte options – including Swabian Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy), there are also set menus. The menu features a wine recommendation for each dish. Chef Nadine Gromann manages the friendly and professional front-of-house team. Delightful terrace – with a view of the vineyards, depending on where you sit.

Name: Ristorante Engel
Description: With almost 200 years of gastronomic history to its name, this place has been in Italian hands for over 40 years. Following in his parents' footsteps, Franco Iaia now runs this ristorante with his wife Yvonne. With a tiled stove and warm wood, the inviting dining space is vibrant and charming. "La Piazza" is their lovely terrace shaded by mulberry trees. Highlights of the "cucina italiana strettamente classica" include homemade pasta, brasato and osso buco.

Name: Meilenstein
Description: A listed building steeped in history is the attractive location that houses this chic restaurant with its bar and lovely terrace. Here, they propose a set menu that you can put together yourself and that draws on modern influences. The front-of-house team is friendly and accomplished. There is also an appealing selection of cocktails at this stylish venue with a variety of spaces you can hire for private events.

Name: bellasLOKAL
Address: Langstraße 15, Bad Soden am Taunus, 65812, Germany
Description: Located in a narrow village lane in Altenhain, Isabelle Pering's restaurant has a pleasantly bright interior done out in a tasteful, minimalist style. With her menu, which you can also choose vegetarian, the chef shows her knack for creating harmonious flavour combinations – this is where her experience gained at top-flight establishments shines through. Most of the ingredients and wines are from the region and certified organic. Delightful terrace.

Name: CARUSO Pastabar
Description: Neapolitan-born Anna and Marcello Caruso, working with Emanuele Barbaro, have come up with a cool concept: a flavoursome, relaxed and lively dining experience, played out in a chic atmosphere. Service comes courtesy of a relaxed, attentive team under the tutelage of the charming proprietress. They serve a three-course set menu, which you can put together yourself and add to as you wish – the main course is flavoursome house-made pasta! N.B. You should allow about two hours for three courses. There are two seatings: 6pm and 8.30pm. Trendy drinks at the bar.

Name: La Mer
Description: Having earned his spurs at some award-winning restaurants, most recently at Seesteg, owner and head chef Hilko Uphoffis, together with his partner Giulia Casto, is at the helm of this smart restaurant located right next to the Michels Thalasso Hotel Nordseehaus, on the edge of the pedestrian/shopping zone. His classically French cuisine also demonstrates the odd modern flourish, as in the North Sea ling, cooked in nut butter, with lobster ravioli. The restaurant itself is also inviting, with its beautifully bright, pared-down and modern interior, as well as its appealing terrace laid out in front of the large window façade.

Name: Goldene Sonne
Description: A quaint historical half-timbered building provides the setting where Heiner Bohnet and Constanza Piccolo welcome diners into their inviting dining space, which has retained its traditional charm. The pair approach their work with tremendous dedication and enthusiasm – she provides friendly and attentive service, and he creates a new vegetable-forward set menu every week, always guided by what is in season. Ingredients are sourced almost entirely from the local area (except for the sustainably line-caught fish from the coast of Brittany). The chef-patron is a member of a farming collective and grows his own vegetables. A great deal of fermenting, pickling and preserving is done in-house, plus they bake their own bread. Tip: They offer three lovely double rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Baron.ess
Description: This trendy and stylish restaurant occupies an old bridge structure on the premises of the Brückenbaron events venue. When you enter, you can take a peek into the glass-enclosed kitchen before being seated in the airy dining space. The large windows look out onto landscaped grounds, complete with a pond and fountain. Gorgeous terrace. The modern set menu made using seasonal produce puts the emphasis on sustainability. Vegetables feature prominently throughout. The same ingredient is often presented in various forms and textures. The service is very friendly, attentive and professional – the chefs are on hand to talk you through the dishes. On the wine list: organic, ecological and natural Franconian wineries.

Name: Pizarro Fine Dining
Description: This small restaurant is chic, modern and upscale, with its impressive open kitchen as the centrepiece. In the kitchen, Julio Pizarro calls the shots; his creative cooking skilfully incorporates his Peruvian roots and many years' experience on the international fine dining scene. He presents an intriguing fusion of traditional Peruvian recipes and Nikkei cuisine, incorporating modern French techniques in the form of a set menu based on fish and seafood. Exciting, flavoursome and meticulously crafted, the dishes showcase premium ingredients. To complement your meal, you can choose between wine pairings and alcohol-free alternatives. Charming and laid back, yet professional service adds to the inviting atmosphere. The terrace overlooking the old half-timbered town hall is a lovely spot for an aperitif.

Name: AIMY
Description: Fans of Thai cuisine are in good hands at this restaurant with an attractive decor, where diners can enjoy flavoursome dishes made from high-quality produce – authentic Thai flavours are guaranteed here. The dishes are accompanied by a varied selection of wines including some rarities. And the cocktail menu is also worth a look. There is also a delightful bar at the back of the restaurant. In summer, the seats in the inner courtyard are especially inviting.

Name: BAR TATAR in der Schreiberei
Description: In the heart of the city, just a stone's throw from Marienplatz, this restaurant is on the ground floor of Munich's heritage-protected chancery (Schreiberei), where the city's history has been recorded since 1552. The attractive interior has a certain brasserie feel and, in good weather, the quiet sheltered courtyard terrace is especially inviting. Made with select ingredients, such as the veal cheeks with truffle polenta, the food is bursting with flavour. The tartare – there are many different variations, including meat, fish and vegetarian options – is a must. Be sure to try one of the delicious desserts, too. The varied à la carte selection is also ideal for sharing. When it comes to the excellent wine list, ask for a recommendation for a glass or bottle to accompany your meal.

Name: Kevin Gideon
Description: Kevin Gideon and his restaurant have moved to a location outside the city centre, into premises that previously housed VINEO. Diners will be pleased to hear that the concept remains the same in the new space. The team is unchanged and the pared-back, modern style of the interior and of the food is also still present and correct. In their kitchen, which is visible through a glass partition, Kevin Gideon and his small team serve up a creative set menu (vegetarian version available); updated on a regular basis, it comprises three, five or seven courses. Friendly and professional service. In short: a restaurant run with great dedication and where the cooking is ambitious.

Name: Danza
Description: On the first floor of the culture and congress centre, Forum am Schlosspark, an interesting restaurant and wine bar concept awaits you. The cuisine is modern, seasonal and international, but also has classical influences; dishes can be ordered as a set menu or à la carte. Good wines, friendly, attentive service and a chic, light and airy space. The terrace with a view over Kastanienallee is delightful. If you are coming by car, you can park on the Bärenwiese opposite.

Name: BRIKZ
Description: At this restaurant in the heart of Charlottenburg – which used to be a jazz café – Arne Anker and his team serve up cuisine that is inspired by the seasons. Choose the five- to seven-course set menu (water included) or go à la carte; you can also put together your own menu from the à la carte selection, and it is possible to make this vegan. The wafer-thin slices of tender entrecôte and spicy guanciale served on wooden skewers are excellent – described by the chef himself with a wink as "our version of a Berlin kebab". The restaurant is happy to cater for food intolerances – it is best to let them know in advance. The alcohol-free drinks are also fabulous, with house-made kombucha, kefir, syrup, tea etc. The ambience is characterised by striking exposed brick walls and decorative art. The service is friendly and well organised, the atmosphere relaxed and informal – even the chef sometimes comes to diners at their tables. Pleasant pavement terrace.

Name: Bernhardhof
Description: This delightfully chic and modern restaurant is to be found at the foot of the hill on which Andechs's famous abbey stands. The Holzinger family used to run a farm here, but nowadays they welcome diners with warmth and dedication. While the father handles the service, the son runs the kitchen with his mother's assistance, preparing delicious dishes using fresh ingredients and drawing on regional and international influences. Think sous-vide neck of Bavarian free-range pork with mashed potatoes, Dijon mustard, onion and pork jus, or roasted root chervil, peanut curry crunch, black cumin mayonnaise and orange yoghurt. You can also stay overnight here in one of the really comfortable and spacious maisonettes or suites.

Name: Anglerstuben
Description: On the banks of the Rhine, this restaurant is tucked away behind a somewhat unprepossessing exterior directly above the angling club. The cuisine, based on excellent ingredients and with fish as the centrepiece, is a master class in finesse. In the evening, there are two five-course menus to choose from (as well as à la carte options); on weekdays, there is a very reasonably priced "Business Lunch" deal. They stock only German wines and the selection is outstanding. There is also a children's menu. The delicious food is served by friendly and attentive staff. In summer, make a beeline for the small terrace with a view of the Rhine and its jetties. Conveniently, the restaurant has a few parking spaces of its own.

Name: sansaro
Description: The minimalist Japanese-style interior of the restaurant is inviting, as is the lovely verdant inner courtyard terrace. As well as sushi and sashimi (which you can also order omakase), the menu offers a five-course set menu with drink pairings, dubbed "Journey to Japan", and a small à la carte selection of Japanese dishes. The short explanations on the menu are a nice idea. There is also a terrific selection of sake and Japanese whiskies.

Name: nagare
Description: Don't be fooled by the rather unspectacular exterior of this corner-plot building! Once inside, you will be immersed in a Far Eastern-style minimalist setting and have the chance to savour Nakagawa's Japanese creative cuisine, which draws on contemporary and French influences. Choose from set menus and à la carte options – sushi and vegetarian dishes are also present and correct. Only fish of the finest quality makes the cut. Professional service comes courtesy of polite, friendly waitstaff, who will gladly provide sake recommendations.

Name: KOSTBAR
Description: Following Marco Akuzun's departure, Daniele di Fabio is the new head chef. As well as a good à la carte selection, a five-course set menu is served in the evening (vegetarian version available on request) and there is an attractive "business lunch" formula comprising two or three courses. The mouthwatering options include ricotta gnocchi with summer truffle and Parmesan, or guinea fowl saltimbocca with olive marinara sauce and basil purée. Furthermore, a creative tasting menu can be ordered in the evening. The upscale interior is both stylish and cosy, featuring warm wood and a minimalist design that creates a welcoming atmosphere. Lovely covered terrace with a working water wheel as the standout feature!

Name: Restaurant Max'es
Description: A chic bistro vibe, friendly hospitality and good food are the hallmarks of the restaurant of the Hotel Wegner, a family-run business since 1957. The cuisine is modern and takes its cue from the changing seasons. The chefs like to give their dishes the finishing touch at your table when they serve, for example, cheese wheel pasta, crêpes Suzette or fillet of sole. Tip: Pre-order beef Wellington, Chateaubriand or the monthly changing set menu. In summer, be sure to secure a table on the quiet, leafy terrace! You can also come for breakfast.

Name: Salt & Silver am Meer
Address: Zum Böhler Strand, Sankt Peter-Ording, 25826, Germany
Description: This restaurant is housed in an 8m-high building on stilts right by the beach, within spitting distance of the sea – an impressive location in which to enjoy fresh cuisine featuring produce from the region. At this "Fish Grill & Beach Bar", the tempting menu includes dishes such as grilled turbot and "fish fingers royal". Good to know: The chicken nuggets on the children's menu are made from regional organic poultry. Wine connoisseurs are bound to find something to their liking on the well-selected wine list. The atmosphere is nice and lively both inside and out on the fabulous terrace. Another Salt & Silver in addition to the two Hamburg restaurants. During the high season and on weekends, be sure to make a reservation. Tip: Park behind the dunes and enjoy the lovely 15min walk to the restaurant.

Name: Atelier Tian
Description: The location in Veitsburg castle is indeed something special. Once you reach the top, not only does a magnificent view of Ravensburg await you, but also Christian Ott's ambitious, flavoursome cuisine. You can put together your own set menu from the dishes on offer – flexibility is the name of the game! You can also look forward to professional and friendly service. Tip: Make your reservation in good time – this location is not only popular with locals.

Name: Momo Ramen
Description: Fancy some Japanese ramen? Then look no further! This hip and laid-back spot serves fresh house-made noodles. The aromatic dishes draw on regional ingredients and dispense with any additives. Reduced menu at lunchtime. An amusing detail: the toilets are wallpapered with Japanese newspapers.

Name: Gasthaus zum Adler
Description: In the centre of this village right on the German Wine Route, this traditional inn at the foot of Landeck Castle is now run by the fifth generation of the same family, with two sisters at the helm. Christine Baumann presides in the kitchen, putting a Latin-American spin on Palatinate cuisine; Franziska Baumann provides friendly service front of house. Regional wines are served with the seasonal cuisine. The appealingly modern, minimalist design successfully incorporates exposed old sandstone walls and wooden ceiling beams.

Name: Löwengrube
Description: Since chef-patron Amadeus Kura took over, this former wine tavern has had a makeover – with fantastic results. The traditional character of the historical building has been intentionally preserved, and combined with sleek, modern elements. The chef's culinary vision is just as contemporary: he primarily uses regional ingredients but also draws on international influences. Delicious dishes such as northern Black Forest salmon trout with peach, pepper and cashews, or veal loin with aubergine and polenta are available in the evening either à la carte or as part of a five-course set menu. A similar selection is often served à la carte for lunch. The well-curated wine list includes a good selection of Baden labels. The sheltered terrace is a lovely spot in which to soak up the Old Town atmosphere. Parking tip: The restaurant is a stone's throw from Schlossberggarage.

Name: Roussel's Restaurant La Bonne Adresse
Description: Thierry Roussel and Jane Kölchens run this place with dedication. The elegant restaurant exudes cosiness, and the extremely friendly service, directed by your hostess, also contributes to the pleasant atmosphere. At beautifully laid tables, upscale classic cuisine is served in the form of set menus (one vegetarian) or à la carte. They are also happy to share their wine recommendations, including some from their own production. Plus: guestrooms where you will feel right at home.

Name: Oma Wilma Heimatküche
Description: This historical thatched-roof house in the heart of Keitum has bags of charm. Inside, diners enjoy an appealing modern take on Frisian decor; outside the gorgeous garden terrace beckons. The friendly front-of-house team provides pleasingly informal but professional service. The concept is dubbed "Heimatküche" – an ambitious blend of traditional and modern styles. A crowd favourite is the madras currywurst. Shorter menu at lunchtime followed by tempting coffee and cake options until 5pm. Tip: Be sure to book (only possible for the evening). The restaurant’s name pays tribute to the chef's grandmother.

Name: Zur Waage M.E.B.
Description: This long-established restaurant enjoys a charming location in the town centre, directly on the Leda River – in summer, the lovely terrace with a view of the museum harbour beckons! Inside, you can expect all the trappings of a traditional inn with the odd rustic maritime touch. Mario E. Brüggemann (who completed his apprenticeship as a chef here) proposes high-quality cuisine at reasonable prices with a strong focus on sustainability. Regional produce goes into dishes such as young herring tartare, plum, tomato – tasty, fresh and pleasingly straightforward! The simpler lunch menu includes a few of the evening options.

Name: Bach & Nurup
Description: This modern brick building in the city centre is named after the duo that run it: Nadia Bach performs the role of manager, sommelier and head of service, while Christian Nurup works away in the kitchen. There’s a small area used for breakfast, pastries and coffee, as well as a lovely terrace, and a delightful main room where a central display case bursts with wine glasses and cookery books. The wide-ranging menus are judiciously created, showing great balance and understanding of flavour. Influences come from Denmark, France and even Asia – if the Imperial pigeon is available, be sure to choose it.

Name: Restaurant BAVN
Description: Purchase a lift ticket and take the 29 second ride to the 44th floor of Denmark’s tallest building, where you’ll arrive at Restaurant BAVN, which boasts stunning 360° views over the city. Head for the enclosed terrace for some truly Instagrammable shots, then take your seat in the understated dining room, where tables topped with colourful schnapps glasses set the tone. Traditional Danish dishes follow the seasons and are generously proportioned – this includes some superb sandwiches at lunchtime, with the fried herring with soft onions and gooseberries a must-try.

Name: Hosiló
Description: Hosiló translates as ‘small room’, an apt name for this single-storey building sandwiched between two larger structures in a side street not far from the House of Collections. There’s a slightly industrial feel to the room, which comes with a high ceiling, a central bar and an unusual trapezoid window to the rear that makes the most of the daylight hours. It’s owned by three friends and, unusually for the city, has a loyal local following thanks to both its laid-back ambience and its concise, market-inspired menu that offers the likes of halibut with sweet potato gratin and miso sauce.

Name: Le Coucou Vert
Description: The popular Coucou Vert sits opposite the Aleksanterin Teatteri theatre and brings a little slice of France to Helsinki with its charming bistro atmosphere and slightly retro feel. A zinc counter set with open-backed high stools takes centre stage and is fringed by white linen-laid tables, and the efficient yet relaxed service comes courtesy of a smiley young team. The cooking is led by Gallic classics, such as Bayonne ham, onion tarte Tatin and crème brûlée, but some Finnish and wider global influences are also evident. A largely French wine list makes the perfect accompaniment.

Name: Aoi
Description: Having first collaborated on a pop-up project, Olli Ruotsalainen and Von Quillao decided to set up shop together permanently not far from the marina. A simple place with a relaxed atmosphere and seating for 26 guests, Aoi comes with green walls, oak parquet flooring and black bistro-style furnishings – and brings together the two friend’s personalities. The short, four-course menu changes regularly, with fresh ingredients attractively presented in dishes such as pike perch with fennel and apple or white asparagus with polypody root.

Name: HimmerRiget
Address: HimmerLand, Lars Larsens Vej 1, Farsø, 9640, Denmark
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The impressive HimmerLand Resort sits in a rural spot, but has everything you need, from hotel rooms and lodges to a spa, tennis courts, bowling and minigolf. It also boasts the small, elegant HimmerRiget, which overlooks the golf course. Both the décor and the cooking are in a modern vein, with the experienced chef creating a seasonal tasting menu that showcases the best of the local larder. Dishes are intricate and well-presented, with a great understanding of balance and flavour, such as in the quenelle of monkfish with beurre blanc and vendace roe. The accompanying wine list is of the highest order.

Name: Izakaya Skostredet
Description: Within the Skostredet Hotel sits this contemporary izakaya of the same name, where you are encouraged to come together and socialise over shared dishes. The chef creates an intriguing à la carte menu via the use of fresh Norwegian seafood, traditional Japanese ingredients and time-honoured Japanese techniques, with dishes ranging from sushi and ramen bowls to agemono (fried dishes) and okonomiyaki (savoury pancakes). For those that simply can’t decide, there are several sharing menus available too. In summer, the best spot to dine is outside on the terrace.

Name: Young Hearts
Description: There is a comfortable and contemporary feel to this restaurant in the neighbourhood of Töölö. The cooking is inspired by the seasons and the well-constructed dishes deliver layers of intense flavours, with texture and acidity also playing a key role. There is generosity in the tasting menu offer, including some servings split across multiple complementary dishes – as with scallop presented both raw and as a dried powder to add flavour to a cabbage salad. Wine pairings are available to enhance the experience.

Name: Kuurna
Description: This small, family-run bistro in the peaceful Kruununhaka neighbourhood is a hit with the locals, who come here to enjoy flavoursome Finnish dishes crafted from regional ingredients. Square black tables are spread over two dimly lit rooms – where empty wine bottles act as vases – and you’ll be warmly welcomed in by Laura, Tom and the whole team. The menu changes every three weeks, in line with the latest seasonal produce available, and is often supplemented by daily specials that are chalked up on the blackboard. If it’s on the menu, the peanut swiss roll with potato skin ice cream is a must-try!

Name: Koizen
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the Gothenburg Natural History Museum and Slottsskogen park, is this 22-seater Japanese restaurant comprising a counter and two high-level tables. It’s owned and run by John and Teresa Chu, who offer an omakase experience encompassing appetisers, sashimi, nigiri, aburi nigiri, soup and dessert – as well as monthly special events featuring the likes of bluefin tuna or Wagyu beef. John carefully crafts the dishes in front of you, presenting them along with an explanation of their make-up, while Alven recommends Japanese drinks, sakes by the glass and even sake pairings.

Name: Kajo
Description: If you’re looking to take a train trip outside the city, then this inconspicuous little restaurant opposite Tampere Central Station makes the perfect stop off. Regional and international ingredients come together in recipes that favour Asian techniques – like chawanmushi with peas and crayfish or sea buckthorn with lime leaf and Arctic cloudberry – and the superb stocks and sauces really show the depth of the kitchen’s skills. The chef is a very affable character, delivering his dishes and explaining their composition, while the young service team present some interesting wine pairings.

Name: Bon Lio
Description: Kitty and Cato will warmly welcome you into their bright neighbourhood restaurant, which offers a friendly experience that’s more relaxed than most. The ground floor Gastrobar is for drinks and bistro-style small plates, while upstairs it’s all about a multi-course tasting menu. Local, seasonal produce is the bedrock of Cato's cooking, which brings together elements from both his Majorcan and Norwegian heritage in a sophisticated manner. You’ll find the likes of perfectly seared turbot with almond, soya and carrot purée, accompanied by some excellent Spanish wine recommendations.

Name: Møntergade
Description: The charming team are a big part of the draw at this lively upmarket brasserie which offers generous, classically based dishes. While the chalkboard displays daily specials, there’s always a place for herring on the menu – with fried, pickled, marinated or even curried options. Their other dishes like Danish beef with black garlic cream and deep-fried goose fat potatoes or apples with white chocolate, lemon verbena and apple sorbet are equally appealing though. There’s a cosy vibe to the place and a small drinks counter where you can chat away with the waiters.

Name: Tavolo
Description: Enter through the huge wooden doors of this old military stable and you’ll find yourself in a large and stunningly converted room with a truly buzzing atmosphere. A huge horse’s head – a copy of Leonardo's Cavallo di Forcione and a reminder of the building’s former life – takes centre stage in the bar, which is a popular spot for a cocktail and some nibbles. When it comes to the food, it’s all about Italy, with the fresh, flavoursome dishes prepared on-view in the open kitchen. From homemade pizzas and pastas to traditional meat dishes, there’s something for everyone here.

Name: à terre
Description: Set in the shadow of the Royal Danish Theatre, à terre is built on family and friendship. It was created in homage to Jean-Louis Le Lay, Chef-Owner Yves’ father, and his spirit lives on in the friendship between Yves and Chef Nicolaj Køster, his close friend. The tasting menu sees global influences added to a classical French base, with good quality ingredients underpinning pared-back, boldly flavoured dishes. Presented alongside each course – maybe a buckwheat galette or brill fried on bread – is a card explaining the recipe’s origins, the ingredients and the chef’s emotional connection to the dish.

Name: Söl
Description: Overlooking the 12th Century Stavanger Cathedral, this cosy restaurant has a friendly touch and offers guests a seasonal set menu. Expect an abundance of vegetables in summer and more meat and fish in winter, but with maximum flavour all year round. The Røros butter and freshly baked sourdough bread are a reason to come alone. They are equally passionate about wine, with one of the biggest natural wine lists in Norway.

Name: Woodstockholm
Description: A compact bistro owned by a group of friends, who set up a furniture making business and now use the bistro to showcase their products. Cooking follows a theme which changes every two months – perhaps a country, a style of food or a famous chef – and the rustic small plates are simple yet full of flavour.

Name: Rolfs Kök
Description: A buzzing neighbourhood restaurant in a lively commercial district, run by a passionate chef-owner. The contemporary interior was designed by famous Swedish artists; sit at the counter to watch the chefs in action. Dishes have big flavours, a classic heart, and a wine match each from the impressive list.

Name: Festningen
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: It may be a former prison whose name means fortress, but you can’t feel more carefree than when seated under a parasol on Festningen's sheltered terrace looking out over the water to Aker Brygge; the period building is charming too though, with a smart yet cosy feel, and the team will welcome you warmly wherever you sit. The terrace menu comprises brasserie classics such as burgers and moules frites, while the modern restaurant menu offers unfussy, attractively presented dishes like hamachi crudo with marinated cucumber, yuzu vinaigrette and horseradish or grilled chicken supreme with rosemary oil and spinach.

Name: Restaurant vRÅ
Address: Clarion Hotel Post, Drottningtorget 10, Gothenburg, 411 03, Sweden
Description: The imposing 1920s city post office is now a hotel, and this glamorous restaurant sits within what was the central hall – the listed cashier booths still on display. A Nordic-Japanese approach sees fine Scandinavian produce meet Asian techniques, and there’s an impressive range of sake by the glass.

Name: Restaurang Atmosfär
Description: A large glass-enclosed terrace greets you at this smart yet relaxed corner restaurant on the main road. Natural light fills the room inside too, whether you’re sitting at the large counter, on high stools by the floor-to-ceiling windows or in one of the comfortable dining rooms. Fresh, unfussy cooking delivers generous dishes that are packed with flavour and a joy to eat, such as halibut with a crayfish bisque and Savoy cabbage or deliciously creamy panna cotta with rosemary caramel and apple granita. The atmosphere becomes more lively in the evening thanks, in part, to the homemade cocktails.

Name: Natura
Description: Well-chosen Finnish ingredients are used to good effect at this intimate restaurant and techniques like fermenting, pickling, salting, chargrilling and smoking all play their part. Choose from a range of colourful modern small plates or opt for the 'All Out' menu – the full range of dishes in miniature!

Name: Savoy
Description: This local institution’s refurbishment has restored much of its original charm and its 8th floor setting boasts superb views over Esplanade Park. Sophisticated classic dishes have a Finnish-French slant and a modern edge, with the occasional Russian touch. The wine matches are first class.

Name: FYR Bistronomi & Bar
Description: This vibrant restaurant sits in the barrel-ceilinged cellar of a striking 19th-century building and its terrace overlooks the adjacent park. Refined, modern bistro cooking includes smørrebrød and snacks at lunch and creative, generously sized dishes at dinner. Environmental awareness is important to the chef, particularly when it comes to their carbon footprint and animal welfare.This restaurant is currently closed due to fire damage.

Name: Falsled Kro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: This charming whitewashed, thatched inn will draw you in with its enticing fireplace and lovely conservatory dining room overlooking the garden. The kitchen takes its cue from the French gastronomy of old, producing rich and indulgent dishes based on quality produce, be it rabbit or langoustine. Many of the ingredients are local, with fruit and vegetables often coming from the estate itself. Watch the chefs in the open kitchen to feel closer to the action.

Name: Matur og Drykkur
Description: This simple little eatery is named after an Icelandic cookbook and shares its premises with the Saga Museum. Old recipes are given modern twists, resulting in delicious dishes with a creative edge. The finest seasonal produce is used throughout the tasting menu, and transformed into refined, well-balanced dishes by the kitchen team. Friendly, professional service completes the picture.

Name: Muru
Description: You’d be hard pushed to find a restaurant with a greater focus on wine than Muru. This cosy little bistro is home to quirky touches such as a wine bottle chandelier, a bar made from old wine boxes and a raised ‘cellar’ – and that’s not to mention the nearby wine bar they run. Simple, tasty dishes are on-hand to accompany the excellent wine list, and the sommelier’s pairing suggestions are spot-on.

Name: Vinkkeli
Description: This charming, deservedly popular restaurant is smartly laid out and run by a delightful team, whose attentive and personable service will make you want to become a regular. The honest, well-judged cooking is a pleasing mix of the modern and the traditional.

Name: Amalie
Description: A charming 18C townhouse by Amalienborg Palace - its two tiny, cosy rooms are decorated with antique prints. The menu offers a large choice of traditional Danish dishes, including herring prepared in various ways; pickled, fried and marinated in curry or port are some of the options available for lovers of the fish. Salmon, salads and smørrebrød are also available, in satisfyingly tasty versions of tried-and-tested classics.

Name: Admiralgade 26
Description: This historic house dates from 1796 and sits in one of the oldest parts of the city. It’s a relaxed place: a mix of wine bar and bistro, with minimalist décor. From oyster mushrooms to actual oysters, the à la carte comprises a selection of vegetable and fish-led dishes. For something a little different, Saturday lunchtimes see a set, Japanese-style 'choushoku' served. Owner Christian is always eager to let you taste some of the 4,000 wines from the cellar.

Name: Vækst
Address: Sankt Peders Stræde 34, Copenhagen, 1453 K, Denmark
Description: Dining outside ‘inside’ is the theme here, and you’ll find plants, garden furniture and a full-sized greenhouse at the centre of the room. Interesting Danish cooking follows the seasons and is light, stimulating and full of flavour.

Name: Restaurant Kanalen
