Description: This quaint building was once the Harbour Police Office, and there's a delightful canal-side terrace from which you can watch the boats bobbing up and down as you eat. Inside it has a bistro-like feel, with long wooden benches and old plank flooring. Dishes are seasonal, unpretentious and full of flavour; some honouring Danish traditions and others bringing Mediterranean ingredients into play.

Name: Mielcke & Hurtigkarl
Description: Set in a delightful spot in Frederiksberg Gardens, its walls painted with garden scenes, is this charming 1744 orangery with a fire-lit terrace. Dishes come from around the globe, with Asian influences to the fore – and an amazing array of herbs from the gardens.

Name: Brasserie Sture 1912
Description: Sture has been an icon of Malmö since 1912, and it’s now been reborn as a classic brasserie with décor to match; think mosaic flooring, closely set tables, a long bar and black-and-white photos of celebrities adorning the walls. A pavement terrace and bustling atmosphere only add to its appeal, as does an extensive menu mixing Swedish dishes with traditional Western European fare like confit rabbit or salad Niçoise. The lengthy wine list has a similar ‘Old World’ focus.

Name: Levi
Description: Japanese and Italian cuisine join forces at this stylish restaurant near Rosenborg Castle Gardens. Expect to find Italian ingredients mixed into recognisable Japanese dishes and vice versa, such as salsiccia gyozas or spaghettoni with yuzu miso. The ambitious, high quality dishes are served by the friendly, attentive team in a strikingly designed room with high ceilings, bare tables and a large glass front.

Name: Mark
Description: The produce of the Danish countryside is the inspiration behind this stylish city centre bistro that also features some classical French methods in the kitchen. There is a wonderful feeling of spaciousness to the dining room, with its central counter, high ceilings and modern décor. Top quality Danish ingredients are seasoned and cooked with real skill, resulting in a roster of refined and well-balanced dishes.

Name: Tollbua
Description: Set within the Brattøra waterside development, this large brasserie provides exactly the buzzing atmosphere you would hope for. Banquettes and a central bar fit the bill décor-wise, while visible ducting and terrazzo flooring lend an industrial edge. Choose from a set menu of either four or six courses, where a signature dish of scallops can be added as an extra – the accompaniments depend on the season, but could include the likes of sea buckthorn, XO and celeriac. It’s beautiful Norwegian seafood like this including, when available, skrei cod of course, that will be among the highlights of your meal.

Name: Eero
Description: Perched on the top floor of the former American Embassy and named after its architect Eero Saarinen, this restaurant and cocktail bar features a wrap-around terrace with views of the Oslofjord on one side and the gardens of The Royal Palace on the other. A wood-fired oven is at the heart of the cooking, which is fish-centric and takes a ‘fin-to-gill’ approach, so you might get cod tongue as a snack, then later its belly on the bone, enhanced by the richness of its liver and roe. Everyone is served at once from a tasting menu, and some of the dishes are presented ‘family style’.

Name: Forma
Description: Chic and sultry, this Södermalm spot delivers the look and vibe of a bar, with the added bonus of flavoursome small plates. The cooking is bang on-trend, blending Nordic and French influences with pan-Asian elements including Korean kimchi, Chinese wontons and a daily selection of Japanese mochi for dessert. If you’re an indecisive diner, go for the keenly priced tasting menu to appreciate the full breadth of the kitchen's talents. Well-versed, professional service is the icing on the cake.

Name: Black Milk Gastro Bar
Description: This intimate restaurant offers great cooking and a fun night out, thanks to its moody lighting, pumping soundtrack and lively cocktail bar. Influenced by South America, Asia and Europe, the creative dishes deliver vibrant flavours and well-judged spicing, while using plenty of modern techniques. Expect to see some luxury ingredients, like Oscietra caviar and Périgord truffles, alongside an enjoyable dose of theatricality, with dishes ranging from courgette flower with cime di rapa, salsa verde and urfa pepper to homemade salted coconut and yuzu gelato topped with Oscietra.

Name: Bistro Ego
Description: Earthy colours set the tone at this relaxed neighbourhood spot, where a huge modern painting takes centre stage and plush cushions and potted plants are dotted about the place. If it’s a more intimate feel you’re after, however, head down the spiral staircase to the cellar, where you’ll be greeted by exposed brickwork and moody lighting. The menu certainly offers something a little different for Helsinki, with French bistro classics given a Japanese makeover; you might find red sole meunière with yuzu, root parsley and spinach ohitashi, followed by chocolate fondant with sesame sugar and shio koji ice cream.

Name: akmē
Description: akmē is much more than just a follow-up to Anaba Sushi – not only does this younger sister occupy Anaba’s former space, but it’s run by two young chefs who used to work on the team. Located in the former industrial harbour district, its youthful, upbeat vibe is a perfect fit for the area, and the energetic staff help to create a memorable experience for its 16 diners. The omakase menu is centred around Japanese-French fusion cuisine – offering the likes of Danish red mullet in bouillabaisse sauce – with the best spot a seat at the counter to observe how the well-conceived dishes are delicately prepared.

Name: Restaurant Anton
Description: Not far from Nyhavn’s picturesque canals sits Restaurant Anton, an impressive 18th-century building that was once an exclusive confectionery store. A restaurant since 1915, it’s now run by the owners behind Marv & Ben, and its appealingly retro dining room still boasts its original murals, along with blue-and-white-tiled tables and Royal Copenhagen tableware. The modern Danish cooking comprises largely of smørrebrød with a twist at lunchtime – such as herring with sour cream, egg, onion compote and tomato – while dinner sees the likes of fried turbot with sunchokes and a gooseberry vinaigrette.

Name: Restaurant Glassalen
Description: You have to pay the theme park admission fee to gain entry to this restaurant hidden within the walls of Tivoli Gardens, so be sure to build in some time for a wander around either before or after your meal. Set within a beautifully restored glasshouse, it’s light, bright and has something of a fairytale feel, and boasts a lovely terrace looking out over the lake. During the day there's a selection of smørrebrød and a three-course lunch, while dinner steps things up-a gear with a seasonal tasting menu and an à la carte of modern Danish dishes such as whole fried sole with mussels and gooseberry sauce.

Name: Abigail & Co
Description: It’s easy to pass by this slightly unusual restaurant, as it’s hidden behind a façade covered with hats – a nod to the building’s former life as a hat shop. A pop-up-turned-permanent, it’s now firmly established on the local dining scene, and its dimly lit semi-subterranean location and closely set candlelit tables give it an appealingly moody, speakeasy vibe. The cooking is perfectly summed up by its tagline – “Seasonal Ingredients, Nordic Roots, Global Inspiration” – with unfussy, pared-back dishes often coming with a playful edge, such as in their signature ‘paint-your-own’ tuna.

Name: Petri
Description: The name is a diminutive version of ‘petrichor’ – which refers to the lovely scent that accompanies rain after a warm period – and there’s a similarly pleasant cosiness to the restaurant itself, thanks to its charming, intimate atmosphere. The set menu follows the seasons, with produce that’s only available in smaller batches offered as optional extra courses, such as pork from Rosa Skattlådan with fermented berries and rose petals. Dishes are well thought out in their creativity, showcasing a good understanding of balance and flavour, while wine and homemade non-alcoholic pairings complete the package.

Name: Flor
Description: Set opposite bigger sister and Green Star awarded Natura, Flor (meaning flower), is a relaxed restaurant-cum-wine-bar built by local craftspeople using primarily Finnish wood and decorated using natural, compostable clay paint. Located on a busy pedestrianised street, it’s the perfect spot to escape the hustle and bustle thanks to its menu of appealing, freshly crafted dishes that are swiftly prepared. Choose from the à la carte or a surprise menu comprising bread, three starters to share, a main, a side and a dessert, with dishes including the likes of organic salmon with citrus-bouillabaisse sauce and honey pomelo.

Name: Fyr
Description: After many successful years as co-owner of Two-Michelin-Starred Gastrologik in Stockholm, Jacob Holmström returned to his birthplace with his wife Emelie and fell in love with this fantastic building on the Tylösand headland. Its design is chic and modern, and the atmosphere laid-back – and you’ll find it hard to decide whether to keep your eyes on the view, the open kitchen or the plate in front of you. The menu opens with snacks and ‘Canned Food’ (roe and caviar), before moving onto ‘Fish from the Cabinet’ and dishes showcasing other regional ingredients such as lamb with nettle purée and artichoke.

Name: Betong
Description: ‘Betong’ translates as ‘concrete’ in English, which explains the bare walls at this buzzy, simply decorated restaurant. Dishes like the Chef's signature ‘Cold Curry’ (available as an added extra to the tasting menu) showcase his creative heart, but the kitchen's classical technique shines through in highlight dishes like butter-poached skrei cod with pak choi. Dining here is a fun experience, in a space bursting with energy and filled with pumping music; but it might not be the best spot for an intimate romantic date.

Name: Essence
Description: Essence is the perfect spot for social types who like to mingle with their fellow guests. Everyone is seated around a big counter and served at the same time, with Chef Stefan Taylor centre stage preparing the dishes and explaining their make-up. He works alone, so there’s a slight pause between courses, and it’s here when the atmosphere becomes animated and you find yourself chatting away. Stefan has an intuitive way of combining flavours and spends hours each week drying, pickling and preparing the various elements in advance for dishes such as wild duck with mushrooms, watercress and thyme.

Name: Brasserie Astoria
Description: The former Astoria Cinema, which dates from the 1870s, has been carefully restored and now boasts a bustling brasserie with all the glamour and opulence of yesteryear. Sit at the counter to watch the chefs at work; quality produce is used to create flavoursome modern brasserie classics with the odd Asian influence.

Name: Ark
Description: It’s bright, it’s buzzing and it’s 100% vegan – and it’s also a concept that’s kind to the planet. Multi-course menus use local and foraged ingredients mixed in with some Japanese flavours; their mushrooms are cultivated on their own farm and the resulting dishes are a highlight. Service is friendly and informative. Go for the well-chosen wine pairings.

Name: La Cucina Italiana
Description: In this cosy, romantic restaurant comprising just eight tables, chef Allesio Fioriniello continues his father’s legacy by cooking up authentic Italian dishes with southern overtones (the family hails from Naples). He is helped along in his mission by childhood friend, Enzo, who takes charge in the restaurant. Carefully prepared, seasonal dishes are a model of their kind and could include the likes of a rich, beautifully textured parmigiana di melanzane or Rossini venison with seared milk bread and panzerotti.

Name: Smör
Description: There’s a well-executed fusion of the old and the new at this charming city centre restaurant located opposite Turku Cathedral (the only medieval basilica in Finland). Stylish, contemporary décor is brought into the vaulted cellar of a 19th-century riverside merchant's house, while the cooking combines traditional techniques with modern presentation. The finest Nordic ingredients run through the creative dishes, with the combinations offering memorable contrasts of flavours and textures. The kitchen team serve many of the dishes themselves, and the sommelier offers some interesting wine pairings.

Name: Brasserie Hansken
Description: A delightfully traditional brasserie, centrally located by the City Hall, with various charming dining areas and a fantastic terrace. Classical cooking follows the seasons and mixes French and Scandic influences; seafood is a speciality.

Name: Kockeriet
Description: In a characterful 17C former grain warehouse, owned by Malmö-born TV chef Tareq Taylor, a young and talented team prepare well-balanced contemporary dishes with great precision. Scandinavian produce is at its heart, with some coming from the kitchen garden. The timbered dining room is relaxed and inviting, the service friendly, and the drinks pairings well-conceived.

Name: Bloom in the Park
Description: Be sure to arrive early for an aperitif on the terrace of this charming lakeside lodge before heading through to the modern, minimalist restaurant. In an unusual twist, both the menu and the matching wine pairings are a complete surprise! You submit your allergies and dislikes in advance, with the components of the dishes only revealed at the end of the meal when you are given a QR code to scan. Combinations could include halibut with satsuma, endive and crab bisque or seared roe deer with pumpkin and forest mushrooms. This element of the unknown stimulates both the mind and the palate through your meal.

Name: Hillenberg
Description: Perfectly pitched for busy Humlegårdsgatan is this stylish take on a classic brasserie. It has a smart, elegant feel and a hugely impressive wine cellar. Appealing Swedish classics are immensely satisfying yet exhibit a subtle modern touch and sense of finesse.

Name: Tango
Description: There’s a feeling of exclusivity to dining at Tango, where the intimate space and décor gives off cool 'Mad Men' vibes; the leather swivel chairs are particularly comfortable. The attractive dishes on the set menu are served and explained by the chefs themselves and feature seasonal ingredients in creative preparations. Wine pairings are well thought-out and service is attentive and charming.

Name: Sjømagasinet
Description: Sjømagasinet means ‘Sea Store’, so it’s no surprise to find that seafood leads the way at this vast, three-roomed restaurant beneath an apartment block. When the weather’s right, start with a drink on the superb waterside terrace; when it’s not, make for the chic lounge-bar. There’s plenty of options when it comes to dining here: you can select something from the crab and lobster tank or choose from the shellfish bar for delicious langoustines, a platter of shellfish landed at the local dock or dishes like lobster with chive butter and burdock chips.

Name: Gaijin
Description: Gaijin comes with dark, contemporary décor, a buzzing atmosphere, attentive service and an emphasis on sharing. Its experienced owners offer boldly flavoured, skilfully presented modern takes on Japanese, Korean and Northern Chinese recipes. The tasting menus are a great way to sample the different cuisines.

Name: Restaurant Sletten
Description: A relaxed former inn in a charming coastal village; most people head to the room with the sea view, although the others with their bold foodie pictures are equally as pleasant. Well-presented modern small plates make up the menu – 2-3 per person is about right. The wine list provides plenty of interest.

Name: Statholderens Mat og Vinkjeller
Description: The more informal sister to Statholdergaarden occupies the same 17th-century salmon-pink building in the heart of the city and, like its sibling, is spread over three different rooms – only this time in the vaulted cellars. A wall of wine greets you at the entranceway, a promise of things to come, while the cooking offers generous, classically based dishes with a twist. A range of menus include a four-course lunch offering ‘The Cold’, ‘The Gently Warm’ and ‘The Warm’, while the 10-course seasonal menu sees the likes of pulled pork on celeriac flatbread or baked char with lemon hollandaise.

Name: Molskroen
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A table on the charming terrace of this relaxed and stylish seaside inn is the perfect spot to enjoy traditional French cuisine, as well as more modern interpretations of the classics. The chef collaborates with a local organic farmer and the restaurant’s comprehensive sustainability programme includes staff welfare.

Name: Høst
Description: Not far from Nørreport station, Høst is a busy neighbourhood restaurant that offers an enjoyable atmosphere and good value cooking. Dishes are modern, boldly flavoured and visually impressive, and the set menus come with lots of extra surprises. Nordic fish and shellfish feature largely, while the vegetarian dishes – like celeriac with truffle and ´Vesterhavsost’ – are some of the highlights of the menu.

Name: Sankt Annæ
Address: Sankt Annæ Plads 12, Copenhagen, 1250 K, Denmark
Description: An attractive terraced building with a traditional, rather quaint interior. There's a seasonal à la carte and a daily blackboard menu: prices can vary so check before ordering. The lobster and shrimp – fresh from local fjords – are a hit.

Name: Kødbyens Fiskebar
Description: This buzzy, industrial-style restaurant is set – somewhat incongruously – in a former butcher’s shop in the old meatpacking district, and was one of the pioneers in transforming the area into a leisure destination. Menus feature freshly prepared seafood dishes which are based around the latest catch, with oysters being a speciality. The terrace is a popular spot come summer.

Name: Sümac
Description: A lively modern brasserie with on-trend concrete walls, burnished leather banquettes and a charcoal grill. Icelandic ingredients are given a Middle Eastern twist, with influences ranging from North African to Lebanese. Cooking is rustic and full of flavour; go for the meze sharing menus.

Name: SOLEN
Description: If there's such a thing as ‘industrial elegance’, then they’ve found it at this bang on-trend spot in the city’s meat-packing district. Exposed wires and concrete pillars combine with white tablecloths in a chic space that’s proving hugely popular with Stockholm’s diners. It’s owned by the experienced operators behind Adam / Albin and is an impressively well-run place; the cooking borrows from around the world, including small selections of tacos and wood-fired pizzas. On a cold day, sit round the impressive fire-lit chimney.

Name: Bistro Bardot
Description: Exposed brick and pipework give this two-roomed brasserie a rustic, slightly retro feel that chimes perfectly with its buoyant atmosphere. It’s a deservedly busy place, named after actress Brigitte Bardot and taking a similarly French outlook on culinary matters too. The extensive à la carte offers all manner of classic brasserie staples, from steak au poivre to tarte Tatin, while the 'menu du jour' provides a simpler, good value selection. The wine list has some appealing French favourites and the friendly team serve the large numbers with ease.

Name: Oxenstiernan
Description: You can’t miss this stylish, orange-painted bistro which stands out against the greenery of a city park. In summer, be sure to dine on the terrace, under the trees. A environmentally conscious ethos runs throughout, from the interior design to the ethically sourced produce used in the unfussy, boldly flavoured Swedish dishes.This restaurant is currently closed and due to reopen in Spring 2026.

Name: Treetop
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view
Description: This elegant wooden cabin with panoramic windows sits amongst the trees in the middle of Munkebjerg Forest. An open fire burns in one corner of the room and the well-spaced tables make for an intimate dining experience. Not only is the setting at one with nature but the menu is too, bringing the outside inside via the herbs, berries and flowers that grace the plates and the shelves. The chefs and the service team work together to tell their story – which is centred around honesty, nature and craftsmanship – through dishes such as grilled scallop with beurre blanc and creamed celeriac.

Name: Shelter
Description: A fun night out is guaranteed at this converted warehouse in a corner of Katajanokka Harbour, close to Uspenskin Cathedral. The serving team are enthusiastic, the atmosphere is contagious, and from the open kitchen come meticulously prepared and appealingly presented dishes that deliver on flavour.

Name: Barr
Description: A laid-back quayside restaurant with wood-clad walls. Its name means ‘Barley’ and it has an amazing array of cask and bottled beers (some custom-brewed), along with beer pairings to match the food. Intensely flavoured, rustic dishes have classic Nordic roots but are taken to new heights; the sweet cake is a must.

Name: Hærværk
Description: A group of friends run this laid-back restaurant, which has something of a bohemian feel thanks to its collection of cookery books, sheepskins and modern art. To say that the set surprise menu is seasonal would be an understatement. Top-quality local and organic ingredients set the tone, and the dishes feel pure, allowing said ingredients to take centre stage in their natural form. Expect delicious salad leaves and the likes of line-caught wolffish with green asparagus, followed by rhubarb tart with rhubarb sorbet and lemon verbena ice cream. Modern, natural wines make the perfect accompaniment.

Name: freyja
Description: Head straight for the roof terrace to kick off your visit with a cocktail and 360° views of Stockholm and, once inside, opt for a seat by the curved window to capitalise on the 13th floor location. The menu includes modernised yet comforting Swedish classics like Kroppkaka, executed with care and confidence, yielding well-balanced flavours. This is a place where you'll feel equally at home dining in a couple or as a group, as it delivers something for everyone.

Name: OTO
Description: Fun, lively and offering something fresh and exciting to the Reykjavik dining scene, OTO is one of the hottest tickets in town thanks to its bustling atmosphere and Italian-Japanese fusion cuisine. The uncommon pairing works a treat, with their shared ingredient-led approach resulting in dishes that showcase clever cross-cuisine combinations and deliver pure, natural flavours – like a take on scallops Florentine enhanced by the piquancy of ponzu and the warming spice of shichimi. If you can’t decide, go for their version of a kaiseki menu.

Name: Uformel
Description: The more casual sister to formel B, Uformel celebrated its 10-year anniversary in 2024 with an extensive renovation that created a brighter space and a more ‘grown-up’ feel. Its smart open kitchen remains but gone is the cocktail bar and, in its place, is an exclusive chef’s table. Dishes are presented either on a five-course menu or as uniformly priced tasting plates – with three to five per person about the right amount – and see traditional Danish flavours joined by Asian notes. Its central location makes it ideal for a visit at any time of day.

Name: Sanchez
Description: The Sanchez in question is Rosio – a former Head Pastry Chef at Noma – and she certainly knows how to put the fun in dining out with this lively neighbourhood spot. Bringing the bold, powerful flavours of her Mexican heritage and presenting them in a small plates concept – accompanied, of course, by a margarita or maybe the mezcal pairing – has proved the perfect recipe for success. The ‘Favourite Servings’, made up of five dishes selected by the kitchen team, is a hit – and there’s always the option to pop in on your way past just for tacos and snacks.

Name: Theo
Description: A hit with the locals of Copenhagen, Theo sits just a stone’s throw from the university – it’s not just students that like to come here though, as it’s popular with plenty of seniors too. The room itself is simply furnished, keeping the focus on the company and on the food, with the cooking take on an unfussy modern style that gives equal attention to vegetarian options as to meat and fish dishes. You might find stracciatella with pumpkin, salsa macha and parsley pesto or cod with mashed potatoes, palm cabbage, mussel sauce and kao soi paste. The lunchtime menu represents good value.

Name: Poppy
Description: Chef-Owner Tobias has created a fun little neighbourhood spot here at Poppy, where groups of friends sit shoulder to shoulder at wooden tables in a trendy bistro-style room. It’s a compact place, with room for just 24 diners – including four seats overlooking the kitchen – but that’s all part of its cosy appeal. The five-course tasting menu offers seasonal modern dishes like monkfish 'binchotan' with tomato gel, hazelnut butter emulsion and mussel broth. Unusually, there’s no wine list, just shelves filled with bottles, their prices marked on them in chalk.

Name: Leijontornet
Description: After a few years as Djuret, this long-established restaurant has returned to its original guise and provides heaps of old-school charm. The dining room is full of character, with armchairs, vaulted brick ceilings and candlelit tables all adding to the appeal. The cooking has heavy French and other European influences, providing bold flavours across a wide selection of generous dishes. Expect plenty of premium produce, from lobster to turbot, and an extensive, similarly luxurious wine list.

Name: Le Ankka
Description: This tiny little restaurant's natural buzz is enhanced by the presence of an open kitchen that feels like it's fully part of the room, while a racing green and matt black colour scheme contribute to the décor’s moody feel. Throughout the cooking, there is a desire to pair Finnish produce with classical French techniques and flavours – exemplified by the use of ‘almond potatoes’ from Lapland to make a vichyssoise. The wine list is made up of mostly natural and organic choices.

Name: Minh Mat
Description: There is a wonderfully personal touch to this well-run Vietnamese restaurant, with posters and old photos adorning the walls, and an array of objects decorating the room. It’s an enjoyably relaxed setting for the cooking, which uses impressive ingredients – some of them from local producers – and mines plenty of flavour from simple-looking compositions. A light, smooth cream of corn sauce, for example, is a skilful and delicious accompaniment to quality grilled prawns.

Name: Varemottaket
Description: Pumping music and a relaxed, friendly team ensure there’s always a fun vibe at this tiny restaurant situated behind the Annis Pølsemakeri butchery and farm shop. You enter via the shop’s deliveries door, hence the name ‘Varemottaket’, which translates as ‘The Goods Reception’. The narrow, intimate space is filled with high tables and stools, where diners can enjoy a tasting menu with a strong element of charcoal grilling. Unsurprisingly, the fabulous dry-aged meats from the butcher’s make an appearance, such as entrecôte of Norwegian beef.

Name: BORD
Description: You’re guaranteed a warm welcome at this sweetly run bohemian bistro. A communal table is at the heart of proceedings, but there are a few smaller tables and some counter seating available too. Starters merge into mains on the daily menu of unfussy, pared-back dishes, where skilful Mediterranean-inspired cooking keeps the focus firmly on the top-quality ingredients. They make their own ricotta on-site and the wood-fired oven is used to great effect, from baking bread in the morning to gratinating langoustines in the evening. Dinner is the main event, but they also open on Saturdays for lunch.

Name: Prospero
Description: There’s a slightly ‘underground’ feel to this small bistro, both figuratively and literally; you enter via a few steps down from street level, into a ‘half-cellar’ dining room where the windows look out at pavement level. The concise, keenly priced tasting menu lists dishes that offer an impressive level of restraint and control, where sauces are a focus. You might find the likes of trout with tomato and langoustine sauce or onglet with ramson and fish sauce, followed by rhubarb with yoghurt and chamomile.

Name: BELLIES
Description: A former factory plays host to this unique restaurant, which brings together exposed brick walls, modern asymmetric tables and designer furnishings. Another unusual feature is the completely plant-based cuisine, which celebrates some often overlooked ingredients. The Italian chef draws on his heritage to inspire the tasting menu, while also adding Asian flavours (such as Sichuan pepper or ssamjang) as well as some Nordic influences (via a range of fermented and preserved components) in order to create original, sometimes playful dishes, like pumpkin, sea buckthorn, gochujang and bergamot ravioli.

Name: Ræst
Description: Pass on the option of a normal table and instead opt for a seat at the shared table in this traditional turf-roofed house with characterful, low-ceilinged dining rooms. Its name means ‘fermented’, and the set menu is indeed centred around fermentation and ageing, with an insight into the heritage of Faroese food and flavours. Dishes are bold, creative and well-balanced.

Name: ROKS
Description: This sister to Ræst is set in an ancient, turf-roofed building and has a rustic inner, a laid-back ambience and chatty staff. The set menus reflect the bounty from the surrounding waters, from local sea-urchins to langoustines and Greenlandic snow crab. All these dishes are cooked with great precision to unlock their natural flavours.

Name: Boulevard
Description: The welcome is warm, the room elegant, and the food heartening and eminently satisfying. The passion and experience of the two chef-owners is evident in all areas of this likeable restaurant. The quality of the fish and shellfish really comes through, thanks to the classic techniques used by the kitchen.

Name: Human
Description: In a quiet residential street behind the 17C Skansen Kronan fortress, you'll find this stylishly decorated restaurant decked out with neutral tones and vintage furniture. The first solo project for Martin Moses, it focuses on New Nordic cooking, which is executed with a skilful touch. In the evening you can sample the quality dishes from either a small or large tasting menu, with a four or five course set menu available at lunch.

Name: Fasangården
Description: In an 18th Century house packed with period charm in the famous Frederiksberg Gardens, there's a bucolic feel to this restaurant that's split over three rooms and comes with bold wallpaper, fine plasterwork and crystal chandeliers. Dishes are generous and well-judged, and accompanied by service from an eager-to-please young team. At lunch, the focus is on classic Danish smørrebrød, plus a couple of more substantial offerings; in the evening, there's a short à la carte and a good-value seasonal menu.

Name: Hotell Borgholm
Description: The beautiful island of Öland is famous for its wild herbs, and that’s reflected in the cooking at this historic hotel’s restaurant, where the chefs enhance their elaborate dishes with thyme, basil and a host of other flavours from the 100-variety-strong garden. The original, boldly flavoured cooking comes in a tasting menu format, marrying classical techniques with subtle modern ones in dishes such as pan-fried red kingfish with spring chlorophyll, pickled cloudberries, saffron butter sauce and bronze fennel. The accompanying wine list is a real treasure trove for oenophiles.

Name: Det Røde Pakhus
Description: Two experienced owners bring their knowledge together at this modern, wood-furnished restaurant set in the centre of Bornholm’s capital. The chef is passionate about good produce and skilfully prepares local ingredients to create refined, imaginative dishes. Desserts are a highlight.

Name: Boen Gård
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Lovingly restored buildings in a beautiful bucolic setting make dining here a memorable experience. The surrounding gardens, meadows and river provide the vegetables, fruits, herbs and fish that are used so respectfully and expertly by the classically trained kitchen; all complemented by an impressive wine cellar. The chef's philosophy of using local ingredients will be explained to you by the excellent service team.

Name: Carbon
Description: There is an elegant quality to this smart, modern bistro de luxe with rich décor and crushed velvet banquettes. The seasonal menu mixes contemporary techniques with a more traditional base and all dishes come with suggested wine pairings; choose between five or eight courses – or come from Monday to Thursday for an additional three-course option. This is a deservedly busy spot where the attentive, personable service adds to the experience. Be sure to look out for the dishes from the Josper oven.

Name: Restaurang B.A.R.
Description: This bright, buzzy restaurant is just a cast away from the waterfront and has a semi-industrial fish-market look. Choose your seafood from the fridge or the tank, along with a cooking style, a sauce and one of their interesting sides.

Name: Lieffroy
Description: A beautiful, yellow-painted house in a lovely location overlooking the sea; inside it’s traditionally furnished, with rustic-chic vibes, a romantic atmosphere and formal service. Classic French cooking features local seafood and is accompanied by a well-chosen wine list.

Name: Lux Dag för Dag
Description: A stylish, red-brick former factory dating back to 1916, set beside the water, is home to this brasserie-style restaurant that has a welcome brightness to both its décor and its atmosphere. Local produce is key to their ethos, including the likes of Östergötland lamb and Ängsö pike-perch, along with plenty of seasonal ingredients such as asparagus and rhubarb. Unfussy, classically based dishes allow this fresh produce to shine, with the flexible courses ranging in size from 'mini' to 'large'. There's also a set Kitchen Menu available for those that can't quite decide.

Name: Farang
Description: The flavours of Southeast Asia are the inspiration behind this stylish restaurant and bar that occupies the building once home to the Stockholm Electric Company. The unusual front door harks back to its former occupation, but once inside it's a chic space with soft lighting and a large open kitchen. The colorful, zingy cooking includes Thai dishes like laab and crying tiger beef, along with Vietnamese-style sashimi and other influences from the wider region. Strong service, sensible prices and a fun atmosphere complete the picture.

Name: NISCH
Description: This pleasantly relaxed little neighbourhood restaurant is sleekly and stylishly decorated with a monochrome colour scheme. For its part, the kitchen produces accomplished dishes and boasts some good eco-credentials. The modern, understated Nordic set menu is inspired by global flavours and changes every few weeks. The interesting wine list is mainly organic and biodynamic in nature.

Name: Boon Nam
Description: A fun, intimate restaurant in the basement of the Hotel St George; the perfect place for a night out with friends. The fragrant dishes cover all the regions of Thailand and are good for sharing. Unsure what to order? Then go for one of the set menus, which also include good vegetarian options. A range of cocktails will help to keep you in the party mood, including some specially made to go with dessert.

Name: Ulla Winbladh
Description: Ulla Winbladh was originally built as a steam bakery for the 1897 Stockholm World Fair and is set in charming parkland beside the Skansen open-air museum. Sit on the terrace or in the older, more characterful part of the building. Typical Swedish dishes include the likes of fish roe and sweet and sour herring.

Name: The Pescatarian
Description: Dine in one of three rooms at this buzzing, minimalist restaurant that, unsurprisingly, features plenty of freshly caught seafood. Choose from the fish-based tasting menu or a vegetarian version, both offered in either 4 or 6 courses. The chef prepares modern dishes with all the typical Danish hallmarks, including preservation techniques and a lightness of touch.

Name: Lyran Matbar
Description: There’s a pleasingly relaxed air at this small, simply styled restaurant, where the experienced team lead the service with a friendly smile. Upstairs it’s more about drinks, so if you’re here to dine then head down the spiral staircase to the rustic cellar. The well-balanced tasting menus come in Mixed, Pescetarian and Vegetarian versions and are created daily from the best local produce available. All you are presented with is a list of ingredients, which are then turned into modern Swedish creations such as ‘yellow beet, skyr, pistachio, cedrat, fennel pollen, burned butter and sherry’.

Name: Trattoria La Strega
Description: Run by passionate, charming owners, this lively little trattoria is nestled within a quiet residential area, and serves the kind of authentic Northern Italian food that you would find in a good trattoria in Piemonte or Triveneto. Boldly flavoured dishes are best enjoyed from the 'Menu Degustazione', accompanied by a candlelit table and a glass of wine from the extensive Italian selection.

Name: Sjömagasinet
Address: Klippans Kulturreservat, Adolf Edelsvärds gata 5, Gothenburg, 414 51, Sweden
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A charming split-level restaurant in an old 1775 East India Company warehouse; sit on the upper floor to take in the lovely harbour view. Cooking offers a pleasing mix of classic and modern dishes, with seafood kept to the fore. The wine list offers a good selection of top burgundies.

Name: Brasserie Blanche
Description: A cosy French restaurant housed in an 18C building which was originally a stable and later spent time as a garage and an interior furnishings store. It has a small front terrace, a bar decorated with wine boxes and a wall made of corks. The chef is a Francophile and creates flavoursome classic French dishes.

Name: Cru
Description: The wine reference in the name is no coincidence – Cru offers up an impressive, largely French wine list that features some particularly fine vintages. In keeping with the Gallic theme, these are joined by a selection of French-inspired dishes where classic flavours come together with Norwegian produce to create the likes of pâté en croûte with cornichons and mustard or chicken vol-au-vent with morels, peas, asparagus and tarragon. The large, high-ceilinged dining room comes in shades of green and grey, and offer views into the open kitchen from its comfy banquettes.

Name: Arakataka
Description: If you’re looking for a relaxed and fun meal out, then Arakataka has you covered courtesy of its cosy atmosphere, friendly service and flexible menus. First, pick your view – beside the huge windows looking out onto the street or opposite the open kitchen – then choose your menu, which comes in a choice of four or six set courses or as smaller snacks. Modern dishes might include halibut tartare with fermented tomatoes or duck breast with cabbage and leeks – and you’ll find the perfect match on the excellent wine list, which offers some impressive verticals from French and Italian producers.

Name: Kolonialen Bislett
Description: Close to the stadium you’ll find this popular neighbourhood bistro, which was previously a grocer’s shop for nearly 80 years. The concise, keenly priced menu includes oysters, cured meats and wholesome Norwegian classics that have been brought up-to-date. There’s a diverse selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Moment
Description: A welcoming glow draws you towards this restaurant, as you navigate the dark streets of the small hamlet of Rønde. It’s clear that sustainability runs through Moment’s veins: its permaculture garden guides the menus, the chefs explain the philosophy behind every dish and there’s a remarkable selection of natural wines. Depending on the day, you can choose between a short and a long version of the tasting menu, where well-presented plant-led recipes give prominence to vegetables with dishes such as ‘greens’ or ‘corn, tomatillo and tomato’. Fully vegan and vegetarian menus are available too.

Name: Nokka
Description: A huge anchor and propeller mark out this harbourside warehouse and, inside, three high-ceilinged rooms juxtapose brick with varnished wood. An on-view kitchen allows you to watch wonderful, sustainably sourced ingredients being prepared in a rustic style. There is a strongly Finnish heart to the cooking, which includes classic dishes like freshly made blini topped with crème fraîche, pickled red onions and vendace roe. Friendly, professional service adds to the experience.

Name: Møf
Description: Ask for a seat at the counter to watch the young chef-owners cook in the open kitchen at this cosy, relaxed restaurant. The cooking is Danish at heart and based on local produce, providing great value in dishes that accentuate the central ingredient, like pumpkin gnocchi with smoked and pickled pumpkin. An impressive selection of organic and natural wines are available, as well as a wide range of orange wines.

Name: Kiin Kiin
Description: Kiin Kiin means ‘come and eat’ in Thai – and you’d be foolish not to take up the invitation. You enter into a dimly lit basement, where you might start to wonder if there’s a restaurant here at all, but this moody lounge is all part of the experience – the spot to enjoy pre-meal snacks comprising refined versions of street food. After this, head up to the tasteful dining room decorated with golden Buddha wall hangings and choose from innovative Thai dishes with a playful edge. You might find tom yum soup prepared in a coffee machine, a savoury creme brûlée or pandan ice cream with burning rum.

Name: Vaaghals
Description: One of the city’s modern ‘barcode’ buildings plays host to this bright, relaxed restaurant, where an open kitchen affords views of the chefs, and a terrace is on-hand to make the most of the warmer weather. Three set menus allow you to choose between four, five or eight courses, with optional extras including cheeses and a sharing dessert platter. Cooking is underpinned by Norwegian produce, with their speciality being the in-house aged and cured hams, which are sliced at your table for an additional dash of theatre. Come on a Saturday for a leisurely sharing brunch.

Name: Kiin Kiin VeVe
Description: Set close to the Kestellet citadel, the chic Kiin Kiin VeVe occupies a space that was once a bread-making warehouse. Sister of Thai restaurant Kiin Kiin, it follows a similar philosophy of serving creative dishes, but this time using only lacto-vegetarian cuisine. Here, Asian flavours are brought to the fore via a range of snacks served at comfy sofas in the lounge, as well as through a six-course tasting menu which revolves around the seasons. Interesting wine and juice parings accompany dishes such as sweet potato with coconut and achiote or bread pudding with geranium and yuzu.

Name: Atelier 33
Description: Bouillabaisse, Paris-Brest and a great selection of burgundies… with a menu like this, it’s hard to believe you’re not in France. Classic bistros and brasseries are the inspiration behind this charming place with a warm, friendly atmosphere. Danish produce is nevertheless at the heart of the cooking, which provides well-executed and satisfying versions of these traditional dishes. The lunch menu includes lighter bites like a croque madame, while at dinner you can pick between the à la carte and a surprise 4 course seasonal menu.

Name: Restaurant Saga
Description: A change of name in 2025 from Spontan Vinbar to Restaurant Saga placed a little more emphasis on the food side of things, but its philosophy remains the same. Striking eclectic art adorns the walls of the relaxed and trendy restaurant, while the adjoining wine bar offers an impressive array of bottles to choose from, with real depth to the list and numerous vintages from heavy hitting producers. The ten-course tasting menu offers modern, restrained cooking and original touches – like a deconstructed XO sauce – that enhance the dishes.

Name: Restaurant Palægade
Description: Enter past the pavement terrace with sheepskin-covered chairs and you’ll find yourself in this beautiful brasserie with a striking black & whited tiled floor, unique brass light fittings and oak & walnut chairs modelled on Finn Juhl’s ‘Reading Chair’. During the day, this is the place to come for smørrebrød – both traditional and modern – from warm fried herring with caramelised onion, ramson and apple to red pickled herring with dark berries and crème fraiche. At night, the menu focuses on contemporary Danish cuisine and an impressive wine list, with the hand-crafted dessert trolley a real feature.

Name: JORD
Description: ‘Forest to plate’ is the message here, with wild and hyper-seasonal ingredients at the fore. Some of the produce is foraged, whilst meat is often hunted by the owner in the surrounding area. The surprise tasting menu delivers a large array of creative dishes with intriguing blends of flavours and textures. Preserving, pickling, smoking and curing are all done in-house, giving new life to the local ingredients.

Name: Washoku TOMO
Description: In the western half of Södermalm, Chef-Owner Tomoko Hayashi is bolstering Stockholm’s Japanese dining scene by offering an omakase experience that doesn’t break the bank. While this is Japanese cooking that’s not entirely focussed on sushi, seafood nevertheless plays a central role in the menu. The produce comes from all over the world, be it Spanish sea bass, Argentinian prawns or Canadian black cod. Tomoko leads the smooth service herself with personality and professionalism.

Name: Madonna
Description: Named in part after the painting by Edvard Munch, it is appropriate that this restaurant sits just a few long strides away from Oslo’s Munch Museum. The dining room is small here and so are the plates, which work well for sharing and provide an appealing range of flavours. The influences are global, so don’t be surprised to see tacos sitting next to chawanmushi on the menu, along with some more typically Norwegian fare. There’s a fun, relaxed vibe in the air, and a pleasing eclecticism to the wine list.

Name: Kappo Andō
Description: Kappo Andō was 10 years in the making, but the wait paid off. It occupies a corner site just outside the city centre and is divided into two different areas, with seats available at a dark wood counter, as well as at regular tables in a second room. The décor is a perfect fit for the contemporary Japanese cooking, where flavoursome dishes are underpinned by quality ingredients. The 'yakitori of the day' allows you to enjoy the smoky flavours of meat cooked over binchotan charcoal and they also open twice a month for ‘Yakitori Sunday’. An extensive sake selection adds to the whole experience.

Name: Bravo
Description: Bravo was opened at the end of 2022 by a young couple on their first venture – and their enthusiasm and friendliness infuse this sweet little restaurant in a converted house. The menu is refreshingly concise and chef-owner Daniel, from his open kitchen, concentrates on clean, seasonal flavours using local ingredients.

Name: Voisine
Description: Homely and cosy, there is a wonderful lack of pretension to this French-inspired bistro. Flavourful dishes from the small open kitchen include classical French desserts like blueberry clafoutis and Paris-Brest. The restaurant has a lived-in feel, with stripped wooden flooring and leather banquettes. The owners have a wine bar next door and it shows in the excellent wine list and shelves stacked full of bottles.

Name: aster
Description: The faux industrial décor feels like an appropriate fit for this restaurant housed in a former warehouse, in an area once home to the city's shipyards. The kitchen forms part of the room, bringing a certain energy to proceedings, and the friendly team also help to create an enjoyable atmosphere. The short menu offers dishes with a rustic edge, where distinct flavours are nicely balanced – such as minty salsa verde with grilled lamb loin, or sharp apple cutting through a rich chocolate dessert.

Name: Moon
Description: Twin brothers have brought a little piece of France to Bergen in the form of this proudly run, intimate bistro, where Jules cooks and Nicolas runs the service. Honest, classically based French cooking makes use of local produce; desserts are a highlight and wine pairings, well chosen.

Name: TIDES
Address: The Reykjavik EDITION, Austurbakki 2, Reykjavík, 101, Iceland
Description: Enviably located between the harbour and the mountains, beside the Harpa Concert Hall, sits The Reykjavík EDITION hotel – and, nestled within it, this sleek, stylish restaurant. Unfussy breakfasts and lunches are followed by an evening tasting menu built around a core of Icelandic produce – such as 1,000-day aged Feykir cheese, Nordic salmon and North Icelandic lamb – while the à la carte offers extensive choice, from handmade lobster ravioli or Uruguayan ribeye seared on the Josper grill to skyr and white chocolate Basque cheesecake.

Name: Rizibizi
Description: Situated in an attractive location on the seafront promenade in Portorož, this restaurant boasts a classic-style interior with a profusion of wood, square tables and a traditional lay out, plus an attractive summer terrace facing the sea. The well-balanced menu offers plenty of choice, including tasting options and an à la carte, all of which showcase carefully prepared meat and fish dishes. In season, truffles add their unique flavour to various dishes – we particularly enjoyed them served with pumpkin and prawns, as well as in the Mediterranean sea bass dish. An excellent wine list completes the picture.

Name: Restavracija Plesnik
Description: A welcoming mountain hotel with a focus on sustainability is the setting for this bright and lively restaurant which, at lunchtime, serves local traditional dishes inspired by the recipes of Marija Plesnika, who cooked here in the 1940s. In the evening, on the other hand, guests are served a tasting menu which is available only by booking ahead for anyone not staying at the hotel. In the kitchen, experienced Janez Bratovž, renowned for his work at the JB Restavracija in Ljubljana, is here in an advisory role, while the talented young Tom Čopar who has experience both in Slovenia and abroad is the resident chef. We particularly enjoyed the Štruklji (dumplings) filled with cheese and lovage (the latter is sourced from the hotel’s own garden).

Name: Hiša Raduha
Description: Every day, Martina Breznik, the fourth generation to run this restaurant, chooses the best produce from her own garden, the nearby forest and from trusted local growers and farmers for her dishes. The result is an immersive introduction to the Luče region, thanks to the early spring vegetables, excellent cheeses and delicious autumn mushrooms that feature on the menu. Whatever the season, the menu changes daily and guarantees an authentic dining experience with a strong local flavour. Don’t miss the trout from the River Savinja served with vegetables from the kitchen garden. Young Filip will be happy to offer wine recommendations, including labels such as the delicate and rounded Meum Chardonnay 2019 from nearby Styria.

Name: Sophia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Open in the evening, the gourmet restaurant at the exclusive Kempinski hotel offers an elegant tribute to the famous Italian actress Sophia Loren, whose unique beauty was as Mediterranean in style as the flavours that inspire the cuisine served here. Influences from Istria, Italy and even France combine harmoniously on a menu that focuses mainly on fish and seafood from the Adriatic (don’t miss the shellfish), although a few carefully selected, top-quality meat dishes and truffle specialities also feature. The turbot steak with prawns, leek and chive-flavoured extra-virgin olive oil is superb.

Name: Restavracija Strelec
Description: The location is truly charming and steeped in history: the panoramic Strelec (Sagittarius) tower of the castle, easily reached in a few minutes by cable car (we recommend checking the return times; alternatively, you can take a taxi or walk along pretty but rather steep and poorly lit streets). The refined dining room, decorated with 1950s sgraffito murals inspired by local folk songs, sets the scene for Igor Jagodic's cuisine and creates the ideal atmosphere for a romantic evening. The chef offers a single nine-course tasting menu, which can be adapted to seven or five courses, with modern and creative dishes that pay tribute to Mediterranean tradition. The wine list is strongly rooted in the local area, with interesting forays into France and Italy. Don't miss a visit to the beautiful castle courtyard and, if possible, the museum exhibitions. When the weather is fine, book a table outside on the ancient ramparts to enjoy an exceptional view of the town.

Name: Ošterija Debeluh
Description: Situated in inland Slovenia, just a few kilometres from the border with Croatia, this is one of the most interesting restaurants in the region. Here, highly experienced owner-chef Jure Tomič has created an excellent network of suppliers from all over Slovenia. His meat and fish dishes are prepared with a modern, precise and technical touch that is unfussy and focuses on bringing out the full flavour of his ingredients. Traditional recipes and ingredients are reinterpreted with a personal twist: examples are the plum extract served with duck and the sweet “butter, honey and milk” dish that takes the ingredients of a typical local dessert and creates something new and original. The chef’s specialities include his Cake Debeluh, a beef tartare with meat macerated in a cold nutmeg broth, goose liver and quail egg spiced with coffee. You’ll have no problem finding the right wine to accompany your meal from the extensive wine list.

Name: Salicornia
Description: A bright and airy restaurant situated slightly away from the centre, where a couple of well-established professionals (Jan front of house and Vjekoslav in the kitchen) serve fresh fish and seafood dishes sourced daily from the fish market. The menu features colourful, generously portioned dishes accompanied by a wine list which focuses on Slovenia, yet also includes labels from Italy, Croatia and France (with champagne from the latter).

Name: Gostilna Vovko
Description: Comprising a bar, wine bar, restaurant and hotel, the Gostilna Vovko is a family-run business with more than 50 years of history behind it, where the traditionally furnished dining room includes a charming wood-fired stove. The cuisine is just as you would expect – authentic and regional, including dishes such as delicious local trout tartare served with horseradish and herbs, and thick, meaty pork chops which are perfect accompanied by a glass of velvety and intensely flavoured 2019 Modra Frankinja wine. The wine list pays tribute to regional labels.

Name: Danilo
Description: Now run by the third generation of the Čarman family (opened by grandfather Danilo), this restaurant continues to offer cuisine that is much appreciated by its guests, with Nina at the helm in the kitchen and her brother Gašper front of house. The menu includes traditional dishes such as Loška smojka, Loška medla and Loška mešta (old peasant recipes from Škofja Loka – hence the adjective Loška – which are based on semolina and served with turnips, pork or potatoes), as well as a few more creative options that also have a regional flavour. Although meat takes centre stage, a few fish specialities from the Adriatic also feature on the menu.

Name: Restavracija Sedem
Description: Seven, like the house number and the Slovenian expression (Sedem!) for sitting down to eat. In a modern and welcoming setting with an open kitchen, students from the town's tourism and hospitality school take their first steps, supported by experienced and consolidated staff. The result is a gastronomic offering that revisits local dishes, with occasional international influences, which can be chosen freely from the à la carte menu or as part of a tasting menu.

Name: AFTR
Description: Situated in the heart of the city, AFTR is a trendy bistro with colourful, modern dining rooms and a charming outdoor space which is perfect for a slightly cooler dining experience away from the busy riverside promenade. The cuisine here, which includes Mediterranean dishes such as taramasalata and Central European options such as suckling pig with kiwi and fennel, is fresh and tasty, skilfully combining delicate ingredients with more intense flavours. Instead of the usual division of courses, the menu has sections dedicated to cold dishes, hot dishes and desserts. The small wine selection includes a number of wines also available by the glass. Our inspector recommends the Vitvoska di Kukanja, an organic white from the Karst which both fresh and mineral.

Name: Gostilna Krištof
Description: The Bolka family continues with their long-established tradition of hospitality in this authentic and welcoming restaurant that immediately warms the heart. The skilfully updated cuisine combines local recipes with a contemporary twist, as demonstrated by dishes such as trout tartare served with sweet and sour ginger, trout roe and a Bernese foam sauce. The menu changes with the seasons and showcases local ingredients such as Krškopolje pork, Carnolian sausage and locally farmed trout. The wine list has the same regional focus, with almost every Slovenian wine available by the glass.

Name: Landerik
Description: This small restaurant on one of Ljubljana’s typical pedestrianised streets boasts a modern, minimalist-style dining room, as well as an attractive outdoor terrace from which to enjoy the views of this picturesque district in the heart of the city. To appreciate the cuisine to the full, we recommend choosing one of the tasting menus. The desserts include a lighter version of the traditional Kaiserschmarrn, featuring small portions of pancake, apricots and a truly mouthwatering vanilla cream.

Name: Stara Gostilna
Description: Situated just off the seafront in lovely Piran, this elegant, stylish restaurant greets guests with the aromas of fresh herbs planted in large vases. The pleasant, intimate dining room serves as a backdrop for two tasting menus and a concise à la carte, all of which feature local, Mediterranean cuisine with a modern touch. Try the lobster ravioli or local sea bass cooked to perfection, followed by a selection of delicious desserts. The wine list offers over 400 labels, all chosen for their excellent pairing potential, plus a fine selection of rums and brandies.

Name: Kendov Dvorec
Description: The history of this magnificent country mansion overlooking the Idrijca river valley dates back to the 14C. Today, the building houses a warm and elegant restaurant, with stylish rooms for winter dining and a beautiful terrace for the summer. The cuisine is traditional and full of authentic flavours, featuring two tasting menus – Katarina (fish) and Jakob (meat). We recommend the latter, especially if it includes the delicious “bati and bakalca” (steamed bread dough and lamb goulash). The entire wine list is dedicated to Slovenia, with all wines available by the glass – the Štemberger Malvazija is particularly good. Charming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: B-Restaurant
Description: This rooftop restaurant at the InterContinental hotel boasts stunning 180° views of the historic centre and castle through its floor-to-ceiling windows, especially at night when the illuminated castle is surrounded by the lights of the city. Inside the restaurant, the contemporary design and open-view kitchen provide the setting for a choice of dishes which is as extensive as the views. As a result, the restaurant has built a well-deserved reputation for its international cuisine, alongside Slovenian specialities. We particularly enjoyed the fresh red prawn ceviche served with a mango sorbet that enhanced the freshness of the prawns, and an excellent tapioca quail with green asparagus and a delicate jus. Before dinner, we recommend a cocktail in the adjacent bar to admire the views of the other half of the city!

Name: Špacapanova Hiša
Description: For more than 50 years, Špacapanova Hiša has been a bastion of Karst cuisine. The restaurant has been run by the Špacapan family since 1973, while its current success is largely due to son and brilliant manager Ago, who has taken the quality of the cuisine to a new level. The regional cuisine is prepared from local ingredients – staff are happy to provide information on the provenance of the ingredients and the human stories involved in their production. Depending on the time of year, don’t miss the lamb and kid, both of which are raised in the Karst and cooked in the oven, then served with cow’s milk curd ravioli. The traditions of the Karst are also alive and well in the wine cellar (the venue for tastings of wine, ham and cheese matured on site). If you’d like to prolong your stay here, the restaurant also offers a few guestrooms, some of which have been recently renovated with period furnishings.

Name: Dvor Jezeršek
Address: Zgornji Brnik 63, Cerklje na Gorenjskem, 4207, Slovenia
Description: In the quiet, idyllic village of Cerklje na Gorenjskem, in the heart of the Kamnik-Savinja Alps, the Jezeršek family has converted several historic buildings featuring traditional architecture into a spacious hotel and gourmet restaurant. The outdoor tables offer a particularly pleasant dining experience, while small windows inside allow guests to watch the kitchen staff at work. A four-course or longer tasting menu is offered in the evening, and can be tailored to suit guests' preferences, with the option of choosing individual dishes from a short list. The cuisine focuses on local produce, with a particular emphasis on freshwater fish and game.

Name: The Restaurant
Description: Situated in the heart of the pedestrian area at the foot of the street leading up to the castle, this restaurant has two entrances: one from the street and the other overlooking the river promenade, where a few tables have been laid out, creating an ideal setting for a relaxing summer meal. The internationally inspired cuisine is at its best in the first courses and the grilled options, with an open grill visible in the middle of the dining room. The specialities here include ribeye, fillets, fish of the day and scampi, all of which are accompanied by lightly sautéed, crispy seasonal vegetables. The wine list includes an excellent selection of Slovenian labels (also available by the glass), such as the Movia Cabernet Sauvignon 2023, which is intense and full of character. We recommend booking a table by the river to enjoy the atmosphere to the full.

Name: Julijana
Description: Housed in the Grand Hotel Toplice which stands amid some of the most popular landscapes in Slovenia, this restaurant boasts truly breathtaking views of Lake Bled from its dining room and its outdoor terrace. Here, the chef offers tasting menus of various lengths featuring meat and fish specialities with the occasional international influence, as well as a 4-course option (the Gorenjska selection menu) with a stronger regional focus. On the latter, the array of local ingredients is showcased via a delicious hazelnut crème brûlée served with ice-cream made from cherries soaked in Terrano liqueur.

Name: Dveri Pax
Description: Nestled in an idyllic setting, the restaurant is reached by crossing gently rolling hills until you discover a charming 16th-century building, once home to the Benedictine monks who started the winemaking business. Today, the winemaking tradition continues, accompanied by tasting itineraries in which the chef interprets local ingredients in a contemporary key, all in the evocative setting of the antique brick-vaulted cellars.

Name: Altrokè
Description: Inspired by Istria and the Mediterranean, the meat and fish dishes served at Altrokè are enhanced by the use of ingredients such as fruit, aromatic herbs and olive oil which are grown or produced on the restaurant’s own property in Plavje near Koper. The ambience here is pleasantly rustic, with exposed stonework and a brick-vaulted ceiling which blend in well with this old district of the city.

Name: Sushimama
Description: Situated not far from the castle and the riverside, in the city lively and pedestrianised tourist district, Sushimama serves elegant and precisely prepared Japanese dishes: sushi and sashimi, of course, in different combinations, but also soups (miso and others), tempura dishes, and cooked meat and fish options. In a simple furnished setting, the service is attentive and courteous.

Name: Restavracija Hotela Marina
Description: Although its immediate setting may lack charm, the position of this restaurant facing the marina is delightful, with its superb sea views through its picture windows. The delicious, authentic and carefully prepared cuisine focuses on fish and seafood “straight from the sea to your plate”. Although there is an à la carte, ingredients are often subject to availability. Seafood, rock fish and pasta served with an array of original sauces are just some of the delicious classic dishes on the menu.

Name: Restavracija Grad Otočec
Address: Grajska cesta 2, Otočec na Krki, 8222, Slovenia
Description: This luxury hotel and restaurant in a spectacular and tranquil location in the middle of the Krka river occupies a charming 13C castle that was demolished and then rebuilt for the purpose. Antiques, a delightful bar with a fireplace and soft comfortable sofas all combine to create the feel of bygone days in the attractive dining room. The cuisine is regional and traditional, featuring carefully prepared dishes and fresh vegetables sourced from the restaurant’s organic kitchen garden. Both the à la carte and the tasting menus follow the seasons. To round off your visit in truly aristocratic style, stay in one of the hotel’s luxurious guestrooms.

Name: PEN KLUB Restavracija
Description: Head up to the first floor to this retro-style restaurant, where you pass a welcoming lounge bar before moving into the main dining room adorned with an attractive fresco. The “culinary journey” offered by the chef here follows the rhythm of the seasons and showcases local traditions, enhanced by the occasional international influence. Although at lunchtime you can order à la carte, in the evening the choice is between three tasting menus (four, six or eight courses) with a wine-pairing option (labels from Slovenia and further afield) or a choice of non-alcoholic drinks. The tiny summer terrace has just a few tables (book in advance).

Name: Miza za štiri
Description: The name of this restaurant (Table for 4) says it all. The business began a few years ago as a type of “table d’hôte” for just four guests, then in 2020, Jure and Mia Brložnik followed their dreams and moved from the city to the countryside. Their restaurant is divided into three rooms, each with just one table – the perfect setting for an intimate dinner! The chef offers a fixed menu of 5, 7 or 9 courses (to be ordered ahead of time) which showcases modern cuisine with its roots in the region and a focus on vegetables and features dishes such as beetroot with horseradish, trout with mushrooms and delicious desserts. For a unique bespoke experience, we recommend the pairing with local wines.

Name: A3
Address: Grad Rajhenburg, Cesta izgnancev 3, Brestanica, 8280, Slovenia
Description: This restaurant, housed in the superbly restored 12C Rajhenburg castle overlooking the Sava river, takes its name from the huge inner courtyard that provides the perfect setting for an aperitif chosen from the many Slovenian sparkling wines served here. In the elegant and stylishly furnished dining room, enjoy a surprise tasting menu (4, 5, 6 or 7 courses) of modern dishes that are full of flavour – the zander with celeriac and the beef with Jerusalem artichoke are particularly delicious. The friendly staff are happy to offer tours of the castle, while the views from the outdoor terrace are truly delightful.

Name: Peti 181
Description: This restaurant’s excellent location is best appreciated in summer, with tables overlooking the river and charming views of the castle lit up at night. The dining room, personally designed by the chef with taste and sensitivity, is also attractive, boasting muted tones and an elegant and intimate ambience inspired by the early 20C. The cuisine is Mediterranean in style, with a focus on fish and seafood – the shellfish are excellent, as is the delicious grilled sea bass with buttered mashed potatoes. One of the house specialities (which must be booked in advance) is the lamb cooked in the wood-fired oven and served with seasonal vegetables – this dish alone makes the journey here worthwhile! The wine list focuses on Slovenian labels, which are also available by the glass.

Name: Grad Štanjel Restaurant & Lounge Bar
Description: If you don’t have the opportunity to stay in Štanjel (something that we highly recommend so that you can immerse yourself in the atmosphere of this charming medieval village), we suggest arriving at this restaurant at least an hour before your meal in order to enjoy a stroll through the narrow streets to the Fabiani Gardens, which boast fine views of the surrounding mountains. You might like to start your meal with a local aperitif – a glass of Teran wine produced using traditional methods by the Jazbec winery would be the perfect choice. Whether you have lunch or dinner here, the cuisine is regional in flavour, featuring many typical ingredients from the Karst area. If it’s on the menu, don’t miss the restaurant’s own cured ham which is truly exceptional. The wine list is concise yet carefully chosen, with labels chosen according to the season. Memorable dishes here include the black gnocchi served with cuttlefish, a delicate herb cream and cherry tomatoes. The friendly and informal service adds to the enjoyment of the experience.

Name: City Terasa
Description: If you’re exploring Maribor, this restaurant is a great place to stop and take a break and has a real holiday feel with its spacious terrace boasting views of the town, the Drava river and the Pohorje mountains in the distance. The menu focuses on fish from the Adriatic (including shellfish and plenty of grilled options), as well as meat recipes that include grass-fed Slovenian beef. There’s a more concise menu at lunchtime, plus a café and the sky lounge, both of which are perfect settings in which to relax.

Name: Gostilna na Gradu
Description: The most scenic way to reach Ljubljana castle, which overlooks the city from the top of a hill, is by funicular – or by foot, if you like walking uphill. However you choose to get here, you’ll find this restaurant in the castle’s spacious inner courtyard, where it serves excellent local cuisine. Among the dishes that we enjoyed most, our favourite was the veal and curly kale – a superb fillet of veal served with the perfect accompaniment of curly kale and a fragrant mushroom cream.

Name: MAK
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Maribor, this restaurant with a slightly eccentric and very individual feel is home to owner-chef David Vračko. The two dining rooms here are decorated with a curious mix of furnishings and tables with attractively simple settings. There’s no à la carte, but instead a long tasting menu created by the chef that features colourful, playful dishes with unusual and occasionally contrasting textures. The theme here is creative, interesting cuisine, including a carefully prepared selection of appetisers, delicious salmon tartare with exotic fruit, superb prawns with cauliflower, and mouth-watering duck. Everything is served with a cheerful smile and a real sense of performance.

Name: Kogo
Description: Situated away from the busy tourist centre yet easily accessible by car, this restaurant is home to an elegant wine bar (on the right when you enter the building) and a modern dining room with a few designer-style features (on the left). Despite the contemporary ambience, the food at Kogo (the name is the Slovenian word for “cook”) is traditional and includes a huge selection of cheese and charcuterie (from Slovenia and further afield), followed by main courses that focus on meat (although fish dishes also feature). There’s also an impressive wine list with detailed descriptions on a tablet.

Name: JB Restavracija
Description: The restaurant is named after Janez Bratovž, regarded as the father of modern Slovenian cuisine and the author of a book detailing his philosophy, ingredients, and forty of his most celebrated recipes. He opened his restaurant in 1992 inside this elegant Secessionist building from the 1920s, designed by the architect Jože Plečnik.Today, in this captivating architectural setting, his son Tomaž leads the kitchen, skilfully blending regional ingredients and flavours with refined classical influences. Don’t miss the iconic JB ravioli, the restaurant’s signature dish, filled with pistachio and cheese and served with foie gras and veal jus.

Name: Restavracija Calypso
Description: Housed within the Perla Resort and Entertainment Centre on the Slovenian side of Gorizia, this renowned restaurant has an excellent reputation in the region for its fish and seafood cuisine. The classically prepared dishes are announced at your table, with options such as raw and baked fish taking pride of place here and a particular focus on fresh fish from the Adriatic.

Name: Gostilna AS
Description: Just a few steps from the iconic Triple Bridge over the Ljubljanica River, you can choose between a dining room with a classic vaulted ceiling or, on milder days, a charming outdoor space surrounded by greenery, offering views of the castle. The menu stays true to tradition, featuring a wide selection of Slovenian meats − primarily grilled − along with fresh Adriatic fish and homemade pasta.

Name: Vila Planinka
Description: Although it takes a while to get to this restaurant, following the magical Jezersko valley to a setting just a few kilometres from the Austrian border, once you’ve reached your destination you realise that the journey was well worth it! Surrounded by splendid mountain peaks, this boutique Alpine hotel and its excellent gourmet restaurant of the same name provide a warm, welcoming haven for guests. The chefs here create elegant, refined dishes that showcase the best Slovenian ingredients, paying careful attention to local recipes. Specialities include bear prosciutto served with bread crackers, hazelnut cream and pear, and smoked trout with camomile-flavoured frothed milk, carrot reduction and pickled celery. The menu always features a few vegetarian options, such as fried celeriac with pinenut butter, poached egg and hollandaise sauce.

Name: TaBar
Description: Housed in a renovated former Rog bicycle factory, TaBar extends over two floors: the lower level serves bar snacks, while the upper floor offers a surprise tasting menu. The industrial setting is the ideal backdrop for modern, unconventional cuisine that is mindful of waste and rich in creativity. Chef Jakob Pintar creates his dishes using seasonal produce from the land, water and garden, enhanced by carefully selected natural wines and cocktails.

Name: Restavracija 1906
Address: Hotel Triglav, Kolodvorska cesta 33, Bled, 4260, Slovenia
Description: 1906 was the inaugural year of the Hotel Triglav, which houses the restaurant, beautifully situated on the hills overlooking the picturesque Lake Bled. The view accompanies the experience both from the bright indoor dining rooms and, above all, from the magnificent summer terrace. Slovenian traditions reign supreme in the kitchen, starting with freshwater fish, accompanied by more international and seafood dishes.

Name: Restavracija Shambala
Description: A “hidden oasis of peace, tranquillity and joy” right in the centre of Ljubljana, just a stone’s throw from the city’s bustling riverside promenade, Shambala serves Asian cuisine amid an Asian-influenced decor that is attractive without being overly decorative. The dishes on the menu (meat, fish and seafood, and vegetarian) are inspired by countries all over Asia, from Japan to Thailand and Vietnam. The desserts feature more European options such as panna cotta, which is served with a mango and date sauce that gives it a more exotic flavour.

Name: Galerija okusov
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The setting for this excellent ‘Gallery of Flavours’ is particularly impressive: a park with an 18th-century Baroque palace, once the castle of Novo Celje, standing in the centre. The welcoming fine dining room and, more importantly, the culinary offerings, always based on local ingredients, prepared and presented with skill and imagination, are definitely more contemporary. The choice is between a concise à la carte menu and a seven-course tasting menu, which can be reduced to five courses. With over 600 labels, the wine cellar is one of the most extraordinary in Slovenia.

Name: Hiša Torkla
Description: The open grill at this restaurant is a regular feature, delighting guests with a wide array of top-quality meat dishes. From Tomahawk to chops, and fillets to picanha steak (the meat is sourced locally, as well as from further afield), the quality is always excellent, while the service is quick yet friendly and discreet. The large picture windows boast fine views of the surrounding hills, giving guests the pleasant sensation of dining outdoors. There’s also a second dining room with a cosy, minimalist feel, which is perfect for winter evenings. Local, seasonal ingredients take centre stage here, such as asparagus, which is served with fuzi pasta and scampi or grilled as a side dish, and truffles, which feature in a number of dishes, including deliciously creamy mashed potatoes.

Name: Jaz by Ana Roš
Description: When a three-Michelin-star chef makes a move, they often have immediate success – and this certainly seems to be the case for Ana Roš’s new restaurant situated right in the centre of Ljubljana. Jaz by Ana Roš is a welcoming, contemporary-style bistro with a young and lively atmosphere, which serves tasty, fun cuisine with a Mediterranean and occasionally Italian flavour, such as in the ceviche of Adriatic white fish with sauerkraut, pomegranate, sweet potato and puffed buckwheat, and the delicious focaccia with oyster mayonnaise, sardines, and tomato and basil salad. There’s a choice of cocktails and excellent wines (also by the glass) to accompany your meal.

Name: Old Cellar Bled
