Description: Said to be the birthplace of phở cuốn in 2000, this spot remains a favourite. Soft rice noodle rolls filled with beef, vegetables and herbs pair perfectly with a sweet-sour dip. The crispy noodle crust of the deep-fried phở with beef gravy creates an irresistible contrast.

Name: Hoi An Sense
Address: 6F, 12 Phan Ke Binh, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Exiting the lift onto the sixth-floor restaurant with a charming lotus pond and iconic lanterns feels like entering the ancient town of Hoi An. The Huế-style rolls with pork and pickled shrimp feature fresh vegetables, a hint of purple sweet potato and a tangy vinegar sauce. Another standout is the grilled sea bass wrapped in pork belly with lemongrass, complemented by pickled radish and shiso leaves. Private dining areas, separated by traditional screens, are available.

Name: MỘC Quán Seafood
Address: 26 To Hien Thanh, Phuoc My Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Enjoy a rustic dining atmosphere that includes an outdoor seating area adorned with fairy lights in the trees. The array of fresh seafood in the large water tank can be served in a variety of Southeast-Asian styles. Gloved staff prepare your shellfish for easy consumption; the chef keeps the kitchen spick and span. The popular lobster is best savoured in garlic butter sauce for optimum flavour. Book in advance to skip the queue and indulge in top-quality seafood.

Name: Béo Ơi
Address: 15/20 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Sai Gon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Off from the main drag, this simple shop is run by the owner-chef, affectionately known as béo ơi or "fat boy" by regulars, who come in droves during lunch hours. The menu features generous portions of Hanoian home-style cooking, including bún riêu cua, a flavoursome tomato crab soup topped with crispy deep-fried tofu. Order a couple of sides for a complete meal. Or go with friends and opt for a hot pot dinner with the tasty soup as a base.

Name: Lüne
Address: 17/14 Le Thanh Ton Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 71006, Vietnam
Description: With offerings such as duck pâté parfait, escargot and pithiviers, the menu seems traditionally French… But the French chef (from Lyon) aims to re-interpret the classics in line with modern forms and aesthetics. The à la carte menu may not be long, but it covers all bases. For those wanting to experience the chef's vision in all its glory, opt for the tasting menu. Again, the wine list isn't overwhelming, being well curated with some solid choices.

Name: Miên Saigon
Address: 50A Dang Dung Street, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 710880, Vietnam
Description: Soft lighting and buckets of atmosphere set the scene in the ground-floor dining room which sports an open kitchen with counter seats for those who want to stay close to the action. The 18-seat private room upstairs is perfect for parties. European dishes are spruced up and given local twists – the beef soup pot au pho melds classic pot au feu with Vietnamese noodles. To sample all the highlights, opt for the tasting menu, but à la carte options abound.

Name: Maison 1929
Address: 2 Cua Dong Street, Cua Dong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 11016, Vietnam
Description: The restaurant, which is established in a historic circa 1929 edifice, is a sister establishment of Chào Bạn. The dining room, spread over two floors and a balcony, features a vibrant colour scheme. The menu is 80% identical to that of Chào Bạn, emphasising a modern approach to Vietnamese cooking. One of the highlights is their array of spring rolls, served hot or cold. Minced beef in lolot leaves boasts a unique aroma and juicy, tender meat.

Name: My Hanh Seafood
Address: 3-5 Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Phuoc My Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: The terrace with panoramic ocean views is one of the biggest draws of this beach-front restaurant. But the well-crafted seafood is more than equal to the setting. The live fish tank heralds a feast of fresh shellfish and fish, to be cooked in various ways. But the stellar attraction is definitely mantis shrimp, boasting firm, flavoursome flesh and rich, buttery roe. Mud crab from Hoi An is another exclusive speciality not found elsewhere in Da Nang.

Name: Bún Chả Cá Bà Hoa
Address: 27 Le Hong Phong Street, Phuoc Ninh Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Since 2009, this simple shop has attracted a loyal fan base with only one item on the menu – bún chả cá – rice noodles in a tangy tomato and pumpkin broth with fresh fishcakes, made in house daily using a variety of fish. Almost 300 bowls are sold every day and customised to order with fishcake only or a combo of fishcake and a chunk of mackerel or tuna. Try it with pickles or a dab of shrimp paste for extra flavour.

Name: Bé Mặn
Address: Lot 9, Vo Nguyen Giap Street, Man Thai Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: One of the most famous seafood restaurants on My Khe Beach, Bé Mặn knows how to bring out the best in every ingredient. Start by picking your own live seafood from the rows of tanks and then specify how you want it cooked. From crabs and lobsters to geoduck and snails, whether deep-fried, stir-fried or steamed, everything tastes as good as it looks. Try the steamed squid with ginger and onion, dipping it in the spicy sour sauce for an extra zing.

Name: Okra FoodBar
Address: 2 Le Van Mien Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 71300, Vietnam
Description: In its new location and managed by a youthful, energetic team, Okra retains its cosy charm. The stylish bar facing an open kitchen is lined with counter seating for an immersive and relaxed dining experience. The chef crafts an unconventional menu from locally sourced ingredients, blending modern and traditional techniques inspired by chargrill and street food. Generous portions and a great selection of wines and cocktails make it a popular spot for relaxing.

Name: Phở Gà Châm (Yen Ninh Street)
Address: 64-68 Yen Ninh Street, Truc Bach Ward, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi, 11117, Vietnam
Description: The phở gà at this small stall might be more expensive than the average, but the chicken is premium quality and the natural chicken flavour of the soup base is impeccably seasoned. Choose from white or dark meat, or a mixture of both, and add chilli sauce, garlic, lime and chilli to taste. Arrive early to ensure the best selection of chicken cuts. This stall, perfect for an authentic breakfast experience in Hanoi, is open until 2:00pm.

Name: Le Comptoir
Address: 16 Che Lan Vien Street, My An Ward, Ngu Hanh Son District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Run by a chef from Lyon, France, this restaurant is the epitome of Gallic authenticity. The á la carte and set menus roll out bistro classics made with premium local and globally sourced ingredients, cherry-picked by the chef. Expect items like roasted beef bone marrow and hand-chopped Wagyu tartare with Melba toast and smoked aioli. The interesting wine list offers a wide range of boutique wineries. Pop into the deli after your meal.

Name: Nén Danang
Address: 16 My Da Tay 2 Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 50506, Vietnam
Description: Reopened in 2022, the first venture of owner-chef Summer Le is tucked away from the main road. The interior is modern and minimalistic, with theatrical lighting to set the mood. To keep it fresh and exciting, the single set menu is tweaked every few months and revamped entirely every 6 months. Each creative Vietnamese dish comes with a hand-drawn card explaining the inspiration and ingredients. Check out the wine- and sake-food pairing.

Name: Bếp Hên
Address: 47 Le Hong Phong Street, Phuoc Ninh Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 840236, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted
Description: Step back in time and immerse yourself in the room’s vintage circa 1990s decor and memorabilia. The family business has been in operation since 2015 and the kitchen is helmed by mum. The extensive menu, which covers all of Vietnam, might seem overwhelming, but rest assured that all the sharing plates are authentic, hearty and comforting. When unsure, check out the section known as ‘mum’s favourites’, for items like fried garlic prawn, or stir-fried morning glory with garlic.

Name: La Fontaine
Address: 2F, Trade Center, River Garden, 170 Nguyen Van Huong Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 70000, Vietnam
Description: This bistro with a vintage Parisian vibe is a spin-off of La Villa, operated by the same French owner-chef. Open for breakfast, lunch and dinner, it serves classic, no-frills Gallic fare ranging from pastries and baguette sandwiches to pork terrine and pâté en croûte. Inspired by the chef’s childhood souvenirs, the rustic Provence-style lamb ragout is unbelievably rich and flavoursome. Also check out the wine list leaning towards French labels.

Name: Phở Tiến
Address: 103 Nguyen Truong To Street, Truc Bach Ward, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi, 11117, Vietnam
Description: This cheerful stall, now located just across from its old spot, is a local favourite for chicken noodles soup, serving a wide range of phố, bún and miến. Diners can choose from chicken offal toppings, and dark or white meat. The clean, cosy space has large windows, and the classic yellow wall adds to the street vibe.

Name: Izakaya by Koki
Address: Basement 2, Capella Hanoi, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Trang Tien Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: Tucked away in the basement of Capella hotel, Izakaya is a modern and chic setting, with various seating areas, including more intimate sofa areas. Guests are welcomed with a complimentary sake with aromatic notes of tropical fruit. Sourcing 70% of its ingredients from Japan, this restaurant has an extensive menu including a specialty of grilled dishes: the grilled black cod with Saikyo sauce is particularly impressive. Be sure to save room for the signature dessert: housemade yame matcha or black truffle ice cream.

Name: Senté (Nguyen Quang Bich Street)
Address: 20 Nguyen Quang Bich Street, Cua Dong Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: Step away from the bustling streets of the Old Quarter, down a discreet alley and into this cosy dining venue, which is strewn with green plants and champions healthy food. The artistically presented, modern Vietnamese dishes use flowers, leaves, seeds, stems and roots of the humble lotus plant to create unique, flavourful inventions. As a starter, the shrimp, pomelo and lotus root salad is refreshing and appetising. Advance reservations recommended.

Name: Tanh Tách
Address: 3 Yet Kieu Street, Nguyen Du Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, 112605, Vietnam
Description: Nestled in a historic French colonial villa, the restaurant occupies two storeys. The chef team exhibits a knack for seafood dishes based on textbook European techniques, thus explaining their prominence on the à la carte menu. Before trying the deftly crafted fish or shellfish, kick off your meal with nori or kimchi rice crackers and tom yum mayo dip. Black chicken consommé is another smash hit.

Name: Etēsia
Address: 14B Lo Su Street, Ly Thai To Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 11007, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: An 18-seat kitchen counter is the focal point of this snug buzzy wine bar. Shelves of empty wine bottles adorn the walls, and the wine list showcases over 350 vintages from the Old World. They offer a vast array of wines by the glass and from a Coravin. The neatly presented, modern dishes are Mediterranean at heart with an Asian twist and deliver accurate, well-judged flavours. Don't miss the homemade pasta: the pride and joy of Etēsia.

Name: Rice Field
Address: 2F, 75-77 Ho Tung Mau Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Spread over three storeys, this delightful venue with an open-air rooftop boasts a rustic décor inspired by local villages and rice fields and serves Vietnamese dishes from the north to the south. The stuffed snails with meat cooked with lemongrass and paired with ginger fish sauce, are succulent, while La Vong fishcakes strike the perfect balance combining vermicelli, marinated fish, fresh Vietnamese vegetables and herbs, shrimp paste sauce and rice paper sheets.

Name: Ốc Đào (District 1)
Address: 212B/D48 Nguyen Trai Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 71014, Vietnam
Description: In addition to regular fish and crustaceans dishes, this legendary restaurant is especially famous for bivalves and sea snails – a plethora of different species are on the menu, many of which are rarely seen elsewhere. The live critters are cooked in traditional Vietnamese condiments with enough seasoning to complement the natural umami without being overpowering. The bustling vibe makes it great for casual gatherings.

Name: Esta
Address: 27 Tran Quy Khoach Street, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Featuring a bar where guests can observe every step of the culinary process and interact with the chefs, Esta promises an elevated dining experience. The menu draws on fusion Asian influences and the chef's Vietnamese heritage. One dish stands out: the local mallard duck, air-dried for seven days and char-grilled to achieve crispy skin and tender meat. Served with a house-made duck jus, it is packed with meaty notes and has a subtle hint of lavender.

Name: T.U.N.G dining
Address: 2C Quang Trung Street, Hoan Kiem Ward, Hanoi, 11006, Vietnam
Description: The TUNG-in-cheek acronym – twisted, unique, natural, gastronomic – encapsulates the philosophy of Chef Hoang Tung's culinary style. His tasting menu, which keeps pace with the seasons and uses local produce, boasts colourful, minimalist dishes, each of which features just 3 or 4 ingredients, whose complexity explodes with every bite. The flavours are balanced and well-judged, with contrasts of texture and temperature, and acidity often playing a key role.

Name: Azabu
Address: 2F, Hôtel du Parc, 84 Tran Nhan Tong Street, Nguyen Du Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the 2nd floor of Hôtel du Parc, bask in the elegant main dining room or watch the sushi chefs at work from the blonde wooden counter. The menu covers all the bases and is great value for money at lunchtime. The extensive à la carte menu offers a fine range of Kaiseki options. Don't overlook the house specialities, including the knockout sushi and sashimi. A smooth, professional operation run by a smart, friendly team.

Name: Labri
Address: 2F, 113 Bui Thi Xuan Street, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, 112306, Vietnam
Description: A neon sign in the upstairs window is the clue to finding this modern-day bistro, tucked away on the 2nd floor of a nondescript building. Abri is French for shelter and the restaurant imbues a sense of cosy luxury. The open kitchen takes centre stage and four huge crystal chandeliers hang from the ceiling. The chef delivers virtuoso cuisine using French techniques and Vietnamese ingredients. For the full experience, opt for the 7-course menu.

Name: French Grill By Jean-François Nulli
Address: LF, JW Marriott, 8 Do Duc Duc Road, Me Tri Ward, South Tu Liem District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list
Description: This elegant hotel restaurant boasts a sleek, spacious dining room oozing with special occasion indulgence. Counter seats offer a view of the huge open kitchen and create a connection between the chefs at work and the diners. The contemporary French culinary score is consummately executed with subtle Asian twists, flanked by equally immaculate, spot-on, courteous service. Private dining rooms are available for everything from date nights to business dinners.

Name: El Gaucho (Hoan Kiem)
Address: 11 Trang Tien Street, Trang Tien Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 11022, Vietnam
Description: This is an outpost of a global chain that specialises in steakhouse classics, specifically premium beef steaks. Certified organic, corn-fed beef from the U.S. and grass-fed cattle from Australia are grilled to perfection Argentinian style – sparingly seasoned and free of sauce to further highlight their natural flavours. Visit the adjoining butcher’s shop to take some quality meat home. Start or end your evening with cocktails at the bar. Reservations recommended.

Name: La Villa
Address: 14 Ngo Quang Huy Street, An Khanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: The culinary Gallic line-up whisks you back to the 1960s with duck foie gras, pâté en croûte, lobster à l'américaine and Grand Marnier soufflé. Decorated with artwork, red velvet curtains and a stunning chandelier, La Villa also offers al fresco dining in the garden. Attentive, suitably formal service, a fine wine list and cheese selection. The starched classical vibe of this restaurant will appeal to those who appreciate vintage charm and nostalgia.

Name: Bánh Cuốn Bà Hoành
Address: 66 To Hien Thanh Street, Bui Thi Xuan Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 112300, Vietnam
Description: This is among the busiest shops in the area because of its steamed rice rolls known as bánh cuốn. Rice noodle sheets are steamed to order and then wrapped around minced shiitake and pork. They also sell bún chả, or grilled pork noodles.

Name: Cơm Gà Lan
Address: 520 Trung Nu Vuong Street, Hoa Thuan Tay Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: As the name suggests, there's only one thing on the menu – cơm gà, or chicken rice, but you can opt for the poultry roasted, steamed or shredded. Served with soup and pickles, the cơm gà xé bóp (shredded version), is especially popular. The lemongrass, coriander and onion lend the juicy chicken extra zing. Given the quality of the food and bargain prices, it's no surprise that this place is always jam-packed. Avoid peak hours.

Name: Du Yên
Address: 26B Street 10, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, 71000, Vietnam
Description: Nestled in a quiet neighbourhood in town, this place occupies two levels with its room exuding rustic chic. The eclectic menu presents Vietnamese dishes plus Western and Thai options. Gỏi cuốn hoa bướm are the photogenic rice paper rolls adorned with edible pansies. The sweet peanut dip works well with the crisp vegetables. Męt bánh Huế is the vegetarian version of the famous steamed rice cake wrapped in banana leaves with fish sauce on the side.

Name: Nephele
Address: 125/12 Nguyen Cuu Van Street, Gia Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Located in the alley of a newly renovated building steeped in history, this dinner-only restaurant serves a single tasting menu. The menu, made with ingredients that the chef selects from diverse regions, is perfectly paired with wine or non-alcoholic drinks. A buzzing ground-floor bar serves pre- or post-dinner cocktails. The 36-hour-fermented sourdough bread, charcoal‐baked to a crisp finish and served with local beeswax and house-made black truffle butter, delivers unforgettable flavour harmony.

Name: The Albion by Kirk Westaway
Address: 23F, Hôtel des Arts Saigon, 76-78 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 070000, Vietnam
Description: Perched on the top floor of Hotel des Arts Saigon, The Albion blends historical charm with modern elegance to pay homage to British heritage. Chef Kirk Westaway's menu reimagines and elevates British classics, such as fish and chips, roast chicken with thyme and Eton mess. The Albion Tomato, with burrata, Dalat heirloom tomatoes and basil-orange sorbet, is a standout. With stunning city views and expert wine pairings, this place showcases contemporary British dining at its finest.

Name: Vi An
Address: 145 Hoang Cau Street, Dong Da Ward, Hanoi, 11515, Vietnam
Description: The owner couple strives to replicate the authentic taste of Northern Vietnam for their Hanoian audience. Unlike the sweet flavours cherished in other parts of Vietnam, here they emphasise umami and saltiness. Chả ốc is one of the most popular dishes. The pork sausage with periwinkle snails is perfumed with herbs and fried until crispy. The pork is juicy and bouncy in texture. Gà xáo gừng is chicken cooked in turmeric and ginger. Simply irresistible.

Name: Năm Đảnh
Address: 139/59/38 Tran Quang Khai Street, Tho Quang Ward, Son Tra District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Tucked away in a residential neighbourhood, Năm Đảnh provides a golf cart shuttle service from Phan Vinh Street. Seafood is the strong suit of this sprawling restaurant, which boasts a huge number of tables. There is even a hut clad in live fish tanks from which diners can make their pick. Lobster, whether steamed, tossed in cheese sauce, or fried with garlic and chilli, is always tasty. Sea whelks in garlic butter exude spellbinding aromas. Early birds get the most choice...

Name: Luk Lak
Address: 28 Bach Dang Street, Thach Thang Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Perched on the banks of the Han River, this outpost of its Hanoian namesake boasts a dining room dripping in lush greenery. This branch shares the same culinary ethos as its flagship – creative Vietnamese fare packed with bold flavours. Grilled ground beef skewer with herbs and lemongrass seduces with aromas. Wrap in rice paper with veg and fruit for a hunger-quenching kick or pair with sticky rice and cassava root in a claypot.

Name: Madame Lân
Address: 4 Bach Dang Street, Thach Thang Ward, Hai Chau District, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: Named after the owner’s late mother, Madame Lân exudes Hoi An flair with its decor and lanterns. The sprawling yellow house is surrounded by water features, boasting both indoor and outdoor seating. The chef rolls out an extensive culinary lineup that covers every facet of Vietnamese cuisine, including the signature dish of Da Nang: fried fish summer roll. Sautéed beef with pepper elder is also a popular salad dish to tickle your tastebuds.

Name: Mía Dining
Address: 12G2 Nguyen Thi Minh Khai Street, Sai Gon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
Description: The soft lighting, minimalist interior and romantic soundtrack make this venue the perfect spot for date nights. The most prized seats are at the counter offering intimate views of the kitchen. Three set menus star modern European recipes jazzed up by a scattering of local produce and seasonings. The must-try duck breast is velvety and juicy, clad in crackling skin as crisp as peanut brittle. Expect sound wine tips from the sommelier.

Name: Thúy 94 Cũ
Address: 84 Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 710000, Vietnam
Description: This popular restaurant specialises in crab, with a menu that shines the spotlight on the crustacean – crab spring rolls, fried rice, salt-baked crab, steamed crab… the list goes on. Crab vermicelli soup brims with umami-loaded crabmeat and roe. The broth features deep, slightly sweet flavours. Soft-shelled crab is fried to order, boasting a crispy crust and firm flesh. What’s more, crab can be replaced by shrimp in most dishes.

Name: Ốc Dì Tú
Address: 144C Quan Thanh Street, Quan Thanh Ward, Ba Dinh District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
Description: Vietnamese for snail, Ốc is the focus of this simple eatery with pila polita, tiger moon, shark eye and canarium snails on the menu. The large melo melo, the tastiest, is grilled until soft and served with scallions and fried garlic; the price depends on its size. The rich variety of seafood options includes prawns, Halong squid, Venus clams and blood cockles. The steamed Venus clams with lemongrass, chilli and pineapple exude a deep umami flavour.

Name: Đông Phố
Address: 57 Ho Xuan Huong Street, Xuan Hoa Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72407, Vietnam
Description: Popular among the locals and tourists alike, this unpretentious eatery shares a bungalow with an ice cream parlour and specialises in traditional Vietnamese dishes and French snacks. If you find the vast menu a bit daunting, the tasting menu is a great way to sample all the signature dishes. Try the assorted spring rolls, featuring a delightful variety of types on one plate, each filled with unique ingredients and crafted in different styles.

Name: Si Dining
Address: 1 Giang Chau 2 Street, Ngu Hanh Son Ward, Da Nang, 550000, Vietnam
Description: This al fresco Italian dining spot is known for its daily catch. The chef's passion for fish shines through in his fresh, seasonal dishes, served in five- or eight-course set menus or à la carte. With soft lighting for a romantic atmosphere, the establishment occupies two floors, with a bar downstairs and the dining room upstairs. The paintings on the walls, by local artists, are available for purchase. The wine pairings complete the experience.

Name: Cô Liêng
Address: 321 Vo Van Tan Street, Ban Co Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 72407, Vietnam
Description: Established in 1995, Cô Liêng serves up a modest take on Southern Vietnamese cuisine. The main draw is the charcoal-grilled bò lá lốt (minced beef wrapped in betel leaves) that features perfect savoury-sweet flavour. They also serve rice vermicelli bundles (bánh hỏi with grilled meat).

Name: The Monkey Gallery Dining
Address: 3F, 91 Mac Thi Buoi Street, Saigon Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Three wise founders, all born in the year of the monkey, have thoughtfully designed this relaxed "gallery" with a minimalist, Japanese-influenced decor, in which the food takes centre stage. The result is a lovely ambience that is perfect for social gatherings. A concrete dining counter faces the open kitchen where the young kitchen team uses modern European cooking techniques. Pick from a selection of dishes for each of the four courses, then choose your drink pairing from the creative list of cocktails and mocktails.

Name: Madame Lam
Address: 10 Tran Ngoc Dien Street, Thao Dien Ward, Thu Duc City, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Indochine-Art Deco design fosters a laid-back ambience in this restaurant where the chef showcases modern Vietnamese cuisine from the central region of the country, where he grew up. The traditional dishes are presented with a refined yet creative touch. Be sure to try the delicious bao ngư nướng mỡ hành (grilled abalone with spring onion oil and fish sauce). The kem chuối nước cốt dừa (banana ice cream with coconut rice and crushed peanuts) is a satisfying and traditional dessert to round off your meal.

Name: Elgin
Address: 27 Mac Dinh Chi Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: Orange banquettes and soft lighting enhance and offset the dark green wall tiles. Run by an energetic and passionate young team, Elgin can be relied upon to pamper its patrons. The menu, which changes regularly, showcases deftly prepared European dishes made mostly with local produce. Try the pork belly with fried brussels sprouts or gnocchi with lamb sugo, both of which are rich in flavours.

Name: Quince Eatery
Address: 37 Bis Ky Con Street, Ben Thanh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list
Description: This Colonial-style house with a vibrant decor, bistro-style furniture and soft lighting serves up a modern take on Mediterranean fare. Pick from a range of charcoal-grilled, wood-fired and oven-baked dishes and eat at the copper counter, which has six seats facing the open kitchen. Top choices include wild Hokkaido scallops and smoked marrow cappelletti, aged barbary duck breast and tasty golden berry with burnt sourdough mousse. Cocktails can be ordered from the bar upstairs.

Name: Cồ Đàm
Address: 68 Tran Hung Dao Street, Tran Hung Dao Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 11019, Vietnam
Description: Named after the Buddha, Cồ Đàm’s eye-catching architecture boasts an ornate exterior inspired by Buddhist and Champa culture and a striking arched entrance of terracotta bricks. Four floors are open for dining, but the ground floor stands out for its tranquil pond and terracotta Buddha. The vegetarian tasting menu comprises creative, modern twists on exquisitely presented Vietnamese classics, rich in flavour combinations.

Name: Octo
Address: 2F, 75 Ho Tung Mau Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: With bare brick walls, a wood-clad high ceiling and black metal accents, the interior is the epitome of faux-industrial. Drenched in sunlight during the day, it is moodily lit at night. Either way, it has a real buzz that makes for a fun visit. Octo, which bills itself as a tapas restobar, is ideal for Spanish tapas, like their famous traditional croquettes, gazpacho and 48-month Iberico ham, washed down with a round of drinks.

Name: Truffle
Address: 73F, Landmark 81, Vinhomes Central Park, Binh Thanh District, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: This French restaurant soars over 300m above Saigon in the Landmark 81 skyscraper. It serves a stunning range of truffles: each tasting menu features the seasonal fungi sourced from different countries. The variety of breads is also impressive, each type boasting its own unique characteristics. The large dining area is surrounded by floor-to-ceiling windows that frame exceptional views of the city – a truly breathtaking experience!

Name: Chả Cá Anh Vũ (Dong Da)
Address: 120-K1 Giang Vo Street, O Cho Dua Ward, Dong Da District, Hanoi, 11511, Vietnam
Description: One of four branches in the city, this bouncy family-run operation offers slick service. The homely vibe is depicted by chequered tablecloths, patterned wallpaper and brightly painted murals. Chả cá, grilled catfish seasoned with turmeric, is the name of the game here, although you can add nem cá, fish spring rolls, canh cá, fish soup, and lòng cá, fish stomach, as extras. The fresh, tasty food delivers an explosion of flavours and textures.

Name: Å by T.U.N.G
Address: 31-33 Dang Dung Street, Tan Dinh Ward, Ho Chi Minh City, 700000, Vietnam
Description: With a ceiling mural of the Northern Lights, the airy dining space is a nod to chef Tung’s stint in Finland. On entering, diners first catch sight of the open kitchen before they are greeted by the chefs. Only one multi-course tasting menu is offered, and it changes every three months in line with the seasons. Chef Tung’s small plates are creative and original, paying tribute to Vietnamese food culture in terms of ingredients, flavours and techniques.

Name: Ngon Garden
Address: 70 Nguyen Du Street, Nguyen Du Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, 112310, Vietnam
Description: On the banks of Thien Quang Lake, this restaurant, reminiscent of an Indochinese-style villa, boasts a patio surrounded by lush greenery. The menu features specialities from all over Vietnam, alongside Asian delicacies of Chinese and Thai origins. From the century-old Bat Dan phở recipe from Hanoi and bún bò huế grilled beef from Nha Trang to fresh veggies from Dalat and live seafood from all over the world, every dish is deftly crafted and delicately seasoned.

Name: Bún Chả Hương Liên (Hai Ba Trung)
Address: 24 Le Van Huu Street, Phan Chu Trinh Ward, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, 113000, Vietnam
Description: Playing on their claim to fame, this joint displays photos of its celebrity guests and offers a Combo Obama, which includes a fried seafood roll, a bowl of the special bún chả and a bia hà nội. The bún chả itself delivers a satisfying blend of rustic flavours, with smoky pork, meat patties, fragrant herbs and fresh salad leaves. They also serve a tasty pork skewer.

Name: Backstage
Address: GF, Capella Hanoi, 11 Le Phung Hieu Street, Trang Tien Ward, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, 100000, Vietnam
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Your inner celebrity will revel in this opera-themed restaurant, whose open kitchen takes front stage. Signature dishes like Capella Pho and Bun Cha Hanoi respect their northern heritage, whilst featuring modern techniques with European touches that will leave your tastebuds singing an aria of delight. The impressive cocktail list offers some intriguing mixes. The theatrical setting showcases stunning costumes from the world’s greatest operas.

Name: Gastro Brisk
Description: Sam Van Landeghem has breathed new life into his family’s restaurant, formerly Michel. The stylish villa is the epitome of friendly, warm and unstarched. While the cobwebs have been dusted off the menu, the establishment’s devotion to the ingredient remains steadfast. Al dente Belgian asparagus with morels, broad beans and asparagus jus. The chef avows a fondness for legible flavours and family favourites, without forgetting the odd Asian twist. Gastro Brisk’s market-fresh cuisine ticks all the boxes!

Name: Jerome
Description: With its black and white chequered floor tiles and bench seats lining the walls, Jerome is reminiscent of a snug Parisian bistro. Alexe, your hostess, supervises the front of house with seamless, classy elegance. Meticulous attention to detail prevails throughout the establishment, including in chef Van der Stappen’s authentic yet subtle Franco-Belgian repertory. The chef is particularly attentive to the plating. A standout: veal blanquette simmered in a creamy succulent sauce with meatballs, slightly tangy button mushrooms, flat-leaf parsley and house-made potato fritters. Gutsy, wholesome flavours – the epitome of indulgent!

Name: LiJo
Description: Chef Jochen Provoost and your hostess, Lien, have superbly refurbished this mansion behind Saint Barbara’s Church in a crisp modern vein. The open kitchen cannot fail but catch the eye with its huge roasting spit and gleaming copper pans. Top-drawer produce, such as Spitsbroek asparagus, is crafted with textbook attention to detail. The chef might prepare a piece of Belgian beef with a creamy Archiduc sauce, green beans, pickled veggies, a gherkin mousse and a pickle potato. This dish is emblematic of the chef’s generous personality and his unstuffy version of fine dining goes down a treat with good vibes galore!

Name: Bistro Camélia
Address: Rue des Fossés Fleuris 38, Namur, 5000, Belgium
Description: Maxime Sanzot and his partner have opened this buzzy bistro with a pavement terrace, (sheer bliss in fine weather), just opposite their wine bar, Anthocyane. Bistro Camélia is equally attentive to the quality of the wine, as the cellar, well-stocked in natural wines, demonstrates. Local, seasonal produce dictates the culinary score and the chef may pair salmon trout in a crispy skin with the acidic tang of lightly pickled Belgian endive, briny samphire and a beurre blanc-style jus made out of fish bones. Unfussy, wholesome food that seeks to shine the spotlight on the delicacies of the Namur region.

Name: Bar Misera
Description: Tightly-packed tables, a scattering of wine bottles and an appetising lineup of dishes with a seafood slant to share set the scene in this buzzy, modern, almost quirky bistro. Bar Misera is THE place to go for a casual meal with the mates in Antwerp’s hip Nieuw Zuid district. Kick off your meal with a few nibbles from the wide-ranging array of snacks on offer, like egg mayonnaise or sardines, before moving onto larger portions. First-class quality and flawless freshness are paired with acidic tangy notes. Think seabass, seared to perfection in its skin, flanked by sea lavender and a herby butter and then coated in a subtle fresh foamy sauce. Diners choose their own sides. An amusing concept, underpinned by a stellar wine cellar.

Name: Belga Queen
Address: Rue du Fossé aux Loups 32, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Following a superlative makeover, the Belga Queen, an iconic culinary landmark of Brussels, is ready to write a new chapter of its story. This majestic edifice, which started out as a bank in the 18C, is famous for its remarkable architecture, boasting dome-shaped windows and imposing columns. Brasserie classics rub shoulders with more up-to-the-minute dishes on the menu, while the seafood bar reflects the chef’s passion. His North Sea waterzooi is made with seabass and plaice, together with crunchy veggies, a subtle velvety fish soup and briny touches of mussels and shrimp. Finish your meal in style with a Brussels waffle, made from scratch on demand. The Belga Queen is back!

Name: Plein 25
Description: Works of art line the walls of Neil Dieryckx-Visschers’ cheerful establishment, but the chef’s true artistry lies in his vibrant cooking. Dieryckx-Visschers sensitively reinterprets time-honoured family favourites and allows the ingredients to shout their name, albeit with the odd Asian tang. Examples include lamb from the Vandewalle butcher’s, served rare with a scrumptious layer of fat, while crisp green asparagus, braised wild garlic, black garlic cream, sautéed morels and a punchy gravy complete the feast. Both the set menu and the à la carte lineup sing an ode to first-class produce. What’s not to like?

Name: LUMA
Description: Diners choose between a dining area near the kitchen and another overlooking the manicured garden. Both are a picture of warmth and elegance. Weather permitting, make a beeline for the covered terrace in the garden. The establishment’s youthful chefs have opted for a forthright bistronomic slant with dishes to suit today’s palates. The sweetbread is juicy and crispy at the same time, while curly kale, bacon, onions and a bearnaise sauce laced in tarragon are among the sides you will find in autumn. LUMA makes no bones about scrupulously respecting the seasons in its menus.

Name: Söma
Description: Not far from the train station, Gare Saint-Paul, this little bistro is buzzing. This is not a place for white tablecloths or pompous service; rather a lively atmosphere, simple, trendy decor, a stylish waitress juggling tables in time to the beat of a well-chosen playlist, and a tiny open kitchen. At the helm is Sarah Hamza, chef and owner. Her cooking is fresh, generous and contemporary, with that unique quality that comes from her Algerian roots. This heritage also inspires her clever twists to dishes such as trout with smoked butter lentil stew, blood orange and harissa-glazed carrots. The menu is short, the dishes on the blackboard change often, and the ingredients speak for themselves.

Name: Les Volets Rouges
Description: This red-shuttered house exudes a subtle Basque feel, a reminder of the origins of the pair of brothers who own this bistro. The elder of the two draws on his extensive experience in Parisian kitchens in a new take on the flavours of South-West France; the younger brother smoothly orchestrates the restaurant floor and provides expert recommendations from the well-crafted wine list. The dishes change from day to day: butternut squash and sage ravioli topped with turmeric butter, Basque lamb confit served with smoked sucrine lettuce and a white chilli sauce. The simple, bold culinary spirit harks back to the owners' roots.

Name: Le Valtrivin
Description: The Le Valtrivin team, previously in Lapoutroie, has a new home in Ammerschwihr, in the heart of the Haut-Rhin vineyards. It's a brilliant move for this establishment, which is passionate about showcasing Alsace wines – and many others. Here within these old stone walls, a couple is at the helm – he takes pleasure in recommending gems from his incredible wine list; she rustles up appealing contemporary dishes, using top-notch local and seasonal ingredients. Be sure to indulge in one of her truly refined desserts. Highly recommended!

Name: Passage Secret
Description: Tucked away in an elegant 19C shopping arcade, this restaurant is aptly named. It is located inside the Caviar de Neuvic boutique, whose wares are available for purchase on the ground floor. On the floor above, a chic bistro-style dining room with period touches welcomes guests when the glass-roofed terrace is not in use. At the helm is Thomas Pasquereau, an unassuming former embassy chef, whose CV includes a stint training under Richard Coutanceau. His classically inspired cuisine is executed to perfection, a case in point being his Richelieu-style pâté en croûte (with foie gras), which showcases truly admirable technique. His passion for great French sauces is also clear, as exemplified by his Choron, Foyot and Maltese sauces.

Name: L'Orangerie
Address: 3 rue de la Marne, Menton, 06500, France
Description: This inconspicuous restaurant in the centre of town is actually home to a culinary powerhouse. The Japanese chef, who was sous-chef to Bruno Cirino at Hostellerie Jérôme, masterfully crafts his own addictive take on Mediterranean cuisine, putting a Japanese spin on locally sourced produce. Thanks to ultra-fresh ingredients, spot-on cooking and well-judged seasoning, everything comes together beautifully: eg artichoke hearts à la barigoule with prosciutto chips; salmon tataki with marinated vegetables, or sirloin steak with yuzu kosho. The terrace, partly covered by an awning, looks out onto a pedestrianised street.

Name: Maison Lagure
Address: 78 boulevard de la République, La Garenne-Colombes, 92250, France
Description: In this bistro, named after a coastal dune plant, chef Julien Dumas (Bellefeuille, Lucas Carton) works hand in hand with his talented associate Lucas Boisseau to cook up tempting bistronomy cuisine. The focus is on the essentials, with a few creative flourishes: fillet of pollack, grilled wild asparagus with a little bite, cockles and onions served in their jus; to finish, a fresh and vibrant fennel and grapefruit dessert rife with contrasting flavours. The concise menu is always evolving, with a good-value set menu at lunchtime and tasting menus in the evening. The sleek and elegant interior features a large mottled mirror, suspended lighting, faux concrete walls, hardwood floors, a glass-fronted wine cellar and eclectic decorative touches.

Name: Taulissa
Address: Maison Albar - Le Victoria, 6 avenue de Suède, Nice, 06000, France
Description: High up on the sixth floor of Maison Albar - Le Victoria hotel, this restaurant boasts a picture-postcard panoramic view, with the city on one side, the sea on the other. In this elegant, light-filled dining space dotted with maritime details, Glenn Viel and his associate Fred Grava put their own spin on Southern French cuisine, using local produce and intensely flavoured jus. Dishes such as catch of the day and confit lamb shoulder are presented tableside by the attentive and friendly team, adding theatricality to a dining experience that allows diners to savour the Mediterranean.

Name: Vinello
Description: The kitchen of this lovely Italian restaurant in the Batignolles neighbourhood is manned by a Sicilian chef with international experience. A trendy interior with exposed stone, an open kitchen and smoked-glass mirrors that make for an unpolished feel. Expect technical and meticulous contemporary bistro cuisine with a decidedly Italian bias. Impeccable ingredients, elevated without frills. In addition to an enticing à la carte menu, there is a wallet-friendly lunch set menu; in the evening, choose dishes à la carte. To be washed down with carefully selected fine Italian and international wines.

Name: Curnonsky
Description: Chef Benjamin Capelier is back at the helm of this restaurant that he already ran once before. Renamed Curnonsky in homage to the famous food critic and his first restaurant in Lyon, the establishment remains true to its original spirit: a wallet-friendly single set menu for lunch and a multi-course tasting experience at dinner. In a very simple and convivial setting, this discreet and focused chef delivers delicious modern cuisine, with each dish reflecting meticulous attention to texture and flavour. He is passionate about wine (an understatement) and recommends the perfect pairings himself from an exceptional wine list at wine merchant prices.

Name: Agora
Address: 19 rue de la Boucherie, Vannes, 56000, France
Description: Guillaume Le Bozec, who earned his stripes in the kitchens of Manoir de la Boulaie, Le Pressoir and Maison Troisgros, is at the helm of this establishment set on a quiet street. At his side, his partner Delphine Dugor attentively manages the restaurant floor. The chef creates modern cuisine using mainly local produce, accented here and there with exotic touches courtesy of subtly deployed spices – and served as a set menu. The contemporary space is decorated with paintings by the chef himself, contributing to a warm and relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Les Nymphéas
Description: Perched on the heights of Chasse-sur-Rhône, the Domaine de Gorneton weaves a magical bucolic spell. This 17C stone-built manor houses guestrooms, a swimming pool and a restaurant, whose name is a nod to the waterlilies on the pond. The simple and inviting dining area features light parquet floors and exposed rafters. Chef Loïc Plestin (ex La Loge Bertin in Manosque) sculpts seriously succulent fare (particularly the jus): chicken fricassee with melt-in-the-mouth spinach, fragrant tomato jus and mushrooms; compressed apple terrine, white chocolate ganache and Breton biscuit.

Name: Hokusaï
Address: Metropolitan Paris Tour Eiffel, 3 rue des Belles-Feuilles, Paris, 75016, France
Description: This hotel on Place de Mexico is introducing a new concept of Japanese cuisine with a South American twist. In a contemporary, minimalist setting, the menu combines signature rolls, sushi and teriyaki chicken with ceviche and Hispanic ingredients such as chimichurri sauce and jalapeño. Freshness and flavour are the order of the day.

Name: La Meunière
Description: Opened in 1921 in the Presqu'île area, this bouchon with an authentic retro setting hasn't aged a bit. The menu features generous, popular Lyonnais cuisine, with specialities such as tablier de sapeur with gribiche sauce, house-made escargot quenelles, kid goat sweetbreads, calf's head, pink praline flan pâtissier. The colourful front-of-house team brings character to this buzzing spot, where locals and tourists in search of delicious food and authenticity rub shoulders.

Name: Glaz
Address: 9 place de la République, Pont-Croix, 29790, France
Description: On the village square, Glaz – a Breton word evoking the sea's shifting hues of green, blue, and grey – strikes a balance between old and new: wrought iron, earthenware and rugs sit alongside wood panelling, copper and plants. Tanios Nakhlé Cerruti presides in the kitchen; Émeline Macé oversees the dining room and wine cellar. Born in Saint-Malo to an Italian mother and Lebanese father, the chef draws on his heritage and his travels to craft precise fusion bistronomy dishes with their roots in French culinary tradition. The menu showcases local ingredients, many organic, skilfully elevated with spices.

Name: L'Auberge des Crus
Description: This traditional bistro has bags of charm, with its wood panelling, 1940s wooden bar and a spacious wine cellar with a dedicated tasting area. The appealing menu features bistro classics made from quality ingredients: pâté en croûte with veal sweetbreads and foie gras, wild Burgundy snails, Black Angus steak tartare, chateaubriand with pepper sauce, and tarte Tatin, 70% Guanaja chocolate mousse. Delicious, confidently executed dishes served in a friendly atmosphere that is reminiscent of a wine bar and has a tempting selection of wines by the glass at reasonable prices.

Name: Osteria Ime
Description: In this pretty, welcoming restaurant, the female chef from Albania, who has adopted Italian culinary traditions over her many years in the country, serves a choice of tasting menus. Her dishes have distinct geographical names and are full of colour and prepared from top-quality ingredients which change with the passing seasons. There are only a few tables available, so booking ahead is always a good idea. You’ll be warmly welcomed with a friendly smile that sets the tone for what is sure to be a highly enjoyable evening.

Name: Alessandro Borghese
Address: Calle Seconda del Cristo 2040, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: This restaurant is situated in the Casinò di Venezia, or to be more precise, Palazzo Ca’ Vendramin Calergi, a 16C building overlooking the Grand Canal which boasts a beautiful garden in which meals are served on warm summer evenings. Chef Alessandro Borghese serves modern and attractive cuisine which is full of enticing flavours. There are two tasting menus available, with the option of adding the chef’s signature dishes to either of these.

Name: Terraforte
Address: Via Bagnoli Terriccio 12, Castellina Marittima, 56040, Italy
Description: In an elegant, country-house setting, Terraforte occupies an old hay barn on the beautiful, vast Il Terriccio estate, where 1 500 hectares of tranquil, bucolic Tuscan landscapes are home to horses, olive trees and the estate’s renowned vineyards (Lupicaia wines). The cuisine focuses on zero-mile ingredients, with an exclusive use of produce sourced from the estate, including beef, game, chicken, vegetables, aromatic herbs and excellent wine. The two menus (three or seven courses) showcase imaginative and well-balanced dishes which never lose the clean, decisive flavours of their top-quality ingredients. In fine weather, don’t miss the opportunity to enjoy the charming outdoor space and even, perhaps, spend a night on the estate by staying at the La Marrana villa.

Name: Pepe Nero
Description: Situated on the western shore of Lake Bolsena, Pepe Nero is a small restaurant with modern furnishings and a maritime air, where attentive and professional service allows guests to appreciate the excellent cuisine (mainly fish and seafood) to the full. Don’t miss the cavatelli pasta with a mussel sauce flavoured with burnt lemon, or the fresh and fragrant fried squid served in a cardboard box. The wine list features labels from the region and further afield, while a small terrace offers lakeside dining right on the beach.

Name: Storico Caffè Grande - Osteria del Centro
Description: Almost all the main dishes at this restaurant are grilled (mostly meat but there are also fish options), plus there’s a good choice of appetisers, including substantial options such as tripe and sweetbreads, with tasting menus that combine starters and main courses. The à la carte features a generous selection of classic, well-prepared dishes made from top-quality ingredients. The restaurant occupies the premises of a historic café that has experienced closures and problems in the past but has now been courageously reopened by three young business partners.

Name: Osteria FraSe
Address: Via Crociata 9, Piove di Sacco, 35028, Italy
Description: In this restaurant, husband Francesco takes care of the wine, while his wife Serena is at the helm in the open-view kitchen, creating dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (including raw options), fresh pasta dishes and classic recipes with the occasional imaginative twist or the addition of exotic fruit. This is a modern and welcoming osteria with a simple decor, where the female staff provide excellent service with a friendly smile.

Name: Machettö
Address: Via Vittorio Veneto 23, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description: Situated amid the picturesque alleyways of the historic centre, this beautiful restaurant boasts an elegant decor and a warm, friendly welcome. Here, the young, talented chef (originally from Campania but now settled in Liguria) serves Mediterranean cuisine with a traditional regional influence cleverly added to each dish. Our favourite dishes included the excellent trenette pasta with octopus ragù and 24-month-aged parmesan fondue, and the timeless “brandacujun”, which is freshly prepared and served at your table by the chef himself.

Name: NUH Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Situated in Tivoli’s historic centre, this restaurant has a young chef at the helm who skilfully pays tribute to the region’s gastronomic traditions. Although the menu also features a few fish dishes and the occasional ingredient from outside Lazio, it is the dishes made from local produce with their intense, delicious flavours that will linger long in the memory.

Name: Nunù Trattoria Moderna
Address: Corso Giuseppe Garibaldi 32, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the seafront promenade, this friendly, colourful restaurant serves delicious, carefully prepared fish and meat dishes inspired by the traditions of Campania yet reinterpreted with a touch of imagination and character by skilful owner-chef Nunzio Spagnuolo. Our inspector’s favourite dish was the ravioli alla caprese with three types of tomato, provolone del Monaco cheese and basil-infused olive oil.

Name: Locanda Sant'Agata
Address: via del Brennero, SS 12 km 5,812, San Giuliano Terme, 55016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Not far from the village, this pleasant boutique hotel is home to a friendly, well-kept restaurant surrounded by a relaxing garden where guests can enjoy alfresco dining in summer. The menu features traditional meat and fish dishes with the occasional modern, personalised twist, such as “calamarotto” – squid (calamaro) stuffed with seafood pancotto, vegetables in dry vermouth and confit plum tomatoes.

Name: Il Sommelier
Description: This small, intimate restaurant next to the elegant Palazzo Roccabruna in the historic centre is slightly off the beaten track despite its central location. Recently opened by the Poletti brothers (one in the kitchen, the other front of house), with an attractive dining room designed by the owners’ father, the restaurant serves top-quality ingredients (especially fish and seafood) in dishes which include modern influences (the mango cheesecake is delicious) and a pleasing classic appeal (raw fish dishes).

Name: Locanda Le Logge
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Classic Cuisine
Description: Occupying a period building in the heart of this beautiful village, with an outdoor dining space laid out under the portico in summer, this restaurant serves typical cuisine from the Marche on its various tasting menus and à la carte supplemented by daily specials. Boasting a rustic and pleasantly informal atmosphere, the restaurant also offers six romantic guestrooms with wrought-iron beds, including a four-poster bed in the Sogno room.

Name: Exforo
Description: Occupying old stables in the square where the town’s livestock market was once held, this restaurant boasts charming views of the Prato della Valle gardens. Also home to a bistro serving aperitif snacks and a cocktail bar for post-dinner drinks, the main restaurant is very much the focal point here, with its dark-coloured, contemporary decor and colourful, modern cuisine. In summer, don’t miss the summer terrace with its fine views.

Name: Mezcal
Address: Carr. Transpeninsular KM. 12.5 Int., Bahía Santa María, Cabo San Lucas, 23450, Mexico
Description: Fine dining with an ocean view? It's the promise behind Mezcal, tucked inside the posh Montage Los Cabos. Those views of the crashing Pacific are best enjoyed on the patio, where heaters chase away the chill from the ocean breeze. From the wines sourced across Mexico to a tasting menu inspired by regional mercados, it's a celebration of all things Mexican. The cooking is on point, and à la carte offerings are equally tempting. Begin with a salad of Xochimilco chinampas squash flower with black bean puree. Entrees include a jocoque-filled plantain mollete served over a bed of mole or tender lamb birria with an onion and cilantro foam. Prickly pear sorbet, presented inside the fruit, is a refreshing closer.

Name: Jabalina
Address: C. Padre Mier 859, Barrio Antiguo, Centro, Monterrey, 64000, Mexico
Description: They've opened elsewhere, but this location in Barrio Antiguo is the original. Sit indoors in the dining room with tall ceilings and raised beds with plants, or outside on the patio with a nice view of their parrilla and bar. Come hungry or with a group, as the plates are large and you'll want to enjoy a leisurely al fresco meal with a cocktail in hand. While there's plenty to choose from, don't miss the arrachera tacos, with three large flour tortillas with a cheese crust and topped with chopped arrachera and guacamole. Chicharrón mixto served with guacamole and quesadillas is another hit. Carrot cake with salted caramel sauce and a scoop of toasted coconut ice cream and cashews is an enticing dessert.

Name: LÍMO Heritage Kitchen at Suelo Sur
Address: Lote 320, Centro, San José del Cabo, 23400, Mexico
Description: Just outside of San José del Cabo, this farm to table, open-air restaurant is the showpiece of Chef Guillermo J. Gómez, who displays his affection for local ingredients on a menu divided by garden, sea, roots, and live fire. Begin with bread crafted from blue corn and organic whole wheat then grilled over a live fire and set with a puree of seasonal vegetables. Appetizers are equally enticing, as in the yellowtail jack that's gently grilled, then sliced sashimi-style and served with a coconut aguachile and plantain puree. Berkshire pig "Matamabre" with toasted sweet corn and poblano chili stew is just one of the alluring main dishes at this garden oasis where a laidback ambience adds to the experience.

Name: Lalo!
Description: Note: This restaurant is temporarily closed.New isn't always best, and this long-standing spot in Roma from the same people behind Maximo is further proof. It's colorful and upbeat here, where cafe lights are strung overhead, a large communal table runs down the center of the space, and an open kitchen adds to the lively ambience. It's all about breakfast and lunch here. Pastries and bread are baked in house and are a worthy order first thing, though there are a number of other strong contenders. French toast is a classic, done here with fresh berries, berry sauce, and a thick, rich whipped cream, or go savory with an oversized bowl of chilaquiles piled with crispy tortilla chips in a vibrant verde salsa. At lunch, sandwiches, pastas, and pizza are available.

Name: Tacos Piedra 1
Address: Lirios 1830, Calle Cerro De La Silla, Monterrey, 64810, Mexico
Description: Located in the Colonia Tecnologico, this long-standing taqueria is best known for one thing—tacos mañaneros, or morning tacos. Order, then find a seat in their clean, organized dining room set with red plastic chairs and tables. They're open early if you're hankering for a breakfast taco filled with eggs and potatoes, but don't skip the chicharron a la Mexicana or their barbacoa, available on corn or flour tortillas. It's all over by 2:00pm, so don't wait too long, and don't forget cash.

Name: Al Pairo at Solaz
Address: Corredor Turistico, Km 19, Acceso B, Cabo Real, Cabo San Lucas, 23405, Mexico
Description: This contemporary Mexican restaurant with a stylish dining room and spacious covered patio enjoys a posh setting inside the luxe Solaz resort. The chef's Veracruz upbringing is immediately evident on a menu that prioritizes Baja ingredients and locally caught seafood. All meals should begin with a basket of tortilla chips and guacamole before moving on to other tempting appetizers like salpicon de Castacan, a mix of raw shrimp and cubed pork belly in a salsa negra. Entrees are seafood heavy, as in the confit Mayan octopus, seared and served atop house-made green chorizo and queso fresco with a tableside pour of savory bean and pork sauce. Do save room for dessert, especially the verbena pastry with cantaloupe ice cream.

Name: Barbacoa Obispo Cocina Rural
Address: Calz. San Felipe del Agua 327, San Felipe, Agencia Municipal de San Felipe del Agua, Oaxaca, 68026, Mexico
Description: The name slightly gives it away, as barbacoa cooked underground in a hot stone-lined oven is certainly a big deal here. However, Barbacoa Obispo Cocina Rural, where Oaxacan cuisine is front and center, also shines a spotlight on birria and jabali, which can be served as memelas, blandos, quesadillas, or tlayudas, as well as tacos al vapor. Decisions aren't easy with so many tempting offerings, but hits include barbacoa blandos (your choice of meat), surtidos (with a blend of cuts), or meat-filled tetelas. Of course, their weekly specials designed for sharing at the table are also a good idea. You may be stuffed, but nothing closes out a meal here quite like a cafe de olla sided by a concha with whipped cream and strawberries.

Name: Ricos Tacos Toluca
Description: In more than two decades, this taqueria has moved three times. It's now situated in the Centro Histórico of Mexico City near the Mercado De San Juan. There are just a few red stools, so come early or you'll eat standing up. This taqueria specializes in handmade Toluca-style chorizo and sausages. Sample individually to appreciate the flavors and unique characters of each chorizo or mix them for an equally satisfying experience. Top with grilled or fresh onions, French fries, cilantro and various salsas. Obispo is a large pork-based sausage, seared ever so slightly for a delicate crisp, while chorizo tamarindo is diced then grilled and delivers a subtle sweetness and terrific flavor.

Name: Casona Restaurante
Address: Casona Roma Norte, C. Durango 280, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, 06700, Mexico
Description: Aquiles is the all-day dining concept inside the Casona Roma Norte but this isn't your average hotel restaurant. This stylish spot just off the lobby is loaded with natural light, and a wall enhanced with a floral mural and live greenery adds to the uplifting ambience. Breakfast and lunch are on offer, but dinner is when the à la carte takes center stage. The cooking is contemporary with Mexican ingredients and inflections. His uncomplicated style is best seen in starters like steak tartare or tortilla soup. Like every good hotel restaurant worth its salt, the burger is a good mainstay, while other main dishes range from hearty braised short rib to lighter dishes like fish en papillote.

Name: Lina
Address: Av. Yucatán 147, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, 06700, Mexico
Description: With a welcoming vibe and an open kitchen, this quaint spot in Roma bursts with contemporary charm. The service is all heart here, where Chef Mariana Villegas Martínez draws on her experiences and travels to inspire her contemporary Mexican cooking. From the seasonal products highlighted to the harmony of flavors, this is cooking that shows great care and thoughtfulness. Far from flashy, it's straightforward but skillful, perhaps best seen in a plate of beautifully charred squash sided by a smoky pine nut sauce. Chicken with crispy skin is set with roasted peaches and a mushroom medley, but it's the rich mole coloradito that makes the dish especially memorable. Close out with a fruit-layered tres leches for a real treat.

Name: Maizajo
Address: Fernando Montes De Oca 113, Condesa, Cuauhtémoc, 06140, Mexico
Description: While their downstairs taqueria is standing room only, upstairs at Maizajo, diners are encouraged to pull up a chair. There is a clear industrial chic aesthetic to this dining room, where I-beams stand in for legs at metal tables and chairs are made from heavy rebar.You'll be greeted with some tostadas and a spicy habanero and pepita salsa at your table as you peruse Chef Santiago Muñoz Moctezuma's menu. Top picks include an oven-roasted blue corn tostada topped with avocado puree and sliced raw yellowfin tuna in a black sesame oil and soy dressing, as well as the tamal de boda. This vegetarian corn tamal filled with stewed poblano chile, leeks, and chard in an achiote, tomato and habanero salsa is topped with thinly sliced tubers for a dish that is equal parts sweet and earthy.

Name: Baldio
Address: Antonio Solá 26, Colonia Condesa, Cuauhtémoc, 06140, Mexico
Description: Taking inspiration from London's Silo, where Chef Max MacLean previously worked, Baldio is zeroing in on zero waste. It's all about a holistic approach to sustainability, going beyond the locally caught freshwater fish and vegetables from chinampas farms to include in-house water purification and recycled corn husk paper for printing. Green practices aside, this restaurant doesn't pull any punches when it comes to cooking. Fire-roasted carrots and broccoli over a bed of creamy pipián make for the perfect opener before moving on to main dishes like their pork, grilled over a live fire and accompanied by a flavorful pataxte mole. Finish with the rich and creamy tarta de chocolate dusted with starfruit powder.

Name: Nois
Address: Avenida José María Morelos 701, Centro, Oaxaca, 68000, Mexico
Description: There are several ways to experience this ambitious, two-story restaurant. The ground floor is a chic lounge where bartenders shake and stir potent, boozy drinks. Up the winding staircase, find an open kitchen committed to crafting a serious tasting menu focused on seafood. To be clear, this is a team that likes to take risks and keep diners on their toes. Familiar ingredients like Oaxacan cheese, chintextle, starfruit, and hoja santa are deployed in imaginative, daring ways. Recent highlights include wild-caught tuna tataki rolled in vegetable ash as well as a refreshingly homey buffalo taco brushed in a rich demi-glace. Gracious, personable servers round out this satisfying, thoughtful experience in the heart of Oaxaca.

Name: Brio
Address: Armenta y López 300, Centro, Oaxaca, 68000, Mexico
Description: With its terraced setting overlooking a church in the center of the city, Brio looks and feels very Oaxacan. It's fitting, then, that the menu echoes the tribute to the region with its focus on local dishes and ingredients given a hint of Mediterranean flair. The wood-fired grill is the centerpiece, with all proteins kissed by the flames. Begin with an appetizer such as the roasted beet salad set atop chile de agua cream sauce and chamomile honey alongside sliced tomatoes and apples. Then, bone-in pork chop benefits from the wood fire, but the peanut mole is the last word. Crème brûlée is given a twist here, infused with poleo for a brightness not often seen.

Name: Castacán
Address: C. Puebla 387, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, 06700, Mexico
Description: There are two reasons to make a beeline to this Roma Norte restaurant and they're both focused on pork. This spot's large staff welcomes diners at both lunch and dinner, but everyone is focused on the food. Cochinita pibil and lechon tacos compete for your attention, so get both. Good quality tortillas get things off to a good start. The slow-roasted, marinated pork that's shredded and enhanced with pickled red onions is top notch, while the lechon tacos plate tender, roast suckling pig with pieces of crispy skin for a standout bite. A wide range of salsas is on offer, from spicy habanero and a sesame aioli to mild yogurt sauce.

Name: Mision 19
Address: Via Corporativo, 2, Misión de San Javier 10643, Zona Urbana Rio, Tijuana, 22010, Mexico
Description: The name is a reference to the 18 Catholic missions that exist in Baja California. Their mission is a bit more down-to-earth: To celebrate the area's food. Located on the second floor of Vía Corporativo, Mexico's second self-sustainable building, the restaurant strives for sustainability by utilizing products that do not travel more than 200km from farm to table. Noteworthy dishes include aguachile, featuring slivers of local rockot dressed with salsa verde and avocado puree. Lechon prensado is an enticing roasted pork plated with a zesty roasted tomatillo salsa as well as reduced pork jus. It is a feast in itself, perhaps best accompanied by a rich tinta from one of the Valle de Guadalupe labels on offer.

Name: Woodend
Address: Maroma, A Belmond Hotel, Carr. Cancún - Tulum Km. 51, Playa del Carmen, 77710, Mexico
Description: Acclaimed Chef Curtis Stone lends his name and refined culinary sensibilities to this seaside retreat, and though he’s unlikely to be present in the flesh, rest assured that you are in good hands regardless. As the first step into the smoke-perfumed room will give away, the cooking here centers around live fire, with a charcoal oven and wood-fired grill lending their aroma to a small menu that leans to bold simplicity. Local seafood and well-marbled steaks from Oklahoma make up the mains, while sides like crunchy potato pavé with jocoque and buttery Parisian gnocchi with endive and poblano are tasty enough to stand on their own. For dessert, a twist on tarte tatin with pineapple, mezcal-tinged caramel, and toasted vanilla ice cream hits just the right mark.

Name: Taqueria El Paisa
Address: Joaquin Garcia Icazbalceta 36, San Rafael, Cuauhtémoc, 06470, Mexico
Description: On a corner in San Rafael, this bustling taqueria is a well-oiled machine. Everyone comes for the suadero, which is best ordered late in the evening when the meat has had hours to braise in its own fat. The al pastor is worth a try too. Whatever the order, tacos are on the small side so aim for three or four per person. Once through the queue, people eat wherever they can: sitting on the curb, leaning against a building, or on the hoods of their cars.

Name: Atarraya
Address: Guerrero 633 Brisas de Zicatela, La Punta, Brisas de Zicatela, 70934, Mexico
Description: Is there a cooler restaurant in Puerto Escondido? Channeling the sleekness of a Japanese zen garden, the outdoor space is picture-perfect and built out with handsome wood beams, a backlit bar, and an old tree that stretches across the dining room. The cooking is familiar fare, seasoned and presented with the right amount of care: Crisp tostadas stacked with pan-fried ribeye, squares of tuna rolled in sesame seeds, and vibrant salsas that upgrade everything they touch. You could make a meal out of the appetizers alone or press on with a chile relleno stuffed with vegetables and blanketed in a smooth manzano pepper sauce. Though the cocktail offerings are succinct and stick largely to the classics, the bartenders shake and stir with notable skill.

Name: Casa Banana
Address: Tulum-Boca Paila Km. 7.5, Tulum Beach, Tulum, 77780, Mexico
Description: Long a favorite of the Zona Hotelera dining scene, this boisterous spot offers more than just a hip, lively atmosphere—the crowds flock here to indulge in a menu of rustic, satisfying Argentine cooking. Centered around a traditional wood-fired oven and parrillada, the menu presents a bevy of options to suit diverse tastes. Signature appetizers like juicy empanadas or roasted artichokes with smoked labne and fried capers are a cut above. For mains, carnivores will find satisfaction with the requisite hearty steaks, which share space with fresh seafood and vegetarian options, as in whole roasted fish, or vegetarian offerings like a gratin of spinach gnocchi. Finish with a sweetly satisfying warm dulce de leche-filled crepe, paired with banana ice cream.

Name: NÜ Tulum
Address: NEST Tulum, Tulum-Boca Paila Km. 8.7, Tulum Beach, Tulum, 77780, Mexico
Description: Although the outdoor jungle-chic setting here fits right in with the numerous restaurants of this heavily trafficked strip, the cooking offers plenty of personality to set it apart from the pack. This menu utilizes a plethora of local ingredients (many from Mestiza de Indias, a regenerative farm in the Yucatan Peninsula), blending tradition with novelty for memorable results. Vegetables play a key role, whether in meat-free dishes like an “agrodolce” of sweet potato and squash enriched with peanuts or in more substantial items like xcatic chiles filled with boudin blanc. A delicious finale of barbecued pineapple and almond cake boasts an elegant simplicity.

Name: Oryx
Address: Blvd. Agua Caliente 10750, Int. 84, Tijuana, 22014, Mexico
Description: This Tijuana favorite is the domain of Chef Ruffo Ibarra. The dining room boasts a dressed-up industrial look with dark earthy colors, exposed red brick walls, wood and tiled flooring, metal beams and warm lighting.The menu is a contemporary take on Mexican cuisine and lists an extensive selection of items including chilled seafood starters and grilled steaks. Consomé de camarón con hongas is presented with chopped raw shrimp, then filled tableside with a hot, deeply flavorful shrimp broth which gently poaches the shrimp. Golden-brown, crisped striped bass shares the plate with creamy onion puree, bits of fried kale and some salsa verde. The stack of churros, served warm and accompanied by bourbon ice cream, make for a fine ending.

Name: Zandunga
Address: Manuel García Vigil 512 E., Oaxaca, 68000, Mexico
Description: Sunlight beams down through an open roof and into this colorful, spacious courtyard set with handsome wooden tables. Pottery, textiles and paintings by local artists adorn every wall in sight. Truly, this restaurant captures the vibrant spirit of downtown Oaxaca. It’s a lovely scene to take in while exploring a curated menu focused on traditional regional flavors. Start with the garnachas, the masa carefully fried and topped with tender, shredded beef and pickled cabbage, before moving on to the crispy plantains stuffed with queso and crema that are both tropical and savory. Tamales come prepared with mole negro, sweet corn or raisins. A generous platter featuring many of these standout dishes offers diners an efficient way to sample everything.

Name: Arbol
Address: Las Ventanas al Paraiso, A Rosewood Resort, Carr. Transpeninsular Km. 19.5, San José del Cabo, 23405, Mexico
Description: Located within Rosewood's Las Ventanas al Paraiso, this beguiling setting hosts diners in an indoor/outdoor space arranged with chunky blond wood tables on a polished stone patio. Lantern-hung branches cast a rosy glow.The large menu is impressively prepared and is founded on Indian specialties. However, the range of offerings is further enhanced by charcoal-grilled meats and seafood, as well as an abundance of Asian specialties. The Punjabi fish masala features the catch of the day, which is gently cooked in a zesty, moderately spiced tomato-based sauce enriched with ground cashews and flecked with herbs and spices. It comes served with spice-tinted basmati pilaf and Indian-style pickled vegetables and is best paired with butter-brushed naan hot off the tandoor.

Name: Entremar
Description: There are plenty of enviable seats at Entremar, though certainly those on the terrace under the awnings and surrounded by plants are first on the list. Inside, try to book on the first floor, with the best tables resting in a row at the back overlooking the Plaza Uruguay.Of course, Entremar is about so much more than a good seat, and some of the best dishes to order include fresh tuna tostadas with chipotle sauce, a little avocado and fried leek, giving them a crunchy touch. Choose wisely when it comes to the aguachile, as the red is spicy, while pescado a la talla is the restaurant's signature dish. The boneless grilled fish is a feast for the eyes with its two sides sharing a red and green sauce. Finish with the tarta de higos or merengue con fresas.

Name: Hugo
Address: Av. Veracruz 38, Roma Norte, Cuauhtémoc, 06700, Mexico
Description: With its terrace shaded by an awning and likable ambience, Hugo is the sort of place you'll want to return to time and again. While the wine list is indeed extensive, giving it its wine bar classification, it's not just about the bottles here; it's as equally well liked for its bistro-style menu. Quality products shine in dishes with pleasing presentations, while the contemporary cuisine remains faithful to traditional flavors.

Name: El Tigre Silencioso
Description: This cool Roma Norte spot has a front courtyard laid with stone blocks, set with tables, and enhanced by old growth trees. The interior dining area is set a few steps above and is fronted by ivy-wrapped columns and a wrap-around terrace for additional al fresco dining. Inside, the space features wood plank flooring, stucco walls, a bar, and open kitchen in back.The menu offers an abundant array of choices, and the creative items are sparked by an intriguing combination of ingredients. Empanadas norteños is a golden-crisped half-moon stuffed with chicharrón prensado and smoked fish. The zesty octopus stew is topped with bits of crunchy menudo and accompanied by freshly made tortillas.

Name: Botánico
Description: Upon first glance, it may not look like much, but the exterior belies the oasis found within. Tall cacti, a lake stocked with fish and a convivial atmosphere make this a natural choice for date night, but this laidback spot is equally well suited to families and groups too. Everyone enjoys being here as they connect over plates like homemade ravioli with blue crab and a pumpkin cream base, or a simple grilled fish with al dente vegetables. Crème brûlée delivers a strange-sounding surprise with the addition of Kalamata olive, but it's a convincing finale.

Name: Kous Kous
Address: Carr. Tecate Ensenada, Km 73.30, Valle de Guadalupe, 22750, Mexico
Description: This stunning restaurant with dramatic views may seem like other outdoor spots in the area but keep down the path and a lively space draped with curtains and Moroccan lamps soon appears, revealing the singular experience. Come for an unexpected yet memorable meal spotlighting Moroccan cuisine. There is plenty of heart and loads of flavor in this family-style selection where guests take their pick of protein for the tagine. Kick the meal off with flatbread, made in-house, along with a refreshing cucumber salad. From the chicken with olives to the honey lamb, the tagine offerings are exceptional, but their namesake couscous, with caramelized onions, garbanzo beans and golden raisins, almost steals the show.

Name: Taqueria La Principal
Address: Principal, Valle de Guadalupe, Valle de Guadalupe, 22750, Mexico
Description: Situated in a warehouse space with plastic furniture, this quintessential no-frills roadside taqueria doesn’t get a lot of points for ambience, but happily the simple, satisfying fare speaks for itself. The compact menu doesn’t call for extensive decision-making: diners choose between three meats (thinly sliced beef asada, spice-marinated pork adobada, and, for the more adventurous, tender tripa), and their vehicle of choice (corn or flour tortilla, burrito, torta, etc.) and then watch the magic come together before their eyes. Lively, well-balanced salsas and perfectly fresh toppings combine with flavorful grill-kissed meats for love at first bite, and the late nighttime hours of operation might be a lifesaver after a busy day of wine tasting.

Name: Sarde
Description: Set in the Roma Norte neighborhood in a charming three-story townhouse, Sarde makes no bones about its specialty—the name says it all. Sarde, which means "sardine" in French and Italian, is focused on the sea, and their contemporary dishes are rooted in the freshest seasonally appropriate product possible from the Mexican coasts. Cold dishes of Japanese cuts like kampachi and macarela stand out alongside modern reinterpretations of familiar favorites like fish and chips.Attention to detail, especially when it comes to presentation, is appreciated in this warm and welcoming spot with exposed brick and wood details. The cozy bar entices with interesting cocktails and is a nice perch for solo diners.

Name: Criollo
Address: Casa Criollo, Av. Francisco I. Madero 129, Oaxaca, 68000, Mexico
