Description: Would you like to experience a distinctive culinary journey? Book a table at Aiô now. Here, the proposal is based on Taiwanese cuisine with international touches that take you on a journey through surprising flavours. Set on the same street as its sister restaurant, Mapu, the establishment features a characteristic glass façade and, inside, a bar at the entrance offering an intriguing variety of drinks: signature, re‑imagined and even Taiwanese‑inspired. The menu is straightforward and makes no distinction between starters and mains, which allows for sharing or opting for an individual tasting menu. A standout dish? O Crudo de Peixe (raw fish) made with aged fish, ponzu, chilli oil and finished with crunchy black‑rice popcorn.

Name: Sud, O Pássaro Verde
Address: Rua Visconde de Carandaí 35, Rio de Janeiro, 22460-020, Brazil
Description: Walking into this restaurant is like entering the home of a friend, as you’ll need to knock on the door or announce your presence in order to be let in. Occupying a house in the quiet Jardim Botânico district, this is the domain of chef Roberta Sudbrack who describes it as a space in which to “tell and eat stories”. Inside, the decor is modest yet welcoming, with an impressive wood-fired oven next to the main dining room, plus a charming open kitchen, from which comforting home-style dishes emerge prepared with ingredients from small-scale local producers. As a result, the menu changes daily in line with market availability and freshness. However, one mainstay that is always on the menu is the superbly textured and irresistibly flavoured chocolate cake (“bolo de chocolate molhadinho”).

Name: Giuseppe Grill Leblon
Address: Avenida Bartolomeu Mitre 370, Rio de Janeiro, 22431-001, Brazil
Description: As the name clearly states, all the dishes (fish and meat) at this restaurant are cooked on the charcoal grill. The menu here includes dry-aged meat options (T-bone, prime rib, bone-in tenderloin etc). Other standout dishes include the Maminha (sirloin trip-tip), the Picanha supra sumo (supra sumo rump cap), the brand’s registered trademark, as well as the slow-cooked Uruguayan lamb shoulder served with its own jus. A number of fish and seafood options are also on display, which vary according to availability on the day. The decor here features exposed stone walls, wooden chairs and leather sofas, all of which combine to add a rustic-elegant touch. Not forgetting the extensive wine cellar in the basement, featuring over 400 labels from different countries.

Name: Chez Claude
Address: Rua Conde de Bernadotte 26 - Lojas Q e R, Rio de Janeiro, 22430-200, Brazil
Description: Run by the famous French chef Claude Troisgros, this dining space has plenty of detail to pique your interest. Firstly, the completely open kitchen in the centre of the room, enabling diners to watch dishes being prepared at close quarters that are based around French cuisine with the addition of some Brazilian-inspired elements and ingredients. And secondly, the fact that dishes on the classic menu are served in bowls for sharing, to add to the sense of family-style cooking. On the à la carte, which changes in line with the seasons of the year, we can recommend dishes such as the stuffed quail with herb farofa, chard confit and grape sauce. The impressively textured melted chocolate gâteau, served with crème fraîche, is the perfect way to round off your dining experience.

Name: Casa Rios
Description: Chef Rodrigo Aguiar, originally from Rio de Janeiro, combined his skills with owner Giovanna Perrone to realise her dream here. This charming restaurant features an open kitchen where guests can view the wood oven and churrasco grill, both of which exude the smoky flavours for which Casa Rios is famous. If you sit at the bar counter, you can watch the preparation process in full flow as well as appreciate the aromas emanating from the kitchen. The cuisine here is based around typical Brazilian cooking with a focus on the south-east of the country, using ingredients from small-scale producers and a constant nod to seasonality. Whether you opt for the tasting menu or à la carte, make sure you try the wood oven-baked pizzeta of merguez sausage made with cornbread – an absolute must!

Name: Trattorita Evvai
Address: Rua Joaquim Antunes 260, São Paulo, 05415-000, Brazil
Description: A more relaxed offering from renowned chef Luiz Filipe. Located just a few metres from its older sibling, this “trattorita” boasts a contemporary brasserie style with a stunning bar by the entrance and an open kitchen upstairs with a wood-fired oven that is at the heart of some of its signature dishes. Felipe’s traditional Italian-style cooking adopts a modern touch here and features a wide choice of pastas, pizzas, meat and seafood... in portions that can easily be shared. One starter that is an absolute must is the Crab Ravioli filled with crab, ricotta and a yolk that simply falls apart when sliced, all of which is then topped with a butter, sage and a freshly grated pecorino cheese sauce. The desserts are equally fabulous, so make sure you save space at the end of your meal to enjoy them to the full.

Name: Bicol Korean Cuisine
Address: Rua José Getúlio 422, São Paulo, 01509-000, Brazil
Description: Bicol is a must if you’re keen to try Korean barbecue-style cuisine. This classic address in the Liberdade district of the city has been run by a South Korean family for three generations. In this spacious restaurant, the tables have their own grills so that guests can cook meat (usually cut super-fine) to their individual taste. Dishes for sharing are the mainstay here, including the Burgogui, Garbi and Samguiopsar combos, always accompanied by Banchan (small side dishes of the day). The Bibimbap (a typical rice dish) and the soups are other interesting options on the menu, not forgetting the delicious kimchi, of course. Why not pair your food with the traditional soju, a typical Korean beverage with differing strengths of alcohol?

Name: Pobre Juan
Address: Rua Comendador Miguel Calfat 525, São Paulo, 04537-082, Brazil
Description: The first Pobre Juan outlet opened in the Vila Olímpia in 2004 and nowadays you’ll find the brand all across the country. Inspired by traditional Argentinian steakhouses, Pobre Juan serves top-quality grilled meats in an informal and rustic setting. Each of its restaurants features a wide array of carefully selected meats, a process that extends from their provenance to the maturing process. Whether you order classic options such as short ribs, ribeye or flank, or the more exclusive centre cut ribeye, porterhouse or Wagyu, every dish here is perfectly cooked. If you’re eating out with friends, you may want to order the Gran Tabla, which serves three people and comes with delicious sides. Fish, seafood and chicken, all cooked on the open grill, are also available, as well as sublime desserts such as the exquisite churros with dulce de leche.

Name: Lilia
Address: Rua do Senado 45, Rio de Janeiro, 20231-005, Brazil
Description: A few metres from the conical Catedral de São Sebastião building, there is a singular restaurant with an unassuming façade that can easily go unnoticed among Lapa’s historic townhouses. Climbing a long, narrow staircase, you will discover a two‑storey establishment with brick walls that lend an industrial, pared‑back and spacious feel. Here, chef Yan Ramos runs a kitchen marked by his creativity, updated daily according to ingredient availability. At lunchtime, a fixed menu composed of three courses is served, while at dinner there is an eleven‑step tasting menu. Do not miss the unmissable Roasted beetroot served on curd, topped with tahini and herbs, and the crispy Barriga de porco pururuca (crispy‑skin pork belly) accompanied by smoked mashed potatoes, green apple and pork demi‑glace!

Name: Mr. Lam
Address: Rua Maria Angélica 21, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-201, Brazil
Description: Mr. Lam gained renowned for his culinary prowess in restaurants in New York and London, however he has run this modern, sophisticated eatery on the edge of the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon for almost two decades. In contrast with other gastronomic restaurants these days, the majority of dishes on the menu have been mainstays since it first opened, in so doing keeping with the tradition of offering the best Chinese cuisine. Featuring a hint of cutting-edge innovation as well as a focus on top-quality ingredients, the menu boasts memorable dishes such as the lightly battered and crispy Senhor Batista prawns, with a delicious sweet and sour sauce. The restaurant is laid out on three floors, with an attractive dining room and welcoming bar on the top floor that includes picture windows and a glass roof that provide lots of natural light and stunning views.

Name: Borgo Mooca
Address: Rua Barão De Tatuí, 302, São Paulo, 01226-030, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Counter dining,Valet parking
Description: Carbonara mille-feuille, tuna tartare sando, gnocchi fritti & squid, Beef Wellington and a Wagyu forequarter burger are just some of the dishes on the Borgo Mooca menu. The stand-out in the dessert section is the Tiramisu soaked in Bardêra doce de leite liqueur, coffee and mascarpone. This gastronomic refuge is located in the Santa Cecília neighbourhood, keeping its roots in Italian cookery while embracing innovation and creative freedom. Founded by Bianca Giacomelli, the restaurant gained renown for its seasonal kitchen, which combines classical techniques with a contemporary, experimental and disruptive approach. The setting features a counter in front of the kitchen and décor with nostalgic touches that recall the little house in Mooca, the restaurant’s former home.

Name: Terraço NOTIÊ
Description: Although only recently opened, this restaurant is already being talked about by the city’s foodie community. Located on the rooftop of the Shopping Light building, its design comes as a pleasant surprise as soon as you walk through the door thanks to its decor of yellow tones, glass-fronted kitchen enabling guests to watch the chefs hard at work and, first and foremost, the 18m panel on the ceiling depicting images of nature. At the helm in the kitchen is Paraíba-born chef Onildo Rocha who impresses with his use of typical Brazilian ingredients and combinations that result in intense and striking dishes. His recipes are based around his journeys to different Brazilian regions every season, and are showcased on 5-, 8- and 11-course tasting menus. The name of the restaurant is a fusion between one of the country’s most colourful birds, the tanager (tiê in Portuguese) and the Portuguese word for night (noite).

Name: Tiara
Address: Rua Ataulfo De Paiva, 270 loja 111, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-900, Brazil
Description: The name Tiara refers to the district (Itacoatiara) in which chef Rafa Gomes was born. Nowadays, he owns two restaurants called Itacoa and, to complete the full name, Tiara. This famous chef is known for his appearance on reality cooking shows and his impressive career thus far, including stints in leading restaurants in New York. Housed in the Rio Design Leblon complex, the restaurant boasts an elegant backdrop of soothing tones for innovative cuisine that relies on modern techniques and the use of seasonal ingredients where possible. Here, the chef elevates duck meat (a key ingredient in his story) to another level. An example of this is the aged duck lacquered with honey and spices served with pumpkin, miso and a “gastrique” sauce – a quite surreal combination!

Name: Jiquitaia
Address: Rua Coronel Oscar Porto 808, São Paulo, 04003-004, Brazil
Description: If you're looking for typical homemade Brazilian cuisine prepared with quality ingredients, then this is the perfect place! Jiquitaia occupies a charming 1950s house surrounded by greenery, with a large, elegantly decorated dining room, where a plethora of wood and beautiful photos on the walls provide the decorative backdrop. Here, chef Marcelo Corrêa Bastos conjures up comforting traditional cuisine that feeds body and soul. During the working week, the playful “executive” menu is complemented by a concise menu featuring delicacies such as “coxinhas de frango caipira” (deep-fried dough filled with chicken), fish “moqueca” with shrimp, and grilled fish of the day served with a tasty pirão porridge. It's also worth noting that Jiquitaia also has a superb array of cachaças from across Brazil which have been carefully selected by the owner.

Name: Ama.zo - Cozinha Peruana
Description: This restaurant occupies the charming garden of an old property known as the Casa da Don'Anna, a 20C house with a strong coffee legacy. The ambience here is delightful, protected by the vagaries of the weather by an almost invisible roof, and features large jabuticabeira trees, tables laid out in the garden, and a semi-open kitchen to the rear. Here, Peruvian chef Enrique Paredes conjures up Andean cuisine that is reinterpreted through the use of local ingredients, strong flavours, pleasant textures and subtle nuances from the Amazon region. Among the starters, the fresh oysters with a Japanese ponzu sauce, physalis and black massago stands out, followed, perhaps, by a main of ossobuco cooked at low temperature with an Arequipeño sauce, and accompanied by a cassava millefeuille. Lovers of cacao will adore the intense and absolutely delicious chocolate x 4!

Name: Rufino Parrilla
Address: Rua Tubira, 43, Rio de Janeiro, 22441-070, Brazil
Description: If you’re keen to experience cooking on an authentic Argentinian parrilla grill without the inconvenience of leaving Leblon, a visit to Rufino is a must. This restaurant, already famous in Buenos Aires, has now opened an outlet in Rio de Janeiro. The menu is prepared by Argentinian chef Agustin Brañas, who brings with him the experience of working in prestigious restaurants outside of the country. In this elegant space, reminiscent of the typical parrilla eateries in neighbouring Argentina, the highlights are undoubtedly the exceptional cuts of meats (such as sirloin, Angus skirt steak, Argentinian Tomahawk, ribeye etc) cooked on the open grill. Desserts include the classic pancake with dulce de leche and banana ice cream. The extensive selection of Argentinian wines is the perfect complement to your meal here.

Name: Vista
Address: Avenida Pedro Álvares Cabral 1301, São Paulo, 04094-050, Brazil
Description: Occupying the top floor of the MAC USP (Museu de Arte Contemporânea da Universidade de São Paulo), this restaurant boasts spectacular views of Ibirapuera and a 360° panorama of the city. The kitchen is run by chef Pedro Oliveira, who offers guests a traditional Brazilian dining experience featuring typical ingredients from the country’s five regions, which he prepares in a harmonious and balanced way and is showcased on an “executive”-style format at lunchtime. On Saturdays, pumpkin shrimp with rice and sweet potato chips is the highlight, with crispy pururuca pork making an appearance on Sundays. The star of the show on the dessert menu is Vista’s own irresistible version of the traditional Portuguese dish “toucinho do Céu”, made with pumpkin, egg yolk and almonds. A special menu of starters and appetisers, plus an impressive selection of cocktails, is available on the terrace.

Name: Shin Zushi
Address: Rua Afonso de Freitas 169, São Paulo, 04006-050, Brazil
Description: If you're on the lookout for a Japanese restaurant where you can eat well in the Paraíso district, this is a perfect option, underlined by the fact that most of its clientele have Asian roots. Shin Zushi has a strong family personality as the business was originally created by the father and is currently run by two brothers (Ken and Nobu Mizumoto). The focus here is on classic Japanese cuisine which can be enjoyed at the counter with an Omakase menu, or at its more traditional tables with exclusive à la carte service. We particularly enjoyed the Omakase menu and service at the counter, which was very friendly and relaxed, and featured superb combinations such as the oyster with horse mackerel.

Name: Marine Restô
Address: Avenida Atlântica 4240, Rio de Janeiro, 22070-900, Brazil
Description: Enjoy one of the most breathtaking views of Copacabana beach at this restaurant on the sixth floor of the luxurious Fairmont Rio de Janeiro Copacabana hotel, where the panoramic terrace and swimming pool come as a highly scenic surprise! In addition to the picture-postcard views of the city, the restaurant boasts a large, contemporary space with an open-view kitchen, where the Brazilian cuisine combines ingredients and spices from different regions around the country, with a strong focus on the grill. As a result, some of the standout dishes on the menu are cooked on the Josper grill, such as the crunchy courgettes with a Serra da Canastra cheese sauce, the mouthwatering Angus skirt steak with a guaraná demi-glaze, and vegetarian options that include the heart of palm moqueca stew, served with manioc farofa with coconut.

Name: Tanit
Description: This charming restaurant has become a reference for excellent Spanish cuisine in the city. In this bright, modern setting with high ceilings, polished cement floors and wood-clad walls, chef Oscar Bosch, who arrived in Brazil in 2009 having worked in leading restaurants in his native Spain such as El Bulli and El Celler de Can Roca, offers Mediterranean cuisine which he adapts to Brazilian tastes via refined technique and elaborate presentation. While tapas and a variety of rice dishes are an integral part of his identity, you can also enjoy other delicious options such as croquetas, patatas bravas and, as a main course, the classic roast suckling pig, cooked at low temperature and served with a velvety roasted carrot purée.

Name: Fogo de Chão
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The Fogo de Chão restaurant is much more than just a place to eat as it represents Brazil’s churrasco tradition that has won admirers in different parts of the world. The origins of this method for cooking meat date back to the gauchos who discovered that skewering pieces of meat on wooden sticks and placing them around a fire transformed a simple cut of meat into a true delicacy. Served as part of “rodizio” all-you-can-eat format, the extensive selection includes beef, lamb and pork, as well as the famous prime rib and dry-aged meats (only available on the à la carte). To accompany the superb choice of meat, there’s also an extensive buffet of salads, rice dishes, carpaccios, cheeses and sausages. In total, there are five Fogo de Chão restaurants in São Paulo, all of which boast a comprehensive wine list. The new addition at the Jardins restaurant is a space dedicated to cigar-lovers.

Name: Aya Japanese Cuisine
Address: Avenida Pedroso de Morais 141, São Paulo, 05419-000, Brazil
Description: This attractive property with a contemporary ambience and minimalist decor has a good location in a busy part of the city, just a few metres from the famous Avenida Rebouças. It is under the baton of sushi chef Juraci Pereira (better known as “Jura”) who, after working as Jun Sakamoto’s right-hand man for 11 years, decided to open his own venture in collaboration with his business partner Beto Ganme. Downstairs, where guests can sit at the counter to watch the expert hands of the chefs in action, the atmosphere is more intimate, while the upstairs is more modern and cosy. The cuisine includes a special Aya omakase menu, various types of sashimi, sushi (à la carte and combos), makimonos and hot dish options.

Name: Chef Rouge
Address: Rua Bela Cintra 2238, São Paulo, 01415-002, Brazil
Description: An authentic French bistro, both in terms of its black façade and red awning and its elegant, welcoming interior. The main dining space is complemented by a charming terrace at the entrance, adorned with two impressive trees and with candlelight in the evening. Some of the tables are also occupied by adorable, large red teddy bears that add to the delightful atmosphere. Understandably, the culinary focus and star of the show is classic French cooking with a contemporary touch that is showcased by top-quality ingredients and delicately prepared dishes. These include the grilled foie gras with figs, served with bitter chocolate, and the classic roast duck breast with orange sauce accompanied by gaufrettes potatoes. The incredible Eclair XXL provides the perfect finale!

Name: Fasano Trattoria
Address: Rua Iguatemi s/n, São Paulo, 01451-010, Brazil
Description: This unique section of the city is home to the super-modern Pátio Malzoni alongside the Casa Bandeirista, an example of 17C Brazilian colonial architecture. Amid these contrasts, you’ll also find this exquisite trattoria paying homage to Southern Italy with its decor combining wood, leather and the flags of Italian football teams, plus a pleasant outdoor terrace. Here, the chef has created a menu featuring traditional recipes and dishes inspired by the region around Naples, including the island of Capri. The extensive choice includes the memorable linguine alle vongole with cherry tomatoes, the classic spaghetti alla carbonara, and the polpettone al forno (baked meatloaf), another excellent choice. Service is also a strong point here, so don’t hesitate to ask for a personal recommendation or choose one of the daily specials.

Name: Cala del Tanit
Address: Rua Pais De Araújo, 147, São Paulo, 04531-090, Brazil
Description: A new culinary venture courtesy of chef Oscar Bosch, who has been on the rise in São Paulo's food scene since he opened the successful Tanit in the Jardins district of the city. Located in Itaim Bibi, in one of the typical three-storey houses in this neighbourhood, Cala del Tanit boasts a terrace at the entrance and a contemporary interior with a predominance of wood, an open-view kitchen and a counter where cocktails are also prepared for guests. The menu retains the essence of Mediterranean cuisine, with Spanish dishes such as tomato gazpacho and delicious rice dishes (Paella Marinera and duck rice socarrat, with grilled octopus and aioli), although the culinary repertoire here also includes an array of pasta dishes and a few Asian touches. A space for small private events, called Sala X, is also available.

Name: Le Jardin
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: An oasis of sophistication and serenity surrounded by nature amid the hustle and bustle of the city. Le Jardin boasts a luxurious ambience in the style of a winter garden in which the decor and atmosphere will leave a lasting impression. This is the perfect space to enjoy at any time of day – for breakfast, which includes an interesting choice of teas and coffees to complement the menu, light snacks or lunch and dinner. The cuisine here is based around classic international fare, and is always showcased by meticulously prepared dishes. One example is the roasted sea bass which is served on a bed of lightly caramelised asparagus and heart of palm and finished with a vermouth emulsion – a combination that will leave a lasting impression on the palate. There’s also a kosher menu (prior booking required), and make sure you save space for Le Jardin’s desserts, which are an absolute must.

Name: Nosso
Address: Rua Maria Quitéria 91, Rio de Janeiro, 22410-040, Brazil
Description: An exclusive restaurant with three completely different floors: on the first, a bar; on the second, a dining space with an intimate ambience for a pleasant supper; and on the third, an outdoor terrace. Here, the relaxed cuisine, which is described by chef Bruno Katz as “contemporary”, features dishes that combine different food cultures from around the world in a creative and harmonious way. One example is the glazed octopus served with fried rice, kewpie mayonnaise, moyashi and nira, which is simply divine and cooked to perfection. Bartender Daniel Estevan elevates his concoctions to another level, combining classic drinks with his experience of the Amazon to create cocktails such as the surprising Tacacá Sour, with its mix of jambu, tucupi, cupuaçu and lemon. An extraordinary experience!

Name: A Figueira Rubaiyat
Address: Rua Haddock Lobo 1738, São Paulo, 01414-002, Brazil
Description: The backdrop here is definitely a surprise, thanks to the majestic Bengal fig, a century-old tree that attracts admiring glances inside this restaurant. The glass roof adds a special touch, enabling guests to admire the immensity of its crown and branches to the full. In keeping with its sister property in the famous Faria Lima, the cuisine is based around the "fork to plate” concept. Both the beef and pork are produced at the group’s own farms and distributed throughout its franchises. Dishes include baby beef, Denver steak, filet mignon, master beef and “tirita de picanha”, all of which are cooked to perfection, although the menu also features a variety of fish, rice and pasta options. Enhance your dining experience with the superb array of labels available on the wine list.

Name: Paparoto Cucina
Address: Av. Pres. Juscelino Kubitschek, 2041 - Térreo, São Paulo, 04543-011, Brazil
Description: Part of the luxury JK Iguatemi complex, this restaurant has a spacious and modern setting with a decor that includes plants and subdued lighting that accentuates the illuminated Italian phrase “Se non ora quando?” (“If not now, when”). Famous chef Dayse Paparoto, who won the first edition of Brazil’s Professional Masterchef, showcases his Italian-inspired menu with an authentic and innovative touch that is based around fresh, top-quality ingredients. The menu features an array of options, such as the excellent egg yolk ravioli with ricotta and spinach, served with a soft egg yolk. Other options include fresh pastas and risottos, although the desserts steal the show here, highlighting the extreme creativity of the chef in dishes such as tiramisu, served with a candy floss tree, which comes as a complete surprise.

Name: Metzi
Address: Rua João Moura, 861, São Paulo, 05412-002, Brazil
Description: Ever wondered what a fusion of Brazilian and Mexican cooking would taste like? The answer is... simply wonderful! Chefs Luana Sabino and Eduardo Nava Ortiz, who met while working at a restaurant in New York, decided to pool their know-how to treat our palates to an incredible concept. The menu marries the techniques and traditions of authentic Mexican cooking with fresh Brazilian ingredients, creating dishes that champion seasonality and celebrate the best of each ingredient. You can choose à la carte or go for the nine-moment tasting menu, which includes the refreshing starter Aguachile de maracujá, sashimi e sauva, passion-fruit aguachile with sashimi and saúva ants; the punchy Camarão al ajillo, queijo tulha e ovas de salmão, prawns al ajillo with tulha cheese and salmon roe; and lightly spicy Wagyu beef with okra and Brazilian shishito peppers. To accompany the experience, there’s a tempting line-up of cocktails!

Name: Cais
Description: A relaxed restaurant with a lively atmosphere and good food, so it’s not surprising that it’s always full. Occupying a charming small house in the Vila Madalena neighbourhood of the city, Cais features tables outdoors next to the window, seats at the counter by the kitchen, as well more traditional tables. Run by Adriano de Laurentiis in the kitchen and chef Catarina Ferraz, its cuisine is centred around fresh fish and seafood. The concise menu is constantly updated in line with the availability and freshness of seasonal ingredients. Having savoured the delicious appetisers on offer here, we particularly recommend the week’s selection of fish and seafood, followed by the creamy and delicate cheesecake served with a milk sorbet.

Name: Animus
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The kitchen here is under the baton of young chef Giovanna Grossi, who has had an impressive career thus far. Having worked in renowned restaurants in France and Spain, she decided to open his own business where she offers creative cuisine that champions local and seasonal ingredients. Occupying a corner location in the charming Pinheiros district, Animus features a decor of warm tones combined with wood, and features an open kitchen where guests can observe the chefs in action. The menu comprises à la carte options and a six courses tasting menu, in addition to an “executive” menu available during the week.

Name: Kubo Zushi
Address: Rua Das Tabocas 158, São Paulo, 05445-020, Brazil
Description: If you’re looking for a classic Japanese dining experience that is truly authentic and steers clear of any form of contemporary influence, especially when it comes to sushi and sashimi, this is the perfect restaurant for you. Here, to a backdrop of simple decor in the residential Vila Madalena district, chef Sergio Kubo prepare edomae sushi, a culinary tradition mastered over many years. The high quality of ingredients is clearly evident in dishes such tuna tartare, tartare with salmon roe, and tobiko and quail egg yolk, as well as an array of combinations. The restaurant is divided into three sections, although it is obvious that the sushi bar is the heart and soul of the property, where guests will enjoy watching and admiring the skill of Kubo Zushi’s chefs. There’s even an attractive play area for kids!

Name: El Tranvia - Itaim Bibi
Address: Rua Leopoldo Couto de Magalhães 1372, São Paulo, 03178-200, Brazil
Description: Those who head to this restaurant should be in no doubt as to its reputation as a culinary institution showcasing the very best flavours of traditional Uruguayan cooking. The beef served here is of exceptional quality and includes numerous choice cuts (beef short ribs, strip loin, sirloin etc) and matured meat options that are enhanced to the full over the flames of the parrilla. You’ll also find fillets of meat of all types and sizes to cater to the many families from every generation who flock here, with the quantity of side dishes depending on the number of guests at the table. The fries and the delicious Uruguayan flan with “dulce de leche” are a must.

Name: Sushi Leblon
Address: Rua Dias Ferreira 256, Rio de Janeiro, 22431-050, Brazil
Description: An exclusive space with a trendy (and renowned) atmosphere in the southern part of Rio de Janeiro, where it has become a popular choice for those who enjoy high-quality Japanese cuisine. Open for almost four decades, the place is always on the up as it maintains its sense of tradition without turning its back on emerging food trends. In an intimate space decorated with a mix of dark tones and wood, the most sought-after spot is the bar counter by the kitchen where incredible dishes such as cubes of salmon with chilli pepper and truffle oil are served. Other options include the unmissable tuna tartare with free-range egg yolk and black roe, “combinados”, sushi, sashimi etc. At lunchtime, there’s more flexibility if you don’t have a reservation, but we recommend booking ahead for dinner.

Name: Ama.zo - Pátio Higienópolis
Description: Located outside of the Pátio Higienópolis shopping mall, it features an attractive room with lots of natural light and an open-air terrace decorated with plants and Peruvian works of art. Here, the Lima-born chef Enrique Paredes, whose philosophy is “Cooking with freedom”, is at the helm of his second venture, where he combines Peruvian flavours and techniques with local ingredients to showcase the flavours of the Amazon, without losing sight of the region’s roots. On the menu you’ll find dishes such as langoustine carpaccio, the traditional Lima dish “causa limeña”, along with various types of ceviche, rice dishes and vegetarian and vegan options. One dessert that you won’t want to pass up is the “Suspiro Limeño” made with delicious Peruvian “dulce de leche”, a dehydrated quinoa and togarashi meringue, praline and chocolate sorbet – a true delight for the tastebuds!

Name: TARAZ
Description: Part of the historic and former Condessa Filomena Matarazzo Maternity hospital complex, now converted into the luxury Rosewood São Paulo hotel, where the menu bears the signature of famous chef Felipe Bronze. In this charming space, the cooking is based around that of South America as a whole, with the open grill featuring prominently in a variety of harmonious dishes prepared with ingredients of the highest quality. Why not start with an authentic South American dish such as the excellent combination of tuna ceviche with caramelised peanuts, shiso, sesame, peanut milk and crispy tapioca? Follow this with a Black pork belly with tucupi, corn cream, marinated tomato and PANC's salad. For those who prefer to eat alfresco, the terrace is simply charming!

Name: OCYÁ Ilha
Address: Ilha Primeira, Rio de Janeiro, 22641-990, Brazil
Description: If you’re looking to take a break from the hustle and bustle of the city and enjoy a meal by the sea, this is definitely a must. Access to Ilha Primeira is exclusively by boat (from several embarkation points) and when you disembark you'll be welcomed by a pleasant outdoor wooden deck along with superb hospitality. Chef Gerônimo Athuel's menu revolves around precisely prepared fish and seafood (some of which are matured in a special chamber built inside the restaurant) mainly cooked on the open grill. Dishes featuring on the menu here include matured raw fish with ajoblanco, octopus with a roasted and creamy tomato rice and basil farofa, and boneless fish of the day served with creamy lemon rice. In addition to the relaxed atmosphere, the wonderful sunsets are one of OCYÁ Ilha’s major attractions!

Name: Mondo
Address: Rua Oscar Freire 30, São Paulo, 01426-000, Brazil
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant where you can enjoy excellent Italian cuisine, this is definitely the right place! Located at the end of the famous Rua Oscar Freire, it boasts an elegant glass façade and a spacious interior, with an open kitchen to the rear. The cooking revolves around classic Italian recipes, including pasta, but without neglecting generous dishes of fish and meat. The menu is teeming with amazing options, including “ravioli al tuorlo”, stuffed with ricotta, spinach and melted parmesan and served with a creamy egg yolk, and “pappardele con ragù d'ossobuco”. If you still have an appetite, we also recommend the majestic “filetto alla rossini”, served with black truffle and potato millefeuille. A midday “mezzogiorno” menu option is also available midweek.

Name: Emiliano
Address: Rua Oscar Freire 384, São Paulo, 01426-000, Brazil
Description: Part of the majestic Hotel Emiliano, along the city’s iconic Rua Oscar Freire, with its array of luxury shops and boutiques, this eponymous restaurant is under the baton of chef Viviane Gonçalves (known as Chef Vivi), who focuses on classic cuisine that combines Brazilian flavours and Italian influences. Her concise menu includes dishes ranging from seared scallops with cauliflower cream and leeks to slow-roasted lamb served with yam purée and lamb stock. For dessert, centre stage is taken by the sweet and crunchy combination of banana, peanut and dulce de leche with vanilla sorbet. The classical decor, enhanced by extensive windows and views of a vertical garden, provides the perfect setting for a delightful meal.

Name: Vinheria Percussi
Address: Rua Bianchi Bertoldi 109, São Paulo, 05422-070, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A family-run Italian restaurant that was a trailblazer for enogastronomy (the pairing of food and wine) in Brazil. It first opened as a wine shop in 1985 with the aim of offering good wine and food to go with it. However, with the arrival of chef Silvia Percussi and her brother Lamberto Percussi (restaurant manager and sommelier) the concept was taken to the next level. In this classic, welcoming setting, enjoy excellent cuisine including fresh pasta, which is a particular highlight. Classic dishes that you’ll want to try include the perfectly creamy tonnarelli alla carbonara, the beef ossobuco, served with a divine sauce, and the tiramisu, which is brought to your table on a platter. Why not pair these delicacies with one of the fines wines on the 300-strong wine list and in the award-winning cellar.

Name: La Villa - Bistrô Francês
Address: Rua Alvaro Ramos 408, Rio de Janeiro, 22280-110, Brazil
Description: This French brasserie occupies a unique property in Botafogo dating back to 1775 and has established itself as a trusted option for those who enjoy authentic Gallic cuisine. Under the management of French owner Gregoire Fortat, La Villa features a simple decor, high ceilings, outdoor tables and a pleasant and hospitable ambience. The menu here is centred around traditional French bistro fare with an added Brazilian touch. The experience begins with a delicious pâté de champagne served with bread baked on the premises, followed by the classic onion soup, and an authentic duck cassoulet. On Sundays, there’s also a French-Brazilian barbecue including an impressive array of fish and seafood.

Name: Nôa
Address: Rua Garcia D'Ávila, 135, Rio de Janeiro, 22421-010, Brazil
Description: This lively restaurant sits in one of Ipanema’s most buzzed-about areas, in a charming 1930s house, and pairs the neighbourhood’s vibrant essence with a warm, welcoming culinary concept. In a space defined by minimalist décor, where strips of napkins hang from the ceiling and Hebrew-inspired paintings adorn the walls, you’ll find international cooking rooted in Brazilian cuisine with French touches. Alongside salads, meats, fish, seafood and fresh pasta, you can choose the fresh fish of the day and pair it with a side dish. Our suggestion? Arroz de moqueca com camarões grelhados, moqueca rice with grilled prawns, and for dessert, Tarta Basca, Basque cheesecake, served with goiabada syrup and cheese ice cream. Enjoy the charming veranda with the refreshing cocktails on offer!

Name: OCYÁ Leblon
Address: Rua Aristides Espínola, 88, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-050, Brazil
Description: Fisherman, diver and chef Gerônimo Athuel is a font of knowledge when it comes to seafood, and is keen to highlight the importance of conscious, selective and artisanal fishing. He is also strongly committed to research into preserving and maturing techniques, as well as the use of all fish and seafood species, prioritising those that are often discarded. With one restaurant in Ilha Primeira already behind him, he has now brought his cuisine to this exclusive space in the Zona Sul. Here, the decor is modern with plenty of natural light and a glass-fronted fish maturing cabinet that highlights his culinary concept. Fabulous options on the menu range from seafood charcuterie to grilled, fried and raw fish dishes which will delight guests’ tastebuds with their surprising flavours and skilful technique and presentation.

Name: Babbo Osteria
Address: Rua Barão Da Torre, 632, Rio de Janeiro, 22411 002, Brazil
Description: An outstanding property in a quiet residential section of Ipanema, whose Italian name (“babbo” is a colloquial Italian word for “dad”) provides an insight into the cuisine served here, a fusion of Italian and “carioca” dishes conjured up by chef Elia Schramm. One of the most popular eateries in the area, Babbo Osteria pays homage to the chef's father, and brings childhood memories and family influences to the cooking on offer. One of the dining rooms, decorated with ornaments reminiscent of a traditional Italian “osteria”, provides the backdrop for handmade pasta dishes such as Uova Pepenara (tagliolini served with small cubes of bacon and a creamy soft egg) – the chef's version of the classic carbonara. Main courses include the “filetto”, a medallion served with a delicious pepper sauce and golden gnocchi, as well as desserts in the purest Italian style, such as tiramisù and a perfect combination of pistachio and lime!

Name: Blaise
Description: Occupying the historic Maternidade Filomena Matarazzo building, this restaurant takes its inspiration from the Franco-Swiss writer Blaise Cendrars. The interior is similar to a wood cabin (similar to where he is said to have lived) and includes Brazilian volcanic stone crystals between the woodwork, rustic decor and subtle lighting provided by the lampshades that illuminate the room. Here, chef Fernando Bouzan, conjures up French cuisine with a Brazilian touch. Our suggestions include the succulent and incredibly tender braised beef tongue, served with potato salad and a refined red wine sauce. The jabuticaba sorbet with jam, jelly and jabuticaba pearls in a delicate “crème diplomate” is an absolute must!

Name: De Segunda
Address: Rua Prof. Tamandaré Toledo, 160, São Paulo, 04532-020, Brazil
Description: Young chefs Júlia Tricate and Gabriel Coelho already have impressive CVs, having won TV food competitions and worked in Michelin-starred restaurants such as Noma (Copenhagen) and Oro (Rio de Janeiro). Following on from these incredible experiences, they decided to open their own restaurant with an open kitchen and a discreet decor that helps to channel the complete focus onto their cuisine. Their modern culinary vision is showcased on a creative menu that champions fresh, seasonal ingredients on a tasting menu, à la carte and midweek “executive” menu”. Combinations such as the pork rib cooked for 12 hours and served with a meat glaze hummus and fried onion, and the restaurant’s classic take on hump of beef, here accompanied by a creamy sweet potato and gorgonzola purée, will definitely leave a lasting memory of this restaurant.

Name: Nelita
Address: Rua Ferreira De Araújo, 330, São Paulo, 05428-000, Brazil
Description: A restaurant that has developed a strong reputation for itself in the city’s Baixo Pinheiros district. Under the baton of chef Tássia Magalhães, an exclusively female team is in charge of the kitchen, conjuring up innovative dishes with an Italian influence. The wine list, carefully curated by Danyel Steinle, showcases Brazilian wines and an astute blend of the country’s wines with those from elsewhere. To a modern decorative backdrop of exposed brick walls and different ambiences, guests can choose between tables at the entrance, the marble counter in front of the kitchen, or a private room which can also be reserved for groups. The menu includes delicious fresh pastas such as linguine with carrots and roe, alongside the mouthwatering pork with pear and toasted bread. The perfect dining experience!

Name: Haru Sushi Bar
Address: Rua Raimuindo Corrêa, 10, Rio de Janeiro, 22040-042, Brazil
Description: Owner-chef Menandro Rodrigues’ passion for Japanese cuisine provides the impetus for everything that goes on at this welcoming restaurant in Copacabana. On the ground floor, enjoy relaxed serviced at the pavement tables, while on the first floor you’ll find a dining room decorated in Japanese style with an impressive bar counter overlooking the kitchen, as well as tables and chairs laid out in different sections. The chef follows the Japanese “Kaizen” philosophy (which translates as “continuous improvement”) and devotes special attention to its techniques as well as to ingredients sourced directly from local fishermen. His cuisine is served as part of an Omakase menu, and includes options such as sushi, sashimi, and special and traditional “combos”. These are complemented by an extensive array of sakis that can be enjoyed in “tasting” measures.

Name: Osso
Address: Rua Bandeira Paulista, 520, São Paulo, 04532-001, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: An address that is much prized by meat-lovers in the Greater São Paulo area. Here, chef Renzo Garibaldi, who is known as the “Master Butcher” in his native Peru, has opened his first culinary venture in Brazil. His cuisine is based around meat sourced from sustainable producers, with the option of dry aged and different maturing times covering an array of different cuts. Beef is the star of the show here, available as ribeye, fillet mignon, picanha and short ribs, alongside special dry-aged pure Wagyu, Vaca Velha and Angus. Dishes such as ceviche, salad, Josper-grilled fish and the rice-based “arroz de costela” also feature on the menu in a modern, elegant space with an extensive and superb wine list.

Name: Escama
Address: Rua Visconde de Carandaí, 5, Rio de Janeiro, 22460 020, Brazil
Description: After visiting a French restaurant with a similar outlook, inspiration struck to open this restaurant serving the best fish and seafood in a relaxed ambience. The focus at Escama is one that showcases the best maritime ingredients, which he always sources fresh from local fishermen. For your main, you can choose how you want to have your fish prepared (grilled, baked or poached), such as the sea bass, which is accompanied by a delicious champagne sauce and roasted onions. The menu also features options such as squid, shrimp, scallops and oysters, plus a splendid seafood feijoada on Fridays. The restaurant is located close to the city’s botanical garden, in a charming two-floor property with an extremely relaxed ambience enhanced by a decor of muted colours.

Name: Mäska
Address: Rua Joana Angélica, 159, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
Description: It's worth braving the frenetic traffic along Ipanema’s narrow streets to eat at this modern but relaxed restaurant with a contemporary bistro feel and a kitchen that opens onto the dining room to savour chef Danilo Parah’s innovative and contemporary cuisine. His recipes showcase ingredients of the very highest quality, including extremely fresh seafood, in dishes such as the unforgettable creamy rice with octopus, and the mouthwatering and perfectly cooked steak served with a truffled aligot mash. Not forgetting the masterfully prepared and delicate spaghetti with beurre blanc and braised prawns. The dining experience and atmosphere are enhanced by Mäska’s array of refreshing cocktails, which are an absolute must.

Name: Marena Cucina
Address: Rua Pais De Araújo 138, São Paulo, 04531-090, Brazil
Description: In the heart of Itaim Bibi, one of São Paulo's most sophisticated districts, you’ll come across this Italian restaurant that oozes personality, both in its warm Mediterranean-inspired decor combining exposed stone and wood, and its unique cuisine. Although it offers an array of pasta and specialities from across the country (Rome, Naples, Tuscany etc), the aim here is to also incorporate the specific flavours of the Puglia region in the “heel of the boot” in the deep south of the country. The cuisine is unpretentious yet delicious, and is showcased in dishes such as artisanally produced Ficchi & Aceto IGP burrata, grilled octopus, and Tagliolini Marena with fresh pasta, prawns, octopus, squid and pomodorini. The mouthwatering prosciuttos here are also a must.

Name: Piselli
Address: Rua Padre João Manuel 1253, São Paulo, 01411-001, Brazil
Description: Piselli is the Italian word for “pea” and this vegetable is highly significant for the owner Juscelino Pereira who still maintains his custom of decorating every plate with three peas. Nowadays, the brand has three restaurants in São Paulo and one in Brasilia, and the cuisine is the same in each of them: namely, high-quality Italian cooking inspired by the Piedmont region. Dishes here are well prepared and full of flavour. Among them, we recommend the incredible “burrata calda al tartufo”, baked in delicious focaccia. Follow this, perhaps, with the homemade tortelloni filled with mozzarella di bufala and served with a fresh tomato and basil sauce, and the classic ossobuco alla milanese with saffron rice. In summary, a simply wonderful culinary experience.

Name: Rubaiyat Rio
Address: Rua Jardim Botânico 971, Rio de Janeiro, 22470-051, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the Jockey Club Brasileiro within the boundaries of the city’s botanical gardens, this restaurant boasts breathtaking views where you can enjoy a meal on the terrace to a picture-postcard backdrop that features the horse-racing track as well as the statue of Christ the Redeemer. Inside, there is a large dining room with a counter that is home to the kitchen, where a large glass window provides views of the churrasco grill. Renowned for its array of premium meats and for managing its own production, the restaurant offers more than ten different cuts, although fish, seafood, rice and a variety of sides also feature on the menu. On Saturdays, don't miss the chance to try the traditional feijoada stew, made with prime cuts of meat, along with milkshakes and an incredible dessert buffet!

Name: Amadeus
Address: Rua Haddock Lobo 807, São Paulo, 01420-002, Brazil
Description: No description of Amadeus can be made without mentioning the Masano family, along with their passion, enthusiasm and dreams. Thanks to rave reviews of their cooking from friends, they decided to open a restaurant known as “fish corner” in São Paulo. Today, the kitchen is overseen by chef Bella Masano, the owners’ daughter, who embellishes the menu with her innovative culinary creations alongside classic dishes which have been given a contemporary makeover. Her cooking is showcased on an à la carte and tasting menu which includes options such as fresh oysters from the family’s own beds in Florianópolis. Amadeus’ signature dishes include the shrimp “à paulista”, prepared with olive oil and garlic, which is full of flavour and perfect for sharing, and the “moqueca Amadeus”, a stew with fish and shrimp, served with plantain and onion farofa – an exquisite combination!

Name: Cantaloup
Address: Rua Manuel Guedes 474, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
Description: A real oasis of elegance that is immediately evident the moment you step through the door. Occupying a former bread factory, Cantaloup features high ceilings and a spacious and stylish dining room complemented by a classic-style bar in the corner. Next to it is an attractive waiting area protected by a retractable roof that provides plenty of light, which combines pleasantly with a charming green space and a fountain that adds a hint of freshness to the overall feel. Chef Valdir Oliveira offers an attractive menu based around international recipes that he creates via strong technique and well-defined combinations. Starters include delicious options such as foie gras, burrata and carpaccio, followed by mains such as duck magret, veal shank and “bobó de lagostim” (a type of crayfish stew). The wine list, which includes a selection of wines from 13 different countries, is the most comprehensive in the city.

Name: Dinho's
Description: Dinho's was opened by Fuad Zegaib (the creator of the strip steak) six decades ago. Nowadays, the restaurant is run by chef Paulo Zegaib, the founder’s son. Occupying a new home on the ground floor of the Hotel Qoya, in the Paraíso section of the city (there’s also a Dinho’s in the Jardins district), it features a spacious, classically furnished main dining room, which is entirely glass-fronted and enclosed by a beautiful vertical garden plus a colourful open kitchen to one side. Renowned for its longevity in this bustling capital city, the restaurant offers superb cuts of beef, as well as feijoada on Thursdays and Saturdays, a buffet of salads and desserts, plus a copious seafood buffet on Fridays.

Name: Toto
Address: Rua Joana Angélica, 155, Rio de Janeiro, 22420-030, Brazil
Description: This is the first venture run exclusively by Thomas Troisgros, who has created a totally unique concept unlike anything we are used to. At Toto, he creates dishes that reflect his food-inspired memories and combine French techniques, Asian influences and top-quality Brazilian ingredients. Don’t expect sophisticated and complex dishes; instead, the concept is much less complicated, with a focus on affordably priced comfort food. Standout features here are the industrial decor featuring neutral tones, the relaxed and informal ambience, and an open kitchen with a dining counter for guests. One particular dish you won’t want to miss is the popular and quite irresistible roasted rib gyoza with a ponzu sauce and watercress.

Name: Rudä
Address: Rua Garcia D'Ávila, 118, Rio de Janeiro, 22421-010, Brazil
Description: At Rudä, chef Danilo Parah champions what he calls “emotional and creative cuisine” in a contemporary bistro-style setting featuring different ambiences and a private room on the first floor. His dishes are colourful, generous and highly flavourful with little fear when it comes to combining lots of ingredients. It’s hard to beat the octopus with jambu fruit (a dish with a profusion of colours and textures that includes pasta cooked in a moqueca sauce) or the delicious cheesecake with an almond tuile, guava syrup and strawberry compote, all of which will linger long in the memory. The hospitality is on a par with the food, the latter presented on a varied à la carte that showcases local ingredients in addition to an “executive” menu.

Name: Clan BBQ
Address: Rua Dias Ferreira, 233 Loja B, Rio de Janeiro, 22431 050, Brazil
Description: To the backdrop of a neon sign “Não apague o meu fogo” (“Don’t put out my fire”) clearly visible above the door, chefs Pepo Figueiredo and Newton Rique showcase cuisine in which fire plays a key role here, enabling them to prepare fresh ingredients imbued with a special flavour. In this industrial-style ambience with a predominance of raw concrete, a sturdy tree takes centre stage in the middle of the dining room. There’s also the option of sitting at the counter by the grill to watch dishes and cocktails being prepared at close quarters. The menu is of course heavily focused on barbecued meats, although you’ll also find other options such as vegetables, fish and burgers. Dishes you won’t want to miss include the creamy oxtail croquettes and cubes of smoked tongue with aioli. The succulent French rack of lamb, served with chimichurri, is cooked to perfection.

Name: Les Présidents
Address: Rua Da Consolação 3527, São Paulo, 01416-001, Brazil
Description: Under the helm of famous chef Érick Jacquin, best known for his appearances on MasterChef, this bistro-style restaurant serves sophisticated cuisine inspired by the chef’s French roots. Occupying a striking building with a completely black façade and red doors, the interior is no less impressive with its myriad paintings and embellishments that add to the typically French ambience. To enjoy the experience to the full, we recommend the delicious langoustine ravioli served with vegetables and a Sauternes emulsion with ginger, or the classic duck foie gras, accompanied by caramelised bananas, an orange reduction and bitter chocolate. A seven-course surprise tasting menu created by the chef is also available, alongside the à la carte and a midweek “executive”-style menu.

Name: Spicy Fish
Address: Rua Maria Quitéria, 99, Rio de Janeiro, 22410-040, Brazil
Description: A restaurant that is the talk of the town when it comes to Asian cuisine, a reputation enhanced by the magnificent building in which it is situated – a four-storey property featuring a decor of neutral tones, soft lighting and lots of plants which add a touch of freshness to the space. The cuisine created by chef Emerson Kim is a fusion of Japanese and Korean cooking, showcased via well-presented dishes with a unique flavour. The menu is extensive and for those unsure what to order, the chef’s selection includes two portions of nigiri, sashimi and the “house special”. Hot dishes include the reinterpretation of the Bibimbap, the finishing touches to which are always added at the table, and the delicious Kagoshima wagyu beef, known as Hot Stone.

Name: Maza
Address: Rua Manuel Guedes, 243, São Paulo, 04536-070, Brazil
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Valet parking
Description: As well as a highly enjoyable dining experience, Maza boasts a relaxing and welcoming setting, where the combination of wood and soft tones is clearly evident as soon as you walk through the door – a decor embellished by the beautiful cherry tree. The cuisine here is based around classic Japanese fare with a modern and personalised touch, including some Korean dishes. The different types of menus on offer include a seven-course option called Shinrai (served exclusively at table), the Omakase (only available at the bar counter), an à la carte. Exquisite dishes include karasumi, ussuzukuri, Wagyu tataki, “shake butter”, as well as sushi, sashimi, temaki. An impressive choice of sakes and cocktails completes the picture.

Name: Henriqueta
Address: Rua Aristides Espínola, 121, Rio de Janeiro, 22440-050, Brazil
Description: This “tasca” style restaurant in the southern part of Rio de Janeiro showcases the best of Portuguese cuisine in a bright environment with a glass façade, open kitchen and Portuguese ceramic decoration. The cuisine on offer dispenses with unnecessary frills, focusing on the quality of the ingredients and dishes designed for sharing, among which the “biff-anas açorianas”, a crispy bread sandwich filled with pork escalope marinated in wine and garlic, stands out. As a main course, we recommend the tender octopus “a lagareiro” roasted in oil, served with onion confit and mashed potatoes, followed by the “toucinho do céu” made with egg yolks, almonds and cinnamon, an authentic Portuguese dish if ever there was one!

Name: Lin Ji Lao Chu
Address: 299 Wensan West Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: The unadorned two-storey house with grey brick walls may not look exciting, but diners have been flocking here for over 20 years for its Tonglu farm-style cooking – it's simple, rustic and delicious. Photos and the names of dishes are shown on a wall of lightboxes on the ground floor, where servers take your order. Try the organic fish from Qiandao Lake two ways: the fish head soup is milky and rich; and the braised fish fillet is silky and mildly spicy.

Name: Chic 1699
Address: L698, 6F, The Mixc, 701 Fuchun Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: The dimly lit space on two levels feels modern and chic, with its mix of bare concrete, glass, and metal structures. The food, meanwhile, is very much in keeping with Fujian tradition. Seafood from the province features heavily on the menu, alongside other Fujian produce. Signatures include honey-glazed grilled river eel with crispy skin and oily, velvety flesh. The raw oysters from Xiamen Harbour dressed in speciality sauce are zesty and summery.

Name: A Bing Bao Shan Mian
Address: 21 Zhonghe Middle Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Experienced chef-owner A Bing honed his skills in a famous noodle shop in town before opening this joint over 40 years ago. Having moved to the current address in recent years, it remains a firm favourite with many locals. Its signature fried eel noodle soup has impressively springy noodles and crispy, meaty eel chunks. Try his "semi" noodle soup, too – noodles dressed sparingly in a thick broth, for a flavour-forward experience.

Name: 28 Hubin Road
Address: 1F, Grand Hyatt, 28 Hubin Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Perched on the shore of West Lake, this hotel restaurant is led by a local chef with over 20 years of experience under his belt. Traditional Zhejiang recipes are given a new spin – to great effect. The braised pork belly pagoda comes in two portion sizes: a mini version served with pumpkin flatbread and a regular one with chestnut pancakes. The wine list features a plethora of Chinese labels from Hebei, Shandong, Shanxi, Xinjiang and Ningxia.

Name: Ming Kitchen
Address: 23F, Zhejiang Culture Building, 370 Tiyuchang Road, Gongshu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: This is the upmarket flagship of an F&B group that has been active on Hangzhou’s dining scene for over two decades. It specialises in refined cuisine that encompasses all the representative flavours of Zhejiang province. Their house-made dim sum is hugely popular, including deep-fried stinky tofu stuffed with radish and Chinese celery from Shaoxing, tofu buns from Jiande, bamboo shoot shao mai from Suichang and tofu pancake from Changshan.

Name: Wu Ming Mian Guan
Address: 17-1 Youdian Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, 310006, China Mainland
Description: The shop has no name because the owner believes his noodles are good enough to keep guests coming back regardless. In over 30 years, the place has not changed – with just six tables set up in the tiny space. But the huge portions of tasty noodles at bargain prices have amassed a loyal fan base. The fall-off-the-bone pork ribs with strong scallion aromas in particular tend to sell out early. The pork liver and kidney are also popular.

Name: Zi Wei Hall
Address: Building 8, West Lake State Guesthouse, 18 Yanggong Causeway, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Set in a manicured Chinese garden by the lake, the traditionally furnished restaurant makes an impression with its grand and airy space. The smart Chinese attire of the service team is also part of the appeal. On the menu: nicely made Jiangzhe and Hangzhou fare. Try the fried shrimp cake with crunchy water chestnut and diced Chinese celery. The Hangzhou crisp fish is a cold appetiser of deep-fried fish braised in sweet soy – delicious.

Name: Shui Mo Hui
Address: 462 Zhongshan South Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: An oasis near a bustling scenic spot in Hangzhou, the building is styled after a typical residence of ancient Anhui. Ask for a table in the courtyard on a sunny day and be bowled over by the views of Wangxian Pavilion. Both the owner and the kitchen team hail from Anhui; most ingredients are also from their home province. Specialities like fermented mandarin fish, wild bracken, sliced cured pork on camphor wood and Anhui dim sum are hard to find elsewhere.

Name: De Ming Fan Dian
Address: 36 Huyu Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: The down-to-earth joint is nestled in a residential neighbourhood. At the entrance of the dining room, dishes are neatly displayed – leafy greens, meat stews in clay pots and of course, the river fish that the restaurant is most famous for. Fried eel in bean sauce is loaded with scallion and garlic aromas. Braised pork intestine is tender and flavoursome, even better with their secret dip. Try also their house-made wines infused with herbs or fruits.

Name: Wulin
Description: Tucked away in a small alley, Wulin has been serving authentic, reasonably priced Hangzhou food since 2008. The drunken prawns marinated in a wine sauce have a sweet aftertaste; the braised yellow croaker with sticky rice cakes is cooked with chilli bean paste and sliced pork for an umami extravaganza. Lamb, especially popular in winter, is prepared in myriad ways. The main restaurant area isn't huge, but there are a few private rooms available to book.

Name: Grand Dragon (Xihu)
Address: 1F, The Dragon, 120 Shuguang Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: This long-established hotel restaurant is famous for its gorgeous garden views, elegant vibe and upmarket menu. Authentic Zhejiang cooking takes centre stage, alongside new creations melding Cantonese cooking techniques. Classics such as sautéed river shrimps with Longjing tea, and crispy eel with shrimps are revisited, the latter as fried eel pieces stuffed with minced shrimp in a sweet and sour glaze. Private dining rooms of various sizes are available.

Name: Li' An
Address: 50F, Conrad Hotel, 228 Xinye Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Atop a skyscraper hotel, this elegant place commands breath-taking views of the Qiantang River. The decor is inspired by the East-meets-West Art Deco style of China around the 1920s. Cantonese classics are broadly covered – from soups and barbecue meats, to stir-fries with plenty of wok hei, plus a few innovative Zhejiang dishes. Don’t miss the crispy skin chicken. The sautéed fish bladder with pickled mustard greens goes well with an alcoholic drink.

Name: Hu Qing Yu Tang Yao Shan
Address: 98 Zhongshan South Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Hu Qing Yu Tang is a renowned Chinese medicine shop and this restaurant is its culinary venture, specialising in medicinal cooking. The chef complements ingredients with the therapeutic properties of herbs to derive maximum benefits. Huang qi river shrimps, steamed fu ling dumplings, and black sticky rice cake with ginseng are all unique creations you won't find anywhere else. For optimum results, pair your food with medicinal wines or healthy drinks.

Name: Fortune Garden
Address: 504-506, 5F, Phase 2, Star Avenue, 1766 Wentao Road, Binjiang, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: This modern, cosy restaurant sits on the top floor of a shopping mall. The menu showcases the best of Cantonese cooking with sophistication, astuteness and precision. Their dim sum lunch is a must, as are the barbecued meats. The honey-glazed cha siu pork, for instance, boasts the perfect ratio of fat and lean meat, as well as smoky and crispy charred edges. Plum sauce on the side cuts through the richness. Book ahead for private rooms.

Name: Wang Shi Shao Bing (Xixi Road)
Address: 60 Xixi Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: This small shop front would be easy to miss, were it not for the queue waiting to order shaobing flatbread and youtiao dough sticks. Right by the entrance the chefs can be seen busily making both items by hand; served piping hot, they are well loved for their fluffy and crispy texture. Locals typically order soymilk or tofu pudding to go with these fried treats, but you can also opt for sticky rice balls with the filling of your choice. Bargain prices.

Name: Yan Zhu Chao
Address: 2-3F, Block C, Zhongying Xinghai, 30 Zhongchuang Road, Binjiang, Hangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Valet parking
Description: The room sports cultural motifs from the Chaoshan region, including a miniature replica of Guangji Bridge, an icon of Chaozhou. Walk-in diners will be seated in the main dining room and served an à la carte menu. Private rooms must be booked in advance, with a tailored menu. The signature marinated “gelato” raw mud crab boasts creamy roe that melts in the mouth. Also try the double-boiled silkie chicken soup with deer tendon and ginseng.

Name: Hotwoods (Xihu)
Address: 1F, Building 27, Xixi Yihao, Ziyun Street, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: This bustling spot serves barbecue in Texan, Brazilian and Argentinian styles. With a wood-fired smokery and ovens on site, the place exudes intoxicating smells. Try slow-smoked beef brisket, either grain-fed from the U.S. or grass-fed from New Zealand: the former is richer, the latter leaner. Pronounced smoky notes complement the beef perfectly. Grilled pineapple in banana walnut sauce for dessert cuts through the richness. The wine list is worth exploring.

Name: Gui Yu Jia Mian
Address: 74 Lower Manjuelong, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: The space may not be huge, but the minimalist Zen-inspired decor is soothing. In contrast to traditional Hangzhou-style noodles with their firm texture, these are handmade to a softer consistency – all the better for soaking up the soup. The spring water beef shin noodles deliver plenty of umami and a hint of spiciness. Sides such as braised bamboo shoot are also worth trying. Round off your meal with ding sheng cake with red bean filling.

Name: Fu Quan Shu Yuan
Address: 5F, Building A, Zijin Plaza, 701 Gudun Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: After renovation, this hub dedicated to Chinese tea, art and all things Zen befits Hangzhou’s moniker as a cultural jewel. Its adjoining eatery still serves vegetarian food with Zhejiang twists; all-time favourites like soy-marinated walnuts, fresh tofu skin in thick broth and red braised stinky tofu are still on the menu. Thickly sliced lurid bolete sautéed with green chillies stands out with aroma and toothsome texture.

Name: Junxihui
Address: 1F, Wanli Building, 1198 Wenyi West Road, Yuhang, Hangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Foreign credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: (The restaurant is temporarily closed.) Crystal chandeliers, chequered floor tiles and olive green banquettes may not evoke your typical Chinese restaurant, but this grand mansion complete with water features and an expansive garden ticks all the boxes for classic Cantonese fare. Dim sum, stir fries, seafood and Cantonese barbecue are some of the highlights. Thick fish soup with fish maw, black fungus, bamboo shoot and dried shrimps shows impressive layers of textures and umami.

Name: Pu Zhu
Address: 122 Dadou Road, Gongshu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Adjacent to Xiangji Temple, this Jiangnan-style villa stands in a manicured garden with bamboo trees, rock works and water features. In the absence of à la carte options, diners pre-order the classic or seasonal set menu. Quality globally sourced produce is finessed by both Chinese and Western techniques into neat creations with potential health benefits. Tree tomato soup with seaweed from the waters of Xiapu kicks off the meal on a refreshing note.

Name: Pan Fang Chun (Zhongshan South Road)
Address: 479-481 Zhongshan South Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: A favourite spot for breakfast among locals, Pan Fang Chun specialises in potstickers – with a nicely charred, paper-thin crust and juicy pork filling, they taste even better dipped in chilli sauce and vinegar. Cut through the richness with a bowl of sweet soymilk. For a lighter option, try the bite-size wonton soup with laver and scallions. Expect to queue at the door for service, and they close before 1pm, so come early to avoid disappointment.

Name: Guan Yan Liu Jin
Address: 3F, Section A, Hubin Yintai in77, 123 Pinghai Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: The theatrically lit main room is a picture of understated elegance, and the private rooms are equally stylish. The head chef, who hails from Chaoshan region, specialises in the cuisine of his hometown. Try the marinated meat platter to sample a few of his signature items and their layered flavours. Deep-fried cloth-wrapped tofu in premium stock boasts a crispy crust and velvety centre. The mild soybean flavour works well with the umami-laden broth.

Name: Jiang Nan Yu Ge
Address: 49-53 Shiwukui Alley, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Tucked away in a historical back street, this place teleports diners to a bygone era. The rustic-style interior is quirky, with bottles of yellow wine, including its own brand, placed on the floor. The kitchen team tailors menus to diners' budgets and the fish-heavy Ningbo fare is rife with bold flavours and umami. Try the steamed crab on pork ribs with distillers grains. With only two tables for two in the main room, it makes sense to book a private room.

Name: Dining Room
Address: 37F, Park Hyatt Hotel, 1366 Qianjiang Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: With exquisite glass lanterns, glass screens and panoramic windows that welcome in river views, the high-ceilinged room is perfect for banquets and business dinners. The menu is dominated by Zhejiang classics, alongside some Cantonese dishes. The poetically named "Sinking Fish, Falling Geese" consists of white fish balls stuffed with bird's nest. The classic braised pork belly is thinly sliced and styled into a pagoda. Reservations recommended.

Name: In Villa
Address: 71 Longjing Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The three-storey villa dates back to the early 20C and its lavish interior melds classical and modern details. The head chef from Hangzhou works closely with two Cantonese chefs to craft recipes that are rooted in Jiangzhe traditions, but spiced up with Cantonese accents. The fried crab with stinky tofu is prepared in typhoon shelter style; stinky tofu is diced and deep-fried with garlic, black beans and scallion. Jinhua ham pastry bursts with meaty flavours.

Name: Nature's Own
Address: 1F, Meifan Plaza Proya, 588 Xixi Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: An oasis amid the bustling city centre complete with a landscaped garden straight out of a Song Dynasty art book. The menu focuses on plant-based dishes of varying origins and styles. Cauliflower fungus tossed in lemongrass with Thai chilli and basil packs extra oomph; sizzling three-cup eggplant in a stone pot seduces with aromas and mild heat. Round off with sticky millet rice balls and a peanut filling. Check out the extensive tea menu.

Name: Xi Xi Liang Chen
Address: 8 Wujiawan Street, Xixi National Wetland Park, Fangxi Road, Yuhang, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: A serene place in a wetland park with a manicured Chinese garden. With just eight private rooms, privacy is guaranteed. Menus are tailor-made to diners' liking in advance, without à la carte options. The kitchen puts a sophisticated spin on authentic Chaozhou and Swatow dishes, with produce such as pickled mustard greens and baby mussels from Chaozhou. Try the soy-marinated goose webs and liver, and sticky rice balls in peanut sesame sugar.

Name: La Lune
Address: L628, 6F, The Mixc, 701 Fuchun Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: The high-ceilinged room is lavishly furnished with elegant chandeliers, ceiling fans and elaborate trims. The kitchen team excels in fusion Chinese cooking that creatively mixes and matches influences and techniques from various regional cuisines. Thinly sliced air-dried mackerel steeped in a special briny-sweet sauce is loaded with umami. The slow-cooked veal in a truffle sauce literally melts in your mouth. The curated tea list is intriguing!

Name: Hang's Delicacy (Xihu)
Address: 92 Zhijiang Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: On the bank of Qiantang River, at the foot of Liuhe Pagoda, this airy, bright and sleekly furnished restaurant is a bit out of the way, but locals come in droves nonetheless. Authentic home-style Hangzhou dishes, such as steamed mud crab on a minced pork patty, are served alongside more novel creations. Portion sizes are generous; come in a larger party to get to sample a wider variety of dishes. Reservations not accepted. Visit early to beat the crowd.

Name: Shuiyang
Address: Xianghu Xiaoyao Manor, 256 Yuewang Road, Xiaoshan, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Xiaoyao Manor hotel opened in Xianghu Lake Resort in 2020. This F&B outlet is set in an idyllic landscape, boasts gorgeous views and serves authentic Hangzhou, Zhejiang dishes, as well as Xiaoshan farmhouse cooking. Made-to-order fish head à la Qiandao Lake can be prepared in various ways and is great for sharing. The peasant-style steamed stinky duo is quite unique and worth trying. The perfect spot to eat as part of your Xianghu Lake itinerary.

Name: Hu Ge Si Fang Cai
Description: Next to a cultural park, this restaurant stands in serene, lush nature. The interior, too, is pleasing, with its retro water town decor. On the menu, Hangzhou classics take centre stage; river fish stands out in particular. The slaughtered-to-order river eel is steamed with preserved mustard greens and has oily flesh and deep umami. The fresh local vegetables and traditional staples such as Hangzhou style tossed noodles and sticky rice cake are also worth trying.

Name: La Villa
Address: Seven Villas, 1 Bapanling Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking
Description: Inside a resort, this ancient monastery-turned restaurant imparts a feeling of serenity. Only open to the public for dinner, it serves a menu that changes every season. Local produce is prepared using impeccable European techniques, artistic plating and unique taste profiles. Pan-fried yellow croaker is crispy on the outside, silky on the inside; the light sauce works magic to accentuate its natural flavour. Ask the sommelier about wine or tea pairings.

Name: Wan Li
Address: 2-3F, Renaissance Northeast Hotel, 607 Renmin Avenue, Nanyuan Street, Linping, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Avant-garde portraits of Chinese opera singers fetchingly set against gilded birdcage chandeliers and window cut-outs. Modern Chinese style is carried through the menu and plating. Diners come here for skilfully made Hangzhou, Zhejiang and Cantonese classics; the signature Hangzhou braised duck has a delicate texture, rich flavours and complex aromas. The hand-torn tofu in a milky broth made with dried shrimps, ham and mushrooms is also unmissable.

Name: The Yue Hall
Address: 58F, Sky Habitat, T1 Raffles City, 228 Xinye Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: On the 58th floor of a skyscraper, this tiny gem with just eight tables affords lovely views of the bustling financial centre. Modernised Chinese motifs are juxtaposed with a futuristic electric glow. Under the supervision of an experienced chef from Hong Kong, the kitchen turns out umami-packed double-boiled soups, such as the whelk and dried scallop soup with matsutake mushrooms. The live seafood, such as fish and crab, tastes divine even when simply steamed.

Name: Kui Yuan Guan (Jiefang Road)
Address: 154 Jiefang Road, Shangcheng, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: A household name for its Hangzhou-style noodles, Kui Yuan Guan also doubles up as a museum that charts life in the city dating back to 1867. Countless inscriptions by historical big shots hint at its importance. For noodles, head to the ground floor; the sliced pork noodles impress with their al dente texture and robust flavours. Classic Zhejiang fare, such as Ningbo shredded eel or fish balls with a trio of vegetables, is served on the second floor.

Name: Tian Lun Inn (Xihu)
Address: 1F, Building No. 7, Ecological Cluster, 550 Xixi Road, Xihu, Hangzhou, China Mainland
Description: Synonymous with delicious crab dishes, Tian Lun Inn serves different species of this crustacean depending on the season, with its multicourse all-crab meals being the most renowned. With firm, plump flesh and rich, creamy roe, hairy crabs from Taihu Lake are extremely popular year round. The crab roe pastry takes 45 minutes to prepare, but it's well worth the wait. Try local specialities such as West Lake beef soup or West Lake vinegar fish, too.

Name: La Quintessence
Description: Housed in a converted 16C Jesuit refectory, this restaurant in the Presqu'île district has plenty of character, with its stone walls, columns and arches, its vaulted ceiling, hardwood floors and tall windows. Chef Anthony Baud cooks up balanced modern cuisine that emphasises the freshness and quality of the ingredients, in dishes such as Arctic char with pak choi, or a delicious persimmon dessert incorporating ginger and pumpkin seed praline.
