Name: L'Auberge
Description: The mix of leather, wood panelling, copper and glass gives L'Auberge the look and feel of an authentic brasserie. Located in Spa's bustling town centre, this restaurant has plenty of regulars, who come to savour traditional Belgian cuisine. The menu features hearty classics such as mussels in white wine (also available in half portions), veal kidneys à la liégeoise, crêpes mikado – the generous flavours will leave you feeling warm and satisfied. The guestrooms are worth a look if you're considering a longer stay.

Name: Basta!
Description: The bright, contemporary dining room is the quintessence of Italian warmth and the garden terrace is ideal for alfresco dining when the weather is fine. Gianni Caruso allows his Sicilian heritage to run riot in dishes packed with exuberant flavours. He might season tartare of tuna with a delicate blend of ricotta, capers and lemon oil, unless you wouldn’t prefer a generous plate of risotto followed by Taglioni al tartufo… One thing is certain: the chef’s immaculate knowhow and craftsmanship do full justice to Mediterranean produce (the wine list is of the same ilk). Unadulterated pleasure is the name of the game at Basta!

Name: Les Gribaumonts
Description: The façade of this restaurant is adorned in colourful frescoes, which also set the scene in the contemporary interior. The harmony between Nicolas’ inspired wine pairings and Lisa’s elegant culinary prowess is irresistible. The chef has a fondness for local ingredients, whose rich flavours are further enhanced by delicate touches and a consummate wine list.

Name: La Croustade
Description: Lovingly tended flowerbeds, a delightful cottage garden and goldfish in the pond - dining on the terrace of this exquisite country house is heavenly in fine weather. Every month, chef Thierry composes a new menu that demonstrates his classical training and know-how. He freely delves into the cottage garden to enhance dishes such as mint-crusted rack of lamb and pan-fried foie gras.

Name: Njord
Description: Make a beeline for the top floor of the amazing ABC edifice and admire the jaw-dropping view over the port and marina below. Luxurious and trendy, the restaurant specialises in ultra-fresh delicacies straight from the local fish auction. Traditional, authentic flavours that respect the character and freshness of the ingredients. Slick service. The seafood platter is also available in individual portions.

Name: Maison D
Description: The customer comes first in the elegant establishment of Delphine and Didier. Delphine’s vivacious personality depicts the front-of-house vibe, while Didier’s enthusiasm is contagious. The chef has a knack for adding a personal spin to fine produce and familiar flavours. He might add a playful edge to consummately crafted turbot, with different textures of parsley, all of which is enhanced by a spicy concoction of clams. The extensive menu embodies the establishment’s desire to pamper. First rate lunchtime menu.

Name: Boîte
Description: What a pity we don’t live down the road from this amusing "box"! “Taste the world, Share the food” is their baseline! The seasoned chef curates her own version of world cuisine, steeped in variety, harmony and exoticism… For example, deftly crafted spicy Lebanese toast, generous tajine, sweet and sour noodles, etc. Even better, diners can choose their own vegetable side dishes and are invited to share the main course with the rest of the table. Perfect for a casual dining experience!

Name: Brabohoeve
Description: Brabohoeve is a villa-restaurant whose smart, modern interior is adorned in arty photos. The terrace overlooking the surrounding meadows is a must when the weather is fine. Franco-Belgian classics take the leading role in the culinary repertory with family favourites like shrimp fritters and vol-au-vent of free-range chicken in star positions, crafted with flawless technique and flanked by a succulent selection of seasonal specials. Examples include fresh, juicy brill garnished with mushrooms and gnocchi, or saddle of hare in season. Expect to find it difficult to make up your mind, such is the range tempting and enticing…

Name: Stable
Description: Enter the former stables of Hof Ter Linden and discover a mysterious world of cosy romanticism. The period wooden timbers, old stone floors and soft lighting underscore the building’s historic character and provide the perfect foil to deftly crafted fare that cleverly mixes old and new. The chef lets his imagination run riot, adding the odd fascinating international touch. The powerful butter sauce, jazzed up with dashi, adds a kick to pure white sablefish, while crispy calf’s sweetbread is boldly paired with anchovy and a hibiscus-laced mousseline. We recommend the set menu to get a genuine insight into Stable’s amazing culinary universe.

Name: Blanco
Description: David and Celine describe Blanco as “highly Instagrammable” and the trendy interior definitely ticks all the boxes: fashionable, spacious and buzzy! After a refreshing cocktail, you will sample dishes of Mexican inspiration: flavoursome tacos, subtly spicy chipotle, home-made ajo blanco (white gazpacho) and fish from the North Sea. A genuine culinary adventure…

Name: Bonifas
Description: Bonifas is steeped in the charm of a country inn with welcoming staff and a warm contemporary ambience. Chef Grégory Duranton is an unabashed fan of Gallic cuisine. You can expect rich dishes that star ingredients such as suave foie gras, intense truffle-flavoured pasta and a cut of Limousin beef crafted with textbook perfection and served with a béarnaise sauce of such depth that it will knock your socks off. The lunchtime and set menus are very popular.

Name: Un temps pour Soi
Description: The lovely countryside around this village is just the ticket for a weekend getaway and where better to start than on the delightful terrace of this quintessentially relaxing edifice? The same mood prevails inside courtesy of a setting oozing in authenticity and serenity. The generous chef is a dab hand at classical cooking, to which he may add a scattering of modern, even global accents. For example, he might sear local asparagus until crispy on a plancha, adding a flamboyant note with ricotta cream laced in lemon, or a fresh, acidic beurre blanc and a herby oil. Market fresh cuisine to die for!

Name: Mamy Louise
Description: This elegant edifice, built out of wood, glass and steel, is home to a brasserie, a cocktail bar with a terrace, lounges and meeting rooms. The equally varied menu ranges from shrimp fritters and sole meunière to veal kidneys and ossobuco in a lineup of Franco-Belgian inspiration, dotted with a few Italian classics, all of which is underscored by a love of cooking and generous helpings. There is something for everyone at Mamy Louise.

Name: Didier Galet
Address: rue du Grand Bru 27, Sprimont, 4140, Belgium
Description: Before you even sit down in this friendly joint done up in an inviting vein, you feel perfectly at home. Christine greets diners with a smile and chef Didier Galet waves a hi from the kitchen. Galet is a champion of his region and committed to working with local ingredients. From wood pigeon to fresh veggies, the chef sources everything locally, crafting each ingredient with infinite respect. His cooking draws on his classical training, jazzed up with expressive sauces. He is equally capable of rolling out a rich mushroom and truffle stock, a light frothy espuma of potatoes or a liberal grating of royal truffle. The alfresco terrace is perfect to sample this ode to Belgian produce and producers.

Name: La Gloriette
Description: Overflowing in charm, this townhouse appointed in a contemporary vein sports an idyllic terrace overlooking the kitchen garden of chef Olivier Bauche. The chef works with sincere affection and a warm heart and doesn’t hesitate to try out new ideas, sometimes surprising us with amusing combinations of sweet and sour flavours or, for example, with a spicy lovage ice cream that he serves with a saddle of medium rare lamb. In season, he frequently has game from Ardennes on the menu. Dive into the wine list safe in the knowledge that La Gloriette Hotel, just opposite, can put you up for the night in style...

Name: le Vugo
Description: Near Mouscron railway station in a relatively nondescript neighbourhood, it comes as something of a surprise to find this contemporary restaurant and its cosy vibe. The chef adds a modern twang to classical recipes, deploying his technical skills and generous personality. He might pair lightly seared calf’s sweetbread, sliced into escalopes, with a warm espuma of lobster sabayon, girolle mushrooms and grilled langoustine. Be forewarned: deciding between the mouthwatering à la carte and set menus is an almost heartrending exploit!

Name: Rizoom
Description: Rizoom blends a design-inspired, post-industrial loft vibe with a cosy feel. Take a seat in the open kitchen or at a beautifully laid table and watch Yves Kerckhoffs wield his magic as he brings his passion for produce to life, invariably courtesy of solid Japanese technique. Sustainability and the seasons guide both the menu and the establishment’s choice of suppliers. You can expect dry-ageing, koji fermentation and a single-minded quest for umami, hence the major role enjoyed by sauces and gravy. For example, brill is wrapped and aged in kombu leaves, before it is sliced into sashimi and then further underscored by a gutsy roast poultry jus. An adventurous culinary score that is enhanced by an outstanding list of wines and sakes.

Name: Hostellerie Stafelter
Description: This hostelry is emblematic of Tom Brosius and his outlook. The interior is warm and elegant, and the flavoursome food is free of fussy frills. He cherry-picks premium market-fresh produce and locally grown ingredients, concocting veggie-led recipes oozing in character. The repertory is rich in pedigree Belgian favourites like pot-au-feu made with fork-tender chuck beef and a delicious green veggie sauce. At lunchtime, choosing between the set and à la carte menus can be something of a conundrum. Comfortable guestrooms await you should you wish to extend your stay in this welcoming establishment.

Name: Eddy Vraie
Description: Chef Eddy’s last name (True) is indeed emblematic of his powerful, honest cooking, free of pointless frills or fuss. Generous helpings of good wholesome nosh await the hungry diner. Examples include melt-in-the-mouth terrine of rabbit, speck and foie gras and the house signatures are salmon smoked on the premises and seared foie gras. A restaurant with a soul, both in the plate and the decor, both of which exemplify the establishment’s commitment to authenticity.

Name: La Fleur de Thym
Description: David and Olivia embark you on an Ardennes adventure that is both familiar and polished in their welcoming house appointed in a modern vein. The chef’s deft, modern score is an ode to first-class ingredients which are allowed to shout their name. He may underscore scallops marinated in sake with a mirin dressing and textures of yellow beetroot, while Anjou pigeon acquires a worldly dimension in two dishes flanked by autumn veggies, fried panisse (chickpeas) and a knockout port wine sauce. Recognisable, contemporary fare with a respectful light touch that takes regional cuisine to new heights.

Name: Du Moulin
Description: The wood-burning fire in the cosy sitting room is the epitome of an Ardennes inn. This nostalgic charm is enhanced by the classical cooking of Jean Goire, who brooks no concessions. He pays tribute to his region, working closely with carefully selected suppliers. His culinary expertise unveils a deep-rooted respect and steadfast commitment to flavours that are gutsy, rustic and traditional to the core.

Name: Bonheur Simple
Description: It is the little things that make us happy. Such as an attractive table setting in a contemporary restaurant, a peaceful atmosphere, and authentic Thai flavours in the creative cooking. Simplicity really is good.

Name: Bistro Rombaux
Description: Pieter-Jan Rombaux and his wife, Tineke, do everything themselves and the focus is clearly home-made. She nurtures the cheerful, unstuffy vibe, while he rustles up dishes that seek to enhance the ingredient’s pure flavours with perfect seasonings. Take a seat on the secluded terrace to admire the chef at work in the kitchen. Rather than gimmicky surprises, you can look forward to heart-warming dishes such as foie gras with brioche or hanger steak with a red-wine sauce to die for.

Name: La Strada
Description: Contemporary restaurant faithful to Italy’s culinary heritage. Chef Pierro hails from Umbria and Tuscan cuisine has no secrets from him. His truffle recipes are standout. His son, Valentino, adds his youthful enthusiasm in the kitchen, while Myriame’s gracious welcome completes this family affair.

Name: De Blauwe Artisjok
Description: Satisfied customers are the raison d’être of this stylish villa, where you are graciously greeted by Nathalie before taking a seat in the elegant dining room. Veteran chef Kurt Verhaege aims to work with fresh, seasonal produce. He boasts a classical training and his textbook perfect champagne sauce is a model of French culinary technique, as are his main courses and side dishes, which also feature a subtle international slant. Delicious eater-friendly prices.

Name: Spaans Dak
Description: The view from this 16C manor house over Zoet Water is quite simply stunning and the modern wing, done up in designer-inspired vibe, also commands a splendid view. The food is modern and meticulously crafted in a bid to create succulent contrasts with the core ingredient. The three-course menu is one of the highlights of this splendid establishment.

Name: Hostellerie De Biek
Description: We wager that before you even set foot in this family-run eatery, you will have fallen in love with the authentic Flemish village. The immense windows of the former brewery overlook the village and a sheltered terrace, while the striking interior sports timber rafters and brick walls. Before relaxing in one of the comfortable guestrooms, treat yourself to something from the extensive menu. Brabançon-style pheasant or bouchot mussels served in a spicy nduja and red curry sauce: the chef adds a kick to Belgian classics thanks to playful, creative inventions. A knockout lineup of regional produce.

Name: Storm
Description: Storms do not prevent fishing boats from mooring in front of the door. The experienced chef pays them tribute with a host of delicacies, using modern techniques (including a passing nod to Asia and Scandinavia). However, relax, the cosy interior and cheerful staff will ensure you weather this storm in style.

Name: Siphon
Description: Be it with sorrel, meunière or à la crème, people flock to this characterful restaurant from near and far to enjoy the house speciality, eel. They also offer grilled lobster and steak, as a quick look at their menu, an ode to tradition, will confirm. Siphon has become something of a culinary landmark in the region, further backed up by an intelligent wine list.

Name: Robuust
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: The contemporary elegance of this delightful villa is more than worthy of a home decoration magazine. Even better, it is flanked by a lovely patio and boasts a small conservatory to the rear. The chef focuses on flavours which he crafts into his own versions of traditional recipes such as classic eels in green herbs and vol-au-vent. High-flying, inspired craftsmanship and lashings of flavour illustrate that Robuust is far from averse to showcasing its delicate facet.

Name: L'air des Sens
Description: Snug, pared-back and arty – the interior of this historic 1900 edifice is equally as fascinating as David Schulz’ fine cuisine. Veggies, herbs and seasonings form the backbone of his cooking. Almost everything is prepared from scratch and many of the recipes star local meat or North Sea seafood. He works hand in hand with the seasons, adding a creative spin, unexpected twists and exciting new techniques. A keen interest in Dutch wines adds the final flourish to this enticing portrait.

Name: Chez Duche
Description: You can expect unadorned dishes that throb with flavour in what is the epitome of a neighbourhood eatery: rib of horse meat with house-made fries, lavishly served cassoulet, piled high with duck confit and Toulouse sausage or a waterzooi of seasonal veggies. A patriotic pageant of French and Belgian classics prepared and served with textbook precision and generosity. Chez Duche has been feeding us well since 1993!

Name: La Bru'sserie
Address: rue du Comte Théodule d'Ursel 14, Durbuy, 6940, Belgium
Description: From Belgium to Asia, via Latin America with stopovers in Spain and Provence, Wout Bru will take your tastebuds on a whirlwind tour with his amazing tapas. We recommend one of the enticing menus if you don’t want to spend all evening dithering over your choice. You may start with the subtle roasted aromas of langoustine tail paired with a gutsy wakame sauce and a vivacious espuma of spicy lemon oil, before digging into one of Wout Bru’s emblematic house signatures. La Bru’sserie, which is the epitome of hip, is just the place for knockout distinctive dishes and a deliciously casual vibe. A trendy version of Durbuy!

Name: L'Atelier Cuisine
Address: voie de l'Air Pur 207, Beaufays, 4052, Belgium
Description: As you set foot in this striking Art deco edifice reminiscent of the 1930s and make your way over a carpet of flowers, you will immediately feel at home. The new venue of L’Atelier Cuisine is a gem! Homemade fare and fresh produce are the name of the game. The patriotic line-up of French and Italian classics has no secrets for the chef who crafts knockout nosh, sprinkled with Mediterranean influences. A bite of the veal escalope alla Milanese will transport you straight to a sunny Northern Italy.

Name: The Chick
Description: Ancient murals and untreated or designer materials paint the picture in this authentic 16C edifice, idyllically located at the foot of Saint Rumbold’s Tower. A glamorous vibe provides the perfect foil for the creative, international set menu. You can expect unusual dishes such as a barbecued slice of watermelon with crumbly feta, pieces of herring, pistachios and crunchy rice noodles. An apparently classical façade hides a treasure trove of surprises. While you’re there, take the time to explore The (wine) Cellar boutique and The Chapel, ideal for events and special occasions.

Name: Brasserie Juste
Description: Back-to-basics brasserie cuisine, fresh ingredients and a chef who adds his own personal touch. “Juste” what it takes to satisfy good food lovers. Even better, the chef is a fan of wood fired Josper ovens. Hand chopped beef tartare with crunchy fries, hearty helpings of vol-au-vent and a made-to-order dame blanche with vanilla ice cream and smothered in chocolate sauce: every dish is a model of culinary generosity. A suitably tasteful trendy interior and an alfresco area overlooking the fields and the vegetable garden.

Name: Gus
Description: Pierre Baeyens and Jonathan Delhière acquaint you with the “brassonomy” concept (beer meets gastronomy) in their cosy brasserie. They skilfully incorporate the many flavours of artisan beer and hops into a Franco-Belgian line-up, in the glass and also in the subtle food. A foamy beer mousseline nestles up to a soft-poached egg and mushrooms or steak is smoked in hops: the chefs add an individual touch to creative recipes. A bubbling Brussels brasserie-cum-brewery!

Name: Controverse
Description: Crisp clean lines set the scene of the modern brasserie of De Kluizen Golf Club (overlooking the greens), which is as well suited to a date night as to a business lunch. It rightly defines its cuisine as authentically characterful, with a classical repertory starring vitello tonnato, asparagus à la flamande and sabayon. The ingredients are outstanding, the cooking bang on and the sauces subtly suave. In season, you will also find game dishes like saddle of hare. The lunchtime menu never disappoints!

Name: Restaurant Mathes
Description: This restaurant, on the scenic wine road of this pretty region of Moselle and near a splendid village that boasts innumerable wine cellars and vineyards, is well known to foodies. Today, the third generation is upholding the family legacy and diners will taste textbook classics with a subtle modern spin served in an elegant dining room overlooking the Moselle or on the sun-drenched terrace. The menu is the epitome of traditional and the house signature remains zander – oven-bake, underscored by a delicate Riesling sauce and washed down with an attractive selection of Luxembourg wines. Just the spot to explore this lovely region.

Name: Le D'Arville
Description: This inviting redbrick, 19C farmhouse features a clever mixture of rustic and modern, while its terrace, furnished with wooden tables, commands a fine view of the countryside. The creative cuisine is depicted by regional recipes and a large proportion of house - made preparations. The Barabas guest rooms offer modern comforts.

Name: Um Plateau
Description: Um Plateau is casual, smart and hip and the soft lighting on the buzzy terrace sets the trendy tone. Start with a glass of wine or a cocktail in the lively bar, before perusing the menu which offers a fine choice of dishes to share and textbook classics. Examples range from razor clams in a subtle parsley jus to a juicy rib steak paired with a pepper sauce spiked in cognac, unless you wouldn’t prefer a ceviche or a big-boned ossobuco. While traditional at heart, this repertory is not averse to whisking you off on a culinary tour from the Mediterranean to Asia.

Name: La Ligne Rouge
Description: This stylish contemporary eatery depicted by crisp clean lines is the epitome of tranquil. On the edge of Soignes Forest, get ready to be pampered by a friendly waiting team. Guillaume Desart himself describes his style as “nouvelle classical cuisine”. Indeed, his passion for top-drawer ingredients and his flair for sauces are indicative of a desire to uphold tradition, albeit scattered with playful notes, such as crispy calf sweetbread flanked by a velvety béarnaise with nasturtium-flavoured vinegar.

Name: L'Art de Vivre
Description: Notable's house cultivates the art of living by way of a pleasant setting and a lovely, modern, à la carte menu with a splash of creativity. Set menus described to you; homemade cakes and desserts.

Name: Céma Passion
Description: The menu features modern French cuisine, which is rich in enthusiasm and sophistication. Seasonal produce takes pride of place on the inventive menu. A genuine culinary experience.

Name: Cuisinez-Nous
Address: rue de la Gare 138, Bertrix, 6880, Belgium
Description: In this tasteful townhouse, Alain and Céline further confirm their excellent reputation acquired at the Rosa restaurant. Céline caters to diners’ every whim in the dining room, while Alain deploys his talents in a traditional French repertory.

Name: Wilford T
Description: The industrial sobriety of Wilford T is underscored by the artwork in the adjoining Wilford X exhibition gallery. Meals are served in an arty ambience steeped in serenity, which provides the perfect foil to a banquet of unadulterated purity. Chef Vermeiren, who doesn’t hesitate to add the finishing touch right in front of diners, is committed to highlighting the ingredient with unusual combinations, that are sometimes complex, but always flavoursome. Should you order venison, for example, it is flanked by an intense spicy sauce and succulent fritters that are still handmade by mum herself.

Name: Resto Wald
Description: Lisa and Walter Wald are keen to maintain the “Small is beautiful” ethic of their hip eatery, which adds to the home-from-home feel. Whenever possible, the enthusiastic chef prepares everything himself using locally sourced ingredients. He draws his inspiration from his many overseas trips and enjoys mixing surprising flavours. He is equally at home with juicy pheasant in a cognac sauce as with a tartare of seabass paired with shellfish oil, vanilla, cucumber extract and goat’s yoghurt and tarragon ice cream. You can expect a flavourful meal with a modern spin in a cosy setting.

Name: De Fakkels
Description: Seppe Bleus and Liese Bams have taken over the business and welcome you to De Fakkels 2.0. They have kept its soul intact, so the imposing building still exudes warmth and a sense of romance. Goose feather lampshades, designer lighting and wooden ornaments make for a unique setting. In a bid to keep up with the times, the menu's feature exciting new combinations, such as the bright and zesty interplay of calamansi and orange with ultra-fresh scallops. The depth of his sauces, like the rich game sauce that graces the venison fillet, is testament to the chef's culinary mastery. This long-established haven for foodies is in good hands.

Name: Den Silveren Harynck
Description: A mother and son team (Els and Sam) welcome guests into the stylishly elegant Van Landeghem family establishment. Floor to ceiling windows lead into the garden which is flanked by a patio. Dad, Luc, can be found rustling up tasty, flavourful delicacies in the kitchen, combining classical training and creative touches, ranging from Rossini tournedos steak to a bouillabaisse jazzed up with subtle, Asian notes.

Name: Savoury
Description: This spruce detached house does sport a faintly English hallmark, the menu, however, unveils a patriotic line-up of classical French cuisine. Kick off your meal with an aperitif in the wine cellar before taking a seat in the modern dining room or on the leafy patio. Subtle classicism depicts the textbook precision cooking, albeit with an occasional Mediterranean twang and a refreshing sprinkling of modernity. Pop into the delicatessen before you leave and take a few delicacies home.

Name: Tafel 10
Description: A black and white tiled floor and an open fire set the scene in this plush bourgeois 19C home, but the comfort is entirely 21C, as is the splendid terrace to the rear. The chef has opted for a playful lineup of international influences, without forgetting his classical heritage. He might pair a tataki of bonito with a sweet-sour vinaigrette, or medium rare veal with black truffles, a tarragon mayonnaise and a bordelaise sauce. A choice of four-, five- and six-course menus, all of which overflow with intensity and flavour.

Name: Gastrobar Hop
Description: Hop is a gastrobar that celebrates wine and craft beer. The head-spinning choice is fortunately accompanied by the owner’s knowledgeable insights. Whether you choose an unusual natural wine or a craft beer, the chefs will always find a playful combination to enhance your dish. Eschewing luxury ingredients, they have honed in on the flavours of yesteryear and subtly textured variations. Gourmet dining in a delightfully casual setting that hits the spot every time!

Name: Upton
Description: Upton is a hip eatery in a buzzy neighbourhood. Experienced chef, Gianfranco Van de Maele, invites you to sample his globe-trotting approach to food. Start with a cold glass of draught lager, before digging into his succulent fresh pasta, the recipes of which come from his “nonna”. Bisque-flavoured homemade spaghetti and super fresh seafood and shellfish – magnifico! A fascinating modern culinary melting pot that blends Italian authenticity with Asian influences gleaned from his travels.

Name: Brasserie des Jardins
Description: If only we lived next-door to this modern brasserie… Slick, seamless service, a peaceful patio and a traditional lineup crafted by expert hands. The calf’s liver, cooked to perfection, is paired with a shallot sauce, the salmon, raw, cooked or smoked, glistens in an unusual starter, flanked by, among others, kiwi, mango and a coulis of red beetroot: the chef clearly knows his business. The knockout wine list further confirms the establishment’s commitment to fine produce.

Name: Bick Stuff
Description: A family-run establishment where you will instantly feel at home. Bick is a local word which literally means ‘beak’ in English but loosely translates as ‘food’. Owners Virginie and Denis Laissy have the same goal: to serve good food in a relaxed atmosphere. Chef Denis rustles up reassuringly classical recipes, adding his own distinctive touch. We recommend the set menu.

Name: Un Altro Mondo
Address: Courte Rue du Rivage 1, Wavre, 1300, Belgium
Description: Quirkily tucked away behind shops, this Altro Mondo acquaints you with the highly personal vision of Luca and Caroline. Italian influences dominate the menu, such as Tagliani in truffles in a powerful gutsy sauce. You can also expect a line-up of more modern dishes that reflect the character of the enthusiastic, charismatic sommelier.

Name: Auberge de la Roseraie
Address: route de la Marache 4, Ohain, 1380, Belgium
Description: The inhabitants of well-heeled Ohain have adopted this 19C farmstead that is a bastion of French cooking served in a relaxed atmosphere. Rather than surprises, you can expect to sample deftly executed recipes by a chef who combines his deep-seated understanding of ingredients with subtle sauces. An example: juicy quail with a crispy skin, lightly seared veal sweetbread and a honey-flavoured jus. Nostalgic flavours of yesteryear!

Name: Royal H.-Bonhomme
Address: rue de la Reffe 26, Remouchamps, 4920, Belgium
Description: This comforting inn is emblematic of the Ardennes countryside and of its history. Eight generations of Daussaint innkeepers have been at its helm since 1768! A wrought-iron pergola provides the romantic setting for a dinner for two featuring classical French fare: fried trout, lobster from the lobster tank, tournedos of venison… Delicious!

Name: La Bottega
Description: The best Italian restaurant of Eupen is on Gospertstraße. Traditional pizza, succulent lasagne and yummy Gamberoni prawn and pasta. The kitchen team combines generosity and wholehearted authenticity, without forgetting the odd, unorthodox twist. The delicatessen counter is a great success.

Name: Bütgenbacher Hof
Description: The second generation has further enhanced the already well-known reputation of this family-run establishment. Diners are welcomed like old friends into a chalet-like interior that provides the perfect foil for a classical lineup with a regional twist packed in generosity, as the chef adds a highly personal spin to all-time family favourites. Examples include an upside-down tart of sweet red onions with a sorbet of red cabbage and cream cheese and chives. The varied à la carte score and set menu that changes daily leave diners spoiled for choice. Go there your eyes closed – possibly booking a room so you can explore the surrounding unspoilt countryside at a more leisurely pace.

Name: Sophie & Nicolas
Description: Seasonal, sustainable and local depict the characterful establishment of Sophie Gigot and Nicolas Septon, which is as pared-back and natural as their cuisine. A seat on the terrace beneath the grapevine trellis is just the ticket for a leisurely meal. Chef Nicolas cooks with spontaneity and flair, changing the menu weekly based on fresh arrivals from local producers, to whom he pays tribute via a small card placed on each table. Is it broad bean season? In which case, they may be flanked by a rhubarb, scented geranium and goat’s milk sauce. Fresh Ondenval trout might be baked in golden, flaky puff pastry and then paired with fermented asparagus and a tangy broth made from fermentation juices. A playful approach to micro-seasonal cooking, gift wrapped in a wholesome setting.

Name: Bistronoom
Description: Bistronoom is an elegant Normandy-inspired villa in the heart of the Flemish Ardennes. The appetising repertory draws on the best of French and Flemish traditions. The menu is deliciously familiar, the flavours are wholehearted and recognisable and the produce is seasonal. Examples include crispy sweetbread in a creamy cognac sauce with chives and fresh fries, unless you wouldn’t prefer a sole meunière or a gutsy osso bucco that explodes with flavour. The extensive menu is just one of the reasons that Bistronoom has earned itself such a loyal crowd of regulars.

Name: Lesco
Description: The authentic décor of this handsome town house is perfectly paired with modern comforts. Wooden floors, elegant mirrors and a trendy vibe. The lovely terrace in the garden is equally enchanting. The surprise menu reflects the creative talents and playful streak of the chefs.

Name: Het Moment
Description: Nicolas Hauman’s former villa is steeped in an exquisite ambience that is quite unforgettable. Whether you opt for the classical à la carte lineup or the more modern menu, you know the ingredients will be first-rate. Lightly seared fillet of veal with a ratatouille and a mustard-spiked gravy or glazed whiting paired with crunchy asparagus, briny Limonium and vin jaune flavoured beurre blanc: a fine dining treat from the appetisers to the dessert, further enhanced by seamless, spot-on service.

Name: Bistro R
Description: Roland Debuyst is inspired by top-quality Belgian produce, but also by his globetrotting background. He focuses on bistro fare with a hint of modernity. Gyosa and ceviche are naturally combined with a dish of game, such as wild boar. This seasoned chef cannot be faulted when it comes to intelligently marrying flavours. The contemporary interior adorned with handsome works of art adds the final flourish to this enticing portrait.

Name: De Normandie
Description: It may look like a ship washed up on the dunes, but don’t be mistaken: this 1936 boat-shaped edifice is home to a well-oiled, contemporary brasserie. Super fresh seafood takes pride of place with lobster dishes playing the leading role! Generous, legible fare with a strong French bias, although the chef has no qualms about adding a new spin to classical recipes.

Name: Bistro Tribunal "Chez Yf"
Description: Have you ever heard of a meat sommelier? Well, in this traditional bistro, one such will help you make your choice among the fine cuts of meat supplied by the prestigious Rondou butchers. A refrigerated meat display counter and a lobster tank catch the eye. Rather than prissy, complex preparations, you can expect spot-on cooking, freshly prepared sauces and regular refills of hot, crunchy French fries. The wine list (splendid selection of Bordeaux wines) is at bargain prices.

Name: Amu
Description: A stone’s throw from the main square, the Amu Food and Wine Bar sports a marriage of elegant and intimate that is both romantic and sexy. In this intriguing setting, chef Marjanne Moonen rustles up genuine delicacies. Her surprise menu, composed of fascinating dishes based on just a few ingredients, is both free of fancy frills and always spot on. Her distinctive culinary signature is a patchwork of Mediterranean influences, spices and fermentation techniques from the Middle East. Examples include her yoghurt and tahini sauce that adds a kick to a dish of sweet potatoes and carrots, suavely blending depth and balance. The affordable wine list is sourced from all over the world.

Name: Floris
Description: As pleasing to the eye as to the palate! Wood and iron prevail in the decor, while the regional cuisine displays a blend of talent and creative flair.

Name: Kokovin
Description: Warm and stylish, Kokovin boasts a superb garden patio, but above all, it is the scene of a successful family adventure. The cheerful lady of the house, Peggy, greets guests warmly, plying them with insightful wine tips along the way, while her hubbie, Dominique, and son, Francis, conjure up recipes that range from modern to classical. In addition to textbook prepared sole, you may sample generous shrimp fritters that melt in the mouth and duckling served with piping hot fries, together with a host of more unusual textures. Consider us smitten!

Name: Bouffard
Description: Bouffard has two different dining spaces to suit different moods: a snug lounge area at the front and a more vibrant room adorned with colourful artworks. Thomas Dockx is very selective when it comes to his ingredients, and he takes a less-is-more approach to preparing them. Eschewing any unnecessary frills, he allows the natural flavours to shine through with the help of robust sauces. In one of his exuberant dishes, he combines golden-brown pan-fried scallops, tender pork cheek and a creamed cheek broth. This chef understands how to create a well-rounded set menu that keeps you engaged from beginning to end!

Name: Fou du Goût
Description: Fou du Goût manages to be both chic and cosy and the conservatory is definitely the best spot in the house. Thomas Cocquyt has a penchant for giving familiar flavours an exotic twist – chicken cooked in a spicy masala sauce, or pan-fried plaice with smoked eel and a beurre blanc infused with a yuzu gel for a tangy citrus burst. But you will also find sole meunière with fresh fries and venison in Arlequin sauce. The chef is a past master in the art of balancing bold flavours with a touch of intrigue. A firm favourite in the Meetjesland region!

Name: M Bistro
Description: Mattias Maertens and Sofie Billiet have lovingly transformed what used to be a small factory into their HQ. The resulting modern, airy interior provides the perfect foil to sample the chef’s no-nonsense culinary lineup. Each ingredient is expressed vividly and flanked by side dishes that embody the chef’s inventive streak and are scattered with international notes. Only the best gets a look-in on his menu, from the market-fresh produce to the catch from local boats. Save room for the addictive desserts, such as an extravaganza of white chocolate mousse and dark chocolate ice cream, whose sweet notes are underscored by different textures of tangy bloody oranges. M-Bistro is a savvy blend of bistronomic fare and youthful talent.

Name: 't Sleutelgat
Description: The daughter Laetitia warmly welcomes guests to this family business, whose terrace overlooks the lush green countryside of the village of Lieferinge. Dad, mijnheer Van Holder, demonstrates his technical precision and eye for detail in dishes served in several plates. From a new spin on traditional flammkuchen to veal jazzed up with a punchy medley of international accents, the food is surprisingly complex and fascinating. Don’t forget to book!

Name: Convento Wijnbistro
Description: Pick out a bottle from the wine shop, take a seat in the pleasant bistro-lounge and get ready to soak up the communicative enthusiasm of Convento. The sommeliers get a real kick out of explaining the wines, hence the low corkage fee. The straightforward, market-fresh menu is perfectly matched to the establishment’s stripped-back concept and stars a fine selection of veggies and authentic flavours.

Name: Zarza
Description: Zarza, an authentic cosy bolthole with a pretty town garden, is the type of place that inspires loyalty. Chef Cordemans pampers his diners with flawlessly sourced ingredients. The patriotic line-up of Belgian fare is jazzed up by the occasional dash of creativity, illustrated by masterfully cooked langoustine, paired with a gutsy shellfish jus and crunchy courgettes. Sophisticated yet full-bodied flavours. The lunchtime menus are always a safe bet!

Name: KAN10
Description: “Original”, “captivating”, “adventurous” and “regional” sum up the ethos of this cosy urban eatery. As a result, you can expect to sample a mind-blowing range of flavours and savours. Asian flair depicts the semi-cooked salmon, underscored by excellent homemade sambal and flanked by a traditional beurre noisette… A culinary banquet! Ask the lady of the house to show you the popular menu of shared dishes and get ready to embark on an exciting voyage of international flavours in a casual vibe.

Name: 't Vijfde Seizoen
Description: Broes Tavernier hails his suppliers as “heroes”, which speaks volumes for his commitment to locally sourced produce. From asparagus and fish from the North Sea to partridges, he unfailingly selects the best. His creative, high-flying approach to cooking aims to let the ingredients shout their name. We recommend the insightful wine-food pairing suggestions. After a fine meal in this friendly establishment (great patio), pop into Eetalage and take a few goodies home.

Name: Jacqueline
Description: This former butchery is named after the grandmother of Evelien Swiers, who is in charge of the kitchen you can see behind the original counter. Good humoured Raf supervises the dining room, which sports a gentrified workshop vibe. Evelien’s delicious, no-frills cuisine revolves around a menu of four or five dishes. Guinea fowl from Maison Garat is cooked in a frying pan and underscored by a knockout jus enriched in miso, while chicory adds a fresh note with a mandarin sabayon. At Jacqueline, the food is rustic, gutsy and wholesome.

Name: Dôme Sur Mer
Description: You are well and truly in the Art nouveau district of Zurenborg, even if this fish bistro would be quite at home in a seaside resort. The produce is outstandingly fresh, embodied by seafood platters overflowing in briny odours, delicately flavoured langoustines, cooked to perfection on a teppanyaki or sautéed fillets of seabass garnished with a gutsy olive oil sauce… In their open-plan kitchen, the chefs demonstrate that such delicacies have no need of prissy details, courtesy of spot-on cooking and ultra fresh side dishes.

Name: Le Mucha
Address: avenue Jules Du Jardin 23, Woluwe-Saint-Pierre, 1150, Belgium
Description: The interior and character of Le Mucha are reminiscent of Parisian brasseries in the 1900s, providing the perfect foil to sample traditional French fare. A host of subtle details such as last-minute fresh fries or an unusual béarnaise sauce with steak bears witness to the ethos of this restaurant whose DNA is firmly characterised by lashings of generosity. A must should you get a hankering for nostalgic nosh, such as veal’s brains or an île flottante (meringue floating on velvety egg custard) – even better if you go on one of the jazz nights…

Name: Cocotte
Description: Jan Mangelschots has clearly pondered and puzzled over every detail of the delightful Cocotte from the Art deco stained-glass, natural light and soothing colour scheme to its swish, uncluttered vibe and art-directed plating. Consummate yet subtle execution and intense sauces depict both the classical à la carte and the set menus. The chef has a flair for adding a sophisticated spin to a terrine of asparagus and squid served with a chilled asparagus soup and cream of smoked eel. Everything, from the food to the service, is bang-on confident and brimming in personality.

Name: Vlass
Description: The Lauwereins family bends over backwards to pamper you in its swish, yet cosy restaurant. Creative chefs Stefaan and Elien deploy state-of-the-art techniques to devise dishes in which every detail is endlessly pondered and puzzled over. The result is unabashedly bold and modern. Take, for example, the crunchy vermicelli of pleurote mushrooms in an earthy truffle cream which is paired with a refreshingly punchy black garlic and spinach puree. Wine waiter Kenzo’s inspired suggestions may surprise but his expertise and insight invariably guide him to suggest the perfect wine-food pairing for each dish and each diner.

Name: Il Trionfo
Description: Il Trionfo is both an elegant restaurant and a family story. The father and daughter-in-law preside front-of-house, and their enthusiasm is infectious. He also has some fantastic wine recommendations up his sleeve. Upon entering the restaurant, you will catch a glimpse of the mother and son at work in the kitchen. You can opt for the more creative set menu or order à la carte from a selection of traditional robust Mediterranean classics like vitello tonnato and spaghetti vongole. Don't miss the osso buco – the meat is unbelievably tender, and that typically rich tomato sauce is simply divine. The quintessence of Italian generosity!

Name: De Kwizien
Description: De Kwizien has become a culinary landmark of Hasselt and this buzzy eatery is right in the zeitgeist. Your delightful hostess pampers you as you tuck into a set lunch menu or a four- or five-course menu, flanked by flavoursome sauces and rich in creative ideas. The chef cooks Atlantic cod according to textbook tradition in its skin, flanking it with a gyoza of North Sea crab and a shellfish emulsion, together with thin slices of pumpkin and a mouthwatering sauce of tonka beans. This dish is one of the house signatures and a best-seller for good reason!

Name: Rascasse
Description: Erwin Denijs is a genuine ambassador of his region, the North Sea and Oosterschelde River. This “North Sea Chef” crafts the best seasonal produce into dishes that combine a tangy freshness with a playful element. For example, beurre blanc flanks a skate wing cooked in butter and paired with mussels and a medley of leeks. Caroline, your cheerful hostess, will ply you with wine, as well as beer tips, all of which in a pared-back setting that provides the perfect foil for striking works of art, starring fish!

Name: Maison Belge
Description: A subtle sprinkling of rustic details lends this modern brasserie a pleasant, homely feel, with the bonus of an equally inviting terrace. The chefs continue to champion Belgian classics, albeit with more modern plating. For example, calf’s sweetbread is reworked with playful textures, without losing sight of the recipe’s soul-warming and hunger-obliterating core, while tartare of lemon-spiked gambero rosso is flanked by red beetroot, unveiling a Mediterranean sensitivity. A pleasing attention to detail combined with reassuring, almost regressive flavours.

Name: Roots
Description: A hip bistronomic venue in the heart of the trendy Patershol district. The establishment’s popularity has nothing to do with luck and everything to do with Kim Devisschere’s uninhibited, no-holds barred cooking, doubled with a commitment to organic, locally sourced ingredients. Examples include North Sea fish, such as gravlax of seabass served with a foaming vichyssoise mousse, green peas in horseradish for added whoomph, oil of wild garlic and finely diced potatoes. The set menu whereby you can choose the number of courses is a hit every time. Splendid wine list (excellent natural wines) and pleasant alfresco area in fine weather.

Name: BÚN
Description: Leave the madding crowd far behind and relax in the hip casual vibe of this trendy Vietnamese eatery. You can expect to sample a fine dining version of characteristic Vietnamese sweet and sour, fermented and spicy flavours. The chef favours local organic produce, an ethos that is reflected in the attractive wine list, rich in natural vintages. The Little Bún noodle shop rustles up gutsy, full-bodied Vietnamese street food.

Name: Het Nieuwe Palinghuis
Description: There is an authentic feel to the dining area of this charming seafood restaurant. Adorned with various nostalgic photos of maritime scenes, it harks back to its opening year: 1983! Over the years, Het Nieuwe Palinghuis has earned a reputation for its classic fish dishes. The menu features langoustine with an intense nantua sauce, sole Véronique in a full-bodied white wine sauce, as well as a distinctively herby eel in green sauce. The dishes here have always been big on flavour, steering clear of any unnecessary frills. A firm favourite!

Name: Villared
Description: Pink flamingos adorn the wallpaper, green marble abounds and gold and ochre depict the colour scheme. Elegant and fashionable, Villared provides the perfect foil to chef Debal’s eclectic score. Melanzane alla parmigiana, sole meunière, Asian-inspired salmon… The enticing menu by a seasoned craftsman has something for everyone.

Name: Deboeveries
Description: This characterful and tastefully renovated farmstead on the edge of well-heeled Sint-Martens-Latem is well known to local foodies, who appreciate the garden terrace and who love the enticing menu and house specials, like the Monday theme menu and the Friday North Sea sole day. The score is a model of rich, traditional flavours. Melt-in-the-mouth game terrine in season, succulent sole meunière with piping hot fresh fries and crispy salad. Everything is spot on in the exuberant culinary lineup, as is the wine list (primarily of French provenance).

Name: The Thrill
Description: Hunting trophies on the walls, sheepskins on the chairs and a huge fireplace-grill in the centre: the rustic stage is set for the friendly, buzzy Thrill in Genk. The extensive menu will make your tastebuds drool, all the more so as you can be safe in the knowledge that Rik Vandersanden is a high-flying craftsman. His ravioli of woodpigeon or his chuck Black Angus, masterfully grilled to rare on the BBQ, demonstrate his talent and generosity. Heaven for lovers of authentic, down to earth flavours.

Name: Les Eleveurs
Description: Les Eleveurs hotel restaurant, a landmark of Halle since 1897, has been run by the De Brouwer family since its foundation. Today, Annelies and Julian are breathing new life into their family heritage. Master Jochen Heyvaerts can be relied upon to ply you with excellent wine tips in addition to seamless service, while chef Borsy orchestrates the highly popular traditional culinary score, adding his own personal melody as he celebrates Pajottenland specialties. The extensive menu ranges from family favourites such as quenelles of pike and melt-in-the-mouth Iberico loin of pork with gherkins and crispy crackling to a bona fide tournedos Rossini. Go there your eyes closed!

Name: Le Mystique
Description: If you’re looking for a romantic getaway venue in the picture postcard perfect city of Bruges, book a table in the restaurant of the Relais & Chateaux Heritage Hotel, whose opulent interior oozes authentic historic details. It is truly the epitome of stylish elegance! The chef avows a preference for French and Mediterranean ingredients, which he delicately crafts into spot-on dishes. Examples include a marinated fillet of mullet paired with sweet-sour fennel, labneh and radish pickles. Each dish is a master class of subtlety and originality. A date night kinda place with which you will immediately fall head over heels.

Name: Lijsterbes
Description: Chef Van Der Bruggen combines creativity with classical training, as his spit-roast veal sweetbread or his seabass in a salt crust demonstrate. High precision cooking that allows the top-notch ingredients to shout their name. The set and lunch menus remain a hit with his faithful regulars, who make a beeline for the lovely terrace. A solid bet every time!

Name: De Vijf Seizoenen
Description: Veg fresh from the field, herbs foraged in the Flemish Ardennes and sustainable seafood… Quality is the bedrock of this stylish establishment that sports elegant Art deco light fixtures. The family-run restaurant (brother, sister and dad in the kitchen, mum and daughter-in-law in the front of house) champions authentic fare and respect for the environment. The creative associations of ingredients and care lavished on the vegetables are truly impressive. For example, their unusual new spin on Flemish asparagus surprises with an incredible concoction of eggs and exciting fermented flavours. A sensational tribute to the seasons!

Name: Les Caprices d'Harmony
Description: If only there were more little neighbourhood hangouts like this one! The owner chef has voluntarily eschewed modes and trends and his traditional menu is music to our ears (and tastebuds): hanger steak with shallots or dame blanche dessert (vanilla ice cream and hot chocolate). Simple, home cooking, prepared to order – at prices that make sense.

Name: Le Passage
Address: avenue Jean et Pierre Carsoel 17, Uccle, 1180, Belgium
Description: This classical establishment in the Saint Job neighbourhood is a favourite with the locals. Kevin warmly greets diners, while his dad, Rocky Renaud, deftly crafts a traditional score, albeit dotted with the odd punchy international twang. A champion of top-notch produce, he never compromises on quality. An example: crispy calf’s sweetbread is paired with a gravy laced in vin jaune and served with potato fritters and morels in a dish that embodies this establishment’s generous nature. Just the ticket for a slap-up meal at lunchtime!

Name: Bachtekerke
Description: Bachtekerke is undeniably smart, but its pride and joy is a blissful summer terrace on the banks of the Leie, whose secluded, idyllic setting makes you feel as if you are on an island! Even better, the chef has no equal for wholehearted cuisine, oozing in flavour and variety. From dim sum to share, crunchy, piping hot shrimp fritters and melt-in-the-mouth steak tartare to a bona fide patriotic Belgian dish – vol-au-vent, it finds favour with everyone, from gourmet gluttons to discerning foodies…

Name: Pazzo
Description: This casual, yet stylish eatery, which sports a terrace opposite, has been a prominent feature of the Antwerp F&B scene for donkey’s years. Seasoned chef Tim Meuleneire crafts, on one side, a lineup of house specials with an Italian slant, and on the other, signature dishes that bear a distinctly Gallic touch. He pays tribute to the ingredient in recipes like pheasant, cooked rare and served with an Albufeira sauce, peppery au gratin potatoes and endive stuffed with a stew of pheasant legs. Vibrant, succulent recipes underscored by a first-rate wine list, without forgetting a jazzy wine bar packed in character upstairs.

Name: Loxalis
Address: 150 Rue de la Libération, Dudelange, 3511, Luxembourg
Description: Immense floor-to-ceiling windows command a splendid view of the surrounding countryside, with the bonus of a peaceful terrace (weather permitting): the scene of Loxalis is set. Diners are greeted by a genuine maitre d’, who carefully takes the time to explain the appetising menu. Chef Boccolini subtly adds a modern spin to characteristic Mediterranean recipes, such as his new take on vitello tonnato flanked by a characterful sauce. Familiar flavours abound but with intriguing new dimensions. The lunchtime menu is a best-seller!

Name: Kwizien
Description: The ingredient plays the star role in this welcoming farmstead. Thomas Coppejans scours the region for produce such as Malines chicken and asparagus, which are often on the menu. He also crafts a ceviche of seabass that will doubtless find favour with younger foodies. Ellen and her team will ply you with insightful tips to help you make your choice between the à la carte, dishes to share and the set menus. Sit back and soak up the infectiously bubbly vibe.

Name: Bar Raket
Description: Convivial and buzzing Bar Raket provides a chic industrial-style setting in which to share a variety of delectable dishes. Flavours from all over the globe are represented here in cuisine that is all about enjoying the simple things: from Catalan bread to the umami of tonkatsu with North Sea crab to super-fresh clams with fried diced guanciale and a delectable hot sauce. The bread is simply divine! With a selection of smaller dishes and three main courses, the menu shows that good food can also be a delightfully laid-back affair.

Name: De Garage
Description: You will probably have guessed from the name and the industrial look that this space to be a garage. Now reimagined as a bistro, the blend of untreated materials and vintage design elements creates a unique atmosphere. The menu puts the emphasis squarely on authentic and familiar flavours, eschewing any unnecessary frills. Think braised pork cheek in a robust sauce, sole meunière with pommes frites or even vegan green curry. Sommelier Fitzgerald Rigole's recommendations are always spot on – and his enthusiasm is infectious!

Name: Elders
Description: Urban and exciting, Elders is just the ticket if you fancy sampling modern cuisine in which veggies play the star roles. Tom Pauwelyn reverently respects the seasons, inventing inspired recipes. For example, he exalts cauliflower by preparing it in several ways, including one with an exquisitely subtle Nantua (creamy crayfish) sauce or he celebrates pears with a sabayon of stout beer. Each meal is a treasure trove of discoveries.

Name: Pluriel
Address: Rue de la Colline 58, Transinne, 6890, Belgium
Description: A slightly smoky aroma tickles your nostrils as soon as you reach the carpark of this former farmstead, which tastefully sports untreated materials to create a warm vibe. Loélia Gachadoat and Vadim Poncelet, steadfast champions of barbecue cooking, demonstrate their combined talents, mingling rustic flavours with a creative festival of occasionally surprising nuances. The symbiosis between these two chefs signs the characterful cuisine.

Name: Bachten De Leie
Description: Burnished copper saucepans and a striking colour scheme set the stylish scene in this welcoming restaurant. The youthful chef, Louis Wauters, is a butcher’s son and proud of it. You will sample perfectly cooked rib of beef with a silky béarnaise sauce and French fries, but the chef is also keen to pamper fish and seafood amateurs. Flavour and generosity are the watchwords here.

Name: Bruun
Description: The cuisine of brothers Ruben and Pieter is as elegant as the decor of their restaurant, whose entirely open-plan kitchen cannot fail but catch the eye. They have a knack for melding French technique with a modern, minimalist vision. Food that is free of fussy frills and in which every detail demonstrates a focus on gutsy flavours, like the scallops arranged like flower petals with radish, green apple and a natural apple and shiso dressing. At noon, the chefs roll out a lunchtime menu, while the evening score is more ambitious.

Name: Cuisine & Nous
Description: Exclusive finishings endow this characterful edifice with elegance and the lush green garden is the ideal spot to bask in the establishment’s warm vibe. The inventive chef enjoys reworking textbook Gallic recipes, adding international influences as the inspiration takes him. Scallops are paired with different textures of endive, while a playful interpretation of vitello tonnato features several seafood versions. Deft craftsmanship and fascinating flavours are underscored by high-flying culinary expertise. Exemplary value for money!

Name: Savage
Address: Rue de la Paix 22, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: The fashionable natural interior of Savage is perfectly at home in the trendy Saint-Boniface neighbourhood. A seat on the pavement terrace is just the ticket to soak up the district’s bubbly vibe, without forgetting to pop into the house grocery-bakery. The single set menu unveils plant-based cuisine, depicted by fascinating combinations of herbs and vegetables. You can choose your own meat or fish from the refrigerated counter near the restroom. Chef Rammelsberg orchestrates a creative score, illustrated by a cream of radishes underscored by yuzu juice and a perfectly balanced combination of marinated carrot and confit kumquat. The deftly crafted, seasonal lineup is legible and enticing.

Name: Amen
Description: Two-star chef Pascal Devalkeneer (Le Chalet de la Forêt) has a knack for picking the best produce. From the contemporary dishes and intense flavours to the range of textures, his dishes are masterpieces of culinary art. Amen!

Name: Odette en Ville
Description: Odette is a well-known eatery of the trendy Châtelain neighbourhood. The stylish 1920’s townhouse aims to combine British style, Parisian sensuality and New York glamour. The highly varied menu is equally fascinating: both classical and international, with an accent on the ingredient. Crunchy nems in a spicy sauce, al dente taglioni in lemon with pink shrimps, scallops and foie gras in a duck stock: a festival for fine food lovers. And why not treat yourself to one of the swish designer-inspired guestrooms to finish your evening in the lap of luxury?

Name: Hostellerie du Grünewald
Description: Fresh, healthy food, but also deliciously generous. This very pleasant bistro with a fine terrace provides an opportunity to sample simple ingredients devoid of unnecessary frills. Save room for the scrumptious desserts. Elegant guestrooms ensure sweet dreams.

Name: Le Monde est Petit
Description: This stylish and intimate restaurant enjoys a pleasant location between Montgomery and Cinquantenaire Park. The market determines what's on the menu here. Chef Loïc Villers incorporates delicious produce into well-thought-out dishes that are as international as his diners. Think quail ballotines stuffed with a delicate farce containing pistachio, a parsnip cream, grapes and juices from the meat. This cuisine is all about pleasure and celebrates the genuine flavours of the ingredients.

Name: La Brouette
Address: boulevard Prince de Liège 61, Anderlecht, 1070, Belgium
Description: Herman Dedapper welcomes you with open arms to his neighbourhood restaurant, decorated in warm colours and adorned with his own photo work. He is an excellent sommelier and loves to share his passion for wine. The chef’s generous, French - inspired dishes are sourced from high - quality produce.

Name: L'adresse
Description: This trendy, stylish establishment is now the lair of chef Julien Malaisse who has added a wealth of nuances and high-flying precision to the culinary lineup. A single set menu guarantees maximum freshness, as the deftly crafted dishes illustrate. The chef uses honest, hearty ingredients which he aims to subtly enhance. Marinated salmon trout is quickly grilled, before he adds a zest of lemon, pairing it with kiwi sorbet, fresh fennel and a subtle aniseed-flavoured creamy sauce. Vibrant, punchy cuisine courtesy of deft, delicate craftsmanship.

Name: Brasserie Nieuwpoort
Description: This is light years from your run-of-the-mill seaside brasserie! The opulent décor will bowl you over, as will the mixologist who rustles up intriguing cocktails behind the bar. Each dish overflows with generosity and is crafted by gifted, veteran chefs who work with the best ingredients. A range of dishes to share and wholesome brasserie fare. Why not start with a fresh, spicy, acidic ceviche of seabass, before pursuing with a royal vol-au-vent served with piping hot crunchy French fries? THE landmark brasserie of Nieuwpoort!

Name: Qin
Description: Emperor Qin provided the inspiration for the team at the helm of the restaurant of Hotel Keiser, hence the dark wood furnishings, soft red fabrics and oriental details like Chinese lanterns and paintings. The Cantonese culinary lineup is the quintessence of authentic, albeit subtly updated to suit today’s palates. The varied range of home-made dim sum dishes are characteristic of this ethos. Stuffed with chopped wagyu beef and a black pepper Chinese sauce, or with ginger and taro - piping hot delicacies that embody the generous character of this aromatic cuisine.

Name: Les Caves d'Alex
Description: Alex and Hugues share a passion for first-class produce. The former has a weakness for cured meats, while the enthusiastic sommelier delights in unearthing great wines to pair with your meal. Chef Alex, a fan of textbook French cuisine, pays tribute to tradition through rich recipes and knockout sauces, such as Ostend-style sole or a subtle Nantua sauce that enhances his pike quenelles. Wine vats and paraphernalia set the scene indoors, while the romantic garden provides the perfect foil for a fine dining experience in summertime.

Name: La Scarpetta
Description: We warrant that you will fall head over heels when you set foot in this pleasant restaurant. Comfort, a warm welcome and generous portions – what’s not to like? Authentic Italian recipes, mainly from Marche, come to life in familiar dishes oozing with flavour. The chef might enhance fresh al dente calamarata pasta with salsiccia and a parmesan and truffle sauce. A banquet of Italian fare! The restaurant has rapidly become a favourite with the locals – booking highly recommended.

Name: Caudalie
Description: Caudalie, a pared-back fine dining establishment, is perfectly at home in the hip Le Carré neighbourhood of Liège. Chef Simon and Manon, in charge of the front-of-house, share a passion for outstanding ingredients and wine. His technical virtuosity and attention to detail shine through as much in the craftsmanship as in the plating. For example, he might add a characterful Thai stock, sesame oil and a combination of onion and mushroom textures to flawlessly fresh rainbow trout. We recommend the monthly changing menu that hits the spot every time, to the delight of its many regulars.

Name: POLLEN
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Surrounded by the gorgeous Meuse Valley, the Naxhelet estate boasts a golf course, a luxury hotel and this cosy restaurant. The natural beauty of the area is best appreciated from the terrace. Chef François Durand strives to maximise the use of local produce, often sourced from the sustainable projects of Terres du Val. His cuisine celebrates vegetables in all their glory. For example, he roasts pumpkin, crisps up the seeds and makes oil from the leaves. The dish is finished off perfectly with a subtly spicy Brillat-Savarin cheese sauce. At POLLEN, the flavours of the seasons come alive.

Name: Lily's
Address: Avenue Emile de Mot 1, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Lily’s, which recreates the vibe of a Saint Tropez or Los Angeles club in Brussels with elegant, premium materials, a pretty green pergola in summer and dancing at the weekends, has become a hotspot of the Belgian capital. Indulge in a glass of wine or a signature cocktail as you cast your eye over the awesome menu. Familiar Belgian favourites, such as immaculately cooked veal chop with fresh béarnaise sauce, are prepared with the same flair and talent as a ceviche of seabass or truffle taglioni. Attracts A-listers like bees to honey for an unforgettable evening!

Name: La Baita
Description: Authentic aromas and flavours of linguine alla Genovese, thickly cut wagyu picanha, grilled rare or a modern take on cannoli: this enchanting restaurant celebrates all the facets of Italian cuisine. Chef Sandro gets a kick out of mixing techniques and textures, adding his own distinctive hallmark to each dish, whilst remaining true to his homeland’s culinary roots – the chef hails from Marche.

Name: Klei
Description: Inconspicuously located on the historic Grand Place, this cosy restaurant has a somewhat mysterious feel to it. At the helm, an experienced duo showcase their talents. Sommelier Carl Couvreur bowls diners over with his astute recommendations, while chef Jonathan Devogel delivers haute cuisine in which intricate sauces and influences from around the globe bring the flavours to life. Though his creations can be elaborate, they are ultimately defined by their boldness. Think marinated weever as the main ingredient in an aromatic dish with fig and celery in various guises. The short menu never fails to intrigue!

Name: Henri
Description: This laid-back bistro perfectly embodies the hip, urban vibe of Brussels’ Rue de Flandres and we warrant you will fall in love with its casual ambience, cobbled terrace and splendid choice of wines and Brussels’ beers. The dishes are free of frills, all the better to allow the ingredients to take front stage. Mussels in a pastis-flavoured sauce, beef tartare with a Thai slant or text-book perfect sole meunière: the chef enthusiastically navigates between influences with a fondness for fresh Mediterranean fare. Fine dining with a Brussels’ signature!

Name: Lola
Address: place du Grand Sablon 33, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Lola has been a firm fixture of the well-heeled Sablon district since 1994. A neutral colour scheme adorns the modern interior, while the terrace, decked in vibrant reds, awaits you in fine weather. The extensive à la carte menu stars a cast of pedigree classics: beef carpaccio à la Harry’s Bar, fork-tender calf’s sweetbread vol-au-vent, linguine in salted butter or a subtle creation of scallops and caramelized endive with a Riesling-flavoured fluffy mousseline. Something of a darling with the foodies of Brussels – and rightly so!

Name: L'Écailler du Palais Royal
Description: L'Écailler is a Brussels institution. The turquoise tiles behind the long bar, the wonderful woodwork, the gorgeous carpets and the nostalgic charm of this building make for an irresistibly inviting setting. A champion of classic cuisine, the chef excels in preparing fish and seafood dishes, but during the hunting season, his game specialities are also not to be missed. Briny oysters, the aromatic bouillabaisse, his inimitable sole meunière… Fans of traditional fare will feel right at home.

Name: Brugmann
Description: If you fancy a slap-up meal in southwest Brussels, make a beeline for this fancy brasserie adorned with modern art and boasting a lovely alfresco space at the rear. Brugmann offers an extensive choice of pedigree Gallic dishes at lunchtime and in the evening. Traditional recipes are treated to modern, particularly Asian, interpretations, such as langoustine in a tempura of crunchy walnuts with a sweet and sour bisque sauce.

Name: La Table du Tribeca
Description: This brasserie sports a swish lounge atmosphere, whilst nurturing a good-natured gregarious vibe and the terrace overlooking the countryside is deservedly one of its highlights. The à la carte and set menus make no bones about their classical bistronomic heritage. Whether it is lobster salad or veal cutlets, you can expect deftly crafted classical recipes executed with flair. From iced coffee to chocolate soufflé tart, the desserts also benefit from the chef’s subtle talent and down-to-earth generosity (you can choose from the à la carte dessert lineup even if you opt for the set menu). The wine list is perfectly suited to the heroically wondrous repertory. What’s not to like?

Name: L'Horizon
Description: L'Horizon is definitely in tune with the zeitgeist. A fashionable interior and meticulously laid tables set the scene. The chef’s Italian roots, Asian influences and regional produce, such as poultry and herbs, are combined in dishes that cater to modern tastes. Delicate, well-prepared cuisine, fully worthy of a visit.

Name: Le Philippe
Description: Rekem, one of the oldest, most authentic villages of Belgium, is rife in nostalgia, further accentuated by the collection of Fiat 500s mustered in front of Le Philippe. This ex-post office now sports a vintage Parisian vibe, including a soundtrack of French songs and also offers a few suites above the restaurant should you wish to stay longer. Danny Vanderhoven will win you over with his distinctive spin on bistronomic classics: frog’s legs in a creamy tomato, garlic and mild red pepper sauce, or slowly simmered melt-in-the-mouth beef bourguignon served with fries cooked in beef tallow, (which is the only way they should ever be fried!). A casual mood sets the scene for consummately crafted and generously served wholesome fare.

Name: Brasserie Fiston
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fiston is a swanky brasserie depicted by a friendly, buzzy vibe. Chef Seynaeve rustles up text-book classics according to best practices. Geert Van Hecke’s pupil sources the best ingredients that he incorporates into home-made recipes. His shrimp fritters, turbot with a signature mousseline sauce and dame blanche dessert hit the spot every time. The suggestions reveal a more modern facet of the chef’s culinary score. Knock-out wine list!

Name: Vinke
Description: The understated modernity of Vinke, which verges on the mysterious, is enhanced by a huge brass counter. Each dish showcases chef Gilles Demeere’s talents, demonstrating a modern culinary repertory of undiluted purity. Classics like sole meunière rub shoulders with more creative inventions, such as pink Steenvoorde pigeon served with a jus of the bones and a mousse made out of the liver and heart for extra depth and flavour. The chef’s generosity is further underscored by velvety mashed potato and thyme-flavoured green peas.

Name: Amélys
Description: This bright, airy brasserie, which is a hit with everyone, serves tasty, scrumptious food all day long, and yummy brunches on Sundays. The varied menu features classical fare, of the likes of steak tartare, vol-au-vent and chicken cordon bleu, and more modern dishes, always with the chef’s international signature. Examples range from a tempura of anchovy to seabass in a herby crust and a delicious medley of veggies with citrus fruits and herbs.

Name: Clairefontaine
Description: Clairefontaine is the epitome of unostentatious luxury. This warm, stylish establishment, whose artistic dimension lends it a distinctive glamorous edge, is located bang in the heart of the city of Luxemburg, behind a majestic façade. Arnaud Magnier, a champion of fine goods from Bresse poultry to scallops from Dieppe, is a past-master when it comes to polished Gallic fare. An example: medium rare rack of lamb in a crispy parsley crust, paired with a velvety fritter of neck of lamb, a big-boned gravy and side dishes of the calibre of roasted artichoke and polenta gnocchi, all of which bear witness to the chef’s virtuoso skills as he orchestrates a symphony of flavours and textures. While remaining loyal to his classical training, he doesn’t shy away from bold inventive side dishes in a bid to stimulate, seduce and satiate our tastebuds.

Name: Riva
Description: Bathed in natural light, this striking minimalist edifice boasts both a holiday vibe and a luxurious designer edge. All of which is further enhanced by the drop-dead view over the Meuse from the idyllically placed terrace. Live lobster, which can be seen in tanks as you enter, is prepared different ways ranging from a familiar pasta dish to a Thai-inspired recipe. Brasserie classics such as filet américain with fries and vol-au-vent are reworked to suit a contemporary palate without losing their original DNA. Riva upholds the best of brasserie traditions and all its trappings!

Name: Brasserie du Quai
Description: The Meuse River is the star of this contemporary establishment, as the splendid view reveals. Take a seat on the terrace or near the floor-to-ceiling windows and treat yourself to traditional brasserie fare crafted by a veteran team. We suggest crunchy shrimp fritters to start, followed by a textbook perfect vol-au-vent, unless you wouldn’t prefer a piece of white cod in a whipped mousseline sauce? Next are the desserts which are equally classical and decadent. The extensive à la carte bill of fare of the Brasserie du Quai is nothing short of irresistible!

Name: Le Mont-à-Gourmet
Description: Nicolas Tournay welcomes diners into his inviting neighbourhood eatery, which sports a warm, homespun feel. The chef crafts a score that is both creative and distinctive with produce from local farmers, as he draws his inspiration from both local traditions and Southern Asian cuisines. For example, he may mix glazed scallops with Chinese artichoke and salsifies cooked al dente in butter, a miso-flavoured beurre blanc and a coulis of spinach. Spontaneous, unencumbered cuisine, oozing in flavour.

Name: La Cravache
Description: The culinary classics have no secrets for Koen Devos, whose team can be relied on to add the odd contemporary touch to pedigree dishes. You can expect a repertory of premium produce such as lobster and partridge and recipes that show a reverence for authentic flavours, albeit with modern side dishes. Chef Devos is a horse lover, as you will quickly discover when you admire the elegant interior of this lavish villa. The B&B offers a view of the horses grazing from the windows.

Name: Komaf
Description: This farm has lost none of its 17C character following a top-to-toe refurbishment with a focus on naturality. Julie Van Gool and Anthony Stoop have masterminded an exquisite venue, courtesy of materials such as wood and marble, curtains that offer cosy intimacy and the Antwerp countryside that sprawls as far as the eye can see. Chef Stoop acquired a love of last-minute recipes and raunchy sauces; he also has a knack for exotic aromas and flavours. For example, he sources his pork neck from a local butcher, which he then enhances with spicy peanut flavours. The chef sprinkles his recipes in carefully judged spices like vadouvan and sweet pumpkin and works with vibrant ingredients, thus adding a fresh kick to familiar flavours. His cooking is crisp, legible and surprising thanks to unexpected combinations of ingredients.

Name: Le Métro
Description: Le Métro in the heart of Bracquegnies displays discreet references to the saxophone, which is Giuseppe’s favourite musical instrument. In the company of chef Rita, the couple invite you to sample authentic recipes and produce from Italy and Sicily in particular. Rita stuffs al dente tortelli with fresh, slightly salty ricotta, which is then served with a heavenly buttery sauce flavoured with mint and sage, before a twist of lemon and Timut pepper add the finishing touch to this heroically satisfying dish, that fully exemplifies Rita’s hallmark of wholesome fare. Food with feeling is the name of the game at Le Métro.

Name: Aster
Description: Veg, fish and fire are the raison d’être of this trendy, urban eatery at the end of Rue Dansaert. The menu rolls out a cornucopia of creative combinations and amusing textures that frequently astound. Examples include quickly grilled Breton lobster flanked by a tangy raspberry sauce and a chawanmushi straight out of the steam oven. Organic tipples set the scene on the expertly presented wine list. Aster is well and truly in the zeitgeist thanks to wholehearted, big-boned flavours and savvy nuances.

Name: Agnes
Description: In a picturesque spot on the doorstep of Sint-Martens-Bodegem Church, Thomas Locus had this former presbytery restored without losing its period charm – and Agnes is the epitome of gracious hospitality. Every detail reveals a respect for the art of fine dining and a passion for outstanding produce from rockfish to hare, without forgetting Burgundy wines, albeit with the odd modern twist. First-rate gutsy sauces and high-precision cooking are exemplified by a juicy slab of turbot cooked on the bone, paired with a Choron sauce, enhanced with an intoxicating blend of spices that is both powerful and mild. Varied sides like shrimp and textures of cabbage complete this generous portrait. We wager that you will fall head over heels for Agnes! Book a room and stay overnight in the nearby (1.5km) B&B if you have time.

Name: Barisdam
Description: As chef Puype casts his culinary spell with top-drawer produce such as asparagus or loin of veal, you know you’re in for a magical bistronomic treat. Examples include a ceviche of rockfish with creamy goat’s cheese to offset the acidity and a crunchy medley of finely diced celery and carrots. Recognisable food crafted with flair thanks to gutsy sauces and intelligently balanced generous flavours. A word of advice: Pieter and Virginie’s friendly eatery is ideal for family get togethers.

Name: Lizanna
Description: Their respective grandmothers, Liza and Anna, bequeathed a love of cooking to chef Levy and your hostess, Stéphanie. The couple shares this passion with guests in their elegant restaurant flanked by a lovely terrace. The chef rolls out his consummate know-how in a classical register.
