He might pair pheasant roasted whole with crispy, fluffy dauphine potato puffs, a creamy fricassée of thighs, cèpes and an exquisite cognac-laced sauce. The pinnacle of French fine dining with a personal twist.

Name: L'aperovino
Description: “Wine, dine and unwind” is the motto of this stylish upmarket bistro. Upstairs is the wine bar where sommelière Julie unveils a knockout selection of prestigious tipples and a fine choice of cocktails. Downstairs, you will sample dishes poised between tradition and exotic innovation, ranging from a winter venison stew to Sebastes fish served with a refreshing tom kha kai. “Where wining meets dining” is their other baseline…

Name: Zicht
Description: Bull’s eye: you can enjoy the knockout view over the Flemish Ardennes as much as you like thanks to Zicht’s immense picture windows. The experience is even better on the terrace. Get ready to be pampered by a veteran couple: Hélène graciously supervises the dining room, while Kwinten crafts a subtle Franco-Belgian score that unveils his talent and craftsmanship. An example: ballotine of pheasant, salsifies and endives, flanked by an amazing sauce made out of the bones and enhanced with cognac and cranberries. There is also a vegetarian version of his seasonal set menu with several courses.

Name: Yirmi
Description: A meal in this stylish villa starts with the solicitous and heartfelt welcome of charismatic Adrien, who will later be your host in the bespoke glazed wine cellar where you are invited to select a bottle yourself. Jeremy Vandernoot has harnessed his creativity to devising menus whose craftsmanship, bordering on complexity at times, invariably unveils a subtle harmony of flavours and textures. For example, on one hand, he prepares a sorbet of confit tomatoes out of which he makes a house-made ketchup that is flanked by a gazpacho, while on the other, he stuffs a cherry tomato with slivers of lemon marigolds, coating them in delicately perfumed tomato water. The team’s enthusiasm and expertise can be tasted in each bite.

Name: L'Épisode
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Grandiose is a truly apt description of the Waillimont Estate, whose lakeside lodges paint an idyllic picture for a country getaway. The restaurant is housed in the splendid stone villa-cum-ranch boasts classy living rooms, a wood-burning fire and works of art. Chef Jordan Boreux, a craftsman of flavours, lavishly shines the spotlight on regional produce in his surprise menu. You may start with wafer-thin slices of smoked ham from the Rochehaut estate’s farm, before sampling a carpaccio of beef with a subtle peanut cream, parmesan, fried curly kale and a sprinkling of edible flowers. The chef’s approach involves treating time-honoured family favourites to savvy creative twists. Don’t miss the bargain-priced lunchtime menu.

Name: CRKL
Description: CRKL may look like an upmarket concrete villa from the outside, but once indoors, you will find yourself in a romantic setting done up in soft pastel shades. Take a seat on the patio and sip an aperitif, as you get ready to sample the chef’s handiwork in which pedigree Belgian produce rubs shoulders with Asian and Mediterranean influences. Examples: Piedmont veal with goat’s cheese and lavender oil or fabulously fresh haddock paired with a creamy sauce based on fish stock and perfumed with miso. You can expect truly fragrant dishes packed in character. Finally, the establishment demonstrates a distinct preference for Belgian wines and olive oil, further squaring the circle in this distinctive venue.

Name: Au Moriane
Description: This 1693 edifice adds a contemporary touch to the historic character of En Neuvice lane by way of bare stone walls and modern comfort. The exquisitely presented food is the handiwork of gifted chef Sébastien, who demonstrates his international eclecticism, delving freely into the establishment’s cottage garden for his fruit and veggies. The accent is on tradition first and foremost. For example, pork belly takes centre stage in iconic onion soup or an Asian-inspired recipe. The set menu changes frequently and is fully in tune with his fine dining vision.

Name: BASK
Description: BASK is depicted by a mix of untreated vintage details and a buzzy, rock’n roll vibe. The refrigerated counter is piled high with seafood treats, which are then cooked over a wood-fired asador grill. The chefs have perfected the art of BBQ and craft a lineup of dishes to share of Basque inspiration, loaded with creative touches. Nibble on a few pintxos with your aperitif, before sampling delicacies like grilled turbot or juicy tender breasts of aged guinea fowl flanked by a rich gravy made from the neck. A festival of fascinating and felicitous flavours and delicate sauces. Should you have forgotten to book, there is generally space at the bar around the kitchen for a snack (or two)…

Name: CucinaMarangon
Description: If you miss the warmth of Italy, make a beeline for this stylish Venetian eatery (with a splendid wine cellar) and take a seat on the charming patio. The bread, pasta and desserts are all the handiwork of the mistress of the house, who fusses over diners like a real Italian mamma! The chef’s northern Italy delicacies range from vitello alla Milanese to pheasant risotto and sign a declaration of love to all foodies!

Name: Brasserie Taste
Description: Taste is worthy of its name alone for its spacious, stylish interior, whose picture windows invite nature indoors. This characterful brasserie oozes classy luxury from every pore. Chef Van Hoecke unveils a passion for traditional cuisine and top-notch produce. The score is familiar yet scattered with unexpected international influences as it seamlessly slaloms between crispy shrimp fritters, royal vol-au-vent, fresh tangy ceviche and grilled duck packed in Asian notes. The plating is emblematic of this attention to detail and sense of refinement. There is something for everyone at Taste!

Name: Auberge de Herborist
Description: Nothing is missing from the picturesque 11C country inn, not even the romantic open fireplace. Admire chef Hanbuckers’ flower-decked cottage garden from the patio and the orangerie. Exquisitely presented dishes that showcase the full diversity of vegetables, combined with first-class ingredients. Suave, sensitive cuisine.

Name: Dah Makan
Description: Cod marinated in miso and grilled on a robata, served with crunchy veg and lashings of frothy beurre blanc spiked with yuzu… Dishes to share such as these explain the success of this snug eatery. The culinary score, depicted by Asian flavours and western influences, demonstrates a clear preference for superior produce such as wagyu beef or crab from the North Sea, which are often finished on a robata grill or teppanyaki griddle. The menu is almost impossibly varied!

Name: Pur Boeuf
Description: The remarkable maturing room and attractive open wine cellar set the scene for chef Hanselaer’s two overriding passions. Son of a cattle breeder, Blanc Bleu Belge beef takes pride of place on the menu, which also showcases the strength and flavour of other fine ingredients. The resourceful chef is never short of creativity, demonstrated by his modern take on Belgian endive baked in ham and cheese and while his carne cuisine occasionally reaches the realm of high-flying, it is never OTT. The cheese and dessert trolley in particular is spectacular! A must if you plan on touring the Lake Donk area.

Name: Yijiangnan
Description: The patterned wallpaper and understated class of this posh establishment are obvious right from the first minute, but it is the alfresco patio that will win your heart. Every detail counts from the first hello to the last farewell. Yijiangnan specialises in straightforward, generous Chinese cuisine. Rather than a never-ending menu, you will find family favourites such as Peking duck, together with a few more modern creations. All the better when you know that the prices won’t break the bank.

Name: Lafarques
Description: This heritage country mansion, gleaming with classy elegance, will take your breath away. Both the surrounding countryside and the stylish guestrooms are exquisite. The cordon bleu chef allows the (preferably local) ingredients to shout their name, whilst seeking to generously and delicately enhance their traditional flavours. Don’t miss the game in season.

Name: Les Abris
Description: Ring the bell and enter this friendly eatery, taking a seat in the lovely sitting room for a drink as you admire the lush green garden. Chef Kristof Timmermans and sommelier Tijs Coessens have pooled their joint talents to create a customised experience. After the host’s insightful explanations, we immediately noticed that everything is cooked to order. The chef’s skill can be tasted in the spot-on cooking and fascinating side dishes, for example, as oxalis and a sweet-sour cream of chickpeas add whoomph to langoustine. Les Abris offers gourmet shelter to foodies in search of sustenance!

Name: Brasserie Côté Cour
Description: This nostalgic brasserie enjoys an idyllic location in the courtyard of Bourglinster Castle. The terrace on the rampart affords stunning views! The food is mostly plant based, but there is also a separate menu including fish and meat. The cauliflower "risotto" combined with marinated tomatoes and crushed hazelnuts is a shining example of this cuisine, which is inspired by the local nature and is all about bold flavours.

Name: Aal Schoul
Description: The school bench at the entrance and the blackboard pay tribute to Aal Schoul’s former vocation as a village school; it is now a warm eatery adorned in huge works of art. Red meat is omnipresent on the menu, but the chef’s bold, unconventional recipes are what most intrigue. For example, his recipe for poultry breasts rolls out a whole series of cooking techniques, while his highly individual take on a Caesar Salad features a sweet-sour vinaigrette with pili that adds a distinctive kick to the entire dish. An intriguing meal awaits you at Aal Schoul!

Name: De Victorie
Description: This imposing historic farmstead, opposite the vineyards of Chateau Vandeurzen winery, is depicted by a stylish interior, whose centre piece is a sculpted flock of birds in flight that is most eye catching. The estate’s excellent wines are paired with a Gallic lineup of contemporary leaning. The chef enjoys pairing sweetbread with truffles or pheasant with Fine champagne cognac, adding a personal twist along the way by playing with the tangy freshness of ingredients such as kalamansi, yuzu and wine vinegar. It has proved a hit with fans of familiar flavours who appreciate an added twist.

Name: Le Jardin des Senteurs
Description: This Scented Garden offers the opportunity to treat yourself to a delightful stay in the Ardennes. Emmanuelle, your hostess, is the third generation at the head of this family venture. The seasoned kitchen team rolls out a sensibly priced menu together with a series of “all inclusive” menus. Delicately crafted, intriguing recipes include the house version of vitello tonnato or juicy Malines chicken in a scrumptious spicy sauce. We highly recommend booking a room to make the most of this authentic venue on the doorstep of Ardennes’ unspoiled countryside.

Name: Pip-Margraff
Description: This family - run hotel restaurant has been open for business since 1876. The customers come for its essentially classical menu. The chef keeps pace with the seasons and game is one of the house specialties. The rooms are flawlessly kept, as is the well - being centre.

Name: la petite Madeleine
Address: rue de la Madeleine 19, Tournai, 7500, Belgium
Description: Behind the authentic historic façade lies a contemporary interior, adorned with arty photos and boasting a fine terrace to the rear. Chef Dufranne enjoys surprising diners with his original recipes and generous helpings. Each dish is a treasure trove of meticulously prepared ingredients and fascinating combinations.

Name: Le Petit Axhe
Description: A journey through the lovely Liège countryside, the owner’s delightful welcome and chef Claes’ scrumptious dishes: get ready to treat yourself from start to finish, safe in the knowledge you are in the hands of an experienced and accomplished chef. You may taste a flawlessly fresh fillet of whiting flanked by an elegant beurre blanc. No compromise on quality is ever tolerated, all the better because the prices make sense.

Name: Maxens
Address: chaussée du Roi Baudouin 117, Saint-Symphorien, 7030, Belgium
Description: Stéphane Grulois, a man of many talents, played a major part in designing the stylish, cosy interior of this arty restaurant. Stéphane is, however, first and foremost a gifted chef. His love of traditional French cuisine shines through in flawless craftsmanship and know-how. He might cook veal medium rare in a parsley and mustard crust, which is paired with a subtle, delicate gravy, fluffy dauphine potato puffs and celery purée. The chef enjoys serving the food himself. Excellent value for money at lunchtime. A multisensory experience awaits!

Name: Le 13
Description: Fashionably revamped manor house: Panton chairs, designer lighting, fashionable colours and a large wall board that forms the menu. Contemporary cuisine and terrace facing the station.

Name: Chez Louis
Description: Chez Louis is a friendly eatery with something for everyone. The menu features Belgian family favourites such as sole meunière and veal kidneys in mustard, as well as chef Lekeu’s more sophisticated culinary score, all of which is depicted by classical generosity. From November to February, a seafood bar is available at weekends. The extensive range of choice is undeniably one of the trump cards of this establishment, as are mussels, in season.

Name: L'artiste
Address: rue de la Gare 85, Falaën, 5522, Belgium
Description: In the heart of the Ardennes forest, make a beeline for this old railway station decorated in modern style. Chef Depuydt’s creative and contrasted menu combines originality with subtlety and the dishes overflow with details that pay tribute to local produce and Asian influences. Culinary art at its best!

Name: Roosenberg
Description: Waasmunster’s discerning foodies make up the faithful clientele of this smart eatery. They come for the elegant interior, friendly vibe and top-quality produce, without forgetting the lure of the wine cellar, well stocked in Burgundy and Tuscan tipples. The à la carte lineup embodies the establishment’s devotion to quality. Chef-owner Bruno De Wilde errs towards flame-licked techniques and seasonal ingredients, together with signature dishes like vol-au-vent, tartare steak, asparagus à la flamande or local game in season. What’s not to like?

Name: Restaurant Rollier
Description: Tucked away in a bend of the River Scheldt, this spacious venue overlooks a typically Flemish landscape of (often) cloudy skies, grassy meadows and water. Maurane is in charge of the attentive service, while Nicolas demonstrates his mastery of classical cuisine (à la carte) and contemporary fare (set menu). Examples include a juicy breast of black chicken, intelligently paired with a knockout poultry jus. International accents also crop up in the menus, demonstrated by a slow-cooked cutlet paired with spicy kimchi.

Name: Ma Passion
Description: Chef Kris and elegant Sandra share a passion for fine food and fine wine! This handsome townhouse with a lovely patio tastefully blends old and new with an inimitable Belgian knack for colours and materials. The chef voluntarily tries his hand at different styles, mixing the classical flavours of foie gras and sweetbread with subtle sauces and fresh, acidic side dishes, demonstrating his playful side and virtuoso talent.

Name: De Kruier
Description: This picture postcard restaurant stands in the shade of an 1897 windmill in a manicured garden. You can count on the Callant brothers to rustle up a delicious line-up of authentic Belgian dishes, calling on flawlessly fresh, deftly cooked ingredients. The extensive à la carte menu traverses the annals of traditional cuisine to the delight of good food lovers. In summertime, the alfresco terrace is the place to be.

Name: Brasserie Latem
Description: There is more to this stylish brasserie on the busy Kortrijksesteenweg than you might expect. Chef Van den Bossche's love of Asia is evident throughout the restaurant, from the decor of the izakaya to the lounge-like terrace and the cigar lounge. Although you will find sashimi options and a bento box on the menu, it is dominated by classic fare. Think sumptuous vol-au-vent, onglet à l'échalote and pan-fried ray wing – prepared the way it should be: generously and using the finest ingredients. The extensive wine list is definitely worth exploring!

Name: L'homard Bizarre
Description: L'Homard Bizarre translates as "the bizarre lobster", but there is nothing at all outlandish about this elegant, cosily decorated villa. The chef does, however, have a predilection for lobster! As he is a champion of classic cuisine, his menu features timeless dishes such as fried foie gras with diced apple, or ultra-fresh lobster Bellevue with house-made sauces and a crisp salad. As ever, seafood lovers and meat enthusiasts are treated to a host of full flavours.

Name: Auberge Napoleon
Description: Auberge Napoleon has been a favourite with foodies for years. With high ceilings and charming old beams, the restaurant is entirely done out in white. The chandelier is a particularly impressive feature. On the terrace, you can take in the full beauty of the garden, a tranquil green escape. The extensive menu features classic cuisine – expertly done, down to the dishes finished table side. Think duck breast with an intensely flavoursome port sauce, sole meunière or hop shoots in hollandaise sauce. Many of the dishes can be shared, which ups the fun factor!

Name: 't Notenhof
Description: Everything works like clockwork in the lovely ‘t Notenhof establishment. The seasoned owner welcomes guests, sharing his insightful wine tips along the way, while the rich flavours of classical cuisine, albeit with a modern twist, have no secrets for his wife. Eels, Anjou pigeon and seabass are frequent guest stars on her deftly cooked and generously served menu. The lunchtime menu is a steal.

Name: Pegasus
Description: Pegasus is poised to take wing at the entrance to this restaurant housed in a magnificent 18C abode. While you immerse yourself in the classical interior (woodwork, old tiles), run your eye over the menu. This will reveal a wide choice of balanced dishes, all of which are made with fine produce. Lovely terrace.

Name: August Wijnbar
Description: Just off Lennik’s market square, August welcomes you into its warm, offbeat universe. In a casual, wine bar vibe, Sam Verstuyf demonstrates a preference for Pajottenland produce as he finetunes his unusual vision of fine dining. Exotic flavours, a passion for veggies and sophisticated side dishes are presented in a set menu that rolls out the chef’s creative talents without forgetting the odd surprise. A few examples: poached monkfish is treated to a Mediterranean twang courtesy of a choron sauce, crispy pancetta and velvety risotto, while his version of hare Arlequin is grandiose… You are in for a truly fascinating experience. Even better, the fascinating wine list is not only enticing and sometimes surprising, but also at drinker-friendly prices.

Name: Bassud
Description: Bassud is the story of Michèlle and Jan, set in an attractive vintage Scandinavian décor. Chef Jan serves minimalist, no-nonsense dishes, using locally sourced produce and jazzed up by subtle twists, such as fermented ingredients or smoked charcoal oven flavours.

Name: L'Angelo Rosso
Description: Welcome to the lair of the Catania family. Filippo welcomes patrons to a smart restaurant flanked by a lovely garden terrace. Chef Roberta, his partner, conjures up a feast of pedigree Italian classics with a modern spin. She has a preference for simplicity, creating intense flavours steeped in Mediterranean exuberance, illustrated by taglioni al dente served with a peppery velvet parmesan sauce, crispy pancetta, a 63° boiled egg and a lavish grating of truffle. You may be interested to know that sgroppino sorbet (vodka, prosecco and lemon) is served before the main course. As for the titbits served with coffee – they are truly squisito!

Name: De Refugie
Description: Franco-Belgian foodies are in seventh heaven in this eatery in a friendly neighbourhood. You are first greeted by your gracious hostess, before you sample the manifold talents of chef Van Vlemmeren. He prepares the food to order each time and cannot be faulted for his exquisite sauces or impeccable technique. The sole is gently sautéed in butter, the butter sauce is sprinkled with parsley and the crispy fries are piping hot. Good food worth writing home about - the epitome of bistronomic dining!

Name: Hof Ter Doest
Description: A 17C monastic farmstead and its 13C barn depicts the picturesque setting of this country restaurant, run by the Dendooven family. You will taste delicious local turf (beef and poultry in particular) and surf (oysters and lobsters from the tank) produce. Hearty, wholesome cooking such as crispy shrimp fritters or Belgian Blanc Bleu beef roasted in a wood-fired oven. Luxurious guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Greenroom
Description: Make a beeline for the terrace to make the most of the lush green countryside. If the weather is fickle, never mind, the interior is equally attractive. The Green Room doesn’t distinguish between starters and main courses, which gives you more freedom to compose your menu. A classic seafood béarnaise or Flemish-style asparagus with a modern twist – sea lavender and guanciale. The bargain-priced wine list (available to take home) adds the final flourish.

Name: Table Vaccin
Description: Veteran chef Ivan Daelemans is equally at home with classical Belgian, Gallic and Italian cuisine. His impressive culinary skill can be sampled in the magnificent former home of a doctor, done up in a modern vein. The dishes are intended to be shared, but you can order individual portions. As you dig into timeless classics such as vitello tonnato, tomatoes stuffed with shrimps or a perfect poached egg, served with a light mousseline, al dente asparagus and hand-shelled shrimps, you remember why such dishes remain so popular. Even better when washed down with a fine glass of wine – the perfect vaccine for foodies!

Name: Het land aan de Overkant
Description: Leuven’s urbanites don’t hesitate to desert their city centre in favour of a seat in this smart edifice. Natural light, artwork and a lovely terrace all combine to paint a pleasing portrait. First run your eye over the beverage menu and start with a refreshing glass of Gueuze beer, before moving on to peruse the wine list. The exquisitely presented dishes reveal unexpected combinations of ingredients, such as al dente confit of celeriac with cream of goat’s cheese and foie gras, smoked eel and chilled consommé of celeriac, eels and verjuice. At lunchtime, there is only a single set menu.

Name: De Ceder
Description: Vintage black and white photos, the father-in-law’s old bicycle and a Berkel meat slicer add a quirky note to this restaurant’s fresh, stylish interior. De Ceder has been a blue-ribbon establishment in the area for some 40 years now. Genuine Franco-Belgian cuisine has no secrets for the chef, who often whips things up at the last minute, as is demonstrated by his steak with a subtle pepper sauce and fresh fries or the succulent piece of cod served with a beurre blanc. He’s also keen on full-bodied oriental spices and Asian notes. We warrant you will adore the attractive wine list and, why not, even treat yourself to a night in the B&B…

Name: Escabèche
Description: The trendy welcoming interior of Escabèche is a hit with the inhabitants of Knokke. They pop in to chat with the friendly hostess, Lisbeth, and to sample the delicacies rustled up by chef Verhasselt, a virtuoso in the art of enhancing first-class ingredients. Blessedly free of fancy frills, you can expect a wholesome lineup of pedigree Gallic nosh, flanked by subtle side dishes and occasionally jazzed up with Mediterranean or Oriental twists. The extensive appetising menu ranges from a hamachi-based festival of Asian flavours to a juicy fillet of turbot in a Dijon mustard sauce or the gamey earthiness of pheasant à la brabançonne during game season. The vast menu is heaven for foodies!

Name: Va et Vient
Description: A sweeping view of the Lys River and the Broel Towers thanks to the establishment’s huge windows and riverside terrace awaits diners. A “rough and refined” (their words) décor provides the perfect foil to Matthias Speybrouck’s creativity, which shines through in recipes that star local veggies and fish from the North Sea, jazzed up with fresh acidic, even quirky (their words again) notes, while exotic ingredients are crafted into punchy sauces. Subtle cuisine throbbing with character.

Name: VEST
Description: Take a seat in this modern, elegant restaurant by the ramparts and you may hear the moving ‘Last Post’ ceremony that takes place at the nearby Menin Gate every evening at 8pm… Local Westhoek delicacies, cooked creatively and playfully, are rich in the distinctive, crisp flavours that depict the spontaneous, market-fresh cuisine of chef Jeroen. Gracious Séverine can be relied upon for her insightful wine-food pairing tips. Book a room at the B&B, ideal to explore the fascinating heritage of Ypres.

Name: Culinair
Description: The refined interior and gracious welcome are a foretaste of the exquisite culinary experience awaiting the diner. You will be able to observe the chef at work, wielding modern culinary techniques as he updates classical dishes. The same desire to pamper guests is palpable in the modern B&B of the Culinair.

Name: Potiron
Description: Friendly Dirk and Sophie aren’t shy of demonstrating their phenomenal know-how. They smoke their own salmon, the ice cream is homemade, and they are justly proud of their 3-acre vegetable garden (visits by appointment). Vegetables and aromatic herbs add a playful twist and authentic purity to updated recipes. Distinctive French cuisine that eschews jargon and fancy frills.

Name: Brasserie Grand Cru
Description: Red and white chequered tablecloths and a rustic interior set the delightfully vintage scene in this brasserie. The huge open kitchen is equipped with both spit-roasting and barbecue facilities. Lovers of hunger-obliterating wholesome fare will be in seventh heaven as each dish hits the spot from the Flemish stoofpotje made with Belgian beer, the vol-au-vent or sole meunière to calf’s liver in madeira sauce – an authentic lineup of no-nonsense familiar brasserie cuisine. The extensive menu has something for everyone and is a genuine ode to the cooking of yesteryear. A great vintage indeed!

Name: Appelsveer
Description: As you bicycle along the banks of the Scheldt, Appelsveer cannot fail to be a welcoming sight. This listed house is flanked by a fine terrace overlooking the countryside. The chef serves regional dishes, to which he adds his own creative flair, using modern techniques. You may also be tempted by the “ice house”.

Name: Den Duyventooren
Description: The spruce, traditional façade of this ancestral castle-farmstead hides a vibrant modern interior adorned in warm colours. The peaceful terrace feels light years away from Bellem. The establishment has acquired a faithful cohort of regulars, lured back by Inge Herteleer’s enticing set and à la carte menus. Her seasonal cooking throbs with generosity and is dotted with contemporary touches to which she adds a Mediterranean twist come summertime. The shrimp fritters are stuffed to the brim, while a suave cognac sauce enhances pheasant and green peas and mint contrast with fresh prawns. Searingly good food prepared on the spot! Don’t forget to book!

Name: d'Afspanning
Description: Dark floor tiles and bare brick walls set the scene in this historic edifice of Beernem, albeit elegantly paired with modern fixtures and fittings. Diners can choose between cosy nooks or the spacious glazed extension. The varied menu appeals both to fans of classical fare and to those keen to try out world cuisine. The veteran chef is equally at home with the ubiquitous shrimp fritter as with an Asian take on steak tartare. Honest, wholesome fare.

Name: Franco Belge
Description: The trendy, cutting-edge establishment of Tomas Puype is a culinary treasure trove, enhanced by an alfresco dining space to the rear and a theatrically visible kitchen, where you can see the ingredients respectfully, generously and traditionally curated. The chef is a genuine craftsman with a keen eye for detail and a love of vegetables. Succulent breast of guinea fowl with crispy skin is served with al dente green asparagus, morel mushrooms and a subtle jus of guinea fowl and tarragon. Highly popular at lunchtime.

Name: U Eat & Sleep Antwerp
Description: U Eat & Sleep is one of the hotspots of the buzzy Eilandje district thanks to a drop-dead view over the MAS and marina and a glammed-up interior oozing vibrant sensuality. After kicking off your meal with a knockout cocktail and tapas, we recommend the extensive menu which features light, quirky dishes as well as big-boned brasserie classics and exotic delicacies. Whether you opt for chicken gyoza, a sole meunière, lobster and linguine or game in winter, you can rely on the establishment’s funky ethos: u-stronomy!

Name: La Traverse
Description: La Traverse is the quintessence of a contemporary brasserie, sporting a warm, welcoming interior and a menu that mingles Flemish classics with more up-to-date dishes, of which shrimp fritters and braised pork cheeks or dimsum and cauliflower steak are just a few examples. We recommend the matured beef, cooked to perfection in a Josper oven. On Saturday evenings, La Traverse offers a menu of varied dishes to share and a platter of cured meats to nibble on.

Name: Restaurant VOS
Description: Tucked away behind a tennis and padel club, VOS, bathed in natural light, sports a wall garden and a warm ambience. Chef Stijn and his youthful team craft a set menu that is in tune with the seasons and founded on Franco-Belgian classics. The kitchen’s hallmark is creative, playful cuisine depicted by fresh notes and grilled dishes. The grilled ribeye steak is coated with a punchy veal gravy that is just the right consistency and emblematic of the chef’s know-how. The lunchtime formula ticks all the boxes!

Name: Salto!
Description: At this hip urban bistro, ingredient quality is paramount. As far as chef Duys is concerned, that goes as much for the Brussels sprouts as for the sea bass. He is also not averse to working with traditionally overlooked produce, such as pig's head. Whether he is rustling up a vegetable dish based on winter leeks, or pan-searing pheasant to be paired with a fine champagne sauce: generosity is key. His creations are not unnecessarily complicated, but they are brimming with flavour. Diners can also look forward to an expertly curated selection of wines and beers.

Name: Octopus
Description: Claude and Sylvie bend over backwards to pamper guests in their seafood eatery near the seawall. Sylvie’s warm welcome and service are framed by distinctive artwork (of octopi), while Claude sensitively adds a new spin to a classical repertory, all of which in a playful vein. Grilled pork fritters, pedigree vol-au-vent, fish from the North Sea (his passion) or rice pudding with strawberries: it is always a pleasure to return to the Octopus.

Name: Moretti
Description: Check out the goodies lined up in La Cantina delicatessen before taking a seat on the terrace or indoors, in the cosy dining room laid out around an open-plan kitchen. Moretti knows how to put on a show of mouthwatering dishes that illustrate the manifold facets of Italian cucina. Tiana and Alexander curate a concise menu at lunchtime with a wide range of pasta dishes and a more modern lineup in the evenings. Textbook perfect vitello tonnato, homemade pasta flanked by an aromatic sauce and painstakingly crafted desserts: if you’re hankering for an authentic escapade to sunny Italy, make a beeline to Moretti.

Name: Maxime Colin
Description: Maxime Colin’s artistically appointed romantic establishment was made for a date night (or lunch), while the patio, tucked away in the garden of Jourdain castle, drips with alfresco charm come summertime. The menu quickly reveals the chef’s passion for stellar ingredients and international influences. His modern culinary style features subtlety, spot-on craftsmanship and a constant quest for innovation. For example, he may coat scallops wrapped in a cabbage leaf in a house-made XO sauce and pair them with a salad of green peas jazzed up by a zest of refreshing lemon juice.

Name: Restaurant Dirkjan Decock
Description: Dirkjan and Hilde warmly welcome guests to their stylish establishment depicted by a cosy, tranquil vibe and flanked by an exquisite patio. Chef Decock enthusiastically gets on with the job in his open-plan kitchen. He works with top-notch ingredients, creatively preparing vegetables and also adding the odd hint of exoticism to jazz up the dishes. Stripped-back, subtle and fascinating food.

Name: De Huifkar
Description: Fish and lobster are the specialties of this vintage-modern restaurant. Admire the quality and freshness of the produce in the lobster tank at the entrance. The chef is keen on classical recipes and generous flavours, depicted by timeless dishes such as monkfish with shrimp, local-style poached cod, without forgetting Belgium’s family favourite, veal kidneys in mustard sauce. Affordable gastronomy!

Name: Schatteman
Description: This imposing villa tucked away in the woods is a real gem. Modern artwork, a log burning fire and a wine cellar set the stylish scene, further enhanced by a manicured garden and terrace, ideal for a drink in fine weather. While Marieke spoils guests in the dining room, owner-chef Gregory demonstrates his inventive flair in a modern score, courtesy of cherry-picked ingredients from the region. Seasonings and fermentation techniques add a distinctive touch to his signature cuisine and he enjoys surprising and pushing culinary boundaries, but always with a deft, subtle hand. We recommend the set tasting menu which offers a choice of number of courses (three at lunchtime).

Name: ROSS
Description: Glenn Ross often waves a hi to guests from his open-plan kitchen overlooking the buzzy dining room; we recommend asking for a seat in the rear. The trendy vibe is the perfect foil for creative Gallic cuisine, paired with exotic delicacies and modern techniques, all of which in a bid to keep the flavours legible and familiar. The chef might pair a gutsy game dish with a powerful sauce and autumn veggies with a touch of acidity by adding the subtle bitterness of endive. The savvily curated wine cellar means that there is the perfect tipple for every dish of this culinary feast. At lunchtime, the repertory is limited to a choice of two main courses, but the offer is more extensive in the evenings.

Name: a food affair
Description: As soon as you set foot in this eatery of oriental inspiration, you will feel the serene vibe, further enhanced by the exquisite terrace to the rear. Chef Locquet shares his passion for Thailand and Vietnam. Traditional recipes made with first-class ingredients and dishes that shout the talent and deft touch of their chef. An Asian excursion steeped in subtlety and enthusiasm.

Name: Père et Mère
Description: This family bistro overflows in good humour, as Jelle in the kitchen and Magali in the dining room are still regularly helped out by the restaurant’s founders, Frans and Ria, further upholding their eatery’s legacy. The menu pays a genuine tribute to family cooking, to the delight of foodies everywhere. Cognac and tomato delicately underscore North Sea fish soup, while beer highlights the intensity of rabbit in prunes: the classics have no secrets for the chef, who is determined to keep the prices sensible. Hearty, wholesome, country cooking at its best depicts this mum and dad!

Name: Bruut
Description: The initial impression of romanticism conjured up by the wisteria-clad historic edifice in which Bruut is located, quickly gives way to a rough, graffiti-adorned, almost brutal interior that is emblematic of its high-profile chef. Bruno Timperman sources most of his produce within a 30km radius of the restaurant to craft a single surprise menu that elegantly showcases his unconventional creativity and technical ingenuity. A few examples include a pizza meets tartlet dish that blends characteristic Mediterranean flavours of the likes of tomato and burrata with the strong distinctive taste of venison, cooked medium rare, and a gutsy gravy. An unorthodox chef and score, backed by a fine cellar of organic and natural wines.

Name: Verschil
Description: Verschil is clearly a champion of the farm-to-table concept, as you will see when you look at the estate’s farmland that is managed by your hostess and which supplies the restaurant in a cornucopia of delicacies. The chef slaloms between classics like saddle of hare, served medium rare and paired with a powerful sauce and modern recipes of the likes of kohlrabi and smoked eel with tomatoes and a subtle tomato gazpacho. We recommend the à la carte lineup, but at lunchtime, you can’t go wrong if you decide to order the delicious soup and dish of the day.

Name: Le Cirque
Description: Come in, come in - take a seat and enjoy and the show! Do not be misled by the apparently low - key interior - the climax of the performance comes on the plate! The chef is a fervent disciple of modern culinary techniques and masterfully produces recipes whose texture, structure and colour are both stunning and delicious. A treat for your taste buds!

Name: Mardaga
Description: The oldest hotel of Limbourg gracefully marries period fixtures with modern details. This classical-contemporary patchwork extends to the elegant food, depicted by classical recipes, gutsy sauces and subtle nuances whose fresh, acidic notes add a final flourish to an intelligently crafted menu. Legible flavours which bear the hallmark of gifted chefs.

Name: Dolce Amaro
Description: As you admire the mural depicting Piazza del Campo in Sienna and the patio to the rear, you may almost forget you’re in Brussels’ Louise district. Dolce Amaro is a 100% authentic, bustling Italian trattoria. The food is equally genuine: orecchiette al dente in an aroma-packed tomato sauce and juicy chunks of pork or super-fresh seabass exquisitely paired with melt-in-the-mouth aubergine… Outstanding flavours that will knock the socks off your tastebuds. Let’s not forget the wine list, an Aladdin’s Cave of Italian tipples.

Name: Le Coq en Pâte
Description: The Bacchetta family has been regaling diners since 1972 in their stylish establishment. You will taste the best of fine Italian fare in the company of a loyal band of regulars. Chef Olivier delves into Mediterranean tradition, adding a creative spin that combines visual flair and a love of contrasts. His veal alla Milanese and his asparagus risotto are second to none. The lunchtime set menu is a firm favourite with the regulars.

Name: Toucan Brasserie
Description: The buzzy vibe of the Châtelain district sets the scene in this modern take on a traditional brasserie, embellished with a design twist. The locals flock here for its friendly, casual atmosphere and its wholesome no-nonsense nosh. Flawlessly fresh oysters, platters of seafood, melt-in-the-mouth steak, terrine or andouillette: the focus is on top-quality traditional fare served generously.

Name: Colonel Louise
Description: Red meat lovers fall head over heels with this swish brasserie on a street corner near Avenue Louise. As soon as you cross the threshold, you are struck by the array of cured meats on the counter. You must then decide whether you want Aubrac, Wagyu or Holstein beef, before you dig into impeccably cooked steak flanked by fresh sauces and fries cooked in beef tallow as tradition demands. The menu also features a host of other delicacies ranging from bone marrow to vitello tonnato and crispy sweetbread. Perfect for a single dish, lunch or a full-blown dinner – what’s not to like?

Name: Eyckerhof by Nicolas Mylle
Description: The charm of a period farmstead and a tasteful colour scheme of natural shades set the scene at Eyckerhof, which is the epitome of stylish. Your gracious hostess, Charlotte, and chef Nicolas have taken over the helm of this well-known restaurant and continue to uphold its heritage. The core remains classical, but now features a sprinkling of creative, vibrant notes. The chef may pair juicy turbot with a house-made XO sauce and an unctuous, hunger obliterating risotto. The lunchtime menu sports a splendid lineup of enticing dishes, while in the evening, diners choose how many courses they want from the menu.

Name: InVINcible
Description: Take a seat at the counter and soak up the warm atmosphere of inVINcible. You can admire chef Burssens and his team crafting traditional Gallic bistro fare. Examples include seabream in a sea salt crust for two, veal kidneys with green peas, Holstein entrecote steak, rare and flanked with a bone marrow, mustard seed and anchovy butter… Big boned, heroic flavours overflowing in character are the hallmark here. The wine list is equally first-rate, particularly thanks to a splendid choice of wines by the glass. You can even ask to taste your tipple before choosing – further proof that inVINcible is determined to bend over backwards to pamper its guests.

Name: Le Coriandre
Description: This is the type of restaurant that won’t let you down from the warm, welcoming interior appointed with fine works of art to Agnès, who confidently supervises the front of house and chef Vanderhoeven’s enticingly generous set menu. The food is deftly crafted and subtly strewn with exotic influences. How about a dish that mixes the earthy flavours of pigeon with the multiple facets of furikake spices, green asparagus and seaweed? The veteran chef knows just how to find the right balance every time. You may be interested to know that they also run cooking workshops on Saturday mornings…

Name: Le Brasero
Description: Photos of the Venice carnival adorn the walls of this modern restaurant, but the real masterpiece is in the plate. In addition to his mastery of Italian classics, the chef offers an attractive range of charcoal - grilled meat dishes. A blue - chip value since 1995!

Name: Cul'eau
Description: Kick off the evening in style with an aperitif and nibbles, before sampling Master Karim’s excellent nosh. The extensive menu of this modern brasserie reads like a classical cookery book with vol-au-vent and sole meunière, together with aged meat and the plating is exquisite. Spot-on cooking, entirely from scratch and jazzed up with occasional inspired note. Connoisseurs will drool over the wine list!

Name: Chou
Description: Chef Abdelhakim Akandar has been the darling (chou in colloquial French) of the European civil servants who work in the area and also of a loyal crowd of locals for a decade now. His gastronomic bistro is the quintessence of Mediterranean extravagance and exuberance. He may underscore a ballotine of Malines poultry with subtle side dishes and a bisque sauce or pair a ravioli of gutsy oxtail with Emmental, and don’t get us started on the exquisite rack of lamb… The extensive menu is quite simply irresistible.

Name: Brasserie de la Patinoire
Description: A grandiose Normandy-inspired edifice sets the scene for this characterful luxurious brasserie at the entrance to Bois de la Cambre, which can be admired from the spacious terrace. The chef favours nostalgic recipes, with the occasional more modern touch. A patriotic line-up of Belgian brasserie classics takes the limelight on the menu, including shrimp fritters, sole meunière and vol-au-vent. The shellfish bar, open all year round, is heaven for seafood lovers.

Name: Origine
Description: The whimsical décor of the Origine is depicted by colourful creatures and plants, setting the scene for a modern restaurant run by Xavier Lizen, who demonstrates great maturity despite his youth. The menu is renewed each month and illustrates the chef’s international and original approach, in which each flavour lives up to expectations.

Name: Le Buone Maniere
Description: Maurizio Zizza’s hard work and dedication has firmly established his stylish restaurant, which boasts a splendid terrace to the rear, on the culinary scene of Brussels. Zizza, who is assisted by Martin Denis, enjoys serving the food himself. Together they subtly rework an authentic Italian lineup, adding a new spin, illustrated by vitello tonnato that is rich in characteristic flavours while sporting playful textures or by a ‘light’ tiramisu flavoured with marsala. Family favourites with the odd kick and ubiquitous elegance are the hallmark of this fine establishment.

Name: De l'Ogenblik
Description: Mirrors, wainscoting and sand on the floor set the scene in this buzzy brasserie that hasn’t lost a scrap of its period authenticity or character since it opened over 55 years ago. In the same vein, the menu stars Franco-Belgian classics: crispy shrimp fritters, veal kidneys served rare and sole sautéed in butter with piping hot fresh fries. Rather than fancy frills, you can expect gutsy food in which everything tastes of something. Tradition is alive and kicking here!

Name: Philema
Description: A gourmet festival of summertime flavours awaits you at Manos Makrygiannakis. The chef, who hails from Crete, shines the spotlight on ingredients that are steeped in Mediterranean spices and aromas. Authentic food based on top-quality produce (on sale at the shop). A friendly vibe depicts this establishment, ideal to share a delicate spanakopita, grilled cuttlefish and melt-in-the-mouth baklava with friends. A Greek feast!

Name: Fico
Description: At Fico, Nadia Bruno pays tribute to Sicily and her mamma, Grazziella. The cosy ambience and vibrant, vintage-inspired decor make for the perfect setting in which to savour her sun-drenched cooking. The chalkboard displays a tempting array of authentic dishes. Think al dente fettuccine elevated with sea urchin, an intensely flavoursome semifreddo made with grappa, honey and saffron. Here, bold flavours meet Italian finesse, with no room for pretension. Don't forget to make a reservation!

Name: Nast
Description: Dean Masschelein has added his inimitable stamp to a former chicory factory, retaining the original rough brick walls, but cleverly dotted with modern fixtures and fittings. The chef is a genuine West Flemish lad, as his exuberant personality and passion for regional produce quickly reveal. The food is succulent, straightforward and international and he might mix presa iberico with a sweet-sour baba ghanoush and Mediterranean fregola, all of which comes together thanks to an emulsion of bacon. Creative seasonal cooking, rendered even more flavoursome when paired with gueuze beers or organic wines.

Name: Stad 10
Description: Don’t be misled by appearances, because behind the unassuming façade lies a high-flying gourmet lair. Bert Brouwers is forging his own path after learning the ropes with some of Limburg’s top chefs. The four- or six-course menu reveals a devotion to detail in terms of plating and craftsmanship. You can expect dishes such as scallops with a North Sea crab rémoulade, ponzu dressing and celeriac ice cream or mandarin-flavoured panna cotta with fruity textures, yuzu-laced whipped cream and a green tea coulis - all of which are emblematic of the chef’s ambition and subtlety. The sweet-toothed finale illustrates the chef’s playful side and elegantly concludes your meal. Enthusiasm and know-how are the standouts of this first-class eatery.

Name: Ivresse
Description: Ivresse is a warm trendy establishment that sports two different vibes. The friendly bistro rolls out a lineup of staples of the likes of grilled bone marrow or mushroom and smoked garlic risotto. The excellent restaurant stars a parade of spot-on dishes that are presented in a succulent menu with a focus on sustainability, local producers and fresh premium ingredients. Veggies and gutsy, full-bodied sauces have clearly been cast in the leading roles of this culinary revue. Fans of organic and natural wines will be enchanted by what is on offer in both venues.

Name: Gioia
Description: Although the sound of traffic may be somewhat deafening outside, venture into this swish restaurant done up in tasteful light colours, taking a seat on the exquisite rear terrace when the weather is fine. The homemade pasta is out of this world! Rich flavours, fresh ingredients and Italy’s renowned “simplicity” are the hallmarks of this establishment. A new spin on familiar family favourites.

Name: Atelier Acqua e Sale
Description: It is no surprise that this friendly neighbourhood bolthole, the epitome of Italian hospitality and a spin-off of the nearby Dolce Amaro, has quickly attracted a faithful crowd of locals. Nicola seamlessly supervises the front-of-house, explaining the menu and its numerous dishes with great flair. The score is packed in full-bodied, authentic, no-fuss Italian flavours, e.g. melt-in-the-mouth ravioli stuffed with burrata and paired with sweet tomatoes and a lemon- and spice-laced sauce. Hearty, affordable, flavoursome food!

Name: Nesta
Description: As you enter the lifestyle boutique, you will notice the snug restaurant at the rear leading into a pretty garden, where, as you sit on the patio, you may even be forgiven for thinking you’re in Italy! Chef Kayes Ghourabi soaks his recipes in Italian sunshine as recognisable Mediterranean aromas and flavours unfold and captivate our tastebuds. Examples include a pedigree vitello tonnato or a breast of duck with a hazelnut crumble and a drizzling of subtle cooking juices. Bang on every time and always open to new twists.

Name: Resto 136
Description: Make a beeline for this peacock blue townhouse at number 136 where you will be pampered by Niels and Laura. Their elegant contemporary establishment upholds tradition and while the chef clearly enjoys mixing spicy Asian flavours with Mediterranean extravagance, he is equally capable of winning you over with a flawless piece of cod flanked by knockout beurre blanc and creamy mashed potato.

Name: Sanzaru
Description: Behind the Cubist-inspired façade lies a pleasant, airy, colourful establishment devoted to creativity. The chef reverently respects the season in dishes that subtly draw on influences from all four corners of the earth. An example: a characteristic caprese salad to start is given a crisp modern perspective courtesy of surprising textures, while pollock cooked in butter is served with mashed potato and leek-flavoured ice cream. The contents of the various surprise menus (including vegetarian) are pleasantly true to their names and there is an attractive lunchtime formula. You can expect a score in the zeitgeist that is both surprising and balanced, and guaranteed to set your tastebuds tingling!

Name: Toucan sur Mer
Description: Superlative seafood platters piled high in oysters and whelks, crispy shrimp fritters, textbook skate wing with capers, an oriental tempura of soft-shell crab, without forgetting the house delicacy – lobster straight out of the tank… Fish and seafood are the DNA of this lively bistro with its sea-faring theme and delightful pavement terrace. All the ingredients are flawlessly fresh and bursting with irresistible briny flavours. Toucan sur Mer is without doubt the foremost fish restaurant of Ixelles.

Name: René
Address: place de la Résistance 14, Anderlecht, 1070, Belgium
Description: René takes us back to a time when life was simple. This former chippy, upgraded into a natty vintage bistro, shines the spotlight on down-to-earth Belgian classics. Mussels stuffed with parsley and garlic butter, rare steak with fresh béarnaise sauce and nourishing stews are all served with heaps of French fries. Huge helpings of searingly good food! What’s not to like?

Name: La Brasserie de la Gare
Description: To get a real taste of authentic Brussels, head for this historic café, whose pores ooze vintage charm with a bustling, almost boisterous brouhaha to match. The chef pays tribute to tradition with a patriotic line-up of no-nonsense Belgian classics, such as shrimp fritters, steak and fries and dame blanche (vanilla ice cream and hot chocolate sauce). The Brasserie de la Gare provides conclusive evidence that some things never change!

Name: Cinq
Description: The young and not so young come here to be spoiled rotten in this contemporary villa near the ring road of Brussels. Chef Verzele rustles up a varied menu in tune with the zeitgeist, adding a new spin to his classical background. Examples include perfectly poached fillets of sole, paired with fried prawns, a velvety saffron-flavoured risotto and a knockout fish sauce. Cinq is the sort of place that invites you to dig into meals steeped in gutsy, big-boned flavours whilst enjoying the casual buzzy vibe. Should you have cause for celebration, we can recommend the lobster menu.

Name: De Gouden Muts
Description: This elegant villa is so cosy and inviting, and with the warm welcome extended by Evi, your charming maître d', you are sure to feel right at home. In the open kitchen, chef Rudy puts his own spin on French and Belgian recipes, adding in the requisite zing and occasional Japanese nuances. For instance, he uses miso to enhance flavours, but he also stays true to tradition with dishes such as pigeon cooked on the bone and served with beetroot and foie gras. He takes a detailed approach to his cooking, and his rich sauces are a key part of his dishes.

Name: Couleur Rouge
Description: This eatery gives European ingredients a subtle Asian twist. For example, smoked duck breast with a maki of vegetables and a tangy, orange-laced dressing, or marinated oriental-style pork brochette with marinated veggies. This quirky fusion approach sets the tone of the entire menu, endowing each dish with elegance and structure. The bright décor, the lush, peaceful interior garden and the delightful terrace, which will almost make you forget you are in the heart of Eupen, further enhance the overall serenity that pervades the establishment!

Name: Seir
Description: The sunny conservatory of this swish restaurant immediately catches the eye. The leather-seated lounge is ideal to sip a drink while admiring chef Thomas at work. An accomplished artist, he composes his visual masterpieces right on the counter. Intelligent combinations, precise and meticulous cooking. This youthful chef gives a free rein to his creative flair and is clearly determined to go places! A genuine treat for the senses.

Name: Steeg
Description: The narrow lane leading to this buzzy eatery, near the Grand-Place of Dendermonde, would be quite at home on a historical movie set. Willem Vervaet once again demonstrates his love of live fire cooking and his creative flair. First, he grills scallops, before pairing them with raw celeriac seasoned with parsley and capers, and then adding a final flourish by way of a divine baked apple sauce. This chef enchants and surprises with nuances of grilled fruit and veggies. The menu is a treasure trove of playful combinations that never cease to intrigue and delight.

Name: Feast
Description: With Feast, Donaat and Guy have created a vintage-style haven where you come to relax and enjoy yourself. The presence of record players makes it clear that music is central to the experience here and you can even customise the background music with your own records. The menu features a variety of international dishes presented in tapas-sized portions. Think smörrebröd topped with scallops and kohlrabi, or oven-baked leek with a satay sauce – playful and packed with flavour, without a hint of pretentiousness. With a wide range of natural wines and well-known favourites, the wine list has plenty of gems in store.

Name: Gusto Naturale
Description: Walk through the sleek grocery store (we recommend stopping off to make a few purchases as you leave) to take a seat in this urban eatery. The chef adds his own spin to authentic Italian dishes. For example, he might pair homemade tortellini stuffed with shredded beef and veal with a spot-on veal gravy. He has a knack for mixing powerful, rich flavours and his flair for vegetables and fresh textures is entirely in the zeitgeist.

Name: Viticolo
Address: Rue du Bon Voisin 117, Oisquercq, 1480, Belgium
Description: A stopover in this red brick edifice on the outskirts of Oisquercq will whisk you off to Italy. The interior and the peaceful patio are both stylish and comfortably cosy. The produce is local, illustrated by the garden-fresh herbs coating the pluma iberico. Juicy octopus is enhanced and underscored by a sauce featuring the subtle acidity of cime di rapa. The pasta is naturally fresh and home-made in this restaurant, determined to uphold Italian traditions.

Name: Dante
Description: This old farmstead in a country village, tastefully converted into a friendly eatery, is the HQ of Otis and Sven. Your cheerful hostess attends to your every need, while the chef’s repertory bears the stamp of his open-minded outlook and commitment to quality. Exotic, often Asian twists add a refreshing dimension to his playful recipes, illustrated by his excellent steak tartare enhanced by a variety of tomato textures and flanked by olive-laced ice cream and wafer-thin slices of Secreto 07, or swordfish jazzed up with ponzu and furikake. The spot-on menu changes regularly, to the delight of the loyal crowd of patrons.

Name: Chez Flo
Description: In this snug neighbourhood hangout, Florence Porignon cleverly blends generosity with delicacy. She may pair grilled veal, cooked rare, with a flavoursome spring roll or a gutsy veal stew, simmered patiently and lovingly with velvety, melt-in-the-mouth Reblochon mashed potato and a delicate scattering of capers and olives for a Mediterranean kick. This chef goes straight to the essentials and underscores the legible flavours with her subtle, delicate hallmark. The sauces are out of this world! Even better, the set menu with choices is proof that first-class cuisine need not break the bank!

Name: Sardis
Description: Tiziano Cappai welcomes diners warmly into this stylish red-brick terraced house, which boasts a cosy interior, sensual artwork on the walls and a blissfully peaceful patio at the rear. Chef Eveline Cappai deftly updates a pure-bred lineup of Italian classics. For example, she might pair bigoli pasta with a subtle stock, to which she adds white wine, parsley, savoury vongole and a hint of umami thanks to kombu. The tiramisu manages to underscore authentic flavours with an amusing new spin thanks to a play on textures. Attention to detail is the watchword here.

Name: Guzzi
Description: This characteristic town house with a small garden is a stalwart champion of Italian simplicity. The chefs add a new, yet respectful spin to authentic flavours. The menu is devised according to the availability of fresh, preferably organic ingredients, occasionally jazzed up with a Mediterranean twist. We recommend their sourdough pizzas cooked in a clay oven – your tastebuds won’t know what has hit them!

Name: Fortuin
Description: Huge vats of beer and a remarkable tree sculpture immediately catch the eye as you step foot in the Staminée. Continue on to the elegant brasserie, where a trendy playlist and hip décor set the cosmopolitan scene. Veteran chef Stijn Rotthier puts his own spin on classical recipes. Examples of Fortuin’s focus on gutsy, authentic flavour include house-made fritters stuffed with hand-shelled grey shrimp or fork-tender cutlets flanked by crispy, piping-hot French fries cooked in tallow. Parents may be interested to know that children are more than welcome (special menu) and that there is a playground almost next-door to the restaurant. Accessible and easy-going set the scene here.

Name: Osteria Romana
Description: Don’t even try to resist the appeal of this Osteria Romana - you will be bowled over by the romantic allure of the mansion, the cocktail bar and the immaculate tailored service. Roman specialties and tableside preparations set the scene. Delicacies include Roman-Jewish deep-fried artichoke, carbonara pasta, pasta with tuna tartare, pepperoncino, combava and ginger in a lineup whose subtlety, generosity and flavour are to die for! What more proof do you need that Italians do it better!

Name: Talloor d'Or
Description: It is difficult not to succumb to the feelgood vibe of the snug interior, depicted by soft lighting and a view of the open kitchen. Chef Matthias rolls out a seasonal menu that shines the spotlight on cherry-picked veggies and gutsy sauces. High-precision craftsmanship, flawless cooking and the odd Asian twang set the scene. An example: melt-in-the-mouth suckling calf flanked by a gutsy veal gravy enhanced with miso for a distinctive hint of umami. Be it lunchtime or evening, choosing either the menu or à la carte is always a challenge, but Nikki is close at hand to help out!

Name: L'Esprit Village
Address: Place Obert de Thieusies 10, Thoricourt, 7830, Belgium
Description: Christine and Pascal couldn’t have found a better name for their establishment. Everything from the warm greeting and service to the wholesome, rustic fare smacks of genuine sincerity. Chef Pascal forgoes fancy frills in favour of generous dishes piled high with top-notch familiar ingredients. He may underscore the full flavour of Iberico ham with a gutsy gravy, while the salty tang of clams is paired with a velvety pumpkin purée and a spicy cream of piquillo pimentos. A market-fresh menu that hits the spot every time – the epitome of a country village eatery!

Name: De drie ridders
Description: Welcome to a page of history of Western Flanders. An authentic red and green colour scheme, a huge fireplace and period floors set the scene in this 18C edifice: for example, the aperitif is served near the old livestock weighbridge. Take a seat and soak up this magnificent setting, as Emily and Bart enthusiastically reveal their love for their work, characterised by a focus on local produce, a new spin on time-honoured recipes and a delicate, creative touch. They are committed to using traditional cooking techniques as evidenced in the medium-rare duck fillet, grilled on the bone, accompanied by a juicy slice of celery, fermented figs and a puree of chickpeas. The carefully curated wine list shines the spotlight on small wineries. Soulwarming, indulgent cuisine, bundled into a single set menu.

Name: Les Petits Oignons
Address: rue de la Régence 25, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: Outdoors, diners are sheltered from the bustling Rue de la Régence by wooden decking, while indoors, a luxurious brasserie décor provides the perfect foil to a lineup of Gallic classics and stellar Mediterranean fare. The extensive menu offers dishes that star time-honoured family favourites like calf’s brains in a zesty lemon sauce, tagliata of beef, veal kidneys in mustard and desserts such as French toast. Les Petits Oignons delivers spot-on cooking every time as it bends over backwards to pamper and spoil its regular customers and passers-by in the Sablon district.

Name: Cômo
Description: Renato Favaro pays tribute to his roots in this buzzy trattoria depicted by a smart urban vibe and a sprinkling of amusing decorative details (like a bumper of the iconic cinquecento car). Old school family favourites set the culinary scene including pizzoccheri della valtellina and fettuccine al ragu, unless you wouldn’t rather sample paccheri al dente in a rich tomato sauce enhanced by shitake mushrooms, parsley, fennel-laced sausage and lashings of parmesan? Free of fancy frills, the focus is on authentic flavours and familiar family favourites. The cherry on the cake is chef Favaro’s fun-loving personality.

Name: Vismet
Description: This watering hole in Brussels’ fish market never disappoints. Everything is authentic from the characterful premises to the open kitchen and the bubbly vibe. The owner-chef unveils his talent in the kitchen, while your hostess supervises the dining room. The seafood-centric score calls upon top-drawer ingredients and high-flying craftsmanship. Impeccably grilled sole flanked by a rich tartare sauce embodies the classical textbook register of this fine food establishment. Fresh and traditional are the watchwords here.

Name: Bistro Berto
Description: Zulte-Waregem football club has hired a new striker! In the southern stand, David Bertolozzi hits the bullseye every time with his generous dishes. Start with a range of snacks to share, like generous nuggets of plaice dipped in tartare sauce, before digging into a modern version of classical recipes, such as pheasant with winter side dishes or a heart-warming vol-au-vent. Attractive lunchtime menu.

Name: Jaco
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Valet parking
Description: Jaco blends the well-heeled ambiance of Fort Jaco with a vintage interior dripping in contemporary elegance and luxury depicts the tiniest details. From Puglia, Francesco de Vita and Dario Trimigno recreate authentic Italian flavours using outstanding premium ingredients which they craft into unusual, attractive dishes. Don’t miss their version of vitello tonnato or a pistachio soufflé that is daringly paired with a bitter ice cream. Come early and sip a cocktail at the bar, before or after stocking up in the delicatessen store. Jaco is a culinary universe in a class of its own!

Name: Taverne du Passage
Address: Galerie de la Reine 30, Brussels, 1000, Belgium
Description: This emblematic Art deco brasserie, which is housed in the exclusive Galerie du roi, just a stone’s throw from the iconic Grand Place, takes you back in time to the Roaring Twenties. Its vintage charm is enhanced by a host of elegant details like the flock of golden origami birds hanging from the ceiling. The equally nostalgic menu features a splendid lineup of Belgian family favourites together with a few more modern recipes. Start with crunchy shrimp fritters, before moving onto veal kidneys in a creamy mustard sauce, to finish with a warm chocolate mousse and butterscotch ice cream. Living proof that tradition and generosity are timeless values!

Name: Black Smoke
Description: Black Smoke packs a distinctly American punch. The dimly lit, unpolished, rough and rugged interior is steeped in the smoky aroma of BBQ. The pitmasters have perfected the art of grilled meat in true Texan fashion. Traditional techniques, Latino influences and local produce for meals rich in big-boned, heart-warming flavours. Examples include lamb tacos jazzed up with a spicy za’atar, jalapeno pepper and fresh lemon. Or how about a cut of premium beef from the De Laet & Van Haver butcher’s shop? The drinks menu is practically as long as the food menu, while the ‘Bonanza Experience’ is billed as the ultimate sharing experience! So, let’s crank up the heat!

Name: Vividu
Description: The sun always shines in Gavermeer thanks to Vividu, a restaurant established in a villa that is reminiscent of Tuscany, albeit with a rock n’ roll soundtrack. The spontaneity of Nicky who is never far from your table makes the experience even warmer. Chef Laurent Messine demonstrates his passion for outstanding produce and Italy, adding his own inimitable stamp. For example, he may coat a loin of Iberico pork in a crust before cooking it in milk and then using ragusano cheese to create a gutsy sauce, all of which flanked by super-fresh side dishes. The legendary bistecca di Chianina is the house specialty, but requires pre-ordering.

Name: Ander
Description: Fire is central to everything at this cosy home restaurant run by hostess Hermien and chef Arno. They have devised a set menu comprising five to six courses, showcasing local produce from the land and the sea. The chef imbues venison fillet with a distinct smoky flavour and serves it with a colourful red cabbage accompaniment. Fillet of Steenvoorde pigeon comes with a rich jus and a confit leg. Rest assured: this young couple knows how to show their diners a good time.

Name: La Rigue
Description: The stunning La Réserve hotel boasts a brasserie that is fully the equal to its classy host. The Zegemeer landscape, visible from the handsome terrace, provides the perfect foil to this urbane restaurant. Local foodies swarm here, like bees to a hive, for its lineup of patriotic and Gallic favourites, jazzed up with a delicate new spin. For example, a subtle carpaccio of scallops is paired with tart green apples, avocado and salmon roe, while a bouillabaisse of North Sea fish, langoustine and lobster explodes with big-boned gutsiness… Finish your meal with a flamboyant flambéed crêpe suzette. A tailored culinary experience overflowing in generosity and a capacity of some 120 diners. Be it for a snack or a special occasion, La Rigue ticks all the boxes.

Name: Soixante
Description: The window of this hip eatery extends an enticing invitation to step inside and the interior lives up to its promises with tightly packed tables and lashings of distinctive character. The chef has a weakness for veggies and seafood and enjoys surprising us with unexpected pairings and intriguing blends of earthy and acidic textures. He might flank a generous piece of brill with fermented tomatoes and salsifies or an exquisite sauce made out of brill bones and a meaty jus. Big-boned food in tune with the seasons.

Name: Delphine Ronsyn
Description: Chef Delphine Ronsyn designed this spacious restaurant, less than a kilometre from her family farm, and whose picture windows and terrace command fantastic views of the surrounding fields and meadows. Naturally enough, Delphine is a champion of local produce and her region, courtesy of unfussy bistro fare that is deceptively simple and straightforward. She may serve lobster glazed in aromatic tomatoes, flanked by mozzarella cream, tender artichoke and rocket leaf salad. The chef frequently pops out to ask diners for their thoughts about her cuisine. A word of advice: bookings are highly advised as this establishment is almost always packed to bursting.

Name: iOda
Address: Rue de la Victoire 23, Saint-Gilles, 1060, Belgium
Description: iOda defines itself as a vegetarian rotisserie. Rather than meat, expect vegetables and fruit without forgetting a few delicacies from the North Sea. Chef Hoed unveils his creative talents in dishes such as leek roasted on the rotisserie, shining the spotlight on small local producers whenever possible. Playful, delicate and gutsy – the seasons are reverently respected, allowing the ingredients to shout their name. The trendy, buzzy interior of vintage details and untreated materials is perfectly in tune with the hipster Saint Gilles district.

Name: Graspoort
Description: Graffiti on the walls and a homemade tropical tree hung with brightly coloured leaves set the scene in this fun, offbeat eatery. Thibault Van Stratum cooks instinctively and frequently finds his inspiration in Asia. Highly creative fusion cuisine brimming in influences, illustrated by croaker and marinated mussels jazzed up by smoked oil-perfumed dashi.

Name: Le Roi de Trèfle
Address: Avenue Baron Louis Huart 12, Namur, 5000, Belgium
Description: On the banks of the Meuse, Brigitte Dekoninck and Patrick Kleeblatt welcome diners to their characterful abode, which sports a lounge vibe oozing in charm. The veteran chef is a champion of classical fare and is all for allowing the diner to choose their own main ingredient and side dishes. His craftsmanship is showcased in melt-in-the-mouth foie gras or in the subtle vin jaune sauce that flanks crunchy sweetbread and cèpe mushrooms. Lovers of nostalgic nosh will fall in love with this King of Clubs.

Name: Bink
Description: If you’re looking for good food in a romantic-cum-industrial bistro vibe, make a beeline for the former Brepols printing works, where an open kitchen sets the tone of the establishment. You can choose between a primarily classical menu or a more modern repertory, strewn with Asian influences. The seabass in a salt crust is emblematic of the knowhow of the chef, who enjoys surprising diners with winter side dishes and a tangy sauce jazzed up by Sichuan pepper over a fillet of venison.

Name: Ukiyo
Description: The former presbytery of Stekene is in a class of its own, boasting a sleek, trendy cocktail bar, four luxurious guestrooms and a classy contemporary restaurant leading into a manicured garden. Brothers Timothy and Bodi de Munck bend over backwards to pamper their guests. Their passion for Asia is reflected in the extensive à la carte and Omakase menus and in the beverage list. Gallic flavours with subtle Japanese nuances set the scene, exemplified by a delicious ponzu-flavoured sauce that delicately underscores fish or Anjou pigeon, cooked rare, flanked by morel mushrooms and a gravy so rich it will knock your socks off!

Name: De Oogappel
Description: This 1760’s edifice, graced in period floors and wardrobes, is now the venue of a friendly bistro serving traditional fare to the joy of discerning gourmets. The appetising menu of starters to share displays a more modern twist with Asian influences. We recommend the crispy sweetbread 'fine champagne' – the house signature dish. Go there your eyes closed.

Name: d'Oude Schuur
Description: Wine takes front stage in this pretty farmstead with a courtyard patio and warm lights twinkling indoors. In addition to adorning the walls, it is above all the passion with which the wine is served that sets the scene. Burgundy takes pride of place on the wine list, a genuine bible. The chef adds subtle, modern twists to traditional recipes, underscoring tuna tartare with Asian accents, for example, while the sole meunière is quite simply the summum of textbook perfection.

Name: Julia Fish & Oysterbar
Description: A fishmonger (Mare Nostrum) at the head of a fish bistro, complete with a maritime interior, right down to the fish scales? It sounds so authentic that it just has to be true… Fish and oysters from the “sea to the fork” and the best shrimp fritters of the Belgian coast into the bargain. Julia’s simple, generous cooking is heaven for foodies.

Name: 't Kantientje
Description: Pille Senior and Junior work side by side in the kitchen of this elegant canteen in the picturesque village of Ramskapelle. In summertime, the terrace is very popular. The food is stripped back, handcrafted and traditional with a weakness for fish. Shrimp fritters, lobster belle vue and freshly prepared sabayon: delicate flavours that appeal time and time again. The fine wine list is fully in tune with this high-class establishment.

Name: Brasserie Boulevard
Description: This swanky, spacious brasserie flooded in light is invariably packed to the seams. Thomas endeavours to ensure that your dining experience is as pleasant as it is flavoursome. Classic brasserie fare enhanced with a few spontaneous personal touches. The inspiring choice ranges from snacks to share, luxury vol-au-vent or trendier recipes….

Name: De Stadt van Luijck
Description: A meal in this former solicitor’s home oozing in character will be one to remember. The stylish interior, which sports a refined Renaissance slant, and the garden are a treat for the eye. Your tastebuds will be pampered by chef Warren Vandevelde who demonstrates just how much his carefully crafted cuisine is in line with the zeitgeist. The chef works tirelessly to create surprising associations, constantly adding new twists to familiar flavours. For example, he may pair a tartare of warm langoustine with a tomato coulis, a langoustine bisque and sea lavender oil. The lunchtime menu is not be missed!

Name: Bistro Mathilda
Description: A modern bistro on Leopold II Laan. The enthusiastic owners shine the spotlight on North Sea delicacies sourced from local boats, together with brasserie dishes and a set menu with choices in a more contemporary vein. The chefs may craft rye cheeks à la meunière, flanking them with a buttermilk puree for a tangy fresh note, fresh fennel and a subtle buttery sauce. Big-boned flavours packed in varying nuances. A safe bet every time for a slap-up meal in Ostend.

Name: La Coupole
Description: La Coupole has been a blue - chip value since 1989. Diners enjoy the low - key, trendy atmosphere. The lobster and fish specialties are served by chef Bonnez’ brother, further proof of the establishment’s quality. Excellent wines.

Name: Wasserette
Description: The washing hanging from the ceiling is a reminder of the former laundromat that has morphed into a hip eatery firmly part of Nieuwpoort’s culinary scene. The menu features mouth-watering dishes served in small and large portions, flanked by a fine wine list. Unfussy recipes, often prepared à la minute, such as grilled brill with Belgian endive, velvety mash potatoes and a flavoursome shrimp sauce.

Name: Numerus Clausus
Description: You don’t get to be a culinary benchmark by accident! Chef Steven and his sommelière Annelies have devoted themselves body and soul to make this restaurant a beacon of French cuisine in Lier. That said, they aren’t afraid of dusting the cobwebs off culinary traditions or adding a personal spin, such as mustard-flavoured ice cream served with steak tartare. The intelligently curated wine list is perfectly paired to the food.

Name: Pot au Feu
Description: Christine Van Deun has settled down in this lovely Art deco villa. Trendy interior with vintage details, inviting bar and conservatory overlooking the terrace - garden. The chef pampers our taste buds with comforting traditional recipes. The extensive menu makes choosing a conundrum!

Name: Mondieu
Description: OMG! Not only is the view over the polders from the terrace jaw-dropping, the bright interior of this former 17C cloister is equally exquisite. You can expect an appealing lineup of bistro staples, with the odd exotic touch, from which diners are invited to compose their own two- or three-course menu. Fresh shrimp fritters, a coq au vin in a heroically wondrous sauce or lemon sole that is subtly underscored by an emulsion of green herbs: such are some of the authentic dishes, blessedly free of superfluous fancy frills you may taste here.

Name: Resto JETT
Description: “Just enjoying time together” is the thinking behind this small, elegant eatery. Cheerful Sarah supervises the dining room, while Dries can be seen in the open kitchen crafting dishes to be shared with friends and family. Convincing recipes that combine the rich classicism of Gallic tradition with exotic influences and a scattering of original ideas. Exceptional ingredients are the norm here, like pan-fried turbot paired with smoked eel, a beurre blanc infused with fennel pollen together with an exquisite range of delicately crafted textures. Just the ticket to just enjoy together!

Name: Messeyne
Description: The locals adore this cosy restaurant and its terrace in the adjacent gardens. The French cuisine is up - to - the - minute, full of flavour and unfussy.

Name: Patyntje
Description: A meal in this elegant colonial-style villa is a must for any self-respecting food aficionado.
