The boss herself heads up the kitchen and presents a pleasingly concise seasonal menu featuring classic and regional dishes with a modern twist, such as celeriac with a cheese foam, apple and buckwheat, or saddle of venison served rare with Brussels sprouts, red cabbage and potato pillows. The emphasis is firmly on locally sourced ingredients. Heavily centred on Austria, the excellent wine list also showcases French and Italian labels. A range of natural wines is additionally available.

Name: 1er Beisl im Lexenhof
Address: Am Anger 4, Nußdorf am Attersee, 4865, Austria
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This idyllic lakeside house has been in existence since 1447. With their wood panelling and tiled stove, its rooms have a cosy atmosphere that draws on the region. The cuisine is Austrian-influenced, but also has an international lilt. There is a choice of à la carte dishes or you can opt for the "Genuss-Menü" (set menu), or indeed pick and choose individual courses from the latter. The veal fillet and braised veal cheek, for example, is really delicious. On Mondays, a surprise menu comprising three or five courses is served. The restaurant is located in Hotel Lexenhof, which offers charming, cosy guestrooms.

Name: Lilli Fine Dining
Description: The fine dining arm of the Lilli gastronomy concept offers foodies the chance to savour an ambitious set menu created by Walter Triebl and his team. It comprises four, five or six courses, such as sturgeon, Alpine caviar, iced beurre blanc, cauliflower and hazelnut, or Amur carp with pörkölt (Hungarian paprika stew), parsnip and capers. The ingredients are outstanding and sourced with a clear emphasis on regional producers. The restaurant's modern interior is just as inviting as the adjoining garden area, separated only by a glass partition that can be fully opened in summer, lending the indoor space an almost terrace-like feel. The comprehensive wine menu features an excellent regional choice, along with wines from Germany, France and Italy. Service is very friendly and attentive.

Name: Restaurant im Parkhotel Tristachersee
Description: The romantic lakeside location is an attraction in itself – here on the shore of Tristachersee, the dedicated Kreuzer family run both the lovely hotel and the restaurant. The dining space is inviting; the winter garden extending out over the water is wonderful – in summer it gets turned into a terrace! The menu draws on good-quality, mostly local produce – char, trout, Danube salmon etc are from their own fish ponds nearby. They serve various set menus and an à la carte selection. The hotel also has its own spring water, which is offered free of charge throughout the premises.

Name: Im Hofgassl
Description: A thoroughly enchanting establishment! In a 16C townhouse in the heart of the city, dedicated hosts Susanne and Michael Pilz have created a cosy restaurant featuring beautiful vaulted ceilings and a truly idyllic outdoor dining area with trees, grapevines, shrubs and herbs. The chef-patron crafts regional and seasonal dishes with modern influences (think veal lights with brioche dumplings or sea bass with melted tomatoes and saffron gnocchi), the lady of the house expertly directs the service with warm hospitality. In addition to the restaurant, they operate café-bar 10 B, located on Rathausplatz. Recommended excursions: Lake Neusiedl or the Roman quarry in Sankt Margarethen.

Name: fischerhaus
Description: This lovely country house is located just a stone's throw from Wörthersee. The restaurant boasts a chic, elegant interior, as well as a delightful terrace. The menu features a diverse range of dishes prepared with the finest ingredients, covering everything from Austrian classics and Asian cuisine to truffles and caviar. Regulars and newcomers alike are treated with the same warmth and professionalism by the friendly staff.

Name: Beletage Zum Schwarzen Kameel
Description: The setting alone is a huge draw: the first floor of a 1901 Jugendstil building in a super-central location. The interior decor is at once elegant yet cosy, and the front-of-house team is experienced and pleasingly laid back, while operating in the classical style, like a well-oiled machine. And, of course, there is the exceptional food: a celebration of Viennese classics, elevated by creative seasonal additions. There is a well-curated à la carte selection with a set menu option – diners are spoilt for choice, with dishes such as the rustic hand-carved ham being just as tempting as the oven-baked pike-perch with a ginger and citrus butter.

Name: Die Gersberg Alm
Description: This restaurant overlooking Salzburg boasts a wonderful location and stunning views. The atmosphere in the pretty wood-panelled dining area is cosy. The cuisine is rooted in the region but also draws on international influences, with a house speciality of Zitronen-Rahm-Herz vom Milchkalb (milk-fed calf's heart in a creamy lemon sauce) featured alongside dishes such as venison yellow curry served with spiced rice. There are set menus, one of which is vegetarian, an à la carte menu and an additional afternoon snack menu – there really is something for everyone. This lovely spot, which is also a favourite among locals, is housed in the hotel of the same name.

Name: Weitmoser Schlössl
Description: In the setting of this picturesque centuries-old castle, you can savour classic cuisine with an Austrian twist. The dishes are meticulously crafted from first-rate ingredients including organic beef from the restaurant's own on-site farm. Be sure to try the Wiener schnitzel and the Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) – the side dishes are also excellent, such as the exquisite creamed spinach. Adept service comes courtesy of a friendly front-of-house team. Delightful terrace.

Name: Steak Boutique
Description: The name says it all: it is all about high-quality dry-aged beef from Austria and Nebraska, served as a variety of exquisite cuts. Whether you choose tenderloin, bone-in rib-eye, bone-in New York strip, T-bone or porterhouse, exceptional quality of meat and perfectly cooked steaks are guaranteed. Be sure to sample the wonderful house-made steak fries. Tip: The light-filled atrium with its lovely arched ceiling is especially delightful. The restaurant is housed in the same building as Boutique Dom Hotel building, in the centre of Graz.

Name: Terra
Description: Johann Schmuck runs his chic modern restaurant in the basement of a historical mill that dates back to 1581 – tables on the terrace overlooking the Stainzbach River are coveted in summer. He and Maximilian Grandtner are jointly in charge of the kitchen. They devise two seasonal surprise menus: one comprising four courses and the seven-course "Terra" set menu. Most of the ingredients used are sourced from the region. The friendly and professional service team includes sommelier Joachim Retz, who specialises in wines from Styria and Burgenland. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif in the bar lounge. There is also a menu of small snacks – ideal if you just want to drop in for a glass of wine.

Name: Black Sheep
Description: The fine dining restaurant of Bergland hotel boasts a chic interior with a stylish dark colour scheme. The cuisine is entirely dedicated to the Alpine region. Ingredients are sourced within a 200km radius, with Austria and South Tyrol being the main suppliers. Much of the produce comes from the immediate vicinity, including herbs from the restaurant's own garden. They even raise their own sheep. The cooking style is very contemporary and incorporates subtle Japanese influences. For example, the six-course set menu includes dishes such as Alpine prawn katsuobushi with tomato and yuzu bisque, or Tyrolean catfish and broad beans.

Name: Kliemstein Vino Vitis
Description: You could easily miss the entrance leading into this small restaurant housed in the Salzamt, with its beautiful, brightly lit vaulted ceiling and sophisticated ambience. Michael A Müller – a highly accomplished trained chef and restaurateur – has dedicated many years to this establishment. The owner enjoys interacting with guests and recommending the perfect wine from his extensive cellar of over 1 200 labels and 50 000 bottles. And he has found a congenial right-hand man in chef Andreas Zika. Diners choose from three surprise menus: the shorter "Theater Menu", the "Bistro Menu" and the "Gourmet Menu". The latter features such shining examples as "sashimi of yellowfin tuna, shiso, ginger-kefir broth" and "saddle of venison, gremolata breadcrumbs, Chinese artichoke" – dishes showcasing highly intense and nuanced flavours and exceptional craftsmanship. The wine tasting event that they hold once a month is another interesting date for the diary.

Name: Kammer5
Description: This converted farmhouse has been given an upscale, modern makeover, without any of its original character being lost in the process ("old exterior, new lease of life"). A relaxed, understated elegance reigns in the restaurant housed in what was once the cowshed. The beautiful brick cross-vaulted ceiling lends a special atmosphere to the space. The seasonal set menu, which comprises four or six courses, showcases regional produce. Sophisticated and meticulously prepared dishes, such as mushroom, thyme and sherry, or venison, black salsify and pomegranate, are packed with bold flavours. In addition to wine, there are also delightful non-alcoholic pairings available.

Name: Zum Verwalter
Description: Its origins dating back to the 17C, this site is steeped in history. Today the building houses pretty hotel rooms and an extremely tasteful restaurant with authentic charm – plenty of wood and low ceilings make for a really cosy atmosphere. In summer, the terrace, too, is very inviting. When it comes to the food, the kitchen draws on what the market has to offer. Top-notch ingredients are used to create classic veal tartare with pan-fried sweetbreads, for example. The marvellous selection of 600 wines, including top wines from Austria, Italy and France, is a must for wine lovers. The service is friendly and proficient – while always on hand, the staff's presence is by no means intrusive.

Name: Gutwinski
Description: This boutique hotel in the centre of the old town is the epitome of elegance – when it comes to both the guestrooms and the restaurant serving excellent cuisine. First-class ingredients – many of which come from the region – go into creating delicious dishes replete with international influences. The pan-fried fillet of Ramschwag char served with grilled baby leek, beluga lentil risotto, and a honey and lime foam is one appetising example. Choose from the set menu and à la carte dishes. At lunchtime, the slightly more limited selection includes a short lunch menu. The wine list, which counts around 250 labels, focuses on Austria. Handy for motorists: the Am Jahnplatz multi-storey car park is just a few minutes' walk away.

Name: Goldader - Alpine Kulinarik
Description: Housed in a modern building in a rural setting, this is an interesting location. The interior is stylish and minimalist with a soothing colour scheme – don't miss your chance to take in the lovely view from the terrace. The dishes served here are a modern take on Austrian cuisine showcasing the finest local ingredients including game and fresh trout. There is a tasting menu with a flexible number of courses. Friendly and attentive service.

Name: Sitzwohl
Description: The smart, modern interior design of this place verges on the minimalist, creating an inviting and really stylish atmosphere. First and foremost, though, it is Elisabeth Geisler's cuisine that draws guests to this restaurant on the first floor of what was once the Gilmschule, whose listed façade forms an interesting contrast with the modern architecture of the Stadtforum. Aromatic dishes with a clear structure, such as turbot fillet with a beautifully spiced and reduced beurre blanc or crispy tarte Tatin of carrot, parsnip and celeriac are available as part of a set menu or à la carte. A good selection of wines and friendly, efficient service are also part of the experience. Diners may like to go to the bar and the Geislerei delicatessen on the ground floor.

Name: Das Kraus
Description: This small restaurant with six tables is housed in what used to be a coffee house – the sign outside simply reads "K". They serve a six-course set menu made using seasonal ingredients, into which chef Daniel Horner (previously sous-chef at Japanese restaurant Mochi) and his team cleverly incorporates the odd subtle Asian flavour. Drawing on a selection of Austrian and international wines, sommelier Vanessa Schober recommends pairings for the set menu. Non-alcoholic tea accompaniments are also available. Diners can alternatively opt for a shortened tasting menu comprising just four courses. The cheerful, modern decor has an urban feel. You can also take in temporary art exhibitions here – the proprietor owns a gallery.

Name: Kutschker 44
Description: This relaxed and friendly, modern restaurant is very popular with locals, and no wonder given the delicious fare on offer. Menu options include chanterelle terrine with walnuts, lamb’s lettuce and bresaola as well as Viennese specialities such as veal lights and Black Angus rib-eye steak. The terrace looks onto the pedestrian zone.

Name: Fabios
Description: The clientele of this fashionable urban restaurant is a veritable Who's Who of Vienna! The Italian cuisine served is modern and pared back, in keeping with the minimalist interior design – two good reasons to come here for a meal! Plump for one of the house classics such as fried calamari or vitello tonnato. Or perhaps you would prefer saffron risotto with Norway lobster? Friendly and attentive service, a large terrace in summer, and a bar that is ideal for a light bite or a pre-dinner drink.

Name: Döllerers Wirtshaus
Address: Markt 56, Golling an der Salzach, 5440, Austria
Description: This place has a long culinary tradition to its name, dating back to 1909. The Döllerer family's inn is located in the town centre, not far from the parish church and the castle. The atmosphere is pleasantly lively and with a cosy, rustic charm. Food is served by friendly waitstaff in two dining spaces with historical vaulted ceilings or on the terrace to the rear of the building. The menu features mouthwatering dishes such as sturgeon with Piedmont hazelnuts or Rauris venison ragout, not forgetting the signature dessert Schwarzbeernock'n (blueberry dumplings) with sour cream ice cream. Delicatessen goods are also available for purchase, including meat products, cheese specialities and delicacies such as jams, Alpine spices, mustard etc. Overnight accommodation available at the adjoining Hotel Döllerer.

Name: Heunisch und Erben
Description: Due to its being an interesting mix of wine bar and restaurant, this place has a remarkable wine list and around 120 open wines to accompany the ambitious modern cuisine. Diners put together their own four- to nine-course menu from a lovely selection of dishes. The service is relaxed, attentive and experienced. The terrace is a popular spot on warm summer evenings.

Name: Do & Co Restaurant am Stephansplatz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Up on the seventh floor, this is one of the city's hotspots: a modern, elegant restaurant with a great terrace and a view of St Stephen's Cathedral. In the open kitchen the team cooks up international cuisine. Alongside the many Asian-influenced dishes, including sushi, the menu also features Austrian classics.

Name: Schloss Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Set in a phenomenal location, the renowned Rosewood Schloss Fuschl has many admirers, and not only among its hotel guests. With its exceptionally upscale and tastefully elegant interior, the restaurant strikes a perfect balance between grandeur and cosy comfort. The large windows offer a magnificent view of the lake. The set menu and à la carte dishes are prepared with select regional ingredients, including produce from the restaurant's own fish farm. The impressive wine list is extensive and includes some prestigious labels. In fine weather, you can also dine on the lakeside terrace one floor up.

Name: Paradoxon
Description: The atmosphere here is pleasantly down-to-earth, and the waitstaff laid-back and friendly. The cuisine is modern and seasonal. Along with à la carte options such as char ceviche or local ribeye steak, there is a set menu comprising four or six courses. Tip: Brunch is also served on Sat and Sun (10am-2pm). N.B. cash payments only. The restaurant also has an online shop selling home-made goods (sauces, pesto, jam etc), as well as beer and wine.

Name: Gasthaus Haberl
Description: The Haberl-Fink family is dedicated and passionate about this inn with a tradition dating back to 1924. Just as the establishment itself is divided into a rustic space with a tiled stove and a chic, modern restaurant, there is also a dual culinary concept: traditional regional fare à la carte or a modern and seasonal set menu ("Fine Dining Menü"). A fantastic selection of wines also awaits, especially for fans of Styrian labels. Fink's Terrassen-Nest is open during the day, serving a small selection of hot and cold dishes, as well as house-made ice cream. Tip: A variety of delicious food items are available for purchase in the delicatessen. Cakes, pastries and other sweet treats can be pre-ordered to take home.

Name: La Torre
Address: Grabenstraße 39, Sankt Veit an der Glan, 9300, Austria
Location: Sankt Veit an der Glan, Austria
Description: The keep of the medieval St Veit fortress is a truly remarkable setting. Nestled within the historic walls and surrounded by greenery, the small terrace is a particular highlight. This restaurant is run by husband-and-wife team Rosemarie and Ammar Trabelsi, who create a welcoming atmosphere with a personal touch. The Sicilian presides front-of-house and has charm in his blood. His dapper, old-school style is anything but stuffy. She is in charge of the kitchen and cooks up ambitious Italian and Mediterranean cuisine using select ingredients. Her dishes are pared down to just a few components, allowing their natural flavours to shine through. Turbot with samphire and datterini tomatoes or house-made paccheri with wild prawns, tomatoes and rocket are prime examples. Fish and seafood take centre stage and vary depending on what the market has to offer. The tasting menu is definitely worthwhile, but you can also order à la carte. Italian wine list.

Name: Seespitz
Description: An absolute highlight here is the location right by the lake! The trendy, elegantly designed restaurant flows seamlessly into the terrace – you can take in the lake view from every table. Two creatively inspired slow food set menus are on offer, one of which is vegan. In addition, the menu features classics, including familiar favourites such as Wiener schnitzel. Regional ingredients underpin it all. The wine list is predominantly Austrian, supplemented by Old World and a few New World wines, as well as a selection of sparkling wines. Stylish guestrooms at the Falkensteiner Schlosshotel Velden, to which the restaurant is connected via an underground passageway.

Name: Buxbaum
Description: This lovingly run restaurant is tucked away in the Heiligenkreuzerhof, a Cistercian monastery dating back to the 12C, and its assortment of pretty dining rooms creates a genuinely cosy, welcoming atmosphere. The lovely tranquil courtyard terrace is also not to be overlooked, and the charming service is the icing on the cake. On the menu: internationally inspired dishes and Austrian classics – think wild red prawn with rhubarb, nasturtium and sweet potato, or Wiener schnitzel served with potato and lamb's lettuce salad, lingonberries and lemon. Tip: wines from selected Austrian vintners.

Name: Weyerhof
Description: On the outskirts of Weyer, this farmstead, the presence of which was first documented in 1130, lies at the start of the Habach Valley. It has been owned by the Meilinger family since 1832, and today the hotel and restaurant are in the capable hands of siblings Elisabeth and Franz Meilinger Jr. The chef and his team cook up traditional regional cuisine with seasonal influences, served either à la carte or as a tasting menu, and accompanied by an all-Austrian wine list. A five- or seven-course surprise menu is available Fri-Mon by pre-booking (one day in advance). The cosy space with a beautiful vaulted ceiling has a rustic feel; the terrace commands a view of the Hohe Tauern mountains.

Name: Edlingers Tempel
Description: This restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a courtyard, which boasts a charming terrace for pleasant weather. Both here and in the inviting interior – notable details include vaulted ceilings and distinctive prints hung on the wall – diners are treated to very friendly service and delicious regional cuisine. The seasonally oriented menu features items such as marinated fillet of Arctic char on beetroot tartare with a horseradish foam, alongside classics like Wiener schnitzel. The wine list is well curated and distinctly Austrian – expert guidance is available. Tip: Look out for their special seasonal set menus.

Name: Duchardt
Description: An inviting gem in the Old Town! In this restaurant in a listed building brimming with Viennese charm, the vaulted ceiling is a particular highlight. Chef-patron Marcus Duchardt and chef Lars Zeltmann share duties in the kitchen, crafting classic French cuisine with a regional twist. Choose from two set menus – one accompanied by Champagne – or dine à la carte. The signature dish: Breton lobster for two.

Name: Vestibül
Description: With a penchant for seasonal and regional produce, this restaurant serves flavoursome dishes including freshwater fish specialities or classics like Wiener schnitzel. The food and drink are Viennese in style. The imposing historical building, which also houses the famous Burgtheater, makes for a unique location with a stylish interior that has a typically Viennese feel with its striking columns and gorgeous stuccowork. There is also a bar area, where small plates are served. Incidentally, the restaurant premises were once a private carriage entrance for Emperor Franz Joseph I and Empress Elisabeth when they attended the theatre.

Name: Huber's im Fischerwirt
Description: People have been flocking to Andrea and Harald Huber's Fischerwirt for years – and with good reason. This is hospitality at its finest. In the charming and elegant indoor area or out on the cosy little terrace, diners are attended to by a thoroughly affable team managed by your cordial hostess. And, of course, there is the delicious food – seasonal specialities from the region and traditional classics are served throughout the day. The extensive menu has something for everyone – from braised Borettana onion with crosne and charred leek to Backhenderl (breaded fried chicken) and Kalbsrahmbeuschel (veal lights ragout), every dish looks tempting. Be sure not to miss out on the wonderful desserts such as Topfenknödel (curd dumplings) or Heidelbeer-Datschi (blueberry cake). Tip: The four- to seven-course "Fischerwirts Chef Menü" comes with optional wine pairings. The well-curated wine list is dominated by Austrian labels and also includes a good selection of Champagnes. Plus there is a delicatessen selling chocolates, jam and spices etc.

Name: Bergfried - Chefs Table
Description: You're right in the thick of it here! From the high tables in this stylish little space, you can watch the kitchen buzz with activity – there's never a dull moment! A distinctive aspect of the proceedings is the way the individual dishes are presented: with a proper explanation and background music that is occasionally rather loud. For his nine-course surprise menu, chef Sebastian Stock likes to work with locally sourced ingredients to create clearly structured modern dishes brimming with intensity and flavour. Franz Stock curates superb wine pairings to complement the food. The service is essentially a family affair, and the dedication of the team is palpable. All of this promises you an entertaining, thoroughly enjoyable evening and a truly memorable experience! The best place for an aperitif is the cosy bar of Hotel Bergfried, which houses the restaurant.

Name: Esskultur by Unterlechner
Address: Reith 23, Sankt Jakob in Haus, 6392, Austria
Description: In this small "adults only" boutique hotel, you will find cosy guestrooms and an attractive restaurant with pale wood furnishings. Owners Christian and Nadja Unterlechner put their heart and soul into making you feel at home – it is clear that good service and a rapport with guests are top priorities here. They serve a three- to six-course set menu packed with sophisticated fare that draws on classical culinary foundations and regional ingredients. The food is served on crockery they produce themselves – pottery is one of the owner's passions, wine is another. You can enjoy the judiciously selected pairings or choose from the interesting wine list yourself.

Name: Neuwirt
Description: There's something for everyone here! The varied menu features "Neuwirt Classics" such as beef roulade with mashed potatoes, alongside more international options like halibut with peas and grapefruit. Along with the good food, you can look forward to a pleasant setting combining modern and Alpine decoration. The terrace beneath the arcades in front of the building is also inviting. Skilful and charming service. The restaurant is located in the Schwarzer Adler hotel.

Name: Altes Gericht
Description: The building itself is really quite something. Dating back to the 13C, this former courthouse – also known as the Schmiedhaus – has retained its original charm both on the outside and in its five dining areas, which feature plenty of old wood and historical details. A cosy atmosphere prevails throughout. Diners are served cuisine in a classical vein that draws on high-quality ingredients. Think variations of scallop – carpaccio au gratin and crispy scallop on a bed of mango and avocado salad. In summer, the garden planted with chestnut trees makes for a romantic setting.

Name: Grünerhof
Description: Young chef Maximilian Grüner's cuisine stays close to nature – his dishes take their cue from what the region and the seasons have to offer, and are served à la carte and in the form of a four- to six-course set menu. Among his appetising dishes are a potato and wild garlic soup served with baked egg and Jerusalem artichokes, and Schlutzkrapfen>/i> (Tyrolean ravioli) with cranberries, Gruyère and beetroot. The owner and her friendly, attentive team run the show front of house. Located in the eponymous hotel, which boasts a central location close to the ski slopes and attractive, cosy guestrooms, the restaurant has a lovely modern decor with an Alpine touch.

Name: Fux
Description: This chic restaurant is very much at home in Lech. Behind the large glass-paned façade a tastefully designed space with a modern feel awaits. The open kitchen certainly plays its part – you can watch the chefs from almost anywhere. The cuisine is a fusion of Asian and European – a style to which they have been committed for years. The wine list absolutely deserves a mention, being one of the finest in the country – the Champagne and Burgundy selection leaves nothing to be desired. The bar area is also inviting – ideal for an aperitif or a nightcap.

Name: Rote Wand Stuben
Description: This charming restaurant in the Rote Wand Gourmet Hotel serves traditional Austrian cuisine at its best, whether it's a perfectly souffléd Wiener schnitzel, delicious Buttermilchschmarrn (shredded, fluffy buttermilk pancake) or fabulous fondues! Diners can also look forward to cordial service and an extensive and well-curated selection of wines. At lunchtime, dishes are served à la carte, including fondue chinoise (Swiss-style hot pot) and cheese fondue. In the evening, culinary tradition is presented in appealing set menus. Compose your own two-, three-, or four-course meal from a range of options, or select one of five fondue set menus.

Name: Elysium Bergblick
Description: Set on a rise overlooking the village, Hotel Bergblick not only boasts charming guestrooms and attractive spa facilities but also offers a culinary experience well worth discovering. With just five tables, this small restaurant exudes tasteful elegance, with gentle piano music drifting in from the reception area. Diners are treated to a refined seven-course tasting menu that is rooted in classic culinary tradition yet infused with modern flair. Service is friendly and professional. Austrian labels dominate the well-curated wine list. Pairings by the glass are available to go with the set menu. Tip: Given the limited capacity, it's essential to book. An impressive collection of clocks is on display, as is a stylish 1912 French vintage car – complete with MICHELIN tyres!

Name: Reznicek
Description: All you would hope for from a contemporary-minded traditional inn! The regional and seasonal cuisine, which takes inspiration from classic Austrian fare, showcases carefully selected ingredients and impressive craftsmanship. Diners delight in dishes such as beef soup with shredded pancakes, organic char meunière, Backfleisch (breaded and fried meat) and Palatschinken (crêpes), as well as a selection of increasingly hard to find offal dishes. The extensive and well-curated wine list includes an appealing range of wines by the glass. Service comes courtesy of the friendly and attentive front-of-house team. Guests are seated at simply yet elegantly laid tables in an inviting dining space with all the charm of a Viennese tavern. Be sure to cast an eye over the well-stocked cheese display case.

Name: LAGANA
Description: Housed in Hotel Voco, this elegant restaurant adjoins the bar and has a hip and modern feel. It draws a good crowd with its delightfully lively atmosphere and gorgeous riverfront setting. Opt for the fine dining set menu or order sophisticated international creations and regional classics à la carte. The delicious dishes showcase select produce such as the fantastic lamb or the excellent scallops. Short but well-curated wine list.

Name: Lamark - Stube
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located right next to the cable car station, Hotel Lamark is run by Alexander Fankhauser. The restaurant boasts a number of cosy, tastefully designed dining areas with classic Alpine-style decor. The varied menu features both traditional regional fare and more ambitious creations to be ordered à la carte or as part of a set menu. Options include veal lights in a Riesling sauce, Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) with all the trimmings and confit char fillet with pointed cabbage, greaves dumplings and a mustard sauce. There is also a fine selection of wines. Affording panoramic views, the terrace is a delightful spot all year round.

Name: Animo by Aigner
Description: Having worked together at Hangar 7, Elisabeth (Lizzy) and Jakob Aigner have now opened their own place here, introducing a charming new concept to the area. While he presides front-of-house, providing friendly and attentive service and astute wine recommendations, she prepares Mediterranean fare in the kitchen. Made from the finest ingredients, her dishes are flavoursome and unfussy – the offerings are written up on a blackboard. The terrace is delightful in summer.

Name: Bistro Südsee by Hubert Wallner
Description: Here, on the southern shore of Wörthersee, you could almost fancy yourself in the South Pacific. This beach restaurant enjoys a gorgeous lakeside location, where the reeds sway to the beat of the trendy background music. Relaxed bistro atmosphere, friendly down-to-earth service and good food including regional classics such as house-made Carinthian Kasnudeln (cheese dumplings) and Mediterranean specialities like freshly made pasta or fish dishes. How about a nice cocktail to top it off?

Name: muto
Description: This charming establishment is situated in a pedestrian area in the old town of Linz. A few steps lead down from the entrance to a brightly lit, vaulted room done out in a modern and minimalist style. The creative cuisine playfully experiments with textures and flavours – hence the restaurant's name, which is derived from the Latin verb mutare (meaning "to change"). The service is really friendly and pleasingly informal – the front-of-house team keeps things casual in its interactions with guests. Tip for motorists: You can park at the Garage Promenade.

Name: Hofmeisterei Hirtzberger
Address: Hauptstraße 74, Wösendorf in der Wachau, 3610, Austria
Description: This building has a long history. Built in 1320, it was originally part of a monastery – Stift St Florian. Today, it is home to a charming and elegant restaurant with a lovely vaulted ceiling. The kitchen serves a modern take on classic cuisine. In addition to two set menus with four to seven courses, there are daily specials. Standout dishes include "Irish rock oyster with a clear Bloody Mary and celery stick", sweetbreads with pimientos, chipotle and lime, and Wiener schnitzel with potato salad. Everything is prepared using select ingredients. To complement the food, there is a fantastic wine list comprising over 2 100 labels. The champagne and Veltliner selections are especially enticing.

Name: Der Holzpoldl
Description: Manuel Grabner and Claudia Stiglitz describe their concept as a "culinary balancing act between a country inn and a fine dining restaurant". This holds true for the decor (a blend of traditional and modern), but especially for the cuisine. From an appealing array of dishes, you can compile your own set menu as you please – with starter and main course portions available, you are free to choose the sequence yourself. There are also classics such as Wiener schnitzel. The well-curated wine list displays a certain inclination towards Austrian picks but also includes international wines.

Name: Liebsteinsky
Description: Behind the large windows of this pleasant restaurant located between the opera house and the Stadtpark, a charming bistro atmosphere reigns in the airy, high-ceilinged room. The food is presented in two formats: at lunchtime, people come for the casual, no-frills "Business Lunch" deal that won't break the bank; in the evening, the modern dishes and a tasting menu comprising four or six courses take things up a notch in the sophistication stakes. Whether in the "miso salmon - Label Rouge fillet, pan-seared, celery, beetroot & sea asparagus" or "Wiener schnitzel, potato and cucumber salad & cranberry", only the finest ingredients are used.

Name: Am Mahrbach
Description: This U-shaped property is set in a quiet and secluded location in the Königsdorf mountains, surrounded by meadows, forests and greenery – the perfect backdrop for Cathrin Maric and Philipp Kroboth to live out their concept of sustainability and self-sufficiency. On their organic farm, they grow vegetables, fruit and herbs, keep goats and chickens, and harvest honey from their own bees. Everything else is sourced from like-minded producers in the immediate vicinity. Diners are served a seasonal surprise menu featuring flavoursome, ingredient-led dishes. The proprietor himself recommends the wines and gladly shares insights into his organic ethos. Housed in the former stables of the farm, the space is attractive: modern design, wood and stone, and floor-to-ceiling windows with an unobstructed view of the outside. Up to 16 people can be seated at four tables in front of the open kitchen. This creates a personal and intimate atmosphere, which is enhanced by your two hosts' warm and natural presence – it feels a bit like dining with friends. The owner also runs her veterinary practice next to the restaurant.

Name: Langwies Wirtshaus
Description: A self-proclaimed "lodge hotel for gourmets", Langwies Wirtshaus combines several facilities under one roof: a restaurant, a spa hotel, a conference centre and long-stay apartments. The menu features a contemporary selection of regional classics, steaks and seasonal dishes, as well as vegan and vegetarian options. There are several attractive dining spaces – for example, you can book a table in the cosy, spruce-panelled bay room.

Name: Petrus Café Brasserie
Description: The popularity of this place is down to the pleasant combination of café and brasserie, the great location in the centre of the old town – and the delicious food. In this centuries-old building (in which it started out as an inn in 1911), in a charming, understated decor, guests enjoy dishes such as beef tartare, pasta, risotto or coq au vin, and then of course there is the house speciality: mussels. Sandwiches are also available at lunchtime. In addition to wine, they serve beer from Belgium, where the owner and his wife lived for a time. The terrace in front of this building in a pedestrianised area is also a nice feature. Tip for motorists: parking at the Rathaus-Parkplatz 50m away.

Name: Die Weinbank - Wirtshaus
Description: Gerhard Fuchs and Christian Zach opened this tavern as a counterpoint to their fine dining restaurant. Serving seasonal dishes made with regional produce, the concept has proven to be a hit. Gerhard Fuchs brings many years of culinary experience to the table, and the team led by passionate sommelier and host Christian Zach provides attentive service with Styrian charm. Flavoursome dishes such as Leutschach pata negra pork brisket with chanterelle mushrooms and gnocchi with herbs can be accompanied by wine – the list comprises over 4 000 labels – or beer. The interior design is a modern take on rustic style, and there is also a lovely vine-covered terrace. Tip: Due to the popularity of this place, reservations are recommended. Delicious food items and wines can be purchased to take home. The name "Weinbank" is apt: you can hire lockers in which to store your fine wine purchases.

Name: Landgasthaus Essl
Description: Located in the village centre, this delightful inn has an inviting and cosy atmosphere. Pale wood panelling and finishings lend the spruce interior a rustic charm, and the covered garden is a popular spot during the warmer months. The food is regional and seasonal – options range from hearty classics such as Rahmbeuscherl (veal lights ragout) or Backhenderl (breaded fried chicken) to a more sophisticated set menu.

Name: Seerestaurant 1884
Description: As the name suggests, this restaurant enjoys a splendid location. Housed in the long-established See-Villa hotel, right by Lake Millstatt, it has a wonderful terrace that extends right to the water's edge! The elegant interior has floor-to-ceiling windows affording unobstructed views of the lake. The menu is rather diverse, featuring international, regional, traditional, seasonal fare – game and freshly caught fish from the lake take centre stage. The bar in the middle of the restaurant is sure to draw the eye.

Name: echt JAN AIGNER
Description: Housed in forumKLOSTER, a seminar and events centre, this is a modern and trendy restaurant with artistic decor that would be right at home in a city such as Graz or Vienna. Jan Aigner serves up dishes that draw on international influences and showcase regional and seasonal produce – you can order à la carte or take a punt on the surprise menu. Friendly and attentive service. There is also a bar and a terrace. Tip for motorists: There is a public car park next door (charges apply until 6pm).

Name: Steirerschlössl
Description: This elegant restaurant is located in an attractive Art Nouveau villa in manicured gardens. Beneath the high ceiling, take a seat at beautifully laid tables and relish the friendly, attentive service. The restaurant serves contemporary cuisine made with seasonal ingredients in the form of an à la carte or set menu. The reasonably priced lunch menu is popular. There is a charming terrace with a view of the countryside. Tasteful guestrooms are available for overnight stays in a separate guesthouse and the premises are close to the Red Bull Ring Formula 1 racetrack.

Name: Schloss Farrach - Das Restaurant
Description: Behind its striking mosaic façade, this 17C castle houses a beautiful restaurant with a cross-vaulted ceiling. There is also a delightful terrace. In the evenings, diners have a choice of two set menus showcasing seasonal and regional specialities; at lunchtime, the options are more limited. Some of the ingredients come from organic farms or the restaurant's own garden. Owner Alexander Stöhr is in charge of the kitchen; his son manages the front-of-house team and expertly recommends wine pairings. Tip: Various cultural events take place on specific dates. This is also a fantastic venue for private functions.

Name: Geschwister Rauch - Wirtshaus
Description: Wirtshaus is the second restaurant that siblings Sonja and Richard Rauch run in these premises located next to the church. They cook seasonal dishes, which are served as a set menu or à la carte; they also cover regional classics. The beautiful vine-covered garden offers a pleasantly shady spot in summer. Right opposite, in the pretty Villa Rosa, which dates back to 1913, there are attractive guestrooms and a cookery school. Tip: There is also a small shop selling items from the kitchen and the cellar.

Name: Zum Goldenen Hirschen - Hirschenstube
Description: Dating back to 1624, this venerable old building in the centre of Gmunden used to be an inn and is now a boutique hotel and restaurant. Chef Christoph Parzer expertly transforms fresh ingredients into flavoursome dishes that range from regional specialities to modern international cuisine. This interesting mix is presented in the form of an appealing à la carte selection including steaks and Alpine sushi, and the "AURUM" fine dining menu served in the evening. The interior impresses with its attractive blend of traditional elements – such as a tiled oven, a timber ceiling and brick vaulting – and modern touches (artwork and clean lines). Pretty terrace in the courtyard. Austria is particularly well represented when it comes to the wines.

Name: Keplingerwirt
Address: Sankt Johann am Wimberg 14, Sankt Johann am Wimberg, 4172, Austria
Description: Family-run since 1938, this traditional inn is essentially the original nucleus of the present-day hotel, which boasts a number of comfortable guestrooms. Diners can expect a refined atmosphere and exceedingly friendly service, as well as delicious seasonal cuisine prepared by a kitchen brigade headed up by chef Andrea Lunson, sister of owner Heinz Keplinger. The menu features a good balance of classics and contemporary dishes. In the evening, you can order à la carte or opt for a four- or six-course set menu. At lunchtime, the choices are more limited.

Name: Himmelreich
Description: Housed in a beautifully restored building dating back over 300 years, this restaurant is located right next to the wine estate Weingut Josef Fritz. The interior is elegant and attractive, with minimalist-style decor; outside, the courtyard offers a delightful setting for summer dining. Following stints in a number of top kitchens, chef Marco Gangl presents a set menu that draws heavily on regional produce. It is predominantly plant-led but also features meat and fish. The dishes have real character, eg "broccoli, grape, soft goat's cream cheese, radicchio" or "char, cucumber, beer vinegar, sesame". A nice idea: the ingredients used are presented on a board. The kitchen also makes good use of the herb garden in the courtyard. At lunchtime (Sat. + Sun.), a slightly shorter version of the set menu is available. With prior notice, both the lunch and evening menus can be made vegetarian or pescetarian. The wine list, featuring around 400 labels, is also worth mentioning, with numerous Austrian regions represented – including a substantial selection from Weingut Fritz. Service is attentive, charming and highly competent, with the chef lending a hand serving the dishes.

Name: Ratschen
Description: Set in a gorgeous location amid the vineyards, this is an interesting concept combining a restaurant, traditional tavern and lounge, as well as charming wooden bungalows for overnight stays. The restaurant is contemporary in style and serves a modern four- to seven-course set menu of bold dishes that are brimming with flavour. Nab a table by the floor-to-ceiling windows and take in the wonderful views. Tip: On Sundays, they are also open for lunch – there is an à la carte selection featuring classics such as clear beef soup with liver dumplings, plus dishes from the evening menu.

Name: Poll's Kaiserterrasse - Gourmet Restaurant im Weissen Rössl
Address: Markt 74, Sankt Wolfgang im Salzkammergut, 5360, Austria
Description: The spectacular lakeside location at Wolfgangsee is one of the main draws of this place. Combined with the stunning views of the lake and mountains, the classically elegant decor and live piano music in the background make for a truly romantic atmosphere. Incorporating local produce and drawing on classic and modern influences, the food is equally impressive. Diners have a choice of three set menus: "Poll's Menü", "Rössl Menü" and "Fondue Erlebnis" (must be pre-ordered). The outstanding wine list showcases Austrian labels. Friendly service. Overnight accommodation is available at Romantik Hotel Im Weissen Rössl, which also houses this restaurant. Steeped in tradition, this establishment owes much of its fame to the celebrated Peter Alexander film of the 1960s, Im weissen Rössl (The White Horse Inn).

Name: Zur Dankbarkeit
Description: Steeped in tradition, this restaurant in the centre of Podersdorf has been run by the same family for four generations. Their ties to the region are reflected in delicious dishes made with ingredients from the owner's native Burgenland. The handwritten menu features classics such as veal liver and schnitzel, as well as options including pan-fried Arctic char fillet with pak choi and celeriac cream. In summer, the courtyard behind the house is especially inviting, with a spacious gravel terrace shaded by trees. The estate's own wines are well represented on the menu. The establishment also runs a wine tavern nearby (open Fri, Sat and Sun), and has five cosy and inviting double rooms.

Name: Das Loewenzahn
Description: There are several reasons why you feel at home here: first, there is the charming decor, which is fresh and contemporary yet retains a certain regional flavour, plus the terrace with a lovely view over the lake. Secondly, the food – you can expect cuisine that, although of a regional bent, is also open to international influences. Served in the form of a five- to eight-course set menu, the dishes, such as "octopus, cauliflower, Amalfi lemon, saffron" or "lamb, meadow herbs, tomato, romaine lettuce", always have a modern, creative twist. And then there are your friendly hosts Jakob and Lilly Lilg, who make sure each guest feels well looked after.

Name: Endlich
Address: Dorfstraße 61, Sankt Anton am Arlberg, 6580, Austria
Description: Coming here is like being invited to dine with good friends in their home – such is the feeling conveyed by your very friendly hosts, Henrik Helmuth and Henriette Olsen, who are the couple at the helm here. In their modern, tastefully decorated restaurant, the Danish-born owners create an incredibly charming, intimate atmosphere and make a point of doting on their guests. There is no menu or wine list. Instead, Henrik prepares a surprise menu made up of three courses, while Henriette is on hand to recommend the wines to best accompany your meal.

Name: Stammtisch am Paulustor
Description: Near the Hauptplatz, this spruce historical building – once part of the city's defensive wall – now accommodates this chic restaurant. The interior decor sees a beautiful, bright vaulted ceiling successfully combined with clean-lined modern design and pops of colour. The menu features delicious, freshly prepared dishes such as carpaccio of Styrian Alpine ox, veal Wiener schnitzel or steaks cooked on the charcoal grill. From Wednesday to Friday, there is a two-course "Stammtisch Lunch" deal as well as an a la carte selection. The articulate, polite team provides brisk service and is happy to advise you. The terrace in the inner courtyard is also pleasant. Tip: In summer they offer BBQ on Wednesdays. Plus: monthly visit of a guest winemaker including a set menu with wine accompaniment.

Name: Gasthaus Csencsits
Description: There is a good reason why so many diners are drawn to this tranquil, rural village nestled among forests and meadows right by the Hungarian border. Jürgen and Melanie Csencsits run an upscale restaurant that maintains an inviting, laid-back feel. In a kitchen centred on an old wood-fired oven that is core to their culinary philosophy, the chef-patron and his team prepare a seasonal five- to seven-course set menu. Based on produce from the surrounding area, the cuisine mirrors the chef's strong connection to his Pannonian heritage. The charming proprietress manages the service team, who recommend excellent wine pairings by the glass. The extensive wine list is also well worth exploring. Delightful covered wooden terrace. Tip: Ask about their popular Buschenschank evenings, on which good, simple food is served (summer only).

Name: Triad
Description: Drawing on their experience at renowned restaurants and hotels, Veronika and Uwe Machreich run this idyllic establishment in a quiet, rural village setting. They have a lovingly tended garden that provides herbs and vegetables for the kitchen. The cuisine strikes a good balance between traditional and innovative elements. A shorter version of the evening menu is available at lunchtime – it features modern dishes with a twist, such as Waldviertel organic chicken, pepper and corn pancake and pimientos de Padrón. At lunchtime, delicious options on the "Wirtshauskarte" menu include Kalbsrahmbeuschl (veal lights ragout) or Zwiebelrostbraten (fried beef and onions in gravy). Or why not take a punt on the surprise menu? There is also a small farm shop selling delicatessen and house-made items. Overnight accommodation available.

Name: Gut Purbach
Address: Hauptgasse 64, Purbach am Neusiedler See, 7083, Austria
Description: This lovingly restored 16C farmhouse first became an inn in 1860. The bright, welcoming and modern interior tastefully combines historical elements and decorative art. Tables on the courtyard terrace, shaded by trees and shrubs, are also popular. The kitchen team keeps things seasonal and regional – honest food plain and simple. There are two set menus to choose from, but you can also mix and match à la carte. Renowned for its offal dishes, the restaurant also serves unconventional specialities such as beaver meat, horse tongue or pig's ear, along with the signature "poularde en vessie" (chicken cooked in a bladder). Many of the ingredients – as well as wine – come from the estate itself. Highly professional service comes with natural charm and heartfelt warmth. Tip: Ask about the dates for the traditional "Sautanz" (pig-slaughter feast).

Name: Walserstuba
Description: Diners immediately feel at home here! This is thanks to both the cosy atmosphere and the outstanding cuisine turned out by owner Jeremias Riezler, who has embraced a sustainable culinary approach. He uses top-notch seasonal and regional produce, and even rears pigs himself. Select – predominantly organic – ingredients are showcased in a multi-course set menu, the name of which translates as "Culinary Mountain Adventure". Dishes such as fried Walser veal sweetbreads with cranberry aioli demonstrate a distinctive culinary style. The chef presents his dishes himself and talks diners through the idea behind them. In an original touch, he also hand-carves the wooden cutlery with which some of the dishes are eaten. Your hostess heads up a charming front-of-house team. The hotel of the same name provides cosy Alpine-style rooms for overnight stays – the establishment as a whole is certified organic.

Name: DiningRuhm
Description: Housed in a corner plot building in an inconspicuous location in the 4th district, this restaurant serves an interesting mix of Nippon and Nikkei cuisine – ie Japanese- and Peruvian-inspired dishes are in the spotlight. This unpretentious cuisine also goes wonderfully well with the interior, which is decked out in warm colours and characterised by modern lines. The sushi bar is located in one of the three rooms. Try the delicious finger food, sushi (including lobster nigiri with a creamy spicy sauce) or main courses such as black cod yuzu miso. Attentive service from staff who also provide good wine recommendations from a selection that highlights Austrian labels. Unless you would prefer a sake…

Name: Kellerbauer
Description: Your congenial hosts Roman and Maria Mailänder represent the second generation of their family at the helm. They put their heart and soul into running this establishment that is typical for the region, and the service is friendly and welcoming. Imbued with the rustic charm of the Alps and adorned with decorative paintings, the ambience is warm and inviting. Alexander Rettenbacher is in charge of the kitchen and devises two three- to five-course set menus – there are one or two alternative main courses available. The cuisine is modern and seasonal, drawing on regional and Mediterranean influences. Vegetables and herbs from the restaurant's own garden are also used. The west-facing terrace affords views of the surrounding countryside and is a lovely spot from which to enjoy a beautiful sunset. There are a few guestrooms available next door.

Name: OPUS
Description: Located on the famous Ringstraße, the fine dining restaurant of the legendary Hotel Imperial, which dates back to 1873, truly reflects the zeitgeist. Nikolaus Platteter leads the kitchen team, who produce dishes rooted in classical French cuisine with international influences. Diners can savour a four- or six-course tasting menu (vegetarian alternatives available on request) or order à la carte. Charming and professional service. The interior is decorated in the style of the Wiener Werkstätte of the 1930s and makes for an elegant setting.

Name: Lackner
Description: The splendid location of this restaurant with a wonderful terrace overlooking Mondsee is as much of a draw as the cuisine of chef-patron Martin Lackner. His dishes have classical leanings and take their cue from the seasons. The quality of the ingredients – many from the region – is exceptional. Order the set menu or à la carte, taking your pick from appetising dishes such as "Hausruck beef tartare, ciabatta-parmesan ice cream, oven-baked tomato". The in-house wine shop is also worth a look. For overnight guests, Seehotel Lackner offers tasteful guestrooms, a beautiful spa and sauna area, plus direct access to the lake.

Name: HAUSBAR Wien
Description: Tucked away in the basement of the remarkable Künstlerhaus, this appealing modern restaurant also boasts a gorgeous covered terrace in the inner courtyard. The friendly team serves an imaginative vegetarian set menu comprising eight courses. You can also opt for a vegan version or the inclusion of a course featuring fish or meat. As a prelude to the meal, images of the main ingredients are presented. The waitstaff then proudly talk you through the dishes at your table. Perfectly paired cocktails are available (with or without alcohol).

Name: Floh
Description: Tapping into the region is the name of the game here. In the cosy setting of a traditional country inn, diners are served flavoursome dishes that celebrate local ingredients. Top-quality produce is prepared without fuss – the emphasis lies squarely on taste. There is a wide selection of vegetarian, meat and fish dishes, as well as the classics of this type of establishment. Highlights include salmon trout – pan-fried with white carrots and gnocchi, and Grammelknödel – a potato dumpling stuffed with cracklings and chilli, served with summer cabbage, Red Amposta onion and courgette. Choosing a wine is no mean feat either – the list boasts more than 2 800 labels! There is a separate menu for Veltliners, white wines, red wines, international wines and magnum bottles.

Name: Frierss Feines Haus
Description: The Frierss family are renowned for their sausages and other meat products. These wares are on site in their butcher's shop and well-stocked delicatessen, and are also to be found on the menu in this modern restaurant. Barbecued steaks feature among the mouth-watering specialities of the house, but there are fish and vegetarian options prepared in the open kitchen. Good selection of wines. A budget-friendly lunch deal is available, too. The staff are incredibly dedicated and friendly. Tip: You can also have breakfast here.

Name: Aurea
Description: Alexandra Debre and Armin Rauscher, the dedicated duo behind this small but perfectly formed restaurant on a side street in the centre of Villach, are elevating the city's dining scene with their culinary expertise. In the open kitchen, the chef-patron prepares an ambitious four- or five-course set menu, which you can extend with an additional course of "Aurea Happen". The aromatic dishes include, for instance, "potato, Belper Knolle cheese, bacon, chives" or "dentex, Thai flavours, carrot, almond", to be accompanied by high-calibre Austrian wines by the glass. The charming hostess provides service with a personal touch – supported by the chef, who likes to bring his dishes to the table himself – and helps create a pleasingly intimate and relaxed atmosphere in this upscale modern restaurant.

Name: Bär & Schaf Wirtschaft
Description: What started as a pop-up has now become a permanent fixture in the historical Gasthaus zum Prinz Johann. The proprietor duo, Martin Nuart and Philipp Medved, offer their guests a very personal dining experience. Philipp manages things front-of-house with delightful ease, friendliness, and proficiency, while Martin heads up the sustainability-focused kitchen. His intriguing plant-forward set menu showcases select seasonal ingredients from his family's own farm or neighbouring agricultural producers. In terms of wine, Austria takes centre stage, and is accompanied by offerings from Slovenia and Italy. The setting is wonderfully inviting – with lovely old floorboards, simple wooden benches and chairs and decorative contemporary artwork, the historical charm of the centuries-old inn has been retained with style.

Name: Schmidhofer im Palais
Description: In close proximity to the Graz Museum, this restaurant has a tasteful, modern interior and a high vaulted ceiling. The street view from the tables right by the window means you can watch the world go by as you eat. The terrace in the courtyard is wonderful in summer. International dishes such as "tuna sashimi rolls meet tuna tartare" are served, as well as Austrian dishes such as the impeccably prepared Wiener schnitzel – the salad of Graz-grown butterhead lettuce is a great accompaniment. The extremely polite and attentive service – the team is always on hand with a smile – also contributes to the pleasant atmosphere.

Name: Kolm
Description: Here in the natural surroundings of the Waldviertel region, you can enjoy not only the beautiful view of the surrounding area but also the ambitious cuisine of Michael Kolm and his team. The dishes are rooted in the region but with a cosmopolitan edge, as demonstrated by creations such as veal fillet, ravioli, wild broccoli, and hamachi, rutabaga, avocado. You can choose between the set menus – "Bärentrail Menu" and vegetarian "Animal-Friendly Menu" – and à la carte options. The service team is pleasant, cordial and competent – the first appetisers are plated in the restaurant itself. The bright, friendly ambience is aptly described as "casual". In winter, the fireplace is lit for a cosy feel. Interesting fact: The Bärenwald bear sanctuary run by the Four Paws association is right next door. Considering staying overnight? There are five lodges a little way down, set in the greenery.

Name: Bärenwirt
Description: Claudia and Manuel Ressi bring warmth and dedication to the running of this charming restaurant on the main square. The cuisine showcases select regional ingredients, which are presented in a kind of hybrid concept. On the one hand, there are the Austrian "Wirtshaus-Klassiker" à la carte (including Wiener schnitzel, Tafelspitz, Gailtaler Ripperl, and Backhendl), and then there is the four- to eight-course "Bärenwanderung" set menu with creative, modern dishes such as "Hühnerhof – organic chicken, beans, wild mushrooms, savory, buckwheat". You can also choose individual dishes from the set menu. The extremely friendly and attentive manager is happy to explain the provenance of the ingredients, giving guests an insight into the regional philosophy. The restaurant has two dining areas: one distinctly traditional small space and a more modern area, plus a nice terrace in front of the building. Der Kleine Bär located directly opposite has three inviting, nicely done out guestrooms. They also put on cookery courses and have an online shop – some of the produce available is made in-house.

Name: Umar Fisch
Description: Here at the famous Naschmarkt, the name "Umar" is synonymous with the freshest fish. The establishment has housed a fish shop since the mid-90s and this simple restaurant since 2003. It owes its success to the quality of the fish, which is served in the form of classic dishes.

Name: Skopik & Lohn
Description: The wonderful painted ceiling – the work of artist Otto Zitko – is the first thing to catch your eye here. The staff are friendly and attentive, and the food is delicious. Among the Austrian classics on the menu is Wiener schnitzel with potato salad and lingonberries. For dessert, try the île flottante! In front of the building there is a lovely terrace shielded from the street by greenery. The location in the Karmeliterviertel is another draw – just a stone's throw from Schloss Augarten with its porcelain manufactory and museum, as well as its park grounds.

Name: Zum weissen Rauchfangkehrer
Description: This cosy restaurant is divided into four traditionally decorated rooms – in one of them, gentle piano music provides the soundtrack to your evening meal. Delicious Austrian cuisine is the order of the day, including house specialities such as "Rauchfangkehrers Wiener Schnitzel". The wine list is exclusively Austrian and organised according to grape variety.

Name: Le Salzgries Paris
Description: A slice of Paris in Vienna? Mais, oui! This lively brasserie with a distinctly chic feel has become an institution in the city and – in no small part thanks to patron and chef Denis König – brings to life the concepts of "bistronomie" and savoir-vivre. If you are a fan of fresh seafood, then you've come to the right place: just order the plateau de fruits de mer! The beef tartare is another fine example of the French classics served here. At lunchtime and in the evening, you can also choose an appealing five-course set menu. An exclusively French wine selection and charming service contribute to that Parisian feeling.

Name: UNKAI
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: A pleasantly light and modern restaurant where you can eat either at authentic teppanyaki grill tables or more conventionally. You will also find the Unkai sushi bar on the ground floor serving a sushi brunch on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.

Name: Silva
Description: What must be one of the smallest fine dining restaurants in the country awaits you at Naturhotel Forsthofgut. With space for just 10 diners and its stylish interior design, the place has an air of exclusivity. Michael Helfrich is in charge of the kitchen and serves up interesting modern dishes that showcase the flavours of the forest. The menu takes its cue from the changing seasons – fermentation and smoking also play a role. There are two set menus to choose from: "Wald" ("Forest") and the vegetarian "Wiese" ("Meadow"). All courses are also available à la carte for maximum flexibility. Service is pleasingly individualised and personal, and the excellent beverage pairings (with or without alcohol) are elegantly presented at your table.

Name: Gasthof Schloss Aigen
Description: The history of this place dates all the way back to 1402! The kitchen team puts a modern spin on traditional Austrian cuisine, and diners can opt for a set menu or order dishes à la carte. Our tip: Try the boiled beef, which is prepared in a range of different ways. The charming interior is tastefully decorated and exudes an appealing family atmosphere. In summer, don't miss the gorgeous terrace laid out in the courtyard beneath the boughs of the chestnut trees.

Name: Brunnauer
Description: In the lovely historical setting of Villa Ceconi, Sybille and Richard Brunnauer's restaurant is the place to experience fantastic Austrian-style hospitality and cuisine. The dishes draw on French and international influences but give pride of place to the region and the seasons. Shining examples are the Styrian Alpine prawns with Marchfeld asparagus and creamed peas, or Tauern lamb with potato and leek mash and wild cauliflower. There are also vegan options. Everything is freshly prepared using premium ingredients. The themed speciality weeks are worth seeking out – from "Veal Offal Specialities" and "Fish & Shellfish" to "Truffle Specialities", seasonal classics take centre stage. Well-curated wine list. Tip: reasonably priced lunch set menu. The stylish modern interior is also attractive and the view of the fortress from the terrace is fabulous!

Name: Gasthof Auerhahn
Description: Run with great dedication, this friendly, family-owned restaurant is located at a slight remove from the city centre, close to the train station, but it's well worth making the detour for the excellent food. The cuisine is regional, seasonal and pleasingly down-to-earth. Their appealing range of dishes includes venison ragout with bread dumplings and chanterelles, as well as delicious desserts such as Topfenknödel (curd dumplings). Order à la carte or opt for the set menu, which comprises three to five courses – a vegetarian version is also available. Dine in the inviting interior or out on the charming terrace to the rear of the building. The adjoining hotel has well-appointed guestrooms.

Name: Rauter Stube
Description: An establishment run with dedication by the Obwexer family in a building steeped in history. Old paintings, wood panelling and a tiled stove lend plenty of charm and a certain elegance to the refined, rustic-style decor of this restaurant. Diners take their seats at beautifully laid tables to enjoy pleasingly informal service that includes reliable wine recommendations courtesy of owner Michael Obwexer – you will discover his enthusiasm for Austrian, Italian and French wine estates. In the kitchen, Max van Triel is the man behind flavourful dishes such as pan-fried fillet of turbot, with spinach, horseradish, hazelnut and lemon ravioli… and classic Wiener schnitzel. Opt for the tasting menu or order à la carte. You may also like to spend the night in style at the Hotel Rauter.

Name: Gasthaus Stern
Description: Tucked away in a residential area at a remove from the tourist trail, this restaurant is well worth the detour. In keeping with its charming traditional decor – the floorboards, wooden panelling on the walls and high ceilings evoke the atmosphere of an old-style Viennese inn – it proposes straightforward and delicious regional cuisine, which is popular with locals too. In addition to classic dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, offal and game take pride of place on the menu – the chef is a keen hunter himself. Check out the "Stern im Glas" range for delicious options to enjoy at home.

Name: FinESSEN
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Located at TAUERN SPA wellness hotel, this chic little contemporary-style restaurant is separate from the hotel but accessible from inside it. Seating is limited to 14 diners, who are served a six-course ingredient-led set menu. With his menu titled "Reise durch Salzburg" ("Journey through Salzburg"), ambitious chef Christof Schernthaner showcases regional and seasonal cuisine, highlighting exceptional ingredients such as home-grown woodruff, Lungau Eachtling potatoes and Alpine prawns. Wine pairings are available on request. The service is cordial – the chef serves and explains his dishes personally. N.B. Advance reservation is advised (before 11am on the day).

Name: lichtblick
Description: The location of this restaurant is not only spectacular, but also handy for doing a spot of shopping in the RathausGalerien mall before taking the lift up to the seventh floor for dinner. Here on the top floor, the upscale restaurant has all-round windows and a magnificent view of Innsbruck and the surrounding mountains – in summer, the charm of the terrace is irresistible! In the 360° bar you can drink in the marvellous panoramic view as you enjoy an aperitif, nightcap or coffee. The kitchen serves delicious international and regional dishes. In the evening there are three set menus comprising three to four courses; at lunchtime the à la carte selection is somewhat simpler.

Name: Der Luis
Description: Luis Thaller represents the sixth generation of his family to run this establishment, which has been going since 1875. Made primarily from locally sourced ingredients, the dishes served here are sophisticated and packed with flavour. These are presented in the form of an ambitious surprise menu comprising four to seven courses. The chef's signature dish is the farm-fresh egg with celeriac, greaves and pig's head. To complement your meal, there is a good selection of wines and non-alcoholic beverages. The restaurant is housed in Der Thaller hotel along with Wirtshaus, a more down-to-earth alternative.

Name: Wirtschaft Traube
Description: Tanja and Tobias Schöpf's establishment is pleasingly informal. She provides cordial and proficient service in the inviting wood-panelled dining space, occasionally taking a seat alongside diners at their table. Her husband, meanwhile, prepares five flavoursome dishes using regional ingredients, for you to select à la carte or as a set menu. Tantalising examples include Riebelmais (dry-milled corn), onion, Vorarlberg mountain cheese, or chicken leg, Savoy cabbage, leek, parsley root. He likes to keep things natural and seasonal – he goes hunting and forages for mushrooms, buds and herbs. The wine pairings, too, are carefully selected – an alcohol-free alternative is also available.

Name: Gasthof Stanglwirt
Address: Kaiserweg 1, Going am Wilden Kaiser, 6353, Austria
Description: Dating back over 400 years, this traditional inn now operates as a combination of organic farm and luxury spa hotel. The regional menu takes its cue from the seasons and also includes classics such as roast chicken and Tyrolean goulash. With 65ha of grassland and 52ha of Alpine pasture, they can produce milk, quark, butter, yoghurt, cheese and bread on site. Food is served in the cosy rustic-style interior – one area has a view of the cowshed – and on a lovely terrace overlooking the garden.

Name: Zuma
Description: Here you will find an international concept that has already made a name for itself in London, Bangkok, Las Vegas, Doha and Capri… Stylish, sleek design, dimmed lighting and subtle music create a lounge-like atmosphere; the large bar in the centre is an invitation you can't refuse – to have a cocktail. The extremely courteous English-speaking waitstaff bring you the extensive menu, which offers something for everyone. There is sushi, meat and vegetables from the robata grill (eg aubergine with aka miso is a great side dish) or modern dishes such as crispy fried squid, green chilli and lime. The restaurant is housed in the tasteful and history-laden Weisses Rössl hotel, very close to the charming old town.

Name: Greisslerei beim Taubenkobel
Description: Barbara Eselböck and Alain Weissgerber offer a delightful alternative to Taubenkobel restaurant with this charming eatery located in the adjacent building. The atmosphere is friendly, relaxed and completely unpretentious, and the food is simply delicious. Select ingredients go into flavoursome dishes such as Alsace-style snails, Wiener schnitzel and gnocchi with fresh truffles. The interior is wonderfully cosy and has a vintage feel to it, with charming decorative touches and shelves displaying house-made and Pannonian food items, as well as regional wines. By the entrance, there is a counter displaying desserts. A small terrace shaded by an old tree is just outside.

Name: ice Q
Description: Beyond its sleek design, this large glass cube delights with a spectacular panoramic view of the mountains. The restaurant is located on the ground floor and proposes a modern tasting menu (vegetarian version available) as well as an à la carte selection of more classic dishes such as beef consommé, Wiener schnitzel and rib-eye steak. The service is friendly and attentive. Alternatively, tapas are served in the lounge on the top floor. Diners can also head outside to the lovely terraces. When it comes to wine, the PINO 3000 is attention worthy – it is aged at this altitude, over 3 000m above sea level! The well-curated wine list includes a decent selection of picks available by the glass. This incredible site also served as a filming location for the James Bond film Spectre. 007 Elements cinematic installation is right next to the restaurant – well worth a visit!

Name: Starcke Haus
Description: This restaurant boasts a truly unique location, clinging to the side of a steep slope – and affording a magnificent view over Graz! In what used to be a winegrower's house (built in 1820), your charming hosts, Manuela and Milivoj Novak, are at your service. He is the chef but also assists Manuela front of house. Their single surprise menu is served to all guests, beginning at 7pm. You can opt to have five or seven courses featuring dishes such as halibut with Beluga caviar, saffron beurre blanc and courgette. Amuse-bouche is included, and a cheese course can be added for an additional charge. Arrive a little earlier to take in the fantastic view of the city from the small terrace. There are three ways to get here: on foot along the Schlossbergsteig, on the Schlossbergbahn funicular followed by a 5min walk, or the lift up through the mountain to the Clock Tower, a nearby landmark.

Name: Pichlmaiers zum Herkner
Description: Well worth a trip to the outskirts of the city. The inn formerly run by famous Viennese chef Heinz Herkner has been given a successful makeover that combines modernity and tradition – this applies to the warm and charming setting as well as the food. The Austrian and classic French dishes are peppered with modern touches. The pretty terrace extends over two floors.

Name: Kommod
Description: This popular restaurant serves a set menu – you can decide to have five or six courses and whether or not you want fish and meat. Salzburg caviar, cheese from the trolley and wine pairings are available upon request. The kitchen places great emphasis on carefully selected, high-quality ingredients, with vegetables grown locally. The chef personally presents and explains each dish to diners. Temporary art exhibitions make for an extra point of interest.

Name: Sonnenstüble
Description: Housed in Hotel Birkenhöhe, this restaurant enjoys a tranquil location and is run by two generations of the Bantel family (Matthias and Felix), who serve up flavoursome modern-inspired dishes with an emphasis on locally sourced seasonal ingredients. Matthias – the father – bakes the delicious bread. Diners are also treated to friendly, attentive service and an excellent wine selection that includes some rare finds from Italy and France. Warm wood panelling and a tiled stove make for a cosy atmosphere. Tip: Request table no 32 for a stunning view of the Widderstein and Bärenkopf mountains. A small lunch menu is available daily until 2pm, and coffee and cake are served 2-5pm.

Name: Infinity The Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Located in the architecturally striking Scheiblhofer The Resort hotel, this stylish modern restaurant is nestled amid the vineyards. The glass-walled dining area affords stunning views while you savour contemporary cuisine with a Pannonian twist. The menu features dishes such as hamachi sashimi with caviar, apricots, passion fruit, yellow pepper, leche de tigre and maize, or Pannonian pike-perch bisque. The property also boasts a winery, Weingut Scheiblhofer, and wine is also an important part of the experience – the impressive selection naturally includes many of their own making.

Name: AD VINUM
Description: This restaurant done out in a chic modern-Alpine style is part of the small Chalet Resort Sölden, which boasts five cosy and tastefully decorated log cabins. From 4pm, classic fare in the vein of braised veal cheeks or beef tartare is served; from 7pm, the "Gourmet-Menü", comprising four or six courses, draws inspiration from the region (eg "Pike-perch, white cabbage, mustard" or "Venison, carrot, Savoy cabbage"). Diners can opt for a supplementary cheese course. The produce used is almost exclusively regional, as the friendly, well-trained and attentive service team will explain when talking you through the menu. Be sure to ask for their recommendations when it comes to choosing a wine – the cellar contains over 8 000 labels, including many from Austria. Fondue is also served – in an appropriately cosy atmosphere. Tip: Reserve your table!

Name: Rauchkuchl
Description: Established over 100 years ago, this is a charming traditional restaurant with Alpine-style decor that perfectly complements the cuisine. The Bacher family have made it their mission to showcase local flavours. Led by son Tobias, the kitchen team creates a seasonally inspired surprise menu using excellent regional produce, some of which comes from their own garden. The delicious bread served before your meal comes from the family's village bakery. In one of the dining rooms, food is even cooked on an antique wood-fired stove, right before your eyes – the name of the restaurant translates as "Smoke Kitchen". The wine cellar contains a fine selection of Austrian and South Tyrolean wines.

Name: Bergergut
Description: This tasteful restaurant in the charming hotel of the same name promises elegant modern decor and a pleasingly quiet, almost intimate atmosphere, as well as attentive and proficient service, and – last but not least – really good food based on carefully selected ingredients. Quality and craftsmanship shine through in dishes such as creamy ragout of Mühlviertel milk-fed veal lights with Serviettenknödel (bread dumplings). Brunch is served Mon-Sat, Wirtshauskuchl (traditional hearty Austrian fare) at lunchtime, and fine dining in the evening. Sundays feature a "gourmet brunch" with live music, and classic tavern cuisine is served for lunch.

Name: Charles' & Frank's
Description: With its clean lines, exposed concrete and warm wood finishings, the minimalist design of this restaurant feels both elegant and modern.
