The spacious two-storey layout with a bar on the upper level adds architectural intrigue. Large windows afford panoramic views of the surroundings. There is also a lovely terrace. For his seasonally inspired five- or six-course set menu, chef Robert Bauer prepares select ingredients, including local produce, to create contemporary cuisine with a cosmopolitan twist. A vegetarian version is available. On Wednesdays and Thursdays the enticing "Genussmenü für zwei" is a deal for two that includes a bottle of wine. In addition, wine tastings and special evening events are held regularly. The name Charles' & Frank's is a reference to the founders of Peneder, the company in whose building the restaurant is located.

Name: Lois Stern
Description: Maria and Lois Stern have been welcoming diners to their restaurant in a traffic-reduced zone in the centre of Kitzbühel since 1994 and have built up a loyal following. An inviting atmosphere reigns in the modern interior. The focal point is the open kitchen, where the chef-patron cooks up Asian-European fusion dishes. The quality of the ingredients is excellent. In addition to the regular menu, there are daily specials. The friendly proprietress and her well-trained team provide attentive service.

Name: Restaurant SCHLOSSBERG
Description: What a view! It would be worth coming up here if only to drink in the panoramic vista over Graz and far beyond the city limits. The tables right by the floor-to-ceiling windows are particularly popular. Seasonal dishes and classics are served. At lunchtime they have cheaper options, but you can also choose from the evening menu. If you would like to walk, you can get up here on foot via the Schlossbergsteig; alternatively the Schlossbergbahn funicular will get you to the restaurant in just a few minutes. Tip: Take a look at the clock tower or the Schlossberg Museum.

Name: Goldener Hirsch
Description: This restaurant in the eponymous hotel in the old town serves modern dishes that draw on international influences as well as Austrian classics. You can dine à la carte or opt for a set menu (vegetarian option). Be sure to peruse the decent wine list with an emphasis on Austrian labels. A striking white vaulted ceiling, lovely parquet flooring and delightful nods to tradition in the decor contribute to the atmosphere. Parking at Altstadtgarage A.

Name: Kehlberghof
Description: The location overlooking Graz is a real draw – it is about a 15min drive from the city centre up to this friendly restaurant with a gorgeous view. From the fantastic terrace in particular, you can drink in the view over the surrounding meadows and the city. The cuisine is seasonal and uses predominantly regional ingredients. At lunchtime and in the evening there is an à la carte menu plus a surprise menu comprising six or seven courses, and at lunchtime there is also a small menu of the day. The "Wirtshausklassiker" include Frittatensuppe (pancake soup) and Tafelspitz (beef boiled in broth). Charming service.

Name: Dolce Vita
Description: In this compact restaurant in the city centre, you feel a bit like you are on holiday when you taste the Mediterranean cuisine that leans into fish, seafood, house-made pasta and risotto (they do also serve meat). The ingredients take centre stage, with a focus on premium quality, and all of the fish is wild caught. Each dish boils down to just a few components, eg the excellent meagre is accompanied by grilled courgettes and fluffy mashed potatoes; the delicate gnocchi are harmoniously complemented by clams in a white wine broth. In the evening, an ambitious surprise menu comprising five, seven or nine courses is served; the lighter lunch menu is somewhat more limited - the dinner set menu is also available on request. The wine list includes a selection of orange and natural wines. There is a cosy "living room" atmosphere, and friendly service is also part of the deal.

Name: SHIKI Brasserie & Bar
Description: This minimalist-style brasserie with its large terrace is SHIKI’s less formal eatery. It offers a wider range of dishes from miso soup to tempura and sushi – the latter prepared before you as you sit at the sushi bar.

Name: LABSTELLE
Description: An appealingly upmarket bistro setting with a relaxed bar area, Labstelle serves ambitious seasonal and regional fare à la carte or as a set menu (conventional or vegan). Examples of the appealing dishes include pickled salmon trout, flank steak, and mushroom goulash. The chef makes a point of working with high-quality produce from Austria. Reduced menu at lunchtime. Gorgeous verdant courtyard.

Name: Pastamara - Bar con Cucina
Description: Housed in the luxurious Ritz-Carlton, Vienna, this restaurant allies the hotel's classic elegance and a modern feel. The pleasingly professional team serve traditional Sicilian cuisine with a modern twist. There are no compromises when it comes to the quality of the ingredients, as shown in dishes such as vitello tonnato and spaghetti gambero e limone – the expertly prepared pasta also deserves a mention. A highlight for dessert is the cannolo siciliano. In addition to the à la carte selection, a six-course surprise menu is available in the evening. There is also an appealing, moderately priced two-course lunch deal. There is additional seating at the large open bar in the middle of the room.

Name: Luckys Restaurant Haus am Hang
Description: The "place to be" is a pretty apt way to describe this restaurant from which you can take in a wonderful view of the lake (Wolfgang See), Sankt Gilgen and the surrounding mountains. As you can imagine, the sophisticated terrace is coveted in summer… and then there is the good food added into the mix. Susanne and Lucas Bocsa have been putting their heart and soul into their role as hosts for many years and, over time, have established a chic restaurant where Lucas Bocsa cooks up flavoursome dishes, both classic and international. With the two set menus, "Luckys" and "Luckys All Around the World", you can also dip in and go à la carte. The glass wine cabinet in the entrance area whets your appetite for a good glass of wine off the bat. The friendly and professional service team is headed up by the likeable Susanne.

Name: Erlhof
Description: First mentioned in records in 1137, the Erlhof can look back on a remarkably long history. Since 2002, the Brüggler family has been running this hotel and restaurant set in a beautiful location with a view of Lake Zell and the mountains – the terrace beckons in summer. In the kitchen, father-and-daughter team Josef and Sonja deliver classic cuisine and traditional regional fare with international influences, while mother-and-daughter front-of-house team Renate and Kathrin take good care of their guests. The warm, rustic-style interior complete with vaulted ceilings is inviting; one dining area has an open fireplace. In addition to cosy guestrooms, hotel patrons have private access to the lake just down from the hotel.

Name: Weibel's Wirtshaus
Description: Just a few minutes' walk from St Stephen's Cathedral, this popular spot is the archetypal Viennese restaurant – wonderfully cosy, rustic, simply charming! The lovely garden terrace in the little alley is also inviting. The cuisine is, of course, Viennese, and the wine list, with its emphasis on Austrian labels, is well worth exploring.

Name: SHIKI Japanese Fine Dining
Description: As the name suggests (shiki translates as "four seasons"), this tastefully elegant fine dining restaurant takes its cue from the seasons. The kitchen presents a seven-course set menu made entirely with top-tier ingredients – they deftly marry classic French techniques with Japanese nuances and incorporate regional produce. Prime examples of dishes include Atlantic lobster and egg yolk, turbot and artichoke, and banana and miso. The central location is also fantastic, with the State Opera around the corner.

Name: Humbachstube
Description: The Alpenhof Jäger hotel's restaurant may be small but what it lacks in size it makes up for in atmosphere! With plenty of wood, a tiled stove and pretty decorations, the cosy and homely Humbachstube is completely in keeping with the rustic charm of the 380-year-old regional-style building in which it is located. In the kitchen, Florian Jäger and his father Martin cook with market produce, creating dishes based on the classic repertoire, such as sirloin of local mountain lamb roasted with aromatics, fresh spinach leaves and potato and Parmesan gnocchi. The wine list is all about Austria's own production. Diners will enjoy friendly, attentive service with a real family touch.

Name: Brandstätter
Description: A real Salzburg institution! The atmosphere in the various dining areas is perfect for a cosy dinner, but in the summer, you might prefer to sit out on the gorgeous terrace. Traditional Austrian fare dominates the menu – be sure to try the wonderful creamy veal goulash with dumplings! For those who prefer something a little more upscale, there are options such as sole and beef fillet. The service comes courtesy of an attentive and well-drilled front-of-house team. Comfortably furnished guestrooms are available for overnight stays. Good to know: You can buy house-made jams to take home. Practical for motorists: There is a large car park right in front of the building.

Name: Spitzbuam
Description: The compact restaurant has a distinctly casual atmosphere fostered by a young team. The small à la carte selection comprises an interesting assortment of modern dishes that win diners over with their full-bodied flavours, from dim sum with prawns to entrecôte or tuna. Alternatively, there is a five-course surprise menu. Consult the wine list for a bottle to accompany your food choice. Friendly, professional waitstaff, joined by the chef, who also gets involved.

Name: Der Unterwirt
Description: This inn dates back to 1490. In cosy, charmingly decorated dining rooms with touches of elegance, or out on the wonderful garden terrace, diners are invited to savour creatively inspired cuisine with regional foundations. Dishes such as "clear mushroom consommé, chive oil, game ravioli", or "red catfish, cucumber, rhubarb" are accompanied by a fine selection of wines with a focus on Austrian winemakers. The guestrooms are a real home away from home.

Name: Hirschen
Description: The concept of sustainability shines through in Jonathan Burger's cuisine. Ingredients are sourced in the region, the fruit and vegetables are predominantly organic or grown by neighbouring farmers, and a nose-to-tail approach is applied to all produce. The latter philosophy is evident, for example, in a dish of grilled chicken hearts, pumpkin, Schupfnudeln (finger-shaped potato dumplings). They also conjure up vegetarian fare, especially in winter when in-house fermentation methods play a major role – for example, their Vetterhof radish with gochugaru and miso broth. The setting is also beautiful: Housed in the Hirschen hotel, a hub of art and tradition that dates back to 1755, the restaurant's tastefully decorated dining rooms draw on a sense of history. At lunchtime, only salads, light bites and cakes are served.

Name: Jägerstube & Walserstube
Description: In the small fine dining restaurant of Hotel Jagdhaus Monzabon, Michael Broger and his team deliver interesting modern cuisine that is big on flavour. Guests will also enjoy the charming service and expert wine recommendations that come courtesy of junior chef and sommelier Tobias Schneider – who also happens to be a sake sommelier. The food, which delves into the region and uses many ingredients from local suppliers, is also decidedly cosmopolitan. From an appealing selection of dishes – for example, "Buddha – red Carabinero prawn, macadamia, Buddha's hand lemon & crustacean bisque" or "Teriyaki venison, morel, pointed cabbage, praline from the leg & kohlrabi" – you can put together a four- to six- course menu of your own. An alternative is the chef's 4-course tasting menu. There is also a cosy bar for an aperitif. Tip: Make a reservation, as there are only a handful of tables.

Name: Trippolt Zum Bären
Address: Hauptplatz 7, Bad Sankt Leonhard im Lavanttal, 9462, Austria
Location: Bad Sankt Leonhard im Lavanttal, Austria
Description: "From the Alps to the Adriatic" is the guiding theme of the Trippolt family restaurant. You could start your culinary journey with a foam soup of aged Parmesan with fried sage leaves and follow that up with spit-roasted young venison accompanied by creamy ricotta gnudi, shallots and strawberries marinated in balsamic vinegar – such dishes highlight not only the kitchen's dedication to the region but also chef Josef Trippolt's passion for hunting. For dessert, the classic apricot dumplings never fail to delight. Diners can choose between two set menus or order individual courses à la carte from each. Check the board for daily specials. The upscale, lovingly designed interior oozes traditional charm and is as pleasing as the secluded verdant courtyard. The small on-site shop sells delicacies including Bärmut, their own hand-crafted "lifestyle aperitif" inspired by vermouth – also the perfect way to kick off your meal.

Name: Mama Konstantina
Description: Following on from Konstantin Filippou and O boufés, chef Konstantin Filippou has established another culinary hotspot in Vienna – this time in the city's 19th district. In a high-ceilinged space with a snazzy open kitchen, diners sit together at a large communal table in the thick of the action. At lunchtime (Mon-Fri), there is a short menu, also available to pick up and take away; in the evening a wonderful à la carte selection awaits you. First-class ingredients go into creating modern Greek fare, in a nod to the chef's roots. The congenial, charming service includes helpful wine recommendations. You may be interested to know that the owner named his restaurant after an olive farmer friend – and inspiration – of his, who hails from Kalamata.

Name: Trattoria Martinelli
Description: Nestled in the courtyard of the splendid Baroque Palais Harrach, this restaurant has been run by the Barbaro family for 40 years. They champion authentic southern Italian cuisine prepared with ingredients they import directly from Italy. The menu spans handmade pasta, ultra-fresh seafood and time-honoured family recipes. The house speciality is branzino, either baked in a salt crust or grilled – for one or two diners. The inviting interior has a lovely vaulted ceiling; outside, there's a charming courtyard terrace. Practical for motorists: You can park at Garage Freyung, just a short walk from the restaurant.

Name: ONYX
Description: The location is fantastic! On the sixth floor of DO & CO Hotel in the avant-garde Haas building, a trendy restaurant with a lounge feel awaits. It boasts a breathtaking view of St Stephen's Cathedral – a table by the large floor-to-ceiling windows is practically a must! The menu features exciting Asian dishes designed for sharing, along with sushi, sashimi and specialities from the Robata grill.

Name: Fuhrmann
Description: An exceptionally friendly restaurant that feels almost neighbourly with its inviting, cosy atmosphere and friendly service. As for Mike Feierabend's truly tasty Austrian cuisine, choose à la carte or go for the five-course set menu that changes every month. At lunchtime there is a cheaper three-course menu. Your hosts will be more than happy to recommend a local wine, but big names from Europe are also served, including some spanning numerous vintages. On that note, it would be remiss not to mention owner and sommelier Herman Botolen, whose genuine passion for wine is plain to see. Tip: be sure to book, as places are limited! In summer, make a beeline for the pleasant terrace in the courtyard.

Name: Rote Bar
Description: This restaurant in the famous Hotel Sacher, a piece of the city's history, epitomises the charm of this great Viennese establishment with its striking red interior, elegant oil paintings and crystal chandeliers. The menu features dishes that draw inspiration from modern culinary trends as well as Viennese and Austrian traditional specialities, including Tafelspitz and Sachertorte. Gorgeous little veranda.

Name: Léontine
Description: An authentic little corner of France, tucked away in a quiet yet central location near the Stadtpark. The bistro atmosphere is charming, the service provided by the owner is cordial and professional, and the modern French cuisine is delicious. The dishes revolve around the seasons and are made with select ingredients. The pair serve a five-course tasting menu and an à la carte selection; at lunchtime there is the more affordable "Menu du Midi" – a three-course set menu. The wine list takes you through the regions of France.

Name: O boufés
Description: Industrial-chic design and soaring ceilings set the tone in this inviting modern bistro, complemented by a cosy bar area for pre-dinner drinks that adds to the laid-back, welcoming vibe. The kitchen serves Mediterranean-Greek inspired dishes, reflecting the cultural heritage of owner Konstantin Filippou, whose fine dining restaurant happens to be located right next door. The dishes are usually served as smaller portions, making them ideal for sharing. For the main course, you can choose between meat, fish and veggie options, which change periodically. There is also a pleasant outdoor dining area.

Name: Meissl & Schadn
Description: Here, the Wiener schnitzel is the obvious choice – it's best to order it "mit allen Schikanen" (with all the trimmings)! At this attractive restaurant on the Ring that encircles Vienna's old town, good food is accompanied by classical music, Viennese service culture and an elegant yet pleasantly down-to-earth atmosphere. In the open kitchen (which is also visible from outside), you can see the schnitzels being pounded. Why not take part in the weekly schnitzel course. There is even a book for sale: The Wiener Schnitzel Love Book.

Name: Schulhaus Tirol
Description: The steep approach to this beautiful inn situated above the village is well worth the effort – both for the fantastic view of the valley and for the delicious food. Classic cuisine and traditional regional fare are served here, in the form of aromatic dishes packed with flavour. The menu features local char as well as Tristan rock lobster, Tauern lamb two ways, and a classic Wiener schnitzel. Diners can also look forward to a good selection of wines. An experienced team provide friendly service; cosy atmosphere.

Name: FUXBAU
Description: This building's traditional shingle façade demonstrates its affinity with the region, as does its smart interior drawing on modern straight lines and natural materials such as wood and stone. Markus Grittle conjures up cuisine that also takes its cue from the region. In the evening, the interesting set menu is formed of three to five courses (dishes include THE ELEGANT FISH – sturgeon, carrot, purslane); at lunchtime, a three-course version is served. Slightly more traditional fare is available à la carte. The terrace affords a view of the ski slopes. Overnight accommodation is to be had at the Fuxbau Lodges and, just around the corner, the Das Johann hotel, through which you can also book the Arlberg Lodges.

Name: Lechtaler Stube
Description: This restaurant is located in the car-free village of Oberlech, more precisely in the Burghotel (an almost legendary place that started off as a small milk bar in the 1960s), right by the ski slope. In a cosy and tastefully designed setting, you can savour classic and regionally influenced dishes for lunch and dinner. Examples include beef tartare made from local fillet of beef, brook char fillet cooked on a salt stone, or pink-roasted venison crown from the hotel's own hunting grounds. In the evening, there is an additional seven-course fine dining set menu, which features mouthwatering creations such as venison entrecôte Rossini with celeriac done three ways and a truffle jus.

Name: Severin*s
Description: The Alpine Retreat is a luxurious little hotel, and this is its restaurant. Blending modern design and Alpine charm, its chic interior has a rather intimate and private feel to it. Tuck into dishes such as horseradish fagottini with celeriac and parsley, or gently cooked char from Zug with cauliflower done two ways and a vegetable jus. Tip: Don't miss out on your chance to try Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake)! In the evening, you can opt for a set menu or order à la carte; at lunchtime, there is a separate à la carte menu. The good food is complemented by an excellent selection of wines. Friendly, attentive and professional service. N.B. Open in winter only.

Name: Heimatbühne
Description: This alternative to the fine dining restaurant at Hotel Trofana Royal also serves culinary delights right next to the ski slope. In an inviting decor, diners can choose from an appealing à la carte selection of freshly prepared Tyrolean dishes. These are made with the finest regional produce, such as Paznaun Highland beef, Diasbach trout and traditional Alpine cheese. Open to the lobby and bar area, and with only a handful of tables, this restaurant is done out in lots of warm wood, creating a pleasantly cosy feel. Exceptionally courteous and friendly service.

Name: Pfeffermühle
Description: If you want to savour classic French-influenced cuisine without having to commit to a set menu, the lovely, cosy restaurant of Hotel Pfefferkorn is just the place for you. The à la carte menu lives up to the establishment's name, incorporating a unique touch of exoticism with one of 13 peppers in each dish. Think carabineros prawn with fruity curry, pickled golden beet, tomato, ginger, and Indian mountain pepper, or pigeon à la royale with pear, parsnip, fried onion, and smoked Malabar pepper. There is no reason to worry that the food will be excessively spicy – chef Christian Wild has a light touch with the pepper, so it enhances the flavour without overpowering it. Diners can also look forward to very friendly service and a fine selection of wines.

Name: Das Vogelhaus
Description: In the heart of Klagenfurt, Stefanie Falkenberg and Fabian Kautz welcome you to their charming little restaurant with vaulted ceilings and a friendly atmosphere. Courtesy of the restaurateur couple, guests enjoy cordial and attentive service as they tuck into flavoursome and varied cuisine. The food is served in the form of a three- to five-course set menu that changes monthly and is prepared with fresh seasonal ingredients, some from the region. The chef likes to come out of his kitchen and present his dishes to diners. On request, there is a wine pairing to match the food or, alternatively, non-alcoholic beverages, which they produce themselves for the most part.

Name: Sicher
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Garden or park,Terrace
Description: This is a great place with a host of standout features: picture a converted old sawmill that is set in a quiet, idyllic location and boasts a sensational garden terrace with tables within spitting distance of the neighbouring forest! Works by various artists adorn this charming spot. The interior, too, is beautiful, combining traditional charm (the elaborately carved wooden ceiling is striking) with modern features. On top of this, the cordial Sicher family are strongly invested in their work in the kitchen and on the restaurant floor. They propose an ambitious and creative seasonal set menu as well as more down-to-earth à la carte dishes, such as whole trout or char. Pride of place is given to the restaurant's own fish farm, as well as produce sourced from its own farm or regional producers. The speciality is the famous "Sicher" char caviar.

Name: Blaue Quelle
Description: Behind the doors of this place that looks like something straight out of a picture book, dine in the pretty, wood-panelled space that oozes rustic charm – or on the gorgeous terrace. Gaby and Alexander Struth are the third generation to take the helm of this family business: she oversees the friendly service; he takes care of the cooking. The menu ranges from Austrian classics including Wiener schnitzel, Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) and Schlutzkrapfen (mezzelune pasta) to fresh pasta dishes and Asian specialities such as spicy Thai soup and Indian butter chicken. Then there is the freshly caught fish from nearby waters! You can also spend the night in one of their well-kept guestrooms.

Name: Gasthof Goldgasse
Description: The dishes served here present a new take on old Salzburg recipes from a cookbook published in 1719! Located in the heart of the old town, the restaurant is incredibly cosy, thanks to its rustic light wood finishings and lovely vaulted ceiling. The friendly service adds to the charming atmosphere. The menu of Austrian classics naturally includes Backhendl (breaded fried chicken), Wiener schnitzel and Topfenschmarrn (shredded curd pancake). Tip: Book well in advance! The 700-year-old building also houses a chic little boutique hotel – you might be tempted to stay a little longer!

Name: Eckel
Description: This family-run restaurant in Vienna's beautiful 19th district has its fair share of regulars who come for its range of classic, flavoursome Austrian specialities. The menu features familiar favourites such as Wiener schnitzel, seasonal dishes with game, but also seafood – the lobster soup is a highlight. The attentive waitstaff and cultivated atmosphere add to the appeal of this place. In summer, be sure to nab a table on the lovely garden terrace.

Name: Glasswing by Alexandru Simon
Description: Chef Alexandru Simon and his team present thoughtfully composed dishes rooted in classic French culinary tradition, meticulously prepared yet never overwrought, and balanced perfectly in flavour. Carefully selected ingredients are given space for their aromas to unfold fully. The regularly changing seven-course set menu features memorable creations such as tortelloni with Swiss chard, sea urchin bisque, hoshigaki and XO sauce, or celery with dulce de leche, coffee and pickled quince – each course enhanced by the astutely curated wine pairings courtesy of maître d' and sommelier Max Populorum and his team. The interior is tasteful, modern and elegant, with designer chairs, gorgeous hardwood floors, original oil paintings and a striking crystal chandelier. Many tables afford views into the open kitchen. Both the restaurant and its home, the exclusive Hotel The Amauris, are named after different species of butterfly.

Name: Das Loft
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The location on the 18th floor of lifestyle hotel SO/Vienna is undeniably spectacular – the view of Vienna is phenomenal! Add to that the attentive, laid-back service and cuisine that draws on modern influences. Great wine selection. There is also a popular cocktail bar.

Name: Veranda Brasserie & Bar
Description: The restaurant in the Hotel Sans Souci is smart and fashionable. It proposes modern Austrian cuisine, which can be ordered à la carte or as a set menu in the form of a "culinary voyage through Austria". Wine list with a focus on Austria and a wide selection of champagnes.

Name: das grander
Description: Diners come here to enjoy the friendly and vibrant atmosphere and delicious food. In the evening, you can compose your own seven-course set menu from the featured dishes or order à la carte. Alternatively, there is a surprise menu comprising three to five courses as well as a set menu of Japanese cuisine. At lunchtime, they serve a reasonably priced set menu that changes on a daily basis, the "weekly gourmet set menu" and a range of à la carte classics such as beef carpaccio, Kalbsrahmbeuschel (calf lights ragout) or Wiener schnitzel, as well as modern fare such as sea bass with saffron foam. In summer, you can sit on the terrace facing a small square laid out like a park. Tip: Your best bet for parking is the underground car park Am Kirchplatz.

Name: Zum Buberl Gut
Description: More than just a pretty face, this gorgeous 17C country estate, located on the outskirts of the city, is also a delightful setting for a delicious meal. The cosy interior marries classic elegance with charming regional touches, creating a welcoming atmosphere. In the summer, the lovely garden beckons. The cuisine is a flavoursome blend of Austrian and Mediterranean influences. The wine list, too, is definitely worth a look. Tip: Come at lunchtime for the small, moderately priced menu available.

Name: Stubn 1972
Description: Just a short walk from the Fleckalmbahn cable car, Minglers Sportalm hotel boasts tastefully decorated guestrooms, a spa and this charming little restaurant with just four tables. The dining space is done out in light, warm wood from floor to ceiling, which makes for a cosy setting. The kitchen team conjures up a set menu that draws on modern culinary trends – you are free to choose the number of courses. You will be skilfully looked after by your host, including good wine recommendations from a predominantly Austrian list.

Name: Wälder Stube 1840
Description: This restaurant is named after the year in which Das Schiff, the tasteful hotel that houses it, was founded. Done out in an abundance of wood and featuring delightful decorative details such as pictures and lamps, the dining nooks with their classically laid tables are the epitome of cosiness. In his set menu, chef Bernd Reimer places great emphasis on regionality, but also incorporates international flavours. The quality of the produce is exquisite – as exemplified by Black cod with miso, salicornia, chanterelles and wild garlic gnocchi. Dominated by labels from the tri-border region, the wine list boasts plenty of tempting options. Service with a personal touch adds to the charm of the overall experience.

Name: Gourmetrestaurant Fuggerstube
Description: The historical Fuggerstube – dating back to the 15C – is a real gem of a place. The beautiful wood panelling and the old stove cultivate a cosy atmosphere and old-world charm. There are just four tables, at which diners tuck into a seasonal set menu packed with regional ingredients. The wine pairings recommended to go with each course are excellent, and the wine cellar has quite a few bottles from which to choose. The restaurant is located in Der Böglerhof, a wellness hotel that has expanded over the years.

Name: Post Lech
Description: The venerable Gasthof Post has a series of charming Alpine-style dining areas, and in all of them the same à la carte menu is served: an ambitious selection of Austrian classics such as Tafelspitz and Wiener schnitzel, as well as international dishes. An exclusive fine dining set menu is served in the Jägerstube upon advance booking. Diners can also look forward to a good wine list and attentive service. Individually decorated guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Haller's
Description: Perched in a fantastic high-altitude location, Haller's Geniesserhotel boasts lovely, comfortable guestrooms and a spacious spa, as well as this appealing fine dining restaurant with a welcoming Alpine atmosphere. At lunchtime, a selection of sophisticated à la carte dishes is on offer; in the evening, diners take their pick from the set menu. The tempting options range from classics like Wiener schnitzel to creations such as tail of rump, celeriac two ways, curd cheese and amaranth pastry pockets. The wine list with a focus on Austria is also enticing. And don't miss out on the terrace with its magnificent mountain view!

Name: Wunderkammer - Herbarium
Description: Located near the Schlegelkopf piste, the luxurious Almhof Schneider hotel, built in 1929, is home to this fine dining restaurant, which is only open during the winter. At lunchtime and in the evening, you can enjoy Austrian cuisine with international influences: the menu includes Fiaker goulash, Wagyu steak, Riesling Beuschel (offal ragout) with bread dumplings and, for dessert, Kaiserschmarrn (shredded pancake). The wine list, comprising over 1 200 labels, is superb. Meals are served in two tastefully decorated dining spaces: Wunderkammer, designed by artist Paul Renner, and Herbarium, featuring beautiful woodcuts by Christian Thanhäuser.

Name: Gasthof Adler
Description: This pretty inn, established in 1852, embodies the true spirit of hospitality – and has been doing so for seven generations. The old timber chalet has had a lovely contemporary extension added, without any of its historical character being lost along the way. Whether in the cosy parlours or out in the gorgeous Kastaniengarten, diners tuck into flavoursome seasonal cuisine in a regional vein. Fruit, vegetables, salads and herbs come from the own garden, meat from the own farm, game from the nature park... Cordial and professional service. Food items made in-house can also be purchased to enjoy at home. Well-appointed guestrooms and a holiday flat can be booked for overnight stays.

Name: Verwallstube
Address: Kandaharweg 9, Sankt Anton am Arlberg, 6580, Austria
Description: At an elevation of 2 085m, the gondola ride up here (free with your reservation) is even worthwhile for non-skiers. In addition to the breathtaking view, you can expect ambitious cuisine made from high-quality ingredients that doesn't limit itself to a specific style – rather it showcases traditional, regional, Mediterranean and even Asian influences. Appetising options include yellowfin tuna sashimi, Wiener schnitzel and risotto alla carbonara. The exceedingly friendly and charming waitstaff will be happy to recommend the right wine from the extensive list.

Name: Winterstellgut
Description: It is worth making the journey here for the stunning views of the surrounding mountains from the sun-drenched plateau some 1 000m above Annaberg – and they are even better from the terrace. At this 16C farm building, dine in cosy, rustic-style nooks or on the light-filled veranda. The kitchen is open all day, serving traditional regional and seasonal cuisine that draws on the odd international influence, such as Kalbsrahmbeuscherl mit Semmelknöde (veal offal ragout with bread dumplings) and lobster gyoza with an Asian-style bisque. Alternatively, opt for the set menu. Everything is made with good-quality, fresh ingredients, including preserves. Tip: House-made goods can be purchased to enjoy at home. For overnight stays, there are a few attractive guestrooms and suites, plus a natural pond for bathing.

Name: Meissl & Schadn
Description: The schnitzel reigns supreme at this restaurant in the heart of the old town. Even from the outside you can peer into the open kitchen and see the house speciality, Wiener schnitzel, being prepared. The rest of the menu is worth perusing too, with other Austrian classics such as Tafelspitz, Esterházy lentils, or goose (when in season). And be sure to save room for dessert – traditional treats like Salzburger Nockerlor classic apple strudel are too good to miss! Highlights also include a nicely curated wine list and professional service that's both warm and attentive. The setting has its own appeal: inside, stylish details across two floors create a welcoming brasserie feel, and outside, the inviting terrace opens directly onto the iconic Getreidegasse. Tip: Leave your car in the multi-storey car park Altstadtgarage A.

Name: Murmeli
Description: This restaurant on the ground floor of the hotel of the same name serves ingredient-led cuisine in which traditional regional dishes are allied with international influences. Service is provided by a charming and experienced front-of-house team. Diners can also look forward to an unrivalled view of the Lech mountain landscape – especially from the terrace, of course! But you can also enjoy the view from the tables in the refined inside space. The hotel's cosy guestrooms are conducive to booking an overnight stay.

Name: La Fenice
Description: As well as tasteful, individually designed guestrooms, Hotel Arlberg is home to this elegant restaurant, which is accessed via a separate entrance. Ornate details such as warm wood finishings, a partially painted ceiling, stylish upholstered armchairs and classic-style wall lamps create a wonderful atmosphere, which is complemented by experienced and attentive service. Then there is the Alpine-Mediterranean cuisine, which they dub "Monte e Mare". The tasting menu, comprising five to eight courses, also comes in a vegetarian version. One outstanding dish is the tender, juicy lobster medallion in a courgette "coat", accompanied by an aromatic blood orange gelée and a vadouvan foam that harmonises perfectly with notes of Indian spice. The fantastic wine list, which is predominantly Austrian, Italian and French, includes over 1 000 labels, with around 15 000 bottles stored in the cellar.

Name: Aurelio
Description: This is the restaurant of the luxurious Aurelio Hotel & Chalet Lech, which slightly overlooks the village right next to the Schlegelkopf piste. The interior is chic and the gorgeous terrace affords fabulous views of the 2 557m-high Omeshorn. The polished and attentive service really enhances the refined yet relaxed atmosphere. At lunch and dinner, the daily à la carte menu features mouthwatering options such as pan-fried char with fregola sarda, beurre blanc, peas and dill, or the classic Wiener schnitzel. Fri-Tue evenings, the team led by head chef Karl Eggetsberger presents a modern and creative fine dining set menu by pre-order (minimum 24hr), with the number of courses tailored to your preference: "Intro", "Classic" or "Grand". Signature dishes such as chamois meat with Alpine salsa, spruce tips and black garlic demonstrate finesse, balance and a clear culinary identity. N.B. The restaurant is normally only open in winter.

Name: Schulhus
Description: In a building that once housed the village school, this restaurant has a history that stretches far back. Gabi and Herbert Strahammer never tire of treating their guests to a relaxed yet stylish gourmet experience – their accessible cuisine is always connected to the region. In a friendly, pared-back ambience, they serve pleasantly uncomplicated, fresh and flavourful dishes, such as ravioli with Langenegger Schottenkäse smoked cheese, herbs, spinach, lemon sauce, or pike from Lake Constance, spinach leaves, roast vegetables, ricotta gnocchi. On-point wine recommendations from the owner.

Name: Picea
Description: Mountains, snow, a fantastic panoramic terrace and great food to boot! With its fresh and down-to-earth regional cuisine, this cosy Alpine-style restaurant at Burg Vital Resort makes a great alternative to Griggeler Stuba. The very friendly and competent waitstaff serve up delicious dishes such as Alpine char with red lentils, artichoke, tomato and winter tarragon. This is complemented by the same sensational wine selection as is served in the fine dining restaurant.

Name: Oniriq
Description: Located in the city centre, on the Old Town side of the Inn River, this is a compact restaurant with clean, modern decor. Working in an open kitchen, the chefs craft two distinct set menus – one vegetarian, the other with meat and/or fish. The cuisine is ambitious, rooted in classic culinary tradition yet refined with modern techniques. Select ingredients go into harmoniously flavoursome dishes such as "Alpine prawn, Swiss chard, peanut, plum" and "venison, porcini, spinach, berbere". Fine wine pairings and homemade non-alcoholic beverage pairings available. Attentive, professional service.

Name: Hospiz Alm
Address: St. Christoph 18, Sankt Anton am Arlberg, 6580, Austria
Description: Just so you know: This place is a haven for wine connoisseurs! The Gothic wine cellar is a real treasure trove, boasting a unique collection of large bottles that is world-famous, not least for its Bordeaux selection. Magnums, primats: you name it, they have it. Be sure to take a look at the impressive Wine Dome with its private dining table for exclusive tastings. In the restaurant itself, a typical ski hut feel prevails at lunchtime, but in the evening, it's all about fine dining in a lovely cosy setting brimming with Alpine charm.

Name: Sunrise
Description: One of the most attractive restaurants in the city centre, Sunrise occupies the ground floor of an old Bourbon palazzo, extending right to the back of the building where you’ll find the delightful “literary veranda” and, beyond the large windows, a beautiful outdoor space surrounded by a garden planted with citrus trees. The menu has an exclusive focus on fish, with a combination of classic options and light, modern dishes, while an entire page is dedicated to raw fish and seafood. The wine list includes several champagnes.

Name: Mammà Isola di Capri
Description: Situated within the multi-functional Sondo building (also home to a museum, offices and exhibition spaces), this large restaurant decorated in contemporary, post-industrial style provides the backdrop for chef Raffaele Amitrano’s Mediterranean cuisine which is strongly influenced by the flavours of Campania. His plin pasta dish pays tribute to the region and is particularly interesting thanks to ingredients such as cacio cheese, pepper and raw prawns. Make sure you arrive early if you want to visit the building and maybe even take advantage of the large sharing table.

Name: Al Pozzo
Description: The cuisine at this restaurant is almost exclusively based on fish and seafood, with three main points of focus – an extensive array of raw dishes; ageing of almost all the fish to accentuate flavour and texture (as well as making the skin pleasantly crispy); and the grilling of some courses. Top-quality ingredients and delicious desserts complete the picture.

Name: Acqua & Sale
Description: The enthusiastic owners of Acqua & Sale have transformed what was originally a simple fishmonger’s into a restaurant with the addition of an informal, well-appointed dining room on the side. Here, guests enjoy unfussy fresh fish dishes, including an array of raw options and Mediterranean recipes with the occasional personal touch. Recipes include grilled octopus with black broccoli and wine-fermented plums, and porchetta-style tuna with a green sauce, fried new potatoes and sweet and sour peppers. The perfect choice for fish-lovers!

Name: Dasuke
Address: 375-2 Siwei Road, Da'an District, Taipei, 106, Taiwan
Description: The chef, who hails from Niigata, Japan, reinterprets flavours from his home prefecture using first-rate local ingredients, such as root vegetables in a flavourful stew known as noppe. À la carte is available, but the omakase is where the magic lies. Try Das burger – a deep-fried patty of varying ingredients ranging from ground beef to sashimi in a house-made bun. The impressive sake list offers some 60 by-the-glass options with detailed tasting notes.

Name: fumée
Address: B3, Regent Hotel, 3, Lane 39, Section 2, Zhongshan North Road, Zhongshan District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: The sister restaurant of the Osakan yakitori institution Ichimatsu sports a dark colour scheme, reminiscent of an opera house. The young Japanese chef sources local poultry such as Hsinchu free-range chicken, and Wenchang chicken for his kebabs along with local herbs like prickly ash and maqaw. The set menu with 10+ courses showcases an array of textures and flavours. Consider paying extra for rare cuts such as shiro reba and kinkan.

Name: J Parc
Address: 1 Dexing Street, Sanmin District, Kaohsiung, 80751, Taiwan
Description: After formal training in the US, the chef-owner launched J Parc in 2023. His 10-course prix-fixe aligns with the seasons, presenting audacious creations that celebrate local vegetables and Japanese seafood, underpinned by French, Italian and American techniques. Mildly sweet bread made with chestnut flour is a nod to the harvest season. Ask for counter seats for up-close views of the chef at work in the semi-open kitchen.

Name: Yung Yen
Address: 528 Chenggong 1st Road, Cianjin District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan
Description: Formerly known as Yun Lai Fang, this place was renamed and relocated to this address in 2024. The light-drenched room over two levels has wooden furnishings that impart a home-like feel. Regulars will find all their favourites on the menu; these are impeccably made to order by the chef, the son of Yun Lai Fang's founding chef. His signature scrambled egg comes with bouncy, umami-laden shrimps enrobed in silky half-set egg.

Name: Su Lai Chuan
Address: 4, Lane 176, Section 3, Heping West Road, Wanhua District, Taipei, Taiwan
Description: Famous for ba-wan and taro cake, this institution celebrated its 70th anniversary with a facelift in 2024. The third-generation owner still makes ba-wan like his grandparents did – freshly ground rice milk is poured into a bowl before a filling of pork shin, shiitake, chestnut and bamboo shoot is added. The steamed dumpling is then poached in oil, and drizzled with a sweet bean paste and miso sauce. Add garlic purée or home-made chilli sauce for an extra kick.

Name: Gallina
Description: A delightful bistro-restaurant that focuses on the quality of its cuisine as well as the connection between art and gastronomy. In this vibrant setting, featuring elegant marble tables and a completely open-view kitchen where you can observe the chefs at work, chef George Rekatsinas combines French and Greek traditions in his elegant and impressively textured cuisine. His dishes include fish, seafood and a varied selection of meats (including an array of matured cuts). A particular highlight on the menu are the raw Greek red prawns from Koilada, served with a hint of freshness and a balanced combination of flavours. The impressive wine list with more than 800 labels from different countries provides the perfect complement to Gallina’s dishes, while a private room on the top floor is available for those seeking a more exclusive and intimate experience.

Name: Merceri
Description: This welcoming bistro, close to the Herakleidon Museum is run by two chefs with experience gained at luxury hotels on the island of Santorini. Here, they showcase their talents through contemporary dishes with an international flavour, but which are based around typical Greek recipes. The offer is available à la carte or in a tasting menu, with wine pairing options.

Name: VERi TABLE
Description: A pleasant French-style bistro away from this delightful city’s main tourist haunts but which comes as a pleasant surprise thanks to its cuisine and friendly service. In this informal space, which is nonetheless elegantly decorated in dark tones and bathed in subdued lighting, savour dishes inspired by Provençal cuisine with a Mediterranean touch. True gourmet-lover and chef Aladin Parodi infuses his dishes with superb technical skill, with a focus on top-quality ingredients, as witnessed by the duck à l’orange – an absolute must here. The dining room is overseen by his wife, Christine Parodi, who devotes herself to providing exquisite service as well as managing the enticing wine cellar, featuring an extensive choice of French labels.

Name: GB Roof Garden
Address: 1A Vasileos Georgiou A street, Athens, 105 64, Greece
Description: If you’re on the lookout for a restaurant that is a little bit special, this could be an excellent option on the 8th floor of the Hotel Grande Bretagne, thanks to its elegant setting and superb picture-postcard views of the Acropolis from both the delightful terrace and dining room. Despite not being overly extensive, the Mediterranean-inspired à la carte focuses specifically on fresh seasonal ingredients, with a special emphasis on Italian cooking, including a small section dedicated to pasta and risotto.

Name: Annie Fine Cooking
Description: This attractive neighbourhood restaurant, located along a tranquil tree-lined street away from the busy tourist heart of the city, boasts an everyday, informal ambience, along with a simple pavement terrace and striking touches of color in the dining room, with its open kitchen. It’s mainly local clientele flock here to enjoy dishes from the concise à la carte that are an updated take on Greek recipes and based around fresh, seasonal and locally sourced ingredients that showcase the country’s cuisine to the full.

Name: Linou Soumpasis & Co.
Description: A casual and contemporary “new-age taverna” in the central Psiri district of the city where it occupies a former candle shop (whose products are still sold here to this day). Greek cooking is based around unpretentious yet delicious dishes that always showcase the restaurant’s commitment to organic ingredients.

Name: Ovio
Description: Run by celebrity chef Panos Ioannidis, this restaurant is, without doubt, an excellent choice for those exploring the busy streets of central Athens. In this spacious setting, divided into three dining areas (one on the ground floor, a few tables upstairs, plus a pleasant terrace) the chef offers a menu based around Italian cuisine. This includes homemade pastas, such as the delicious Gnocchi with a velvety sauce, diced pear, grated walnuts and finished with gorgonzola in two textures. These are complemented by meat dishes and pizzas cooked in the wood-fired oven, plus an extensive selection of Italian wines and a balcony where guests can savour an array of impressive cocktails.

Name: Simul
Description: Personality, irreverence, risk, youthfulness, technique and quality are the words that spring to mind when we think of Simul, a restaurant that is always focused on cuisine prepared “in-situ” with the very best seasonal ingredients. In the informal dining room, chef Nikos Thomas (perhaps better known for his appearances on MasterChef) offers his guests a choice between a continually evolving and creative à la carte and an impressive tasting menu.

Name: Aleria
Description: Time seems to have stood still in this beautiful restaurant occupying a neo-Classical residence from the mid 1800s, where the delightful patio, contemporary decorative features and 19C spirit come as a pleasant surprise. Here, the focus is on updated Greek cuisine presented in two menus (both with 5- or 6-course options): one entitled Earth & Sea, the other, the vegetarian-based Garden & Nature.

Name: Aneton
Description: Aneton’s location in a narrow street tucked away in the historic centre of Athens is perfect for a break after exploring the city’s array of tourist sights. In this charming restaurant, decorated in soft tones and bathed in lots of natural light, chef Vasilis Zois conjures up vibrant and attractive cuisine with a strong Greek identity and memories of his childhood. The cooking here, which is dictated by the seasons and changes frequently, features fresh dishes prepared with the best local and seasonal ingredients. In addition to the friendly and welcoming service, Aneton also has a small bar where you can enjoy its exclusive cocktails and a superb selection of local Greek wines.

Name: Dolli's
Description: If the thought of enjoying a pleasant meal with an idyllic view appeals to you, then this could be the place. This restaurant is located on the fifth floor of the luxury The Dolli at Acropolis hotel, a historic mansion that has been completely remodelled and boasts picture-postcard views of the Acropolis. The menu here is a combination of Mediterranean cuisine with Asian options prepared by a chef who conjures up dishes within full view of guests in the dining room. Precise and meticulously presented, his dishes are always based around top-quality seasonal ingredients. The gourmet experience is more extensive in the evening and is complemented by the extensive array of wines, including labels from leading wine estates as well as artisanal vineyards.

Name: SENSE
Description: Located on the 7th floor of the AthensWas Hotel, SENSE boasts a stunning panoramic terrace with truly spectacular views of the Acropolis at sunset. The cuisine is centred around two tasting menus plus an additional vegetarian option, on which the innovative dishes are a fusion of international cooking and authentic Greek flavours, with plenty of creative detail as an added touch. Many of the aromatic herbs used in the dishes here are grown on the roof terrace.

Name: Vezené
Description: If you’re a fan of wood-fired cuisine, we recommend a visit to Vezené (located next to the Evangelismos metro station), a bistro-style restaurant with plenty of elegant decorative touches and an impressive glass porch. The menu is based around traditional Greek cuisine, in which fire plays a key role and via which the majority of the ingredients are prepared, endowing dishes with their unique flavour. It also includes various types of seafood sourced from local producers, as well as aged meats and impressive pastas. At the weekend, the generously portioned Sunday roast is available, which can be enjoyed with all the family, along with the restaurant’s famous signature dessert and a real must: Ari's Deal Closer!

Name: Varoulko Seaside
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant with an authentic maritime flavour, this eatery overlooking the small yet attractive port of Mikrolimano will come as a pleasant surprise. Here, the relaxing ambience is in perfect harmony with superb views of the fishing boats moored out front. Traditionally, Piraeus is known as the port of Athens, hence the plethora of tavernas and restaurants specialising in fish and seafood located here. Varoulko Seaside follows the same influence, although chef Lefteris Lazarou takes his maritime cuisine to another level. The freshest ingredients are key to his cuisine which is based around the catch of the day (sea bass, red mullet, grouper, tuna, shrimp, prawns etc) and presented on an à la carte and two tasting menus.

Name: see|ds
Description: A restaurant with plenty of personality located in a residential district of the city and which takes its name from the combinations of the word “see” and the initials of young chef Dimos Samouraki to create “Seeds”. The simple, modern cuisine, centred around locally sourced seasonal ingredients and a minimalist aesthetic, is showcased on two tasting menus (Short Talk and Long Story) that show French culinary influence and vary only in their number of courses. In addition, an interesting vegan option is also available. For those who prefer more exclusivity, the floor upstairs has a loft with an elegant dining space for 10 guests, where they can enjoy a more personalised experience seated next to the superb wine cellar.

Name: Okio
Description: Located just a few minutes from a number of the city’s main tourist attractions, this charming corner restaurant is perfect for a drink and a pleasant meal after a day's sightseeing. Here, chef Panagiotis Giakalis, ably supported by right-hand man George Tsolkas, creates contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with a strong hint of Asia, resulting in carefully balanced dishes and unexpected textures. Prepared using seasonal ingredients, dishes can be enjoyed via the à la carte and two tasting menus, and include perfectly prepared dishes such as bonito tuna with almonds, watercress, maple and sweet chilli sauce. In addition to the charming lounge space, you can also enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of a table on the terrace. The private space upstairs can also be booked for larger groups.

Name: Esthiō
Description: This restaurant, the name of which translates as “eat and treat” in Ancient Greek, occupies a charming neo-Classical building dating back to 1931 close to the heart of the city. Here, Albanian-born chef Elvi Dimitris Zyba curates Balkan-inspired cuisine which offers a fusion between different cultures and combines the traditional with the contemporary. His cooking takes its inspiration from recipes that his mother used to prepare when he was a child to which he adds a more sophisticated and refined touch. Examples include the traditional “Giaourtotavas”, made with lamb sweetbreads, yoghurt and rice, and various seafood-based options, such as the Octopus stew, wrapped in handmade filo pastry with a sublime salmon roe cream. Desserts also have a Balkan touch, such as the Grape juice cream served with grape must cookies.

Name: Sir Elly's
Address: 13F, The Peninsula Hotel, Bund 32, 32 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Named after the hotel's founder, the opulent space punctuated by red accents commands gorgeous river views. The upscale ambiance makes this a perfect venue for a date. The kitchen turns local ingredients into original creations with bold flavours, dramatic plating and modern Asian twists. The substantial wine list will keep any oenophile happy. If you're not quite ready to call it a night, consider heading to the rooftop bar for digestifs.

Name: Yè Shanghai
Address: 3F, Infinitus Mall, 168 Hubin Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Though moved into a shopping mall, the grey-brick façade is reminiscent of Shikumen architecture style. In stark contrast, the interior sports velvet sofas in gold and modern art for a touch of glamour. Start your night with creative cocktails from the bar. Then sample their Shanghainese classics like braised pork belly, sautéed shrimps with wild garlic, or xiao long bao. Try also hairy crab dishes such as stuffed crab shell when available.

Name: Pop
Address: 7F, Bund 3, 3 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Blue and white sofas work well with the wood and marble décor to exude a casual, yet elegant vibe, but it’s the breathtaking river views from the terrace that leave everyone in awe. Classic European choices abound on the menu, especially grilled meats and seafood. Try the house-made foie gras pâté, or pasta with black truffle. Pop also serves brunch every morning – so you can start your day with bacon and eggs with gorgeous vistas in the gentle morning sun.

Name: Lin Jiang Yan
Address: 216 Fucheng Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Remodelled from a heritage building (c 1902), this restaurant is perfect for banquets and entertainment. The main area and private rooms all share the same river views. The young head chef, who used to work for a hotel in Shanghai, updates traditional Jiangzhe cooking with creative twists. Pre-order his Fukubukuro Yanduxian – tofu skin pouches stuffed with ground pork and shepherd's purse in a rich broth of cured and fresh pork with bamboo shoots.

Name: Xin Yuan Lou
Address: Building No.4, InterContinental Ruijin Hotel, 118 Ruijin Er Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A 1920s villa plays host to this Cantonese restaurant boasting plenty of old-world charm thanks to its period furniture, fireplace and Chinese artwork. It’s spread over two floors and includes a bar, a lounge, a tea room and several private rooms. The menu is mostly Cantonese with some Shanghainese dishes. Try marinated meats, roast goose, salt-baked chicken or char siu pork. Seasonal offerings, like the mushroom menu in autumn, need pre-ordering.

Name: Wei Xiang Zhai (Yandang Road)
Address: 14 Yandang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: For over 80 years customers have been flocking here for its noodles. No one seems to mind the congested, somewhat tired room – just as long as the flavour in the bowl remains unchanged. The menu is set in two frames: noodles on one side, toppings on the other. Those in the know order a bowl of noodles dressed in sesame sauce, alongside spicy chopped pork topping and beef clear broth. Chilled noodles also hit the spot in summer.

Name: Hakkasan
Address: 5F, Bund 18, 18 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Though its name means Hakka people, this chic restaurant on the Bund serves modern Cantonese fare with Western influences, but not necessarily of Hakka origin. The must-try Peking duck with caviar boasts interesting layers of flavours. Top-notch ingredients are used for the hand-made dim sum; and the dim sum set lunch offers great value. Don’t miss the cocktails featuring local liquors. The sweeping river views are a beauty to behold.

Name: Legend Taste (Jingan)
Address: 1025 Kangding Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: The no-frills space is dotted with photos of Yunnan and blue tie-dyed tablecloths; the style of service is equally simple. The team use mushrooms and herbs extensively in cooking inspired by ethnic Dai tradition. Slow-cooked for at least five hours, the flavoursome beef broth warms the heart and soul. In mushroom season, don't miss dishes such as sautéed porcini and chanterelles with green chilli. Try the rice noodles with savoury tofu pudding, too.

Name: Cuivre
Address: 1502 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Echoing its name, this welcoming bistro in the French Concession amusingly features copper trimming on its walls and dinnerware. The kitchen excels in reinventing bistro classics with modern techniques and subtle Asian twists. L’agneau, or rack of lamb, is nicely charred on the outside and juicy on the inside. Round off with baba Zacapa. The wine list offers vintages from French small-batch wineries, alongside affordable new world choices.

Name: Coquille
Address: 29 Mengzi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Next to Italian trattoria Scarpetta, its younger sibling, Coquille, occupies two floors. On the seafood-focused menu, French classics come with subtle Asian twists. Signature dishes include foie gras crème brûlée and oven-roasted Dungeness crab. Finish off with coconut soufflé – golden and fluffy and with sea salt coconut ice cream on the side. Besides à la carte choices, there is a set menu for two. The beef Wellington needs to be pre-ordered.

Name: Nan Xing Yuan
Address: Building 12, 1728 Middle Huaihai Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Helmed by a team of Sichuan chefs, this restaurant takes a deposit upon booking and serves only tailored menus, which diners pre-order. A typical menu builds a progression of flavours with classics such as napa cabbage in chicken consommé, and sautéed shredded pork with green chilli. Authentic dishes are meticulously prepared to showcase the 24 flavour profiles of Sichuanese cooking. Only private rooms are available, and reservations are a must.

Name: Scilla
Address: 504 Panyu Road, Changning, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: Scilla is a blue-flowered Mediterranean plant, a nod to the fact that this restaurant focuses on the region's food, but with a twist – local ingredients, especially seafood, are given the Mediterranean treatment, for a unique fusion cuisine. The signature BBQ Taizhou yellow croaker with bouillabaisse and rouille boasts crispy skin, rich broth and creamy sauce. The underground wine cellar carries some rare finds from the Mediterranean coast.

Name: Yong Jiang Zhen
Address: Sinan Mansions, 55 Sinan Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, 200000, China Mainland
Description: This all-private-room restaurant in a four-storey mansion is furnished with retro glamour. The owner hails from Jiangyin City and his connections with the fishermen along the Yangtze River guarantee a steady supply of the freshest catch. The tapertail anchovy in red sauce tastes sweet and rich without being overly greasy. Braised puffer fish in white broth is another recommendation; the milt and liver are especially delicious.

Name: Jean Georges
Address: 4F, Bund 3, 3 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, 200002, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Those who are familiar with Jean-Georges Vongerichten’s New York flagship will recognise some of the menu items here at his Shanghai outpost, such as toasted egg yolk with caviar, and tuna tartare with avocado. The cooking is light and fragrant, with plenty of choice on offer. The comfortable room comes with views and an open kitchen; it’s warmly lit and run by a well-organised and professional team.

Name: Xuji Seafood (Xuhui)
Address: 500 Zhaojiabang Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Since 1999, the Hunan brand has been expanding its footprint across the nation, and this multi-storey branch is its Shanghai flagship. Thanks to close ties with fishermen and farms, locally and globally, it secures sources for the best-quality and freshest seafood. Try the live scallops from the East China Sea blanched at your table in a boiling, milky sea perch stock. Xuji glass noodles in a casserole are the Hunan speciality you can't miss.

Name: Scarpetta
Address: 33 Mengzi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This two-storey restaurant takes its name from the act of using bread to mop up the last bit of sauce left on the plate. Homemade pizza and pasta, such as pizza vongole, and other specialities like Wagyu carpaccio topped with shaved black truffle slices, mean you’ll certainly not want to waste anything. The last facelift in 2018 left the dining room with a warm and romantic ambiance, making it an ideal choice for a date.

Name: Dining Room
Address: 87F, Park Hyatt, 100 Century Avenue, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This high-ceilinged room with full-length windows affords panoramic river views, while the home-style furniture, warm lighting and booth seating make for a cosy feel. On the menu, Jiangzhe classics meet creative recipes that are rarely found elsewhere, such as steamed belt fish with fermented grains. Nicely pleated xiao long bao with umami-loaded soupy filling are simply unmissable – as are the appetisers.

Name: La Scene Ronde
Address: LG1-13, The Roof, Lane 458, Madang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: As the name suggests, the open kitchen is dramatically lit, like a stage with front-row seats at the semi-circular counter. The single tasting menu changes every season, alongside options of wine, tea or non-alcoholic drink pairings. Well versed in classic French cuisine, the Japanese chef deftly uses local seasonal produce and seafood for unique French fare jazzed up by Asian touches. Try his deeply flavoured Wagyu beef stock, and Ibérico ham sushi.

Name: Frasca
Address: 1F, The Middle House Residences, 366 Shimen Yi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In northeast Italy, a frasca, identifiable by a branch hung over its doorway, was a gathering place for sharing farm-style food. In stark contrast, this stylish hotel restaurant boasts a modern vibe and a menu focused on authentic Italian home-style favourites. The handmade pasta stands out, especially the al dente ravioli. Try their Pinsa Romana and meats roasted on the Josper grill. The wine list has a nice selection of Italian vintages.

Name: Arva
Address: 6161 Yuanjiang Road, Minhang, Shanghai, 201111, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The committed chef passionately advocates a farm-to-table philosophy and reinterprets traditional recipes from various Italian regions with modern touches. From the dazzling array of homemade pasta, be sure to try his ravioli. The airy interior is cosy and elegant; the al fresco barbecue lunch at weekends exudes a backyard party vibe. Arva is nestled in a remote luxury resort, so driving here is the best option. Reservations are mandatory.

Name: Cellar to Table
Address: 1A, 1F, 20 Donghu Road, Xuhui, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: With an Italian chef on board since 2024, this place exuding an appealing wine-bar vibe has a revamped menu that is unmistakably Italian. The dishes are rife with bold flavours and the extensive wine list meanders across the globe. The handmade pasta is perfectly al dente; the grilled Shandong red prawn smoky and juicy; Sichuan tomatoes and Yunnan mushrooms work magic in Italian recipes. On a balmy night, ask for a courtyard table.

Name: 1515 West Chophouse
Address: 4F, Jing An Shangri-La Hotel, 1218 Middle Yan'an Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: They’ve certainly nailed the classic American look at this nicely styled chophouse. Start with a cocktail in the masculine, wood panelled bar before passing by the inviting bakery into the restaurant. All the favourite steakhouse dishes are here, from Caesar salad mixed at the table to steak tartare and cheesecake. However, it’s the grill that takes centre stage – the various cuts of dry-aged Australian beef are chargrilled to perfection.

Name: Villa Le Bec - Bistro 321
Address: 321 Xinhua Road, Changning, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A lovely renovated villa, dating from 1924, is home to this French bistro. It is divided into several rooms, each decorated differently; the garden terrace is a delightful spot for a round of drinks on a balmy night. Classic bistro dishes include an excellent pâté en croute and côte de boeuf prepared barbecue style. From time to time, the kitchen rustles up seasonal creations that feature local Chinese produce prepared in traditionally French ways.

Name: Shanghai Club
Address: L-418, 4F, North Building, HKRI Taikoo Hui, 789 West Nanjing Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: A premium brand from the Jardin de Jade Group, the restaurant serves old Shanghai classics with an emphasis on finesse and attention to detail. Walnut-crusted duck fillet square in bean paste is a rare gem that is painstaking to make. Live seafood is another highlight on the menu, while some Cantonese dim sum are served at lunch. Ask the servers about the seasonal offerings which truly embodying the essence of Shanghainese cooking.

Name: De Xing Guan (Guangdong Road)
Address: 471 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Foreign credit cards not accepted
Description: Founded in 1878, this two-storey noodle shop is something of a local landmark thanks to its gilded sign and elaborate façade. Chefs start work at 4am, making noodles and dim sum from scratch. The ground floor serves 20 different noodle and rice dishes, including the famous three-treasure soup noodles (fried eel, fried fish and pork hock). The dining room upstairs offers more comfort and a bigger Shanghainese menu, from soups to hot dishes and dim sum.

Name: Hai Wei Guan (Jingan)
Address: 18 Kangding Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Behind the white façade of this two-storey building, new and old collide in a charming way. Embracing innovation while respecting tradition, the owner puts a new spin on Shanghainese classics with ingenious creativity. His signature crispy roast chicken with Périgord truffle that imitates Nakhi cooking needs to be pre-ordered. The sautéed conch with diced shrimp on a sizzling pot is wrapped in shiso leaves with crisp rice.

Name: Épices & Foie Gras
Address: A1-05, 309 Hankou Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: It’s no great surprise that foie gras is the speciality here. It comes in different preparations, so try the ‘Trilogy’ if you want to sample various types. This ‘modern French bistrot’ is run by a young French couple and they wisely also serve other classic Gallic dishes, like roasted lamb rack with crispy pistachio and a light garlic infused cream sauce. Lunch sets offer exceptional value. The main dining room is somewhat diminutive but it is pleasantly decorated.

Name: Kanpai Classic (Huangpu)
Address: 5F, Bund 5, 20 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: If anything demonstrates how international a restaurant is, it’s this: a Shanghai restaurant from a Taiwanese group, specialising in Australian Wagyu beef that also serves Japanese dishes. Premium Wagyu cuts, along with other meats and seafood, are grilled on charcoal stoves at each table. Caramelised and juicy, the thick-sliced skirt steak strikes a balance between toothsome texture and meaty flavour, with yuzu kosho to cut through the richness.

Name: Lin Family of One - The Bund
Address: 4F, The Central, 123 East Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: This upmarket dining concept nests in a shopping mall where century-old buildings are connected by a glass dome. The owner Mr Lin, a Taizhou native, has been cooking since the age of 19 and he ensures dishes are as authentic as they can be. Homestyle braised pomfret boasts a velvety texture and deep flavours, served with hand-made glutinous rice cake. Marinated tofu, and sweet potato noodles with sea anemone are also worth trying.

Name: Shanghai
Address: 2F, Central Hotel, 555 Jiujiang Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Perched on the second floor of the Central Hotel is this sister restaurant to the famed hairy crab restaurant, Wang Bao He. You’ll find this speciality here in season but it’s equally known for its authentic Shanghainese cooking. Their classic dishes use quality ingredients and are prepared with care. One highlight is the house-manufactured yellow rice wine, which you can buy to take home with you, along with various other ingredients.

Name: Beef & Liberty (Jingan)
Address: Shop 111, Shanghai Centre, 1376 West Nanjing Road, Jingan, Shanghai, 200040, China Mainland
Description: For those times when only a burger will do, there is Beef & Liberty. New Zealand grass-fed beef is ground in-house twice a day, in time for lunch and dinner, and then served in homemade buns. The ribeye burger boasts a juicy, 220g patty cooked medium or medium-well, alongside caramelised onions, mustard mayo and cheese. Their super-rich milkshake, made with just ice cream and whipping cream, is also well worth a try.

Name: Lao Xing Xian (Huangpu)
Address: 5F, Parkson, 918 Middle Huaihai Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Xian, or umami, is the fifth core flavour of food; it also means “fresh” in Chinese. At Lao Xing Xian, the owner aims to serve the freshest seafood, caught by his own fleet in the East China Sea that is deftly crafted with a knockout umami kick. The fish is neatly displayed for diners to choose – beltfish and yellow croaker taste best when steamed plain. Braised wild rice paddy eel is lightly seasoned to accentuate its natural flavour.

Name: Mercado 505
Address: 505 North Wulumuqi Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Judging by its name, this restaurant on a corner strives to create the buzzing vibe of a market; judging by the blue and white stripes on its sign, it has a nautical theme. Yes and yes. Imported seafood such as live oysters, scampi, carabinero shrimp and baby eel are deftly prepared in myriad ways. The signature Spanish seafood stew loaded with umami has to be pre-ordered. You can enjoy alfresco dining on a sunny day or reserve a private room for groups.

Name: Summer Palace
Address: 3F, Jing An Shangri-La Hotel, 1218 Middle Yan'an Road, Jingan, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This smart and sumptuously decorated Cantonese restaurant is divided into three distinct areas, each serving a different speciality. You'll find dim sum in the Pantry, claypot dishes in the Lantern and sophisticated Cantonese classics in the Imperial. Every facet of Cantonese cuisine is covered, alongside seasonal offerings such as hairy crabmeat and roe for a Shanghai twist. The private rooms are impressive, as is the wine list.

Name: Jade on 36
Address: 36F, Grand Tower, Pudong Shangri-La Hotel, 33 Fucheng Road, Pudong, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Even when this longstanding restaurant gets a makeover, nothing is really able to compete with the stunning views of Huangpu and the river. With an experienced French chef at the helm, the menu ushers in some sophisticated creations; they may be deeply rooted in traditions, but they are also jazzed up by modern touches and subtle Mediterranean influences. Blue lobster can be ordered in three servings and the lunch menu offers good value.

Name: Hong 0871
Address: 5F, Shanghai Chengtou Holding, 130 Wusong Road, Hongkou, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: In Chinese, ‘Hong’ means vast and deep, aptly describing the menu and the Yunnanese food culture that the owner from Kunming wants to popularise. Over 90% of the ingredients ship from Yunnan and the mushroom feast in summer is especially spectacular. Start with Nuodeng ham cured for 3 years alongside paper-thin dry cheese called rushan. Try also lard-layered buns, either steamed or deep-fried, with ‘winter melon’ pork and bean sauce filling.

Name: Ding Te Le Zhou Mian Guan
Address: No. 22, Lane 494, Middle Huaihai Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: To the passer-by, this simple shop hidden in an alley on Huaihai Road looks pretty much like any other. What sets it apart, however, are the authentic noodles it serves. It is particularly famous for its shredded pork noodles with scallions, its yellow croaker noodles with pickled vegetables, and its deep-fried pork chops. You can also enjoy congee, rice and snacks – and it stays open 24 hours a day.

Name: Royal China Club
Address: 3F, Bund 5, 20 Guangdong Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
Description: Operated by London’s Royal China Group, this Cantonese restaurant specialises in dried seafood like abalone and fish, along with other assorted seafood dishes. The quality of the seafood is good, with some of the ingredients imported from the UK, such as lobsters from Scotland. Dim sum is popular at lunch and, during Chinese festivals, handmade products like glutinous rice dumplings and mooncakes are provided.

Name: Mr & Mrs Bund
Address: 6F, Bund 18, 18 Zhongshan Dong Yi Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, 200002, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the city's dining scene for over 10 years, Chef Pairet's brasserie never ages. Lovely service, great music, a terrific wine list and bags of French joie de vivre make dining here a real experience. In the modern space – inside a former bank dating from 1922 – diners feast on chilled seafood platters, and charbroiled steaks and seafood. Original creations such as lemon & lemon tart with a sorbet-filled whole lemon also stand out.

Name: Shanghai Tavern
Address: 1F, Shanghai Edition, 199 East Nanjing Road, Huangpu, Shanghai, China Mainland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: It may be located within the contemporary backdrop of the Edition Hotel but the Shanghai Tavern celebrates a bygone era; the elegant space shows off its original 20C heritage and there are potted palms, waiters in white jackets, a champagne chariot and even a dessert trolley.
