Name: Landgasthof Ochsen
Description: Here at this inn dating back to 1288, the food is terrific – the skilful chef clearly pours a lot of love into his cooking. As well as regional dishes and classics, Asian and Mediterranean influences make their way onto the menu. A meal in their Gaststube is a somewhat simpler affair. There is a lovely terrace overlooking the pond, plus a charming smoking lounge. They offer comfortable and functional guestrooms, along with a charging point for electric vehicles.

Name: Panorama - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This charming family-run establishment has been going for 40 years. With Manuela and Rolf Fuchs at the helm, it proposes this bistro as an attractive alternative to their fine dining restaurant Cayenne. The excellent food is moderately priced: ostensibly simple dishes are crafted with care and premium ingredients, consistently featuring a modern twist. Local sourcing and seasonality are key – and you can really taste the difference! Friendly and adept service. Both restaurants share the same wine list. The wonderful views are best enjoyed from the tables by the windows or on the splendid terrace.

Name: Kaiserstock
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: This charming establishment perched in a small mountain village is your reward after the narrow, steep drive up! The fact that the restaurant has many regular customers is of course mainly down to its tasty traditional cuisine. The dishes are prepared with flair from good, fresh produce from the region. Popular options include stews and ravioli. A four- to seven-course set menu is also available if you pre-book (two days in advance). Seasonal specialities such as venison and chamois or Metzgete (pork platter) are also worth considering. Tip: Soups, sausages, jams and other delicacies can be purchased to take home. There are pleasant rustic-style guestrooms for overnight stays. N.B. Cash only!

Name: Casa Casutt - Ustria
Description: In this house with a long history, Linus and Therese Arpagaus serve up excellent cuisine made from fresh ingredients. The menu takes its cue from the region and includes Mediterranean influences. Expect classics such as capuns and pizochels, as well as offal specialities such as sweetbreads, veal liver and tripe. At lunchtime, there is also an inexpensive menu of the day. The interior is charming with its pretty traditional Stube, and the presence of many locals makes for a lively atmosphere. Expert service is overseen by the cordial lady of the house. The secluded garden terrace is a wonderful spot in summer! In addition to Ustria, there is Sala, where a "Gourmet Menu" is also served.

Name: Chez Philippe
Description: Philippe Chevrier from the Domaine de Châteauvieux is the brains behind this huge restaurant inspired by New York-style steakhouses. Relaxed atmosphere, meats sourced from the renowned Boucherie du Molard, fish caught by small-scale fishermen, dishes cooked over a wood fire, a truly authentic cheesecake and an expansive wine list. A real favourite!

Name: Bistrot du Lion d'Or
Description: In the restaurant of this hotel dating from 1750, the team conjures up a cavalcade of delicate, expertly crafted Gallic dishes, made with seasonal produce. Examples: artichoke, smoked whitefish from the nearby lake and buckwheat, or pan-fried calf’s sweetbread, morels and asparagus. The well-curated wine list is definitely worth a gander. The cheerful front-of-house team enjoys explaining the finer points of each dish. The interior sports small bistro tables, there is a peaceful terrace to the rear that is heavenly in fine weather and a casual, affable spirit reigns throughout.

Name: Le Lab by Adel & Niko
Address: Route de la Crottaz 5, Corseaux, 1802, Switzerland
Description: Between Vevey and Corseaux, this establishment sports a warm, contemporary interior, depicted by a striking claret-coloured wall and a long wooden counter. The simple, spot-on concept revolves around a set midday menu and creative dishes to share in the evening. The culinary lineup shines the spotlight on premium produce: carpaccio of tuna with ponzu and miso, roast pork cutlet and a creamy blackberry and raspberry delight to finish. Alfresco dining on the patio in fine weather and cheerful, professional front-of-house service courtesy of the smiling owner. The establishment also organises private cookery and pastry workshops (on request).

Name: Njørd café
Description: In a seamless fusion of a cafe and a brasserie, Njørd Café adroitly rolls out a savvy mix of Scandinavian and Swiss delicacies. Wind down in the casual vibe as you savour finely crafted fare, underpinned by first-class produce that is always in tune with the seasons: lovage-flavoured hemlagade köttbullar (meatballs), carpaccio of veal with pine nuts and black garlic, smörgås (sandwiches) of North Sea shrimp… The buzzy, verdant terrace is a hit in fine weather. Weekend brunches and other regular events further enhance the establishment’s appeal. The Hemma Hotel provides minimalist, tastefully decorated accommodation.

Name: Zum Alten Stephan
Description: This restaurant in the middle of the old town is not only steeped in history, it is also a treat for epicureans. Top-notch, down-to-earth cooking, staff who go the extra mile and a buzzing atmosphere make for a perfect dining experience. While Tamara Bader heads up the service team with effortless charm, her husband Stefan whips us delectable dishes rooted in classic tradition. Think pan-fried sweetbreads with mashed potato, spring vegetables and a morel sauce. House classics such as the cordon bleu are also in high demand. The impressive wine list is dedicated to Swiss, French and Italian labels. Delightful terrace in front of the building.

Name: Bistro by Regina Montium
Description: Whether you hike up or take the mountain railway (ideal from Vitznau), it's well worth stopping off here. The location is idyllic – at 1 550m above sea level, the terrace is wonderful – and the "natural cuisine" is another big attraction! Many of the ingredients are drawn from the immediate surroundings or harvested from the restaurant's own garden. The menu features smaller plates and regular dishes such as "terroir burger", ragout or medium-rare cuts of Rigi organic beef. Vegetarian options include organic potato gnocchi or "Alpine omelette". Friendly and well-informed staff talk you through the individual ingredients. And as an apéritif, why not try an alcohol-free"Chrüterwässer" made with garden herb extracts and cherry juice? Both the Bistro, for lunch, and fine dining restaurant, Regina Montium, for dinner, are housed in Kräuterhotel Edelweiss, where you can stay overnight after your meal.

Name: Restaurant Schlüssel - Schlüsselstube
Description: A feel-good spot through and through, this bistro run by the Kalberer family owes much of its appeal to the unmistakable warmth of its hospitality. The elegant historical setting and attentive service provided by staff in traditional dirndl attire add to the charm. And then there's the wonderful food, which is both sophisticated and fairly priced. Classics such as braised veal cheeks and Hacktätschli (meat patties) are delicious. Highly recommended: the seasonal set menu featuring three to four courses. Impressive wine selection. Tip: The cosy garden restaurant opens in summer.

Name: Chappeli
Description: In this pleasantly laid-back restaurant overlooking the village, the Hausmann/Köhli husband-and-wife team propose a really fun dining experience! The chef-patron cooks up delectable dishes that are delightfully down-to-earth: drawing inspiration from the region, they are big on flavour, with options including, for example, leek and bacon ravioli with fresh morels, or pork steak with Meaux mustard, mashed potatoes and vegetables. Nicely curated wine list and highly attentive service courtesy of the lady of the house, whose natural charm shines through. Be sure to bag a table on the delightfully verdant garden terrace!

Name: Centrale
Description: Particularly well-known and frequented by locals, this restaurant with its delightful, rustic, family atmosphere offers delicious regional cuisine that can be enjoyed – weather permitting – on the lovely terrace as well. In summer, the menu is enriched with dishes made exclusively from vegetables and garden produce.

Name: Bacchus Bistro & Genussmanufaktur
Description: You'll feel right at home here and that is down to the pleasant atmosphere, friendly service and excellent, fresh cuisine cooked up by Werner Tobler. The set menu, "La Table chez Bacchus", comprises four to six courses; the small à la carte selection includes dishes such as roasted pike-perch with pine nuts, ratatouille and white tomato butter. At lunchtime, there is also the option of a two- to four-course set menu. The setting is tasteful and upscale, with decorative touches in the form of bookshelves and a large mural; floor-to-ceiling windows allow plenty of light to flood in. Tip: You can buy cheese, spices, cakes, wines and more in the shop.

Name: Wirtshus zum Wyberg
Description: The journey out to the countryside is well worth it for the experience of cuisine cooked with heart and passion. The menu ranges from lobster and wild boar entrecôte to classics of regional cuisine such as house-made Kalbshackbraten (veal meatloaf) and beef fillet stroganoff. Plump for the set menu or dine à la carte. In both the simple Wirtsstube (ground floor) and the more upmarket Pratum (first floor), the atmosphere is cosy – the latter also has a pretty terrace for summer days; it is converted into a fondue parlour from November to February. Tip: Their Wyberg Shop has lots of tasty treats that you can purchase to enjoy at home.

Name: Edo
Description: This welcoming, zen-inspired establishment with a panoramic terrace at the foot of the mountains invites you to sample authentic Japanese fare. In their open kitchen, the brigade painstakingly crafts iconic dishes, such as crispy gyoza, nigiri (fatty tuna, grilled eel, tamago) and perfectly crispy Katsu chicken. Some of the house specials require pre-ordering well ahead, like the Japanese fondue and fresh fish chirashi. The menu also features a lineup of classics among which miso soup or a Japanese rendering of a café gourmand with mochi and matcha-flavoured sweet titbits. The warm, friendly vibe, attentive front-of-house team and exemplary value for money make it an establishment not to be missed, be it to dine in or take away.

Name: La Fleur de Sel
Description: Bang in the heart of the historic centre, this charmingly quaint establishment boasts a summer terrace opposite the protestant church on picturesque Temple Square. High whitewashed wooden ceilings and sandstone arches rub shoulders with light, modern fixtures in the spacious dining room. The culinary score stars tasty Gallic recipes (including a vegetarian menu) of modern inspiration crafted with first-class ingredients. The sommelier can be relied on for insightful tips and wine-tasting evenings with savvy food-wine pairings are regularly organised. The front-of-house team is professional and attentive. Booking recommended.

Name: Birdy's by Achtien
Description: Perfect for anyone who loves to share! For lunch and dinner, chef Christian Vogel (aka Birdy) provides an exciting dining experience. With the "Sharing is Love" concept, he puts the onus on communication as much as culinary enjoyment in a relaxed, modern atmosphere. The cuisine is predominantly vegetarian, but can be supplemented with fish or meat – both of which are of the highest quality. Choose à la carte dishes such as cauliflower tempura, soy sauce, peanut, salted lemon, or roast Hokkaido pumpkin, peanut, Thai curry, kumquat, with optional fried Gotthard zander. The sharing surprise menu for two is also on point – ten dishes are served in three courses.

Name: Bazaar
Description: At this restaurant in the chic Alpine CERVO Mountain Resort, located at the end of a ski slope, you are whisked away to an exotic and predominantly vegetarian world of flavours, ranging from Arab to Chinese specialities, from baba ganoush (smoked eggplant, tahini, pomegranate and garlic) to the Indian dal makhani (black lentils, sweet potatoes, mustard tarak and chapati) and dim sum such as "Phoenix Eye" (tofu, glass noodles, black mushrooms and wombok) or Tibetan tse tang churo momos, and sweet mezze for dessert. The atmosphere is nice and laid back. From the conservatory you can look out over Zermatt and the Matterhorn. The open kitchen is another focal point, as are the distinctive decorative items, almost all of which are available for purchase – just like at a bazaar!

Name: L'Agape
Description: This lovely old-school bistro ticks all the boxes when it comes to good vibes. It has been tastefully refurbished to showcase features such as its original tiling, wooden banquette seating, mirrors on the walls, a large chandelier fashioned out of old copper pans and a small service counter. As for the food, chef Clément Thellier has designed a short, savvy menu that makes your mouth water with its well-crafted and beautifully presented dishes: sweetbreads en barigoule, bacon crisps, split peas with bacon; beef tenderloin, toasted bread, pan-fried foie gras, mini vegetables and potato emulsion; poached and glazed pineapple, toasted pain d'épices and rum ice cream. A lovely dining experience at a reasonable price – not to be sniffed at in Geneva!

Name: Adler
Description: The name of the game here is "Gasthaus at its best" – this applies to the cosy space, the cordial, attentive service, and chef Daniel Jann's cuisine. Whether you opt for Murmeltierpfeffer (marmot stew), Gitzi-Bratwurst (a goat meat and beef sausage) or asparagus dishes, meticulous craftsmanship and flavour are guaranteed. The focus lies squarely on the region. Eating here is fun! Stylish guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Gasthaus Schupfen
Description: With a history dating back to 1455, this lovely half-timbered house is really something special. In an inviting atmosphere, food is served in three charming rooms and on the idyllic terrace overlooking the Rhine. The menu features Swiss classics such as fillets of perch with tartare sauce or Kalbsgeschnetzeltes Zürcher Art – Zurich veal ragout with rösti, alongside seasonal dishes such as asparagus salad with herb vinaigrette, served with smoked trout and fresh horseradish. If you are looking for a good location for a wedding or event, the premises can also be rented out.

Name: PINOT
Description: The location in the side wing of the modern Klinik Gut private hospital may be a little unusual, but the food here is excellent… thanks to Sebastian Titz (previously at Verve by Sven in Bad Ragaz), who cooks up regional and seasonal cuisine that cuts to the chase. Lunch is the main affair here: dish of the day, a small à la carte selection and set menus (fish/meat or vegetarian), as well as a weekly special and "Our House Speciality". A tasting menu is served on Thursday evenings. The decor is trendy and minimalist in style, with an open kitchen; the view of the mountains and the surrounding area is fabulous – tables on the terrace are understandably coveted.

Name: Sonne
Description: At the Häfliger family's lovely 100-year-old restaurant, diners can look forward to fresh, flavoursome food and attentive service provided by experienced staff. Classic Swiss cuisine is served in the form of a seasonal or surprise set menu. Alternatively, you can order à la carte. This place even has its own excellent spring water! Pleasant terrace to the rear of the building. Tip: Delicious cheese is sold in the cheesery next door.

Name: Stadthaus
Description: In the restaurant of the grand Hotel Stadthaus, whichever one of the different rooms you are seated in, the same delicious cuisine is on the menu – from Swiss classics, such as Zürcher Geschnetzeltes, to vegetarian dishes and a set "Bistro Menu". There is also an ambitious "Gourmet Menu" on Thu-Sat evenings. The selection of wines by the glass and by the bottle is also impressive. In summer, you can enjoy your meal on the arcaded terrace at the entrance.

Name: Agorà
Address: Via Muro degli Ottevi 10, Brissago, 6614, Switzerland
Description: Located in relaxing Brissago, this historic bistro features a pleasantly retro ambience and well-maintained wood furnishings. The courteous service is accompanied by the delicious flavours of dishes that follow the seasons and include traditional and Mediterranean touches. The ravioli del plin stuffed with braised wild boar are a highlight.

Name: Josef
Description: This trendy, urban restaurant and bar is located in the middle of a residential area in Kreis 5 (Zürich's fifth district). The atmosphere is lively and bustling, and in light of their interesting concept, it comes as no surprise that the place is well frequented: they serve tasty modern European cuisine with dishes in starter-sized portions (four is a good number to order). Mouthwatering options include the likes of veal shank ragout with mashed potatoes, confit garlic and Trevisano. Alternatively, there is a five-course set menu – available in omnivore and vegetarian versions. Good wine list and cocktail selection.

Name: AuGust
Description: This restaurant with its charming brasserie atmosphere is located in what was once the "butcher's quarter" – and in keeping with its history, the meat theme has been taken up here. Besides design features such as lamps and wall tiles, the open kitchen really draws the eye. They rear their own meat or source it from Swiss producers. Vegetarian alternatives are also available.

Name: Gül
Description: This place has all the makings of a cherished favourite restaurant! Tucked away in a courtyard, it has a pleasingly vibrant and laid-back atmosphere. Closely spaced tables and Turkish background music add to the bustling feel. In the open kitchen, modern Turkish dishes are prepared: expect dishes packed with bold flavours and sometimes with a touch of heat. Shining examples of dishes made using the grill and wood-fired oven, which play a major role, include mini lahmacun (freshly baked bread with lamb, yoghurt cream and onions) and manti (potato ravioli with yoghurt, salca butter and parsley). Be sure to try the baklava. Drawing on Middle Eastern culinary tradition, the menu features an array of smaller dishes and larger platters that are ideal for sharing. The "Gülty Menü Sürpriz" is also an excellent choice (for the whole table only). Tip: Creative cocktails are mixed at the restaurant's own bar.

Name: Zum Kaiser Franz
Description: Here, you won't want to miss out on the Austrian specialities such as Backhenderl (breaded fried chicken), Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef) or Topfenknödel (curd dumplings)! Available in a large or small portion, the Wiener schnitzel is a real highlight. Be sure to ask about the fish of the day, freshly caught from the adjacent Lake Zug. As well as the good food, diners can look forward to professional and attentive service in a cosy and stylish setting – the Austrian charm of the decor is the perfect match for the cuisine. The lakeside location provides a lovely backdrop. The nearby multi-storey car park is handy.

Name: Fischerstube
Description: At this long-established restaurant, Alain Koenig serves up dishes that are pleasingly down-to-earth and packed with flavour. Fish takes centre stage, but there are also a few meat and vegetarian options. You can dine à la carte or opt for one of two set menus: "Complet" (four courses) and "Degustation" (three to six courses). The tasteful decor is classically elegant in style, the service attentive and friendly. Decent wine list. Tip: For private dining or celebrations, book the historical vaulted cellar.

Name: Pensiun Aldier
Description: If you like your food straightforward and pared down, without compromising on taste, then you'll love the excellent Engadine cuisine served here. In the pleasingly unpretentious restaurant of the charming little hotel of the same name, the dishes forgo any frills to showcase select, fresh local produce. Good wines at fair prices. Shorter menu at lunchtime. Highlight: The hotel houses a museum (admission fee) exhibiting graphic works by renowned Swiss sculptor and painter Alberto Giacometti and some objets d'art by his brother Diego.

Name: Alpenblick - Swiss Bistro
Description: This bistro, part of Alpenblick hotel (some 500m above sea level), makes for a pleasant dining alternative to Gourmetstübli. The space is cosy, and the food is excellent. On the menu: delicious regional and seasonal dishes, as well as classics such as Simmentaler Kalbfleisch-Geschnetzeltes (slices of Simmental veal in a creamy sauce) and cheese fondue. And be sure to try the rösti! On Tuesday evenings the restaurant hosts a meat fondue buffet.

Name: Rigiblick Züriberg Beiz
Description: In this restaurant in the upper reaches of the city, a rather elegant yet relaxed atmosphere awaits you. The kitchen team showcases in-season regional produce in really delicious dishes. While Ronny Zipfel presides in the kitchen, maître d' Nicolas Schumnik heads up the experienced front-of-house team. In summer, head for the leafy terrace. Tip: It is easy to get here by taking the no 10 tram or the Funicular Rigiblick.

Name: Café de Peney
Description: Located on an arm of the River Rhône, this popular, bustling eatery, decked out in a profusion of nostalgic paraphernalia, calls to mind a vintage picture postcard and also boasts a wisteria-covered terrace. Fine ingredients are consummately and delicately crafted into delicious dishes, examples of which are the flawlessly cooked Black Angus steak or raspberry tartlet with a refreshing raspberry sorbet.

Name: Gasthof zum goldenen Kreuz
Description: This restaurant is steeped in tradition, and much sought after for its excellent seasonal cuisine. The chef's expertise and his knack for preparing select ingredients with real flavour are evident in dishes such as spicy smoked trout tartare with dill mustard and marinated apple and beetroot salad, and braised veal cheek, Bramata polenta and green beans with dried bacon. At lunchtime, you can order à la carte or opt for one of four three-course set menus. In the evening, there is a tasting menu in addition to an à la carte selection. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and well-organised front-of-house team. Goethe himself was a guest here – the pretty Goethe-Stübli is named after him – and the well-preserved painted panelling from the 17C adds rustic charm. The terrace is a delightful spot, secluded from the street by abundant greenery. Modern, functional guestrooms are available for overnight stays. Tip for motorists: public car park behind the building.

Name: Linde
Description: The secret of Linde's success is a formula of classic Swiss cuisine made from good ingredients coupled with reasonable prices. A lively atmosphere reigns in this attractive, well-run place with its various dining spaces, large bar area and glassed-in kitchen. Steak tartare and Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (veal) are among the permanent fixtures on the menu. For lunch, the offer is somewhat reduced. The wonderful terrace comes into its own in summer, and there are well-kept guestrooms too.

Name: Osteria della Bottega
Description: This lively restaurant is located on a steep little street in Geneva's old town. Against a chic industrial-style backdrop with an open kitchen, diners are treated to modern, seasonally inspired Italian cuisine and fine wines, plus attentive and friendly service. It's best to book, as Osteria is very popular! Across the street there is a lovely terrace.

Name: Collonge Café
Description: This modern restaurant boasts a great location next to the historical town hall and has a charming terrace laid out in the garden. The seasonally inspired menu successfully brings together modern Italian and French cuisine, while keeping an open mind when it comes to international influences. Cordial and competent service. Tip: the competitively priced lunch menu.

Name: Café du Levant
Address: Rue du Vieux Four 53, Aire-la-Ville, 1288, Switzerland
Description: A sleepy village deep in the countryside is the venue of this pleasant guesthouse that extends a warm authentic welcome. Take a seat on the pretty terrace surrounded by meadows and breathe in the fresh air. You can expect regional seasonal fare, steeped in big-boned aromas and washed down with a fine selection of wines from the Geneva area.

Name: SALZHAUS
Description: An attractive blend of urban cool and historical ambiance is the backdrop here and the exposed old brickwork certainly adds to the effect! On regular evenings, the kitchen serves up regionally inspired dishes with an international twist, either as a set menu or à la carte. The chicken cordon bleu with ham, Gruyère, Schupfnudeln (finger-shaped potato dumplings) and spring vegetables is an especially delicious example. Thursday evenings are dedicated to Japanese fusion cuisine. More limited options at lunchtime. Attentive, charming and adept service. Thanks to the beautiful old town location right by the Aare River, tables on the waterfront terrace are coveted in summer.

Name: Grotto della Salute
Description: A rustic grotto-style restaurant with a warm and welcoming ambience, where staff are happy to advise you on the seasonal dishes on offer. A whole page of the menu is dedicated to classic favourites, all of which are influenced by Mediterranean cuisine – the veal shank with mashed potato and salted butter is particularly delicious. There’s also a small menu of daily specials which changes according to market availability. The terrace shaded by huge plane trees provides a pleasant setting for summer dining, while an excellent wine list adds to the appeal.

Name: Balm - Bistro
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The charming and laid-back second restaurant at Hotel Balm also serves ambitious cuisine. This can be enjoyed in the form of a set menu of three or four courses which you can mix and match as you see fit. Options include dishes such as Lake Lucerne whitefish fillet with a champagne sauce, morels, leaf spinach and new potatoes. It is also possible to dine à la carte. At lunchtime on Wednesday to Friday, the moderately priced two-course set menu draws a crowd. The terrace is a delightful spot.

Name: Gommerstuba
Description: Diners are assured of a pleasantly informal atmosphere and great food at this little inn run by Yvonne and Lars Dederscheck on the outskirts of Niederernen. Their dishes are inspired by modern culinary trends and made using the freshest select ingredients. Think lukewarm char, celeriac, apple and horseradish, or duck breast, pulled duck leg, Jerusalem artichoke and kale. A fine à la carte selection is available, along with a three- to seven-course set menu and a three- or four-course vegetarian set menu s. Valais wines are recommended as an accompaniment. The welcoming interior has a contemporary feel – as well as an attractive stone-clad counter, there are pleasing decorative touches including some lovely paintings that are also available to purchase. Last but not least, the inviting terrace overlooks the Rhone Valley.

Name: Wiesner Mysterion – Werkstatt Kost
Description: Anyone heading to see the "Wizard of Entlebuch" in Bramboden should be prepared for something special. Like Wiesner – Zauber, Werkstatt – Kost is housed in the Weitsicht hotel. The location is simply magnificent; the terrace is idyllic, boasting one of the loveliest views in the whole region. Stefan Wiesner brings his nature-inspired culinary philosophy to the plate. For his four-course set menu, he sources ingredients from nearby woods and meadows, as well as the on-site garden – and prepares them using fire, embers and smoke. Tip: It's well worth spending the night. That way, you will have the opportunity to go rambling through the breathtaking scenery and to cook your own dinner over an open fire. In the morning, the chef leads a short guided foraging walk for wild herbs, during which some of the ingredients for breakfast are gathered – a one-of-a-kind experience! Another unique touch: you can even catch a ride here on the local PostBus at the weekend.

Name: Myò Sushi Bar
Description: Set in the Esplanade de Montbenon park, opposite the courthouse, this Japanese restaurant will win you over with its peaceful setting and quality cuisine. In summer, the terrace boasts a breathtaking view of the lake. Comfortably perched on a high stool, you can savour a variety of authentic Japanese dishes, including delicate sushi, tasty teppanyaki, beef tartare with wasabi, and a refined take on soba noodles. This is a popular place, so booking your spot at the counter is strongly advised.

Name: DAR
Description: This charming sister restaurant of KLE has moved to a new location. As before, the cuisine is plant-based and shaped by the Spanish and Moroccan heritage of chef-patron Zineb ("Zizi") Hattab, who was born to Moroccan parents and grew up on the Costa Brava. Her modern take on the culinary styles of Spain and Morocco results in dishes that are brimming with personality. The plates are also ideal for sharing, making this the perfect place to spend a cosy evening with friends. Feel free to enjoy a drink before or after your meal; you can also drop in for a coffee or aperitif during the day. Brunch is served on Sat and Sun.

Name: Bären
Description: Diners come here for straightforward seasonal cuisine that is not only prepared with fresh produce but, most importantly, is utterly delicious. In the evening, you can opt for the set menu, which comprises three to six courses, or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the options are more limited, with the three- to four-course "Gourmet Express" set menu, and an à la carte selection. The house specialty is Parmesan cheese wheel spaghetti. The lovingly decorated Gourmetstübli is a particularly appealing space. There is also an attractive room for events.

Name: Mont-Rouge
Address: Route de la Télécabine 19, Haute-Nendaz, 1997, Switzerland
Description: The standouts of this alpine chalet-inspired eatery are its warm, stylish atmosphere and its enthusiastic owner chef, who has been hard at work here since 2003. He invites you on a culinary journey, packed with surprises and strewn with forgotten heritage recipes, as he acquaints you with the region’s delicacies: lamb from Val Ferret, veal of the Herens breed, Valais black truffles… Alternatively, head to the small adjoining brasserie and sample its daily specials: poached sole roulade, home-made sauerkraut and champagne-laced beurre blanc… a real treat! Pleasant guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Asia
Description: After climbing just over ten steps, you settle comfortably into this delightful restaurant with relaxing colors and a splendid view of the lake and mountains. Of course, when the weather is nice, the terrace is the best place to book: your gaze drifts off over the vast blue expanse, while bamboo plants brighten up the outdoor area. The kitchen offers all the great Asian classics: traditional or fusion sushi, sashimi, delicious Thai curries, dim sum, and much more. Choosing won’t be easy!

Name: Alpenblick - Bistro
Description: This hotel's bistro may be cheaper than its upscale restaurant, Stuba, but the food is nonetheless tasty and fresh. Whether you come for lunch or dinner, the no-frills market-inspired cooking won't break the bank. They are keen to use produce from the region, in dishes such as "Hüttler's hamburger" or house speciality "Dad's steak tartare". Another of their classics is the spicy Thai red curry, which has just the right amount of heat! In keeping with the Alpenblick style, the atmosphere is nice and relaxed, and the service charming and attentive. In summer, the covered terrace in front of the entrance is inviting. The wine list is the same as at Stuba.

Name: Natürlich
Address: Rue de la Coulouvrenière 38, Geneva, 1204, Switzerland
Description: Just a few metres from the River Rhône and the BFM theatre, this popular restaurant appeals with its trendy and relaxed bistro-style atmosphere. It serves seasonal modern cuisine based on quality regional ingredients, in dishes such as roast cuttlefish, purple potatoes and cime di rapa. The food is accompanied by a terrific wine list including organic options. And for an even more convivial experience, plates are designed for sharing! Friendly service, too.

Name: Le Restaurant
Description: The stylish restaurant of the tasteful and historical La Couronne hotel not only has a unique atmosphere but also promises exquisite French and Swiss-inspired cuisine served by a friendly and attentive front-of-house team. The location in the old town, nestled beside Kathedrale St Ursen, is a draw in itself; the terrace in front of the hotel makes for a delightful spot in which to "see and be seen" – especially during a romantic sunset. The wine list comprises some 150 moderately priced labels and includes a decent selection of half bottles. The fantastic wine bar is ideal for a nightcap. Smaller lunchtime menu. Tip: Complement your culinary adventure with a leisurely stroll between Baseltor and Bieltor.

Name: Grotto Valmaggese
Description: Situated in an excellent location slightly above the road, this traditional grotto-style restaurant with a large car park is quiet and cool in summer, with a dining room warmed by a fireplace in winter. In this delightful location, enjoy classic, well-prepared and generous cuisine with personal touches made using top-quality, seasonally inspired ingredients. Make sure you try the venison tartare with marrow gratin and pear jelly, as well as the delicious artisanal ice creams. The highly welcoming and attentive service is clearly in evidence in the dining room.

Name: Alla Cantina
Description: Although all the staff at this beautiful historic restaurant on the village square hail from Sicily, they have been working in Switzerland for years. Here, authentic Sicilian cuisine is served in a rustic and welcoming setting that also provides the backdrop for regular music events: the only concessions to Ticino are the polenta-based dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the sarde in “Beccafico”(stuffed sardine roulade with breadcrumbs, sultanas, pine nuts and orange peel). There’s also a pleasantly cool and tranquil outdoor space for summer dining, plus four attractive and inviting guestrooms on the top floor.

Name: Stiva Grischuna
Description: In this traditional Bündnerhaus dating back over 300 years, the wood-panelled rooms abound with charm, and the down-to-earth cooking looks to the region for inspiration. Whether traditional dishes such as capuns and maluns or classics such as "Norbert's Stroganoff" and cordon bleu – this is simply tasty fare! The prices are also very reasonable. It's best to book. Locals also dine here.

Name: Didi's Frieden
Description: A fun dining experience is guaranteed at this delightful restaurant with its inviting decor – the wine-glass chandeliers are certainly original! In the evening, there is a set menu comprising three, four or five courses, featuring dishes such as Appenzell mountain lamb and meat patties, served with green beans and chanterelles, thyme jus and Ribel polenta with mascarpone. There are also regular daily specials. Authentic Swiss cuisine based on craftsmanship, free from showmanship or trendy gimmicks – it resonates with locals and tourists alike. Well-curated wine list. In summer, the charming, spacious terrace beside the restaurant beckons. Each lunchtime brings a new selection of dishes to choose from.

Name: Bauernschänke
Description: This gem of a restaurant is somewhat tucked away in a narrow alley in the city centre. In a historical setting with a cosy, rustic feel, diners tuck into international dishes such as king mackerel with radicchio tardivo, coconut and calamansi, as well as regional specialities such as pork belly gröstel (a traditional Tyrolean potato-based fry-up) with cucumber and butterhead lettuce. Order dishes to share à la carte or take a punt on the five-course surprise menu. The staff will be happy to provide wine recommendations. The well-curated selection is international and includes a decent range of natural wines (unfiltered and sulfite-free). Options are somewhat reduced at lunchtime.

Name: D'Chuchi
Description: This small restaurant in a side street in the old town has a charming, down-to-earth and almost intimate atmosphere. It also serves really good food, cooked up by chef-owner Jan Schmidlin from almost exclusively regional produce. Shining examples of his delicious modern seasonal fare that are not to be missed include the excellent local trout fillet served with wild broccoli, nuts, dill and beurre blanc. Alongside the four-course set menu, there is an à la carte selection of dishes, plus a good range of regional wines, which are also available by the glass. Extremely pleasant, cordial hospitality awaits you.

Name: Netts Schützengarten
Address: Sankt Jakob Strasse 35, Sankt Gallen, 9000, Switzerland
Description: Housed in the Schützengarten Brewery building, this trendy restaurant is popular, not least among the locals! The decor here is lovely – rather rustic at the front, more elegant in the area to the rear. The terrace and beer garden are delightfully secluded – the brewing happens next door, so you're often greeted by pleasant malty aroma. Along with Swiss classics such as Züricher Geschnetzeltes (sliced veal served in a cream and mushroom sauce) or beef Stroganoff, the menu includes Asian-inspired dishes and vegetarian options. Tip: In the courtyard, the brewery has a small bottle museum – well worth a short detour.

Name: Candela
Description: This pleasantly lively place is located right in the city centre. With high ceilings, dark wood panelling, exposed brickwork and large windows, the restaurant is really atmospheric. Swiss classics are served alongside international cuisine. A diverse range of vegetarian and vegan dishes is also available. The menu features options such as creamy Riesling soup with grapes and parmesan, tuna and Scottish salmon sashimi with ponzu sauce and wasabi mayonnaise, or veal liver with herbs, onions, port wine jus and buttery potato rösti. In addition to a terrific wine list, there is an interesting selection of digestifs.

Name: Alpenblick
Description: Run by the Anderhalden family, this remotely located establishment is a delightful spot. Dine in the restaurant-cum-parlour – the lounge area with its fireplace is ideal for an aperitif – or the cosy Stübli with its beautiful wooden floor and elegant table settings. The chef-patron serves up flavoursome Swiss cuisine, drawing on fresh seasonal produce and international influences. The menu ranges from beef fillet stroganoff to Mediterranean-inspired pasta dishes and Indian lamb curry. Service comes courtesy of the attentive proprietress, who is always on hand.

Name: Albrun
Description: The journey up to this enchanting mountain village is something of an adventure, but the food makes it worth it! In a rustic chalet-style setting, diners tuck into flavoursome regional dishes prepared with seasonal produce – the chef is always happy to showcase Swiss ingredients. The menu features mouthwatering options such as "Mario's Signature Black Forest" (beef sirloin, sour cherries, cocoa, kirsch 40% volume) and the "Alpen Tapas" starter. Friendly and charming front-of-house team.

Name: Colani Bistrot
Description: Located just off the reception area of the tasteful and well-appointed Hotel Colani, Colani Bistrot is the alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The food served here – Mediterranean cuisine with a local twist. We can certainly recommend the "Ravioli of the Day". Meat eaters should ask about the main dish centred on venison or veal – showcasing a different cut every day. Friendly service, a laid-back atmosphere and modern interior design featuring light wood and a whole host of decorative details.

Name: Brasserie Le Gogant
Address: Route de France 8, Le Brassus, 1348, Switzerland
Description: Both the restaurant, and the Hôtel des Horlogers in which it is housed, are the epitome of sleek, cutting-edge cool. In addition to an elegant designer interior, guests can savour panoramic vistas of nature through huge picture windows. The seasonal lineup harmoniously blends classical and traditional flavours (succulent stocks and addictive sauces) and is crafted from primarily regional ingredients. An uncluttered decor provides the perfect foil to bold, modern plating and high-quality recipes. If you are dining in a party, don’t hesitate to order the dishes to share, but before that, it would be a crime to skip the delectable gruyere-flavoured malakoffs (fried cheese balls) – ideal with an aperitif. The entire team, from the slick front-of-house staff to the crack white-jacketed brigade, is polished and professional. The hotel offers top-of-the-line guestrooms in the same vein that enjoy a view over the forest of Risoud.

Name: Auberge Communale Le Mont
Address: Place du Petit Mont 4, Le Mont-sur-Lausanne, 1052, Switzerland
Description: Burgundy ham terrine, gherkin and fresh herb condiment; Jorat veal belly, pistachios and green asparagus: the Burgundian chef and Meilleur Ouvrier de France definitely knows his stuff. This is a fine dining version of modern French cuisine that highlights local and fresh ingredients and showcases small-scale producers. He successfully pulls it off, and keeps it affordable. Fine selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Gasthof zur Sonne
Description: This 500-year-old heritage-protected inn is run by Patricia and Cäsar Meyer, who represent the second generation of their family here. He has a penchant for fish caught in Lake Zurich, just a stone's throw away – you can't get any fresher or more regional than that! Meat and vegetables, too, are sourced from the immediate vicinity. Besides the whitefish and perch, the Stäfa venison is especially worth trying, such as the overnight-braised shoulder with Pinot Noir sauce. This commitment to regional ingredients underscores the kitchen's sustainable approach. Food is served on the first floor of the building, in cosy yet stylish dining rooms that exude historical charm. A wonderful terrace balcony affords stunning lake views. The staff are very attentive and cordial – you're sure to want to come back! Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Anker
Description: In this first-floor restaurant, wood panelling and low ceilings create a snug and welcoming atmosphere, perfectly matched by seasonal cuisine made with fresh produce and brimming with flavour. The menu is sure to whet the appetite, with options such as veal liver with onions, sage und rösti, vegetarian loaf with mashed potatoes, carrots and creamy mushroom sauce, and the classic Chateaubriand (for two or more diners). The meat comes from the restaurant's own butchery. For overnight stays, there are well-appointed, modern guestrooms. Convenient: The tram to St Gallen stops right nearby.

Name: Zum Pflugstein
Description: Considered the largest erratic boulder in the canton of Zurich, the Pﬂugstein is located just above this distinguished half-timbered house dating from 1750 and lends its name to this idyllic restaurant 550m above sea level. The interior comprises an attractive wood-panelled space and a room with a fireplace; outside, the terrace beneath the boughs of plane trees comes into its own in the warm seasons. The service team overseen by the charming Jeannine Meili also deserves a mention. The kitchen prepares classic, regional and seasonal dishes made from fresh ingredients – à la carte or as a set menu. Tip: try the tender boiled beef!

Name: au violon
Description: This place exudes brasserie appeal thanks to its charming, stylish atmosphere and unfussy, honest seasonal menu, which also includes classic dishes. Despite its proximity to the centre, the location is pleasantly quiet – outside, an attractive terrace with shady trees beckons. There are well-kept guestrooms for overnight stays. Tip: Take the opportunity to visit Basel Historical Museum opposite.

Name: Les Curiades
Description: A truly historic restaurant which has been serving food since 1850. The present chef has experience in some of the finest restaurants, and it shows! His cuisine is elegant and refined, including dishes such as chuck beef braised in beer (paying tribute to the chef’s Belgian origins) and a delicious vegetarian menu which is always available. An unqualified success!

Name: Schüpbärg-Beizli
Description: This restaurant is a little out of the way, but it's worth the journey to this remote location, knowing that a cosy, rustic-style space awaits diners, as well as a lovely terrace, which is very popular in summer! But let's not forget the cooking of owner Christoph Hunziker: his flavoursome dishes show strong ties to the region, follow the seasons, and are occasionally given a modern twist. You can choose à la carte or opt for the set menu ("Geniesser-Menu"). The service is charming – even the chef likes to get involved front of house. Tip: At lunchtime, the set menu is a bargain.

Name: Le Bistro by Décotterd
Description: Like its fine dining counterpart, Le Bistro promises diners a stunning view, whatever the season and whatever the weather, particularly if you ask for a window table when booking! A modern interior and a simpler culinary score, but quite the equal of its sibling in terms of taste and culinary know-how. Dishes to share include rillettes of Grisons salmon, lemon zest, herbs and croutons; platter of Armand Stuby saucisson and dried meat. Examples of main courses: gruyere-flavoured malakoffs (cheese balls); pike from Lake Geneva in puff pastry; stew of lamb from Dents-du-Midi, and of course, the house signature, chocolate tart!

Name: La Trattoria
Description: In the charming Hotel Walther, one of Pontresina's most emblematic hotels, this lovely Trattoria has an authentic, lively atmosphere and a stylish rustic feel. The appetising menu embraces all regions of Italy, with delicious pasta as the centrepiece and the focus firmly on flavour and freshness. Friendly Italian service and a good selection of wines.

Name: Eintracht
Description: In this restaurant dating back to 1870, the dedicated Meier family have cultivated a sense of tradition while also introducing modern influences. This approach makes itself felt in the bistro and the more elegant restaurant area as well as in the cuisine – from classics such as veal cordon bleu to a gourmet set menu composed of three to five courses. Excellent wine selection. Simple daily specials are also available in the bistro.

Name: Casa Caminada
Description: This restaurant enjoys a lovely quiet location in the castle grounds. Inside the bright, high-ceilinged space, modern design meets warm wood; outside, there is a delightful terrace. A charming team provides competent service. They serve regional cuisine, in which seasonal ingredients sourced from select local producers go into extremely flavoursome dishes – the produce steals the show! Andreas Caminada's take on Grisons classics can also be found on the menu. Be sure to try his quark bizochels, for example. Tip: You can buy bread baked in the on-site bakery and other goods in their shop next door.

Name: Le Bologne
Description: Next to the Fine Arts School, this vintage bistro cuts a fine figure with its cement tiles, designer light fixtures and bare bulbs, as well as a bar, banquettes and bistro chairs. The bistro lineup is packed with first-rate, carefully crafted seasonal ingredients: risotto-style celery, truffle and foie gras, confit lamb shoulder, cumin, asparagus and labneh or braised aubergine to die for… Take a peek through the small window that separates the dining room from the kitchen and admire the white-jacketed brigade hard at work. Bookings recommended as it is invariably packed with regulars! Pleasant pavement terrace.

Name: Philipp Blaser
Description: A popular place to eat! A relaxed atmosphere reigns in this inviting contemporary interior, where diners tuck into pleasingly unpretentious dishes that impress with their flavours and craftsmanship. The menu features not only traditional regional dishes, including classics such as beef tartare, but also Asian specialities in the "Thai Corner" section of the menu, such as gaeng mussaman – a mild Thai curry with peanuts and king prawns. There is also a pleasant terrace with a magnificent view of the mountains of the Bernese Oberland. Next to the restaurant, the small Hotel National has cosy guestrooms. It also has its own confectioner's.

Name: Golden Dragon
Description: The Asian restaurant at the Grischa hotel serves a combination of Chinese and Japanese dishes. Tip: Some dishes are designed for sharing. If you fancy the Peking duck for two, which is absolutely to be recommended, be sure to pre-order (at least 48hr in advance). You also have the option of taking your pick of many of the ingredients and having them put together as you wish. The sleek, authentic design of the restaurant is also appealing.

Name: SUAHOY
Description: It quickly becomes clear that this friendly, buzzy venue is light years from your average Thai eatery. Everything is made from scratch with fresh, first-class ingredients and the flavours are both refined and rugged. Examples include fried rice balls with pork (Laab Nem Tod) and fried rice with crab and spring onions (Khao Pad Pool), without forgetting the starters that are ideal to share. The friendly, casual front-of-house team sets the tone and in summer, a few tables are laid on the pavement. A word to the wise: booking is essential, even at lunchtime!

Name: La Bottega di Mario
Description: Housed in a historical building (1913), La Bottega is a wonderfully inviting and lively ristorante and salumeria under one roof. Guests are spoilt for choice between the tasty dishes, clearly influenced by Ticino tradition, and the superb selection of salami and ham at the counter – here, the friendly mastri salumieri serve up the cold cuts. Tip: Try the house wine, Merlot di Ticino, poured from a six-litre bottle!

Name: Gaijin Izakaya
Description: This place with a name that can be translated as "foreigner bar" is a cool spot that channels the style of a Japanese izakaya (casual bars that serve drinks and food). A team led by chef-patron Daniel Shu, who trained in Chicago and New York, and his business partner cook up creative Asian soul food – in the form of an omakase menu or à la carte. The lunch menu is more limited. Modern music plays in the background, fostering a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Joontos
Address: Dar Tantora The House Hotel, 375 Old Town, AlUla, 43562, Saudi Arabia
Description: Named after the Spanish word for ‘together’, this is one of the best places to dine while admiring the architecture in AlUla’s Old Town. Part of Dar Tantora The House Hotel, the Spanish-inspired Middle Eastern restaurant is an ensemble of renovated traditional buildings resembling a medina, with its maze of narrow streets and walls covered by cob. Interiors are adorned with traditional frescoes, Persian carpets and wooden furniture. As for the food – generously portioned – the appetisers feature Levantine mezze and Iberian tapas, while mains are more international with clever hints of local produce like black lime with rich aioli. Finish off with a date and citrus soufflé.

Name: Tameesa
Address: King Abdul Aziz Branch Road, Alyasmin, Riyadh, 13326, Saudi Arabia
Description: Open from early in the morning until mid-afternoon and often referred to as a traditional Saudi Arabian breakfast restaurant, this place is much more than that. A bright, colourful and slightly retro interior has the chefs visible in their glass-fronted kitchen. Dishes stem from Hijazi-style cuisine with must haves, all designed for sharing, include foul (fermented fava bean puree), moutabbal and mutabbaq. Be sure to order plenty of bread freshly prepared in the tandoor oven, along with tamees, and finish with a bowl of sweet areeka. Expect generosity in flavour and portions, all appealingly priced.

Name: Mirzam
Address: Takamul Plaza, Altakhassusi Street, Alnakheel District, Riyadh, 12383, Saudi Arabia
Description: Get your breakfast fix at this contemporary Saudi eatery located a short distance from Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District. Served from early morning to mid-afternoon, the food here proudly represents the country’s regions, particularly in its ingredients and spices. Start with the Mirzam platter, a selection of appetisers including hummus, foul and salads all served with warm flatbreads fresh from the oven. Their Egg Maghash and Kibda Hijazi – aka lamb’s liver – are must haves but do leave room for dessert – the maasoub is the chef’s speciality – and come with friends as sharing is encouraged.

Name: KAYZŌ
Address: 2752 Prince Musaid bin Abdulaziz bin Jalawi Street, As Sulimaniyah, Riyadh, 12234, Saudi Arabia
Description: The vibe is set from the moment you enter this chic and stylish restaurant with its large open kitchen counter. The extensive menu of Japanese contemporary dishes are all designed for sharing. Plates are colourful, at times traditional and others imaginative, show well-judged creativity and layers of flavour. Sushi and makis are offered here, alongside their tasty beef takikomi gohan and salmon filo. Pair your meal with some of their creative mocktails and you’ll have a great experience and one that’s good value. We recommend heading there at night for the low lights and thumping tunes.

Name: Anyukám Mondta
Description: Anyukám Mondta is everything a good neighbourhood restaurant should be. It offers something to appeal to everyone, while prices cover a wide range to suit all occasions. Excellent produce is prepared with care, resulting in hearty, flavoursome dishes, and service is smooth, well-paced and comes with plenty of personality. Choose from homemade pizzas, refined modern Italian dishes and tempting daily specials – where you might find some Middle Eastern flavours too. The focaccia cooked in the wood-fired oven is a must.

Name: Platán Bisztró
Address: Platán Manor, Kastély tér 6, Tata, 2890, Hungary
Description: Part of the Platán complex – which also includes a hotel and spa – this charming bistro sits within the same historic castle outbuilding as Two Michelin Starred Platán Gourmet. It has a pleasingly relaxed, contemporary style, and in the corner is a small shop selling desserts and ice cream. In summer you can dine beneath the branches of a 230-year-old sycamore tree on a charming stepped terrace which borders the lake. The concise menu sees robust Hungarian dishes given a refined bistro-style makeover while still staying true to their roots. Service is fittingly warm and chatty.

Name: Macok Bistro
Description: Set on a cobbled street in the Old Town, alongside the castle walls, this bright, colourful bistro is known by food-lovers across the country – and it certainly deserves its reputation. It’s family-owned and professionally run by a friendly team, and the menu is an appealing mix of colourful Hungarian and Mediterranean dishes. While classic flavours are in abundance, presentation is decidedly modern; the wild boar soup is not to be missed, as is the beef cheek goulash. As well as a wine shop, they also have bedrooms, and in summer you can sit in the courtyard beside the working water wheel.

Name: Sparhelt
Description: Head away from the lakeside to seek out this honest all-day bistro with a smart modern interior and a popular terrace. Dishes have a Hungarian heart and perfectly reflect the seasons, with the likes of chilled fruit soups in summer and hearty, warming dishes in winter. Meat-lovers should order the mangalitsa Wellington if they see it on the menu, while fish fanatics should come on Fridays for the special seafood menu. They offer wines from around the world, but don't pass up the opportunity to try some of the superb local Lake Balaton options.

Name: Casa Christa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Roads fringed by almond trees and terraced vines lead to this stunning hillside spot; a restful place that comes with seven restored press houses that now play host to designer bedrooms with private saunas. Within the grounds sits this beautiful whitewashed restaurant with a simple bistro-cum-farmhouse style and a lovely terrace affording far-reaching views over the countryside towards Lake Balaton. The generous cooking has a similarly Mediterranean feel, with bright colours and bold, contrasting flavours – expect the likes of lamb soup with sour cream, followed by chicken with pea risotto.

Name: Cabrio
Description: Tucked away in the city centre on a small square, Cabrio’s tree-shaded terrace is the perfect place to kick back with a glass of wine. A 100% natural wine bar, it offers generously priced bottles from both Hungary and across Europe, and comes with a vintage look and a trendy vibe. The friendly team are keen to offer recommendations when it comes to both the wine and the concise selection of seasonal small plates (three per person is about right). Boldly flavoured, well-judged combinations could include burnt celeriac carpaccio, salmon trout tartare with green gazpacho or raspberry chocolate crémeux cake.

Name: Goli
Description: Set within the former Goldberger textile factory, Goli refers to the nickname the locals gave to this historic building. It’s a small place with a simple terrace and a colourful, cramped interior, but it’s gloriously friendly and positive vibes simply pour out of the kitchen. Sit at the counter to talk with the chefs, who are eager to guide you through the menu of fresh, tasty Middle Eastern favourites, from warm pita, vibrant salads, and green beans with chilli and lemon, to charred entrecôte with tahini. Deliciously fruity soft drinks and cocktails complete your meal.

Name: Iszkor
Description: This lovely neighbourhood restaurant sits in a small village in the Bükk Mountains and is run by charming couple Adam and Luca. It couldn’t be a bigger part of the community. Not only does it reside in Adam’s home village, but the locals get involved by growing produce for them – and that's without considering the host of events on offer, from live music and guest chef evenings to seasonal Farmers' Markets. The generously proportioned, country-style dishes change with the seasons and use every part of the ingredient. In summer, sit on the decked terrace; in winter, cosy up beside the fire.

Name: N28 Wine and Kitchen
Description: You’ll be greeted as if you’re a regular diner here, even on your first visit, which immediately sets a cheerful tone. The welcoming team come, in part, from the Bock Bistzró stable – and they know how to look after their guests. The surroundings might be modern, but there’s a traditional element to the menu, which looks to the Hungarian larder for its base. Expect seasonally changing dishes such as a tasty vichyssoise soup, followed by juicy wild boar and then a delicious poppy seed cake. 95% of the wines are Hungarian, and everything comes at a great price.

Name: Morzsa
Description: ‘Crumbs’ is a new wave bakery-cum-bistro with a relaxed urban style, owned by a charismatic and exuberant designer. Sit inside to watch the making of the delicious loaves and pastries or head out to the terrace for some people-watching in the part-pedestrianised lane. Modern, flavour-packed small plates are served throughout the day and can be accompanied by something from the biodynamic wine list. Naturally, a pastry is a must to finish, but with so many delicious options it can be hard to choose... and if you simply can't decide, there's always the option to take something home for later too!

Name: Kistücsök
Description: A short walk from the southern shores of Lake Balaton, Kistücsök is part of a small hotel which comes complete with its own swimming pool. Well-regarded locally, the restaurant is known for its consistently good interpretations of classic Hungarian dishes, which have been modernised both in their composition and their look. Flavours are fresh, with the occasional global influence, and prices are reasonable. The ‘Taste of the Region’ menu with wine pairings is always a great choice, and the floating island dessert has become something of a speciality.

Name: Újváros Bisztró
Description: If you’re in eastern Hungary, it’s worth heading over to this ultra-modern restaurant on the banks of the Holt-Körös River. It occupies a space on the ground floor of a modern office building and is accessed via steps that lead to the river path, where you’ll also find the charming terrace with views of Bolza Castle. Choose between three tasting menus: ‘From Here’ (built around local ingredients), ‘From There’ (reinterpreted Hungarian recipes) and ‘From Everywhere’ (dishes with international flavours). An interesting selection of Hungarian wines accompanies, arranged on the list by region.

Name: 94' Konyha & Bar
Description: It would be easy to pass by this unassuming restaurant, but to do so would be a mistake, as inside a warm welcome and great value food awaits. A central bar divides the pared-back room in two, while a rear window offers tantalising glimpses into the kitchen. The super-fresh, vibrantly flavoured cooking has a clear Vietnamese heart, with dishes including a tasty pho and creations such as their own 94' Gohan – a blend of beef, fried rice and XO sauce – but you’ll find some other Asian flavours at play here too. The ‘Lunch Break’ menu is a particular steal and always be sure to finish with a Vietnamese coffee.

Name: Bistrôt Chapeau
Description: Bistrôt Chapeau exudes French elegance: white tablecloths, warm tones, typical chansons playing in the background and a terrace where you can relax. Chef Nicky Quarz cooks here with classic precision and a penchant for dishes that are too often forgotten. No frills and full of flavour. Think homemade wild boar pâté with lively garnishes that provide a nice counterbalance, or juicy guinea fowl stuffed with tartufata and served with soft pommes fondantes and a creamy mushroom sauce, among other things. This cuisine remains true to its roots. And more good news: the full menu is also available for lunch.

Name: Café Visscher
Description: You could definitely call Arie Visscher's "café" a luxury brasserie. An abundance of red velvet, marble and copper give the place a remarkably warm and welcoming feel. Open all day from 11am, it's a great option for lunch, dinner or a quick bite at the bar. Chef Visschers specialises in French classics such as steak tartare elevated with smoked eel, or sea bass with a delightfully buttery potato mousseline and artichoke. He also showcases his creativity with a modern dish based on hispi cabbage. This Rotterdam native sticks to a single set menu, crafting beautifully balanced no-nonsense cuisine.

Name: Lucie Cocina
Description: Lucie Cocina boasts a hip, lively atmosphere that captures the essence of an authentic tapas bar. From the moment you step inside, you will be won over by the decor with its vintage-style globe chandeliers, floral-patterned mosaic floor and bar stools at the counter where the seafood is displayed. The menu features an irresistible array of options, from traditional ham croquettes and tortillas to more inventive tapas creations. How about steamed zamburiñas with antiboise, finely chopped jalapeño and a hollandaise foam? Or rather braised veal cheeks with mojo rojo and deep-fried potato cubes? The fantastic value for money means you can sample a wide variety of dishes without breaking the bank. ¡Buen provecho!

Name: Basaal
Address: Dunne Bierkade 3, The Hague, 2512 BC, Netherlands
Description: With a delightful waterside terrace for sunny days and a cosy interior with a Scandinavian and vintage feel for when the weather is cooler, this inviting neighbourhood restaurant has plenty going for it. But, of course, the focal point is the kitchen, where chef Daan van Munster creates honest market-fresh cuisine. Whether you prefer to share with your dining companions or go solo, you can compile your own set menu from a tempting list of options, including some rather unconventional dishes. Think creamy veal neck and foie gras terrine, or tender veal tongue with coco de Paimpol beans and a robust veal stock sauce. This chef takes his cue from the seasons, and vegetables are always a key part of his dishes. The moderately priced wine list is the icing on the cake.

Name: Auberge - cuisine française
Description: You might start with the pâté en croûte or the onion tarte Tatin with a light cream and Gruyère sauce, follow that up with a rich bouillabaisse or crépinette filled with veal mince, bacon and foie gras, served with a vegetable velouté, and finish with an airy chocolate mousse. Choosing is a real challenge in this classic bistro, where timeless classics of the genre are presented with generous flair. In its wallet-friendly à la carte and prix-fixe menus, there are plenty of tempting options, and the same goes for the expertly curated selection of French wines. The decor is simply enchanting with its copper pans, elegant glass wine cabinet and undeniable je ne sais quoi. Ah, la douce France…

Name: Bovenmeester
Description: The warm, contemporary interior of this former school (coat hooks still in place) exudes a lively brasserie atmosphere. Chef Raymond crafts à la carte dishes and a tasting menu, presenting classic flavours with modern precision. Think succulent veal cheeks served with crispy pommes dauphine, onion compote and Belgian endive braised in orange. Two rich sauces – one mustard-based, the other a Spanish wine reduction – complete the dish. Confident cooking, in generous portions that leave a lasting impression.

Name: De Watergeus
Address: Simon van Capelweg 10, Noorden, 2431 AG, Netherlands
Description: The drive alongside the canals affords a foretaste of what awaits at this refurbished restaurant: the views over the water are simply sublime. Inside the tastefully appointed country house, diners are warmly received by a highly attentive and professional team. The chef unites classic cooking methods and generosity with modern textural elements to create dishes that are balanced and wide-ranging. Take, for example, his refined starter of salmon mousse, herb vinaigrette, ripe olives and pickled cucumber. Be sure to enquire about overnight stays and boat trips (with a picnic basket) on the Nieuwkoopse Plassen.

Name: Restaurant élevé
Description: The 11th floor of WTC Hotel is home to a rooftop bar and restaurant with a cosmopolitan feel. Lounge seating, soft atmospheric lighting and windows all around the dining space affording views of the city make for a stunning setting. Chef Mike Kalkman presents modern cuisine that blends Dutch accents with international influences. Think hand-cut Frisian Black Angus beef tartare with a celeriac and mature cheese sorbet, or flawlessly cooked cod with pumpkin risotto, a vibrant Champagne mousseline and a sweet-and-sour pumpkin soup. Élevé is refined yet approachable, all in a decor that never ceases to impress.

Name: Landgoed de Holtweijde
Description: Classic country elegance and a setting radiating natural charm await you at this stunning estate. Inside, the wooden beams, terracotta floor and crackling fire create a special atmosphere. Regional ingredients come into their own in indulgent dishes. The tasting menu is outstanding, but the à la carte options – such as the classic tournedos Rossini – are equally tempting. For example, chef Berry Thuss serves a terrine of succulent short rib and white leek, with crispy asparagus tempura, al dente vegetables and an onion dressing. Definitely worth the journey!

Name: Bij Mette
Description: Picturesque Linschoten is worth a visit in its own right, but be sure to seek out this beautifully converted grocery shop with its distinctive spiral staircase, a stone's throw from the leaning clock tower. This is old Dutch charm at its best! Chef-patron Carel Alberts welcomes you personally before going on to showcase his expertise in the French classics, with the occasional Mediterranean flourish. Wonderful local produce, intense sauces, respect for tradition: it all makes for an enjoyable culinary experience. Take, for example, the generous duck breast dish with a jus from the duck itself, laced with just the right amount of chilli, served with accompaniments such as roasted cauliflower and Brussels sprouts. Ask the chef about his wine list; he will be happy to elaborate. The Bib Gourmand set menu is always a good choice!

Name: De Witte Gans
Description: This rustic restaurant is a favourite pit stop for walkers, cyclists and food lovers. The terrace is one of its main draws; another is the superb Bib Gourmand-awarded menu, which features local produce, nods to the East, and vegetarian options. The creative chef works his ingredients hard and prides himself on the presentation of his dishes.

Name: Bistro Aragosta
Description: A warm and intimate atmosphere reigns in this cosy place, where diners are treated to cordial service with a personal touch. French classics dominate the menu, but there are also Italian-influenced specialities, as well as lobster dishes. Think perfectly pan-seared langoustines with a lobster bisque mayonnaise, accompanied by an aubergine croquette and a curry sauce. Or how about a rich and creamy blanquette de veau? Should you wish to swap out a standard set menu item for one of the daily specials, the team will be happy to oblige. Expect genuine hospitality and fantastic value for money!

Name: Prix de Rome
Description: As far as Maastricht foodies are concerned, all roads lead to Prix de Rome. Inside this impressive building just outside the city centre, a cosy interior awaits, in which exposed beams are seamlessly integrated into the modern design of the place. The view into the open kitchen at the back is a nice touch, and the terrace is a must on sunny days. Chef Wouter alternates between inventive, elaborately prepared creations and more ingredient-led dishes. For example, he pairs lobster with the exotic nuances of mango and a tom kha kai sauce, then he serves up medium-rare saddle of venison with a robust game sauce. Familiar flavours and innovative ideas go hand in hand in the outstanding set menu!

Name: Café Samabe
Description: The spicy aromas hit you the moment you enter this colonial-era building dating from 1899. An abundance of wood and an exotic colour scheme make for a uniquely charming setting inside – this place calls itself a café because of its casual atmosphere. The home-style Indonesian cuisine, with a slight preference for Balinese specialities, is indulgent and packs a punch. Think aromatic martabak, rich authentic rijsttafels (including vegetarian options) with spicy rendang and intensely flavoursome sambal goreng telor… At Café Samabe, a feast awaits!

Name: Bistrot Regent
Description: This timeless bistro is a slice of la douce France. It serves classics such as egg mayonnaise, and both the menu and excellent wine list showcase the best of what that country has to offer. Chef Robbert van Sonsbeek is a master sauce maker and treats his ingredients with respect. In a dish featuring succulent roasted farm-raised chicken, he includes the tenderloin, pairing it with pan-fried chanterelles and a refined butter sauce infused with vin jaune. From a tempting array of indulgent dishes, you can order à la carte or create your own Bib Gourmand set menu. Robbert and Heleen clearly put their heart and soul into running Bistrot Regent.

Name: De Wilg
Description: The low-mounted coat hooks and ballet bar serve as reminders that the location was once a primary school and ballet hall. But there are no more strict rules here – the building has been transformed into a warm and welcoming restaurant. Boy van Gerwen steers clear of over-complicating matters, winning diners over with, for example, the fresh earthy notes of a beetroot tartare, the vibrant flavours of confit duck leg accompanied by a robust veal jus with morels, but also the spiciness of a lentil dahl. De Wilg represents generous cooking and great value for money.

Name: Restaurant ñ
Description: The yellow façade already hints at a Mediterranean vibe. Inside, the atmosphere is lively and informal, with closely set tables – a perfect space in which to share delicious food. Start, for example, with Spanish tapas such as boquerones, Ibérico ham or pimientos de Padrón, before moving on to Mediterranean dishes that pair fish and meat in unexpected ways – for example, tender pork belly topped with a thin slice of raw sea bass and leek oil. The tasting journey highlights freshness, simplicity and nuanced fermentation.

Name: Tabkeaw
Description: Tabkeaw is a perennial favourite that captivates diners of all ages. With its bamboo panelling, "pagoda" bar and traditional figurines, the entrance makes for an immersive experience. Plus, you get the lively atmosphere of the Wyck neighbourhood thrown in for free. The food is just as authentic as the decor: aromatic, delicately walking the line between sweet and sour, spicy but never overwhelmingly so – think beef strips with al dente vegetables, sticky rice and a delicate green curry and coconut sauce. A culinary adventure!

Name: Bistro Nijeholt
Description: Located on the beautiful verdant Lauswolt estate, this atmospheric bistro is wonderfully relaxed. There is a fantastic set menu with a choice of generous options for each course and no unnecessary frills. An example would be a slice of intensely flavoursome pâté with dried fruit followed by al dente local asparagus, smoked salmon, a poached egg and hollandaise sauce. Top off your meal with a warm clafoutis with blueberries and verbena ice cream, and you will understand why Bistro Nijeholt is the epitome of a Bib Gourmand restaurant.

Name: Raedthuys
Description: With its own bakery, patisserie and even a smokehouse, Marion Thus's bustling restaurant, once a café, is a place where nearly everything is made from scratch. Her enticing à la carte and set menus include plenty of vegetarian options. The chef's trademark generosity, rooted in tradition, shines through in dishes such as perfectly pink fillet of Gaasterland herb-fed pork with rösti, al dente vegetables, a mousseline sauce infused with ras-el-hanout and a sauce enriched with Gerardus Tripel beer. There's no holding back when it comes to bringing bold flavours to your plate. Be sure to peruse the beer list and treat yourself to something on tap.

Name: Scheepskameel
Description: To clarify the name: Scheepskameel (literally "ship's camel") refers to the wooden floats once used to help ships navigate the shallow waters near the naval dockyard at low tide. Today, a repurposed warehouse on the site is home to a bright and bustling restaurant that seats over 100 diners in an informal setting. Working in a completely open kitchen, the chefs turn out unpretentious cuisine that emphasises vegetables and contemporary flavour combinations. Expect dishes such as ripe green tomato carpaccio with whipped cream, anchovies, puffed quinoa for crunch and parsley for a subtle herbal accent. Or share a côte de boeuf or roasted whole sea bream with your party. The wine list is entirely German and complements the food beautifully.

Name: A-Fusion
Description: A-Fusion immediately captivates diners with its vibrant atmosphere. On the menu is an appealingly exotic blend of Chinese, Japanese, Thai and Korean flavours. On entering, you will see sushi being made to order, and as you head further in you will notice the barbecue and the dim sum and wok kitchen. Thanks to the reasonably priced à la carte menu and small portions, you can try everything. The depth of flavour of the minced pork dumplings, the spice and umami of the XO sauce, the ultra-fresh salmon topping the nigiri... This is one of Amsterdam's best Asian restaurants!

Name: Promessa
Description: With "Food is art" as their motto, the chefs at this trendy and laid-back restaurant treat their plates like canvases, placing a strong emphasis on aesthetics. But fear not: these visually stunning dishes are also packed with flavour. Koen van den Kerkhof's creativity draws on the culinary traditions of the Netherlands, France and more far-flung locations, with his limitless imagination reflected in a wide-ranging menu. Diners enjoy dishes such as albacore tuna poppadom, classically prepared pheasant breast with a rich veal jus, succulent beef rendang, or spaghetti aglio e olio. They have the art of indulgence down to a T!

Name: LEV Foodbar
Description: The relaxed atmosphere at LEV perfectly matches the concept behind this food bar: sharing dishes and enjoying good food together. The dishes (in snack-sized portions) are not overcomplicated; a couple of ingredients suffice to create amazing taste sensations. Steak tartare, pork tenderloin, cauliflower tempura, truffle risotto... At LEV, the table quickly fills with irresistible delicacies, often prepared using produce from the Achterhoek region. The perfect accompaniment to one of the many beers!

Name: Serre Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: A bright space with a gorgeous canalside terrace, Serre has a Japanese minimalist feel. Reflecting the international atmosphere of the luxury Hotel Okura, this restaurant serves fusion cuisine with a slight penchant for the Far East. Start, for example, with a wonderful sea bass ceviche, in which the interplay of grapefruit, sweetcorn and coconut milk with mezcal and lime juice creates layers of refreshing acidity and slight sweetness. Next, you could choose one of the sharing dishes or opt for the appealing set menu, which showcases sophisticated cuisine with fresh, cosmopolitan twists. And those who prefer to avoid meat and fish are sure to find something to their liking.

Name: Gitane
Address: Jan Pieter Heijestraat 146, Amsterdam, 1054 MK, Netherlands
Description: This restaurant's pavement terrace, where you can soak up the atmosphere of the trendy Oud-West neighbourhood, and its round windows certainly draw the eye. The Zen-style interior with its distinctive 1970s feel is equally impressive. This is a casual dining establishment, which opens its doors at 10am, every day of the week. The Mediterranean dishes served here have a lot in common with the recipes of Yotam Ottolenghi. Take, for example, the braised pork cheeks with creamy orzo, crunchy oyster mushroom, Petroto cheese and a fresh yoghurt and celeriac purée – what a beautiful plate of food! The chef makes sure that there are plenty of vegetarian and vegan options on the menu, and he keeps his prices affordable. One of Amsterdam's gems!

Name: Resumé by 6&24
Description: A glass of crisp rosé with a fine selection of cured meats in the wine bar or on the canal-side terrace, a few small plates to share, or a complete meal in the restaurant, with its floral, slightly tropical-looking decor… You have plenty of options here. The tempting menu includes an intensely flavoursome ceviche, a vegetarian dish based on dry-aged beetroot, and a rich tarte Tatin.
