The terrace is the perfect spot to sit and their Saturday brunches are a must. The appealing menu marries French and Italian cuisines; expect dishes like scallop Grenobloise, oxtail ragu, or crispy charred sea bass. The food is perfectly paired with a cool, light and airy space dotted with locally sourced pottery.

Name: Em Sherif Sea Café
Address: Rosewood Abu Dhabi Hotel, Zayed the First Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Meaning “mother of Sherif” in Arabic, this restaurant pays homage to the original Beirut branch first opened in 2011. Situated inside the Rosewood hotel, this light, contemporary space offers far reaching views of the water surrounding Al Maryah Island and interiors boasting Portuguese Azulejo hand-painted wall tiles. The authentic menu is seafood focused – make sure you check out the seafood counter as you arrive – and has a wide variety of vibrant, well-balanced Lebanese dishes made for sharing.

Name: Meylas
Address: Al Raha Beach, Al Muneera, Abu Dhabi
Description: It may be a little hard to find but this all-day eatery hidden away among the apartment blocks of Al Muneera Island is well worth seeking out. It began life as a food truck but now the two sisters behind it have a thriving business where their passion for their country and its food culture are clear for all to see. The chefs in the on-view kitchen prepare a menu of authentic and satisfying Emirati dishes.

Name: Punjab Grill
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Grand Canal, Venetian Village, 3rd Street, Al Rawdah, Abu Dhabi
Description: There are Punjab Grills dotted around the world and this outpost, located in the Venetian Village, part of the sprawling acreage of the Ritz-Carlton hotel, is one of the more established branches, having opened in 2015. Ask for one of the booths and sit back and enjoy the Northern Indian specialities and the attentive service. They also have an attractive waterfront location and a terrace from which to enjoy it.

Name: La Petite Maison (LPM)
Address: L1, The Galleria, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The history of La Petite Maison (LPM) began in London in 2007, with further outposts opening around the world in the years since. Here in The Galleria, customers can judge it for themselves, with cuisine prepared with French-Mediterranean touches and served by a well-trained team in elegant surroundings. Dishes like thinly sliced octopus or salt-baked sea bass will put you in a sunny mood; and be sure to leave room for desserts.

Name: NIRI
Address: Building 9, Mamsha Al Saadiyat, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Grab a seat at the counter of this contemporary Japanese restaurant to watch the chefs prepare your dishes over the robata grill. The ingredients are top-notch, and the kitchen is clearly motivated. The pared-back interior is very on-trend and comes complete with a sakura tree. People-watchers and anyone who enjoys a good sea view will prefer a seat on the terrace as this spot on Mamsha Al Saadiyat is hard to beat.

Name: Paradiso
Address: Yas Bay Waterfront Pier 71, Yas Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: A partnership between celebrated French chef Pierre Gagnaire and Nicole Rubi of La Petite Maison in Cannes resulted in this bright and colourful restaurant. It’s the perfect backdrop to their favoured cuisine – that of the Mediterranean, so expect everything from snails and roast poussin to fritto misto, pizza and assorted pasta dishes. The terrace overlooking the water is nicely decked out and a very pleasant spot.

Name: Cafe Milano
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, The Galleria Level 1, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Powerbrokers, movers and shakers in Washington DC will be familiar with the original Café Milano. This elegant sibling is in the Four Seasons – and if you want to be seen enjoying la dolce vita, then start with an aperitivo in the bar. The Italian chef and his team confidently prepare authentic Italian dishes; the homemade pastas are a highlight. There’s also a great terrace.

Name: Oak Room
Address: The Abu Dhabi EDITION Hotel, Al Bateen Marina, Abu Dhabi
Description: Dressed like a smart London club, all wood and leather – but with the music turned up loud – Oak Room is all about meat. Steaks, largely from Japan and Australia, come in various cuts and are accompanied by an impressive selection of sides; don’t miss the triple cooked chips. Sunday roasts are popular and there’s a wide variety of other dishes on offer too, from fish and chips to burgers.

Name: Novikov Abu Dhabi
Address: The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Level 2 Luxury Collection, South Plaza ADGM, Abu Dhabi
Description: This Abu Dhabi outpost of the global franchise is housed in The Galleria Mall on Al Maryah Island. The spacious interior with smartly laid tables has a large open kitchen with a counter – decorated with seasonal ingredients – wrapped around it. Mediterranean cuisine shines, with some highlights being the freshly made daily pasta, fish, chilled gazpacho and berry tart. Their lunch menu is great value and the a la carte offers something for everyone. The experience is completed with a lovely pianist belting out tunes all day.

Name: Al Farah
Address: Khalidiyah St, Al Khalidiyah, W8, Abu Dhabi
Description: The first thing you’ll notice at this bright, contemporary restaurant is a queue of people picking up their orders of manaqeesh and the fresh breads coming out of the oven. The extensive menu offers a range of flavoursome Middle Eastern dishes and it’s a popular destination for breakfast. The restaurant is right in the heart of Al Khalidiyah and is part of a group of family-owned establishments.

Name: Li Jiang
Address: The Ritz-Carlton Abu Dhabi, Grand Canal, Khor Al Maqt'a, Abu Dhabi
Description: Southeast Asian dishes lead the way at this restaurant within The Ritz-Carlton hotel. All dishes are prepared with equal care – the Szechuan chilli lamb loin will certainly get your taste buds excited – but it’s the wok dishes that are their speciality. Order dishes like wok-fried scallops and butter prawns, then watch the chefs working dexterously and skilfully behind the glass screens. The friendly team run the place well and service is smooth and professional.

Name: Dai Pai Dong
Address: Rosewood Abu Dhabi Hotel, Zayed the First Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: Cantonese is king and sharing the thing at Rosewood’s good-looking Chinese restaurant. Whether you enjoy roasted duck, braised brisket, crispy chicken or double-boiled soups, there’s plenty for you to enjoy here, and if you prefer something a little more fiery there are Sichuan dishes too. Weekend brunches are hugely popular too; while Wednesdays host ‘All You Can Grill’ nights.

Name: Finz
Address: Beach Rotana Hotel, 10th Street, Al Zahiyah, Abu Dhabi
Description: Eating seafood by the sea – there aren’t many things in life that can beat it. At Finz the fish and shellfish come in a variety of styles to suit all tastes, so if you want to feel you’re holidaying on the Med you can order fruits de mer or moules marinières, while those who prefer a more Asian theme can try the tempura roll or teriyaki salmon. The charming service is another delight here.

Name: Oii
Address: Al Qana Marina South, Al Maqta’ Street, Abu Dhabi
Description: Meaning ‘hi’ in Portuguese, Oii is located in Al Qana Marina, next to The National Aquarium. On the inside, this relaxed and casual spot is light and airy, thanks to its floor to ceiling windows, while the outside’s spacious, shaded terrace is ideal al fresco dining. Expect a wide-ranging breakfast menu, followed by a Mediterranean-inspired selection of smaller and larger colourful plates, snacks and salads. One way to start your meal is with a grilled octopus with vibrant mojo rojo, followed by the spiced peri peri baby chicken and finish with fruity passion fruit semi freddo.

Name: Martabaan by Hemant Oberoi
Address: Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental Hotel, West Corniche Road, Al Ras Al Akhdar, Abu Dhabi
Description: In contrast to the huge Emirates Palace hotel in which its located, this Indian restaurant occupies a surprisingly small and intimate space. Its eponymous chef has considerable experience around the world and the menu encompasses all his favourite dishes. The tasting menu is the best form of discovery. The enthusiasm of the service team is thoroughly infectious, and their recommendations are always worth heeding.

Name: Butcher & Still
Address: Four Seasons Al Maryah Island Hotel, 2 Global Market Street, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Those who like a classic steakhouse will find this one at the luxurious Four Seasons ticks all the boxes. Leather banquettes? Check. Prime American beef? Check. Great cocktails? Check. Start with the generously proportioned crab cake before diving into a steak – there are plenty on offer, from ribeye to porterhouse. To finish, there’s New York cheesecake of course, but the more adventurous should take on the challenge of the Tribune Tower chocolate cake.

Name: Fouquet's
Address: Louvre Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Cultural District 1, Al Saadiyat Island, Abu Dhabi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: As befits the remarkable Louvre Abu Dhabi, its restaurant is not only one with a famous name serving classic French cuisine, but is also one decidedly grander than its ‘brasserie’ moniker would suggest. The huge, laminated menu offers something for everyone, from glazed duck breast to chicken supreme; finishing with crêpes Suzette will set you up nicely for more gallery viewings.

Name: Catch at St. Regis
Address: Nation Riviera Beach Club, Corniche Road, Abu Dhabi
Description: A lovely spot on the beach provides the ideal setting for this seafood restaurant. Service is warm and quietly confident; the room is bright and spacious; and the menu wide and varied. There’s quite a Japanese influence, with plenty of nigiri and sashimi; there are also plates for sharing, and good use is made of the charcoal grill. The ‘Blow Torch Dynamite Roll’ makes for an explosive start!

Name: Grand Beirut
Address: Unit 12100-1201 (FB), Level 2, The Galleria Al Maryah Island, Adgm Square, Al Maryah Island, Abu Dhabi
Description: Under the same management as Beirut Sur Mer, this restaurant offers just the thing for refuelling after a gruelling day of shopping around Abu Dhabi. The colourful space is decorated with floral printed chairs, vibrant vines adorned with pink flowers, a massive Sakura tree in the centre and an inviting open kitchen to watch the chefs at work. Served with a heartfelt smile, the Lebanese dishes are designed for sharing and generously sized; they are full of flavour and founded upon quality ingredients. Be sure to leave room for their delicious kunafa.

Name: Villa Mamas
Address: Muroor Road, Eastern Road, Al Rawdah, Abu Dhabi
Description: Bahraini chef Roaya Saleh leaves her mark in Abu Dhabi with this elegant Khaleeji restaurant. The interior is a little like a conservatory, with plants all around, colourful artifacts, fresh fruits on display, and shelves of homemade spices, syrups and chefs’ cookbooks. The menu showcases flavours and dishes loved in the region, such as chicken machbous and hummus topped with lamb cubes.

Name: terra
Description: At the quieter end of Al Qana yet still with a view of the boats in the marina, sits terra – relatively new to Abu Dhabi but with a well-established branch in Dubai. Being a Mediterranean restaurant, it’s appropriately relaxed in style and the great music makes it a particularly good choice for dinner. Most of the countries that line the Med get a mention and all the classics are here, including raw dishes and pizza, starters like burrata and croquettes, and plenty of pasta dishes and meats from the Josper oven.

Name: Entresol
Description: Set on the ground floor of a grand city centre property, this small restaurant offers two experiences in one. The front area is filled with memorabilia and has more of a vintage lounge feel, while the raised area behind has a less-cluttered look. The good value tasting menu changes twice a year and offers a selection of modern dishes with a pleasingly unfussy approach, allowing the flavours of the excellent quality produce to shine.

Name: Chef's Corner Restaurant
Description: A friendly team welcome you into this chic city centre brasserie, where you’ll do well to start with a cocktail while choosing from the classic brasserie-style menu. There's plenty to choose from, but the emphasis is on steaks from the Netherlands, the UK and the USA, with those to share proving a particularly popular choice. Other options include everything from tartares, burrata and oysters to burgers, pastas and game – with some seasonal options thrown in – making this spot a hit with locals and visitors alike.

Name: The Catch
Description: Sister to Snatch is this lively, intimate basement izakaya that sits beneath a vaulted brick ceiling. You enter past a small marble-topped sushi counter and can either sit in this room or continue on through the curtain to the cosier room at the rear. Dim lighting and delicious cocktails add to the atmosphere, as do the friendly team, who keep things running like clockwork. The menu covers all bases, from carefully crafted sushi and tempura to dishes from the robata grill and an assortment of bowls – think tom kha, ramen, unagi don and gyudon. The freshly baked madeleines are a must to finish.

Name: B7
Description: Be sure to book ahead at this homely neighbourhood restaurant,which has an experienced chef at its helm. The room has a pleasingly simple rusticity, and the atmosphere and service have a laid-back feel, with the owner both cooking for and serving the guests himself. Pick from around 16 dishes – sharing 4 between two diners is a great way to sample a range of flavours – or simply choose the tasting menu. The flavoursome modern cuisine takes its influences from around the globe, ranging from Cantabrian anchovies to salmon ceviche; desserts are a highlight and the wine list offers great value.

Name: COD
Description: Make for the sultry basement bar for a cocktail or two before heading back up to the atmospheric ground floor restaurant with its dim lighting and on-trend soundtrack. The chefs here might be Latvian, but the cuisine is contemporary Japanese. Start with a selection of sushi and tempura, then choose something from the robata grill. The gyoza of the day is a must, the black cod with sweet miso is a hit, and the mochi ice cream is the perfect way to finish. There’s a vibrancy and freshness to the cooking, yet it still respects the fundamentals of Japanese cuisine.

Name: 3 Chefs
Address: Torņa iela 4, Jekaba Arcade 2b, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: Located in Jacob’s Barracks – a restored 18C building overlooking the Powder Tower and Swedish Gate – this restaurant lives up to exactly what you might expect. It’s run by three chefs – who help serve the dishes and love chatting with their guests – and the menu sticks with the traditional theme by offering classical flavour combinations, albeit updated with touches of creativity and a little refinement. The tasting menu is the best route to having a great all-round experience, and they hold cookery classes for those who like to get hands-on.

Name: Akustika
Description: Set on the ground floor of the well-known Post and Telegraph building, this faux-industrial neighbourhood bistro was created by three friends and designed as a place they themselves would like to dine. Tasty, modern dishes are informed by the seasons, with local produce taking the lead, be it pikeperch from nearby Lake Burtnieks or locally reared lamb, while the Latvian char is a real hit. Be sure to ask the team for their advice when it comes to both the food and the wine. Occasional music performances add to the appeal, as does the terrace in the warmer weather.

Name: Māsa
Description: The contemporary-looking ‘Sister’ sits at the heart of Riga’s Central District and is run by a friendly young team. Muted grey, beige and light wood tones provide a calming feel, yet at the same time the atmosphere is lively and animated. Start with a cocktail and some starters to share – maybe cold-smoked Baltic sprats with salted lemon, capers and wild garlic – before moving on to more substantial dishes like glazed chicken with spring carrot cream and grilled green onion. The fresh ingredients might originate from Latvia, but influences come from across the Mediterranean and occasionally Asia.

Name: MO
Description: Beside the promenade in the historical canal area sits Julianna’s Courtyard, where the 19C printing house and later 20C factories have been lovingly restored to create one of Liepāja's go-to areas. Here you’ll find MO, which offers a satisfying meal out at a fair price. Ask for a table either on or overlooking the terrace, then choose from the wide-ranging menu that includes tartares, carpaccios, sharing plates and main dishes such as beef with truffle mash. Locally produced beers and cocktails make the perfect accompaniment.

Name: TAURO
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This über-smart steak restaurant is secreted away on the ground floor of the Zunda Towers skyscraper and comes with cowhides mounted to look like bulls, hence the name. Forgo starters and enjoy a generous plate of cured meats and salamis from their farm, then move on to a superb steak from Latvia, Spain, California, Japan or Australia. Accompany this with a side – the crispy potatoes with thyme are a must – and one of their freshly made sauces in myriad flavours. The 300+ bin wine list is beautifully curated, with some of the North American classics creating the perfect pairings.

Name: Pavāru māja
Description: A former maternity hospital on the edge of a rural village plays host to this smart, modern restaurant. Here, you are encouraged to relax in their lovely nature observation garden – a place to sit back, listen and watch – before taking time to really savour your meal. Their raised beds and foraging trips provide the kitchen with vegetables and herbs, while the rest of their produce is locally sourced. The four-course lunch and eight-course dinner are informed by what’s fresh and available each day.

Name: Ferma
Description: Sit inside at the chef’s table for a view of the chefs hard at work, or outside on the large terrace to take in views of the city’s oldest park. Chef-Owner Māris’ dishes reflect his love of native produce, with local beef and seafood to the fore, especially herring. The à la carte menu is concise and supplemented by a great value option at lunch, and friendly service completes the picture.

Name: LOWINE
Description: Naturally, wine leads the way at this snug bar located on the very edge of the city. Inside it has a rustic look and a laid-back feel, and on warmer days you can sit outside in the enclosed rear courtyard. The appealing, keenly priced wine list keeps natural wines to the fore and changes weekly, providing plenty of interest for the regulars. Similarly, the seasonally changing menu also lists something for everyone, from the traditional to the modern, with an extensive brunch menu offered earlier in the day and the likes of salmon with ponzu sauce followed by Latvian meatballs in the evening.

Name: Kest
Description: The town’s former fire station is now home to a restaurant which provides an experience of two parts. You start in the bright restaurant, where you dine from a tasting menu made up of modern dishes that keep local produce to the fore. This is accompanied by an interesting alcoholic drinks flight, which also includes some cocktails. After dessert, you then head through to the dark, moody lounge-bar for the second part of your evening, where you enjoy a post-meal drink to a relaxing jazz soundtrack. The team run the place with genuine warmth and their cheery nature can't help but rub off on you.

Name: Stage22
Description: Set on the top floor of the Grand Hotel Kempinski Riga, this sumptuous restaurant affords superb views out over the park and the city skyline. Start with a drink in the chic cocktail bar or out on the lovely narrow terrace, then settle into plush chairs to enjoy your evening. This is an ideal place for celebrating and you will be looked after with consummate ease by the professional team. The wide-ranging Asian menu includes the likes of spicy tuna roll and Argentinian beef fillet with shallot cream, while the crispy vegetable tempura with dashi sauce is not to be missed.

Name: Neiburgs
Description: The crowds thin out as you wind your way down the cobbled streets of the Old Town and find yourself in this peaceful spot. Located on the ground floor of a boutique hotel, this restaurant is the place to dine if you’re looking for a smart environment but with a pleasingly unpretentious atmosphere; there’s also a lovely terrace for warmer days. The menus offer fresh, unfussy dishes with some Mediterranean influences, and the seafood options are particularly appealing. The crab and tiger prawn ravioli with bisque sauce is a real winner, while the herring dishes are always a popular choice.

Name: Barents Cocktail & Seafood Bar
Description: It’s worth booking a table in advance at this elegant hidden gem – not only is it compact, but it also acts as the cocktail bar for next door Barents, so can get very busy. The drinks list is joined by a concise menu; the seafood platter is a feast for the eyes, but don’t overlook the delicious 'small bites' which change with the seasons. Naturally, you should start and end with some cocktails from their thoughtfully curated selection, which range from the well-known classics to their own signature creations with a Nordic twist.

Name: Zoltners
Description: You'll find the Zoltners Brewery in the heart of the glorious Zemgale countryside, along with this slick, modern restaurant and an attractively restored period house that’s now a small hotel boasting modern bedrooms; make a weekend of it by dining, staying the night and visiting the Tērvete Nature Park. Menus showcase local produce in an appealing mix of flavoursome northern European dishes, and the simple starters go perfectly with their home-brewed beers and local spirits.

Name: Tails
Description: There’s a choice of two bistro-style dining rooms at Tails, but the raw bar counter really is the place to sit to make the most of the experience. The chefs take fish seriously here by adopting a tail to gill approach – and there’s even a drying room on show. They cure their own fish, make their own ceviches, and their sharing shellfish platter is something to linger over. Keep an eye out for the daily specials too, which often feature something a little different. For the ultimate indulgence, accompany your meal with a bottle of champagne.

Name: Barents
Description: An impressive early 20th-century art nouveau property in the Old Town plays host to this large restaurant with a spacious front terrace and a distinct Nordic style. The seasonally changing menu comprises modern dishes that are made up of numerous elements and combine many flavours and textures in great harmony. Seafood, such as smoked eel with oysters, velouté and Spruce needles, is a strength – sourced from local and northern waters – and the produce is displayed on ice in the middle of the room and explained to diners as they arrive. The champagne selection provides a noteworthy accompaniment.

Name: Seasons
Address: Grand Palace Hotel, Pils iela 12, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: The luxurious Grand Palace Hotel plays host to this sumptuous restaurant, as well as a supremely comfortable bar which comes packed with antiques and fine art – be sure to either start or end your night here. Seasonal dishes are themed around the world’s greatest painters, so are naturally both visually striking and full of colour. The likes of lightly smoked trout with béarnaise sauce are a joy to eat, and if you spot the toffee pudding with buttermilk sorbet, be sure to order it. The wine list contains some premium bottles, and plush bedrooms mean you don't have to far to go once fully sated.

Name: JOHN
Address: A22 Hotel, Ausekļa iela 22, Riga, 1010, Latvia
Description: Set within the striking A22 hotel, this chic restaurant overlooking the historic Viesturdārzs park is named after John F Kennedy, who stayed here back in 1939; be sure to keep an eye out for some of the original art nouveau features, which have been carefully restored. The room now has a romantic feel, helped along by a ceiling bedecked in roses, and the menu is modern too, with a diverse selection of dishes highlighting seasonal local produce, from Arctic char to locally farmed ostrich. The King crab with lemon aioli and pickled apples is a hit, as is the delicious honey cake.

Name: Whitehouse
Address: Vermane Park, Terbatas iela 2, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: Whitehouse's dining terrace is one of the most sought after in the city thanks to its views over the colourful flower displays of Vērmanes Garden, but its signature cocktails ensure that the place really comes alive too. It’s a sizeable spot, with a long, narrow room, stylish décor and even a living wall. Menus blend influences from across the globe with a range of fermentation techniques, and there’s a touch of theatre to the presentation. The seasonal tasting menus reflect the locality – as do the smaller local producers on their wine list – and desserts are a particular highlight.

Name: BABO
Description: BABO is currently something of a lesser-known gem. Set up by a pair of experienced restaurateurs, it’s split between two rooms and a smart terrace. One of the owners hails from Georgia and it’s this that informs the menu. Delicious breads are cooked in the pizza oven and the charcoal grill adds a lovely flavour to the various meats and fish. Order two dishes each and share – maybe beef and pork khinkali (dumplings), salmon in bazhe (walnut) sauce or chicken tabaka with salt and lemon. The superb wine list showcases a unique mix of classic and modern Georgian wines, which they import directly.

Name: 36.Line Grill Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Beachside locations don’t come much better than this, as you can walk straight in off the sand. Those after some respite from the sun can stay inside, while those wanting to feel the sea breeze should head for the glass-fronted terrace. The accessible menu covers all options, from lighter sushi and tartares to dumplings and hearty grilled fish and meat dishes. The tiramisu laced with the famous Black Balsam – their national drink – is a must-try, and the extensive selection of wines and cocktails is perfect for watching the sun go down.

Name: Le Dome
Address: Dome Hotel & Spa, Miesnieku iela 4, Riga, 1050, Latvia
Description: Tucked away down the cobbled streets of the Old Town is a 400-year-old building which is home to both a boutique hotel and this intimate restaurant. Dine in the long, narrow room or, in summer, book a spot on the rooftop terrace overlooking the Daugava River. Cooking has a classical French heart, pepped up by influences from the wider Mediterranean, and while the chef is classically trained, he brings the dishes up to date with modern execution. Top-quality seasonal ingredients are the stars of the show, their flavours shining through thanks to the carefully balanced flavours and the finesse of the seasoning.

Name: Riviera
Description: This long-standing brasserie has stood the test of time, and it's easy to see why. The room has a fresh, unfussy elegance and a warm Mediterranean style – and the menu is the perfect match. Good quality ingredients feature in an appealing range of classic Mediterranean dishes, with everything from oysters and tartares to fish and steaks of offer; the vitello tonnato is worth a mention, as is the tiramisu. Everything is generously sized, with well-defined flavours and textures, and the sizeable wine list (1,000+) offers some great choices from around the globe. In summer, the terrace is the place to be.

Name: Das Wolf
Description: Here, you can expect classic cuisine made with top-notch ingredients and free of unnecessary embellishments. It is the pair of set menus, one of which is vegetarian, that are the centrepiece. Standout dishes include "ikejime sea bass, charred leek, salted lemon" and "scallop, kohlrabi, yellow pepper". Alternatively, there is a small selection of simpler options available à la carte. Austrian labels feature prominently on the impressive wine list. The food is served in different spaces – some with a rustic feel, others more modern – or out on the terrace. Tip: The restaurant is easily accessible by public transport – the train station is just around the corner.

Name: Das Markthof
Description: This restaurant is part of the Edhofer family's organic farm, nestled in the heart of the little village. The welcoming atmosphere can be attributed in no small part to your gracious and attentive hostess, Angelika Edhofer, whose passion for hospitality is shared by chefs Fabian Schasching and Max Eichberger. Highly skilled and dedicated, they masterfully bridge the gap between hearty traditional fare and fine-dining cuisine. The dishes showcase ingredients from their own farm – including organic Angus beef – alongside carefully selected international items such as halibut and lobster. The inviting decor is enhanced by charming modern touches and features a glass façade that can be opened up completely in summer – and let's not forget the splendid garden terrace!

Name: JOLA
Description: Jola takes its name from the charming duo behind this venture: Jonathan Wittenbrink, who delivers outstanding vegan cuisine, and Larissa Andres, who manages the service in the compact dining space with charm and aplomb. Seasonal and regional ingredients go into the creative surprise set menu, which features memorable dishes such as raviolo stuffed with aubergine ragout, served with courgette, lightly toasted pine nuts and a wonderfully intense tomato essence. Choose between wine and alcohol-free pairings. The setting is stylish and modern yet pleasingly laid back – the open kitchen certainly adds to that. A nice touch: The menu is printed on plantable seed paper – take it home and see what blooms!

Name: BOU4
Description: First things first: be sure to book, because the Bouvier family's small restaurant has just four tables (hence the name "BOU4"). Junior manager and maître d' Julian Bouvier attentively hosts a maximum of 14 diners. Chef Christoph Gschwendtner also joins in front of house, proud to personally present his creations at the table. His cooking leans towards classic French cuisine, with Asian or Levantine accents adding variety. The dishes are elaborate and technical, as you will see from the get-go with the array of appetisers. Diners can opt for a four- or six-course format of the set menu, the dishes in which change weekly. The meal starts for all diners at 6pm. The curved black wooden tables make for a distinctive feature in the pared-back, modern interior. The restaurant is on the premises of Hotel Jägerhof.

Name: Wirtshaus by Vitus Winkler
Address: Kirchweg 2, Sankt Veit im Pongau, 5621, Austria
Description: This modern Alpine tavern is a wonderful alternative to the fine dining restaurant here at Hotel Sonnenhof. Windows between the two dining areas foster a nice and airy feel and mean there is a view of the magnificent mountain landscape from almost every table. The tastefully designed upscale interior with a hint of rusticity is the perfect setting in which to enjoy a contemporary take on Wirtshausküche (tavern cuisine) based on select, mostly regional ingredients. Think "Alpine fish soup – paprika fish soup, Alpine prawns, fennel agnolotti" or "Pongauer Fleischkrapfen (meat and sauerkraut dumplings), coleslaw, bacon chips, chives". Go à la carte or choose a three- to five-course set menu. Wine lovers will appreciate the wine list from the hotel's fine dining restaurant, Kräuterreich. The whole experience is rounded off by the very cordial and dedicated team – clearly passionate about what they do, and laid-back but sophisticated.

Name: Gasthaus Steinberg
Description: If you want to combine a hiking trip with a really wonderful meal at a fair price, the Grafl family establishment is the place to go! In this typical regional inn in a wonderfully idyllic location, the cuisine is traditional, aromatic, and perfectly crafted. The Pressknödelsuppe (dumpling soup) and Almrindsülzchen (Alpine beef aspic) are full of flavour, not to mention classics such as beef goulash and schnitzel. In summer, the terrace boasting a view of the surrounding countryside and mountains is a joy. Overnight accommodation is also an option.

Name: Addiert
Description: There is only space for a handful of diners at the L-shaped chef's table in this restaurant's minimalist dining space. A nine-course set menu is prepared in the fully open stainless steel kitchen – this culinary journey through Korea lasts approximately three hours. Authenticity is key, but local ingredients and European cooking techniques still find their place. This results in intensely flavoursome dishes such as "gochujang ceviche": slices of Austrian trout marinated in chilli paste, topped with a tangy grapefruit sabayon and finished with a delicate basil oil. The service is charming and attentive to every guest's needs and enjoys sharing insights into the finer points of Korean cuisine.

Name: Gamskogelhütte Fine Dining by Stefan Lastin
Description: Boasting a fabulous location at 1 850m above sea level, this small fine dining restaurant is a place where you can truly unwind. In a cosy Alpine-style space featuring rustic wood and charming natural stone, diners sit at elegantly set tables to savour an ambitious three- to six-course set menu complemented by elaborate amuse-bouches to start and sweet treats to finish. Interesting well-matched wine pairings are available, and the list itself includes some rare gems worth sampling. Service is exceptionally friendly and attentive – chef Stefan Lastin presents his dishes personally, and proprietor Peter Aschbacher takes genuine pleasure in interacting with his diners. N.B. In summer, you can drive up the somewhat arduous mountain road yourself, or alternatively take the bus or walk. In winter, you will be picked up by snowmobile, or can ski in – the restaurant is right by the slope.

Name: El Patio de Claudio
Description: Located within the walls of the Hotel Único Madrid, in the city’s Salamanca district, this restaurant boasts a bistro-style ambience, a classically furnished and renovated interior design, plus a terrace in the courtyard. At the helm here is experienced chef Mario Valles, who showcases traditional cuisine with a Mediterranean flavour and the occasional international flourish. His à la carte features sharing and tapas-style options, alongside dishes such as grilled brown crab with avocado and chilli pepper, the delicious Cornish hen and, for dessert, the candied lemon with citrus ganache.

Name: Yo, Cocina Contemporánea
Description: For elaborate cooking with a difference, we recommend heading to this restaurant in Seville that serves cuisine direct from the Sardinian capital, Cagliari, in Italy. Through this new venture, Chef Stefano Deidda, who had already enjoyed considerable gastronomic success on the island, is seeking to develop a much more relaxed and personal project in a city that he and his partner (Eva Urru) have fallen in love with. His creative and contemporary cuisine, which is only showcased on two tasting menus (Esencial and Esencia), is both delicate and teeming with Andalucian and Gallic nuances. One dish that came as a particular surprise was the delicious and creamy onion and cheese ravioli with onion soup and white wine.

Name: Villa Más
Address: Passeig de Sant Pol 95, Sant Feliu de Guíxols, 17220, Spain
Description: This restaurant occupies an impressive setting in an old Modernist-style villa overlooking Sant Pol beach, as well as boasting a pleasant terrace that gets very busy in the evening. The traditional, maritime-inspired à la carte features top-notch fresh fish straight from the auction (sea bream, John Dory, grouper, sea bass etc), a few rice dishes and fideuàs. The extensive wine list has a particular penchant for wines from Burgundy.

Name: Ruge
Address: Embalse de La Jarosa, Guadarrama, 28440, Spain
Description: This attractive family-run restaurant in the heart of nature and just a stone's throw from the La Jarosa reservoir is the perfect setting in which to re-energise close to Madrid. Grilled meat and rice dishes are the mainstays on the à la carte, although you’ll also find an impressive selection of tapas and several Japanese-inspired dishes. The rustic-minimalist interior comes as a pleasant surprise, as does the charming chillout terrace.

Name: Pazo de Toubes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace
Description: Located in the heart of the Ribeiro wine region, this restaurant bearing the name of a winery occupying an 18C manor house surrounded by vineyards, comes as a pleasant surprise, courtesy of its contemporary cuisine with a local flavour enhanced by touches from further afield. The à la carte is complemented by two tasting menus, one entitled Floración (7 courses), the other Envero (9 courses), both with a wine-pairing option. We can highly recommend the sea urchin and red prawn dish, with its focus on top-quality ingredients, as well as the more traditional combo of egg with fried pig’s ear and smoked potato parmentier.

Name: Ona Cuina Oberta
Address: Duc Carles de Borja 28, Gandia, 46701, Spain
Description: The couple at the helm, with Paco Castelló at the wheel in the kitchen and Gabri Tarín in charge of the dining room, declare themselves to be 100% Mediterranean, so that gastronomic culture is evident in every dish. In this small restaurant, located in a pedestrianised street in the old town (the area known as La Ciudad Ducal), you will find a proposal that revolves exclusively around surprise menus (Ona and Ona Cuina Oberta) that change daily, depending on the market and always giving a great deal of prominence to fish and vegetables. We have loved their tiger nut ajoblanco with cherry granita, and the vegetable carbonara!

Name: Toc al Mar
Description: A restaurant right on the beach? Originally a simple fishermen's hut, this restaurant is practically on the sand and has the feel of a traditional beach bar, with fantastic views of the sea and sunbathers enjoying the sun. The menu offers a fine selection of Catalan seafood dishes, rice dishes for two and wild fish by weight, which are usually grilled over holm oak wood. In season, given the large number of visitors due to its exceptional location, we recommend you book in advance.

Name: Mengem
Description: This attractive bistro is located in El Cabanyal-El Canyamelar, the picturesque fishing district of Valencia, where typical shacks coexist alongside unpretentious fishermen's houses and beautiful buildings designed in a more modern style. The couple in charge of the kitchen create impressively flavoured and well-structured cuisine that is rooted in Gallic tradition and can be enjoyed on a concise and contemporary seasonal à la carte and three set menus (Mediodía, El Trío, and Mengem).

Name: Maleducat
Description: This restaurant, located just a few steps from the San Antoni market, has made a name for itself thanks its mix of cuisine from the sea and the mountains. Here, they like to say that they create food for “nonconformist gourmets”, for whom they have created varied cuisine with a modern touch and an impressive array of dishes and tapas, along with daily specials and main dishes made for sharing. We particularly enjoyed the rice dish with red Palamós shrimp tartare, shrimp head emulsion and pig’s trotter carpaccio, a dish that pays homage to the legendary Els Tinars restaurant in Llagostera. There’s also a menu entitled “At your service, chef!”

Name: Leña Barcelona
Address: Plaça de Pius XII 4, Barcelona, 08028, Spain
Description: This glamorous restaurant, part of the dining options available at the Grand Hyatt Barcelona, bears the hallmark of chef Dani García and follows the aesthetic look established by his brothers in Madrid, Marbella and Dubai. This spacious restaurant, with its elegant, urban steakhouse philosophy, combines the usual presence on the menu of its famous “yakipinchos” and premium red meats (different cuts and periods of aging) with other more local dishes, such as Butifarra de Perol croquettes, and vegetable-based specialities including delicious grilled avocado from Malaga. A live DJ makes an appearance on some evenings, along with a brunch at the weekend. You also have the option of taking home your own personalised knife!

Name: Jaylu
Description: A family-run restaurant located midway between Los Remedios and Triana that has made a name for itself thanks to three key criteria: namely, quality, tradition and full respect for the ingredients they use. The elegant, classically styled interior provides the backdrop for an à la carte specialising in fish and seafood of the day, cooked simply without detracting from the quality of the ingredients used (many caught using traditional fishing methods). As a starter, don’t miss the delicate salmorejo with shrimp.

Name: Fronda Pasaje
Description: If vegetarian cuisine is your go-to, you have to go to El Born and try it at this restaurant, located just a stone’s throw from the famous basilica of Santa Maria del Mar. The proposal, with a choice of à la carte and two set menus, bears the signature of Argentinean chef-biologist Máximo Cabrera, who shows us how plant-based cuisine is not only healthy, but also tremendously tasty. The dishes, which in some cases are presented as a surprising trompe l'oeil, successfully combine science and creativity.

Name: Fūmu
Address: Marqués de San Esteban 5, Gijón, 33206, Spain
Description: This restaurant, just a stone's throw from the marina and the Fomentín dock, boasts a young atmosphere and has a good sushi bar (for eight diners), although it also has a few tables. The two chefs in charge, Álvaro Gragera and Carlos Fraguas, propose a cuisine with Japanese roots based on the excellent products of the Bay of Biscay and Mediterranean recipes, through a small menu of bite-size nibbles (here the nigiris stand out for their technique, size and flavour) and an Omakase menu designed for sharing. They age the fish themselves!

Name: DESACATO
Description: A restaurant with a relaxed, informal feel and an industrial-style decor in Seville’s historic quarter, where sections on the menu entitled The Preliminaries, Sharing is Living, Carnal Temptations, and From the Cantabrian Sea to the Mediterranean set the scene for what is to come. The restaurant describes itself as committed to “irreverent cuisine” in which fusion influences and Andalucian and Basque flavours all play their part. You’ll also find constantly changing fish and seafood dishes that don’t feature on the menu.

Name: Cornamusa Cibeles
Description: A restaurant with a unique location? This one is truly unique, as it is located on the rooftop of the iconic Palacio de Cibeles, where Madrid's City Hall is located. It has a contemporary interior design, with a central cocktail bar and the tables are divided between the dining room, in two sections, and the terrace on the upper floor. The menu, with a contemporary feel and some of the dishes finished before your eyes, offers an interesting mix of Madrid-style recipes and signature dishes. At lunchtime, on weekdays, they also offer an executive menu!

Name: Els Comdals
Description: Located about 5km southeast of Cervera, this restaurant is striking for its setting in an historic farm boasting large stone archways that was once the granary for the Montserrat monastery and the occasional residence of its abbot. The updated take on traditional Catalan cuisine (choose between the à la carte and an “executive” menu), is based around top-quality ingredients, many of which are, where possible, sourced locally. Els Comdals is also popular with groups and as an event venue.

Name: Converso
Description: Converso is located within the walls of the luxurious Castilla Termal Monasterio de Valbuena hotel, a beautiful 12C Cistercian complex that has been converted into an oasis of tranquillity. It is accessed via the hotel's own restaurant, as this gourmet dining space occupies a charming dining room with an open-view kitchen and no little charm. The cuisine here, overseen by award-winning chef Miguel Ángel de la Cruz and available on two tasting menus (Essentia and Centum), showcases traditional Castilian recipes and flavours but with a focus on modern technique and creativity, plus a firm focus on locally sourced ingredients (vegetables from his garden, black truffles from Canalejas de Peñafiel, honey from Olmedo, the superb, sustainably produced prawns from the fish farm in Medina del Campo, artisanal bread from Quintanilla de Onésimo etc). One dish that stands out for its elegance, simplicity and flavour is the truffled yolk from eggs from the property with crispy pork.

Name: Fontané
Address: Carrer Major, Sant Julià de Ramis, 17481, Spain
Description: Fontané is located on the summit of the Sants Metges mountain in a location that the restaurant describes as “between heaven and earth”. Here, the focus is on the traditional Catalan cuisine that the Roca brothers, in a tribute to their mother (Montserrat Fontané), conjure up at the Hotel Esperit Roca, in the Castillo de Sant Julià de Ramis. The dining room, with its wooden deck and impressive views, provides the setting for cuisine that evokes the delicious dishes that their mother used to make at the original Can Roca, and which they have recreated here with a modern twist. We were pleasantly surprised by the “suquet de cabracho”, with a tomato tartare base unlike the usual preparation of this typical fish stew.

Name: Bevir by Lopesan
Description: After enjoying such resounding success in the capital of Gran Canaria, this restaurant is embarking on a new venture in the luxurious Lopesan Costa Meloneras Resort & Spa hotel. The goal? To offer diners an even more hedonistic culinary experience. The restaurant is found in an interior courtyard with large windows overlooking it, opting for a minimalist aesthetic and with chef José Luis Espino at the helm, a man loyal to Canarian produce who tries to define his cuisine under the concept ‘Where the vegetable garden meets the sea’, always paying homage to local flavours and the importance of making the most of natural ingredients. You will find two tasting menus, with a modern twist, which seek to pay tribute to Benito Pérez Galdós's most famous characters and celebrate this distinguished Canarian writer: Fortunata (11 courses) and Jacinta (14 courses). The standout dish? We loved the beetroot with beurre blanc and dill oil for its excellent combination of flavours and textures.

Name: Can Bo
Description: The name of this tapas and wine bar is a subtle phonetic tribute to Francesc Cambó, founder of the historic building in which it is located. The menu here features tapas and dishes to share, all of which showcase the quality of ingredients and local cuisine, all accompanied by pairings from the extensive and carefully curated wine cellar of over 150 labels. The overall look here is one characterised by elegant Mediterranean-style decor, with decorative detail inspired by Catalan Modernism, large windows that flood the space with natural light, and a cosy atmosphere that provides an enjoyable backdrop.

Name: Berso
Description: Berso occupies a tastefully renovated house with a striking contemporary interior design, featuring walls embellished with colourful canvases and decorative details that relate to the town’s renowned music band. The chef at the helm, Martín Mantilla, has created an updated traditional menu that works with the seasons and ingredients that he sources locally. The pleasant patio-terrace is an added bonus.

Name: AlKostat del Mar
Description: Part of the Finca Victoria Hotel & Spa. From the hotel reception you are accompanied to the restaurant, which is accessed via the terrace overlooking the swimming pool. Boasting a rustic-Mediterranean ambience, the dining space is laid out around a bucolic open courtyard surrounded by covered archways where most of the tables are positioned. The aim of the cuisine here, under the stewardship of award-winning chef Jordi Vilà, is to pay tribute to traditional Catalan cooking, albeit with a more contemporary twist, on a menu that includes delicious appetisers, enticing starters, a variety of “senyoret-style” rice dishes (from the Empordà and Girona regions, plus an option entitled “from the boat”) and grilled dishes that that showcase the best of the sea and mountains.

Name: sushi imagine
Description: The name means ‘making the most of the moment’. The chef is a kitchen team of one, pouring his passion into all things sushi. Side dishes are prepared with attention to modulations in flavour that keep the sake flowing. Use of red vinegar to make sushi rice reflects experience in Tokyo. Nigiri are moulded to place the main ingredient front and centre. Fish is thick-cut, sushi rice restrained in quantity. From start to finish, the chef’s determination to satisfy with fish in season shines through.

Name: JIANG NAN CHUN
Address: 37F, Four Seasons Hotel Osaka, 2-4-32 Dojima, Kita-ku, Osaka, 530-0003, Japan
Description: Jiang Nan Chun, meaning ‘springtime in Jiangnan,’ is borrowed from a four-line poem of the Tang dynasty. The chandelier with its plum motif symbolically echoes this poem of early spring. From its perch on a high floor of a tall building, the restaurant offers sweeping views of the Osaka cityscape. The chef, a native of Hong Kong, exercises his talents in traditional Cantonese cuisine. Deferring to yum cha tradition, dim sum is served at lunchtime only. Seasonal fare, served prix fixe only, is a delight.

Name: wabiya
Description: The hearth and the wood-fired oven in the centre of the open kitchen catch the eye. The chef flexes his culinary muscles with yakitori grilled over charcoal and wood flame. Fire is manipulated to smoke the poultry, which is mainly free-range chicken and duck raised in Kyoto. While various cuts are chargrilled on skewers, larger pieces are patiently roasted over wood flame. Ramen or curry made with chicken dashi is served to close out the meal. The flavour of chicken can be enjoyed to the full.

Name: Brasserie RÉGINE
Address: 1F, The St. Regis Osaka, 3-6-12 Hommachi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0053, Japan
Description: Casual French dining in St. Regis Hotel Osaka, where prix fixe menus change with the seasons. Supervising the cuisine is the chef from Ryuzu in Tokyo. Classic techniques meet a simple, modern décor and a deep respect for French tradition is reflected in the emphasis on quality ingredients. The house features a spacious interior, mosaic floor and outdoor terrace—de rigueur for a brasserie.

Name: KOGA
Description: The chef prizes ‘combinations of flavours and aromas’. His mentor in Paris, Christian Le Squer, taught him to seek out new flavours by developing the sensibility of a perfumer. Experience and ideas come together in the ‘Warm Salad’. Vegetables picked in the Takagamine district of Kyoto’s Kita Ward are cooked in a variety of ways, drawing the flavour of each to the fore. Interplay of aromas between char-grilled meat dishes and their sauces express this fare’s unique character.

Name: Hanhan
Description: The name means ‘half and half’, as the omakase set menu features half meat and half vegetables. Following kappo and sushi apprenticeships, the chef was inspired to try some unique takes on meat dishes, substituting kaiseki fish dishes with beef, pork, chicken and other meats. Chicken wings stuffed with enoki mushrooms wrapped in kombu and norimaki of Chinese yam showcase practised skill and imaginative licence in equal measure.

Name: bistrot neuf
Description: The stylish, retro interior of this bistro is decorated with pop posters from France. The name can mean ‘nine’ or ‘new’ – because the chef hopes guests will visit this nine-tsubo (30 sqm) space feeling fresh and new each time. Standards include oeufs mayonnaise, pâté de campagne and beef cheek stewed in red wine. The chef’s experience in Italian cuisine brings pasta to the table as well. Portions are generous, the better to enjoy sharing.

Name: isolata
Description: The restaurant, named after the Italian word for ‘outbuilding’, is housed in a refurbished storehouse, once a dressmaking room at a girls’ finishing school, beside a retro-style building. The original ceiling and beams lend the space a stately ambience. The chef, who honed his skills in several regions of Italy, pays special reverence to local cuisines. Using techniques suited to the climate of each season, he interprets Italian culinary lore with a modern sensibility.

Name: Ryoriya EN
Description: The shop curtain emblazoned with a large circle in a single, bold brushstroke catches the eye. The symbol echoes the restaurant’s name, ‘EN’, which means ‘circle’ or ‘connection’ in Japanese, affirming the importance of connections among people. The restaurant harvests its own vegetables thanks to close bonds with the farmers in the Kamigamo and Shugakuin Imperial Villa areas; they are picked in the morning, so always arrive vibrant and fresh. A full range of accompaniments are available to join the freshly cooked white rice, and the house makes generous use of them. With the passionate conviction that cooking reflects the person, the restaurant forms a harmonious circle with its guests.

Name: Oryori Nonohara
Description: The restaurant weaves the culture and traditional ceremonies of Japan into its menu. In the seventh lunar month, to celebrate Tanabata, the Star Festival, wanmono is served in lacquer bowls featuring the Milky Way in powdered precious metal. Other tableware also reflects the seasons. One wanmono item features a pairing of hamo and samatsu mushroom in a dish that recalls the tale of Hikoboshi and Orihime: the stars Altair and Vega, two lovers destined to meet but once a year. Sweets include umegae mochi, from Dazaifu Tenmangu Shrine in Fukuoka. Tea from the Yame area of Fukuoka is served in homage to the chef’s hometown.

Name: Fuyacho Kuraku
Description: Names of dishes cram the menu. The menu is replete with fish dishes, so you can enjoy the ‘fruits of the sea’ to the full. Fish from Wakasa Bay, in the chef’s native Fukui Prefecture, is a point of pride. Whether served as sashimi, grilled with salt or boiled in soy sauce, their inherent flavours shine through. ‘Heshiko’, fish pickled in rice-bran paste, is a Fukui hometown favourite. Fukui sakes are ordered in, spreading the appeal of the Echizen and Wakasa regions. Standards such as potato salad and deep-fried horse mackerel are perennial hits as well.

Name: Empathie
Description: This restaurant strives to ensure that what you eat leaves an impression. No-nonsense preparations place the ingredients front and centre and the menu oozes luxury, with French ingredients such as caviar, foie gras and truffles. Counter-style service conveys the message of each dish directly to diners in their own language. True to its name, meaning ‘empathy’ in French, the restaurant creates in chef and diner a shared anticipation of each coming season.

Name: Haberbüni
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The atmosphere here is one of a kind! Housed in the airy hayloft of a 19C farmhouse with rustic beams, this place has a special feel to it. The tasteful interior is complemented by a secluded garden terrace with trees and shrubs. The food is fresh and made with high-quality ingredients. In the evening, there is a set menu and an à la carte selection. The latter is also available at lunchtime, supplemented by daily specials and a "Business Lunch" option. Excellent wine list featuring plenty of rarities and magnums.

Name: Le Cerf
Description: This century-old culinary institution is a renowned name in the region. Reinvented from top to bottom, it now serves good old unpretentious dishes in a traditional vein: for example, strips of veal from the Pays d'Enhaut, golden rösti and green salad… and let's not forget the malakoffs – fried cheese balls made with PDO cheese from the old fort in the valley – and the fondues! Cosy, rustic-style ambience, plus a superb terrace with mountain views.

Name: Weinlaube
Description: A wonderful place where hospitality is truly a way of life. With its family feel and warm-hearted service, Weinlaube exudes a cosy, welcoming charm. In this converted farmhouse nestled in a quiet hamlet near the Austrian border, diners take their seats in cosy Stube-style dining rooms or out on the gorgeous terrace and tuck into honest, seasonal fare with the odd international twist. The menu features dishes such as pan-fried char from Brüggli fish farm, Béarnaise sauce, peas and potatoes, or tajarin, agretti, cured egg and bottarga. Open-fire cooking also plays a key role – a barbecue, fire ring and smoker are set up outside the kitchen. The wine list boasts an impressive selection.

Name: Ciani Lugano
Description: Located between the Palazzo dei Congressi and the Ciani Garden, this modern and cosmopolitan venue is a true gem. Renowned regional chef Dario Ranza focuses on Mediterranean cuisine, prepared with skill and precision to guarantee delicious flavors. Among his specialties: Lostallo salmon “Caini style,” a variety of risottos, sole meunière, and salt-crusted sea bass, filleted directly at the table. The selection of exclusive wines and Champagnes is truly remarkable.

Name: Trübli
Description: There are plenty of reasons to stop off at this historical inn (1785) located in the heart of the old town – the cosy and relaxed atmosphere, the friendly and experienced team, the wonderful food… In the evening, the concept is a surprise set menu comprising three courses (a vegetarian version is also available), to which you can add an extra dish and/or a dessert. A supplementary cheese course is also available. The extremely dedicated chef brings a personal touch to the service, and his passion for wine is palpable, not least in his excellent recommendations drawn from the nicely curated wine list with a focus on German estates. Pretty terrace out front. Tip for motorists: Parkhaus Eulachpassage is 200m away.

Name: Matière
Description: This vibrant, authentic and generous eatery is tucked away in a side street. Vintage furniture, an open kitchen, a few alfresco tables on a patio and a funky soundtrack from another era set the scene. The spotlight is on tradition and regional fare: pickled pork pâté en croûte (pork pie) with a perfect balance between texture, port wine jelly and gutsy seasoning. Juicy, tender, impeccably grilled lamb is served on a bed of fried cabbage with an acidic herby cream. A subtly daring chocolate and mushroom tartlet adds the final flourish to your meal.

Name: Paradiesli
Description: The journey to the village of Betlis may not be the most straightforward (the road from Weesen is only open for five minutes at a time on the half hour or hour), but the stunning elevated location more than compensates with a view of nearby Lake Walen and the mountain landscape. There is greenery at every turn – on the terrace in particular you feel like you are in a corner of paradise. The interior is attractive and sleek, its wooden decor exuding traditional charm, fostering a pleasingly unpretentious and relaxed atmosphere. Choose between small plates such as pickled vegetables or "lettuce leaves, herb quark, popped buckwheat" and larger dishes such as "pork cheeks (organic, Uelihof), Serviettenknödel (bread dumplings), raw fennel salad". Alternatively there are three versions of the set menu: meat/fish, vegetarian or vegan. The restaurant Wirtschaft im FRANZ in Zurich belongs to the same establishment.

Name: Blaue Ente by Alex
Description: Historical industrial architecture outside and a trendy, lively atmosphere inside – the old machinery really draws the eye! The relaxed yet efficient front-of-house team contributes to a pleasingly casual vibe. Select ingredients are at the heart of the contemporary, seasonally inspired dishes. The menu features, for example, "fillet of smoked organic trout from the Glauser family, beetroot and shiitake mushroom tartare and horseradish" or "cordon bleu of Toggenburg veal with Graubünden mountain cheese, pommes alumettes and root spinach". A good selection of wines. The terrace is very popular. At lunchtime, there are also simpler, constantly changing daily specials.

Name: Les Ateliers
Description: After having been deserted for some 25 years, this former metal engineering workshop just behind the railway station has been revived by Jean-Sébastien Ribette and Sahondra Verdan. An off-kilter, smart industrial vibe sets the scene for a two-pronged culinary offer: brasserie fare on one side and a more ambitious menu in the gourmet section. Market availability dictates the score, hence the freshness of the ingredients, both at lunch and at dinner. Examples: tartare of red tuna in ginger and sake; confit of duck, shredded green beans and dressing; savarin of confit of lemon drizzled in limoncello. Friendly, on-the-ball service and excellent tips to try local wines.

Name: Fiskebar
Description: A Nordic enclave at the Ritz Carlton in Geneva, Fiskebar has made a name for itself thanks to its delightful fish- and seafood-based cuisine. The finest ingredients are sourced via short supply chains and skilfully prepared by an expert kitchen team. Diners are treated to fresh and healthy Scandinavian cuisine, enhanced with subtle Mediterranean touches – smoking and fermentation techniques are also put to good use. In a setting that tastefully combines rustic materials with more modern touches, diners take their seats at tables that look onto the open kitchen or afford a view of the lake. On top of that, the wine list abounds with pleasing discoveries, including a range of biodynamic wines.

Name: Le Roc
Description: The restaurant of the Hôtel de Rougemont serves classic French cuisine with a contemporary twist. The house-smoked salmon, green asparagus in breadcrumbs, salsa verde emulsion and citrus fruits makes a lasting impression… enjoyed in a delightful Alpine interior, tastefully decorated (old wood, light-coloured banquettes and seats, modern lighting), or on the terrace, with views of the mountains.

Name: Schlüssel
Description: Tanja Grandits, known from the Stucki in Basel, has created a deliberately relaxed and accessible concept here. The cuisine is fresh, modern and creative, and the menu also features one or two Grandits classics. There is a 3- to 5-course menu (regular and vegetarian), plus an appealing à la carte selection. Appetising options include ‘crustacean bisque, prawn dumplings, tomato compote’ or ‘spinach dumplings, mountain cheese, caraway seeds’. A lunch menu is also available at midday. Marten Harder's cuisine is complemented by a carefully curated wine list featuring excellent wines, mainly from Switzerland. The service, under the direction of Edi Magalhães (formerly of Casa Caminada), is pleasantly experienced, well-coordinated and attentive to guests' needs. You feel welcome and warmly cared for. A nice idea: on request, you can have various cookbooks by Tanja Grandits brought to your table – perfect for browsing through. The ambience is minimalist and modern, with a cosy little lounge in the entrance area and a nice, quiet terrace away from the street.

Name: Tredecim by Monika Jans und Thomas Huber
Description: Thomas Huber (the 13th generation) and Monika Jans are dedicated to their work in the Krone, an establishment steeped in history. While she is responsible for the cordial and professional service, he takes care of things in the kitchen, preparing seasonal, traditional dishes. They will also prepare a creatively inspired set menu if you order in advance. The cheese trolley selection is fantastic! The wood-panelled interior exudes charm and contributes to the delightful atmosphere. Should you wish to stay overnight, there are attractive individually decorated guestrooms.

Name: Krone am See
Description: Right by the lake, complete with a small harbour, this modern, low-rise building stands next to the traditional Krone restaurant after which it is named. Inside, an upscale contemporary decor with clean lines welcomes diners; outside, the terrace beckons. As for the food, the good à la carte selection of Mediterranean, French and regional dishes has a pronounced emphasis on local, seasonal ingredients, such as Thurgau rainbow trout and salmon from Lostallo. In addition, there are two three- or five-course set menus, one of which is vegan. The extensive wine list features over 160 labels. For a more casual approach, the separate "Krone Easy" self-service and takeaway concept operates throughout the milder seasons.

Name: Paradies
Description: The former guild house dating from 1616 beautifully marries historical and modern elements in the old town. In the comfort of a tasteful space with a striking original wooden coffered ceiling, diners are invited to enjoy a seasonal set menu in which regional ingredients meet international influences. It comprises four to seven courses and is also available in a vegetarian version. Service is gracious and professional – even the chef gets involved front of house. There is also a bar and cigar lounge. In summer, you can dine al fresco on the small cobblestone square that fronts the building.

Name: Brasserie du Château
Description: The brasserie is a wonderful addition to the gourmet restaurant ‘Louis’ on the magnificent historic castle estate. Here you can enjoy French brasserie cuisine made from fresh produce, from ‘Beef tartare classique’ and ‘Moules marnière’ to ‘Veal ragout Blanquette de Veau’ or dishes for two, such as ‘Chateaubriand’, in a classic ambience for lunch and dinner. The well-stocked and extensive wine list is the same as that of the ‘Louis’. In summer, the terrace facing the moat under shady old plane trees is an idyllic spot.

Name: Gourmet Louis
Description: This idyllic 13C water castle is a tranquil haven nestled just outside Basel. Surrounded by a moat, the property with its old trees can be accessed from two sides via wooden bridges. This establishment boasts two culinary concepts: a brasserie and this fine dining restaurant. Head chef Guy Wallyn, having already worked at the castle for several years, serves up classic French cuisine in the form of a four- to six-course set menu, which can be supplemented with cheeses from the trolley. To complement this, a selection of fine wines is available. Up to 20 guests can be accommodated in the lavishly renovated historical Steinsaal (or "stone hall") in the left wing of the castle – the 18C stuccowork is stunning. The small private dining space in the tower is ideal for groups. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif or coffee in the castle's courtyard.

Name: Bad Schauenburg
Description: Whether you're seated in the Basler Stübli, the Gaststube or the Veranda, the fine dining restaurant of Hotel Bad Schauenburg serves classic French cuisine that takes its cue from the seasons in all its lovely rooms. Some of the produce comes from the hotel's own garden. The highlight in summer is of course the delightful terrace!

Name: De la Gare - La Table des Suter
Address: Avenue de la Gare 13, Lucens, 1522, Switzerland
Description: This elegant family-run institution opposite Lucens railway station always hits the spot thanks to its buzzy, friendly vibe and professional service. The carefully crafted repertory is rolled out in polished lunch and dinner menus. Some of its high-flying signature dishes include “Belles Demoiselles” (langoustines cooked in several ways with a Thai sauce), “Patte Noire de Bourgogne” poularde (young chicken) stuffed with truffles and a citrus fruit and chocolate extravaganza. Top-notch produce is enhanced by the know-how of its seasoned kitchen team. Savvy selection of Swiss wines, also available in magnums and half bottles. Pleasant guestrooms for overnight stays. An elegant interior and slick polished service for a gourmet experience – what’s not to like?

Name: Marktküche
Description: One tip at the outset: be sure to reserve in good time – this restaurant always gets booked up, so it's hard to secure a table! The clue is in the name: the cuisine takes its cue from what the market has to offer, dispensing with meat and fish. Diners can look forward to a 100% vegan surprise menu made up of four to eight courses, with optional wine or alcohol-free pairings available. A special lunch set menu is served on the penultimate Friday of every month. In summer, head for the pleasant pavement terrace.

Name: La Soupière
Description: This sophisticated restaurant on the first floor boasts a stylish interior and professional service. As for the menu, it offers modern variations on classic French cuisine.

Name: White Elephant
Description: This restaurant at the Zurich Marriott Hotel is a must for fans of authentic Thai cuisine. Made with market fresh produce, the food is authentic and authentically spicy! Whatever you do, don’t miss the curries.

Name: Chez Vrony
Description: This chalet perched at 2 100m above sea level right by a ski slope boasts an incredible view of the Matterhorn – unsurprisingly, tables on the terrace are in great demand! Inside, the abundance of wood and attractive decor spread a rustic warmth, and the service team is attentive and charming. The traditional cuisine has a regional twist, and features delicious creations such as mountain goat cheese ravioli with thyme and nut butter, caramelised Valais pear and dried pear purée, or "Vrony's organic platter” of dried meats, Alpine cheese and house-made sausage. The restaurant can be reached on foot in around 20min from Sunnegga funicular station, passing through the picturesque little village of Findeln.

Name: Ornellaia
Description: At this restaurant, dishes such as filetto Rossini, lobster carpaccio and house-made tagliatelle al ragù are cooked up in an open-view kitchen. This modern take on Italian cuisine is complemented by an appealing wine list that includes a selection from the famous Tuscan wine producer, Ornellaia. Front of house, host Antonio Bordone and team pull out all the stops. This gem of a restaurant is located in a beautifully refurbished building that was once a bank – the door even opens automatically. Sleek design meets decorative art and the historical charm of sandstone walls, lending the distinctive high-ceilinged space a modern and elegant Tuscan ambience. At lunchtime, there is a small selection of additional dishes.

Name: L'Appart
Description: In the heart of pedestrian Lausanne, this demure eatery reveals an elegant, tastefully appointed upstairs dining room with an open kitchen, a buzzy vibe and slick, seamless service. The several course menu, mainly vegetarian or vegan, is entirely seasonal and locally sourced. Amusingly the establishment boasts a self-service wine cellar, most of whose contents is produced locally and according to biodynamic methods, from which diners make their own pick. The house also provides an alcohol-free beverage-food pairing option.

Name: Wirtschaft am Schlössli
Description: Christian Kuchler from Taverne zum Schäfli in Wilgoltingen is also behind this culinary hotspot here in nearby Bottighofen, in a lovely location by the marina. Under the direction of head chef Monika Huber (formerly sous-chef to Christian Kuchler), the food is ambitious. The menu is divided into "France", "Italy", "Iberian Peninsula" and "Classics". Your Mediterranean journey ranges from "rabbit roulade, raw ham, sage, courgette" to "scampi, fregola sarda, lemon, pepperoncini" and "Ibérico pork Alenttejana" to "tortelloni, tomato, burrata, Taggiasca olive". Accompanied by a well-curated wine list with a fine selection from Switzerland and Europe. Enjoy your meal inside in a relaxed bistro atmosphere or out on the gorgeous terrace on the shores of Lake Constance. Tip: Tapas are also served all day on a separate terrace – Lästermeile – on the marina promenade.

Name: Azalée
Description: The Von Siebenthal family welcomes you with dedication and genuine hospitality – both at the stylish Boutique-Hotel Alpenrose and in the restaurant. In an elegant traditional setting, diners tuck into classic cuisine with a contemporary twist. You can choose between a vegetarian or a conventional tasting menu, with the option to order individual dishes à la carte – such as porcini ravioli with Alpine cheese, shallots and sun-dried tomatoes, or perch fillet in rice paper with green asparagus, verjuice, sorrel and gnocchi. In summer, a pared-down version of the menu from Sammy's Grill Restaurant & Bar, which is only open in winter, is also available. Exceptionally warm service is provided by the proprietress and her daughter. Stunning terrace overlooking the mountains!

Name: Auberge des Montagnards
Address: Route de la Poya 23, Estavannens, 1665, Switzerland
Description: Behind its wooden façade, this cosy restaurant in the heart of the village is making a strong statement about its commitment to sustainability. Just as simple and pleasant as the interior, the small terrace at the front is a charming setting in which to enjoy carpaccio of Lake Geneva whitefish, with a tangy cream and crunchy vegetables, or one of the delicious game dishes prepared using animals hunted in the surrounding forests.

Name: Al Braciere
Address: Via Livurcio 50, Ronco sopra Ascona, 6622, Switzerland
Description: Situated just above Ascona, about 1km from the town centre, this friendly hotel boasts panoramic views of Lake Maggiore, the surrounding mountains and the island of Brissago. Enjoy modern, carefully prepared cuisine in the comfortable dining room or on the idyllic outdoor terrace in summer.

Name: Gandria
Description: Chef-patron Adriano Peroncini is originally from Puglia, but his years of travelling took him all over Italy and far beyond. Since 2016 he has had his own restaurant, here in Zurich's Seefeld district. In this delightfully cosy space, where an inviting atmosphere reigns, he introduces diners to his fresh southern Italian-inspired cuisine – highlights on the menu include the salted cod or Piedmontese Fassone beef and, of course, the delicious pasta dishes! Opt for the five-course "Degustazione Esperienza Italiana" or order à la carte. The wine list is predominantly Italian, but some French labels also feature. Diners can also look forward to "servizio alla maniera italiana" – authentic hospitality that will make you feel at home! There is a lovely little terrace in front of the building.

Name: Kindli
Description: A place steeped in history and full of charm – from the hotel's pretty, individually designed guestrooms to the restaurant, in which old wood panelling exudes cosiness. In a pleasant and lively atmosphere, they serve good classic cuisine in the form of dishes such as sea bass with a lemon and caper butter, or Geschnetzeltes Kalbsfilet Zürcher Art (veal strips in a mushroom and cream sauce). At lunchtime, check out the additional daily specials for a quick meal. Tip: Don't forget to make a reservation, as they always get booked up!

Name: Rechberg 1837
Description: A charming establishment with a unique concept: They cook only with regional ingredients that would have existed in the year 1837 – when the building was constructed and before the industrial age. Take a punt on the surprise menu, which comes in four or six courses, or go à la carte. Mouthwatering options include dishes such as "baked beetroot, soft goat cheese, buckwheat" and "trout from Glauser fish farm, Swiss chard, beans". The atmosphere is welcoming, and a charming and adept front-of-house team provide attentive service, including insightful explanations of the dishes and the restaurant's sustainable ethos.

Name: Löwen
Description: In this cosy little restaurant in the vaulted cellar, you can look forward to the "Gourmet Menu", which is served at lunch and dinner, with the option of up to seven courses. At lunchtime, Beiz serves a set menu, as well as a choice of à la carte dishes. There is also a decent wine selection, and the front-of-house team is friendly and competent.

Name: Stapferstube da Rizzo
Description: Here at Stapferstube, a well-known Zurich eatery, Italian dishes such as tris di pasta della casa, gamberoni aglio olio peperoncino, and brasato di manzo al Barolo are a hit with diners. In this vibrant and welcoming restaurant, regulars and first-time guests alike are treated to Mediterranean hospitality and a cosy atmosphere. Their quick lunch at a reasonable price is also popular.

Name: Restaurant Chastè
Description: In their delightful little hotel, the Pazeller family offers not only attractive, comfortable guestrooms but also sophisticated cuisine. The restaurant combines two concepts: "Ustaria Chastè" with an upscale evening menu and a simpler lunchtime menu, and "Bocca Fina Chastè" with an evening fine dining set menu. The interior is tasteful and cosy, the service friendly and attentive.

Name: Paradiso
Description: In good weather, you can take in breathtaking views up here at 2 181m above sea level. This down-to-earth Mountain Club restaurant appeals to diners of all ages. You can look forward to good food and a great wine selection, as well as a relaxed atmosphere, partly thanks to the music and DJs. Note: there is an entry fee for non-members. Accessible by chairlift and a short walk (10min).

Name: Rössli
Description: The first floor of this 16C half-timbered building makes for an exceedingly pleasant setting. Each area has a cosy, rustic feel, plus there is a small conservatory overlooking the lake – not to mention the lovely terrace. The menu features traditionally inspired cuisine with seasonal touches, including classics such as Hereford beef entrecôte and fresh veal liver. Attentive and adept service, as well as wine recommendations are provided by the sommelier.

Name: La Sorgente
Address: portich da Sura 18, Vico Morcote, 6921, Switzerland
Description: This welcoming restaurant overlooking the lake in the charming village of Vico Morcote serves simple cuisine with a focus on local ingredients, many of which (biodynamic wines, vegetables, olive oil etc) come from the restaurant’s own farm. It’s fantastic to be able to enjoy such fresh produce at reasonable prices – make sure you try the open ravioli with a rabbit ragu, Gotthard cheese fondue and pepper.
