Guests are advised to leave their car at the garage at the entrance to the village and then walk the short distance to the restaurant. In summer, meals are served under a pergola on the charming terrace.

Name: Schotte-Sepp-Stube / Flickflauder
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether you choose to dine in the cosy Schotte-Sepp-Stube, the bright Veranda or the contemporary, minimalist-style Flickflauder, you’re guaranteed good-quality, seasonally inspired cuisine and friendly service at this restaurant, which hosts an “Appenzell evening” with a buffet every Wednesday. The à la carte is available to non-resident guests from 8pm onwards.

Name: Seebistro Belvédère
Description: The location right by Lake Lucerne is fabulous! This modern bistro shares its premises with the fine dining restaurant and benefits from the same stunning views over the water. Here, too, Fabian Interbitzin and his team are responsible for the food, serving up contemporary French cuisine with the odd Mediterranean influence. The set menu comprises two to six courses, which can also be ordered à la carte. A range of classic dishes is also available. The cuisine is pleasingly accessible without sacrificing elegance.

Name: Villa am See by Sandro Lüthi
Description: Housed in a villa in a beautiful location, this restaurant is run with great dedication by a young couple – Sandro Lüthi (kitchen) and Paulina Soares (service) – and their small, friendly team. Working in tandem in the kitchen, the owner and his chef Robert Fiedler devise two three- to six-course set menus in the evening, one of which is vegetarian, plus à la carte dishes. Expect modern, seasonal and ingredient-led cuisine – predominantly French and Mediterranean in style, complemented by international twists and a dose of creativity. Examples include "baked egg, spinach, Parmesan, truffle" and "kingfish, Granny Smith, green shiso, wasabi". Lunch, too, is a sophisticated affair, based on a sharing concept (dubbed "Geteilter Genuss"). Accordingly, there is a set menu including starters to share as well as mains and desserts to choose from. The atmosphere in the modern and elegant interior is pleasantly relaxed, but it is the terrace, separated from the lake by a mere strip of greenery, that is the highlight! The glass-paned pavilion is a great alternative for cooler days.

Name: Locanda Locarnese
Description: Hidden away in a little alley, this pleasant, modern-style restaurant offers Mediterranean and traditional cuisine made with excellent ingredients. Among its unmissable dishes are the honey and mustard pork belly, thyme-roasted eggplant with cherry tomato cream, and the chocolate fondant with passion fruit sauce. The large fireplace gives character to the setting, while the warm and friendly service makes guests feel as if they are visiting a private home.

Name: RICO'S
Description: A restaurant with a special atmosphere! Cosy, colourful and packed with art – a tastefully eclectic blend of styles and highly individual decorative details. In addition, the service is pleasingly laid-back and professional. Classic cuisine with Mediterranean influences is served in the form of a three- to eight-course set menu. To accompany it, choose from the nicely curated wine list, which has a particularly good selection from Switzerland and France. There is a set lunch menu Wed-Fri. In summer, it is pleasant to sit in the small garden behind the restaurant. Tip for anyone looking for a venue for private events: you can book Rico's Privé.

Name: Oberer Mönchhof
Description: The dining rooms in this lovely, centuries-old half-timbered building are tastefully and comfortably furnished. Outside a fabulous terrace is laid out under chestnut trees overlooking the lake. The cuisine is seasonal, traditional and international with an additional tasting menu on offer at lunchtime and in the evenings.

Name: Au Chat Noir
Description: This bouncy, authentic bistro seems to have stepped out of another era, as does the full-bodied menu: sautéed calf’s head, warm poultry pâté in puff pastry, prawn risotto or warm chocolate pie. The rustic slate menu overflows in heartwarming dishes skilfully crafted with lashings of love. On-the-ball service and a warm vibe near the theatre. Be sure to book!

Name: Spettacolo
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the Lenkerhof spa resort's elegant restaurant, hotel patrons who opt into the "Gourmet Package" can look forward to an appealing half-board set menu, while others, including external guests are treated to a high-quality and modern take on classic cuisine that also draws on international influences. Pick four to six dishes from a selection of 15 to create your own menu. The excellent wine list spans sizes from half bottles to magnums. Friendly and knowledgeable waitstaff. The best view of the mountains and valley can be enjoyed from the light and airy conservatory – and, of course, from the terrace.

Name: La Brasserie du Royal
Description: Hosted in the Royal Savoy hotel, a favourite haunt of the Spanish monarchy, the Brasserie shines the spotlight on an enticing cast: timeless elegance, polished cuisine and spot-on service. The first-rate “Menu du Marché” and “Menu de la Brasserie” feature four courses that exemplify the establishment’s high-flying culinary hallmark: crab meat, shellfish mayonnaise, Granny Smith apples, celery and lovage; seafood, aioli and crunchy fennel; juicy, melt-in-the-mouth Swiss steak, velvety mashed potato; mille-feuille laced in Madagascan vanilla. The duo of sommeliers knows their glazed wine cellar inside out. The terrace is a hit for alfresco dining come the fine weather.

Name: L'Arabesque
Description: The Arabesque’s attractive decor of gold mosaics, white leather and black lacquerware conjures up pictures of the mysterious Orient, in particular Lebanon. It provides the perfect foil for a pedigree Mediterranean lineup, including hot and cold mezzes and Kibbeh Labanieh, the chef’s signature dish of meatballs, and Samak mechoui, grilled seabass with a sesame sauce. Excellent range of vegetarian dishes.

Name: Hirschen
Description: Classic, seasonal and regional food is the name of the game here. Guests can enjoy fine dining and vegetarian options in the Zeitgeist restaurant, as well as house classics, including the signature dish: chateaubriand. Tip: The chocolate cake with coffee is sensational! Alternatively, you can order burgers, pasta etc in the cosy Hirschenstube. Popular terrace for summer meals, plus comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Restaurant Hôtel de Ville
Description: This restaurant with a vibrant and upbeat atmosphere is run by a chef who is brimming with energy. He regales diners with delicious and indulgent cuisine that draws on local produce. Daily lunchtime menu inspired by local market fare; fine dining tasting menu in the evening. The opulent interior (a former apartment) is decorated with numerous works of art: paintings, photos, sculptures etc.

Name: 4 Saisons
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Attractive picture windows, elegant pale wood, and a menu that takes the four seasons as its starting point, as reflected in the market-fresh ingredients. Locally grown vegetables, fish from the nearby lakes and Swiss meats are accompanied by an appealing wine list that focuses on local producers. Delight in dishes such as morel stuffed with Agria potatoes and Vully asparagus tips. Friendly service and attractive guestrooms at Hotel Cailler.

Name: La Coupole - Matsuhisa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: "Irasshaimase" – this is the exclamation with which diners are greeted here. Housed in the building that was once home to Europe's first indoor tennis courts, Nobuyuki Matsuhisa's restaurant buzzes with infectious vibrancy. The wide-ranging menu features a fusion of Japanese and Peruvian cuisines – everything is prepared in the open kitchen (there is also a sushi bar). The black cod miso is definitely worth trying.

Name: Zum Goldenen Schäfli
Description: Dating back to 1484, this place has a palpable sense of history. It is the city's last surviving guild house and is brimming with charm, not least due to the wood-panelled interiors. One quirk of the Zunftstube (guild room) is its sloping floor – you might find yourself sitting at a bit of a tilt! The kitchen follows a classic approach, emphasising regional and seasonal fare. Be sure to sample the hand-cut beef tartare, available mild, medium or hot to suit your taste. Or perhaps the St Gallen veal sausage with red wine onion sauce is more your thing. Service is attentive and genuinely warm.

Name: Le Bocca - Restaurant
Description: Under the management of chef Alexandre Luquet and his spouse Ana Ronc, Le Bocca offers a mouthwatering gourmet experience that combines elegance and modernity. Whether you are seated in the bright interior or on the lush alfresco patio, you will sample cosmopolitan contemporary French cuisine focused on outstanding produce. Wild langoustine, sole meunière fished by small boats and Araguani chocolate soufflé bear witness to the establishment’s bold, minimalist signature. Flexible evening menus (3 to 6 courses), well thought out lunchtime menu, a fantastic wine cellar and slick friendly service. The marriage of sophistication and sincerity.

Name: Restaurant Pony
Description: Nestled in a small town at an elevation of 770m, this third-generation family business serves classic seasonal fare with a Mediterranean twist in an elegant light-filled extension. There are two set menus (one of them vegetarian), from which you can also order à la carte. Tempting dishes include Sigigen trout fillet with wild garlic, and timeless favourites such as "Suure Mocke" (marinated beef roast). Or why not share the Chateaubriand beef fillet for two? Friendly service. For a more rustic dining experience, head to Beizli & Sonnsyte, which also doubles as a lounge. Another option is to dine on the gorgeous terrace, where you can order from either restaurant.

Name: Casa Alva
Description: This restaurant has an upscale modern interior that beautifully incorporates original architectural features from the former parsonage in which it is housed. The cosy setting is complemented by the warmth and dedication of your hosts, creating a truly inviting atmosphere. Ambitious cuisine is served as the "Chef's Choice Menü", in a five- to eight-course format. Mediterranean, French and regional influences go into dishes such as "scallop, peas, chorizo, shallots" or "ricotta and wild garlic tortellini, asparagus cream, morels". Attractive guestrooms available for overnight stays. Tip for motorists: multi-storey car park nearby.

Name: Landhaus
Description: This 16C farmhouse has been turned into a really charming restaurant boasting a splendid view of Lake Constance. Featuring warm wood finishings and sleek design, the decor embodies a winning combination of the old and the new. Hostess Ariane Cresta provides cordial service in the cosy dining area, while chef-patron Lino Cresta cooks up his modern take on classic cuisine with a regional touch. On the menu, you will find veal cordon bleu, as well as beef tenderloin and brasato with potato, cauliflower, parsnip and XO, or even porcini tortelloni. In the evening, the à la carte selection is complemented by an ambitious three- to five-course set menu (vegetarian version available) and at lunchtime, by daily specials and a "Business Lunch" deal. In summer, head for the gorgeous terrace. There is a hall for events in the modern converted barn.

Name: First
Description: Somewhat tucked away, this delightful restaurant in the Zurich Oberland has plenty of regulars. One draw is the wonderful view – in good weather you can see Mt Säntis. The interior is an attractive blend of cosy and traditional, with more modern touches. In summer, make a beeline for the gorgeous terrace in front of the building. The menu changes with the seasons. Choose à la carte or take a punt on the four- or five-course surprise menu, which also comes in a vegetarian version. Friendly and dedicated front-of-house team.

Name: Arté al Lago
Description: A classic setting with a touch of modernity and romance, this venue offers a breathtaking view of the lake. The cuisine follows the seasons: the menu features Mediterranean influences, while the two tasting menus are more regional in character.

Name: Da Enzo
Address: Via Ai Grotti, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: This Ticino-style stone house boasts a sun-blessed, verdant setting and a beautiful garden-terrace. Take a seat at one of its typical granite tables, either crowned by stone vaulting or shaded by trees, where you can savour exquisite Mediterranean on several tasting menus (including vegetarian) and an à la carte that includes daily specials. Other features include a well-stocked wine cellar and two romantic rustic-style guestrooms. Open for over three decades, Dan Enzo is now run by the second generation of the family.

Name: Drei Könige
Description: This restaurant has a charming bistro feel and serves delicious food expertly prepared with fresh, carefully selected ingredients. At lunchtime, there is a set menu with options, and the atmosphere is upbeat and lively. In the evening, the pace is a little slower, and the food even more sophisticated.

Name: Guarda Val
Description: In the fine dining restaurant of the wonderfully located Maiensäss Hotel Guarda Val, the rustic charm of a 300-year-old cow byre meets modern simplicity. Service comes courtesy of a friendly and experienced team. When it comes to the food, the spotlight is shone on regional specialties. The two set menus (one is vegetarian) and the à la carte dishes are made almost exclusively from Swiss produce. At lunchtime, the offer is somewhat simpler – there is a three-course lunch menu, as well as à la carte dishes.

Name: Sapori
Description: This restaurant's stylish historical setting alone, in the hotel Victoria-Jungfrau, is worth a visit: wonderful hardwood floors beneath your feet, impressively lofty painted ceilings complete with mouldings overhead. When the sun is shining, you should definitely dine on the terrace and take in the magnificent view of the mountains. The cuisine is Italian – the pizzas are a must!

Name: Gasthaus Höhwald
Description: In this gorgeous restaurant boasting a stunning view, the atmosphere could hardly be more welcoming. Since December 2023, a dedicated couple have been at the helm, bringing their superlative fine dining experience to the table: Mara Graef cheerily oversees the team front of house, while Thomas Graef prepares tasty seasonal dishes. His is regional cuisine for the most part, but some dishes are clearly influenced by the owners' Austrian homeland: for instance, their classic Tafelspitz (prime boiled beef), available as a Monday special. Hot meals are served throughout the day. Wonderful terrace. Tip for motorists: You can reserve a parking space in the garage.

Name: Mulania Brasserie
Description: With its combination of sleek, contemporary style and rustic ceiling beams, this old Graubünden building provides an attractive setting. Host couple Yvonne Marx and Sascha Meyer have reimagined their place as a brasserie, serving tried-and-tested regional specialities such as capuns (chard rolls) or quark pizokels (buckwheat spaetzle), plus brasserie classics like moules frites or beef bourguignon. Last but not least, there are some delicious seafood options – the chef's first love. Delightful terrace. Open from 3pm.

Name: Gildo's Ristorante
Description: If you’re in the mood for some authentic, upmarket Italian food, you should try the line-caught sea bass, cime di rapa, garlic, pine nuts and peperoncino at this restaurant. Expect excellent service, plus a stylish Alpine ambience.

Name: Auberge du Prévoux
Description: This inn on the edge of a forest in the heart of the Neuchâtel mountains is well known to fine food lovers, who flock here to enjoy heartwarming, honest cooking. Fish from the lake, game and more exotic ingredients set the scene on the flavoursome, adroitly crafted score. The lunchtime 3-course Midi Gourmet menu requires pre-ordering, as does the full-blown evening lineup. They organise regular theme evenings, like “Périgord black truffles” or “Shellfish and seafood”. Lovely guestrooms should you be able to stay overnight.

Name: Moosegg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Up here, at an altitude of around 1 000m, there is much to get excited about: the phenomenal view of the Emmental and the Alps – either from the modern, elegant restaurant with its large window front or the magnificent terrace – is complemented by good food with a regional and seasonal focus. For a cheaper but equally indulgent alternative, head to Beiz. The terrific wine selection boasts around 900 different options. Chic guestrooms are available in the adjoining boutique hotel.

Name: Cavigilli
Description: Combining modern features with the original wood and stone, plus cordial service and a pleasingly down-to-earth atmosphere, this charming 15C Grisons building provides a wonderful setting in which to enjoy seasonal ingredient-led cuisine. The focus is on the essentials, so the flavoursome dishes are served in pared-down combinations. Tip: Make the most of the quiet terrace in summer! There is a small and simple lunch deal.

Name: Rössli
Description: Rössli is a pleasant restaurant decorated along clean, modern lines in warm colours. Enjoy the smart place settings and friendly service led by the lady of the house and Ueli Kellenberger’s flavoursome, contemporary cuisine. The mouthwatering offerings include open ravioli with spinach, egg, parmesan and beurre noisette.

Name: Perroquet Vert
Description: This intimate, lively restaurant on the Place de la Fontaine exudes the Belle Epoque charm of the Parisian brasseries of old. A feel that chimes perfectly with the traditional, French dishes chalked up on the blackboard. Favourites include scallop risotto, entrecôte and tarte tatin.

Name: Le Bistrot des Ours
Address: Route du Pas de l'Ours 41, Crans-Montana, 3963, Switzerland
Description: A sloth of hungry bears would be right at home in the rustic, alpine vibe of this bistro which commands a fantastic view over the valley and the surrounding peaks. The accent is on ambitious French-Mediterranean cuisine that will find favour with discerning omnivores, together with an insightful array of Valais wines. All of which is courtesy of chef Franck Reynaud, who is also at the helm of the Michelin-starred L'Ours. We warrant it will set your tastebuds tingling!

Name: Wildenmann
Description: This gorgeous building, which started out as an inn in 1708, boasts an idyllic location just a few metres from the shore of Zugersee. Run by a mother-and-son team, the restaurant serves classic cuisine, with fish from the lake playing an important role, for example. A fine dining menu is also available, and in summer the charcoal barbecue is put to work. The service is charming and professional, and the atmosphere in the dining area is cosy. The fantastic terrace is understandably popular – it's wonderful to sit in the shade of the large trees and drink in the view of the lake!

Name: Elisa - Bistro & Terrasse
Description: The restaurant of the venerable Grandhotel Giessbach (dating back to 1875) stands right at the foot of the waterfalls of the same name and boasts a wonderful view of the nearby lake, Brienzersee. The tasty food is regional and seasonal, made primarily from produce grown in the hotel's own 2ha vegetable garden. The other ingredients are sourced from local producers and small-scale growers: fish from the lake, veal from a neighbouring farmer. There are also a number of vegetarian options, such as "Giessbach agnolotti, broccoli, hazelnut". In the evening, the "Tour du Domaine" surprise menu for sharing (for two or more people) would be our top recommendation. Tip: Public (paid) parking is available about a 10min walk away. You can also get here by boat and the historical Giessbach funicular.

Name: The Mansard Restaurant
Description: Located on the ground floor of boutique hotel Miiro The Mansard, this restaurant has a modern and elegant brasserie-style interior with an Alpine feel. There is a terrace with a few tables out on the pavement – this is a place to see and be seen. The kitchen serves up seasonal cuisine with international influences, using select ingredients, many sourced from Switzerland. You can also look forward to a well-curated wine list and friendly service. From Wednesday to Friday, there is an affordable lunch menu. Tip: For a cool rooftop bar experience with stunning views, head to the bar The Mansard Rooftop on the fourth floor, which serves drinks, cocktails and a small selection of snacks. Thanks to its central location very close to the Gstaad promenade, the hotel is also an ideal starting point for a stroll.

Name: Pinte
Description: At this exceedingly well-run establishment dating from the 19C, you have the option of dining in either a snug tavern or an elegant restaurant. The shady terrace to the rear of the building is delightful in summer! Adept service comes courtesy of a friendly and laid-back front-of-house team. The cuisine emphasises regional and seasonal elements. Among the menu classics, the Wiener schnitzel clearly stands out. In the evening, order à la carte or opt for a six-course set menu. Lunchtime options are more limited and budget-friendly.

Name: Auberge de la Couronne
Description: Housed in a tastefully renovated traditional edifice, the Auberge de la Couronne morphs from a simple bistro at lunchtime into a fine dining gourmet establishment in the evenings. Generosity and indulgence are the order of the day in dishes such as crisp golden roasted sweetbread served with fresh crayfish and crunchy glazed mini vegetables. The front-of-house team is on hand to help you find the perfect food-wine pairing as you take a seat in the handsome vaulted dining room.

Name: Le 1913
Description: This elegant restaurant, complete with a terrace commanding a knockout panoramic view of the mountains and valley, is located in the recently refurbished Villars Palace. The ambitious, structured cuisine combines regional and Mediterranean dishes in four- or six-course set menus. The creativity of the "Gambero Rosso", for example, a carpaccio of red prawns contrasted with a perfectly presented dill sorbet, is a case in point. The open kitchen means you can see Christian Bertogna's team at work!

Name: Millennium - La Brasserie
Description: Set in the prestigious Millenium complex, a state-of-the-art business and conference centre, the elegant Brasserie is helmed by A-grade chef Fabien Foare. It is the go-to place for a power lunch, offering a “Summer Menu” and a “Brasserie Menu”, as well as a wide range of à la carte dishes. Steak tartare prepared tableside to your specifications is one of the house signatures, without forgetting trolleys piled high with cured meats and pastries that will have you drooling from the aperitif to the dessert! A gourmet grocery shop is open in the afternoons, selling wine and some of the chef’s iconic creations, including his addictive house-made chocolates.

Name: MOzern
Description: This part of the Mandarin Oriental's culinary portfolio serves food all day. In addition to lunch and dinner, you can have breakfast and afternoon tea here – all in tasteful surroundings that combine a stylish, old-world feel with a brasserie atmosphere. The menu features international cuisine including classics like Angus beef tartare and raclette cheese burger, as well as Asian bar snacks such as crispy duck rolls. The bar serves an excellent assortment of drinks. Tip: Drop in at the Grand Casino next door.

Name: Jacques Restaurant
Address: Rue de la Barre 5, Lausanne, 1005, Switzerland
Description: Now located in the historic city, chef Jacques Allisson's establishment sports elegant rooms spread over two floors and a spacious alfresco area. The modern Gallic score is precise and expressive and flanked by seamless, spot-on service. Three 3- to 5-course menus and an à la carte lineup means that there is something for everyone, from wild mullet, leeks and beurre blanc, followed by venison, beetroot and spatzli, to an iced parfait and a crispy praliné to finish. Splendid wine cellar of French and Swiss vintages. Pleasure and technique go hand in hand in this renowned culinary landmark of Lausanne.

Name: Alex
Description: A real gem! The restaurant of the elegant Alex Lake Zurich hotel is laid out over two levels, right by Lake Zurich – the setting is modern and lively, with large windows affording unobstructed views of the water. It goes without saying that the terrace is also wonderful. Fine Mediterranean cooking is the order of the day, with an appealing set menu available at lunchtime.

Name: Le Restaurant / Le Relais
Description: If you are looking for excellence and elegance, you are in the right place at Le Restaurant or Le Relais of the venerable Badrutt's Palace! In an atmosphere of luxury, the attentive front-of-house team provides classic service. The flavourful cuisine is made from exclusive ingredients and the menu also features a number of dishes that are prepared at your table, e.g. flambées, tartar etc. Whatever you opt for, there is a first-class selection of wines from the best vineyards to accompany your meal. Tip: You can also have breakfast here - accompanied by views of the lake and mountains.

Name: S.Zimmer
Description: In Tünde and Stefan Zimmermann's cosy, intimate little restaurant, a very warm and friendly atmosphere awaits you, as well as flavoursome cuisine, incorporating many regional ingredients. They serve a set menu of up to seven courses. The wine list is where influences from Hungary – the owner's homeland – are particularly evident, and it is certainly worth considering her recommendations! Although located inside the building of Hotel Viktoria Eden, the restaurant is run independently.

Name: Restaurant de l'Hôtel DuPeyrou
Description: This lavish 18C palace in the town centre ticks all the boxes and is polished yet unconventional, classical yet quirky. Chef Edmond Bavois rustles up a traditional Gallic lineup, enhanced by subtle Asian twists in elegant creations of the likes of fillet of poached turbot and Valle Maggia risotto or verbena-flavoured pigeon from Poitou. Each dish enhances painstakingly sourced produce and meals are served in a majestic setting whose high ceilings, soft lighting and gleaming parquet floors are perfectly underscored by slick unobtrusive service. An establishment dripping in charm and ideal for connoisseurs of fine food and premium locations.

Name: La Place
Description: Cristina and Vincenzo De Rosa run this restaurant with passion and enthusiasm. Throughout the year they delight guests with their modern and colourful cuisine, with dishes such as lobster ravioli in a Thai red curry sauce featuring on the menu.

Name: Martin Göschel
Description: As if the exclusive Alpina Gstaad's hotel credentials were not impressive enough, it also comes up trumps with this wonderful restaurant. It is something special in several respects: first, there is its distinctive decor, which sees rustic charm elegantly blended with modern sophistication; second, the fantastic panoramic terrace and, last but not least, Martin Göschel's seasonal tasting menu. The Mannheim-born chef, who previously earned MICHELIN stars at Hotel Paradies in Ftan and Alte Post in Nagold, successfully weaves modern influences into classic cuisine, using exclusively Swiss ingredients. Comprising three to five courses, the set menu also comes in a vegetarian version.

Name: La Grappe d'Or
Description: A restaurant where superb flavours and a friendly atmosphere go hand in hand. Chef Theotim Bioret is strongly inspired by northern Italy, from Venice to Ventimiglia: Piedmont-style agnolotti del plin, sage and a parmesan jus; calf's liver saltimbocca, spinach and polenta. In addition to the à la carte menu, the chef serves a more affordable weekly dish. Meticulous plating, precise cooking and delicious sauces combine to create a faultless dining experience.

Name: La Croix d'Ouchy
Description: A culinary landmark of Lausanne for over 30 years, this establishment can be relied upon to deliver a fresh, seasonal, pedigree score, founded on top-drawer, sometimes regional produce. The “suggestion menu” (lunch and evening) shines the spotlight on the chef’s talent and knack for sauces. The best tables are near the window or in the quieter room to the rear. Some dishes are available to take home. The Royal Savoy public carpark is conveniently located opposite. Bookings advised.

Name: La Terrasse Brasserie
Description: Befitting the elegance that characterises the Victoria Jungfrau Grand Hotel & Spa, which is steeped in tradition, a classically refined atmosphere awaits you here. The location against the impressive backdrop of the mountains is a real draw in itself. In summer, make a beeline for the terrace on the promenade! The menu includes a broad assortment of Arab, Asian, Mediterranean and Swiss dishes – flavoursome food made from high-quality ingredients.

Name: Chrüz
Description: This centrally located inn has tables in the stylish conservatory or a simpler dining room where you can tuck into traditional fare that often draws on international influences. The wide-ranging menu includes spaetzle with Sbrinz (hard cheese) and truffle, cordon bleu with Alpine cheese, "Vorässä 2.0" (beef stew with a twist) and salmon green curry. The service is friendly and attentive. Lunchtime options are more limited and moderately priced.

Name: Vieux-Bois
Address: Avenue de la Paix 12, Geneva, 1202, Switzerland
Description: Just behind the United Nations, Geneva's hotel management school (EHG) invites the general public to step into its restaurant, which is devoted to upholding traditions of excellence. In an elegant, historical setting and under the eagle eye of their teachers, students craft a seasonal lineup that combines respect for the ingredient with textbook technique. Examples include a cappuccino of celeriac with crunchy hazelnuts and brioche bread, or a roast breast of duck flanked by a gutsy gravy and melt-in-the-mouth carrots. On the dessert side, an explosive chocolate bar and pear sorbet add a decadent final flourish to your meal. The perfect place to sample pedigree recipes of flawlessly cooked traditional fare at extremely attractive prices for Geneva.

Name: Pfändler's Gasthof zum Bären
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Steeped in over 200 years of history, this building makes for a really delightful setting: Bärenstube and Orangerie are full of charm and attention to detail. The garden is also attractive – a truly idyllic spot! The seasonal food has regional and Mediterranean influences. You will feel right at home in the pretty guestrooms.

Name: Essort
Description: In the attractive Kirchenfeld district, this restaurant housed in what was once the US embassy has an inviting atmosphere – the modern interior design features a harmonious combination of clean lines, warm wood finishings and muted tones, complemented by an open kitchen. The terrace to the rear of the building beckons in summer. The commitment of the owners, Sara and Benjamin Jann is palpable – both when it comes to the charming and attentive service from a team who go out of their way to cater to guests' every need, and the delicious food. The latter includes tender Bäggli ragout made from Aaretal Duroc pork with a delicate potato foam, aromatic chive oil and crunchy potato brunoise. In addition to the seasonal six-course set menu in the evening, there is a small lunch menu or a business lunch with three to five courses.

Name: Bel Etage
Description: Starting at the bar on the ground floor of Der Teufelhof hotel – the perfect spot for an aperitif – make your way up to the first floor, where the stylish salons of Bel Etage harmoniously blend into the historical setting. The lovely decor features the original parquet flooring, elegant double doors, high ceilings with crystal chandeliers, as well as art on the walls. In the kitchen, Michael Baader and his team focus on preparing classic cuisine. Diners can either order à la carte or choose between the two set menus – one with three courses, the other with six. The well-curated wine list comprises 450 labels. In summer, head for the pretty terrace and nab a table under the awning in the hotel's garden.

Name: Käserei
Description: This restaurant with a modern yet rustic feel and a cosy atmosphere is located in the former cowshed of a typical Engadin house. The restaurant still has a focus on cows and dairy products today, serving dishes such as cheese fondues, raclette, capuns and even Chinese fondue. Cheese-making demonstrations are held regularly in the evenings.

Name: Seven Toc Toc
Description: The views extend from the lake to the mountains in this informal restaurant, where windows into the kitchen allow guests to watch the chefs busy at work. The menu features creatively reinterpreted, classic-style dishes, with the option of choosing between meat and fish, while the delicious bread comes from the Bottega del Gusto in Porto Ronco. At lunchtime, there’s a bistro-style menu with lighter but equally delicious options such as salads, antipasti and primi, hamburgers, club sandwiches, baked seabass and grilled Tomahawk steak. There’s also a lounge bar plus a wine bar of the same name, the latter offering an interesting array of labels (also available by the glass), as well as cocktails which are a perfect pairing for the dishes on offer. Given the restaurant’s superb location, the tables on the terrace are much sought after in summer, so it’s best to book ahead! Three luxury apartments are also available if you’d like to extend your stay here.

Name: FIVE
Description: Ensconced in the prestigious Guarda Golf Hotel & Residences resort, FIVE is the epitome of swish luxury with a matchless view of the Swiss peaks. Levantine cuisine takes the limelight here with mezze to share and a festival of exquisitely crafted oriental flavours in dishes such as crispy borek and grilled aubergines. This banquet ends on a sweet-toothed European finale, illustrated by chocolate tartlet and delicate fruit mousses. The three-course customisable menu is highly recommended. Slick professional service, a refined interior and a wine cellar for connoisseurs make this establishment the perfect destination for a gourmet escapade on top of the world.

Name: Ilge
Description: Set in the heart of the historical little town with its picturesque painted façades, this restaurant is housed in an old half-timbered building. The interior design is chic and tasteful, and in fine weather there is a lovely terrace overlooking the pedestrian zone. Serbian-born Zoran Baratovic presides in the kitchen, turning out dishes that draw on classical and Mediterranean influences. We highly recommend the mouthwatering veal shank ravioli. And to accompany your meal, the attentive maître d', who is always on hand, will provide you with a well-curated wine list. Feel free to enquire about magnums of red wine – there are a few stored in the cellar.

Name: La Dispensa
Description: Let yourself be courted by culinary creations in which the Mediterranean meets elegant Gallic cuisine. The house signature, Bottoni Carbonara, delicious raviolis with a melt-in-the-mouth centre, are flanked by a fragrant Parmesan mousse and crispy slivers of pork crackling. The tender veal fillet, enhanced by a velvety sauce, is truly worth writing home about. Make yourself comfortable in the glamorous, clean-edged interior, or on the terrace in summertime. A carefully chosen selection of wines by the glass completes this gourmet interlude. An address to discover forthwith!

Name: LOFT FIVE
Description: This stylish restaurant stands directly on Europaallee, not far from the railway station (Hauptbahnhof). But it's not only the chic interior and relaxed atmosphere that are inviting – the food is also a definite draw! Flavoursome modern-inspired international cuisine is on the menu. The service is friendly and competent, and there is a good selection of wines and cocktails.

Name: Schloss Wartegg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The elevated location between Lake Constance and the Alpstein massif is quite something! As it is in the small castle hotel, the focus in the restaurant is on all things organic and ecological. This translates into sustainably produced ingredients and organic produce from local suppliers, plus vegetables and herbs from the hotel's 2 500m2garden. In the evening, diners enjoy adept service and dishes such as fillet of perch caught by professional fisherman Claudio Görtz from Altenrhein, saffron foam, leek and Parisian potatoes, or roasted lettuce, lentil vinaigrette, creamed potato and herb oil. Options are more limited at lunchtime. From the terrace there is a wonderful view of the countryside and Lake Constance.

Name: Aroleid Restaurant
Description: Located right by the ski slopes just above Furi gondola station, this restaurant is housed in a modern and stylish chalet that exudes rustic charm. As well as stunning views, diners can look forward to a diverse menu of delicious dishes inspired by the chef's international travels. Incidentally, the coffee comes from the hotel's own roastery and the crockery is also made in-house. For those who don't mind the long walk, it's a 1.5hour hike from Zermatt to the restaurant.

Name: La Muña
Description: In this elegant, contemporary-style setting, friendly waitstaff serve up food that is an interesting fusion of Peruvian and Asian cuisine. The four- or six-course omakase menu is highly recommended. Alternatively, there is a good range of à la carte dishes listed under four headings: "Crudo", "Gyoza & Crujiente", "Caliente" and "Guarnición". Housed in Schweizerhof hotel, this restaurant is only open on winter evenings, presenting an authentic culinary experience using top-quality ingredients. Incidentally, la muña is a medicinal plant in the Andes that is said to help against altitude sickness.

Name: L'Écorce
Description: In this convivial, tastefully furnished restaurant in Carouge’s old town the chef conjures up fresh, aromatic cuisine that combines classic and modern dishes such as mi-cuit tuna with a beetroot and watermelon bouillon and raw and cooked vegetables. Charming service, plus a small summer terrace.

Name: Heugümper
Description: This venerable townhouse enjoys a fantastic location in the heart of Zurich – the small terrace is a lovely spot in the summer. With its elegant contemporary decor, the interior is also inviting, and the charming hostess provides attentive service. Prepared using select ingredients, the dishes draw on Mediterranean and Asian influences. Options on the menu range from veal cordon bleu with truffle Brie to tuna with sesame and a ginger and mango sauce. Shorter, simpler menu at lunchtime.

Name: Marée
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Park Hotel Sonnenhof's wonderful location and comfortable accommodation options are not its only trump cards. The restaurant, run by chef Hubertus Real, is also in high demand. In a tastefully elegant setting, at attractively laid tables, diners are served classic cuisine made with first-rate ingredients. The friendly and attentive front-of-house team also provide expert advice on their very extensive selection of wines. The magnificent terrace also has a viewpoint – the "Adlernest" (eagle's nest) – from which you can take in the stunning view.

Name: Izumi
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace,Valet parking
Description: The atmosphere is truly international: top-notch ingredients go into a fusion cuisine of Japanese and other Asian influences. Perhaps you will be tempted by the Wagyu beef gyoza with a spicy ponzu sauce, or the izumi rolls? The lively atmosphere and chic, modern look of this restaurant on the seventh floor of the Four Seasons Hotel are just as much of a draw as the food. Don't miss the rooftop terrace, one floor up, with its breath-taking view over Geneva, the mountains and the lake. Make a reservation without delay!

Name: Bergwelt - BG's Grill Restaurant
Description: Modern chic with an Alpine touch: Done out in warm tones, with lovely hardwood floors, striking designer lamps and an open kitchen complete with an impressive charcoal grill, this restaurant – part of the equally attractive Bergwelt Grindelwald hotel – has a truly unique atmosphere. The cuisine, inspired by the region, is also very appealing. For meat lovers, the fragrant, golden-brown Wiener schnitzel is sure to whet the appetite, and the same goes for the top-quality signature cuts from the barbecue. Vegetarian options are also available. The well-curated wine list predominantly features Swiss and French labels.

Name: Loy Fah
Description: This chic restaurant on the fourth floor of the tasteful Panorama Resort & Spa boasts a stunning panoramic view over Lake Zurich. Inside, you are served by an extremely friendly and attentive team. The food is a modern take on authentic Thai cuisine, which is also adapted to European palates in terms of spiciness. You can put together your own menu.

Name: Löwen Gourmet
Description: ‘Löwen Gourmet’ and ‘Land-Brasserie’ is the new dual concept of this traditional establishment. Jonas Ingold is in charge of this charming inn and offers a fixed 8-course menu for a maximum of ten guests in the evening under the name ‘Gourmet’. A lovely, uncomplicated alternative is the ‘Brasserie’, which focuses on regional cuisine (à la carte or as a set menu) and grilled dishes. Seasonality is important here, with many products sourced from the region. You will be looked after in a friendly and attentive manner. In summer, the outdoor seating is particularly appealing.

Name: La Muña
Description: Do you fancy Peruvian-Japanese cuisine? This restaurant on the sixth floor of hotel La Réserve Eden au Lac, on the shores of Lake Zurich, serves interesting and unfussy dishes made from top-notch ingredients. Up here you can dine in a cosy atmosphere beneath the exposed roof beams or out on the fantastic rooftop terrace – the view over the lake and the old town is magnificent! Exclusive wine list.

Name: AURA
Description: A stylishly urban restaurant, a top-flight events venue, a lounge or a club? AURA is a little bit of each, but above all the place to be for lovers of modern crossover cuisine with a weakness for grilled food – just watch the chefs at work! Located near Paradeplatz in the old stock exchange building.

Name: Gasthaus am Brunnen
Description: The picturesque Gasthaus am Brunnen sits in the centre of this Graubünden mountain village. Locals meeting for lunch or a drink favour the rustic dining room, while the smart, minimalist-style restaurant is more elegant. The food is modern and uses exclusively local produce. Try the veal tenderloin cooked on a rock salt slab and served with herb caviar, mustard and garlic risotto and vegetables. The female chef's desserts are delicious.

Name: rémy
Description: Located in a listed post-war building that was designed by architect Dominik Burlet and built between 1957 and 1960, this pleasingly unpretentious restaurant is run with great enthusiasm by a friendly team. In the evening, the food takes the form of a four- to six-course surprise menu. The contemporary dishes, which draw on local and seasonal produce, are crafted with care and an eye for detail. A simple, inexpensive lunch set menu is served Tue-Thu. You can also just stop by for a drink or a quick bite. The atmosphere is relaxed and friendly, and a DJ provides music after dinner some weekends. You might like to know that the restaurant is named after Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where the chef's grandfather produced wine.

Name: Concordia
Description: A former pub has been transformed into a relaxed, urban restaurant serving entirely vegetarian cuisine in the form of a menu that is designed for sharing. In the evening, the "Kleines Menü" comprises 12 dishes in five courses and a "Grosses Menü" made up of 15 dishes organised into seven courses – ideal for sharing! Delicious dishes such as "watermelon sashimi with kimchi broth, fermented radish, ponzu gel and black garlic mayonnaise" mean that even non-vegetarians won't miss meat or fish. At lunchtime, choose between a simple, quick lunch, a slightly more sophisticated "Business-Lunch" and the small evening menu. The atmosphere is inviting: historical elements such as high ceilings and traditional wood panelling have been beautifully combined with modern interior details. Service is provided by an experienced and charming team, under the direction of Fiamma Sarro.

Name: Auberge de la Croix-Blanche
Description: This delightful, tastefully appointed inn boasts a warm gregarious interior and a handsome terrace surrounded by greenery in summertime. At the helm of this popular, buzzy eatery are chef Enzo Buffarini and his wife Cinzia, both veterans with stints in world-class establishments. Italian cuisine at its best: fresh, flavoursome and meticulous courtesy of premium ingredients. The à la carte repertory features pedigree classics that rub shoulders with a four-course surprise menu. Their vitello tonnato deserves special mention. Beautifully maintained guestrooms also available.

Name: Le Jardinier
Description: This smart restaurant on the first floor of The Woodward hotel boasts high ceilings and mesmerising views of Lake Geneva, with the bonus of an idyllic summer terrace. Created by Alain Verzeroli and helmed by chef Olivier Jean, formerly of L’Atelier Robuchon, its contemporary seasonal score, founded on textbook classicism, is delicate and veggie-centric. Top-notch produce, spot-on technique, exquisite plating and a wide choice of vegetarian and/or gluten-free dishes. The restaurant also serves an exceptional breakfast and afternoon tea. Slick service and velvety cocooned ambience.

Name: Les Montagnards - Brasserie
Description: Fine dining is not the only option! Hotel Les Montagnards offers a culinary experience that goes beyond its renowned restaurant Le Sommet. The Brasserie can hold its own! The attractive modern interior featuring warm wood and sleek design is as much of a draw as the friendly service and, last but not least, the good cuisine. Here, the focus is on the region and the changing seasons. One of the house specialities, for example, is stuffed morels with a cream sauce. The pike-perch, fished from local lakes, is another popular choice. Tip: Try to get a window seat, then you can take in the view of Gruyères Castle and the surrounding area while you eat!

Name: Beaufort
Description: This small restaurant is located in the Marina Fallenbach clubhouse, on the outskirts of Brunnen. The place has a lovely friendly atmosphere, refined decor and beautiful views of the marina, lake and mountains, not to mention a wonderful terrace! Their modern and cosmopolitan cuisine is made with good, fresh seasonal produce. In addition to à la carte dishes, there is also a three- to five-course seasonal set menu. Inexpensive lunch menu.

Name: KCC by Mauro Colagreco
Description: KCC stands for Kulm Country Club. The handsome L-shaped building is located right next to the ice rink and has a garden for summer days. Local produce takes centre stage in the dishes, which often draw on Mediterranean influences. As well as an appealing selection of starters and pasta dishes, the menu includes dishes for two, such as beef cutlets and lamb shoulder. Much of the food is flame-grilled or roasted over embers. The atmosphere is relaxed and the decor tasteful – the vintage sledges adorning the ceiling are bound to draw the eye! There is also a fabulous terrace. Live music and vinyl sessions provide the acoustic backdrop.

Name: Kakinuma
Description: This small restaurant in the lively Eaux-Vives district is definitely worthy of its current success. The couple that run it create fresh and elegant dishes that include the most exquisitely sliced fish, tempuras that are as light as a feather, and silky chawanmushi (an egg flan). A feast for the senses!

Name: Osteria Del Centro
Description: This small, very friendly restaurant offers a successful mix of tradition (the setting is an old house in the centre of Comano), minimalist furnishings and modern cuisine. In the evening, enjoy a surprise tasting menu (five or seven courses) which is almost entirely vegetarian, with the option of choosing your main course. 95% of the ingredients are organic and the owner-chef will be happy to discuss his philosophy on organic food during the course of your meal. The elegant, original dishes include options such as beef wellington with kohlrabi, chimichurri and mushrooms, accompanied by artisanal wines from Switzerland and further afield.

Name: Le Soleil de Dugny
Description: In this restaurant standing at an altitude of 1 000m, the friendly and dedicated family at the helm offers guests a seasonal menu that can also be ordered as a half-portion, on which numerous local products are used to create tasty classic dishes such as the speciality “local veal with Valais gnocchi”. Spectacular views of the valley and mountains, plus a stunning terrace in summer!

Name: Weisses Rössli
Description: At the Weisses Rössli, good-quality ingredients are used to create dishes inspired by French cuisine with Mediterranean and seasonal influences, including options such as monkfish with gnocchi, beetroot, radicchio and cassis. In the rear courtyard away from the street, there is a quiet terrace that can be covered by an awning. We recommend parking in the nearby car park on the Hürlimann site.

Name: Tao's
Description: Tao's has you covered if you are in the mood for Euro-Asian cuisine. The wide-ranging menu includes sushi and sashimi, steak tartare, poke bowls and dim sum, plus "Signature Grill" dishes such as Thai-style fillet of sea bass, lime, herbs, ginger, soy. The dishes are accompanied by a fantastic and extensive international wine list. A pleasantly relaxed yet stylishly elegant atmosphere prevails. In summer the cosy terrace is a huge draw, and there is also a bar.

Name: Nouvo Bourg
Description: In the heart of historic Saillon, this stylish restaurant boasts two terraces, one of which overlooks a peaceful pedestrian street. Several menus, including one vegetarian, an à la carte lineup and dishes of the day depict the culinary programme. Examples include a starter of runner beans, potatoes and basil, followed by expertly cooked pollock and a chocolate, sweetcorn and coffee extravaganza to finish. Slick, seamless service, handcrafted tableware and a casual ambience provide the perfect foil for polished Mediterranean fare with Sicilian overtones inspired by regional and seasonal ingredients.

Name: National da Sergio
Description: A pleasant and down-to-earth restaurant in the historic old town, right next to Klosterplatz square. The former “Felsenburg” team offers classic Italian cuisine made from top-quality ingredients, including dishes such as Spaghetti Scampi and the classic Piccata Milanese. As you’d expect, Italian wines feature on the wine list.

Name: Eder's Eichmühle
Description: A terrific place that is understandably popular! The picturesque location on a hill with a wonderful garden and view of the lake is its calling card – needless to say, the terrace is a big hit in summer! Dining inside the Eder family's traditional inn is also an excellent option, whether in the more cosy dining area or in the airy, modern extension. The service is friendly and professional with a personal touch. As for the sophisticated dishes, choose à la carte or opt for one of three set menus – omnivore, vegetarian or fish and shellfish. Another stand-out feature is the extensive, top-notch wine list. Their lunch menu is also an appealing option.

Name: Haus zum Rüden
Description: This beautiful guild house on the Münsterbrücke bridge, only a stone’s throw from the town hall, dates back to 1348, as does the unique 11m-wide wooden barrel-vaulted ceiling in the Gothic Room. Dishes are based on seasonal ingredients and include classics such as Zurich-style veal and mushroom ragout in a cream sauce. Less expensive menu at lunchtime, plus a selection of dishes available in the modern bar with a terrace.

Name: The Omnia
Description: A lift whisks you up here from the pedestrian area – to some breathtaking views! In the restaurant of the eponymous hotel, the focus lies squarely on vegetarian cuisine. Dishes such as baked cauliflower with wild mushrooms, cedar nuts and mountain thyme can be complemented by meat/fish specialties. Those in the mood for a culinary adventure can opt for the five-course "Chef's Choice" set menu (with meat/fish or vegetarian), with optional wine pairings. The wine list boasts a fantastic selection of labels from Switzerland and France – especially Burgundy and Bordeaux. The interior is modern and upscale, featuring clean lines and large granite-topped tables. Tip: Enjoy an aperitif by the fireplace.

Name: Sternen
Description: In this gorgeous inn, a winning father-and-daughter team conjures up modern takes on classic dishes. They propose a surprise menu – slightly cheaper at lunchtime than in the evening. Incidentally, they smoke the salmon themselves. If you would like a vegetarian menu, please indicate this when making your reservation. Well-stocked wine list. Tip: Across the road, there is a terrace shaded by plane trees, right by Lake Zug and with a view of the Rigi – in fine weather the sunsets are magical!

Name: Bianchi
Description: A slice of la dolce vita! Located right by the Limmat River, this ristorante boasts a bright and modern interior where excellent service comes courtesy of a cheerful and adept front-of-house team. Made with top-notch produce, the Mediterranean-style fish and seafood dishes here are in high demand. Gorgeous little terrace.

Name: Montalbano by Mirko Rainer
Address: via Montalbano 48, San Pietro di Stabio, 6854, Switzerland
Description: Located on the hill of the same name and recently reopened after renovations under new management already well known in the area, this charming spot features a beautiful veranda and a terrace for summer enjoyment. The kitchen offers many delicacies, such as “cold” spaghetti with seafood crudo, pistachio, and oregano, as well as grilled dishes of the Big Green Egg. In the surprise menu, meat reigns supreme, while the à la carte selection is more varied. If you choose a bottle of Champagne from the well-stocked wine list, it’s not unusual for the restaurant owner to open it for you with a dramatic saber (“sabrage”).

Name: La Sitterie
Description: Here you can tuck into appealing French-Mediterranean cuisine with plenty of creative touches, spices and aromatic herbs. There are several risottos, but also a tomato tartlet with serac ice cream; crumbled Appenzell duck leg confit with savory; iced vacherin with red berries. Quality ingredients, good workmanship and a delightful landscaped garden terrace.

Name: Casa Tödi
Description: Manuel Reichenbach represents the third generation of his family to run the kitchen here. The cuisine showcases regional and seasonal ingredients of the finest quality. Sustainability is also a core value at this restaurant. Take a punt on the surprise menu, which comprises four to seven courses, or go à la carte. The friendly and adept front-of-house team is managed by the proprietress.

Name: Balm - La Pistache
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The elegant restaurant of Hotel Balm has a classical feel when it comes to both the service and Beat Stofer's cuisine – this is unpretentious fare made with excellent ingredients. Diners can opt for a tasting menu with four to five courses or order à la carte. There is also a well-curated wine list. In good weather, the terrace is a fabulous spot from which to enjoy the mountain views. This place is always busy, so be sure to book well in advance! Cheerful guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: Krone
Description: This restaurant in the hotel of the same name stands within a medieval castle complex on top of the mountain – the view couldn't be more beautiful! The stylish decor is a winning combination of modern design and historical charm. Drawing on classic influences, the cuisine takes its cue from the changing seasons and is made with fresh produce sourced from Switzerland and the region – be sure to try the porcini in season or their novel pasta dishes such as "tagliolini, white truffle, pecorino foam". Choose à la carte Tue-Thu; on Fri and Sat, there is a fine dining menu. The service is friendly and professional. N.B. Due to the location in a reduced-traffic zone, you will need to park a few minutes' walk away – the hotel also provides a shuttle service, to be booked in advance.

Name: Gasthaus Bären
Description: This restaurant serves flavoursome traditional cuisine made from local produce à la carte or in the form of an ambitious set menu comprising three, four or five courses. There are also appetising options for two, such as Chateaubriand. Berner Haus, which first appears in records as a tavern in 1542, makes for an enchanting setting with its charming wood-panelled interior. The lovely old turquoise tiled stove, adorned with Langenthal porcelain, provides comforting warmth in the winter months.

Name: Tenne
Description: Your welcoming hosts run this long-standing family business with great dedication. Done out in a contemporary take on Alpine style, the cosy interior is very pleasing. The menu takes its cue from the seasons and includes some exquisite game dishes – the chef himself is a hunter! In the evening, you can choose between two set menus – one of which is vegetarian – or order à la carte. At lunchtime, the selection is a little smaller, but there is also a set menu. The appealing wine list showcases the best of the Valais region. For overnight stays, there are well-kept, modern guestrooms.

Name: Da Valentino
Description: Although it is the beautiful terrace that first catches the eye at this restaurant, the friendly welcome and attentive service offered by Valentino in the kitchen and Sabine front of house add to the appeal. Mediterranean specialities and traditional classic dishes feature on the menu, while an open fireplace creates a warm ambience in winter.

Name: Stiva Veglia
Description: Situated in an idyllic little village, this lovingly restored Graubünden house dating back to 1761 is replete with Alpine charm. The interior is exceptionally pretty with its wood-panelled rooms that are welcoming and stylish in equal measure. Make a beeline for the terrace in summer. Tino Zimmermann delivers modern regional cuisine. There is a set menu of up to nine courses. A classic of the house is the "Schmauser 45-minute egg". A vegetarian menu is also available upon request. Fantastic produce such as Val Lumnezia Arctic char demonstrates a clear connection to the region. Diners are waited on by a dedicated and friendly front-of-house team, with the chefs themselves making an appearance from time to time in order to talk diners through their dishes. Tip: house-made specialities such as liqueurs, grape jelly, herb salt and lemon salt are also available to buy.

Name: Auberge de la Gare
Address: Rue de la Gare 1, Grandvaux, 1091, Switzerland
Description: The first thing that impresses guests here is the stunning panoramic view of Lake Geneva. The dishes are simple and fresh – house classics include tartare and fillets of perch from the lake served with fries. Family atmosphere and a lovely terrace. Comfortable guestrooms are available for guests wishing to stay the night.

Name: La Bagatelle
Description: Here you can look forward to classic French cuisine made from top-notch ingredients, including an appealing selection of dishes for two. The cosy ambience created by warm wood, soft lighting and a touch of elegance is inviting. Plus they have a terrace with a stunning view. The service is charming, and there is a terrific wine list – half bottles are available, too. For an overnight stay: Hotel Le Grand Chalet has cosy rustic-style guestrooms.

Name: Nagomi
Description: Two distinct restaurants in Les Pâquis district, run by a Japanese family: one dedicated to sushi, prepared by the father (who you can admire at work if you are seated at the counter); the other to tempura dishes cooked by the son. Both places have an authentic atmosphere, straightforward service, and top-notch ingredients: you're in for a simple treat.

Name: Le Patio
Description: Philippe Chevrier (chef at the Domaine de Châteauvieux in Satigny) has opted for an original twin-pronged culinary concept here based around beef and lobster, alongside a selection of traditional French bistro dishes, such as pan-fried frogs’ legs with sweet garlic, and crispy snails with mushrooms. A highly enjoyable dining experience!

Name: Buffet de la Gare
Description: An old-fashioned restaurant of the type that is quite hard to find these days. It has Art Deco-style wood panelling, enamel plaques and coloured windows, as well as a terrace overlooking the surrounding greenery. There is also a traditional feel to the menu, which includes perch from Lake Geneva.

Name: Ristorante della Stazione
Description: There’s a change of guard at this Ticino dining institution where young couple Eloa Geiser and Yanick Walker have taken over the running of both the kitchen and front of house service. Eloa, the charming female half of the partnership, is also a qualified sommelier and takes very good care of her guests, while Yanick, adds his classic-French culinary stamp without neglecting his Valois roots, although he is not averse to adding some Mediterranean flair to his cuisine. In addition to its usual menu, on Tuesdays guests can order the “Stazione” veal liver, and on Saturdays the special braised beef with Merlot. The gracious building housing the restaurant with its beautiful views remains unchanged, as do the comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Lusi Brasserie
Description: A tip before we get started: In fine weather, be sure to nab a table on the terrace in front of the building, from which you can take in stunning views of the Matterhorn! But the brasserie of the long-established Grand Hotel Zermatterhof also provides a delightful, classically elegant setting with its lovely walnut panelling and partially glass-paned vaulted ceiling. The cuisine is French and draws on international influences. The menu includes "Lusi Classics" such as calf's head, and traditional dishes such as Wiener schnitzel, steak tartare, burgers and flammkuchen – and there is always an evening special.

Name: Brasserie du Poisson
Description: This contemporary brasserie close to the lake offers unpretentious cuisine. Fish has the starring role (tuna tartare, perch fillets), as well as hearty traditional recipes such as croûte aux morilles (with morel mushrooms) and veal cutlets. A real treat for the taste buds, particularly as everything (including the bread and ice cream) is homemade.

Name: Panorama
Description: The name says it all! The location at an altitude of over 1 000m makes for a fantastic panoramic view of the surrounding mountains – it would be a crime not to enjoy it from the terrace in summer. The Rindisbachers have been running their establishment since 1985 already, serving food influenced by tradition, made with quality ingredients and paired with good wines. The pasta is manufactured in their own workshop. Panoteca sells delicatessen wares.

Name: Eden - Belle Époque
Description: At the restaurant of the Hotel Eden Spiez, diners can savour classic cuisine that showcases regional and seasonal produce including homegrown fruit and berries. The hotel also has its own herb garden. Take in stunning views of Spiez Castle, Spiez Bay and the imposing mountains from the stylishly elegant interior or the covered terrace – both spaces are equally delightful. A shorter menu is available at lunchtime.

Name: Groven
Description: A small restaurant with a focus on simple local dishes. If you stop here for lunch on the terrace, you’ll find a different menu every day inspired by whatever ingredients are in season. There’s also a tempting selection of cheeses and game such as venison and wild boar during the hunting season, plus an interesting wine list.

Name: Du Théâtre
Description: This bistro, depicted by a stripped-back minimalist decor is conveniently located for a meal before or after a show at the Crochetan theatre. The chef conjures up creative, well-crafted dishes made from top-notch produce with regular nods to his native Italy. Dishes include specialities such as a ‘gargouillou’ of asparagus, fresh morels and spring veggies. The talented sommelier is a font of wine knowledge and fully worthy of our applause!

Name: Salmen
Description: A delightful place with a lively atmosphere! This elegant 19C townhouse opposite the Church of St Martin houses a charming brasserie with decorative details such as old photos, a striking chandelier and attractive parquet flooring. There is also a heritage-protected dining room with stuccoed ceilings. Chef-patron Daniel Bitterli cooks classic, traditional dishes that take their cue from the seasons and draw on Mediterranean influences. Dishes such as the sole fillets with two kinds of asparagus and hollandaise sauce exemplify the restaurant's commitment to fresh, high-quality ingredients and flavoursome cuisine. The waitstaff are very attentive, friendly and adept.

Name: Seven Lugano - the restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the rooftop of the casino and accessible via a glass-sided lift, this restaurant boasts fine views of the lake. In summer, the popular seats on the terrace need to be booked well in advance, while the lounge bar on the ground floor is perfect for a post-dinner cocktail. The cuisine here is varied and wide-ranging, both on the set menus and the à la carte, plus there’s an excellent choice of wines featuring labels from around the world.

Name: Principe Leopoldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Situated in a panoramic and picturesque location outside the town centre, Principe Leopoldo is the gourmet restaurant of a classic-style hotel with an intimate ambience. Take a seat on the veranda with its stunning views of the lake and mountains or make yourself comfortable in the elegant dining room in winter. The cuisine here is based on solid traditional technique and is prepared from seasonal local and Mediterranean ingredients, with an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. The wine list has something for all tastes, including a selection of memorable vintages.

Name: Landgasthof Bären
Description: The exterior of this 17C half-timbered house exudes historical charm; the interior is traditional and lovingly decorated with upscale furnishings. It is the garden terrace, though, that is the real highlight! In the evening, there is an ambitious set menu, its appealing vegetarian alternative, or regional classics and modern dishes à la carte. More limited options at lunchtime. There is also a good wine list, and service is cordial and competent. Contemporary guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Seegarten
Description: For over 30 years, this elegant restaurant with a pleasant terrace has been making the most of its wonderful location on the marina. The menu is inspired by the seasons; there is also an appetising set menu, which changes on a monthly basis, but the classics are just as much in demand. Book your spot at the traditional seafood festival – Festival de Fruits de Mer – from late November to late January. Other highlights are the extensive wine list, and friendly, professional service.

Name: Gasthaus im Feld
Description: The journey up to the village of Gurtnellen, at an altitude of 935m, is well worth it! Chef-owner Beat Walker is the fifth generation of his family to run this charming restaurant dating back to the 19C. He is assisted by Roland Gloor, who takes excellent care of diners. Behind the wooden shingle façade that is typical of the region, the atmosphere is inviting, from the Gaststube on the ground floor to the elegant wood-panelled Urnerstube on the first floor. There is also a beautiful terrace with mountain views. At lunchtime, there are à la carte dishes (eg trout with Siiwgagglä (fried potatoes) and Gmiäs (vegetables), or Chalbschopfbäggli (veal chops) with Gschtunggetä Härdepfel (mashed potatoes) and Gmiäs), and in the evening you will be surprised with the "Äs" set menu (four, five or six courses). There are four cosy guestrooms for diners who wish to extend their time here.

Name: Adler
Description: A little off the beaten track, this inn is delightfully cosy with its wood-panelled interior. The chef, who hails from South Tyrol, serves up classic cuisine with a modern twist, making a point of working with regional produce. The attentive front-of-house team includes his partner, a trained sommelier – the wine cellar boasts over 800 labels. There are a few attractive guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: La Cantine des Commerçants
Description: A neo-bistro in the old abattoir district of the city, characterised by white and bright green walls, retro decor and a large counter where you can sit and eat. The varied menu is very much in keeping with the times: risotto with prawns and wild herbs, grilled fish and pan-fried fillet of beef.

Name: Brasserie Les Trois Rois
Description: In the left wing of hotel Les Trois Rois, this classic, elegant brasserie has tasteful and sophisticated interior decor, with a wonderful view of the Rhine. The food expresses its French and Swiss influences in classic dishes from the cannon, such as beef tartare and sole meunière, but more modern dishes, for instance "loup de mer, green tomato, young artichoke, lemon, verbena", also feature on the menu. The terrific wine selection, too, has a penchant for Switzerland and France. The service is friendly and attentive. Brunch is served on Sundays. Tip: You can look into the kitchen through a window in the corridor leading to reception.

Name: L'Artichaut
Description: Only the street separates this appealing restaurant from the River Arve. You will feel completely at home here, thanks to both the pleasant bistro atmosphere, including decorative paintings and posters of vintage advertisements, and the French cuisine reinterpreted with seasonal influences. Excellent wine list.

Name: Le Vallon
Description: This stylishly appointed classical inn with a pretty pink façade and green shutters welcomes you with open arms. The tastefully luxurious interior is decked in bouquets of fresh flowers and floral wallpaper. In his open kitchen, David Thomas concocts traditional fare with an extremely subtle sprinkling of modern touches (Lyon-style frog’s legs, sweetbread à la meunière). Friendly, attentive service and a splendid wine list (among which a noteworthy selection of reds, also available in magnums). In fine weather, alfresco dining on the terrace and in the lush green garden is heavenly. A country chic interior with overtones of romanticism – perfect for a date night!

Name: CAAA by Pietro Catalano
Description: The location right next to an art gallery (from which you also have direct access to the restaurant) could not be more fitting, as the theme of creativity is omnipresent here in the restaurant, too. The chic, modern interior is all curved lines, with the relief of the original ceiling as its centrepiece! Pale tones and the sleek design of the tables and chairs lend a Nordic feel. All of the activity in the open kitchen can be followed by diners – in the evening, a tasting menu comprising three, five or seven courses is created here. Served at lunchtime, the three-course "Chef's Mood Menu" changes on a weekly basis. The proprietor, who happens to be the chef's sister, manages the service in concert with the chefs, and ensures a pleasant atmosphere. She is happy to provide information about the regional ingredients and the restaurant's nature-based philosophy. The cocktails and mocktails served at the bar are an integral part of the culinary experience here.

Name: Auberge du Lion d'Or
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a chic setting with a romantic view of the Jura mountains and Lake Geneva, you can enjoy modern, creative fare with a weakness for vegetables, illustrated by flame-licked roast watermelon paired with a marigold stock. The enticing lineup is paired with a fine wine list that boasts a few Swiss and French gems. The swish, luminous private room upstairs is the epitome of contemporary good taste.

Name: Namun
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: For fans of Thai food, this restaurant in the luxurious Grand Resort Bad Ragaz is the place to be! The focus is on Thai cuisine, but there are also Chinese dishes. Elegant and minimalist, the Far Eastern-style decor makes for the perfect setting. Tip: Ask about the Thai curry – even if it's not on the menu. In case you were wondering, the name Namun translates as "lukewarm water" and is a reference to the local thermal spring.

Name: Römerhof
Description: This beautiful building, the origins of which date back to the 16C, is run with dedication by Dominique and Gerald Bergue-Hunziker. Classic and international dishes are served in an elegant setting – the coffered ceiling is striking. In the evening, there is a choice of two set menus (one of which is vegetarian), each comprising three to six courses, and an à la carte menu. At lunchtime there is a shorter menu including a reasonably priced set menu. You can also relax in the cigar lounge or the pretty salons. Cosy and charming guestrooms are available in the hotel of the same name.

Name: GLACIER
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: What a great location right in front of the Eiger North Face! The fine dining restaurant of the chic boutique hotel (also called Glacier) makes the most of its surroundings with a floor-to-ceiling window front – and a wonderful terrace with a magical view. The dishes are based on select regional ingredients: you can either opt for the set menu or go à la carte, and sharing is also possible. The set menu is accompanied by harmonious wine pairings from the 320-year-old wine cellar, which is home to some 500 labels, over 200 of which are available by the glass. The enthusiastic sommelier provides astute recommendations.

Name: OX'n
Description: Where the old Ochsen inn once stood, the new OX'n stands today with its eye-catching modern design – all the glass gives the place an airy feel and a pleasing sense of transparency. The overall atmosphere is trendy yet inviting. In good weather, the terrace beckons. Friendly service. A surprise menu is served Wed-Sat evenings, and there is an additional à la carte selection Wed-Thu. At lunchtime, a simplified version of the evening surprise menu is available. Alternatively, you could opt for the set menu that changes every week, or something from the à la carte selection. Featuring ingredients sourced from local producers, this is flavoursome seasonal cuisine. The Entlebuch trout with asparagus and beurre blanc is a must-try. Tip: If you fancy an after-work beer or a cocktail, pop into the bar for a quick drink, or feel free to stay a while longer.

Name: Lindenhofkeller
Description: This place takes home-style cuisine up a notch with its "feinbürgerliche Küche". But soul food is also a very apt description of what is served in this gorgeous traditional restaurant in a desirable location in the old town. Sebastian Rösch delivers genuinely feel-good fare by combining his Franconian culinary heritage with Swiss influences. Options such as "Spätzle, Bergkäse, Périgord truffles" or "Zander from Lake Maggiore, goulash broth, Krautfleckerl (noodles with caramelised cabbage)" exemplify his ability to put a contemporary spin on traditional dishes. Premium-quality produce is always used. The "Brotzeit" (for two) is another interesting proposition. Diners can go à la carte or opt for the "Chef's Choice" set menu (with or without meat). The modern decor and relaxed ambience are reminiscent of a chic, trendy gastro pub; the courtyard terrace is also pretty. Extremely friendly waitstaff. Real passion has gone into curating the wine list – a fine selection of well-established names but also lesser-known or smaller winegrowers. On Wed they are also open for lunch (shorter menu). Tip for motorists: Parkhaus Urania is just a short (if steep) walk away.

Name: EMOTIONS by Guy Ravet
Description: The classic elegance of the Grand Hôtel du Lac, designed by architect Ernest Burnat, is the perfect setting for Chef Guy Ravet's ambitious cuisine. The finest ingredients are used with mastery and skill, as in the case of the fillet of wild turbot, seared, with cauliflower mousseline, red onion and mustard seed condiment and beurre blanc with chives.

Name: SACHI
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The luxurious Mandarin Oriental hotel complex houses this restaurant presided over by chef Mitsu – a former disciple of master chef Nobu Matsuhisa, who has earned his spurs in the world of Japanese fine dining. In a resolutely contemporary setting, he serves set menus rife with delicious modern marriages of flavours, plus a fine selection of sushi. You might like to sample these at the counter of Omakase Bar, as you watch the master at work. Alternatively, head for the terrace alongside the Rhône.

Name: Osteria San Gallo
Description: This agreeably lively little osteria stands on the edge of the pedestrian precinct, with a terrace area in front of the entrance. The attractive interior is comfortable, with simple bistro chairs, polished wooden tables and an open kitchen. An ambitious team cooks up authentic Italian dishes – try, for example, the "gnocchetti di Mamma Bruna" – house-made potato gnocchetti al ragù della casa – or sea bass "alla spigola in sinfonia mediterranea". At lunchtime, options are more limited but include short set menus for a quick lunch.

Name: Afghan Anar
Description: Take advantage of the rather rare opportunity to discover Afghan cuisine! Here you can sample some of the country's most popular dishes, such as bolani, kabuli pulao or baklava. The atmosphere is laid back and down to earth, which is in part down to the open kitchen and authentic decor. As an alternative to the conventional tables and chairs, you have the option to dine on traditional mats.

Name: Repas
Description: Fancy a delicious meal above the rooftops of Biel?
