On the sixth floor of the Hotel Elite, in this central location near the railway station, you get a great view of the city and the Jura. The atmosphere is unpretentious, the service is friendly and the cuisine is contemporary, with regional and Mediterranean influences. If you're coming as a group, order a few of the finger food dishes ("Amuse") to share.

Name: Café des Banques
Description: In the heart of Geneva, this chic bistro is the lair of Yoann Caloué who draws upon seasonal ingredients and high-flying technique to craft contemporary French cuisine. The classy yet cosily chummy setting provides the perfect foil to dishes of the likes of carpaccio of scallops enhanced by a sea urchin mayonnaise or free-range chicken served with a truffle-flavoured gravy. Wine buffs will be enchanted by the cellar, which stars mostly French wineries, with the odd international gem. The desserts are also meticulously crafted, illustrated by two signatures: soufflé à la chartreuse and lemon tart with a limoncello sabayon. This smart venue manages to combine fine dining with a friendly buzzy vibe.

Name: Kronenstübli
Description: Premium materials, tasteful fabrics and attractive pinewood panelling make for a cosy yet elegant atmosphere – just the right backdrop for the sophisticated cuisine served here, which is classic French with Italian influences. Tip: Try the canard à la presse – pressed duck – (available if ordered by at least two of your party). The restaurant is housed in the traditional and stylishly luxurious Grand Hotel Kronenhof.

Name: Bodega Noi
Description: A really attractive restaurant: sleek, modern, spacious and – thanks to the large glass frontage – pleasingly bright, not to mention the view of the beautiful countryside. The leafy terrace with its shady chestnut tree is also very inviting. On the menu: flavourful cuisine prepared using excellent ingredients and drawing on Mediterranean and regional influences. Lunchtime options are more limited and more moderately priced.

Name: Taverne zur Krone
Description: This stately, beautifully restored historical building proposes two dining options: an elegant wood-panelled restaurant as well as a modern-style brasserie. In summer the terrace is particularly delightful. You'll find a great selection of traditional and classic dishes on the menu.

Name: La Cène
Description: This establishment draws the eye with its refined decor as much as it appeals with its two mouth-watering set menus: the weekly lunch menu ("Inspiration de la Semaine" – three to five courses) and the evening menu ("Éclosion des Sens" – three to seven courses), which is changed every month. Diners enjoy modern seasonal cuisine with a dash of creative flair, which keeps them coming back for more. A food and wine pairing event is also organised one evening a month.

Name: Bistrot du Boeuf Rouge
Description: This restaurant is well known in the local area for its simple yet gourmet Lyonnaise specialities: rosette sausage, hot saucisson, pike quenelles, etc. The Farina family's culinary skill is demonstrated on a daily basis, to a backdrop of attractive old-fashioned decor.

Name: Schloss Binningen
Description: This stylishly furnished restaurant housed in an attractive 13C castle serves contemporary international cuisine with Mediterranean and Asian influences. At lunchtime choose between the "Business Lunch" deal and the four-course "Sorpresa" set menu; in the evening, they serve a four- to six-course "Emozione" tasting menu – or you can dine à la carte, which includes a vegetarian alternative. Under the direction of the dedicated sommelier, the service is friendly and proficient. In summer, the terrace is inviting. The hotel area beautifully combines modern and historical features. Tip: There is covered parking next door; if you prefer to get here by tram, line 10 stops right by the castle grounds. The narrow River Birsig also flows past here.

Name: moment
Description: Set in the historical heart of Bern, this trendy, modern restaurant spread over two floors serves creative cuisine with a focus on regional and seasonal produce. The "Carte Blanche" menu offers a choice of two four- to five course set menus, – one completely plant based. A laid-back front-of-house team takes care of the service. There are entrances on both Postgasse and Gerechtigkeitsgasse.

Name: Langosteria
Description: This is a place to see and be seen on the ski slopes overlooking St Moritz. The terrace affords magnificent views, making it a delightful spot in which to savour freshly prepared Italian cuisine. Langoustine, lobster and fish, truffle pizza and pasta are the specialities of this restaurant, which also has locations in Milan, Paris and Paraggi. If you're not skiing, the best way to get here is by taxi.

Name: Bären
Description: Culinary passion is alive and well in this charming 17C inn! Owner Christian Mutschler is always on hand, advising and serving, but also sharing stories about the eventful history of the place. The no-frills food is tasty, and most of the ingredients come from the region. The game dishes are definitely worth trying – made with game hunted by the owner, they could hardly be fresher or more seasonal. The lunch menu is more limited, but depending on the number of reservations you may still be able to order from the regular menu. The wine list is also dominated by Swiss labels, and there are plenty of good bottles to choose from. Be sure to make the most of the terrace and the great view it offers!

Name: Madre Nostra
Description: Classic Italian cooking is served in the charming restaurant of the modern hotel CERVO Mountain Resort, which is located a little above the village and right next to the slopes. The produce and flavour are the main focus here. At lunchtime, they offer a limited selection from the evening menu, as well as highlights from the establishment's other restaurants. The terrace is impressive!

Name: Sala of Tokyo
Description: Classic Japanese cuisine made from top-notch ingredients is the name of the game here. The sushi and sashimi, tempura, and robata grill specialities, as well as the sukiyaki and shabu shabu stews all come highly recommended. Another draw of this place is its inviting interior, which is sleek and simple, yet cosy at the same time. You can watch the sushi master at work at a small counter.

Name: MURA
Description: At this restaurant in the heart of the popular Seefeld quarter, contemporary Japanese cuisine is the name of the game. At lunchtime, the deluxe bento boxes are a good option; the evening meal revolves around an omakase menu comprising 11-12 courses. The interior is appealingly minimalist, with clean lines, warm wood tones and Far Eastern decorative touches. The atmosphere is friendly and the service attentive.

Name: AMEO
Description: This restaurant certainly lives up to its tagline of "fine dining with arts". The creative cuisine takes inspiration from an in-house art exhibition, which changes every quarter. Chef Julien Mühlebach and sommelier Maximilian Dullinger, who met and became friends while working at EquiTable, have joined forces and opened their own intimate dining spot. The decor is deliberately pared down and minimalist, keeping the focus firmly on the food and the art. The surprise tasting menu – four, five or six courses, as well as an optional cheese course – showcases locally sourced ingredients from small-scale producers. Diners can expect precisely crafted dishes that are rife with original combinations, resulting in striking contrasts in flavour and texture. The friendly front-of-house team provides detailed explanations of each course. You can also count on Maximilian's expertly curated wine pairings to round out the experience. At lunchtime on Wed and Thu, a simple two-course set menu is available.

Name: Williams ButchersTable am Hegibachplatz
Description: If it's high-quality meat you're after, look no further than this steakhouse located just outside the old town. The butcher's counter is sure to whet your appetite – here you can hand-pick your preferred high-quality cuts. The fantastic national and international selection includes US Prime Black Angus Beef, Swiss LUMA Pork and pata negra bellota, as well as New Zealand lamb or bison and Japanese Wagyu beef. There are also "specials" and "dailies" available at lunchtime. Diners can bask in the nostalgia of the charming brasserie setting. To the front of the restaurant, the terrace with shady trees is appealing, too. Tip: Take the bus or train directly to the door. If coming by car, park in Parkhaus Feldegg, just a few minutes' walk away. It's worth noting that even non-diners like to buy their meat here. A second Williams ButchersTable can be found in the city centre near the Limmat River.

Name: Casino Restaurant
Description: In the beautiful building of the Casino Bern, which opened in 1909 in the centre of the old town, the mixture of a great historical setting and brasserie chic exudes a special flair, which continues in summer on the wonderful large terrace - here you can enjoy the view of the Aare under shady trees. The menu features classic dishes as well as Italian influences. There is a menu (also vegetarian) as well as an a la carte offer in addition to ‘Grosses pièces’ for two people. Next to the restaurant is the ‘Salon d'Or’ with bistro bar - here you can enjoy coffee and cake as well as wines and cocktails throughout the day.

Name: Baur's
Description: The chic, rather imposing deluxe brasserie of the famous Baur au Lac hotel does full justice to the top-notch spirit of gastronomy with which the grand hotel is synonymous. It serves international cuisine firmly rooted in the classics and made with excellent ingredients. The wine list is compiled by one of the best sommeliers in the world.

Name: Le Deck Restaurant
Address: Route de la Corniche 4, Chexbres, 1070, Switzerland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Opposite Le Baron Tavernier boutique spa hotel, you can expect pedigree Gallic fare with strong Mediterranean accents in a score that changes monthly. Both the signature and à la carte menus are defined by top-drawer produce, e.g. crudo of wild gambero, violet fig dressing and toasted buckwheat; local lamb cooked two ways, stuffed nidi di rondine (swallow’s nest pasta) and crispy chickpea fritters; strawberry and matcha tea tiramisu. For a jaw-dropping view of Lake Geneva, bag a seat by the window. In summertime, the outdoor bar is heaven for drinks, before or after dinner.

Name: Alter Torkel - Huus vum Bündner Wii
Description: Even from the outside, Alte Torkel, which is located right on the road through the vineyards, is liable to turn heads! The old stone house at a remove from even its closest neighbours has maintained its regional charm while incorporating modern touches; the wine theme is omnipresent. In keeping with its "Fine Wineing" motto, the menu is characterised by a regularly changing selection of wines by the glass. A contemporary influence makes itself felt in the seasonal, regional cuisine. The hosts are cordial and dedicated. In summer, the terrace with a view of the valley is a real boon!

Name: Rosa Pulver
Description: In this pretty, traditional house in the centre of town, the cosy atmosphere and warm, attentive service alone are enough to ensure a truly enjoyable evening. Another draw is the seasonal cuisine, which includes both classic dishes such as braised beef with black cabbage and modern creations such as barley with fermented koji and dried carrots… and then there is the delicious bread served as an appetiser. The "Rosa Pulver" set menu – conventional or vegetarian – comes in four, five or seven courses. On Wed and Thu, there is also a three-course set menu called "Die Kleine Rosa" ("Little Rosa"). You can opt for the hand-picked wine pairings to go with the set menu; an alcohol-free drinks pairing is also available.

Name: Le 42
Description: This stylish restaurant, part of the snug, yet very swish Le White Hotel, stands on the way into the village, facing the Dents du Midi mountain range. The chic rugged alpine interior is a draw in itself with seating spread over two levels furnished in a sleek modern vein and complemented by reclaimed wood and quarried stone. The eclectic menu stars an intelligent lineup of pure-bred French, hearty alpine and sun-drenched recipes from southern France.

Name: Les Touristes
Description: This restaurant, which has been a culinary landmark for decades, is in the hands of two chefs from the region. Spot-on combinations illustrate their enticing repertory crafted from cherry-picked, primarily local produce. In the evening, we recommend the “Signature” or “Veggie” menu, while the lunchtime score is very sensibly priced. The splendid cheese trolley of well-matured delights is another highlight, all the more so as the sommelier is never far away, ready to introduce you to fascinating wines from local sustainable wineries. A buzzy vibe, a stylish interior and alfresco dining on the terrace - heavenly come summertime.

Name: Landgasthof Wartegg
Description: Run by the Frei family since 1982, this long-standing restaurant with its well-maintained shingle façade serves fresh, flavoursome seasonal fare rooted in classic cuisine and crafted from excellent ingredients. The set lunch is very popular. Tip: There is an especially fine selection of Swiss wines. Diners can choose between rustic cosiness and refined elegance in the various indoor spaces or head for the lovely tree-shaded terrace. Cosy guestrooms are available for overnight stays.

Name: PUR Hurden
Description: The location by Lake Zurich is quite something – the terrace overlooking the water is dreamy, not least on account of the mountain views! The restaurant boasts further charms indoors: regional cachet shines through, beautifully combined with chic, modern style. The menu includes classics – beef tartare and crispy battered fish bites are a must – and contemporary dishes such as lake fish ceviche or, for dessert, "wild cacao from Bolivia".

Name: Marguita
Description: This restaurant in the magnificent Grand Hotel Baur au Lac, which dates back to 1844, exudes all the glamour of the Riviera. In the hands of interior designer Martin Brudnizki, the airy, light-filled rotunda has been imbued with an extremely elegant, luxe ambience with eye-catching features such as a stylish Art Deco chandelier and wonderful mosaic floor – although the beautiful view of the garden or the Schanzengraben steals the show. The Mediterranean-inspired menu includes numerous French and Italian classics, many of which have been given a modern twist. Seafood lovers should definitely look out for the "Lobster Love" dishes. You can count on the dedicated front-of-house team for attentive and courteous service.

Name: Luciole Restaurant
Description: Luciole is the quintessence of seasonal, spot-on cooking. The exclusively vegetable lineup of this dinky establishment in La Chaux-de-Fonds celebrates produce from the garden and nearby. Entirely ruled by the seasons, they deploy ancestral and modern techniques: fermentation, cryoconcentration, wild herbs and flowers. The menu may skip from tomatoes, rhubarb, peach and basil to absinth-laced grilled green peas or violet-perfumed sweet titbits to finish. An open kitchen, lovely tableware and delightful service set the scene in this eatery run by a nature-loving couple whose commitment to excellence is second to none. Note: maximum of eight guests per service.

Name: al lago
Description: Housed in a type of winter garden with a charming terrace (the jewel in the crown!), this restaurant serves dishes that combine modern influences with more classic touches, all prepared using ingredients of the best quality. Make sure you try the risotto made from Carnaroli rice with red pepper, green sauce and Cantabrian anchovies, as well as the Guanaja chocolate mousse and ice cream with mixed berries. An excellent selection of wine and young, friendly service complete the picture.

Name: la p'tite maison
Description: This ‘dinky’ house seats no more than fifteen in a warm interior that blends bare stone walls and contemporary notes. Since 2021, the couple, Margaux, in the kitchen, and Jeremy, in charge of the front-of-house, conjures up a different five-course seasonal surprise menu every month. The à la carte lineup unveils a delicate culinary signature: a new spin on vitello tonnato; vegetarian ceviche and sweet potato fries; fillet of pork lacquered in sesame seeds with black garlic, girolles, aubergine and kohlrabi. Bang-on flavours and sensible prices.

Name: Amaru by Claudia Canessa
Description: A taste of Peru in the heart of the Upper Engadine. At the restaurant housed in the elegant Kulm Hotel St. Moritz, the charming, attentive and professional front-of-house team welcomes you in a tastefully decorated and cheerful space with a handsome vaulted ceiling. In the kitchen, Claudia Canessa and her team bring Peruvian cuisine in all its diversity to the plate, cooking up modern-inspired dishes using excellent ingredients. Intriguing options include "El Choclo y sus Gambas" (grilled corn cake, red prawns, pickled onions, ocopa) and "Tuna Chicano" (aka ceviche).

Name: Carlton
Description: This tasteful, elegant restaurant is located in a historical building that was erected in 1913 to house a department store and later converted into the Carlton Elite hotel. They serve classic, top-notch cuisine; in the evening a more modern five-course menu with beef Wellington, tartar and crêpes Suzette is also available. Great wine list, including an impressive selection of 40 or so types from the Domaine Romanée-Conti.

Name: Badalucci
Description: A historic restaurant with its roots in Italian cuisine. Originally from the island of Procida in southern Italy, the chef here focuses mainly on fish-based dishes, although the menu also features delicious meat options and vegetarian recipes for each course – whatever you order, seasonal ingredients are to the fore in this urban-style eatery situated slightly away from the centre. The wine list highlights the owners’ passion for champagne via highly respected labels from interesting small-scale producers.

Name: Le Rossignol
Description: At Le Rossignol (which is French for nightingale but also happens to be the chef's name), Willy Rossignol finds a captive audience for his smooth classical repertoire of indulgent, flavoursome and well-balanced dishes, prepared using fresh ingredients. Mara, his wife, extends guests an attentive welcome in the simple, well-kept space or out on the terrace in fine weather. Dishes to try include the Gragnano paccheri with wild mushrooms with an aged Parmigiano Reggiano gratin, or thinly sliced chamois with Kampot pepper.

Name: Sauvage
Description: This place has been dedicated to hospitality for over 500 years. Not only does the long-standing Hotel Wilden Mann have charming, individually styled guestrooms, it is also a bastion of fine dining. The tastefully elegant Sauvage serves classic and traditional dishes made with select, exceedingly fresh ingredients. In addition to the à la carte selection – featuring, for example, flam-seared Brüggli char or sautéed veal liver – a set menu is available. At lunchtime, the options are slightly more streamlined but include dishes from the evening menu. Tip for motorists: the Kesselturm multi-storey car park is just a short walk away. Alternatively, you can park on the other side of the river, stroll through the beautiful old town and then cross the bridge (Reussbrücke).

Name: Accademia del Gusto
Description: This restaurant is a smash hit with its many regulars, which is hardly surprising considering the terrific food and lively and buzzing atmosphere. Over time, various dishes have achieved classic status. While Stefano Piscopo conjures up delectable creations such as home-made pasta (eg veal ravioli with sage butter) or marinated tuna tartare, his charming wife presides front-of-house. The handful of tables on the pavement tend to get snapped up quickly.

Name: Zum See
Description: A pleasant walk in the mountains leads to this charming restaurant with a romantic terrace. Simple, good cuisine is served.

Name: parkhuus
Description: The restaurant at the luxurious Park Hyatt business hotel is spacious and high-ceilinged, with an open kitchen, upscale furnishings and sophisticated modern lighting; the glassed-in wine library is well worth seeing! The outstanding wine list features plenty of international labels and an interesting selection of natural and organic wines. The chefs serve up modern dishes that are available as a set menu or à la carte. If you're undecided, the grilled dishes won't disappoint – think top-quality tomahawk steak or a Chateaubriand for two, both irresistibly appetising. In season, opt for the delicious truffle gnocchi.

Name: La Maison du Village
Address: Rue de la Fontanette 41, Sauges, 2024, Switzerland
Description: With its resolutely relaxed ambience, this auberge is far from the traditional image of a high temple of gastronomy. Here, Marc Strebel, a young chef from the Valais, conjures up dishes very much inspired by a return to nature. Superb view of the lake from the terrace.

Name: Brasserie 1809
Description: The restaurant is done out in a modern Alpine style, with an interior that is upscale, sleek and at the same time inviting. As for the food great store is set by regional produce and sustainable farming. Select ingredients go into creating tasty seasonal dishes. It is pleasant to eat on the lovely terrace, and not only in summer! The Capra hotel has wonderful inviting guestrooms.

Name: Sonnenhof
Description: The mountains of the Saanenland provide a stunning backdrop – and in summer the terrace is pure bliss! Beyond the idyllic outdoor spaces, the interior welcomes diners with rustic elegance and tasteful design, elevated by the warmth of reclaimed wood. And then there's the outstanding cooking of chef-patron Erich Baumer: Using top-quality ingredients, he creates regional and classic dishes with a Mediterranean twist – think warm scallops with asparagus salad and pink grapefruit fillets, or Austrian saddle of venison with chanterelles, rösti and sweet-and-sour plums. The ever-present proprietress brings a heartfelt touch to the service.

Name: Kronenhalle
Description: This Zurich institution located on Bellevueplatz has housed a restaurant since 1924. Be sure to look around – the walls are adorned with original art by Joan Miró, Marc Chagall, Pierre Bonnard! You can choose to dine in the lively atmosphere of the Brasserie or the more intimate ambience of the Chagall Room. There is also the Swiss Gallery on the first floor. In this beautiful, stylish setting, diners tuck into classic, traditional cuisine at its most heartfelt and satisfying! Much of the food is presented to diners tableside. A signature dish is their Kronenhalle sliced fillet of veal with rösti.

Name: Wirtschaft zum Frieden
Description: This centuries-old inn enjoys a prime location right on Marktplatz, and its charming ambiance, redolent of a bygone era, will have you yearning to return. The dedication of your hosts is also infectious. While maître d' Heidi Bischoff graciously attends to diners in the cosy wood-panelled dining areas, chef-patron Fabrice Bischoff cooks up classic, home-style fare using fresh, high-quality ingredients. Some dishes also incorporate a Mediterranean twist. On the menu you will find beef fillet Stroganoff, as well as Swiss salmon steak with accras. A simpler set menu of the day is also available at lunchtime. The verdant terrace is a delightful spot in the summertime!

Name: Donatz
Description: Cornelia and René A Donatz run their business with great dedication. In an elegant rustic-style decor, they serve good fresh cuisine, including classic veal dishes, Angus beef "bestsellers", vegetarian fare and fish such as Graubünden salmon from Lostallo. They stock some 550 wines (20 available by the glass) – a passion of the owner. Donatz Wine Bar proposes a smaller menu. Hotel Donatz has appealingly modern and comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Brücke
Description: The superb location on the River Aare is a big draw here, and it goes without saying that a spot on the terrace is highly prized! The food is fresh and aromatic, with emphasis laid squarely on the quality and seasonality of the produce. The "Tavolata" set menu, which also has a vegetarian counterpart, includes starters to share, a palate cleanser and a choice of different main courses. There is also an à la carte menu, reprising, for example, the starter selection from the set menu.

Name: Osteria del Centenario
Description: A restaurant that has been renovated in contemporary style, in complete harmony with its attractive setting overlooking the scenic lakeside promenade. Talented chef Egon Bajardi conjures up interesting Mediterranean cuisine with a focus on creative technique and the occasional exotic touch. Don’t miss his selection of desserts, including Crema Catalana with pumpkin, orange and bay leaf gelato.

Name: La Table du Palafitte
Description: The “Menu Découverte” carries guests away on a journey inspired by the time-honoured culinary traditions of the Mediterranean coast. Choose between the dining room or the large waterfront terrace.

Name: L'Auberge
Description: Choose between the two dining areas – one modern and minimalist, the other more elegant – or, in summer, a delightful garden terrace. Made with top-quality ingredients, the modern French cuisine is infused with a Mediterranean character. There is also a solid wine list and very friendly service overseen by the ever-present proprietress, a trained sommelier. At lunchtime the menu is simpler. Tip: Book a stay at the tasteful hotel of the same name.

Name: MEGU
FacilitiesAndServices: Credit cards not accepted,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This stylish restaurant brings a modern and cosmopolitan take on Japanese cuisine, serving up sushi, sashimi and rolls, as well as Wagyu beef and chicken teriyaki. Fittingly, star designer Noé Duchafour-Lawrence drew inspiration from the Far East to create the sophisticated and distinctive interior. There is also a sushi counter, where – as you might expect in an establishment of this calibre – sushi master Tsutomu Kugota works his magic. In summer, the terrace is a delightful spot.

Name: De la Cigogne
Description: Trained in some of the world’s leading restaurants, the chef at De la Cigogne creates fine French cuisine which is full of flavour and always beautifully presented. Choose between the “old school” interior decor of mahogany panelling and padded chairs or the pleasant terrace in fine weather.

Name: Kreuz
Description: Take a seat in one of the gorgeous dining spaces, or on the lovely, pleasantly peaceful garden terrace, to enjoy traditional and regional fare. The menu features, for instance, local lake fish; European perch from the Lötschberg mountains is also popular. The good food is complemented by a really friendly family atmosphere, which comes courtesy of the attentive service team. In the simpler Gaststube, you can order the dish of the day.

Name: mille sens - les goûts du monde
Description: At this pleasantly lively, modern restaurant on the first floor of the Schweizerhof Passage near the train station, chef Domingo S. Domingo takes you on a culinary journey around the world, also drawing on his Australian and Filipino roots. At lunchtime, options include a small set menu ("Business Lunch") and the "Quicktray" comprising four dishes on one plate. In the evening, guests can choose from the "Domingo Pur Menu Surprise" and "Tavolata" – also available in a large portion to share. The small selection of bowls is available at both mealtimes.

Name: Roter Bären
Description: This pretty restaurant in the red-light district has a rather original concept that is popular with diners: in an open kitchen, the chefs conjure up ambitious appetiser-sized dishes that draw inspiration from modern culinary trends – three are recommended, then maybe a dessert to round things off. Great bar.

Name: da Frappa
Description: Fabio Imparato, who hails from the Italian province of Salerno, is the head chef at this restaurant not far from the lake. After working in various fine dining restaurants, he now devotes himself to Italian and Mediterranean cuisine. The seasonal surprise menu comes in a four- or five-course format. The wine list, too, draws on labels from the chef's homeland. Service is friendly and professional, and the aesthetic is appealing, refined and upscale. Conveniently, there is a public car park nearby.

Name: Belle Vue
Description: To make the most of the simply stunning mountain views, opt for a table near the large glass-planed front – or on the delightful terrace! Complementing the wonderful scenery, the interior of the Bellevue Parkhotel & Spa restaurant boasts a sleek design that provides the backdrop for the fine dining menu: classic dishes such as roast duck breast with potato galettes are served in the evening, and a simpler à la carte selection is available at lunchtime. Choose an accompaniment from the exquisite wine list.

Name: Landgasthof Rössli
Description: Since 1995, Susy and Markus Sager-Meyerhans have been the friendly faces behind this long-established restaurant with its roots in the 18C, when it was a tavern. In addition to cordial service, you can expect a hybrid of traditional and modern-meets-classic cuisine; at lunchtime there is a somewhat reduced menu. Outside you will find the Rosenterrasse and Rössligarten. Charming guestrooms are also available.

Name: Silex
Description: This restaurant is located in a lively residential area. Plenty of Swiss produce goes into the modern seasonal dishes, which are created in the partially visible kitchen. The restaurant is just as committed to sustainability as it is to wine – selected by connoisseurs, the distinctive wine list is testament to a true passion for the grape. British-born chef George Tomlin, previously sous-chef at London's The Clove Club, expresses his creative streak in dishes such as grilled slices of elm mushroom with roasted black onions and a creamy buttermilk and roasted yeast espuma. You can opt to go à la carte or take the five-course tasting menu (also vegetarian). The vibe is deliberately kept simple, with a decor boasting clean lines, and there is a nice terrace outside, in front of this corner plot. The service is friendly and laid back. Just the sort of restaurant you would want in your neighbourhood!

Name: PRISMA Expérience
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace
Description: Housed in the exclusive Park Hotel Vitznau, which dates back to 1903, this summer-only restaurant whisks you away on a culinary voyage. Japanese fusion cuisine is the name of the game here. There is an omakase menu (for two or more diners) and an à la carte selection including sushi, sashimi, Wagyu dishes and ramen. The vibe is casually elegant. The location overlooking the lake is a draw in itself, and it goes without saying that tables on the terrace are highly coveted.

Name: Au Vieux Manoir
Description: A truly magical location! Built in 1882 by renowned physician Dr Victor Guénebaud, the property combines heirloom features with an outstanding location and boasts what is probably one of the finest terraces in the Valais canton! The interior is the epitome of vintage charm from the lovely old parquet floor and beautifully sculpted coffered ceiling to the retro fabric wallpaper. What’s more, the chef-owner’s French-centric cuisine alone merits a visit: a set three- or five-course menu (depending on the time of day) that is savvily crafted with top-notch, super-fresh, seasonal ingredients. To make the most of the manor’s knockout position, book one of the five comfortable guestrooms done out in a tasteful, classical style.

Name: Equo 1706
Description: Records of this building go back to 1706, at which time it was a tavern. Today, the restaurant of the Rössli hotel, which is not far from Vierwaldstätter See, has a nicely pared-back interior and a pleasant terrace. It serves ambitious modern cuisine with seasonal and international influences – you can order à la carte or opt for the four- to seven-course set menu, which is available in two versions: meat/fish or vegetarian. Hotel patrons get to enjoy well-kept guestrooms and the spa facilities.

Name: Le Partage
Description: Located in the luxury Aïda Hotel and Spa, this restaurant’s concept is downright intriguing. The set menu is served in courses, each of which is comprised of several small dishes and diners choose either 10 or 15 "tasting portions" to be shared. The ambitious cuisine rolls out a regional score courtesy of a wide range of local ingredients. Established on two floors, the Alpine-inspired interior is both welcoming and stylish thanks to a profusion of reclaimed wood and dressed stone, elegant herringbone parquet flooring and an open fireplace, complemented by high-quality fabrics and splendid solid wood tables, without forgetting the knockout view from the terrace. The front-of-house staff is friendly, attentive and polished. Teatime in the lounge and brunch on Sundays.

Name: Potato-FINE FOOD RESTAURANT
Description: In the evenings, this delightful little restaurant in a lively street (Bahnhofstrasse) promises warm hospitality in a down-to-earth and friendly atmosphere. Flavoursome modern dishes are served in a set menu format – choose between a three- and five-course version, with pescetarian alternatives available in both cases. The top-notch ingredients are locally sourced. The wine list exclusively features Valais labels, and the selection is impressive.

Name: Ochsen
Description: Located just metres from the monastery, the venerable Ochsen dates back to 1596. In its current iteration with an avant-garde look, it is part of the three-building Hotel Caspar, which has stylishly designed guestrooms. In the open kitchen, regional ingredients go into modern and creative cooking – interesting cuisine that is "close to nature", with fire, aromatic woods, smoked and grilled dishes play a central role.

Name: Chasellas
Description: This charming restaurant in the Suvretta House hotel at the entrance to the skiing and hiking area has found a winning formula, offering rustic specialities for lunch and more sophisticated dishes in the evening, such as herb-crusted rack of lamb, mashed potatoes, chanterelle-asparagus ragout and baby carrots.

Name: Wirtschaft zur Rosenburg
Description: Wherever you look, there's history – the old fortified tower is magnificent! After 33 years, the business has changed hands, but new owners Lukas and Evelyn Christen are committed to keeping the tradition alive. The menu continues to feature both regional and international dishes. Look out for the label "Guets vo hie" on the menu, which indicates the local specialities such as topside beef carpaccio with horseradish, red onions and fried mushrooms. The courtyard terrace is especially pleasant. Tip: This pretty restaurant also makes an ideal venue for weddings and other celebrations.

Name: Hide & Seek
Description: If you like to dine in a lively, modern atmosphere, the restaurant of Hotel Giardino Mountain is for you. The decor features a combination of trendy, chic features and rustic wood. Attentive front-of-house team and Mediterranean and Swiss dishes that are aromatic and flavoursome, made with fresh, often regional produce. Lunch is served in the bar-lounge.

Name: Des Balances
Description: This place boasts an enviable location in the old town and, in summer, the terrace overlooking the River Reuss beckons – the views are stunning! You will find a chic setting in both the restaurant and the Bar & Lounge. On the menu: specialities from the barbecue as well as French and Mediterranean dishes, all made with top-quality regional and seasonal ingredients. The restaurant is located in the gorgeous Hotel Des Balances, so why not stay the night?

Name: dr Egge - das restaurant
Description: Located in Muttenz's old town, this compact restaurant delights diners with its stylish and charming decor, warm hospitality and Italian-inspired cuisine. They propose a seasonal set menu made using regional produce wherever possible; the "Piedmontese Autumn Menu", featuring Alba white truffles, is also a popular choice. Astute wine recommendations come courtesy of the maître d'.

Name: Restaurant Olivo
Description: Its Belle Epoque style lends this restaurant on the first floor of the Grand Casino a distinct elegance and charm that hark back to a bygone era. Under a high ceiling with moulding and chandeliers, Mediterranean-inspired cuisine is served in the form of a set menu or à la carte. The "Dinner & Casino" packages are also worth mentioning. Fabulous balcony terrace with lake and mountain views. Tip: Park in the casino garage.

Name: Auberge d'Onex
Description: Since 1977, this inn has been nestled in verdant surroundings in the former clubhouse of Geneva's first golf course. It serves traditional Italian cuisine, including the chef's specialities of penne with vodka and penne alla Norma (a Sicilian dish that pays tribute to the composer Vincenzo Bellini, who was from the island), but also classics such as vitello tonnato. The dessert trolley features Italian specialities and a choice of fresh fruit.

Name: Spices Kitchen & Terrace
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The manifold dining options available at Bürgenstock Hotel & Alpine Spa include this modern restaurant, which is the perfect choice for fans of Asian cuisine. Premium ingredients go into the Japanese, Chinese, Thai and Indian dishes prepared in an open kitchen. Tip: "Signature Peking duck" (by pre-order only). From the idyllic location overlooking the lake, at over 800m above sea level, the views are sensational – and the terrace is wonderful! Should you prefer to focus your attention on the action in the kitchen, book a table by the kitchen pass.

Name: t3e terre
Address: via Vecchia Stazione 2, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: Owned by the Meneganti family, this beautiful house is home to a restaurant with an attractive dining room and stunning terrace that provide the backdrop for delicious Mediterranean cuisine. A charming hotel with welcoming guestrooms (additional rooms are under construction) adds to the appeal.

Name: Centovalli
Address: Via Vecchia Stazione 5, Ponte Brolla, 6652, Switzerland
Description: This attractive restaurant boasting rustic yet modern dining rooms and a beautiful terrace shaded by a pergola has offered the same format for over 20 years – a single risotto-based dish (the house speciality) served with a delicious meat option, nearly always lamb fillet, and very few fish dishes. Reasonably priced, with everything of an excellent quality.

Name: Oliveiras
Description: The friendly Oliveira family runs this establishment, making sure guests feel at home in the harmonious and deliberately informal atmosphere. They are attentively looked after as they tuck into Mediterranean cuisine made from excellent produce. All of this is accompanied by a fantastic selection of wines from the owner's Portuguese homeland.

Name: Auberge aux 3 Tilleuls
Description: If you're passing through Genolier, be sure to stop off at this charming Auberge! Filipe, the young chef here, serves fresh, tasty cuisine infused with contemporary flair: think fillet of turbot grilled skin on, with pesto and crunchy vegetables. An enjoyable mealtime.

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye de Montheron
Description: Located in a former Cistercian monastery that dates back to 1442, this restaurant proposes food that is very much of the moment. The original and exciting dishes draw heavily on local organic produce and heritage vegetables. Diners are won over by thoroughly modern fare that has been devised with a genuine concern for sustainability, such as suckling lamb served with pak choi and rhubarb. Appealing terrace on the edge of the forest, and a young and trendy atmosphere. A winning formula.

Name: Löwen - Gaststube
Description: Run by Rita and Domenico Miggiano-Köferli, Gasthof Löwen's second eatery is a delightful and more down-to-earth alternative to the fine dining restaurant. The atmosphere is inviting, not least because of the warm hospitality provided by the waitstaff. The freshly prepared, flavoursome dishes include pan-fried Lötschberg perch fillet with lemon thyme and almond butter, and Zurich veal ragout with glazed vegetables and butter rösti. Vegetarian options available. Popular lunch deal.

Name: Le 1424, La Fabrique Cornu
Description: On the top floor of "La Fabrique", the swish modern 1424 restaurant commands a knockout view over the Vaud Alps. In addition to a tasty lunchtime menu, in the evening you have a choice between three leisurely 3- to 6-course menus that slalom between regional produce and international twists: cappuccino of squash, venison with cèpes and pears poached in red wine. The monthly brunch is a hit with foodies. Friendly, on-the-ball service, generous helpings and spot-on, expressive cuisine. Children under the age of 12 are invited to try a smaller (and lower priced) version of all the dishes on the menu!

Name: Le Guillaume Tell
Address: Route de la Petite Corniche 5, Aran, 1091, Switzerland
Description: This spruce pink house in the heart of a wine-producing village overlooks Lake Geneva. Since 1989, chef Denis Velen has been crafting gastronomic fare with a focus on premium produce, like duck with choucroute or a duo of scallops seared on a plancha griddle. Devise your own 3-course menu at lunchtime, while tasting and surprise menus set a more relaxed pace in the evening. Alfresco dining on the terrace is sheer bliss in summertime.

Name: Thai Garden
Description: You could almost fancy you are in Thailand: with dim lighting, Far Eastern background music, Thai decoration, large ceiling fans and a babbling fountain, the setting alone transports you to an exotic world. Complementing this is exceptionally friendly service and authentic Thai cuisine – the spiciness can be adjusted to suit diners' individual preferences. Tip: The appealing lunch deal is available in two variations: the "Thai Box" and the "Vegi Box".

Name: Käserei
Description: Whether you are seated at a bare or beautifully set table, in this listed former cheese dairy, the dedicated hosts serve high-quality international and regional cuisine that is not only a hit with the locals. Tip: From Tuesdays to Fridays, an inexpensive lunch is served. Incidentally, the building is located in the heart of the pretty old town – perfect for a stroll!

Name: L'Etoile
Description: Whether you are seated in the chic bistro, in the winter garden or in the attractive shaded garden, this family-run establishment offers a warm welcome and a friendly atmosphere. The seasonal menu, with dishes prepared to order, features local producers. The thick and creamy crème brûlée, delicately flavoured with orange, is unforgettable. The set lunch menu is a must!

Name: Le Café Suisse
Description: This former village café has morphed into a buzzy, friendly eatery decked in colourful cartoon murals. Youthful Marie Robert, assisted by an almost woman only team, wholeheartedly regales diners with creative, light-hearted dishes that are in tune with the seasons to be washed down with excellent local tipples. Robert has a flair for spontaneously showcasing seasonal ingredients. Examples include a mousseline of seabream enhanced by a whipped beurre blanc or an incredibly powerful and heady duo of blueberry and chocolate. Be bold and opt for her surprise menu – a hit with regulars, it is as playful as it is indulgent.

Name: Auberge Les Platanes
Address: Rue du Vieux Collège 2, Chéserex, 1275, Switzerland
Description: This elegant 17C mansion marries bourgeois comforts and French fine dining with an accent on rich sauces and seasonal produce. Flawless, spot-on service and a subtle hint of nostalgia courtesy of old sewing machines turned into side tables set the scene. Highlights of the flavoursome menu include textbook-perfect steak tartare, prepared at the table by your hostess according to each diner’s personal preferences and served with piping hot fresh fries – a traditional meal, rich in ritual and with all the trimmings!

Name: Vecchia Osteria Seseglio
Description: Chef Ambrogio Stefanetti presents a menu of traditional recipes, flavorful and well-crafted, using local and seasonal ingredients. Among his offerings, the pike with crispy skin à la meunière, carrots and green asparagus, or the savarin soaked in yuzu limoncello, lightly sweetened white chocolate ice cream, and finished with raspberry flakes. This place has a genuine soul – it’s impossible not to fall in love with the region in summer! – and the wine list (featuring Italian and regional selections) is truly appealing!

Name: Hide & Seek
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Ayurvedic philosophy inspires a special section of the menu, where Mediterranean cooking styles and ingredients merge with chef Francesco Leone’s colorful and joyful vision. His cuisine, not without international influences, finds its ideal setting in this refined restaurant inside the “Giardino” hotel. In the warmer months, dining on the magnificent terrace overlooking the garden with its pond and floating flowers is unmissable: a corner of priceless tranquility and beauty.

Name: Scalottas - Terroir
Description: At this trendy Alpine-style restaurant, the kitchen works exclusively with regional produce, much of it their own. Seasonality and sustainability are a central tenet – the staff will be happy to tell you more about their concept. To order, simply mix and match the dishes on the menu that pique your interest. The wines are also sourced from the region and surrounding areas – astute recommendations come courtesy of the friendly service team.

Name: PURO
Description: The restaurant on the first floor of the Mövenpick Hotel serves interesting and ambitious cuisine. This comes in the form of a very appealing fusion concept of Asian and Latin American-inspired dishes made with plenty of regional produce, but also ingredients from around the globe. The food is down to earth, flavoursome and fresh! This is complemented by an international wine list, extremely friendly service and a stylish interior.

Name: La Fontana Restaurant & Bar
Address: Via ai Monti della Trinità 44, Locarno, 6600, Switzerland
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Splendidly located inside the Hotel Belvedere, at an altitude of approximately 240m, this elegant south-facing restaurant boasts a splendid terrace and a lounge space. Depending on where you sit, watch the chef at work in the kitchen or enjoy the impressive views through La Fontana’s ground floor picture windows overlooking its verdant surroundings. The culinary focus here is on modern and seasonal Mediterranean cuisine without neglecting the region’s gastronomic roots. In addition to the classic menu, you can also choose the 4- or 5-course tasting option as well as the restaurant’s signature dishes such as the La Fontana tartare, the Chateaubriand, and the Raviolini del Plin. The extensive glass-fronted wine cabinets at the entrance provide an impressive backdrop.

Name: Riva
Description: Perhaps the only true fish restaurant in Ascona where fish specialities are nothing short of exceptional, but meat lovers will not be disappointed either. Situated inside the Seven Boutique Hotel, Riva offers a maritime atmosphere with colourful touches that recall the blue expanse and a tasty cuisine declined in tasting or à la carte menus, from ‘I Crudi’ with oysters & co. to ‘Sogliola alla mugnaia with lettuce, capers and spring onion’. Definitely a great address!

Name: Schmitte
Description: This is the fine dining restaurant of the long-established Hotel Schweizerhof. The small space is inviting, with an elegant and cosy feel, and service is provided by a friendly and attentive team. The dishes are rooted in classic cuisine and draw on modern influences and the seasons. The six-course set menu is predominantly made up of regional ingredients. A vegetarian version is also available upon advance request. N.B. The set menu price is to be paid in advance. In the hotel garden, there is a sun terrace and a bar.

Name: Sablier
Description: Definitely one of the coolest restaurants in town! On the eighth floor of a newly built section of the airport, the incredibly high ceilings, chic interior design, two large glass-fronted wine cabinets and stylish bar are really impressive. The menu features French-inspired cuisine, with an additional lunch deal available daily and brunch served every Sunday. The rooftop terrace has to be the highlight! Tip for motorists: park in Parkhaus 4, south exit.

Name: Chez Be
Description: The dedication of the experienced couple at the helm, Romy and Beat Amrein, is palpable. Tasty Mediterranean and French dishes are Beat's speciality – this is pleasant, straightforward cuisine. Romy is in charge front of house, serving guests in her natural and cordial manner. It is worth perusing the wine list, which reveals a penchant for French and Swiss picks. The lunch menu is shorter. The charming modern bistro-style interior with its open kitchen and the terrace giving onto the little square (Mühleplatz) are both lovely places to sit and eat.

Name: Yamada
Address: 16 Elizabeth St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
Description: Chef Isao Yamada's life's work has been kaiseki, and this impressive venture adds an interesting facet to the roster of high-end Japanese dining in New York. Diners here are treated to a personal expression of seasonality, with each course highlighting a distinct method of preparation. An array of sashimi bears impressive fish; the owan, or clear soup course, may brim with King crab dumplings; and the gohan, or rice course, may be a seasonal delight folded with Maine lobster, Nantucket sweet corn and maitake mushrooms from the Catskills.The chicly spare room is reserved for a handful of diners at an L-shaped counter, while the pale, earthy aesthetic is enhanced with ikebana and a windowed Japanese dry garden.

Name: Gui
Address: 776 Eighth Ave., New York, NY, 10036, USA
Description: Dining in the heart of Times Square isn't always a good bet, but Gui Steakhouse changes the narrative. A natural choice for pre- or post-theater dining, it's also worth a trip without show tickets to experience their traditional steakhouse classics with Korean influences in a sleek setting. The menu includes raw bar items (Alaskan king crab leg) before shifting the focus to steaks with Japanese wagyu and USDA Prime meat. With a beautiful sear and deep grill marks, the aged steaks are finished simply with a sprinkling of Maldon salt. While steaks are indeed the raison d'être, the menu also features traditional American dishes like flounder and grilled chicken alongside Asian-inspired plates like dan dan noodles and wagyu fried rice.

Name: Creepies
Address: 1360 W. Randolph St., Chicago, IL, 60607, USA
Description: Don't let the name fool you; there's nothing remotely creepy about this charming neighborhood restaurant next door to Chef David and Anna Posey's Elske. They've taken style notes from the classic bistro with stone and wood walls lined with art, black-and-white checkered tile floors and a mix of banquettes and tables, while the menu pulls from French cooking with some Midwestern flair thrown in for good measure. It's a concise offering, with dishes like Parisian gnocchi in creamy gruyere sauce with crispy ham and a drizzle of egg yolk or steamed halibut with sauce homard and dumplings. The simple but well-executed theme continues to dessert, with raspberry sherbet meringue cake or baguette soft serve with chocolate and brown butter crumbs.

Name: Your Only Friend
Description: Your Only Friend blends the laid-back feel of a neighborhood sandwich shop with the polish of a cocktail bar. The menu is cheeky—think sandwiches like the "Hot Nug" with chicken nuggets and Nashville hot sauce, the “Caul Me Maybe,” a roasted cauliflower number, or the "Mortz & Mootz" piled with mortadella, mozzarella and pickled red pepper jelly. Not everything is between the bread, and rotating specials might include blue cheese-brined wings with a crispy coating and their self-described strip mall-style garlic parm. Sides like Seattle fries and pimento dip, as well as bar snacks like miso Chex mix are a worthy order. The cocktail list is short but sharp, with drinks like the orange creamsicle-tasting Irish Cream Soda.

Name: Markette
Description: Right on 7th Avenue in Chelsea, walls of mirrors, modern lights and cozy banquettes make for a stylish stage where Chef India Doris crafts an impressive, nicely trimmed menu that pulls European and Caribbean influences. Carefully prepared and packed with flavor, the best dishes are the most personal: Salt cod fritters arrive with a fiery habanero aioli, and braised oxtail capped with cheddar polenta is a dreamy pie that would outclass its British pub relative. To finish, strawberry cheesecake prepared as a Swiss roll is a clever, beautiful effort. A gorgeous cocktail bar framed in recessed lighting shakes and stirs all night long.

Name: La'Shukran
Address: 417 Morse St. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
Description: La' Shukran feels like a discovery, as you'll need to walk down an alley, look for a green door and climb the stairs to arrive at this cool spot with a funky, retro vibe. It's definitely a hot spot for drinks, but the Levantine cuisine designed for sharing is far from second place.From escargot and sweetbreads to labneh with Maryland crab, summer peppers and corn in green harissa, some dishes lean less traditional, while others, like haswei, or fried rice with seven-spice lamb, seem simple but are spot on. Every table needs an order of their soujek dumplings. Filled with beef and lamb shoulder and resting in a vibrant smoked corn and tomato brodo with urfa chili crunch and toum, it's easy to see why reservations are snapped up so quickly here.

Name: Lei
Address: 15-17 Doyers St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
Description: In the beating heart of Chinatown on Doyers Street, Annie Shi’s little wine bar is a gift to the city. Rare wines are everywhere. They line the edges of the room, and they fill countless boxes stacked to the ceiling. People are everywhere, too, sitting elbow to elbow and even spilling out onto tables in the alley. This talented team doesn’t waste a single square inch of space – and that includes the kitchen, which turns out smart, thoughtful modern Chinese dishes. Chilled celtuce with shallots and red wine vinegar is an essential starter. Other hits include fried whiting with seaweed, scallops with lily buds and ginger, and hand-rolled noodles with braised lamb.

Name: Karravaan
Address: 325 Morse St. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
Description: Chef Sanjay Mandhaiya takes diners on a journey along the Silk Road at Karravaan. The wide-ranging menu promises bold flavors and generous portions intended for sharing. To begin, swipe the smoky eggplant dip, layered with labneh and pureed Italian eggplant with caramelized onions and pomegranate seeds, onto a piece of piping hot, house-made flatbread for a delicious introduction to the meal. Then, perfectly cooked, medium rare duck breast glazed with harissa honey is set over a bed of forbidden rice for a particularly skillful dish. Fluffy jasmine rice tucked with seasonal vegetables is served within a colorful tagine for an impressive dish that pleases the eye and the palate.

Name: Muku
Address: 412 Greenwich St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list
Description: This intimate counter is a tight squeeze, but that’s hardly a deterrent for the guests who come for Chef Manabu Asanuma’s inspired kaiseki. From raw and grilled to simmered, steamed and fried, the menu is rooted heavily in the seasons, pulling ingredients from surrounding areas as well as prized seafood and meat from Japan. Soba noodles made with buckwheat from the chef's hometown are constant fixtures that read personal and sincere. Dessert is playful, most recently featuring strawberries, sake lees ice cream and strawberry foam. Sharply dressed servers standing nearby keep close watch over the evening’s proceedings, ever ready to assist. Do not miss the superb, well-stocked sake program that will delight even the most devoted collectors.

Name: Bánh Anh Em
Description: Long before doors open, a queue quickly forms along Third Avenue. Indeed, the demand for this no-reservations hotspot is serious – and well justified. Carefully prepared and astutely seasoned, the dishes coming out of this Vietnamese kitchen make a striking impression. Just-baked baguettes for the banh mi are top-notch: airy, light, flaky and warm. Brisket, tendon, tripe and steak come together in a soulful pho served with homemade noodles. There’s more, like steamed rolls with minced pork (bánh cuốn) and crispy, golden crepes served with bundles of fresh herbs (bánh xèo). Bring friends, order generously and crowd every square inch of the table.

Name: Elmina
Description: Elmina is the kind of place with wide-reaching appeal, where a warm spirit and a stylish, contemporary decor encourage lingering over Chef Eric Adjepong's modern West African/Ghanian cuisine. Choose between a multicourse tasting menu or the à la carte bar menu, a play on Ghana’s popular, counter-service-style “chop bars,” with snacks like tartare, okra fries and pork belly. Those who opt for the tasting will be rewarded with the likes of scallop crudo with cucumber granita and coconut broth, as well as braised goat with fufu, or pounded plantain and cassava, and a tableside pour of creamy, deep orange-red nkati nkwan sauce. Malva pudding cake with sweet, pickled apricot and vanilla gelato is a delightful ending.

Name: Bartolo
Address: 310 W. 4th St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
Description: Oozing with style and class, this little West Village hideout feels like a secret. A cozy front bar, thick wood-beams across the low ceiling and handsome banquettes strike an intimate, amber-hued mood. Rich, hearty Spanish cooking is front and center, so you’ll want to share everything. Start with cristal bread lined with butter and topped with anchovies or, for something lighter, ajo blanco with honeydew sorbet. Larger plates are well-suited to serious appetites: Grilled Iberian pork, oxtails braised in red wine, and roasted suckling pig and lamb. A lengthy cocktail list and sharply dressed servers keep the night moving along.

Name: Sushi Akira
Address: 317 E. 75th St., New York, NY, 10021, USA
Description: Chef/owner Nikki Zheng polished her skills at some of New York's top sushi restaurants, including Masa and Sushi Nakazawa, before striking out on her own with Sushi Akira. It's a special place, located on the Upper East Side and catering to a dozen guests with a well-priced, 18-course omakase featuring a variety of chilled appetizers, nigiri and dessert. Chef Zheng showcases a calm and precise rhythm as she prepares plates like Japanese tilefish and tofu with dashi broth, and nigiri like minced squid with shiso leaf, soy-marinated bluefin tuna and hairy crab, among others. The meal ends on a light note with a slice of Japanese melon and custard.

Name: Providencia
Address: 1321 Linden Ct. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
Description: You could easily dismiss this small space as just a (really good) bar with its moody ambience and smashing cocktail list. That is, until you taste the food from co-chefs Erik Bruner-Yang and Paola Velez. Their cooking presents an enticing mash-up of Asian, Caribbean and Latin American cuisines and traditions. Equal parts nostalgic and creative, dishes like papusa with salsa verde or pan de playa, with shredded crab in a Caesar dressing and tomato gochujang mayo tucked inside toasted brioche, show off unlikely yet successful flavor combinations. Even dessert is wild and unexpected, with a Japanese twist on baked Alaska featuring kakigori-style shaved ice with guava and strawberry puree and coconut lime sauce enrobed in a torched meringue.

Name: Sal Tang's
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list
Description: It's classic Cantonese American with a modern twist at Sal Tang's, where everything from the dining room to the kitchen's dishes feels nostalgic, albeit with a refined, modern twist. Red lanterns are suspended from the ceiling, paper mâché dragons and cherry blossom wallpaper line the walls, and dark wood anchors this space that's just right for a weeknight meal. Meanwhile, the kitchen delivers nostalgic favorites and updated takes on beloved Chinese American dishes. Don't even think about skipping the egg roll, with its crispy shell and overstuffed filling. Another can't miss? Wonton soup, with its light, savory broth bobbing with pork wontons. Beef and broccoli is yet another classic dish before two refreshing scoops of bright and bold blood orange sorbet.

Name: Astor Club: Chef's Table
Address: 24 E. Goethe St., Chicago, IL, 60610, USA
Description: You don't need to be a member, but you'll feel like one at Chef's Table, tucked inside the private Astor Club. There are just ten seats a night, so reservations are a must for this tasting menu experience where all guests are seated and served together. Chef Trevor Teich is a fine dining veteran, and befitting the setting, the ingredients lean luxe. A single oyster topped with champagne espuma and a quenelle of cucumber sorbet makes for a refreshing opener. A porcini mushroom tart filled with duxelles and caviar is earthy and savory; poached Novia Scotia lobster tail with a tableside pour of a vin jaune beurre blanc is tender and flavorful. Finally, mandarin sorbet over vermouth gelee is crowned with a Campari and champagne foam for a delightful dessert.

Name: Raw Omakase
Description: There may be plenty of restaurants to choose from on busy 14th Street in Logan Circle, but it's worth going to the third level (above Takara 14) to find this new counter helmed by Chef John Yi. It's small, with room for under ten guests, and there are only two seatings nightly for this impressive omakase experience. A pan-fried tomato set over onion mayo and topped with salmon roe shares a spectacular flavor combination before a smart progression of nigiri with seasonal nods. Kinmedai is given a quick sear; Hokkaido scallop is set with yuzu and flaky salt; and salmon belly is torched for a delightful texture. Honeydew sorbet with yuzu rounds out the meal. The list of aged sake is certainly worth a perusal.

Name: Cenadou
Address: 721 Titicus Rd., North Salem, NY, 10560, USA
Description: Named after the Provençal word for “dining room,” Cenadou is warm and welcoming with crisp white walls, dark wood tables and royal blue chairs. Large windows line the room, framing views of the lush greenery just outside. In fact, this North Salem address is home to two enticing spots, with sibling La Bastide located one level down. Expect French bistro classics with a modern, Provence-inspired update, as in poached vegetables with a warm aioli emulsion or rack of lamb over a smoked eggplant purée with olive tapenade, lamb jus and herb oil. Even dessert offers a twist on tradition with baba au rhum given a tableside pour of rum as well as a dollop of Earl Grey whipped cream.

Name: PhoXotic
Address: 103 Rhode Island Ave. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
Description: It's strictly first come, first serve at this compact spot in Bloomingdale just north of the Union Market district. Some order takeout at the touch screen, while others pull up a seat at the counter and order via QR code. It's all very straightforward, as is the menu with a narrow focus on spring and summer rolls, as well as impressive pho. Chef Hai Le has a background in butchering, perhaps best seen in signatures like the Butcher’s Choice with brisket, bone-in rib and beef shank, or The Works, with an array of different cuts topped with torched bone marrow. The broth is rich and savory, and while set bowls are always a good choice, the build-your-own option is equally appealing. Order a Vietnamese iced coffee or salted lime soda to go with these skillfully made offerings.

Name: Rose Marie
Description: Rose Marie is the free-spirited little sister to Yellow Rose, the beloved Tex Mex spot in the East Village from Chef Dave Rizo and Krystiana Rizo. This Williamsburg offshoot has a more freeform groove, along with a rustic charm. Meanwhile, the menu leans contemporary American with a few Southern flourishes. It's the kind of place you'll want to drop in for a cocktail and a snack, or stay for a satisfying dinner, choosing from items such as sprouting cauliflower salad, saltine-crusted fish with Carolina Gold rice, steak tartare. A patty melt with griddled onions, Vermont cheddar, bacon and pickled green tomato and an order of crispy potatoes with mayo might just be the perfect order.

Name: Comal
Address: 116 Forsyth St., New York, NY, 10002, USA
Description: Welcome to Mexico City by way of the Lower East Side. Sporting wood tables, tile and a touch of greenery, this vintage room is where you’ll want to settle in and see where the night goes. Chef Gaz Herbert brings contemporary touches to a tight menu packed with flavor. Think al pastor but in skewer form and carefully charred. Mussel with corn custard, mil hojas potato, crab tostada with eggplant – the cooking is seasonally minded and smartly prepared. With a side of rice, the smoked half-chicken is a must-order and channels all the nostalgia of a backyard barbecue. To finish, soft serve ice cream is a cute, sweet send-off.

Name: Fish Shop
Address: 610 Water St. SW, Washington, DC, 20024, USA
Description: If the name isn't a clear sign and the location facing the waterfront doesn't give it away, one look at the sophisticated nautical decor will set you straight. The large space includes a semi-open kitchen but the patio with marina views is the place to be on warm days.The menu echoes their sister spot in Scotland with a clear focus on fish, though here it's given a Mid-Atlantic update. The Maryland crab crumpet perfectly illustrates that across-the-pond connection and is a perfect opener. The fish is sourced from the Chesapeake region and from a D.C. farming operation, and the menu presents plenty of interesting items, like sugar toads, or northern puffer fish, served whole and crispy fried. Order the Virginia peanut tiramisu for a twist on a classic.

Name: Olmo
Description: Olmo has a true neighborhood feel, where communal tables encourage new friendships, and light wood and plenty of white create a soothing ambience. The food is inspired by Mexico City with a focus on nostalgic, approachable flavors. Find everything from chicharrón preparado and eggplant milanesa to lacto-fermented crudités on this menu. There are so many winning dishes, but the grilled branzino over a bed of stewed beans with a colorful circle of morita salsa is surely one to consider. Carne asada is another can't miss, with a 12-ounce steak topped with a bright salad of verdolaga greens and shaved fennel, but it's that smoky chipotle bearnaise that steals the show. The flan paleta drizzled with caramel hits all the right notes.

Name: Tama
Address: Our Habitas AlUla, Ashar Valley, AlUla, 43511, Saudi Arabia
Description: Come here for picturesque views of the Ashar Valley and tasty Middle Eastern dishes. This modern restaurant in Our Habitas AlUla is located by a pool which overlooks an incredible landscape. The food is fitting for the setting; it is modern Middle Eastern at its core, with the use of many ingredients grown in Saudi Arabia or caught in the Red Sea, but with a gentle creative touch added in. Dishes like carrot hummus, a salad with local greens and a coffee dressing, or the feather-light vegan pavlova are real delights.

Name: Harrat
Address: Southern Reception, Banyan Tree AlUla, Ashar Valley, AlUla, 43563, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the Banyan Tree Hotel, located in the Ashar Valley, this contemporary restaurant offers one of the most scenic views of the desert. From the off, the friendly team warmly welcome you and are ready to guide you through the varied options of the menu. The Pan Arabic list of specialties include umami-packed muhammara paste served with a soft flat bread, the margoog, a generous lamb and vegetable stew made to share, and for dessert, the must-try lightly layered cake made with moringa. If you’re not staying at the hotel, just show them your restaurant reservation for smooth access.

Name: Ruhi
Address: The Zone, 7236 Al Takhassousi, Al Mohammadiyyah, Riyadh, 12362, Saudi Arabia
Description: Located in The Zone, an open-air commercial complex with different pavilions, with most of them being restaurants. This attractive one stands out with its decoration, where industrial elements are juxtaposed with traditional paintings. The eye of the diner is caught by the kitchen behind glass walls where the brigade can be seen in full swing: one chef slapping the breads inside the tandoor, another hanging the long skewers of meat in the traditional oven, or another stirring large pots of stew. The food is North Indian with special care brought to the spicing to respect the natural flavour of the produce.

Name: Hōchō
Address: Ground Floor, VIA Riyadh, Al Hada, Riyadh, 12912, Saudi Arabia
Description: It’s all about Kobe beef here. Located in the luxurious VIA Riyadh, this simple yet contemporary restaurant with a large open kitchen finds itself sitting pretty in the high-end shopping district. While Kobe beef-based dishes are the star of the menu, it also features some modern and well-crafted sushi that are worth exploring. Finish off with a date, walnut and Saudi coffee tart – a sweet delight.

Name: Karamna
Address: The Jeddah Yacht Club, 2387 Al Kurnaysh Bridge Road, Jeddah, 23613, Saudi Arabia
Description: You can dine inside, on a terrace overlooking superyachts or even on a bobbing moored boat while enjoying Lebanese classics. This modern and bright place, located in the Jeddah Yacht Club, serves up a fine selection of dips – the beetroot moutabbal is a must – tasty grills and fresh salads that come in generous portions, so be aware of that when ordering. Finish off with the baklava – it’s not to be missed.

Name: Yaza
Address: 6315 Prince Sultan Road, As Salamah, Jeddah, 23446, Saudi Arabia
Description: As you enter, you’re warmly greeted by a smiling team who offer you fresh dates and Saudi coffee, also known as gahwa. Modernity is found throughout, from the interior design to the food. Grab a cosy side seat and order from a menu filled with a mix of contemporary and classical Saudi plates, all bursting with flavour. Order Josper-grilled meats and shellfish, like their tasty roasted prawns with mint sauce, or rich, fruity lamb with Hijazi debyaza served with freshly baked bread. Finish off with their specialty dessert, their twist on a traditional Om Ali dessert.

Name: Café Boulud
Address: Ground Floor, Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh, Kingdom Centre, Olaya Street, Al Olaya, Riyadh, 11321, Saudi Arabia
Description: Chef Daniel Boulud brings his Café Boulud to the Four Seasons Hotel at the Kingdom Center. A series of elegant pastel decorated rooms including a bar, lounge and orangery make up the space. The all-encompassing menu blends creative French classics with subtle tastes of the Middle East in refined and eye-catching creations. Turophiles will appreciate the fine selection of French cheeses – they even have a cheese chef who will help you with your choices. On weekdays, make use of their good value business lunch menu, while Fridays offer a brunch menu.

Name: Tofareya
Address: Anas Ibn Malik Road, Al Malqa, Riyadh, 13522, Saudi Arabia
Description: Regional cooking of Saudi Arabia is celebrated here at this neighbourhood restaurant. The space is decorated with brightly coloured kilims around the pillars and an array of basketwork shades hanging from the ceiling. Pick up an Arabic coffee infused with cardamom from the cart as you enter. The menu includes Hasawi meat kebabs from the eastern Al-Ahsa region, the well-known Mandi rice dishes from the Aseer and Al Bahah regions in the south, and Marqooq, which is recognised as the official dish of Riyadh. Desserts, like Om Ali, are a must have.

Name: Rüya
Address: 5140 Prince Muhammad Bin Abdulaziz Road, Al Aziz, Al Sulimaniyah, Riyadh, 12243, Saudi Arabia
Description: This modern upmarket brasserie has a lovely feel to it. It’s equipped with an open kitchen and is elegantly designed with matt brass shelving full of Turkish and Middle Eastern bowls and jars, a large contemporary chandelier and a mirrored bar. The menu offers a great choice of contemporary Turkish dishes, specialising in the Anatolian region of the country. Start with a selection of hot and cold mezze style dips and plenty of Pide bread, continue with lamb dishes, kebabs or slow-cooked beef ribs, and of course, a baklava or their traditional Anatolian rice pudding to finish. Their creative mocktails are a great addition to the meal.

Name: Myazū
Address: Al Basateen Mall. Prince Mohammed Bin Abdulaziz Road, Al Rawdah, Jeddah, 23431, Saudi Arabia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Journey to Japan at this restaurant in the heart of Jeddah's city centre. The spacious eatery boasts a modern Japanese style with various seating options – sit at the counter to watch the sushi chefs in action or pick a table in the main hall or on the patio area. As for the menu, you can expect a wide selection of classics and modern interpretations – you’ll find popcorn shrimps from the tempura section, fine Wagyu kushi grilled skewers from the robata section and freshly prepared nigiri at the sushi section. Four dishes per person should suffice, with the chicken gyozas being a must-try!

Name: Niyyali
Address: Shangri-La Jeddah, Ash Shati, Corniche Road, Jeddah, 23611, Saudi Arabia
Description: Accessed via the main entrance of the shimmering Shangri-La Jeddah, with the fabulous terrace being the first thing that grabs your attention on arrival. The space is huge, with great views of the Red Sea. Inside, it’s all set around the central, traditionally styled domed oven, with a few private cabins also available. The menu is extensive, and offers an appealing mix of Lebanese dishes, some traditional, others with a modern makeover alongside numerous signature dishes. The flavours and textures are excellent, especially the kebabs. Bespoke mocktails add to the all-round experience.

Name: Maiz
Address: Al Bujairi Terrace, Diriyah, Riyadh, 13711, Saudi Arabia
Description: Nestled in historic Diriyah, known as the birthplace of Saudi Arabia, this Saudi restaurant boasts dishes originating from the country’s 13 provinces. Dishes like the lamb mantu (steamed dumplings), mandi lamb shoulder and freshly baked breads served with dips and local honey are delivered with obvious pride. To get the full experience, opt for one of their tasting menus – one offers six courses and the other has eight.

Name: Toki
Address: Leylaty, Al Malik Road, Al Khalidiyyah, Jeddah, 23422, Saudi Arabia
Description: The sultry vibe of this art deco-Shanghai inspired space is the first thing you notice as you walk in. The mocktail bar, soft lighting and pumping music add to the ambiance. The super attentive and very friendly team will guide through their extensive menu that features Peking and Cantonese classics alongside some dim sum specialities. Their lunch menu is also great value, with their mocktails crafted with equal pride. A great spot for a romantic evening.

Name: Kircherhof
Description: A 17th-century farmstead run by the same family for four generations, initially as a produce farm (fruit and vegetables) before the younger generation expanded into dining in the early 2000s. The offering, based entirely on organic, sustainably sourced ingredients, is compelling, particularly delicious, and rooted in local traditions while casting a savvy, curious eye toward the present. Dishes are colorful and very generous; the all-female service team is warm and happy to explain the house philosophy. There’s also a shop where you can stock up on treats before you leave.

Name: Capasanta
Description: Just steps from the Shrine of Our Lady of the Rosary, young, talented chef Paolo Del Giudice delights with sea-driven, modern cooking. In a minimalist, marine-inspired space, he serves vibrant, flavorful dishes grounded in contemporary technique. Don’t miss his crudo selections and the irresistible scallops wrapped in lardo with spring pea purée and buffalo stracciatella. Excellent wines and a rich selection of house cocktails round out the experience.

Name: Vincenzo Degasperi
Description: Situated in the busy heart of the town, the Zur Post hotel offers its guests a warm, homely welcome, discreet charm and Alpine elegance, while its contemporary-style wine-bar boasts a relaxed and friendly atmosphere. Here, Vincenzo Degasperi, the soul of the restaurant, oversees his guests’ experience with elegant professionalism and genuine hospitality, serving delicious Italian cuisine prepared from the best fresh ingredients. The superb wines are showcased on a skilfully chosen wine list, from which intriguing pairings are also available by the glass.

Name: UMA Roma
Description: If you’re looking for a restaurant with innovative dishes and excellent value for money, you’re in the right place. The setting is pleasant, well cared for, and features a minimalist design. Most tables offer a direct view of the open kitchen, allowing guests to watch the chefs at work. A vegetarian menu with paired wines is also available. Service is always friendly and attentive, making the dining experience even more enjoyable.

Name: The View Milano
Description: MasterChef winner Valerio Braschi has taken up residence in the heart of Milan, with views of the Duomo and the piazza, visible from the windows of the elegant dining room and, above all, from the splendid terrace (fifth floor) devoted to cocktails but also offering slightly more casual dining. The cooking is contemporary, the menu even includes dishes such as “Risotto, saffron and ossobuco” and “Costoletta alla Milanese...and then some.” Choose the full tasting menu or order à la carte; in either case, dishes are crafted with balance and completeness of flavor, starting from top-quality ingredients.

Name: Resilienza
Description: Steps from the sea, just beyond the train tracks, a spot with an all-white decor welcomes guests in style, with outdoor spaces perfect for the warmer months. In the kitchen, his son reinterprets regional traditions, balancing seafood and land-based dishes, while his mother runs the dining room with warmth and professionalism. An authentic experience combining flavor, simplicity and a relaxed atmosphere.

Name: Il Paguro
Address: Via Cala Capra, Capo d'Orso, Palau, 07020, Italy
