Description: The small bay of Cala Capra is truly romantic and exclusive. Advance reservations are advised; without one, the barrier at the top of the road down to the marina won’t be raised. Hotel Capo d’Orso, which houses the Paguro restaurant, shares the same atmosphere: with a gorgeous Mediterranean-style terrace overlooking this little slice of paradise. The food suits the setting: classic, straightforward cooking built mostly around excellent local catch. A place that’s genuinely hard to leave.

Name: Ottavi Mare
Description: In the heart of Bevagna, just steps from the picturesque Piazza Filippo Silvestri, this small, welcoming, and well-cared-for restaurant offers cuisine that blends seafood flavors with Umbrian tradition, serving balanced yet never predictable dishes. There are three tasting menus, each available in full or reduced versions, allowing for a personalized culinary journey.

Name: Osteria Giorgione da Masa
Address: Calle Larga dei Proverbi, 4582/A, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: Just steps from Campo Santi Apostoli, Chef Masa weaves together homestyle Japanese traditions with Venetian cicchetti, transcending the classic distinction between courses: here, dishes arrive all at once, without rules. For those who prefer to be guided, there’s a tasting menu offering a wide array of bites. Desserts are a true surprise, especially the yogurt, caramel, and matcha mousse, a favorite of our inspector.

Name: Mizuna Restaurant
Description: Just outside the charming village center of San Pantaleo, this is easily one of Sardinia’s best Japanese restaurants. It’s the realized dream of an Italian chef who learned the craft while working around the world and who, in a minimalist, welcoming setting, deftly prepares an array of sushi and gyoza, plus mushi-pan (steamed cakes), soups, and more. Pristine flavors are assured by the kitchen’s reliance on mostly fresh Sardinian fish. To finish, creative Italian-inspired desserts appear alongside classic oriental mochi.

Name: Mia Ristorante
Address: via Borgotufi, Castel del Giudice, 86080, Italy
Description: If you're not already in the area, plan some time to get there, traveling through a green, hilly landscape to reach Borgotufi, a "diffused hotel" spread among stone houses. In the former stables transformed into a restaurant, Marco Pasquarelli, a talented young chef, offers a modern take on various local ingredients, with a few seafood dishes as well.

Name: LeBolle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The “bubbles” promised in the name are five romantic private pods set in greenery, but you’ll also find beautiful comfort in the garden-side outdoor area and the more contemporary indoor dining room. After all, you’re inside the luxurious Boutique Hotel Stresa, and the same high standards are fully carried through. The kitchen took off with the arrival, in early 2025, of chef Salvatore Pacifico, who offers several tasting menus and an à la carte selection of modern dishes that at times reference the lake, the surrounding mountains, Campania, and also his native Puglia (especially apparent in the house-made breads). Expect balanced flavors and intentional lightness, along with harmonious presentations.

Name: Le Viste
Address: via del Falcone (spiaggia delle Viste), Portoferraio, 57037, Italy
Description: Leaving the port area, you climb toward the historic area of the Medici fortresses and then descend again along the opposite side until you reach a small beach. Here you’ll find the restaurant, charmingly and characteristically simple, right in front of the water’s edge. The cuisine is pleasantly traditional and essentially offers classic Italian seafood dishes.

Name: Il Posticino
Description: A tiny gem in the historic center, just steps from the San Michele towers. A very intimate setting, with a refined yet informal atmosphere. The cuisine? Seafood with a seasonal twist, including standouts such as the surprising Brandapolenta: creamy baccala, crispy polenta, taggiasca olive pâté. Reserving a table – especially for outdoor seating – is a must!

Name: Da Gianfranco
Address: via delle Orchidee 5, Alba Adriatica, 64011, Italy
Description: Gianfranco Verdecchia, restaurateur and heir to a family of butchers, has always cooked the food that sustained his people. After running a restaurant in Sant’Omero – a hill town known for its festival dedicated to baccalà (salt cod), a staple in the area’s cuisine – he returned to his hometown of Giulianova. Here, in a stylish, secluded space away from the sea, he has kept baccalà as the sole seafood option, devoting an entire menu to it alongside a wide selection of dishes highlighting his first love: meat.

Name: Da Rinuccio
Description: On the slopes of "a muntagna," one of the respectful nicknames for the volcano in the area, just outside the town with ample private parking, you'll find a family-oriented setting offering predominantly meat dishes, fresh pasta, and mushrooms. The dishes are carefully prepared, with generous portions, and meals are always enjoyed in a lovely glass-enclosed veranda. The wine list focuses mainly on Sicilian and particularly Catanese selections.

Name: Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto
Address: Fondamenta Madona de l'Orto, 3500, Venice, 30121, Italy
Description: Hidden within the elegant walls of the NH Collection Palazzo dei Dogi, far from the bustling tourist crowds, Da Lorenzo – Al Giardino Segreto is an oasis of taste created by Paulo Airaudo, a multi-starred Spanish chef, who is assisted in the kitchen by the young Salvatore Paladino. Every dish at this restaurant is a refined combination of culinary technique, elegance and local flavours, enhanced by sophisticated Japanese accents. To immerse themselves in his gastronomic vision, guests can choose between two evocative tasting menus: Emozioni and Sensazioni – two experiences that convey the soul of this restaurant with style.

Name: Da iumén
Address: Via Vittorio Emanuele II 26, Castelnuovo Belbo, 14043, Italy
Description: Since 1869, five generations have reinterpreted Piedmontese tradition through a modern lens. In an elegant, intimate setting, the restaurant serves dishes that fuse history and innovation – don’t miss the potato-and-hazelnut gnocchi with robiola cream. In the warmer months, reserve a table on the panoramic terrace: the view of the town hall and the hills of Castelnuovo Belbo is pure poetry.

Name: Club Morera
Description: Nestled in Mediterranean scrub just beyond the hills overlooking the coast, this rustic farmhouse welcomes guests amid centuries-old olive trees and restorative quiet. Inside, exposed stone and beams frame a relaxed yet elegant setting, with a small garden terrace perfect for summer evenings. Chef-owner Vincenzo has realized his dream here: to offer genuine hospitality and regional cooking revisited with a contemporary taste. Don’t miss the candele pasta with knife-cut Cilento ragù and goat’s cacioricotta, or the tagliolini with four tomatoes, basil, and shrimp crudo. The cellar stocks 300-plus labels to pair thoughtfully with every dish.

Name: La Bursch
Description: The Cervo Valley has its romantic refuge: La Bursch, a wonderful village tastefully converted, thanks to an entire family’s passion, into a structure dedicated to sustainable hospitality. Inside is the eponymous restaurant, guided by the very young chef Erika Gotta. In its spaces, enhanced by furniture and fabrics collected by the owners over the years, with soft lighting and very welcoming service, you breathe an almost magical atmosphere. The dishes showcase the territory’s finest ingredients in carefully prepared presentations – like the precision of the beef Wellington – beautifully presented and lightened with a modern touch.

Name: JOHANNS
Address: Via Selva dei Molini 9, Molini di Tures, 39032, Italy
Description: Tina Marcelli returns to "her" Valle Aurina, picking up where she left off in her previous regional experience: fermentation, no waste, overall sustainability, and collaboration with local farmers and producers, sometimes even family members (such as her sister and uncle). The chef indeed wants every guest to fully embrace her culinary vision, which is why she has completely renewed the tasting menu, now offered in two distinct itineraries designed to showcase territory, technique, and emotion: “About TM” is a journey into Tina’s world, available in either seven or five courses, while “La Cucina di casa” is a four-course menu that changes daily, just like in a family home. The space is intimate and contemporary, featuring large windows overlooking the mountains, and is part of a brand-new, elegant hotel aligned with the same modernity. The chef herself presents some of the dishes, supported by a young and enthusiastic staff providing attentive service.

Name: Majorelle
Description: Named after the vibrant botanical garden in Marrakesh, this Moroccan restaurant, set in an impressive five-storey building boasting a balconied frontage, certainly won’t disappoint. All the Moroccan greats are here, from pastilla and briouats to zaalouk and tajines, and Chef Saad imports his spices directly, so his dishes burst with authentic combinations of spicy and sweet. Sharing is a given, but maybe not when it comes to the delicious jawhara (crisp layered pastry filled with orange blossom cream). The fresh mint tea is a must-try, delivered by a warm, friendly team.

Name: Dereszla Bisztró
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: There are few places more relaxing to dine than on the stepped riverside terrace of this modern wood and glass building located in the heart of wine country. Szabó and his front-of-house team warmly welcome you in, while his brother Bém works behind the scenes in the kitchen preparing a concise menu of modern Hungarian dishes. Good quality produce comes from their carefully selected suppliers, whether that’s local Mangalitsa or trout from Lillafüred, which could arrive served ‘kárpáti’ style with a creamy fish bone sauce. Considering the location, a Tokaj wine is the natural accompaniment.

Name: Víg Molnár Csárda
Description: This traditional-looking tavern comes with plenty of character and is certainly a hit with the locals. There’s a rustic, slightly Mediterranean feel to the décor, which works well with its location near the lake, but the best place to sit is on the large terrace beside the working water wheel. Fairly priced, hearty Hungarian classics are the order of the day, with the meat-stuffed pancakes a speciality. Children have their own menu too, and you’ll be well looked after by the friendly owners and their team. It’s a place for every occasion, so can get very busy at peak times.

Name: Padi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: If wine’s your thing, you can’t go wrong with a visit to this striking hillside building in the heart of wine country. You must open, of course, with one of their own Sauska wines in the smart bar, before heading through to the sleek restaurant whose wonderful terrace offers views over the vines below. There’s a small à la carte of refined, eye-catching dishes as well as two tasting menus on offer, one themed around Tokaj itself – choose this option along with their local wine recommendations to fully immerse yourself in the region. To really complete the experience, ask for a peek into their winery below.

Name: Végállomás Bistro&Wine
Description: It might be tucked away in the suburbs, but this neighbourhood bistro is so highly regarded that plenty of people come from further afield. The cosy terrace has its own wooden bar, and the split-level interior has a relaxed, traditional feel. The ever-evolving menu of seasonal dishes offers something for everyone, and the lunchtime options are great value; keep an eye out for the Bird’s milk and orange egg white foam dessert.

Name: Tiszavirág
Description: A recently restored Victorian townhouse that was formerly home to a goldsmith’s now plays host to this smart restaurant. Start with a drink in the cosy bar before enjoying boldly flavoured dishes that come with a refined look but a traditional Hungarian heart, such as Mangalitsa fillet with gnudi and cottage cheese. In warmer weather, these are best enjoyed in the enclosed courtyard, along with a bottle or two from the proudly Hungarian wine list. Service is smooth and eager to please, and comes together with elegant bedrooms and a mini spa in the basement to help create a charming picture.

Name: Csopaki Resti
Description: There’s no denying that a meal at Csopaki Resti provides something a little different, as this tiny restaurant comprises just six seats and sits within the old village railway station. Because of its compact size, every diner can watch the chefs preparing the dishes in the on-view kitchen, but the four counter seats are undeniably the best place to be; wherever you sit, the chefs will serve you personally. The multi-course set menu takes on a refreshingly modern approach, while still keeping traditional Hungarian flavours to the fore.

Name: Szaletly
Description: Whether you’re after a drink, a snack or a full meal, this neighbourhood spot is for you if you’re after a laid-back vibe. It’s a spacious place, with a large terrace-cum-garden to boot, but the efficient team cope well with the numbers. Dishes offer a diverse range of influences, but there’s always a Hungarian vein running through their hearts. The tasting menus with matching wines are worth ordering, the gödöllő chicken breast is delicious and, for dessert, it has to be the esterházy. You can even buy a post-dessert ice cream for the way home.

Name: Natura Hill
Description: It’s all in the name at this sustainably led restaurant. The climb up the steep, narrow lane to the two-hectare estate results in breathtaking Danube Bend views, which become all the more special at sunset. The kitchen follows a ‘slow food’ ethos; ingredients from their nearby farm and the local area underpin the cooking, and menus evolve twice a day as new produce arrives. Dishes are fresh, unfussy and vibrantly flavoured – come for the ‘Spontaneous Bistro Lunch’ or the tasting menu at dinner. An overnight stay is a must, with the holistic experience also including a sauna and wellness centre.

Name: Fausto's
Description: The super-elegant Fausto’s might not have been open in this location all that long, but it’s owner, Chef Fausto Di Vora, can proudly claim over 30 successful years in the city. Following a move from Pest to Buda, his rebirthed restaurant remains as personally and professionally run as ever, but now with an added vigour. The glass-enclosed terrace is a great spot to enjoy Italian dishes such as shrimps with butternut squash and vegetable vinaigrette, whose presentation is a match for the wonderful surroundings. This is certainly a place to sit back, relax and let la dolce vita run through your soul.

Name: Spago by Wolfgang Puck
Address: Matild Palace Hotel, Váci utca 36, Budapest, 1056, Hungary
Description: The Matild Palace Hotel – one of a pair of matching belle époque palaces bult by the Archduchess of Austria – is a grand building in a stunning setting beside the Elizabeth Bridge. It’s fitting then, that it’s home to a smart restaurant run by an Austrian Chef. Wolfgang Puck’s fun dining concept brings something a little different to Budapest’s culinary scene, with a selection of appealing, well-executed dishes that draw their inspiration from across the world. From Hungarian buffalo steak tartare and Austrian wiener schnitzel to scallop pad thai and some delicious pastas, everything is here.

Name: Sauska 48
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Find a table on the spacious terrace of this modern winery to enjoy wonderful views out across the vineyard and the hills; on a warm summer’s day, it doesn’t get much better than this. The well-curated wine list covers Hungary and Europe, and includes reds and rosés from the vines you see in front of you, as well as whites from the owners’ other winery in Tokaj. The concise selection of contemporary dishes take their inspiration from the Hungarian kitchen but exhibit a level of refined creativity. The passionate team will share their knowledge to help you find the perfect wine match.

Name: UMO
Address: Monastery Boutique Hotel Budapest, Ponty utca 1, Budapest, 1011, Hungary
Description: Housed within a boutique hotel, Umo comprises two parts: a contemporary brasserie in the atrium, and an enclosed courtyard towards the back of the building. The latter was formerly a monastery and is a wonderful place to sit – it even comes complete with an open kitchen where dishes are cooked over flames and smoke. Menus showcase the best of Latin American flavours, with everything from ceviches and a baja shrimp cocktail to a selection of fire-cooked meats and some delicious churros. A fine range of gins is on offer alongside the in-depth wine list, and the super-friendly team bring the whole experience together.

Name: Zelna Borbisztró
Description: A smart, modern wine bar in the livelier part of this seasonal town, Zelna is named after the wine company whose biodynamic wines it serves – and also offers for purchase. This is a place to kick back and relax, and the small menu mixes light bites with more substantial Hungarian dishes so you can tailor-make your own experience – the beef cheeks are a hit and be sure to save room for the golden walnut dumplings for dessert! Every table is located on the large terrace, which stays open until 2am.

Name: Petrányi Csopak
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: If you’re looking to immerse yourself in a traditional Hungarian experience, then head straight for Petrányi Csopak. Perched high on the hillside, this period house sits within the sloping Petrányi Pince vineyard and affords lovely views out over the countryside and towards Lake Balaton in the middle distance. The menu offers a range of dishes that are inspired by the traditional home-cooked meals of the past – the kind of dishes that most Hungarian households have their own family recipes for, such as soups, stews and ragouts. The salmon trout with leek, potato, béchamel and lemon is a great way to start.

Name: Alelí
Address: Dorothea Hotel, Wekerle Sándor utca 3, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description: Romance is in the air at this elegant, high-ceilinged restaurant inside the Dorothea Hotel in the heart of Budapest. Start with a classic cocktail in the chic bar, then move on to Italian favourites, from delicious focaccias and salads dressed at the table to freshly made pizzas, pastas and risottos. The spaghetti cacio e pepe is not to be missed, and the tiramisu is large enough to share. Much of the produce is imported from Italy and the authentic flavours shine through. Service is friendly and professional, with the staff keen to recommend both dishes and wines.

Name: Cut & Barrel
Description: Set away from the city centre in the old Goldberger textile factory, this lovely warehouse conversion comprises a wine shop, an impressive bar, a large dining room with a terrace and a smaller anteroom offering counter dining. The stunning shop comes complete with an incredible selection of wines from around the country – including from the owner’s vineyard (Haraszthy Wines in Etyek) – as well as a Harley Davidson, a Porsche and a Rolls Royce. The food has a strong Latin American base but it’s their own charcuterie and succulent steaks from the Josper grill that lead the way.

Name: LAMAREDA
Description: Located in the pedestrianised streets of the beautiful baroque city of Győr, this long-standing restaurant fits in perfectly thanks to its traditional, low-key elegance. Head past the bistro area at the front to the bright room behind, where they serve a menu which mixes Hungarian, Mediterranean and even some subtle Thai influences. The bright, vibrant dishes come in generous portions, with well-judged flavours – be sure to save room for a comforting dessert such as the gundel or zsabo pancakes. The smart pavement terrace is a hit come summer.

Name: Hosszú Tányér
Description: This romantic little restaurant sits in an attractive courtyard setting and is keenly run by its hands-on owner Franciska. Nothing is too much trouble for her when it comes to her guests, who she encourages to relax and fully appreciate the experience. The five-course tasting menu comes with plenty of little extras and the flavour-packed dishes are truly beautiful to look at – with flavours to match. In an all-encompassing experience, the contemporary artwork on the walls changes every two months along with the menu – and the ceramic dishes are specially designed by the chef himself.

Name: MÁK restaurant
Description: Rustic charm abounds at this laid-back restaurant, from the décor to the vaulted brick ceiling. Seasonality is key here and Chef János takes time to visit his small, artisan suppliers personally. His travels inform the interesting set menu (go for the longer version), with vegetables treated as reverently as meat and fish, and curing, pickling and ageing all playing their part. Knowledgably prepared, consummately seasoned dishes have a delicate touch and could include grey catfish with buckwheat or duck with celery and pine. The unobtrusive, expertly paced service is spot-on too.

Name: BiBo Budapest
Address: Dorothea Hotel, Apáczai Csere János utca 11, 7th Floor, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description: Take the dedicated lift up to the seventh floor of the Dorothea Hotel and you’ll be warmly greeted with magical views across the river towards Budapest Castle. Start with one of their signature cocktails on the terrace to take it all in, then choose from a menu that fuses Hungary and Spain with aplomb. From rock prawn tempura to their signature ‘Garcia’ burgers or chicken stuffed with morels – as well as dishes to share – everything is generously proportioned and expertly delivered. Providing a perfect match is a wine list that favours, you may have guessed it, Hungary and Spain.

Name: Bilanx
Description: Located in an old townhouse midway between the Széchenyi Chain Bridge and St. Stephen's Basilica, Bilanx takes a fresh, modern approach to dining out. Its interior is sparsely decorated, with varnished wooden chairs set at white-tile-topped tables, while neon light strips create glowing archways above and pop music plays through the speakers. The chef offers a tasting menu which combines his two loves – Hungarian produce and classical French techniques, so you’ll find dishes like Mangalitsa pork with choron sauce and parsley root cream. There’s also an interesting three-course menu available at lunch.

Name: Arany Kaviár
Description: As its name implies, caviar plays a starring role here, with a range of almost 20 Hungarian and Siberian options on offer, as well as two different caviar tasting experiences. French and Russian influences guide the cooking, with the à la carte featuring a selection of dishes which have appeared on the menu since their opening under the heading 'Since 1990', and the tasting menu showcasing the chef's favourite creations. Sit in the opulent, richly appointed dining room or the more modern extension which opens out onto the garden – or book the Chef’s Table to really get in on the action.

Name: Alkimista Kulináris Műhely
Description: Its name means ‘Culinary Workshop’ but that feels like doing it an injustice, as this is a beautiful, elegant spot. It's hidden away behind locked gates in a city centre courtyard and everyone is greeted at 7pm by the infectiously enthusiastic chef-owner. Seasonal ingredients feature on a highly personalised tasting menu which cleverly blends the old and the new. Flavours are memorable, sauces are a highlight and the chef describes every dish with heartfelt passion. The price also includes a carefully curated selection of drinks featuring many local biodynamic and organic wines.

Name: Zincenco Kitchen
Description: Offering something a little different, this restaurant is located within a residential apartment, but there’s certainly nothing amateurish or domestic about it; it's even licensed. There are six tables – for a maximum of 14 diners – and all guests are asked to arrive at 7pm, which helps contribute to the supper party atmosphere. You ring doorbell 31 and are greeted by your host Igor Zincenco and his team, who go on to fully explain each well-balanced, satisfying dish which features on a modern surprise menu inspired by Hungarian classics. Do opt for one of the two well-chosen wine pairings.

Name: Graefl Major Kétútköz
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: 25 acres of gardens and grounds surround this wonderfully restored art nouveau mansion house – and it is here that they grow, raise and rear all of the produce that is served in the dining room. If it’s in season, you will find it on the menu, from an incredible array of fruit and vegetables to game. They cure their own meats, use their own wheat for the bread, and their beer is an artisan brew. You can also stay overnight in this gloriously peaceful spot.

Name: Neked Főztem
Description: This inviting roadside pub sits in an elevated spot and is fronted by a pleasant terrace. Inside it’s warm and welcoming with a rustic feel – thanks to a log burner crackling away on colder nights. Its name translates as ‘I cooked for you’. The concise menu lists all things Hungarian and the friendly team are happy to talk you through it and offer suggestions. The gutsy home-cooking has plenty of flavour and can be paired with a selection of local wines.

Name: St. Andrea Restaurant
Description: This stylish bar-cum-restaurant is owned by a small boutique winery and the creative dishes are designed to match their wines – some of which aren’t sold anywhere else in the world! The evening sees an à la carte menu that appeals to all, while during the day there’s a great value set lunch that’s a hit with the business community. Dishes are refined and well-presented, with a mix of local and international flavours; you might find salmon trout with blueberries and goat's cheese or Mangalitsa shoulder with butternut squash and peach. For the full experience, go for the 'Made in Hungary' chef’s menu.

Name: Botanica
Address: Hotel Botanica, Nyárfa utca 57, Dánszentmiklós, 2735, Hungary
Description: Lovely gardens surround this delightful, family-owned country house, which comes with bespoke designer bedrooms and charming service. Start with a drink in one of the comfortable lounges before heading through to the elegant restaurant, where a spot on the terrace is a must in summer. The multi-course menu showcases refined, modern creations in dishes which pay tribute to the locality, as well as the chef’s Swabian roots. Both wine and non-alcoholic drinks pairings are on offer, along with fermented beverages crafted from local fruits and vegetables.

Name: KOLLÁZS
Address: Four Seasons Hotel Gresham Palace, Széchenyi István tér 5, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description: The Four Seasons Gresham Palace hotel is a beautiful art nouveau building which was constructed in 1906 for the Gresham Life Assurance Company. Set in the heart of Budapest, directly opposite the Széchenyi Chain Bridge, its restaurant makes the perfect place to dine when visiting the city. The relaxed, cosy atmosphere is matched perfectly by a menu of familiar French brasserie classics, with a few Hungarian dishes thrown in. The steak tartare is made at the table, the roast chicken for two is carved in front of you and the rum baba is a hit.

Name: NOON
Address: Lua Resort, Anna Sétány 3, Balatonfüred, 8230, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An exclusive lakeside resort plays host to this elegant restaurant (if you’re not staying the night, then pre-booking is essential in high season). Grab a cocktail in the stylish bar before enjoying a carefully curated selection of contemporary Hungarian dishes which fuse tradition with inventive modern touches. Local wines are a feature, and the smooth service shows the team’s knowledge and care. If the chocolate and cherry dessert is on the menu, be sure to choose it.

Name: Costes Downtown
Address: Prestige Hotel, Vigyázó Ferenc utca 5, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
Description: 2025 sees Costes Downtown celebrate its 10th anniversary. Located on the ground floor of the Prestige Hotel, this stylish restaurant features a striking interior with a living wall and ceiling that bring nature indoors. Ask for one of the cosy booths or book the chef’s table for a close-up view of the action in the open kitchen. The set-priced lunch and dinner menus are joined by a tasting option at dinner, with the visually impressive dishes seeing Hungarian favourites reinterpreted in an elaborate modern manner.

Name: Tihanyi Vinarius
Description: Take in lovely views over the countryside and the lake from the terrace of this charming thatched building dating from 1822. The interior is full of historic character – it even boasts a hidden vaulted brick-built room which is used for private events – and the formal service suits the style of the place. Some unusual and rarely seen ingredients feature in well-crafted dishes; Tihany is famous for its lavender, so the ‘vinarius 200 tortaszelet’ dessert is a must.

Name: Teyföl
Description: Owners Brigi and Bence have created what they feel is their perfect restaurant in Teyföl, whose name translates as ‘sour cream’ – an ingredient used frequently in Hungarian cuisine. The restaurant sits within a characterful period building on a narrow cobbled street in the Old Town, and its bright, modern bistro-style interior provides a complete contrast. Multiple flavours, textures and colours come together in classically based dishes with a well-restrained level of creativity, such as confit chicken pancakes or a gypsy-style roast.

Name: VIRTU
Address: MOL Campus, Dombóvári utca 28, Budapest, 1117, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Located on the 28th floor of the tallest building in Budapest, the MOL Campus, VIRTU affords stunning views out over this historic city and the River Danube. Start with cocktails in the smart bar, then head through to the spacious, two-roomed restaurant. The menu offers something for everyone, with a pleasing mix of modern and classical dishes. If it’s available, the Keszthely sturgeon with orda cheese gnocchi and champagne sauce is delicious – and ensure you finish with the strikingly modern somlói trifle. A fine selection of wines and professional service from a caring team complete the picture.

Name: Stand25 Bisztró
Description: There’s always a contented buzz to this neighbourhood bistro on the Buda side of the Danube. It’s owned by the same team as Stand, so their ethos around quality is the same, and you’ll be looked after by a slick team. Cooking focuses on Hungarian classics with a Mediterranean edge and, while dishes are hearty with robust flavours, they also have a refined edge.

Name: Rutin
Description: Three hours pass in a flash at this intimate little restaurant, which is proudly run by a friendly couple. Dinner starts at 7pm, with Fanni welcoming guests and looking after their every need. Dávid, meanwhile, is behind the scenes preparing a very personalised 10-course set menu that combines classic Hungarian favourites with family recipes and his childhood memories. Dishes have a feel-good factor, from fried bread drizzled with bacon fat followed by mama’s grilled chicken to an isler sponge cake – and Dávid tells their story to the room as he brings them out of the kitchen or finishes them at the table.

Name: Hoppá! Bistro
Description: This contemporary eatery stands out amongst the myriad choices on vibrant Október Street, both for its smooth service and its modern, well-presented cooking – and it's certainly a popular spot. The menu sees traditional Hungarian recipes brought up-to-date, and there’s a range of daily specials and an excellent value lunch menu on offer too. You might find smoked catfish with onions and sesame seeds, followed by veal with bread dumplings and sage, then, for dessert, crème brûlée accompanied by seasonal fruit. Local beers and wines complete the picture.

Name: Onyx
Description: Pinpointing the Onyx experience can be a challenging task, as this is a place that undergoes constant evolution in the pursuit of self-improvement. What can be said, is that you will be part of a truly immersive experience, as you arrive at the same time as your fellow guests, ready to share a memorable evening together. The communal experience is a stimulating, sensory and provocative one, that uses a multi-course tasting menu to showcase the development of food in the past, present and future. Without giving too much away, your night here will include light, sound, capes and contemplation!

Name: Nobu Budapest
Address: Kempinski Hotel Corvinus Budapest, Erzsébet tér 7-8, Budapest, 1051, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
Description: Wherever you hail from, there’s a high chance you’ll have heard of Nobu, as the group’s restaurants now span the globe. At the Budapest branch – which sits inside a chic hotel – you’ll find a stylish, minimalist aesthetic that takes in wooden tables, fretwork screens and Japanese lanterns. The extensive menu follows the usual Nobu format, with a wide range of sushi and both hot and cold Nobu classics (such as miso black cod or yellowtail tartare with caviar), and there’s also a section dedicated to Wagyu beef. Bento boxes are available at lunch and there’s an omakase on offer for the undecided.

Name: Lokal at the Lake
Description: It’s all in the name. Set in a small village on the southern banks of Lake Balaton, just a stone’s throw from the water, this intimate bistro follows a purely local ethos. From the fixtures and fittings to the furnishings and the food, everything you see has been produced in the region. The rustic small plates have a fittingly traditional Hungarian heart and come with bold flavours – you might find green pea soup with goat’s cheese and mint, followed by rabbit with vegetable sauce and bread pudding. Choose four per person or opt for the excellent value Chef’s Menu of current kitchen favourites.

Name: Zazie Bistro
Address: MOL Campus, Dombóvári utca 28, Budapest, 1117, Hungary
Description: Zazie Bistro sits within the tallest skyscraper in Budapest, the MOL Campus, and offers some great views out over the city. It’s a spacious place that incorporates a large open restaurant, a terrace and even a café. The chef brings with him plenty of experience, which shines through in the well-executed, classically inspired, rustic dishes. These could include chilled fruit soups in the summer, or a top-class schnitzel with deliciously creamy potato salad – with the potatoes supplied by the chef’s brother-in-law. There’s also a great value business lunch on offer.

Name: Villa Kabala
Description: Perched high up the hillside in the Badacsony region, with far reaching views of Lake Balaton, this period villa was once home to artist István Farkas. Now under the ownership of an ambitious and enthusiastic couple, the team here are establishing it as something of a destination restaurant. A concise lunch offering is followed by a well-balanced tasting menu – you won’t get much more local than this, with the cheese, salami, sausages, beers and wines all family made. They even have their own coffee roaster and pottery workshop too. Book a bedroom with a terrace and look forward to a fantastic breakfast.

Name: IKON
Description: Set on a main street in the heart of the city, IKON stands out among the other eateries for its smart look, structured service and confident cooking. The chef spent time working in England and his dishes are an intriguing mix of reworked Hungarian classics and some British influences – go for something from the ‘Traditions Reborn’ section and be sure not to miss dessert. For a more immersive experience, book the chic Kitchen Table.

Name: FELIX Kitchen & Bar
Description: FELIX Kitchen & Bar sits behind the breathtaking neo-renaissance façade of the Várkert Kioszk, a building whose original function was to pump water to the Royal Palace. Today, along with a gallery, it’s now home to this plush restaurant boasting a stunningly restored ceiling and an air-conditioned terrace. While maintaining a certain air of elegance that’s suited to the historic building, it takes on something of a Mediterranean vibe, serving an extensive range of dishes that covers everything from carpaccios and risottos to mezze plates and lobster to share.

Name: GÓRÉ
Description: A góré is a barn used to dry cereals, and that was this sleek restaurant’s former function – although it's hard to imagine that following its chic refurbishment. Climb the stairs to the raised dining area beneath the beams to enjoy the view out through the floor-to-ceiling windows; alternatively, enjoy an al fresco experience on the covered terrace. The heart of the menu has strong classical foundations, but unique additions offer innovation and originality, with fermentation techniques featuring highly. The restaurant is remotely set in a sleepy village, so the comfy bedrooms are a real bonus.

Name: Tati
Description: The owners of this restaurant in up-and-coming District 7 also have a farm in Biatorbágy, on the outskirts of the city, where they grow their own fruit and veg. Menus comprise a mix of meat, fish and plant-based combinations, and the use of traditional Hungarian recipes results in hearty, wholesome cooking. There’s a natural feel to both the appearance and the flavour of the dishes, as well as to the accompanying natural, biodynamic and organic wines, which are sourced from vineyards in close proximity to the city.

Name: Talu
Address: Andrássy Kúria & Spa, Fő út 94, Tarcal, 3915, Hungary
Description: The Andrássy Kúria & Spa hotel sits within a 200-year-old manor house once used as a hunting lodge by the Andrássy family, and the warmly run talu restaurant occupies its impressive vaulted cellar – as well as spilling out onto its terrace in the warmer months. The chef reinterprets traditional regional and family recipes to create modern versions of old favourites, with Hungarian produce such as Mangalitsa pork kept to the fore. Local Tokaj wines are also a draw, with many available by the glass; a stay one of their bedrooms provides the perfect excuse to sample more than one!

Name: Horgonyzó Kisvendéglő
Description: Simplicity leads the way at this endearing restaurant set just a short stroll from the River Tisza. The room has an unfussy lodge style and there’s plenty of outdoor space courtesy of both a front and rear terrace. Cooking is fresh and well-executed, and offers something for everyone, from Hungarian classics to pizzas, burgers and street food. The wood-fired oven plays a key role, and everything is prepared with love and care.

Name: A Konyhám Stúdió 365
Description: Take the lift to the 3rd floor of the Balaton Üzletház shopping mall and you’ll find this bright restaurant with a smart interior and a partial view over the lake. Chef and well-known personality, Gabriella Szikra – kitted out in her trademark cap – has a genuine desire to please, and her modern Hungarian dishes come with bold flavours and arty presentation. Be sure to go for the excellent local wine pairings.

Name: 67 Sigma Restaurant
Description: Start with a stroll around the pretty Old Town, then head to this historic property tucked away on a cobbled street; you enter via an enclosed courtyard and terrace, into a smart restaurant with plenty of atmosphere. Good quality produce is used to create fresh, flavoursome Hungarian dishes in a modern style. Courteous service comes from a local team.

Name: MoszkvaTéЯ Bisztró
Address: Monastery Boutique Hotel, Fő utca 30, Budapest, 1011, Hungary
Description: The younger sibling of Arany Kaviár sits on the ground floor of a characterful hotel that was once a monastery. The cuisine here, too, has a Russian theme, with plenty of favourites such as chicken Kiev and some delicious pelmeni (dumplings). The young team are bright and friendly, and a concise list of Hungarian wines completes the picture.

Name: Avalon Ristorante
Address: H3519 Miskolctapolca, Iglói utca 15, Miskolc, 3519, Hungary
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Expectation builds as you follow the winding road that leads up to the Avalon Resort & SPA hotel in the Bükk Mountains. A village unto itself, it’s a family friendly place – and the restaurant’s menu reflects this. There’s something for everyone here, from pizzas and pastas to Wagyu cooked on the Josper grill, while the wine list offers a great selection to accompany your meal. Sit in the stylish bar beside the open kitchen or head through further into the conservatory.

Name: Textúra
Description: Set almost opposite its sister restaurant, Borkonyha Winekitchen, is this stylish, design-led brasserie with a relaxed atmosphere, a living wall of moss and a central wooden ‘tree’. Seasonally led dishes are ambitious and creative, and there are some real gems from Hungary on the wine list.

Name: Il Gattopardo
Description: Il Gattopardo is a charismatic Italian restaurant that possesses a certain je-ne-sais-quoi. The chef personally comes to your table to present his signature Sicilian dishes, which he continuously revamps with exciting new takes – for instance, crème brûlée made with butter-soft octopus alongside an exquisite potato cream enhanced with seaweed. He is meticulous both when crafting intricate sauces and filling home-made ravioli with gorgonzola. Be sure to peruse the wine list, which features a tempting array of fine Italian wines.

Name: Tres
Description: Descending into Michael and Emy's intriguing cellar is the start of a special adventure. Tres is raw and pure, vintage and warm. As soon as you enter, you are presented with products from local artisans, mostly sourced from within a 30-kilometre radius. At the expansive dining counter, you will be fascinated by the inventiveness of the self-taught chef. The freshness of fermentations, the depth of garums, the complexity of maturations, the creativity with which products are used in their entirety, processing with the latest techniques... For example, the chef glazes dry-aged turbot with yeast and combines it with pickled wasabi and a dashi with horseradish and garum. A tribute to the seasons that will surprise you more than once!

In this cheerful restaurant, the open design and abundant natural light set a relaxed scene. Wine recommendations come courtesy of hostess Saskia, who brings both enthusiasm and expertise to the table. Her astute pairings elevate chef Rik's creative, internationally inspired dishes to new heights. He keeps things simple, concentrating on three or four elements that enhance each other's intensity. For example, tub gurnard perfectly seared on the skin, set on a bed of fregola with a subtle kick of harissa and served with a tangy orange cream and a full-bodied yet airy smoked herring sauce. This clear style of cooking never fails to impress.

Name: Robuust
Description: This warm and welcoming restaurant is run by two larger-than-life brothers: chef Raimon and maître d' Peter Ian. You can look forward to dishes brimming with distinctive flavours, as in the finely spiced beurre blanc that lends a touch of indulgence to a perfectly fried slice of cod. Such culinary excellence characterises their classic fare as well as the more creative set menu. Be sure to ask your expert host for his beer recommendations – he has some real gems up his sleeve!

Name: Concours
Description: Located on Utrecht's Biltstraat, this stylish restaurant is in keeping with its lively and inviting surroundings. Alex Zeelenberg likes to keep the courses of his set menu a secret right up until they are served, and they never fail to impress. Whether he is spicing up a pan-fried pink duck breast with a harissa-infused poultry stock, seasoning a lentil beignet with Middle Eastern spices or incorporating the sweet earthiness of beetroot into a dessert, his creativity will take your taste buds on a voyage. Their commitment to sustainability, both in the dishes and the overall dining experience, is an added bonus.

Name: Kale & de Bril
Description: Be careful not to walk right past this unassuming building – you'd be missing out. Chef-patron duo Marc ("the bald one" or "Kale" in Dutch!) and Niek ("the one with glasses" – "de Bril" in Dutch) immediately set a relaxed, welcoming tone. Zeeland produce (also from the lobster tank) and vegetables prepared in a multitude of ways are showcased in creative dishes. For example, scallops are combined with various salsify and pear creations, as well as a lobster salpicon and a vanilla-infused broth. In both the set menu and the lobster menu, the seasons and the Zeeland terroir are the stars of the show.

Name: Bistro Sophie
Description: Don't let the name fool you; this is an upscale restaurant with a stylish interior that features vintage decor and natural materials. Working in an open kitchen, Dejan Gavric is clearly keeping up with the times. He is a chef who likes to incorporate Mediterranean influences and techniques. This is evident in the dish comprising pan-fried sea bass fillet with mussels and sea lavender and featuring a variety of garnishes. The wine list, while not too extensive, is international, well curated and great value for money.

Name: Oesterbeurs
Description: Lobster, oysters, sea lavender and mussels are just some of the Zeeland delicacies served in this restaurant which is decorated in warmly gilded tones. More than 80% of the dishes served here are fish based, with a richly flavoured classic bouillabaisse featuring on the menu alongside more creative fare. A true ode to Zeeland.

Name: Hendrik van Maurick
Description: A visit to this medieval castle (1257) is an experience in itself. The wooded surroundings, the drawbridge, the courtyard… This is a truly romantic setting, further elevated by a gorgeous terrace overlooking the moat. Inside, all that historical character meets with modern comfort. The imposing fireplace and the portrait of the knight Van Maurick holding a smartphone immediately catch the eye. The menu may seem classical at first glance, but it features inventive dishes in which Dutch produce is given a French twist. Think North Sea crab salad with cucumber sorbet and jus, celery oil, pickled daikon and wakame. This is sophisticated, vibrant and ambitious cuisine!

Name: Maes, Cuisine du Terroir
Cuisine: Seasonal Cuisine, Cuisine from the Marches
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Fifty kilometres upstream and downstream along the Meuse River is the area where this terroir cuisine sources its ingredients. This is an ode to Limburg products that are given every opportunity to shine. Whether the chefs are giving langoustines a boost with a “Limburg” bouillabaisse or accompanying local lamb with oriental seasonings such as a pastilla of lamb neck with spices, you can expect refined dishes with lively and cosmopolitan nuances that accentuate the local richness. The beautiful surroundings also shine on the wonderful terrace, where you can look out over the wooded surroundings of the Van Oys luxury hotel, to which this luminous restaurant belongs.

Name: Reverie
Description: United by a shared passion, Stuart and Luca, who met at hotel school, have turned their dream into reality with this sleek, intimate and rather minimalist restaurant. The bonsai tree in the middle of the dining space is a nod to the Far Eastern-inspired cuisine they serve. In the evening, they propose two set menus: "Taste of Reverie" and "Indonesian Menu". Drawing on classic French foundations, they add the sweetness and piquancy of Asian seasonings. The perfectly pan-seared duck fillet is accompanied, for instance, by an intense duck jus infused with the heat and slight sweetness of finely chopped chilli. A pumpkin cream married with ginger brings out the umami flavours. A vibrant and ambitious place.

Name: MEI
Description: (MEI opened the pop-up Dichtbij MEI at its familiar address in 2026) In the exceptionally charming centre of Amersfoort, this restaurant offers a relaxed and intimate dining experience complete with warm hospitality and astute wine recommendations. Ingeborgh Blok leads the front-of-house team with effortless grace while Marco gets on with creating dishes that showcase local ingredients with his intuitive approach. Vegetables, herbs and infusions dominate, with fish or meat making occasional appearances. Highlights include with vibrantly presented aubergine and a delicately acidic tomato and chamomile broth, or morel ravioli with subtly salty black olives. MEI is all about simplicity and depth.

Name: Céline
Description: The austere appearance of Fort Jutphaas is in marked contrast to the restaurant it houses, which boasts an intimate atmosphere with subdued lighting and cosy terrace. Chef Rick works principally with Dutch produce, such as Dutch yellowtail, which he likes to season with subtle Asian flavours. This is original and modern cuisine, in which vegetables take pride of place. In fact, why not opt for the appealing vegetarian set menu?

Name: Boompjes Restaurant
Cuisine: Country cooking, Cuisine from the Marches
Description: As you enter, you pass the brasserie, where you can enjoy a casual lunch or snack. The space at the rear of the restaurant is like an oasis, with trees, plants and wood setting the tone. The terrace seamlessly merges with chef Jaap Volman's kitchen garden. An ambassador of Dutch cuisine, his cooking style is very much French-inspired, but his creative use of vegetables and fruit adds lightness and freshness . The velvety consommé with its subtle acidity accompanying the succulent pork cheeks was just as delightful as the vibrant medley of garden-fresh vegetables and herbs. What a way to showcase Dutch produce!

Name: Restaurant De Hoefslag by Mark Minkman
Description: The cosy atmosphere at Restaurant De Hoefslag envelopes you in its warm embrace. Views of the garden, where vegetables and vines grow, contributes to this, as do the attentive service and the pared-down cuisine. The menu features both classic dishes and more sophisticated options. Whether it's the game jus to accompany the venison fillet or the beurre blanc to go with the catch of the day, this chef knows the importance of a good sauce and takes care to present visually appealing plates.

Name: De Knip
Description: Tables on the sunny terrace and in the conservatory are much in demand at this long-established restaurant. The view of the shimmering Vliet canal is breathtaking! Marcel van Teijlingen's culinary creations are a testament to his attention to detail and refined palate, both in their presentation and their flavour profiles. He likes to add playful touches to his dishes, which are classic in their foundations. Think celeriac mousse finished with onion and a ponzu oil, adding vibrancy to a rich millefeuille of celeriac and oxtail. The old and the new join forces at De Knip.

Name: De Watermolen
Description: This watermill, which is over 600 years old, is without a doubt the star attraction of this charming restaurant. Both the warm and welcoming interior and the secluded terrace are popular. Ramon Klaassen takes great pride in his work, which you cannot fail to notice during his interactions with diners. His unique take on classic dishes never disappoints. For example he rolls up soft-boiled duck ham and fills it with a rich poultry mousse. Playful garnishes such as an onion chutney with nuts and reduced balsamic vinegar add that little something extra. The set menu (with options) is a hit – even for those who do not eat meat or fish.

Name: La nouvelle Auberge
Description: This intimate restaurant could easily be called an inn 2.0. Be sure to ask for a table in the chic conservatory to fully enjoy the green surroundings. Fans of rich dishes will be right at home here. The chef works with local delicacies, cooks according to French tradition and pays attention to global influences. He charms with a saignant piece of beef with a powerful gravy and surprises with a dessert featuring red cabbage, ruby ice cream, pear, vanilla and red wine vinegar. The young team brings it all to the table with flair and creates a fresh dynamic.

Name: Infini
Description: Modern art meets rustic elements such as the terracotta-colour tiles and exposed beams in the stylish interior of this elegant villa. The verdant terrace is one of the prettiest in South Limburg! Hostess Kirsten greets diners with a warm welcome while chef Michael lets his take on contemporary French cuisine do the talking. Each dish is meticulously crafted with an eye for detail and a commitment to local sourcing. His set menu might feature Livar pork belly with a sweet potato cream, smoked almond and Espelette pepper crumble, tabbouleh and a subtly fiery nduja sauce that adds a touch of liveliness. This couple knows exactly how to pamper their guests!

Name: Bosq
Description: The name of this restaurant is inspired by the Spanish word bosque ("forest"). This warm and welcoming spot stands on the edge of the National Park, affording stunning views of the lush landscape – the terrace is a real highlight! Robin Koenen combines finest local produce from Texel with Mediterranean flair and Asian nuances. His penchant for umami and barbecue notes shines through in dishes such as succulent pan-seared turbot with briny shellfish from the Wadden Sea, sweet tomatoes and a beurre blanc made with fish fumet and a judicious splash of soy sauce. His cuisine packs a punch and, thanks to the smaller-sized portions, you can sample it extensively.

Name: De Gaffel
Description: De Gaffel offers a dining experience steeped in rustic charm, beneath the thatched roof of a Saxon farmhouse warmed by a crackling open fire. The chef grows his own vegetables on site. He works with the finest ingredients and accentuates their quality with contemporary techniques. Featuring dishes such as an original take on vitello tonnato, and tender venison with a patiently reduced jus, a single surprise menu is served – you can choose to have four or five courses. Either way, the depth of the flavours and excellent value for money are guaranteed to have you smitten.

Name: Brasserie Goeie Louisa
Description: This brasserie shares the medieval charm of the upscale hotel, Karel V, to which it belongs. Once a monastery, the property has been elegantly decorated but has retained its original character. The chefs here like to put their own unique spin on classic recipes. They understand the value of a decent béarnaise sauce with a succulent cut of meat, but they also enjoy playing with the tartness of orange to elevate a dish based on lobster and fennel. This cuisine presents familiar flavours with an exciting twist.

Name: Het Oude Gemeentehuis
Description: Once the town hall, this is the ideal place for convivial dining. Original features provide a striking contrast with the modern design and warm colours. Indulgence is the name of the game when it comes to the food. Whether you opt for the rich lobster bisque, the sea bass with the rich beurre blanc or their contemporary take on tiramisu, you will be bowled over by the skill and charm of Niels Minkman and his team.

Name: de Molenaar
Description: The charm of the converted Hunsingo windmill (1855) is as captivating as this picturesque village, and it houses a really special restaurant. Chef Kooijker works only with a surprise menu in which he brings to bear all his creativity, paying special attention to the presentation, creating elaborate garnishes and giving a new perspective on familiar flavours. Rest assured, you are in good hands here. And why not treat yourself to an overnight stay in the mill or granary?

Name: In Den Rustwat
Description: In Den Rustwat is a premier destination set in a charming old inn dating back to 1597. Its thatched roof, period tile floor and Delft Blue ceramics, plus an idyllic terrace overlooking the arboretum make for a refined and comfortable setting. The service is exceptionally attentive. Marcel van Someren is a seasoned chef who cooks with clarity and purpose. His creativity and expertise shine through in dishes ranging from an Asian-inspired concoction with avocado, wasabi and a soy dressing, or turbot with a full-bodied beurre blanc. A true mainstay on the culinary scene.

Name: Bistro de Holterberg
Description: Experience the charms of each season in this cosy bistro, whether it's winter by the large open fireplace or summer on the stunning terrace, offering an awe-inspiring vista of the Salland Ridge National Park. The extensive set menu features authentic French dishes that each showcase one or two bold flavours. Crispy fried sea bass fillet, langoustine sauce and boiled fresh vegetables: unadulterated flavours at their best.

Name: The Bishop
Description: The Bishop is where the bustling centre of Leiden truly comes alive. The wooden beams and supporting columns are a reminder of the building's past, yet the trendy decor and lively atmosphere give it a contemporary feel. Take a punt on the surprise menu or order from the small à la carte selection – the chef's creations include subtle nods to his Indonesian heritage. He draws inspiration from all over the world, dabbling in international flavours to create exciting dishes: serundeng and Asian spices are added to the rendang, kimchi and gochujang to the veal tartare, hot and spicy aji amarillo to the kingfish. This place is a surefire hit, especially because of the terrific wine list. Be sure to make a reservation!

Name: Restaurant 55
Description: Set in the Heggenstraat, a cosy spot in the old city centre, is this pleasant restaurant with an atmospheric, baroque-style interior. It is immediately apparent that the kitchen is run by a young team – even if they do keep the flavours classic. The prices are very reasonable too!

Name: Kasteel TerWorm
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This 14C castle is brimming with character, and a meal here promises an experience beyond compare. With its wooden floors, medieval paintings and old stone walls, the setting couldn't be more enchanting. The waterside terrace overlooking the verdant surroundings is an absolute delight! Dave Beckers's approach is refreshingly modern and his sophisticated creations frequently feature flavour profiles based on koji, yuzu and koshi. For instance, he adds extra depth to his lamb fillet and crispy braised lamb neck by incorporating powdered seaweed into the potato mousseline and kombu into the rich lamb jus. This is easy-to-enjoy cuisine that also pushes boundaries. An overnight stay in the castle makes for the ultimate grand finale.

Name: La Cebolla
Description: Cees Timmerman is a connoisseur of fine ingredients, which he prefers to source locally, but he also embraces influences from the Mediterranean and places further afield. This is reflected in the tempting and extensive menu featuring both small plates and more elaborate dishes. His style is defined by his knack for reimagining familiar recipes, eg elevating a (whole!) turbotin with the typical sweet-and-spicy nuances of Indonesian fare, or a new take on cheesecake, paired with a refined Granny Smith sorbet and crunchy granola. This welcoming restaurant on the first floor of De Witt cinema invites you to savour authentic flavours in a laid-back atmosphere.

Name: Red Orchids
Description: Bold graffiti art and a dark palette of black and red create an intimate and laid-back feel. In the kitchen, the cuisines of Japan, China, Thailand and Indonesia artfully rub shoulders. The chef always manages to dose just the right spices, creating dishes full of rich flavours and crisp textures. Whether you opt for sushi, dim sum, Peking duck or sea bass with panang curry, this Asian culinary adventure puts authenticity front and centre.

Name: Oogst
Description: With its warm and welcoming atmosphere, Oogst is right at home in the cosy Buurtschap Centrum 2005 neighbourhood. There is something of the lively Parisian bistro about this place, which makes it all the more enjoyable to dine here. The set menus are always determined by what the Laantje Voorham vegetable garden has to offer. The versatility of vegetables and herbs provides subtle nuances. By incorporating herbs into ice cream and broths, the chef gives dishes a new twist. His modern and always generous creations are fragrant with punchy flavours.

Name: Bøg
Description: "New Nordic Restaurant" is a term that sparks the imagination. The sleek, rather understated decor of Bøg is certainly in line with what one would expect. Diners can choose between a vegetarian and fish/meat set menu, both equally creative and appealing. The finest ingredients, often locally sourced, are balanced with a minimalist approach and a sure touch. Pork, for example, is barbecued and served with al dente vegetables, a tart touch of cassis, a spicy sauce and a chilli-infused jus. Subtlety meets exuberant flavours in this fabulous restaurant.

Name: De Kromme Bistro
Description: Walk through the wine cellar to discover this charming bistro, an extension of the renowned De Kromme Watergang. The lush garden and open kitchen, complete with a sturdy charcoal grill instantly catch the eye. With every bite, you will sense the chefs' deep-rooted passion for the seafood of Zeeland, which is showcased here in all its briny glory. Think cockles with finely chopped chives and a rich beurre blanc infused with the cockles' juices and a hint of lemongrass. But rest assured, they can just as easily barbecue a bavette steak or whip up a vegetarian creation. Brasserie cuisine with a unique twist.

Name: Puur Sanh
Address: Zevenheuvelenweg 87, Berg en Dal, 6571 CJ, Netherlands
Description: Puur Sanh's cuisine is captivating with its creative, daring, and exciting flavours. Chef Witte focuses on plant-based dishes and likes to think outside the box. For instance, he combines textures of pineapple with a sweet potato beignet, coconut and curry cream, spicy fennel and sesame seeds, and a potato crème brûlée. Daring, but it absolutely works! Treat yourself to a seat on the terrace and sample the wonderful selection of whiskies and wines. A feast for the senses!

Name: Osteria Porta Sud
Description: Walk through the heritage Passage Zuidpoort and you will come to this fine example of Dutch interwar architecture. The first impression is enchanting: curved woodwork, the bar, the tiled floor and the colourful glass details. Yonna and Ralph keep their modern osteria intimate to preserve its Italian soul. Quality ingredients and those characteristic Mediterranean nuances are prepared with finesse and a contemporary edge. Highlights include a vibrant and unique take on vitello tonnato with the depth of a veal-jus-based vinaigrette and house-made agnolotti stuffed with mushroom, chestnut and hazelnut, finished with vegetable jus and truffle – familiar flavours which the chefs subtly inject with their own character.

Name: Restobar Rosie
Description: Rosie is a bustling yet cosy establishment where foodies can indulge uninterrupted from noon. A love of wine pervades the place and music fills the air – the record player spins nostalgic tunes regularly. From shrimp croquettes to Jerusalem artichoke with labneh or a no-nonsense meat or fish dish: the international menu has something for everyone. This straightforward cuisine makes the most of the versatility of vegetables. Reservations are recommended!

Name: Broederenklooster
Description: The authenticity of this former monastery (1293) has been preserved in every detail. Where once the friars used to take their meals, you can now enjoy a luxurious dining experience in a historical setting. The ultra-modern open kitchen immediately catches the eye. Niels van Dooijeweert brings a penchant for bold flavours and contemporary techniques to French dishes. Succulent pan-seared sea bream with a brunoise of tomato, papaya, onion and pak choi, in a curry sauce finished with lemon oil – this is the kind of cooking that draws so many diners; exceptional ingredients take the spotlight. The lovely guestrooms are perfect for a good night's rest.

Name: Hemel & Aarde
Description: Rene van der Weijden welcomes you to the majestic-looking building of Nox Hotel. Once a stately gentlemen's club, it is now also home to a restaurant with striking decor in soft shades of green. The high, sculpted ceilings are stunning. In the open kitchen, the chef creates inventive, occasionally daring dishes that always highlight the finest Dutch ingredients. Think raw kingfish rolled in herbs, accompanied by various textures of red cabbage, including an aromatic kombucha and a horseradish ice pearl. The presentation is elegant, the flavours often bold and the chef's ambition shines through in the thoughtful details and generous touches. Be sure to pay a visit to the adjacent wine to enjoy a select vintage and some bar snacks.

Name: Kook Atelier op Oost
Description: Nature takes centre stage at this tastefully converted 18C farmhouse, which also includes a boutique hotel. The restaurant's Nordic-inspired design and large windows that make you feel connected to the outdoors reflect the house's commitment to sustainability. The menu is centred on ingredients from the Wadden Sea and Texel, which they have either grown themselves or sourced from trusted local purveyors. Chef Joram structures his menu around the elements of earth, air, fire and water. For example, cured hamachi from Zeeland, brushed with a fruity glaze and served with pickled vegetables and a cucumber jus. Fermentation and other artisanal methods lend the dishes extra character. This exploration of Texel's ecosystems is truly captivating.

Name: Nazka
Description: You might, for a moment, feel as if you have stumbled across a wine cellar, but you will soon see that this hip South American eatery is very much at home in this cosmopolitan city. Nazka unleashes a whirlwind of bold flavours on your palate, from pisco cocktails to ceviche and other Peruvian specialities. This is exhilarating cuisine featuring a captivating interplay of spicy and sweet chilli peppers, Asian umami and the zing of leche del tigre. The well-curated selection of wines from around the globe adds extra character to this unique dining experience.

Name: Bij Hammingh
Description: It is impossible to resist the authentic charm of this former ferry house, from the terrace of which you can fully appreciate the lovely views across the canal and drawbridge. Inside, you can sense the building’s rich heritage, where the chef focuses on regional delicacies that showcase modern techniques and natural finesse.

Name: The Green Rose
Description: Jin Hu lives according to the rhythm of the micro-seasons and lets nature determine his creativity. Local artisans inspire him, and he uses every part of his own livestock. This close connection and respect for his environment are the common thread running through his French/Asian fusion dishes. Pure. Intense. For example, the chef surrounds al dente leeks with a delicate cream made from the vegetable, salty cockles from the North Sea with chives and a butter sauce with yuzu for a delicate freshness. Surprises lurk in every dish here, as they do in the special selection of natural wines and speciality beers.

Name: Oesterput 14
Description: The oyster tanks and the Eastern Scheldt reveal all their secrets in this sparkling establishment, which is the height of contemporary cuisine. Fish-lovers are well placed here for mouthwatering sea delicacies delivered fresh and unadulterated to the plate. Those who opt for a delicious piece of meat will also find tailored dishes on offer.

Name: DOYY
Description: DOYY offers an intimate and relaxed atmosphere with a touch of Middle Eastern elegance, reflecting the Azerbaijani-Turkish heritage of owner Yavuz. Chef Daan van Lieshout knows his French classics, as evidenced in the à la carte selection, which includes dishes such as steak tartare and tournedos Rossini. However, he also likes to incorporate Asian and Middle Eastern influences into his cooking – it is his set menu that really showcases his creativity. Think salty-sweet langoustine tartare with citrus chiboust, confit tomatoes, crispy chicken skin and a frothy bisque jus. Brace yourself for bold flavours with a spicy kick!

Name: Bistro Bord'o
Description: The moment you enter this welcoming restaurant, the emphasis on French and European wines is unmistakable. So, an aperitif is definitely in order before settling down to the food, which is rooted in French culinary tradition and includes occasional international influences. No fancy foams here, just top-notch ingredients. Think rare ribeye accompanied by a full-bodied bordelaise sauce, or sea bass ceviche marinated in calamansi and red chilli, seasoned with pezo and served alongside fresh snow crab, coastal vegetables and fennel prepared with a crisp, acidic dressing. This is a chance to savour a wealth of flavours in a laid-back setting – in summer, you can even do it on a boat!

Name: Sillyfox
Description: Located at the top of a converted grain-processing plant, this delightful space combines a raw, industrial aesthetic with modern design elements. It also boasts a roof terrace affording panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. With years of experience, Joppe Sprinkhuizen meticulously crafts each dish, blending timeless French cooking techniques with international influences. For example, the entrecôte, cooked rare, is served with a bitterbal (Dutch meatball) filled with rendang, alongside beans cooked in red curry and lemongrass, plus a peanut cream and a red berry cream providing sweet and fruity nuances. The set menus are fantastic!

Name: De Mandemaaker
Description: De Mandemaker has plenty of aces up its sleeve, such as a terrace on the inner harbour, the captivating blend of chic and cosiness both indoors and out, and guestrooms across the way. The extensive menu (slightly more limited at lunchtime) highlights the chef's versatility and his predilection for fish. Succulent tournedos with a full-bodied sauce infused with summer truffle and a decadent potato mille-feuille followed by a multi-textured dessert exploring the flavours of a cocktail of Martini and coffee… this cuisine is both playful and full of character. Essential dining when visiting Spakenburg!

Name: DYLANS
Address: Oude Zeeweg 63, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CJ, Netherlands
Description: The founder of Alexander Hotel was born a butcher's son and can be proud of this restaurant for meat lovers. The trendy intimacy of the decor, the gold elements, the hip lounge and cocktail bar all make for a magnificent venue. Many of the modern dishes are prepared on the Josper charcoal oven, resulting in robust, pure flavours. A fine côte de boeuf, a salt-crusted tenderloin to share, a choice cut of Japanese Wagyu beef: a feast for carnivores!

Name: Auberge des Moules
Description: Mussels, lobster and other seafood from Zeeland are the stars on the menu at this atmospheric inn. Here, these delicacies have for decades been prepared according to old family recipes. The black and white pictures on the walls demonstrate the rich history.

Name: Scherp
Description: Mart Scherp's restaurant, which also offers accommodation, merges the historical charm of Middelburg's town centre with a trendy vibe. The talented chef likes to work with Zeeland's local produce and Asian seasonings. Enticing flavours and subtle spiciness are common features, so it's no surprise that he has gathered a loyal following.

Name: 't Vlasbloemeken
Description: Eric van Bochove's honest and ingredient-driven cuisine showcases exceptional local produce such as Eastern Scheldt lobster and Zeeland lamb. His style is anchored in tradition, yet enlivened by contemporary touches. Think weever in mandarin oil with fennel foam, or briny oyster invigorated by the fruity sparkle of raspberry granita – this chef reimagines the familiar with bold creativity. The charming hostess extends heartfelt hospitality, ensuring a relaxed dining experience whether you are in the stylish interior, with its warm colours and thoughtful design, or out on the inviting terrace.

Name: Woods
Description: The view of the Oude Rijn and the authentic sawmill charms you as soon as you walk into this characterful restaurant (that terrace!), but chef Van der Pluijm's cuisine also deserves attention. His style is modern and restrained, with subtle cosmopolitan accents. For example, he cooks bavette to a beautiful pink and serves it with a creamy parsnip purée, mushroom duxelles, pommes dauphine and a slice of fried goose liver. The plates are beautifully presented and combine classic touches with refined creativity, without excess.

Name: De Hinde
Description: Harmen Ligthart has converted his grandfather's café into a cosy restaurant with an endearing and authentic soul. The view over the IJsselmeer (also from the two luxury guestrooms) is truly stunning! A stroll through the village and down by the boats is a must. Whether you opt for fish or game, you can rest assured that the ingredients are locally sourced and that the classic sense of generosity is adhered to. The pâté and fine Riesling wines are firm favourites here.

Name: Dudockx Bar & Kitchen
Description: Architect Dudok is the designer behind this trendy 1930s pavilion. Each table overlooks the Hilversum Canal, which really is something to behold as you sit on the gorgeous terrace. The resolutely modern cuisine shows a preference for organic and local produce, yet remains down-to-earth. For a variety of fish dishes with Asian nuances or a perfectly cooked piece of meat with an exquisite sauce, this is the place to come. The daily specials never disappoint. The restaurant also rents out boats!

Name: Auberge de Veste
Description: Settle in for a cosy dinner in this characterful property nestled beside a little river and dating back to 1849. Each month, Ruben Coonen unveils a new surprise menu, continually justifying his guests' faith in his culinary talents and wine recommendations. Whether he serves up a tender piece of veal with an aromatic jus de cuisson, or a pristine cod fillet with the fine nuances of a dashi vinaigrette, his market-fresh cuisine is at times intricate and always brimming with flavour.

Name: De Luytervelde
Description: Karin Smits is the heart and soul of De Luytervelde. She has been welcoming guests at this converted farmhouse (1912) just outside the city centre since 1992. Diners are smitten with the stylish decor and delightful garden terrace, but the main focus remains, of course, the modern interpretation of classic flavours and the well-curated wine list. The chef will expertly fry a veal sweetbread until golden brown and knock up a robust sauce Périgueux, but he is just as adept at giving venison an exotic twist with five-spice powder. A perennial favourite!

Name: Hanasato
Description: Hanasato exudes the understated simplicity associated with Japanese culinary culture. The kitchen follows the Washoku tradition, upholding authenticity and the celebrated subtlety of East Asian cuisine. Expect dishes such as sashimi made with ultra-fresh fish and served with fresh wasabi and a full-bodied soy sauce, or umami-rich chawanmushi with a rich, complex dashi. Be sure to try the shabu shabu – diners cook thinly sliced vegetables, meat and rice by dipping them into a rich broth. This is Japanese cuisine that leaves a lasting impression. Please note that the six-course set menu or the à la carte need to be pre-ordered.

Name: Mezger
Description: Mezger is the dream of Jeroen and Sanne Tanis who found the perfect setting in this orangerie which they have redecorated with wood and trendy furniture. His cuisine highlights his own experience, which respects the seasons and products from the Zeeland region. He adds to this mix perfect cooking techniques and ingredients that work together to create a dream that is now a pleasurable reality!

Name: Het Weeshuys
Description: Striking murals with a culinary theme give this orphanage chapel (1310) real individuality. The vibrant decor indoors is certainly a sight to behold, but there is also a courtyard terrace that is idyllic in fine weather. Opt for the lunch set menu or simply let the chef surprise you with inspired and delicate creations such as choucroute and prawns with an Asian twist, or a new take on wild boar terrine – a feast for the senses is guaranteed!

Name: Zuid by Adrian Zarzo
Description: Adrian Zarzo brings the world to your plate in this trendy, chic establishment. For example, you start with dim sum, then move on to an intense bouillabaisse and continue your journey with a Mediterranean take on sea bass. Zuid advocates a relaxed approach to gastronomy and is run by a chef who knows how to win over the modern diner. Be sure to drop by the bodega next door for some delicious snacks and a good glass of wine.

Name: Carelshaven
Description: Carelshaven has been providing comfortable overnight accommodation since 1772. This elegant restaurant is located on the splendid Twickel Castle estate, and its leafy terrace overlooks the grounds. The chef tends his on-site kitchen garden, incorporating its bounty into fine French dishes that are plant-forward and include influences from around the globe. By enriching his duck jus with mole, he imbues duck breast with spicy-sweet nuances; textures of kumquat give the sweetbreads an exquisite twist – each plate is full of surprises.

Name: Arles
Description: Arles brings Provence to Amsterdam. The prints on the walls of this bustling little bistro hark back to the hometown of the chef, who also shares his love of jazz music here (get a table in the dining room at the front if you prefer a quieter space). His culinary style is neo-bistro – a fresh take on the familiar flavours of French cuisine. Think the earthy flavour of beef cheeks cooked in red wine with buttery carrots or a new take on rice pudding. The set menu changes monthly and offers unbeatable value for money!

Name: 't Arsenaal
Description: At 't Arsenaal, historical details such as an old spiral staircase and rustic tiles are seamlessly incorporated into the bright and rather sleek decor. There is an atmospheric bar, and the courtyard garden terrace between the buttresses of the Lebuinuskerk is an ideal setting for a romantic dinner. Yolande and Rob ensure a refined dining experience front of house while the chefs serve up enticing dishes à la carte or as a surprise menu. From crisp pork belly with kimchi to lamb enhanced by a rich cumin sauce, the cuisine is wonderfully in tune with the times, with just enough international influences to add intrigue to each dish.

Name: Visaandeschelde
Description: Visaandeschelde has been a haven for seafood enthusiasts since 1999.
