The maritime theme of this brasserie is emphasised by details such as anchors and fish drawings on the tiles, scale patterns on the windows and the blue and white colour scheme. In this lively establishment, you can savour briny oysters, sumptuous seafood platters and the freshest fish. The dishes are rather traditional in style – it is the quality of the produce that counts. When you order lobster, expect it to be perfectly cooked and served with a subtly sweet olive oil vinaigrette with parsley and a crisp salad. The lunchtime menu comes highly recommended!

Name: De Ertepeller
Description: The steady stream of boats passing by provides a captivating backdrop for this bright and airy restaurant located at a point where three rivers meet. Large windows afford uninterrupted views. During the week, Arjan Kuipers serves up an appealing selection of simple dishes, including crispy battered fish and freshly cut chips. Alternatively, you can opt for a more ambitious and adventurous set menu. A variety of textures and international flavours are expertly combined, and the dishes are beautifully presented. With an accomplished chef at the helm, De Ertepeller offers the best of both worlds, and the quality is second to none.

Name: Bistro Madeleine
Description: As typical as the name sounds, this place is far from being your average bistro. Rather than a stuffy decor, you can expect a 21C take on the standard bistro setting. The chef conjures up the same impression on the plate. Upon entering, you are greeted by the delicious aroma of fresh bread. Here, simplicity is synonymous with robust flavours. The modern touches he brings to the dishes add a surprising twist. Think ray wing with a roasted pepper sauce vierge, creamed celeriac and a frothy tarragon sauce. The carefully curated wine list is second to none. An atypical bistro!

Name: Villa la Ruche
Description: This alluring, chic and inviting 19C villa is the splendid setting in which Marko Karelse showcases his mastery of classical cuisine and his creative flair. Whether ordering à la carte or opting for the "JRE" set menu or the more upmarket "Prestige" option, diners witness a chef equally adept with vegetables, meat and seafood. Lobster with finely chopped razor clams and a miso-infused bisque, or morels with a touch of bright acidity and a mushroom jus – this is sophisticated cooking. Be sure to sample the asparagus specialities in season!

Name: Cèpes
Description: Hotel de Sterrenberg's restaurant draws on its natural surroundings. The interior is sleek yet warm, combining lots of wood with concrete, and a large wooden stag's head that draws the eye. The chef believes in sourcing his produce locally, using local suppliers such as Gert van Eldik and the Veluwe asparagus farm. Diners are served a surprise menu composed of intricate and beautifully presented dishes. Think venison from the region with carefully considered vegetable accompaniments and a game jus enhanced with vermouth. A proud ambassador for the Veluwe!

Name: Huson
Description: This stylish urban restaurant combines sophistication with vibrant energy. The menu spans creative dishes with exotic twists, sharable signature plates and more exclusive specialities such as ribeye dry-aged in Himalayan salt – there is something for every palate. Chef Mark van Wijngen is a bold culinary artist with impeccable technique and intuition, masterfully balancing subtle refinement with bold, punchy flavours. Take his medium-rare lamb saddle and confit lamb neck paired with a robust natural jus, green asparagus, lemon zest, polenta with smoked egg yolk and an asparagus cream. A Rotterdam dining experience not to be missed!

Name: Damianz
Description: In what was once Roermond's prison, you will be served bread and water first of all. But fear not: any culinary nods to the past vocation of the premises end there. At this restaurant, which is part of Het Arresthuis hotel, historical details and contemporary design elegantly intertwine. Chef Jeroen van Gansewinkel masterfully incorporates international influences and rich sauces into his dishes. From lamb with typically Middle Eastern seasonings such as za'atar and smoked paprika to langoustine with a tangy beurre blanc infused with basil oil, the food is complex and brimming with flavour. As they say themselves – it's criminally delicious!

Name: Flores
Description: Owner and sommelier Elroy Slijkhuis has transformed this family-run business into a cosy gastro bistro – the tables on the patio by the wine store are much in demand! He has a clear vision for this enterprise: The emphasis is on plant-forward cuisine, with a commitment to using home-grown/local produce and ensuring the welfare of all parties. Natural wines dominate the wine list. Chef Luuk Freriks's dishes tend to be daring – even unsettling at times. He painstakingly transforms vegetables such as carrots and beetroot into a remarkable "charcuterie" platter. Koji is a tool he frequently uses to create depth, for example drying beef heart in it and then shaving it over a cut of meat to imbue it with profound intensity. At Flores, nature's bounty is showcased in the most innovative of ways.

Name: Restaurant MANNA
Description: MANNA blends fashion and cosmopolitan flair in a building full of character. Out front, there's a charming city terrace; inside, no fewer than five private dining rooms await, along with luxurious hotel rooms upstairs. Fish takes centre stage here, but meat lovers and vegetarians are equally well catered for. The plates presented are just as on trend as the setting. Whether you are in the mood for a bento box starter, followed by a succulent entrecôte with a balsamic-infused roasting jus, or sea bass baked in a salt crust, MANNA delivers. Alternatively, indulge in a super fresh seafood platter from the fish bar. This is your go-to spot, open daily for both lunch and dinner.

Name: Breakers Beach House
Address: Koningin Astrid Boulevard 5, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 BK, Netherlands
Description: Welcome to the "Dutch Riviera", where dining with your toes in the sand is sure to give you that holiday feeling. The relaxed terrace affords a wonderful view of the sea, or you can enjoy the trendy brasserie ambience inside. This is the place to come for a plate of ultra-fresh oysters and seafood, followed by classically prepared dishes in which the produce (mainly fish, of course) steals the show. Simple and delicious!

Name: Restaurant Eindeloos
Description: The biggest draws of this warm and welcoming restaurant are Willem Schaafsma's culinary prowess and the exquisite pairings dreamt up by his sommelier. Here, you can savour dishes made with top-quality ingredients that are sourced as locally and sustainably as possible – and all at excellent value for money. A firm favourite!

Name: Etablissement 1880
Description: Etablissement 1880 is much more nuanced than the black and white that dominate its colour scheme. The charm of the decor and the location on Groede's historic market square make for a cosy setting. For her surprise menu, chef Mariëlla draws on flavours from around the globe and Zeeland produce. With an eye for detail, the creative chef focuses on subtle touches such as zesty garnishes and rich sauces that bind her dishes together. If you wish to extend your stay, book one of the two guestrooms upstairs.

Name: Het Binnenhof
Address: Bocht van Guinea 6, Goes, 4461 BC, Netherlands
Description: Het Binnenhof exudes all the charm of Goes's historic centre. A narrow alleyway leads you to this stylishly refurbished restaurant, which is tucked away in a courtyard and boasts an inviting terrace. The seafood comes directly from the Vismijn Colijnsplaat fish auction; the vegetables and meat are also locally sourced. Chef Arjen spoils you for choice with his à la carte and set menus, and it doesn't stop there! Generous and highly accomplished, he whips up the most fabulous sauces.

Name: Restaurant Old Skool
Description: Druten's old school has been converted into a restaurant with a charming retro-modern location and a menu offering a choice of modern, traditional and vegetarian dishes. Although the chef will readily produce a game dish based on pheasant, he tends towards the contemporary end of the spectrum. This manifests itself in his use of seasonings from around the globe and the presentation of the dishes. A delicious lesson for any foodie!

Name: Bistro T-bone
Description: Everything revolves around the charcoal grill in this atmospheric establishment pleasantly situated in a quintessential old Dutch building. Whether he's barbecuing T-bone steak, a rack of lamb or sole, the chef bends the flames to his will with a sure touch. The results are dishes that are generous and brimming with typically robust flavours and character. The jovial owner will be happy to guide you through the menu, which also includes classics such as snails and onion soup – there are plenty of mouth-watering options.

Name: Le Moulin
Description: Le Moulin has been running like a well-oiled machine since 1986, thanks to charming hostess Yvonne and chef Frans Glas. This warm and cosy restaurant makes for an ideal setting in which diners (re)discover the distinctive cuisines of France and Flanders. Ultra-fresh North Sea sole, for instance, is pan-fried à la meunière in time-honoured tradition and served alongside a potato gratin with a golden brown crust. No gimmicks, just authentic flavours and wonderful sauces. Salmon is still smoked according to an old family recipe. And when it comes to wine, you're in great hands with Yvonne.

Name: Het Bosch
Description: Breathtaking – that's the word that comes to mind as the view over the Nieuwe Meer marina unfolds before you. This modern pavilion takes full advantage of its surroundings, and the terrace is the prime spot. The extensive menu features classic French brasserie fare elevated with inventive twists and includes steak tartare, vegetarian options and lobster dishes. Alternatively, you might like to try the poached salmon with a beurre blanc elevated by dashi and parsley oil – a feast for the eyes and the palate!

Name: Restaurant Judith
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Kasteel Engelburg is a gem of a castle estate that boasts charming guestrooms and top-tier golf facilities. First, make your way to the 19C greenhouse, where you can take in the views of the peaceful natural surroundings. The chefs cook with reverence for classic techniques and a penchant for freshness and bright flavours. They work with the finest ingredients and know how to elevate them with exuberant sauces seasoned, for example, with the perfect amount of curry. This cuisine is sophisticated and, at times, delicate. Be sure to explore the selection of South African wines; after dinner, an impressive whisky collection awaits you in the lounge.

Name: Wolf Atelier
Description: Michael Wolf likes to experiment with sophisticated flavours and surprising ideas, giving diners the opportunity to test them out and then refining them to retain their best features. He is just as happy to cook up a turnip-based vegetarian take on Beef Wellington as he is to concoct surf and turf combinations that put a new spin on familiar flavours. The name Atelier is therefore particularly appropriate in this trendy, industrial-style restaurant, which is located on an old railway bridge with a beautiful view of the IJ.

Name: BAK
Description: Take the stairs to the third floor of this unobtrusive warehouse (you'll need to ring the bell in the evening) to discover this rather rugged yet inviting restaurant with its splendid view over the IJ River. Benny Blisto sets great store by the origin of his ingredients, be it a carrot or ray wing. Locally sourced, seasonal produce is the inspiration behind his creativity. For instance, with slightly tart rhubarb and an exquisite beetroot sauce, he elevates a venison fillet to new heights. An exciting dining experience is guaranteed!

Name: R21
Description: Start off with an aperitif at the marble counter, then meet the chefs in the kitchen on your way to the dining area, divided into sections, all of which exude a certain Scandinavian elegance. Having long worked with Sergio Herman, Orlando David has developed a vibrant style of cooking. He might, for example, serve herring on top of a potato and apple salad, accompanied by citrus gel, sea banana and pickled shallot. At R21, the dishes are exciting and creative, and the sommelier has a keen understanding of the cuisine and complements it with judicious wine pairings.

Name: SEAson - Arsenaal
Description: Originally erected in 1688 as a military barracks, this building was converted many years later by renowned interior designer Jan des Bouverie. Today, the place is chic and inviting, and the terrace is a real draw on sunny days. Dennis Koopmans specialises in seafood, but does cater to meat eaters as well. If you're looking for a plateau de fruits de mer or the freshest of seasonal fish, it doesn't get much better than this. Think pan-fried red mullet and a rich shellfish bisque, with finely chopped fennel providing a hint of zesty flavour, complemented by salty samphire and crispy croutons. As the name suggests, this restaurant is a celebration of the finest and freshest seasonal produce.

Name: Barres
Description: Edwin Dingemanse and Sjoerd Dooge's bar/restaurant exudes youthful elegance – everything here is impeccable without being stiff. Their sincere commitment to guests manifests itself in the cuisine. Diners are bowled over by the complex interplay of local delicacies – Zeeland shellfish, for instance – with influences from all around the globe. The sauces are rich and the garnishes playful, yet it is always the core ingredient that steals the show.

Name: Wielinga
Description: Housed in a historical building, this charming restaurant has more of an intimate feel at the front than at the back, thanks to the natural light. However, the best spot is the canal-side terrace – perfect for soaking up Leiden's vibrant atmosphere. The chef proposes an appealing set menu with options for each course (priced higher in the evening than at lunch) alongside an à la carte selection that showcases premium ingredients. From sole fried in butter to skrei topped with a Taggiasca olive crumble and accompanied by a bright sauce vierge, lobster tartare and a rich lobster bisque, her dishes highlight classical technique at its best. She cooks with precision and is unafraid to add subtle modern twists. Be sure to peruse the expertly curated wine list.

Name: Restaurant Markant
Description: This cosy little establishment outside Breda city centre bears its name well. The fact that the staff take great pleasure in spoiling their diners is palpable. Decorative features such as wine crates show that Markant is driven by a passion for wine as well as food. Be sure to take a look at the wine list, which features all sorts of great finds, before perusing the extensive à la carte menu. The young chef's repertoire includes classics such as œuf en gelée, as well as vegetarian options and the occasional Asian-influenced creation. His attention to quality is evident in the generosity of flavours and depth of the sauces. Some dishes are prepared right at your table, which is a nice touch.

Name: Rura by Naomi & Joey
Description: Naomi & Joey embrace the concept of casual fine dining in their cosy restaurant, where the atmosphere is intimate and laid back. The meticulous detail and thoughtful preparation of each dish stands out. Chef Joey loves to transform his ingredients; rich sauces and influences from around the globe add punch. Vegetables play a central role in his cooking, with both a vegetarian and a meat-and-fish set menu available. A prime example of his ingenuity is a dish featuring toasted brioche topped with ratatouille, in addition to both white and green asparagus, pommes soufflées and a buttermilk and lavas oil sauce. The couple's enthusiasm is nothing short of contagious!

Name: Senses
Description: The chic and artistic interior design of The Albus hotel's lounge-like restaurant is bang on trend. Get ready for an explosion of flavours as Eastern spices meet a burst of acidity and a healthy dose of creativity. Vegetables take centre stage in the chef's culinary artistry, as exemplified by the potato spaghetti with autumn truffle and katsuobushi, accompanied by a creamy maitake mushroom sauce and the tangy zest of tosazu. The fact that the chefs like to serve their dishes personally is a sign of their enthusiasm. The exquisite wine list is the icing on the cake.

Name: Valuas
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The stunning view of the Maas River from the terrace here is something you won't soon forget. The same goes for the warm welcome you will receive and the genuine hospitality that is so characteristic of the Limburg region. At this restaurant, they aim to please, as you will see from Eric Swaghoven's extensive menu. The range of delectable options includes a rich North Sea crab remoulade with textures of potato and an exquisite shrimp bisque, a guinea fowl and rabbit paté en croûte, mackerel sashimi, as well as a Mediterranean-style risotto. The experienced chef's versatility shines through, and the value for money is exceptional. Oenophiles will delight in the extraordinarily extensive wine list.

Name: De Silveren Spiegel
Description: These two step-gabled houses from 1614 take you back in time . From the open fireplace with matching tiles to the romantic candlelit setting, silver cutlery and beautiful porcelain plates, everything here exudes Dutch charm at its best. The menu features exquisite, intricate dishes that showcase Dutch produce. The young chef has a keen eye for freshness, as demonstrated by the foamy mussel sauce he uses to elevate the salty symphony of mussels and seaweed. With its good selection of natural wines and a penchant for French labels, the wine list is definitely worth a look.

Name: Restaurant Vannu
Description: Today's culinary landscape is characterised by a shift towards plant-based, zero-waste dishes underpinned by long-established techniques such as fermentation and pickling. At Restaurant Vannu, Gijs Kemmeren gives his creativity free rein, incorporating all those elements into a multi-course set menu. With seaweed, for example, he adds nuance to the earthiness of beetroot and fresh celery. He also whisks up an intensely flavoursome chanterelle sauce to tie together al dente vegetables and a millet polenta cake. His cuisine is sophisticated, playful and certainly intriguing. The accompanying natural wines and juices underscore the ethos of this establishment. A memorable dining experience is guaranteed.

Name: NOÏS
Description: Laura is a warm and welcoming host, and she knows the outstanding wine list like the back of her hand. Her recommendations are absolutely spot on! If you like surprises, chef Vincent is your man. There's no written menu here; your options are presented verbally only, and your trust is rewarded with imaginative, plant-forward cuisine. Whether he's imbuing various textures of celeriac with zingy flavours, or putting pork belly centre stage in an Asian-inspired dish with a bay leaf cream sauce, his elaborate culinary creations are full of flair.

Name: Bistro Refter
Description: Roelfien Steen and Cor Klevering's cosy bistro is a firm favourite. Don't expect creative excesses here, just authentic classic fare cooked up by an experienced chef; he draws much of his inspiration from French cuisine but also likes to express his love for Mediterranean flavours. This is the kind of place where you can feast on an intense bouillabaisse and a choice cut of meat with a bearnaise sauce prepared in time-honoured tradition.

Name: Le Jardin
Description: Behind the dark blue façade on the Mariaplaats, plants and cacti dominate the floral decor at Le Jardin. The front of the restaurant is more intimate; the back is brighter and airier, but it is cosy and inviting throughout. This is a lively place, both in terms of the atmosphere and the cuisine. "Groentenomie" is the name of Tamara de Borst's culinary concept, which builds on vegetables and herbs; meat or fish can be added, if you wish. Rooted in French tradition, her cuisine incorporates innovative twists and occasional Asian seasonings. Think fleshy pumpkin with a herby crunch, a fruity jus with mandarin and a succulent pollock fillet. Garden produce at its best!

Name: De Mark
Description: Leave your car outside Durgerdam and embrace the charm of this dike village as you walk to De Mark. From the terrace, you have an exceptional view over the water – simply breathtaking! The attractive interior is done out in natural tones and makes the most of the character of the building. Dinner here is a cosy affair. Each dish revolves around three main ingredients, cooked over the wood fire. Think textures of onion – from crisp and crunchy to sweet and grilled – elevated with a Zaandam mustard ice cream. The experienced chefs offer a fresh perspective on natural flavours. If you really want to explore the extensive wine list, luxurious guestrooms are available on the first floor.

Name: Arca
Description: Renowned Portuguese chef Henrique Sá Pessoa is the creator of the enticing set menus at this trendy, cosmopolitan establishment. Home-style dishes are expertly given a modern twist, perhaps even a little Asian finesse, but the portions remain typically generous. Raw yellowtail, for example, is thinly sliced and dressed with a zesty coriander and citrus marinade, complemented by dried mulberries for a hint of sweetness, bread croutons, sea buckthorn and radish julienne. Delicious! The bespoke cocktails are fabulous, as is lunch in the cool bar.

Name: Reblochon
Description: Elise and Jurgen have transformed a charming cottage into a cosy living room-style restaurant, welcoming diners with genuine hospitality. The chef only serves a surprise menu, which he executes masterfully. Expect no gimmicks, but rather carefully crafted dishes with occasional influences from far-flung places. For instance, he combines pickled salmon with the earthy sweetness of beetroot and the umami of miso. Be sure to try the cheese board – a delicious way to discover the inspiration behind the restaurant's name.

Name: Putaine
Description: The Rotterdam skyline and Nieuwe Maas river form the backdrop to your dining experience at Putaine. On a pontoon floating in the Rijnhaven, this on-trend restaurant has large windows and a fabulous terrace. You could happily spend the whole day here working your way through the creative à la carte menu. Chef Schook makes a point of working with Dutch produce, giving vegetables special emphasis; he has a penchant for crisp, vibrant nuances. A cosmopolitan and exciting place!

Name: VanOost
Description: Part of Pillows Grand Boutique Hotel Maurits at the Park, VanOost Restaurant is housed in a lavishly converted university building dating back to 1908. Period features including authentic wood finishes and high ceilings harmonise elegantly with the fully open kitchen. From a seat at the counter you can watch Floris van Straalen channel both international influences and regional produce into intricate and imaginative cuisine. His delicate touch with flavour contrasts is demonstrated by his dish featuring langoustines cooked to perfection and glazed with katjang pedis and sambal, accompanied by a curry foam and sweet-and-sour vegetables. Before (or after) dinner, head to Fitz's Bar on the lower ground floor for an expertly mixed cocktail in a setting that transports you back to the Roaring Twenties.

Name: Wijnhuis De Blauwe Camer
Description: The medieval site of Sint-Catharinadal convent is an oasis of charm. The coach house has been turned into a modern restaurant bathed in natural light and with a rustic vibe. There is also a kitchen garden and several hectares of vineyards (hence the wine barrels at the entrance). The chef always starts with quality ingredients, often from his own garden, and distinguishes himself through expressive flavours, bold combinations and cosmopolitan influences. Expect dishes such as charred sea bass with marinated green apple and smoked feta ravioli, or lamb shoulder in red curry with coconut milk and mint. The experience ends with a mignardise bearing a QR code underneath that recaps your entire tasting journey.

Name: Restaurant Moustique
Description: Located in the heart of Haarlem, Moustique boasts stylish interior design and a terrace overlooking the Grote Kerk, plus it's open every day of the week – what a treat! The chef showcases his experience through an appealing à la carte selection and a multi-course tasting menu. He is just as adept at jazzing up fish with pickled cucumber, horseradish and jalapeño as he is at putting his own spin on steak tartare. The kitchen team thrives on excitement and daring combinations, but never at the expense of harmony on the plate.

Name: Mont Blanc
Description: From the cosy chalet vibe and the cowbells in the lavatory to the food and the delightful surprises on the wine list, everything about this place is an ode to Savoie, the homeland of chef Thibault, who runs the business with his wife Dieuwerjte. His unique signature style is shaped by authentic flavours, creative impulses and technical ingenuity, with a special emphasis on spiciness and vibrancy. For instance, the catfish comes in three intricate dishes, one of which features a fillet aged for eight weeks and marinated with miso and sourdough, accompanied by a frothy beurre blanc, parsnip purée and a sweet-and-sour vegetable chutney. Be sure to sample something from the outstanding cheese trolley! Expect Alpine cuisine with natural undertones and a focus on preparation techniques.

Name: Bistro Margaux
Description: Djailany van de Laarschot’s ambition is clear: to celebrate life à la française, and to bring his vision to life he has transformed a former estaminet into this charming, ever-buzzing bistro. The extensive menu embraces French culinary tradition – think foie gras pâté with brioche to start, followed by juicy rotisserie poussin and, finally, an indulgent crêpe Suzette. Traditional flavours are served up with abundant generosity in a heartwarming feast for any foodie.

Name: Veneur
Description: Veneur has an old-school vibe. The nostalgic charm of this building, with its wooden panelling and beautiful mouldings, has been subtly rejuvenated with details such as modern lighting. The terrace? It could easily be in Paris. The menu also has a bold edge. Yoran Jacobi and Moriaan Koeleman's product-driven kitchen gives pride of place to meat, grilled dishes and fire. For example, you start with a canapé of black pudding with grey shrimp, while briefly grilled rabbit is accompanied by morels and a creamy gravy with cognac. And how about pigeon with a cherry glaze and a gravy thickened with the giblets? Lovers of strong flavours will want to try everything on the menu! Be sure to check out the wine list, which has been expertly compiled.

Name: De Coterie
Description: De Coterie sits off the tourist trail and gives you a taste of The Hague's hip side. Locals drop by this stylish gastrobar for a glass of wine or a refreshing cocktail, followed by a spread of sharing plates. The appealing menu is broadly European, emphasising Mediterranean influences while celebrating Dutch ingredients. The chefs bring the dishes to life with touches such as an intensely reduced veal jus or pickled wild garlic buds. One highlight is the various textures of tangy rhubarb with fruity strawberry sorbet and a subtly spiced elderflower syrup with red pepper oil. Exciting flavours guaranteed!

Name: Holsterhof
Description: With the hard work of hostess Lissa and chef Kaj, the restaurant at Holsterhof camping farm has gradually evolved into a sought-after culinary destination, set in a modern, light-filled space surrounded by lush greenery. The service is relaxed and friendly. The chef is an expert sauce maker who creates daring combinations on the plate, without making things overly complicated. His exquisite red curry with coconut milk adds depth of flavour to the tender quail leg with black lentils. Working with two set menus, he consistently surprises with subtle nuances.

Name: Bistro LOF
Description: Chicory (lof in Dutch) grows in the kitchen garden that surrounds this laid-back restaurant, which is modern with a raw edge. Set in a converted farmhouse on the Parc Broekhuizen estate, where diners sit beneath the handsome timber roof trusses, the design brings nature indoors, creating a soothing, zen-like atmosphere. The chef cooks in step with the harvest, showcasing Dutch produce and using spices to add verve. A dish might feature cherry tomatoes plucked straight from the garden and herbs folded into a mayonnaise to accompany briny mussels, chopped watermelon and a complex mussel jus with yellow curry. Her cooking is sophisticated and indulgent. In this bistro, you can both see and taste how the seasons enrich the land.

Name: Hof aan Zee
Description: Just 500m from the North Sea, Hof aan Zee is set in a historical Scandinavian farmhouse nestled in tranquil natural surroundings. The chef has developed his own Zeeland-inspired Nordic style – playful and expressive, with notes of fermentation, hints of smoke and a full appreciation for local produce such as Eastern Scheldt fish and seaweed. He adds punch to raw wild duck tartare with wild garlic capers, finely chopped shallot, a potato emulsion and blackcurrant powder for herbal vibrancy. This is a culinary journey defined by purity and a deep reverence for the local environment. Take the opportunity to stay in one of the guestrooms by the kitchen garden – an experience not to missed!

Name: Villa Coucou
Address: Laan Van Meerdervoort 6, The Hague, 2517 AJ, Netherlands
Description: Villa Coucou radiates sophistication: hardwood floors, marble tables, and artwork on the walls create a luxurious setting. Start with an aperitif at the bar or in the wine cellar (with its own pétanque court!) before heading upstairs to admire the garden vista. The chef specialises in French classics with a playful twist: tomato terrine with basil ice cream and goat's cheese foam, or succulent ribeye with grilled sweetcorn and a herb-scented jus. A single set menu is served at lunchtime; both à la carte and a set menu are available in the evening. This chic spot might just become your new favourite.

Name: Domenica
Description: Domenica is the place to come to experience the bustling Jordaan neighbourhood. Whether you are dining outside on the terrace or inside at the bar of this modern bistro, there is always a lively atmosphere here. Authentic Italian seasonal dishes are served up with great skill and a proper sense of generosity. Think octopus with crispy skin and tender meat served alongside robust bell pepper and broccoletti. Owner Flavio pays tribute to his heritage with every vibrant plate. Be sure to check out his French and Italian wine selections too.

Name: Pollevie
Description: Martin Berkelmans has a passion for vegetables. He sources them from a food forest and a local farm and likes to experiment with them in his fermentation lab. The versatility of vegetables makes his dishes both playful and intriguing – they dictate the culinary direction, although meat and fish are also incorporated into his cooking. The succulent partridge breast and the rich stew are elevated to new heights with parsley root, a vegetable and walnut purée and a robust sauce featuring cassis for a sweet-and-sour note. The slightly industrial feel and organic vibe lend this inviting restaurant a unique character.

Name: Plantage 87
Cuisine: Modern Cuisine, Cuisine from the Marches
Description: With views over the surrounding marina, tables on the terrace at Plantage 87 are coveted, but the interior is just as inviting. Stephan Möllers's biggest source of inspiration lies a little further away, in his generously sized vegetable garden. He likes to express his creativity by preparing vegetables so that they yield the right acidity or spiciness to bring out the best of the main ingredient – letting it speak for itself. Elegant sauces lend each beautifully plated dish its own character. One example is a beurre blanc enhanced with tosa dashi as a delicate accompaniment to sea bass seared on the skin, with miso- and sake-glazed aubergine and crisp vegetables. The aim is always to highlight the natural flavours of the main ingredients.

Name: The Church
Address: Ir J.P. Van Muijlwijkstraat 19A, Arnhem, 6828 BP, Netherlands
Description: With its stained-glass windows, sculptures, murals and old pews, this Lutheran church has been beautifully preserved. The juxtaposition of modern opulence with the venue's rich past is truly inspired. Take in the spectacle of the open kitchen while enjoying a meal prepared right before your eyes. Nestled in the church's rafters, there are a few cosy guestrooms. But first, it's time to let yourself be spoiled by Bart Leussink, a chef who embraces creativity and boldness in his cooking. For instance, he elevates lamb neck with a crispy herb crust and lamb fillet with a vibrant sweet-and-sour cucumber garnish and a rich lamb jus. The chef has a penchant for fish and seafood dishes, into which he likes weave zesty flavours. An extraordinary experience!

Name: Eden
Description: Eden radiates modern elegance. Natural elements and hues, warm mood lighting and chic decorative features make this open space feel cosy and sophisticated. Dining here is an absolute joy. Chef Herman Cooijmans presents creative, dynamic cuisine that embraces bold contrasts, for instance, working a liquorice vinaigrette with marinated pouting, asparagus and capers into a chocolate dessert – he pushes boundaries, often with surprising results. Explore the expertly curated wine list for the perfect accompaniment.

Name: De Keuken van Arragon
Description: In this former inn on the edge of the Spaarbankbos, Herco van Arragon cooks with his own signature style: seasonal, contemporary and sometimes surprising. A piece of skate wing, for example, is accompanied by grey shrimp, a bisque full of depth and a cream of sweet potato and ginger, powerful and precise. Inside, there is a relaxed, homely atmosphere. Cynthia welcomes guests with a smile and a chat, as if everyone here is a regular. Talk about genuine warmth! This is a place where experience and spontaneity go hand in hand.

Name: Kruiden & Jasmijn
Description: Located just inside the historical city walls, this is an elegantly appointed restaurant featuring modern art and imposing chandeliers. The terrace exudes tranquillity, and the attentive service creates a warm and welcoming atmosphere. A passionate advocate for local produce, chef Patrick de Rade especially loves Eastern Scheldt lobster when it is in season. He also regularly harvests fruit and vegetables from his garden. Sourced from a friendly local farmer, red cabbage adds a touch of sweetness to his venison fillet, perfectly complementing the sweet-and-sour pickled red beets. His rich sauces are testament to his culinary expertise and generosity.

Name: De Haan
Description: Three friends have come up with an original concept: they prepare a single set menu in their open kitchen, serve the dishes themselves thus dispensing with the services of any additional waitstaff. Diners are responsible for getting their own bread and beverages. The chefs enthusiastically explain in detail how they creatively combine complex flavours. They do not shy away from contrasts, but always maintain the right balance. With a vegetarian Stroganoff – intensified by a sophisticated sauce based on Madeira, port and red wine – the chefs showcase their prowess.

Name: Nolet's Vistro
Description: Zeeland oysters, house-smoked salmon, the freshest sole cooked to perfection à la meunière: at Nolet's Vistro, the focus lies squarely on the quality of the ingredients. The chef celebrates the pure essence of the sea's bounty, presenting it without unnecessary embellishment. In this charming bistro by the dyke, simplicity is not a limitation but a deliberate choice. Generosity is woven into the very DNA of this longstanding favourite.

Name: Het Seminar
Description: Het Seminar is an ode to nature that adopts "farm to fork" as its guiding principle. A former monastery, this upscale restaurant stands in its own grounds. From fruit and vegetables to livestock, everything is grown or reared on site – the focus is on sustainability. The chef invites you to create your own set menu from an array of classic-style dishes that showcase bold flavours and the freshest ingredients. For example, he expertly pan-fries duck breast to a rosy pink, elevating it with a lemongrass-infused duck jus; this is served with vegetable accompaniments such as broad beans and caramelised onion, which provides a touch of sweetness. At Het Seminar, the fertility of the Dutch soil speaks for itself.

Name: Mei Wah
Description: Mei Wah has been a beacon of authentic Chinese cuisine since 1965. Unadulterated piquancy and finesse, unyielding to Western palates, and imbued with a touch of refinement by the chef, who represents the third generation at the helm. He makes just about everything in-house, from the spicy chicken broths to the fiery chilli oils, guaranteeing bold flavours. Whenever feasible, he procures ingredients from the vicinity. Immerse yourself in the culinary heritage of far-off lands – think steamed dim sum filled with prawn, ginger and that addictively delectable chilli oil, succulent spicy prawn in a typhoon shelter wok dish, the traditional Peking duck that the chef carves at your table. Wine or sake accompany your food.

Name: Aan Sjuuteeänjd
Description: Sustainability takes centre stage at this cosy farmhouse restaurant with its eye-catching designer lighting. Even before it was trendy, chef Thoma was working with organic produce, mostly from his own vegetable garden. He has now even planted a food forest for the future. This ambassador of local Limburg produce proposes only a surprise menu, demonstrating his close ties with small-scale suppliers. Think rosefish from the North Sea, a beautifully grainy spelt risotto and a spicy/tangy beurre blanc sauce with nettles.

Name: De Beejekurf
Description: De Beejekurf manages to blend a cosy, inviting atmosphere with sophisticated elegance. Hostess Hanneke's warm welcome and attentive service make dinners feel at ease right away. Chef Mathijs Jacobs allows his local suppliers to dictate what goes into his set menu. His creativity knows no bounds, yet his dishes, although made with an eye for detail, are remarkably straightforward. For example, he transforms poached veal tenderloin with its exquisite jus and sweetbreads into an interesting concoction with aubergine, a hollandaise sauce espuma, potato mousseline and truffle. This is cuisine that packs a punch!

Name: DIELS
Description: Dietmar and Elsko's bustling "Restobar" is a cosy, laid-back place where anything goes and nothing is compulsory. Drop in for a casual drink or settle in for a sumptuous dinner. The host presents an excellent wine selection at appealing prices, complementing the chef's à la carte offerings and popular surprise menu. Expect dishes such as kingfish sashimi with a punchy passion fruit and tarragon vinaigrette, medium-rare lamb with a robust lamb jus. This chef has an eye for detail and a solid grasp of the classics, occasionally drawing inspiration from Asia. Good times guaranteed!

Name: Lime
Description: The open kitchen immediately catches the eye at the contemporary Lime, which also has a charming veranda. A table by the kitchen is a must if you want to see accomplished chef Ysbrandt Wermenbol at work. He gives traditional dishes a carefully considered personal twist, often taking inspiration from Mediterranean and Asian cuisine. His surprising ideas dare to be complex, while retaining a sense of generosity and balance.

Name: La Mère Anne
Description: La Mère Anne is a huge business encompassing a range of activities. You can hire the venue for parties, spend the night in modern guestrooms, but above all, enjoy good food! The chef favours regional produce, which he showcases in contemporary dishes. These steer clear of frills, focusing instead on straightforward, delicious flavours.

Name: MARIO
Description: Established by Mario Uva in 1967, this elegant family-run restaurant has become a true institution. Today, his son Emilio and chef Sil Springorum continue the legacy, reinforcing its stellar reputation with a refined wine list and a set menu that brings a modern edge to classic Italian flavours. Here you might be tempted by a perfectly cooked piece of turbot with salted lemon and a beurre blanc made with Franciacorta sparkling wine, or ravioli filled with potato purée and Taleggio, finished with a sauce combining veal jus, foie gras, apple syrup and hazelnuts. The cooking is always marked by generosity and those distinctive Mediterranean accents, often presented with a playful touch. Smart guestrooms available for overnight stays.

Name: Harry's
Description: The luxury brasserie at Hotel Beaumont, a fixture in the Wyck neighbourhood since 1912, is as cosmopolitan as it is vibrant. French flair runs through the ambiance and the menu. International influences and vegetarian options show that the chefs are in tune with the times, without abandoning the classic principles of fine brasserie cooking. Whether you choose the monkfish à la meunière, medium-rare ribeye with an airy béarnaise sauce and freshly made chips or the decadent rum baba, you can expect generous dishes – seven days a week, for both lunch and dinner. Be sure to stop by The Founders Bar opposite Harry's for a stylish finale.

Name: Marque
Description: The open kitchen and spacious bar (which you can eat at) will grab your attention as soon as you walk into this former cheese warehouse (1618). The character of this property is enhanced by the elegant decor. Marque is proud of its Mediterranean soul, and the experienced head chef wins diners over with modern textures, delicate acidic touches, and all the panache and exuberance of the South.

Name: Noble Gastro House
Description: Noble Gastro House is both inviting and sleek, and a seat at the bar is perfect for watching the kitchen team up close. This is the kind of place where anything goes. Whether you're in the market for a quick bite or a multi-course dinner, you call the shots here! The set menu features a variety of interesting dishes, many of which can be ordered as either half or full portions. Monkfish fillet with an exquisite verjus beurre blanc, or al dente asparagus with morels that have been tossed in veal jus, accompanied by a buttery sauce with the subtle tartness of rhubarb: the familiar and the daring go hand in hand here. Drawing on a wealth of experience, the chefs delight in creating dishes with both high-end and everyday ingredients.

Name: Landgoed de Wilmersberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At Landgoed de Wilmersberg nature takes centre stage, beginning with a wonderful view of the landscape of Twente, both on the terrace and in the charming dining room. The chef makes vegetables the focus in his modern dishes. He is bold enough to present the occasional challenging combination, always applying the correct techniques.

Name: Zheng
Description: Zheng takes you back to the banquets of Imperial China. Through a parade of small dishes, often served on three plates, you will discover the traditions of the four main branches of Chinese cuisine. The succulent Peking duck, with its crispy skin, is deservedly a signature dish – it is heavenly when paired with hoisin sauce and the house-made sambal! The typical tableware and objets d'art (also for sale) add to this unique dining experience. Subtle cuisine which nonetheless offers a wealth of flavours.

Name: Lokaal
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nowadays, Villa Ruimzicht is both a hotel and home to this elegant, chic yet warm and welcoming restaurant. The name Lokaal can be translated as "classroom" and is a nod to the building's past as a school. But it is also much more than that: it reflects Bjorn Massop and his team's commitment to sustainability. They source everything from vegetables to meat and fish from local small-scale suppliers who share their values. This dining experience is a real education – you will learn that coffee grounds are used to lend earthy notes to a medlar and sherry dessert. Embracing a zero-waste philosophy fuels the chef's innovation. For example, by fermenting spruce in a vegetable broth, he creates a harmonious accompaniment to trout from De Smallert fish farm. The set menu is a celebration of the riches of the Achterhoek terroir.

Name: Buitenplaats Slangevegt
Description: The River Vecht is the star of the show at this warm and welcoming restaurant – the spacious riverside terrace alone is reason enough to book a table! Further enhancing the charm is the attentive service. The cuisine is playful and creative – classic combinations are revamped with inventive ideas and refined textures. The chef serves cold veal, for example, with a vibrant ensemble of sweet-and-sour accompaniments such as marinated vegetables, tempeh manis and grated coconut. He likes to create contrasts, for instance by introducing a spicy note into his sauces.

Name: Soigné
Description: At Soigné, which might be described as cosy and charming, you are in the right place to discover the contemporary culinary aspirations of Dennis Jong. He makes an impression by complementing familiar flavours with exotic ingredients and rich sauces. The adjoining room can be booked for private dinners.

Name: EN
Description: Whether you opt for one of the seven seats up at the counter or for a regular table, there is no escaping EN's vibrancy. This energy is also reflected in the food. The set menus introduce you to creative Japanese dishes including an original take on tuna sashimi. The à la carte options, on the other hand, are more traditional. Whatever you choose, you can count on the characteristic finesse and richness for which this cuisine is world-renowned. The extensive sake selection is terrific.

Name: Restaurant Renilde
Description: Renilde Hammacher-van den Brande served as a curator at the Museum Boijmans van Beuningen for many years and would no doubt have been proud of the restaurant that bears her name. Located in a creatively landscaped rooftop garden on the sixth floor of what is now Depot Boijmans, this place affords stunning views over the city. In the afternoon, the restaurant is reserved for museum visitors; in the evening, it opens its doors to everyone who wishes to discover chef De Jong's surprise menu. This creative chef has a penchant for vegetables and bold combinations. His culinary audacity shines through in his sublime combination of elderflower ice cream, the subtle bitterness of Belgian endive caramel and rhubarb root. Prepare to be blown away!

Name: Lilou
Description: This restaurant set in a row of townhouses in the centre of Goes evokes the spirit of Paris. Round marble-topped tables, high ceilings, tiled floors, French chansons – this bistro has it all. Both the tempting menu and the wines also draw on French tradition. Well-seasoned hand-cut steak tartare; pan-fried sea bream accompanied by a rich beurre blanc with fresh, zesty notes; a shellfish platter, or profiteroles with vanilla ice cream and chocolate sauce: diners are spoilt for choice! If in need of recommendations, ask the amiable hostess, who will be happy to help.

Name: Bisque
Description: At Bisque, everything is perfectly balanced: the understated luxury of the interior, the precision of the cuisine and the warmth of Sabrina, who welcomes every guest with ease. At the back, chef Niels Schievink runs his kitchen with a steady hand. Understated in style, precise in execution. A dish featuring langoustine immediately reveals his signature style: a perfectly cooked tail combined with carrot, yuzu and a soft bisque with subtle citrus nuances. And whether you finish with a classic soufflé or his own interpretation of tiramisu, this less-is-more approach to French cuisine and celebration of beautiful produce will stay with you.

Name: Les Salons
Address: Joseph Corneli Allée 1, Valkenburg, 6301 KK, Netherlands
Description: The Belle Époque allure of Les Salons is a feast for the eyes. The character of this old castle, the art and murals in the three historic rooms, the modern furniture, the terrace overlooking the meticulously trimmed gardens... Wow! (Psst: be sure to ask about the story behind the bullet hole in the two-way mirror). The chefs give French tradition a contemporary twist. Here, they understand the importance of rich sauces and playful nuances to bring the plate to life, such as that braised halibut fillet with a light mushroom emulsion and crispy parsnips, given just enough vibrancy by grating lemon zest over them.

Name: Lazuur
Description: Lazuur is cosy and welcoming. It's the kind of neighbourhood restaurant everyone wants close by. Chef Sherif Khalil loves rich bistro flavours and likes to add Portuguese or global nuances to them. For example, he cooks red mullet juicily in crispy filo pastry and pairs it with marinated ginger, a deep curry sauce with umami, a touch of yuzu and textures of Jerusalem artichoke. This cuisine is powerful and at times playful. The menu is appealing, as is the chef's menu. And to accompany all these delicacies, Lazuur also has an impressive collection of port and Portuguese wines.

Name: IJssel Restobar
Description: Part of the Pillows hotel, this stylish restaurant encapsulates the best of Deventer. Seating options include a lovely conservatory and a terrace overlooking the River IJssel – the perfect place from which to take in the city's skyline. Wouter van Leeuwen creates a menu that's simply irresistible. Timeless classics such as steak tartare are accompanied by contemporary creations that draw on international influences and feature playful textures. For instance, he serves a combination of North Sea crab, leek and carrot with an espuma and powdered tomato. Foodies are sure to be delighted by the wide range of options.

Name: Suzie's en Van Aken
Description: Chef Tom is no stranger to the concepts of nose-to-tail eating and zero waste. With a keen sense of the zeitgeist, this is a creative chef who draws inspiration from his extensive travels, especially to Asia. For example, a beurre blanc sauce with dashi that adds depth to a salty dish based on oyster and samphire. The jovial Suzanne plays her part, serving up excellent wine and dessert recommendations. The natural vibe of this cosy establishment will make your dinner that little bit more enjoyable.

Name: Morille
Description: At Morille, the warm and welcoming decor gives the impression that nature has taken root inside – and that is entirely by design. Floris Vriens works with ingredients from his own kitchen garden, wild foraging and local producers. He strives to source everything from within a 15km radius of the restaurant – a true taste of Zeeland! The core ingredient is prepared in such a way that its natural essence shines through, even if he likes to explore textures and well-rounded flavours. He brings the dish to life with a carrot tartare seasoned with herb oil, leek purée, zesty magnolia gel, grated egg yolk and a horseradish cream. His sauces and jus are also second to none. Anne, the hostess, supplies a wonderful array of juices.

Name: De Boet
Description: De Boet blends in perfectly with the picturesque harbour of Urk. Get yourself a table by the window of this revamped carpenter's workshop or, better yet, on the terrace. Seasoned chef Cees Kramer cooking is closely in step with the seasons; he has a penchant for seafood and delights in showcasing his contemporary flair. Think kingfish ceviche with a spicy Asian kick, or succulent, perfectly pan-seared sea bass elevated by an indulgent crab stock, dill and cream sauce. In winter, he likes to explore richer flavours in game dishes and stews.

Name: Katseveer
Description: Having taken over Katseveer, chef Leon Vermaire and maître d' and sommelier Paul Labruijere are steadily finding their feet. For many years, they have been working at this restaurant that showcases the best of what Eastern Scheldt has to offer. This former ferry waiting room commands stunning views of passing ships and the surrounding countryside.Zeeland produce reigns supreme in chef Vermaire's culinary world. Whether Zeeland venison or North Sea crab, top-notch, locally sourced ingredients play the starring role. His dishes – often really creative – are beautifully crafted and frequently use acidic Asian flavours for that fresh twist.

Name: 't Golfje
Description: Housed in a quintessential Terschelling farmhouse just outside Midsland, this is a charming restaurant where diners are made to feel right at home. The gorgeous natural surroundings not only foster a mood of tranquillity, but they also determine what ends up on your plate. Many of the ingredients are picked by the staff themselves or sourced from the restaurant's own vegetable garden. These then feature in modern dishes which also draw on Mediterranean and Asian influences. This is no-nonsense cuisine. Think a perfectly fried quail fillet, a robust chicken stock and Jerusalem artichoke in cream and deep-fried. Divine!

Name: Het Roode Koper
Address: Jhr. Dr. C.J. Sandbergweg 82, Leuvenum, 3852 PV, Netherlands
Description: At Het Roode Koper, diners are immersed in the fairytale setting of a romantic decor that exudes luxury and sophistication, set against fabulous English gardens and the forests of the Veluwe all around. Dennis van den Beld's cuisine is rather classical but in keeping with the times. This translates into fabulous sauces, an emphasis on the produce and creative garnishes. The excellent wine list offers both prestigious bottles and finds from small wineries.

Name: Japans restaurant Shiro
Description: Shiro has been famed for serving traditional Japanese cuisine since 1989. In this intimate restaurant you will discover all the delights of kaiseki-ryori cuisine – a traditional interplay of intense flavours and subtle textures. Sushi made with the finest rice and ultra-fresh fish (it's best to order sushi when you make your reservation), beautifully crispy shrimp tempura, a deeply aromatic teriyaki sauce... Accompanied by exciting sake recommendations courtesy of your hostess.

Name: Tante Kee
Description: Tante Kee is a firm favourite. Nestled on a scenic island accessible by ferry, its setting is picture-perfect, with small boats mooring right beside the terrace. The interior is stylish; the exterior has a magical atmosphere. The cuisine is in step with the times and enriched with subtle Asian accents. Think fresh, hand-cut veal tartare with a judicious touch of gochujang providing a spicy Korean kick and a Dutch soya jelly. Impeccable service rounds off the experience. This is one of those warmly inviting places where everything is just right.

Name: Hof van Herstal
Description: What used to be the guesthouse of Lilbosch Abbey is now a classic fine dining restaurant with bags of character. Martin Bruggeman takes great pride in his work, presenting his suggestions to guests and proving every day that he is a master of traditional cuisine. Try the game dishes, especially the venison – the chef slaughters the game himself and showcases the distinctive intense flavour of the meat. His generous sauces are the best evidence of his culinary skill. You can trust his judicious wine recommendations too.

Name: Restaurant De Ölliemölle
Description: Picture the scene: a table by the water, with water lilies floating nearby and an old-fashioned water wheel turning occasionally. Could it be more romantic? Rest assured that De Olliemölle is every bit as enchanting inside. Roel Sieverink has a soft spot for French cuisine and loves serving lobster straight from his lobster tank. The bisque here is full-bodied and spicy, the foie gras terrine is juicy and the veal jus with crispy sweetbreads is deliciously intense. The chef adds the odd modern twist to his classic dishes, introducing brighter flavours while maintaining the rich, hearty taste that his cuisine is known for.

Name: Faulk
Description: Menno and Monique don't need frills to impress – in their cosy, intimate neighbourhood bistro, they are simply themselves. Enhanced by skilful technique and carefully considered pairings that add excitement, their dishes let the ingredients shine. For instance, the succulent guinea fowl breast is served alongside a pastilla made from the bird's leg meat, with a rich jus seasoned with vadouvan spices, and accompaniments of pointed cabbage and celeriac for earthy undertones. Its depth is what truly sets this cuisine apart.

Name: Oxalis
Description: Prepare yourself to be blown away as you drive past fields full of red and white cabbages en route to this cosy little establishment housed in a former post office. Geoffrey van Melick cut his teeth at top-flight restaurants such as The Fat Duck and 't Nonnetje, and it shows in his selection of quality ingredients, the depth of his sauces and his meticulous garnishes. Take, for example, the perfectly pitched and beautifully reduced veal jus that accompanies the rich fillet of veal Rossini, with fine vegetable accompaniments that add their distinctive nuances. This chef proves that creativity need not be at odds with respect for tradition!

Name: Allemansgeest
Description: The Vliet canal provides the stunning backdrop to this stylishly decorated yet cosy farmhouse. The waterfront terrace (with mooring facilities) and the sight of the passing boats captures everyone's heart. This is a magical setting in which to discover a modern approach to French cuisine with occasional subtle exotic nuances. Savour classic lobster soup with crayfish and Cognac crème, or tuck into a medium-rare beef fillet with a bold red wine jus. Deciding whether to go à la carte or opt for the set menu (vegetarian version available) will be difficult!

Name: Elea
Description: Located in a grand building in the heart of The Hague, Elea is a modern restaurant with a Greek soul. This idea finds expression in a fabulous Mediterranean-style setting that incorporates natural materials. Takis Panagakis is an inventive chef who draws on Greek tradition, using ingredients such as smoked yoghurt, caper leaf and fava beans to lend his original creations an individual touch. Vegetables play an important role here, with top-notch vegetarian options, such as a celeriac Wellington. The charming Bibi is on hand to suggest some excellent wine pairings.

Name: Villa de Duinen
Address: Oude Zeeweg 74, Noordwijk aan Zee, 2202 CE, Netherlands
Description: Arriving at this Anglo-Norman-style villa (1902) feels like coming home. The cosy interior, reminiscent of a cottage, and the endearing personality of the hostess are irresistible. The youthful kitchen team favours a resolutely modern approach to cooking. They play with textures, allow the main ingredient to shine and sometimes come up with surprisingly imaginative ideas. Hand them a butternut squash, and they will turn it into something amazing, with great technical skill and subtle influences from around the globe.

Name: De Voetangel
Address: Rondehoep Oost 3, Ouderkerk aan de Amstel, 1191 KA, Netherlands
Description: This cosy family restaurant rises up out of the Ronde Hoep polder, from where it enjoys magnificent views across pastureland and streams. The chefs here veer more towards the traditional, although modern dishes are starting to creep into their cuisine. Organic, vegetarian and international options give the menu extra appeal.

Name: Restaurant De Lage Vuursche
Description: Set in a picturesque village between Hilversum and Amsterdam, De Lage Vuursche has been run by the Van Oosterom family since 1865. The charm of yesteryear lingers: authentic details such as wooden tables, antique crockery and a crackling stove lend character to this bustling restaurant, which fills for both lunch and dinner. The kitchen honours its classical French heritage, presenting generous portions that celebrate the sumptuous flavours of timeless dishes such as eggs Benedict and turbot with beurre noisette, capers and freshly cut chips. And what better than an Eton Mess to finish? Be sure to peruse the wine list, which is curated with the same expert care. This place has soul, and that is precisely what makes it so appealing.

Name: Pirandello
Description: Hotel Winselerhof and Restaurant Pirandello feel like an oasis of calm. This 16C manor farm sits in the Strijthagerbeek valley, surrounded by lush greenery. Pirandello fully embraces its setting, with a glass extension that affords wonderful views of the surrounding vineyards and a stork's nest. The menu sticks to traditional Italian fare, with the chef sprinkling in some more elaborate flourishes now and then. He does this, for example, by incorporating mostarda into the jus he serves with succulent duck breast. To really make the most of the gorgeous location, consider staying overnight.

Name: Sequenza
Description: The intimate Sequenza has won a place in the hearts of its many regulars, with a multi-course set menu rightly appreciated for its distinctive and at times inventive take on classic French cuisine. The chef's choice of top-tier ingredients reflects a deep command of the craft. Red mullet fillet with cherry tomatoes, jalapeño, crushed macadamia nuts, melon balls, a rich crab bisque emulsion and an indulgent hollandaise sauce with shaved tonka bean for a touch of spice – a dish that's likely to steal your heart, too.

Name: 't Havenmantsje
Description: A spot in the conservatory is an absolute must when you come to this restaurant in a converted courthouse – the view of the water and the passing boats is magnificent! The restaurant is open throughout the day, so you can come for lunch, high tea or dinner. The chef skilfully navigates his way between classic and modern culinary traditions. For instance, he won't do too much to a steak tartare, but then he will conjure up a vegetarian dish based on roasted fennel and an apple jus. Be sure to check out the Asian-inspired appetisers.

Name: Het Koetshuis
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The drive to this traditional house with a handsome thatched roof, deep in the woods, showcases the magnificent countryside of the Veluwe region. That same charm carries through to the terrace and the atmospheric interior. The cuisine is imaginative, built on playful textures and influences from around the globe. Picture Arctic char served with deep-fried kale and finely sliced green apple, as well as nasturtium, a cucumber pearl, tarragon ice cream and a herb-seasoned buttermilk sauce. The inspired wine recommendations hit the mark every time.

Name: Lyf's
Description: One of this neighbourhood restaurant's main assets is its convivial atmosphere. The commitment to quality is palpable on every plate that is brought to your table. Martijn Stroosma serves up beautifully presented dishes that showcase his creativity. This astute chef never goes over the top. For instance, he will mellow the combination of langoustine tail tempura and confit bacon with touches of mango and celeriac. He always strikes the right balance, including in the mouth-watering à la carte and lunch options.

Name: Gebr. Hartering
Description: Niek and Paul Hartering's cheerful establishment has the feel of a French bistro. Having become a beloved haunt for many Amsterdammers, the place is always packed – be sure to book! The menu features market-fresh fusion cuisine and, as you might expect, changes frequently, depending on what produce is at its best on any given day. A dish that perfectly exemplifies the chefs' culinary style is their rich chicken liver mousse with toasted brioche, pickled cauliflower and crispy chicken skin. Laid-back, fun and absolutely delicious.

Name: LIZ Restobar
Description: The wooden horse heads on the walls, the impressive chandeliers that call to mind the wheels of a horse-drawn carriage, the partitions between the tables: you can't help but notice that you're dining in the former stables of Amerongen Castle. The terrace overlooking the castle and gardens is breathtaking! The cuisine is characterised by its use of locally sourced ingredients, French cooking techniques and a global outlook. The duck gyoza in a rich game broth with marinated mushrooms and crispy scallions says it all!

Name: Vermeer
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Sebastian Baquero Garces has taken over the reins at this intimate designer restaurant, which is every bit as upmarket as the NH Collection Amsterdam Barbizon Palace, where it is located. A champion of the farm-to-table movement, the chef is passionate about using the freshest locally sourced ingredients, and his creativity shines through in every dish. Think thinly sliced ​​hamachi and zolderspek (aged smoky bacon) with a subtly smoky bacon jus infused with dashi and soy. His cooking is intricate and sometimes complex. And if you would rather not commit to the set menu, you can simply dine à la carte.

Name: Bistrotel 't Amsterdammertje
Description: Brimming with character, this building by the Vecht River is enchanting, but just wait until you're sitting on the terrace… At Bistrotel, you can truly escape the hustle and bustle for a while! Before you retire to your comfortable guestroom, be sure to pop into the spacious bistro downstairs. André Gerrits has assembled a team here who know their way around bistro classics and flavours from all over the world. With options on the menu such as steak tartare, spicy rendang or farmhouse chicken from the spit; this is the kind of place where anything goes.

Name: Sinck
Description: Locals and tourists alike love to meet up at this bustling place. This old building on the Prinsengracht boasts a charming waterfront terrace and a lovely bistro-style interior. The renowned wine list (there is a wine bar at basement level) and modern culinary creations complement each other perfectly. The chef has a no-nonsense approach to cooking – a few elements that are full of flavour plus sauces for a fine accompaniment. This is Amsterdam at its coolest!

Name: Brasserie van Baerle
Description: There is no getting around it: wine is part of the core business of this elegant, ever-inviting luxury brasserie. The impressive selection of wines by the glass and extensive drinks menu will impress even the most seasoned connoisseur. Classics from the brasserie repertoire are served up here with great attention to detail and a sense of generosity. The steak tartare is a real crowd pleaser.

Name: Ledeboer
Description: Ledeboer has been housed in a stately former bank building since 1994, and its elegant industrial decor provides the perfect backdrop for its fine dining concept. The chef champions a modern style of cooking distinguished by meticulous presentation, and relishes working with premium ingredients. For instance, he pan-fries turbot in butter to a succulent finish then tops it with Limburg pork ham and complements it with a Jerusalem artichoke cream, tarragon espuma and a delicate fennel salad. Should time not allow for the full set menu (also available in a vegetarian version), the dishes can be ordered à la carte.

Name: Tollius
Description: With its sleek decor done out in burgundy and white and contemporary artwork on the walls, Tollius has an inviting feel. This is also down to chef Barry's expertise in producing hearty classics such as his wonderfully crispy pithivier filled with a rich combination of quail, foie gras and morels. But he is just as adept at whipping up a surprisingly zesty modern dessert involving wasabi and a lemon gel. If the extensive wine list is anything to go by, this place is certainly run by people with excellent taste.

Name: Beulings
Description: This warm, intimate restaurant is nestled in a quaint little street in the capital city. Bas cooks solo in the open kitchen while Lisja charms diners with her charisma and outstanding wine recommendations. The set menu showcases the chef's wealth of experience through elegant compositions and harmonious flavours. French foundations meet Cantonese influences in dishes such as beautifully seared Ibérico secreto accompanied by subtly smoked king trumpet mushrooms, a cashew cream, dumplings with a creamy minced pork filling and a peppered pork sauce. For foodies, Beulings is a home from home.

Name: Blumé
Description: At Blumé, familiar ingredients are given an unexpected twist. For instance, Jerusalem artichoke is used to impart an earthy quality to a chocolate dessert; cardamom lends spicy depth to celeriac – unconventional ideas meet skilful preparation with exciting results. Head to this elegant restaurant on the edge of Groningen's city centre to discover the set menu for yourself!

Name: Locals
Description: Housed in the same building as Hotel Haarhuis, just across from Arnhem Central train station, Locals boasts a cosmopolitan atmosphere. Ingredients are sourced as locally as possible, according to the principles of Dutch Cuisine. The abundance of plants and warm colours reflects that philosophy. Upstairs, there is even a vertical farm. The chef delights in working with vegetables, eg incorporating lentils from the Netherlands into a curry with herbs from the farm, seasonal vegetables and briny seaweed, and most of the fish and meat are locally sourced. . This place really lives up to its name!

Name: Ambrozijn
Description: Previously a church, Irenekerk (1891) is now a restaurant. Here, design reigns supreme, with a stylish blend of soft and raw materials. The newly built roof truss immediately catches the eye, as do the rugged black walls. Downstairs, the chef's table encircles the completely open kitchen; on the upper floor, there is a magnificent bar built in the shape of an organ. This place is all the more exceptional because of the way Sven Nijenhuis draws on French cooking styles and innovative techniques. With exquisite sauces and precisely judged seasonings, he makes his mark. Think slow-cooked pork cheeks with glazed aubergine, mayonnaise finished with Thai basil, subtly spicy baba ganoush and a veal jus elevated with fenugreek. Simply divine!

Name: MANO Restaurant
Description: Hermanos Daniël and Kevin have been best friends since childhood. In their elegant corner-plot restaurant, which retains the building's original charm, they showcase their combined expertise. The refinement and meticulous attention to detail in the amuse-bouches immediately convey the chefs' ambition. Their resolutely contemporary menu features bold international influences in dishes such as perfectly seared scallops with tender pork belly and an intense bah kut teh sauce made from beef and pork ribs. The front-of-house team provide service with a warm, personal touch. At Mano, technical precision, creativity and hospitality seamlessly come together.

Name: Eetkamer Lamens
Description: This spacious brasserie has a subtle industrial aesthetic, but its atmosphere is nonetheless thoroughly warm and welcoming. In fine weather, the inviting terrace beckons. On the enticing menu, familiar favourites such as steak tartare feature alongside Mediterranean, South American and Asian dishes. Whether through subtle heat, a refreshing lift of acidity or a full-bodied sauce, the chefs set themselves apart. A shining example is chicken breast from the Josper charcoal oven, topped with a fragrant bumbu Bali, brightened by sambal and a finely balanced sweet-and-sour salad of peanut, carrot and apple. The freedom to compose your own set menu from the à la carte options adds further appeal.

Name: Rozewied
Description: Rozewied, "poppy" in Zeelandic, is the joint venture of Ferdy and Noëmie. The two of them do everything themselves in this centuries-old building, into which they have breathed new life, while taking care to preserve its historical character. In the kitchen, classical combinations are given a modern twist. Lamb, for example, is paired with garlic, but with the lightness and playfulness expected by today's diners. The chefs give pride of place to European produce, and have a penchant for fish dishes and delicate sauces.

Name: Restaurant Le Sable
Description: The charm of tranquil Zandoerle permeates this old farmhouse, where rusticity meets stylish intimacy in perfect harmony. Hostess Laura comes outside to give diners a warm welcome and, with her team, provides impeccable service. She draws on a wealth of experience and talent despite her young age (she also makes the delicious sweet treats served with the coffee!). The same goes for chef Chiel, whose dishes reflect youthful energy. Although he draws primarily on French culinary tradition, the chef likes to add his own twist, serving dishes in a series of small plates. For instance, he stuffs sole fillets with a fish farce and serves them with exquisite beurre blanc, then he also fries the tail à la meunière and pairs it with vegetable ratatouille. The palpable sense of ambition at Le Sable makes it all the more appealing.

Name: On Cru
Description: Housed in a listed building, this restaurant with its exposed brick walls is reminiscent of old England. Think Chesterfield chairs, a striking semi-circular counter and dimmed lighting. Kelvin de Pijper's classic market-fresh cuisine lets the ingredients take centre stage, for example, pairing freshly caught cod with a velvety creamed sauce made with fish fumet. Crispy sweetbreads are given a glossy finish with a veal reduction infused with cardamom, lovage and pink peppercorns. This chef honours the natural flavours of the produce while adding subtle, measured nuances. A real gem at the picturesque old port.

Name: Alma Bodega
Description: The more down-to-earth little brother of MICHELIN-starred Alma has its own personality. Chic marble and stylish design give this laid-back restaurant flair. You can drop in any time of day to indulge in a fresh take on familiar flavours. The menu features a variety of dishes that will tempt your taste buds, including gyoza, köfte, pâté en croûte, perfectly done entrecôte with a delicious veal jus, rum baba and more. The skilfully prepared and generously flavoured dishes never fail to impress. The wine list always includes some exciting finds. Be sure to make your reservation in good time to avoid disappointment!

Name: Bar BAUT
Description: With its Banksy-style frescoes, trendy, intimate interior and delightfully relaxed ambience, Bar BAUT is a must in Amsterdam, where guests can choose from the enticing à la carte featuring international ingredients cooked in contemporary style. Enjoy intense flavours, well-prepared produce and original ideas – plus excellent value for money!

Name: Watergang
Description: Set in a quintessential Amsterdam terraced house, Watergang is a charming little establishment that radiates genuine warmth and bohemian spirit. The chefs frequently change their single surprise menu, shifting between French, Italian and even Asian influences. Think gazpacho with tomato, peach and horseradish ice cream, followed by finely sliced, lightly marinated mackerel in a wonderful dashi broth. Inspired, occasionally playful creations that truly deliver.

Name: de Wanne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Part of the elegant Parkhotel de Wiemsel, De Wanne boasts a splendid terrace overlooking the grounds. Inside, the linen, silver and attentive front-of-house team lend the setting a classically elegant feel. Chef Jan Huiskes serves dishes that are rooted in French culinary tradition and incorporate international influences. Think classic beef tartare with Twickel cheese and truffle cream, or saddle of lamb with a shallot and lamb sauce and crispy pommes dauphine. A dependable choice for those who enjoy refined dining in peace and comfort.

Name: De Monnikendam
Description: Originally part of Amersfoort's second city wall, Monnickendam is a watergate dating back to the early 15C. Today, this piece of history has been repurposed to create a unique culinary destination. There are intimate dining spaces within the towers and a waterside terrace affording wonderful views. Thanks to the enthusiasm of hostess Kristel and chef Richard, this establishment has made a name for itself. With each course, the tasting menu seamlessly navigates between the familiar and the exotic: Think hamachi accompanied by a tangy ponzu, or lamb saddle with a crispy crust and a lamb jus infused with rosemary, thyme and wild garlic oil. A memorable dining experience!

Name: Héroine
Description: Housed in an industrial building, this restaurant has a unique feel on account of its decor incorporating retro features and modern design, as well as striking artwork on the walls. The surprise menu showcases exciting combinations, international influences and vegetables. The chef serves crispy breaded scallops, for instance, on a delicate passion fruit cream, finishing the dish with a butter sauce enhanced with coconut and dill. His bold and innovative creations will leave you craving more.

Name: JanZen
Description: Housed in a lovely, meticulously refurbished Art Deco building surrounded by polders, JanZen is a place where you can unwind and dine in good company. Hostess Natasja provides attentive service; chef Jeroen's dishes are beautifully presented and packed with exciting flavours. Order à la carte, or opt for the surprise menu to explore his intricate creations. Think sea bass remoulade with vibrant cucumber and radish garnishes, as well as a clear tomato broth – a true delight for both the eye and the palate.

Name: De Herberg van Smallingerland
Description: Dating back to 1791, this charming inn is full of character and extremely popular. Tables in the gorgeous courtyard garden are in high demand, as are the guestrooms. With a special emphasis on vegetables, Chef Freddy and son Jurmen showcase Frisian cuisine at its best. For instance, they will draw on the distinct flavours of beetroot, cherries and capers to give a fillet of red mullet a special twist. The menu at de Herberg is full of surprises!

Name: Ratatouille
Description: Ratatouille is cosy and convivial, and its spacious terrace on the historical Vischmarkt is understandably very popular. Hostess Cindy and chef Gerwin have gained a loyal following in a short period of time, and that is more than deserved. Whether you order à la carte or take a punt on the surprise menu, the value for money is second to none. The versatile chef is just as likely to serve up an oven-baked fillet of red mullet with a rich white wine sauce and a zingy antiboise as a vegetarian pie with sweet and sour nuances. His cuisine is sophisticated and very much on trend, and he puts a lot of thought into his vegetable accoutrements and his choice of suppliers.

Name: Bar Beurre
Description: Once a traditional café, this place is now a no-nonsense bistro, complete with upbeat background music. Bar Beurre certainly lives up to its name.
