Description: Here, where the Parma river once broke its banks, you’ll find an attractive trattoria with pleasant dining rooms and excellent cuisine cooked over a wood and herb fire, one of the oldest culinary techniques in the world. The main courses feature meat only, with an extensive number of dishes on the menu. Among the home-made desserts, we recommend the fior di latte ice-cream, which is served with a choice of delicious sauces.

Name: Lillotatini
Description: Situated in the heart of a small medieval castle-hamlet, this traditional-style restaurant with an attractive terrace on the historic square provides the setting for local specialities such as freshwater fish and truffles in season. There’s also a wine boutique on the same piazza (reached as soon as you come into the historic centre), which sells typical local produce and a good selection of wine. The latter also features on the restaurant’s wine list, with the family on hand to offer recommendations.

Name: Al Fogher
Address: strada statale 117 bis, Piazza Armerina, 94015, Italy
Description: This small, rustic-style restaurant just outside the centre of Piazza Armerina serves personalised cuisine in which local ingredients take pride of place. Influences from elsewhere in Italy are also evident, with dishes such as artichoke pansotti (stuffed pasta) with local tuma cheese and black truffles on the menu.

Name: Hanswirt
Description: Occupying a former post-house, this restaurant boasts dining rooms decorated in Tyrolean style, as well as a large veranda-style room. Although the focus here is on local ingredients (especially vegetables and meat such as goat kid and lamb raised on the restaurant’s own farm in the Senales valley) and freshwater fish, the menu also features the occasional Mediterranean speciality, such as the excellent braised aubergine tartare with burrata, focaccia and basil-flavoured olive oil. There’s also a hotel of the same name, which is housed in an attractive old building to the rear of the restaurant.

Name: Il Rivale al Lago
Address: via Marconi 93, Padenghe sul Garda, 25080, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lake, this multi-faceted restaurant serves classic Italian dishes, often with a creative twist, alongside top-quality international ingredients such as Cantabrian anchovies and Japanese Wagyu beef. Grilled meats and vegetable dishes also make an appearance on the menu.

Name: Cielo
Description: In the white city of limestone stairways, at the highest point of the village, a skillfully restored ancient residence houses a splendid relais that – fittingly – bears the name La Sommità. The gourmet restaurant Cielo welcomes guests with romantic summer dinners among the citrus trees of the small inner courtyard, or in the barrel-vaulted dining room, where the atmosphere is intimate and evocative. The menu offers a modern reinterpretation of Apulian cuisine: not to be missed are the stewed catalogna with grilled lamb offal and sweet-and-sour lampascioni, or the pasta cooked in spicy tomato water, served with raw red mullet and chervil. At aperitivo hour, it is worth ascending to the splendid terrace to take in the sunset, while at lunch the offering becomes simpler, designed for a lighter yet always refined experience.

Name: I Sette Consoli
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In this simple restaurant boasting an attractive outdoor summer garden and splendid views of the Duomo, chef Anna Rita focuses on carefully selected ingredients from the region and beyond. Highlights include soft egg, pan-fried courgettes and spring onions, and pecorino crumble, as well as soft veal rump, Jerusalem artichoke sauce and home-made pickled vegetables. The wine and spirits selection is particularly appealing – as an example, the Orvieto Classico Superiore Doc “Vendemmia Tardiva” is the perfect pairing for your dessert.

Name: L'Archivolto - Osteria Nostrale
Description: Situated on Ovada’s main square, this restaurant has the pleasant friendly ambience of an attractive trattoria, while its menu takes guests on a delicious culinary journey through the Piedmont region, including local specialities such as home-made tajarin pasta, braised beef in Ovada wine with mashed potato, and the local bunet dessert (finanziera stew also makes an occasional appearance). The restaurant is also a wine bar/boutique offering a selection of wines, including different Barolo labels (presented area by area) and aperitifs served both at lunchtime and dinner.

Name: Gino Sorbillo
Description: In the heart of Spaccanapoli, on the famous “via della pizza”, an institution with an international feel welcomes guests into simple, rustic surroundings steeped in authentic Neapolitan energy. The choice of pizzas, enriched with excellent P.D.O. ingredients, is endless. You'll need to be patient during peak hours and, if you happen to find yourself sharing a table, embrace the magic of Neapolitan friendliness!

Name: Prato Gaio
Address: Località Versa, bivio per Volpara, Montecalvo Versiggia, 27047, Italy
Description: The restaurant trade is in the family genes: already an inn in the 19C, the Prato Gaio takes inspiration from the cuisine of the Oltrepò region. A selection of traditional specialities alongside dishes reinterpreted with flair and imagination are served. An essential stop for anyone looking for local flavour.

Name: Boccon DiVino
Address: via Traversa dei Monti 201, località Colombaio Tozzi, Montalcino, 53024, Italy
Description: In a farmhouse on the edges of town, this restaurant has a rustic dining area with modern tables and chairs and a beautiful summer terrace with a view. Authentic local dishes.

Name: Trattoria di Coronate
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a splendid 16C farmhouse just a few minutes from the beautiful Morimondo abbey, this restaurant has an elegant and friendly ambience. The wooden ceiling and furniture in the dining room gives it a warm and welcoming feel, while the cuisine, deeply rooted in the region, is reinterpreted with a contemporary twist. The delicious options on the menu include highlights such as quail breast with a thigh-meat “lollipop” and ravioli stuffed with braised beef.

Name: Alla Corte Lombarda
Description: Housed in a restored hay barn on the edge of the village, this charming rustic restaurant offers traditional cuisine with a modern twist, a good selection of wine and an excellent choice of beer. Every week, the menu features five records which played a major role in the history of music or which represent an important moment in time for the restaurant owner.

Name: Aimo e Nadia BistRo
Description: A small jewel of elegance and refinement, where the celebrated starred establishment has chosen to offer a simpler, more relaxed cuisine without sacrificing precision or identity. The menu gathers national classics reinterpreted through a contemporary lens – the signature saffron risotto with ossobuco reduction and warm zabaione served with cinnamon ladyfinger cookies are both essential – alongside a tempting selection of shareable dishes. Among these, the gnocco fritto with Colonnata lard and the celebrated mondeghili meatballs stand out, perfect for pairing with one of the cocktails from a list crafted specifically to complement the kitchen’s offerings.

Name: Il Giardino "Da Felicin"
Description: A bastion of classic Piedmontese cuisine, this restaurant housed in a beautiful period palazzo boasts a panoramic terrace and a romantic garden for alfresco dining. The dining rooms echo the palazzo’s sumptuous and traditional feel, as does the timeless, regional cuisine which is carefully prepared and full of delicious flavours. The building is also home to an “albergo diffuso” hotel, with some guestrooms in the building itself and others dotted around the village, including in Palazzo Boeri which also has a small spa (reservation required). The owners are happy to share their knowledge of the Langhe, either on their own guided tours or visits led by another local expert.

Name: Le Vele
Address: via Litoranea Sud 71, Bagni 70, Misano Adriatico, 47843, Italy
Description: This modern, minimalist - style restaurant is practically on the beach and almost within touching distance of the sea. It specialises in fish dishes with a contemporary flavour.

Name: Menegaldo
Address: via Pralongo 216, Monastier di Treviso, 31050, Italy
Description: Menegaldo is a long-established favourite for anyone who loves authentic fish dishes made from top-quality ingredients. Although it feels as though time has stood still in the pleasantly old-fashioned dining room, with its outmoded decor and furnishings, the service here is attentive and enthusiastic. The dishes are traditional and typical of the area, making this an excellent choice for delicious seafood cuisine that is elaborate without being overly fussy.

Name: Locanda Perbellini
Description: Highly renowned in his native Verona, Michelin - starred chef Giancarlo Perbellini has now opened a restaurant in Milan, where he continues to offer traditional Italian cuisine from the north and south of the country, with a nod to new techniques and contemporary trends. Situated in the central Brera district, his warm and welcoming restaurant is small, discreet and, of course, highly elegant.

Name: Marina del Nettuno
Address: viale della Libertà-Batteria Masotto, Messina, 98121, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant and lounge bar is situated right on the jetty of the Yachting Club Messina. Elegant and minimalist - style decor, as well as creative cuisine with a focus on fish dishes.

Name: Josè - Tenuta Villa Guerra
Address: via Nazionale 414, Torre del Greco, 80059, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: 2025 has seen a change at the helm in the kitchen at this restaurant, in line with the new approach introduced by its enthusiastic owners. The full focus now is on the flavours of Campania, served in lighter versions and reinterpretations of traditional recipes. This is the case with the legendary Santa Rosa dessert, which has been transformed into a millefeuille made with the same ingredients as the original dish, namely crispy puff pastry, custard and sour cherries in syrup. Situated in one of the extraordinary villas on Herculaneum’s “Golden Mile”, the restaurant boasts an elegant dining room within this 18C building, as well as a room overlooking the villa gardens where pizzas are served from mid spring to late summer. Wine-enthusiasts will be pleased to hear that the wine cellar continues to offer an extensive selection of superb labels.

Name: San Lorenzo
Description: Situated within the Clitunno hotel, this well-managed family-run restaurant serves classic, seasonal meat and fish dishes, including generous portions of black truffles in some dishes. Recently refurbished, the intimate, elegant dining room also occasionally features live music at weekends, while the outdoor terrace on the small square offers pleasant alfresco dining. Guests are advised to park outside the ZTL (restricted traffic zone) and make their way on foot, via a short walk through the beautiful historic centre.

Name: Particolare di Siena
Description: A fine-dining restaurant which changed tack in 2020, reducing its number of tables to just ten and embracing a sustainable approach to its cuisine. It now prioritises local suppliers and certified organic and environmentally friendly ingredients, while the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, featuring produce grown in line with biodynamic techniques, provides some of the best seasonal ingredients used in the dishes here.

Name: Alpes
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A warm and welcoming setting, where hospitality stands out for its authenticity and attention to detail. The kitchen, under the direction of chef Matthias Kirchler, presents creative, refined dishes designed for those who love to experiment and be surprised. The gastronomic offering has been recently refreshed and now unfolds in two distinct journeys: “Alpes 1988” and “Alpes – Locanda” for culinary experiences that narrate the territory with contemporary flair.

Name: Il Favri
Address: via Borgo Meduna 12, San Giorgio della Richinvelda, 33095, Italy
Description: This inn, which has been serving food since the early 19C, boasts a warm atmosphere with a rustic feel. The beautiful garden makes a delightful setting in fine weather, while the cuisine focuses on traditional dishes from Friuli, such as “frico” (potato, onion and cheese fritter) and cured ham.

Name: Trattoria Ceriati
Address: Località Cangelasio Ceriati 18, Salsomaggiore Terme, 43039, Italy
Description: Situated in attractive countryside where the plains give way to rolling hills (a perfect destination for a Sunday outing), this simple yet well-kept trattoria serves all the usual traditional local specialities. The typical fresh pasta and the desserts are all home-made.

Name: Villa Arcadio
Address: via Palazzina 2, località Villa di Salò, Salò, 25087, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant prioritises beautiful presentation in his modern interpretations of Italian dishes, which are even more enjoyable in summer when meals are served outdoors, surrounded by greenery and with fine views of the southern part of Lake Garda and its shoreline.

Name: I Tigli
Description: An iconic pizzeria which has brought Italy’s favourite street-food snack right up to date! With almost 30 years’ experience behind him, Simone Padoan knows how to make difficult things easy: he uses a mix of wholemeal flours and pays meticulous attention to natural leavening processes to create a dough which has a crispy crust yet soft interior. He also focuses on different types of toppings, including fish, meat and vegetables – whether your preference is for traditional or more imaginative pizzas, every option is of the highest quality. A choice of excellent desserts provides the perfect conclusion to your meal!

Name: Mater Terrae
Description: Situated on the top floor of the Raphaël hotel just behind Piazza Navona, this restaurant serves some of the best vegetarian cuisine in Rome. Each of the elaborate dishes boasts numerous ingredients and every single course is a delightful surprise. Equally stunning is the panoramic terrace overlooking the city’s rooftops, where meals are served in fine weather.

Name: Il Tartufo
Description: Housed in a small villa in the residential area of the village, this intimate and secluded restaurant serves delicious cuisine with distinctly regional roots. In season, locally sourced truffles take centre stage, while fish and seafood dominate the menu at other times of year.

Name: Osteria del Tempo Perso
Description: Situated in a hidden corner of the historic centre, this small bistro-style restaurant has a friendly and welcoming atmosphere, with photos alternating with books, wine bottles and glasses on the walls (the wine list includes a few labels from elsewhere in Europe). Small tables set close together, warm, subtle lighting and an almost Parisian ambience make this a perfect choice for a romantic dinner or a meal with friends. There’s also a small outdoor space for fine weather but seats are limited, so it’s best to book ahead!

Name: L'Acciuga
Description: A reliable city destination for seafood, the venue welcomes guests in nautical-themed surroundings that evoke the interiors of vintage ships. The ingredients are fresh and fragrant, interpreted through tradition and then elevated in personal recipes: raw scallops with cannellini beans, onion, and rosemary; anchovy spaghetti with crispy bread and lemon; monkfish ossobuco. The wine list is complemented by a playful selection of cocktails and kombucha offered at the Bar counter. A maritime atmosphere and warm Romagnolo hospitality round out an experience that delivers on every front.

Name: Acaja
Description: Central, elegant and modern, the cuisine of Acaja winds along two lines: the traditional regional one, with ravioli del plin, cardi gobbi, Piedmont veal and hazelnuts to mention just a few that cannot be missed, but also various fish dishes that are truly remarkable, with a touch of contemporaneity, starting with excellent raw materials.

Name: Da Vincenzo
Description: It's never easy to find the right balance between quality and quantity, especially in a town that is very much on the tourist trail. However, Da Vincenzo has succeeded in doing just this for years, ever since it was first opened by the family’s grandfather Vincenzo in 1958. Today, the founder’s grandson (who shares his grandfather’s name) is at the helm here, creating dishes which focus mainly on fish. Pleasant atmosphere, with a few small tables on the pavement of the street that runs through the centre of Positano. A choice of cocktails supplements the wine selection from lunchtime onwards.

Name: La Corte
Address: via San Pancrazio 41, Palazzolo sull'Oglio, 25036, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in a tranquil street that leads to the centre of Palazzolo sull’Oglio, this stylish restaurant in a 16C palazzo boasts classic elegance and authentic cuisine which is delicious and full of flavour. Here, Aldo and his wife offer guests a warm and informal welcome, always with a smile on their lips.

Name: Essenza Bistrot
Description: A welcoming, original and well-cared for bistro-style restaurant with an intimate feel, where the stone walls are typical of the region’s architecture. Here, chef Massimiliano Villani is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates contemporary cuisine with a focus on regional ingredients. His imaginative flair is also evident in his desserts, which include a liquorice cigar with cocoa nibs and rum. An interesting wine list and attractive outdoor space complete the picture.

Name: La Palomba
Description: Boasting the attractive ambience of a typical Italian trattoria, La Palomba has been run by the Cinti family since 1965 and is now in the hands of the third generation. The menu features Umbrian specialities including delicious home-made umbrichelli pasta served with various sauces.

Name: Tola Rasa
Description: This elegant, minimalist-style restaurant serves two tasting menus (Classici and Contemporanei – the names tell you all you need to know!) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. When we ate there in late autumn, we particularly enjoyed the rabbit with saffron and porcini mushrooms prepared in the open-air kitchen. There are just a few beautifully laid tables, plus a wine list that includes a selection of labels from Italy and France.

Name: Da Miky
Address: via Fegina 104, Monterosso al Mare, 19016, Italy
Description: Situated right on the seafront, Miky is one of the best restaurants for fish (including the famous Monterosso anchovies) in the region, serving cuisine which is more and more exciting and individual every year. There’s also a small shop selling local produce.

Name: Caruso Roof Garden
Description: In a city already rich with rooftop restaurants, this address stands out as one of the most prestigious, both for its clientele and for its panoramic views: Castel dell’Ovo, Capri, the Sorrento Coast, and Vesuvius. Besides the sea! Chef Petrosino loves to express himself through several tasting menus; for those who prefer it, à la carte options are also available. Whatever the choice, Campanian products take center stage: abundant seafood, vegetables, and even some meat, all accompanied by the professionalism of excellent service and the breathtaking beauty of the Gulf of Naples as a backdrop.

Name: Osteria Il Maialetto
Address: via Della Repubblica 348, Monsummano Terme, 51015, Italy
Description: This lively restaurant with a young, vibrant atmosphere stands next to the butcher’s shop run by the same family. The menu features delicious Tuscan cuisine, including dishes such as pappa al pomodoro and Florentine steak, which you choose from the display counter. Good wines and friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: La Notizia 53
Description: Although situated away from the tourist centre, Enzo Coccia’s pizzeria continues to be considered one of the best places for pizza in Campania. Featuring classic Neapolitan pizzas with soft, stringy dough, the menu offers traditional and creative toppings alike. The “'mpustarella”, a five-grain and wholemeal flour roll with different fillings, more than compensates for the lack of “fritti” on the menu. The first historic restaurant at number 53 has now been joined by a second address at number 94/a nearby.

Name: Controcorrente
Address: via XXV Luglio 23, Morciano di Romagna, 47833, Italy
Description: A welcoming restaurant with a rustic - style dining room, a young, lively atmosphere and beautifully prepared dishes with an emphasis on fish – it is difficult not to be impressed!

Name: SaQua by Il Frantoio
Description: This restaurant, previously known simply as “Il Frantoio”, now has new out-of-town premises but any regret you may have at leaving the town centre will soon disappear, thanks to the wide range of modern Tuscan dishes prepared by the chefs in the new, larger kitchen. A further attraction is the outdoor space which boasts beautiful sunset views in summer.

Name: Fattoria delle Torri
Description: A slice of paradise in Modica’s historic center: delightful terrace service among the lemon trees and a professional legacy carried on by chef-patron Peppe Barone's daughters – Carla in the dining room and Francesca in the kitchen – who, with youthful energy, champion a highly original gastronomic offering that balances innovation with tradition. They draw freely from the island’s culinary history, enriching it with exotic touches often characterized by gently spiced flavors. The wine program is equally impressive: guests can confidently rely on their recommendations to discover something special from an excellent wine list.

Name: Zero Milano
Description: “Zero” compromises when it comes to care and quality: the cuisine here is built on exceptional ingredients and rigorous Japanese technique. Under the guidance of Hide Shinohara, the crew presents pure Japanese gastronomy, centered on the highest quality products and the art of form. Beyond the à la carte, the Omakase tasting menu is highly recommended, where the chefs construct a blind journey of great interest and refinement. The dining room features white onyx panels, elegant minimalism, and soft lighting; at the traditional counter, in addition to observing the chefs’ dexterity up close, you can opt for a tasting prepared in the moment, further elevating the sensory experience.

Name: Dimora Ulmo
Description: The three tasting menus (Contaminazioni, Dimora Ulmo and A mano libera) served at this restaurant housed in an old restored palazzo with a splendid summer terrace overlooking the Sassi feature a balance of modern cuisine and traditional local dishes. The dining room is equally attractive, while the interesting wine list includes labels from the region alongside a selection of wines from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Trattoria Al Passo
Description: Successive generations of the same family have run this pleasant restaurant just outside the city for over 70 years. Enjoy a selection of fish and seafood dishes (raw, grilled or fried with numerous condiments to accompany your starters) in a maritime themed dining room or on the light and airy veranda. There is a good selection of desserts to round off your meal.

Name: Osaka
Description: A new home for this historic restaurant, with minimalist interiors that embrace a full‑on oriental aesthetic to showcase authentic Japanese cuisine. A set menu at lunch and à la carte at dinner from which we recommend the Makimoto rolls of amberjack with shiso leaves, sesame seeds and freshly marinated wasabi. Or the festive Sukiyaki, a Japanese take on a bourguignon where meat and vegetables are cooked in a simmering broth at the table and shared among guests. The menu is extensive and rich with other succulent offerings from the Land of the Rising Sun.

Name: Rovello
Description: Although it has a new venue, this restaurant has retained its attractive friendly feel in a dining room that acts as a backdrop for substantial dishes that are full of flavour. The interesting classic menu is supplemented by a selection of daily specials, with meat, fish and vegetables (some grilled) prepared in front of guests seated at the counter. There are also traditional tables available and the lively atmosphere remains that of a friendly, welcoming bistro. Interesting wine list, including a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Il Liberty
Description: Nestled in an Art Nouveau palazzo just a short walk from Porta Nuova, the restaurant offers a welcoming yet refined atmosphere: a main dining room, a romantic balcony, a small open‑kitchen lounge, and a communal “social table.” The Mediterranean‑inspired menu showcases both sea and land. The standout seafood dish is the “super chitarrino” pasta, a tribute to Abruzzese tradition dressed in a Sicilian‑style sauce of fresh anchovies, saffron, raisins, pine nuts, and toasted bread with anchovies. On the meat side, a premium Milanese veal cutlet arrives with crisp fresh‑cut potato chips, house‑made ketchup and honey‑mustard.

Name: Al Segnavento
Address: via Gatta 76/c, località Santa Lucia di Tarù, Zelarino, 30174, Italy
Description: An elegant restaurant run by an entire family, whose philosophy could be summed up in the phrase “from farm to fork”. Fruit, vegetables, mutton, lamb, pork, plus a delicious breed of duck are all showcased in this zero-kilometre restaurant. If you’re looking for simpler fare and wine by the carafe, the restaurant also has a more informal bistro nearby. Charming guestrooms also available for visitors wanting to prolong their stay.

Name: Pacifico
Description: Although its dining rooms are fairly small, this restaurant, which acts as an ambassador for Peruvian cuisine with the occasional Asian influence, has an attractive, trendy ambience and a theatrical feel. Excellent choice of ceviche – raw fish or seafood dishes marinated in lemon and flavoured with spices such as chilli pepper and coriander – which are a typical speciality of Latin American countries along the Pacific coast.

Name: La Cantina di Manuela
Description: The dining room in this young, dynamic restaurant is surrounded by bottles of wine. Elaborate dishes feature on the menu, with antipasti available in the evening. At lunchtime these are replaced by various salads aimed at a business clientele in a hurry. Milanese-style cutlets are the house speciality.

Name: Terrazza Gallia
Description: On the seventh floor of Hotel Gallia, with panoramic views of the square and Central Station, the restaurant’s limited seating is arranged in a room with modern furnishings and features a cuisine inspired by products and recipes from throughout Italy. A rewarding gastronomic destination in a refined setting.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Address: via Privata Fratelli Gabba 7/b, Milan, 20121, Italy
Description: Housed within the Bulgari hotel, a secluded haven of elegance right in the heart of the most exclusive district in Milan, this restaurant alternates the trusted chefs at its helm, all of whom continue to serve light, contemporary Italian cuisine in dishes that focus more on substance than form. Choose between tasting menus and a generous à la carte selection featuring meat and fish dishes alike, including classic local favourites such as risotto and vitello alla Milanese (breaded veal cutlet).

Name: La Fugascina Ristorante
Description: Situated on a small square with an attractive outdoor space, this restaurant offers a menu which features fish from the lake and other seasonal produce prepared with both modern and traditional techniques, but always with a contemporary flair. The focus is on locally sourced (zero-mile, wherever possible) produce.

Name: Darmagi
Description: Small villa in secluded position with warm, homely atmosphere, especially in the nice room with fireplace. The range of cuisine is rich in tradition.

Name: Oberwirt
Description: The various Stube-style dining rooms in the Oberwirt hotel restaurant have a typical Tyrolean ambience, while the cuisine is decidedly traditional with its focus on seasonal and regional ingredients, although a few fish options also always feature on the menu. Wine-enthusiasts will be delighted with the excellent wine selection.

Name: Foresta
Address: via Litoranea 2, Marina di Pisa, 56128, Italy
Description: Overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea, all the tables at this restaurant offer sea views, whether you’re sitting in the winter dining room or on the outdoor summer terrace. The menu here focuses on top-quality fish dishes, which are classic in style, as is the background music and wine list, although the desserts have a more imaginative flavour.

Name: Taverna Rovita
Description: Situated just a few metres from the main square of old Maratea, this tavern is a historic and typical restaurant with a kitchen area that dates from the 18C and a decor featuring Vietri ceramics. The chef delights in introducing guests to local recipes, such as the “polpo murato” (stewed octopus), one of the house specialities. The wine list boasts around 400 labels, with a particular focus on France and small-scale producers from Italy and further afield. Small groups (a maximum of 6 people) can choose to dine in the wine cellar surrounded by old bottles, many of which are collector’s items.

Name: MikEle
Description: An elegantly contemporary dining room punctuated by large portholes seems to herald the menu’s seafood focus: fish dishes arrive at the table, moderately creative yet firmly anchored to prime ingredients. The “nudo e crudo” is the essential selection of the day’s catch served simply, typically featuring at least six different varieties, while the tagliolini with langoustine is elevated with caviar and a creamy white cabbage purée finished with Martini. The heart of the experience, however, remains the quality of the ingredients, the absolute and memorable stars.

Name: Da Guido
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The story of this restaurant began in 1967, when Guido and Giovanna Fasan, both of whom still work front of house, met in Germany. They then moved back to Italy, where they opened Da Guido in the early 1990s. White dominates in the elegant, contemporary-style dining room, while the cuisine features delicious seafood dishes with a focus on grilled specialities. In summer, there’s a welcoming bar in the garden, which boasts a romantic atmosphere. Together with other restaurant-owners from Venice, the Fasan family also have a kitchen garden on the Venetian island of Sant’Erasmo, where they focus on sustainable growing methods.

Name: Il Merlo
Address: Viale Sergio Bernardini 660, Lido di Camaiore, 55041, Italy
Description: Situated right on the beach, Il Merlo boasts a welcoming dining room decorated in elegant, contemporary style. The owner is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates dishes with a focus on fish and seafood, such as the raw seafood platter and the salt-baked catch of the day. A few delicious meat options, such as plin pasta and pigeon, are also available.

Name: Battipalo
Description: An intimate and atmospheric venue, ideal for a romantic lakeside stop, where you can enjoy a relaxing break thanks to Italian and lake cuisine, sometimes reinterpreted with a more contemporary approach, but with little affectation and, instead, excellent substance. Enthusiasts will appreciate the snails with bread, butter, and parsley, accompanied by a garlic cream and seasonal mushrooms. Above all, the use of quality raw materials is fundamental.

Name: Del Fagioli
Description: A historic city landmark, this rustic and sincere trattoria welcomes guests with a simple, warm atmosphere, where the open kitchen at the entrance serves as an immediate calling card. The distinctly familial ambiance makes it beloved by many, so much so that reservations well in advance are required. The table sees straightforward, fragrant recipes: excellent Florentine steaks, pici with aglione sauce, pappa al pomodoro, twice-cooked beef with sautéed green beans, and to finish, house-made cantucci. A stop that celebrates the most authentic Tuscan tradition with genuine spirit.

Name: Riso Amaro
Description: A classic, elegant and welcoming restaurant situated in the historic centre. The owner-chef demonstrates ability and real passion in his cuisine, offering tasting menus alongside an array of modern meat and fish dishes.

Name: Trita Pepe
Address: via Gabriele D'Annunzio 4, Manoppello Scalo, 65024, Italy
Description: Situated on the road that passes through Manoppello Scalo, this restaurant with a car park right in front of the building boasts a spacious, simple dining room and is our recommended choice in the region for anyone keen to try typical Abruzzo cuisine. Meat takes pride of place among the main courses (with an exception for salted cod), while menu highlights include excellent fried gnocchi with local salumi and cheese.

Name: Taverna dello Spuntino
Description: This Roman trattoria has a particularly striking interior. From its old tufa passageways converted into a wine cellar in the basement, to its charming dining rooms with brick - vaulted arches where hams, flasks of wine, fruit and antipasti all form an attractive display.

Name: Le Cicale in Città
Description: A classic-style dining room adorned with mirrors and silverware acts as the backdrop for fish and seafood dishes at this restaurant. The raw fish is particularly excellent, as are the mupa (a little-known fish that lives in the deep waters of the Mediterranean), prawns (in season) and home-made primi served with delicious sauces, such as the chicken plin with brown gravy. For special occasions, we recommend the table to the rear of the room near the arte povera-style dresser. Cheerful, friendly service adds to the appeal.

Name: Cacciani
Description: Run by the Cacciani family for over 100 years, this is one of the most famous restaurants in the Castelli Romani region. Demonstrating a real passion for regional traditions and eschewing modern trends, the menu continues to offer a tempting selection of delicious classic dishes from Lazio, including a couple of fish and seafood options. The focaccia, which is served with the bread, is superb and well worth a mention. The dining room evokes the long history of the restaurant, while the panoramic terrace is a firm favourite with guests.

Name: Tana de 'l Ors
Address: via Roma 28, Forno di Zoldo, 32012, Italy
Description: A favourite with food-lovers, this restaurant serves lighter meals at lunchtime which are nonetheless carefully and imaginatively prepared (don’t miss the orsoburger!). In the evening, the best daily ingredients are prepared with a lightly modern touch – meat is the undisputed start of the show, although a few fish dishes also feature. One-room and two-room apartments are also available.

Name: Trattoria 'petito
Description: Located on the outskirts of Forlì’s charming historic centre, this simple, modern yet attractive restaurant serves eclectic and varied cuisine. More traditional fare on offer includes an excellent selection of hams and grilled meats, as well as delicious tagliatelle al ragù, while the menu also features a few more creative options including a few fish dishes.

Name: Villa Fiordaliso
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Fiordaliso is one of the beautiful early 20C villas that line the lake front. Surrounded by verdant grounds and extending out into the lake on a pontoon, the restaurant serves creative, modern cuisine. The chef is equally at ease with fish and meat dishes, while the extensive wine list suggests that you’ll have no problem finding your favourite wine here.

Name: Osteria Antico Brolo
Description: Situated in the upper part of the town near the Vittoriale estate, this rustic 18C building is the setting for regional cuisine prepared using seasonal ingredients. The charming small courtyard offers shade for summer dining, while the interior dining room also includes a single table on a small balcony which needs to be booked well in advance.

Name: Cibrèo
Address: via A. Del Verrocchio 8r, Florence, 50122, Italy
Description: A historic city institution and essential stop for anyone arriving in Florence, this establishment welcomes guests into an elegant dining room reminiscent of a private salon, where cordial, graciously measured service frames a cuisine of bold flavors. The menu features dishes that have become true house classics, capable of narrating the territory through recipes that time has rendered iconic: pork liver with lemon, tortellini timbale, squab stuffed with mostarda, rabbit roulade with sweet-and-sour borettane onions, and, to close, a cheese tart accompanied by marmalade.

Name: Locanda del Molino
Description: This rustic yet charming restaurant occupies an old family mill. It has attractive guestrooms that reflect the elegant simplicity of the Tuscan countryside. In the kitchen, the female chef creates traditional specialities such as fried rabbit and nettle with ricotta cheese gnudi (ravioli filling without the pasta) in a fresh tomato sauce.

Name: Brindo
Description: The service is characterized by a cohesive and friendly team in welcoming guests to their small home. Brindo is an informal reality, where the cuisine is fun, engaging and more than simply territorial: raw foods, tartar and fish of the day are at the top!

Name: Osteria della Chiocciola
Description: Situated in the historic centre just a stone’s throw from the elegant Via Roma, this restaurant is decorated with paintings by renowned modern artists such as Pignatelli, Andy Warhol, and Valerio Berruti. The ground floor is home to a colourful wine bar, while the first-floor restaurant serves traditional cuisine made from local ingredients with a natural focus on Piedmont. There is also a fish alternative for non-meat-eaters.

Name: Pierre Alexis 1877
Description: Situated in the historic heart of Courmayeur, this old house dating back over a century, once used as a stables and later as a carpenter’s workshop, is now home to a warm and welcoming restaurant. Here, traditional recipes are updated with creativity and enthusiasm, as demonstrated by the venison Rossini. The ingredients used are mainly local, including wild herbs for added flavour, while the wine list offers an impressive selection of labels.

Name: Osteria del Teatro
Description: Enjoy traditional cuisine served in an elegant 16C dining room with a fireplace or in more informal trattoria-style rooms, all of which are decorated with the same theatrical theme. The recipes here focus on local traditions and seasonal ingredients, resulting in colourful, well-balanced and beautifully presented dishes that are full of flavour. There are just a few tables on the small terrace near the entrance overlooking the pedestrianised street, so if you want to sit outdoors make sure you book well in advance.

Name: La Capuccina
Address: via Novara 19/b, località Capuccina, Cureggio, 28060, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A new chef brings fresh energy and ideas to this excellent restaurant housed within a 16C farmhouse that is surrounded by countryside and which has been restored in elegant style. The chef focuses on top-quality ingredients (including vegetables from his own kitchen garden) and contemporary recipes with a classic flavour, as well as personalised recipes created with just a few ingredients for which he uses a mix of classic methods (“express” cooking) and modern techniques (such as whipping siphons) in order to achieve comforting, classic flavours. With the exception of a few champagnes, the wine selection showcases the region, especially the areas closest to Upper Piedmont, such as Ghemme, Gattinara, Boca and Sizzano – plus, of course, the wines produced on the restaurant’s own estate!

Name: Kandoo Nippon Restaurant
Description: Contemporary spaces spread across two floors, plus a veranda terrace, make this solid restaurant a great choice for lovers of Japanese specialties – both cooked and raw preparations of meat and fish – executed with a light touch and clean, distinct flavors. At lunch (weekdays only), the kitchen also offers rice bowls and noodle dishes accompanied by various sides. Wine enthusiasts will appreciate the dedicated Champagne section on the wine list.

Name: La Casa degli Spiriti
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The Chignola family has been welcoming guests in this beautiful, restored farmhouse – a luxurious residence with one of the best views of Lake Garda – for almost 30 years. The ground-floor restaurant occupies a veranda surrounded by greenery facing the lake, where young chef Filippo (following in his father’s footsteps), together with his brother, sommelier Lorenzo, offers his guests an enjoyable dining experience with its roots in the cuisine of the region. The first-floor terrace is home to the Osteria Spiritino, which is more informal in both its cuisine and atmosphere. The remarkable wine cellar is housed in a room adorned with 18C frescoes and boasts more than 1 300 labels, with a particular focus on champagnes.

Name: Rosita
Description: Decorated in the same simple and rustic style as the Hotel Rosita in which it is housed, this restaurant boasts an attractive terrace overlooking the sea and the coast (call in advance to book one of the tables with the best view), which more than compensates for the narrow, winding road that you have to follow to get here. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, including seafood options such as the excellent stuffed baby squid in a sauce served with mashed potatoes, and meat dishes that include a tasty rabbit casserole.

Name: Trattoria Leoni
Description: Situated amid gently rolling hills, this restaurant with large picture windows boasts fine views of the surrounding countryside, which can be enjoyed even more from its summer terrace. For many years, the Leoni family have served Parma specialities here, including excellent salumi and recipes handed down by their grandmother, as well as typical mountain ingredients such as mushrooms and game.

Name: Tanzer
Description: Located beneath the belltower in a small hamlet, this restaurant has two romantic 17C Stube-style dining rooms, where Melanie and her sommelier husband Michael delight guests with regional, modern and imaginative cuisine. Most of the ingredients are sourced locally, including from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden. The home-made syrups and jams are highly recommended.

Name: Al Vedel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: A temple for the production of culatello ham, which features in the dishes served and is also matured on the premises for 16, 26 and 38 months (the maturing rooms are well worth a visit), Al Vedel also serves other regional specialities, as well as more imaginative fare. The menu features dishes such as gran lesso(boiled beef and chicken), delicious Bourguignon-style snails, tortel dols (tortelli pasta with a hint of sweetness), and specialities enhanced by the addition of Parmesan cheese and red butter. The wine list, which will delight Lambrusco enthusiasts, boasts a selection of French wines including newer wine-producing regions, while the cheese trolley offers a selection of regional and Italian cheeses, plus a few options from further afield such as the famous Brillat-Savarin with its natural, bloomy rind.

Name: Albergaccio di Castellina
Address: via Fiorentina 63, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
Description: In the heart of one of Italy’s most iconic landscapes, Chianti Classico, with its harmonious hills and vineyards tracing picture-perfect panoramas, Albergaccio, considered Tuscany’s oldest historic restaurant, welcomes guests with a perfect balance of past and present. The interiors preserve the authentic charm of the setting, while the kitchen reinterprets traditional dishes with a contemporary touch, never betraying their essence. In the dining room, Francesco greets guests with grace and professionalism, guiding them in selecting the wine best suited to enhance the gastronomic experience. An establishment that celebrates history, terroir, and a timeless vision of hospitality.

Name: Il Verso del Ghiottone
Description: This restaurant housed in an 18C building has a warm, rustic feel with terracotta, stone and brick decor and black tables with American-style place mats, resulting in a vibrant yet elegant atmosphere where the service is informal and yet also highly professional. The cuisine is inspired by regional recipes which are reinterpreted and given a lighter flavour. There’s no shortage of interesting fish dishes, including the exquisite red shrimp, which is half-cooked, half-raw and served with passion-fruit caramel.

Name: Da Orlando
Description: Simply arriving in Cusago near Milan, where the imposing castle dominates the attractive centre, puts you in a good mood. At Da Orlando, the menu is equally balanced between top-quality fish dishes such as the “bollita di mare” and meat-based dishes that will delight food-lovers, such as snails with trumpet mushrooms and duck breast with ginger. Two elegant dining rooms are the perfect setting for a romantic evening, while the attractive outdoor space comes into its own in summer. A good restaurant with over 40 years of history.

Name: Da Ercole
Description: Situated on Crotone’s seafront, Da Ercole is a culinary institution for anyone who loves fish, with the benefit of 40 years in the business behind it! The salty tang of the Ionian sea is celebrated on an extensive menu, although if you really want to enjoy yourself to the full, let owner-chef and old-school host Ercole guide you in your choice (including some excellent raw fish dishes).

Name: Quel Fantastico Giovedì
Description: After forty years of experience, their consistency and care make this one of Ferrara’s most sought-after tables (best to book well in advance!). Guests enter intimate dining rooms of welcoming warmth, where service is gracious and precise. The menu is fragrant with the sea: fish dishes prepared with classic elegance and modern touches, such as the green bean and vegetable velouté crowned with raw scampi, fresh and glistening. Meat offerings are equally rewarding, rich and flavorful, with the celebrated potato sformato and gratinéed salama da sugo releasing intense aromas from the oven.

Name: Sichelburg
Description: Treat yourself to a great meal in an idyllic setting in this village restaurant occupying the first floor of a castle dating back to the 13C. The romantic dining rooms are furnished with wood, while the creative cuisine focuses on typical mountain produce.

Name: Tavola di Guido
Address: Località Le Piazze 41, Castellina in Chianti, 53011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The menu crafted by Guido, a chef attentive to seasonality and estate products, is a tribute to the land. The extra virgin olive oil comes from Poggibonsi or Castellina, both from the same farm. Among the signature dishes is the beetroot risotto with pancetta, crème fraîche, and nasturtium – but only when in season! The wine cellar features Tuscan, Italian, and international labels, with a special treat to try: Amphoreum, a home-produced orange wine made from Trebbiano, known for its salinity and medium body.

Name: San Michele
Address: via Castello di Fagagna 33, Fagagna, 33034, Italy
Description: Situated next to the ruins of the old castle and the small church of San Michele, this 13C building, thought to have once housed a guardroom, is now home to a small restaurant serving regional, seasonal cuisine with a modern twist. During the week, the restaurant offers a lunchtime menu of top-quality snacks (the Venetian “cicchetti”), as well as a few “primi” and desserts.

Name: Osteria de l'Umbreleèr
Description: Situated in Cicognolo in the Lower Po valley, where early morning mists create an evocative atmosphere in autumn, this traditional restaurant with a rustic feel serves specialities from Lombardy with a focus on delicious starters and top-quality meat. Our inspector particularly recommends the white onion gratin soup and the Burgundy-style snails. A simpler menu is available at lunchtime and there’s a small garden for alfresco dining on summer evenings.

Name: Osteria dell'Oca Bianca
Description: In the heart of a small town, right opposite the church, this typical village osteria run by a friendly family serves traditional cuisine from the Piedmont, including goose dishes. Highlights here include the rustic, welcoming ambience, an excellent wine list, a wine cellar that can be visited, and a charming glass-fronted veranda that is used throughout the year. There are also three beautiful guestrooms reserved exclusively for guests dining at the restaurant.

Name: Maré
Description: An unexpected gourmet restaurant in a typical private beach club on the Romagna coast, with a dining room that opens on to the beach with its long line of beach umbrellas. The dishes here are carefully prepared and occasionally creative, and all of good quality. We particularly recommend the monfettini (fresh egg pasta) mantecati with cuttlefish, clams, mantis shrimp and ink, which looks like a risotto and is absolutely delicious. The restaurant also boasts a good wine list with an excellent choice of champagnes.

Name: Feel Como
Description: Wild regional produce, game and freshwater fish take pride of place on the menu at this elegant restaurant which celebrates nature in all its glory, despite its town-centre location. The dishes prepared by chef Federico Beretta have a contemporary feel, while the tasting menu is dedicated to wild ingredients foraged from the woods.

Name: Doc
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 1, Borgio Verezzi, 17022, Italy
Description: Quiet, well - kept restaurant located in an aristocratic, early twentieth - century villa surrounded by a pretty garden.

Name: Cascina Lautier
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated outside the town on top of a small hill, this elegant restaurant serves modern country cuisine, with some personal interpretations.

Name: Antinè
Description: Manuel Bouchard’s cuisine impressed our inspectors thanks to striking features such as his minimalist approach and the use of just a few well-chosen ingredients. Traditional recipes, such as plin pasta and Fassona beef, feature on the menu alongside more alternative, imaginative dishes (including fresh- and saltwater fish). This elegant restaurant is located on the first floor of a building in the old town, just a stone’s throw from the medieval tower. A warm welcome and an excellent wine list complete the picture.

Name: Il Giardino delle Esperidi
Description: The ideal starting point for an exploration of the area. In summer one dines on the terrace located in the heart of the historic centre while drinks and cigars may be enjoyed in the lounge bar.

Name: Stube Ladina
Description: The hotel owner is also the chef, serving carefully prepared and well - presented dishes made from regional produce in a quiet Stube - style dining room. An interesting wine list provides the icing on the cake.

Name: Marina Grande
Description: Situated directly on the beach, this pleasant restaurant with a contemporary decor boasts splendid sea views and a small private beach club. Although the setting obviously has a tourist feel, the traditional cuisine served here is full of flavour. We particularly recommend the “gamberi in carrozza” (shrimp) with fior di latte and a variation on puttanesca sauce.

Name: Villa Baroni
Description: This romantic restaurant on the lakeshore has a welcoming, elegant ambience and a delightful terrace for summer dining. The cuisine pays particular attention to top-quality, seasonal ingredients prepared in traditional recipes with a focus on fish. Cosy, Provençal-style guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Antica Osteria da Penacio
Description: A family - run restaurant in a villa on the edge of a wood: inside two refined dining rooms and a small, but well stocked, wine bar; traditional cuisine.

Name: Il Pavone
Description: Situated in the heart of Alghero and with a beautiful veranda overlooking the sea, this restaurant has been in business for almost 50 years. Fish and seafood take centre stage here, served in classic dishes which are full of flavour and prepared using top-quality local ingredients. Specialities include fresh pan-fried and grilled fish, delicious bavettine pasta with scampi and fried mussels, and the island’s famous “seadas” served with Sardinian eucalyptus honey or home-made ice-cream.

Name: Roof Garden
Description: Make sure you ask for one of the tables next to the glass wall in this restaurant, which boasts romantic views of Bergamo’s Città Alta. The innovative, inventive cuisine is tempting and full of flavour.

Name: Opificio
Description: A modern restaurant in the province of Padova which, over the past ten years, has grown and evolved from a gastro pub to the top-quality eatery that it is today. The cuisine is fairly eclectic, featuring meat and fish dishes alike, with the option of a lighter menu at lunchtime. The best dishes are showcased on the à la carte and are often made using luxury ingredients such as foie gras, scampi and Wagyu beef. The impressive wine list demonstrates a passion for international sparkling wines, while the excellent selection of wines by the glass is further enhanced by a choice of cocktails (also available at midday).

Name: Anticofurlo
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Country cooking
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the Gola del Furlo nature reserve, this restaurant is run by the talented and enthusiastic Alberto and Roberta, whose focus is on typical Marche specialities such as fresh pasta, cured hams, fine cheese and regional dishes full of intense flavours. The picturesque grotto carved into the rock is perfect for an aperitif, while the inn also offers charming guestrooms.

Name: Il Carpaccio
Description: This traditional family restaurant has been recently renovated to include an attractive veranda - style dining room overlooking the valley. Typical dishes from Calabria, fish specialities by prior arrangement, and a good wine list all add to the appeal.

Name: Da Peppe
Description: Situated in the historic centre of a small village in the Parco del Pollino, this long-established restaurant serves traditional and copious local dishes that are always expertly prepared. Guestrooms are also available in the family B&B of the same name.

Name: Dogma
Description: This restaurant may be small (booking is recommended) but it has a big personality. The focus here is on fish and seafood, with nearly all the dishes cooked (at least partially) over the barbecue grill, including desserts! The talented, original young chef creates dishes full of intense and convincing flavours.

Name: RistoFante
Description: Run by the reliable and experienced “Titta” in the kitchen and Silvia front of house, this elegant, contemporary-style restaurant serves simple, modern dishes in which fresh, seasonal ingredients take centre stage. The focus here is on fish, with a menu that includes a fine selection of raw seafood options, as well as a simple yet tasty sea bass carpaccio which cooks quickly on a bed of hot porcini mushrooms.

Name: Ventuno.1
Description: Major refurbishment at this renowned restaurant has given it the feel of an informal, welcoming contemporary bistro. Don’t miss the “Napule” tasting menu, which offers just four courses that include anchovies, cavatelli pasta and Neapolitan meatballs in a nod to the owner’s origins. Over time, the wine list has been extended and improved, with wines now stored in a new cellar. Some of the ingredients used in the dishes can also be purchased to take home.

Name: Hostaria dai Musi
Description: Offering a limited à la carte that includes fish dishes (including raw options) which vary according to market availability, this restaurant serves what it describes as “typically modern cuisine”. The breaded and fried anchovies with a typical saor sauce and lemon gel are particularly good, plus the menu features a selection of typical regional specialities. The pleasant setting is enhanced by the backdrop of the large central square in a pedestrianised area on the edge of the old town. The drinks menu includes an excellent selection of wines, plus a good choice of local beers.

Name: Ca' Del Moro
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated within the La Collina dei Ciliegi wine estate amid the verdant Valpantena hills, this first-floor restaurant (lift available) is home to two chefs – he is from Calabria, while she is from Puglia. Together they create exciting, modern Mediterranean cuisine using ingredients from their native regions, including their signature dish – homemade spaghetti served with a delicious, well-balanced 'nduja, smoked ricotta and tomato ristretto sauce. Top-quality local ingredients take pride of place, as demonstrated by the Brogna mutton, which is raised on site, barbecued and served with an exquisite caper sauce and seasonal mushroom pie. The concise wine list features labels from the Veneto alongside a few French options.

Name: Locanda del Marinaio
Description: Delicious cuisine full of the flavours of the Mediterranean (prepared by the German owner - chef! ) in a delightful little restaurant in the bustling centre of Cefalù. Simple surroundings but excellent food!

Name: La Veranda
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: In summer, the terrace by the lake offers a splendid view and is the perfect setting for dishes that highlight Italian tradition but also satisfy the most cosmopolitan palates. The foie gras escalope served with parsnips, apple compote and pink grapefruit, for example, is excellent. If the weather's not so great, you'll be just as comfortable in the elegant indoor dining room overlooking the lake (the most popular) or the garden. The evening dress code is elegant (we are, after all, inside the luxurious Villa d'Este hotel).

Name: L'Argaj
Description: In the Piedmontese dialect, “Argaj” translates as “satisfaction” and never has a restaurant name seemed more appropriate! In a simple, colourful and welcoming dining room with windows looking out at the hills, all the attention is on cuisine which is skilfully balanced between classic local dishes and more creative options. Choose between the à la carte and tasting menus, all accompanied by an excellent array of wines.

Name: Trattoria del Bivio
Description: Situated in the Alta Langa region, this old restored farmhouse is now home to an elegant restaurant with a contemporary rural feel. The cuisine has strong regional roots, although the menu also offers a few fishes dishes. Excellent food, as well as attractive guestrooms and a warm, family welcome.

Name: Il Doretto
Description: Housed in an attractive farmhouse, this restaurant serves seasonal cuisine that includes delicious fish and seafood (raw dishes as well as more elaborate options), alongside meat dishes, including some delicious game recipes.

Name: I Salotti
Address: Località Querce al Pino, SS 146, Chiusi, 53043, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In summer, the outdoor spaces at this restaurant, such as the garden gazebo, are the perfect setting for a candlelit dinner in total harmony with nature, while in winter, the elegant dining room with just a few tables (book well in advance) really comes into its own. Creative cuisine prepared using produce from the restaurant’s own farm, plus a long-established wine cellar that has been extended over the years so that it now boasts over two thousand different labels from the region and elsewhere in Italy, many of them of the highest quality.

Name: Oste Scuro - Finsterwirt
Description: Run by the capable Mayr family, this long-established restaurant has occupied a narrow alleyway in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen) since the late 19C. The dining rooms are decorated in historic style, plus there’s a charming terrace for alfresco dining in summer. Dishes are presented on different tasting menus with the option of choosing traditional or Mediterranean dishes à la carte style – we highly recommend the soup made with Sylvaner wine from the Isarco valley, as well as the Tirtl (fried pie) stuffed with ricotta, spinach and cinnamon. Guestrooms are available in the nearby and recently renovated Adler Historic Guesthouse, which is run by the same owners.

Name: Lanzani Bottega & Bistrot
Address: via Albertano da Brescia 41, Brescia, 25127, Italy
Description: This modern restaurant (open from 7am to 11pm), once the family butcher’s, is also a delicatessen and wine boutique. It serves top-quality produce such as Pata Negra and other hams, anchovies from the Cantabrian sea, an excellent selection of cheeses and more elaborate dishes. At mealtimes, the venue transforms into a proper restaurant, with a smaller menu available at lunchtime.

Name: Clandestino Susci Bar
Description: Built on stilts, the Clandestino is a unique restaurant with a simple yet trendy ambience, which overlooks a beautiful unspoilt beach with views of the sea from all the windows and a distinctly romantic feel at night. Here, Moreno Cedroni focuses on gourmet cuisine at lunchtime as well as in the evening. In addition to two tasting menus (Eros & Susci and Susci Memories), for lunch there’s a small à la carte.

Name: Gardenia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Even if you’re not a local, you’ll feel at home in this old property which offers a glimpse of the Piedmont of old. In this 19C building, with a typical balcony running along the inner courtyard, the atmosphere continues into the dining room and, of course, via the dishes on the menu. Here, regional cuisine is celebrated to the full, so you’ll find lots of meat (although some fish options are also available), accompanied by a carefully selected choice of vegetables, some grown in the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Il Portico
Description: Chef Lopriore returns to his native region with this new restaurant which offers an original format – the lunchtime menu focuses on single course options, while in the evening the tasting menus comprise an interesting combination of imaginative fish, meat and vegetable dishes which can be combined as you wish. Cuisine with an emphasis on seasonal market ingredients where locally sourced produce takes pride of place.

Name: Kürbishof
Description: This romantic inn with guestrooms occupies an old farm with a hay barn. In two typical Stube-style rooms, one of which offers views of the Cembra valley, enjoy cuisine prepared by a mother-and-son team. They work side by side, preparing dishes from mainly regional ingredients (the menu often includes the names of producers) each in their own individual way, which is highlighted on the menu: to the left, you’ll find the traditional dishes made by the mother, Sara, while on the right you can choose from a selection of modern, creative options prepared by young chef Mathias. Our inspectors were delighted with their combination of choices from both lists!

Name: Phi Restaurant
Address: località Forte Cappellini, Baia Sardinia, 07021, Italy
Description: Glamour and fashion are the hallmarks of this restaurant in Phi Beach, one of the most attractive nightclub-cum-lounge bars on the Costa Smeralda. Take a seat on the terrace right by the water and soak up the romantic sunsets and sea views as you enjoy Italian and Mediterranean dishes created by a famous chef from Lombardy who adds just the right touch of contemporary flavour. Also open for lunch, with some of the evening menu dishes available alongside an array of simpler options.

Name: La Conchiglia
Description: This small restaurant with a vaulted ceiling provides the setting for dishes that have by now become classics thanks to their focus on top-quality ingredients. The cuisine is light and simple rather than bold and elaborate, with a focus on bringing out the full flavour of the fish (a few meat dishes are also available). If you’re keen to learn more about Ligurian gastronomic specialities, take time between courses to chat with the friendly owner, who has an impressive knowledge of the region.

Name: Granoturco Bistrot
Description: Although the external façade of this restaurant recalls its former life as a pub, the building is now home to a restaurant run by a young chef whose experience working abroad has done nothing to dim his love of the Piedmont. Here, he serves some of the best regional cuisine in the area, with a few more creative options also featuring on the menu.

Name: All'Osteria Bottega
Description: Enjoy top-quality Emilian cuisine at this restaurant, which focuses on the region’s most traditional, best-known and authentic recipes. Featuring a superb selection of hams and salamis, fresh pastas, meat and desserts, the menu offers a real feast for the tastebuds that will linger long in the memory.

Name: Enoclub
Description: Under the arcades of a piazza named after Michele Ferrero, this restaurant has a simple, modern ambience with walls covered with wine bottles, as well as friendly, efficient female staff. The beautifully prepared Piedmontese cuisine is showcased on an à la carte and a tasting menu, accompanied by an impressive selection of quality wine.

Name: Maso Runch-Hof
Description: Surrounded by woods, a trip to this restaurant housed in an 18C farmhouse is like taking a journey back in time. Take a seat in one of the wood-adorned Stube-style rooms and enjoy generous portions of delicious home-cooked Ladin specialities featured on a single tasting menu, including cajinci t’ega (spinach-filled ravioli), excellent pork ribs with polenta, and apple strudel. The small wine list has the same local focus, featuring labels from the Alto Adige region. A recent addition, the restaurant also now has a few spacious, welcoming chalets available for guests.

Name: Radimare
Address: via Beato Piergiorgio Frassati 5/a, Monopoli, 70043, Italy
Description: There’s no tasting menu at this restaurant but instead a tempting à la carte featuring modern Mediterranean cuisine based on top-quality seasonal ingredients, with fish and seafood taking centre stage. Citrus fruit and a few spices, especially ginger, are used carefully and sparingly, as are aromatic herbs which add a touch of fresh flavour to the dishes. The contemporary decor, enhanced by plants and a profusion of wood, plus friendly service add to the appeal.

Name: Da Nilo
Description: In the heart of Cetona's square, a well-tended outdoor area among hedges welcomes guests with warmth and smiles. The cuisine is authentically Tuscan and well-crafted. Don’t miss the selection of local cured meats and the classic pici all’aglione, a true must-try!

Name: Lou Ressignon
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description: Founded in 1966 and now run by the fifth generation, the Lou Ressignon family trattoria (in local dialect the name translates as “the night snack”) serves authentic cuisine full of character which showcases the produce and traditions of the Aosta Valley. The dishes include a delicious Valpellinese soup and excellent tripe with borlotti beans and polentina. In addition to the first-floor dining room, there’s also a historic taverna, while four welcoming guestrooms are available for anyone wishing to extend their stay.

Name: Il Labirinto
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated on the outskirts of Brescia, this long-established restaurant has an elegant retro atmosphere. The cuisine is varied with a balance of fish and meat dishes, as well as some excellent home-made salumi.

Name: La Porta Restaurant
Address: piazza Vieira de Mello 4, Bologna, 40128, Italy
Description: Housed in a futuristic building which extends like a bridge over Via Stalingrado, La Porta Restaurant is a multi-purpose establishment which includes a café (accessible from the garage), a bistro serving simple meals at lunchtime, and an elegant restaurant with wood decor where gourmet cuisine can be enjoyed in the evening. The menu features an array of fish, meat and vegetable options, while service comes courtesy of a mainly female team, all of whom are extremely friendly and welcoming.

Name: Badessa
Description: This restaurant has a surprising location in a 19C cheese factory which once produced parmesan. Although the purpose of the building has changed, the love of the region remains the same – the chef goes out of his way to source local ingredients and search out old recipes, serving traditional Emilian dishes often with a modern twist. The fresh pasta and other ingredients are produced by the restaurant, while the carefully chosen wine list focuses on natural labels in particular.

Name: Pescarino-Sapori di Terra e di Mare
Description: Warm and inviting atmosphere with wooden walls and ceiling. The kitchen, recently renovated alongside the terrace, remains unchanged in offering: relatively simple in some concoctions, more creative in others, aiming primarily to highlight the product quality, predominantly seafood, with Ligurian nuances but extending to other regions. Considering the isolated location, seizing the opportunity to rest in the rooms may be worthwhile.

Name: Già Sotto l'Arco
Description: A historic gourmet restaurant, with an equally historic setting on the first floor of a Baroque palazzo fronting an elegant piazza. A fine staircase leads up to the simple yet stylish dining room, which is skilfully run by a father and his offspring. In the kitchen, his wife Teresa prepares creative, regional cuisine, which is showcased on a surprise menu of four, six or eight courses and which features locally sourced meat and fish. If you’d like to book the delightful table on the small terrace for just two fortunate guests, make sure you do so well in advance!

Name: La Locanda del Cardinale
Description: Situated right in the centre of Assisi, La Locanda del Cardinale occupies an old palazzo that is home to the perfectly preserved remains of a Roman villa dating back to 70 BC in a fascinating setting full of history. The menu features simple recipes such as crispy organic egg with asparagus and marjoram, as well as more elaborate, modern dishes including quail and Danubio brioche with barbecued artichoke. It’s not surprising that this delightful restaurant also boasts a superb wine cellar with an array of carefully chosen labels that will delight wine-enthusiasts.

Name: La Veranda del Color
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This aptly named restaurant in the Color Hotel just a short distance from Lake Garda boasts a modern, colourful decor and cuisine worthy of its name. Dishes are inspired by Mediterranean traditions and are showcased on a number of different tasting menus.

Name: Piacentino
Description: Restaurant with pension near the old town, where you can enjoy Piacentine dishes served outdoors in nice weather and in the airy indoors dining hall during the colder months. The rooms are in two styles, one with wrought iron beds and Arte Povera furniture, the other being more modern.

Name: Trippini
Address: via Italia 14, Civitella del Lago, 05023, Italy
Description: Just a few tables and spectacular views of Lake Corbara characterise this restaurant, which has been run by the same family since 1964. The delicious cuisine is regional in flavour, showcasing home-cooked recipes and typical Sunday favourites yet with a contemporary twist that incorporates plenty of intense flavours.

Name: La Terrazza
Description: A salon en plein air overlooking Asolo’s historical center, this charming spot offers attentive service and Italian cuisine presented with a modern touch. The menu spans land and sea, with vegetarian options as well. A classic and welcoming atmosphere makes it an ideal setting for a romantic dinner.

Name: Il Focarile
Address: via Pontina al km 46,5, Aprilia, 04011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The sumptuous entrance gives an elegant tone to a large bright dining room with well spaced out tables; a touch of Tuscany with a cuisine rich in tradition and also imagination. Now offers new, elegant rooms.

Name: Loewengrube
Description: This building has been home to a restaurant since the 16C, making it one of the oldest in Bolzano. Today, it houses an elegant restaurant that serves a combination of traditional Alpine cuisine and classic Italian dishes with a contemporary twist, such as carbonara tortelloni filled with parmesan cream and crispy bacon. The attractive wine cellar boasts a selection of approximately 1 000 wines from the region and elsewhere in Italy, as well as a choice of labels from further afield.

Name: Osteria Taviani
Address: Via del Monte Ovest 25, Bientina, 56031, Italy
Description: Housed in a small Art Nouveau-style villa, this restaurant boasts an elegant yet warm and friendly ambience. The cuisine here is modern and full of flavour, with a focus on meat dishes (although a few fish options also feature) with their roots firmly anchored in Tuscan traditions (such as the fried steak). During the hunting season, the contemporary-style game dishes are particularly delicious. The wine list includes a few French labels, plus there’s a small, attractive outdoor space in the courtyard to the rear which overlooks a beautiful garden.

Name: La Fermata
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the countryside around Alessandria, this 18C farmhouse has a modern, minimalist decor which serves as a backdrop for traditional Piedmontese cuisine with a clever modern twist. The chef offers just the right amount of creativity, with a focus on meat dishes and satisfying, memorable flavours that appeal to the emotions as well as the palate. Adding to the appeal, the elegant and exclusive ambience is the result of careful refurbishment, which has transformed the dining room into a triumph of art and design.

Name: In Riva a Numana
Description: Riva is the Hotel Vista’s fine-dining restaurant, situated just behind Numana’s beach with fine panoramic views. The restaurant serves top-quality ingredients from the Adriatic and surrounding countryside in creative dishes full of flavour which are showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: Januarius
Description: Named after San Gennaro (St Januarius) whose relics are said to lie in the cathedral nearby, this restaurant celebrates traditional, authentic specialities from Campania, such as octopus alla Luciana, zito pasta in a traditional ragu and salted cod with Napolitan-style endives. The entrance opens into a boutique selling top-quality ingredients (mainly charcuterie and cheeses), with two original dining rooms on either side.

Name: Delicato
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval hilltop village in the province of Rieti on the border with Umbria, this restaurant serves cuisine that is influenced by different regions and traditions. Choose between the minimalist-style dining rooms with exposed stone walls and, in fine weather, a charming outdoor space at the foot of Contigliano’s church. Here, chef Carlotta Delicato brings out the best of local ingredients in dishes that are kept deliberately simple and unfussy yet are full of flavour. We highly recommend the “spaghettone mare e lago” with a light brunoise of courgettes. As the restaurant is situated in Lazio, guests can enjoy good local wines made by small-scale producers, such as the Cabernet Sauvignon Masseria Baroni, which is of medium intensity with broad and pronounced aromas. .

Name: Scatto
Description: From Turin’s beautiful Piazza San Carlo, you head through an inner courtyard to this restaurant’s modern dining room with its open-view kitchen. Whether you opt for the à la carte or tasting menu, you’ll find a balance of traditional Piedmontese and more creative dishes, all of remarkable quality, in keeping with the superb wine list.

Name: Osteria Ricanatti
Description: This cozy little restaurant, backed by attentive and impeccably polished service, reveals a regional cuisine that is both flavorful and thoughtfully reinterpreted, available through several tasting menus as well as à la carte. Ingredient sourcing is exacting, with all vegetables harvested from the family’s garden just a few kilometers away – a guarantee of freshness and seasonality. Among the most representative dishes: the pecorino and potato tartare dressed with chimichurri, Argentina’s signature green sauce, or the perfectly al dente paccheri with a two-tomato coulis, raw bluefin tuna, and fried capers – a plate that strikes an ideal balance of intensity and harmony.

Name: Belvedere
Description: Over the years, this family restaurant has become one of the most popular along this coastline. An informal dining room provides the backdrop for the decidedly Mediterranean cuisine served here, where the focus is the fish display cabinet that changes daily and from which guests can make their choice. The friendly and professional approach of the two brothers that run the restaurant has contributed to its success, while the brand-new terrace-lounge, with its stunning view, is the perfect spot for an aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Millo Ristorante
Address: via Garibaldi 4, Santa Teresa Gallura, 07028, Italy
Description: A charming restaurant with fair prices, Millo offers dishes infused with the flavors of the sea, sometimes with a creative twist (such as spaghetti with a garlic, oil, and chili emulsion, red prawn carpaccio, and a crispy bread crust), other times inspired by tradition (such as the seafood soup cooked in a jar). There are also a few meat options available. The lovely summer terrace is perfect for taking in the lively local scene.

Name: Nugolo
Description: A restaurant with a friendly ambience and a chic, colourful decor and design that includes an open-view kitchen. In the latter, the young, talented chef uses seasonal ingredients to create contemporary-style dishes with an imaginative twist.
