The enthusiastic front-of-house team provides friendly and attentive service.

Name: Seta Sushi Restaurant
Description: It was friendship and passion for Japanese cuisine that prompted two young business partners to open this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the heart of Bologna. Situated in a courtyard with medieval origins, Seta Sushi Restaurant has a modern bistro-style dining room, as well as plenty of outdoor space for summer dining. The menu features an impressive selection of traditional Japanese dishes with the occasional personalised touch, all made from top-quality ingredients. Don’t worry if you’re new to Japanese cuisine – Maurilio is front of house to offer guests friendly, expert advice on both food and beverage. The latter includes a choice of sake for those wishing to immerse themselves fully in the Japanese dining experience.

Name: Enotavola Pino
Description: The entrance to this restaurant through a wine-bar can be misleading, as you are eventually led to simpler – yet still attractive – dining rooms. In this wine-themed setting, enjoy delicious fish and seafood dishes with the occasional creative twist, accompanied by a particularly extensive selection of wines by the glass. A highly recommended address for fish lovers, situated right in the historic centre of Padova.

Name: Al Petes
Description: Situated amid the alleyways of the historic centre, Al Petes has a pleasant contemporary feel and is run by young, welcoming and friendly owners. Marko’s menu demonstrates an obvious preference for seafood, most of which comes from the Adriatic, and which is served with Mediterranean and even occasional Asian influences. The surprise tasting menu is highly recommended. Just around the corner, the restaurant’s small hotel (James Joyce) is the ideal choice for overnight accommodation.

Name: Futura
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre overlooking the monumental Piazza San Giustino, this restaurant has a traditional feel in keeping with its location, enhanced by typical brick walls in dining rooms arranged on two floors. In contrast, the predominantly meat-based cuisine is contemporary in style, with some interesting technical and creative twists.

Name: Il Presidente
Description: This restaurant situated in an alleyway in the historic centre just a few metres from Lucera’s cathedral was once home to the stables of an old palazzo. Nowadays, the dining room, which is crowned by a stone-vaulted ceiling and decorated in shades of black and gold, is divided into small sections. In the middle room, two glass cabinets display the wine selection, which includes over 400 different labels. The Mediterranean cuisine served here is modern and colourful, with vegetables often accompanying the fish and seafood (red tuna, swordfish, prawns, scampi and a delicious seafood focaccia). The ingredients are more important than the technique, resulting in dishes that are full of flavour!

Name: Osteria della Tana
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Occupying the same red house as chef Alessandro Dal Degan’s gourmet restaurant, the Osteria is where this chef turns his attention to more traditional dishes (meat and fish alike), which are often typical of the Veneto. There’s one highly recommended exception, however, namely the carbonara dell’Osteria, prepared with top-quality ingredients from the region. Also popular are the baccalà alla vicentina (dried cod) and the tripe, both of which feature on a menu with a wide selection, including renowned dishes from the chef’s Michelin-starred restaurant. Full-bodied flavours that will delight the palate.

Name: Belé
Description: The name says it all – in Milanese dialect, “belé” means beautiful and the word is an apt description of this restaurant. Belé is charmingly lit by an old-fashioned chandelier on which the pieces of crystal create a play of light resembling an intricate and shifting lace-like pattern. The dining rooms are decorated in attractive contemporary colours, with comfortable armchairs and acoustics perfect for conversation, while the cuisine is Italian with a modern twist.

Name: Kosmo Taste the Mountain
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the centre and also accessible from the ski slopes in winter, this contemporary, Alpine-style restaurant boasts a spacious dining room and large picture windows. The cuisine reflects the traditions of the Valtellina mountains, with a dedicated space for the charcoal grill and an excellent selection of cheeses. The extensive wine list pays particular attention to mountain wines produced by wineries with a sustainable focus.

Name: Concezione Restaurant
Description: This minimalist-style restaurant is home to one of the most interesting young chefs in Catania. In this historic building with beautiful ceilings, enjoy top-quality Sicilian cuisine created by Manuel Tropea, who focuses in particular on specialities from Catania which he interprets in a highly personalised way with a real focus on tradition. Dishes such as “L’Asina e la lattuga” and “Good morning in Catania” are good examples. The chef’s surprise menu takes guests on a culinary journey full of contrasts which is inspired by his own memories and experiences.

Name: Essentia
Address: piazza San Nicolò 2, Castrocaro Terme, 47011, Italy
Description: Situated at the foot of the fortress in the historic centre of Castrocaro, this restaurant has an interesting young chef at the helm, Andrea Giacchini. The cuisine often (but not always) has a local influence and demonstrates remarkable technical expertise that is neither overly ostentatious nor an end in itself, but rather a way of skilfully showcasing the top-quality ingredients used.

Name: Frades La Terrazza
Address: SP94 - Località Abbiadori, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: Situated in a panoramic location on Cala di Volpe bay, this trendy restaurant serves excellent cuisine with a focus on Sardinian specialities and other Mediterranean dishes. There’s a beautiful terrace for an aperitif, plus tapas options to share and a good selection of sparkling wines. Young and enthusiastic staff.

Name: La Loggia Bistrò
Description: Tucked into a slightly secluded courtyard yet still in the heart of the city, this venue offers alfresco service of discreet charm during the summer months. The interiors surprise with dramatic hot-air balloons descending from the ceiling, design details that help create a distinctive and welcoming atmosphere. The culinary offering moves between dishes rooted in local tradition and more creative forays, including some appealing fish options.

Name: Gennaro Di Pace
Address: vicolo della Chiesa 8, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: The owner-chef’s Calabrian origins are evident on a menu that combines Mediterranean cuisine (including fish and seafood) with Piedmontese specialities and showcases beautifully presented dishes prepared using contemporary techniques. This small modern restaurant situated near Perno castle is also open at lunchtime (by prior reservation only).

Name: Regio Patio
Address: via San Francesco d'Assisi 23, Garda, 37016, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the lakefront, this elegant gourmet restaurant in the Regina Adelaide hotel boasts an attractive English-style garden, as well as a beautiful outdoor patio and stylish dining room. The two tasting menus served here (one of which is vegetarian) showcase the traditions of Lake Garda and its surrounding region with a creative twist using vegetables from the property’s own kitchen garden and a focus on seasonal ingredients. There’s also an extensive wine list.

Name: Trattoria al Ponte
Address: via Bertolda 27, località Bornio, Lusia, 45020, Italy
Description: Recognized as the only “Historic Establishment of Italy” in the province of Rovigo, this inviting, family-run trattoria offers traditional cooking with a strong emphasis on meat dishes, served in typically generous portions. The menu is enhanced by daily specials, shared verbally, which can be enjoyed in the warm, welcoming dining rooms or on the charming terrace at the entrance. A park with a natural pond and swimming pool provides an ideal setting also for events.

Name: Degli Angeli
Address: località Madonna degli Angeli, Magliano Sabina, 02046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: The family that runs this excellent restaurant with views of the surrounding countryside has been doing so with passion and experience for over a century. The menu here focuses on the culinary traditions of Lazio, while the wine and extra-virgin olive oil are also sourced locally. The restaurant is part of a hotel and includes a shop (La Bottega delle Delizie) selling home-made produce.

Name: La Sosta di Ottone III
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Ask for directions to this restaurant when you make your booking, as you’ll need to leave your vehicle in a private car park at the entrance to the village and then make your way uphill on foot. Situated in one of Liguria’s most typical and picturesque inland villages with views of the sea in the distance, the restaurant offers outdoor dining under a wisteria in fine weather. The menu features a small choice of regional dishes, with the same focus on Liguria evident on the wine list.

Name: Ristorante 1500
Address: via Pavicolo 43, funivia per raggiungere il ristorante in via Villa 3, San Vigilio, 39011, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: If you’re not a guest at the Vigilius Mountain Resort hotel where this restaurant is situated, leave your car in Lana and take the short cable-car ride to Monte San Vigilio where you’ll find the hotel at an altitude of 1 500m (remember to check the time of the last cable-car back down the mountain!). Decorated with a profusion of wood, the dining room has the same modern feel as the creative mountain cuisine prepared by the new chef who started here in 2023.

Name: Osteria del Guà
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in the “barchessa” of a Palladian villa dating from 1541, this restaurant boasts an elegant dining room with an open fireplace. The cuisine here is creative and of excellent quality, with many of the main meat courses cooked over the barbecue grill. All in all, a romantic setting and superb food that is not to be missed.

Name: da Omar
Address: via Dante Alighieri 21, Lido di Jesolo, 30016, Italy
Description: Passion and enthusiasm overcome all obstacles and lead to the best results: this summarises the professional journey of the chef at this restaurant. He prepares fish dishes inspired by classic Italian cuisine, sometimes with a modern twist, but always using the best quality produce.

Name: Vino Buono
Address: via Castello 20, Grumello del Monte, 24064, Italy
Description: Housed in an old 17C hay barn near the Duomo belltower, this interesting wine bar offers around 400 different labels to accompany an array of simple yet well-prepared traditional dishes (including a few fish options). Highlights include the cured hams, cheeses and the excellent starters.

Name: Osteria dai Mazzeri
Description: Once the town hall of Follina, this building dating from 1704 is now home to a restaurant run by two brothers who serve delicious regional and seasonal cuisine here (in winter, don’t miss the spit-roasted chicken, veal or pork cooked according to local tradition). A beautiful mulberry tree, the old symbol of the village that was once involved in the silk industry, graces the outdoor dining space.

Name: Corsaro Nero
Address: Località Portu Maga, Marina di Arbus, 09031, Italy
Description: A wide choice of fresh fish and a menu with a firm focus on fish and seafood served in a large dining room offering views of the spectacular sunsets.

Name: Crotto Valtellina
Address: via Fiume 11, località Valle, Malnate, 21046, Italy
Description: For over fifty years, the Valbuzzi family has passionately maintained this enchanting crotto, now in its third generation. The atmosphere is elegant and refined while staying true to its origins: wooden tables, period furnishings, and floral touches. The summer veranda is particularly stunning, overlooking a lush garden and a sandstone wall. The menu balances traditional dishes – the pizzoccheri are unmissable – with more contemporary creations, such as the surprising saltimbocca of larded quail with fennel, escarole gel, pickled apricot, and zucchini flan.

Name: Vesta Versilia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within Twiga beach establishment, in a setting where glamour reigns supreme, multifunctional and equipped with a fully-fledged cocktail bar, the cuisine favours classic recipes and cooking methods, but equally dedicates substantial attention to raw seafood and pizza. From our last visit, the seafood salad—boasting excellent varied citronette-dressed products—and the roast turbot with lemon potato cream and asparagus stand particularly memorable.

Name: Giglio
Description: Housed in a beautiful 18C palazzo, Giglio boasts a superb location in one of the many squares in Lucca’s charming historic centre, as well as a delightful outdoor space. The meat and fish dishes on the menu here are inspired by traditional Italian recipes and reinterpreted with a light modern touch – a good example is the siphoned potato which is sprinkled with bottarga and served with a squid sauce, chanterelle mushrooms and spicy parsley cream. The bread is always excellent.

Name: La Rosina
Description: With over 100 years of history behind it, La Rosina is still looking good, thanks to renovation work carried out a few years ago which has given the restaurant a new look. Situated in an attractive location in the hills around Marostica, this excellent restaurant is a sound choice for good food in the province of Vicenza, serving modern regional and Italian dishes which are full of flavour. Enjoy beautiful views of the surrounding hills from the guestrooms.

Name: Buca di Sant'Antonio
Description: Just a stone’s throw from Piazza San Michele, in the heart of the beautiful historic centre of Lucca, the Buca di Sant'Antonio dates back over 200 years and is one of the city’s oldest restaurants. Here, the old copper pots and pans that hang from the ceiling add to the warm, romantic atmosphere, while the cuisine unsurprisingly showcases traditional Tuscan specialities including meat dishes and home-made pasta.

Name: Osteria Il Bagatto
Address: via XX Settembre 16, Limone Piemonte, 12015, Italy
Description: Nestled amid the stone houses of Limone Piemonte, this charming gourmet restaurant is situated in a typical historic passageway. Influenced by the seasons and the chef’s creative skills, the menu includes interesting dishes such as char, gnocchi with blue goat’s cheese and delicious sweetbreads in butter with cannellini beans and cavolo nero. To accompany your meal, you might like to indulge in a bottle of vintage Barolo chosen from the concise yet carefully chosen wine list. The 2013 Michele Chiarlo Barolo Cerequio, produced in a cold and rainy year, has aged well thanks to its powerful tannins.

Name: Nicolin
Address: via Paisiello 4, località Maggianico, Lecco, 23900, Italy
Description: Restaurant-hotel not far from the centre, but in a quiet, residential area, this is where you can find some of the best cuisine in town. The cook revisits some national dishes in a personal way, with a few seafood offerings as well.

Name: Duo Ristorante
Description: This elegant, intimate restaurant with subdued lighting is the perfect choice for a romantic gourmet dinner. Showcased on tasting menus and a concise à la carte, the excellent cuisine focuses on typical recipes and specialities from Puglia, often with an added personalised and creative twist.

Name: La Tavola
Description: Situated in the Il Porticciolo hotel, this restaurant will appeal to anyone who enjoys a lakeside setting. Leave your car in the car park, then take the lift down to the dining room with its windows overlooking the water and views of the opposite shore of Lake Maggiore. The lake also takes pride of place in some of the creative, elaborate and personalised dishes on the two tasting menus created by Riccardo Bassetti, many of which feature freshwater fish.

Name: Cavalluccio Marino
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Imaginative cuisine in a long - established family restaurant, which is constantly updated by each generation. Situated away from the town centre, yet easily accessible, the restaurant boasts an enviable seafront location. Excellent selection of local and international wines.

Name: Ruris
Address: Via Spiaggie Rosse, località Mazzotta, Isola di Capo Rizzuto, 88841, Italy
Description: Despite its rural setting inland, this restaurant is still situated within the Capo Rizzuto e Mar Ionio protected marine reserve, which helps to explain the focus on fish and seafood dishes demonstrated by owner-chef Natale Pallone on the menu. The wine cellar boasts over 200 different wines and more than 60 internationally renowned spirits.

Name: Antica Osteria Magenes
Description: This fascinating restaurant occupying an old house renovated in modern style comes as a surprise given its location in a small village deep in the countryside. Enjoy traditional cuisine reinterpreted in a playful and original way in the well-tended garden, where six exclusive tables provide the perfect setting for an intimate and romantic alfresco dinner.

Name: Osteria Borgo Ronche
Description: With only a handful of tables – all the more reason to reserve – and a contemporary, streamlined yet welcoming setting, this intimate spot showcases the chef-owner’s resolutely seafood-focused cuisine, though a couple of meat options round out the menu. Preparations and pairings remain largely classic, as seen in the gratinéed Breton scallops, while raw seafood also makes an appearance, sometimes unexpectedly atop pasta, as in the standout spaghettoni with cacio e pepe and red prawn tartare.

Name: Filippino
Description: Opened in 1910, this historic restaurant with an attractive shaded outdoor pergola serves an extensive array of delicious local fish prepared in traditional recipes. Enjoy a selection of typical Sicilian specialities prepared by the Bernardi family, including the highly recommended “Nonno Filippino” fish soup.

Name: Bistrot Royal
Description: Inside the refined Grand Hotel Royal e Golf, the Bistrot offers the opportunity to savor the delicious flavors of Valle d’Aosta in a refined and lighter interpretation. In recipes where the quality of the raw ingredients takes center stage, you’ll be pampered by excellent service while comfortably seated in spaces that interpret Alpine style with personal touches.

Name: Il Pescatore
Address: via Acqua Dolce 7, Cala Gonone, 08022, Italy
Description: This Mediterranean-style restaurant has the evocative feel of a seaside village with its beautiful photos of the coast on the walls. It’s best to book ahead if you want one of the tables on the small terrace overlooking the sea. To avoid confusion, note that the Il Pescatore that we recommend is situated at 7, via Acqua Dolce.

Name: Botero
Description: Close to the city centre and within walking distance of the Cathedral, the restaurant is located inside a beautiful historic building. The cuisine is fragrant, and the menu alternates between seafood offerings – depending on market availability – and a few more traditional recipes such as hand-pinched Cremasque sweet tortelli. The jovial welcome, streamlined service and interesting wine list (with a few "natural" offerings for enthusiasts) explain why there is a large turnout for both lunch and dinner. Better make reservations!

Name: Osteria dai Coghi
Address: via Alcide De Gasperi 9/13, Albarè di Costermano, 37010, Italy
Description: This well-kept, welcoming restaurant with a colourful decor and wine bottles adorning the walls serves imaginative dishes with modern combinations – our inspector particularly enjoyed the guinea fowl supreme with smoked black tea, carrots and beluga lentils. The well-chosen wine list features labels from Italy and further afield.

Name: Osteria dalla Peppa
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Traditional Cuisine
Description: A trattoria in the old town, with rooms filled with memories and nostalgia, offering an atmosphere that makes you feel at home, just like the traditional cuisine. The fresh-egg pasta rolled out with a rolling pin (also on sale in their nearby shop) is the main attraction here, with main courses featuring various types of meat, and fish dishes on Fridays.

Name: Ai Torchi
Description: Occupying a 17C olive oil press in the heart of a charming medieval village, this restaurant has retained its old stone mill and wooden press in its vaulted dining room, which provides the backdrop for imaginative fish and seafood dishes prepared using top-quality local ingredients. The delicious Italian-style ceviche is made from the catch of the day, while the Mare Mare mixed fish dish is baked in a casserole with cherry tomatoes, courgettes and bay leaves. If you’re looking for a simpler option, try the I Torchiettibistro on the corner of the same street.

Name: L'Antico Giardino
Description: A menu steeped in Ferrarese tradition, served in a welcoming and comfortable setting, energised by the friendly charm of the owner, who offers valuable advice on the best wine and food pairings. The menu features flavours that seduce the senses: passatelli drenched in a velvety cheese fondue, enriched with morel mushrooms and the intense aroma of autumn black truffle ; soft and juicy larded pheasant breast accompanied by a Castelmagno custard that caresses the palate; and to finish, a soft cheesecake with double white chocolate and pistachio mousse, topped with a blackberry sauce. And, season permitting, the king of the table: the white truffle, ready to enhance every dish.

Name: Aurora
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the Concattedrale di San Pietro Apostolo, Aurora boasts a cheerful and contemporary-style dining room with colourful furnishings, soft lighting and plenty of wine bottles on display. The carefully prepared cuisine includes Italian and regional meat and fish specialities with a light, modern twist.

Name: Emilio
Address: via Girardi 1, loc. Casabianca, Fermo, 63900, Italy
Description: With 60 years of history behind it, Emilio can definitely be described as a leading light on the region’s restaurant scene. The restaurant is renowned for its excellent fish, which is usually cooked in classic style (fish stew and mixed steamed fish served on steamed vegetables are prime examples) and often announced at your table, although a concise menu is also available. The elegant dining room is enhanced by a collection of striking works of art.

Name: Osteria Vecchio Borgo
Description: Described as a “meeting point between Piedmont and Liguria”, this quiet, welcoming restaurant in the historic centre of Cuneo focuses on ingredients and recipes from these two regions – the family, all of whom are involved in the restaurant (the women in the kitchen and the men front of house), are from Liguria. The generous, top-quality cuisine is prepared using seasonal produce with a personalised touch and is accompanied by a good selection of wine, also available by the glass.

Name: 4 Ciance
Description: Two bright rooms in the heart of the old town welcome guests with warmth and professionalism, courtesy of the all-female staff. A refined atmosphere, the scent of wood and meticulous attention to detail create the backdrop for the dishes created by the two chefs, conceived to delight both the eyes and the palate. The menu is based on solid traditional foundations, but with contemporary and creative touches. Choose from two tasting menus and an à la carte menu, featuring dishes made with seasonal ingredients. The focus is on meat, as is traditional in Piedmont, but there are also refined seafood alternatives for those looking for different flavours.

Name: La Meridiana
Description: In business for over 50 years, this long-established, centrally located restaurant has changed its look over the years and is now a modern bistro with an attractive outdoor summer space overlooking the magical town centre. Here, the owner-chef serves fish prepared in two different ways, either in typical Italian tradition or in a style inspired by his native Spain – his paella is definitely worth sampling! The front of house is overseen by the owner’s friendly wife, who is also at hand to help with your wine choices.

Name: Cucina Bacilieri
Description: A small restaurant in the heart of the city, refined and romantic, where soft spotlights cast a gentle glow over the tables, creating an intimate, comforting atmosphere. The flavors are entrusted to chef-owner Bacilieri, who crafts modern, harmonious dishes rooted in seasonality and the freshness of ingredients, spanning both meat and fish. Not to be missed: the dessert course, here it is a true indulgence for the palate. Service, led by a young, passionate team, attends to every detail of the experience with warmth and care.

Name: Menzaghi
Address: via San Giovanni 74, Fagnano Olona, 21054, Italy
Description: Once you’ve found the car park, make your way to this restaurant’s small, traditional dining room where you will be warmly welcomed by the owner (a real wine enthusiast) and well looked after by his friendly yet efficient staff. Generous cuisine with plenty of attention paid to local, seasonal ingredients and daily specials that come highly recommended.

Name: Mirko's
Address: discesa Annunziata 1, Castellammare del Golfo, 91014, Italy
Description: This small restaurant, located near the steps to Cala Piccola, is run by an entire family and is beginning to earn an excellent local reputation. The son is at the helm in the kitchen. Having gained experience elsewhere for many years, he decided to start his own venture, which shows every sign of having paid off. Enjoy excellent fish and seafood specialities cooked in Mediterranean and Sicilian style in a quiet, beautifully kept dining room.

Name: Entrà
Address: via Salde Entrà 60, località Entrà, Finale Emilia, 41034, Italy
Description: Make sure you use your sat-nav to get to this restaurant as finding the right road through the countryside can be a challenge, although once you’re here you’ll be glad you made the effort. The trattoria occupies a wine shop dating from 1919, from which it has retained a few attractive and nostalgic touches despite its renovation. The cuisine focuses on a few regional dishes which are announced at your table by the owner himself.

Name: Alla Lanterna
Description: On the Adriatic coast road south of Fano, run by the same family since 1976, the year it opened, this restaurant is a must for seafood lovers. The dishes are essentially inspired by the seafaring traditions of the Marche region.

Name: Nni Lausta
Address: via Risorgimento 188, Santa Marina Salina, 98050, Italy
Description: Fish plays the starring role here, where the authentic traditional flavours and ingredients of Aeolian cuisine are skilfully interpreted with a touch of imaginative flair. If it’s not too hot to sit outside, ask for a table on the pleasant, shaded terrace on the first floor.

Name: La Bottega del 30
Address: via Santa Caterina 2, località Villa a Sesta, Castelnuovo Berardenga, 53019, Italy
Description: There’s a story behind the name of this restaurant: on the 30th day of every month a travelling salesman used to stop in this small, delightful village. In the meantime, a young French chef, Hélène, arrived here and fell in love with Chianti and its cuisine. She named her restaurant after the travelling salesman and the name has been kept in his memory. In a typical setting of stone walls and old rural objects from bygone days, Hélène is now front-of-house taking care of guests, while Nadia Mongiat has replaced her in the kitchen, where she continues with the restaurant’s tradition of creating simple Tuscan cuisine. The focus here is on preparing ingredients in traditional ways, such as pork liver (the thinnest part of the liver is used) cooked at a low temperature and then stored in lard with fennel for a few days before being re-heated sous-vide in a bain-marie. As a result, the liver (served lukewarm on a bed of Tuscan green beans) is soft and delicious.

Name: Il Galeone
Description: In a bright, elegant and modern dining room inside the Elisabeth Due hotel, Galeone is one of the city's finest gastronomic destinations. The menu focuses on fish, with dishes that draw on local traditions, such as “brodetto alla fanese” fish soup (available by advance order), alongside more creative offerings.

Name: Locanda Gulfi
Description: In an isolated but well‑marked location that doesn’t escape the notice of oil and wine enthusiasts, Locanda Gulfi produces both, as you can tell from the view of the wine cellar visible from the dining room. The cuisine offers revisited Sicilian dishes, with the possibility of overnight accommodation and, naturally, tastings of the estate’s products, accompanied by dedicated menus or simple snacks specially designed for the occasion.

Name: Lord Nelson
Description: Set right on the seafront, with a delightful outdoor seating area, this historic restaurant – opened in 1969 and dedicated to the famous English admiral – boasts classic elegance with mahogany furnishings and light-coloured curtains reminiscent of unfurled sails. Mediterranean-inspired cuisine plays with modern and creative touches, such as slow-cooked amberjack served with baby spinach, pine nuts, marjoram and date tomato sauce.

Name: SaleGrosso
Address: viale II Giugno 15, Milano Marittima, 48015, Italy
Description: One of the town’s authentic favourites, this fish restaurant has a pleasant, light - coloured decor inspired by the sea. The eclectic cuisine includes tapas and raw fish dishes.

Name: Ristorante Mas-cì
Description: Situated in the charming historic centre, this hotel and restaurant are now run by the third generation of the same family. Welcoming dining rooms with a fireplace provide the setting for cuisine which makes the most of local produce while also including dishes from elsewhere in Italy. Don’t miss the black truffle specialities!

Name: Galileo
Address: via IV Novembre conc. 25, Civitanova Marche, 62012, Italy
Description: Boasting a dining room overlooking the beach, Galileo is a typical Adriatic restaurant serving fish and seafood dishes that are popular with many Italians. Options include seafood salad, a selection of antipasti, fish and seafood pastas, assorted small fried fish, and grilled recipes. In other words, delicious, traditional and unfussy cuisine in which fish takes centre stage.

Name: Carlo Magno
Description: This restaurant housed in a country house dating from the 19C offers elegant period dining rooms and a menu featuring Mediterranean-style meat and fish dishes.

Name: Pantagruele
Description: Situated in the town centre just a stone’s throw from the port, this small, typical trattoria is renowned for its delicious fish and seafood, including an excellent antipasto buffet and fresh fish cooked mainly on the grill. The large outdoor area is perfect for summer dining. Informal service.

Name: La Porta Antica
Address: via Quarto dei Mille 16, Brescia, 25128, Italy
Description: Contemporary interiors and a prime location in a quiet residential neighborhood provide the backdrop for a seafood-focused kitchen that balances measured creativity with precise flavors. The shellfish selection excels: from prized Sicilian red prawns to steamed jumbo shrimp, refined and elevated by a soft bean purée with crispy guanciale.

Name: Villa Tiboldi
Address: via Case Sparse 127, località Tiboldi, Canale, 12043, Italy
Description: A delightful combination of good food and a romantic ambience in this old restored farmhouse surrounded by hills. Top - quality cuisine and a wine cellar that is well worth a visit.

Name: Alle Codole
Address: via XX Agosto 27, Canale d'Agordo, 32020, Italy
Description: ‘Codole’ is the nickname of the family that runs this restaurant and whose ancestors once worked in the copper mines in the area. Today, the family has exchanged mining for cooking, offering guests specialities such as ricotta and black truffle ravioli with a lamb ragù, and loin of venison in a porcini mushroom crust.

Name: La Madia
Description: This authentic rural trattoria overlooking the valley and Franciacorta specialises in regional produce and typical Italian cuisine. Each dish on the menu lists the origin of the ingredients used, plus the name and address of the producer. Specialities include tagliolini pasta sautéed in a walnut sauce with tuna. Top quality cuisine offering excellent value for money.

Name: La Bul
Description: Here, in one of Bari’s most interesting restaurants, chef Antonio Scalera serves top-quality cuisine accompanied by intelligently chosen wines with fascinating stories behind them. The dishes often feature traditional recipes and ingredients from Puglia yet are creative and of the highest quality.

Name: Al Carroponte
Description: This restaurant is renowned in Bergamo for its good choice of varied cuisine, as well as its lively, buzzing atmosphere. The excellent, tasty cuisine is typically Italian and contemporary in style, and includes luxury ingredients such as lobster and caviar, while the “classic” à la carte is enhanced by a selection of cured hams, cheeses and finger food. But the Carroponte’s beating heart is owner Oscar Mazzoleni’s passion for the world of wine, with an incredible selection of over 2 000 labels that puts many more famous Michelin-starred restaurants in the shade.

Name: Matteo Ristorante
Description: In elegant and intimate spaces with soft, muted tones, guests enjoy the contemporary cuisine of Matteo Marra. Meat and fish feature equally on the menu, with a constant emphasis on meticulously crafted and spectacular presentations of dishes. A small outdoor area sits under a portico, with tables that must be reserved well in advance during the warmer months. Coffee and aperitif service is also available at the adjacent Laboratorio, at No. 10.

Name: Macelleria Motta
Address: strada Padana Superiore 90, Bellinzago Lombardo, 20060, Italy
Description: Motta has established a reputation for quality, especially for its meat which is carefully sourced from farms in the Piedmont region. Some of the excellent options on the menu are aged in a large fridge near the entrance, along with different types of delicious salumi which are produced and cured by the restaurant. Various types of meat feature here – these are cured or cooked using classic methods with the occasional modern touch. Piedmontese beef is one of the highlights, with different cuts grilled on the barbecue or served boiled. Make sure you try the 300g hamburger with Aosta valley Toma cheese, BBQ sauce and caramelised onions served in a sesame-seed bun. Enjoy alfresco dining in a typical Lombardy courtyard in summer.

Name: I Carracci
Description: Attention: from 29/06 to 14/09/2025, service will be temporarily transferred to the '800 Hall. The ceiling entirely adorned with marvellous frescoes from the Carracci school—extraordinary Bolognese painters of the sixteenth century—already serves as a compelling incentive for selecting this venue for gourmet pauses. Young and talented Chef Agostino Schettino offers a cuisine drawing inspiration from across Italy, elaborated through a modern lens. Particularly noteworthy is the homage to Bologna with a tasting menu dedicated to the city—"La Dotta, la Grassa e la Rossa"—featuring classic 36-month Parmesan cream tortellini.

Name: Locanda San Michele
Address: SS 491 3, Contrada Camerale di Tossiccia, Montorio al Vomano, 64046, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Practically on the slopes of Gran Sasso with views of the verdant landscapes of the Abruzzo, this restaurant is home to a local chef who has returned to his roots having spent time away gaining experience in Michelin-starred restaurants. Here, he serves regional cuisine with a modern, contemporary twist and a focus on meat and fish alike (examples include tuna tartare with strawberries finished in the dining room with lemon “snow”) in generous portions that are typical of the Abruzzo.

Name: Antica Trattoria Giovanelli
Description: Situated in a charming rural setting at the foot of the surrounding hills, this trattoria has been run by the same family (now on the third generation) since 1939. Regional cuisine is to the fore here, with cured hams and roast and boiled meats all featuring on the menu, as well as its highly recommended homemade pastas and the almond tart with zabaione.

Name: Barbieri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Enjoy your meal in the classic - style dining room or on the outdoor terrace in fine weather. The menu here is seasonal, with a focus on delicious Calabrian cuisine, while the wine list also features exclusively local options.

Name: Frosio
Description: Housed in a 18C villa which was once a family inn, this restaurant is run by the dynamic and professional Frosio family who have over 30 years’ experience in the restaurant business. There’s nothing improvised about Frosio, where Camillo guarantees impeccable service front of house and Paolo is at the helm in the kitchen, creating carefully prepared dishes with a classic-modern feel and an equal emphasis on meat and fish, often made from traditionally “gourmet” ingredients such as scampi, lobster, foie gras, pigeon and caviar. The wine list continues to offer an excellent selection, with one section dedicated to Italy and another to the rest of the world. Decorated with austere elegance, the wine cellar in the 13C tower is home to more than 1,000 different labels. Attractive outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: 177 toledo
Description: On the fifth floor of 177, via Toledo this restaurant exhibits works of art by contemporary artists in its elegant dining room. Delightful artisanal skills from Campania are also featured on the menu, which is made from handmade paper from Amalfi; the manner in which the menu is written recalls the game of Tombola (which originated in Naples), in original and creative reinterpretations of classic regional dishes.

Name: Agriturismo Ferdy
Address: Località Fienili, fraz. Scalvino, Lenna, 24010, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Once you’ve left your car in the car park and crossed the Brembo river, you enter a fairytale setting of meadows and horses surrounded by the Orobic peaks. Here, the cuisine is a declaration of love for the mountains – although occasionally elaborate, the carefully prepared dishes are substantial and full of flavour, with the same solid character as the inhabitants of these valleys and with meat and dairy produce taking centre stage. The cheese trolley at the end of your meal is a real highlight – there’s something here for all tastes! The wine list is also full of character, featuring a personalised selection which showcases regional labels and natural wines. It’s worth noting that between 30 to 50 different labels are available by the glass at different times of year. Guestrooms and a shop selling typical local produce complete the picture at what is an extraordinary, high-end agriturismo.

Name: Crotasc
Address: via Don Primo Lucchinetti 63, Mese, 23020, Italy
Description: Here one can choose between a smaller, typically mountain style dining room with stone paving and open fireplace and a larger room in contemporary rustic style. In summer one can dine on the terrace.

Name: Ai Do Campanili
Address: via Marco Polo 2, località Treporti, Cavallino, 30013, Italy
Description: Both the building in which it is housed and the dining room of this restaurant are on the small side, but the quality of the food more than compensates for the lack of space. Run by young and enthusiastic staff, the restaurant specialises in fish and seafood with raw options and modern dishes featuring on the menu. Excellent selection of wine, also available to take away.

Name: La Nicchia
Description: This tastefully decorated restaurant is housed in a late - 18C building, which is marked on an old map from the Napoleonic era. Here the best local ingredients are selected to create regional dishes with the occasional contemporary twist.

Name: Der Unterwirt
Description: Occupying a private house, this restaurant boasts a couple of charming Stube-style dining rooms, one of which is highly romantic and dates back to the 13C – although the vintage wood looks as though it may have come from elsewhere, it has in fact been here for centuries. Owner-chef Thomas Haselwanter creates carefully thought-out dishes which combine precision and classic comfort with the occasional modern touch, harmoniously combining the flavours of the Alto Adige with Mediterranean influences, with a particular focus on fish. A welcoming outdoor terrace for summer dining and seven modern guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Coeur de Bois
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Classic Cuisine
Description: The name of this elegant restaurant was inspired by its wooden ceiling. Surrounded by spruce decor dating from the 18C, antique furniture and paintings, enjoy interesting traditional cuisine in this excellent gourmet restaurant, which is all the more attractive thanks to its location in the Gran Paradiso national park.

Name: Osteria Cascina dei Fiori
Description: This restaurant’s warm, elegant and rustic atmosphere with wooden furniture and exposed beams provides the setting for its seasonally inspired, regional cuisine. The experienced owners are welcoming and attentive, while the menu features specialities such as frogs’ leg and courgette flower risotto.

Name: Zur Kaiserkron
Description: In the heart of Bolzano, on the ground floor of the refined Palazzo Pock which grandly overlooks the piazza, Zur Kaiserkron (The Imperial Crown) welcomes guests in elegant, contemporary surroundings enhanced by striking vaulted ceilings that lend a touch of theatricality to the experience. Since 2025, chef Sinisgalli’s vision unfolds along two distinct paths, designed to suit different guests and moments of the day. The first offers a light, dynamic cuisine firmly anchored to the territory, where traditional flavors are reinterpreted with contemporary spirit, ideal for a city in constant motion. The second, housed in a gilded dining room with an almost suspended charm, represents the chef’s deeper, more creative soul: a gastronomic journey that delves into research, technique, and imagination, delivering an immersive experience of great intensity.

Name: La Luge
Address: Perreres, loc. Varvoyes, Breuil Cervinia, 11021, Italy
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Italian
Description: Situated in a tranquil, panoramic location on the road to Breuil-Cervinia (less than 4km away), this old farm has been transformed over the past decade into an intimate little hotel with a good restaurant decorated in attractive mountain style and enhanced by a fireplace that is always lit in winter. Here, you can enjoy simple, authentic cuisine prepared from top-quality ingredients with careful attention paid to seasonality. The owner himself oversees the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: Wine & Dine
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: In the center of Canazei, this restaurant within the Croce Bianca hotel occupies wood-paneled rooms that foster a relaxed, informal atmosphere, with a few charming alcoves for more intimate seating. Meat reigns supreme, notably a dedicated selection of grilled main courses. A good assortment of wines by the glass.

Name: Extra
Description: Situated slightly inland behind Marina di Carrara, Extra (the name refers to the quality of the region’s world-famous marble) is a bright, modern restaurant with a menu inspired by the area’s fish and seafood culinary traditions. The menu is slightly more elaborate and the ambience more elegant in the evening and on Saturday lunchtimes.

Name: Tenuta del Gallo
Description: Whether you dine indoors in the charming, romantic dining room or outdoors with views of the surrounding countryside, you’ll enjoy traditional local cuisine and classic Italian favourites at this restaurant. Our inspectors particularly enjoyed the excellent beef carpaccio with truffles and the local guinea fowl with chickpeas. Comfortable guestrooms are also available.

Name: Antica Osteria dei Camelì
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Within a sixteenth-century farmhouse of intact charm, where historic rooftops now coexist with modern solar panels in a clear gesture of sustainability, this establishment represents a successful encounter between classic elegance and contemporary design. The kitchen follows the same philosophy: tradition and innovation converse naturally in dishes that place great emphasis on nutritional balance and wholesome pairings, thanks in part to ingredients sourced from trusted local farmers. In the dining room, service maintains the professionalism and courtesy it has always been known for, affirming an approach that has lost neither rigor nor warmth over time.

Name: Paolo Teverini
Address: via del Popolo 2, Bagno di Romagna, 47021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the charming village of Bagno di Romagna and surrounded by beautiful rolling hills, Teverini is a culinary name full of history in this area. The cuisine here demonstrates different traditions – the local region is an obvious influence (especially its mushrooms), but fish and seafood also feature along with plenty of vegetables.

Name: Lu Pisantinu
Address: viale Giovanni Maria Orecchioni snc, loc. Liscia di Vacca, Porto Cervo, 07021, Italy
Description: A terrace framed by granite columns overlooks the coast, the sea, and Porto Cervo (about 2 km away): both the culinary style and the overall décor of the welcoming spaces are classic. The menu features primarily seafood, though there are also dishes and flavors from the inland area, with nods to Gallura traditions, such as the strictly handmade chijusoni gnocchetti. Welcoming you is a local family that has been operating here for over 40 years.

Name: La Fiaschetteria
Description: Enjoy excellent reinterpretations of Emilian classics in this large 18C farmhouse. It is lit with modern designer - style chandeliers and warmed by a large fireplace. The three splendid guestrooms combine elegance with typical regional decor.

Name: Pascalucci
Address: via Appia 1, San Nicola Manfredi, 82010, Italy
Description: A traditional restaurant serving regional cuisine, as well as skilfully prepared fish dishes made from fresh produce. Specialities include Beneventano beef fillet and octopus in aspic jelly.

Name: Parco Gambrinus
Address: via Capitello 18, San Polo di Piave, 31020, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A rustic and romantic setting provides the backdrop for the traditional and creative cuisine served here. It is made from typical local produce with an emphasis on ethical and sustainably produced ingredients (vegan and gluten - free options are also available). Exotic animals inhabit the park, where a stream is home to the house specialities of crayfish, eels and sturgeon. The restaurant also offers a few comfortable guestrooms nearby.

Name: Bistrot La Perla
Address: strada Col Alt 105, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list
Description: Take a culinary journey from the north of Italy to the south from the comfort of your table at the Bistrot La Perla, where guests are enthusiastically introduced to the many delightful flavours and ingredients this beautiful country has to offer. Excellent fish specialities also available.

Name: Babette
Description: Situated just beyond the centre of Albenga in a beautiful location right on the beach (with only a small private beach club separating it from the sea), this restaurant has been in business for over 20 years (10 years on this site, and 10 in the town centre before that). It is renowned for its excellent, modern cuisine that focuses on top-quality, fresh and seasonal fish. A lighter (yet equally excellent) menu is also available at lunchtime.

Name: Il Baretto
Description: Il Baretto on the outskirts of Padova is a must for anyone who loves classic, traditional fish and seafood, thanks to its menu which includes a number of typical Venetian dishes. The top-quality fish is skilfully prepared to bring out its full flavour and distinctive characteristics, providing a real treat for the tastebuds in this inland temple to the sea.

Name: Locanda dell'Arcimboldo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the town gates, a friendly inn with a family atmosphere in a fine building, with a pleasant veranda. Fish dishes prevail on the menu, featuring an interesting selection of oysters. At midday there is also an easier set menu.

Name: Coltivare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: This small restaurant next to the Brandini winery has chef Luca Zecchin at its helm, a true connoisseur of Langhe culinary traditions and one of the more recent disciples of Lidia Alciati (known as the “queen” of Piedmontese cuisine). Nearly all the ingredients used here are sourced locally, some even from the property itself, such as eggs and vegetables from the kitchen garden. The dishes are divided between those which pay tribute to the traditions of the region (don’t miss the “plin”) and others which showcase the chef’s personal style, including a menu dedicated to the barbecue grill. The latter is even used in some of the sweets, such as the smoky-flavoured bread and chocolate dessert. The wine list demonstrates the same affection for Piedmont, as well as featuring a selection of champagnes. During the day, enjoy the splendid view through the picture windows that surround the dining room, which also boasts a large fireplace.

Name: Locanda di Nonna Ida
Address: Località Pontarola 12, Marano di Valpolicella, 37020, Italy
Description: A welcoming inn nestled amid the last vineyards of Valpolicella and the first pasturelands of the lower Lessinia region, where a young chef serves cuisine with a focus on local ingredients and classic Italian recipes with a modern twist. In summer, the terrace offers a fresh, cool setting with extensive views. The barbecued meat is superb.

Name: Corte Federiciana
Description: The dining room at this restaurant housed in the Palazzo Baronale’s old outbuildings in the historic centre of Apricena boasts an attractive brick-vaulted ceiling. The cuisine, which focuses mainly on fish and seafood (raw, cooked, baked in the oven or served with pasta), effortlessly combines traditional and modern flavours. A delightful welcome and friendly service complete the picture.

Name: Hostaria del Teatro
Address: via Ordanino 5b, Castiglione delle Stiviere, 46043, Italy
Description: This welcoming restaurant with an open-view kitchen serves cuisine influenced by the traditions of Mantova and the Veneto, alongside more creative dishes inspired by the chef’s imagination. The chef’s wife provides a friendly welcome front of house, plus there’s a delightful garden for alfresco dining in fine weather.

Name: La Capanna di Eraclio
Address: Località per Le Venezie 21, Codigoro, 44021, Italy
Description: Whenever we cross the threshold of Capanna di Eraclio, we are embraced by a rare and wonderful feeling, as if we were coming home. Opened in 1922 and now run by the fourth generation of the Soncini family, time seems to have stood still inn this restaurant, which offers the same authenticity that once transformed the inn into a kitchen. The atmosphere is nostalgic and familiar, understated but enhanced with touches of refined elegance. The aromas of the Po delta inspire a repertoire that celebrates water and land: delicate Goro sole, steamed and served with fresh mayonnaise; maltagliati pasta that captures the flavour of clams and savoy cabbage; and the obligatory “arost in umad” eel, golden and succulent, served with white polenta. A unique detail: the dining room is seven metres below sea level, offering guests a truly unique experience.

Name: Le Colonne
Description: In a dining room with marble columns and flooring and enhanced by a beautiful grand piano, Rossana Marziale serves Mediterranean dishes that showcase the ingredients of Caserta and the Campania with a perfect balance of comforting classic flavours and creative modern ideas. Buffalo mozzarella takes pride of place here, presented in many different ways, including in some of the desserts.

Name: Carne & Spirito
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: On the outskirts of the city, meat lovers will find their paradise: the kitchen selects some of the finest breeds from around the world (almost exclusively beef), offered in a variety of cuts and cooked over a Josper charcoal oven: an authentic delight. Cured meats also feature among the starters, alongside fresh pasta and excellent desserts. The wine selection is equally noteworthy, as is the selection by the glass.

Name: San Marco
Description: This long-established restaurant in the Asti region has been open for over 70 years and is still renowned for its regional cuisine served in a classic-style dining room. Dishes include cardoons with Raschera cheese fondue, the famous agnolottini del plin (a type of ravioli), and the Piedmontese bunet which is part of a trio of desserts that includes hazelnut tart and zabaglione with Canelli muscat wine.

Name: Trattoria del Cimino dal 1895
Description: Situated on the hill leading to Palazzo Farnese, this restaurant occupies the oldest building in the village, which dates back to 1370. Since 1940, the Calistri family have been delighting their guests with delicious specialities from Lazio, including excellent cured hams, fresh pasta (the amatriciana is particularly renowned), grilled meats and an impressive selection of cheeses and desserts. Excellent wines and spirits complete the picture.

Name: L'Angolo d'Abruzzo
Description: For almost 40 years, the Angolo d’Abruzzo restaurant has been home to the Centofanti family, who act as excellent ambassadors for the region by offering the best local, seasonal ingredients (for this reason, there’s no fish on the menu) in a host of traditional, regional recipes. Specialities such as cured meats, local ham, bruschetta and fresh home-made pasta (including “chitarra” spaghetti) take centre stage, while main courses include grilled dishes (porcini mushrooms in season, cuts of beef and veal at any time of year) and stews (mutton etc). When it comes to dessert, make sure you try the crème caramel with Navelli saffron. A misleading sign saying “sagrestia” (sacristy) actually indicates the well-stocked wine cellar.

Name: Il Ristorantino - Da Dino
Address: via XXV Aprile 11, Anzola dell'Emilia, 40011, Italy
Description: Hidden among the houses, Ristorantino da Dino is a gem with a family feel, loved by locals and discovered by passersby. The menu is broad and varied, featuring sea, land, and garden offerings. Don't miss the Zuppa Inglese – it's a dive into the authentic flavors of the past.

Name: La Locandiera
Description: At the bottom of a steep valley, a rustic restaurant that offers fine cuisine, much appreciated in the area, with a great preference for local products. Old traditional recipes are revisited with a personal touch.

Name: Bacco
Description: Nestled within the historic centre, you’ll find classic and charming Apulian stone environments of a fourteenth-century building, while the kitchen sends forth predominantly fish dishes, along with some meat offerings, in classic Italian tradition recipes with a few modern twists.

Name: SottoSopra
Description: A pleasant and colourful restaurant in the village centre, divided into several dining rooms. The owner-chef prepares a range of eclectic dishes with passion and enthusiasm, offering a menu which includes meat dishes alongside fish options (salt- and freshwater), as well as a few regional specialities.

Name: Madama Vigna
Description: This restuarant has a good wine list with a focus on local labels, as well as an excellent selection of regional specialities on the menu. Dishes include agnolotti (a type of stuffed pasta) with fondue, Piedmontese beef, Villanova chicken and the inevitable bunet dessert.

Name: Benedikto
Address: via Eremo delle Carceri 1/a, Assisi, 06081, Italy
Description: On the edge of Assisi's historic center, within the elegant setting of the Nun hotel, Benedikto offers some typical Umbrian products, but the culinary experience is primarily creative, thanks to the talented chef Enea Barbanera (his dessert of apricots, pine nuts, and rosemary is especially noteworthy). In good weather, dining on the terrace with a view of the Assisi fortress adds a touch of romance.

Name: Acqua Pazza
Description: Although this restaurant is not in the centre, if you’re looking for excellent fish (mostly from the Mediterranean) personally selected by the owner - chef, then it’s well worth the few minutes it takes to find a parking space here. Beautifully cooked food, which is simply prepared using top - quality produce.

Name: Oltre.
Description: This restaurant in the lively Mercato delle Erbe district has an entrance adorned with hundreds of stickers, giving it the appearance of a record shop rather than a contemporary-style eatery with a bar counter and a highly original surfboard table near the entrance. The modern cuisine has its roots in the region yet also includes skilfully prepared dishes from around the world (we highly recommend the Bolognese ramen, which includes tagliolino in a mushroom broth, with parmesan, quail eggs marinated in balsamic vinegar, and spinach). There’s also a choice of cocktails to start or round off your meal. Booking is highly recommended.

Name: Sale Grosso
Description: This restaurant describes its cuisine as Mediterranean and it’s true that fish and seafood dominate the menu. However, other dishes also feature and during our visit we particularly enjoyed the carefully prepared fried artichoke heart accompanied by a fresh white Tuscan Montecarlo wine. Friendly, informal service in a simple dining room with a distinctive bistro feel.

Name: Osteria Al GiGianca
Description: Although the out - of - town location is a slight drawback, this restaurant passionately run has a welcoming atmosphere. Seasonal, regional cuisine, plus a good choice of wine and beers.

Name: Serpillo
Address: via di Mezzo 1, località Torre del Colle, Bevagna, 06031, Italy
Description: Situated in a charming medieval village which is also home to a couple of small hotels, this attractive, rustic restaurant in an old olive mill acts as the backdrop for regional and Italian cuisine. Dishes with a touch of modern flavour are presented on a menu which, although not extensive, offers good value for money.

Name: Trattoria Battibecco
Description: Although it calls itself a trattoria, this restaurant situated in a narrow street in the city centre has an elegant ambience, welcoming guests with friendly service and serving an equal balance of meat and fish dishes. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the foie gras sautéed with Lambrusco blueberries and pan brioche, and the “finché c’è bottarga c’è speranza” (“while there’s bottarga, there’s hope”) spaghetti served with tuna tartare, mullet roe, lime and pistachios.

Name: Osteria dell'Arco
Description: Enjoy a warm family welcome at this centrally located restaurant with an internal courtyard, where the menu features a good choice of traditional and authentic dishes full of flavour. The restaurant is run by the same friendly managers as the renowned and popular Boccondivino in Bra, where the Slow Food concept was born. Booking ahead is always a good option.

Name: Zest
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: Situated within the luxury Grand Hotel La Favorita in the centre of Sorrento, this restaurant has the traditional, opulent style of a grand hotel, while the outdoor terrace boasts the romantic charm that is typical of Sorrento. In the kitchen, the chef creates top-quality cuisine influenced by Campania and enhanced by his own creative touches, resulting in dishes such as marinated tuna with tonka beans, lemon gel and ginger mousse. There’s also a vegetarian tasting menu. A recently opened restaurant that is growing in popularity.

Name: Aubergine
Description: Situated in a town famous for its thermal baths, this classically elegant restaurant serves meat and fish cuisine including specialities from the Veneto such as Berico ham, bigoli pasta with sardines, and veal liver with onions.

Name: Arca
Address: viale Rinascimento 143, San Benedetto del Tronto, 63074, Italy
Description: After years of serving fine cuisine in Alba Adriatica, chef Massimiliano Capretta has moved around 15km away to the Hotel Smeraldo. Here, he pays careful attention to the use of organic produce, creating meat and fish dishes that are inspired by local traditions and prepared in a style that is a combination of classic and modern influences. Desserts remain in the capable hands of his sister Dalila, whose millefeuille is one of her standout dishes.

Name: Lalibera
Description: In the heart of Alba, just a stone's throw from the cathedral, this refined and elegant restaurant offers guests a warm and simple welcome. The aromas of Langhe cuisine combine with the chefs' creativity to deliver dishes that reflect the region's flavours with taste and harmony. The wine list, lovingly curated by Flavia, offers a wide variety of labels, with Piedmontese wines taking centre stage.

Name: Due Pini
Address: via Spinale 37/bis, Madonna di Campiglio, 38086, Italy
Description: Although recently restored, this restaurant has retained its strong Alpine character. The cuisine is regional in style and reinterpreted with an imaginative and contemporary twist.

Name: Alla Laguna - Vedova Raddi
Description: Situated in a charming small town criss-crossed by canals, this restaurant serves traditionally inspired fish-based dishes. The restaurant stands on the port facing the fish market, so it’s no surprise that the fish served here is of the freshest quality.

Name: Sustànza
Address: Galleria Principe di Napoli 13, Naples, 80135, Italy
Description: Within the Galleria Principe di Napoli, entry is through the nineteenth-century café chantant ScottoJonno, a space that once housed the municipal treasury and, following extensive restoration, regained its splendor with a 2023 reopening. From here, an elevator ascends to the restaurant’s Liberty-style dining rooms, steeped in an atmosphere redolent of history and refinement. A brief welcome in the salon, amid soft lighting and period details, precedes the experience at generously sized tables, where Marco Ambrosino’s cuisine reveals itself as bold and personal: complex dishes, vibrant with modernity, drawing on Mediterranean and North African traditions and ingredients, enriched by fermentations and touches of live embers. Intense flavors, harmonious contrasts, and spiced aromas speak of a “Mediterranean creolity” that will surprise those seeking to venture beyond more familiar gastronomic territory.

Name: Amanõ
Description: The tilde accent over the “o” in the name of this restaurant is a subtle allusion to the sea that lies between Campania (the chef’s native region) and Sardinia (his adopted home). With just a few tables and an open-view kitchen, the dining room here is adorned with hand-made decorations, hence the name of the restaurant (“a mano” means “by hand”). The chef makes full use of Sardinian ingredients in his elaborate and creative cuisine, so this is a good choice for anyone seeking a change from traditional fare.

Name: Luminist Cafè Bistrot
Description: Situated on the ground floor of the splendid Banco di Napoli building that is also home to the Gallerie d'Italia museum, this restaurant also includes a bar and pasticceria. The varied restaurant menu features international dishes (for a quicker meal), fish based around recipes from around the world, alongside more creative dishes and regional specialities from Campania. The latter, from the aubergine parmigiana to the candele pasta served with a Neapolitan ragu, and the popular babà, are truly delicious and showcase all the colours and flavours of Neapolitan cuisine.

Name: Il Ristorante - Niko Romito
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the Hotel Bulgari with views of the Mausoleum of Augustus, this restaurant boasts a spacious terrace and an elegant, welcoming dining room with mahogany walls adorned with works of art. To reach the dining room, you pass through the lively bar, where we recommend starting your evening with an aperitif. Once at your table, the menu offers a concrete expression of three-Michelin-star chef Niko Romito’s culinary approach which focuses on lighter, elegant versions of traditional Italian dishes in a sequence of courses that take guests on a culinary tour around Italy. Spaghetti in tomato sauce, artichoke soup, saffron risotto and Piedmontese “bonet” dessert all feature on the menu.

Name: Quintogusto
Address: piazza Sandro Pertini 54 r, Savona, 17100, Italy
Description: Recently opened in the renovated section of Corso Italia in central Savona, Quintogusto is a small, contemporary and minimalist-style restaurant occupying one side of the former hospital. Here, the owner-chef (once sous-chef at the excellent Michelin-starred Il Vescovado in Noli) cements his reputation with Ligurian-influenced cuisine to which he adds his own modern and imaginative touches.

Name: Forme Restaurant
Description: Forme Restaurant is a modern, ever-evolving venue located outside the city center within the Atena educational complex, which also houses the Sottoforme bistrot. At the helm is Abruzzese chef Arianna Gatti: her cooking is a contemporary narrative, vivid in color and bold in flavor, rooted in Italian tradition yet reimagined with restraint and sensitivity. Her dishes evoke the comforts of home: the spice-scented ventricina, Navelli saffron butter that gently caresses the palate, and artisanal Abruzzese spaghettone celebrating authentic simplicity.

Name: N'uovo Vino e Cucina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled in the refined Antico Borgo di Sutri resort, in the heart of the lush Tuscia Viterbese, this restaurant offers an intimate and modern atmosphere, characterised by soft lighting and large windows overlooking the surrounding greenery. The talented young chef Lezzerini offers cuisine inspired by the local area, revisiting traditional regional recipes with modern techniques and using local food excellences. The tasting menu offers various options, from 4 to 8 courses; among the à la carte dishes, we highly recommend the saffron raviolini with marinated young rabbit and a delicious sauce. Also not to be missed is the Carnaroli Riserva San Massimo risotto, served simply but finely, with smoked robiola, wild nettles and celery.

Name: Su Murruai
Address: via Giuseppe Garibaldi 36, Riola Sardo, 09070, Italy
Description: In a small village overlooking the Sinis Peninsula, the restaurant has been established within an old mill and is dedicated to 'su murruai', Sardinian for the scent of aged Vernaccia. Contemporary Mediterranean cuisine is curated by young chef Ivan Matarese, who seeks quality regional ingredients—from both the mainland and the Gulf of Oristano—to reimagine modern recipes. Additionally, some Campania influences—being the chef's origin—are evident, especially in the desserts, half of which draw inspiration from renowned Campanian sweets (reimagined pastiera and babà).

Name: VeRo - Venetian Roots
Description: Within the elegant Ca’ di Dio, in the beating heart of the Biennale, VeRo is an exclusive restaurant with contemporary flair. The cuisine reflects the chef’s soul: essential, personal, never predictable. Two tasting journeys, with freedom to choose between dishes and desserts, complete the experience.

Name: Autem*
Description: The entrance opens onto the open kitchen where the charming chef Luca Natalini welcomes you, and who will also attend to your table with all his Tuscan flair. The selection centers on a limited list of handwritten dishes to accommodate daily arrivals. You dine in the soft lighting of elegantly atmospheric rooms, and the gastronomic experience is of the highest level. Among the most interesting offerings are the plin ravioli filled with duck and tomato seeds, Italian-style sauce and pepper leaf, as well as the grilled milk-fed lamb with bitter herb salad and chanterelles.

Name: Osteria de' Mercati
Description: Slightly set back from the bustling streets of the historic centre yet still in the heart of the town, this delightful small restaurant is a recent addition to Sassari. It boasts a modern, elegant decor, friendly staff and a menu featuring carefully prepared fresh, seasonal dishes. Our inspector particularly recommends the seafood risotto. A choice of regional wines completes the picture.

Name: La Corte Gourmet
Description: An interesting choice of wine with plenty of options by the glass, attentive service in a classic yet contemporary-style dining room, and good, honest cuisine prepared by owner-chef Paolo. The seasonal menu features classic favourites such as Fassona beef tartare and breaded veal cutlets cooked in butter alongside imaginative pasta dishes and truffles (in season). Guests have the option of dining in the attractive “champagneria”, surrounded by exposed brickwork and bottles that have been carefully selected by Antonella, the life and soul of the restaurant.

Name: Alajmo Cortina
Description: Situated in the restored premises of the historic El Toulà restaurant, Alajmo Cortina is home to a bar on the ground floor, with the restaurant occupying the two upper floors (no lift). Although traditional in feel with a profusion of wood, the restaurant is run by a young and enthusiastic team. The cuisine focuses mainly on the region, although the menu also features fish and other imaginative options on tasting menus and an à la carte.

Name: Io Osteria Personale
Description: The young owner of this restaurant has an interesting background – a former vet with a passion for food. He has opened one of the most fascinating restaurants in Florence, serving original dishes to diners looking for a change from more traditional fare.

Name: La Refezione
Description: An imaginative cuisine for the elegant "club - house" located inside a sports centre; managed by two great enthusiasts of the culinary art. You will receive a hearty welcome.

Name: Ora d'Aria
Description: Situated behind the Uffizi, this restaurant boasts a large open-view kitchen and an original approach that focuses on creating meaningful dialogue between guests and the chefs in the kitchen. The restaurant owes its name to the old Florentine Le Murate prison nearby, as well as its stated aim of providing guests with time to breathe and relax. In this charming small gem of a restaurant with a gold-leaf frescoed ceiling, Marco Stabile serves two tasting menus, one dedicated to meat, the other to fish. Although the menu features some Tuscan ingredients, the emphasis here is on creative cuisine which provides guests with a fascinating dining experience.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Situated in the heart of the historic centre, this restaurant occupies an old spinning mill ("filanda") that has been completely restored without losing any of its original charm. Here, self-taught chef Barbara serves traditional dishes reinterpreted with real flair, such as the involtino di ciaffagnone filled with Maremma beef on a bed of melted pecorino cheese and crispy leek. The chef’s husband oversees the wine list, which includes a selection of Tuscan labels.

Name: Il Trillo
Description: Situated in the hills overlooking the town, this restaurant occupies an old house that is also home to the estate’s wine cellars. Charming setting and cuisine full of flavour, with the option of alfresco dining on the panoramic terrace in summer.

Name: Stefano Paganini alla Corte degli Alfieri
Description: Within the walls of Castello di Magliano Alfieri – a place suspended in time, with a magnificent frescoed hall and soaring ceilings overlooking the hills of Langhe and Roero – chef Paganini’s cuisine takes shape, deftly balancing local tradition and innovation. Two main offerings are available: the traditional menu, “Viaggio in Piemonte (Journey Through Piedmont),” and the “A Occhi Chiusi (Eyes Closed)” menu, customizable in three, four, or five courses according to guests’ preferences. It is in this latter menu that the chef gives full rein to his creativity, crafting bespoke dishes and personalized interpretations designed to make every experience unique.

Name: Osteria Boccolicchio
Description: Having gained experience in various restaurants throughout Europe, Tespi has now returned home to open this delightful small osteria in the historic centre, just a stone’s throw from the sea. His huge passion for fish is evident from the menu, where fish dishes feature in numerous regionally influenced recipes. The excellent wine cellar includes a good choice of sparkling wines.

Name: Voltalacarta
Description: A tiny doorway leads to this simple, friendly and intimate restaurant with just a few tables, where booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s excellent reputation in the city. Its renown stems from the owner-chef’s cuisine, which focuses mainly on top-quality fish prepared in imaginative and personalised recipes using classic techniques. If it’s on the menu, make sure you try the “cappon magro” (a type of seafood salad), which is so good that it even has its own identity card!

Name: Locanda del Falco
Address: Castello di Rivalta 4, Rivalta Trebbia, 29010, Italy
Description: In the heart of a medieval village, an inn of authentic charm welcomes guests with the captivating aromas of Piacenza cuisine and imaginative creations that surprise the palate, accompanied by local wines and distinguished labels from beyond the region. Heritage dishes speak of time-honored flavors, revisited with modern touches, while the inspector’s favorite remains the grilled cardoncelli mushrooms: intense aroma and pure taste. In the dining room, Sabrina radiates energy and smiles, presenting each dish with infectious passion. On winter evenings, crackling fireplaces warm the atmosphere; in summer, a centuries-old wisteria drapes the courtyard tables in fragrant, romantic shade.

Name: Toe Drûe
Address: via Corsi 44 r, Sestri Ponente, 16154, Italy
Description: Opened at the beginning of the 20th century to feed shipyard workers, this historic establishment still retains the authentic flavour of its origins. The name “Toe Drue”, which means “thick tables”, refers to the sturdy tables of the old inn. Today, the restaurant continues to celebrate Genoese tradition in an informal and welcoming atmosphere, with iconic dishes such as “cappon magro”, stockfish and other Ligurian specialities that tell a story of sincere and timeless cuisine.

Name: La Pineta
Address: via Gualco 82, località Struppa, Genoa, 16165, Italy
Description: Now a gastronomic institution in the city, in a secluded setting immersed in nature, La Pineta occupies the ground floor of a nondescript building in which the simple, “dated” yet comfortable decor provides the backdrop. Although there is a menu (but no wine list), the dishes are usually announced in person at your table by the owners. Simple, traditional and abundant cuisine which is mainly cooked on the open grill in the centre of the room, including meat (its signature speciality) and fish.

Name: La Gallina
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Villa Sparina is an elegant rural resort named after its winery. The Orangerie hosts guests, whereas fine dining unfolds at La Gallina restaurant: amid rustic and elegant settings, contemporary cuisine is presented, drawing ample inspiration from Piedmont, as well as nearby Liguria (the dessert "Good Morning Genoa" playfully mimics breakfast with cappuccino and focaccia), though Campania references, the chef's homeland, never falter. Personalised wine selection: exclusively Champagne, abundant Piedmont choices, with particular emphasis on Barbaresco and Barolo.

Name: La Leggenda dei Frati
Description: After an uphill approach if you’re arriving here on foot, you come into the Villa Bardini museum complex and from there into this elegant and welcoming restaurant which provides the setting for delicious, creative and modern cuisine. Here, chef Filippo Saporito, never one to rest on his laurels, continues to experiment and perfect his cuisine, which focuses mainly on Italian culinary traditions and a scrupulous selection of top-quality ingredients, preferably from sustainable supply chains (various types of meat, bread and pasta), all showcased on different menus, including a vegetarian option. In summer, enjoy your meal on the romantic terrace surrounded by greenery and the scents of herbs, with a glimpse of Santa Croce church as a backdrop. Although the centre of Florence is not far away, it seems as though you’re already in the Tuscan hills, even with the occasional sound of cicadas in the background.

Name: Posillipo
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Boasting a superb location above Gabicce Monte, this excellent restaurant run by the third generation of the same family offers breathtaking views of the Romagna coast. Posillipo’s superb fish dishes have made the restaurant a must in the region, with options ranging from raw fish to traditional pasta specialities and delicious main courses (fish fillets, catch of the day, fried options etc). There’s also a tempting dessert trolley and an excellent wine list.

Name: Da Bibe
Description: At the gates of Florence, at the precise point where the city dissolves into the green of the countryside, Bibe welcomes guests beneath the leafy canopy of its summer terrace and within the warm interiors of a trattoria safeguarding over one hundred and fifty years of history, now in the hands of the sixth generation.
