Here, Tuscan cuisine remains the absolute protagonist: artisanal cured meats, traditional crostini, pici al ragù, and iconic dishes such as beef peposo. Not to be missed are the fried or grilled chicken and, for devotees, a fiorentina that interprets the classic canons in the most authentic manner.

Name: Trattoria del Vicolo
Description: Overlooking the piazza for almost 50 years, this restaurant has been modernised but has nonetheless managed to retain its friendly ambience, especially in the outdoor space facing the narrow alleyway. The owner-chef serves regional specialities reinterpreted with his own individual twist, such as his famous swordfish rolls served in a type of pie.

Name: La Kuccagna
Address: via Milano 14, località Barbuzzera, Dovera, 26010, Italy
Description: La Kuccagna's fresh, quality offerings are bolstered by management that is always full of energy; menus range between land (tripe with legumes, squash and mushrooms) and sea (amberjack with coconut sauce, sea urchin and herbs), while the grill is always ready to accommodate the most suitable cuts of meat. A fine selection of wines starting with labels from beyond the Alps. The location is exquisitely bucolic, while the interior is modern and comfortable.

Name: Gratschwirt
Description: Housed in a building which dates back to the 16C and is part of the hotel of the same name, this Stube-style restaurant at the foot of the Tre Cime is typical of the Alto Adige, as is the simple, abundant regional cuisine served here. Highlights on the menu include dumplings in broth, herb-crusted lamb, apple strudel and the less traditional but excellent beef tartare which is seasoned at your table.

Name: Sapereta
Address: via Provinciale Ovest 73, località Mola, Porto Azzurro, 57036, Italy
Description: A working farm (producing wine and olive oil) that features charming interiors, though the real highlight is outdoor dining beneath a pergola draped with fragola grapes, overlooking a meadow. The menu features both meat and seafood, rooted in Tuscan tradition but often elevated with creative flair.

Name: Castel Toblino
Address: località Castel Toblino 1, Castel Toblino, 38076, Italy
Description: Situated in a bucolic location in the Trentino where the excellent Vino Santo is produced (we recommend rounding off your meal with a glass of the equally superb grappa), this restaurant and adjacent bar occupy a fascinating medieval castle (tours of which can be arranged) jutting out into the lake of the same name. The generous, modern meat and fish dishes are featured on various tasting menus, along with an extensive à la carte. In summer, make sure you book a table on the charming terrace overlooking the lake.

Name: Da Poli alla Stazione
Address: viale della Repubblica 10, Castelnovo di Sotto, 42024, Italy
Description: In the centre of a town known for its carnival and many allegorical floats, this family-run restaurant housed in an old railway station dating from the early 20C serves traditional regional dishes. The house speciality is charcoal-grilled cuisine, with an equal emphasis on meat and fish options.

Name: Locanda del Feudo
Address: via Trasversale 2, Castelvetro di Modena, 41014, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic upper section of this picturesque village, this romantic restaurant serves imaginative and colourful cuisine including some excellent local cured hams. There are also six elegant, recently renovated suites with a historic feel, plus a small, charming outdoor space overlooking the main street.

Name: Agorà
Description: Michele Rizzo is the owner-chef of this interesting restaurant situated in a modern part of Rende. His menu focuses mainly on fish (although a few meat dishes are also available) which he prepares in light, modern dishes with an emphasis on local ingredients. There’s also an interesting wine list.

Name: Rosso di Sera
Address: via Pietro Nenni 2, Castelletto sopra Ticino, 28053, Italy
Description: Situated closed to the motorway exit, this restaurant’s rustic exterior belies its young, colourful and contemporary interior. The dishes are as modern as the decor, yet they have their roots in strong local traditions. The owner has a real passion for French and sparkling wines, including around 160 different champagnes and a wide selection of Burgundies, plus a good choice of wines by the glass, craft beers and cocktails.

Name: Da Noemi
Description: The mother of the current owner opened this busy restaurant in a medieval alleyway in the historic centre, giving it her own name. The historic dishes here reflect the culinary traditions of Ferrara, with specialities such as salama da sugo (pork sausage) and pasticcio di maccheroni (a baked pasta dish) on the menu. A must for anyone looking to sample local dishes already famous during the time of the Este family.

Name: Punta Lena
Address: via Monsignor Di Mattina 8, località Ficogrande, Stromboli, 98055, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, dine under a pergola with superb views of the sea and Strombolicchio – the perfect setting for any occasion. The menu focuses on fish, including raw and dry-aged fish options. The first courses have a local flavour and are particularly delicious.

Name: Feva
Description: Situated in the historic centre of Castelfranco Veneto, this restaurant has an intimate, elegant and contemporary-cum-minimalist feel despite its period courtyard setting and original wooden beams in the first-floor dining room. Nicola Dinato’s cuisine is showcased on two tasting menus, namely Anima and Corpo. The former offers a selection of new dishes created by the chef, who is constantly updating his cuisine, while the latter features his historic signature specialities (don’t miss the scampi “busara” risotto). A lighter, less expensive menu is also available at lunchtime. The wine list includes an interesting selection of French labels, as well as some superb Italian wines, such as the 1999 Case Basse Soldera Brunello di Montalcino.

Name: Casa D'Angelo
Address: via San Nicola 5, Fara Filiorum Petri, 66010, Italy
Description: Housed in what was once an old family home, this elegant restaurant serves delicious regional cuisine. The menu includes dishes that have been skilfully and imaginatively enhanced by the chef, such as warm pheasant terrine with apple, alongside more traditional fare, from cured ham to charcoal-grilled local lamb and potato gnocchi with a duck sauce. The restaurant’s own extra-virgin olive oil often adds further flavour to the dishes. The 4-course tasting menu deserves a special mention for its excellent value for money.

Name: Antico Ristorante Pagnanelli
Description: In business since 1882, yet constantly evolving, this restaurant boasts a superb location overlooking the lake. The menu features meat and fish dishes, enhanced by wild herbs. The extensive wine selection is presented on two wine lists. Don’t miss the famous wine cellars built into the rock, plus the small wine museum.

Name: Leone Felice
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: The new chef at this restaurant focuses on highlighting produce grown in the property’s own kitchen garden, as well as meat from the farm in the Grosseto area that is also run by the Andana estate. The classic-style cuisine on the à la carte features occasional personalised touches (for example, aubergines baked in fig leaf with oregano, and perch or sea bass fillet served with coloured beets and soft potato), while in the evening a tasting menu is served in a dedicated part of the restaurant. The expertly explained wine list focuses on the estate’s own labels and the Franciacorta region in general, yet at the same time includes a selection of wines from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: El Gato
Description: Chioggia is famous as one of the more active fishing ports in the region and this restaurant takes full of advantage of the local catch. Situated on the central promenade of this picturesque town, the restaurant serves fish of truly exceptional quality served in traditional recipes from the Adriatic.

Name: Locanda dei Salinari
Description: In the old village of Salinari, a young enterprising chef runs this simple restaurant. His creative cuisine is prepared with the best regional produce of Romagna.

Name: Miil
Description: Housed in a converted 15C mill on the Kränzelhof wine estate, this smart, elegant restaurant provides the backdrop for excellent, contemporary-style cuisine prepared wherever possible using locally sourced (and always top-quality) ingredients.

Name: Pinocchio
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This reliable restaurant is well run by a highly professional and experienced family. In the classic-style dining room, where the decor eschews fashionable trends, enjoy typical Piedmontese cuisine lightened by the occasional modern twist. The restaurant’s contemporary version of “paniscia” is a good example – a type of risotto with beans, salami and vegetables, in which the latter, instead of being cooked directly with the rice, are added on top of the mixture in the form of vegetable cream, giving the dish an attractive splash of colour. The menu always features a few fish-based recipes, including both salt- and freshwater species.

Name: Magiargè Osteria Contemporanea
Description: The dining rooms in this lively, typical restaurant in the upper, historic part of Bordighera appear to be almost dug out of the rock. Here, a local chef with plenty of experience behind him creates predominantly Ligurian cuisine (and not just fish and seafood), accompanied by an excellent and extensive wine list, including labels from outside Italy and a good selection of champagnes. Attentive service completes the picture here.

Name: Romolo Mare
Description: Situated in a private beach club facing the sea, this restaurant combines a relaxed atmosphere with an elegant feel thanks to its professional owners who have worked as restaurateurs for many years. Here, they serve excellent fish and seafood cuisine with a focus on raw dishes, plus a choice of daily fish specials. A selection of interesting local wines completes the picture.

Name: Alla Fassa
Address: via Nascimbeni 11, Castelletto di Brenzone, 37010, Italy
Description: Although the beautiful views of the lake (with only a cycle path between the restaurant and the water) and mountains on the opposite shore can be admired from the dining room, in fine weather it’s a race for the outdoor tables just a few metres from the water. The cuisine is as impressive as the setting, with a fine balance of classic and modern dishes featuring fish from the lake (such as the “il lago in un piatto” – the lake in a dish – starter) and the sea. A few guestrooms with views of the lake are also available.

Name: Residenza del Lago
Description: Boasting a tranquil, homely atmosphere typical of the region and with a name that pays homage to Lake Candia, this restaurant occupies a mid-18C farmhouse that is now located within the town. Its traditional cuisine includes popular dishes such as potato cake with seared shrimp and artichokes, “tajarin vecchio Piemonte” (pasta with a meat sauce), and beef cheeks cooked in Erbaluce di Caluso wine.

Name: Locanda Alpina
Description: Situated in the enchanting Val di Non with its castles and apple orchards, this restaurant housed in a 19C building has been run by the same family since 1933. It serves excellent cuisine that makes good use of regional produce alongside occasional ingredients from further afield, such as the delicious pistachio ice cream.

Name: Enoteca di Canelli - Casa Crippa
Description: Occupying a late-19C palazzo, in what was a historic wine cellar right up to the late 1960s, this family-run restaurant serves carefully presented, regional cuisine with a lightly creative and contemporary twist. A good example is the “carne cruda alla monferrina” (a kind of beef tartare) served with a Parmesan cream and hazelnuts.

Name: Nido del Picchio
Description: This restaurant with a low-key, hushed atmosphere has the feel of a tastefully furnished private home, with an open fire lit in winter and a cool, welcoming outdoor dining space for the warmer months. The restaurant has built up a well-deserved reputation for its fish dishes, although the menu here is equally divided between fish and meat. Options such as anolini in brodo (filled pasta in broth) pay tribute to the region’s traditions, while most of the dishes served here are highly creative. Originally English, the owner’s wife runs the front of house with skill and a warm, friendly manner. The wine cellar is home to more than 700 of the best Italian and international wines, with a curious emphasis on labels from cooler climes.

Name: Antica Locanda
Address: piazza della Seta, località San Leucio, Caserta, 81100, Italy
Description: This establishment is practically a trattoria; one can dine in either of two characteristic rooms separated by a brick archway. The cuisine is typical of the Naples area and rice dishes are the specialty.

Name: Mistral
Description: Situated at the tip of Bellagio’s promontory where the two branches of the lake meet, this villa occupies a superb panoramic location, with its restaurant housed in a covered veranda boasting delightful views of the opposite shore, its little villages and exclusive residences. The atmosphere here is reminiscent of a grand hotel, with background piano music in the evening and guests from all around the world. The moderately creative cuisine offers a choice of Italian dishes alongside more international options.

Name: Lamberti
Description: This restaurant is situated just a stone’s throw from the sea in a building dating from the 1930s. It serves traditional, regional dishes made from carefully selected ingredients. Don’t miss the fish and the pesto sauce.

Name: Da Giovanni
Description: The 18C ceramic stove, bright, colourful decor (both period and vintage), long family tradition and excellent cuisine all contribute to making this restaurant which opened half a century ago a bastion of fine cuisine in Piacenza and the wider Po valley. Meat and fish both feature on the menu, although it is the latter that has become renowned as the restaurant’s speciality over the years. The excellent service is friendly and informal yet highly professional, while the extensive wine list also includes a good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Pernambucco
Description: This restaurant boasts a garden setting with a pleasant outdoor dining space, plus a long, narrow interior decorated in decidedly classic style. Fish and seafood take pride of place on the menu, with a focus on local fish, including excellent tartare (usually either seabream or tuna, depending on the catch of the day) and shellfish (cooked in salt, baked or grilled). The vegetables are sourced from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Collina
Address: via Ca' Paler 5, Almenno San Bartolomeo, 24030, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A family style trattoria has now been converted into these modern premises that, while jealously upholding their homely origin, offer dishes of contemporary inspiration. One small dining hall has an open fireplace and the other gives a panoramic view.

Name: Le Cicale
Description: A grandparents’ home has evolved into a charming bistro-like restaurant, while outdoors, the owner-curated garden beckons a peek. The cuisine is simple and classic, comforting, with certain regional dishes alongside fish courses, while an entire menu page is dedicated to risottos.

Name: Bis Osteria Italiana Contemporanea
Address: Via 20 Settembre 50, Colle di Val d'Elsa, 53034, Italy
Description: In the glorious premises of the old Arnolfo restaurant in the old town, this restaurant is run by the same management as previously, although with a new young chef at the helm in the kitchen. The delicious yet concise menu features “Italian specialities” (the name given to all the main courses) with a focus on meat and fish, accompanied by excellent bread options (you can even order “scarpetta” dipping bread for mopping up the remains of a Cinta Senese pork sauce). The house speciality is a delicious pigeon dish. In fine weather, guests can dine on the beautiful, tranquil terrace.

Name: Locanda La Posta
Description: This traditional restaurant boasts small dining rooms adorned with wooden ceilings, which were redecorated a few years ago with evocative photos and documents depicting its history. The restaurant’s interesting cuisine is also traditional in style, featuring home-made pastas, a typical boiled meat trolley (“carrello dei bolliti”), and an excellent rabbit stew served with a generous portion of peppers. The selection of delicious home-produced fare includes vegetables, preserves and pastries.

Name: U' Vulesce
Description: First opened over 60 years ago, this restaurant has been built up into a successful business over the years by the Di Donna family, who serve top - quality produce from this fertile region, including meat and fish dishes, cured hams and cheeses, all accompanied by a selection of good wines.

Name: Scola
Description: Situated in the heart of the Ligurian hinterland, this country house is a real gem, surrounded by a garden that resembles a painting with an English-style lawn that ripples in the wind. Since 1926, the Scola family, now in the fourth generation, have offered guests a friendly welcome here, serving cuisine that is a delight for the tastebuds. In the warm dining room, where the wooden floor and exposed beams hint at the building’s history, guests enjoy traditional local dishes that have been reinterpreted with a modern twist, such as spaghetti with grapefruit, purple prawns and sea lettuce – an explosion of flavours!

Name: Al Camin
Description: On the road to Misurina lake, this friendly restaurant with a modern Alpine style offers dishes of the regional tradition with imaginative touches and modern technique. So a great deal of practicality, then, as in the beef tenderloin wrapped in speck dry-cured pork with cep mushrooms and Ampezzo-style potatoes. The chef and sommelier Fabio Pompanin manages a wine list with approximately 200 labels. In the warmer season, take advantage of the open-air service.

Name: Malenco
Address: via Funivia 22, Chiesa in Valmalenco, 23023, Italy
Description: This typical family-run restaurant serves typical mountain cuisine, although a few fish dishes also feature on the menu. Highlights include game, cheese and the delicious homemade pizzoccheri pasta. Ask the young son for recommendations from the wine list, which includes labels from Valtellina.

Name: La Lumira
Description: In a town synonymous with tortellini, Lumira offers an authentically regional experience with a touch of modernity; contemporary interiors and warm service ensure a memorable visit. The menu draws on the generosity of Emilian and Romagnolo cuisines, a natural expression of the chef-owner, born right here. The house-made fresh pastas are essential: from tortellini in capon broth to pumpkin tortelli dressed with garlic, olive oil, chili, and broccoli. Special praise goes to the bollito misto, served with excellently crafted sauces.

Name: San Quintino Resort
Description: Once you have crossed the plain and climbed up into the San Quintino hills, you come to this restored farmhouse surrounded by an attractive garden. The restaurant is divided into a brick - walled dining room and a winter garden, while the charming guestrooms make this a romantic place to stay. Creative dishes with a focus on local ingredients and a few fish specialities feature on the menu.

Name: Miseria e Nobiltà
Description: The name of this restaurant occupying a late-18C palazzo with attractive flooring and Murano glass chandeliers alludes to the peasant traditions that influence its cuisine (miseria) and the creative, elegant dishes served here (nobiltà). The menu features excellent home-made pastas, vegetables and meat dishes, including boned rabbit with leeks and Annurca apples and white and black truffles from the Molise in season.

Name: Luigi Pomata
Description: This famous classic restaurant in Cagliari serves top-quality cuisine in its modern dining rooms and on an outdoor terrace. The menu features interesting reinterpretations of Sardinian dishes among other options, including their own tuna (the house speciality), which is also available in tins to take away.

Name: Osteria Casale Ferrovia
Address: via Stazione 1, sulla SP 34, Carovigno, 72012, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in what was once the 20C dwelling of an old olive mill, this restaurant boasts elegant decor, including a few antique family pieces and Art Deco - style tables. The female owner - chef prepares light and modern dishes with a regional flavour, while the wine list also showcases the best of Puglia. As the name suggests, the railway lies to the rear of the property, although there’s very little noise and no disturbance at all.

Name: Da Tonino
Description: The chef at this restaurant serves decidedly contemporary cuisine with its roots in traditional recipes. His creative flair results in modern dishes in which each detail is carefully curated, with bold combinations that come as a surprise yet always feature a perfect balance of flavours and textures. The restaurant, situated in a quiet residential area away from the hustle and bustle of the small town, is the perfect choice for anyone looking for a relaxed and yet elegant dining experience.

Name: Il Barolino
Description: The Emilian authenticity of the Barolo brothers and their team fills the air with smiles and warmth, making every visit to this simple and welcoming restaurant a pleasure, the perfect place to enjoy the company of friends or colleagues. The menu is steeped in tradition: it is impossible to resist their pasta dishes, such as the creamy and satisfying “gramigna sporcafaccia” or tortellini covered in a velvety smooth Parmesan cream sauce. Desserts include a crunchy “sbrisolona” cake served with zabaglione made with passito wine, while the “zuppa inglese” trifle releases deliciously smooth notes to end the meal on a sweet note.

Name: Ginevra
Address: Rupi di via XXIX Settembre 12, Ancona, 60122, Italy
Description: Situated on the fourth floor of the Seeport hotel, this restaurant boasts a summer roof garden offering stunning sea views. The chef, a native of Ancona who trained with Gualtiero Marchesi, serves traditional local dishes prepared using ingredients from the region, as well as remaining open to the rest of the world (just like his town and its port). Lighter fare is available at the Seeport Bistrò.

Name: Cravero - Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Warm colours such as teal and ochre give this restaurant a cosy and welcoming ambience. The cuisine here is authentic and traditional in style, with dishes based on top-quality local ingredients accompanied by a choice of regional wines. There’s also an outdoor area for summer dining.

Name: Antica Cucina 1983
Description: Overlooking a square in the city centre, customers are welcomed into elegant surroundings, where almost exclusively fish dishes are served, in classic and tasty preparations, without too many complications to enhance the catch.

Name: La Filanda
Description: Housed on the first floor of an old silkworm factory, with a contemporary-style dining room that opens out on to a beautiful terrace in fine weather, this restaurant is one of the few in the province to serve top-quality fish and seafood, including a good selection of raw options. The cooked dishes on offer demonstrate a light modern touch and are prepared whenever possible using vegetables from the restaurant’s own garden.

Name: Caffè Meletti
Address: via del Trivio 56 (piazza del Popolo), Ascoli Piceno, 63100, Italy
Description: Housed on the first floor of the historic café where the aniseed liqueur of the same name was created, this restaurant serves simple yet creative, regional and maritime - inspired cuisine. Don’t miss the terrace with views of Piazza del Popolo. Faster options available at lunchtime.

Name: Locanda Baggio
Address: via Bassane 1, località Casonetto, Asolo, 31011, Italy
Description: Nestled in the greenery behind Asolo, just steps from the Canova Temple, this inn celebrates the region with excellent ingredients and a modern, surprising cuisine. Must-try classics include butter, anchovy, and pepper linguine, or Piedmontese fassona on the grill with potato puree. Let Enrico's stories about the wines charm you, and allow him to choose for you: you won't be disappointed...

Name: Duomo
Description: Bright and inviting is the dining room of this small resource aspiring towards contemporary culinary offerings—grounded in seasonal products—and numerous homemade preparations. The two siblings at the helm also unveil intriguing regional recipes with apt personal touches. For the wine lovers, an appropriate label awaits every need, whilst the setting further enhances the enjoyment: located in the town’s alleyways, just steps from the Cathedral.

Name: Opera|02
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An oasis of taste combining farm, guest rooms, spa and bistro, where the menu celebrates the local area with elegant reinterpretations: irresistible passatelli with Parmesan fondue and black truffle, alongside timeless classics such as tiramisu. The farm's own produce – including exquisite balsamic vinegar – are available to purchase, allowing you to take a little piece of this experience home with you.

Name: Laurin
Description: In the magnificent setting of the exclusive Parkhotel Laurin, this restaurant is one of the best in Bolzano, boasting a Liberty-style dining room and tree-shaded tables in the garden for summer dining. The traditional cuisine also includes a few modern touches with ingredients and techniques from all over Italy and beyond, such as the grilled trout and leek terrine wrapped in nori algae in the shape of a flower. The menu features meat and fish dishes, with a small section dedicated to traditional local specialities.

Name: Baita Fraina
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Warm little bar rooms, reminiscent of the German wine bars or "Stube", a summer terrace and well - prepared regional dishes: for those who want to escape the mundane life of Cortina for the silence of an isolated "baita" [mountain hut]. Delightful rooms, colourfully furnished in warm tones so you can better enjoy the silence and scents of the mountains.

Name: Sa Cardiga e Su Schironi
Address: strada statale 195 rotonda per Capoterra, Capoterra, 09012, Italy
Description: Since 1967, this small restaurant has been delighting locals and visitors alike with its vast array of fish and seafood dishes, including grilled and skewered specialities. The fresh fish display cabinet at the restaurant entrance is one of the highlights here, as is the extensive selection of antipasti which includes tuna and mullet bottarga, “agliata alla bosana” (blue shark with tomatoes in a light sweet and sour sauce) and “burrida alla cagliaritana” (with dogfish). Other dishes include fresh and pasta with various seafood sauces, fried fish, soup, lobster, barbecued fish and even eel.

Name: Fiamma Cremisi
Address: via De Gasperi 37, località Viadana, Calvisano, 25012, Italy
Description: Italian cuisine that strikes a balance on several fronts: while the chef’s dishes include nods to Brescia’s culinary tradition, they are also enlivened with creative touches. In summer, service extends outdoors beneath a gazebo; in the colder months, the main dining room is warmed by a fireplace. At lunchtime the menu is shorter, more affordable, and there is a business menu.

Name: I 5 Campanili
Address: via Luigi Maino 18, Busto Arsizio, 21052, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Contemporary cooking with an emphasis on Mediterranean fare in tune with the seasons is to the fore in this elegant restaurant occupying a 20C building with an attractive veranda to the rear. Fish takes pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on raw dishes and shellfish, but the splendid desserts are also worthy of note, such as cherries in sour cherry juice with fior di latte ice cream.

Name: Marsupino 1901
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Marsupino family has been running this trattoria enthusiastically and warmly since 1901. The chef's suggestion pays homage to the territory in accordance with tradition and the wine cellar, managed by the friendly expert Luca, is immense, with an excellent choice by the glass. Five rooms and two suites in the adjacent late nineteenth-century palazzo.

Name: Vitis
Description: A modern wine bar in the centre of Bressanone (Brixen), situated in the same building as the delightful family restaurant, the Oste Scuro. Here, small armchairs, benches and stools are dotted among low square tables and higher tables, all surrounded by walls completely lined with wine bottles. The contemporary cuisine features tempting, generous dishes such as cod with cauliflower, cavolo nero and beurre blanc. Accommodation is available just two minutes’ away in the historic Adler Historic Guesthouse run by the same owners.

Name: Elephant
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the famous Elephant hotel (with which it shares a name), this restaurant has a unique, historic ambience thanks to its decor of antique wood panelling. The cuisine here is regional with a modern twist, featuring dishes such as char with cream of celery and green apple on a bed of fragrant elderflowers. The interesting wine list boasts a selection of almost a thousand different labels.

Name: Castello Malvezzi
Address: via Colle San Giuseppe 1, Brescia, 25133, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: This elegant 16C hunting lodge offers a modern menu of fish dishes and regional specialities. Particular attention is paid to the excellent Calvisano caviar, with a dedicated menu. There’s an attractive outdoor dining area facing the gardens with views of the city of Brescia.

Name: Osteria da Nando
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Aosta Valley, Traditional Cuisine
Description: Operating since 1957 in the heart of the historic center, Nando is a go-to spot for those wanting to experience Valdostan cuisine: excellent cured meats (usually served with the famous fontina), polenta and fondue, fondue bourguignonne, rustic polenta tart with goat milk gelato... all prepared with top-quality ingredients and served in a simple yet atmospheric setting. The wine selection is excellent, focusing mainly on the Aosta Valley, with over 100 different labels, many of which are available by the glass. Among the desserts, the rothia is a must-try: white wine custard, spiced bread, and a sprinkle of cinnamon – intense, rich, and delicious.

Name: Il Riccio
Description: Situated just a few metres from the Blue Grotto and perched right above the water, Il Riccio is the quintessential Mediterranean fine-dining restaurant thanks to its tasteful and elegant decor. Undoubtedly one of Capri’s iconic addresses, it focuses uniquely on fish and seafood dishes. Whether you have a sweet tooth or not, a visit to the tempting dessert buffet to admire its array of delicacies is a must!

Name: Momento al 25
Description: Housed in a late-19C palazzo, this restaurant serves a good selection of meat and fish dishes with both traditional and creative cuisine on the menu. Delicious flavours typical of the Emilia region.

Name: Tosca
Description: This restaurant has a charming decor that combines classic elegance and typical Tuscan features such as stone arches and walls, as well as stylish sofas and comfortable armchairs. The cuisine is heavily influenced by local traditions, albeit with a fresh and innovative twist.

Name: Il Credenziere
Address: via Quattro Strade 12, Annone Veneto, 30020, Italy
Description: Situated in a small country hamlet, this restaurant is run by a chef from Puglia, whose origins can be glimpsed here and there in his dishes. The influence of the Veneto, where the chef has been working for some time, is also evident in the local dishes which appear alongside more creative options on the menu.

Name: Le Chiavi d'Oro
Description: Situated in Arezzo’s historic centre, this restaurant boasts an original, minimalist ambience with an elegant wood decor. The main focus here is on the cuisine, which is among the best not only in the city but also in the region. Skilful interpretations of traditional dishes, with a focus on Tuscany, where the gastronomic pleasure increases with each course.

Name: Ca' 7
Address: via Cunizza da Romano 4, Bassano del Grappa, 36061, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a charming 18C villa, this elegant restaurant overlooks its attractive garden in a magical setting which is typical of the Veneto. The cuisine also has a regional focus, with classic recipes featuring on the menu alongside more creative dishes (fish appears more often than meat).

Name: A' Paranza
Description: For more than 30 years, this restaurant run by the Proto brothers has been a popular choice for visitors to the beautiful Atrani valley. Simple cuisine served in a simple and informal setting (dishes are nearly always announced at your table rather than listed on a menu), with a focus on Mediterranean and Campanian dishes.

Name: Regallo
Description: An excellent restaurant situated less than five minutes from the town centre, Regallo has a contemporary decor with features that recall its former function as a factory. At the helm in the kitchen, skilful chef Claudio Ravinetto prepares dishes with an exclusive focus on fish, including interesting options such as cuttlefish tagliatelle with cream and diced winter roots such as celeriac, served at the table with an excellent hot vegetable broth.

Name: Rifugio Col Alt
Address: Stazione monte cabinovia col alto, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: During the day this restaurant can be reached in just a few minutes by cable car, providing you with breathtaking views of the Dolomites, while in the evening (when the service is more attentive – things are faster paced at lunchtime) you have to arrange transport via snowcat. The name “refuge” refers only to the location as the cuisine is definitely that of a restaurant: although the menu features hearty mountain fare, it also includes modern options and a few fish-based recipes, including oysters. Last but not least, there’s a good selection of wines.

Name: Lio Pellegrini
Description: Despite its location in the town centre, the attractive outdoor terrace of this restaurant offers a peaceful atmosphere with its decor of light drapes. The red - coloured dining room makes a pleasant backdrop for the modern, Mediterranean cuisine served here. Elegant ambience.

Name: Posta
Description: A corner of Tuscany in Bologna, where famous soups such as ribollita and pappa col pomodoro are followed by pappardelle pasta with wild boar, tripe, beef pepper stew and, of course, Fiorentina steak, although there’s also room on the menu for local specialities such as tagliatelle and tortellini. Many of the wines served also come from Tuscany.

Name: Baretto di San Vigilio
Address: via al Castello 1, San Vigilio, Bergamo, 24129, Italy
Description: In the small piazza that welcomes the funicular’s arrival station – with a small public parking area right at the top of the climb – lies a venue of retro charm, with Anglo-Saxon touches and an authentic soul. It serves as both bar and restaurant, where tradition meets modern accents in generous, thoughtfully composed dishes. The undisputed stars are the meats, accompanied by bread and desserts made strictly in-house. In warmer months, service moves to the panoramic terrace, offering enchanting views over the city (and, for the more intrepid, even in winter when the sun permits). Inside, two rustic-elegant dining rooms are warmed by cordial, convivial service that completes the experience.

Name: Quintilio
Description: For over a century, and from generation to generation, Quintilio has acted as a junction between two beautiful regions, Liguria and Piedmont – and not just in a geographical sense. These regions take pride of place on the wine list (overseen by the friendly and talented owner Lorena) as well as on the menu, which is created daily with dishes made from top-quality local ingredients full of flavour. Regional specialities such as plin, Ligurian-style rabbit tortelli, risottos, vitello tonnato (veal) and brain are all skilfully reinterpreted with a modern twist by owner-chef Luca Bazzano.

Name: Dispensa Franciacorta
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: The decor at this restaurant features bottles of wine on the walls (there are around 700 labels on the wine list, with an unsurprising focus on sparkling wines from the local Franciacorta region), while the menu celebrates some of Italy’s best produce, as well as ingredients from further afield, with a focus on Mediterranean flavours. There’s also an excellent cheese selection which will delight cheese-lovers.

Name: Visione Restaurant and Living
Address: Strada Nicolini Basso 34, loc. Tre Stelle, Barbaresco, 12050, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, new chef Emanuele Bellomo serves three tasting menus – one focuses on traditional dishes, another has a more modern and imaginative flavour, while the third is a surprise menu which allows the chef to demonstrate his skill to the full (all dishes are also available à la carte style). Situated in the Casa Nicolini hotel in a quiet, panoramic location, the restaurant boasts fine views of the hills through its dining room windows and from its terrace, where a bar and bistro with a more concise and reasonably priced menu are set up in the summer months.

Name: Umami
Address: Via Ugo Secondo Partigiano 1, Badalucco, 18010, Italy
Description: A young chef with experience in renowned restaurants has taken over the old kindergarten in this village and transformed it into a delightful restaurant. Here, he serves contemporary cuisine, often influenced by local traditions and showcased on tasting menus from which individual dishes can be ordered à la carte style. In summer, there’s an attractive outdoor space practically on the banks of the Argentina river, which gives its name to the valley in which this village is situated.

Name: Ristorante de LEN
Address: Via Cesare Battisti 66, Cortina d'Ampezzo, 32043, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the central and very busy Corso Italia, this restaurant has an elegant Alpine feel. Here, subtle lighting, soft background music and larch wood cladding on the walls create an ambience with an attractive blend of the modern and traditional. The cuisine takes inspiration from the local region, with specialities interpreted with a contemporary twist, including a focus on vegetable- and cheese-based dishes such as the excellent “fonduta di Saporito d'alpeggio” (fondue).

Name: San Baylon
Description: Not far from Piazza del Popolo and Rome’s most exclusive shopping streets, this restaurant is situated in the elegant Palazzo Ripetta, in what was once the refectory of a 17C monastery. Today, the ambience here is more informal, with an almost bistro-like feel, while the cuisine is inspired by classic Italian dishes, including various grilled options among the main courses. Meals are served in the palazzo’s inner courtyard in fine weather.

Name: Lo Scalco Grasso
Description: A small, intimate restaurant with a welcoming ambience and simple yet lively feel, where the owner-chef at the helm in the kitchen also makes an appearance front of house. Mantuan traditions are evident in the generous portion sizes as well as in dishes such as the legendary pumpkin tortelli (served with butter or a tomato and sausage sauce), while other options are more creative in style – the Emilian lamb tartare delicately flavoured with its own cooking juices, and served with sautéed chard, savoury sbrisolona cake and black truffles from the lower Mantova region in season is particularly delicious.

Name: Ortica
Address: via Giovanni Migone 4, Pieve Ligure, 16031, Italy
Description: You drive along 4.5km of winding, narrow (occasionally extremely narrow) roads to get to Ortica, the restaurant at the Tenuta Golfo Paradiso about 35min from Genoa. As is often the case, once at your destination the extensive views of the Tyrrhenian Sea from the restaurant more than compensate for the effort of getting here. Neither will you be disappointed by the cuisine, which is prepared using top-quality ingredients such as vegetables from the restaurant’s own kitchen garden, local fish and carefully selected meat. Dishes are fresh and modern, and occasionally cooked over the barbecue grill.

Name: Marc Lanteri
Description: Situated right next to the Fratelli Massucco winery, with which it shares its comfortable outdoor spaces as well as stunning views of the surrounding hills and vineyards, this restaurant is run by Marc Lanteri and Amy Bellotti, partners in life and work, who have chosen this setting for their new Piedmontese adventure. Their cuisine is full of individual character, with three tasting menus (including a vegetarian option featuring produce grown in their own garden) and dishes also available à la carte style. Local ingredients and recipes naturally take centre stage, always enhanced by small touches of colour and imagination. The wine list showcases the property’s own wines, as well as offering a choice of labels from elsewhere in Italy and further afield.

Name: Blum
Description: A magnificent location directly in a gazebo where you can count the waves breaking on the beach, but in case of bad weather, there’s also an equally intimate and elegant indoor dining room available. Pampered by attentive and exceptionally kind service, follow the chef’s creations along tasting journeys, including vegetarian options, or à la carte dishes from both land and sea, always served with great aesthetic taste, often built on local products crafted with contemporary and colorful sensibility. In short, enjoy the complete experience that two hours in this exclusive corner of Sicily will offer you!

Name: Ladinia
Address: strada Pedercorvara 10, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: Both the Berghotel Ladinia and its restaurant of the same name boast a warm, vintage Alpine-style ambience, with wood decor that tells the story of this business which opened as a simple inn back in 1930. Little has changed since then and guests return here time after time thanks to the warm welcome and attention to detail offered by the Costa family. The traditional cuisine has the occasional modern twist, while the few Ladin-style guestrooms are decorated with a profusion of wood.

Name: Carusu
Description: Along the road through the archaeological park, two small rooms on different floors host an elegant and refined restaurant, born from the Mangione family's passion – nomen omen. In the kitchen, young Alen, after significant experiences in renowned restaurants, offers his reinterpretation of Sicilian cuisine, with a strong focus on vegetables, many of which are grown on the farm tended by his uncle. At the entrance, you'll find father Francesco, while in the dining room, his equally young brother Dominique is available for conversations about wine.

Name: Kohaku
Description: Although the extensive choice on the menu includes dishes that you would expect to find in a Japanese restaurant, the quality of the cuisine served here is well above average, with a choice of different types of fish, dumplings, ramen, fried dishes, and ingredients cooked on the yakimono grill – everything comes as a pleasant surprise. And if you’re keen to experience a complete immersion into Japanese cuisine, the 8-course kohaku kaiseki tasting menu served in the evening is the perfect choice.

Name: Al Malò - Cucina e Miscelazione
Description: The double entrance to this restaurant can be seen under the arcades in beautiful Piazza Cavour: the first door leads to the ground-floor cocktail bar (open in the evening) while, hidden to the left, there’s a lift which takes guests up to the restaurant itself on the first floor. Here, the contemporary-style dining room is enhanced by bright wallpaper that echoes the imaginative cuisine served by the owner-chef, which is modern, colourful and creatively and carefully presented. The chef is equally skilful with meat (his pigeon cooked “duck à l’orange”-style is superb) and fish, plus the menu features a few vegetarian options, as well as half portions. In the evening, the cocktail list adds to the enjoyment, alongside an impressive wine list which has an obvious emphasis on the Franciacorta region.

Name: Ca' Apollonio Gourmet
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list
Description: At the foot of Monte Grappa, surrounded by vineyards, meadows, and trees, once you pass through the main gate and travel down a 1000-foot-long avenue, you’ll reach the restaurant's entrance, where you’ll be welcomed by a luxurious and elegant setting. There are two menus to choose from at the time of booking: Familiarity, which is tied to "home” flavors, and Conjunction, which focuses more on the sea and the garden. The wine cellar boasts around 800 labels from both small and large producers, offering a selection that will satisfy even the most discerning palates.

Name: Nello
Address: Via IV Novembre 66, San Casciano in Val di Pesa, 50026, Italy
Location: San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Italy
Description: Michele, in the kitchen, and pastry chef Chiara, who also works front of house, have renovated this historic local address and transformed it into a restaurant offering a modern interpretation of Tuscan cuisine. On the varied and intriguing menu, you’ll find dishes such as the intense and highly technical ravioli filled with Parmesan cream (made with milk from Reggiana “red cows”) with chanterelle mushrooms and onions. The concise wine list focuses on nearby Chiantis but also includes bottles from elsewhere.

Name: Josef Stube
Address: Località Certosa 29, Madonna di Senales, 39020, Italy
Description: Run with passion by the two owners who continue the long family tradition in this hotel-restaurant is one of the most picturesque sights in the Val Senales. Its beautifully kept dining room is romantic and typical of the region, providing a backdrop for just a few dishes which are prepared by the chef with a focus on local ingredients. A hint of Mediterranean influence adds to the appeal.

Name: Locanda San Martino
Address: via Don Ermolao Barattin 23, Chies d'Alpago, 32010, Italy
Description: Founded in 1952, this inn has been run by the same family – and especially its female members – ever since. It now boasts the presence of a chef whose many years of experience are evident in his dishes. Much of the meat (especially lamb) is raised in the restaurant’s own farm nearby, while the dishes on the menu are seasonal and classic in style yet with a hint of modern flavour. When the weather allows, make the most of the large terrace boasting fine views of the sunset over the surrounding Alpago region.

Name: Ling's Ravioleria Migrante
Description: A young couple (she was born in China; he’s half-French, half-Italian) have settled in this quiet residential district where they now run a tiny yet successful restaurant with around 20 seats in the dining room and a few small tables outdoors in summer – booking is essential! The menu includes various types of Chinese ravioli as well as dishes described by the couple as “migrant”, in other words “which draw inspiration from different cuisines from around the world, not only Asia but also the Mediterranean, France and Italy, with Emilia Romagna at its heart”. Examples include Peking-styleMora Romagnola coppa ham and pink Adriatic prawns marinated in mirin and soy sauce. The menu changes daily in line with market availability and the inspiration of the chef. Drinks include tea, beer and a small selection of wine.

Name: Il Gusto di Xinge
Description: The dining room plays on warm brown tones reminiscent of a teapot, enlivened by touches of brilliant blue and modern leather chairs that lend a contemporary edge to the space. The Chinese chef presents authentic cuisine from her homeland – dim sum included – while drawing inspiration from Italian and French culinary traditions, all infused with a decidedly “pop” creative flair. To best begin the experience, consider an artisanal cocktail at nearby DrinX, the perfect prelude to dinner.

Name: ES Cantina&Ristorante
Description: Situated within the Gianfranco Fino wine estate, this tuff building houses a restaurant on its first floor with large picture windows that look out at the vineyards and a spacious terrace offering views of the surrounding countryside. Here, chef Simone Profeta from Naples serves modern meat and fish dishes, often cooked using wines from the estate, such as in the deliciously tender braised veal cheeks served with a full-bodied ES reduction. There’s also a vegetarian menu that features organic vegetables grown in the estate’s own kitchen garden. The wine list showcases the winery’s own labels of different vintages.

Name: Osteria Grande
Description: This restaurant overlooking the magnificent Piazza Grande and the Loggia Vasariana that takes up one whole side of the square was opened in the summer of 2022 by the enthusiastic Fatjon and Lorenzo (if you ask, they’ll happily share their knowledge of Arezzo’s history with you). The former is at the helm in the kitchen where he expresses his passion for cuisine in seasonal, contemporary-style dishes such as pigeon breast, leg and fillet (each cut is prepared in the appropriate way) served with sweet onion and cocoa nibs, while the latter oversees the wine selection and recommends suitable pairings to guests. For the chef’s pigeon speciality, he may, for example, suggest an original Maturato Tiberini 2018 (a white wine made from grapes that are left to ripen on the vine). Cocktail staff are also hand for guests keen to choose an aperitif or an after-dinner drink from the extensive cocktail list.

Name: La Casina
Description: This large farmhouse with attractively renovated rooms overlooks the verdant landscapes of the Sarca valley from its wisteria-shaded summer pergola. Young chef Giada Miori prepares regional ingredients with skill and precision, serving specialities such as traditional potato fritters and “carne salada” (salted meat) preserved by the restaurant itself, as well as char, meat from the Trentino region and mushrooms. The Miori family also grow their own red berries, which often make an appearance in their desserts, along with their own sweet chestnuts.

Name: aldìVino
Description: Shelves stacked with wine bottles line the walls at this smart bistro-style restaurant, which also boasts a quiet outdoor space for summer dining. The cuisine is contemporary and creative and is showcased on three tasting menus from which dishes can also be ordered à la carte. We highly recommend the pink shrimp, broad beans, lovage and almond dish – one of the chef’s iconic specialties. Courses here are divided into meat, fish and vegetable sections (Terra, Acqua and Vegetale).

Name: Quadri Bistrot
Description: A modern bistrot with cocktail bar, fashionable furnishings, soft lighting and lounge music in the background, also featuring a small sidewalk terrace that requires advance booking. The cuisine, imaginative and creative, is guided by a talented chef who ensures personality and excellent seasonal products. Try the Mediterranean-style red mullet, while the tiramisu features a refined pairing with Sauternes. We also note a menu dedicated to caviar.

Name: InAlto Alfio Ghezzi Dolomites
Address: Passo San Pellegrino 32, stazione a monte della funivia Col Margherita, Moena, 38035, Italy
Description: At Col Margherita, perched at 2,550 meters and accessible by cable car in winter (departing from Moena via Passo San Pellegrino), a new ski bar bears the signature of Alfio Ghezzi. The menu favors Alpine traditions, though a more elaborate, creative selection showcases several not-to-be-missed dishes from the chef. In warmer months, the venue is also reachable on foot or − for the more athletic − by bicycle (two charging stations available for e-bikes).

Name: Felter alle Rose
Address: via Gasparo Da Salò 33, Salò, 25087, Italy
Description: A trattoria that tells stories of family and tradition, renewed under the guidance of those who have made hospitality and quality their vocation. The spaces open up into different atmospheres: the authentic warmth of the dining room, the closed veranda that filters the soft light of the seasons, and the cellar, where the scent of wine accompanies tastings and aperitifs. The kitchen serves Italian dishes, prepared with simplicity and good taste, using fresh, seasonal ingredients: genuine flavours intertwined with the pleasure of feeling at home.

Name: Savô
Description: The reopening in 2022 of the Hotel Windsor with its romantic vintage decor, is a real bonus for Laigueglia, especially the hotel’s new gourmet restaurant Savô (which translates as “flavour” in Ligurian dialect). Here, a contemporary dining room and an outdoor space with views of the beach and the sea provide the setting for modern cuisine prepared from regional, seasonal ingredients with a focus on fish (there is also a meat option for each course). The impressive selection of wine and choice of cocktails from the elegant Windsor Bar adds to its appeal.

Name: Il Grottino
Address: piazza Beato Ugolino 5, Gualdo Cattaneo, 06035, Italy
Description: Situated in the old medieval village of Gualdo Cattaneo, amid the gentle valleys not far from Foligno, Il Grottino is the perfect choice for anyone keen to sample the authentic flavours of Umbrian cuisine. Here, truffles and zero-km produce take pride of place on the menu, with a particular focus on meat which is carefully cooked on the open-view barbecue grill. Alongside locally sourced produce, you’ll also find a choice of carefully selected Prussian beef. Comfortable and welcoming guestrooms complete the picture.

Name: Faraglioni Restaurant
Address: lungomare dei Ciclopi 115, loc. Aci Trezza, Aci Castello, 95021, Italy
Description: Situated next to the hotel of the same name (a reference to the Faraglioni islands just off the coast here) but with its own entrance, this restaurant overlooks the beautiful Riviera dei Ciclopi. Sicilian ingredients take pride of place here in traditional and creative dishes with a focus on fish and seafood (vegetarian options are also available).

Name: Trattoria da Me
Description: Lively and always bustling, this trattoria run by the energetic Elisa owes its success to a winning balance of tradition – featuring fresh pasta prepared by skilled pasta makers, and sold in the neighboring shop – and specialties that use more contemporary techniques. On Sundays only, traditional lasagna alla Bolognese delights those who love the flavors of the past. The outdoor area can be used even in winter.

Name: Osteria Bakaré
Address: Via Venezia 30, Peschiera del Garda, 37019, Italy
Description: This small but beautifully kept restaurant set back from the lakeside serves contemporary-style cuisine that includes a good balance of meat and fish recipes, all made from top-quality, seasonal ingredients. Dishes are creative and full of individual character, with the occasional nod to Asia. Attractive enclosed veranda.

Name: KELINA Fine Dine
Address: Strada Lech de Boà s.n., Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: From Corvara, take the ultra-modern Boè cable-car to this restaurant (accessible also on skis or by foot) which is one of the dining options at the Piz Boè Alpine Lounge (for access, turn right as you exit the cable-car). Open at lunchtime only, KELINA serves unexpectedly gourmet cuisine in a minimalist-style dining room which allows the stunning views of Sassongher, Santa Croce and La Varella to take centre stage through the restaurant’s large floor-to-ceiling windows. The dishes are always modern and creative, combining Alpine ingredients with fresh fish – the red prawns with scampi mayonnaise and sea asparagus sorbet is a good example.

Name: Terrazza Tiberio
Description: Housed on the first floor of the Tiberio hotel, this elegant restaurant boasts a terrace overlooking the rooftops of Capri. The regional and island specialities on the menu leave a lasting memory, such as the “montanara” (fried pizza), “casatiello” (a savoury bread from Naples) and the caprese-style ravioli, although more creative options also feature, especially among the desserts. All in all, an elegant dining experience.

Name: Pellico 3
Description: Situated in the luxury Park Hyatt hotel just a few metres from the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele, this restaurant is home to a young chef who serves elegant and occasionally complex cuisine. His dishes include sauces and traditions learned from his time working in France, as well as plenty of vegetables and Mediterranean influences.

Name: Il Giardinetto
Address: Piazza Giuseppe Garibaldi 10, Mandello del Lario, 23826, Italy
Description: Looking out over the calm blue water, this classic restaurant serves traditional cuisine with the occasional imaginative twist. Fish from the lake feature on the menu, as do meat and seafood options with something for everyone. There’s also a small outdoor terrace where guests can enjoy a pre- or post-dinner drink.

Name: Cucina
Address: Via Giano della Bella 3r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: At this restaurant, local ingredients (mainly from the market) take pride of place on the daily menu which changes in accordance with whatever produce is available at the time. The rustic-style dishes are full of intense flavours, with meat and vegetables often cooked in the wood-fired oven. The pleasantly informal dining room with its many cookery books dotted here and there was designed by the owner-architects themselves.

Name: Campocori
Address: via di Santa Maria de' Calderari 49, Rome, 00186, Italy
Description: Housed within the Chapter Hotel and designed by South African designer Tristan Du Plessis, this restaurant is conceived as a nighttime place with a dark atmosphere, “ferrying” into the capital a contemporary, cosmopolitan take on fine dining, blending Roman, Italian, and international references.

Name: Pentole e Provette
Description: This restaurant run by Luca Trabalzini and his partner Rossella is a real gem in the small town of Fasano. Their story, which began in Australia, adds a fascinating touch to this gastronomic project. The atmosphere here is warm and lively, making this the perfect setting in which to enjoy the chef’s innovative cuisine, which he showcases on three distinct menus dedicated to meat, fish and vegetarian dishes respectively. Luca’s cuisine is modern and elegant, with particular attention paid to flavours and textures so that each and every dish offers a fully rounded sensorial experience.

Name: Locanda Sensi
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A country retreat that captivates with simplicity and passion: modern, comfortable rooms open onto a landscape that embraces the hills of Piacenza, while outdoor dining offers glimpses of light and nature. The menu invites guests to enjoy a tasting menu in which the grill releases intense aromas, or à la carte dishes that range from land to sea to garden, in a balance of scents and colours. Two cosy suites, a holistic wellness centre scented with natural essences and, in fine weather, a Zen garden that invites you to relax, complete the experience.

Name: L'Agave
Description: Be cautious not to be misled by any potential misdirections from satellite navigation systems. Head directly to the tourist marina of the quaint locality overlooking the sea—a place offering one of the most striking vistas in the area. Here, dishes crafted by a young chef and wines selected from remarkable regional highlights boldly declare a love for Liguria. From Albenga’s artichokes and asparagus to Pigna beans, pine nuts, 'prebugiun', olives, and of course, seafood—all elements here speak of this land. The concept encompasses tasting menus, with dishes available à la carte.

Name: Calvi Ristorante
Description: This welcoming, contemporary-style restaurant with a large open-view kitchen serves two different types of cuisine – one regional and Mediterranean in style, the other more creative allowing the chef’s culinary skills to take centre stage. The black rice tacos with roasted eel, green beans, soya bean sprouts and spicy hummus mayo are truly delicious – definitely to be eaten with the hands!

Name: Masseria Moroseta
Description: Chef Giorgia Eugenia Goggi offers a unique and authentic gastronomic experience that focuses on fresh ingredients (mostly vegetables), many of which are sourced from small organic gardens. The 90€ menu celebrates Mediterranean cuisine to the full, with colourful dishes that are full of flavour and in which the freshness of the ingredients is allowed to shine through. The beautifully kept, rustic dining room provides an ideal setting for an unforgettable dinner, while the selection of natural Italian wines offers the perfect accompaniment to the chef’s dishes, further enhancing your dining experience. There are six comfortable guestrooms available should you wish to extend your stay and immerse yourself in these peaceful rural surroundings. Booking in advance is highly recommended given the restaurant’s popularity and unique appeal.

Name: Stilla
Address: Località Casette 1, Colognola ai Colli, 37030, Italy
Description: Run by an enthusiastic and committed young couple who left the big city to restore the family home and transform it into an elegant, welcoming restaurant, Stilla stands in a tranquil location surrounded by vineyards. Here, Silvia creates original, generous and colourful cuisine which is showcased on an à la carte with just a few dishes which change regularly. We particularly enjoyed the freshly seared bonito served with wild spinach, sour cherries and a cherry barbecue sauce. Meals are served on the outdoor terrace in summer. Accommodation is also available in five beautiful yet functional guestrooms. Well worth a visit.

Name: Remulass
Description: They call it ‘Cucina con le radici’ (Cuisine with roots) and you only need to cross the threshold to understand why: a small, lively restaurant with warm colours, which gets very busy, especially in the evening, when booking is essential. The menu is simple, featuring just a few carefully planned dishes, mostly vegetarian, where seasonal freshness is paramount. Every recipe releases authentic aromas and genuine flavours, while leaving room for creativity: such as the variations on pumpkin, with oven-baked Mantovana and Hokkaido julienne in a sweet and sour sauce, caressed by tamarind cream and little cubes of blue goat's cheese. A combination of textures and aromas that tells the story of the land with elegance and creativity.

Name: I Due Buoi
Description: Choose between tasting menus (including a vegetarian menu) and an à la carte at this restaurant, where the chef prepares creative dishes, including various types of offal on his Quinto Quarto menu. The à la carte offers an extensive choice, featuring an array of local specialities and excellent bread options. There’s also a superb wine selection with a focus on Asti and its surrounding area, as well as on the Langhe region.

Name: Urubamba
Description: Situated amid luxury boutiques and historic palazzi in one of Naples’ most exclusive districts, this restaurant boasts a chic and romantic dining room with soft lighting on the first floor, as well as an exclusive outdoor terrace for fine weather. The cuisine is totally in keeping with the trendy setting, featuring a successful combination of two different gastronomic cultures (namely Peruvian and Japanese) that blend together perfectly.

Name: John Restaurant
Address: via Santa Maria la Nova 35, Afragola, 80021, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: Follow the signs to Casamadre (the specialist food shop next door) to get to this gourmet restaurant, where the chef surprises guests with modern cuisine that is full of character. The dishes served here are inspired by classic recipes which are reinterpreted with creativity and a respect for local traditions, resulting in highly distinctive flavours. Each course reflects the region’s history, with a common thread running through the menu to create an authentic culinary experience. To accompany your meal, the wines are presented on a practical tablet which makes it easy to explore the different labels available. Among the different options, the excellent Costa D'Amalfi “Selva delle Monache” 2022 is particularly striking thanks to its fresh, earthy aromas.

Name: Indiniò
Description: Located in a charming little village, Indiniò is an extraordinary place to discover Carnic cuisine. The ingredients tell the story of the local area, but chef Gloria Clama transforms them into refined creations that are sometimes bold and surprising. The dining rooms, furnished with wood and modern details, evoke tradition in an elegant way, creating a warm and romantic atmosphere.

Name: Oltremare
Description: Situated on the fifth floor of the Due Torri hotel, the restaurant has recently been refurbished, giving it an even more charming and atmospheric feel than before. The cuisine is creative in style, almost always using ingredients and recipes from Campania as its inspiration – a good example is the many different ways tomato is used, including tomato water distilled in an alembic still. Chef Alfonso Crisci’s recipes are complex and always full of different ingredients and colours, with a selection of delicious and generous desserts to finish your meal.

Name: Cocun Cellar Restaurant
Address: strada Prè de Vì 31, San Cassiano, 39036, Italy
Description: In the cellars of the Ciasa Salares hotel, you dine surrounded by bottles – after all, cocun in Ladin means cork, and not by chance the wine selection is vast. The chef creates dishes with ingredients and influences from every corner of the world and makes frequent use of the grill.

Name: Salvo
Description: Situated opposite the Villa Comunale gardens, this restaurant serves some of the best pizzas in Naples (classic Neapolitan-style pizza which is soft and so big that it spills over the plate) as well as a selection of delicious appetisers, such as superb pasta fritters with various toppings. Welcoming ambience, with a more elegant feel than that of a typical pizzeria.

Name: Principe di Belludia
Description: The Principe di Belludia is the gourmet restaurant at the Il San Corrado di Noto hotel, a luxurious resort in a secluded rural location with two enormous swimming pools. The new executive chef Martin Lazarov showcases his love for Sicily, with a particular attention to vegetables dishes.

Name: Essencia Restaurant
Address: piazza Santa Maria la Nova 9, Naples, 80134, Italy
Description: Having spent many years living in Spain, the young chef at this quiet, elegant restaurant offers an appealing combination of Spanish and Italian dishes, resulting in his own interesting interpretations of Mediterranean cuisine. Situated in the heart of the historic centre, the restaurant has an open-view kitchen and chef’s table for four guests near the entrance, while the main dining room is on the first floor.

Name: DA MÓ
Description: This new, restored restaurant in the upper part of the Sassi (yet still near the centre of Matera and its car parks) has a warm friendly ambience and boasts a small, charming outdoor space. Here, an entire family (father in the kitchen, mother and daughter front of house), who moved to Matera from Venosa (home of the Latin poet Horatio), serves regional cuisine with a contemporary twist and no little skill and professionalism. Various tasting menus are available, as well as an à la carte. An interesting wine list completes the picture.

Name: Dama
Address: Via Mulino 2, località San Gaudenzio, Cervesina, 27050, Italy
Description: Situated just a few kilometres from Voghera in the Bassa Lomellina area, this gourmet restaurant run by a young chef occupies the old stables of the Castello di San Gaudenzio. Alongside local specialities such as baked onion and 24-month-old Grana Padano cheese, the menu also features more creative dishes based around authentic recipes. The wine list includes some particularly interesting labels from the Oltrepò region.

Name: Mogano
Address: via del Praticello Alto 7, Formello, 00060, Italy
Description: Aiming to promote craft beers as a worthy pairing for gourmet cuisine, the Faenza family opened Mogano – a modern, elegant restaurant with a wood-inspired decor, soft lighting and just five tables, right next to their Ritual Lab brewery. One of the sons (Matteo, the chef here) greets guests before dinner with an aperitif served in the kitchen. With plenty of international culinary experience behind him, he combines Italian flavours with influences from all around the world. Despite the focus on beer, a wine list is also available.

Name: Impronta
Description: An elegant restaurant that has the feel of a private home, with its beautiful light-wood tables. The Sicilian origins of talented chef Andrea Colombara are reflected in his dishes, which have a strong Mediterranean flavour. Highlights on the menu include delicious mullet with caponata which is served with onions, pine nuts, capers and small vegetables in a sweet and sour sauce.

Name: Cala Luna
Description: Refined fine dining at the boutique hotel "Le Calette." In the summertime, Cala Luna is hosted in a splendid garden surrounded by plants and flowers, with breathtaking views of the bay, the Caldura sea stacks, and the Rocca. The dishes are a technical and creative expression of Chef Dario Pandolfo’s experiences, who applies what he has learned working in prestigious restaurants in Italy and abroad to Sicilian ingredients and traditions. The result is a vibrant and colorful cuisine, sometimes with strong flavors, always creative and deeply Mediterranean. "Green" notes are evident not only in the "Fiori di Luna" menu, dedicated to Sicilian vegetables, herbs, and flowers, but also in the sustainable approach to using raw materials, enhancing every part of them, and focusing on reducing waste without ever compromising quality.

Name: Cut
Description: Situated right in the heart of the Bergamo plain in the small town of Caravaggio, famous for the painter of the same name and for a much-visited pilgrim shrine, this welcoming restaurant boasts a modern decor and vintage furnishings. At lunchtime, it serves a good, competitively priced business menu, while in the evening the more elaborate à la carte features contemporary-style meat and fish dishes (mostly the latter).

Name: Locanda Viola
Description: A refined restaurant where the design plays with tables and seating of varied, original craftsmanship, yet it is the cuisine that captures attention, thanks to the talent of Filippo Moriggi. The starters are the calling card: an exotic-tinged journey that surprises with the fish bao, a soft steamed bun also available with BBQ sauce, or with the empanadas chilena, filled with white Sorrento scamorza, shrimp, and coriander-cumin mayonnaise. The journey continues toward more familiar flavors: well-executed pastas and risottos, fish dishes, and Bergamo lamb, leading to desserts that play on the freshness of gelato, served simply or affogato-style, for a light, flavorful finish.

Name: La Foresteria
Address: Contrada Passo di Gurra SP 79 km 91, Menfi, 92013, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Planeta’s elegance is reflected in this property nestled among Sicilian vineyards. The rooms bear the signature of the celebrated winery, while the restaurant offers modern Sicilian cuisine, with an à la carte menu and two tasting journeys. Don’t miss “Casa Planeta”: five iconic courses inspired by the monsù, the chefs of ancient noble residences.

Name: Enoteca Meucci
Description: Occupying a restored farmhouse at the foot of Cortona, this restaurant has two different dining areas: a wine bar on the ground floor where you can enjoy excellent aperitifs or buy local food produce, and a restaurant on the first floor that serves a traditional yet constantly evolving menu with a focus on seasonal ingredients. There’s also a beautiful outdoor space for summer dining.

Name: Campo Cedro
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the centre yet away from the tourist crowds, this restaurant is well worth the effort needed to find it! Here, Japanese chef Sugihara, who has more than 20 years’ experience working in Italy, creates modern and skilfully prepared Italian meat and fish dishes which are fresh and elaborate. You’ll nearly always find seafood risotto on the menu, which is made with fish, mussels and finely chopped shrimps all cooked together with rice and then sprinkled with crumbled seaweed and dotted with tomato paste. Excellent value for money!

Name: SOMS
Description: In the heart of the seaside area, within a pedestrian zone, the historic *Società Operaia di Mutuo Soccorso* (SOMS) is now a delightful venue with a cozy, slightly contemporary dining room. It offers cuisine tied to Abruzzese traditions, both land and sea, executed with originality. The discreet and knowledgeable service, including the wine selection, along with an outdoor space to enjoy pleasant summer evenings, completes the experience.

Name: Qualia
Description: Situated in a side street in the centre of this charming small town, this restaurant boasts a dining room with exposed brickwork and glimpses of the kitchen, plus a small outdoor space with a few tables for alfresco dining. The dishes here are full of flavour and focus on regional ingredients and fresh fish.

Name: Al Moro
Address: via Pietri 1277, Marina Di Campo, 57034, Italy
Description: Situated away from the main tourist area, in a rustic building that is striking for its attractive outdoor space shaded by a wooden gazebo, this restaurant boasts an informal and relaxing atmosphere. The Mediterranean cuisine is full of character and prepared with top-quality ingredients, including a small selection of oysters.

Name: Portanova
Cuisine: Cuisine from the Marches, Italian Contemporary
Description: A new restaurant in Urbino’s beautiful old town, where the designer-style decor blends harmoniously with the historic architecture. The modern, contemporary-style cuisine finds inspiration in ingredients from the Marche, as well as featuring flavours and traditions from other regions of Italy such as Sardinia, Campania and Lazio.

Name: Contrasto
Description: Lucio Testa, chef-patron, has returned to his native village perched at an altitude of 937 metres, opening this restaurant in a former sheepfold on the outskirts of the village. The perfectly preserved stone façade, several small rooms spread over several levels, exposed beams and contemporary lamps give the ambience a modern touch. His is a creative cuisine, in which traditional Molise recipes are revisited, combining local and seasonal products (often from his own garden) with sauces, dressings and emulsions, learnt from working with French chefs; mulard duck is a favourite, several tasting menus guide the discovery of the territory, and finally, for those who prefer, a la carte choices. Among the wines, we suggest tasting a Tintillia del Molise Rutilia 2019 from Cantine Salvatore.

Name: FØRMA contemporary restaurant
Description: Situated in a secluded residential district that is part of L’Aquila’s historic centre, this intimate restaurant with an elegantly minimalist ambience is home to skilful owner-chef Simone Ciuffetelli. Having gained experience working abroad, Ciuffetelli showcases local ingredients in his creative, contemporary dishes, with the occasional use of fermented products and a frequent focus on just three ingredients. A good example is his dessert featuring cream and crunchy toasted hazelnuts generously coated with a white-chocolate mousse that is “disguised” as an Italian-style meringue thanks to a sprinkling of liquorice powder.

Name: Bolle
Description: We are in the Agnelli showroom, a well-known manufacturer of cookware for professional kitchens. The modern shop is located on the ground floor, while the first floor hosts the restaurant with its elegant tables in a refined minimalist and contemporary environment. On the menu, dishes with an impressive balance of ingredients, including occasionally exotic choices.

Name: Anastasia
Description: This cocktail bar on the seafront is also a restaurant specialising in fresh fish served in a selection of classic dishes (such as tartare) and more elaborate recipes. The dining room is modern and spacious, plus there’s an outdoor terrace for alfresco dining in fine weather. Guestrooms and luxury apartments are also available (swimming pool on the roof).

Name: Cuculia
Description: An establishment of measured elegance, with refined interiors that evoke the atmosphere of a contemporary French bistrot, enhanced by a small library displaying culinary volumes and beyond. Chef Oliver Betancourt, originally from Venezuela, built his training through notable kitchens in France, Spain, and Italy: a journey that today translates into a gastronomic approach rich in nuance, nourished by diverse traditions and constructed around seasonal local products, alongside more exotic ingredients such as kombu, soy sauce, and koji. Vegetarian options are clearly marked on the menu, together with several dishes suitable for vegans as well.

Name: Restaurant 700
Address: largo Michele Ayroldi Carissimo 14, Ostuni, 72017, Italy
Description: Situated at the entrance to Ostuni’s historic centre, this restaurant is part of the luxury Paragon 700 hotel. The charming dining room combines historic features with a more modern decor, while the exclusive garden is perfect for dining alfresco in fine weather. The menu offers a concise selection of classic Italian dishes at lunchtime, while in the evening the chef conjures up more high-level and elaborate dishes showcasing strong technique.

Name: CiPASSO
Description: A small restaurant which combines a contemporary feel with a hint of vintage style in its decor. The menu is inspired by Roman and regional traditions, with the occasional imaginative twist and other more Mediterranean-inspired dishes, all showing a strong focus on seasonal ingredients. The impressive wine list includes an excellent selection of regional wines, with a particular focus on wines by the glass. Friendly yet professional service from the young team completes the picture.
