Name: Soul & Fish
Description: From the centre of Sorrento, you follow a succession of roads downhill to Marina Grande, the town’s old, picturesque fishing village that is well worth a visit. Here, facing the water, you’ll find Soul & Fish, a seemingly traditional seaside restaurant that actually serves superb fish and seafood on a menu that combines traditional dishes with more creative options.

Name: Palazzo Utini
Description: A historical palazzo in the town center has been given new life after its purchase by a local entrepreneurial family, who also bestowed their name upon it. Just steps from the heart of Italy’s famed food valley, it now serves as a refined hospitality venue: the ground floor hosts a bar and bistro, while upstairs are elegant spaces devoted to gourmet cuisine. Tasting menus are available, with dishes also offered à la carte, alongside an extensive and well-curated wine list. The upper floors feature intimate, stylish guest rooms, designed in the same reassuring style that runs throughout the building.

Name: Etra
Description: Etra is an anagram of the Italian word “arte” – an apt name for this restaurant, which is housed in Palazzo Doria De Fornari on the beautiful and famous Piazza Ferrari. This palazzo is one of Genova’s magnificent “Rolli” palazzi (noble palaces once used to house famous visitors to the city). Despite the setting, the dining room is modern in style and adorned with elegant works of contemporary art. Here, chef Davide Cannavino consolidates his reputation with a concise menu of creative dishes: around a dozen meat and fish options inspired by the beauty that surrounds him and showcased on two tasting menus from which individual dishes can be chosen à la carte style.

Name: Duo
Address: via Cavour 7, San Felice del Benaco, 25010, Italy
Description: Situated in the historic centre of the charming small village of San Felice del Benaco, Duo is the project of chefs Daniele Ghedini and Federico Pelizzari (the latter also oversees the front of house). Their personalised, modern cuisine is Mediterranean in style and features meat-based dishes, vegetarian options and fish recipes (salt- and freshwater), with a focus on matured fish which also has its own dedicated tasting menu. This colourful restaurant also boasts an outdoor space shaded by a pergola and surrounded by walnut trees.

Name: Ca' del Profeta
Description: Situated in a beautiful location in the Asti countryside overlooking rolling hills and the estate’s own vineyards, Ca' del Profeta lies just a few kilometres from the provincial capital. A modern dining room and panoramic terrace provide the backdrop for decidedly innovative Piedmontese cuisine, which is inspired by traditional recipes and seasonal ingredients and then transformed by the chef into personalised dishes. Ingredients from further afield, such as root vegetables (black salsify, celeriac and beetroot) also make an appearance in three creative recipes inspired by the Orient. The service is friendly yet professional, plus a few modern guestrooms are also available. A panoramic swimming pool completes the picture.

Name: AlpiNN by Norbert Niederkofler
Address: Plan de Corones, alt. 2275, Brunico, 39031, Italy
Description: Situated at an altitude of 2 000m in the Plan de Corones ski area, this restaurant is accessed via the cable-car from Riscone and then, in winter, by walking (or skiing) for around 150m through the snow. This impressive project by famous chef Norbert Niederkofler showcases his “Cook the Mountain” philosophy, where a modern approach and Alpine traditions combine to create perfect dishes full of flavour, all inspired by the seasons with a focus on using the whole ingredient with no food waste. The five tables with the best views are reserved for guests who choose the tasting menu, which has to be booked ahead of time. NB: the last cable-car leaves at 5pm!

Name: Carlo e Camillo
Description: This intimate and elegant bistrot is the second restaurant of the Grand Hotel Sitea, a charming jewel box where you can enjoy Italian cuisine that gives ample space to Piedmontese tradition along with some other Italian regional dishes, as well as off-menu specialties that appear on the menu for brief periods.

Name: PS Ristorante
Address: via di Petriolo 7, Cerreto Guidi, 50050, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Situated in the beautiful countryside outside Cerreto Guidi, PS Ristorante is housed in the magnificent Medici Villa Petriolo which is also home to 36 luxurious guestrooms. The restaurant’s appeal is enhanced not only by the charm of the villa and its delightful garden (overlooked by the restaurant terrace), but also by the property’s delicious home-produced ingredients, such as extra-virgin olive oil, wine, Cinta Senese pork, meat and chicken, produce from the kitchen garden, traditional cereals and other zero-mile ingredients, all reinterpreted in a creative, modern style by the chef (as in the egg and artichoke dish). The estate’s wine is also highly recommended – we particularly enjoyed the organic red Golpaia, a medium-structured blend of Merlot and Sangiovese with characteristic soft aromas.

Name: Capriccio
Description: Young chef Graziano Accolla has returned to his native city where he serves creative cuisine of the highest quality, while at the same time raising Augusta’s gastronomic profile. Thanks to his experience in Michelin-starred restaurants, he offers highly interesting dishes which focus on the use of top-quality ingredients.

Name: Meraviglioso Osteria Moderna
Address: largo Gelso 16, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: A few metres from Modugno’s statue and a breathtaking sea-facing balcony, with picturesque houses perched above Polignano, you’ll find exceptional cuisine, the creation of Andrea Vicario, whose hands craft predominantly seafood dishes with high effect and quality, showcasing a great passion—amongst mains—for charcoal cooking.

Name: Filia Ristorante
Description: In Borgo Trento, an elegant residential quarter just steps from the historic center, Filia plays the card of a modern, minimalist setting, where just five tables find their place. Tasting menus are served, with dishes also available à la carte. The cuisine is modern and creative, at times revisiting classics of the Italian tradition.

Name: Casamare
Description: Elegant and refined, this top-quality restaurant is the perfect choice for special occasions. Vietri ceramics, an open-view kitchen, fish on display and a successful mix of traditional and modern decor all combine to create an atmospheric setting in the dining room. As the restaurant’s name suggests, this is a good option for anyone who enjoys delicious classic fish and seafood dishes (mostly from Campania).

Name: Ca' Mia
Description: This welcoming restaurant in the hills surrounding Lake Alserio makes guests feel completely at home. The two young chefs with plenty of experience behind them create modern dishes with a preference for quick cooking methods and a focus on a wood-fired oven and barbecue, as well as fermented ingredients.

Name: La RiMa
Description: This restaurant in the heart of the town serves excellent contemporary cuisine (meat and fish, plus a few vegetarian options). The menu features dishes such as fregola sarda (a type of couscous) with tomato, buffalo mozzarella, friggitelli peppers and fried capers, with a personalised twist added by talented owner-chef Matteo Ridoni.

Name: Sücar Brüsc
Description: This interesting new restaurant in the historic heart of Mantova takes its name from a phrase in local dialect with translates as “sour” sugar. The cuisine here is regional yet modern, served in an informal dining room where traditional Mantuan sayings are written on the ceilings. For some months now, the restaurant has also offered an interesting caviar menu.

Name: Ménage
Description: Situated in the heart of the city near the Teatro Bellini and Piazza Università, this restaurant occupies an Art Nouveau-style building. Here, a trio of experienced young chefs from Catania have brought new life to the old “Da Turi Finocchiaro” restaurant, which has always been very popular with the city’s high society. Offering a small outdoor space near the entrance, the quiet, intimate dining room on the ground floor provides the backdrop for reinterpreted, contemporary Sicilian cuisine with an exclusive focus on meat (especially barbecued dishes which are the restaurant’s trademark), while the first floor is home to a cocktail bar run with passion by one of the partners. Two frescoes painted by Giuseppe Barone in 1930 add to the appeal.

Name: 85 Bistrot
Address: piazza Martiri di Via Fani 85, Sesto San Giovanni, 20099, Italy
Description: This simple, modern, family-run trattoria with a welcoming ambience is the kind of restaurant that everyone would love to have as their local. The owner-chef, who has plenty of experience working in Milanese restaurants, is a real culinary expert who creates traditional dishes from Milan but also from further afield. Here, the popular breaded cutlet is served thick so that the delicate flavour of the veal can be enjoyed to the full.

Name: La Botte
Description: A modern and welcoming contemporary bistro situated in the heart of Stresa’s historic centre. Run by an entire family, the restaurant serves modern and imaginative fish and meat dishes where the focus is always on seasonal ingredients. The interesting wine list also includes a selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Strattoria
Description: Situated in the foothills around Lake Maggiore, this welcoming restaurant has a pleasantly relaxed ambience. The chef is equally at ease with meat and fish, creating colourful modern dishes that demonstrate his individual take on contemporary Italian cuisine. Unsurprisingly, Piedmont takes centre stage, including desserts such as bonet with a traditional cake base which is then topped with dark chocolate and a crispy sphere filled with a kind of custard- cream mixture. Lighter options are also available at lunchtime.

Name: Gunè San Frediano
Address: via del Drago d'Oro 1r, Florence, 50124, Italy
Description: The chef at this small gastronomic restaurant serves cuisine which acts as a bridge between Basilicata and Tuscany, the two most significant regions in his life, resulting in creative, delicate and beautifully presented dishes.

Name: I 5 Sensi
Description: The whole family (mother and four children) is involved in the running of this restaurant, both front of house and in the kitchen. If you’re looking for top-quality cuisine which focuses on local ingredients yet is also creative and innovative, then this is the place for you! Classic-style dining room with the occasional modern decorative touch, plus a well-stocked wine cellar offering a selection of 700 labels.

Name: Mesadoria Restaurant
Address: Piazza De Honestis Cavallino, Sassari, 07100, Italy
Description: This reliable restaurant has moved from the coast to simple, modern premises in the town of Sassari, where it has a new look and new chefs at the helm. The cuisine is as good as ever, with a focus on fish and seafood yet also including a few meat options, in dishes that are classic with a modern twist and cooked using predominantly Sardinian ingredients.

Name: Metodo
Description: In a romantic setting of eighteenth-century farmhouses, you will find the same rustic atmosphere inside the restaurant as well, but combined with elements of modern elegance, starting with the solid wood tables left bare, with no tablecloth. Chef patron Stagi offers a single tasting menu (you can, however, choose between the full or abbreviated version, and the dishes are, in any case, also on the menu) with a creative and sometimes very elaborate character.

Name: Fàula
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Il Fàula – "fairytale" in Piedmontese – represents the gourmet offering of Casa Langa, a property that opens like an elegant amphitheater overlooking the valley. In the kitchen, young chef Daniel Zeilinga presents a cuisine that weaves Piedmontese tradition and modern interpretations with natural ease, always with a personal touch. The tasting menu dedicated to vegetables from the estate garden speaks to a sincere attention to product, while the à la carte selection moves with balance among meat dishes, fish, and vegetable offerings. A well-curated wine selection and the gracious professionalism of the service complete a harmonious, thoughtfully constructed experience.

Name: Cosmo Restaurant
Description: Although the cuisine at Cosmo is influenced by the ingredients and culinary traditions of Campania, this restaurant is also an excellent choice for those in search of more elaborate and creative fare. Top-quality, complex dishes prepared by two young chefs.

Name: Bottega Lucia
Description: A charming bistro-style establishment, with exposed wood and brick creating a warm, informal atmosphere, offering immediate and flavorful Italian cuisine – the spaghetti alla chitarra cacio e pepe with black truffle is emblematic – alongside forays into the nearby Iberian Peninsula and playful international influences. Among these, the steamed bao with pulled pork and coleslaw and the celebrated Milanese-style gyoza stand out, the latter filled with ossobuco and served with saffron cream. Meat and fish appear in equal measure, in a menu designed to satisfy diverse tastes without losing coherence. Just steps away is Casa Lucia, a more informal iteration of the same establishment, ideal for simple dishes and good pizza.

Name: Il Cugnolo
Address: contrada Cugnolo 19, Torre di Palme, 63900, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This gourmet restaurant housed in a restored period residence that once belonged to the counts of Adami is surrounded by the green maquis and hills of the Marche, with the sea visible in the distance just a few miles away. Here, the young Neapolitan chef creates cuisine that is surprising for its attractive, clean lines, providing a real explosion of flavours and a tribute to the region and the Mediterranean in general. The restaurant also owns a nearby agricultural estate which provides many of the wines and olive oils served during tastings.

Name: Gennaro Amitrano
Description: The large picture windows at this restaurant offer fine views of the Tyrrhenian sea, where the blue of the sea blends with the elegance of the dining room. The view of the bay is truly spectacular, providing the perfect backdrop for a dining experience that is both traditional and innovative. The chef here serves classic dishes alongside Italian specialities reinterpreted with a modern twist, surprising guests with combinations that are bold yet always balanced. A good example is his elegant lemon tartlet served with a caper and pepper powder.

Name: Locanda Perbellini al Mare
Description: The flavors of Sicily – and not just seafood – are reimagined in a modern way, with personal touches (such as the tuna cutlet cooked and raw with soy mayonnaise and mashed potatoes), as well as vegetarian recipes inspired by the multi-starred chef Perbellini, executed with good technique and a dedication to taste. This all takes place in a modern beach establishment, complete with loungers and umbrellas. In the summertime, the windows open, and you practically all dine on the terrace, surrounded by the scent of the sea.

Name: Altriménti
Description: A bistro with a contemporary soul, where the informal atmosphere mingles with a subtle elegance that captivates without ostentation. The scents that waft out from the kitchen reveal the seasonality of the ingredients: fresh, carefully selected from small producers, transformed into dishes that speak Italian, with a harmony between sea and land. Every course is an invitation to discover something new, every detail a sign of attention. When it comes to wine, let the owner guide you: his enthusiasm will steer you towards pairings that enhance every nuance of flavour.

Name: Lupaia
Address: Località Lupaia 74, Torrita di Siena, 53049, Italy
Description: Situated in a charming Tuscan hamlet nestled in the hills between Montepulciano and Montefollonico, this restaurant boasts stunning sunset views from its garden in the summer months, while guests in the dining room can enjoy views of the open kitchen in winter. The cuisine changes daily, with the chef offering a tasting menu based largely around produce from his own farm. The journey to get here is bucolic to say the least – an occasionally tortuous dirt track of more than 2km which requires careful driving! Booking ahead is essential if you’re not staying in the hotel.

Name: Innesti
Address: via San Pietro 8, Pergine Valsugana, 38057, Italy
Description: Daniele and Elisa are a couple of young restaurateurs who are familiar to us from their time at Blumenstube in Sant'Orsola. Having moved on, they have now opened their own restaurant in Pergine, where both the decor and the cuisine are contemporary-Alpine in style. As in currently in vogue, their dishes are showcased on three tasting menus (short, medium and long) from which dishes can also be chosen à la carte style. All the recipes have a creative feel, demonstrating the chef’s playful approach to his contemporary ingredients.

Name: Le Cementine
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This rustic, vintage-style country restaurant run by the Alajmo brothers stands on the banks of the Sile river, just a few minutes from the Venetian lagoon, and overlooks a vegetable garden, vineyard and beautiful green meadows. The cuisine demonstrates a strong focus on seasonal, regional ingredients, featuring meat and fish alike, with vegetables taking centre stage in many of the dishes.

Name: Ichikawa
Description: Ichikawa is one of the culinary masters who played a part in introducing Japanese cuisine to Italy. After decades in the country working in various restaurants, this chef has finally opened his own eatery, where he serves top-quality Japanese cuisine ranging from familiar favourites such as sushi and sashimi to other less-known family dishes and street food from the land of the Rising Sun. A good place to discover the joys of Japanese cuisine!

Name: Zàghara Restaurant
Description: Housed in the elegant Relais Villa Flora, this restaurant occupies a natural terrace with breathtaking views of the Nissene hills. The dishes are predominantly regional in style yet reinterpreted with a modern twist. There’s also a good wine selection with a focus on Sicilian and Italian labels.

Name: Materia Prima
Address: Località Piana Santa Liberata, Castel di Sangro, 67031, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A pleasant and intimate terrace overlooks the shores of an artificial lake dedicated to sports activities. The glass windows provide the same view from the modern, sleek, and minimalist interior rooms, just like the dishes: creative, yet reminiscent of local cuisine, such as the simple but tasty Pallotta Cacio e Ova, offered among the welcome bites. There are also various daily specials according to the market. The service is friendly and attentive, with a young and motivated team overall.

Name: La Società Milano
Description: Situated near Porta Venezia and its lush gardens, Giulia and Andrea’s restaurant boasts a warm and original ambience. Three dining rooms adorned with tapestries and an entrance with a fine white marble fireplace act as the setting for Mediterranean cuisine with the occasional exotic twist. Don’t miss the amberjack caponata in which the ceviche flavours contrast with the sweetness of the fried breaded aubergine.

Name: Bites
Description: The cuisine at this tiny, simply furnished restaurant includes barbecued dishes and fermented ingredients, all of which feature on a tasting menu. Guests can also choose à la carte: the small portions (as the restaurant name suggests) make it possible to taste several dishes at a reasonable cost. Booking is essential in the evening and also advisable at lunchtime.

Name: Le Macine
Address: via Lino Carlo del Favero 11, Vittorio Veneto, 31029, Italy
Description: Housed in a recently renovated 18C mill on the banks of the Meschio river, this restaurant is run by brothers Giuseppe (front of house) and Adriano (in the kitchen), who serve top-quality cuisine with its roots in local traditions and the occasional imaginative twist with warmth and professionalism. It is even more appealing in summer, when meals are served on the beautiful outdoor terrace.

Name: Osteria del Posto
Address: via Calderini 15, loc. Chiugiana, Corciano, 06073, Italy
Description: Housed within an ancient mill in the village of Chiugiana, a small hamlet of Corciano, the osteria offers contemporary cuisine deeply rooted in the local area. Ingredients are carefully selected, and the wine list tells the stories of small producers, both local and national, with a special focus on artisanal and natural wines.

Name: Cucina Rambaldi
Description: Regional dishes with the occasional subtle contemporary twist are to the fore here. The chef’s culinary techniques bring out all the flavour of the carefully selected and preserved ingredients, with a focus on cooking temperatures and the cut of the meat, resulting in excellent cuisine. The menu also features a few specialities from Ferrara, the chef’s native city.

Name: Comi 107
Description: Situated near the lake at the entrance to a narrow street dotted with various shops, this small contemporary-style restaurant boasts an equally tiny outdoor space for summer dining and is run with skill and professionalism by a young couple. The friendly, welcoming wife oversees the front of house, while her husband creates dishes full of character in the kitchen.

Name: Vecio Macello
Description: A former early 20th-century slaughterhouse, today you’ll find a restaurant with a pleasantly classic atmosphere and a kitchen that, despite the building’s original purpose, serves predominantly seafood dishes, though with some meat classics.

Name: Antica Osteria il Ronchettino
Description: An authentic Milanese trattoria in operation since the late 17th century as a post station, while the apartment buildings of Gratosoglio rose up all around it in the 1960s, the interiors still preserve their historic charm. The cuisine fortunately remains faithful to the spirit of the place, offering some Milanese classics, such as mondeghili (meatballs), risotto alla milanese (with or without ossobuco), and the “elephant ear” cutlet.

Name: Madama Piola
Description: The aptly named Madama Piola (in Piedmontese dialect, “piola” is a village inn) has a simple yet attractive and friendly ambience that serves as a backdrop for typical Piedmontese dishes. Highlights include the memorable stuffed onion, as well as tonnato, braised cheeks and hot zabaglione. Regional wines take pride of place on the wine list, which includes a good selection by the glass.

Name: San Tommaso 10
Description: In 1895 Luigi Lavazza opened here a grocery store where he immediately began blending coffee. 129 years later the place hosts a modern restaurant with a superb kitchen run by a chef who, despite hailing from the Marche region, treats guests to one of the most authentic interpretations of Piedmontese cuisine in the city, often with a creative touch. Among the options on offer here, the trolley of antipasti is a must.

Name: Zanze XVI
Address: fondamenta dei Tolentini, sestiere Santa Croce 231, Venice, 30135, Italy
Description: Although the setting and convivial atmosphere in this restaurant recall that of a typical Venetian bàcaro , the cuisine is completely different in feel. The ingredients are sourced from the best markets and local producers, resulting in unique dishes that reflect the culinary traditions of the lagoon and its surrounding area. The few tables arranged outdoors with views of the tranquil canal add to the appeal, while the professional yet friendly service helps to put guests completely at ease.

Name: Quattro Sensi
Description: Perched on a hill just a few kilometres from Torgiano, Quattro Sensi boasts a veranda with views of Perugia, which is perfect for a quick lunch, and an elegant dining room in which you can enjoy regional dishes such as pappardelle egg pasta with a Cinturello Orvietano pork ragù with orange and fennel.

Name: Trattoria Margherita
Description: Don’t be fooled by the relatively simple ambience of this trattoria which is situated in the centre of a town with an interesting history linked to the reclamation of the marshes and the dairy industry. Dedicated to the owner’s two grandmothers, the restaurant serves some of Sardinia’s best-known meat and fish specialities.

Name: Radicì
Description: The name of this restaurant alludes both to the chef’s origins in Isea (“radici” translates as “roots”) and his passion for vegetables, which make a strong appearance in his dishes. He offers three tasting menus, one dedicated to fish from the lake, a second which is more creative, and a third focusing on seasonal vegetables, with the option of choosing individual courses from each menu à la carte style. Whatever you choose, be prepared for complex, elaborate and surprising cuisine!

Name: Diana's Place
Description: Facing the square in front of Termini station, this wine bar-cum-restaurant is striking for its fresh and creative approach to cuisine. Nearly all the top-quality ingredients are local and can be purchased from the food counter. The excellent staff are happy to help with your choice of wine, which is also available by the glass.

Name: Casa Rapisarda
Description: This small welcoming restaurant on the famous Scalinata della Costarella in Numana, with a tiny terrace for summer dining and just a few tables, serves delicious cuisine with an imaginative twist. Originally from Sicily, the highly talented owner-chef has spent much of his life in the Marche and has plenty of experience in leading restaurants. Given the limited capacity here, booking is essential, especially in summer.

Name: Tano Passami l'Olio
Description: In an elegant residential neighbourhood, Tano Simonato's restaurant welcomes guests with modern design and a refined atmosphere, a prelude to cuisine that tantalises the senses. Italian tradition is clothed in creativity in the dishes: the famous “tirami su” made with cuttlefish and potatoes releases marine aromas and velvety notes, while the honey-glazed pigeon, baked in salt, delights the palate with contrasting sweet and savoury flavours, accompanied by spinach and savoury cherries. Tano sees food as a source of pleasure and enjoyment: the chef comes to the table, tells stories and suggests pairings, with every glass of wine becoming part of an experience that seduces all the senses.

Name: Saur
Description: An unexpected restaurant hidden among the fields of a small hamlet in the Bassa Bresciana region. Although the menu features a few regional dishes, the focus here is on creative cuisine with an emphasis on herbs and vegetables, some of which are grown in the restaurant’s own kitchen garden.

Name: Ensama Pesce
Address: via Aristide Dondarini 4, Sala Bolognese, 40010, Italy
Description: A menu which focuses only on fish (from the daily market) which is prepared with a hint of Puglia, the chef’s native region. As soon as guests are seated at their table, they are brought a selection of homemade breads, including taralli bread rings and focaccia. Owner-chef Sabino is the heart and soul of this restaurant, where guests can be sure of a memorable culinary experience!

Name: Osteria alla Chiesa
Description: Genuine warmth in the dining room and interiors that recall the inns of old: the building is historic, and the discreet creak of the wooden staircase contributes to a d’antan atmosphere. Among the most intriguing offerings is a raviolo accompanied by fried artichokes and a sweetbread “carpaccio,” completed by an almond sauce that rounds the dish with gentle, measured succulence.

Name: L'Ostì
Address: strada Sassongher 2, Corvara in Badia, 39033, Italy
Description: A minimalist-style restaurant featuring a wood decor, an extensive display of bottles, and some windows boasting partial yet splendid views of the Dolomites. The chef here prepares creative cuisine using local ingredients alongside produce sourced from other regions. The wine list includes a wide selection of natural wines.

Name: Antica Osteria Moirago
Description: This old monastery in Moirago, overlooking the Naviglio Pavese canal, was founded in 1250 and converted into an inn as early as 1478. Centuries may have passed, but the tradition of hospitality continues in the building’s enclosed painted portico, as well as in its two warm and atmospheric dining rooms. The chef’s Puglian origins explain the abundant use of vegetables and raw fish dishes, while in winter the cuisine takes on a more northern Italian flavour. Good selection of wines by the glass.

Name: Antiche Carampane
Address: rio Terà delle Carampane, sestiere San Polo 1911, Venice, 30125, Italy
Description: From the typical floors to the wall decorations, everything here speaks to the heart to tell you about a historic trattoria where people joyfully return each time to enjoy local seafood specialities. Sarde in saor, baccalà mantecato, fried moeche (spring and autumn), cuttlefish in nero to name but a few. The recipes are crafted with skill and fidelity to tradition. In addition to the dishes listed on the menu, each day you will be verbally presented with off-menu specials. An excellent wine selection ranging from Italian to French labels with good value for money.

Name: Repubblica di Perno
Address: vicolo Cavour 5, loc. Perno, Monforte d'Alba, 12065, Italy
Description: Situated in the heart of the gastronomic Langa region, this small, renovated restaurant in the centre of town (reservations required) is imbued with the passion of the couple at the helm (he’s in the kitchen, while she’s front of house). In keeping with Piedmontese tradition, you catch a glimpse of the open-view kitchen as you make your way to the first floor, which is laid out with just five tables. Enjoy traditional cuisine in a rustic, bistro-style setting where the daily menu showcases dishes with a strictly regional focus. Three guestrooms are also available.

Name: Locale Firenze
Description: Within a palazzo steeped in history, spanning from its medieval underground cellars to the Renaissance piano nobile housing the restaurant, guests enter through the ancient courtyard, now a refined lounge bar with a large counter dedicated to mixology and small tapas-style bites. From here you reach the splendid interior dining rooms, the ideal backdrop for an avowedly creative cuisine shaped by the chef’s international experiences across Australia, Japan, and France. The evocative medieval cellars also house “Labo-ttega,” an exclusive experience combining avant-garde cuisine and mixology, available by reservation for up to four guests. A vibrant destination brimming with energy and quality, interpreting contemporary gastronomy with distinct personality.

Name: Dulchemente
Description: A contemporary-style restaurant which serves modern dishes alongside simpler, more classic options, with a notable focus on fish. A splendid outdoor terrace for alfresco dining and friendly, professional staff complete the picture.

Name: Osteria del Tasso
Address: via Bolgherese km 3,9, località San Walfredo, Bolgheri, 57020, Italy
Description: Just a stone’s throw from the famous Viale dei Cipressi avenue in one of Italy’s best-known wine-producing areas, this restaurant occupies one of the region’s most famous wineries, namely Guado al Tasso, renowned for its excellent wines. In fine weather, guests can dine in the shade of plane trees looking out over the vineyards. Simple, delicious and well-prepared cuisine, mostly traditional in style, plus specialities such as cured hams and grilled dishes.

Name: Lofficina
Description: This building with a minimalist, contemporary design is situated on the edge of the historic centre at the Sant'Erasmo belvedere, from where, in summer, panoramic views extend over Monte Conero and the sea (booking ahead is recommended). In the kitchen, owner-chef Davide Breccia conjures up creative dishes featuring original combinations and mainly inspired by the sea. There are two tasting menus, Iconico and Idee, for guests who like to be guided, plus an à la carte for those who prefer to choose their own courses.

Name: Gainn
Description: Since 2007, Gainn has showcased the fascinating and delicious flavours of colourful Korean cuisine, with its rice-based dishes, soups, meat, fish, plenty of vegetables and soya. The best way to experience the food here is to order a selection of different dishes to be shared with your dining companions. Those with a sweet tooth, be warned – there are no desserts on the menu.

Name: Milano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: From Lake Maggiore, the road climbs up to Mottarone, about 1,400 meters above sea level, to this late 19th-century former hunting lodge. Here, you’re welcomed by a young self-taught couple who pour their hearts into everything they do. And their dishes speak for themselves... Fragrant land-based offerings and a few lake specialties are served also outdoors on a panoramic terrace. The pair show great respect for seasonality and possess thorough knowledge of the entire supply chain of their ingredients. There’s a strong focus on game, strictly from Ossola. In addition to the à la carte menu, they offer the “Sentiero” tasting menu, a summary of their ten years of work. Both the wine list and the selection of wines by the glass are noteworthy.

Name: Pescheria
Description: The name of this restaurant between the historic centre and the seafront refers to the main item on its menu, which is dedicated almost exclusively to fish (fresh and not farmed). Fish and shellfish are displayed in a glass cabinet and aquarium respectively, both of which are situated to the rear of the long, narrow dining room near the open-view kitchen. Classic fish dishes full of flavour (served raw, baked, cooked in salt, in water or grilled) are to the fore here.

Name: Asina Luna
Address: via della Resistenza 23, Peschiera Borromeo, 20068, Italy
Description: A restaurant with an attractive atmosphere, thanks to its profusion of wood, soft lighting and contemporary colour scheme. Meat aged for different periods takes pride of place on the menu. Sourced from different countries, it includes sweet Piedmontese Vicciola beef fed on hazelnuts and tender and delicately marbled Australian Scottona beef. Good selection of strongly flavoured and aged meat options.

Name: Al Persef
Description: In the small, contemporary dining room of Hotel Sporting Family Hospitality, overlooking the Alps, diners can watch the kitchen staff as they work, creatively and paying close attention to locally sourced ingredients. Excellent wine list.

Name: Retrobottega
Description: Minimalist decor and clean lines characterise this restaurant decorated in dark tones, which is open from breakfast to late in the evening. The two owner-chefs, both of whom have experience in various Michelin-starred restaurants in Italy and further afield, are full of brilliant ideas and inspirations, all of which result in an entertaining and exciting dining experience.

Name: MARdiVINO
Description: Inside a recently renovated 1800s farmhouse, MARdiVINO's kitchen offers fresh seafood specialities inspired by Apulian tradition. Do not hesitate to try the barbecued rock octopus, marinated in scapece, accompanied by potato and speck mille-feuille.

Name: San Domenico
Description: Perched high on the tufa cliffs overlooking the Costa degli Dei, this contemporary-style restaurant boasts superb views from its dining room and especially from its panoramic summer terrace. The cuisine served by the young owner-chef is as modern as the setting – dishes are light and almost exclusively focused on local fish.

Name: Feria
Description: A modern restaurant with an Indonesian-style decor, plus an attractive open-view kitchen which creates a warm and welcoming ambience. Here, Marco Feltrin, an Italian chef with experience in Indonesian cuisine, serves typical dishes from this country with a contemporary twist. We particularly enjoyed the noodles, squid and leeks, and the charcoal-grilled snapper. The wine list includes a good selection of organic and biodynamic labels which are the perfect accompaniment to the Asian food served here. Feria has two distinct spaces – the bistro-cum-bar which serves cocktails and some street-food snacks and the gourmet restaurant.

Name: Veranda
Description: Alberto Faccani, the chef at the Magnolia restaurant in the hills inland from Cesenatico, oversees the cuisine at this restaurant, which occupies an elegant veranda on the town’s main avenue – a busy promenade in summer. Fish takes centre stage here, in unfussy dishes that faithfully reflect the maritime traditions of the Adriatic. The menu, alongside daily specials announced at your table, features dishes that include raw fish and seafood, gratins, seafood salads, pasta and risotto, while the main courses feature a selection of grilled, baked and fried fish.

Name: Gallery Bistrot Contemporaneo
Description: Modern cuisine, prepared with meticulous attention and enriched with carefully selected seasonal products. Tradition meets originality, as in the surprising risotto with clams, cauliflower and a dash of cocoa. Only twenty places in a spectacularly designed dining room: walls and ceilings clad in undulating light wood panels that weave together in a dynamic arch, creating an impression of movement that envelops the dining experience.

Name: Alla Locanda
Description: A colourful, contemporary-style restaurant within the Locanda degli Artisti Art Hotel, a new address that is striking for its large art collection displayed throughout its various rooms. The cuisine here focuses on seasonal ingredients which are used to create personalised and imaginative dishes showcased on tasting menus and an à la carte. Interesting wine list, with a special emphasis on labels from the Trentino-Alto Adige region.

Name: GioEle
Description: Situated in the town centre, this colourful and discreetly elegant restaurant offers friendly and professional service. The classic cuisine served here is modern in style, offering a choice of meat and fish dishes as well as a convenient business lunch menu. In summer, tables are arranged outdoors on the terrace and in the small courtyard.

Name: Il Marchese - Osteria Mercato Liquori
Description: Boasting a sumptuous Art Deco setting that contrasts pleasingly with the traditional cuisine served here, this restaurant is the Milanese sibling of Il Marchese in Rome which pays tribute to the famous Italian film “Il Marchese del Grillo” starring Alberto Sordi (it is also the first bar in Europe to offer more than 600 “amaro” liqueurs). The culinary philosophy here is based on traditional Roman cuisine with a contemporary flavour, including delicious specialities such as pasta with carbonara, matriciana and gricia sauces, veal saltimbocca, pork belly and much more besides!

Name: Azotea
Description: Situated in a central location with a small outdoor space, this restaurant boasts a striking interior with old walls, a verdant decor and climbing plants that add a South American feel. The cuisine shines the spotlight on the chef’s native Peru, with appetisers such as potted umbrine tacos and delicious yet atypical antipasti such as raw squid with saltwort and peas. Soy sauce, umeboshi, and yuyo seaweed sauce provide added exotic flavour. We highly recommend one of the excellent cocktails, such as the slightly sour Americano with yuzu.

Name: Aria
Description: The Villa Riviera resort home to this restaurant is situated slightly inland and uphill from the sea in a tranquil oasis of greenery. The modern, minimalist veranda-style dining room is welcoming and elegant, while the summer terrace has a romantic ambience with superb views of the coast, especially at sunset. The menu features modern, occasionally creative cuisine with Ligurian influences evident in dishes such as the “La mia Liguria” dessert which combines ingredients such as basil and olives with white chocolate, pine nuts and fiordilatte ice cream.

Name: Angiò-Macelleria di Mare
Description: The phrase “macellaria di mare” translates as “fish and seafood butcher’s”, a reference to the cured and seasoned fish that features on the menu here. The restaurant has recently changed the way that guests order – you now make your way to your table in a simple yet attractive dining room with an open-view kitchen, where you choose from three tasting menus and à la carte. Our advice is to give young chef Alberto Angiolucci free rein!

Name: Musciora
Description: The father-and-son team (chef and sommelier respectively) at this excellent restaurant not far from the town centre put heart and soul into their work, offering guests three tasting menus: one dedicated to fish and seafood; another to inland ingredients and meat; and the third, entitled “Completo”, simply offering a combination of the first two menus. The recipes are inspired by the island’s produce, which is prepared simply and with real skill. Our inspector particularly enjoyed the raw mullet tartare encased in a “fake” tomato made from tomato and raspberry jelly. The wine list also showcases Sardinia, with a focus on small-scale wineries, although bottles from elsewhere (including natural wines) also feature.

Name: MaMe Restaurant
Description: Situated in central Viareggio near the town’s shipyards, MaMe occupies a long, narrow space that is reminiscent of Oriental restaurants with its long bench running alongside one wall and small bistro-style tables. This informal yet beautifully kept dining room is the backdrop for cuisine with interesting technical details such as the home-made mayonnaise served with the highly recommended steamed fish dish, and the delicious sourdough loaf which is freshly baked and served warm.

Name: ConTatto
Description: Situated in a small town just a few kilometres from the capital, this restaurant run by two young food enthusiasts serves regional dishes with a modern touch, such as cuttlefish with asparagus and a Bernese sauce. Guests can visit the interesting tufa-rock cellar, where the chef experiments with old preserving techniques and special flavourings. In addition, the cellar is used as a venue for exhibitions by different art galleries every season.

Name: Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Housed in an old butcher’s shop right in the village centre, this intimate and elegantly simple “osteria” is run by a young couple. In the kitchen, Agnese Loss, who was only born in 2001 yet has already acquired significant experience, creates personalised and carefully prepared cuisine. Her dishes are showcased on tasting menus (with an option to choose two or three of the courses), including the “Quinto Quarto” menu which is dedicated exclusively to offal, almost in tribute to the building’s former role. The chef’s partner, Davide, runs the front of house with elegance and competence, including overseeing the wine list.

Name: Soprattutto
Address: via Noalese 124, Santa Maria di Sala, 30036, Italy
Description: This tiny, welcoming restaurant with a bright, simple decor has long since come of age, having been opened and run by the same family for years. The wife supervises the front of house, while the husband (whose past experience includes working as a metalworker as well as a chef) is at the helm in the kitchen, where he creates classic fish dishes which are full of flavour and simply prepared from top-quality ingredients. As the restaurant is very popular with its regular clientele, booking in advance is essential – you won’t be disappointed!

Name: La Pista
Address: Centro Commerciale Lingotto - via Nizza 262, Turin, 10126, Italy
Description: The top floor of the Lingotto shopping center – a quintessential Turin landmark, once a Fiat factory whose rooftop test track has been transformed into a visitable botanical garden – is the site of this restaurant, easily reached thanks to clear signage at the entrance guiding visitors through the complex. Once seated, guests may choose from four tasting menus crafted by Alessandro Scardina (all available à la carte): Radici, rooted in Piedmontese tradition; the pared-back Essenziali; the vegetarian Botanic World; the creative Zero/100 Km/h; or Trust, a blind journey guided by the chef’s sensitivity. Whichever path is chosen, the results are compelling: solid, harmonious dishes with clear, well-calibrated flavors.

Name: Gallo Nero
Description: Situated on the edge of the Leocorno contrada (district) just a stone’s throw from the Piazza del Campo, this restaurant with medieval origins has a recently renovated, designer-style dining room with a modern feel. The cuisine focuses on local traditional meat and fish dishes, while the attractive wine cellar is open to guests.

Name: Il Mirto
Description: When you arrive at the luxury Botania hotel, you’ll be accompanied through 3ha grounds of lush Mediterranean vegetation to the restaurant. You couldn’t have a better introduction to the cuisine that awaits at Il Mirto, where you can choose between two long tasting menus or a shorter four-course option featuring dishes from these menus. One of the menus is vegetarian, the other vegan and almost all the vegetables are sourced from the property’s own kitchen garden or from other local growers from Ischia. A delightful experience in a beautiful natural setting, with excellent service provided by young, friendly staff.

Name: Hydra
Description: Situated in the picturesque historic centre of Salerno, this is one of the city’s best restaurants. The dining room here is almost minimalist in style, yet thanks to the soft lighting and beautiful background music it has a pleasing atmosphere; in fine weather, tables are set out in a charming inner courtyard. The cuisine is Mediterranean and contemporary, with a selection of light and creative meat, fish and vegetable dishes featuring on the menu.

Name: iPalici
Address: via Antonello da Messina 3, Viagrande, 95029, Italy
Description: Situated behind Acireale at the foot of Mount Etna National Park, this restaurant is located within the Relais San Giuliano. Deceptively uninteresting from the outside, this historic building and its inner courtyards boast a charm and grandeur that will take your breath away. A huge 16C wine press provides the backdrop for fine cuisine that is more than equal to its impressive setting. Here, the menu makes full use of vegetables and other Sicilian ingredients in dishes that are influenced by the island’s culinary traditions yet reinterpreted with a skilful contemporary twist by the chef.

Name: Donevandro
Description: Up until a few years ago, the owner-chef at this restaurant was working as a painter – a fact that is evident from the artistic touch in his cuisine. His recipes are modern and personalised, with careful attention naturally paid to harmonious presentation, while the flavour of his dishes is brought out by ingredients that are skilfully chosen from the Abruzzo inland area. In 2024, the restaurant moved to new, centrally located premises which have an intimate feel and are elegant and minimalist in style.

Name: Dry Aged
Address: via Cesare Da Sesto 1, Milan, 20123, Italy
Description: Two partners with significant experience opened this lively venue: the rooms combine modern and classic styles in an industrial-New York style decorated with works by major street artists. At the entrance, the glass counter shows off meats of different breeds to be enjoyed even charcoal grilled, but there are also other specialties: appealing dishes with a modern preparation and homemade pastas.

Name: Mirepuà Food Lab
Description: Situated in a picturesque medieval village in the Monferrato hills, this restaurant serves classic Piedmontese cuisine with plenty of meat options, alongside a few specialties from the chef’s native Liguria, including fish and seafood dishes.

Name: Antica Farmacia
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant was used as a pharmacy until the late 1970s. In 2010, it was taken over by owner-chef Juri who now runs his own restaurant here, serving Tuscan-inspired cuisine made using local ingredients and recipes which he reinterprets with a light touch. Full of flavour, dishes include highlights such as baked marrow and Tuscan Chianti beef stew.

Name: Gimmi Restaurant
Address: via San Pietro in Lama 23, Lecce, 73100, Italy
Description: The building is a former Dominican monastery dating back to 1442, which also houses a boutique hotel. The restaurant, on the other hand, is decidedly modern and furnished in a minimalist style: light-coloured floors, mighty stone columns, vaulted ceilings and a room with a view of the wine cabinet. The service is very efficient, attentive and friendly, and the cuisine reaches high levels. Among the most recommended specialities are palamita with fennel tarallo, burrata, salad, bell pepper extract, tarragon oil, and among the main courses the grilled snapper, its extract with saffron pistils, artichoke and provolone mousse.

Name: Caffè delle Rose Bistrot
Description: Occupying an early 20C building in the heart of Pallanza’s picturesque historic centre, this authentic bistro now has a young and contemporary feel. Run by Massimiliano Celeste, a talented chef who is very well known in the region, the restaurant specialises in Mediterranean cuisine prepared with a touch of imagination. There’s a small chef’s table in front of the kitchen, plus an old ice-house (now a small wine cellar housing some excellent wines) which is well worth visiting.

Name: Artifex
Description: This restaurant is situated within the Feuerstein Nature Family Resort, a 5-star property which continues to expand and which nestles in the verdant Val di Fleres, not far from Vipiteno and even closer to the Austrian border. In the small, elegant dining room here, the focus is on creative, regional cuisine, with dishes often accompanied by herbs and vegetables sourced from the property’s own kitchen garden where they are grown without the use of chemicals. Top-quality seasonal ingredients take pride of place in the cuisine here, while the well-stocked wine cellar features a good selection of labels decanted in the dining room by the talented sommelier.

Name: Specus
Description: This charming restaurant’s name comes from the Latin and refers to the small grotto carved out of the tufa rock in the courtyard, which is home to just a few tables. The restaurant is run by a young couple, with Flavia front of house and Alessio at the helm in the kitchen. The cuisine is authentic in style, with imaginatively named dishes such as “Quel viaggio che non scordo” (“This journey I’ll never forget”) and “Dal 2014” (“From 2014”). The Riso Acquerello with fermented goat’s cheese, black truffle and herb pesto is truly memorable, while the desserts (especially the apple strudel) are equally delicious.

Name: Cucine Nervi
Description: Inside the Cantine Nervi, a contemporary restaurant where the kitchen is totally open, you can choose to eat on the large counter or at more classic tables. The young chef Matteo Piana delights in a contemporary and creative style. If it seems obvious that there is no lack of meat dishes, you will be pleasantly surprised by the presence of some incursions from the sea (try the raw tuna to dip in different tasty sauces, some of oriental inspiration). There is a good wine selection, naturally the house wines are the most represented: many also served by the glass.

Name: Filo
Description: From the splendid lakeside position, the view extends to the opposite shore, Comacina Island, and Villa Balbianello. An enchanting terrace overlooking Lake Como, surrounded by greenery with hills as a backdrop like a painting, is where you can savor Mediterranean-flavored dishes. Choose from three tasting menus ("Freestyle," "Classics," and "Vegetarian"). Or opt for the à la carte menu, with offerings such as purple prawns with goat cheese cream, berries, and bisque: an explosion of flavors!

Name: Podere Belvedere Tuscany
Address: via San Piero a Strada 23, Pontassieve, 50065, Italy
Description: Occupying a tower house dating from 1700, this restaurant is surrounded by typical Tuscan scenery of olive groves and vineyards, as well as vegetable gardens and farms which produce many of the ingredients featuring in the dishes here. The friendly self-taught chef celebrates the best of Tuscan country cuisine, with a focus on meat, including grilled dishes and top-quality vegetables, as well as the occasional more creative dish – the result is cuisine of a very high standard. The restaurant also has a few guestrooms – a convenient option given the property’s attractive secluded location.

Name: Jamantè
Address: via San Vito 97, Polignano a Mare, 70044, Italy
Description: Located not far from the historic centre and the picturesque Lama Monachile beach, Jamantè is an elegant restaurant with well-spaced-out tables perfect for a stylish night out. As is traditional in Puglia, there’s a wide selection of raw options to start, followed by dishes with a focus on fish and seafood. Elaborate and creative cuisine is to the fore here.

Name: Pierre - Trattoria Sartoriale
Description: On the edge of the historic center, this is a simple restaurant with just a few tables, set in modern spaces accented with 1920s-inspired touches. True to its name, the focus here is a “tailored” approach to cuisine. The menu reflects the best the market has to offer, interpreted with creativity, especially in the three tasting menus, while never going overboard and always prioritizing flavor. The restaurant is run by two passionate young professionals (the chef has gained excellent national and international experience). At lunchtime, a business menu is also available.

Name: Innocenti Wine Experiences
Description: Innocenti Wine is a venue with a dual identity: on one side, a wine shop boasting an ever-evolving collection of over 1,200 labels spanning Italy’s finest wine regions and international terroirs; on the other, a restaurant where contemporary cuisine finds expression through three tasting menus or à la carte selections. A place designed for those who approach wine as exploration and the table as its natural complement.

Name: Giano
Description: Conveniently situated in a quiet setting just off Via Vittorio Veneto, Giano is housed within the modern Hotel W with which it shares a comfortable cocktail bar and attractive garden. The atmosphere here is modern and informal, with simple dishes served at lunchtime and more gourmet dining options in the evening. The resident chef is supported by the experienced Ciccio Sultano from the Michelin-two-star Duomo restaurant in Ragusa, whose influence is evident in some of the reinterpreted, contemporary-style Sicilian dishes. Iconic dishes such as spaghetto taratatà (with a tuna and bottarga sauce), caponata and carpacci are highly recommended, as are desserts such as the reinterpreted millefeuille. Sicilian cuisine takes pride of place here and the service is excellent.

Name: Bottega Aleotti
Description: Situated just a stone’s throw from the splendid Santa Croce church, this charming restaurant should not be missed. The cuisine combines Emilian traditions with fresh, local ingredients, and includes dishes with a more contemporary touch. The excellent bread and home-made pastries add to the overall dining experience.

Name: Marixx
Description: Located well away from the busy city centre and overlooking the luxury yachts and boats moored in the harbour, this restaurant opened in the summer of 2021, at the same time as the modern Cala del Forte marina in which it is situated (the name of the marina comes from the Forte dell'Annunziata, the ruins of which are visible from the side facing the sea). Fish and seafood take pride of place here (especially raw fish dishes), served with classic, seasonal accompaniments, as well as snacks, while an oyster bar is an added attraction. Although the best tables are in the glass-fronted veranda overlooking the pedestrian promenade, the contemporary-style dining room is also attractive. The owner-chef has plenty of experience behind him, especially working in the region.

Name: La Kucina
Address: via Giulio De Petra 67, Foggia, 71121, Italy
Description: This modern, welcoming restaurant on the outskirts of town serves contemporary cuisine on a varied menu which also includes simpler options to suit all budgets, especially at lunchtime. In the dining room, a cabinet for ageing meat houses some excellent Iberian hams.

Name: Michelasso
Description: Situated in the city centre, this refined restaurant with an elegantly classic decor is perfect for a romantic, intimate dinner. The menu features meat and fish, with traditional dishes reinterpreted thanks to the chef’s expertise and proven experience. In summer, choose a table on the pleasant outdoor space overlooking the lively Via Santa Brigida.

Name: Tuorlo
Description: Decorated in elegant bistro style and skilfully renovated with contemporary furnishings, Tuorlo serves dishes based on traditional Piedmontese recipes reinterpreted with modern techniques and personal touches. Good choice of wines, plus an attractive little courtyard to the rear for relaxed summer dining.

Name: Aquadulcis
Address: contrada Tenda, Vallo della Lucania, 84078, Italy
Description: Following careful restoration, this old mill has been transformed into a gourmet restaurant with just a few tables. Here, skilful young chef Vincenzo Cucolo delights guests with his cuisine – a combination of creative dishes and old recipes focusing on traditional Cilento ingredients.

Name: Agriturismo Il Cavallino
Address: SP 55 Saturnia-Semproniano, località Fibbianello, Semproniano, 58055, Italy
Description: A property located in a very peaceful setting within an organic farm stay. The management is driven by great passion: he works in the kitchen, carrying forward the family business tradition; she manages the dining room with grace and attention. The recipes offered are tied to the territory, with dishes that are generous, flavorful, and colorful, showing particular attention to the lightness of the preparations. The quality of their organic extra virgin olive oil is particularly noteworthy.

Name: L'Ambasciata
Address: piazzetta Ambasciatori del Gusto 1, Quistello, 46026, Italy
Description: This has long been one of those restaurants in Italy where the opulent interior decor has no equal – at Christmas, the mirrors, rugs, silverware, chandeliers and piles of books are joined by the largest and most ornate Christmas tree that you’ll ever see in a restaurant. The cuisine created by owner-chef Matteo Ugolotti is inspired by Mantuan traditions and the restaurant’s previous famous owners, occasionally going all the way back to the Renaissance. Special mention should be made of the extraordinary chocolate salami – a dessert coated with a delicious, frothy, warm zabaglione poured from a copper pan at your table. The menu also features more modern recipes and tasting menus.

Name: Da Bob Cook Fish
Description: Working in partnership with the nearby fishmongers which supplies it with fresh fish and seafood, this restaurant occupies a building once used for storing oranges that dates back 400 years. Although there is a menu, given the restaurant’s close relationship with the fishmongers we recommend asking the serving staff about the catch of the day and taking a look in the glass cabinet where the fish are displayed. Dishes are classic and traditional, allowing the full flavour of the fresh fish to shine through.

Name: Ape Vino e Cucina
Description: This attractive restaurant in the heart of Alba, the gastronomic capital of the Langhe, is home to chef Damiano Nigro who has previous experience in Michelin-starred restaurants in the area. The restaurant serves aperitif snacks, tapas and top-quality cocktails alongside its delicious, generously portioned meals which, as you might expect in Piedmont, have a traditional flavour. The pasta, bread, desserts and ice-cream are all homemade, while on our last visit in the summer we particularly enjoyed the maccheroncini with scampi and peppers, and the exquisite Fassona beef with a red-wine sauce and seasonal vegetables. Booked ahead is recommended.

Name: Alessandro Feo
Address: via Angelo Lista 24, Marina di Casal Velino, 84040, Italy
Description: In a beautiful stone-vaulted building (an old 17C monastery) on the town’s seafront promenade, young owner-chef Alessandro Feo has made his mark in this region that perhaps has fewer gourmet restaurants than many places elsewhere. Here, he creates dishes that combine traditional influences and classic favourites from Campania with his own individual flair and creativity. His focus is on local, seasonal ingredients, including produce from his two kitchen gardens and fish sourced from local fishermen as well as from his own ventures out to sea.

Name: Radici Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Having moved to the pedestrianised section of historic Gallarate, Radici Osteria Contemporanea has also adopted a new look, with a lounge-bar ambience that is young and trendy, making it the perfect setting for its aperitifs and superb cocktails. The restaurant’s excellent, modern and personalised cuisine remains unchanged, however.

Name: Aprudia
Description: A restaurant tucked into an intimate corner of the historic center, with spaces characterized by brick vaulting that creates a pleasant contrast with some modern touches in the furnishings. Here, Enzo Di Pasquale – through a tasting format where diners freely choose dishes and quantities – celebrates the seasonality of mostly plant-based and local products, sometimes sourced directly from his own garden. The dishes are absolutely original (like the restaurant’s name: if you're curious, ask for an explanation from the staff) and always very colorful. The philosophical thread is a commendable “no waste” approach.

Name: Locanda Nelli
Address: via Vittorio Veneto 15, Pietra Ligure, 17027, Italy
Description: A friendly and welcoming little restaurant in the heart of the town’s historic centre. It’s no surprise that the specialities here focus mainly on fish and seafood, with an emphasis on Mediterranean cuisine, homemade pasta and the use of extremely fresh ingredients – the menu changes daily depending on market availability. The charming outdoor space boasts tables set out along the small pedestrianised street.

Name: Sa Domu Sarda
Description: Despite being an island, Sardinia’s traditional cuisine tends to focus on meat dishes, and you’ll find some of its best-known specialities served at this restaurant, with its simple dining rooms and typical local décor. Enjoy evocatively named dishes such as “sitzigorrus cun bagna” (snails in a tomato sauce), Bue Rosso “bombas” (meat balls), delicious Sardinian pastas such as “malloreddus”, “culurgiones” and “fregula”, stews, casseroles and meat fillets, as well as the famous “sebadas” and “su pappai biancu” (a type of blancmange) desserts.

Name: Hazama
Description: Japanese cuisine in a small restaurant with a minimalist mood echoed in its cooking. Here, young chef Satoshi Hazama offers – in addition to the à la carte menu – a 7‑course Kaiseki journey or a 4‑course tasting menu. Kaiseki cuisine employs five fundamental techniques applied to seasonal ingredients: raw, grilled, fried, boiled, and steamed, in a crescendo of intensity that showcases Japanese haute cuisine (advance reservation required).

Name: La Maison de Filip
Description: Situated at the entrance to the pedestrian section of the beautiful city of Trento, this intimate restaurant has a modern, minimalist and vaguely Nordic style, with just a few solid wood tables and stools of different sizes. The menu features a concise selection of carefully thought-out dishes, with starters, first and main courses (meat, fish or vegetarian) that are elegant, well prepared and contemporary in style. Beautiful presentation completes the picture.

Name: I Giardini dei Rodo
Address: via Bonomo Alto - Scauri, Pantelleria, 91017, Italy
Description: As its name suggests, this restaurant’s guests can enjoy their meal surrounded by verdant gardens, which are planted with palms, flowers and citrus trees. Regional flavours take centre-stage in the modern dishes in this romantic and original setting.

Name: Rear Restaurant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant with a modern, elegant dining room in which an entire wall is taken up by the open-view kitchen serves varied cuisine. In addition to more elaborate dishes, there’s also a choice of street food such as fried dishes, sandwiches, Spanish prosciutto and tacos, as well as raw fish and seafood, classic and more creative options, and various fish and meat main courses, many of which are cooked over the barbecue grill. The superb wine list includes a fine array of champagnes.

Name: Duo
Description: In this restaurant housed in a historic palazzo in the centre of Chiavari, the owners have used the structural beauty of the building to showcase the skills of local artisans, resulting in a very attractive ambience. The modern cuisine is simple in style, allowing all the flavour of the ingredients to shine through.

Name: Villa Pignano
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A veritable Garden of Eden just 15km from Volterra, this 300ha estate is home to a restaurant with a strong zero-mile philosophy. This is backed up by its careful use of ingredients grown or produced on the estate itself, such as vegetables, olives and grains, as well as chicken, pork and honey – a sustainable approach that results in delicious, contemporary cuisine. The dishes here are fresh and full of flavour yet elaborate and modern in style (note the simpler menu at lunchtime). The interesting wine list explores Tuscany through its choice of top-quality organic labels as well as including wines produced from the estate’s own vines.

Name: Brezza fish and chill
Description: An alternative eatery amid the Abruzzo dining options, situated on the beautiful seafront promenade at Soverato. The idea is simple: fish takes centre stage, served in rolls, on "broast" and “friselle” bread, as well as raw or fried, although generous salads and delicious desserts are also available. The ingredients, full of flavour and always simply prepared, result in copious and colourful dishes. Good quality wine is available by the glass, plus a fine choice of cocktails which is enhanced in the evening by the addition of creative home-made options. Friendly female staff, plus excellent background music. A pleasant address serving quality food at very reasonable prices!

Name: Marechiaro
Description: This smart, elegant restaurant, which has a particularly romantic ambience in the evening, has been serving top-quality fish in Bolzano for over 20 years. Prepared in traditional Italian style, the dishes here focus on the flavour and quality of the fish and seafood on offer, most of which comes from the Mediterranean. The two friendly brothers who run the restaurant are originally from Naples, which explains the specialities from Campania and the excellent pizza which also features on the menu. A simpler selection of dishes is available at lunchtime.

Name: La Locanda di Fabio e Vale
Description: Young, informal and friendly owners Fabio and Vale welcome guests to their restaurant in Offanengo, just a few kilometres from Crema. A good choice for anyone looking for a change from traditional cuisine, the restaurant serves moderately creative dishes including a good selection of fish options (the Mazara del Vallo red prawns served with green gazpacho, caviar and lemon are particularly delicious).

Name: Gina casa con cucina
Address: via Croce di Città 25, Aosta, 11100, Italy
Description: This restaurant in the old town has a simple and informal feel, with two rooms in the basement built between the Roman walls of Aosta. The quality of the cuisine here is remarkable – the menu features dishes inspired by local traditions, alongside a selection of modern and personalised Italian dishes (including meat options).

Name: Novo Osteria
Address: piazza De Cristoforis 30, Borgonovo Val Tidone, 29011, Italy
Description: Originally a monastery, this building dating back to the 11C was later transformed into an inn. Having closed at the beginning of this century, the building has now been fully renovated and restored to its original function, while retaining much of its original architecture. In addition to the restaurant, which serves traditional local cuisine with a modern focus and plenty of flavour (we particularly enjoyed the savoury zabaglione gnocchi with porcini mushrooms, Jerusalem artichokes and currants), there are also seven guestrooms available in the adjoining Locanda Borgo Impero.

Name: Verbano
Address: via Ugo Ara 2, Isola dei Pescatori, Stresa, 28838, Italy
Description: Within the confines of the small, charming Verbano hotel on the beautiful island of Pescatori, chef Marco Sacco serves top-quality cuisine in what can only be described as a stunning setting. The contemporary-style dining room boasts panoramic windows, while the outdoor terrace with its views of Palazzo Borromeo and Isola Bella is the perfect setting for dinner in fine weather.

Name: Enoteca L'Armadillo
Description: Situated in the district of La Palud at the foot of Mont Blanc, this small wine bar serves interesting cuisine created by a talented Japanese chef who adds his own personal twist to the valley’s top-quality ingredients. Dishes include the occasional fusion option, such as capon salad with yuzu, puntarelle and black garlic, while wine is chosen directly from the shelves in the intimate dining room. Booking is recommended, especially in high season.

Name: La Taverna di Bacco
Description: A small restaurant just a stone’s throw from the sea which is memorable for its chic decor and intimate ambience. The cuisine combines traditional influences with an innovative approach resulting in ambitious, creative and modern dishes. The wine list is particularly worthy of note.

Name: Mater Bistrot
Description: A small bistro situated in a street just behind Piazza Cinque Giornate, with a few tables and small lights that give the setting a cosy feel. The dining room is minimalist in style, with just a few tables and a counter where you can sit and watch chef Alex (Alessandro) at work in the kitchen. Guests have the option of two tasting menus or a selection of smaller dishes to share. A choice of natural wines accompanies the chef’s imaginative dishes.

Name: Pepenero
Address: piazza del Duomo 4, San Miniato, 56028, Italy
Description: In its new home in Piazza del Duomo, in beautiful San Miniato, in the hands of chef Gilberto Rossi Pepenero continues to serve cuisine that showcases the best ingredients (both meat and fish) from this bountiful region, with delicacies such as excellent truffles featuring on the menu throughout the year. Prepared with a light and modern touch, meals are served in a spacious dining room where the many windows offer glimpses of the town centre.

Name: Casa Fantini/Lake Time
Description: Situated on the lakefront in the attractive town of Pella, this modern and welcoming restaurant occupies an old building which has been restored and furnished with a stylish and harmonious decor. Offering simpler options at lunchtime, the restaurant serves traditional cuisine reinterpreted and presented with a contemporary flavour. A lounge, garden, swimming pool and 11 guestrooms add to the exclusive appeal.

Name: Osteria della Foce
Description: A lively and contemporary bistro that celebrates Mediterranean cuisine with a modern twist, offering meat and fish dishes characterised by distinct flavours and refined techniques. Highlights include yellowtail tartare with celery, rose syrup and seed crackers, and the delicious pavé of striped bass accompanied by mashed potatoes, sautéed artichokes and lemon sauce.

Name: Osteria degli Angeli
Description: An attractive restaurant which offers a friendly and informal welcome and service, alongside an elegant, personalised yet classic decor. The cuisine is mainly Mediterranean in flavour, emphasised by the use of local and seasonal ingredients. The self-taught chef here is passionate about his cuisine.

Name: Locanda Marchesani
Description: In addition to specialities such as oysters and caviar, this restaurant serves sophisticated classic, traditional cuisine reinterpreted with a modern twist. Choose between à la carte options or tasting menus prepared with refined ingredients of the highest quality.

Name: Vert Osteria Contemporanea
Description: Housed in a rustic building on the green slopes facing the lake, this restaurant has a welcoming feel with its stone and wood decor and large windows looking out at a beautiful, shaded garden where meals are served in fine weather. Delicious Italian cuisine takes pride of place on the menu.

Name: Osteria Billis
Description: Almost ten years after it opened, this restaurant run by the Billis twins is moving towards what its owners describe as a “new tradition” – a personalised way of interpreting local traditions through the lens of global influences. While maintaining roots in solid Piedmontese traditions, the cuisine combines local ingredients with international techniques. Examples include “roasted rice”, a dish which is cooked in the oven and then flavoured according to the season and whim of the chef, and the “Carpaccio in Ramino”, beef which is lightly seared in a copper pan with rosemary, bay leaf, salt and pepper. The veranda’s retro ambience immediately catches the eye of passersby in the nearby park, adding to the appeal of this fascinating building dating from the early 20C.

Name: Terrazza Fiorella
Address: via Vincenzo Maggio 5, Massa Lubrense, 80061, Italy
Description: Housed in the Villa Fiorella Art Hotel, this restaurant boasts a stunningly located terrace with spectacular views of the Bay of Naples and its islands. The cuisine pays tribute to Campania and its top-quality ingredients which the chef uses to create imaginative dishes reinterpreted with his own personal twist.

Name: DaV Mare
Description: The classic, wrought-iron outdoor dining space at this restaurant overlooks one of the most romantic little squares in Italy, while the view takes in the promontory dominated by its castle – a picture-postcard view that is famous around the world. The experienced Cerea family from the famous three-starred Michelin Da Vittoria restaurant in Bergamo are at the helm, serving consistently top-quality cuisine whether you’re here for a quick lunch or a gourmet dinner. It’s best to book ahead as the few tables are much in demand!

Name: Motelombroso
Description: An old, carefully restored road worker’s house on the Alzaia Naviglio Pavese canal is the setting for this modern, stylish restaurant where Alessandra and Matteo welcome guests in a graceful, elegant and yet informal manner. The menu features contemporary meat and fish dishes accompanied by a good choice of wines. If you’re curious about the restaurant’s name, ask the owners for an explanation: could it be something to do with the private dining room perhaps?

Name: Andree
Address: via San Martino della Battaglia 16, La Spezia, 19121, Italy
Description: In the centre of Spezia, the restaurant unveils an impressive open kitchen, developing into a cosy room with vaulted brick ceilings in a more contemporary-styled setting. Similarly, the cuisine line reflects modern tones, with locally sourced fish at its finest expression, offering flexible options between tasting menus and à la carte choices, supported by a wine list of character.

Name: La Ciotola
Description: A fresh, dynamic venue along the road to Pordenone, thoughtfully run by the Cover brothers. The kitchen tells tales of both land and sea: earthy, satisfying dishes such as the juicy young heifer entrecôte wrapped in golden potatoes with mustard dressing, and tempting seafood offerings such as the fragrant, comforting linguine with scampi alla busara. Quality ingredients take center stage! At lunch, the menu streamlines and service quickens, with lighter prices to match; come evening, the carte expands and the experience becomes complete and gratifying.

Name: Hosteria Toblino
Address: via Garda 3, Sarche di Madruzzo, 38070, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The most welcoming section of the extensive Cantina Toblino complex is home to the large, contemporary and minimalist-style Hosteria. Here, a young chef serves simple reinterpretations of regional dishes with a focus on zero-mile produce with the occasional yet astute use of ingredients from further afield.

Name: Augurio
Address: via Dietro le Mura B 16, Trento, 38122, Italy
Description: Opened by three brothers (Augurio is the family name), this restaurant in the city centre successfully combines the traditional and the modern in both its cuisine and its decor. The dining room, with an open-view kitchen on the ground floor, boasts an old, vaulted ceiling, while its wood furniture adds a contemporary look. The menu features local and Italian dishes reinterpreted with flavour and style. Lighter options are available at lunchtime; the grande carte needs to be ordered ahead of time.

Name: Corbezzoli
Description: Situated in the Relais Bellaria hotel, the Corbezzoli restaurant takes its name from the magnificent garden visible through its large picture windows. The cuisine, which is both creative and full of flavour, includes a wide array of dishes that range from vegetarian to meat and fish options, with the possibility of choosing from three tasting menus and an à la carte. Make sure you leave room for one of the delicious desserts, which include an unmissable Neapolitan-style baba with pastry cream and sour cherries.

Name: Radici
Description: Accursio Craparo has returned to his “Roots”: in two simple and elegant dining rooms, or in the spacious and enchanting outdoor summer space overlooking the historic center – weather permitting – the offering is based on traditional Sicilian cuisine, presented in consistently generous dishes, sometimes enriched with a touch of personal interpretation.

Name: Bottega Culinaria
Address: contrada Pontoni 72, San Vito Chietino, 66038, Italy
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Nestled amid a charming landscape of olive groves, this restaurant is not particularly easy to find, so make sure that you use a satnav or ask for directions when booking. A simple, minimalist-style dining room provides the backdrop for imaginative cuisine which includes plenty of vegetables and is full of contrasting flavours and reinterpreted regional influences.

Name: Locanda La Raia
