Its mission is to showcase local traditions and regional ingredients – an initiative mission it fulfils with conviction. The enticing menu (you can't argue with the prices!) makes choosing a challenge. Will you go for the baked potatoes topped with crumbled blue cheese, dill and a rocket salad on the side? Or the juicy lamb cooked in the tandoori oven, served with rice mixed with almonds, currants and cinnamon? Whatever your decision, you are in for a treat. And the portions are large enough that they can easily be shared. At this lively establishment, which has a cosier dining area on the upper floor, you are fully immersed in local life.

Name: Mandalya
Address: 19 Mayis Caddesi, No: 4/A, Güvercinlik, Bodrum, 48200, Türkiye
Description: In this tranquil fishing village, you stroll along a street lined with all kinds of restaurants, yet this stone house, with its rather rustic decor and lovely waterside terrace, immediately catches your eye. A glance at the display counter, brimming with a vibrant array of mezze, is enough to draw in any foodie. Sea bass in olive oil, accented with just the right amount of vinegar and peppercorns, that melts in your mouth, is served alongside grilled aubergine and peppers with a delicate balance of sweet and heat: utterly blissful. You can also choose from a variety of fish, prepared simply but served exceptionally fresh. Mandalya is the place to be for house-made, authentic cuisine at fantastic value for money.

Name: Parvus Kalamış
Address: Zühtüpaşa Mahallesi, Rüştiye Sokak No:4/A, Kadıköy, Istanbul, 34724, Türkiye
Description: Parvus Kalamış is a modest little establishment with just a handful of tables that see a steady stream of diners throughout the day. The chefs describe their cuisine as simple and delicious, and we can only agree. Think ravioli generously stuffed with ricotta and broccoli, bathed in a sage-infused butter sauce, or perfectly medium-rare lamb fillet served with bulgur risotto and carrot purée laced with Middle Eastern spices. This fusion of Turkish and Mediterranean culinary traditions delivers deep, indulgent flavours that are nothing short of irresistible. Beyond the extensive à la carte selection, there is a thoroughly appealing set menu that changes daily (available 12-6pm). A real gem!

Name: Mahir Lokantası
Address: Cumhuriyet, Tavukçu Fethi Sokak No:28/B, Şişli, Istanbul, 34380, Türkiye
Description: The long queue of locals that forms before opening time speaks volumes – this bustling place is hugely popular. So, be sure to arrive on time and you will be handsomely rewarded with a generous menu featuring expertly prepared Turkish classics. Options include an intense lahmacun with lamb, black Urfa chilli and fresh herbs, a salad that balances spicy, zesty and sweet nuances, and dolmasi with a filling of lamb, beef, rice and herbs. Deciding will not be easy, but you are bound to leave sated thanks to the outstanding value for money. A cherished spot that has truly earned its praise!

Name: Yanyalı Fehmi Lokantası
Address: Osmanağa Mahallesi, Yağlıkçı İsmail Sokak No:1, Kadıköy, Istanbul, 34714, Türkiye
Description: Located in the heart of Istanbul's bustling old quarter, this establishment invites you to enter a slice of living history. Since opening its doors in 1919, the restaurant has remained a family affair, currently run by the third generation. The interior exudes timeless nostalgic charm with its elegant woodwork and Chesterfield banquettes. Watch the pastry chefs at work in the front section (takeaway available), then peruse the wide range of traditional treats in the display counter. You could start with the slow-cooked aubergine with minced lamb and cheesy béchamel sauce, follow that with the leg of lamb accompanied by roast potatoes and crisp vegetables, then finish off with the irresistible crispy pistachio-filled kadayıf – all at reasonable prices.

Name: Nazende Cadde
Address: Caddebostan, Sembol apt, Caddebostan Plaj Yolu Sokak No:13/A, Kadıköy, Istanbul, 34728, Türkiye
Description: (Temporarily closed. Moves to Caddebostan, Bagdat Street, Kinayman B Blok 345A, Kadiköy) Head to the neighbourhood of upmarket Bağdat Avenue and experience the convivial and friendly atmosphere of Nazende Cadde. This is a charming place, in which to share all kinds of delicacies with friends. The tempting menu changes daily to take advantage of the best market offerings and is simply irresistible. The chefs put their heart and soul into every creation and have a few signature dishes up their sleeves, including succulent, boldly spiced grilled squid rings. They like working with offal, pairing tenderly cooked lamb brains with fresh parsley, diced tomatoes, olive oil and lemon. At this lively establishment, generosity comes from the heart. A real gem!

Name: Ali Ocakbaşı Karaköy
Address: Arap Camii Mahallesi, Tersane Caddesi, Kardeşim Sokak No:45 Kat 4, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34421, Türkiye
Description: A narrow street leads you to this somewhat hidden gem. The waterside setting is a draw in itself, but the main attractions are the barbecue and tandoori oven. With a sure hand, the chefs flame-grill aubergine, for example, and then season it with chilli and five-spice powder. Their marinated lamb and beef are cooked to juicy perfection, generously spiced and served with lavash bread that has been briefly crisped up on the barbecue. The various mezze, salads and desserts such as halva stay true to tradition. And for this price point, the value is fantastic!

Name: Bağarası
Address: Bitez, Pınarlı Caddesi No:59, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
Description: "Authentic" and "welcoming" are two words that sum up what Bağarası is all about. This is the place to come to enjoy delicious food in a relaxed setting. At the display counter, you can order some of the fragrant mezze from a selection that changes regularly. Their take on traditional manti is not to be missed: crispy deep-fried filo pastry, a yoghurt cream and ragout generously seasoned with oregano and mint. Do leave room for dessert, because you absolutely must try the sweet artichoke confit with milk ice cream – a house speciality. It is a nice touch that you can choose your portion sizes, so you can add one more little plate and sample all of these delicious treats. It's well worth it!

Name: Adil Müftüoğlu
Address: Mithatpaşa Caddesi No:159, Balçova, Izmir, 35330, Türkiye
Description: This spacious family-run restaurant welcomed its first diners in 1955. Today, the third generation is at the helm of what has become a firm favourite with locals, who flock to the large counter to choose their favourite mezze, soups and hot dishes. You can start with the lentil soup made with plenty of vegetables and a robust broth, follow that with some delicately presented spinach with silky yoghurt and fresh mint, and finish off with a delicious sweet and creamy rice pudding. The hearty stews, made in time-honoured tradition, reflect the establishment's long culinary heritage. All these authentic treats are freshly prepared, so once they're gone, they're gone.

Name: LA Mahzen
Address: Kuşçuburun Mahallesi, Başmimar Sinan Caddesi No:81, Yazıbaşı, Torbalı, Izmir, 35860, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Domaine Lucien Arkas vineyards are well worth a visit. Take some time to stroll among the vines – highly romantic if you have that special someone by your side. The same romantic feeling prevails whether you dine outdoors overlooking the vineyard or indoors with a view of the wine cellar beneath you (bottles are for sale at the entrance). The chef tempts you with unfussy Mediterranean dishes that perfectly complement the quality wines produced here. Charcoal-grilled leg of lamb with a bold lamb jus enriched with mustard, then a wonderfully sweet strawberry magnolia for dessert – honest flavours are paramount, both in the glass and on the plate.

Name: Happena
Address: Aydınlı Mahallesi, Yavuz Sokak No:1, Göreme, Nevşehir, 50180, Türkiye
Description: Happena transports your taste buds back to the era of the Hittites, who founded an empire in Anatolia thousands of years ago. Drawing inspiration from ancient texts, the chefs bring this distant past vividly to life on your plate. Expect traditional spices, crisp grilled meats and tender cuts, such as lamb cooked over a wood fire until beautifully caramelised, served with pita bread, a honey and ginger sauce, and fermented pickles and grapes. The extensive menu is simply wonderful, as is the setting. Set on higher ground, this restaurant is part of the Kelebek Special Cave Hotel and brims with enchanting traditional charm. From the terraces, the views over Göreme are truly breathtaking – a journey through time you won't soon forget.

Name: Arka Ristorante Pizzeria
Address: Çarşı, Cumhuriyet Caddesi No:102, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: With its red-and-white check tablecloths, photographs and paintings from Italy, vintage decor and a terrace overlooking the pebble beach, this trattoria is the embodiment of Mediterranean charm. The menu features an extensive range of tempting traditional dishes. The Neapolitan-style pizzas and creamy risotto with super-fresh seafood are especially popular. There are also 12 different dishes with house-made pasta to choose from. This generosity is just one example of why Arka has been a Bodrum favourite for so long – and rightfully so!

Name: Tatbak
Address: Valikonağı Caddesi, Akkavak Sokak No:38/B, Nişantaşı/Şişli, Istanbul, 34365, Türkiye
Description: Tatbak has been the go-to kebab place for many an Istanbulite since 1960, and at no point in that time has it compromised on quality. With its lovely stained-glass windows and marble finishings, the vintage-style decor is attractive, but the local vibe and fantastic value for money are the main draws. Take, for instance, the Gaziantep version of spicy lahmacun (Turkish pizza), generously topped with vegetables and parsley, or the kebab with lamb sausages and minced beef – both are house favourites. The experienced chef skilfully balances sweet, spicy and tangy nuances, without losing sight of the importance of the right textures. Tatbak is a mecca for foodies!

Name: EFENDY
Address: Nisbetiye Caddesi No:13, Levent/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34330, Türkiye
Description: Famed local chef Somer Sivrioğlu has assembled a talented team at EFENDY, a vibrant restaurant with a warm Middle Eastern-inspired ambiance, located slightly outside the main tourist area. Here, traditional Anatolian cuisine is reimagined with a twist. Ancient techniques meet open-fire cooking and fresh ideas to create dishes that deliver real pleasure. Creamy hummus is elevated with just the right amount of tahini and herb-infused olive oil, and served with deep-fried chickpeas and capers. Be sure to sample the lahmacun with its wonderful aromas from the wood-fired oven. A delightful juxtaposition of old and new – accompanied by outstanding cocktails.

Name: Tavacı Recep Usta Alsancak
Address: Atatürk Caddesi No:364, Konak, Izmir, 35220, Türkiye
Description: As soon as you are seated in this very spacious and warmly decorated restaurant with its striking modern conservatory, you are served some mezze. This gesture speaks volumes about the generous nature of your hosts. The dishes here – especially the grill specialities – showcase the aromatic depth of traditional Turkish cuisine. Lamb shoulder, oven-roasted and succulent, is infused with spices, paprika and green chilli. A platter of assorted grilled meats is a must. Tea is of course served with a few complimentary desserts, such as fabulous baklava. There is no way that you will still be hungry when you leave!

Name: Partal Kardeşler Balık Restorant
Address: Balıklıova, Balıklı Ova Caddesi No:297, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: The tail fins of large fish hanging as centrepieces in this charming family-run establishment are a good indication of the kind of food to expect. The sea, which you can see shimmering nearby, is the main source of produce. The uncle goes out fishing, the father takes his place behind the grill, the mother creates sumptuous mezze dishes, and the son provides a warm reception. You might like to start your meal with yoghurt seasoned with red chilli marinated in oil, before moving on to crispy deep-fried calamari and succulent grilled sea bass. A heartwarming place, where you can savour authentic cuisine without breaking the bank.

Name: Old Greek House
Address: Davutlu, Şahin Caddesi No:12, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, 50420, Türkiye
Description: Yes, this is indeed an old Greek house from the 19C, and what a beauty it is! The striking façade with its distinctive traditional balcony, the arcaded courtyard adorned with old frescoes and the open dining area under a canopy of vine leaves make you feel as though you've wandered onto a 1970s film set. Brimming with charm, this is also a true family-run establishment – several members of the Özturk family were even born within these walls. In the kitchen, the matriarch prepares dishes that blend Turkish tradition with Greek influences. A crisp seasonal salad with just enough vinegar and the gentle sweetness of tomato, succulent sac tava, rich baklava with candied nuts… Every bite is a joy. Consider booking an overnight stay in one of the guestrooms – Old Greek House is a perfect base for discovering the region.

Name: Casius Antioch Kitchen
Address: Kılıçalipaşa Mahallesi, Akarsu Yokuşu Caddesi No:36A, Cihangir Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: Some restaurants just feel right from the moment you walk in, and Casius Antioch Kitchen is one of them. Whether you come to this trendy establishment for breakfast, lunch or dinner, you can expect a warm welcome and attentive service. The rich dishes are traditional with a fresh twist; many are baked in the brick oven. Examples include thin, crisp lahmacun with lightly spiced minced meat, tomato and parsley, as well as roasted pepper with crushed walnuts, onion and pomegranate molasses. Expect a feast of flavours, an impressive menu and great value for money.

Name: Beğendik Abi
Address: Tatar Cami Sokak No:12, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: There is a rustic charm about this place that is reflected in the food. At the counter, there is an impressive selection of mezze and hot dishes that you can also order straight away. Market-fresh Turkish cuisine is prepared with great passion and respect for tradition. Take, for example, the green beans cooked in a tomato sauce with onion and smoked aubergine, served with well-seasoned yoghurt, or the lamb stew with a light stock made from tomato, garlic and pepper, enhanced with cumin and coriander. At Beğendik Abi you are guaranteed a delicious and affordable dining experience. The queue that often forms at the door doesn't lie.

Name: Otantik Ocakbaşı
Description: The barbecue and wood-fired oven will catch your eye as soon as you enter this congenial establishment, which has a cosy terrace in the lane to the rear. The chef expertly tames the open fire to cook delicious dishes, such as kebab and grilled dry-aged steak. The mixed grill is a signature dish here: a variety of juicy meats, oven-fresh bread and a judicious sprinkle of sumac. This restaurant offers great value for the money, serving delicious food without pretensions.

Name: Aravan Evi
Address: Ayvalı Köyü İç Yolu, Ayvalı Köyü, Ürgüp, 50400, Türkiye
Description: Welcome to the home of the Yazgan family, which they have transformed into a boutique hotel with a restaurant. Today, the third generation is at the helm, bringing their own vision to the establishment. At the charming Aravan Evi, the kitchen garden is the primary source of produce, and diners are occasionally invited to stroll through it – it's a passion that the chefs are happy to share. Whether freshly picked, pickled or cooked in the wood-fired oven, vegetables and fruit are elevated here in remarkable ways, with an emphasis on punchy and tangy flavours. Take the dried apricots stuffed with nuts cooked in grape molasses, accompanied by a candied nut bonbon and warm halva for body. This is a captivating family story that celebrates tradition and terroir, expressed through a distinctive set menu.

Name: Mörwald Grafenegg Restaurant
Description: In the grounds of Schloss Grafenegg, this restaurant is housed in what was once the castle tavern. It comprises a series of tastefully decorated, high-ceilinged rooms with beautiful hardwood flooring, large mullioned windows, chandeliers and classical paintings as well as the rustic and cosy Schlossstube. Tables are also laid out on the lovely terrace in front of the establishment. The friendly and attentive waitstaff serve up predominantly Austrian fare made with market-fresh produce – veal shank carpaccio or Topfenstrudel (curd cheese strudel) are examples of the tempting dishes on offer.

Name: De Copain
Description: Two mates, Michael and Niels, welcome guests to their aptly named joint in the heart of Dilbeek complete with a lovely garden patio. The pair, who does everything themselves, shares a devouring passion for produce-centric cooking. They cherry-pick all the top-drawer ingredients ranging from veg from local market gardeners to fish fresh from the North Sea, crafting them in an uninhibited, complex-free manner, strewn with inventive nods, like surprising textures and vibrant fermented flavours. For example, they may cook duck whole, serving it rare with a gutsy sauce and a cream of red beetroot and raspberries. Now add an enticing wine list and on-the-ball service and you will know why it is such a hit with discerning foodies.

Name: Mariette
Description: Dad and son-in-law in the kitchen, mum and daughter in the front of house: Mariette is the quintessence of a family-run establishment. Adorned in elegant details, it also boasts a lovely patio in the garden. A Franco-Belgian lineup with the occasional international twist sets the tone of the varied menu, many dishes of which are ideal for sharing. The quality of the ingredients, like the turbot and scallops, is superlative. The juicy pheasant is fork-tender and served with lightly caramelised endives, hand-rolled fritters and a cognac sauce. A warm authentic vibe and big-boned family favourites.

Name: La Fontanella
Description: The family-run La Fontanella, which opened back in 1977, is today in the hands of the second generation. The visitor is immediately struck by the elegant warmth of the premises, depicted by artwork, soft lighting and bouquets of fresh flowers. The entire team is cheerful and good-natured, particularly when they liberally scatter shavings of white alba truffle on your taglioni alla parmigiana. In addition to reverently crafting a purebred Italian lineup (the house specialty is osso bucco), the chef enjoys adding contemporary twists, together with nods to Belgian cuisine, like pheasant à la brabançonne in autumn. Highly popular so bookings are advised.

Name: Restaurant Coquo
Description: Corentin Lonnoy, affectionately known as "Coco," has realised his childhood ambition by transforming his family abode into a delightful restaurant adorned with nostalgic photographs of Bierwart. Having honed his skills alongside Pierre Résimont, his genuine enthusiasm for high-quality ingredients shines through in his culinary creations. One standout dish features Anjou pigeon fillet complemented by intriguing accompaniments such as potato millefeuille, confit beetroot, blackberries, and a robust jus. The tempting set menu offers the perfect opportunity to savour this approachable yet refined cuisine.

Name: Flacon
Description: “Shall we get a bottle?” is something of a recurring theme when Pierre Guérin and his mates get together. This idea of a fine glass of wine in good company is the keystone of this friendly bistro, to which the chef adds uninhibited bistronomic cooking, presented in an excellent lunchtime menu and à la carte in the evening. Deftly crafted, respectful of the ingredient and spot on every time. For example, the chef might add a kick to pork, spinach and purslane in crispy puff pastry courtesy of a red wine and wholegrain mustard jus, a blend of spices and chickpeas. Rather than unnecessarily complex or fussy frills, you can expect to taste bold, reassuringly recognisable flavours.

Name: Subtiel
Description: Stéphane Buyens and Ellen Duist have left their iconic Le Fox hostelry and moved to this lovely seaside villa. The enthusiastic couple welcomes you into a warm interior which provides the perfect foil for their virtuoso skill and flair. Ellen seamlessly supervises the front of house, while Stéphane crafts a delicate classical score with a soft spot for fish and seafood. Some of their iconic signature dishes include shrimp fritters, fluffy shrimp omelette and turbot in a pastry crust. In season, the menu often features game, exemplified by textbook-perfect, fork-tender saddle of hare flanked by a big-boned pepper sauce made with fresh pepper in a subtle touch that finds favour with fans of traditional cooking. Don’t miss the lunchtime menu.

Name: Basile
Description: Basile De Wulf has set up shop in the lovely Béguines Chateau. The property’s historical stamp is reflected in the restaurant, albeit underscored by elegant design details and an eye-catching open-plan kitchen. The gourmet score is founded on the chef’s experience gleaned in top-of-the-range establishments and his own fresh youthful vision. An example: pigeon cooked whole so that the meat remains fork tender, flanked by juicy confit legs, blackberry coulis and gravy made with tripe, celery and carrots. This consummate chef constantly pushes the boundaries of his culinary skill as he rolls out a single set surprise menu that reverently respects the seasons.

Name: Amore, Pasta e Gioia
Address: Rue de la Crêche 11, Ixelles, 1050, Belgium
Description: The name of this family-run osteria rather says it all! In the company of Giuseppe and Karina in the kitchen and Kevin in the dining room, you know you are in the hands of a team you can trust. Start with an array of flavoursome antipasti, like beef carpaccio and shavings of parmesan laced in a tangy dressing, followed by a dish of house-made pasta, like al dente tagliatelle in a gutsy meat sauce. Next what about a succulent Angus rib steak alla tagliata? Each dish is packed in indulgent Italian scents and flavours and rather than fussy frills, you can expect familiar, heartwarming flavours. Go there your eyes closed!

Name: Moscou By Danny Horseele
Description: Veteran chef Danny Horseele and his team have set up shop in the Moscow district. The unstuffy luxury of this gilt-edged eatery sets a warm inviting tone. Classical cooking has no secrets for this consummate chef, who is not averse to adding the odd modern touch. The sauces (pepper, cognac and foie gras) that flank the saddle of hare demonstrate his superlative grasp of the finer points of traditional cuisine. That said, he may also marinate scallops in koji berries to accentuate their umami, adding an oriental kick with a dusting of daidai powder, dashi and a buttery sambai dressing, among others. Whether it is à la carte or a set menu, you are in a for a flavoursome feast crafted by a chef on a quest for perfection.

Name: Bloesem
Description: Venture over the threshold of this seemingly nondescript house and you will find yourself in a cheerful eatery with a few counter seats and a table that will embark on a fascinating culinary adventure. The chefs roll out a single set menu of some fifteen dishes with a strong seasonal focus, courtesy of playful, exuberant recipes. Examples include king trumpet mushrooms rolled in chicken breadcrumbs and deep-fried, served with a sabayon of fresh garden herbs. The open-minded kitchen team enjoys playing with textures and your gracious hostess will ply you with insightful suggestions (alcoholic and otherwise) to pair with the distinctive culinary lineup.

Name: Collage
Address: 2F Ananti at Gangnam, 11 Nonhyeon-ro 136-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06051, South Korea
Description: Just like the visual art technique of collage, Chef Jin-sung Noh draws upon his extensive understanding of ingredients to create dishes that balance various flavours. His refined culinary skills are richly expressed through the harmonious blend of ingredients' inherent flavours and dense sauces. By incorporating seasonal local ingredients with fermentation techniques, he gives traditional French cuisine a modern, diverse touch. Enjoy his distinctively stylish dishes in a charming dining space.

Name: Myungbodang
Description: Drawing from her experience at a top New York restaurant, Chef Hyeon-ju Lim develops a creative approach to Nu-American French cuisine. Known for her bold ingredient choices and keen sense of composition, Chef Lim delivers dishes that highlight the character of each element. The signature Truffle features a crisp shell filled with fermented mushroom and truffle cream—rich and refined. The meal concludes with a distinctive chocolate foam, offering a memorable finish.

Name: SAN
Address: B1, 6 Eonju-ro 168-gil, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, 06020, South Korea
Description: SAN blends modern cuisine with a creative flair. The flavours of seasonal ingredients are highlighted and paired with sauces to create a balance of complexity and restraint. Lobster jeotgal and chamoe dongchimi are fine examples of Chef Seong-hyun Jo's imagination. Milmyeon and dweji-gukbap deliver the robust flavours of Korean cuisine, elevated by the chef’s unique interpretation. Quiet service and thoughtful wine pairings add to the dining experience, which is further enhanced by the forest ambience of the space.

Name: Matsuzaki
Description: This intimate restaurant offers authentic kaiseki omakase by the chef who trained at a renowned culinary institute. The petite yet cosy space is decorated with fine tableware and glassware, along with paintings by the chef’s mother. The meal opens with a flavourful soup, followed by a beautifully composed hassun of seasonal bites, and concludes with a nabemono of freshly cooked rice, vegetables, and fish—Japanese cuisine that remains faithful to its fundamentals.

Name: Songheonjip
Address: 18 Millak-ro 19 beon-gil, Suyeong-gu, Busan, 48285, South Korea
Description: With successful businesses built around traditional liquor and noodle soup, the owner-chef now ventures into tteokgalbi at Songheonjip. Thick, charcoal-grilled patties are smoky and juicy, served with rice, delicate banchan, and a rich doenjang jjigae. Set in a renovated two-storey house, the restaurant evokes the cosy atmosphere of a 1990s home. Dishes are served on low tables for a homey yet hearty dining experience. Shoe-off required when entering the room.

Name: 1969 Buwondong Kalguksu
Address: 3 Gudeok-ro 22 beon-gil, Jung-gu, Busan, 48954, South Korea
Description: After several relocations, the restaurant continues to serve diners the same traditional flavours. The menu is extremely simple yet highly focused, offering only kalguksu and mandu. The kalguksu is a must-try: house-made noodles with a firm, chewy texture paired with a clear, deeply savoury broth. For spicy lovers, the bibim kalguksu captures distinctly bold and tangy Busan-style flavours. A larger portion can be requested at no extra cost.

Name: Meerok Super
Description: Meerok Super is a small six-seat restaurant that serves outsize creativity. The vegetables grown in the on-site vegetable patch, aged fish and meat, and seasonal ingredients are transformed into the day’s tasting menu. The grilled meat course, cooked over charcoal for aroma, texture, and juiciness, and served with rice, creates a seamless transition from Western to Korean flavours. Expect to be delighted by unexpected yet harmonious flavour combinations that change daily.

Name: Zandunga
Address: 41 Dongcheon-ro 108 beon-gil, Busanjin-gu, Busan, 47247, South Korea
Description: Tucked away in a quiet alley, this spot combines an industrial, chic interior with lively music for a relaxed, inviting atmosphere. Inspired by his passion for Mexican cuisine, the chef started this restaurant. Everything from tortillas to fillings and sauces is made in-house. Fresh tortillas are prepared every morning, with colourful variations crafted from different corn varieties. The pork taco is a must-try. Warm, attentive service completes the dining experience.

Name: IAán
Description: This restaurant showcases bold contemporary flavours derived from classic French and Korean cuisine. The dish names are Korean, yet the sauces and plating are distinctly French. The chef's remarkable ability to balance sauces suggests even more promising work to come. Cosy carpets and minimalist tables create an atmosphere that is warm, calm, and refined, much like the food. This is a lovely, quiet place to unwind over good food and wine.

Name: 3rd Samgyetang
Description: Now in its third generation after opening in 1973, 3rd Samgyetang is well-regarded among Seocho locals for its restorative soup. The signature samgyetang features a rich broth of over 40 ingredients, topped with mung bean and pine nut purées, and mugwort paste. The grains give the broth a satisfying body, and the meat from young chickens falls effortlessly off the bone. Spoon some glutinous rice into the broth, add a pinch of glasswort salt, and enjoy the bowl of cosy porridge. Arrive early to avoid long lines during peak hours.

Name: Cølbo
Description: Armed with an impressive CV, chef-patron Moritz Techet presents a modern, creative concept. Diners are treated to a surprise menu comprising 10 smaller or larger courses, each one technically polished and precisely executed. The dishes are pared down to the essentials and based on select, predominantly regional ingredients. The kitchen team maintain the restaurant's herb garden, forage for mushrooms and berries, and employ fermentation and preservation techniques. The emphasis is on vegetarian cuisine. The charming and dedicated waitstaff are led by Jansý Frederiksberg, assisted by the chefs, who personally elaborate on their creations. Both the wine pairing and the non-alcoholic beverages match the menu beautifully. The minimalist, clean-lined interior design is extremely chic. Places are limited and in high demand, so reservations are strongly recommended. Please note that dinner begins for all guests at 7pm.

Name: Zum Ackerbürger Can Basar
Description: This long-standing inn in Stuttgart's Bad Cannstatt district is in one of the area's oldest half-timbered buildings, dating back to the 15C. The setting is cosy and rustic, with lots of aged wood creating a charming, old-world atmosphere. The kitchen is headed by Can Basar, who previously worked at several renowned establishments. The menu includes seasonal and international cuisine alongside timeless classics – the roast beef is a favourite. In addition to an à la carte selection, there is also a four- or five-course set menu.

Name: WELA
Description: This little restaurant in the city centre promises a truly authentic Thai dining experience. Premium ingredients are precisely prepared for optimum flavour – the chef hails from Thailand and brings experience from esteemed establishments. In the evenings, guests can choose between a five- or eight-course set menu. On Wed, Thu and Sat, a shortened menu is served at lunchtime. The setting is upscale and tastefully designed, enhanced by attractive Thai decorative elements. The two very cordial proprietors provide attentive and adept service. Travel tip: The restaurant is not far from the main railway station and is well connected to public transport. Drivers can use the multi-storey car park in Stresemannstraße.

Name: OTSUKA
Description: In this tiny – perhaps even the smallest – restaurant in Berlin, authentic sushi is served in a minimalist setting as an affordably priced omakase menu. The nigiri are the highlight: crafted with excellent ingredients and impressive skill by the owner, who prepares them right before your eyes and presents them himself from behind the simple wooden counter. There are three seatings: 1pm, 5pm and 8pm. N.B. The restaurant is somewhat hidden inside a building directly at Nordbahnhof that also houses an organic supermarket.

Name: Hong
Address: Ritz-Carlton Riyadh, AlHada Area, Mekkah Road, Riyadh, 11493, Saudi Arabia
Description: Luxury, elegance and Chinese cuisine come together on the second floor of The Ritz-Carlton Hotel, Riyadh at this restaurant overlooking the hotel’s leisure club pool. The extensive menu boasts a wide range of authentic and bespoke Chinese dishes such as tasty dim sum, classic Peking duck, spicy Sichuan beef and the ever-so-loved sweet and sour prawns. Come Saturday night for a special-priced menu showcasing their dim sum selection.

Name: Tanjiah
Address: Imam Saud Bin Abdulaziz Bin Mohammed Road, King Fahd, Riyadh, 12274, Saudi Arabia
Description: Set within the King Fahd neighbourhood, not too far away from the bustling Financial District, is this Moroccan restaurant with its eye-catching décor. A feeling of warmth starts from the welcome to the interior design, and continues with the service. A sea of lampshades hang from the ceiling and authentic artefacts are strewn across a spacious room, creating an intimate setting, similar to that of a Moroccan home. The menu offers some hearty and flavoursome dishes, with the pastilla and tagine being particularly memorable.

Name: OVUN Bistro
Address: ِAlDabab Street, 4096 Prince Abdulaziz Ibn Musaid Ibn Jalawi Street, As Sulimaniyah, Riyadh, 12223, Saudi Arabia
Description: With its welcoming light décor, this popular Lebanese restaurant seems to tick quite a few boxes for the locals, who frequent the place. It’s open from breakfast to late in the evening, offering authentic, generously sized and well-priced dishes mainly focused on Lebanese cuisine, but with some influences from across the region. Sharing is always recommended by the friendly team. Opt for tasty dips, such as muhamarrah with warm breads to start, kebabs are the way to go for mains, and save room for the delicious, rich mouhalabiya milk pudding to finish.

Name: The Rubi Room at Hōchō
Address: Ground Floor, VIA Riyadh, Al Hada, Riyadh, 12912, Saudi Arabia
Description: Tucked away within Hōchō – in the luxurious VIA Riyadh shopping mall – this place is where chef Hassan's imagination runs free. The omakase-style menu has around 19 servings and is made up of dishes that will certainly intrigue you. Halal Kobe beef is at the heart of the menu, with various preparations and cuts appearing throughout. Dishes are created with numerous processes and techniques, while being playful in parts too. While the team comprehensively explain the dishes, you will still leave here with a sense of wonder at what you have just experienced.

Name: Namu
Address: The Esplanade Mall, Prince Turki Bin Abdulaziz Alawwal Street, King Saud University, Riyadh, 12371, Saudi Arabia
Description: Korean barbeque meets a fun and elevated setting. It’s on you to cook up the meat as you like on a hot plate at the centre of the table. Get yourselves a couple of starters to share before choosing your preferred cut of beef. Expect a generously portioned selection of pickles and kimchi to complement your barbeque experience. If you’re still looking to prolong your evening, make your way to the nearby bowling alley and cinema for the ultimate fun night out.

Name: Julien by Daniel Boulud
Address: Ground Floor, Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh, Kingdom Centre, Olaya Street, Al Olaya, Riyadh, 11321, Saudi Arabia
Description: Hidden inside Café Boulud, set in the Four Seasons Hotel Riyadh within the landmark Kingdom Tower, is this 12-seater counter dining restaurant. Taking the name of both acclaimed chef Daniel Boulud’s son and father, this elegant space offers a 10-course tasting menu. Modern French dishes take inspiration from iconic plates blended with local influence, which are refined and prepared in front of you. Both flavour and texture are mastered in enjoyable combinations and paired with a selection of non-alcoholic wines and mocktails. The friendly team are also on hand to keep you entertained without intruding too much. It’s a three-hour experience, but time passes quickly.

Name: Tamees House
Address: Al Amir Fawwaz Al Junoobi, Jeddah, 22431, Saudi Arabia
Description: A large cafe cum Hijazi-style restaurant located in a busy parade of shops away from the city centre. Its bright interior and even brighter team add to the delightful experience. The menu has something for everyone, from great flavoursome salads, fine beetroot tabbouleh, fresh kebabs – the chicken kebabs are noteworthy – and rich indulgent desserts. Be sure to have some Saudi coffee with dates at the start.

Name: Taleed by Michael Mina
Address: Bab Samhan Hotel, 7628 King Faisal Ibn Abd Al Aziz Road, Riyadh, 13712, Saudi Arabia
Description: Within the Bab Samhan Hotel, with its neo Najdi architecture, sits this restaurant, set over two floors. The space is split into a series of smaller rooms and terraces, which makes it feel like a home. Chef Michael Mina, who is known for restaurants in the USA, was born in Egypt and his menu here shows regional nods. Mezze-style sharing dishes are brought to the table when ready – falafel topped with tahini and tuna, and the creamy rice pudding dessert is a nod to Egypt. The use of prime ingredients is apparent, while the faultless service adds to the experience.

Name: Yokari
Address: 2nd Floor, Centria Mall, 210 Olaya Street, Al Olaya, Riyadh, 11672, Saudi Arabia
Description: Enjoy a small break from shopping at this Japanese restaurant located on Centria Mall’s second floor. Take in the relaxing atmosphere and serene modern surroundings while you wait for your food. As for the menu, you’ll have plenty of options, from classic sushi to crisp tempura, robata and yakitori grills. The dishes are best enjoyed with a few friends so you can try as many dishes as possible. Be sure to order one of their mocktails, as they are some of the best in the city.

Name: Aseeb
Address: Anas Ibn Malik Road, Alyasmin, Riyadh, 13325, Saudi Arabia
Description: It’s all about celebrating Najdi culture here. From the off, the charming team will meet you at the door and guide you upstairs to a super chic restaurant. Take your pick of formally laid table, majlis-style seating or on the floor. The traditionally dressed team offer dates and Saudi coffee before you start your meal. Classic Najdi cuisine is full of flavour; go for the chicken mubahar rice flavoured with their special spices. Should you have room for dessert, get the tasty mini cheese and honey sambosa. A word to the wise: book ahead.

Name: The Globe
Address: Mandarin Oriental, Al Faisaliah Tower, King Fahd Road, Al Olaya, Riyadh, 11491, Saudi Arabia
Description: Inside the sphere atop the iconic Al Faisaliah Tower sits this modern restaurant, which has been a culinary landmark in Riyadh since 2000. The 360˚views of the cityscape, with the Kingdom Tower in the distance, are impressive. The friendly team deliver impeccable service for a truly exceptional experience. Here, the cooking is very much rooted in the classical repertoire but also comes with a modern touch and a nod to local produce. Some noteworthy dishes include hamour in a herb crust and white beans paired with a citrus beurre blanc or the more classical navarin-styled pressed lamb shoulder.

Name: Next Door by Imperial
Description: Located directly opposite its parent establishment, Café Imperial, this restaurant boasts an elegant blend of modern and classical aesthetics. In a stylish and invitingly vibrant setting, a highly competent and well-organised team provides attentive service. To the rear of the dining space you can see the chefs crafting classic dishes in the open kitchen: braised beef with a creamy sauce and bread dumplings, or sautéed rabbit kidneys with mustard sauce – the extensive menu has something to offer every palate! Breakfast is also available, and the restaurant remains open continuously throughout the day.

Name: Dergi Praha
Description: If you want to experience authentic Georgian cuisine, this restaurant in a commercial building just a few metres from the Vltava River is the place for you. Be sure to sample the classic khinkali, available with various fillings – they are second to none! The barbecued dishes, which are also packed with flavour, come accompanied by typical sauces. The setting is wonderfully spacious and cheerful: it features decorative elements such as traditional colourful pendant lamps and patterned fabrics. Live Georgian music adds to the atmosphere.

Name: STeaK Restaurant
Description: Calling all steak lovers! The quality of the meat served here is fantastic, and the perfectly cooked premium steaks, as well as the sauces and side dishes are testament to the skill of the kitchen team. Tip: The cuts are rather large, which makes them ideal for sharing – consider booking for a small group. Adorned with rustic-looking decorative features, the decor is stylish and has an urban feel – the focal point is the open kitchen with its impressive barbecue. This place draws plenty of diners, who receive attentive service from the front-of-house team.

Name: Bockem
Description: Good food and warm hospitality await in this 1905 townhouse located near the Vltava River and Kinský Garden. The enthusiasm of the team is palpable. The cosy, somewhat shabby-chic decor and the extremely dedicated, friendly and courteous front-of-house team make for a wonderful atmosphere. The food is cooked with respect for tradition, but also with a modern twist. In the morning, everything revolves around breakfast, but in the evening, the five-course set menu takes centre stage – think mouthwatering dishes such as beef cheeks with rose hip, cranberry and truffle, or the classic Bohemian sour soup.

Name: Benjamin
Description: Ten seats are set around a horseshoe counter, chefs interact with guests, presenting carefully executed, boldly flavoured dishes, which are inspired by the Czech cuisine using only local products. The tasting experience starts at a fixed time in the evening, beginning with an introduction to the region's seasonal products staged in eight to ten courses. Wine pairings are offered to match.

Name: Sansho
Description: The atmosphere here is trendy and lively with a friendly neighbourhood vibe. You'll enjoy an Asian-inspired cuisine, served by friendly staff – the "Beef smoked red curry: homemade sausage, pastrami & braised shin, spiced potatoes & fried shallots" is a tempting option, for example. Importance is placed on regional and seasonal ingredients, organic whenever possible. You can choose dishes à la carte or go for one of the set menus, which come in classic or vegetarian options. The affordable lunch set menu is particularly enticing.

Name: Pot au Feu
Description: In his charming little restaurant, Jan Kracík serves food inspired by classic French cuisine and the culinary experiences he made during his years of travelling. Dishes such as veal sweetbreads with morels in sauce à la crème, or fillet of seabass with shallots and white wine sauce are available à la carte and as part of the "Menu Pot-au-Feu" or "Menu of the Season" (with options for each course). There are also a few daily specials. The welcoming atmosphere is enhanced by the friendly and laid-back, yet dedicated and knowledgeable front-of-house team, as well as a cosy modern decor with wine racks and art as decorative details.

Name: CottoCrudo
Description: There are many reasons to visit this restaurant in the elegant Four Seasons Hotel: the charming location by the Vltava River, the chic ambience, the beautiful large bar and the terrace overlooking the river… And, of course, the Italian cuisine with a modern twist. Dishes such as vitello tonnato, house-made pasta, fresh sea bass or duck breast show off the exquisite quality of the ingredients.

Name: Yamato
Description: This restaurant tucked away in the basement of a residential building is done out in a bright and minimalist modern style. As the name suggests, the cuisine is Japanese. In addition to classic hot dishes, there is a good selection of sushi and sashimi. To go with your food, there is sake and whisky from Japan.

Name: Aromi
Description: This attractive restaurant is accommodated in a spruce historical house. The elegant modern interior, high ceilings and large, floor-to-ceiling windows make for a pleasing, airy feel. The open kitchen in the middle turns out contemporary Italian dishes – highlights include the fish and meat cooked on the oven grill. The excellent pasta is also a tempting option. Attentive and experienced service rounds off your dining experience.

Name: Grand Cru
Description: Access to this elegant modern restaurant is via a cobbled courtyard. Inside, a warm colour scheme creates a pleasant atmosphere, and the front area features a light and airy winter garden. The classic cuisine with a Mediterranean touch is made with ingredients of the highest quality; example dishes include lobster soup or sea bass with white wine sauce. There are also different grilled dishes every day. Plus they have good wine recommendations up their sleeve.

Name: Na Spilce
Description: This restaurant stands on the premises of the Pilsner Urquell brewery. Diners are seated in a lofty vaulted cellar featuring a modern-meets-rustic decor and a striking service station in the middle of the space. Modern Czech cuisine and traditional hearty beer-hall dishes are all meticulously prepared and packed with flavour. The chefs put a premium on regional ingredients sourced from local suppliers. Of course, a good beer goes well with it. Tip: For special occasions, you can book the ‘Schalender’ in the brewery's lager cellars. Also interesting: brewery museum and shop.

Name: LEAF
Description: The restaurant is located in a residential area near the university. Behind the large windows, the decor is sleek and modern, with a raised bed of various types of cress and spices – which is integrated into the counter – providing a focal point. The food, mainly vegetarian, is served in the form of a four- or seven-course set menu. Ingredients are sourced from regional producers, with meat and fish used only sparingly. A wine flight has been devised to match the dishes. The service is friendly and professional.

Name: Malá Dvorana
Description: In a side wing of the historical Grandhotel Pupp, this restaurant is accommodated in a magnificent hall. Elaborate mouldings on the ceiling and walls and an imposing crystal chandelier are a stylish throwback to bygone days; decorated with gold leaf, the modern glass bar in the middle of the room is also noteworthy. The contemporary dishes include pan-fried mackerel, sliced beetroot, leek mousse, honey, or chicken ballotine, Jerusalem artichoke, sautéed kale, chicken demi-glace.

Name: PRIME STEAK
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: The attractive modern interior of this restaurant tucked away in a building complex may come as a surprise – the small glass dry-aging refrigerator at the entrance and the kitchen, visible through a large window, draw the eye. As the name makes clear, steak is the mainstay of this joint, but there are other appealing mains, starters and desserts. Fish and seafood are available only if ordered when you book. At lunchtime, additional – and some simpler – dishes such as goulash soup or bratwurst make for a quick and inexpensive meal. The quality of the meat and the side dishes is on point! N.B. Parking can be tricky.

Name: Amano
Description: This pleasant establishment that serves excellent cuisine is located on the edge of the old town. An interior with exposed brick and concrete walls, vintage-style furnishings and decorative wine racks creates a charming atmosphere. The open kitchen at the end of the dining area turns out modern Italian specialities. The dishes cooked on the open grill, which change every day, are highly recommended; be sure to try the pasta and risotto as well, and the all-year truffle specialities. In addition to an à la carte menu, there is a four- or seven-course set menu. A fine selection of wines is also available.

Name: Divinis
Description: In this really lovely spot, guests sit at tables laid out in several areas on different levels, surrounded by appealingly disparate furnishings. An abundance of individual details make for a charming backdrop – beautiful old floorboards, mismatched tables and chairs, original figurines, numerous books and designer lamps. The kitchen sends out refined Italian dishes that impress with their elegance and, above all, their flavour. The chef's signature dish is braised veal cheeks with Marsala, spinach and mashed potato with truffle butter. The friendly waitstaff are happy to advise you on the food and your choice of wine from the Italian-centric selection.

Name: Piano Nobile
Description: This wonderful castle estate, steeped in history and boasting superb grounds, now also accommodates not only a stylish spa hotel but also an appealing dining option. The elegant dining room boasts beautiful chandeliers, high ceilings and striking decorative porcelain displayed on shelves. When it comes to the classical French-style cuisine, choose between ambitious dishes à la carte or in the form of a tasting menu. They also serve a children's menu and event menus, eg Halloween or Christmas.

Name: Le Marché
Description: This restaurant housed in a small hotel with a handsome Classical villa façade is a popular establishment. For starters, it enjoys an attractive location on the outskirts of the town, right on the banks of the Teplá – the riverside terrace is a romantic spot in summer. The seasonal cuisine is imbued with Mediterranean influences. In the evening, you can put together a three-course meal from a choice of several dishes or order the six-course tasting menu. At lunchtime, there is a somewhat simpler three-course set menu. Service comes courtesy of a well-staffed, very friendly and competent service team. Tip: While you are here, take a look at the spa centre with its colonnades.

Name: 420 Restaurant
Description: Talk about an amazing location! Right outside the door, the centuries-old town hall with its famous astronomical clock dating back to 1410 captures everyone's attention – tables on the terrace are naturally coveted. Inside, the scene is no less arresting: This gorgeous building in the heart of the old town feels almost like a sacred space. With its soaring ceiling and period architecture, the restaurant is reminiscent of a church nave. Striking details such as a distinctive glass roof, phenomenal wall decor and sleek modern furnishings create compelling contrasts. In the open kitchen in the entrance, the chefs prepare contemporary dishes with classic foundations and influenced by regional traditions. Think pike-perch with semolina porridge, or Escoffier veal schnitzel with truffle sauce. Tip: The rustic vaulted stone cellar houses a shop selling house-made baked goods and meat products.

Name: Vallmo
Description: An exceedingly inviting atmosphere awaits you in this restaurant tucked away in a small side street in Prague's New Town. The decor features light natural tones, modern furnishings and wall art. Chef Martin Makovička serves up seasonal Czech cuisine, combining traditional and contemporary influences. He also makes a point of using locally sourced sustainable produce. In the evening, a tasting menu comprising five or eight courses is available. The sommelier recommends the perfect wine to accompany your meal - there is a beautifully curated selection. Shorter menu at lunchtime.

Name: QQ Asian Kitchen
Description: A lively establishment, where it is fun to have a meal! This is partly down to the stylish atmosphere and the adept service from the pleasingly laid-back front-of-house team, but it is first and foremost thanks to the tasty and honest Asian cuisine, prepared for you by the Asian-born chef-owner duo. They will treat you to beautifully authentic street food and soul food dishes... the task of choosing is not an easy one. Sharing is also an option if you would like to try more of a variety. Tip: The cocktails are fantastic too!

Name: Monarch
Description: The sort of steakhouse dreams are made of! The focus is, of course, on great cuts of meat – prepared to perfection. The USDA-certified dry-aged Black Angus rib eye is one nice variation on the theme, but there is also Czech steak. Onion rings are a worthy side, along with chimichurri sauce. Fish and seafood as well as pasta and risotto also feature on the menu. The whole experience is rounded off by the friendly, welcoming atmosphere and attentive service – the team is happy to advise you on your choice of steak. The wine list is also of interest.

Name: V Zátiši
Description: This modern city centre restaurant is a popular spot. Its name means ‘timeless’ and with its clever blend of modern Czech and international dishes, it looks set to stand up to its name. In the open kitchen selected products are used. You can dine à la carte or in the form of a set menu, accompanied by the matching wine.

Name: Apelace21
Description: The team here takes a highly professional approach, which is evident not least in the food. Dishes such as "St Jacob's mussels, blood orange, yuzu, crispy wafer, miso mayonnaise" and "lamb shoulder in diaphragm, Brussels sprouts, pumpkin croquette, almonds, pickled shallots" are prepared skilfully prepared with an emphasis on flavour. Easygoing yet highly competent and attentive, the service is also a highlight, including astute wine recommendations. Furthermore, the minimalist interior design, featuring decorative details such as a distinctive wine rack, artworks and modern pendant lamps makes for a truly gorgeous setting. Practical: The restaurant is located in a residential neighbourhood and is easy to reach by tram.

Name: Marie B
Description: Set in a 14C townhouse, the restaurant is accessed through a covered courtyard entrance. Behind a somewhat shabby-looking front door covered in graffiti, a minimalist and trendy interior with an urban feel awaits. Beneath a rustic old vaulted ceiling, diners sit at a counter forming a U-shape around the open kitchen, they can watch the action up close. There are also two modern light installations by Berlin artist Anselm Reyle that draw your attention. Another interesting detail is the cookery book dating back to 1894, on display behind glass – it was written by chef Marie B Svobodová, after whom the restaurant is named. Comprising four courses, the carte blanche menu features creative modern dishes rooted in Czech culinary tradition. The nicely curated wine list places the emphasis on Moravian labels. The establishment also operates Vin de Marie wine bar in the same building.

Name: Taro
Description: Since setting up shop in these new premises, brothers Giang Ta (maitre d') and Khanh Ta (chef) have been hosting diners in a trendy urban counter-restaurant. The chefs can be seen at work from the large U-shaped bar around the kitchen. A lively yet stylish atmosphere reigns, underscored by modern music. The food is heavily influenced by Vietnamese cuisine; the elegant dishes are full of flavour. A three-course set menu is available at lunchtime, and a five- or six-course format in the evening, with optional add-ons. The duck meat is dry-aged on site – you will notice it in the fridge behind the bar.

Name: Chapelle
Description: With its chic design, clean lines, light wood and palette of natural hues, this restaurant is blessed with good looks. If you are lucky, you will be seated at a table with a front-row view of the chefs preparing the dishes in the open kitchen. The modern cuisine has international and Czech influences. Attentive and cordial service. Hotel U Kapličky located in the same building has attractive guestrooms for an overnight stay.

Name: ARRIGŌ
Description: There's plenty to like here: The trendy concept not only covers lunch and dinner, but also breakfast, plus it has a café with pastries and delicatessen items. The space is modern and exudes a bistro flair; the open kitchen, in which seasonal dishes and smaller plates are rustled up, tends to draw the eye. The game dishes and the items cooked on the Josper grill, for example, are interesting options. Reasonably priced lunch.

Name: Babiččina zahrada
Description: This restaurant in a quiet suburb of Prague has bags of charm. The interior is done out in a country-house style complete with lovingly chosen decorations. Outside, the terrace laid out in a gorgeous garden is inviting. The kitchen, which can be seen from the front section of the dining area, serves seasonal, regional and traditional dishes; a favourite is the beef broth with liver dumplings, vegetables and noodles, which is served in a pot to scoop yourself. And the steak tartare is prepared at your table. Friendly service. The hotel has cosy, attractive guestrooms, and the charging station for electric vehicles is a handy amenity. By the way, the name of the restaurant means "grandma's garden".

Name: Grandrestaurant Pupp
Description: What could be better suited to this time-honoured setting than classic Czech cuisine? The lavish restaurant of the venerable Grand Hotel Pupp is housed in a magnificent space boasting high ceilings, an abundance of mouldings and stylish details such as fine chandeliers and mirrors, elegant fabrics and heavy curtains, all exuding a sense of history. An adept front-of-house team serves classically rooted cuisine with Czech and international influences. Both a set menu and à la carte options are available.

Name: Borgo Agnese
Description: You'll feel as if you've been whisked away to the Mediterranean! The menu features tempting dishes such as "shrimp confit, potato, saffron aioli, radish", "gnocchi, mushrooms, pine nuts, beetroot, goat cheese, herbs" or "boar, cream, cranberries, semolina". Simply order à la carte, or opt for one of the tasting menus compiled from the same options. The delicious food can be accompanied by something from the extensive wine list, which features European labels, including some big names. Furthermore, diners enjoy attentive and adept service in a bright and classically elegant setting – a unique detail of the decor is the excavated historical church wall, protected by glass.

Name: V Bezovém Údolí
Description: This handsome 17C half-timbered house in a picturesque village stands out for its unique architecture – it is one of the few remaining buildings of its kind in the Czech Republic. The attractive interior is minimalist in style and features a rustic wooden ceiling and a distinctive brick floor. Only regional, sustainably sourced ingredients are used in the kitchen, and the menu is intentionally concise. Dishes such as beef tartare with wild garlic mayonnaise, pickled shallot and herbs are refreshingly simple. Many components are produced in-house, including jus, oils, jams and compotes; the team also do their own fermenting and pickling. For overnight stays, there are five modern minimalist-style guestrooms and an apartment, all in a separate timber building.

Name: La Finestra in Cucina
Description: Set in Prague's Old Town, this is a great establishment for top-notch Italian food. Made with select ingredients and clear craftsmanship, dishes such as calamari fritti, brasato al Barolo or spaghetti alla carbonara are sure to impress. Also of note is the fine selection of aged meats cooked on the grill. The tasteful decor teamed with red-brick vaulted ceilings is also inviting – and you can see into the kitchen through a window.

Name: Café Imperial
Description: A truly magnificent setting! The restaurant of the Art Deco Imperial Hotel, a time-honoured establishment, occupies a stylish high-ceilinged room in which gorgeous historical ceramic detailing on the ceiling, walls and striking columns draws the eye. The atmosphere is lively without being hectic, and the service is well organised and professional. Featured on the classic-leaning menu is a good selection of dishes, including Czech favourites. As the place is worth seeing and attracts many guests, it's wise to book! Also open for breakfast, brunch, coffee and cake.

Name: Portfolio
Description: Laid out over two floors of a charming historical townhouse, this restaurant is a popular spot that exudes modern chic. Clean lines, high-quality materials and warm hues create a tasteful setting. The inviting atmosphere is also enhanced by the friendly, attentive and well-trained service team. The internationally influenced menu whets the appetite with dishes such as duck breast, pumpkin with ginger, apple-rhubarb chutney and duck jus with red Kampot pepper, or dishes made from US prime beef. Good selection of wines.

Name: SAVOYA
Description: The combination of a chic, modern vibe and modern regional cuisine with international influences is nothing if not inviting. The tasting menu gives you the best overview of the appealing range of dishes. The à la carte selection meanwhile has further options in store – and children are also catered for. The wine list includes well-known vineyards and names from the Old World, as well as a fine selection of champagnes. The restaurant is located in the Hotel Savoy, which is affiliated with the neighbouring Hotel Soyka.

Name: Kohout NA VÍNĚ
Address: Dům umění města Brna, Malinovského nám. 652/2, Brno, 60200, Czechia
Description: This charming modern restaurant on the premises of the House of Arts is a cosy setting. The names of artists who, through donations, have contributed to the upkeep of the establishment are displayed on the ceiling. Wine plays an important role here, as the eye-catching floor-to-ceiling wine store suggests. As well as two tasting menus and a vegetarian set menu, there is an à la carte selection. The terrific wine list focuses on the Czech Republic, Slovenia and Hungary. They also use the Coravin wine system. Tip: Be sure to reserve, especially on weekends – they get fully booked quickly.

Name: Mlýnec
Description: This restaurant enjoys a stunning location by the Vltava River in the heart of the city, right next to Charles Bridge. The chic and modern interior has floor-to-ceiling windows opening out onto a balcony terrace directly overlooking the bridge – you can also appreciate the view from some of the tables inside. In the open kitchen, the chefs create contemporary dishes, drawing on traditional Czech and international influences. Order à la carte, or opt for one of the set menus ("The Most Popular", "Tartare & Steak" or "Vegetarian"). There is also a lunch deal, and brunch is available on Sat and Sun. Attentive service comes courtesy of a friendly and adept front-of-house team.

Name: Pavillon Steak House
Description: This restaurant boasts a gorgeous location in a small park near the centre. Sleek and chic design, high ceilings and large windows make for an airy atmosphere. As the name suggests, the focus here is on meat and different steaks. You choose the size and how you would like it cooked – the kitchen takes care of the rest. There is a variety of side dishes and sauces to accompany the meat.

Name: Parzival
Description: After years at Prism in Berlin, Gal Ben Moshe is rising to a new challenge in Prague, bringing his Levantine-inspired cuisine to the elegant restaurant of boutique hotel Bookquet. A six-course set menu has been created under his direction – it is influenced by his Israeli homeland, but Asian influences can be detected, too. The wine pairings are also of interest. Almost all of the wines on the short menu are available by the glass. Enjoy an aperitif in the chic lounge in the hotel's lobby.

Name: Antricote Steakhouse
Description: Just a short walk from the Vltava in Prague's Old Town, this is the place for steak lovers. The decor is trendy and urban with an industrial edge. In the open kitchen, the focal point is the wood-fired grill on which premium cuts of meat are cooked to perfection. These are accompanied by an array of side dishes and sauces. To kick off, there is also a tempting selection of appetisers. Tip for motorists: Old Town Parking is convenient.

Name: La Veranda
Description: In this restaurant with the flair of an Italian country house and decorative shelves full of cookbooks, small tables make for a friendly, elegant ambience. The modern european cuisine is served à la carte or as a set menu. The front-of-house team provides attentive, competent service, and there is a good selection of wines to choose from.

Name: Sůl a Řepa
Description: Once you have located the slightly hidden entrance, you find yourself in a world of fermentation, pickling and preserving – countless jars of various vegetables, mushrooms and the like are everywhere you look. The restaurant is pleasingly pared back, and some tables afford an interesting view over the pass into the kitchen. They source all ingredients from the region and, wherever possible, process these themselves. You can clearly see their sustainability concept in action here. The menu is seasonal, and the friendly waitstaff are happy to advise you as you choose.

Name: Cattaleya
Description: This villa in a somewhat secluded location in the mountains is home to a small hotel with seven rooms, a spa and a terrific outdoor event area – and this elegant modern restaurant. In the beautiful light and airy glass pavilion with a round floor plan, ambitious contemporary dishes are served à la carte or as a seven-course set menu, with wine pairing on request.

Name: Tlustá Kachna
Description: This inviting restaurant is located directly on the market square next to the small church. The two inviting dining rooms are done out in white with light wood furnishings and lovely cross-vaulted ceilings. There are also a few tables on the terrace in front of the building. The menu features flavoursome home-style regional fare such as braised rabbit leg with red cabbage and dumplings. Attentive service. The reasonably priced lunch deals are especially popular – reservations are recommended. In the evening, the cuisine is a little more upscale. Tip: Factor in enough time for a stroll through the pretty old town.

Name: STŮL
Description: A little outside the city centre, surrounded by greenery, this restaurant is located right next to its sister establishment, U Matěje. There are just a handful of tables in the modern yet rustic dining space, all with a direct view of the open kitchen. Here, the young team of chefs creates an ambitious 5- or 10-course suprise menu. Attentive service comes courtesy of charming waitstaff. Tip for motorists: You can park in front of the building – using a parking app is recommended.

Name: U Štěpána
Description: This small restaurant may be a little off the beaten track, but it's well worth coming here for the regional cuisine. Quality ingredients are skilfully prepared to impart plenty of flavour. The restaurant rears its own cattle, hence the focus on beef – delicious dishes include beef tongue with celeriac purée and horseradish foam, or beef ribs with coleslaw and bread. The interior has a charmingly rustic quality; in summer, dine out on the terrace, which is surrounded by greenery. Should you wish to soak up this rural idyll a little longer, there is also a campsite.

Name: Coda
Description: Classic elegance is the name of the game here. The restaurant is located in the hall of the Aria Hotel Prague – herringbone floorboards, chandeliers and interesting objets d'art contribute to the stylish atmosphere. With its magnificent view over Prague, the roof terrace is a huge draw in summer! The restaurant serves refined Czech cuisine, a signature dish being their kulajda – a mushroom soup with a poached egg.

Name: Salabka
Description: On the outskirts of the city, this restaurant is located in a vineyard with a wine-growing tradition dating back to the 13C. A combination of exposed old wooden beams, quarry stone walls and sleek modern furnishings creates an atmospheric setting. The view of the vines is best enjoyed from the tables at the windows on the first floor, which is actually a gallery constructed under the open gable roof. In summer, tables on the terrace are coveted. Meticulously prepared with great technical precision, the dishes are visually stunning and often feature produce from trusted farmers. Tip: Book a wine tasting or tour of the estate. For overnight stays there are six cosy, tastefully furnished apartments.

Name: ELEMENT
Description: Lively and very much on trend, this restaurant enjoys a very central location in the city. Beyond the bar by the entrance (ideal for a cocktail), the dining space has an urban, industrial feel and features an open kitchen. The modern dishes created here – such as "grilled pork belly, ginger spinach, fermented black bean sauce" and "zander filet, confit leek, bean purée, parsley, Jerusalem artichoke" – are visually appealing and impress with their quality and bold flavours.

Name: Soyka
Description: With its unpretentious feel, trendy modern-bistro style tweaked with a rustic touch, and pleasingly friendly service, this restaurant ticks all the boxes. And, last but not least, there is the regional, seasonal cuisine, in the form of a small but perfectly formed à la carte selection, including specialities from the Josper grill. Located in the hotel of the same name, this is the sister hotel of the Savoy right next door.

Name: S5 by Angie
Description: Marked only by a discreet green sign by the main door to a residential building in northern Belgrade, you might miss this establishment if you don’t keep a sharp lookout. On the first floor you’ll find two dining rooms and a vintage-style lounge that is ideal to start the evening over an aperitif while a turntable plays vinyl records. Youthful chef Anđela ‘Angie’ Risimić, not yet thirty, is back in Serbia after learning the ropes across Europe and has taken over the restaurant where she worked prior to embarking on her globetrotting tour. She puts her international training, especially what she learned in Italy, to excellent use, crafting a menu that seamlessly slaloms between crisp Italian flavours, such as rabbit-filled ravioli with mushroom sauce or tiramisu, and pedigree Serbian dishes. Our inspector was particularly impressed by the zander, served over a freshwater fish soup seasoned with peppers and finished with a delicate cauliflower cream.

Name: SkyLounge
Description: On the eighth floor of the Hilton Hotel, the stylish dining room, enhanced by soft lighting and music, perfectly embodies the plush, international vibe one expects from such an establishment. The culinary score demonstrates a similar global leaning with Asian-inspired dishes such as Tom Yum soup, Gyoza dumplings, and a wide range of nigiri, sashimi and maki rolls. Simpler and occasionally Mediterranean recipes, both meat and fish, are presented tableside from a trolley, along with crab, lobster and a selection of fresh salads.

Name: Homa
Description: It may be located in the historic Dorćol quarter, but Homa sports a thoroughly modern look and feel. Take a seat on the leafy terrace during the day or in the softly lit restaurant come nightfall to enjoy creative cooking with subtle Italian accents with a choice of two tasting menus and an à la carte lineup of vegetarian, fish and meat dishes. The tables are beautifully laid with white linen tablecloths, while the pleasant alfresco space is just the ticket for candlelit dining in summer.

Name: Legat 1903
Description: This highly recommended restaurant, though located outside the city centre, is well worth the trip. The sleek, stylish interior and polished service set the scene for one of Belgrade’s foremost fine dining experiences. The repertory features meat and fish, crafted into sensibly creative recipes and each dish stands out by balanced, crisp, legible flavours. While the must-tries are shoulder of lamb and meat dishes, excellent Adriatic and freshwater fish, as well as pasta and risotto also figure on the menu.

Name: Gušti mora
Description: This is the place for anyone who appreciates fish crafted simply and with respect for tradition, allowing the freshness and quality of the ingredients, the true stars of each dish, to shout their name. In addition to the menu, ask the staff about the catch of the day. Fans of Italian cuisine will also find risottos and spaghetti among the lineup. Located just outside the city centre, the restaurant boasts welcoming dining rooms with a rustic slant that add to its warm, authentic vibe.

Name: The Square
Description: Just behind the bustling Knez Mihaliva shopping street, this restaurant takes its name from the Square Nine Hotel, one of the capital’s most exclusive hotels, in which it is housed. Located on the ground floor, soft lighting paints the sleek, stylish portrait in the evenings, while a pleasant garden piazzetta is perfect for alfresco dining. The à la carte lineup unveils a contemporary score with a weakness for modern Serbian specialties. The knockout wine list is flanked by one of the city’s best cocktail menus, served in The Lobby Bar.

Name: Restoran 27
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In a quiet residential neighbourhood, on the outskirts of Belgrade, rather than flashy signs, just look for number 27, which is both the address and the restaurant’s name, so it’s not too hard to find. A classical, stylish decor complete with a fireplace sets the stage for the spot-on front-of-house team to do their stuff, courtesy of seamless, authentic service and infectious good humour. The owner, who is talkative yet also an attentive listener and one of the city’s most beloved hosts, has a genuine knack for understanding his diners and guiding their choices. The kitchen never fails to deliver the goods, including premium meat sourced mainly from Serbian farms, as well as Mediterranean fish that comes from Montenegro, Albania and occasionally Croatia. The culinary score of international inspiration and scattered with personal touches, is deftly crafted and often reveals a fondness for the Mediterranean, including fresh house-made pasta. Equally deserving of praise, the wine cellar boasts some 150 labels and reflects not just scope but genuine passion in the selection. In the establishment’s own words, “…irreparably in love with its guests”, aptly captures the feel-good vibe and ethos of 27.

Name: Puter
Description: This sleek, modern bistro stands just opposite the lively Kalenić market. The interior may be compact, but its trendy design and seamless bar service lend the place a bustling, playful vibe (booking ahead is recommended if you want to be sure of a table). True to bistro traditions, the menu is simple and classical as it balances purebred Serbian recipes - the horseradish-leaf rolls filled with ham hock are excellent, as is the slow-braised lamb with roasted eggplant, kaymak fondue and bay leaf oil, with French accents, such as foie gras, snails and Camargue rice, which occasionally even make their way onto the playlist. The wine list follows the same binational theme and stars mostly Serbian and French vintages.

Name: Prime
Description: Located on the ground floor of the Crowne Plaza and with its own private entrance, this restaurant is a favourite with fans of Mediterranean, particularly Italian cuisine, with a distinct preference for meat main courses, although an entire section of the menu is devoted to pasta, risotto and gnocchi. The exquisite desserts, which unveil a subtle French slant and artful plating, are definitely worth writing home about!

Name: Pinòt
Description: This contemporary-looking bistro is located in Novi Beograd, the modern business and shopping district across the Sava River from Belgrade’s city centre. The menu shines the spotlight on seasonal produce and changes throughout the year depending on market availability. In addition to a concise lineup of daily specials announced at your table, you can order a tasting menu flanked by an insightful wine pairing options (one of the owners, youthful Vuk Vuletić, is an award-winning sommelier).

Name: Salon 1905
Description: Located on the first floor of the grandiose 19C Geozavod edifice, this opulent, aristocratic restaurant occupies one of Belgrade’s most eye-catching, iconic landmarks, whose marble, stucco, brass and gilt decor creates a glitzy special occasion vibe. In this sumptuous setting, the young chef crafts a high-flying culinary repertory, depicted by consummate execution and exquisite plating. The goal is to highlight top-drawer Serbian produce and thoroughbred recipes, all of which viewed through a contemporary lens. There is no à la carte menu; instead, guests are invited to enjoy a surprise tasting menu, with the only choice being the number of courses.

Name: The Twenty Two
Description: Located on the rooftop of the Metropol Palace Hotel, this restaurant offers jaw-dropping views of the city skyline and St. Mark’s Church, along with delicious cocktails and gourmet international cuisine. Take your pick from the excellent steaks, (highly recommended), washed down by a choice of Serbian or international wines. It is just the ticket for an aperitif or a late-night drink with its soft background music.

Name: Klub Književnika by Branko Kisic
Description: The youthful chef of this culinary and cultural landmark, popular with the locals and tourists alike, has been at the helm since 2019. Diners can choose to eat in a winter garden or in the dining room, often accompanied by live music during the colder months. The menu showcases a patriotic Serbian lineup, including the Krempita dessert that has been served here since the restaurant opened in 1946, and other Serbian specialties (there’s a 25-minute wait for the savoury Gibanica dish), with the occasional interesting, personalised touch and a focus on plating. Since it opened at the end of the Second World War, the ‘Writers’ Club’ has been a magnet for authors, journalists and politicians and it continues to host cultural events, including exhibitions and concerts. Sustainability issues, such as reducing food waste, are at the core of the ethos of this quintessentially traditional establishment.

Name: Na Ćošku
Description: Situated to the east of the city just outside the historic centre, a romantic tone sets the scene in this restaurant, which is something of a surprise when compared to its exterior. The dining room boasts all the trappings of a French bistro with small tables, background music (often French) and a few cubby-holes that are perfect for couples. Deeply rooted in Balkan traditions, the menu rolls out wholesome soups and stews, such as lamb in white wine served with mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables, a lineup of fresh pasta dishes and vegetarian options like vegan curry with chickpeas, sweet potatoes and green beans.

Name: Mezestoran Dvorište
Description: The bright decor and colourful tableware of this restaurant reflect its happy-go-lucky, joyful Mediterranean spirit, as does the tempting culinary score, which includes chickpea fritters, tzatziki, different kinds of olives, typical ‘Dokos’ from Crete (imaginatively flavoured croutons), as well as chicken and pork gyros. A pleasant, informal setting in which to enjoy traditional Greek cuisine, flanked by an alfresco patio area in a refreshingly shady courtyard that further adds to its appeal and makes it very popular with locals.

Name: Magellan
