Description: Located in Novi Beograd, the modern part of the capital, the dining room of this restaurant is dominated by a striking aquarium. The veteran local-born chef is backed up by a slick, spot-on front-of-house team. Both the tasting menu and the extensive à la carte selection showcase original recipes and internationally inspired dishes with a zest of Italian flair (including pasta and risotto), complemented by cherry-picked Serbian produce. In keeping with the restaurant’s namesake, the chef takes guests on an adventurous gourmet journey full of surprises and exceptional quality.

Name: L'Adresse
Description: Housed in the swish Saint Ten boutique hotel not far from San Sava church in the Vračar district, the dining room, appointed in a contemporary vein, lies just past the welcoming open-plan hotel lobby-cum-lounge. European-influenced cuisine takes front stage here, with a weakness for meat (try the Hoisin duck or the Saint Ten beef fillet - the latter is the house signature), although the menu also features a few fish dishes, including tuna fillet and grilled or steamed salmon. Vegetarians will enjoy the kale rolls. The plush, cosy Lounge Bar is perfect for a relaxing aperitif or after-dinner drink.

Name: Ebisu
Description: As soon as you exit the lift on the seventh floor of the Square Nine Hotel, you will find yourself in this swish, yet snug restaurant (named after the Japanese goddess of Fortune). You can choose between a bar stool, the sleek glazed interior or the rooftop terrace that commands jaw-dropping views of the historic city. The score is 100% Japanese, including sushi, sashimi, maki (the tuna maki with jalapeno pepper is particularly delicious), tempura (soft-shell crab served with wasabi mayonnaise and pickled ginger), teppanyaki, at least one ramen, and much more besides. The desserts, on the other hand, are modern European in style. The adjacent bar also offers a menu of saketini-inspired cocktails.

Name: Comunale Caffè e Cucina
Description: When the sun shines, head for this knockout riverside spot in the shadow of Belgrade Fortress. It is one of several whitewashed former customs warehouses flanked by waterside terraces, but this one is owned by an architect, hence the sleek, stylish decor. The score is purebred Italian, starring traditional recipes such as tagliatelle al ragù, bruschetta, tiramisu and a scattering of pizzas. Impressive choice of liqueurs and spirits, in particular gin, and a fine selection of cocktails and mocktails.

Name: Suvenir
Address: Novi Beograd Blok 44, Gandijeva BB, Beograd , Serbia, Belgrade, 11070, Serbia
Description: Picture a floating house, idyllically located on the River Sava and framed by lush green banks, which are perfect for a stroll before your meal. The roomy interior features a refined, yet snug inviting vibe, setting the scene for a memorable dining experience. The kitchen rises to the occasion with an extensive lineup of traditional dishes that showcase the quality of the meat, complemented by excellent seafood and freshwater fish options.

Name: Schwarzfischer
Description: This restaurant enjoys a gorgeous location in a modern cuboid building by the monastery pond – the terrace affords stunning views of the surroundings. Inside, you can peek into the kitchen and watch freshly caught fish being grilled over an open charcoal flame. Specialities such as char tartare, teriyaki‑glazed fillet of stick‑grilled fish, or "milkmaid-style" trout all feature fish from the restaurant's own on-site fish farm – talk about local sourcing! The extensive à la carte selection caters not just to fish enthusiasts but also features vegetarian options and meat dishes. Cap off your meal with house-made Tyrolean milk soft ice cream. Tip: Located on the Inn River cycle route, this place is the perfect spot for a mid-ride pit stop.

Name: Zur goldenen Birn
Description: In this restaurant of the historic Parkhotel – first documented as an inn in 1574 – you are taken on a "culinary journey back in time" to the days of the Habsburgs. Anecdotes and old recipes from that period provide the inspiration for cuisine reimagined and served in the form of charmingly plated dishes full of nuances and intense flavours. Guided by the seasons, this is food with classic foundations and an imaginative modern twist. The single set menu of eight or four courses features creations such as "duck, blueberry, mulberry, red oxalis, red cabbage" or "red mullet, oyster, Osietra caviar, Arctic char roe". "Pea, pearl barley, koji, Parmesan" also captivates with its exciting aromatics and distinctive character. Attentive and adept service comes courtesy of a dedicated team, with the chefs personally presenting their work. The tasteful and upscale decor sees historical charm seamlessly fused with contemporary design.

Name: Hermann's Jagdstube
Description: The exclusive little restaurant in the luxe chalet hotel Bergwiesenglück promises a very special culinary experience. If you pre-order it, they serve a game-based set menu, comprising eight small courses made using meat solely from animals hunted by the chef himself – the unusual dishes include, for example, black grouse liver, chamois brain, deer bone marrow or deer tongue. The wine list includes regional and international classics. Optionally you can order the wine pairings devised to accompany the set menu. The friendly and laid-back service is infused with a personal touch. Warm wood and clean lines make for a chic and modern Alpine interior. There are just four tables. A floor-to-ceiling glass façade affords a view of the terrace and the mountains.

Name: TIAN Bistro am Spittelberg
Description: Like its MICHELIN-starred sister restaurant, this bistro serves excellent vegetarian/vegan food, with a commitment to a responsible, seasonal and local concept, as well as an emphasis on organic and Demeter-certified produce. Creations such as "TIAN Tatar, Joseph Bread", "Kohrabi, Elderflower, Pea" and "Risotto, Chanterelles, Fennel" stand out on account of their select regional ingredients and have all the qualities of signature dishes. Designed for sharing, the set menu is very reasonably priced. The location is in the heart of the lively Spittelberg neighbourhood, which is teeming with places to eat and drink. Inside, the atmosphere is vibrant, and the minimalist, clean-lined interior reflects a deep-rooted affinity with nature. Gorgeous covered courtyard.

Name: Der Schützenwirt
Address: Schützenweg 3, Sankt Jakob am Thurn, 5412, Austria
Description: In 2020, following stints at top-flight establishments, Andrea and Robert Rübsam fulfilled their dream of opening their own restaurant, which is located in a picturesque and tranquil spot some 20min south of Salzburg. Their culinary approach is grounded in seasonality and local sourcing, with 25 regional producers supplying fresh top-notch ingredients. The dishes reflect Austrian tradition, elevated with imaginative twists and influences from around the globe. The menu is written up on a board, featuring options such as "Gazpacho andaluz, bell pepper, jalapeño, croutons", "Pickled trout, cucumber, sour cream, rapeseed" or "Braised beef roulade, mashed potato, kohlrabi". The outdoor garden is a particular source of pride – arguably one of the loveliest in the Salzburg area. Warm, attentive and professional service, led by the proprietress, is the icing on the cake.

Name: RAR Fine Dining
Description: Following stints at renowned establishments (including Bobby Bräuer's ‘EssZimmer’ at BMW Welt in Munich), Maximilian Reuter has found the ideal setting to pursue his ambitions as chef at the fine dining restaurant of die HOCHKÖNIGIN hotel. His culinary vision comes to life in his two set menus: "Asian Alpin" and the entirely vegan "Asian Green" – both available in five or seven courses. Combining Alpine tradition with Asian flavours, the dishes are made using a wide range of regional ingredients, including herbs from their kitchen garden and organic beef from its own farm. The kitchen team present each course themselves, which brings a personal touch and makes your dining experience even more special. Another draw is the intimate atmosphere – the cosy little space with its vaulted ceiling and upscale furnishings accommodates only a few diners, who enjoy dedicated and attentive service. The alcohol-free drink pairings created by the bartender are also excellent. The petits fours are a unique touch – there are a few surprises in store!

Name: Chef's Table by Gesser
Description: A wonderful family-run restaurant, now with two dedicated brothers from the next generation at the helm. Clemens Gesser is in charge of the kitchen and serves up ambitious regional cuisine made exclusively with ingredients sourced from the surrounding area. A surprise menu is the sole proposal – diners can choose to have between four and seven courses. Meticulously crafted dishes such as smoked salmon trout tartare with buttermilk and herb oil, or flavoursome pumpkin ravioli with milk foam showcase the chef's skill. Up to eight diners share one large table positioned right next to the kitchen and are served by a friendly, highly competent team led by Markus Gesser. The restaurant is part of the family's small hotel, which caters to holidaymakers with its well-kept guestrooms and excellent half-board accommodation.

Name: La Vallée - Das Bistro im Casino
Description: In the casino building in the centre of Riezlern, a seasoned duo bring dedication to the table. Charming and competent restaurant manager Lillian Rot looks after diners; meanwhile chef-patron Sascha Kemmerer (known from Kilian Stuba in A-ROSA Ifen Hotel Kleinwalsertal in Hirschegg) is in charge of the kitchen. His dishes draw on French classics and impress with their craftsmanship, flavour and the quality of the ingredients underpinning them. The atmosphere is inviting and friendly: modern bistro style, Alpine details from bygone days, such as tiled stoves and wood-panelled ceilings, and "Culinary Timepieces" – limited edition prints by Annette Sandner – form a beautiful impression. There is also a bar and terrace. Tip: Why not visit the casino before or after your meal?

Name: Wirtshaus im Dorfhotel Mayer
Address: Sankt Martin am Grimming 9-12, Sankt Martin am Grimming, 8954, Austria
Description: This place has kept it in the family since 1854. Now the seventh generation, embodied by daughter Lisa Mayer, is at the helm. This certified sommelier takes care of matters front of house; behind the scenes, her husband Stefan Ell-Mayer is responsible for the food. He cooks up a seasonal à la carte selection, which changes every two to three weeks. Without overwhelming diners with choice, it still promises something for everyone, from traditional beef soup or beef tartare to coq au vin with Zehentmoarhof Riesling, young vegetables, Brandteigkrapferl (traditional Austrian pastries), or golden trout, buttermilk, beurre blanc, cauliflower, pistachio, saffron. Those who prefer something a little more modern and creative could take a punt on the four- to six-course surprise menu. They also offer well-kept, individually designed guestrooms.

Name: Strasserwirt Gourmetstuben
Description: A true home from home! The restaurant is housed in Hotel Strasserwirt, whose history – dating back to 1399 – in no small way contributes to the wonderful atmosphere. The dining area is divided into three charming "parlours", which could hardly be more different in their individual designs and tasteful details: Swiss stone pine panelling and sacred art (Blaue Ofenstube), handmade emerald-green floor tiles and ceramic stove (Ambrosiusstube) and exposed walls combined with spruce furnishings finished with white soap (Stube1399). The set menu, comprising up to five courses, features delicious dishes made with select regional ingredients – think marinated char, pickled chanterelles, spruce pesto, marigold mousse and ginger dumplings with apple chutney.

Name: Gasthof Rössle
Description: Currently at the helm of this restaurant, once an inn (dating back to 1775), is Valentin Bargehr, the third generation of the family. On the first floor of this building next to the parish church, Pfarrkirche St Nikolaus, diners are welcomed in a number of inviting dining spaces (some wood-panelled), or outside on the pretty terrace shaded by trees. The menu features delicious regional cuisine made from seasonal, almost exclusively local ingredients. In addition to à la carte dishes such as "Rössle fish soup" or roast chicken, mixed salad, lingonberries, parsley potatoes, there is also a choice of two lovely three-course set menus, one of which is vegetarian. These include mouthwatering veal cheeks, chanterelles and noodles or pumpkin capuns and grilled vegetables, respectively. While Valentin Bargehr takes care of things in the kitchen, his brother Martin provides charming service. Don't forget to book at this very popular place. Tip: They have cosy contemporary guestrooms for overnight guests.

Name: Kirchenwirt
Description: The new project by Barbara Eselböck and Alain Weissgerber is not far from their other restaurant, Taubenkobel. The traditional character of this long-established inn has been deliberately preserved – the food being no exception. The handwritten menu includes dishes such as Tafelspitz, goulash and cordon bleu, not to mention the fantastic apricot dumplings! Although down-to-earth, the dishes impress with the high standards in terms of quality and craftsmanship ensured by Karlheinz Ruttmann. Previously chef at Freisinger Hof in Munich, he is a long-time friend of Alain Weissgerber and they worked together at the restaurant Steirereck. The location on the cobblestoned main square, flanked by a church on each side, is also appealing. A spot on the terrace is highly sought after in summer. You may not always be lucky enough to get a table on the spur of the moment, so it's best to book.

Name: Collina am Berg
Description: This charming and trendy restaurant is located in the heart of Vienna's vibrant Spittelberg neighbourhood, known for its bars, restaurants and shops. The centrepiece is the large counter and open kitchen, where unfussy seasonal dishes are prepared. The ingredients are exclusively Austrian, mostly organic goods sourced from trusted suppliers. The house speciality is game, which the chefs also hunt themselves. Dishes include venison carpaccio with pickled celeriac and celeriac mayonnaise, and game schnitzel with potato salad and lemon. The exceptionally friendly and attentive team serves either a five-course tasting menu or individual dishes à la carte. During summer, the rain-protected pergola, with its open front of windows, provides a terrace-like setting. N.B. Parking in the immediate vicinity is difficult, but the nearest underground station, Volkstheater, is only a few minutes' walk away.

Name: Restaurant am Hochfuchs
Description: "Traditional – innovative – down-to-earth – modern" is the motto of Margit and Michael Oberreiter. It is also an apt description of the modern-inspired Austrian and regional fare served here, which ranges from Backhendl (breaded fried chicken) with potato and cucumber salad and lingonberries to sheatfish fillet with lardo, chamomile butter broth, blini and wild broccoli. The four-course "Michaels Menü" comes highly recommended, but the extensive à la carte selection of traditional dishes and tavern classics is also tempting. And on Sundays and public holidays diners can tuck into Sunday roast – oven-fresh roast pork with bread dumplings and cabbage salad. The wine list boasts a solid selection of Austrian labels. Friendly and attentive service is provided in an attractive space that blends modern design and regional charm, featuring clean lines and warm wood. And from this altitude, you have a magnificent panoramic view over the Flachgau region. In summer, the tranquil terrace beckons. Tip: They have well-kept, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Teppanyaki WAJO
Address: 12F, The St. Regis Osaka, 3-6-12 Hommachi, Chuo-ku, Osaka, 541-0053, Japan
Description: This is teppanyaki mixed with the essence of French cuisine and refined. Appetisers showcase modern creations, prepared with seasonal mood in mind. A double sauce of soy sauce and red wine transforms wagyu steak into an evolution of flavour. Overseeing the kitchen is Ryuta Izuka, the chef back when Joël Robuchon introduced teppanyaki dishes here. Enjoy the action in the kitchen, the sounds, the aromas, and the conversation.

Name: Hachi
Description: The proprietor of this refined, modern sukiya-style structure displays a unique approach while honouring tradition. The wanmono broth draws in the sweetness of kombu and the sharpness of shaved bonito. Sashimi showcases the chef’s disciplined knife technique. Generous amounts of seasonal ingredients are grilled over bincho charcoal. Even the handmade soba imparts a sense of season. ‘Omogashi’, the main sweet served in the tea ceremony, and usucha draw the meal to a close. Service is in the spirit of the tea ceremony.

Name: Wagyuchugokusai Kumanohanare
Description: In this Chinese restaurant, Japan’s famous wagyu beef is the star. ‘Wagyu Chugoku-sai’ means ‘Chinese cuisine made with wagyu’, and the restaurant has created unique prix fixe offerings with that theme. The chef, who has studied Japanese cuisine, draws on extensive experience to challenge tradition. Ingredients at their peak are woven into the menu to capture a sense of each season. Char-grilled chateaubriand is wrapped in Peking duck pancakes. Building on Chinese techniques, the cuisine weaves Japanese and Western influences to create its own new and unique style of Chinese cooking.

Name: Sushi Shigenaga
Description: The sign’s calligraphy was done by the proprietor himself. Sake vessels made of Satsuma cut glass reflect Kagoshima hometown pride. Fish is mainly shipped in from Kitakyushu, but some are selected at the Tsuruhashi and Kuromon markets. For vinegared rice, the house favours the sour flavours of eastern Japan to the sweeter varieties of the west. In Edo style, rice from the previous harvest is cooked relatively firm, vinegared and kept at body temperature. Sushi of fatty tuna is formed with salt for a more striking flavour. Sea-urchin portions are generous. Even the rolled omelette shows the practised hand of the skilled sushi artisan.

Name: Naniwaryori Satou
Description: The chef honed his skills at a Naniwa (Osaka-style) kappo. The restaurant’s name, ‘Satou’, adds a kanji for the ‘u’ to his surname, Sato, in homage to the shop where he apprenticed. The long Japanese menu is written right-to-left, like a scroll. His speciality, passed down from his mentor along with his cherished serving bowls, is ‘Tenjin Kobai Mushi’, savoury egg custard prepared with dried-plum broth and finished with a delicate plum glaze. The chef prides himself on his quick thinking in picking up guests’ preferences. An heir to the spirit and skills of Osaka cuisine.

Name: Osteria Ottanta Sette
Description: Franciacorta is a sparkling wine from Italy’s Lombardy region. The couple who run this osteria used to run one back in Italy and now offer both Lombardy wines and cuisine. Dishes are faithful to tradition: risotto is made with Carnaroli rice; pasta is served al dente. The number ‘87’ in Italian is ‘ottanta sette’. This is a play on the phrase ‘ho tanta sete’, meaning ‘I’m thirsty’. Wet your whistle on some Italian bubbly.

Name: Kushikatsu Daibon
Description: This restaurant opened with a mission: to preach the gospel of kushikatsu, a beloved Osaka speciality of deep-fried meat, vegetables or seafood on a skewer, to a wider world. ‘Daibon’ is a mashup of the owner-chef’s name and the shop where he apprenticed; the sign was hand-lettered by the mentor himself. A devoted lover of fish, the chef makes seafood the star of his kushikatsu prix fixe. His tiger prawn, a standard item, is fried rare to draw out its sweetness. His motto, another gift from his mentor, is ‘Craft, Character, and Passion’. The skill of the kushikatsu gourmet shines in his cheerful demeanour and devotion to his craft.

Name: Sumibi Iwata
Description: Locally raised chickens from Kagoshima are shipped directly to the restaurant and grilled over Bincho charcoal. The appetiser for the prix fixe menu is lightly seared chicken thigh. Yakitori is almost always salted, so as to bring the high quality of the meat to the fore. Yuba tofu, soy milk thickened with starch, is the house’s renowned palate cleanser. The flavour of the chicken melts into the soup of the soy-sauce ramen that brings the meal to a close. Adding oyakodon is warmly recommended. As befits the restaurant’s name, which starts with ‘sumibi’, ‘charcoal flame’, the interior is ash-grey.

Name: Sushi Takumi
Description: The sushi at Sushi Takumi is the product of personal connections times curiosity. Tuna, a must-have for nigirizushi, is sourced from the only wholesaler with whom the chef had a personal connection when he became independent. His work draws strength from a knife set he specially ordered from a knife store in his homeland of Fukui. From the same region comes a renowned Japanese mustard, paired with sushi toppings that best complement its flavour. Each piece of sushi weaves together personal connections, skill and a far-away homeland, enclosing sincere wishes.

Name: Sumisho Mikuriya
Description: The proprietor shares his extensive knowledge of yakitori with a touch of humour—occasionally warning that it might be a long story. He constantly experiments with types of charcoal, flame settings, how the fat drips, and when to turn the skewers over. Salt, not sauce, brings out the flavour of the chicken. Another cherished view is that effective flame modulation can yield impressive results even if the chicken is not top-grade; for that reason he dares to use broiler chickens for neck and heart meat. This is the path of the ‘charcoal master’.

Name: Loris
Address: 125 Porto Arabia Drive, The Pearl, Doha, Qatar
Description: It’s a pure Lebanese experience at this eatery located on The Pearl. Everything from the plush décor to the food alludes to the country located to the east of the Mediterranean. The flavours are all authentic, almost as if grandma was cooking up the dish. Of course, the dishes are made for sharing, with silky hummus and tasty kebab with cherry being the most popular choices. Aish el Saraya is a notable dessert that you mustn’t skip. After dinner, take a stroll on the walkway nearby to take in the city vistas.

Name: Carbone Doha
Address: Al Maha Island, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
Description: This branch of New York’s famed Italian American restaurant is found on the edge of Al Maha Island. A fun spot, it has all the iconic dishes from the original, including their signature spicy rigatoni, which is certainly worth coming for. Other must-haves include steaks, lamb chops and the desserts presented on a trolley; the cheery and attentive team are also all ready to recommend their own favourites. It’s a brasserie-style interior with a stage set up for a crooner to sing classic songs if you’re lucky; we suggest taking a seat on the terrace for fantastic views of the city.

Name: Masala Library
Address: Katara Tower, Fairmont Doha, 6th Street, Marina District, Lusail City, Doha, Qatar
Description: The Fairmont Doha is a striking property by Lusail Marina and this Indian restaurant occupies a position on its first floor, with full-length windows facing the ever-changing landscape. The plush white surroundings are matched by a well-organised service team, while the kitchen produces colourful and artistically plated dishes – their kulcha is a must for enjoying the excellent dals. There is also a subtle influence from West Bengal so you can expect plenty of fish. Be sure to save room for the bebinca dessert.Currently closed for rebranding.

Name: MURU
Address: 5th Floor, Waldorf Astoria Doha, Al Shaghya Street, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: There’s plenty of panache and no little swagger to this large Mauro Colagreco restaurant on the fifth floor of the Waldorf Astoria. The self-styled ‘elemental cooking’ is centred around fire, water, earth and air, with the four elements also providing the different themes for the interior design – a table somewhere between ‘Fire’ and ‘Water’ is the best spot. The global menu offers everything from ceviches and tiraditos to grilled and wood-fired dishes that provide a fusion of exhilarating flavours.

Name: Liang
Description: Carefully prepared Cantonese dishes, adapted somewhat to suit local tastes, are the order of the day at this elegant restaurant located at the rear of the Mandarin Oriental Hotel. Other regions of China are also represented on the wide-ranging à la carte, with dishes like Kung Pao tiger prawns and Peking duck likely to appear. The attractive and contemporary dining room features modern screens for a sense of privacy, with a charming service team always on hand if you need any recommendations.

Name: SAWA by Sanad
Address: Mohammed Bin Jassim Street, Msheireb, Doha, Qatar
Description: The first floor of a private members’ club in Doha’s rejuvenated downtown plays host to this impressively chic dining room. The menu offers a showcase of contemporary Levantine dishes, many of which are perfect for sharing. The kitchen takes things up a notch in the evening, including some dishes served from the trolley for an extra dash of theatre. You don’t need to be a member to eat here, but you’ll be tempted to join up after you’ve experienced the caring service and delicious food.

Name: Salt Road
Address: Andaz Doha Hotel, 23 Diplomatic Street, Zone 61, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: As the name suggests, the owners hail from South Africa as does the cuisine of their restaurant located in the Andaz Doha hotel. The space has shelves stacked with salt from around the world, as it’s used for curing and pickling, which is how they used to preserve food back in the day. The menu has a variety of sharing options – the 5 cured brisket is delicious as are the Josper roasted mushrooms – but the steaks are particularly notable here. If you’re unsure what to order, the well-informed team’s advice is a good guide. Try some of their South African wines, offered by the glass or bottle.

Name: Em Sherif
Address: Al Maha Island, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
Description: This fast-growing Lebanese household name is ideally located on the bustling Al Maha Island. Inside, it’s an elegant affair with cosy seating radiating a luxurious feel – try and get a seat on the large covered terrace for incredible city landscapes. The menu is authentic and the emphasis is on flavours, with something for everyone: puffy breads, delicious fattet barek, creamy fassoulia, muttabbal – the list goes on. This is really a place to dine with family or friends as everything is made for sharing.

Name: Rivaaj
Address: The St. Regis Doha, Al Gassar Resort, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: ‘Heritage Indian Cuisine’ under the aegis of Surjan Singh, better known as ‘Chef Jolly’, is the order of the day at this elegant and moodily lit restaurant at the St Regis hotel. That means a menu offering an appealing range of dishes, from elevated street food to elegant curries and biryanis. The undecided should consider the ‘Signature Board’ offering a range of meats and seafood from the tandoor, plus salad and chutney. The service is always endearingly sweet-natured, adding to the restaurant’s appeal.

Name: Desert Rose Café
Address: Ground Floor, National Museum of Qatar, Museum Park Street, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
Description: Beaming smiles greet you from behind the counter at this easy-going and friendly spot tucked away in the National Museum of Qatar. When it comes to ordering, start off with their arancini or ‘Dynamite shrimps’ then go traditional with keema, khabees and Chef Noof’s madrouba that’s made using a special recipe – and no visit here will be complete without the date cake. A great strawberry mojito or a cup from their vast array of speciality coffees will set you up nicely for your museum visit.

Name: La Petite Maison (LPM)
Address: Al Maha Island, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
Description: Up in Lusail on Al Maha Island, this outpost of La Petite Maison has a prime location on the waterfront; the sunsets are always impressive. It’s very chic and elegant – and that’s just the service. The open kitchen offers bright, flavour-packed Niçoise and Mediterranean cooking – try the crevettes, confit de canard and finish with the tarte aux fraises. Add in an appealing cocktail, mocktail and wine list and you have all the ingredients for a fun night out, although it’s also worth coming during the day for their business lunch, which is a steal.

Name: Hakkasan
Address: St Regis Doha, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: This branch of the global brand sits in the grounds of the St Regis hotel but feels entirely independent of it. The dining room features an impressive back-lit counter and remains a place ‘to be seen’ in the city. The extensive menu features plenty of appealingly presented dishes, including all the signature classics – like their Peking duck and dim sum platters – while the desserts are more than an afterthought. If you're not sure what to order, you can't go far wrong by opting for one of their Signature set menus.

Name: Gymkhana
Address: Katara Hills, Doha LXR Hotels & Resorts, Doha, Qatar
Description: A franchise of the established – and highly acclaimed – London headquarters, this Indian restaurant is located just inside the Hilton Resort in the Katara Hills area. It’s a striking place that resembles a lodge, with a terrace at the back and a clubby, colonial feel inside. The open kitchen, which adds plenty of animation to the room, takes its inspiration from the menu offered in London which was, in turn, inspired by the clubs of India. Lunch represents good value and the service is polite and welcoming.

Name: Koo Madame
Address: 1st Floor, Rosewood Hotel, Marina District, Building 11, Street 309, Zone 69, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
Description: The Rosewood Hotel is home to this 1920’s-inspired Chinese restaurant. Dark and moody, the space has an open kitchen, an enclosed wine cellar and a smartly dressed team that are ready to serve. The menu is a roll call of some familiar and enjoyable dishes. They serve dim sum, wonderfully fresh-pulled noodles – the Fried Flying Dagger is the one to choose – and of course, the signature Beijing Duck is beautifully lacquered, flavoursome and carved at the table – don't worry, the kitchen will do a half if you can’t manage a whole. Their tea selection is also worth exploring.

Name: Dar Yema
Address: Doha Oasis, Al Khaleej Street, Doha, Qatar
Description: Step into this beautiful and spacious dining room and you’ll be warmly welcomed by the gracious team. North African Maghrebian cuisine is the appeal here, with a particular focus on Morocco. Homemade breads are plentiful and delicious, with highlights of the traditional menu including Moroccan tagines – the chicken tagine with lemon and olives is particularly good – and Algerian boureks. The kitchen puts plenty of heart into the cooking and the team even make their own ice cream to satisfy sweet-toothed diners.

Name: Chicago Rare
Address: 127 Porto Arabia Drive, The Pearl-Qatar, Four Seasons The Pearl-Qatar, Doha, Qatar
Description: If you’re craving a steak with all the trimmings, a glossy lamb shank, enormous crab legs or a fine lump crab cake then this restaurant within the Four Seasons Hotel is where to come. The Josper oven and grill are used to great effect and desserts also go all in, with the likes of ‘Campfire Alaska’; you’ll certainly leave feeling comfortably satisfied. Live jazz adds to the Chicago atmosphere, while the team channel the Blues Brothers in their look and zip around the room providing attentive service.

Name: SMAT
Description: At the southern end of the Corniche sits this wonderfully decorated restaurant that features bold colours and an opulent edge, with comfortable sofa seating and polished tiled flooring adding to its appeal. The authentic Qatari and Gulf State dishes are generous in size, eye-catching in looks and yield refined flavours and textures. You could start your meal with crisp Mzatara Samboussa, then move onto one of the particularly good lamb main courses, before the Donafa Ain Helaitan provides a satisfying conclusion.

Name: Saasna
Address: Barahat Msheireb Street, Sikkat Al Maiz, Doha, Qatar
Description: The dream of the late Sheikha Ahmed Al Meer – author of 'The Art of Qatari Cooking' – lives on through the proud and caring team who run this restaurant and who are determined to continue her desire to preserve and celebrate the country’s culinary past and to bring it into the 21st century. The traditional cooking is fresh and full of flavour; start your visit with a samosa or the Saasna salad, then the majboos for main course; the wonderful date ice cream is a great way to finish. They have a terrific range of freshly ground seasonings and spices for you to purchase to replicate the flavours at home!

Name: Zuma
Address: Al Maha Island, Lusail, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Notable sake list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: With Winter Wonderland theme park opposite, this branch of the international group has always been popular with families at certain times of the year; its weekend DJ, large terrace, island bar and on-view kitchen also make it a favourite with groups of friends looking for a fun night out. The menu offers an extensive selection of contemporary Japanese dishes, which are all designed to be shared; this includes a range of options from the robata grill like marinated lamb chops and salmon teriyaki.

Name: Kai’s Songbird
Address: Porto Arabia, The Pearl, Corinthia Yacht Club, Doha, Qatar
Description: Kai London and their songbird have flown east – with no expense spared – to this spot at the Yacht Club. The glamorous interior is certainly something to behold, but there is much to be said for a table on their air-conditioned terrace. The menu fuses original and modern Chinese Nanyang cuisine, so expect plenty of seafood like their standout soft shell crab or wok-hei prawns; there are other London classics too such as their legendary aromatic crispy duck.

Name: yūn
Address: 44th Floor, Waldorf Astoria Doha, Al Shaghya Street, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Take the elevator to the 44th floor of the Waldorf Astoria Doha to this opulent Chinese restaurant with its jaw-dropping views. We suggest you start off at the bar and opt for a creative mocktail made using a range of teas before heading to dinner. The Cantonese and Taishanese menu is suitably authentic. Chef Victor hails from Chengdu and has around 20 years of professional experience. All the classics are here; ensure you kick off your meal with the 'Premium selection' of dim sum, followed by their speciality 'Forbidden City' roast duck served two ways and be sure to save room for dessert. The welcome is fulsome and genuine, the service smooth and engaging.

Name: Mr & Mrs Hawker
Address: 3rd Floor, Andaz Doha Hotel, 23 Diplomatic Street, Zone 61, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: Whether you come here to rekindle your memories of Singapore or just to experience something a little different, this restaurant delivers on the famed Hawker street food. Wherever you sit in the spacious interior dotted with subtle Asian touches, the focus is firmly on the chefs at work in the lively open kitchen. The menu is headed up 'From the Garden City', 'From the Pot', 'From the Wok' and 'From the Hawker Street.’ Expect all the vibrant Singaporean classics, from chilli crab to mango sago pudding, all carefully prepared. Ensure you let them know your spice tolerance, as they don’t hold back.

Name: Hunters Room & Grill
Address: The Westin Hotel Doha, Salwa Road, Fereej Bin Mahmoud, Zone 23, Doha, Qatar
Description: To find this spacious restaurant and some of the best steaks in the city, look out for the huge statue of a stag at the heart of the Westin Doha Hotel. As the name suggests, it’s all about the grills here. Premium quality and full-flavoured Australian Black Onyx steaks, a nice piquant sea bass aguachile and even homemade bread flavoured with meat juices are all must-tries on the menu.

Name: Bayt Sharq
Address: Al Doha Gardens, Al-Sharq Street, Doha, Qatar
Description: This characterful, restored Al Khulaifi house is around 100 years old and even has its own little museum; if you want a glimpse of Old Doha, this is where to come. It’s located just off the Corniche and offers a variety of seating options: in the restaurant or on its veranda, in the gardens or even in a cabin. The classic and authentic Qatari dishes are brimming with flavour and generosity, from mutabbel or majboos to delicious saffron mahalabia; whatever you choose, the only certainty is that you won’t leave hungry!

Name: Dalchini
Address: Diplomatic Street, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: With a palette of purple, cyan blue and orange, there’s a bright and colourful feeling to this restaurant situated within the Centara West Bay Hotel. The name is Hindi for cinnamon and the cooking is described as ‘Progressive Indian’, with all regions represented on the menu. Dishes are confidently made and neatly presented, with the chefs delivering an original touch and a well-judged balance of vibrant and subtle spicing.

Name: Coya
Address: W Doha Hotel & Residences, Diplomatic Street, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: Buzzy, colourful and lively, with a hint of Aztec style, this restaurant has all the ingredients for a fun night out. Take a seat in the moody and intimate split-level dining room, where you can see the chefs working in an open kitchen on a range of Peruvian-inspired dishes designed for sharing. Quality ingredients run throughout and there’s a freshness and vibrancy to the flavours. Engaging, attentive service completes the picture.

Name: Shanghai Me Doha
Address: Dafna Street, Area 61, 801 Building 138,, Doha, Qatar
Description: Come for their tasty kung pao chicken, stay for their zodiac-inspired cocktails at the bar. This plush and intimate restaurant in the heart of the city makes a great spot for a romantic evening out. The décor’s 1930’s feel, its moody ambiance and the elegantly dressed team all complement the mix of dishes hailing from China and Japan. Modern and classic dishes go hand in hand, such silver cod with yuzu miso and wonderfully flavourful short rib gyoza, along with dim sum and sushi.

Name: TONO
Address: 6 La Croisette, Porto Arabia The Pearl Island, Doha, Qatar
Description: This restaurant’s narrow ground-floor entrance belies the glitzy, capacious dining room you’re greeted with two floors up. For wonderful waterfront views, you can also try to secure a table on the enviable terrace. The Nikkei cuisine, curated by international chef Akira Back, is a worthy match for the glamorous surroundings; the ‘prawn cigar’ will raise a smile, while the classic sea bass ceviche should always be ordered. The smart service team are chatty and alert. Look out too for the weekly offers.

Name: Morimoto
Address: Mondrian Doha, West Bay Lagoon, Doha, Qatar
Description: From the catwalk entrance to the DJ, from the theatrical cocktails to the uber-contemporary hotel in which it sits, it quickly becomes obvious that this is a beautiful restaurant for beautiful people. The sushi counter is striking and there are booths for those wanting privacy, but for most guests a night out here is more about seeing and being seen. The contemporary Japanese menu offers something for everyone, with wagyu a speciality along with items like king prawns and lamb chops cooked on the robata grill.

Name: BiBo
Address: The Pearl, Costa Malaz Bay, Doha, Qatar
Description: Acclaimed Spanish chef Dani García’s BiBo is found on a small island within the grounds of the palatial Marsa Malaz Kempinski Hotel and shares a detached property with its sister op, Lobito de Mar. Dani’s travels as well as flavours from his native Andalusia inform the menu; the tapas and sharing plates have a modern edge but a traditional heart. ‘Langostinos fritos’ and oxtail brioche are just two of the dishes not to be missed, while the chocolate tart is enough for two people. The room has a clubby feel, with a centrepiece fish tail hanging from the ceiling.

Name: La Mar by Gastón Acurio
Address: Street 900, Bldg. No. 25, Zone 61, Al Dafna, Beachfront, InterContinental Doha, West Bay, Doha, Qatar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Come for the beachfront location, stay for the vibrant Peruvian dishes at this light and airy restaurant within the grounds of the InterContinental Hotel. Gastón Acurio is a fine ambassador for Peruvian food and all bases are covered here, from ceviches to anticuchos. The colourful, rustic dishes deliver plenty of punchy flavours and are perfect for sharing. As you sit and soak up the lively atmosphere, you’ll be struck by what a fun night out it all is. And the wallet-friendly prices make it even more appealing.

Name: Curiosa by Jean-Georges
Address: Four Seasons Hotel, The Corniche, Doha, Qatar
Description: The eponymous Jean-Georges is none other than the world-famous Vongerichten, who has brought a sassy Latino vibe to the elegant Four Seasons Hotel. Ask for a table in the bar for the Gulf views, and then sit back and wait for the band to start playing as you enjoy a sparkling selection of Latin and globally influenced dishes. That could mean a classic ceviche, tacos and tortillas, sizzling shrimp or crispy fried chicken. End with the ‘Salted Impossible Flan’ or the vast passion fruit sundae and you’ll be gliding out happy.

Name: Nobu
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Counter dining,Great view,Notable sake list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: The location is a huge draw at what is the largest branch of this globally recognised restaurant brand. Part of the Four Seasons Hotel, this Nobu sits in a stunning futuristic building surrounded by water, located at the end of a narrow peninsula, and offers impressive views of the Corniche promenade. Choose from a wide range of Japanese dishes, with South American influences adding a lovely twist. An open kitchen, stylish bar and cool music ensure a chic atmosphere accompanies the food.

Name: Kardeşler Restoran
Address: Tiyatro Yanı, Taşpazar Adese Yolu, Ebulfeyz Elçibey Caddesi, Aksaray, 68100, Türkiye
Description: Meat is the house speciality at this large restaurant, as the well-stocked chilled display counter and grill in the centre of the open kitchen make clear. Grab a table – the terrace is an oasis of calm in the middle of the city – and choose from the enticing array of local classics. From succulent grilled lamb cutlets with pide bread, onion, sumac and yoghurt and tomato dressings to sac tava, a sizzling meat dish alive with spices: this is the sort of abundance that foodies truly relish. It is a bonus that you can drop in for breakfast, lunch or dinner. The friendly service comes with a smile at no extra cost.

Name: Sofram Restaurant
Address: Aşağı Kayabaşı, Özdemirler Sitesi İç Yolu No:30, Niğde, 51200, Türkiye
Description: This spacious restaurant on Niğde's main boulevard is particularly convivial after dark with its dimmed lighting, yet what really stands out is the sincere hospitality of the staff. You immediately feel at ease here. Don't expect elaborate theatrics, but rather succinct, flavour-focused cooking. Turkish generosity is expressed here, for example, in a dish of succulent confit lamb neck served with flatbread, boldly seasoned tomato and yoghurt. The extensive menu and the convenience of being open every day are guaranteed to win you over. There is even a small play area provided for younger guests.

Name: Uzundere Kapadokya Mutfağı
Address: Aydınlı - Orta, Mahalle Uzundere-1 Sokak No:1, Göreme, Nevşehir, 50180, Türkiye
Description: Diners are welcomed with a complimentary spread of various little appetisers and sweet beverages, a gesture that immediately reflects the importance placed on hospitality here. This is the cosy halal restaurant on the first floor of Şah Saray Cave Suites, which affords wonderful views over the valley. The menu is a celebration of the culinary traditions of Turkey and the Islamic world. Imagine an earthenware bowl filled with finely sliced beef elevated by dried plums, onion and herbs, served with a side dish of rice with almonds and raisins. A delicate sweetness runs subtly throughout, always beautifully balanced. Please note the dress code; for example, legs must be covered.

Name: Emektar Kebap
Address: Evka 3, 129/7. Sokak No:16, Bornova, Izmir, 35050, Türkiye
Description: This very spacious and vibrant establishment, with its warm decor, is located at a remove from the city centre, but this in no way diminishes its popularity among the locals, who flock here to savour delicious treats straight from the large wood-fired oven or the imposing grill. Emektar Kebap is defined by honest, traditional cooking. From iskembe (a rich beef tripe soup) to lahmacun (Turkish pizza) baked in the oven with minced meat and tomato, and succulent spit-roasted lamb served with yoghurt and aubergine, this is the kind of authenticity that keeps foodies returning for more.

Name: Gün Lokantası
Address: Asmalı Mescit, Gönül Sokak No: 8/A İç Kapı:1, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34430, Türkiye
Description: Small, cosy and lively, this gastrobistro encapsulates the cool vibe of the Beyoğlu neighbourhood. In the open kitchen, the grill and open flames immediately draw the eye. The chefs handle the fire with skill, bringing the essence of each flavour to the fore – the cuisine is modern, unpretentious and carefully considered. Lamb hearts grilled to a pink finish with white beans in a lamb jus enriched with miso, or crisp-grilled sea bass accompanied by pickled grapes and a lemon beurre blanc: these ingredient-led dishes are nuanced and fun. The à la carte options are irresistible and great for sharing. An experience not to be missed!

Name: Balmumu Dükkan Lokanta
Address: Alsancak, Kültür Mah, 1388. Sokak No:5 D:C, Konak, Izmir, 35220, Türkiye
Description: Venture down this side street on the edge of the Konak district to savour traditional Aegean cuisine as the locals do. The chefs work with fresh ingredients purchased at the market that very morning and showcase their offerings in the display counter, from mezze to the side dishes you choose with your main course. Vine leaves are stuffed with boldly seasoned rice, lamb is slowly cooked to retain its succulence and accompanied by a buckwheat ragout; pumpkin is cooked with cinnamon, cardamom and bay leaf and finished with a sweet caramel sauce. These are dishes with soul, prepared with personality.

Name: Seyhan Et
Address: Yelaltı, Nur Dikmen Caddesi No:20, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: Once a butcher's shop, this establishment has evolved into a restaurant for meat lovers, and you can also purchase cuts to take home. The range is outstanding, in terms of both variety and quality. But come and see for yourself! Why not start with a few mezze, before moving on to the succulent lamb cutlets, or try the rump steak, marinated for a week in milk and herbs and cooked to perfection. There are small pots of spices on the tables, including cumin and oregano, so you can season your meat to your liking. Having said that, it is so exquisitely grilled that any sauce would really be entirely superfluous.

Name: Okra İstanbul
Address: Osmanlı Sokak No:1/B, Taksim, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: Take the lift up to the 20th floor of The Marmara Taksim Hotel and absorb the scene for a moment. Okra's expansive windows afford breathtaking panoramic views of the Bosphorus and cityscape beyond. Treat yourself to a crisp cocktail and browse through the wine list, which features some outstanding Turkish labels. The chef delights his diners with exceptionally fresh fish from the local market, often cooking it over an open fire. His silky manti, for instance, are filled with succulent meat and served with a tomato and bell pepper sauce and yoghurt. And then there is the seafood platter, brimming with salty goodness… As you might have guessed, reservations are essential at this coveted destination.

Name: Lil'a Restaurant
Address: Tekelli Mahalles No:2, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50240, Türkiye
Description: At Lil'a, the long-lost flavours of Anatolia are brought back to life. Chef Saygın Sesli and his team unite time-honoured techniques, meticulous craftsmanship and locally sourced produce – much of it from the restaurant's own garden – to create a vibrant expression of farm-to-fork dining. For instance, succulent grilled lamb is glazed with sesame and honey and served with a silky aubergine cream, grilled lettuce and yoghurt finished with pistachios. Theatrical presentation enhances the experience, with steaming dishes arriving under a cloche. The setting, too, evokes the past, with an array of Turkish artefacts on display, staff dressed in traditional attire, and a romantic atmosphere. This restaurant at the Museum Hotel truly lives up to its name!

Name: Hus Şarapçılık
Address: Kuşçular Mahallesi, 8018/1. Sokak No:39, Urla, Izmir, 35437, Türkiye
Description: The terrace of this inviting restaurant is the best place to experience the charm of the Hus wine estate to the full. The sight of the vines and olive trees immediately has a calming effect. Be sure to sample the wines produced on site – your charming service team is on hand to offer expert guidance. These wines pair perfectly with the food, which is a contemporary take on Mediterranean cuisine prepared to order. Having started with the addictive house-made focaccia, for example, you could move on to the perfectly cooked medium-rare lamb saddle seasoned with rosemary, accompanied by a robust lamb jus and a roasted garlic cream to really bring out the characteristic flavour of the meat. Finish off with a Turkish coffee for a burst of intensity!

Name: Lokanta by Divan
Address: Asker Ocağı Caddesi No:1, Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
Description: The Divan hotel, close to Taksim Square, boasts a restaurant named Lokanta that exudes the same traditional splendour. The first room is dominated by a piano, which is regularly used for performances. The cocktail bar is the focal point of the second room, and the last room is ideal for family gatherings. In this exquisite setting, you can order à la carte from a selection of traditional Turkish dishes. Tempting options include layers of brick pastry stuffed with braised lamb, tenderised mutton and paprika, and steamed sea bass with an aromatic pil-pil sauce. Lokanta offers a fine dining experience featuring bold, no-nonsense flavours.

Name: AZUR
Address: Yeniköy Mahallesi, Köybaşı Caddesi No:71, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34464, Türkiye
Description: As you make your way through this chic restaurant, you will certainly be drawn to the modern works of art and the panoramic view of the Bosporus. But what really catches the eye at AZUR is the seafood on display. The quality is second to none! All that excellent produce is showcased in dishes that fluidly blend Turkish and Mediterranean culinary traditions. Think Atlantic bluefin tuna tartare with creamy stracciatella, super-fresh fish on the plancha, paella or pasta. Meat fans are also well catered for. The servers will be happy to give you a few pointers to help you get the most out of this culinary adventure.

Name: Yeni Lokanta
Address: Kumbaracı Yokuşu No:66, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: Tucked away down a side street off the famous İstiklal Avenue, this is a bright Mediterranean-style space with a bustling yet welcoming atmosphere that perfectly reflects Istanbul's spirit – welcome to Yeni Lokanta! The chef's original and sensitive approach brings a fresher, lighter quality to Turkish flavours without sacrificing their exuberance. For example, slices of beetroot are confit and accompanied by dried sour cherries, hazelnuts, Ezine cheese and a herb oil in a bold starter. Order à la carte or opt for the set menu (a curated selection) to see how the focus on vegetables, local produce and Turkish wines makes this dining experience all the more engaging.

Name: Topaz
Address: Ömer Avni Mahallesi, İnönü Caddesi, No:42, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34427, Türkiye
Description: Take the lift to the seventh floor of The Artisan İstanbul MGallery hotel and marvel at the breathtaking views over the city, which this elegant rooftop restaurant proudly showcases. At Topaz, a favourite among Istanbul’s food connoisseurs, Mediterranean dishes are given a distinctly Turkish twist, and bold flavours abound. For example, the chef slowly braises lamb shoulder so that the meat is meltingly tender and deeply aromatic. He then serves the succulent meat with a robust sauce made from the cooking juices, along with barley risotto prepared with plenty of cream and chives, black trumpet mushrooms and salted lemon. After your meal, savour the experience a little longer with a drink at the cocktail bar.

Name: AQUA
Address: Yıldız, Çırağan Caddesi No:28, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Everything revolves around water at the fish and seafood restaurant of the Four Seasons Hotel, which is also right on the waterfront. Not only can you enjoy a unique view of the bustling strait and Bosphorus Bridge, but this elegant restaurant also provides a romantic backdrop. Delicious seafood is showcased in typical Mediterranean fare, modern Asian creations and dishes cooked on the grill. Aromatic, subtly spiced, accompanied by rich buttery sauces: this is generous cuisine prepared using premium produce.

Name: Kasap Fuat Alsancak
Description: You enter a butcher's shop with an impressively well-stocked counter and are guided to the restaurant tucked away at the back. An almost magical atmosphere reigns in the colourful dining areas, and that is added to by the old Turkish classics playing on vinyl records. This place is certainly one of a kind! The grill and house-reared meats take centre stage. Take your pick from the counter, where you'll find top-quality dry-aged steak and beef burgers, and order some mezze that are bursting with flavour. The chefs grill lamb ribs, for example, to a perfect rosy pink with the fat cap crisped to perfection. For local colour, you need look no further.

Name: Loft Elia
Address: Gölköy Mahallesi, 325. Sokak No:7, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The olive trees around you and the views over the bay accentuate Loft Elia's Zen feel. Although this lounge-style restaurant is fully open to the elements, it nonetheless has an intimate atmosphere. The natural vibe suits the menu down to the ground. A commitment to local produce and sustainable practices are part of their ethos underpinned by respect for the planet. The kitchen team's inspired, fine dining-quality dishes are deliciously spicy. For example, their airy feta sponge cake is freeze-dried with three varieties of tomato to give it delicate sweetness and tang. This cuisine is truly inspiring!

Name: Herise İstanbul
Address: Reşitpaşa Mahallesi, Kongre Caddesi No:15/A, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34467, Türkiye
Description: Asude and Bahadir are ambassadors for Anatolian cuisine. She will gladly tell you all about their concept while providing attentive service and bringing refreshing mocktails to your table (no alcohol served here). He works to a single set menu that celebrates traditional flavours. Variations of tomato and pepper are a common theme in his diverse range of dishes, whether vegetarian or meat-based. His less-is-more approach is exemplified by the millefeuille of dry figs with Aegean olive oil, or the refined combination of rosewater, saffron, currants and rice. Herise Istanbul is one of a kind.

Name: Liman İstanbul
Address: Kılıçali Paşa Mahallesi, Meclis-i Mebusan Sokak O2 Blok No:8 D:102 Galataport, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: Start with a cocktail in the bar on the ground floor before moving up to the first floor, where Liman is ensconced in a laid-back yet stylish setting boasting a stunning terrace overlooking the Bosphorus. Time-honoured recipes are given a refined modern twist with meticulous attention to detail. Examples include crispy lahmacun bursting with the rich flavors of lamb and beef, finished with fresh herbs and lemon, or sourdough pide with house-made pickles. Then for dessert: katmer with pistachio and Maraş ice cream. These chefs masterfully balance a reverence for tradition with cutting-edge technique – therein lies their genius.

Name: Monteverdi Ristorante
Address: Cihannüma, Saray Caddesi No:5, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34353, Türkiye
Description: Enter the luxurious Conrad Hotel and allow yourself to be escorted to the equally stylish Monteverdi Ristorante. The kitchen team specialises in Lombard cuisine but draws inspiration from across Italy's regions, so Neapolitan pizzas feature on the menu, too. Whatever takes your fancy, authentic flavours reign supreme here, dish after dish. Think creamy risotto with porcini and Parmesan, or ultra-fresh sea bass with sun-dried and fermented tomatoes, olives and courgette ribbons wrapped around mascarpone. This is food that strikes a balance between the familiar and the complex. Attentive service puts the finishing touch on this thoroughly Italian culinary journey.

Name: Sapa İstanbul
Address: Küçükbakkalköy Mahallesi, Rüya Sokak No:12/18A, Ataşehir, Istanbul, 34750, Türkiye
Description: Stylish and spacious, Sapa is located in a predominantly corporate neighbourhood and caters to breakfast, lunch and dinner crowds. We especially recommend the set menu, available from 2pm. (N.B. The 12-course menu is for a minimum of two people.) The chef has a penchant for open-flame cooking and a knack for balancing robust flavours with contemporary culinary lightness. He accompanies succulent grilled rockfish with a salmon cream paired with chestnut and capers for a touch of fresh acidity. A drizzle of syrup adds a hint of sweetness – a refreshing spin on Turkish cuisine!

Name: Ernest's Bar by Çok Çok Pera
Address: Meşrutiyet Caddesi No:54/A, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34430, Türkiye
Description: Exotic artwork by a Singaporean designer gives this elegant restaurant a distinctive South Asian feel. Having spent time in Thailand, the chef has gained an intimate understanding of the nuances of its cuisine. Skilfully balancing spicy and sweet notes, he presents a diverse spectrum of flavours. As an example, he tempers a chilli sauce with the sweetness of fruit and a bold fish sauce. Signature dishes such as green curry with scallops and red curry with duck unfurl their depth and umami-rich profiles here. A slice of Thailand in the heart of Istanbul!

Name: Ruby
Address: Yıldız Mahallesi, Ortaköy Salhanesi Sokak No:5, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
Description: With stunning views over the Bosphorus, a roof that can be fully opened when the weather is fine, and a terrace that turns into a DJs' playground at weekends: Ruby is one of the hot spots in Ortaköy. The menu comprises dishes for sharing, traditional Turkish fare and a tempting range of pasta and risotto options. And whether you opt for the penne puttanesca or the grilled sea bass with spinach and orzo in a cream sauce, rest assured that your meal will be indulgent and brimming with rich flavours.

Name: Zuma Bodrum
Address: Cökertme Caddesi No:36, Yalıkavak Marina, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: Zuma is not at all out of place among the impressive yachts and luxury boutiques. This izakaya has a sophisticated feel with its phenomenal sea views, clubby vibe and laid-back atmosphere. From May to October, this is the place to discover a trendy take on Japanese cuisine, in which the robata grill and sushi take centre stage. They serve a variety of nigiri, succulent grilled tiger prawns or teriyaki-marinated grilled salmon with pickled cucumber. Meat lovers might prefer the 700g dry-aged ribeye. The extensive menu is full of irresistible options! Prolong your experience at this hip establishment with a refreshing cocktail at the bar.

Name: Sait
Address: Yalıkavak Marina, Çökertme Caddesi No:2 D:06 Blok, Yalıkavak, Bodrum, 48990, Türkiye
Description: The luxury yachts and chic boutiques may call to mind Saint Tropez, but you are in fact sitting on a terrace on Yalikavak's marina. The restaurant's maritime decor leaves no doubt that fish and seafood are the speciality of the house. The day's catch is displayed on ice, and you are handed an extensive menu of irresistible options. Begin, for example, with dolmas filled with aromatic rice and meat, then move on to the prawn ceviche infused with orange, lime and dill. Each plate bursts with colour, fragrance and generous flavours. Home cooking is at the heart of this family-run place – and the key to its success.

Name: Nobu İstanbul
Address: Süzer Plaza, Askerocağı Caddesi No:6, Elmadağ/Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Located in the Ritz Carlton Hotel, the Istanbul branch of the Nobu restaurant chain embraces the Eastern facets of this cosmopolitan city. Whether you choose a table on the large terrace, in the bar or in the restaurant, the setting is as hip as it is minimalist. The stunning view over the Bosporus and the Asian part of the city is quite a sight to behold. Modern Japanese and South American influences are blended here with great precision. Think sea bass cooked in a light tempura batter and served with a vinaigrette in which chopped pineapple and orange create surprising nuances. The menu is impressive, and the omakase menu aptly captures the essence of the kitchen's offerings. The selection of signature cocktails, Turkish wines, and sakes is simply delightful.

Name: Itsumi
Address: KULE - İşkuleleri Kule 2 Entrance floor No:43, 4.Levent/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34330, Türkiye
Description: You'll have to venture out of Istanbul's city centre to find this rather unassuming-looking restaurant, but the trip is well worth it. At Itsumi, authentic Japanese cuisine is expertly prepared using the finest ingredients. Whether it's lightly warmed sea bass sushi, omelette filled with grilled glazed eel, or noodles simmered in chicken stock with finely chopped vegetables and chicken, you can rely on the chef to deliver the specialities of his homeland with all the requisite nuances. At lunchtime, both a set menu and à la carte options are available. N.B. The omakase menu has to be booked in advance.

Name: Şans Restaurant
Address: Hacı Adil Caddesi, Palmiye Sokak No:1, Levent/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34330, Türkiye
Description: This elegantly appointed villa has been a favourite destination for business clientele since 1992. They come for the attentive service, private dining options and expert wine recommendations (be sure to try one of the Turkish reds!). But the principal draw is undoubtedly the cuisine: a fusion of authentic Turkish flavours and Mediterranean influences. From steaming cheese dumplings to a creamy mushroom risotto and slow-cooked lamb neck with barbecued vegetables: generosity is always on the menu here. A firm favourite with many foodies.

Name: Alaf
Address: Arnavutköy, Kuruçeşme Caddesi No:19, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34345, Türkiye
Description: Alaf is a bustling restaurant with a fabulous cocktail bar on the roof terrace – perfect for a romantic dinner for two overlooking Istanbul's eastern coastline. Chef Deniz cooks up dishes with various influences: sometimes it is inspired by Yörük cuisine, sometimes Kurdish, the list goes on. With his wood-fired oven, he enthusiastically melds authentic traditional Turkish recipes with new-age cooking methods. Whether it's al dente squid with an exciting Mediterranean twist using sun-dried tomatoes, or medium-rare goose breast elevated by satsuma and harissa, a diverse journey of discovery awaits your taste buds!

Name: The Red Balloon
Address: General Yazgan Sokak No:6, Asmalımescit, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34430, Türkiye
Description: Settle in for a convivial dining experience beneath the sparkling chandeliers of this intimate restaurant, part of the RUZ hotel in the Pera district. The chef works with quality local ingredients, North Aegean influences and Mediterranean freshness to create his own distinctive culinary style. For example, slow-cooked beef neck is pressed into shape and served with a subtly spicy apricot sorbet and tangy pickled matsutake mushrooms. This is inspired cooking that gives familiar flavours an interesting twist. You can tailor your menu to include fish and meat, or choose exclusively vegetarian or vegan options. Round off the evening with a digestif in the rooftop bar.

Name: GALLADA
Address: Kemankeş Karamustafa Paşa, Kemankeş Caddesi No:34, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Gallada is the epitome of luxury. Located on the fourth floor of The Peninsula hotel, this exclusive restaurant seats more than 200 guests! Diners are drawn in by the stunning views of the Bosporus, the upscale decor and delicious cocktails served at Topside Bar. But they mainly come for the captivating fusion of Turkish and Asian flavours over the course of a culinary journey along the Silk Road. The melt-in-your-mouth tuna is first marinated in soy sauce, yuzu and ginger then combined with a tahini and yoghurt cream. You should also definitely try the tandoori duck and the restaurant's own version of baklava. At Gallada, an extraordinary experience awaits you.

Name: ADA Restaurant
Description: Head to the wooden pier at Şat Burnu, board the Sovalyece which will take you (free of charge) to Şövalye Island in under 10min and, finally, settle in at the chic ADA Restaurant. Your trip is rewarded with a dining experience with romance and charm in abundance. The views over the water and the city of Fethiye, the sound of the waves, the sunsets… Wonderful Turkish bread arrives immediately while you peruse the diverse menu. Succulent grilled sea bass with spicy roasted potatoes, smoked aubergine from the wood-fired oven with yoghurt, tandoori lamb or chicken curry: traditional Turkish cuisine is given a Mediterranean twist and presented in all its unembellished glory. Simply irresistible!

Name: Tık Tık Kadın Emeği
Description: Be careful not to drive right past this rather unassuming-looking corner-plot building, as it would be a shame to miss this restaurant. Its cosy charm is irresistible, from the creaking wooden floor to the red-and-white check upholstery. The women's cooperative at the helm delivers wonderful traditional dishes based entirely on home cooking. You can watch them in their small kitchen as they prepare manti with local cheese and top it with tomato sauce, or shaping meatballs and cooking them in a rich tomato jus. The menu is concise, and it's wise to arrive early to avoid disappointment, but the reward is a heartwarming experience that offers an authentic taste of Cappadocia.

Name: Hodan Yalıkavak
Address: Kudur Mevkii Sehit Engin Buyuksoylemez Caddesi No:9, Bodrum, 48890, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: Çiğdem Seferoğlu invites you to the Avantgarde Refined Yalikavak Hotel, home to her open-air restaurant that boasts a magnificent view of the sea. More compelling still is her personal take on the region's culinary bounty. Her light and elegant cuisine highlights fish and seafood with a feminine touch. She confits gurnard in olive oil, which renders the texture wonderfully soft, and serves the fish with fennel seasoned with turmeric and coriander seeds, a blend of purslane and mint leaves with nectarine, and warm Turkish bread. The chef also prepares meticulous vegetarian dishes and proves that healthy food can indeed be profoundly flavoursome.

Name: Yakamengen III
Address: Yaka Mahallesi, Yaka Küme Evleri No:70, Datça, 48900, Türkiye
Description: This charming restaurant is housed in a converted olive oil mill on the Reşadiye peninsula. The building has been beautifully restored without compromising its authenticity, and boasts a lovely garden where you can dine beneath the olive trees. Duru Akgül's cuisine is contemporary and draws on the best the region has to offer. She tends her own kitchen garden and enjoys working with lesser-known seafood such as blue swimmer crab. She binds the crab meat with a yoghurt cream, for example, and serves it with a mixed vegetable brunoise and crisp courgette fritters topped with local herbs. Her dishes are always beautifully presented and packed with bold flavours. Do take time to peruse the interesting selection of local wines.

Name: Lokanta 1741
Address: Alemdar Mahallesi, Profesör Kazım İsmail Gürkan Caddesi No:34, Cağaloğlu Hamamı, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
Description: This beautiful contemporary restaurant with a romantic roof terrace is right next to Cağaloğlu Hamam. It serves Turkish culinary classics, some dating back to 1741, with a modern twist. The chef sometimes introduces surprising textures and flavours but never loses sight of tradition. In the evening, they serve only a more sophisticated fine dining menu. Here, you can savour a zesty sea bass ceviche, as well as lamb brochettes with distinct barbecue notes and a punchy aubergine caviar. Oenophiles should definitely take the opportunity to explore the wine cellar.

Name: Eleos Yeşilköy
Address: Yeşilköy mahallesi, Yeşilbahçe Sokak No:9, Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34149, Türkiye
Description: This exciting restaurant, reminiscent of a Greek tavern and complete with a lovely terrace, lies just a couple of streets from the marina in Yeşilköy, a residential area on the outskirts of Istanbul with the feel of a seaside resort. The wonderful seafood on display also takes centre stage on the menu, which includes a variety of mezze brimming with Mediterranean zest and beautifully crispy-fried red mullet with skin-on potatoes and a fresh salad. Expect a relaxed dining experience – unpretentious and focused on honest flavours.

Name: Calipso Fish
Address: Küçükyalı Sahil, Cumhuriyet Caddesi No:2, Küçükyalı/Maltepe, Istanbul, 34840, Türkiye
Description: Istanbul residents come to this sun-drenched restaurant to escape the hustle and bustle of the city. The waiters give expert advice on the wide selection of mezze in the display fridge – the salads are beautifully fragrant! And that's just the beginning, because the traditional preparation methods accentuate the rich flavours of super-fresh fish and seafood. Whatever you choose, the chef will cook it according to your wishes: the bluefish, for example, can be barbecued whole and served with al dente vegetables. This is ingredient-led cuisine that never fails to impress.

Name: Orfoz
Address: Kumbahçe Mahallesi, Zeki Müren Caddesi No:13/1, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The beautiful bay this restaurant overlooks is the pride of the Bozçağa brothers – not only for the azure waters, but also the bountiful fish and seafood they have to offer. Their family-run restaurant specialises in seafood and plant-forward cuisine. A commitment to locally sourced ingredients and short supply chains ensures exceptional quality. The chefs' love for the sea is palpable in every dish, from sea snails cooked in a court bouillon and finished with a herb cream accented with a pronounced hint of garlic, to eel that is confit and lightly smoked, resulting in a buttery texture. It is worth perusing the wine list, as it is clearly a passion of the owners and even includes some of their own labels.

Name: Seraf Vadi
Address: Ayazağa, Kemerburgaz Caddesi No:7G, İç Kapı No:7, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34396, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Start your meal with the wood-fire grilled onion stuffed with rice, spices and currants – a speciality of the house. And be sure to sample the other mezze, such as the piping-hot lahmacum topped with succulent lamb, mint, parsley and a judicious squeeze of lemon. The main courses featuring various cuts of lamb are to die for. This contemporary restaurant close to Vadistanbul Shopping Mall and Galatasaray's football stadium is a celebration of Anatolian culinary heritage.

Name: Muutto Anatolian Tapas Bar
Address: Kılıçali Paşa, Meclis-i Mebusan Caddesi No:8, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: To soak up Galataport's trendy atmosphere, a spot on the front terrace overlooking the passing boats is the place to be. But whether you sip your cocktail alfresco or inside the modern bistro, you're in for an exceptional evening. The restaurant specialises in Spanish tapas reimagined through a Turkish culinary lens. You might start with prawns accompanied by a spicy cherry cream, move on to a shared plate of patatas bravas and grilled squid, and choose a more traditional main dish such as a pide or baked sea bass. The chefs have a flair for reinvention and have curated an enticing menu. Eating at Muutto makes for a great night out!

Name: Malva
Address: Torba, Kaynar Caddesi No:15, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: Housed in luxury hotel Susona, this restaurant feels both elegant and hip. But the most stunning feature of all is the breathtaking view of the coastline. The chef and his team will be happy to tell you about their commitment to sustainability, including a zero-waste approach and close collaboration with their suppliers. Their creative cuisine draws on traditional and modern influences, celebrating the authentic flavours of the ingredients. For instance, the courgette flowers stuffed with rice and chopped mussels are seasoned with a classic blend of herbs and a judicious twist of lemon. The charcoal-grilled mussels add delightful smoky nuances. A compelling dining experience guaranteed!

Name: Amavi
Address: Alaçatı Mahallesi, 13003. Sokak No:1, Çeşme, Izmir, 35937, Türkiye
Description: Alaçati is a picturesque town with a lot to offer, but Amavi is the place to be for foodies. Walk through the cocktail bar, where DJs play in the evening, and take a seat in the trendy restaurant, which exudes its own unique elegance. Seafood takes pride of place here – there's even a fish aging cabinet visible in the open kitchen. Each dish is creative, vibrant and bears the chef's signature. A compelling dining experience defined by playful textures and intense, layered flavours.

Name: Ritüel
Address: Şifne Mahallesi 5495. Sokak No:26, Çeşme, Izmir, 35000, Türkiye
Description: Head to GAIA BY THE SEA hotel, follow the path to the rear and immerse yourself in the romantic atmosphere of this outdoor restaurant. The view of the water is utterly captivating! You even make this a regular treat: Chef Tolga Kamiloğlu brings his experience to bear in a contemporary take on Turkish cuisine, which is detailed and elevated with the occasional Asian influence. Highlights include the charcoal-grilled baby calamari with cherry tomatoes in a jus of tomato, vinegar and mirin, and the orange-themed dessert with lime sorbet, yuzu sorbet and yuzu jelly – each plate delivers an experience. The wonderful à la carte selection is guaranteed to delight.

Name: Reserved Restaurant
Address: Adnan Menderes Caddesi, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50000, Türkiye
Description: This country house possesses a certain rustic elegance, with its characteristic stone architecture, wood features and numerous period details. The lounge atmosphere is also incredibly inviting. After a refreshing cocktail or a local wine, savour traditional dishes brimming with character, presented in a contemporary style. Mezze include crispy courgette strips fried in batter with a yogurt and dill dip, and manti filled with meat, served with creamy yogurt and spicy oil – a true taste of the sun on your plate. In the evenings, a DJ provides a lively musical backdrop for no extra charge.

Name: Mori
Address: Fevzi Çakmak Caddesi No:24, Fethiye, 48300, Türkiye
Description: With the azure sea against the backdrop of the majestic mountains in the distance and the palatial yachts in the marina just a few metres from your table, the terrace here is the place to be. Located at Yacht Classic Hotel, this restaurant specialised in Italian cuisine eschews unnecessary frills and focuses on flavour. Think al dente linguine with a light velouté sauce and ultra-fresh seafood such as tender squid and pink prawns. The extensive menu will not disappoint!

Name: Barbarossa
Address: Adnan Menderes Caddesi No:89, Asarlik Mevkii PK 225, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The luxurious Caresse resort's Mediterranean restaurant offers a delightfully laid-back dining experience. Watch the chefs at work in the outdoor kitchen while cocktails are shaken in the bar and chill-out music fills the air. The view of the sea and the moored yachts never gets old! Seafood takes centre stage here, cooked up in traditional Greek and Italian ways. Wonderfully crispy deep-fried squid with a fresh tartar sauce, barbecued sea bass with perfectly seasoned vegetables: the best of Mediterranean cuisine served up without any fuss. Reserve a poolside spot ahead of time and enjoy a refreshing swim after dinner.

Name: Seraf Mahmutbey
Address: Mahmutbey Mahallesi, Peyami Safa Caddesi No:38/D, Bağcılar, Istanbul, 34200, Türkiye
Description: Sinem Özler sets great store by goods from local producers. You can taste and see this for yourself, because they are also for sale in the shop of this spacious, modern restaurant, just outside the city centre. For example, she works with Trakya Kivircik lamb in a bid to keep traditional recipes alive. The İçli Köfte with the same lamb is an absolute must. To bring those ancient Anatolian flavours to the table, this chef likes to use a wood-fired oven, and she never loses sight of the changing seasons and her surroundings.

Name: 1924 İstanbul
Address: Istiklal Caddesi, Olivya Geçidi No:7, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34435, Türkiye
Description: This restaurant was opened in a previous incarnation by Russian refugees in 1924. Today diners can relive those glory days in a beautifully restored and opulent setting that exudes historical grandeur and features eye-catching panelling and mirrors. Live piano and accordion music makes for a buzzing atmosphere. The chefs put a modern spin on Russian specialities, including stuffed pirozhki, delicate smoked salmon with warm blini, and beef Stroganoff. Generous portions, juicy meat and amazing flavour. And to drink? A glass of vodka from their impressive selection, of course!

Name: Deraliye
Address: Divanyolu Caddesi, Alemdar Mahallesi, Ticarethane Sokak No:10, Sultan Ahmet, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
Description: Deraliye is a landmark of the historical Sultanahmet neighbourhood, where there is one tourist restaurant next to the other. The colourful, opulent decor immediately catches the eye and, like the cuisine, is a tribute to the Ottoman Empire.
