The extensive menu features an array of dishes devised for sharing and specialities such as mezze, barbecued offerings and kebabs. Tempting options include duck stew in filo pastry with fragrant spiced rice, or a lamb and tomato dish, slowly simmered in an earthenware pot to let the flavours meld. Here, you can savour sumptuous Ottoman cuisine, occasionally presented with a touch of showmanship. Good to know: Deraliye also organises cookery classes.

Name: Levan
Address: Kuşçular, Kuşçular Caddesi No:3, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: Dining with a view of the vineyards, or on the terrace surrounded by the grapevines, is an experience that will leave a lasting impression. Levan offers a convivial atmosphere in a charming and intimate setting. On the chalkboard, you will find a dozen dishes, from mezze to share to main courses to savour on your own. The traditional cuisine of the Aegean coast is given a contemporary twist: Examples include sea bass marinated in lemon before cooking and served with a crisp salad, or house-made ravioli stuffed with various cheeses and accompanied by a Parmesan and cream sauce. Get ready for a Mediterranean feast!

Name: OCAK
Address: Hobyar Mahallesi, Mimar Vedat Sokak No:5, Fatih, Istanbul, 34112, Türkiye
Description: OCAK has breathed new life into this former tobacco warehouse in the Old City, turning it into an intimate restaurant with exposed brick walls, soft lighting and marble finishings. The chef proposes only a single set menu that showcases his unique take on Turkish cuisine. He elevates chickpeas to new heights in a variety of dishes, including an amazing crispy deep-fried creation. He consistently strikes a perfect balance between tradition and modernity. Your curiosity will be piqued by every dish.

Name: Birinci Kordon Balık Restoran
Address: Alsancak, Atatürk Caddesi No:196/A, Konak, Izmir, 35220, Türkiye
Description: Fish, fish and more fish – that's what you can expect at this rather simple restaurant. The refrigerated display counter immediately catches the eye as the charcoal grill works overtime in the kitchen. After some freshly prepared mezze, for example, allow the chef to delight you with succulent barbecued calamari rings in a chilli crust, or just as expertly flame-grilled sea bass. Such incredible flavours! No frills here: the focus lies squarely on unadulterated top-quality produce. A gem among the many restaurants on the quayside.

Name: Moniq Restaurant
Address: Aşağı, Gedik Sokak No:8, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50280, Türkiye
Description: Nestled in one of the stylishly transformed caves that together form the remarkable Taskonaklar hotel, Moniq Restaurant showcases the rugged stone beauty of Cappadocia. The opportunity to take an aperitif on one of the terraces overlooking the stunning Pigeon Valley is not to be missed. Inside, the ambiance is charming and inviting. Chef Mustafa Türkten works with local women from nearby villages to create a menu built on traditional recipes and regional ingredients, with a few modern touches thrown in. Highlights include manti with roasted aubergine or hearty lamb casserole with stewed peppers and tomatoes, finished with a spiced lamb jus and served with pita bread. If you visit on Friday or Saturday, be sure to try the Ottoman mutancana.

Name: Basta Neo Bistro
Address: Caddebostan, Operatör Cemil Topuzlu Caddesi No:39, Kadıköy, Istanbul, 34728, Türkiye
Description: Kaan Sakarya and Derin Aribaş honed their skills in top-flight European restaurants before opening this lively bistro. A seat at the counter offers the best view of how they blend European and Turkish traditions with a street-food twist. Their seasonal, market-fresh cuisine is beautifully showcased in the sweet brioche filled with tomato jam, onion and stracciatella. The pan con tomate with perfectly salted anchovies is simply irresistible. The appealing menu demonstrates the chefs' knack for infusing every dish with personality.

Name: Apartıman Yeniköy
Address: Yeniköy, Köybaşı Caddesi No:153, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34464, Türkiye
Description: A mostly youthful and hip crowd frequents this pleasant bistro, which matches the energy of its neighbourhood. Lounge music plays in the background, the impressive drinks list features a notable selection of orange wines. The kitchen is run by a female chef who has composed an extensive and enticing menu that combines Mediterranean verve with Middle Eastern spiciness. For instance, she barbecues lamb to medium-rare and serves it with orzo cooked in a kokoreç broth and greengage. Tip: For a truly filling meal, consider ordering an additional starter.

Name: ÇARK balık Çeşme
Address: 16 Eylül, 3047. Sokak No:7/A, Çeşme, Izmir, 35930, Türkiye
Description: This family-run Turkish osteria is tucked away in one of Çeşme's charming side streets, making it the perfect stop after a day of shopping or relaxing on the beach. Super-fresh fish and seafood is served straight off the boat at lunchtime, in simple dishes that showcase the natural flavours of the produce in all their glory. Start with mezze such as artichoke hearts with spring onions and crushed raspberries, then move on to prawns grilled to that perfect point of translucency, with an exquisite jus just begging to be mopped up with every last piece of bread – no unnecessary frills, just the briny richness of coastal cuisine with Mediterranean flair.

Name: Rumelihisarı İskele
Address: Yahya Kemal Caddesi No:1, Rumeli Hisarı/Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34470, Türkiye
Description: At this classic waterfront pavilion, every table enjoys panoramic views of the mighty Bosporus, with its endless stream of boats – a breathtaking setting in which to savour the finest seafood. Having sampled the aromatic mezze presented at your table, you pick your fish from the abundant selection and indicate if you would like it steamed, barbecued or deep-fried. The kitchen puts the emphasis squarely on flavour, without any unnecessary flourishes. The Iskele special, a seafood pan with octopus, prawns and more, is seasoned only with paprika and chilli.

Name: Sunset Grill & Bar
Address: Kuruçeşme Mahallesi, Yol Sokak No:2, Ulus/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34345, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Sunset Grill & Bar could be in a Hollywood film. This spacious, upscale restaurant is located in the heights of Ulus Park, providing a magnificent view of the city and the Bosporus – be sure to ask for a table by the window. The well-heeled clientele is drawn by the attentive service, and the extensive menu, which features classic French cuisine, Asian-inspired dishes and trendy sushi options, as well as the impressive wine list. Treat yourself to one of the barbecue specialities – think butter-soft beef fillet with a brown sauce enhanced with yuzu and mustard. An exhilarating dining experience!

Name: Tuğra Restaurant
Address: Çırağan Caddesi No:32, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34349, Türkiye
Description: At Tuğra, diners are made to feel like royalty. Marble columns frame a view of the glimmering Bosphorus. Here, you can bask in the historical splendour of the magnificent Çırağan Palace – the opulence never fails to impress. And the terrace is simply breathtaking! The impeccable service leaves you wanting for nothing. As for the food, Ottoman culinary heritage goes hand in hand with haute cuisine, with traditional flavours elevated by the chef's expert touch and elegant plating. For instance, tender beef fillet is paired with a robust brown jus and clever accompaniments such as a quenelle of fermented milk, mashed potatoes with pine nuts and an exquisite onion confit – a fascinating combination.

Name: Mürver
Address: Novotel İstanbul Bosphorus, Kemankeş Caddesi No:57-59, Karaköy/Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Take the lift to the top floor of the Novotel Istanbul Bosphorus and discover the world of Mürver. You can start with an aperitif in the hip cocktail bar, then soak up the romantic atmosphere of the restaurant. Finally, take in the breathtaking views of the metropolis from the fabulous terrace. An open fire is the centrepiece of the kitchen, where you can also see meat and fish drying. Smoky and barbecue notes form the basis of captivating creations featuring regional produce and original combinations. The dishes are spicy, bold and fiery. Think grilled squid rings with green beans and a subtly spicy muhammara sauce, or 28-day aged ribeye. This buzzing establishment is the place to be!

Name: Beyti
Address: Şenlikköy Mahallesi, Orman Sokak No:6, Florya/Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34153, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Beyti Güler is a living legend in Istanbul. Since the 1980s, Istanbulites have been coming to dine in this stylish building, a fine example of nostalgic Turkish charm, with its little fountains at the entrance and sculptures in the garden. And this historical establishment boasts no fewer than 12 dining rooms! The charcoal grill is at the centre of the kitchen, where the experienced chefs cook all kinds of meat to perfection. Take the imam bayildi, for example: meltingly tender braised aubergine topped with tomatoes, bell peppers and onions, cooked just long enough to bring out all their flavours. And be sure to try one of the kebabs, too. Traditional Turkish fare just as it should be.

Name: Borsa Restaurant
Address: Vaniköy Caddesi No:12, Adile Sultan Sarayı, Üsküdar, Istanbul, 34684, Türkiye
Description: The Adile Sultan Palace is an events venue that is as spectacular as its name suggests. A stroll through the building will give you a sense of its grandeur and splendour – characteristics that Borsa is fortunate to share. To dine against a breathtaking backdrop of the Bosporus, head to the terrace. This upmarket restaurant showcases traditional Turkish cuisine on an à la carte basis. In his dish featuring medium-rare lamb ribs, spinach and roast potatoes, the chef allows the distinctive flavours of the ingredients to shine through. Less is more at Borsa. Make sure you leave room for dessert – the classic katmer (crispy filo pastry filled with pistachio) is very tempting!

Name: Aila
Address: Büyükdere Caddesi No:76/B, Mecidiyeköy/Şişli, Istanbul, 34394, Türkiye
Description: Aila exudes luxury and grandeur. Smooth marble, high ceilings, dark wood: the decor is a feast for the eyes. Turkey's rich culinary heritage is given a contemporary twist with meticulously prepared premium ingredients. They put the focus on spices – they even have a spice library – and the provenance of the ingredients, which is detailed on a small informative card on your table. For example, the chef grills grouper over an open fire and serves it with beurre blanc infused with orange and sumac for a unique balance of rich, zesty and bitter nuances. Be sure to indulge in a glass of raki (they have an outstanding selection!) to complement this modern homage to culinary tradition.

Name: Akira Back İstanbul
Address: Ataköy 2-5-6. Kısım Mahallesi, Rauf Orbay Caddesi No:2/1 LB, Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34158, Türkiye
Description: The view of the Sea of Marmara is the highlight of this modern and inviting restaurant located in the JW Marriott hotel. Be sure to go for a spot on the terrace! Akira Back has restaurants all over the world and has appointed one of his right-hand men as head chef in Istanbul. The dishes embody a distinctive fusion of predominantly Japanese and other Asian cuisines. Fine sushi, tasty gyoza, beef tataki that melts in the mouth, perfectly robata-grilled prawns… You will definitely want to come back for this contemporary whirlwind of Eastern flavours.

Name: Sia Eli
Address: Gümüşlük Mahallesi, 1120. Sokak No:108, Gümüşlük, Bodrum, 48970, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Counter dining,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Surrounded by gardens dotted with olive trees, with the sea, which supplies the day's catch, just a stone's throw away, and the rolling hills providing a lush backdrop, Sia Eli is the perfect setting for a romantic dinner for two. This open-air restaurant also has a trendy edge, with cool lounge music setting the mood. The kitchen keeps pace with a menu of contemporary international dishes ranging from ceviche to an original take on mezze. This is one of those laid-back places where you can savour crispy red mullet tempura accompanied by a fragrant herbaceous salad, sip a refreshing cocktail and appreciate just how wonderful life can be.

Name: SOTA ALAÇATI
Address: Alaçatı Mahallesi, 11039. Sokak No:18, Çeşme, Izmir, 35937, Türkiye
Description: The lobster and oyster tanks give away the fact that this open-air restaurant's main supplier is the sea. SOTA's Mediterranean soul is evident in everything from its mosaic tiles to the fresh seafood on the menu. The squid has the perfect firm texture and is seasoned to have just the right amount of zing. The seafood is super fresh and wonderful in combination with al dente tagliatelle. This restaurant is dedicated to showcasing the sea's rich bounty.

Name: Orkide Balık
Address: Göltürkbükü Mahallesi, Sahil Sokak No:34, Bodrum, 48483, Türkiye
Description: At Orkide Balik, you can almost feel the sand between your toes as you enjoy your meal, and, on warm days, the terrace beneath the tall trees is especially inviting. The chef takes full advantage of the restaurant's seaside location to serve fish at its absolute freshest. But before you order your main course, be sure to sample starters such as "seacuterie" (seafood charcuterie) and stuffed mussels, and don't miss out on the mezze displayed in the refrigerated counter. The dishes are prepared without any fuss, and with that traditional sense of generosity. Think marinated squid or deep-fried sea bass with aubergine and a bechamel sauce seasoned with mustard. It is always a good idea to round off your meal with the exceptional soğuk baklava. Sometimes the best things in life are the simplest.

Name: İsabey Bağevi
Address: Gölcükler Mahallesi, 901. Sokak İstasyon Mevkii No:38, Menderes, Izmir, 35470, Türkiye
Description: The Isabey wine estate grows mostly Sauvignon Blanc, but you will find more than impressive rows of vines on its land. Indeed, there is a magnificent terrace on which to dine in the shade of a majestic plane tree that is over 350 years old. This restaurant is committed to serving food and wine of the highest quality. The buttery lamb stock with medium-rare lamb chops and the squid stuffed with minced lamb and accompanied by a fine white wine sauce are testament to the depth and flavour of this classic cuisine.

Name: AŞEKA
Address: Müeyyedzade Mahallesi, Arap Oğlan Sokak No:6, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34425, Türkiye
Description: Tucked away in a side street in the Karaköy neighbourhood, this somewhat inconspicuous historical building reveals a tastefully decorated interior featuring intimate lighting, a palette of dark brown hues, and regularly changing artwork. Diners can choose from a tempting à la carte selection or opt for one of the creative set menus. The dishes are not unnecessarily complicated but are bursting with flavour – it is the seasoning and robust sauces that set them apart. Take, for instance, the succulent agnolotti del plin, filled with slow-cooked oxtail and served with a Parmesan cream and fine breadcrumbs. Be sure to stop by the handsome bar to sample one of the cocktails.

Name: Zuma İstanbul
Address: İstinye Park No:461, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34460, Türkiye
Description: The Istanbul branch of this chic Japanese restaurant is on a par with its London, Dubai and other outposts. That means top-notch ingredients that are showcased by a contemporary approach to authentic Japanese cuisine. On the menu: sushi (you can watch the chef meticulously preparing it at the counter), tempura, fish from the robata grill, vegetarian options… There's so much to choose from! Replete with subtle East Asian nuances, the ingredient-led, intensely flavoursome dishes never fail to hit the mark. The gyoza, filled with minced beef and lamb and seasoned with paprika, chilli, sesame and lemongrass, are simply irresistible. Rest assured: The cosmopolitan Zuma feels right at home amid the most exclusive fashion boutiques of Istinye Park shopping centre.

Name: Esca
Address: İstinye Park AVM, Bahçelerarası Mahallesi Şehit Bnb. Ali Resmi Tufan Caddesi No:3, Bağımsız Bölüm No:Z95, Balçova, Izmir, 35330, Türkiye
Description: Located at one of the entrances to the glamorous Istinye Park shopping centre, Esca has a contemporary yet cosy feel – perfect for an intimate dinner for two! The lovely terrace beckons in fine weather. Osman Sezener expresses his passion for Mediterranean cuisine and local produce through an international menu. With options ranging from sushi and gyoza to house-made pasta and succulent lamb chops with a pistachio sauce, every palate is catered for. The tiramisu, with its beautiful balance between the bitterness of the coffee and the creaminess of the mascarpone, has already become a house favourite. Treat yourself to one of the signature cocktails.

Name: Gorgoli
Address: Yılmaz Sokak No:10, Mustafapaşa, Ürgüp, 50400, Türkiye
Description: This simply appointed restaurant is nestled in the charming university town of Mustafapaşa. The Gorgoli Valley is just nearby, and for the chef it's a privileged source of all manner of produce. The extensive menu reflects his deep respect for his terroir and local culinary tradition. Aubergine and peppers are grilled just right for a rich smoky-sweet starter; lamb is slow-cooked to succulent perfection and served with a creamy wheat risotto. Nothing is overworked – every dish is a celebration of true flavour.

Name: Saklı Konak Cappadocia
Address: Tekelli Mahallesi, 2. Karlık Sokak No:3, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50000, Türkiye
Description: Located just outside Nevşehir's tourist hub, this convivial and inviting restaurant is the perfect place to take a break and delve into the region's cuisine. They take pride here in their testi kebabs and unique versions of kofta, but be sure to sample the manti, too – made with grilled aubergine, butter and tomato sauce, and topped with a yoghurt dressing and a sprinkling of dried herbs, they are simply divine! The combination of local produce and traditional recipes ensures that each dish is a joy. Consider extending your experience with a stay in one of the guestrooms.

Name: Kasap Fuat Çeşme
Address: Altınyunus, 3435. Sokak No:66, Çeşme, Izmir, 35930, Türkiye
Description: The moment meat lovers walk into this cosy establishment with its delightful terrace at the back, their spirits are lifted. An array of cuts, expertly prepared by the butcher, awaits in the refrigerated display counter, and in the background, you can see the barbecue where the magic happens. Options include marinated ribeye, perfectly rare and with a crispy fat cap, as well as succulent burgers in house-made buns. What you see is what you get, and it's absolutely delicious!

Name: ONNO Grill & Bar
Description: A free boat ride takes you from Göcek Marina to the island where ONNO Grill & Bar is located in just 10min – during which time you can fully unwind and take in the beautiful surroundings. At this open-air restaurant, you dine right by the water's edge, which certainly adds to the charm of the venue. The cuisine is very much in keeping with the times, Mediterranean in spirit and centred on delicious seafood. The chef also likes to age certain fish for extra depth. His command of cooking techniques is impeccable, as exemplified by an octopus dish with crisp skin and exceptionally tender flesh, served with a sauce in which tomato, pepper, bacon, onion and candied lemon zest create a rich, Mediterranean-style blend of flavours. An experience to be savoured.

Name: Havuş Lokantası
Address: Ataköy 2-5-6, Rauf Orbay Caddesi Kapı No-4 İç Kapı No-7, Yalı Ataköy, Bakırköy, Istanbul, 34158, Türkiye
Description: Leave the bustle of central Istanbul behind and head to Ataköy, where celebrated chef Ömür Akkor – television personality and prolific cookbook author – welcomes you to his latest project. On your way to the modern dining space, you pass a delicatessen brimming with all manner of tempting treats. The à la carte selection features traditional fare, spotlighting specialities from Kilis, the chef's hometown. The rice with sautéed pistachios, served alongside a succulent leg of lamb is a good example. This is not overcomplicated cuisine, just straightforward dishes packed with flavour. The set menu is guaranteed to have you smitten.

Name: Kornél
Address: Bitez, Adliye Caddesi No:34/A, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
Description: Terracotta and sandy hues perfectly complement Kornél's cosy ambiance, and the terrace to the rear has that appealing Ibiza feel. The bar serves up incredible cocktails that change with the seasons, while in the kitchen, the charcoal oven works overtime baking delicious pizzettas and more. The extensive menu includes a beautiful zesty sea bass ceviche, hearty pasta dishes and a vegetarian creation featuring beetroot and dukkah. Kornél offers a relaxed dining experience with great food all year round.

Name: Roka Bahçe
Address: Hacımemiş Mahallesi, 2027. Sokak No:6, Çeşme, Izmir, 35937, Türkiye
Description: The narrow, stone-paved streets of Alacati are always buzzing with activity. Tucked away in one such lane is this alfresco restaurant, whose lively atmosphere instantly draws you in. Gökhan Safkan allows Turkish flavours to seamlessly merge with Bosnian influences, creating a heady mix in dishes such as artichokes cooked with onion and garlic in an orange-infused broth, or succulent pljeskavica (Balkan meat patties) and delicately grilled, ultra-fresh sea bass. This laid-back place puts the emphasis on fun, and the steady stream of dishes emerging from the kitchen is testament to this. You have been warned: the charm of Roka Bahçe is irresistible.

Name: telezzüz
Address: Kuzguncuk, Koç Topluluğu Spor Kulübü, Kuşbakışı Caddesi No:16, Üsküdar, Istanbul, 34674, Türkiye
Description: Even before you walk into this colourful establishment, the ornate exterior hints that nature is celebrated at Telezzüz. The location, in a sports complex, is also rather unique. The restaurant clearly prioritises sustainable practices such as local sourcing, a zero-waste approach and plant-forward cooking. The chefs are creative in crafting delicious vegan dishes. Think mushroom ceviche, or deep-fried artichoke with a rich mushroom ketchup, a sweet plum and chilli sauce, olive oil mayonnaise and crunchy vegetables. And what better than a refreshing cocktail to accompany such deliciously natural food?

Name: Gula Urla
Address: Kuşçular Mahallesi, Kuşçular Caddesi No:46, Urla, Izmir, 35430, Türkiye
Description: Whether you're soaking up the sun on the verdant terrace or cosying up by the fireplace, Gula Urla is inviting all year round. The fresh fish on display makes it clear that the sea is the restaurant's main supplier; vegetables and cheese are also sourced locally. After a delicious cocktail or glass of local wine, tuck into shrimp salad with mango and avocado, or perhaps a tandoori-style squid dish, before finishing off with a creamy katmer with red berries. The extensive menu is a seafood lover's dream come true (plus, there is a separate set menu featuring meat from the wood-fire oven).

Name: Spago Istanbul by Wolfgang Puck
Address: Mim Kemal Öke Caddesi No:35, Nişantaşı/Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
Description: The rooftop of the upscale St Regis Hotel is the place to soak up those hip Istanbul vibes. Sip a delicious cocktail on the terrace that affords sublime views of the city (such romantic sunsets!), sit at the long bar, or simply enjoy the lounge music and modern luxury that surrounds you. The kitchen is overseen by Wolfgang Puck, who creates a unique blend of Italian, Californian and Asian influences. Expect sophisticated flavours and techniques, home cooking and international panache. Be sure to try the smoked salmon pizza, as well as the duck spring rolls with their spicy hoisin sauce and sweet plum sauce. There are also some very appealing modern sushi options for sharing. For the perfect accompaniment, select a bottle from the fabulous wine list, which includes some Turkish labels.

Name: Lokanta Feriye
Address: Yıldız Mahallesi Çırağan Caddesi No:44, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34347, Türkiye
Description: Dining in the gardens of the fully refurbished Feriye Palace is a new experience each time. Here on the edge of the Bosphorus – some diners even arrive by boat – you have the ever-evolving backdrop of the constant coming and going of the ships. And there is something magical about the view of the illuminated Ortaköy Mosque and Bosphorus Bridge, especially when you have a delicious cocktail in hand. This restaurant strikes a fine balance between chic and relaxed, and the service is attentive. The chefs, who can be seen at work in the open kitchen, let the ingredients speak for themselves. Their dishes are not overly elaborate, but rather classic fare with subtle zesty and spicy nuances. They give aubergine purée a delightful tang by mixing in yoghurt, making it an excellent accompaniment to barbecued lamb.

Name: Fauna
Address: Küçükbakkalköy Mahallesi, Işıklar Caddesi, Ahmet Muhip Dranas Sokak No:9/A, Ataşehir, Istanbul, 34750, Türkiye
Description: Lunch at Fauna is the perfect excuse to visit the Ataşehir district, just outside the city centre. Diners sit at long tables, often side by side with others, while the chefs get to work making fresh pasta. At Fauna, Italian and Turkish cuisine come together in generous shareable dishes. Think ravioli with a bold Obruk cheese filling cooked al dente and accompanied by a light butter sauce with a subtle tartness and sage. Local ingredients take centre stage in this ongoing pursuit of culinary finesse. Advance booking is strongly recommended!

Name: Tuti
Address: Yokuşbaşı Mahallesi, Suluhasan Caddesi No:18, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: The castle and rooftops of Bodrum, the azure sea, even some Greek islands – the view from the top floor of The Marmara hotel is truly breathtaking! The restaurant has a Mediterranean feel, and that spirit carries through to the menu. The chef takes pride in skilfully elevating local ingredients and traditional recipes, for example, house-made pasta cooked al dente, tossed in a robust herb cream and topped with grated goat's cheese from the region, basil leaves and dried fruit. Be sure to treat yourself to the legendary baklava, too!

Name: Hakkasan Bodrum
Address: Göltürkbükü Mahallesi 314. Sokak No:12/1, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: Located in the Mandarin Oriental hotel, against the wonderful backdrop of the glistening Aegean Sea, and with an elegant dining space with wood finishes, this floating open-air restaurant is stunning. Hakkasan, a renowned chain, brings a luxurious take on Cantonese cuisine to your table. Think wonderfully chewy lobster dim sum set enticingly on the plate, or a beautiful fillet of sea bass, grilled skin-on and glazed with honey for a pronounced umami note, complemented by hoisin sauce. Be sure to sample the signature cocktails; oenophiles will want to peruse the exclusive wine list. For a chic night out, Hakkasan is just the place – so don't forget to reserve a table in advance!

Name: Terakki
Address: Alaçatı, 12000. Sokak No:21, Çeşme, Izmir, 35930, Türkiye
Description: Rustic yet refined, warm and welcoming – Terakki is a gem. Nab a table on the terrace by the well and observe how the chefs skilfully balance authenticity and modern influences in their own take on generous Aegean cuisine. Think crispy fried veal liver seasoned with thyme, garlic and parsley, or succulent wild sea bass fillet with cherries for a hint of fruity vivacity and accompanied by a velvety cauliflower purée. The exceptional ingredients speak for themselves, requiring no embellishment. The hospitality of the service team comes as a delightful bonus.

Name: Sıralı Kebap
Address: Nispetiye Caddesi No:74, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34340, Türkiye
Description: Located in the heart of Beşiktaş, Sirali makes quite an impression. With its high ceilings, large windows and spacious kitchen, this restaurant is lively but still feels elegant – ideal for an intimate dinner or for larger parties wanting to sample a range of traditional Turkish food. The menu includes lahmacun with beef and lamb, fresh from the wood-fired oven, as well as succulent kebabs accompanied by a subtly tangy salad of tomatoes and olives. Whatever you choose, the chefs add thoughtful finishing touches and handle the fire with real skill. With such a striking array of dishes, you may not know where to start!

Name: Maromi İstanbul
Address: Asker Ocağı Caddesi No:1, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
Description: In Maromi, the Divan hotel boasts an excellent sushi restaurant, where you can dine at a regular table or sit at the counter – we highly recommend the latter to watch the chef in action. See how he tucks tender octopus and pickled daikon into a cradle of warm rice, or how he rolls salmon, spring onion and a fiery chilli pepper sauce in a mantle of toasted sesame seeds. Choose your sushi à la carte, or opt for the omakase menu and let the chef decide. On Tuesdays there's even an all-you-can-eat option!

Name: The BARN
Address: Gazitepe Mahallesi, Akören Cadddesi, Ören Çiftliği, No:114, Silivri, Istanbul, 34570, Türkiye
Description: Leave central Istanbul behind and head to Grandma's Wonderland in the Silivri district. This establishment set in verdant surroundings has both a hotel and this cosy restaurant, as well as a farm that supplies poultry, vegetables and other ingredients. Local produce is treated with great respect and, specialising in plant-forward cooking, the kitchen team adopts a zero-waste approach. The menu features skewers, veal tongue pastrami with cherry sauce, kasseri cheese tortellini, spinach and a butter sauce with white wine and sage. The farm-to-table concept is taken seriously here. A spot on the terrace, in the company of the resident dogs, and with a glass of wine from the estate in hand, is a must!

Name: Seten
Address: Aydınlı Mahallesi, Çakmaklı Sokak No:35, Göreme, Nevşehir, 50180, Türkiye
Description: Make your way from the centre of Göreme, past the charming boutiques, to the grounds of Sultan Cave Suites, home to the town's highest-altitude restaurant. The approach has a touch of magic to it – a feeling confirmed the moment you take in the magnificent view from the terrace. This is the perfect spot for watching the sunset! The menu reveals a clear devotion to traditional Anatolian cuisine: yoghurt with candied and fresh fruit or generously stuffed dolmas to start, followed by Cappadocian ravioli stuffed with minced lamb, accompanied by gently simmered chickpeas and yoghurt flavoured with dried herbs. Fruit and vegetables often come from their own garden, and even wine is made on site. Be sure to arrive early as they do not take reservations.

Name: Nahita Cappadocia
Address: Tekelli Mahallesi, Kayabaş Sokak No:23, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50240, Türkiye
Description: Nahita immediately impresses with one of its finest assets: you enter via the magnificent terrace, which affords romantic views over the valley. Inside, the stone walls are adorned with elegant details. The kitchen team sources ingredients from within a 60km radius to ensure the utmost authenticity in their local cuisine. Think warm dolmas with rice infused with the aroma of the vine leaves and sweet-and-sour cherries, finished with a few cherries and dill – pure pleasure on a plate. The chefs pack bold flavours into every dish, such as the distinctive herbs accompanying pan-fried liver. Set within the Argos hotel complex, this is a dining experience not to be missed.

Name: Terrazza Italia
Address: Levazım, Zorlu Center, Koru Sokak No:2, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34340, Türkiye
Description: Eataly is a world-renowned concept that celebrates the finest Italian foods. It always includes a large speciality market alongside superb dining options, such as this chic restaurant with its expansive terrace overlooking the cityscape. It should come as no surprise that authentic Italian cuisine takes centre stage. Think vitello tonnato with its delicate harmony of veal and tuna, al dente tagliatelle with pistachio pesto and red prawn tartare, or a creative take on tiramisu – the chefs pay tribute to traditional flavours while introducing a touch of flair. The extensive menu will definitely leave you spoilt for choice!

Name: Balıkçı Kahraman
Address: Rumeli Kavağı Mahallesi, İskele Caddesi No:15/1, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34450, Türkiye
Description: Be sure to try the fish kokoreç, a traditional dish made with grilled fish offal; the perfectly grilled turbot, which is the house speciality, is also a must; and let's not forget the dried mackerel, nor the buttery-soft tuna lakerda prepared with house-made olive oil. A word to the wise: The best way to experience Kahraman Altun's cosy fish restaurant is to bring friends and sample as many of his traditionally prepared delicacies as possible. Afterwards, you should definitely take the time to explore the surrounding fishing village of Rumeli Kavağı (also known for its figs). This peaceful corner of Istanbul is sure to enchant you.

Name: Park Fora Balık ve Deniz Ürünleri Restoranı
Address: Muallim Naci Caddesi No:54/A, Cemil Topuzlu Parkı İçi, Kuruçeşme/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34347, Türkiye
Description: Grilled, meunière, steamed, tandoori – however you like your fish, Park Fora has it covered. At this traditional seafood restaurant, the produce is always in season and super fresh. As you enter, you will see crates of the day's catch stacked and waiting and numerous aquariums filled with king crabs, lobsters and other creatures. Specify your cooking preferences – for us, it was sole à la meunière – and then savour! It will be cooked to perfection and accompanied by carefully prepared accoutrements. Factor in the waterfront location, with views of the boats coming and going on the Bosphorus, and you will really feel like you are on holiday!

Address: Ulus Mahallesi, Ahmet Adnan Saygun Caddesi, Ulus Parkı İçi No:71/1, Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34340, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: As soon as you enter, you realise how exceptional this upscale restaurant is. The views of the bustling Bosphorus, the enchanting minarets and the Istanbul skyline are unparalleled! To really make the most of your fine dining experience at the elegant 29, book a table on the expansive terrace. The generosity and spiciness of traditional Turkish cuisine are given a subtle modern twist, often incorporating Mediterranean touches. Both the authentic mezze and the smooth mushroom risotto make this place the trip. Featuring an impressive selection of top-flight labels, the extensive wine menu is worthy of attention.

Name: Kıyı Restaurant
Address: Haydar Aliyev Caddesi No:186/A, Tarabya/Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34457, Türkiye
Description: If you're looking for an atmospheric seafood restaurant adorned with beautiful paintings and affording breathtaking views of the picturesque marina, then this perennial favourite is the place for you (ask for a table upstairs)! Start with a selection of mezze and then choose from the bountiful array of fish and seafood, which will be prepared according to your desires. Our inspector opted for sole from the display fridge, which was flawlessly pan-fried before being filleted at the table. It's all about the produce here!

Name: Hakkasan İstanbul
Address: Muallim Naci Caddesi No:62, Kuruçeşme/Beşiktaş, Istanbul, 34345, Türkiye
Description: Luxury chain Hakkasan likes to establish itself in vibrant cities, and Istanbul is obviously no exception. This restaurant enjoys a prime location at the Mandarin Oriental Bosphorus, which boasts stunning views over the water and exudes Asian elegance with a personal touch. The crispy duck salad, a classic of the house, is a shining example of how Cantonese cuisine is revamped here: the duck skin is incredibly crispy, the meat combines a fine spiciness with a mild sweetness, and the salad offers an interesting contrast with juicy pomegranate. Delicious! And it's absolutely worth taking a look at the exclusive wine list.

Name: BİZ İstanbul
Address: Atatürk Kültür Merkezi, Gümüşsuyu Mahallesi, Mete Caddesi No:2, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34337, Türkiye
Description: Head to the world-famous Taksim Square and take the lift to this spacious restaurant on the seventh floor of the Atatürk Cultural Centre. The interior is elegant and modern, complete with a stylish bar, but nothing compares to the terrace and its stunning views of the city and the Bosphorus. The menu celebrates the diversity of Turkish cuisine through contemporary interpretations of traditional dishes. For instance, a combination of subtly smoky aubergine purée, braised lamb, walnuts and a creamy lamb jus makes for a deeply layered main course. The chefs have an eye for detail, but it is the rich flavours that truly steal the show.

Name: Avlu Restaurant
Address: Cankurtaran, Tevkifhane Sokak No:1, Fatih, Istanbul, 34122, Türkiye
Description: Once a prison, the Four Seasons Hotel Sultanahmet now exudes luxury down to every last detail. Nestled in the inner courtyard, Avlu has a casual feel, a Mediterranean oasis in which you can escape the bustle of the city. Your meal starts with some delicious bread from the wood-fired oven and continues with this fresh take on indulgent Turkish fare. The chef prepares turbot both pan-fried to a succulent finish and folded into dumplings with cauliflower and spinach, rounding off the dish with the fine contrast of a rich sauce and a fresh salad. Between the wide-ranging à la carte selection of Anatolian classics and the tempting set menu (also available in a vegetarian version), making up your mind is the hardest part.

Name: Khorasani
Address: Alemdar Mahallesi, Ticarethane Sokak No:9/B, Fatih, Istanbul, 34110, Türkiye
Description: The Sultanahmet neighbourhood is known for all its tourist restaurants, where menus consist of photographs of dishes. In that respect it's no different at the rustic-style Khorasani, but what sets this grill restaurant apart is the chef's dedication to quality. The meat, barbecued to order, and the kebabs are second to none. We thoroughly enjoyed the kebab with succulent lamb, crisp vegetables and, of course, the wonderful pita bread that comes with it. For flavoursome food with no nonsense, Khorasani is the place.

Name: Seki Restaurant
Address: Tekelli, Kayabaş Sokak No:23, Uçhisar, Nevşehir, 50240, Türkiye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Seki is located on the ground floor of luxury hotel Argos, which was once a monastery built into a hillside that makes for a truly magnificent setting. Be sure to allow time for a stroll along the paths leading through the garden. Inside, you can have an aperitif in the romantic lounge and take in the breathtaking view of the valley, then move into the restaurant itself, which has that distinctively welcoming Cappadocian feel. In these splendid surroundings, diners tuck into local Anatolian dishes with a Mediterranean twist. For example, the chefs balance the sweetness of confit pumpkin with a light tahini paste, sesame seeds and chopped walnuts. The extensive menu encompasses classics such as mezze, salads and lamb specialities, as well as pasta and vegan options. Featuring some 300 labels, the wine list is certainly worth exploring.

Name: Karnas Vineyards
Description: As soon as you drive onto this family-owned wine estate, you sense that something special is about to happen. The large pond with its fountain draws the eyes, and the terrace overlooking the vines has a delightful Mediterranean feel – it's the stuff of dreams! The allure of this place leaves no one indifferent. Don't miss the chance to sample the estate's wines – the perfect introduction to Bodrum's terroir. The chef operates on a farm-to-fork principle and is also committed to sourcing local produce wherever possible. She sets great store by her ingredients, which often come from her own garden. For example, she perfectly pan-fries ultra-fresh sea bass and combines it with braised seaweed, mandarin marmalade, a butter oil emulsion and lime zest – this is a chef who brings a unique and nuanced perspective to traditional dishes.

Name: Lokanta Limu
Address: Yeniköy, Köybaşı Caddesi No:158 D:B, Sarıyer, Istanbul, 34464, Türkiye
Description: With its bright interior and appealing artworks, Lokanta Limu stands out even in this bustling neighbourhood. The decor radiates a sense of serenity, and the closely spaced tables create a convivial atmosphere. Sara Tabrizi and her team of chefs delight in creating generous mezze spreads that bring a fresh perspective to authentic Turkish flavours. Think tuna marinated in raki and served with parsley, apple and red onion, or briefly seared lamb's liver with fried potatoes and onion. The extensive menu features plenty of enticing options that lend themselves well to sharing. To explore a wide range of dishes without breaking the bank, choose the Çilingir Sofrası set menu.

Name: Scappi
Address: Alsancak, Gaziosmanpaşa Bulvarı No:1, Konak, Izmir, 35210, Türkiye
Description: Take the lift to the ninth floor of Swissôtel and immerse yourself in the elegant setting of Scappi. It's definitely worth trying to secure a spot on the terrace, where you get to take in the views of the bay and the sea – the sunsets are simply divine! But perhaps you would prefer to home in on the action in the partially open kitchen complete with pizza oven. With great skill, the chefs rustle up dishes such as a creamy risotto with barbecued squid, al dente house-made pasta with an aromatic tomato sauce, or freshly caught sea bass with a saffron-infused lime sauce. This is a popular place, so don't forget to make a reservation.

Name: St. Regis Brasserie
Address: Mim Kemal Öke Caddesi No:35, Nişantaşı/Şişli, Istanbul, 34367, Türkiye
Description: This chic, urban-style luxury brasserie at the St Regis Hotel would not seem out of place in Paris. Begin with a cocktail – the house take on the Bloody Mary, made with raki, is a must. The extensive à la carte menu truly offers something for everyone, from Asian dishes (eg gyoza) and Turkish mezze to Italian pasta and risotto – the choice is yours! The kebab with succulent meatballs, grilled peppers, a silky butter sauce with just the right level of heat and a thick yoghurt paste is rightly a house signature. Dishes are down-to-earth and generous, bringing together flavours from around the globe – always balanced and lovingly prepared.

Name: Giritli
Address: Yenigüvey Sokak No:9, Cankurtaran/Fatih, Istanbul, 34122, Türkiye
Description: In summer, Giritli welcomes you to its atmospheric terrace, where the kitchen is also located. If the weather lets you down, you can always cross the street to the romantic Mediterranean-style sister restaurant. Be sure to explore the enticing mezze set menu (drinks included), which inventively showcases the traditional flavours of Crete. The perfectly seasoned and generously portioned dishes feature impeccably fresh produce. Think marinated sea bass with fresh herbs, or potato salad with a judicious touch of vinegar and vibrant tzatziki. A real feast!

Name: Aheste
Address: Asmalı Mescit Mahallesi, Meşrutiyet Caddesi No:107/F, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34430, Türkiye
Description: Once you enter the premises, leaving the bustling Pera district behind, you have a choice between a trendy bistro and a more romantic dining space with a vaulted ceiling. In either case, you'll be charmed by the mystical ambiance and the staff's enthusiasm and dedication – and that's before you've even discovered the restaurant's modern take on mezze! Traditional Turkish specialities, such as barbecued lamb heart with roast potatoes, share the menu with in-vogue options, including vegetarian dishes. The tasting menu offers a wonderful opportunity to savour delicacies such as flaky pastry filled with a creamy tuna tarama.

Name: Kurul Bitez
Address: Bitez Mahallesi, 1936. Sokak No:2, Bodrum, 48470, Türkiye
Description: In the heart of the bustling centre of Bitez, there is a large garden where you can unwind amid olive and lemon trees while enjoying delicious food. Welcome to Kurul Bitez, where kebabs are the speciality of the house. You can see this for yourself at the entrance, where the spit is always turning and the bread oven is working at full tilt. Chef Kemal Karataş gives Gaziantep cuisine a contemporary twist, as in the crisp pistachio roll filled with creamy sheep's cheese, generously topped with pistachios and a nut cream, and accompanied by a quenelle of sour cream. Be sure to try his aromatic mezze, too – they are simply too good to be missed!

Name: Dereköy Lokantası
Address: Dereköy, Dereköy Caddesi No:133, Bodrum, 48960, Türkiye
Description: Zişan Altınçaba's culinary approach is creative while maintaining a respect for tradition. She welcomes you warmly in her garden restaurant, where she also has a home accessories shop, and then she lets her cooking do the talking. Fruit is often incorporated for its characteristically refreshing sweetness, eg ripe nectarine lends the scorpionfish ceviche a delicate touch of acidity. However, she proves her classical know-how with her rich pâté of lamb brains and neck. Her dishes are bold – but within reason – with a penchant for fresh and zingy flavours.

Name: Kısmet Lokantası
Address: Çırkan Mahallesi, Çelebi Kaptan Sokak No:3/A, Konacık, Bodrum, 48400, Türkiye
Description: If you're on the hunt for a lively place in which to have lunch among the locals, look no further. Kismet Lokantasi serves delicious food at great value for money in a laid-back atmosphere. Peruse the counter for traditional delicacies prepared by the chef, then choose your favourites. Think succulent meatballs with grilled aubergine and tomato sauce, and, for dessert, a rich patisserie with walnuts and just the right amount of sweet syrup – foodies will be in seventh heaven! This indulgent dining experience will leave a lasting impression.

Name: ROKA
Address: Kılıçalipaşa Mahallesi, Meclis-i Mebusan Sokak No:14/2E, Beyoğlu, Istanbul, 34433, Türkiye
Description: ROKA boasts stunning Bosphorus views, thanks to its location on the Galataport promenade. Inside, the atmosphere is trendy and vibrant. Kick off with a stylish cocktail or an expertly selected wine, then prepare to experience a cuisine that marries Japanese seasonings with influences from around the globe. Fans of Asian cuisine can choose from an abundant menu of dishes that are perfect for sharing, including an extensive sushi selection, king crab dumplings, succulent chicken and yuzu miso-marinated cod from the robatayaki grill.

Name: DAMES
Description: Once a transport café between Saint-Malo and Mont-Saint-Michel, this establishment has been transformed by Marine Hervouet (trained by Alain Passard and Bruno Verjus) and Pascaline Albicini (taught by Robuchon and Etchebest). The premises have been renovated in a bucolic style characterised by exposed stone and contemporary wooden furniture and exude the warmth of a family home. The menu, focused on carefully selected local produce, is exceedingly high calibre. With flambéed tomato compote and a tomato caramel sauce, the vegetable agnolotti impresses with its aromatic depth. The audacious desserts – crispy choux pastry puff garnished with smoked aubergine, sorrel ice cream and hot caramel – hit the mark.

Name: Le Limonadier
Description: This century-old café in La Croix-Rousse serves a few dishes for sharing over drinks. But head upstairs to sample the creative, plant-forward cuisine of Jorge Lara, a Mexican chef who was previously at Têtedoie. Carefully sourced ingredients – mostly organic and local – are brought to life through flame cooking and various fermented foods, which are preserved in jars that adorn the space. The combinations are precise and stimulating, to be chosen from a deliberately short menu. Organic vegetables from Courzieu, wines from independent winemakers, including many biodynamic picks – proof, if proof were needed, that sustainable options taste just as good.

Name: Maison Seed
Description: In a narrow pedestrian street of Millau, near the Fontaine du Mandarins, the dinky Maison Seed is the lair of a globe-trotting couple. A vaulted dining room provides the backdrop to indulgent, fusion-style dishes that incorporate oils, vinegars, sourdough bread, etc, all made in-house, and available to take home. An intimate, eco-conscious restaurant that combines flavours from near and far.

Name: Les 9 névés
Address: 130 route des Balcons, Arêches, Beaufort, 73270, France
Description: From its perch in the upper reaches of Beaufort, this restaurant commands breathtaking views of the village of Arêches and the surrounding peaks. With light wood fittings and a mountain atmosphere, the setting is inviting; the terrace is set against an Alpine backdrop. Local chef Benoît Chauchaix devises a single set menu comprising several courses. It centres on local seasonal produce enhanced by original herbal notes (hogweed, yarrow, meadowsweet). His modern, colourful and fragrant cuisine is absolutely on point. Cindy (his wife) takes care of things front of house. The establishment also has five guestrooms.

Name: Breizh Café Megève
Description: In the heart of the village, on the pedestrian street next to the church where a large Christmas tree is erected in winter, this converted chalet is home to an authentic Breton eatery. Yvon Madec oysters are served alongside Breton pancakes – buckwheat galettes and wheat flour crêpes – enhanced with Japanese or Savoyard touches, for instance "Breizh Roll" with Reblochon cheese, or raw milk raclette galette. Locally sourced produce, cheese from a refiner in nearby Manigod and a fine selection of ciders and wines… plus wallet-friendly prices.

Name: Le Café de la Poste
Description: Home to the post office, bread shop and bistro, this regional-style building embodies the convivial spirit and hospitality of this mountain village. In the morning, locals stop by to pick up their bread while it's still warm or post a letter at the counter decorated with vintage postcards. The wood-panelled interior, Baumann chairs and Badonviller plates may exude the warmth of a traditional inn, but the cuisine cooked up by the young chef-owner is contemporary: butternut squash soup, pattypan squash and hazelnut cazette salad, pork belly cooked in beer, local-style affogato with meadowsweet and Villaz coffee. This hive of activity also serves meat dishes for sharing and generous snacks.

Name: HANADA
Description: On the Left Bank, on Quai Voltaire, this new sushi restaurant is hidden behind a discreet black façade without a sign, simply bearing the number 15. Inside, Masayoshi Hanada (formerly at Sushi B) builds a single omakase menu around exceptional fish – Mediterranean bluefin tuna, Auvergne trout, catch from Brittany – absolutely masterfully cut and prepared. Affording a view of the chef and his assistants meticulously going about their tasks, the superb solid hinoki (Japanese cypress) counter seats just 10 guests. Finely crafted nigiri, maki, soups and binchotan-grilled dishes are served on refined tableware at the intersection of tradition and contemporary design. A short wine list and nine types of sake round off this memorable and special experience.

Name: Jip
Address: 112 rue de la Roquette, Paris, 75011, France
Description: After various stints in kitchens in Australia and France, Korean chef Esu Lee opened Jip – which means "home". In his tiny restaurant with minimalist decor, diners sit cheek to jowl at the counter. He creates a nuanced dialogue between France and Korea: eryngii mushrooms with jalapeño and sauce Béarnaise; duxelles mandu with gochujang; octopus stew with sambal and spring onion sabayon. This signature French-Korean cuisine is a reflection of the chef's intelligence and personality.

Name: Philia
Description: Inside a house oozing character on the pretty Place du Mercadial, this restaurant boasts a charming decor with rough stone walls and an intimate dining area. Chef Thomas Biasutti, originally from Carcassonne, settled here in the Lot after completing stints at several bistronomy restaurants in Toulouse. In his cooking, he showcases local produce – organic vegetables from neighbouring market gardeners, free-range guinea fowl, lamb from Aveyron, pork from Cantal – in contemporary, fresh and well-constructed dishes, with jus and herbs enhancing the classic foundations without complicating them.

Name: HuThoPi
Description: Run by Hugo, Thomas and Pierre – aka HuThoPi – this compact restaurant a stone's throw from the Marché d'Aligre boasts a vibrant, unpolished decor with exposed stone walls, hardwood floors, jars of fermented vegetables and an open kitchen. Having worked at some top eateries, from luxury hotels to trendy restaurants (Le Meurice, Plaza Athénée, Oka, Cobéa, L'Ours etc), the three friends serve vegetable-forward, wholesome and balanced cuisine based on seasonal produce: Marmande tomatoes and piperade espuma, yellowtail crudo and ajoblanco, red mullet with saffron sabayon, Paimpol beans and lardo di Colonnata.

Name: Erre
Description: Set in a stunning estate complete with a golf course and spa, this former hunting lodge has been turned into a hotel and fine dining restaurant. The vaulted dining area with white tablecloths and an understated contemporary decor looks out onto the green. Originally from the Cévennes, Clément Vergeat (formerly at Guy Savoy and Alliance in Paris, Kokkeriet in Copenhagen) has devised a surprise menu that combines produce from Southern Europe with Northern European techniques: Camargue oysters with dried duck; smoked prawn tartare smørbrød style; fermented strawberries and matured lamb. Marine Mateos, an experienced pastry chef and the chef's partner, gracefully handles the desserts and front-of-house service.

Name: L'Andouille
Description: Jean-Pierre and Jarlène Vasseur have opened this welcoming neighbourhood restaurant on the corner of a residential street in his hometown. Trained under Thierry Breton, he cooks up sincere and hearty bistro cuisine with nods to Brittany. Cream of pumpkin soup finished to order, andouille de Guémené and grilled pork belly with buttery mashed potatoes, apple kouign amann or Paris-Brest-Paris in homage to his former mentor: delicious, well-made dishes to be enjoyed in a simple but lively setting.

Name: Chalet Flachaire
Description: This chalet in the upper reaches of the village has been converted into an intimate restaurant by young couple Thomas and Estelle Flachaire, who met while working at the renowned Maison Troisgros in Ouches. The chef boasts a near-perfect CV and his experience makes itself felt in a series of healthy, light dishes crafted from seasonal, often locally sourced ingredients. Served in the form of a single set menu with poetically named courses, his cuisine embraces smoky, fruity and zesty flavours, in tune with the zeitgeist. A warm welcome awaits.

Name: Maison Akène
Description: Isma'il and Inès Guerre-Genton (formerly of Empreinte in Lambersart) can now be found in Ardres. Behind a spruce façade on the town's main square, the interior is elegantly understated: a palette of cream and beige tones, brushed walls, sand-coloured light fixtures and immaculate crockery. In the kitchen, the chef remains true to his style, with a single set menu that echoes the stages of a flower's development – bud, bloom, achene – and personal dishes with bold flavours. The top-notch ingredients are local and seasonal (line-caught fish, chicken from Licques Volaille), the presentation is always meticulous and the genuine commitment behind each dish is palpable. The sauces are a delicious leitmotif – green pepper on the starter, delicate fish jus, an intense poultry jus – revealing painstaking work behind the scenes.

Name: Le M - Domaine de Montagne
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: Set in the Vosges mountains, surrounded by pristine wilderness, this luxurious chalet hotel complete with a spa is conducive to truly unwinding and recharging. High up in these mountains, tranquillity, and an almost monastic atmosphere reigns – indeed the site was the Ermitage du Père Joseph prior to becoming a small ski resort. Fine dining has been brought to this unique setting by Benoit Potdevin (Le K at Domaine de la Klauss, MICHELIN-starred in Moselle), supported by a local chef. Inspired by regional terroir, their menus (one of which is vegetarian) are a feast of precision and refined flavours: gently cooked trout, chanterelles and a silky vin jaune sauce; Vosges pigeon served in two courses, turnips and cherry condiment. Beautiful dishes served by a congenial and efficient team.

Name: Gourmand
Description: On the premises of his previous restaurant, Guillaume Scheer has opened this aptly named bistro for all the gourmands out there. In a cosy setting with a laid-back atmosphere, diners tuck into mouth-watering traditional cuisine, eg frogs' legs with parsley sauce, duck foie gras, sea bass with hollandaise sauce or rib steak with Choron sauce. These delicious, generous dishes are expertly prepared by his former sous-chef. There is a quiet terrace to the rear.

Name: Le Sonney
Description: Sonney, near Place de Jaude, is the surname of the chef's great-grandmother and references the sonnet with its fourteen-line structure. The restaurant is run by chefs Caroline Vallance and Benjamin Faure, a couple who are 100% committed to this very personal project of theirs. Everything is made from scratch, from the bread to the ice cream; the decor of this intimate setting, designed from recycled materials, is also their own. Benjamin Faure composes a 14-dish "poem" inspired by family memories and the Auvergne terroir. A sincere and down-to-earth place.

Name: L'Artémisia
Address: 20 rue de la Parrachée, Val-Cénis, 73500, France
Description: This hotel restaurant in the heart of the Haute-Maurienne and Vanoise areas is the perfect place to recharge your batteries after a mountain hike. The interior design may look simple, but the food served here is a far cry from your average resort fare, as chef Victor Heiries strives to treat diners to something unexpected. His wonderfully fresh surprise menu varies according to the ingredients available on a given day: Arctic char, Aubrac Wagyu beef, Duroc pork belly or Termignon blue cheese – fantastic. Aromatic herbs and wild plants elevate the vegetable-forward dishes. There are rooms for overnight guests.

Name: Thelma
Description: Chef Jean-François Pantaleon has opened a second restaurant a few metres from Roza, his fine dining restaurant, also in the Graslin area, near the Musée Dobrée archaeology museum. This vintage bistro has a friendly atmosphere where you can enjoy a down-to-earth meal. In addition to the reasonably priced lunch menu, classic suggestions are written on the mirrors: eggs mayonnaise, terrine, calf's head or veal chop with mashed potatoes. The evening menu features additional dishes designed for sharing, although you might not want to. Simple, traditional, well-made food – the perfect complement to Roza.

Name: Lulu le Bistrot
Description: The building is modern, but inside the establishment the decor leans into an old-fashioned bistro theme, which is also evident in the dishes: eggs mayonnaise, terrine de campagne, steak with peppercorns, chocolate mousse or île flottante. At the helm, chef Ludovic Pouzelgues (Lulu Rouget) spoils diners at this relaxed restaurant in the Création neighbourhood, a stone's throw from the Les Machines de l'Île attraction. At lunchtime, good traditional home cooking is served at wallet-friendly prices, perfect for a meal between visits.

Name: Les Loges
Address: Cour des Loges, 6 rue du Bœuf, Lyon, 69005, France
Description: After a prodigious makeover, Les Loges, located in a magnificent Renaissance edifice, has reopened in the heart of historic Lyon. The romantic vibe, depicted by a Florentine courtyard flanked by galleries, columns and spiral staircases and protected by a steel and glass roof, mingles a respect for heritage with subtle modern details. Ever faithful, Anthony Bonnet continues to enhance regional produce, in which veggies play a central role, courtesy of delicate craftsmanship. From the starter to the dessert, each dish is crisp and vibrant, enhanced by grassy, peppery or piquant notes. The tableware, the work of local artisans and chosen by the chef himself, adds a final flourish to this festival that is more than worthy of our esteem.

Name: Les Dodus
Description: Here in the Cahors vineyards, overlooking the Lot, this couple, with stints in prestigious MICHELIN-starred kitchens under their belts, have struck the perfect note in their convivial bistro. On weekday lunchtimes, a single, simplified set menu brings in the regulars; the rest of the time, a short à la carte menu and a five-course set menu (excellent value) are served. Antoine Pépin cooks fresh, precise cuisine; Amandine extends a warm welcome and provides expert wine recommendations. Local produce, tableware by artisans, wines from the Lot: the terroir is showcased with sincerity. Booking advisable.

Name: Métive
Description: After Baston in Bordeaux, chef Julien Borie and baker Pauline Celle have taken the same enticing concept of a restaurant-bakery, and rooted it even more in the terroir. The chef, who is from these parts, thus has an opportunity to work with local artisans and seafood. The result is confident and masterfully executed bistronomy cuisine, incorporating precisely prepared local produce – particularly the matured fish that can be seen in a display case in the dining area. The bakery turns out natural sourdough breads using organic flour and drawing on genuine artisanal expertise. The decor features stone walls, vintage posters and pale wood furniture; you pass through the bakery to get to the restaurant with a counter and open kitchen.

Name: Le Camélia
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: In this 19C château built in the brick and white stone that is typical in northern France, the spruce and welcoming decor charms with its blend of old and new: first, a cosy bar that leads on to a dining room flooded with light from the windows on two sides, and giving onto a wooded park. The à la carte menu features carefully selected ingredients and precise, flavourful cuisine, cooked to perfection. A whole lobster, shelled and roasted, is served pearly white in the middle: the tail firm and flavourful, the claws tender, with crunchy or melt-in-the-mouth vegetables, a fragrant sauce with herring roe and a rich potato mash. The turbot in a beautifully golden bread crust is served with baby spinach leaves and a creamy beurre blanc sauce. The delicious dishes are straightforward and full of personality.

Name: La Bagatelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: La Chaumière's bistro is run by Laurent Barberot, a chef with impressive references (Plaza Athénée, Clos des Sens, Bastide Saint-Antoine). During the week, operating in the same contemporary space as the fine dining restaurant, he serves up indulgent modern cuisine. It is both precise and generous, eg soft-yolked egg with mushrooms simmered in their frothy jus, or duck breast accompanied by roasted figs and butternut squash. On sunny days, tables are set up on a pleasant terrace facing the garden. On weekends, the fine dining restaurant takes over with its single set menu.

Name: L'O de Source
Description: Up until 1969, passenger trains stopped in this former station, as the old railway line visible in the well-tended garden bears witness. Today this authentic abode is home to a pleasant restaurant, where you will be pampered by Karine and Xavier. She seamlessly supervises the service, while he pays a culinary tribute to the Liège region and the seasons. An example: leeks from a local market gardener or venison from the Ardennes forests are cooked to perfection and flanked by intense sauces and playful sides in a score that is the epitome of vibrant. Just the ticket if you feel in need of a spot of TLC!

Name: Le Castellane - Château Le Prieuré
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: Le Castellane, part of the Château du Prieuré, serves modern fare that keeps tabs on the seasons and is predominantly local. You can choose between the Empire-inspired dining room or the terrace overlooking the Loire. Each of the guestrooms is individually appointed and fully in keeping with the historic character of the valley of kings.

Name: L'Ouvrière
Address: 5 bis place de la Mairie, Montamisé, 86360, France
Description: Housed in an inviting building in the heart of the village of Montamisé, this welcoming restaurant continues to polish its concept. Ludovic Dumont's purposely creative approach is primarily focused on fish and seafood and vegetables, using which he devises multi-course blind menus that are aligned with the seasons. The space is intimate, bright and spruce, and the service is very cordial. There are three welcoming gîtes to extend your stay here.

Name: Le Pré Fillet
Address: 784 route du Pré Fillet aux Molunes, Septmoncel-les-Molunes, 39310, France
Description: This former farmstead, turned into a restaurant three generations ago, stands in a landscape of meadows and woodland at an altitude of 1200 metres. Simplicity and generosity are the bywords of this establishment which shines the spotlight on the region’s knockout produce. The chef crafts wholesome, hearty fare: calf sweetbread flambéed in Jura marc and asparagus in flaky pastry or melt-in-the-mouth knuckle of lamb braised in assorted veggies. To be sampled and enjoyed in a dining area overlooking the unspoiled countryside. Diners are pampered by attentive staff.

Name: Keri
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Shoes must be removed
Description: The name ‘Keri’, an archaic term for ‘duck’, is in tribute to the ancient and unbroken culture of duck cuisine. The menu features a wide variety of cuts, including dishes that let diners enjoy the freshness of gizzard or liver. Roast duck is suffused in the aroma of the charcoal grill; duck hot pot is cooked with stock rich in the flavour of duck fat. Western preparations, including pâté and tartare, are available as well. The chef’s deep study of duck cuisine shows in the breadth of the menu.

Name: das Schrei
Description: Hosts Jakob Schmid and Daniel Reifecker form an owner-and-chef duo who clearly take great pleasure in their work. They serve a creative surprise menu comprising four to seven courses, with a vegetarian version available by pre-order. The ingredients, which are of outstanding quality, are sourced primarily from the region. Friendly, adept service includes personal presentations of some dishes by the kitchen team. For pairings, there are wines, non-alcoholic options or a combination of both. The excellent wine list highlights bottles from Austria, Germany and France. The interior is stylish and chic, combining clean modern lines with warm, soothing tones. The focal point is the open kitchen in the middle of the room, where the chef's table is set up to offer a special up-close experience. In good weather, they also set up tables on the terrace.

Name: Flores Raras
Description: This centrally located restaurant, formerly known as El Poblet, changed its name and took a new direction under the leadership of chef Carolina Álvarez, a native of Mexico, who spent six years working as the right-hand woman of award-winning chef Quique Dacosta at his iconic three-star restaurant. In their own words, Flores Raras ‘shares the creative DNA and gastronomic rigour of the three-Michelin-starred Quique Dacosta Restaurant in Dénia’.Here, their elaborate contemporary offering, built on technical mastery, aesthetic sensitivity and a close relationship with the product, revolves around three tasting menus: 1988 (available from Tuesday to Thursday, for dinner only, and on Friday at lunchtime), Esencia and Flores Raras, always with the option of wine pairing. Working alongside her on the project to maintain high standards and enhance the experience are Delia Claure, who manages the dining room, and Hernán Menno, the sommelier.

Name: JAJA
Description: The vibe here is lively, loud and hip, yet an intimate atmosphere reigns in the minimalist interior done out in a trendy rustic style. The menu revolves around modern plates for sharing – based on organic ingredients, dishes such as "mussels, spaghetti, XO sauce" or "pork belly, red cabbage, horseradish" are deliciously prepared and complemented by a fine selection of natural wines. The owner is a sommelier – let her guide you!

Name: Arc Restaurant
Description: If you want to make a reservation here, you'll have to be quick! The urban-minimalist restaurant has only a few tables, and they are in high demand. In the open kitchen, a pescetarian set menu comprising 10 small courses is devised. The creative dishes – eg "oyster, potato and gooseberry" or "king oyster mushroom, radicchio and elderflower" – may appear minimalist at first glance, but they are complex and full of detail. A vegetarian variant of the set menu is also available. They set great store by select seasonal ingredients, the majority of which are sourced from suppliers operating just outside of Hamburg – you can read about all of them in the book ("Freundebuch") the restaurant has put together. The well-curated wine list is worth browsing; wine pairings, or house-made alcohol-free pairings, have been devised to accompany the set menu.

Name: Brasserie Tafern
Description: Elegant yet accessible – a concept designed with your comfort and well-being in mind, and a wonderful alternative to Epicures, the fine dining restaurant here at the Boutique Hotel Residenz Winkler. Executive Chef Daniel Pape is the man responsible for both kitchens, and the classic and Mediterranean cuisine impresses with its finesse and lightness. It can be sampled from an appealing à la carte selection (eg "artichoke consommé, tomato concassé" or " Senfrostbraten (pork roast with mustard, rainbow vegetables, red onion"), which is complemented by seasonal daily specials. In fine weather, diners can enjoy the view of the Chiemgau Alps from the magnificent terrace (Bergterrasse). Good to know: It opens at 3pm, and at noon on Sundays. Fun fact: The name "Tafern" is a throwback to the establishment's roots – as far back as the early 15C there was a tavern on this site.

Name: Gestütsgasthof Offenhausen
Description: On the idyllic grounds of Marbach stud farm, which is steeped in history, the centuries-old steward's house has been turned into a tasteful and cosy restaurant. Here, chef-patron Marc Winter serves up his regional and seasonal dishes, to which he adds just the right dose of modernity. Game is hunted by the chef or his hunter friends to appear in tempting dishes such as roast venison shoulder in juniper cream or cordon bleu of wild boar loin with a hazelnut crumb topping. The menu also includes smaller bites. The lovely terrace commands a view of the surrounding historical buildings including the 13C monastery church, which now houses the stud farm museum (Gestütsmuseum). Incidentally, the source of the Lauter River is also located on the site.

Name: Assonica
Address: via Don Santo Carminati 9, Sorisole, 24010, Italy
Description: Situated in the hills just beyond Bergamo, this smart, elegant and well-run restaurant has the Manzoni brothers (Alex and Vittorio) at the helm in the kitchen, where they create some of the most interesting cuisine in the region, while the capable Giovanna Danzo oversees the excellent service in the dining room. Creative and surprising, the dishes here are striking for their complex and original flavours, which combine vegetables with a clever use of herbs and spices without overwhelming the palate. The chargrilled veal sweetbreads (slightly crunchy on the outside and soft inside) are delicious, served with a selection of mushrooms and a fir extract that provides a hint of bitterness. There’s a strong focus on sourcing local ingredients in order to create cuisine which is both contemporary and sustainable at the same time.

Name: SUSHO
Description: Just outside Geneva, this small sushi joint is frequently packed to the seams. Two young chefs wield their high-precision skills, rolling out impeccable nigiris, lemony hamachi, flambéed salmon. Ten out of ten for their spicy Crispy Shrimp Roll and the rich, comforting Shoyu Ramen. Sheltered terrace, tightly packed tables and a vibrant energy depict this on-the-ball eatery!

Name: HYG Restaurant & Bar
Description: The name "HYG" is a nod to the Danish word and concept of hygge, which describes the combination of cosiness, conviviality and culinary enjoyment. The motivated young team and trendy, modern decor foster just that relaxed, feel-good atmosphere. Choose between a sharing menu for two or more people and an à la carte menu with dishes such as "yellowfin tuna, tomato, daikon", "linguine, wild-caught Argentine red shrimp, Amalfi lemon" or "crispy Alpstein chicken, roasted vegetable cream, smoked almonds". The wine list, which comprises around 500 items, also includes well-known names and great wines. The space is done out with a Nordic-inspired aesthetic that is bright and cheerful, and the service is pleasingly laid-back and professional. Note for motorists: You can park in a public car park a few minutes' walk away.

Name: La Scarpetta
Description: As of July 2025, it has been possible to enjoy La Scarpetta's truly delicious and authentic Italian food in Zurich as well as in St Moritz. The appealing à la carte selection includes dishes such as carpaccio di gambero rosso and ossobucco & risotto allo zafferano. There is also a tempting lunch menu. The cosy interior sports beautiful wood panelling. In one of the two separate dining areas, there are also a few spots at the bar, on which an impressive espresso machine and a large wine cooler catch the eye. A pleasingly lively atmosphere reigns, and the service is friendly and relaxed. There is an excellent, high-calibre wine list. The small terrace is inviting in summer.

Name: Maza
Description: At Maza, the food tells a tale of travel and love between Robin and Julien Burnier, a cosmopolitan couple with stints in Japan, America and France. Together they sign a vibrant, indulgent score that involves dishes to share of European, Asian and Oriental influences, like tartare of trout on polenta chips or ginger-laced tataki of rump steak. Meticulously sourced local produce, well curated wine cellar and a pleasant patio in a pedestrian neighbourhood – bookings essential.

Name: Les Jardins de la Tour
Address: Rue de la Placette 16, Rossinière, 1658, Switzerland
Description: Ludovic Garnier (chef) and Christelle Huguenin (front of house) welcome guests into a deliciously inviting 19C house appointed in a wood-rich, chic rustic vein where a wood-burning stove is lit in winter. Diners choose between one of two menus with three or four courses that aim to highlight fresh, regional produce: seared foie gras with peaches, freshly caught zander and a chocolate mint delight to finish. A snug cocoon with small tables and spot-on service set the scene for a truly relaxing meal. Bookings recommended, particularly if you want to dine alfresco.

Name: Berghuus Radons
Description: The magnificent location alone – against a stunning mountain backdrop – makes it worth coming to Berghuus. The interior decor is just as charming: carefully restored, the historical timber house oozes charm with its upscale aesthetic combining rustic style and modern touches. The cuisine features regional ingredients, the provenance of which is stated on the menu. In the evening, choose from six dishes, half of which are vegetarian, to put together a three-course meal. There is also a small à la carte menu featuring traditional regional classics. And be sure to take a look at the wine list, which includes some well-known names. The cosy guestrooms are in keeping with the inviting feel of the whole place – making an overnight stay an appealing option. N.B. You will need a permit to drive to the property, which is accessible via narrow roads – please enquire in advance!

Name: Genießerei am Markt - Steiermark(t)dinner by Alexander Posch
Description: This rustic market stall on Kaiser-Josef-Platz is the rather distinctive setting in which Alexander Posch's sophisticated cuisine is served. In the evening, the "Styrian Market Dinner" set menu usually consists of 10 courses of different sizes. The small open kitchen sends out dishes such as "beetroot, tarragon, trout" and "venison, chanterelles, redcurrants" – dishes that impress with their expressiveness and finesse, are stripped back and at the same time beautifully crafted. They are based on seasonal and regional ingredients sourced from the market right outside the door. Julia Glanzer and her front-of-house team create a pleasant, relaxed atmosphere with their cordial approach and expertise – even the chef helps to serve and presents his dishes. The somewhat simpler lunch menu is also of interest.

Name: Gasthaus Fuchs
Description: After completing stints at renowned establishments, Thomas Fuchs has brought a breath of fresh air to his parents' restaurant in the middle of this Burgenland village. His delicious dishes range from classics such as schnitzel, Tafelspitz (beef boiled in broth) and the like to "salmon trout fillet, chervil root, fregola" or "goose liver, fig, chocolate, Buchtel (sweet yeast buns)". In addition to an à la carte selection, there is also a three- to six-course tasting menu in the evening and a smaller set menu at lunchtime. The well-kept dining area (divided into rooms – some with a rustic touch, some more modern) is complemented by a pleasant terrace in summer.

Name: Zimmerl
Address: Heidenreichsteiner Straße 28, Waidhofen an der Thaya, 3830, Austria
Description: An interesting concept, of the kind you might expect to find in a big city rather than in the tranquil Waldviertel region. The design is upscale and chic, with nice low lighting and just four tables making for an intimate atmosphere (the name "Zimmerl" is very apt). The set menu comprises 23 small dishes, so you need to allow plenty of time – but the 4hr or so flies by, because the cuisine, peppered with sophisticated contrasts and original ideas, simply makes for a fun experience! The dishes are complex and packed with flavour – think fresh Tyrolean Alpine prawns made into a delicate, creamy tartare and perfectly finished with togarashi, or fantastic hand-dived scallops with a beautiful roasted note, served on a caramelised white cabbage foam and refined with Tasmanian mountain pepper. Based on classic French cuisine (the sauces are wonderful!), they recipes combine the flavours of the Waldviertel with Japanese influences.
